issues.title: MCP OAuth (interactive): authorization code is received and the success page is served, but the code->token exchange never runs — server stuck "Connecting"

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

For a remote HTTP MCP server using Entra ID OAuth (Azure DevOps remote MCP,
`https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>`), the interactive CLI completes the browser
round-trip but never exchanges the authorization code for a token.

Observed with Copilot CLI running **inside WSL2** (Ubuntu 26.04 on a Windows 11
host). I have not tested native Windows or native Linux, so I cannot say whether
this is WSL-specific — see the note at the end.

Observed sequence:

1. On startup the CLI auto-connects, gets the expected `401` with
   `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://mcp.dev.azure.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/<org>"`.
2. Metadata discovery and dynamic client registration succeed — a registration
   record is written to `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/<key>.json`, with
   `authorizationServerUrl`, `clientId: aebc6443-996d-45c2-90f0-388ff96faa56`,
   `redirectUri: http://127.0.0.1:41003/`.
3. The CLI logs `Opening browser for <server> authentication...` then
   `Requesting access token for <server>...`.
4. I complete the sign-in. The browser lands on
   `http://127.0.0.1:41003/?nonce=<nonce>&code=<code>` and **the CLI's own
   callback page renders** ("Authorization Successful"). So the code reaches
   the CLI's listener.
5. Nothing further happens. The TUI stays on "Authenticating: <server>" /
   "Connecting to <server>...". No `<key>.tokens.json` is ever written, and no
   log line is emitted after this point.

The `<key>.verifier` file is **not** removed. Per the runtime's own state
machine (`MCP OAuth token exchange completed; saving tokens` ->
`MCP OAuth tokens saved; clearing code verifier`), a surviving verifier means
the exchange never completed successfully.

The MCP transport worker meanwhile keeps cycling:

```
[ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed,
  when Client(OAuthChallenge { www_authenticate_header: "...oauth-protected-resource/<org>",
  response: McpOAuthHttpResponse { status_code: 401, ... } })
```

### The failure is in the CLI, not the environment

I reproduced the identical flow manually with a small script — **same client ID,
same scope, same `vscode.dev` relay, same loopback pattern** — and it succeeds
on the first attempt:

```
TOKEN EXCHANGE: HTTP 200 SUCCESS
  scope        : https://mcp.dev.azure.com/Ado.Mcp.Tools https://mcp.dev.azure.com/.default
  token_type   : Bearer
  expires_in   : 4102
  refresh_token: present
```

Driving the MCP server with that token also works:

```
[initialize] HTTP 200   serverInfo: {"name": "AzureDevOps.Mcp", "version": "1.0.0.0"}
[tools/list] HTTP 200   tool count: 43
```

Writing that token into `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/<key>.tokens.json` in the
CLI's own schema (`accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `expiresAt`, `requestedScope`,
`scope`) makes the server connect normally. `grant_type=refresh_token` renewal
against the same endpoint also works.

So tenant config, consent, scopes, app registration, the `vscode.dev` relay,
loopback reachability and the MCP server are all confirmed working. The only
step that fails is the CLI's own code->token exchange.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`:
   ```json
   {"mcpServers":{"ado-remote-mcp":{"type":"http","url":"https://mcp.dev.azure.com/<org>"}}}
   ```
2. Start `copilot`. It auto-connects and begins the OAuth flow.
3. Run `/mcp auth ado-remote-mcp`, press `c`, open the URL, complete sign-in.
4. Browser shows the CLI's "Authorization Successful" page.
5. `ls ~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/` — no `.tokens.json`; the `.verifier`
   remains. The TUI never leaves the connecting state.

### Expected behavior

After the callback is received, the CLI proceeds to `exchanging_code`, stores
the tokens, clears the verifier, and connects the server.

### Additional context

- **No diagnostics are available for this step.** `RUST_LOG` is accepted but
  produces no additional output, and the process log contains nothing at all
  between the callback and the stall. The runtime has specific failure strings
  (`ExchangeResponseFailure`, `failed to clear OAuth code verifier after
  authorization failure`) but none reach the log file. Surfacing the token
  endpoint's response on failure would make this self-diagnosable.
- `ctrl+g` (device code) does not help: `mcp.dev.azure.com` advertises no
  device-code support, so the CLI logs `Server does not support device code
  flow - falling back to browser` and retries the browser path.
- The callback arrives as `?nonce=<nonce>&code=<code>` with **no `state`
  parameter** — `vscode.dev/redirect` consumes `state` (the CLI encodes the
  nonce in the state fragment). If the handler validates `state`, that may be
  relevant. Unverified.
- Possibly related: #4994, #5192, #4695 — all ACP-mode or cross-session reuse.
  This one is plain interactive mode on first sign-in.
- **Environment caveat (WSL2).** This was only observed with the CLI running
  inside WSL2; I have not reproduced it on native Windows or native Linux, so I
  cannot confirm whether the platform matters. Two WSL-specific points, both
  ruled out as causes:
  - WSL has no browser launcher by default (`xdg-open`/`wslview` absent), so the
    CLI's `Opening browser...` step is a silent no-op until `BROWSER` is set.
    That produces a *separate* earlier symptom (no prompt at all). After adding a
    launcher the browser opens correctly, and the stall described above persists.
  - Windows→WSL loopback forwarding works. An independent listener inside WSL
    received the browser's redirect on `127.0.0.1` (including the follow-up
    `favicon.ico` request), so the callback path itself is sound.

issues.title: Regression: default-context Sol models rejected before first prompt after tool definitions grow from 15K to ~260K tokens

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Beginning around 2026-10-14, `gpt-5.6-sol` and `gpt-6.1-sol` at the default context tier fail before accepting a prompt:

```
compaction_static_context_blocked: Static system messages and tool definitions exceed the model's usable context budget. Reduce static context or switch to a larger-context model.
```

Selecting `long_context` immediately makes the same model, session, MCP configuration, and prompt work. Usage telemetry then reports `maxPromptTokens: 922000` and approximately 258K-260K tool-definition tokens.

This did not occur previously with the same broad tool configuration. A successful October 9 session on CLI 1.0.92 used `gpt-5.6-sol` with the default tier and reported 615 tools / 15,457 tool-definition tokens. The current configuration reports 676 tools / approximately 260,000 tool-definition tokens: roughly 10% more tools but a 17x increase in tool tokens.

The local standalone MCP configuration was unchanged during this period. A historical default-tier session that worked before the rollout also failed with the same warning when resumed on October 14.

### Affected versions

- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.93, 1.0.97, and 1.0.98
- macOS 26.7.1, Apple Silicon
- Models: `gpt-5.6-sol` and `gpt-6.1-sol`
- Agency versions observed during the rollout window: 2026.10.13.x and 2026.10.14.3

Because 1.0.93 also began failing after the rollout window, this may involve remotely supplied tool catalogs, Agency integration, or context-budget metadata rather than only a 1.0.97 client change.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start Copilot CLI with a broad enterprise MCP/tool configuration.
2. Select `gpt-6.1-sol` with the default context tier.
3. Submit a short prompt.
4. Observe `compaction_static_context_blocked`, followed by `No response was returned`.
5. Switch only the context tier to `long_context`.
6. Resubmit the prompt; it succeeds.
7. Repeat with `gpt-5.6-sol`; default context fails and `long_context` succeeds.

### Expected behavior

The default tier should continue working with a tool configuration that worked previously. At minimum, the CLI should:

- avoid offering a model/tier combination that cannot fit its own static context;
- lazy-load or defer tool schemas instead of eagerly injecting hundreds of definitions;
- identify the largest static-context contributors;
- clearly report the effective default-tier prompt budget.

### Additional evidence

- October 9, CLI 1.0.92: 615 tools, 15,457 tool tokens, default-tier `gpt-5.6-sol` worked.
- October 14-15: approximately 258K-260K tool tokens; default-tier Sol models fail before a model request.
- `long_context` reports a 922K prompt allowance and succeeds without changing the tool setup.
- Related issues: #5042 and #3542.

Please investigate whether tool schemas or descriptions changed around October 13-14, whether more definitions are now eagerly materialized, or whether static-context token accounting/default-tier reserves changed. I can provide redacted event excerpts or confidential debug logs privately.

issues.title: cli cannot interact with sandbox

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

labels.name: area:enterprise
labels.description: GitHub Enterprise (GHE/GHES) support, org policies, and enterprise settings

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

# Copilot CLI sandbox enforcement preflight fails with `CreateProcessW` error 2 on supported Windows host

## Describe the bug

On a managed Windows 11 device whose enterprise policy requires local sandboxing (`sandbox.enabled: true`, `failIfUnavailable: true`, `allowBypass: false`), every session is blocked at the sandbox enforcement preflight:

```text
This session is blocked because your organization's sandbox policy requires enforcement, but the sandbox is unavailable: backend_error: CreateProcessW failed with error code 2 (0x00000002). (CreateProcessW(PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_SECURITY_ENVIRONMENT) failed: WIN32_ERROR(2) (working directory: C:\Users\<user>\sandboxes\test (from process.cwd))). Start a new session after resolving the sandbox problem.
```

The host supports the sandbox. Outside Copilot, `@microsoft/mxc-sdk` 1.0.0 (the version bundled in Copilot 1.0.105) and 1.0.1 both successfully launch `cmd.exe`, Windows PowerShell 5.1, and PowerShell 7.6.9 on the same machine.

The standalone MXC tests use the same working directory and the same filesystem/network policy reported by `/sandbox policy`.

The failure has only been reproduced through Copilot's sandbox enforcement preflight. Because Copilot does not log the preflight image path or command line, I cannot determine which path is producing `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`.

**Important**: Local sandboxing works successfully on the same device when the enterprise-managed sandbox settings are not applied. The failure occurs when the enterprise-managed sandbox configuration is present and Copilot performs its managed sandbox enforcement/revalidation preflight.
## Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105, installed via WinGet (`GitHub.Copilot`).

WinGet reports:

```text
Name: GitHub Copilot CLI
Id: GitHub.Copilot
Version: 1.0.105
Installer Type: wix
Dependency: Microsoft.PowerShell >= 7.0.0
```

The standalone installation is located under:

```text
%LOCALAPPDATA%\GitHubCopilotCLI
```

and contains:

```text
copilot.exe
copilot-taskbar-activator.exe
GitHubCopilotCLI.sparse.msix
```

The same failure occurs through the VS Code Copilot shim and when invoking the standalone `copilot.exe` directly.

The 1.0.105-1 prerelease bundles the same `mxc-sdk` 1.0.0.



### Affected version

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use Windows 11 Enterprise 25H2, OS build 26200.9711.
2. Apply these managed settings from a GHE.com tenant:
   - `sandbox.enabled=true`
   - `sandbox.failIfUnavailable=true`
   - `sandbox.allowBypass=false`
3. Change to an empty local folder.
4. Run Copilot CLI and send any message.
5. Observe that the session is blocked by the sandbox enforcement preflight.

This occurs:

- on every new session;
- after restarting Windows;
- from different working directories;
- through the VS Code Copilot shim; and
- when invoking the standalone executable directly:

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\GitHubCopilotCLI\copilot.exe"
```

## Expected behavior

The sandboxed session starts.

If the enforcement preflight cannot launch its process, the error or debug log should identify the image path and command line passed to the process creation operation.

## Additional diagnostics

### MXC platform support

Using `@microsoft/mxc-sdk/v1`:

```text
getPlatformSupport():
  isSupported: true
  isolationTier: "base-container"
```

`probe()` returns `base-container` with no warnings.

The following capabilities are reported as available:

```text
baseContainerApiPresent
baseContainerSupportsDenyPaths
baseContainerSupportsEnumeratePaths
baseContainerSupportsIngressHostLoopbackAllow
baseContainerSupportsIdentitylessLoopbackProxy
```

### Standalone MXC using Copilot's sandbox policy

A standalone MXC test uses:

- all 21 paths reported by `/sandbox policy`;
- egress allow;
- host loopback allow; and
- the same working directory that fails from Copilot.

Results:

| Program | mxc-sdk 1.0.0 | mxc-sdk 1.0.1 |
|---|---:|---:|
| `cmd.exe` | exit 0 | exit 0 |
| Windows PowerShell 5.1 | exit 0 | exit 0 |
| PowerShell 7.6.9 | exit 0 | exit 0 |

This is significant because `mxc-sdk` 1.0.0 is also the version bundled with the affected Copilot CLI release.

### PowerShell resolution checked

PowerShell 7.6.9 is installed per-user without relying on the WindowsApps alias:

```text
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe
```

`Get-Command pwsh.exe -All` returns this executable before:

```text
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe
```

and:

```powershell
pwsh.exe --version
```

returns:

```text
PowerShell 7.6.9
```

The executable reports product/file version `7.6.9.500`.

The standalone MXC test successfully launches this unpackaged PowerShell executable.

### VS Code shim eliminated as cause

Both Copilot installations are visible on PATH:

```text
C:\Program Files\Microsoft VS Code\bin\copilot-shim\copilot.exe
C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\GitHubCopilotCLI\copilot.exe
```

The VS Code shim is normally resolved first.

However, explicitly bypassing the shim and running:

```powershell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\GitHubCopilotCLI\copilot.exe"
```

produces the same sandbox enforcement failure.

Therefore, the failure is not specific to invoking Copilot through the VS Code shim.

### Other troubleshooting already performed

None of the following changed the error:

- Installed PowerShell 7.6.9.
- Put an unpackaged PowerShell 7 executable ahead of the WindowsApps alias on PATH.
- Verified that the real `pwsh.exe` is selected by `Get-Command` and `where.exe`.
- Added `C:\` and the PowerShell directory to `sandbox.userPolicy.filesystem.readonlyPaths`.
- Set `sandbox.auth.git=false`.
- Set `sandbox.auth.gh=false`.
- Set `allowLocalNetwork=false`.
- Confirmed those settings through `/sandbox policy`.
- Used different working directories.
- Restarted Windows and started fresh sessions.
- Bypassed the VS Code shim and invoked the standalone CLI directly.
- Reproduced equivalent MXC launches successfully using both mxc-sdk 1.0.0 and 1.0.1.

## Logs

With `--log-level all`, the relevant output is:

```text
[WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::services::sandbox_service] managed sandbox enforcement revalidation refused the session {"error":"...CreateProcessW failed with error code 2..."}

[ERROR] [sandbox] enforcement preflight failed: Error: ...same message...

[WARNING] Failed to process event type 'session.sandbox_enforcement_blocked' for timeline reconstruction: Error: Unhandled event type in timeline: session.sandbox_enforcement_blocked
```

No image path or command line for the failed preflight process appears in the log.

## Current findings

The tests appear to rule out a general lack of MXC/base-container support on the host:

- MXC reports the platform as supported.
- MXC `probe()` succeeds.
- mxc-sdk 1.0.0 successfully creates sandboxed processes.
- mxc-sdk 1.0.1 successfully creates sandboxed processes.
- The Copilot-reported sandbox policy works in the standalone MXC test.
- The working directory works in the standalone MXC test.
- `cmd.exe`, Windows PowerShell, and PowerShell 7.6.9 all launch successfully through MXC.
- PowerShell 7 resolves to the real executable rather than the WindowsApps alias.
- Bypassing the VS Code shim does not change the result.

The remaining difference I have been unable to inspect is **the exact image, command line, and process creation configuration used by Copilot's managed sandbox enforcement preflight**.


### Expected behavior

Sandbox works without error

### Additional context

_No response_

issues.title: disable-model-invocation: true makes a skill unreachable, not manual-only (Skill not found on explicit invocation)

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Summary

A project skill whose `SKILL.md` frontmatter carries `disable-model-invocation: true` is not reachable from the CLI at all. `copilot skill list` shows it under **Project skills**, but the model's `skill()` tool returns `Skill not found: <name>`, so an explicit user request for the skill fails too.

In Claude Code (where the field originated) and in Cursor, `disable-model-invocation: true` means "the model may not select this skill on its own; the user can still invoke it by name". The CLI appears to treat it as "do not expose this skill at all", which leaves no way to run the skill.

### Version / environment

- `GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.79`
- Linux (Fedora, kernel 7.0.13)
- Skill directory: `<repo>/.github/skills/socratic-method/`, inside a git repository

### Reproduction

Using a published skill that ships the field ([socratic-method](https://github.com/grammy-jiang/socratic-method)):

```bash
pipx install socratic-method
cd "$(mktemp -d)" && git init -q .
socratic-method setup copilot --copy   # writes .github/skills/socratic-method/
```

1. The CLI discovers it:

```console
$ copilot skill list
Project skills:
  socratic-method - Interrogates the user's idea with disciplined Socratic questioning until hidden assumptions, ...
```

2. The model cannot reach it, even when named explicitly:

```console
$ copilot -p 'Use the /socratic-method skill. Before asking me anything, reply with exactly
  one line of JSON: {"loaded": true|false, "path": "<SKILL.md path>"}' --allow-all-tools --no-color

✗ skill(socratic-method) Skill not found: socratic-method

{"loaded": false, "path": ""}
```

3. Delete the `disable-model-invocation: true` line from `.github/skills/socratic-method/SKILL.md` and re-run the same prompt — the skill loads normally:

```console
● skill(socratic-method)

{"loaded": true, "path": "/tmp/tmp.XXXX/.github/skills/socratic-method/SKILL.md"}
```

### Isolation

Same sandbox, same prompt, only the frontmatter differs:

| Frontmatter | Result |
|---|---|
| `disable-model-invocation: true` + `user-invocable: true` | `Skill not found` |
| `disable-model-invocation: true` only | `Skill not found` |
| neither key | loads normally |

`disable-model-invocation` alone reproduces it; `user-invocable` is not involved. YAML comments elsewhere in the frontmatter are present in all three cases and are not a factor.

### Expected

`disable-model-invocation: true` should keep the skill out of automatic selection while leaving it invocable when the user names it — matching the semantics of the agent that introduced the field, and matching what the field is for: skills with side effects, or long interactive workflows, that should only run on request.

If the CLI intends different semantics, that is worth documenting. [Adding agent skills for GitHub Copilot CLI](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/add-skills) documents only `name`, `description`, `license` and `allowed-tools`, so today the behavior is silent: the skill installs fine, lists fine, and only fails at the moment of use.

### Impact

Portable skills written against the shared `SKILL.md` format and published for several agents carry this field to get manual-only behavior wherever it is supported. On the CLI those skills are silently dead — nothing in `skill list`, in install tooling, or in the docs signals a problem until a user tries to run one.

Related but distinct: #3095 (adding capability declaration fields to frontmatter).

issues.title: MCP OAuth: pre-registered (static) client's secret isn't sent at token exchange → invalid_client
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

With a **pre-registered (static) confidential OAuth client**, Copilot CLI completes the browser authorization step, but the authorization server rejects the code-for-token exchange:

```
Authentication failed: MCPOAuthError: Token exchange failed: Server returned error response: invalid_client: Bad credentials
```

The client ID and secret are correct. They work in Claude Code, VS Code and others.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105 (macOS 26.6.2, arm64)

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Use a remote HTTP MCP server whose authorization server doesn't support dynamic client registration, and register a confidential OAuth client (client ID + secret) for it. We used `https://mcp.pagerduty.com/mcp`, with authorization server `https://app.pagerduty.com/global/oauth/anonymous`.
2. Add the server, either in `/mcp` or from a plugin's `.mcp.json`:
   ```json
   { "mcpServers": { "pagerduty": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.pagerduty.com/mcp" } } }
   ```
3. Connect it in `/mcp`. The CLI logs `Client registration failed: Authorization server does not support dynamic client registration` and shows the client credentials form.
4. Enter the client ID, press Tab, and enter the client secret (not marked as a public client).
5. Register the redirect URI shown in the browser's `redirect_uri` on the OAuth app (see the port note below), then approve in the browser.
6. The token exchange fails with `invalid_client: Bad credentials`.
7. `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/<hash>.json` contains the client ID but no `clientSecret`:
   ```json
   {"serverUrl":"https://mcp.pagerduty.com/mcp","authorizationServerUrl":"https://app.pagerduty.com/global/oauth/anonymous","clientId":"<redacted>","redirectUri":"http://127.0.0.1:62372/","resourceUrl":"https://mcp.pagerduty.com/mcp","isStatic":true,"httpsRedirect":null}
   ```

Reproduced 3 times, both with a plugin-provided server and with one added by hand in `/mcp`. The token exchange error only appears in the UI, not in `~/.copilot/logs/*.log`.

### Expected behavior

For a static confidential client, the CLI should store the client secret and send it at the token exchange, using `client_secret_basic` or `client_secret_post` as the server's `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported` advertises.

### Additional context

**Redirect port:** the loopback callback uses a random port on every attempt (`53676`, `54429`, `55205`, `62372`...), so a pre-registered client can't have a stable redirect URI on servers that require an exact match. The config schema has `auth.redirectPort` (`McpServerAuthConfigRedirectPort`), but setting `"auth": {"redirectPort": 8080}` in a **plugin's** `.mcp.json` has no effect: the port stays random. Please honor `redirectPort` for plugin-provided servers and document it.

**Comparison:** VS Code, with the same server, OAuth app, client ID and secret, succeeds once its redirect port is registered.

issues.title: Autopilot task-completion enforcement can override explicit user instructions

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:agents
labels.description: Sub-agents, fleet, autopilot, plan mode, background agents, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In Copilot CLI autopilot mode, the task-completion enforcement behavior can cause the agent to continue taking action after the user has explicitly narrowed the task to research/explanation only.

In my case, the user explicitly instructed the agent to **do nothing besides respond** and asked for an explanation/research task. After the agent answered, a follow-up enforcement message appeared:

> “You have not yet marked the task as complete using the task_complete tool. If you were planning, stop planning and start implementing.”

That message appears to push the agent toward implementation/action even when the active user request is intentionally non-implementation work.

## Why this is a problem

This can lead to the agent making unintended workspace changes despite the user explicitly asking for diagnostic or explanatory help only. The issue is especially risky because the enforcement message is framed as higher-priority continuation guidance, so the agent may treat it as expanding the user’s requested scope.

## Suggested improvement

Adjust the completion enforcement prompt/logic so it preserves the current user’s scope constraints. For example:

- If the user asks for research/explanation only, completing the answer should be considered sufficient.
- If the user explicitly says not to modify files or take action, the continuation message should not direct the agent to “start implementing.”
- The agent should be encouraged to call `task_complete` with a concise summary when the requested non-code task is complete.

## Notes

This may be related to autopilot/task-completion behavior introduced or changed recently. The problematic phrase above is included because it seems useful for locating the relevant enforcement path.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.77.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start a Copilot CLI session with autopilot mode enabled.
2. Ask for a research-only or explanation-only task, and explicitly prohibit action. For example:
   > Please help me understand this behavior. Do not edit files, run implementation steps, or make changes. Just explain what is happening.
3. Let the agent provide a complete explanatory answer without calling `task_complete`.
4. Observe that task-completion enforcement sends a follow-up message similar to:
   > “You have not yet marked the task as complete using the task_complete tool. If you were planning, stop planning and start implementing.”
5. Observe that the agent may interpret this as a directive to take implementation/action-oriented steps, despite the user’s explicit “do not act” instruction.

### Expected behavior

If the active user request is clearly research-only, explanation-only, or explicitly says not to modify anything, task-completion enforcement should allow the agent to finish by calling `task_complete` with a research summary, rather than nudging it toward implementation.

At minimum, the enforcement text should not say “start implementing” when the current task has no implementation component or when the user has explicitly prohibited changes.

## Actual behavior

The agent was nudged to continue with implementation-oriented behavior after completing an explanatory/research response, despite the user saying to do nothing except respond.

### Additional context

- Copilot CLI: 1.0.77
- Mode: autopilot enabled
- OS: Linux devcontainer
- Shell: bash
- Terminal emulator: Herdr-managed terminal session

issues.title: Support OSC 7501 agent-status reporting for herdr-app/herdr-core
issues.body:
## Feature request

Please add native OSC 7501 (Program Status Protocol) reporting to Copilot CLI so terminals such as the new Herdr app can display Copilot sessions and track their activity.

## Current behavior

Copilot CLI launches and works inside a Herdr-managed terminal, but does not appear in the Agents sidebar.

For the running Copilot terminal, `hc get <terminal>` reports:

```json
{
  "reported": false,
  "status": null
}
```

Codex running in the same Herdr instance appears in the sidebar and reports:

```json
{
  "reported": true,
  "status": {
    "app": "codex",
    "state": "idle"
  }
}
```

This remains reproducible when launching Copilot manually from a Herdr terminal or through Herdr’s agent-launch menu.

## Expected behavior

Copilot reports its identity and lifecycle state through OSC 7501, allowing Herdr to distinguish:
- Idle and ready for input
- Working
- Waiting for permission or user input
- Finished or errored

Status reporting should be observational only and should not change permission handling.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the new Herdr desktop app backed by herdr-core.
2. Launch `copilot` inside a Herdr terminal.
3. Observe that Copilot runs but is absent from the Agents sidebar.
4. Run `hc get <terminal>` and observe that `reported` is false and `status` is null.
5. Launch Codex in another Herdr terminal and observe that it reports status and appears in the sidebar.

## Environment

- OS: macOS, Apple Silicon
- Copilot CLI: 1.0.106-2
- herdr-core: 0.1.16

## Context

This concerns the new `herdr-app` / `herdr-core`, not the older Herdr TUI. The new core relies on program-emitted OSC 7501 reports rather than screen scraping.

Herdr’s protocol overview:
https://herdr.dev/core/#status-from-the-source

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Since the unified Sessions browser became the default, `copilot --resume` without a session ID no longer lets me pick a session. Each launch creates a new empty session ("Session 1"). The Sessions list is shown for only ~2 seconds, then the UI switches to that new session's "Current" tab. In a folder that is not remembered as trusted, the "Confirm folder trust" dialog then appears on top of the empty session and consumes my first Enter, so I end up in a blank new session before I can use ↑/↓ on the list.
 
 The list is still reachable with Tab or /resume, but this is not obvious, and it makes `--resume` look like it simply creates a new session.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.102

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

 1. cd into a local folder that has earlier Copilot sessions and is not remembered as trusted.
 2. Run `copilot --resume` (no session ID).
 3. After a "Resuming session…" spinner, the Sessions tab appears. The highlighted first row is a brand-new empty "Session 1".
 4. About 2 seconds later the UI switches to the "[Current]" tab and shows "Confirm folder trust".
 5. Press Enter ("1. Yes").
 6. Result: I am in the new empty session. ↑/↓ does nothing here. Pressing Tab (footer: "tab next tab") or typing /resume brings back the Sessions list, where ↑/↓ works.

### Expected behavior

`copilot --resume` without an ID should keep the session list focused until I choose a session or cancel. It should not auto-switch to the newly created placeholder session, and the folder-trust prompt should not take focus or Enter from the picker. Alternatively, it should reopen the most recent session for the current repository, as the 1.0.64 changelog describes for --continue/--resume.

### Additional context

- macOS 26.7.1 (25G241), x86_64; Terminal.app 470.2; zsh; installed via Homebrew cask, auto-updated to 1.0.102.
 - Timeline from a 120x40 pty capture: ~0.7s "Resuming session…"; ~1.1s Sessions tab with list; ~3.0s switch to "[Current]" plus the trust dialog. I could not test a remembered-trusted folder, so I don't know whether the auto-switch is caused by the trust prompt.
 - Each launch also creates an empty session directory (only workspace.yaml, no events.jsonl). Related: #3908, #5204.
 - Changelog 1.0.100: "Use the unified Sessions browser by default for /sessions, /session, and /resume." I did not bisect other versions.
 - Workarounds: `copilot --continue`, `copilot --resume <name|id>`.

issues.title: macOS sandbox blocks Gradle daemon connection despite local networking being allowed

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Gradle cannot execute even an offline `help` task inside the Copilot CLI macOS sandbox when outbound and local networking are configured as allowed.

The Gradle daemon starts successfully and listens on localhost, but the Gradle client cannot connect to it:

```text
java.net.SocketException: Operation not permitted
```

The identical command succeeds with the Copilot sandbox disabled. Restarting Copilot with the sandbox enabled does not resolve the failure.

### Affected version

Copilot CLI `1.0.95`; also observed on `1.0.93`.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. On macOS, enable the Copilot CLI sandbox and allow both outbound and local networking. The configured network settings are:

   ```json
   {
     "allowOutbound": true,
     "allowLocalNetwork": true,
     "allowedHosts": [],
     "blockedHosts": []
   }
   ```

   `/sandbox policy` reports outbound and local networking as allowed.

2. In a Gradle 9.1.0 wrapper project with Java 21 selected, ask Copilot to execute:

   ```bash
   ./gradlew --offline --no-daemon --console=plain --stacktrace help
   ```

3. Gradle launches a single-use daemon to honor the project's JVM settings. The daemon binds a localhost port, but the client connection fails with `Operation not permitted`, before any task executes.

4. Disable the Copilot sandbox and repeat the identical command. It succeeds, executing only `help`.

### Expected behavior

When local networking is explicitly allowed, Gradle should be able to connect to its localhost daemon.

If that setting intentionally excludes host-loopback connections, the policy display should make this distinction clear and document a supported way to permit the required connection without disabling the entire sandbox.

### Additional context

**Environment:** macOS `26.6.2`, ARM64; Gradle wrapper `9.1.0`; Java Amazon Corretto `21.0.6.7.1`.

The command uses offline mode, so dependency downloads are not involved. `--no-daemon` still launches a single-use daemon in this project.

**Kernel-confirmed denial**

In one sandbox-enabled run, the daemon listened on `127.0.0.1:53774`. The macOS kernel log recorded:

```text
Sandbox: java(5913) deny(1) network-outbound remote:*:53774
```

**Effective policy from a separate failing run**

Copilot's debug log identified the generated policy used for the command. Its network section was:

```json
{
  "network": {
    "egress": {
      "default": "deny"
    },
    "ingress": {
      "default": "allow",
      "hostLoopback": "deny"
    },
    "runtimeConfig": {
      "networkProxy": "http://127.0.0.1:55437"
    }
  }
}
```

In that run, the Gradle daemon listened on `127.0.0.1:55438`, not the proxy port `55437`.

This appears consistent with the client being denied a direct host-loopback connection despite `allowLocalNetwork: true`. Gradle's daemon protocol uses raw TCP, so the HTTP proxy cannot carry that connection.

Please investigate whether `allowLocalNetwork` is being mapped correctly to the effective macOS policy, or whether a separate supported host-loopback permission is required.

**Related reports**

- [github/copilot-cli#4854](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4854): a Windows `/sandbox policy` display issue. Unlike that report, the display here says networking is allowed, while the generated policy and kernel denial demonstrate an actual blocked connection.
- [github/copilot-cli#4516](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4516): JVM filesystem-grant failures on macOS, with a recent comment also describing remote-repository/proxy problems. This report concerns the local Gradle daemon connection, without dependency downloads.

Only sanitized excerpts are included here; no project source, credentials, or full conversation/debug logs are attached.

issues.body:
Copilot CLI 1.0.105 on macOS (Apple Silicon), signed in with an Enterprise Managed User account whose organization policy sets `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh`.

The CLI sometimes hangs indefinitely at startup or on `--resume`. It has happened repeatedly over the past few days.

- The server policy is fetched successfully (`serverFetchFailed=false`).
- About 30 s later the log shows `Managed MCP policy application exceeded its settings settlement deadline; independent enforcement continues` (logged twice).
- Nothing is logged after that. Only 1 or 2 of the 11 configured MCP servers (5 stdio, 6 HTTP) are started, the UI never becomes usable, and after about 2 minutes all connections to github.com are closed. I waited more than 3 minutes before killing it.
- On resume, the session also logs: `Plugins required by your organization admin could not be checked… Error: Managed settings could not be confirmed`.

It happens intermittently with the same configuration. Starting with every `--disable-mcp-server` flag usually works, but it isn't tied to a particular server, because turning them back on one by one didn't reproduce it.

CLI processes left running from closed terminals seem to make it more likely, but stopping them doesn't always fix it.

Logs available on request.

issues.title: No indication when `cli_remote_control_enabled` is false — desktop setting is inert and GitHub Mobile returns a bare HTTP 422

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:enterprise
labels.description: GitHub Enterprise (GHE/GHES) support, org policies, and enterprise settings

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When the signed-in account's Copilot entitlement has `cli_remote_control_enabled: false`, neither the desktop app nor GitHub Mobile indicates it. Instead the feature appears available and fails opaquely:

- **Settings → General → "New sessions remote access"** can be changed and the preference persists, but has no effect.
- Sessions are created and run normally, but availability is never published for remote control.
- Sending a message to such a session from GitHub Mobile fails with a bare **HTTP 422** and no explanation.

The result is a feature that looks configurable and simply isn't. Diagnosing this took a long investigation across the app database, the app log, and the shipped binary before `/copilot_internal/user` revealed the cause was an account entitlement rather than a misconfiguration or a local fault.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot desktop app 1.1.6 (macOS, Apple Silicon); Copilot CLI 1.0.79-5; GitHub Mobile on iOS.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Sign in to the desktop app with an account whose `/copilot_internal/user` returns `cli_remote_control_enabled: false` — for example an enterprise seat where the policy is turned off. Note that `cli_enabled`, `chat_enabled`, `copilot_app_enabled` and `cloud_session_storage_enabled` may all be `true`.
2. Open **Settings → General** and set **New sessions remote access** to the permissive option.
3. Create a new repository-backed session and let it run.
4. On GitHub Mobile, open that session and send a message.

The mobile app returns HTTP 422. Nothing is logged on the desktop side, because the request never reaches the host.

### Expected behavior

Any one of the following would make this self-diagnosing:

1. Disable or grey out **New sessions remote access** when `cli_remote_control_enabled` is false, with a note such as "Remote access is turned off for your organization."
2. Return an actionable error to GitHub Mobile instead of a bare 422 — for example "Remote control is not enabled for your account."
3. Include a machine-readable reason in the 422 response body.

Option 1 alone would be sufficient, since it prevents the user reaching the failure state at all.

### Additional context

Evidence gathered while diagnosing, in case it helps locate the gap.

**The desktop app never checks the entitlement.** The string `copilot_internal/user` appears **0 times** in a 5.4 MB app log covering a full day of use. The app's complete outbound API surface over that period was: repository issues, PR timelines, PR comments and reviews, `copilot_internal/.../merge_status`, `alive_internal/websocket-url`, `cmc_internal/api/agents/.../automations/v2`, and telemetry. Nothing entitlement-related and nothing session-registration-related.

**Availability is never published, and nothing surfaces that.** In `~/.copilot/data.db`, across all 19 sessions created between 2026-05-28 and 2026-08-08, the columns `remote_availability`, `remote_prompt_delivery`, `remote_create_state` and `remote_connect_target` have been NULL 100% of the time, and `remote_availability_revision` has never held any value other than 0. That is consistent with the client correctly declining to publish for an unentitled account — the issue is purely that the decision is invisible.

**The stored preference is honoured locally, then ignored.** `app_state.remote-session-default` reads `{"state":{"defaultRemoteSessionMode":"on","hasUserSetPreference":true},"version":1}`, and newly created sessions carry `remote_session_mode = 'on'` with `remote_control_enabled = 1` at both session and project level. So the setting writes through correctly and then silently does nothing, which strongly implies a local misconfiguration to anyone debugging it.

**Failures leave no local trace at all.** No genuine HTTP 422 is ever logged on the desktop side, and the app holds only two established outbound connections to GitHub — the REST endpoint and the Alive socket, the latter carrying only PR resource snapshots. There is no local signal a user could use to work out what happened.

**What continues to work is what made this confusing.** Plain non-repository chats work from mobile, and cloud sessions work from mobile. Both are consistent with `chat_enabled: true` and `cloud_session_storage_enabled: true` while only `cli_remote_control_enabled` is false — but from the user's side it just looks like "some sessions work from my phone and some return 422."

Related: #2751 notes that `/remote` cannot be invoked at all unless an admin has enabled remote access, so the CLI does gate on this. The desktop app and mobile app appear not to.

Happy to supply further detail from the app database or log if useful.

releases.body:
**Fixed**
- apply_patch no longer counts one extra line for each file it adds or deletes, so the timeline summary, permission prompt, /usage and exit summary show the real line counts
- `copilot config` now warns when a value of the wrong type makes settings.json ignored, instead of reading every setting as unset and reporting writes into that file as if they took effect
- Deleting text in front of Chinese, Japanese or Korean characters in the prompt no longer leaves the line garbled until the next edit.
- Markdown output no longer turns colon-delimited text such as file.ts:100:5 or crate::id::Id into emoji.
- A top-level SKILL.md in a skills directory now produces a warning in /skills explaining that subdirectories are resources, not separate skills, and how to load them.
- A message sent while the agent is working that mentions a file or directory (`@path`) is no longer rejected with "Submission failed" when an earlier one is still waiting.
- /keep-alive busy releases sleep prevention once all tracked sessions finish working, including background turns and standalone local-shell commands
- Git URL caches use short paths and diagnose path-length failures. Old caches are copied, not moved, and kept for older CLIs; delete the originals manually when no longer needed.
- ACP session/prompt and session/cancel stop only the active turn, keeping background tasks and shell commands running
- Long conversations now recover from oversized requests by trimming historical reasoning and retrying.
- Prompt before out-of-workspace access through dangling symlinks
- Rewinding and resubmitting a prompt now keeps image and file attachments.
- Sessions recover from unavailable program endpoints and continue answering prompts
- Skill calls explain when model invocation is disabled instead of reporting the skill as not found
- /memory now reports when Memory is disabled for the session by an experiment and clarifies /memory on behavior.

issues.title: session: -s <id> from another project 404s and silently creates a shadow session with the same ID
issues.body:
## Summary

After updating from V1 to V2 (2.2.5), `opencode -s <session-id>` run from a different project directory does not restore the session. The server answers `404`, and because `-s` means "continue, or create if it does not exist", the CLI silently creates a **new empty session reusing the requested ID** in the current project. From that point the V2 API resolves that ID globally to the shadow session, so the original session's history becomes unreachable through V2 (even from its own project directory). Separately, ~20 of the most recent V1 sessions were never migrated to `session_v2`, which is what made the lookup 404 in the first place.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.5 (channel: latest, npm global install)
- OS: Microsoft Windows [Version 10.0.26200.9457]
- Terminal: xterm-256color (`TERM_PROGRAM` not set)
- Shell: `C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe` (plus an `ocode.cmd` wrapper that sets proxy env and forwards to `opencode`)
- Install/channel: latest release
- Active plugins: one local plugin (`~/.config/opencode/plugin/gigacode.js`); one MCP server (`MCP_DOCKER`, local `docker mcp gateway`); no project-local `opencode.json` in the affected directories

## Reproduction

1. On V1 (observed with 1.19.5), have a session in project A, e.g. `ses_e6679db72ffeQnC18FcKq3j2sT` in `C:\Work\xray` (286 messages).
2. Update opencode to 2.2.5.
3. From a different project directory `C:\Work\router`, run `opencode -s ses_e6679db72ffeQnC18FcKq3j2sT` (in V1 this restored the session from any folder).
4. Observe: instead of the original history, an empty session opens. The server log shows:
   `GET /api/session/ses_e6679db72ffeQnC18FcKq3j2sT → 404`, then a new `session_v2` row is created with the **same ID** but `directory=C:/Work/router`.
5. Afterwards, even `cd C:\Work\xray && opencode session export ses_e6679db72ffeQnC18FcKq3j2sT` returns the router shadow, not the original. `session list` in xray no longer contains the original session at all.
6. DB check: V1 `session` table still holds the original row (286 messages / 961 parts intact); `session_v2` holds only the shadow. Totals: 267 rows in `session` vs 259 in `session_v2`; the ~20 missing IDs are the most recent V1 sessions.

## Expected Behavior

One of: resolve `-s <id>` globally across projects (V1 behavior — this was heavily relied upon), or fail with a clear "session not found in this project" error. A never-existing-in-V2 ID must never be reused to create a new session that shadows an existing V1 session.

## Actual Behavior

- Cross-project `-s` lookup 404s (also because recent V1 sessions were not migrated to `session_v2`).
- The CLI then creates a new session with the requested foreign ID in the current project.
- The original session is masked globally by ID collision; its history is only reachable by reading the V1 `session`/`message`/`part` tables directly.

## Additional Context

- Frequency: consistent, reproduced twice (`04:44:56` and `04:46:32` UTC, same 404 → shadow pattern).
- Workaround for migrated sessions: pass the project directory positionally from anywhere, e.g. `opencode -s <id> C:\Work\xray`. `opencode api get /api/session/<migrated-id>` resolves globally, confirming the lookup itself is not project-scoped — only the TUI `-s` path 404'd for the unmigrated ID.
- Manual recovery performed: converted the V1 transcript (user text + reasoning/text parts, `bash`→`shell` tool rename, `todowrite` calls flattened to text) into V2 `session export` JSON shape with fresh `ses_`/`msg_` IDs and imported it via `opencode session import --directory C:\Work\router`. Two friction points there: import preserves message IDs, so a cloned import fails with `UNIQUE constraint failed: session_message.id` (had to regenerate all message IDs); errored tool calls are rejected with `400`/`Missing key ... ["state"]["error"]` unless `state.error = {"type": "tool.execution", "message": ...}` is present.
- Related second defect (same root story): V1→V2 migration silently skipped the ~20 newest sessions; no warning is surfaced for unmigrated sessions.
- Logs quoted above from `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` (`role=server`, `GET /api/session/... 404`; `role=cli`, `args=["-s","ses_..."]`).

issues.title: opencode-go: Authorization header invalid for certain models (MiniMax, MiMo, GLM, etc.)
issues.body:
## Summary

When using the `opencode-go` provider, Qwen models work fine, but switching to other models like MiniMax M3.1 Flash, MiMo-V2.6-Pro, GLM-5.3-Flash, etc. fails with `Header 'Authorization' has invalid value`. This happens consistently for non-Qwen models under the same `opencode-go` provider.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.2.5
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.26200 (win32 x64)
- Terminal: TERM_PROGRAM=vscode, TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor
- Shell: PowerShell / cmd.exe
- Install/channel: latest (release)
- Active plugins: @slkiser/opencode-quota@latest

## Reproduction

1. Open OpenCode with the default `opencode-go/qwen3.7-plus` model — works normally.
2. Use `/models` to switch to a different `opencode-go` model such as `MiniMax M3.1 Flash` or `MiMo-V2.6-Pro`.
3. Send a message (e.g., "hi").
4. The request fails with `Retry in 1s · attempt 2 · Header 'Authorization' has invalid value`.

## Expected Behavior

All `opencode-go` models should work with the same authenticated session, since no separate API keys are needed for the `opencode-go` provider.

## Actual Behavior

Qwen models (qwen3.7-plus, qwen3.8-flash, qwen3.8-max) work fine. Non-Qwen models under `opencode-go` (MiniMax, MiMo, GLM, Step, DeepSeek, Grok, GPT-6, etc.) all fail with:

```
AI.Error: Header 'Authorization' has invalid value
```

Log entry from `opencode.log`:
```
message="Failed to drain Session" cause="AI.Error: Header 'Authorization' has invalid value"
    at POST
    at SessionStep.attempt (B:/~BUN/root/chunk-vc4s6e38.js:477:4041)
```

## Additional Context

- The `opencode-go` provider auth is configured (`auth_state: configured`) and the live probe succeeds.
- Weekly quota shows 87% remaining, monthly shows 94% remaining — the account is active and not rate-limited.
- The global `opencode.jsonc` config has no custom provider keys (just the quota plugin), which is correct for `opencode-go`.
- Restarting the service does not resolve the issue.
- This is reproducible 100% — happens for every non-Qwen `opencode-go` model.
- Suspect: this may be a plan/subscription restriction or a server-side auth routing bug on the OpenCode Go backend.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Expose durable execution continuity to server plugins
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

I'm using a server plugin that persists inference accounting and blocks unsafe automatic continuation. After an OpenCode restart, it cannot distinguish a session that previously finished safely from one interrupted during execution.

A concrete example is a completed session receiving a PR notification days later. The notification should be able to resume already-authorized work, but the plugin currently has to refuse it because the previous process's authorization cannot be verified.

In OpenCode 2.2.5, `experimental.idle` helps, but runs before execution settles. It can still be interrupted or followed by more input in the same execution. The public session timestamps and `model.request` payload don't expose a durable execution identity or continuity binding.

Could the plugin API expose enough host-owned execution lineage to:

- Correlate a plugin checkpoint with an execution that successfully finished idle.
- Detect intervening execution, interruption or deletion that invalidates that checkpoint.
- Document when exclusive ownership is guaranteed, including managed versus standalone servers.
- Return an explicit unknown state when continuity cannot be established.

OpenCode already maintains [durable execution claims for restart recovery](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.2.5/packages/core/src/session/execution.ts). I'd prefer to reuse that authority rather than introduce a separate ownership mechanism in the plugin.

The plugin would preserve its existing episode, counters and replay history. Genuine pauses and explicit stops would remain blocking. Historical records without sufficient proof would still require fresh user input.

The important validation cases would be a crash while already idle, a crash between the idle hook and terminal commit, failed checkpoint invalidation, and a stop racing with the handoff.

Is there an existing supported contract for this, or would a small execution-continuity addition be welcome?

issues.title: [FEATURE]: /goal: let plugins declare background work in SessionIdle.background
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

## Problem

`/goal`'s idle judge (`packages/core/src/plugin/goal.ts`, v2.2.5) only sees background work the host itself tracks in `SessionIdle.background`: `subagent`, `image` and `shell`. It skips judging while the Session's own subagent or image job runs (lines 150–153). It offers `wait` only while one of the Session's own shells runs (lines 126–127).

A plugin can run work in other sessions and wake this one when that work finishes, but it has no way to say so. opencode-courier, for example, spawns child sessions that report back to their parent with a `session.synthetic` message. So a root with an active goal that spawns children and ends its turn to wait for their reports looks finished or stalled to the judge. The judge answers `continue`, the root is prompted on instead of waiting, and after `MAX_STALLS` rounds the goal pauses with "Not making progress".

Reproduced on 2.2.4 with a scripted reviewer: three continuations within a second of the spawn, then the goal paused, 25 s before the child reported. The same happened with children created with `parentID` set to the root.

## Proposal

Let a plugin add entries to `SessionIdle.background` for a session, for example:

```ts
{ kind: "plugin", sessionID, description: string }
```

`/goal` would treat these the way it treats a subagent: the plugin's own wake (a synthetic message) runs the hook again, so the judge can simply return. It could also offer `wait` for them. Its `WAIT_LIMIT` watchdog would still pause a goal whose plugin work never reports.

Another option: let `/goal` hold back while any plugin reports pending work for the session, through a hook or a field on the idle event.

## Context

- Plugin: https://github.com/ivopogace/opencode-courier (issue #421, write-up in PR #425)
- A plugin's own `experimental.idle` hook can't work around this: built-in hooks run before package plugins (`plugin/supervisor.ts`), so `/goal`'s continuation is already admitted when ours runs.

issues.title: [FEATURE]: Forward promptCacheKey to GitHub Copilot GPT (Responses) requests
issues.body:
- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

On v2.2.5, Copilot-hosted GPT models never receive a `prompt_cache_key`. That leaves them without the session affinity anchor that OpenAI-native models already get.

- **OpenAI-native already gets it.** `session/model-request.ts` sets `request.promptCacheKey` from session affinity, and `packages/ai/src/protocols/openai-decisions.ts` forwards it.
- **Copilot GPT doesn't.** Those models (`gpt-*` and other non-Claude models on `github-copilot`) skip `packages/ai`. `github-copilot/models.ts` routes them to `Provider.aisdk("@ai-sdk/github-copilot")`, and `packages/core/src/aisdk.ts` never reads `request.promptCacheKey`.
- **The Responses converter would honour it.** `github-copilot/responses/openai-responses-language-model.ts` already reads `providerOptions.copilot.promptCacheKey`; nothing on the AI-SDK path fills it in.
- **The compatibility flag can't help.** Setting `compatibility.supportsPromptCacheKey` for `github-copilot` has no effect, because only `packages/ai` protocol code reads it.

The change I'm asking for is to merge `request.promptCacheKey` into `providerOptions.copilot` for `@ai-sdk/github-copilot` Responses calls, gated on `supportsPromptCacheKey`. This mirrors the OpenAI path. It could live in `aisdk.ts` or in the `github-copilot` plugin's `language` hook.

Benefit: long agent sessions on Copilot GPT keep landing on the same cache shard, the same way OpenAI-native sessions do. #59868 shows Copilot GPT already gets implicit cache reads; this keeps them stable across turns.

I have not verified that Copilot's `/responses` endpoint accepts `prompt_cache_key`. Related: #59868, #55244, #51931.

issues.title: config: global config directory watch fails when ~/.config/opencode is a symlink (inotify ENOTDIR), so edits are never hot-reloaded
issues.body:
## Summary

When the global config directory (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode`, e.g. `~/.config/opencode`) is a symlink to a real directory, the service fails to subscribe its directory watcher with `inotify_add_watch ... failed: Not a directory`. As a result, edits to the global `opencode.json` are never hot-reloaded; only `opencode reload` or a service restart picks them up. A real (non-symlinked) directory works.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.27
- OS: Linux 6.18.40.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 (WSL2, ext4)
- Terminal: TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor
- Shell: /bin/bash
- Install/channel: latest
- Active plugins: not relevant; the isolated reproduction below uses an empty config with no plugins

## Reproduction

Isolated, using temporary XDG directories:

```sh
R=/tmp/symrepro; mkdir -p $R/real/opencode $R/xdg $R/data $R/state $R/cache $R/proj
echo '{"agent":{"probe":{"description":"v1","prompt":"x"}}}' > $R/real/opencode/opencode.json
ln -s $R/real/opencode $R/xdg/opencode     # trailing slash or not makes no difference

cd $R/proj
XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$R/xdg XDG_DATA_HOME=$R/data XDG_STATE_HOME=$R/state XDG_CACHE_HOME=$R/cache \
  opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 47123 --print-logs
```

1. In another shell, request `GET /api/agent?directory=$R/proj` (basic auth `opencode:<printed password>`). The `probe` agent has description `v1`.
2. Edit the config: `sed -i 's/v1/v2/' $R/xdg/opencode/opencode.json` and wait several seconds.
3. Request `GET /api/agent` again.

## Expected Behavior

The config directory watcher starts (following the symlink), and step 3 returns description `v2`, just as it does when `$R/xdg/opencode` is a real directory.

## Actual Behavior

The directory watcher fails when it starts, and the edit is never picked up (step 3 still returns `v1`):

```
level=INFO  message="watcher subscribe" path=/tmp/symrepro/xdg/opencode type=directory ignores=3 role=server
level=ERROR message="failed to subscribe" directory=/tmp/symrepro/xdg/opencode cause="Error: inotify_add_watch on '/tmp/symrepro/xdg/opencode' failed: Not a directory
    at Config.reconcileWatches (/$bunfs/root/chunk-xnspstqv.js:118:33644)
    at ServerProcess.start (/$bunfs/root/chunk-c1a0vz4v.js:2:7540)"
```

| `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode` | Directory watcher | Value after edit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| symlink → real dir | `failed to subscribe … Not a directory` | `v1` (stale) |
| symlink with trailing slash in target | same failure | not separately tested |
| real directory | `watcher started … backend=inotify` | `v2` |

File watchers on paths inside the symlinked directory (`AGENTS.md`, `skills`, using `backend=node`) start normally. Only the `type=directory` inotify watch on the symlink itself fails. This suggests the inotify backend subscribes with `IN_DONT_FOLLOW`/`IN_ONLYDIR` on the unresolved path. Resolving the directory with `realpath` before subscribing (and mapping events back) would probably fix it. This is an inference; I have not verified it in the source.

## Additional Context

- Happens consistently on every service start and on config reload, for the real `~/.config/opencode` symlink (a dotfiles-style setup) and in the isolated reproduction above.
- Workaround: run `opencode reload` or `opencode service restart` after editing global config.
- A symlinked global config dir is a common dotfiles pattern and was usable with V1.
- Related but distinct: #52240 (stale plugin module cache under a symlinked config dir) and #53763 (retargeted plugin directory symlink). This issue is about the config directory watch failing to subscribe at all.

prs.title: feat(core): schedules can run a shell command, with or without a session
prs.body:
**A schedule can now run a shell command, like cron, and doesn't need a session.**
Today every schedule sends a prompt into a chat, so a background job needs a session and a model call each time. Now a schedule is a "when" plus a command. The command can call back into OpenCode through the CLI or API for anything else. Prompt schedules keep working as before.

💡 **Why**
The team wants schedules to be general background automations: a schedule that spawns a hidden session, posts somewhere or runs a script, without being tied to a chat.

🆕 **Now you can**
- Run `bun scripts/nightly.ts` every night with no session and no model call.
- Keep the existing `if` / `until` checks. They still run on each tick without a model, and the check's message reaches the command on stdin and as `OPENCODE_SCHEDULE_MESSAGE` (plus `OPENCODE_SCHEDULE_RUN`, the run number).
- See each run's exit code, duration and the last 32 KB of output in the schedule's `lastRun`. A non-zero exit, timeout or spawn error counts toward the existing pause-after-failures rule; a success resets it.
- List, pause and delete session-less schedules over HTTP (checked against the global `experimental.schedules` flag).

🚦 **How it ships:** schedules are already behind `experimental.schedules`.

```diff
- action: { type: "prompt", prompt }           // every schedule needs a session
+ action: { type: "prompt", prompt }           // still needs a session
+       | { type: "shell", run, cwd?, timeout? } // session optional, runs in the background, 10 min default timeout
```

🧱 **Stack:** this is the core. The `schedule_create` / `schedule_list` tools and `/schedule` learn the shell action in the follow-up PR stacked on this one.

↩️ **Undo:** revert isn't enough, because migrations add `last_run` and `run_failures` columns and shell schedules written meanwhile won't decode on the old code.

👀 **Read:** `packages/core/src/schedule.ts`, how a session-less row is authorized and fired without an instance, and how a finished shell run feeds the failure count. The rest is routine.

prs.title: fix(core): keep payload-free images out of the inline budget cut
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #61391

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

`boundImages` picks how many images to replace by walking `sizes` in order, then applies that `cut` by document position. `mediaBytes` returns `0` for `url` and `ref` media because they carry no local payload, so those images still take slots in the removal queue. The budget loop subtracts `0` from `kept` but advances `cut`, and `replaceMedia` then replaces the remote image too. With two remote images followed by two 13 MiB inline images (26 MiB total), three images were replaced instead of one.

The loop now skips zero-byte entries when choosing what to drop, and the replacement pass only counts images with a non-zero payload. Remote and provider-referenced images stay in the request, so removals always free payload. The source-order prefix that keeps the prompt cache stable is unchanged for images that carry payload.

### How did you verify your code works?

Added a regression test in `packages/core/test/session-model-request.test.ts` with two remote images followed by two 13 MiB inline images. On `dev` it fails with `Expected: 1, Received: 3`; with the fix it passes.

- `cd packages/core && bun run script/test.ts test/session-model-request.test.ts` -> 11 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run check` from the repo root -> 35 successful tasks, 0 errors
- `bun run typecheck:tsc` from `packages/core` -> clean

### Visual

Not a user-facing visual change; no new UI.

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A (request shaping only).

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(app): retry inbox branch loads and lease keybind suspension per caller
prs.body:
## Bugs

**Inbox branch loads** (`shell/titlebar/inbox-model.ts`)

- **A failed lookup is never retried.** One transient git or HTTP error marks the location settled, and the `queued` set blocks it for as long as the Inbox stays mounted. The row never shows its branch.
- **One slow lookup stalls the whole queue.** Lookups ran in barrier batches of 4 (`await Promise.all`). One hung request kept the other 3 slots idle and stopped the queue, and the branch loader stayed on forever.
- **A synchronous throw jams the queue.** `drain.running = true` had no `finally`, so one throw from `location.info`/`syncInfo` stopped every later load.
- **Writes after unmount.** Late completions wrote to the store after the Inbox closed.

**Command keybind suspension** (`shell/commands/command.tsx`)

- **A double release turns shortcuts back on while another caller still holds them.** A suspends, B suspends, then A releases twice: the counter goes `2 → 1 → 0`, and global shortcuts fire while B still captures keys.
- **A repeated `keybinds(false)` turns shortcuts off for good.** Two `false` calls and one `true` call leave the counter at 1, so every shortcut and the palette stay off.

## Machines

```ts
// inbox-branch-machine.ts: one entry per location
type InboxBranchEntry =
  | { phase: "queued"; server; initial; failures }
  | { phase: "loading"; server; attempt; initial; failures } // holds one of BRANCH_BATCH slots
  | { phase: "retrying"; server; attempt; failures } // backoff, holds no slot
  | { phase: "ok"; server }
  | { phase: "failed"; server } // rests until its server reconnects

type InboxBranchState =
  | { status: "active"; issued; connected: ReadonlySet<string>; queue: readonly string[]; entries }
  | { status: "disposed" }

// suspend-machine.ts
type KeybindSuspendState =
  | { status: "active"; issued: number }
  | { status: "suspended"; issued: number; holds: readonly number[] } // 0 = keybinds(false), 1..N = suspend() leases
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> queued: enqueue
  queued --> loading: slot free (pump)
  loading --> ok: load.succeeded
  loading --> retrying: load.failed / load.timed-out (15 s), failures < 2
  loading --> failed: load.failed / load.timed-out, failures = 2
  retrying --> queued: retry.due (1 s, 2 s)
  retrying --> queued: server reconnects (budget reset)
  failed --> queued: server reconnects (budget reset)
```

| Suspend state | Event | Next |
| --- | --- | --- |
| any | `suspend()` | adds lease `issued + 1`; returns a release for that lease only |
| any | `keybinds(false)` | adds hold `0`; same state if hold `0` is already there |
| `suspended` | release lease `h` / `keybinds(true)` (`h = 0`) | removes `h`; `active` when no holds are left |
| any | release a hold it does not have | same state |

- Each settled lookup frees its slot and `pump` starts the next queued location at once. This is a sliding window, not barrier batches.
- Every result event carries its `attempt`. A late answer from a timed-out request is ignored.
- `selectBranchLoading` is true only until the first attempt settles. Background retries and reconnects do not show the loader again.
- The driver dispatches `disposed` on cleanup, which clears every timer. Late promises reach a disposed state and change nothing.

## Deleted

- `vcs.settled` store, `queued` set, `queue` array, `drain.running` and the `run` loop in `inbox-model.ts`.
- `store.suspendCount` in `command.tsx`.

## Product calls

- A lookup retries twice (1 s, then 2 s) and then rests as `failed`. It does not retry again until its server reconnects, so re-renders do not spam git.
- A lookup that does not answer in 15 s frees its slot and counts as a failure.
- `useCommand().suspend()` is new and returns a per-caller release. `keybinds(enabled)` keeps its signature and maps to one idempotent shared hold, so `settings/keybinds/keybinds.tsx` (in flight in another PR) needs no change.

## Deviations from the design

- `suspend-machine.test.ts` sits next to the machine, not in `command.test.ts`, the same layout as the other `*-machine.test.ts` files.
- The stories `useCommand` mock is unchanged: no story calls `keybinds`, `suspend` or `suspended`.
- `disposed` always emits `timers.clear`, which also drops the cached lookup targets.

Off the hot path (branch lookups and keybind toggles), so there is no benchmark.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none" stroke="currentColor">
  <style>
    .s{animation:s 3s linear infinite}.s2{animation-delay:.6s}.s3{animation-delay:1.2s}.s4{animation-delay:1.8s}
    @keyframes s{0%,100%{opacity:.25}40%{opacity:1}}
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.s{animation:none;opacity:.8}}
  </style>
  <g stroke-width="1">
    <rect x="12" y="10" width="216" height="12" opacity=".3"/>
    <rect x="12" y="30" width="216" height="12" opacity=".3"/>
    <rect x="12" y="50" width="216" height="12" opacity=".3"/>
  </g>
  <g fill="currentColor" stroke="none">
    <rect class="s" x="180" y="13" width="40" height="6"/>
    <rect class="s s2" x="180" y="33" width="40" height="6"/>
    <rect class="s s3" x="180" y="53" width="40" height="6"/>
    <rect x="20" y="13" width="90" height="6" opacity=".5"/>
    <rect x="20" y="33" width="70" height="6" opacity=".5"/>
```

prs.title: fix(desktop): drive the IPC port handshake and event stream through state machines
prs.body:
### Bugs

- **New window misses storage changes.** The preload reads its storage snapshot at revision `R0`. The window gets an event queue only when its port binds on `did-finish-load`, through an async handoff fiber. A `StorageChanged(R0 + 1)` from another window in that gap hit `emitIpcEvent` with no queue and was dropped. The new window kept a stale namespace until that key changed again.
- **Reload drops events.** During a reload, events went into the old document's queue, and the new port's bind then shut that queue down. If the old port closed first, the queue was gone and events were dropped. A reloading window also skipped its own `pagehide` flush (`StorageUpdate` on the old port) when the flush landed after the new snapshot, because `origin === win.webContents`.
- **Missing port hangs everything.** The renderer's port was a one-shot `Promise` with no timeout. If main never posted it, every `invoke` waited forever, and startup sat on the splash until the 5-minute sidecar timeout.
- **Abort before the port still ran the RPC.** Aborting a `cancellable` request before the port arrived queued an `Interrupt` behind the already-queued `Request`, so main started the request anyway.

### Main: `ipc-machine.ts`

One state per window (sender). The draining port is kept for the previous document: it answers in-flight RPCs, such as the `pagehide` storage flush, and receives no events.

```ts
type IpcSender =
  | { status: "awaiting-port"; sender; buffered: Item[]; draining: { clientId; port } | undefined }
  | { status: "bound"; sender; clientId; port; events: Queue<DesktopEvent> }

type IpcTransportState =
  | { status: "open"; nextClientId; senders: Map<senderId, IpcSender>; clients: Map<clientId, senderId> }
  | { status: "disposed" }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> awaiting: sender.prepared (did-navigate / snapshot)
  [*] --> bound: port.bound
  awaiting --> awaiting: event.emitted (buffer, cap 1024)
  awaiting --> awaiting: client.closed (draining port, keeps buffer)
  awaiting --> bound: port.bound (flush buffer, close draining port)
  bound --> awaiting: sender.prepared (shut queue, notify disconnect, port drains)
  bound --> bound: port.bound (replace client)
  bound --> [*]: client.closed / sender.destroyed
  awaiting --> [*]: sender.destroyed
```

| Event | From | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sender.prepared` | absent | `watch-sender` |
| `sender.prepared` | `bound(c0)` | `shutdown-events(q0)`, `notify-disconnect(c0)` |
| `port.bound` | `awaiting` | `close-port(draining)`, `end-client(draining)`, `attach-port`, `offer-events(buffered)` |
| `port.bound` | `bound(c0)` | `shutdown-events`, `close-port`, `notify-disconnect`, `end-client`, `attach-port` |
| `client.closed` | draining client | `close-port`, `end-client` (sender keeps its buffer) |
| `client.closed` | bound client | full release, `unwatch-sender` |
| `disposed` | `open` | release every sender; a later `port.bound` closes the port |

- `emitIpcEvent` is unchanged for callers. While bound, it reads `selectBoundEventQueue` (one `Map.get`) and calls `Queue.offerUnsafe`, so delivery allocates nothing. Only unbound senders dispatch `event.emitted`.
- `handoff.bind` is synchronous now, so the queue exists before `postMessage` hands the port to the renderer.
- `ipc.ts` prepares a sender on main-frame `did-navigate` to a renderer URL. `storage/snapshot.ts` does the same just before it reads a snapshot.
- `StorageUpdate` broadcasts unless the caller is the window's current client (`handoff.isCurrentClient`). A draining document's flush therefore reaches the window's new document.
- `DesktopEvents` streams `handoff.events(clientId)`, so an unloading document never reads its successor's queue.

### Renderer: `ipc-client-machine.ts`

```ts
type IpcClientState =
  | { status: "awaiting-port"; queued: { id; message }[]; pending: Map<id, IpcPending> }
  | { status: "connected"; port; pending: Map<id, IpcPending> }
  | { status: "closed"; reason: "timeout" | "disposed" }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> awaiting
  awaiting --> connected: port.received (post queued in order)
  awaiting --> closed: handshake.timed-out (30 s, reject pending)
  awaiting --> closed: disposed
  connected --> closed: disposed (close port, reject pending)
  closed --> closed: request.started (reject) / port.received (close late port)
```

- An abort while `awaiting-port` removes the request from `queued`, so main never sees it. An abort while connected posts `Interrupt`.
- A connected request is posted in the same turn, not on a microtask, so `pagehide` flushes leave before the port closes.
- The `Chunk` path stays off the machine: `selectPendingChunk` plus the existing ack.

### Deleted

- Main: the `handoffs` queue and fiber, `bindings`, `senderBindings`, `nextClientId`, the module-global `queues` map, `bindIpcEvents`, `ipcEventStream`.
- Renderer: the `port` promise and the module `pending` map.

### Product calls

- **30 s handshake timeout.** If main has not posted the port after 30 s, pending and new requests reject with `Desktop IPC port handshake timed out`. Startup then shows its failure screen instead of a 5-minute splash. A port that arrives later is closed, so main releases that client.
- **Buffering across loads.** A window holds events from the moment its new document commits (or asks for its snapshot) until its port binds, capped at 1,024 events. Events past the cap are dropped and `emitIpcEvent` returns `false` for them. Before, all of these events were dropped.
- **Earlier deep-link requeue.** Deep links now hear `onDisconnect` when a document starts unloading, not when its replacement binds.

### Deviations from the design

- Prepare on `did-navigate` (commit) instead of `did-start-navigation`. A started navigation can still be cancelled, and that would leave the live document without events. A commit is ordered before the same load's `did-finish-load`.
- Inbound RPC messages keep the existing queue and fiber instead of one `runFork` per message, to keep message order and per-message cost.
- `closing` and `dispose.started` were cut: no phase reads them. The driver runs `beforeDispose`, then dispatches `disposed`.
- The driver allocates request ids, and `request.started` carries the built message. Ids identify requests; they are not phase state.
- The main machine keeps no separate client status. Draining is derived: the client's sender is `awaiting-port`.

### Performance

- Off the hot path. Bound event delivery does the same work as before (one `Map.get` and `offerUnsafe`). The renderer's `Chunk` path is unchanged. Requests now post synchronously instead of through `port.then`. No benchmark was run.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none" stroke="currentColor">
  <style>
    .e{animation:f 3s linear infinite;opacity:.8}
    .e2{animation-delay:-1s}.e3{animation-delay:-2s}
    .doc{animation:r 3s steps(1) infinite}
    @keyframes f{0%{transform:translateX(0)}60%{transform:translateX(118px)}100%{transform:translateX(118px);opacity:0}}
    @keyframes r{0%,40%{opacity:.25}41%,100%{opacity:1}}
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.e,.doc{animation:none}}
  </style>
  <rect x="8" y="18" width="52" height="36" opacity=".6"/>
  <text x="34" y="40" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">main</text>
  <rect x="96" y="26" width="44" height="20" stroke-dasharray="3 2" opacity=".5"/>
  <text x="118" y="22" font-size="8" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" opacity=".6">held</text>
  <rect class="doc" x="176" y="18" width="56" height="36"/>
  <text x="204" y="40" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">window</text>
  <circle class="e" cx="64" cy="36" r="3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/>
  <circle class="e e2" cx="64" cy="36" r="3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/>
  <circle class="e e3" cx="64" cy="36" r="3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/>
```
