prs.title: fix(gui-plugins): drive the Pierre file tree through one state machine
prs.body:
The file browser and the review's change tree drive `@pierre/trees` `FileTree` imperatively. `pierre-tree.tsx` encoded the tree's lifecycle in a `ready` signal, two re-entrancy booleans, seven `rendered*` snapshots, `knownPaths`, `scrolled.active` and a `widest` counter. This PR moves all of it into one union with a pure transition in `pierre-tree-machine.ts`; the component keeps only the DOM and widget handles.

### Bugs

| Trigger | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Expand `src/` in the file browser, delete `src/` on disk, recreate it with its files, expand it | The browser blanks: the reconciler forgets `src/` but keeps `src/a.ts` in `knownPaths`, then asks `FileTree` to remove it (`Path does not exist: "src/a.ts"`) | The removal of `src/` purges every known path under it; recreated files are added again |
| Collapse `src/` in the review while the file browser (mounted, hidden behind it) has it open | The browser keeps `src/` open with frozen children: it only ever called `expand()` | The browser collapses `src/`; the review also follows folders the browser closes |
| A throw from a handle (`expand`, `select`, …) inside a programmatic sync | `syncingExpansion` / `syncingSelection` stay `true`: folder toggles stop persisting, selection freezes | `runPierreTreeSync` ends the sync in `finally` |
| `active` changes twice in one tick, or the tree unmounts | The first scroll microtask still scrolls to the old file | The microtask carries an attempt; only the current one scrolls |
| `active` is a loaded file under a collapsed folder, then the folder opens | `scrolled.active` was set although nothing scrolled, so opening the folder never scrolls to it | A hidden file is not remembered as scrolled to; it scrolls once it shows |
| Workspace root changes with the same relative `active` | No scroll in the new tree | Scrolls again |
| `allowed` toggles between `undefined` and a list after mount | `resetPaths` on a tree built for the other mode (wrong `initialExpansion` and `sort`) | A new `FileTree` for the new mode (no production caller does this today) |

### State

```ts
type PierreTreeState =
  | { status: "unmounted" }
  | (Mounted & { status: "live"; root; model; knownPaths; treeExpanded })
  | (Mounted & { status: "allowed"; model; collapsedDirs; labels })
  | { status: "disposed" }

type Mounted = {
  sync: "none" | "expansion" | "selection" | "both" // echoes of programmatic changes are ignored
  active: string
  selectedPath: string
  scroll: { status: "idle"; scrolledPath; issued } | { status: "pending"; path; attempt }
  kinds; kindsStatus; ignored // git status layers
  widest: number
}
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> unmounted
  unmounted --> live: synced (live input) / mount-tree
  unmounted --> allowed: synced (allowed input) / mount-tree
  live --> live: synced / reset-paths | batch-paths, sync-expansion, patch-git-status, select, schedule-scroll
  allowed --> allowed: synced / reset-paths | sync-expansion, rerender, patch-git-status, select, schedule-scroll
  live --> allowed: synced (allowed input) / mount-tree
  allowed --> live: synced (live input) / mount-tree
  live --> disposed: disposed / cleanup
  allowed --> disposed: disposed / cleanup
  unmounted --> disposed: disposed
```

Inside a mounted variant:

| Event | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `tree.expansion-changed` (not syncing) | `reset-width` when widened, `persist-expansion`; allowed: `schedule-scroll` when it uncovers `active` |
| `tree.selection-changed` (not syncing, drifted) | `select(selectedPath)` |
| `list.measured` wider than `widest` | `set-min-width` |
| `scroll.flushed` with the current attempt | `scroll` → `idle` |
| `sync.started` / `sync.ended` | `sync` only |

### Large trees

- One `createKeyed` source feeds one `synced` event; each field is compared by reference first, so the duplicate `sameStringMap` scans in `equals` and the callback are gone.
- `buildLiveTreeInput` fills `pathSet` and `expandedSet` in its single pass; the two extra `new Set(...)` per live sync are gone.
- `treeExpanded` mirrors the tree's open folders, so a file-watcher update touches no folder handles unless expansion changed (before: `getItem` + `expand` for every expanded folder on every update).
- Git status is two layers (`kindsStatus`, `ignored`): a folder toggle that leaves the change kinds alone diffs only the ignored entries instead of rebuilding the whole status map.
- An unchanged listing returns `knownPaths` and `treeExpanded` by reference; `knownPaths` is copied only when the batch is non-empty.

### Deleted

`ready`, `syncingSelection`, `syncingExpansion`, `appliedStatus`, `renderedAllowed`, `renderedLabels`, `renderedKinds`, `renderedIgnored`, `renderedRoot`, `scrolled`, `widest`, `syncSelection`, `applyAllowedCollapsed`, `toFileNode`, `originalPath`, and five `createKeyed` reconcilers.

### Product calls and deviations from the design

- Both trees follow shared folder state both ways (the review's allowed tree now also collapses a folder the file browser closes).
- New `allowed` paths (agent edits) do not re-scroll to the same active file; only a root change or a mode change does, as on `dev`.
- One `synced` event replaces the design's `mounted`, `live.synced`, `allowed.synced`, `labels.synced`, `status.synced` and `active.synced`.
- A root change resets the tree with `resetPaths(paths, { initialExpandedPaths })` instead of `resetPaths([])` plus a batch of every path.
- Collapsed allowed folders are a fresh `Set` per memo run, not a shared empty set.
- Off the per-frame paths (scroll, pointer, resize); the reconcile work per update is the same order as before or less.

### Visual

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Review collapsed `src` | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab1acf05-70f6-4813-97ad-1f5631f250f9) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/776e0caf-6b67-4c97-82f8-32a8991e2574) |
| `src` deleted, recreated, opened | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ce3af381-482a-4979-ac18-c5cfc6760f51) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d86d9868-4440-4b1c-9add-0993e989da0e) |

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 240 72" width="240" height="72" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">
  <style>
    .chev{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:center;transform:rotate(90deg);animation:chev 4s ease-in-out infinite}
    .kid{animation:kid 4s ease-in-out infinite}
```

prs.title: fix(core): find Microsoft Store PowerShell 7 on Windows
prs.body:
On Windows, OpenCode never picks PowerShell 7 when it comes from the Microsoft Store. The shell tool and terminals fall back to Windows PowerShell 5.1, even with `"shell": "pwsh"` in config. A configured absolute alias path throws `EACCES`.

- **Cause:** Store apps put an app execution alias (an `IO_REPARSE_TAG_APPEXECLINK` reparse point) in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps`. It launches like any `.exe`, but `stat` rejects it with `EACCES`, so `which@6` skips it and `ShellSelect.executable()` throws.
- **Fix:** When `which` finds nothing on Windows, `which()` looks for an alias on PATH. `ShellSelect` accepts a rooted alias before it calls `stat`.

| Call | `lstat` | `stat` | `access` | Launches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `WindowsApps\…\pwsh.exe` (Bun 1.4.4 and Node 26) | symlink, 85 B | `EACCES` | ok | 7.6.9 |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["which('pwsh')"] --> B{which@6}
  B -- "stat EACCES: skipped" --> C["alias on PATH? (lstat symlink + exists)"]
  C -- yes --> D["WindowsApps\…\pwsh.exe"]
  B -- found --> D2[path]
```

| Shell resolution on a machine with Store PowerShell 7 | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Default (no config) | `powershell.EXE` 5.1 | `pwsh.exe` 7 |
| `"shell": "pwsh"` | `powershell.EXE` 5.1 | `pwsh.exe` 7 |
| `"shell": "…\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe"` | throws `EACCES` | `…\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe` |

- **Spawn:** `cross-spawn` has the same `which` blind spot, so it still starts the alias through `cmd.exe /d /s /c`. Its argument escaping keeps `%`, `&`, `|`, `^`, `<>`, `!` and quotes intact.
- **Tests:** Tests cannot create an app execution alias, so the new cases borrow one from the user's `WindowsApps` and skip where none exists.

### Visual

prs.title: fix(app): drive pane sizing and the question dock through state machines
prs.body:
Pane resizing and the question dock (both variants) now run on explicit state machines. This fixes a pause in a drag that turned pane animations back on, a custom answer that unpicked the option with the same value, controls that came back on for a question already answered, drafts kept for forms that are gone, a reply that could hang the dock forever, and switch-animation bookkeeping that measured mid-flight, left copies behind and allocated every frame.

### Bugs

| Area | Sequence | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pane sizing | Hold a resize handle, pause for more than 120 ms | `touch()` timer fires mid-drag, `active()` goes false, panes animate under the pointer | A held pointer stays `dragging` until `pointerup`; moves arm no timer |
| Pane sizing | Right-click a resize handle | `active` latches true until blur | Only the primary button starts a drag |
| Question dock | Multiselect: check **Changed files** (`files`), type `files` as the custom answer, uncheck custom | `files` is filtered out of the one shared answers array, **Changed files** unchecks and the reply sends `{}` | Picked options and the custom text are kept apart; the reply sends `["files"]` |
| Question dock | Submit, HTTP `204` arrives before SSE `form.replied` | `isPending` flips false, every control re-enables, a second Submit sends again | `sending → replied` stays busy until the form leaves |
| Question dock | Form settled by SSE (or another client) while the dock is open, then the dock unmounts | `onCleanup` writes the dead form's draft into `questionCache`, which never shrinks | `resolved → replied` deletes the entry; the cache keeps at most 100 drafts |
| Question dock | Submit on a stalled connection | Dock stays disabled forever | 30 s timeout aborts, gives the dock back with the draft and shows the failure toast |
| Experimental switch | Resize, then switch before the next frame | Queued measure runs mid-switch and snaps the height springs | The measure is deferred to the end of the switch |
| Experimental switch | Resize mid-switch, then motion turns off | The deferred measure is dropped; the max height stays stale | `still` keeps it and measures |
| Experimental switch | Unmount mid-switch | Ghost copies stay in the DOM; a wake with nothing moving starts a frame job | `disposed` removes them; a resting wake only measures |

### State

```ts
// packages/app/src/session/sizing-machine.ts
type SizingState =
  | { status: "idle"; attempt: number }
  | { status: "dragging"; attempt: number }
  | { status: "settling"; attempt: number } // a resize without a held pointer, settles after 120 ms

// packages/app/src/session/requests/question-machine.ts
type QuestionDraft = { selected: readonly string[]; customText: string; customSelected: boolean }
type QuestionDockState =
  | { status: "answering"; attempt: number; tab: number; drafts: readonly QuestionDraft[] }
  | { status: "sending"; attempt: number; tab: number; drafts: readonly QuestionDraft[]; action: QuestionSendAction }
  | { status: "replied"; attempt: number; tab: number; drafts: readonly QuestionDraft[] }
  | { status: "disposed"; attempt: number }

// packages/app/src/session/requests/question-switch-machine.ts
type QuestionLoopState<TInto, TGhost> =
  | { phase: "idle" }
  | { phase: "measuring" } // a layout read queued for the next frame
  | { phase: "running"; measureDeferred: boolean; into: TInto | undefined; ghost: TGhost | undefined }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  direction LR
  state "Question dock" as Q {
    answering --> sending: send (attempt + 1)
    sending --> replied: request.succeeded(attempt)
    sending --> answering: request.failed / timed-out(attempt)
    answering --> replied: resolved (SSE)
    sending --> replied: resolved (SSE)
    answering --> disposed: disposed / cache.save
    sending --> disposed: disposed
    replied --> disposed: disposed
  }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  direction LR
  state "Switch loop" as L {
    idle --> measuring: measure.requested / wake(resting)
    idle --> running: wake(moving) / switch.started
    measuring --> idle: measure.completed
    measuring --> running: switch.started / wake(moving) [measureDeferred]
    running --> measuring: frame(nothing left) / still [measureDeferred]
    running --> idle: still
    running --> running: frame (same object while no copy finishes)
  }
```

- `sizing`: `resize.touched` while `dragging` returns the same state with no effect, so a drag move costs one comparison. Stale `settle.due` timers are fenced by `attempt`.
- `question`: one driver, `createQuestionDock` (`question-controller.ts`), is shared by the classic and experimental docks. Focus, the custom field's editing state and minimizing stay in each variant; they are view state, not lifecycle.
- `switch`: the driver applies phase changes in one place (`applyLoop`): it cancels the queued measure, stops the frame job, and removes a ghost's elements when the ghost changes. A frame reuses `FRAME_MOVING_EVENT` / `FRAME_RESTING_EVENT`, and `tick` and `paint` write into scratch poses and looks, step the springs directly and build masks without arrays, so a running switch allocates no objects per frame.

### Deleted

- `helpers.ts`: the `active` store flag and the `let t` 120 ms timer.
- Both docks: `tab`, `answers[][]`, `custom[]`, `customOn[]` store fields, `let replied`, `replyMutation`, `rejectMutation`, the duplicated `customUpdate`, `pick`, `toggle`, `submit`, `answered` and the unmount cache write.
- Experimental dock: `let ghost`, `let into`, `let stop`, `let measuring`, `dropSwitch`, and the per-frame `Object.values(foot)`, element arrays, `Pose` and `Look` objects and mask layer arrays.

### Product calls

- A reply already sent keeps going when the dock unmounts (as `useMutation` did); only its timeout is cleared. Its draft is not saved.
- A custom answer is appended after the picked options in a multiselect reply, and is not repeated when it equals one of them.
- The dock still waits for SSE `form.replied` / `form.cancelled` to close; it no longer re-enables in between.
- Timeout for a hanging reply or dismiss: 30 s.

### Deviations from the design

- `side-panel-presence` stays out of scope: `createPanelMotion` already owns it (design §1).
- `model.ts` is untouched (batch L4 owns it). The dock evicts its own entry on `form.replied` / `form.cancelled`, and the cache drops its oldest entry past 100 for forms settled while their dock is away. SSE events reach the dock inside the connection's `batch`, before any unmount.
- Focus, minimize and custom-field editing are not in the question machine: they are not lifecycle phases and differ between the two variants.
- `question-state.ts` keeps only the bounded cache; the driver lives in `question-controller.ts` so the pure tests can import the cache without Solid.
- A `wake` with nothing moving from `idle` goes to `measuring` instead of staying `idle`: the old frame job measured after it, and the RO callback relies on that to repaint snapped heights.
- `switch.dropped` is its own event instead of a `dropSwitch` flag on `wake`.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 240 72" width="240" height="72" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="10">
<style>
.c{opacity:0;animation:c 4s infinite}
.s{opacity:.35;animation:s 4s infinite}
@keyframes c{0%,30%{opacity:1}38%,100%{opacity:0}}
@keyframes s{0%,55%{opacity:1}62%,100%{opacity:.35}}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.c,.s{animation:none}}
</style>
<rect x="8" y="8" width="150" height="24" opacity=".3"/>
<rect x="15" y="14" width="12" height="12"/>
<path d="M17.5 20l3 3 4.5-5.5"/>
<text x="35" y="24" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">Changed files</text>
<rect x="8" y="40" width="150" height="24" opacity=".3"/>
<rect x="15" y="46" width="12" height="12"/>
<path class="c" d="M17.5 52l3 3 4.5-5.5"/>
<text x="35" y="56" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">files</text>
<g class="s">
<rect x="172" y="24" width="60" height="24"/>
<text x="202" y="40" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" text-anchor="middle">Submit</text>
</g>
</svg>
```

### Screenshots

Multiselect question: check **Changed files**, type `files` as the custom answer, uncheck the custom answer; then Submit (the mock answers `204` and sends no `form.replied`).

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Custom answer turned off | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ec3fe41-22c5-4f4f-a110-a2efd66dc63e) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bbdb00e4-39f3-49f9-aec0-a6e5f43c6530) |
| After the reply's response | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/990f2f61-1606-467e-bb64-1c88f42d9400) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2c3b6093-bd70-45ef-b3f6-10dd4f09fc73) |

### Performance

The switch loop runs every frame while the experimental dock animates. `packages/app/perf/question.bench.ts` (new) switches four questions on and four back, each key one frame into the last switch, with the dock's motion on.

prs.title: feat(process-daemon): protocol v8 for shell commands
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #

Supersedes #60701 (its three commits are included here, rebased).

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Protocol v8 for `opencode-pty`, so OpenCode can run its local shell commands in the daemon (pipe mode) and keep them across a planned server restart. This is a breaking bump: a v8 server discards a v7 handoff and starts a fresh daemon, so persistent terminals start fresh once on upgrade.

Pipe output file (from #60701, plus changes):
- `create_pipe` takes `output_path`; the reader writes every chunk to it before forwarding. File is truncated on open, default mode (umask), symlinks refused, closed before `exited`.
- No replay buffer for pipe processes (the file is the buffer).
- Write errors set `output_error` on the process and on `exited`.

New requests:
- `get { id }`: direct lookup.
- `wait { id }`: held open until the process exits, then one `exited` reply. Replies at once if it already exited; `error "terminated"` if it's terminated first.
- `signal { id, signal }`: SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGKILL to the process group without removing it, so `wait` still gets a normal exit. Safe because the zombie stays unreaped until `terminate`.
- `set_metadata { id, metadata }`: opaque JSON the server stores with the process (≤ 1 MiB).

Daemon-recorded data: `output_lines` (newlines actually written to the file, counted in the reader), `started_at` / `exited_at`.

Cleanup enabled by the bump:
- `TerminalInfo` → `ProcessInfo`, with `pty` / `pipe` groups for mode-specific fields.
- `create` split into `create_pty` and `create_pipe`; `list` requires `mode`.
- No feature flags (`features` is required and empty); compatibility shims for older peers removed.
- Unknown requests get `error "unsupported request: <op>"` instead of a dropped connection; bad fields get `invalid <op> request: …`.

Windows pipe mode is out of scope: on Windows, `create_pipe` and `signal` return errors.

The OpenCode side is in #61876. This needs a 0.5.0 release before that one can merge.

### How did you verify your code works?

On Linux: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --locked --lib --test service --test runtime --test ownership --test pipe --test rows --test ghostty-effects`. New tests cover the v8 wire format, `wait` (single/multiple waiters, already exited, terminate and shutdown while waiting, client disconnect), `signal` (trapped SIGTERM then SIGKILL, background child, after exit, after terminate), output file mode/truncation/symlink, line counting (partial writes, batching, write errors), metadata and timestamps. The OpenCode client's tests also pass against this build.

Not run: Windows clippy/tests (the `#[cfg(windows)]` paths were updated by reading) and macOS.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(desktop): preserve theme alpha so terminal can be transparent
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Part of #61858 — this PR removes the app-side clamp; the render-side fix in ghostty-web (`parseColorToHex`) is tracked in the issue and sent as a companion PR.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`resolveV2Token` in `packages/gui-plugins/src/terminal/terminal.tsx` truncated every 8-digit `#rrggbbaa` token to 7 digits before building the ghostty-web theme, so a terminal background authored with an alpha channel arrived as an opaque color. This deletes the special case; the token now passes through as authored.

The earlier revision of this PR also flipped `allowTransparency` to `true`. Review found that option is stored but never read in the pinned ghostty-web, so that change is dropped — transparency comes entirely from the alpha in `theme.background`.

One caveat, documented in #61858: with an alpha-bearing theme, ghostty-web's `parseColorToHex` misreads `#rrggbbaa` as one 32-bit integer and shifts the channels (`#16161600` → RGB(22,22,0)), which also corrupts OSC 11 background queries. Fixing that needs a small companion patch in ghostty-web; without it, this PR is a no-op for the built-in themes (all `ff` alpha) and only takes effect once the renderer side is fixed.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `tsc -b` clean, `bun test src/terminal` 40 pass in `packages/gui-plugins`.
- Dev build (`bun run dev` in `packages/desktop`), `oc-2.json` dark `v2-background-bg-base` set to `#16161600`: terminal container computes to `rgba(22, 22, 22, 0)` (previously `rgb(22, 22, 22)`), and with the ghostty-web parse fix applied the canvas center pixel reads `[0, 0, 0, 0]` — the window backdrop shows through the terminal, screenshots below.
- Pixel-level checks via CDP: canvas2d accepts `#rrggbbaa` fillStyles (verified `[22,22,22,128]` for `#16161680`), so once the emulator parses alpha correctly the renderer's existing transparent path works unmodified.

prs.title: fix(app): drive the Settings Models provider reveal with an explicit state machine
prs.body:
Picking a provider on Settings > Providers opens Models and reveals that provider. The reveal was one `createEffect` that cleared the search, waited for the section, expanded it and scrolled in an uncancelled frame. It only told `RootSettings` it was done on success, so any other outcome left the target set, and the effect then wiped every character typed into "Search models". This PR moves the reveal into a machine where every exit consumes the target.

### Bugs

- **Collapsed OpenCode Console blocked the reveal and the search.** Collapse OpenCode Console on Models, then pick a Console provider (for example Google) on Providers. A nested provider mounts only inside the expanded group, and the effect checked for its section before expanding the group, so it never expanded, never scrolled and never finished. Every keystroke in "Search models" was then cleared.
- **A provider with no models, or leaving Models early, left the target sticky.** Search typing was wiped, and a later visit to Models (or another server listing that provider) jumped unexpectedly.
- **Uncancelled frame.** The scroll ran in a `requestAnimationFrame` that a tab or server switch never cancelled, and a rerun could schedule two.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Console stays collapsed and "gem" is wiped | Console and Google expand, Google is focused, the search keeps "gem" |
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f9bf7c06-36f5-4bba-adac-11534577e557) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0696f61-eafd-4172-8429-d328e5eccdb8) |

### State

```ts
type ModelsRevealState =
  | { status: "idle"; attempt: number }
  | { status: "waiting"; attempt: number; provider: string; expanded: boolean } // 5 s timeout
  | { status: "scrolling"; attempt: number; provider: string } // one animation frame
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  idle --> waiting: target.synced (Models active) / clear filter once, start timeout
  waiting --> waiting: catalog.synced, section not mounted / expand Console and provider
  waiting --> scrolling: section ready / cancel timeout, schedule frame
  scrolling --> idle: frame.completed / consume target
  waiting --> idle: timed out / consume target
  waiting --> idle: filter.typed, tab left, disposed / cancel, consume target
  scrolling --> idle: filter.typed, tab left, disposed / cancel frame, consume target
```

- `transitionModelsReveal` in `settings/models/machine.ts` is pure; timeout and frame results carry the attempt, so a stale one changes nothing.
- `models.tsx` is the driver: it owns the timer and the frame, syncs the target and (only while revealing) the catalog, and reports a section as ready from its `ref` a microtask later, once it is in the document.
- `onReveal` is now `onConsumeTarget`, called on every exit, so `RootSettings` never keeps a stale `modelProvider`.

### Deleted

- The multi-branch reveal `createEffect`, its `list.clear()` on every run with a filter, and the bare `requestAnimationFrame`.

### Product calls

- Typing in "Search models" during a reveal ends the reveal instead of being cleared; a search typed before the reveal starts is still cleared once.
- A provider that never appears (no models, catalog still loading) gives up after 5 s.
- Deviation from the design: the target stays in the `RootSettings` store instead of moving to the route, and there is no `consumed` marker. Every exit now consumes the target synchronously, which removes the sticky state without touching `route.ts` or `surface.tsx`.

Off the hot path; no benchmark.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5">
  <style>
```

prs.title: fix(app): resolve settings server availability and retry with explicit state machines
prs.body:
Settings decided whether a server's pages can load in five places, with three different predicates (`!!item.connection`, `settingsServerReachable`, `sdk.connection.status() === "connected"`). They disagreed, so a signed-out or offline HTTP server left Project Settings blank. This PR resolves one `SettingsServerAvailability` per server, from the runtime machines that #61763 made explicit (plugin status, health, signed-out controller), and every Settings surface reads selectors of it. The Retry button gets a small machine fenced to the server it shows.

### Bugs

- **Blank Project Settings.** Open `/settings?server=<http>&project=<dir>` for a server that answers 401 or is offline. The redirect saw `connected: true` (every HTTP server has a connection) and kept the route, while the page had no project to render. It now falls back to that server's Projects page, which explains and offers Retry.
- **Redirect during plugin sign-in.** While an SSH server authenticates, the plugin entry still says `auth` but the connection says `starting`. The redirect read the entry and left the project page mid sign-in. A plugin that reports `ready` without an endpoint kept its connection although its status was `failed`.
- **Search and pages disagreed.** Search indexed a server's settings from its SSE stream state, so results vanished while the stream reconnected and stayed while `/api/info` failed. Search now indexes exactly the servers whose pages open.
- **Switcher badges.** A starting server read "Unreachable", and an unprobed stopped plugin server got a red dot instead of the faint one.
- **Retry stuck across servers.** Retry on hung server A, then switch to server B: B's Retry stayed disabled (the page stays mounted), and A's late answer re-enabled B's Retry while B was still retrying.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `/settings?server=<401 server>&project=…` | Falls back to that server's Projects page |
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5a2f12e-bc00-4fe1-8aa9-9840f6ad7b6d) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/995dce0f-a742-4572-a0d5-2983bb7c65f6) |

### State

```ts
type SettingsServerAvailability =
  | { status: "ready"; connection; health: healthy | checking | undefined }
  | { status: "starting" }
  | { status: "unauthorized"; connection? }
  | { status: "unreachable"; reason: "offline" | "incompatible" | "stopped"; connection? }

type ServerRetryState =
  | { status: "idle"; server: ServerConnection.Key; attempt: number }
  | { status: "retrying"; server: ServerConnection.Key; attempt: number }
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  conn[plugin status] --> R[resolveServerAvailability]
  src[plugin entry, unlisted only] --> R
  health[health record] --> R
  signed[signed-out controller] --> R
  R --> A[SettingsServerAvailability]
  A -->|serverPagesConnection| pages[per-server pages, Project Settings, Servers list]
  A -->|canHoldProjectRoute| redirect[settingsViewRedirect]
  A -->|canIndexServerSettings| search[Settings search]
  A -->|selectSettingsServerHealth, isSettingsServerUnreachable| switcher[server switcher]
```

| Retry state | Event | Next | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `idle` | `retry.clicked` | `retrying` (attempt + 1) | `retry.run` (35 s timeout) |
| `retrying` | `retry.settled` (this attempt) | `idle` | `timeout.cancel` |
| `retrying` | `retry.timed-out` (this attempt) | `idle` | none |
| any | `server.synced` (another server) | `idle` for that server | `timeout.cancel` if retrying |
| `retrying` | `disposed` | `idle` | `timeout.cancel` |
| any | result for an older attempt | unchanged | none |

- `resolveServerAvailability` reads the plugin connection's status first, so a sign-in in progress (`authenticating`) is `starting`, and a `ready` entry without an endpoint is `unreachable`.
- `useSettingsServers` keeps a server's object while its availability does not change, so health polls do not remount the Servers list rows.

### Deleted

- `settingsServerReachable` and the `connected`/`starting` booleans of `RedirectServer`.
- The `ServerDot` fallback that turned a missing health into `unreachable`.
- The inline `isServerFailed`/`isServerUnauthorized` checks in `servers.tsx`, and the `retrying` store in `unavailable.tsx`.

### Product calls

- A signed-out or unreachable server leaves Project Settings for its Projects page instead of keeping the route; a starting server still keeps it. This matches what `dev` already did for stopped plugin servers.
- A server whose controller was signed out reads as unavailable even before its next probe answers, since its pages have no controller to load from.
- Search indexes a server's settings while its health is `checking` or `healthy`, not by its SSE stream state.
- Deviation from the design: `SettingsServer.connection` stays (labels and the Servers list rows read it), next to the new `availability`; `editableHttpServer` was not needed because the unavailable page already reads the connection.

Off the hot path; no benchmark.

### Visual

prs.title: fix(app): drive the settings search session with an explicit state machine
prs.body:
Settings search kept its session in seven store fields plus two closure variables in `SettingsScreen`. Any page reached without the search (a link inside the page, history, the Command Palette) still saw the old `selected` and `origin`, so Back and Escape jumped to the wrong place. This PR moves the session, its result activation and its reveal into one machine.

### Bugs

- **Back and Escape return to a stale origin.** Search "Projects" from Preferences, open the result, then open a project card. The project page says "Back to settings", and Back or Escape opens Preferences instead of Projects.
- **Command Palette jumps fake a search session.** `Ctrl+K` → a project setting → Enter set `selected` without a query or origin, so the project page said "Back to settings" while Back went to Projects.
- **Escape on a project page cleared a hidden search.** With a root query typed, the first Escape on a project page silently cleared the invisible sidebar query instead of leaving the page.
- **Reveal observer leak.** A target that never mounts kept a `MutationObserver` on the whole screen until Settings closed. A reveal now times out after 5 s, and a found row's highlight after 2.5 s.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Escape on the project page opened Preferences | Escape opens Projects, its parent |
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0be4900-712a-4f7e-b31e-1e7d13919359) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64ca4ba7-ecda-46f7-8ef7-45a291582319) |

### State

```ts
type SearchReveal =
  | { phase: "navigating" | "seeking" | "highlighting"; view: SettingsView }
  | { phase: "done" }

type SettingsSearchState =
  | { status: "idle"; query: string; activation: number }
  | { status: "revealing"; activation: number; reveal: SearchReveal } // Command Palette jump
  | { status: "browsing"; query; origin; highlighted; scrollTop; expanded; activation }
  | { status: "opened"; ...browsing; selected: string; reveal: SearchReveal }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  idle --> browsing: input.changed (non-blank)
  browsing --> opened: result.opened / navigate
  opened --> browsing: back or Escape / navigate(origin)
  opened --> browsing: view.synced without this activation
  idle --> revealing: palette.opened / navigate
  browsing --> revealing: palette.opened
  revealing --> idle: reveal completed or timed out
  revealing --> idle: view.synced without this activation
  browsing --> idle: cleared, blank input, Escape on a root page
  opened --> idle: cleared, blank input, Escape on a root page
```

| Reveal phase | Event | Next | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `navigating` | `view.synced` with this activation | `seeking` | `reveal.start` (5 s timeout) |
| `seeking` | `reveal.highlighted` | `highlighting` | `reveal.highlight` (2.5 s timeout) |
| `seeking`, `highlighting` | `reveal.completed`, `reveal.timed-out` | `done` (`idle` for the palette) | `reveal.cancel` |
| `seeking`, `highlighting` | `screen.unmounted` | `navigating` | `reveal.cancel` |
| any | result from an older activation | unchanged | none |

- `transitionSettingsSearch` in `settings/search-machine.ts` is pure. Components read selectors (`selectSearchQuery`, `isSearchActive`, `canReturnToSearchOrigin`, ...).
- `surface.tsx` is the driver: it holds the state in a signal, runs `navigate`, `exit` and reveal effects, and owns the one reveal timer. `SettingsScreen` attaches its root and syncs each view it shows.
- `startSettingsSearchReveal` is a stateless DOM helper. It returns a cleanup (an `AbortController`), and only the machine decides when to call it.

### Deleted

- The `search` store (`query`, `origin`, `selected`, `highlighted`, `scrollTop`, `activation`, `expanded`).
- `let viewType` and `let activation` in `SettingsScreen`, and the `disposed` flag in `search-reveal.ts`.
- The three Escape branches in `shell.tsx`; one `escape.pressed` event replaces them.

### Product calls

- A Command Palette jump ends a sidebar search session, so the sidebar query clears. Before, the jump reused the session and pointed Back at a search the user did not make.
- Typing after opening a result keeps the opened page, its highlight and its way back, as before. Typing during a palette reveal cancels that reveal's highlight.
- Deviations from the design: no `scope` field or focus effects in the machine (focus after a view-type change stays a small effect in `SettingsScreen`, reading `isSearchExpanded`), and the reveal starts from `view.synced` instead of in the same event as `navigate`, so it never searches the previous page while the route commits.

Off the hot path (keyboard and click events only); no benchmark.

### Visual

prs.title: fix(desktop): native menu routing and plugin instance lifecycle as state machines
prs.body:
Moves the desktop native menu (install and command routing) and the per-plugin instance lifecycle onto explicit state machines, and fixes the bugs their implicit state allowed.

### Bugs

- **Menu shortcuts during the startup splash were dropped.** `Cmd+,`, `Cmd+N` or *Export Debug Logs* fired before `AppInterface` mounted hit `trigger === null`. They now queue and run in order once the interface binds.
- **An unmounted `AppInterface` kept receiving menu commands.** `bindDesktopMenu` never unbound, so a command after the error boundary tripped ran on a disposed command context. `DesktopEffects` now unbinds in `onCleanup`; commands after that are dropped, not replayed on a later mount, and a stale unbind from an earlier owner is ignored.
- **A language push could install the menu before main did.** `AppSetNativeTranslations` called `createMenu(...)` with a copy of the deps, so a bundle that arrived before `installMenu()` (or while quitting with no restored window) installed the menu. It now only records the bundle; `ipc.ts` rebuilds an installed menu on `onNativeTranslations`.
- **Menu actions did nothing while detached DevTools held focus.** Actions used `BrowserWindow.getFocusedWindow()`, which is `null` then, so *Reload Webview*, *Zoom In* or *Delete* had no target. `selectMenuActionWindow` now falls back to the visible, unminimized window whose DevTools are focused; with no such window an action still does nothing, so *Close Window* or *Paste* never reaches a window the user cannot see.
- **A restart handoff's kept plugin could be replaced or killed.**
  - Plugin `a` reloads, then calls `ctx.lifecycle.restart(handoff)` while the new code loads. The stop skipped `a` without ending its reload; when the handoff failed and the app resumed, the load finished and disposed the restart's caller.
  - A reload during the handoff disposed a kept instance whose setup had not finished.
- **A failed fallback stayed as the fallback.** `a1` good, reload to `a2` fails setup, fallback `a1` also fails setup: `last` still held `a1`, so the next failed reload started `a1` again. Skipped `activate`/`reload` calls also leaked an `AbortController` per call.

### Machines

```ts
// main/native/menu-machine.ts
type MenuState<Deps> =
  | { status: "uninstalled"; provider: MenubarProvider }
  | { status: "installed"; deps: Deps; provider: MenubarProvider }

// renderer/platform/menu-machine.ts
type MenuRouterState =
  | { status: "starting"; queued: readonly string[] } // before the first bind only
  | { status: "bound"; handler: MenuCommandHandler }
  | { status: "unbound" } // after an unmount: commands are dropped

// main/plugin/lifecycle-machine.ts: one entry per plugin, no entry = stopped
type PluginEntry<R, Rev> =
  | { status: "failed"; error }
  | { status: "loading"; attempt; kept?: { running; revision }; fallback?; replies; queue }
  | { status: "creating" | "preparing" | "setting-up"; attempt; revision; fallback?; isFallback; running?; replies; queue }
  | { status: "active"; running; revision; error? }
  | { status: "disposing"; attempt; running; fallback?; next?: { revision; isFallback }; after; replies; queue }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> loading: activate / reload
  loading --> creating: load.succeeded (no kept)
  loading --> disposing: load.succeeded (kept, next = new)
  loading --> active: load.failed / cancelled (kept)
  loading --> creating: load.failed (fallback, isFallback)
  loading --> failed: load.failed
  creating --> preparing: instance.created
  preparing --> setting_up: instance.ready (canRun)
  preparing --> disposing: instance.ready (stopped)
  setting_up --> active: setup.succeeded
  setting_up --> disposing: setup.failed (next = fallback unless isFallback)
  disposing --> creating: dispose.settled (next, canRun)
  disposing --> failed: dispose.settled (error)
  disposing --> [*]: dispose.settled
  active --> loading: reload (kept = running)
  active --> disposing: deactivate / stop
  loading --> active: stop (keep = kept scope)
```

| Event | Effect on the queue |
| --- | --- |
| `activate` while busy | waits in `queue`; resolves at once if the step ends `active` |
| `reload` | supersedes whatever is in flight or waiting; waits only for a `disposing` instance |
| `deactivate` / `stop` | never waits: disposes the instance now, settles everything queued, runs `after` before its reply |
| any result with a stale `attempt` | ignored; a stale `instance.created` is disposed |

- The driver in `lifecycle.ts` commits each transition before running its commands, queues events raised by commands, and runs each command isolated, so `deactivate` still withdraws contributions synchronously before it returns.
- `canRun` (`enabled && !isQuitting(app)`) and `keptScope(app)` come from `lifecycle/machine.ts` and ride on the events.

### Deleted

- `native/menu.ts`: `let installed`, `let menubar`.
- `ipc-handlers/app.ts`: the duplicate `createMenu({...})` and its deps.
- `renderer/platform/menu.ts`: `let trigger`.
- `plugin/lifecycle.ts`: the `active`, `queues`, `generations`, `last` and `errors` maps, `Running.good`, `until()`.

### Product calls and deviations from the design

- Commands chosen during the splash run once the interface mounts, in order (no dedupe). Commands chosen after it unmounted are dropped, as on `dev`.
- Menu commands keep `getLastFocusedWindow()`; menu actions fall back only to the window whose detached DevTools are focused, never to a minimized or hidden one. The design unified both on `getLastFocusedWindow()`.
- A reload of the handoff's kept plugin is dropped, not resumed after a failed handoff; the plugin keeps the code it had.
- A `deactivate` (disable, uninstall) during a handoff still stops the kept plugin: the user's explicit request wins, as on `dev`. The design protected it.
- A revision that throws while preparing now records a setup failure (and falls back) instead of rejecting the caller.
- No `disposed` variant in the renderer router and no HMR re-subscribe guard: `index.tsx` is `@refresh reload`, so the page reloads instead.
- No `StopWaiter` list in state: `stop()` sends one `stop.requested` per plugin and awaits their replies.
- Off the hot path; no benchmark.

### Visual

```svg

  <rect x="8" y="16" width="72" height="40" opacity=".35"/>
  <rect x="160" y="16" width="72" height="40" opacity=".35">
    <animate attributeName="opacity" values=".1;.1;.6;.6;.1" keyTimes="0;.45;.5;.95;1" dur="4s" repeatCount="indefinite"/>
  </rect>
```

prs.title: fix(app): move sessions to new worktrees through one state machine and recover orphan worktrees
prs.body:
Moving a session from the location menu to **New worktree** ran as a detached `try/finally` inside a menu that unmounts on click. This PR turns it into one state machine (`details/workspace-move-machine.ts`) with a plugin-scoped driver, and adds a recovery dialog for a worktree that was created but did not receive the session.

### Bugs

- **Orphan worktree.** `worktree.create` succeeds, then `location.syncInfo` or `session.move` fails or hangs → toast, `created.directory` forgotten, worktree left on disk with no retry or cleanup.
- **Session moved mid-run.** Session idle at the click → it starts running during `worktree.create` (git + the project's start command) → `session.move` still runs and pulls the checkout away mid-run (reproduced on `dev`: the move request goes out while the composer shows Stop).
- **Stale worktree list wins.** Menu open starts list #1, `worktree.updated` starts list #2, #2 answers first, #1 answers last and overwrites the newer inventory.
- **Duplicate moves.** Picking an item unmounts the menu and its `store.selected`; reopening during the move shows enabled items and starts a second create/move. No request had a timeout.

### State

```ts
type WorkspaceMoveState =
  | (Base & { status: "idle" })
  | (Base & { status: "creating"; attempt })
  | (Base & { status: "moving"; attempt; destination; created?: CreatedWorktree; dialog?: RecoveryDialog })
  | (Base & { status: "recovering"; dialog: number; created; reason: WorkspaceMoveFailure })
  | (Base & { status: "removing"; attempt; created; dialog: RecoveryDialog })
  | { status: "disposed" }

// Base: mounts, issued (attempt counter), projectID, directories, listing?: { attempt, refresh }
type RecoveryDialog = { status: "open"; attempt; reason } | { status: "dismissed" }
type WorkspaceMoveFailure = { type: "failed"; error } | { type: "timed-out" } | { type: "running" }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  idle --> creating: New worktree
  idle --> moving: existing worktree
  creating --> moving: worktree.created (idle session)
  creating --> recovering: worktree.created (session running)
  creating --> idle: create.failed / timed-out (toast)
  moving --> idle: move.succeeded
  moving --> recovering: failed / blocked / timed-out (created worktree)
  moving --> idle: failed / blocked / timed-out (existing worktree, toast)
  recovering --> moving: Retry (session idle)
  recovering --> removing: Delete worktree
  recovering --> idle: Keep worktree / Escape / session arrived / worktree gone
  removing --> idle: remove.succeeded
  removing --> recovering: remove.failed / timed-out
  idle --> disposed: last menu unmounts
```

- Every create, move, remove and list carries an attempt; a result for an attempt the state no longer holds is ignored.
- `run-move` re-checks `session.status` after `syncInfo` and reports `move.blocked` instead of sending `session.move`.
- `worktree.updated` aborts the list in flight and keeps its pending `worktree.refresh`.
- `WorkspaceMoveControllers` in `renderer.tsx` (same pattern as `McpControllers`, #61886) keeps the controller alive while anything runs or the dialog shows; the dialog opens on the shared stack (#61903) with `ctx.dialogs.open` and closes by its own handle.
- The driver queues events, advances in a `finally`, and isolates each effect with `Promise.try`.

### Deleted

- `store.selected`, `store.directories`, the start-only `blocked()` check, and the detached `createWorktree` + `session.move` saga in `workspace-menu.tsx`.

### Product calls

- **Recovery dialog (new UI):** "Session not moved" with **Keep worktree**, **Delete worktree** and **Retry**. Copy is in `details/i18n/en.ts` only; other locales fall back to English.
- **Retry** reuses the created worktree, never creates another. It stays disabled while the session runs; focus starts on Retry, or on Keep worktree while the session runs, never on Delete.
- **Delete worktree** sends `force: true`, as the start command can leave untracked files.
- Closing the dialog keeps the worktree, which then shows under **Worktree**. A retry or delete in flight keeps running after the dialog closes; a late failure shows a toast.
- A move into an **existing** worktree that finds the session running shows a toast ("The session is running. Try again once it finishes.").
- Timeouts: list 15 s (keeps the shown worktrees), create 5 min (start commands often install dependencies), move 30 s, remove 2 min.
- Toasts go through `ctx.toast`, so they close with the plugin.
- Until a list answers, the menu shows the project's sandboxes and worktrees found on disk.

### Deviations from the design

- No `project.synced` or `workspace.removed` events: `menu.opened` carries the project, and a removal elsewhere arrives as `worktree.updated` → list.
- A list closes the dialog for a missing worktree only if it was issued after the dialog opened; an older list can predate the worktree.
- One `toast` effect with `kind` and `reason` instead of three; a `RecoveryDialog` union instead of `number | "dismissed"` plus a nullable `reason`.
- The dialog reports dismissal on unmount and keeps its last content through the exit animation, instead of watching `useDialog().closing`.
- The controller follows `worktree.updated` and the session's directory in its own root, so the dialog still closes on its own after the menu is gone.

### Open questions

- `Worktree.create` registers the worktree before running the start command. If that command fails, the client gets an error without a directory, so this machine cannot offer cleanup. That needs a server change.
- Creating a worktree with a long start command still shows no progress. This PR keeps the `dev` behavior.

Off the hot path, so no benchmark.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none" stroke="currentColor">
  <style>
    .card{animation:pop 4s ease-in-out infinite;transform-origin:150px 36px}
```

prs.title: fix(ui): drive tooltip open and popup suppression through one state machine
prs.body:
## Bugs

- **Tooltip stays hidden after a trigger click.** Hover a menu trigger until its tooltip shows, click it, move away, press Escape, hover again: no tooltip. The press set `justClickedTrigger`, but the menu hid the tooltip before the click, so Kobalte never sent the close that cleared the flag. The next hover's open was swallowed. A press during the exit animation, while `forceOpen` was set, or without a click (drag off) left the same stale flag.
- **Suppression stuck while the trigger keeps focus.** The menu returns focus to its trigger on close. `drop()` kept `block` while focus stayed inside, so every hover stayed blocked until something else took focus.
- **Tooltip flash on menu Escape (masked on `dev`).** The menu's modal layer sets `body { pointer-events: none }`. The trigger gets a `pointerleave` when the menu opens and a fresh `pointerenter` when it closes, with the pointer still. Kobalte then opens the tooltip 400 ms later. On `dev`, only the stale `justClickedTrigger` swallowed that open, so fixing the flag alone makes the tooltip flash.
- **`inactive` toggled while open.** The store lived outside the `inactive` switch, so `false → true → false` remounted Kobalte with `open: true` and no popup observer.
- **`disabled` set while open** left the tooltip open, and Kobalte's warm-up timer could still open a disabled tooltip.

Real event order on a menu trigger (Chromium):

```
pointerdown BUTTON         body pe=auto
aria-expanded=true
pointerleave DIV           body pe=none   ← synthetic, pointer did not move
… Escape …
aria-expanded=false
pointerenter DIV           body pe=auto   ← synthetic, pointer did not move
focusin BUTTON                            ← menu restores focus
```

## Machine

`packages/ui/src/overlays/tooltip/machine.ts`: one signal per active tooltip. Every state, event and transition is a frozen module singleton (33 states), so hover, focus and pointer handlers allocate nothing and a no-op event writes no signal.

```ts
type TooltipState =
  | { status: "unmounted"; disabled }
  | { status: "idle"; hovered; disabled }
  | { status: "open"; hovered; pressing }
  | { status: "suppressed"; popup: "open"; hovered; disabled }
  | { status: "suppressed"; popup: "closed"; disabled }
  | { status: "controlled"; open; hovered; expanded; disabled }
  | { status: "disposed" }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> unmounted
  [*] --> controlled: forceOpen set
  unmounted --> idle: first hover / focus (replay to Kobalte)
  idle --> open: Kobalte open (not disabled)
  open --> idle: Kobalte close (no press) / leave microtask / disabled
  open --> open: press, then its click close (keeps open)
  idle --> suppressed_open: popup expanded
  open --> suppressed_open: popup expanded (ends press)
  suppressed_open --> suppressed_open: pointer move (hovered = inside trigger box)
  suppressed_open --> idle: popup collapsed, pointer away
  suppressed_open --> suppressed_closed: popup collapsed, pointer over trigger
  suppressed_closed --> idle: pointer moves off trigger / trigger focused
  idle --> controlled: forceOpen set
  controlled --> idle: forceOpen cleared
  controlled --> suppressed_open: forceOpen cleared, popup expanded
```

- **Press scoped to one gesture.** `pressing` exists only in `open`. It ends on the press's own click close, on `pointerup`/`pointercancel` (plus one `setTimeout(0)`, after the click), or when the state leaves `open`.
- **Hover measured while suppressed.** While a popup is open, the trigger's own enter and leave events are not reliable. A capture `pointermove` listener compares the pointer with the trigger's box. It is attached only while the state is `suppressed`.
- **The driver derives resources from the state.** `reconcile(previous, next)` attaches or detaches the press listeners, the move listener, and the popup `MutationObserver` from selectors. `disposed` releases all of them.
- **`inactive` is a boundary.** `<Show when={!props.inactive} fallback={props.children}><ActiveTooltip/></Show>`, so an inactive tooltip has no state, and reactivating it starts fresh.

Deleted: the `open`/`block`/`expand`/`mounted` store, `justClickedTrigger`, `controlled()`, `inside()`/`drop()`/`sync()`/`leave()`, the `:hover` and `document.activeElement` checks, and the `onFocusOut` rAF.

## Deviations from the design

- No `closing` phase or settle timer. After a popup closes over the trigger, suppression lifts on user intent (the pointer moves off the trigger, or the trigger itself takes focus), not after a macrotask. The design's timer could not separate the synthetic `pointerenter` above from a real hover.
- No `leaving` mode. `open.hovered = false` plus the leave microtask covers it.
- `pointer.leave` does not lift `suppressed: closed`. While the popup is open, a modal layer fakes it.
- Effects are only `replay` and `schedule-leave`. Listener and observer lifetimes come from selectors, not from add and clear effects.

## Product calls

- Clearing `forceOpen` closes the tooltip. It opens again on the next hover. `dev` resumed an open state that could be out of date.
- A disabled tooltip does not mount Kobalte on hover.
- Touch `pointerenter` does not mount Kobalte. Kobalte ignored it already.

## Screenshots

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/280f141f-2919-4441-90fe-512542444f52) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/67933f99-1e37-40d4-91ba-ffd683dee45b) |

Click "Actions", move away, Escape, hover again. A component test covers this and the still-pointer Escape case (`packages/app/component-tests/tooltip.spec.ts`, story `ui-tooltip--with-menu`).

### Visual


prs.title: fix(session-ui): drive the markdown worker with an explicit state machine
prs.body:
One explicit state machine now owns the Markdown worker's lifecycle and request bookkeeping. A worker failure no longer disables streamed Markdown and code highlighting until the page reloads, and a long answer no longer drops highlighting on its first code blocks. ### Bugs - **One worker error disabled the worker for the page.** A failed `markdown.worker.ts` load (LAN, Tailscale) or one `onerror`/`onmessageerror` set `disabled` for good. Every later request threw `MarkdownWorkerUnavailableError`, and a streamed `` whose `projectMarkdown` rejected kept `projection.latest` empty, so `data-markdown-ready` never appeared. - Now the worker is terminated, every request in flight is rejected once, and new requests reject at once during a cooldown (2 s, doubling on each consecutive failure up to 60 s). The next request after the cooldown spawns a fresh worker. - `markdown.tsx` falls back to the unprojected text when a projection fails, so the block still settles. - **More than 200 code blocks lost highlighting on the first ones.** `highlightStreamingCode` added every key to a 200-key LRU before sending. The 201st request disposed block 1 while its highlight was in flight, and the plain-text fallback was then cached as the completed block. - Now only incomplete streams with nothing in flight count against the limit, so an in-flight highlight is never evicted. - **A lost or failed projection desynced the two threads.** The worker stored its projection before posting the diff, and an `error` reply cleared neither side. The next diff could start past the blocks the main thread held, and `applyProjectionBlocks` dropped the middle blocks. - The worker now keeps a projection only once it is posted. A `from` past the held blocks, or an `error` reply, rejects that request and resets the key on both sides (`dispose`) before the queued snapshot is posted. - **A stalled worker hung every caller.** Nothing bounded a worker that stopped answering without raising `onerror`. - One watchdog timer fails the worker when the oldest request in flight makes no progress across 15 s. It is armed once per busy period, not per delta. - Until a worker's first reply the window is 60 s, so loading its bundle and first grammar over a slow link is not counted as a hang. - **Disposed project replies fell through to the highlight transport.** Both request kinds now share one `requests` map keyed by id, so a reply for a disposed request matches nothing. ### State `packages/session-ui/src/components/markdown-worker-machine.ts` ```ts type MarkdownWorkerMachineState = | (Counters & { status: "idle" }) | (Counters & { status: "ready" watched: number | undefined // oldest request when the watchdog was armed replied: boolean // 60 s boot window until the first reply, then 15 s requests: ReadonlyMap // every unsettled request, posted or queued projectLanes: ReadonlyMap // { active, queued? } per key projections: ReadonlyMap highlightLanes: ReadonlyMap highlightStreams: ReadonlyMap }) | (Counters & { status: "failed"; message: string }) type Counters = { issued: number; attempts: number; failures: number; generationFloor: number } ``` ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> idle idle --> ready: *.requested / spawn-worker(attempt + 1), post, arm-watchdog ready --> ready: requests, replies, disposals (stale attempt ignored) ready --> failed: worker.crashed / spawn-failed / watchdog.fired with no progress\nclose-worker, reject all, schedule-retry failed --> failed: *.requested / reject unavailable failed --> idle: retry.ready(attempt) ``` | Event in `ready` | Result | | --- | --- | | `project` / `highlight` requested, key idle | post, lane `{ active }`, arm the watchdog if disarmed | | requested, key busy | hold as `queued`, reject the previous `queued` as superseded | | reply for the active id | settle, post the `queued` snapshot | | `project` reply with `from` past the held blocks | reject, `dispose` the key, post the queued snapshot | | `error` reply on a keyed request | reject, forget the key's base on both sides, post the queued snapshot | | reply for an unknown id | ignored (same state object) | | `watchdog.fired`, oldest request moved on | re-arm once | | `watchdog.fired`, same oldest request | `failed` | | first `worker.message` | `replied`; later windows are 15 s instead of 60 s | - `markdown-worker.ts` is the thin driver: `createMarkdownWorkerClient(spawn)` runs effects, owns the attempt-keyed workers and timers, and settles promises by id. Each worker's handlers carry their attempt, so a dead worker's queued `message` or `error` cannot touch the next one. - `generationFloor` keeps a recreated stream (after a crash, error or eviction) from reusing a generation the DOM already rendered, so it resets instead of appending. ### Deleted - `markdown-worker-transport.ts` and its test (moved into the machine's lanes and tests). - The module bindings `worker`, `disabled`, `nextID`, `pending`, `projects`, `parses`, `projected`, `states`, `keys`, `latest`, and the two transports' `active`/`queued` maps. - The per-supersede `new MarkdownWorkerSupersededError()` (now a `markdownWorkerSuperseded` singleton, like `markdownWorkerDisposed`) and the `.finally()` wrapper promise in `parseMarkdown`. ### Product calls - Retry is unlimited with backoff (2 s doubling to 60 s, reset by any worker reply) rather than a fixed count, so a transient failure always recovers and a blocked worker does not respawn every 2 s. - A request made during the cooldown rejects at once (plain-text fallback) instead of waiting for the new worker. - The 15 s hang window is per oldest request: a long batch that keeps settling requests never trips it. A new worker gets 60 s before its first reply. - A code block that fell back to plain text during an outage stays plain until it re-renders (unchanged; follow-up). ### Deviations from the design - No `disposed` state: nothing in `session-ui` uses `import.meta.hot`, and the worker lives as long as the page, as before. - No status selectors: no UI reads the worker state. - Backoff added to the fixed 2 s retry. ### Follow-up (not in this PR) Per-chunk allocations in neighbouring modules, flagged by the design and left unchanged: 1. `applyMarkdownWorkerResponse` + `updateCodeBlock` copy every prior `stable` token per completed line (O(N²) over a long code block). 2. `projectMarkdown` / `runProject` structured-clone the whole reply text on every delta. 3. `highlightStreamingCode` / `highlight` send the whole code block every delta, and build token arrays with `Array.from().flat().filter().map()`. 4. `renderCachedMarkdown` / `startMarkdown` allocate a `Symbol`, `Set`, `AbortController` and promise chain per uncached live block per delta. 5. `applyProjectionBlocks` allocates a slice and a spread array per projection response. ### Benchmark The machine runs on every streamed delta, so I ran `packages/app/perf/stream.bench.ts` › "stream a reply" (160 deltas with tables and code fences, 40 a second) on a MacBook Air (M4). Windows was locked. Base `483969a884` (this PR's merge base), head this PR. The only local edit, which is not committed, is `page.idle()` → `page.idle(null)` in the bench file (the "dirty" mark below). | Metric | Before | This PR | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Main-thread work per run (median) | 770 ms | 770 ms | | Frame gap, p95 | 33.3 ms | 33.3 ms | | Dropped frames | 0% | 0% | | JavaScript time per run | 164 ms | 160 ms | | JavaScript heap | 55.0 MB | 51.6 MB | | Sampled allocations in `markdown-worker.ts` (attribution run) | 3.2 MB | 3.3 MB | | Sampled allocations in `markdown-worker-machine.ts` | — | below the 32 KB sampling interval | - Neither direction is decided. Three other benches shared the device (60% background load, 25–28% variance between launches), and strobe estimates ~105 pairs to settle it. No metric moved beyond that noise. - The `markdown-worker.ts` allocations are mostly the structured clone of worker replies, in both builds. The machine's own `Map` copies never reached a sample. strobe · exp_a8c4ec · packages/app/perf/stream.bench.ts · generated # Not decided yet: needs ~105 pairs **Stream a reply:** Main-thread work per 4.3 s run: no clear change in 12 pairs (medians 770 → 770 ms); ~105 pairs would settle it.

prs.title: fix(session-ui): drive the Pierre viewer render lifecycle with one state machine
prs.body:
Follows #61933 (line selection machine). The Pierre viewer instance lifecycle in `<File>` (pool wait, draw, rows, settle, ready, pinned height, reveal, annotations) now runs on one state machine, `packages/session-ui/src/pierre/render-machine.ts`, instead of `ReadyWatcher`, `createPoolReady`, a `rendered` counter, a `WeakSet`, `pendingReveal` and nine `instance*` variables across `TextViewer` and `DiffViewer`.

### Bugs fixed

| Sequence | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Virtualized review diff (a 40-line file) changes to an identical, empty diff | `preserve()` pinned `min-height: 960px`; the reset instance never drew `[data-line]`, so the ready watcher waited forever and the height stayed pinned (and its `MutationObserver` leaked) | The empty diff settles without waiting for rows; the pin is released. Any draw whose rows never come times out after 2 s |
| Streamed diff render 2 arrives before render 1 settled | The effect cleanup unpinned render 1's height, then `preserve()` measured 0 px and pinned nothing; the scroller collapsed | The height stays pinned across draws and is released once, when the last draw settles |
| A normal diff, then a large diff (> 500 000 chars) whose `"none"` pool is still initializing | `createPoolReady` kept a sticky `settled` flag, so the second pool was never awaited; `VirtualizedFileDiff` got an empty pool and anchored to the bottom | Each draw checks its own pool; `awaiting-pool` waits for that pool |
| The pool's `initialize()` rejects or hangs | A rejected pool was still passed to Pierre; a hung one left the viewer blank forever | `pool.settled(ok: false)` and a 10 s `pool.timed-out` draw on the main thread; a timed-out pool is skipped until it reports ready |
| Non-virtualized diff streams `(A1, B1)` → `(A2, B2)` in place | `instanceBefore` / `instanceAfter` kept `(A1, B1)`; `TextViewer` never tracked its pool | Every draw records the drawn spec (`mounted.spec`); one `needsInstanceReset` serves both viewers |

### State

```ts
type ViewerRenderState =
  | { status: "idle"; ...shared }
  | { status: "awaiting-pool"; request; mounted?; ...shared }
  | { status: "awaiting-rows"; mounted; settleFrames; ...shared }
  | { status: "settling"; mounted; framesLeft; ...shared }
  | { status: "ready"; mounted; outcome: "ready" | "timeout"; ...shared }
  | { status: "disposed" }
// shared: attempt, revision, heightPinned, reveal, timedOutPool
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> idle
  idle --> awaiting_pool: render.requested (virtualized, pool initializing)
  idle --> awaiting_rows: render.requested [preserve-height, draw, watch-rows]
  idle --> settling: render.requested (no rows expected)
  awaiting_pool --> awaiting_rows: pool.settled / pool.timed-out (main thread)
  awaiting_rows --> settling: rows.ready
  awaiting_rows --> ready: rows.timed-out [release-height, notify]
  settling --> ready: last settle.frame [release-height, reapply selection, reveal, refresh find, notify]
  ready --> settling: rows.ready (late rows after a timeout)
  ready --> awaiting_rows: render.requested
```

- Every result event carries the draw `attempt`; `pool.settled`, `rows.ready` and `settle.frame` from an earlier draw return the same state.
- `revision` changes on each draw and drives the commented-line marks; `mounted.annotated` replaces the `WeakSet`, so a draw that renders without annotations skips the extra rerender when none are due.
- The driver, `useViewerRender` in `file.tsx`, owns the instance, the row `MutationObserver`, the pool and row timers, the settle frame and the height pin. Effects may dispatch again synchronously (rows already drawn, annotations synced after a draw); the state is assigned before effects run.

### Deleted

- `ReadyWatcher`, `createReadyWatcher`, `clearReadyWatcher`, `notifyShadowReady` (`file-runtime.ts`).
- `renderViewer`, `notifyRendered`, `useAnnotationRerender`, `createPoolReady`, the `rendered` signal, `pendingReveal` and the `instance`, `instanceVirtualizer`, `instanceWorkerPool`, `instanceVirtualHunkSeparators`, `instanceFileDiff`, `instanceBefore`, `instanceAfter` variables (`file.tsx`).

### Product calls and deviations from the design

- A draw whose rows never appear reports ready after 2 s (`ROWS_READY_TIMEOUT_MS`): it releases the height and calls `onRendered`. The row watch keeps running, so rows that are only slow still get the selection, reveal and search refresh.
- `awaiting-root` and `awaiting-rows` are one phase: the driver watches the container for the shadow root, then the root for rows. `drawing` is not a phase; the driver checks rows right after the draw.
- A non-virtualized viewer with a broken pool still passes it to Pierre, as before; only virtualized viewers fall back to the main thread.
- Per streamed update this does less work than before: the old effect called `preserve()` (two `getBoundingClientRect` reads and a `getComputedStyle` walk) on every update; now the height is pinned once per burst. The rest (one transition, one row check, two settle frames) matches the old watcher. No benchmark.

### Visual

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/38e794a6-0ea6-4aed-9aeb-71dc0e173450) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a394cb14-4b4c-4f57-af42-c6b921fb5c22) |

A virtualized 40-line diff changes to an empty one (`file-viewer.spec.ts` "releases the pinned height when a diff becomes empty"). Before, the container keeps `min-height: 960px` and the scroller keeps 960 px of blank space.

## Summary

- Add actionable diagnostics for unavailable Code Mode globals while leaving ordinary typos unchanged.
- Handle inherited object names such as `constructor` and `toString` without misclassifying them.
- Update the execute prompt and docs to reflect the current module model: `require` and imports can load selected host-provided globals, but not arbitrary packages or files.

prs.title: fix(app): settle permission replies and the session header fit through state machines
prs.body:
Two small session-surface lifecycles become explicit state machines: the permission dock's manual reply, and the session header's responsive fit.

## Bugs

**Permission dock** (`session/requests/model.ts`)

- **Second reply and a false "Request failed" toast.** Click **Allow once**. The reply returns `204` before `permission.replied` arrives. `.finally()` cleared `responding`, so the buttons re-enabled while the request was still shown. A second click sent another `POST`, got `404 PermissionNotFoundError`, and showed "Request failed".
- **Buttons re-enabled during the close motion.** `permissionResponding()` returned `false` once the request left `permissionRequest()`, while `<Grow>` still showed the dock closing.
- **False toast when another client answered first.** A `404 PermissionNotFoundError` showed "Request failed" instead of closing the dock.
- **Disabled forever on a hung reply.** No timeout or abort, so a stalled reply kept all three buttons disabled.

**Session header** (`session/header/fit.ts`)

- **Stuck compact after Find closes.** At 680px, open Find (`Ctrl+F`). The usage details compact. Close Find. The fit kept the actions' width *with Find open* (354px) as the cost of expanding, instead of the 82px that compacting freed. The project name and usage details stayed hidden.
- **Flip-flop when Find opens while compact.** The fit forgot the 82px cost (`max(0, 146 - 272) = 0`). It expanded with too little room, overflowed, and compacted again on the next observer pass.

## Permission reply machine

```ts
type PermissionReplyState =
  | { status: "idle"; attempt: number }
  | { status: "responding"; attempt: number; sessionID: string; decision: PermissionDecision }
  | { status: "replied" }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> idle
  idle --> responding: decide / reply (attempt + 1, 15 s timer)
  responding --> replied: reply.succeeded(attempt) or 404 / abort
  responding --> replied: resolved (permission.replied) / abort
  responding --> idle: reply.failed(attempt) / abort, toast
  responding --> idle: reply.timed-out(attempt) / abort, toast
  responding --> idle: disposed / abort
  responding --> responding: decide, stale attempt (ignored)
  replied --> replied: decide (ignored)
```

- `isPermissionResponding(state)` disables the buttons: `responding` and `replied`.
- `isPermissionReplied(state)` drops the request from `permissionRequest()` on `204`, alongside `needsUser(autoApprove.state(id), enabled)` from `auto-approve-machine.ts`.
- `permissionResponding()` follows the last shown request, so the buttons stay disabled through the close motion.
- The driver in `model.ts` holds the states in one signal of immutable records, plus one `AbortController` and timer per active request. `replied` entries are capped at 256.

## Header fit machine

```ts
type HeaderFitState =
  | { status: "full" }
  | { status: "worktree-hidden" }
  | { status: "project-hidden" }
  | { status: "compact"; expandedWidth: number | undefined; saved: number }
```

| From | Event | Next |
| --- | --- | --- |
| any | `measured`, the full location fits | `full` (frozen) |
| any | `measured`, fits without the worktree name | `worktree-hidden` (frozen) |
| any | `measured`, fits without the project name, or no actions | `project-hidden` (frozen) |
| not `compact` | `measured`, nothing fits | `compact { expandedWidth: actions, saved: 0 }` |
| `compact` (entry) | `compact.settled` | `compact { saved: expandedWidth - compactWidth }` |
| settled `compact` | `measured`, nothing fits | same object |

- `saved` is the width compacting freed. The fit adds it back whatever Find or the review spacer do beside the details.
- The driver measures the compact actions immediately after `setState`, because Solid renders them synchronously.
- `measured` and `compact.settled` are reused objects. Title width is an indexed sibling walk without array copies or closures. Unchanged passes write no signal.

## Deleted

- `store.responding` and its unconditional `.finally()` clear.
- `store.collapse`, `store.compact`, and the `let expandedActions` closure.

## Product calls

- **A reply that does not answer in 15 s** aborts, shows "Request failed", and re-enables the buttons. A retry that gets `404` counts as answered.
- **`404 PermissionNotFoundError` means answered**, as in `data.session.permission.reply` and auto-approve.
- **Leaving the session aborts the in-flight reply on the client.** The server usually has it already.

## Deviations from the design

- `INITIAL_PERMISSION_REPLY_STATE` is a frozen constant, not a factory. It lives only in a signal of immutable records, never in a store.
- `reply.failed` always carries `error`, because the driver always has one.
- `transitionHeaderFit` returns the state only. It has no effects.
- No strobe run. The fit runs on resize but now allocates less per pass than `dev` and is not a per-frame path.

## Screenshots

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 680px header after Find opens and closes | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92d6be59-e2e4-4934-93d2-534b9827750d) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/798eb57a-ae9d-480e-9528-28181e86462d) |
| Permission dock after the reply returns `204`, before `permission.replied` | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5cce0f8-6f30-4d68-bcb7-4c12cf466a8e) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4fc4c37e-0f77-4fd9-976a-ee5cae937b30) |

### Visual

```svg
  <rect x="40" y="8" width="160" height="56" rx="6" stroke-opacity=".5">
```
