prs.title: fix(app): drive the terminal pane through one state machine
prs.body:
## Summary

The terminal pane (`packages/gui-plugins/src/terminal/terminal.tsx`) now runs through one explicit state machine, `pane-machine.ts`. This fixes three user-visible bugs:

- **A silent terminal stays invisible.** The pane started at `opacity: 0` and showed only after its first write or a failure. A terminal with an empty snapshot whose shell prints nothing never wrote anything: `writer.ts` drops the empty checkpoint, and the socket sends only `attached` + `replay_complete`. The panel stayed blank for good.
- **A failure leaves the socket open.** Only an `outdated` failure closed the socket. On a socket `error`, the pane showed "Terminal connection failed" while its socket stayed `OPEN` or `CONNECTING`, with live listeners. A `connect()` that resolved after the failure still attached its socket.
- **Loading and connecting have no time limit.** A hung ghostty-web/WASM load, snapshot, ticket or WebSocket handshake kept the pane invisible, with no banner and no `onFailure`.

| Before (`dev`) | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/35b9fa7f-da85-42f0-b912-16ca36fccbf8) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bd422300-66a7-4c37-b57f-75cb0077ed93) |

A silent terminal with an empty snapshot, 1.5 s after its socket opened (component fixture, dark theme). Before: the pane is transparent and the story behind it shows through. After: the pane shows.

## State

```ts
type PaneState<T> =
  | { status: "idle" }
  | { status: "loading" }
  | { status: "opening" }
  | { status: "connecting"; term: T; sizing: PaneSizing; shown: boolean }
  | { status: "live"; term: T; sizing: PaneSizing }
  | { status: "failed"; failure: TerminalFailure; term: T | undefined }
  | { status: "disposed" }

// The size this attachment asks for; `seq` names the pending debounce timer.
type PaneSizing = { seq: number; size: TerminalSize | undefined; pending: TerminalSize | undefined }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> idle
  idle --> loading: mounted / load-ghostty (30 s)
  loading --> opening: ghostty.loaded / open-terminal
  loading --> failed: ghostty.failed, timed-out(loading)
  opening --> connecting: terminal.opened / apply-size, start-connect (15 s)
  opening --> failed: connection.failed / release
  connecting --> connecting: screen.written (shown)
  connecting --> live: socket.opened
  connecting --> failed: connection.failed, timed-out(connecting)
  live --> failed: connection.failed
  failed --> disposed: disposed / release
  idle --> disposed
  loading --> disposed: disposed / release
  opening --> disposed: disposed / release
  connecting --> disposed: disposed / release
  live --> disposed: disposed / release
```

- **Reveal:** `paneRevealed` is true once the pane wrote its restored screen (`shown`), its socket opened (`live`), or it failed.
- **Every entry into `failed`** emits `stop` (cancel the phase timer, measurement and size timer; abort the connect attempt, which detaches the socket listeners; close a `CONNECTING`/`OPEN` socket) and `notify-failure`. The machine only moves forward, so `props.onFailure` fires at most once per mount. That is the contract `surface-machine.ts` needs for its single remount after a reconnect. Unmount emits `release` and never `notify-failure`.
- **Sizing:** `terminal.opened` carries a synchronous `fit.proposeDimensions()` sample, so the first size goes out before `start-connect` instead of one frame later. Unchanged samples arm no timer. A hidden pane (`undefined`) or a bounce back to the current size cancels the pending timer, and `size.debounced` applies only for the current `seq`.
- **Driver:** `createPaneDispatch` queues re-entrant events, such as `open-terminal` dispatching `terminal.opened`. Each effect runs isolated (`Promise.try`). A throwing `load-ghostty`, `open-terminal` or `start-connect` becomes a failure event instead of a stuck pane.

## Deleted

- `disposed`, `revealed`, `measured`, `term`, `socket`, `fitAddon`, `measureFrame`, `sizeTimer` closure variables, the `opened`/`failure` signals, `reveal()` and the imperative `container.style.opacity`.
- The `if (disposed)` checks after every `await`. An `AbortController` per connect attempt fences late results, and its signal removes the socket listeners.
- `debugTerminal(...values: unknown[])` and `typeof document` (anti-slop lint).

## Deviations from the design

- **`shown` on `connecting`:** the pane also reveals on its first write, as `dev` did, so a restored screen does not wait for the WebSocket handshake. Silent terminals reveal on `socket.opened`.
- **One `stop` effect** replaces `cancel-phase-timer` + `stop-sizing` + `close-connection` on failure, and `release` replaces `release-terminal` for a failed open.
- **No `frame` flag in `PaneSizing`:** the driver coalesces animation frames itself. `measure.requested` returns the same state and a shared effect array, so resize drags allocate nothing for requests.
- **Writes continue in `failed`:** output that was already queued still lands, so the last screen is complete. The socket is closed, so no new output arrives. `paneWritableTerm` and `paneCanSend` were dropped: `send` checks the open socket handle.
- **Focus timers clear on unmount only.** A failed pane can still take focus for selection and copy. The pointer-down focus timer is now tracked and replaced, not leaked.

## Product calls

- Timeouts: 30 s for the ghostty-web load, 15 s for snapshot + ticket + WebSocket open. A timeout shows "Terminal connection failed" and reports `onFailure`, like any other connect failure.

## Tests

- `pane-machine.test.ts`: replays each bug (silent reveal, failure stops and fences late events, both timeouts with late `ghostty.loaded`/`socket.opened`), the sizing cases (first size before connect, hide and bounce cancel, only the latest `seq` applies), unmount from every phase, and the driver queue with a throwing `open-terminal`.
- `component-tests/terminal.spec.ts`: "shows a terminal that has written nothing yet and stays silent" mounts the real pane against an empty snapshot and checks `opacity: 1` and no failure. It fails on `dev` (`Received: "0"`).

Off the hot path: no benchmark. Resize sampling does the same per-frame work as before.

### Visual

prs.title: fix(app): track declared session-store retention in an explicit state machine
prs.body:
Declared plugin session stores (`createSessionStore`) now keep their retention in one explicit machine (`runtime/plugin/session-store-machine.ts`), replacing the `entries` map and the `listed` set kept beside it.

### Bugs

- **Stores no tab listed stayed open for good.** A session that was routed and preloaded but never got a tab (an abandoned deep link, a session opened without a tab) stayed in `entries` until the plugin was disposed. Now stores no tab lists are capped at 16 (`SESSION_STORE_MAX_UNLISTED`), and the oldest one closes first. The routed session's store is never closed this way.
- **`get()` after `dispose()` leaked a root.** It created a new `createRoot` that nothing disposed. It now returns an inert handle (`value: undefined`, `ready() === false`, writes ignored).

### State

```ts
type SessionStoreEntry<E> = { retention: "unlisted" | "listed"; order: number; value: E }

type SessionStoreState<E> =
  | { status: "active"; issued: number; entries: Record<string, SessionStoreEntry<E>> }
  | { status: "disposed" }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> unlisted: opened (no tab lists it)
  [*] --> listed: opened (a tab lists it)
  unlisted --> listed: sync (a tab lists it)
  unlisted --> closed: opened/sync past the cap, oldest first, not routed
  listed --> closed: sync (tab gone, not routed)
  unlisted --> closed: disposed
  listed --> closed: disposed
```

| Event | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `opened(key, listed, routed)` | Inserts the entry, then closes the oldest non-routed `unlisted` entries past the cap. |
| `sync(listed, routed)` | Upgrades listed keys, closes `listed` entries whose tab closed unless routed, and applies the cap. Returns the same state when nothing changed. |
| `disposed` | Closes every entry; a later `opened` closes its value at once. |

### Deleted

- `entries` map, the parallel `listed` set, and their hand-kept sync in the render effect, `get()` and `dispose()`.

### Product calls

- **New: unlisted stores are capped.** This is a behavior change. On `dev`, a store no tab lists stays open until the plugin goes away. With this PR, past 16 such stores the oldest closes; reading it again reopens it from storage.
- The cap uses open order, not the last read: the routed session is already protected, and the other unlisted stores are preloads.

### Deviations from the design

- `ensure` became `opened`: the driver reads an existing entry through `selectSessionStoreEntry`, so the event fires only for a new store.
- The retention table is a plain variable, not a Solid store, so no store identity test.
- Off the hot path: no benchmark.

### Visual

prs.title: fix(app): drive the directory picker with explicit state machines
prs.body:
The folder picker ("Open project", "Add project") ran on loose store flags (`loading`, `error`, `rootValid`, `suggestionsOpen`, `activeSuggestion`), a shared `navigation` counter, and two `createResource`s. This PR replaces them with two explicit machines: `tree-machine.ts` (root, listings, reveal) and `combobox-machine.ts` (path input and suggestions).

### Bugs fixed

- **Enter/Tab acted on the previous query's suggestions.** `currentPickerSuggestions` kept the old items while the next search loaded, and the implicit highlight pointed at item 0.
  - Trigger: type `alp`, wait for `alpha/`, type `beta`, press Enter (or Tab) before the search returns.
  - Before: the picker selects `alpha`, or Tab completes it. After: Enter opens `beta`, and Tab does nothing.
- **Concurrent reveals overwrote newer choices.** Two `selectDirectory` calls shared one `navigation` token. A slow reveal could finish later, then select its folder or fall back to a root navigation over the user's newer choice.
  - Trigger: click recent project A (deep path, slow listing), then click recent project B or a tree row.
  - Now `ready` holds at most one `reveal`. A new choice, a tree click, or typing replaces the reveal. A late listing still adds its rows, but cannot move the selection.
- **The picker could stay blank or wipe typed text while it started.**
  - Without a dialog location, a failed or hung `location.get()` left the pane blank with no message.
  - When the location resolved late, the first navigation reset `input` to `""`. Text typed during startup was lost.
  - Now the location request has a 30 s timeout and ends in the read error. The next navigation retries it. The first navigation does not touch the input. Suggestions search again when the location or root arrives.
- **Superseded preloads kept their place in the queue.** `createPriorityTaskQueue` could not drop jobs. Now `clear()` aborts every job, queued or running, and every new root, failed root, and dispose clears the queue.
- **A hung listing loaded forever.** Each listing now has a 30 s timeout that starts when the listing starts, and each search has a 10 s timeout. A child folder that fails or times out goes to `failed` and tries again on its next expand. The root stays readable, and the user can still confirm it.
- **Hung listings no longer block later ones.** Each queue task gets an `AbortSignal`, which goes to `file.list`. When a listing times out, `abort(key)` cancels the request and frees its slot at once, so three stalled listings cannot keep a new root on "Loading".

### State

```ts
type PickerTreeState =
  | { status: "booting"; issued; locating?: number; locationDirectory?; pending?: PickerTarget }
  | { status: "loading"; issued; attempt; root; selectChild?; locationDirectory? }
  | { status: "ready"; issued; root; selected; dirs: Record<string, PickerDirState>; entries; gitRepos; reveal?: PickerReveal; locationDirectory? }
  | { status: "error"; issued; root; locationDirectory? }
  | { status: "disposed" }

type PickerDirState =
  | { status: "loading"; attempt; priority: "user" | "background" }
  | { status: "ready" }
  | { status: "failed" }

type PickerComboboxState =
  | { status: "closed"; attempt; input }
  | { status: "loading"; attempt; input; step?: -1 | 1 } // holds no items
  | { status: "open"; attempt; input; items; active: number | null }
  | { status: "disposed" }
```

`issued` numbers every location and listing request. A result whose attempt is not current is dropped inside `transitionPickerTree`. Combobox results carry the search `attempt` in the same way.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> booting
  booting --> booting: location.requested (no dialog location)
  booting --> loading: navigate (located) / location.resolved with pending root
  booting --> error: location.failed / timed-out
  loading --> ready: dir.loaded root
  loading --> error: dir.failed / timed-out root
  ready --> ready: dir.* child, dir.expanded, directory.chosen inside root (reveal), tree.selected
  ready --> loading: navigate / chosen outside root / reveal target missing
  error --> loading: navigate
  error --> booting: navigate without location (retries location.get)
  booting --> disposed
  loading --> disposed
  ready --> disposed
  error --> disposed
```

| Combobox | Event | Next | Effects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| any | `input.changed` (searchable) | `loading` attempt+1 | `selection.clear`, `search.start` |
| any | `input.changed` (empty, equals root, or no location) | `closed` / `open []` | `selection.clear`, cancel |
| `loading` | `search.resolved` (current attempt) | `open` | — |
| `loading` | `search.failed` / `timed-out` | `open []` | cancel on timeout |
| `loading` / `open` | `context.changed` (root or location changed) | `loading` attempt+1 | `search.start` |
| `open` with active item | Enter / click | `closed` | `choose.directory` / `choose.file` |
| any (no active item) | Enter | `closed` (shows the resolved folder) | cancel, `choose.directory(input)` |
| `loading` | Tab | unchanged, passes through | — |
| `open` with items | Tab | `loading` (folder) / `closed` (file) | `search.start` / `choose.file` |
| `open` / `closed` / `loading` | ArrowUp/Down | step / search with `step` / store `step` | — |

The dialog is a thin driver. Both states live in one `createSignal({ tree, combobox })`, and each write replaces the state whole, so no store merge can share objects between entries. The driver runs each effect isolated (`Promise.try(...).catch`). It owns the queue, the timers, and the search `AbortController`. `createDirectorySearch` now takes `{ signal }` instead of keeping its own token.

### Deleted

- Store flags `root`, `input`, `selected`, `suggestionsOpen`, `activeSuggestion`, `loading`, `error`, `rootValid`.
- The `listings` map, the `gitRepos` set, and the `let navigation` counter.
- The imperative `load`, `navigate`, `selectDirectory`, `complete`, `chooseSuggestion`, and `handleInputKey` functions.
- The `fallbackPath` and `suggestions` resources.
- `currentPickerSuggestions`, `activeTreeNavigation`, and the `let current` token in `createDirectorySearch`.

### Product calls and deviations from the design

- **Tab while the search loads passes through.** It does not complete stale items. Focus moves on, as when there are no suggestions.
- **A trailing backslash counts as a folder path.** `C:\Users\luke\` now behaves like `~/`: Enter submits the folder unless the user steps into the list.
- **IME composition ignores Enter.** An Enter that confirms a composition (`isComposing`) does nothing in the picker.
- **A file picker no longer offers a folder as its result.** When the user chooses a folder in file mode, the tree opens it, but `selected` stays empty. Before, `selected` held the absolute folder path, so "Select file" returned a folder.
- **`aria-expanded` follows the visible listbox.** It is true only when `#directory-picker-suggestions` exists.
- **Simpler machines than the design.**
  - `reveal.id` and the combobox `contextKey` are gone: the driver sends `context.changed` only when the root or location really changes.
  - The design's `tree.deselect` effect is gone. Typing clears `selected` without touching tree rows, as on `dev`.
  - One `cleared` event replaces both `input.cleared` and `reset`.
- **State lives in a signal instead of a store.** Both states sit in one signal, which avoids store merges entirely. So the two-entry store isolation test does not apply.
- **Retries are unchanged.** The replaced resources had no retries (`createResource` has none, and `location.get()` errors were caught as `undefined`), so the machines add none.
- **Off the hot path.** These are dialog interactions only, so the PR has no benchmark.

### Tests

- `tree-machine.test.ts` replays the concurrent-reveal bug. It covers child failure versus root failure, a new root dropping stale listings, the reveal path and its fallback, a home child outside the root, location success, failure, timeout and retry, promotion, the git badge, the file-mode boundary, and dispose.
- `combobox-machine.test.ts` replays Enter and Tab during loading and stale attempts. It covers the implicit highlight table, arrows, Escape, Shift+Tab, IME, hover, Tab and click on folders and files, typing before the location resolves, search failure and timeout, and clear, dismiss and dispose.
- `e2e/regression/directory-picker.spec.ts` has two new keepers:
  - Tab and Enter while the search loads act on the typed folder. This test fails on `dev`.
  - A folder that cannot be listed leaves the root readable and tries again when expanded.

### Visual

| Before (Enter while `beta` searches) | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7912f357-aba9-4615-89fa-bdb6ae4f3569) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/079290a9-0b57-48d4-9987-6d9d3cb1506e) |

prs.title: fix(session-ui): drive file line selection with one state machine
prs.body:
Line selection in `<File>` (file viewer, review diffs, line comments) now runs on one state machine, `packages/session-ui/src/pierre/selection-machine.ts`, instead of seven closure variables in `useFileViewer`, two side variables in `DiffViewer` and the `createLineNumberSelectionBridge` closure.

### Bugs fixed

| Sequence | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Drag lines 3→6 where the browser text selection stays collapsed (whitespace, script events), release in the same frame | `mouseup` cleared the drag before its frame ran; `onLineSelectionEnd(null)`, nothing highlighted | Commits `{ start: 3, end: 6 }` from the drag end points |
| Drag 2→5, release, press on line 10 and drag before the next frame | The first drag's finishing frame fired `onLineSelectionEnd` with the second, unfinished drag (`{10..12}`) | A new press cancels the first drag's frames; only the second drag ends, on its own release |
| Turn `enableLineSelection` off mid-drag | Listeners went away, but `dragStart` and queued frames stayed; turning it back on resumed a ghost drag | `selection.disabled` ends the gesture and cancels its frames |
| Number-column drag | `mouseHit` never read `data-column-number`, so the bridge never saw movement; its `pending` flag leaked into the next selection and could double-fire `onLineNumberSelectionEnd` a frame later | Gutter hits carry their line; Pierre's `onLineSelectionEnd` ends the gesture once, with `fromNumberDrag` derived from the phase |
| Hover with no button pressed | Every `mousemove` walked `composedPath()` and allocated a hit object | `mousemove` returns after one status check unless a gesture is active |
| Diff with an initial `selectedLines` | The controlled effect ran before the instance existed and the range was lost | The machine stores the range; the ready callback applies it |

### State

```ts
type FileSelectionState =
  | { status: "idle"; mode; selected; attempt }
  | { status: "pressing"; column: "text"; origin: SelectionPoint; ... }
  | { status: "pressing"; column: "numbers"; originLine: number | undefined; ... }
  | { status: "dragging"; column: "text"; origin: SelectionPoint; current: SelectionPoint; ... }
  | { status: "dragging"; column: "numbers"; ... }
  | { status: "finishing"; range: SelectedLineRange; ... }
  | { status: "disposed" }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  idle --> pressing: pointer.down
  pressing --> dragging: pointer.move (other line) / selection.changed
  pressing --> idle: pointer.up (click toggles one line)
  dragging --> finishing: pointer.up (text) [cancel-frames, schedule-finish]
  finishing --> idle: finish.frame (attempt matches) [apply, notify end]
  finishing --> pressing: pointer.down [cancel-frames]
  pressing --> idle: pierre.selection-ended / button lost / selection.disabled
  dragging --> idle: pierre.selection-ended (numbers, fromNumberDrag) / button lost / selection.disabled
```

- `drag.frame`, `selection.frame` and `finish.frame` carry the gesture `attempt`; a frame from an earlier gesture returns the same state with no effects.
- `selection.controlled` (the `selectedLines` prop) and `pierre.line-selected` update `selected` in any phase. The render-ready callback reapplies `selectSelectedRange(state)`.
- The driver in `useFileViewer` keeps the state in a plain variable (no signal), owns the three frame handles, and reuses one hit object and one `pointer.move` event, so a move that stays on the same line allocates nothing and returns the same state.

### Deleted

- `createLineNumberSelectionBridge` and `PointerMode` (`selection-bridge.ts`); the range helpers stay.
- `selectionFrame`, `dragFrame`, `dragStart`, `dragEnd`, `dragMoved`, `lastSelection`, `pendingSelectionEnd` (`useFileViewer`); `dragSide`, `dragEndSide` and the `buildDragSelection` / `buildClickSelection` / `onDrag*` adapter hooks (`DiffViewer`); `createLineCallbacks`, `useModeViewer`, `ModeAdapter`.

### Product calls and deviations from the design

- A second press inside the finishing frame drops the first drag's end callback rather than flushing it; the second gesture ends normally.
- A pointer that jitters on the pressed line is still a click, so clicking a selected line clears it as intended. Before, any move made it a drag.
- `onLineSelectionEnd` and `onLineNumberSelectionEnd` never both fire: the number callback fires only for a multi-line number drag when no `onLineSelectionEnd` is passed. No caller on `dev` passes it; the prop stays.
- Ranges the machine builds (click, drag) are adjusted to Pierre's rows inside `apply-selection` and before `onLineSelectionEnd`, not before dispatch, so `pointer.up`, `drag.frame` and `finish.frame` carry no ranges. `dragging(numbers)` keeps no line numbers: Pierre owns that range, and only "moved" matters.
- Off the per-frame hot path: hover now does less work than before, and a drag adds one state object per line change. No benchmark.
- The Pierre viewer render lifecycle (ready watcher, pool readiness, height pinning) follows in a stacked PR.

### Visual

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/945a7aea-61ff-48f7-bbd8-9e84d89a1e8b) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e33e835-64a5-4ac7-820d-e15d06c4495c) |

Drag lines 3→6 with a collapsed text selection (`file-viewer.spec.ts` "commits a drag whose text selection stays collapsed").

prs.title: fix(app): drive the voice WebRTC transport from an explicit state machine
prs.body:
`VoiceTransport` (`packages/app/src/voice/transport.ts`) tracked its WebRTC lifecycle with an `ended` flag, `closing`/`closed`/`ready` promises, a public `AbortController` and ad-hoc `connectionState`/`readyState` reads. This moves that lifecycle into one pure machine, `transport-machine.ts`, beside the merged `call-machine.ts`, `machine.ts` and `reply-machine.ts`. The transport stays the per-attempt WebRTC edge that `call.ts` creates in `join()`. It does not copy any call, delegation or reply state.

## Bugs fixed

| # | Trigger | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Live call → `session.update` (tab switch), `response.create` or `session.commentary.append` rejected with `{ type: "error", error: { type: "invalid_request_error", ... } }` | `Envelope` dropped `error`, and every `error` called `fail()`, so a working call dropped | `protocol.ts` decodes `error.{type,code,message,event_id}`. Once live, only auth, quota and expiry errors drop the call. Other errors keep the call live and are logged with `console.warn`. If Live rejects the `response.create` sent after a tool round, that delegation ends as discarded at once instead of waiting out `RESPONSE_TIMEOUT` (60 s) |
| 2 | Wi-Fi roam or 1–2 s packet loss → `connectionState: "disconnected"` → ICE recovers | Dropped at once | A 5 s grace timer, fenced by attempt. `connected` cancels it. `failed`/`closed` still drop at once |
| 3 | Channel close, peer failure, `session.closed`, an `audio.play()` reject or a startup `error` **while joining** | `dropped()` ran before `join()` rejected. The panel said "The call disconnected." for a call that never connected | Join-phase failures reject `join` with `connection`/`microphone`/`unavailable` and never send `dropped` |
| 4a | End → server closes the channel/peer without `session.closed` | `ended` made `onclose` a no-op, so teardown waited the full 1 s | Channel close, peer close or `session.closed` during the handshake releases the peer at once |
| 4b | Server sends `session.closed` | `session.close` was sent back | No `session.close` is sent to a session the server already closed |
| 4c | End after SCTP opened but before `session.started` | Sent `session.close` and waited 1 s | Releases at once; only a started session gets the close handshake |
| 5 | 35 s join timeout fires during `voice.models`, ICE or `voice.session` | `onicegatheringstatechange` stayed attached and the transport stayed open until `call.ts` closed it; a microphone granted late could stay on | `join.timeout` is a machine event: it stops media, detaches the ICE listener and rejects `join`. A microphone granted after End or the timeout is stopped at once |

## State

```ts
type VoiceTransportState =
  | { status: "idle" }
  | { status: "connecting"; step: ConnectStep; sessionStarted: boolean; seq: number; disconnectedAttempt?: number }
  | { status: "live"; seq: number; disconnectedAttempt?: number }
  | { status: "closing"; step: "handshake" | "releasing" }
  | { status: "closed" }

type ConnectStep =
  | { type: "offer"; viewing; tail }  // resume audio, voice.models, local offer
  | { type: "ice"; viewing; tail }    // wait for ICE gathering
  | { type: "negotiating" }           // voice.session + remote answer
  | { type: "awaiting-started" }      // wait for session.started
  | { type: "mic" }                   // getUserMedia + replaceTrack
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> idle
  idle --> connecting: join
  idle --> releasing: close
  connecting --> connecting: offer.ready / ice.complete / answer.applied / session.started
  connecting --> live: mic.ready (join.resolve)
  connecting --> handshake: close · join.timeout · step.failed · error · audio fail (session started) → join.reject
  connecting --> releasing: same, before session.started · channel/peer/session closed → join.reject
  live --> live: peer disconnected (grace) · connected · non-fatal error
  live --> handshake: close · fatal error · grace expired · audio fail (→ dropped, except close)
  live --> releasing: channel.closed · peer failed/closed · session.closed (→ dropped)
  handshake --> releasing: session.closed · channel.closed · peer closed · close.timeout
  releasing --> closed: peer.released (close.resolve)
```

- Stale step results (`offer.ready`, `ice.complete`, `answer.applied`, `mic.ready`, `step.failed`) match the current `step`. A `disconnect.timeout` must match `disconnectedAttempt`. Anything else returns the same state with no effects.
- Terminal callbacks (`join.reject`, `notify.dropped`) come last in each effect list, after the driver has stored the next state. When `call.ts` closes the transport from inside `dropped()`, it sees `closing` and waits on the same release.

## Deleted

- `ended`, `closing`, `closed`, `ready` and the abort listener that rejected `ready`.
- The inline ICE `Promise` and `AbortSignal.timeout(35_000)`.
- The public `abort` controller. It is now private behind `get signal()` and `get canSend()`. `call.ts` reads those, and no longer checks `abort.signal.aborted` before it forwards events, because the machine stops forwarding once the transport is closing.

## Deviations from the design

- `hasLiveWebrtcModel` stays inline in the driver because only the driver uses it.
- `idle` handles only `join` and `close`. The peer has no transceivers before `join`, so the other close events cannot happen there.
- `send()` does not dispatch `channel.closed` when `readyState !== "open"`; the channel's own `close` event does that. The close handshake catches a send that throws and settles at once.
- `VoiceTransport` takes `voice: client.experimental.voice` instead of the whole `OpenCodeClient`, because it only calls `models` and `session`.
- The audio transceiver is added in the constructor, so `acquire.mic` always has a sender. The m-line order (data channel first) is unchanged.

## Product calls

- **New 5 s grace for ICE `disconnected`.** A call whose ICE stays disconnected now drops after 5 s, not at once. If it reconnects within 5 s, the call continues. `failed` and `closed` still drop at once. This is a behaviour change.
- **Fatal Live errors:** codes `session_expired`, `invalid_api_key`, `insufficient_quota`, `billing_hard_limit_reached`; types `authentication_error`, `permission_error`. Every other `error` keeps a live call, and every `error` still fails a join.
- **A failure while joining shows "Couldn't connect the call." (`connection`), not "The call disconnected." (`dropped`).** `call-machine.test.ts` "a transport failure during join keeps its reason…" still holds for the call machine, but the transport no longer sends `call.dropped` before the join settles.

## Tests

- `transport-machine.test.ts`: pure transitions, with events built through the real `decodeEvent`. It replays each bug above, plus stale steps, stale grace timers, both ICE paths, both `session.started` orders, and late events in `closing` and `closed`.
- `transport.test.ts`: driver tests with fake `RTCPeerConnection`, data channel, `AudioContext` and `getUserMedia` (WebRTC does not exist in CI), and fake timers. They cover a late microphone grant after End, End settling on a channel close, the join timeout, recovery from `disconnected` and grace expiry, and a rejected `session.update`. All five fail on the old `transport.ts`.

The change is off the hot path (connection lifecycle only), so it has no benchmark. There are no screenshots: the mocked e2e harness cannot run WebRTC against Live.

### Visual

```svg

    @keyframes dip { 0%, 30%, 70%, 100% { opacity: 1 } 40%, 60% { opacity: .25 } }
    @keyframes bar { 0%, 30% { transform: scaleX(0) } 60% { transform: scaleX(.6) } 61%, 100% { transform: scaleX(0) } }

  <path d="M20 30h8M24 26v8" stroke-width="1.5" opacity=".6" />
```

prs.title: fix(app): drive the composer morph and Grow springs with explicit state machines
prs.body:
`ComposerMorph` (the composer and request docks sharing one surface) and `Grow` (every dock, the queue panel, its rows and the Go limit tray) kept their animation lifecycles in loose flags: a `stop` handle that doubled as "in flight", a `height` spring that existed only mid-flight, a module-level `WeakMap` keyed by element, an `entering` flag and two effects that raced. This PR moves both into explicit machines in `spring-height-machine.ts` and fixes the bugs the flags allowed. Every intermediate frame is unchanged. ### Bugs fixed - **A queue, dock or tray that opens in a background tab stays invisible.** Inactive session tabs detach their DOM but keep their effects. Sequence: an event opens a `Grow` while its tab is detached → `grow()` writes `height: 0px; opacity: 0` → the first frame sees `!el.isConnected` and drops the flight without finishing it → back on the tab, the surface stays clipped at 0px. A close in a detached tab never reported `onClosed`, so the queue panel kept stale rows. Both now land where they were going. - **Reopening and turning instant in one batch mid-close unmounts the children and reports a false close.** Sequence: the question dock is closing → in one batch `when` turns truthy and `instant` turns on (the question knob off or the classic UI) → the `instant` effect ran first and finished the close (`setPresent(false)`, `onClosed`), then the other effect remounted the dock from scratch. One `sync` event now lands it `present`. - **Turning the question motion off mid-morph never settles the morph.** The settle effect read `stop` (a plain variable) and `untrack(faces)` before `props.instant`, so it tracked nothing and never ran again. It now tracks the machine state, so it subscribes to `instant` as soon as a flight starts. - **A face measured at 0px is treated as unmeasured.** Entering a subagent session with no request docks swaps the composer for an empty `docks` face. `height > 0` guarded the target, so the region held the composer's height for the whole flight and snapped to 0 on the last frame. Heights are now `number | undefined`. - **Turning Reduce Motion on mid-grow freezes the inline height** until the spring rests; it now lands at once. `Grow` also had no `onCleanup`, so its observer and frame job outlived an unmount by a frame; disposal now stops both. - **A morph whose frame job stopped without settling could never start again** (`stop ??= frameLoop.add(paint)` saw the stale handle). The handle is now cleared in one place, on every exit from `flying`. ### State ```ts type MorphState = | { status: "resting"; seq; attempt; face: MorphFace } | { status: "flying"; seq; attempt; height: Spring; entering: MorphFace; faces: MorphFace[]; shown: number } | { status: "disposed" } type GrowState = | { status: "absent"; attempt } | { status: "present"; attempt } | ({ status: "opening" } & GrowFlight) // springs, first-frame layout, per-frame pose | ({ status: "closing" } & GrowFlight) | { status: "disposed" } ``` ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 direction LR state ComposerMorph { resting --> flying: face.changed (new key, not instant) resting --> resting: face.changed (instant: fresh face) flying --> flying: face.changed (retarget, same attempt) flying --> resting: frame (all springs rest) · settle (instant face, Reduce Motion, detached root) · instant change } state Grow { absent --> opening: sync open present --> opening: sync open + appear (mount) present --> closing: sync close opening --> closing: sync close (same attempt) closing --> opening: sync open (same attempt) opening --> present: frame rests · instant · reduced · detached closing --> absent: frame rests · instant · reduced · detached (onClosed) closing --> present: sync open + instant absent --> present: sync open + instant present --> absent: sync close + instant (onClosed) } ``` - **Frames allocate nothing.** A `frame` event (one reused object per driver) steps the springs and writes the pose into the flight in place and returns the same state, so no Solid signal is written until a flight ends. The driver then writes the pose to the DOM directly, exactly as before; `styleFace` takes positional arguments instead of an options object per face per frame. - **Attempts fence stale work.** Each flight carries an attempt; frames, measures, resizes and `detached` from an earlier flight are ignored. Turning back mid-flight keeps the attempt, the springs and the first-frame measure, as before. - **Flight setup runs after the render.** A `Grow` opening from `absent` starts its flight from an effect on the machine state, so the wrapper is mounted and connected when the pre-frame writes run. Deleted: `Face` signals (`value`, `leaving`), `let height`, `let stop`, `present`/`setPresent`, `entering`, the two racing effects, `growing` (`WeakMap`), `Growth`, `grow()`'s closure flags. ### Product calls - A `Grow` whose element is detached when its flight starts, or that loses its element mid-flight, lands where it was going (opened, or closed with `onClosed`). - A key change while the morph's root is detached swaps at rest, and a flight whose root detaches mid-flight settles. - A same-key value update never settles a flight by itself; the `instant` effect settles it if the updated face is instant. - Under reduced motion, an entering face that has not been measured yet keeps the region at its current target instead of snapping it to 0 for a frame. ### Deviations from the design - One `MorphFace` type for resting and flying faces (pose fields are unused at rest), and `leaving` is derived from `entering` instead of stored. - Landing on `frame`, `reduced` or `detached` keeps the attempt; only a new flight bumps it. - Instant mid-flight swaps to a fresh face, as `dev` does, instead of reusing the composer's slot. - `Grow`'s flight setup runs from an effect on the machine state rather than inside `dispatch`, because `setState` inside the input effect does not mount `` synchronously. ### Tests - `spring-height-machine.test.ts` replays each bug (the 0px face, settle mid-flight, the reopen-plus-instant batch, detached and Reduce Motion landings, disposal) and covers retargets, stale attempts and same-reference frames. - `grow.spec.ts` (new fixture `grow.fixture.tsx`) proves through the real component that the reopen-plus-instant batch keeps the children mounted without `onClosed`, and that a `Grow` opened and closed while detached finishes both. Both fail on `dev`. - `session-question-dock.spec.ts` adds that turning the question knob off mid-morph settles `[data-slot="composer-morph"]` on the next frame. It fails on `dev`. ### Before / after A tab in the background (its DOM detached) gets two queued prompts, then comes back. On `dev` the queue panel stays clipped at 0px. | Before (`dev`) | After | | --- | --- | | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd75d42b-1934-4e63-8324-f87ae88db271) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d3c09392-834b-4e84-911d-db3948a336b3) | ### Performance The frame loop changed, so `packages/app/perf/docks.bench.ts` (new) measures it: a permission request morphs the composer into its dock, an MCP elicitation grows in above it and closes, and the answered permission morphs back, over a 20-turn session. One short run on `air` (Apple M4, 60 Hz) while another bench shared the slot. - **Frames are unchanged.** Under a fake clock, the composer docks story (permission and question morphs in and out, the queue panel and its rows growing and closing) writes the same inline styles on `dev` and this branch on every one of 540 frames, with and without Reduce Motion. - **Main-thread work: not decided.** 6 pairs, 38% launch-to-launch variance on `dev`, 21% background load; pairs land at either ~160 ms or ~400 ms on both builds. strobe's caution on late frames (5.1% → 7.5% one frame late, frame gap p95 one vsync: 25 → 33 ms) is inside that noise and needs a quieter, longer run to settle. - **Allocations and self time (one attribution launch per side, noisy discovery evidence, not a verdict):** | Attribution launch (`rec_2a6e16` → `rec_9230ae`) | `dev` | This PR | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Self time in `spring-height.tsx`, the machine has no samples of its own (+ motion loop, springs) | 138 ms (+ 5.1 ms) | 48.3 ms (+ 3.6 ms) | | Sampled allocations in `spring-height.tsx` (+ machine, motion loop, springs) | 1.8 MB (+ 128 KB) | 1.5 MB (+ 288 KB) | | `paintFaces` arrays, `Map` and option objects per frame | 576 KB | gone | | GC per run: minor / major, main-thread pause | 2 / 1, 12.6 ms | 0 / 1, 6.4 ms | What remains per frame is the style strings the DOM writes need, on both builds. strobe · exp_8ad58d · packages/app/perf/docks.bench.ts · generated # Not decided yet: needs ~176 pairs > [!CAUTION] > **Regression:** late frames rose from 5.1% to 7.5% (4 of 6 pairs) **Open and close request docks:** Main-thread work per 3.7 s run: no clear change in 6 pairs (medians 361 → 394 ms); ~176 pairs would settle it. *Other experiments compared these same builds: see Details.*
Details · metrics, pairs, profiles, method #### Metrics | Metric | Before | This PR | Change | Likely range | Verdict | |:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|:---| | Main-thread work per run main | 361 ms | 394 ms | +9.4% | −61% to +157% | inconclusive ~176 pairs | | JavaScript time per run | 79.8 ms | 83.8 ms | +10% | −65% to +192% | inconclusive | | Style time per run | 66.5 ms | 75.2 ms | +13% | −68% to +220% | inconclusive | | Layout time per run | 31.1 ms | 34.4 ms | +13% | −64% to +174% | inconclusive | | Dropped frames | 0.477% | 0.559% | +40% | −39% to +167% | inconclusive | | Frame gap, p95 | 25.0 ms | 33.3 ms | 0.0% | −50% to +100% | inconclusive | | Main-thread busy time | 9.95% | 10.4% | +6.5% | −60% to +152% | inconclusive | Likely range: 96.9% confidence. prs.title: fix(app): drive plugin store loads and deferred writes with explicit state machines
prs.body:
Plugin store loads (`persistedHandle`) and the hand-over of writes to a store that opens later (`deferredHandle`) now run on two explicit machines in `runtime/plugin/store-machine.ts`.

### Bugs

- **A failed storage read looked like loading forever.** `load.catch` only logged: the store had no state that told a failed read from a pending one, every queued write stayed in `queue`, and every later `update`/`set` pushed more without bound. Now the store moves to an explicit `failed` state, drops the queue, and ignores later writes, so the queue stops growing. `whenLoaded` still rejects, as it did on `dev`.
- **One invalid queued `update` wedged a store that loaded fine.** The flush ran the queue in `forEach` before `setLoaded(true)`, so an `update` that returned a value threw, skipped the writes behind it, and left `ready()` `false` for good. Now each queued write applies on its own (`Promise.try`), the store becomes ready, and `whenLoaded` rejects with the contract error.
  - Sequence: storage read held → `update(() => replacement)` → `update(push "valid")` → read resolves. Before: `ready() === false`, value `undefined`. Now: `ready() === true`, value `["stored", "valid"]`.
- **Writes applied backwards when the store opened in the same batch.** `batch(() => { setLocation(dir); handle.update(m2) })` with `m1` queued: `update(m2)` saw the new store through the memo and applied at once; the render effect handed `m1` over afterwards. Now every write first syncs the open store, which takes the waiting writes before the new one.

### State

```ts
type StoreLoadState<T> =
  | { status: "loading"; queue: StoreWrite<T>[] }
  | { status: "ready" }
  | { status: "failed" }
  | { status: "disposed" }

type DeferredStoreState<H, T> =
  | { status: "pending"; queue: StoreWrite<T>[] }
  | { status: "open"; handle: H }
  | { status: "disposed" }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  state "persistedHandle" as P {
    [*] --> loading: async read
    [*] --> ready: sync read
    loading --> loading: write (queue)
    loading --> ready: loaded / apply(queue, each isolated)
    loading --> failed: failed / reject + log, drop queue
    ready --> ready: write / apply (throws to caller)
    loading --> disposed: disposed / reject
    ready --> disposed
    failed --> disposed
  }
  state "deferredHandle" as D {
    [*] --> pending
    pending --> pending: write (queue)
    pending --> open: sync(handle) / handover(queue)
    open --> open: write / forward, sync(other handle)
    open --> pending: sync(undefined)
    pending --> disposed
    open --> disposed
  }
```

### Deleted

- `loaded` signal and `queue` closures in `persistedHandle`; the `queue` closures in `deferredHandle`.

### Product calls

- **Failed reads drop writes.** A store whose read failed never loads, so its writes are dropped instead of held.
- **No load timeout.** Plugin activation already bounds global store loads with its own timeout. A store-level timeout would fail stores whose storage answers late but correctly.
- **Writes made while a store reopens still wait for the next store.** On a detach or a move to another directory, the next store is the same plugin key and scope (the same session's state), so the writes go there, as on `dev`. Dropping them would lose user data.

### Deviations from the design

- Cut `DeferredStoreState.detached`, the transient-location preservation in `locatedHandle` and `host-apis.tsx`, and `storeStatus()`. Nothing in production reads a store status, so `storeStatus()` would be a test-only export. Writes that wait across a reopen are covered above.
- No attempt ids: each handle loads once and only moves forward, so the machine matches on the phase.
- No Solid store identity test: both machines hold their state in a signal or a plain variable.
- Off the hot path: no benchmark.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="10">
  <style>
    .w{animation:m 3s ease-in-out infinite}
    .w2{animation-delay:.4s}
    .r{animation:f 3s step-end infinite}
    @keyframes m{0%,20%{transform:translateX(0)}60%,100%{transform:translateX(110px)}}
    @keyframes f{0%{opacity:.25}60%{opacity:1}}
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.w,.r{animation:none}}
  </style>
  <rect x="160" y="16" width="64" height="40"/>
  <text x="170" y="50" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" class="r">ready</text>
  <g class="w"><rect x="20" y="26" width="16" height="16"/><text x="24" y="38" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">1</text></g>
  <g class="w w2"><rect x="40" y="26" width="16" height="16"/><text x="44" y="38" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">2</text></g>
</svg>
```

prs.title: fix(app): drive model selection through one workspace state machine
prs.body:
### Summary

- **Bug fixed:** a model or variant picked in a session whose tab moved to another directory was saved under the first directory. After a reload the session lost the pick and showed its committed variant again.
- **Fix:** each workspace (server and directory) now owns one explicit selection machine, `ModelSelectionState` in `packages/app/src/providers/models/selection-machine.ts`. The session's own workspace stores every write. It does not matter which provider mounted first or whether a provider shows the workspace.
- **Variant encoding:** `undefined | null | string` becomes `VariantSelection` (`inherit | default | named`). A Default without a model can no longer be stored.
- **Saved selections survive the upgrade:** `ModelSelectionSchema` still reads the old `{ model, variant: null | string }` shape and the v1 `pick` shape, then writes the new `{ choice: { providerID, modelID, variant } }` shape. See [Persisted schema](#persisted-schema).
- **Off the hot path:** a selection changes only on picker clicks, promotions and commit echoes, so no benchmark was run.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: after a reload, the Away session shows Balanced](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/360f0b8d-518c-4e5e-8256-f7cf49da9ee1) | ![After: after a reload, the Away session keeps High](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7804481a-fd3c-4beb-b5e5-90d7267f50d4) |

These screenshots come from the e2e test "keeps a variant picked in another directory's session with that session across a reload". The test opens the Home session (`C:/OpenCode/ModelHome`), switches the tab to the Away session (`C:/OpenCode/ModelAway`), picks **High**, and reloads.

### Bugs and how to trigger them

1. **Write goes to the wrong directory (visible).** `SessionUIProvider` stays mounted while session tabs switch between directories (`session/route.tsx`, "Not keyed"). `LocalProvider` opened its `persisted(...)` store once, with the directory it mounted in. Any later pick went into that first directory's storage.
2. **Module-global `handoff` Map.** `promote(dir, id)` put the selection into an in-memory map. Only a route effect that later visited `id` in `dir` moved it into storage. The map was not reactive, so the move failed when the session route mounted before the promotion. Also:
   - a session tab that was never opened leaked its entry until reload, then lost it;
   - `session.deleted` never removed entries from the map.
3. **`store.promoting` leak.** For a route without a session, `scope()` read `store.draft ?? store.promoting`. When `promote()` ran without navigating to the new session, the next draft took on the promoted agent, model and choices.
4. **Unbounded `pending` commits.** A commit that never got its echo stayed in the map until the session was deleted. A local edit did not clear it. A late echo could then clear an override that was never sent.
5. **`variant: null` without `model`.** The schema allowed it, and nothing could read it.

### State

```ts
type SessionSelectionEntry =
  | { phase: "override"; agent?: string; choice?: ModelChoice; choices: AgentChoices }
  | { phase: "awaiting-ack"; attempt: number; target: CommitTarget; agent?: string; choice?: ModelChoice; choices: AgentChoices }
  | { phase: "committed"; choices: AgentChoices } // the server's selection shows; only per-agent memory is kept

type ModelSelectionState =
  | { status: "hydrating"; attempt: number; sessions: Record<string, SessionSelectionEntry>; deleted: string[] }
  | { status: "ready"; attempt: number; sessions: Record<string, SessionSelectionEntry> }
  | { status: "disposed" }

type ModelChoice = { providerID: string; modelID: string; variant: VariantSelection }
type VariantSelection = { type: "inherit" } | { type: "default" } | { type: "named"; value: string }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> override: edited / session.promoted (not yet committed) / session.restored
  [*] --> committed: session.promoted (create already committed it)
  override --> awaitingAck: commit.tracked (attempt n, starts 10 s timer)
  committed --> awaitingAck: commit.tracked
  awaitingAck --> committed: commit.reconciled, matches, on screen
  awaitingAck --> override: commit.reconciled off screen · commit.cancelled(n) · commit.timed-out(n) · edited
  awaitingAck --> awaitingAck: commit.tracked (attempt n+1)
  override --> committed: commit.tracked, already echoed, on screen
  override --> [*]: session.deleted
  committed --> [*]: session.deleted
  awaitingAck --> [*]: session.deleted
```

| Workspace event | `hydrating` | `ready` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| any entry change | kept in memory, no write | `persist.write` with a fresh object |
| `session.deleted` | entry dropped, ID added to `deleted` | entry dropped, `persist.write(undefined)` |
| `hydrated` | stored entries, minus `deleted`, under the in-memory ones; writes the in-memory entries | ignored |
| `disposed` | `ack-timer.clear-all` | `ack-timer.clear-all` |

A stale `commit.cancelled(n)` or `commit.timed-out(n)` returns the same state object.

### Driver

- **Workspace handle:** `acquireWorkspace(scope, dir)` returns a reference-counted handle keyed by `ScopedKey.from(scope, pathKey(dir))`. Each handle owns its `persisted(...)` store, the state signal, the ack timers and the set of viewers.
- **Provider:** `LocalProvider` holds the handle for `sdk().directory` in a memo, so it moves to the new workspace when the session tab changes directory. It registers its routed session as a viewer.
- **Promotion:** `promote(dir, id, …)` holds the target handle only for the dispatch. When no provider shows `dir`, the handle closes at once, and closing flushes the store. When the desktop store is still loading, the handle stays open until the load settles.
- **On screen or not:** `visible` in commit events comes from the handle's viewers, not from one provider's route. Two providers on one workspace therefore agree about the same echo.
- **Store writes:** `persist.write` builds new objects with `writeStored(...)`, so the Solid store never shares an object with the machine or with another entry.

### Persisted schema

```jsonc
// before (v2), still read
{ "session": { "ses_1": { "agent": "build", "model": { "providerID": "p", "modelID": "m" }, "variant": null,
                          "choices": { "plan": { "model": { "providerID": "p", "modelID": "n" }, "variant": "high" } } } } }
// after (v3), written
{ "session": { "ses_1": { "agent": "build", "choice": { "providerID": "p", "modelID": "m", "variant": { "type": "default" } },
                          "choices": { "plan": { "providerID": "p", "modelID": "n", "variant": { "type": "named", "value": "high" } } } } } }
```

- The migration maps `null` to `default`, a missing value to `inherit`, and a string to `named`.
- A variant without a model is dropped: `{ agent, variant: null }` becomes `{ agent }`.
- Entries already in the new shape pass through unchanged. The v1 `pick` shape still migrates.

### Removed

- `store.current`, `store.draft` and `store.promoting`.
- The module-global `handoff` Map and the route effect that drained it.
- The `pending` Map and `sameSelection`.
- `local.model.variant.selected()`. The variant selectors in `selection-machine.ts` replace it, and the story stubs no longer include it.

### Changes from the design

- **Drafts stay with their provider:** each `LocalProvider` keeps its draft in a signal. The workspace machine does not hold it, because two draft tabs on one directory would then share one agent pick. Promoting clears the draft, so bug 3 cannot happen.
- **Hydration is a phase:** `hydrated: boolean` is now the `hydrating` and `ready` statuses. `hydrating` carries the session IDs deleted while the store loads.
- **`promote()` input:** it takes `{ agent, model, variant, choices }` with the committed variant (`undefined` = Default). Callers no longer pass `variant ?? null`.

### Product calls

- **Echo timeout:** a commit stops waiting for its echo after 10 s and keeps the local selection. This matches what `dev` did for a missed echo, but the wait now ends.
- **Off-screen echo:** an echo that arrives while no provider shows the session keeps the local selection, as on `dev`. When you return, the session shows what you last picked in it.
- **Fallback agent:** with no local or committed agent, the fallback is the first listed agent. `dev` instead remembered the last agent picked in the provider (`store.current`).

### Tests

- `selection-machine.test.ts` tests the pure machine:
  - immediate persistence without a route visit;
  - promotions and deletions during hydration;
  - a local edit that ends the commit wait (bug 4);
  - the bounded echo timeout;
  - stale cancels and timeouts;
  - echoes on and off screen;
  - disposal.
- `test-browser/fixtures/model-selection.ts`: two new `LocalProvider` cases both fail on `dev`:
  - an unnavigated promotion leaves the next draft empty;
  - a promotion into a workspace that no provider shows is written to that workspace only, and two sessions there keep separate per-agent memory.
- The persistence consumer tests decode v1, v2, orphan-variant and v3 entries, and round-trip them.
- e2e:
  - `user-story/model-selection-flow.spec.ts` covers the cross-directory reload. It fails on `dev`.
  - `regression/new-session.spec.ts` checks that a variant picked on a worktree draft stays with the started session after a reload, also when another tab shows during the start.

prs.title: fix(ui): drive createAutoScroll with an explicit state machine
prs.body:
`createAutoScroll` (public `@opencode/ui/hooks` export) kept its follow / pause / settle lifecycle in loose flags (`userScrolled`, `settling`, `settleTimer`, `auto {top,time}`, `autoTimer`, a closure `connected`). This PR replaces them with one state union and a pure transition, and fixes the three bugs those flags allowed. The public API (`AutoScrollOptions` and the returned object) is unchanged.

### Callers

Repo-wide grep (`packages/*`, including `gui-plugins` and `session-ui`) for `createAutoScroll` / `create-auto-scroll`:

| Caller | Kind |
|---|---|
| `packages/app/test-browser/auto-scroll.test.ts` | test |
| `packages/ui/src/hooks/index.ts` | re-export (`@opencode/ui/hooks`) |
| `packages/app/AGENTS.md:104` | docs mention |

No production surface calls it; the session timeline moved to `packages/app/src/session/timeline/machine.ts`. Because of this, I did not run a benchmark (nothing in the app runs this hot path). Scroll and resize still stay allocation-free for steady states. See below.

### Bugs

- **A user scroll near our last write snapped back to the bottom.** `scrollToBottom` armed `auto = {top, time}` for 1.5 s, even when it did not write (`distance < 2`), and nothing consumed it. Sequence: pin to 400 → content grows to 450 → user drags to 399 within 1.5 s → `isAuto` matches (`|399 - 400| < 2`) → re-pin instead of pause.
- **Late content growth after the 300 ms settle tail was not followed.** After `working()` went false, `resize` and `scrollToBottom()` bailed out on `!active()` while `overflow-anchor` was still `none`. A late image or diff left the view above the bottom while `userScrolled()` stayed `false`.
- **`userScrolled` could stay `true` while nothing can scroll.** The resize observer watched only the content. When the viewport grew (window or split resize), the pause stayed. A detached `<Suspense>` viewport that measured `0x0` also cleared a real pause.

### State

```ts
type AutoScrollState =
  | { status: "idle" | "following"; detached: boolean; flight: number | undefined }
  | { status: "settling"; attempt: number; detached: boolean; flight: number | undefined }
  | { status: "paused"; working: boolean; detached: boolean }
  | { status: "disposed" }
```

- `flight` is the `scrollTop` that our own write produced. It is recorded only when the write actually moved `scrollTop`, so a `scroll` event will follow. The next `scroll` event consumes it, whatever that event is.
- `settling` differs from `idle` only in that a text selection still pauses (`selectPausesOnSelection`). Both stay pinned.
- `detached` is set while `<Suspense>` holds the viewport outside `<main>`. It replaces the closure `connected`.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> idle: working false
  [*] --> following: working true
  idle --> following: working true [pin]
  following --> settling: working false [settle.start]
  settling --> idle: settle.elapsed(attempt)
  settling --> following: working true [settle.stop, pin]
  idle --> paused: user scroll / wheel up / pause()
  following --> paused: user scroll / wheel up / selection / pause()
  settling --> paused: same [settle.stop]
  paused --> following: at bottom / no overflow / resume() (working)
  paused --> idle: at bottom / no overflow / resume() (not working)
```

| Event (unpaused) | Result |
|---|---|
| `resize` (overflow) | `[pin.bottom]` in every unpaused phase, which fixes the late-growth bug |
| `scroll` at bottom | clear `flight` |
| `scroll` at `flight` (±0.5 px) | clear `flight`, `[pin.bottom]` (content grew mid-flight) |
| any other `scroll` | `paused` |
| `scroller.detached` / `reattached` | set / clear `detached`; reattach pins |
| `disposed` | `DISPOSED`, `[settle.stop]` if settling |

| Event (paused) | Result |
|---|---|
| `resize` / `pause` / `scroller.reattached` without overflow | resume, which fixes the stuck pause |
| `scroller.changed` (ref cleared or set) | stay paused, as on `dev`; the new viewport's first `resize` resumes if it cannot scroll |
| anything while `detached` | ignored, which keeps the pause through `<Suspense>` |

### Driver (`create-auto-scroll.tsx`)

- The driver holds the state in one signal, so frozen singletons never pass through store merging. `userScrolled` and the `overflow-anchor` value are memos over selectors.
- One native `ResizeObserver` watches both the viewport and the content. Measurements from a disconnected viewport are skipped. This replaces `@solid-primitives/resize-observer` here.
- `pin.bottom` writes `scrollTop` only when the viewport is more than 0.5 px from the bottom. It dispatches `flight.started` only when the write moved `scrollTop`.
- Hot path: `scroll`, `resize`, `pause` and `flight.started` reuse one mutable event object each. Steady transitions return prebuilt frozen `{ state, effects }` objects (asserted with `toBe` in tests). `handleInteraction` checks the selector and `selection.isCollapsed` before it calls `toString()`.
- The settle timer is fenced by an attempt id, and `disposed` clears it.

### Deleted

`store.userScrolled`, `settling`, `settleTimer` as a phase flag, `auto` + `autoTimer` (1.5 s `Date.now()` window), `active()`, `markAuto` / `isAuto`, and the closure `connected`.

### Deviations from the design

- **No flight timeout.** The design bounded `flight` with a 200 ms timer. That timer causes a false pause under a long main-thread task or in a background tab, where timers run but no frame renders: the timer clears `flight` before its `scroll` event arrives. A `flight` that stays recorded affects at most one `scroll` event, because every `scroll` event consumes it. Detach and ref change also clear it.
- **`wheel` and `interaction` dispatch `pause`.** The driver filters downward and nested wheels, and the selection check runs through `selectPausesOnSelection`. The machine sees only `pause`.
- **`working` is not deferred.** The effect dispatches the first value too. The transition ignores a value that matches the current state, so this cannot miss a change between creation and the first run.

### Product calls

- `idle` now follows the bottom on resize and on `scrollToBottom()`, like `following`. Before, it stopped after the 300 ms tail. This is the fix for the late-growth bug.
- On mount, the hook no longer starts a 300 ms settle when `working()` is false. The initial `ResizeObserver` callback pins the view instead.

### Tests

- `packages/ui/src/hooks/auto-scroll-machine.test.ts`: pure replays of each bug, stale settle attempts, detach and reattach, disposal, and frozen-singleton identity on hot paths.
- `packages/app/test-browser/auto-scroll.test.ts`: covers the existing `<Suspense>` reattach for working and idle, a pause that holds through reattach, and a pause that holds when the viewport ref is cleared and set again. It also covers a user scroll next to the last programmatic target, which fails on `dev`, and catch-up after content grows mid-flight.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none">
  <style>
    .thumb{animation:t 4s ease-in-out infinite}
    .grow{animation:g 4s ease-in-out infinite;transform-origin:0 0}
    .pin{animation:p 4s ease-in-out infinite}
    @keyframes t{0%,20%{transform:translateY(0)}35%,55%{transform:translateY(-22px)}70%,100%{transform:translateY(-22px)}}
    @keyframes g{0%,60%{opacity:0}70%,100%{opacity:.5}}
    @keyframes p{0%,30%{opacity:0}40%,100%{opacity:1}}
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.thumb,.grow,.pin{animation:none}}
  </style>
  <rect x="8.5" y="8.5" width="150" height="55" stroke="currentColor" stroke-opacity=".4"/>
  <g fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".25">
    <rect x="16" y="16" width="110" height="5"/>
    <rect x="16" y="27" width="90" height="5"/>
    <rect x="16" y="38" width="120" height="5"/>
    <rect class="grow" x="16" y="49" width="70" height="5"/>
  </g>
  <rect x="150" y="12" width="4" height="47" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".1"/>
  <rect class="thumb" x="150" y="40" width="4" height="18" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".6"/>
  <g class="pin" fill="currentColor">
    <rect x="172.5" y="26.5" width="58" height="19" stroke="currentColor" stroke-opacity=".5" fill="none"/>
    <text x="201" y="40" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif">paused</text>
  </g>
</svg>
```

prs.title: fix(app): keep HostApis writes in call order with an explicit attach machine
prs.body:
HostApis writes that wait for the app interface now drain through one explicit machine (`runtime/plugin/attach-machine.ts`), so plugin writes keep their call order.

### Bugs

- **Nested write jumped the queue.** The flush spliced the whole `early` array before running it. A waiting write that wrote again (a `whenMounted` dialog that opens a tab, `storage.remove`'s nested write) found the queue empty and ran at once, ahead of writes still waiting.
  - Sequence: detached → `write(A)` (A calls `write(nested)`) → `write(B)` → attach → ran `A, nested, B`. Now `A, B, nested`.
- **First-render writes depended on queue length.** With nothing waiting at attach, a write during the interface's first render ran inside that render; with one write waiting, the same write ran after it. Now the machine stays `draining` until the post-render microtask empties the queue.
- **Writes after the plugin root went away.** Writes and cancelled `whenMounted` closures stayed in `early` without bound, and a `ctx.attention.notify(...)` queued before disposal never resolved. Disposal now drops the queue, a detached queue is capped, and a dropped or aborted notification resolves `{ notification: false, sound: false }`.

### State

```ts
type HostApiAttachState<A> =
  | { status: "detached"; attempt; writeId; queue: QueuedHostWrite<A>[] }
  | { status: "draining"; attempt; writeId; attached: A; queue: QueuedHostWrite<A>[] }
  | { status: "live"; attempt; writeId; attached: A }
  | { status: "disposed" }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> detached
  detached --> draining: attach (attempt + 1, schedule.drain)
  draining --> draining: drain.next(attempt) runs head / write appends / cancel removes
  draining --> live: drain.next(attempt) with empty queue
  live --> draining: attach (new attempt)
  draining --> detached: detach(attempt) keeps queue
  live --> detached: detach(attempt)
  detached --> disposed: disposed (drop queue)
  draining --> disposed: disposed (drop queue)
  live --> disposed: disposed
```

- `detach` and `drain.next` carry the attempt; a late one from an earlier mount returns the same state.
- `drain.next` removes the head before the driver runs it, and the driver runs each write through `Promise.try(...).catch(...)`, so a throwing write cannot stall the queue.
- `cancel(id)` removes a waiting write from the queue instead of flagging it.

### Deleted

- `attached` signal, `early` array, `flush`, and the per-call `{ cancelled }` object in `whenMounted`.

### Product calls

- **Queue cap:** a detached queue keeps the newest 1024 writes (`HOST_API_MAX_QUEUE`); the oldest is dropped, and a dropped notification resolves as not shown.
- **Live writes are isolated too:** a write that throws while the interface is live (for example `storage.remove` for an unlisted server) is logged as `[plugin]` instead of throwing to the plugin, the same as a queued write on `dev`.

### Deviations from the design

- `root.tsx` is unchanged: `createHostApis()` registers its own `onCleanup`, and `PluginRoot` calls it under an owner.
- No Solid store identity test: the state lives in a signal (it holds live functions and SDK clients), not a store.
- Off the hot path: no benchmark.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="10">

    .b{animation-delay:1s}.n{animation-delay:2s}
    @keyframes s{0%{transform:translateX(0);opacity:1}30%{transform:translateX(120px);opacity:1}35%,100%{transform:translateX(120px);opacity:0}}

  <g class="q b"><rect x="44" y="26" width="20" height="20"/><text x="50" y="40" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">B</text></g>
```

prs.title: fix(app): drive embed freeze and flight stills with explicit state machines
prs.body:
Native browser embeds (`WebContentsView`) paint above the DOM, so `packages/app/src/runtime/plugin/embeds.tsx` swaps each one for a still while floating content covers it, and while a panel flight or resize drag hides it. Both lifecycles lived in loose flags (`capturing`, `release`, `stilling`, `warming`, `landing`, `bytes`, `pause`, `focused`, `store.snapshot.presented`, `store.flying`). This PR moves them into two explicit machines and fixes the bugs the flags allowed. ### Bugs fixed - **The native page stays painted over a dialog or popover.** `presented` flipped only when Element Timing reported the still. Sequence: cover the embed → `bridge.capture` hangs, or the still never paints (the box hides, the document is hidden) → `freeze()` bails on every later frame → the page floats above the dialog until the cover closes. Now capture times out after 5 s and paint after 300 ms; either way the native view hides over the box background. - **A stale still replaces the fresh one.** Sequence: cover (capture #1) → uncover → cover again (capture #2) → #1 lands while `capturing` names the same embed again, so it installs the old frame, then #2 is dropped as stale. Captures now carry an attempt; #1 is revoked and #2 freezes. - **A still that fails to decode mounts a broken `` and leaks its blob URL.** The driver now revokes it and freezes without a still. - **Another embed taking a covered box kept the previous embed's still and its thaw timer.** Switching ids now gives up the old still in the same step. - **A navigation during a still capture blocked the next page's pre-flight still and polluted the backoff.** `stilling` stayed set and the late capture rewrote `bytes`/`pause` before its page check. A target change (page or embed, including `page: undefined`) now abandons the capture and resets the backoff. - **A hung still capture disabled flight stills until unmount; refocusing mid-capture waited up to 60 s.** Still captures time out after 5 s, and a refocus during one runs the next capture at once. - **A flight that resumed while landing let the 150 ms landing timer end it mid-flight.** `flying → landing → flying` now stops the timer. ### State `embed-snapshot-machine.ts`, one per embed box: ```ts type EmbedSnapshotState = | { status: "live"; issued: number } | { status: "capturing"; issued: number; attempt: number; id: string } | { status: "painting"; issued: number; attempt: number; id: string; url: string } // in the DOM, native view still up | { status: "frozen"; issued: number; id: string; url: string | undefined } // native view hidden | { status: "thawing"; issued: number; attempt: number; id: string; url: string } // still under the repainting view | { status: "disposed" } ``` ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 live --> capturing: covered while shown capturing --> painting: capture.settled (attempt, url) capturing --> frozen: capture.settled without url · capture.timeout 5 s painting --> frozen: snapshot.painted (Element Timing) · paint.timeout 300 ms frozen --> thawing: uncovered with a still frozen --> live: uncovered without a still thawing --> frozen: covered again thawing --> live: thaw.settled 150 ms capturing --> live: uncovered · box hidden · embed gone painting --> live: uncovered · box hidden · embed gone frozen --> capturing: another embed, covered ``` `embed-flight-machine.ts`, two orthogonal machines (a capture can run during a flight or a landing): ```ts type EmbedStillState = // context: id, page, onscreen, focused, moving, reducedMotion, pause, urgent, kept | { status: "idle" } & StillContext | { status: "warming"; attempt: number } & StillContext | { status: "capturing"; attempt: number; target: EmbedPlacement & { page } } & StillContext | { status: "disposed" } type EmbedFlightState = | { status: "idle"; issued: number } | { status: "flying"; issued: number } | { status: "landing"; issued: number; attempt: number } | { status: "disposed" } ``` | Still event | idle | warming | capturing | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `placement.changed` | warming 600 ms if it may sample | re-arm 600 ms | update `onscreen` | | `target.changed` (page or embed) | reset `kept`, `pause` | reset, re-arm | abandon, reset, re-arm | | `motion.changed` (true, on screen) | capture | capture | keep | | `warm.due` (attempt) | — | capture | — | | `capture.decoded` / `unchanged` / `failed` / `timeout` (attempt) | — | — | keep or replace `kept`; next wait `pause` (×2 when unchanged, ≤ 60 s), 0 when `urgent` | | `focus.changed` / `reduced-motion.changed` | gate | stop or re-arm | `urgent` on refocus | A machine may sample only while the view is on screen, the window has focus, no panel moves and motion is not reduced. | Flight event | idle | flying | landing | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `sync` moving, view on screen or box visible | flying | — | flying, stop timer | | `sync` landed visible | — | landing 150 ms | — | | `sync` landed hidden | — | idle | idle, stop timer | | `landing.settled` (attempt) | — | — | idle | UI reads selectors only: `selectSnapshotUrl`, `selectSnapshotHidesNative`, `selectPaintingUrl`, `selectFlightStill`, `selectStillOnscreen`, `selectStillUnchanged`. ### Driver - One `createSignal` holds the three machine states plus document visibility, so frozen singleton states never enter a Solid store. - Each machine owns one timer slot (only one phase at a time has a timer). Every async path dispatches an attempt-fenced result; stale results revoke their blob URLs inside the machine. - `measure()` stays allocation-free on steady frames: `selectSnapshotNeedsSync` skips the `sync` event, `offscreen`/`motion`/`focus` events are frozen singletons, and the popper overlap check is an index loop. - The still capture still goes out in the same task as the motion that starts it, before the view hides: the motion dispatch now sits at the top of the layout effect instead of in a separate effect whose order relative to the hide was not guaranteed. prs.title: fix(app): stop following the timeline end while dragging the scrollbar thumb
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Refs #56285

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Dragging the timeline scrollbar thumb up from the bottom still jumps back to the end for a frame whenever a row is measured, then jumps up again on the next mouse move.

The timeline thumb is mounted in the `session-timeline-visible` track (`thumbContainer={visibleArea()}`), outside the ScrollView root. The capture-phase `pointerdown` listener added in #57831 is on the ScrollView root, so it never sees a thumb press. The follow state never gets the pointer gesture and keeps following through the whole drag, and every resize calls `scrollToEnd()`.

This adds the same capture listener on the visible-area track, so a thumb press reports the pointer like any other press in the timeline.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New e2e regression in `session-panel-scrollbar.spec.ts`: hold the thumb with the real Playwright mouse, drag it up about 80 px, then grow a running shell at the tail. Without the fix the view lands at 0 px from the end (2 of 2 runs). With the fix it stays put (9 of 9 runs with `--repeat-each=3`).
- `timeline-geometry`, `timeline-history` and `timeline-cache`: same results as `dev` apart from the timing-sensitive cold-reveal test in `timeline-cache`, which also flakes without the change on this machine.
- Reproduced by hand in the desktop app on Windows 11 with mouse and touchpad, then confirmed the drag no longer jumps in a desktop build from `dev` with this change. Also checked in the dev web app that the timeline keeps following through a thumb drag without the change and stops following on the first move with it.

### Screenshots / recordings

Before (`dev`) and after (this PR), same drag in the dev web app: the thumb is held and moved up slowly while a running shell at the tail prints more lines.
