prs.title: fix(session-ui): reveal a focused review comment through one state machine
prs.body:
A focused review comment (a composer chip click, `focusedComment`) is now revealed by one explicit state machine, `ReviewFocusState`, shared by `SessionReview` and `SessionReviewFilePreviewV2`.

### Bugs

| Trigger | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parent sets focus A, then focus B (or unmounts the review) before the next frame | A's unguarded `requestAnimationFrame(() => onFocusedCommentChange(null))` fired and erased B | Each request has an `attempt`; an acknowledgement only counts while its attempt is the settled one |
| Focus a comment in a large or slow diff | The request was acknowledged on frame 1, before the comment rendered, which also dropped the file's pin; after 120 frames the poll gave up with a silent `return` | The request stays `revealing` (and pinned) until the comment renders, then acknowledges; after 2 s it settles as `timeout` and acknowledges |
| Focus request handling | `createEffect` mutated `opened`, `selection` and the accordion directly, guarded by a `focusToken` counter | A pure transition emits `open-comment`, `expand-file`, `reveal` and `acknowledge` effects; the driver runs them |

### State

```ts
type ReviewFocusState =
  | { status: "idle"; attempt }
  | { status: "revealing"; attempt; file; commentId }
  | { status: "settled"; attempt; file; commentId; outcome: "revealed" | "unavailable" | "timeout" }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  idle --> revealing: focus.requested (available)
  idle --> settled: focus.requested (unavailable) / acknowledge next frame
  revealing --> settled: reveal.succeeded(attempt) / open comment, acknowledge
  revealing --> settled: reveal.timed-out(attempt) / acknowledge
  revealing --> revealing: focus.requested (new target) / cancel, attempt + 1
  settled --> revealing: focus.requested (new target)
  revealing --> idle: focus.cleared / disposed / cancel
  settled --> idle: focus.cleared / disposed
```

- `transitionReviewFocus` ignores a request for the same target until the parent clears it, so re-emitted or controlled props do not restart the reveal.
- `createReviewFocusDriver` (`review-focus-driver.ts`) owns the frame, the 2 s timer and a `MutationObserver` on the scroll root, coalesced to one check per frame. `poke()` (diff wrapper ref, `File` `onRendered`) checks again. `onCleanup` dispatches `disposed`, which cancels all of them.
- `SessionReview` pins the file while `revealing` (`reviewFocusPinnedFile`); afterwards the comment's `viewing` mode keeps it pinned.
- Availability: the V2 preview needs the focused file and a renderable diff; `SessionReview` waits while the diffs are still empty and fails at once for a missing or binary file.

### Deleted

- Both `focusToken` counters, the two 120-frame `scrollTo` loops and the unguarded acknowledgement frames.
- The `props.focusedComment?.file === file` pin in `SessionReview`.

### Product calls

- The parent's focus clears when the comment is shown, not one frame after the request. The V2 panel keeps the focused file's preview selected for that time (up to 2 s), as `activeDiff` already intends.
- A comment that never renders (a diff over the 500-line limit, a virtualized row out of range) gives up after 2 s, the same budget as the old 120 frames, and then clears the request.

### Deviations from the design

- `revealed` and `failed` are one `settled` variant with an `outcome` field; nothing in the UI tells them apart.
- `reveal.succeeded` emits `open-comment` again, so a comment that arrived after the request still opens. This replaces the design's extra reactive effect on `comments`.
- An acknowledgement is valid only while its attempt is `settled`, so the driver needs no second check of the live prop.

### Tests

- `review-focus-machine.test.ts`: a superseding request with late results from the old attempt, timeout, unavailable target, same-target deduplication, and clear and dispose exits.
- `session-review-comments.spec.ts` (component), on the new `FocusedComment` story, which sets `focusedComment` the way a composer chip does:
  - A focus request opens the comment, and the parent's request clears once it shows.
  - A request for a comment that never renders stays set for the first second (Playwright clock) and clears once the 2 s reveal timeout settles it. With the previous focus code it cleared on the next frame, so this case fails there.
- Off the hot path: the observer runs only while a reveal is pending, at most one check per frame, so no benchmark.

prs.title: fix(desktop): model migration poll, picked files, plugin host follow and zoom as state machines
prs.body:
Four desktop lifecycles move to explicit state machines: one union, a pure transition, and a thin driver each. Each fixes a low-severity race or stuck state.

| Machine | Module | Bug on `dev` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| V1 migration poll and toast | `renderer/migration-status-machine.ts` | One `Failed to fetch` stopped polling and showed "migration failed" during a running migration. A hung request kept the loader toast up forever. |
| Picked-file read authorizations | `main/files/attachment-picker-machine.ts` | A failed read (for example Windows `EBUSY`) consumed the file, so a retry got "not selected". Tokens leaked after a renderer reload or close. |
| Plugin host follow, listing and menubar | `main/plugin/host-machine.ts` | A listing started against sidecar endpoint A applied after the sidecar moved to endpoint B. A hung listing blocked plugin discovery until restart. |
| Renderer zoom and wheel pinch | `renderer/window/zoom-machine.ts` | A refused `setZoomLevel` kept its target, so the next Zoom In skipped a step. A late boot `getZoomFactor` overwrote a reset to 1. A keyboard step during a pinch left a stale `startZoom`. |

### V1 migration poll

```ts
type MigrationState =
  | { status: "waiting" | "polling"; attempt: number; failures: number; progress: MigrationProgress | undefined }
  | { status: "completed" }
  | { status: "failed"; error: string }
  | { status: "disposed" }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> waiting
  waiting --> polling: poll.due (attempt)
  polling --> waiting: running / required (1 s)
  polling --> waiting: poll.failed / poll.timed-out (10 s): keep progress, back off 1 s → 32 s
  polling --> completed: completed
  polling --> failed: status "error" → show-error
  waiting --> disposed
  polling --> disposed: abort
```

- Only an `error` answer from the server shows the failure toast. Transport errors and timeouts keep the last progress and retry with backoff.
- The persistent toast follows `selectMigrationToastVisible(state)` through one handle `{ id, closed, dispose }`. A render after the dismissal disposes its own root.

### Picked-file reads

```ts
type PickedPath = { status: "unread" } | { status: "reading"; attempt: number }
type PickedFileState =
  | { status: "open"; nextAttempt: number; pickers: Map<picker, sender>; selections: Map<token, { sender; remaining; files: Map<path, PickedPath> }> }
  | { status: "disposed" }
```

| Event | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `read.requested` on an `unread` file | claims it as `reading(attempt)`, `read(maxBytes = remaining)` |
| `read.requested` on a `reading` file | `reject(not-selected)` |
| `read.succeeded` (current attempt) | deletes the file, charges `remaining`; `size-limit` if concurrent reads already spent the budget |
| `read.failed` / `read.cancelled` | gives the file back as `unread`, budget untouched |
| `sender.cleared` (main-frame navigation or `destroyed`) | drops that renderer's selections and open dialogs |
| `selection.granted` for a dialog whose renderer reloaded | nothing granted, `openFilePicker` returns `null` |

- The machine emits `watch-sender` / `unwatch-sender` when a renderer gains its first or loses its last dialog or selection. `files/index.ts` attaches `did-start-navigation` and `destroyed` for exactly that span.
- The read runs in the calling fiber. Interruption dispatches `read.cancelled`. A failed read re-raises its own error.

### Plugin host

```ts
type HostState =
  | { status: "stopped"; nextAttempt; menubarQueued }
  | { status: "following"; nextAttempt; menubarQueued; endpoint: HostEndpoint | undefined
      watch: { status: "idle" } | { status: "streaming" | "retrying"; attempt }
      list: { status: "idle" } | { status: "listing"; attempt; queued: boolean } }
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as SidecarCredentials
  participant M as host machine
  participant S as server
  M->>S: start-watch(1, A)
  S-->>M: server.connected → relist.requested(watch 1)
  M->>S: start-list(2, A, 30 s)
  C-->>M: endpoint.changed(B)
  M->>S: cancel-watch, cancel-list (abort), start-watch(3, B)
  S-->>M: list.succeeded(2) from A
  Note over M: stale attempt: ignored, no apply-listing
```

- One listing at a time. Changes during a listing coalesce into `queued`, which runs once after success, failure or the 30 s timeout.
- A stream that ends while its endpoint stays retries through `schedule-watch-retry(1 s)`, which `cancel-watch` clears.
- `stop()` dispatches `stopped`: it unsubscribes from credentials and aborts the stream and the listing. `resume()` queues a menubar publish and follows again.
- `isQuitting(appState())` reaches the machine as a `quitting` field on each event. `plugin/machine.ts`, `plugin/lifecycle.ts` and `lifecycle/machine.ts` are unchanged.

### Zoom

```ts
type ZoomState = ZoomBase & (
  | { status: "idle" }
  | { status: "accumulating"; totalDelta }
  | { status: "pinching"; startZoom; totalDelta })
// ZoomBase: factor, factorSeeded, level, levelSeeded, pinch, nextAttempt, request: { kind: "factor" | "level"; attempt; target } | undefined
```

- `selectRequestedZoom` is the pending request's target, else the confirmed factor. A failed request clears it, so the next step starts from the real zoom.
- `factorSeeded` and `levelSeeded` turn true on the first user action, main event or seed answer. This replaces `1` as the "unseeded" sentinel.
- `level.requested`, an external `zoom.changed`, and turning pinch off end the gesture and cancel its timer.
- `zoom.changed` keeps a newer pending level request (`target !== level`), so rapid Zoom In steps do not fall back.
- Wheel frames reuse one event object and frozen effect lists. Each frame allocates only the next state. This is off the hot path in practice (Ctrl+wheel only, listener attached only while pinch zoom is on), so no benchmark.

### Deleted

- `migration-status.tsx`: `progress` signal, shared `AbortController`, `toastID` / `disposeToast` lets, `while (true)` + `wait()`.
- `attachment-picker.ts`: the mutable `selections` map.
- `host.ts`: `status { sequence, menubarQueued, listing, relist }`, `inventory.watch`, `inventory.stop`, `sidecar.key`, `followPlugins`, `relistPlugins`.
- `zoom.ts`: `requestedZoom`, `pinchZoomEnabled`, `wheelPinch`, `applyZoom`, `resetWheelPinch`.

### Product calls and deviations from the design

- Migration: retries continue indefinitely with backoff capped at 32 s. Only a server `error` answer ends polling.
- Picked files: one `open` phase with possibly empty maps instead of separate `idle`/`active` phases, because nothing distinguishes them. Open dialogs are part of the machine (`picker.opened`/`picker.closed`/`selection.granted`) instead of a local navigation flag around `showOpenDialog`. Reply commands answer each request event, so no reply callbacks are stored in state. An in-flight read whose token was cleared rejects `not-selected` when it settles, not immediately.
- Plugin host: a credential change with the **same** endpoint still restarts the stream (matching `dev`'s "every reconnect follows anew"). The running listing continues because its endpoint is still valid. A different endpoint cancels both.
- Zoom: `setZoomLevel` / `setPinchZoomEnabled` still return main's promise. `zoomIn` / `zoomOut` / `resetZoom` catch the rejection after the machine rolls back, which removes the unhandled rejection.
- No e2e test: each bug is a main-process, IPC or timing race. Pure transition tests replay each one.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none" stroke="currentColor">
  <style>
    .tick{opacity:.35}
    .fail{animation:fail 4s infinite}
    .spin{transform-origin:28px 36px;animation:spin 1s linear infinite}
    .ok1{animation:ok 4s infinite}
    .ok2{animation:ok 4s 2.4s infinite}
    @keyframes spin{to{transform:rotate(360deg)}}
    @keyframes fail{0%,20%{opacity:.35}25%,40%{opacity:1}45%,100%{opacity:.35}}
    @keyframes ok{0%,5%{opacity:.35}10%,20%{opacity:1}25%,100%{opacity:.35}}
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.spin,.fail,.ok1,.ok2{animation:none}}
  </style>
```

prs.title: fix(app): recover the optimistic prompt handoff when its admission echo is missed
prs.body:
## Problem

The timeline shows a steer before the server admits it (the *handoff*), and drops it on the matching `session.inbox.enqueued` echo. Nothing else ended it.

- **Missed echo sticks forever.** The event stream drops across admission, or a retried `POST /prompt` succeeds idempotently with no second echo. The handoff stays until 40 other sessions evict it from a module LRU.
  - A later agent or model switch injects a phantom switch notice above the prompt (screenshot below).
  - Queuing, cancelling or reverting the prompt removes it from the timeline, and the handoff re-appends it at the bottom as a ghost.
- **Leaked listeners.** Every active-session submit built a new `createSessionMessageHandoff` closure; a superseding submit called the new closure's empty `unsubscribe`, so the earlier `session.inbox.enqueued` listener leaked.
- **No owner.** The store and listeners were module globals, created outside any Solid owner, so they outlived server disposal, sign-out and test roots.
- **Aborted promotion.** A failed first send cleared the handoff only from `prompt.settled`, which `submit.aborted` never reaches. A hung send had no bound.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc02ebb3-3365-46a3-8c03-efa04d521b90) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df20acba-a960-49a8-a84f-41318748066a) |

*Missed admission echo, then another client switches Build → Plan. Before: a phantom "Plan → Build" notice stays above the admitted steer.*

## Machine

`packages/app/src/session/handoff-machine.ts`, driven per server by `createSessionMessageHandoffs` on `ServerCtx` (`server.ctx.handoff`).

```ts
type HeldSessionHandoff = {
  phase: "sending" | "awaiting-echo" | "syncing"
  attempt: number
  handoff: SessionMessageHandoff
}

type SessionHandoffState =
  | { status: "active"; connected: boolean; issued: number; entries: Record<SessionID, HeldSessionHandoff> }
  | { status: "disposed" }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> sending: handoff.set (30 s timer)
  sending --> awaiting_echo: prompt.settled (1 s, or 30 s while disconnected)
  sending --> syncing: sending.timed-out, connected
  awaiting_echo --> syncing: echo.timed-out, connected
  awaiting_echo --> syncing: connection.changed(true)
  syncing --> [*]: sync.settled / sync.timed-out (10 s)
  sending --> [*]: echo, delivered, cancelled, moved to queue, revert at or before it, session deleted, send failed
  awaiting_echo --> [*]: same, or a timeout while disconnected
```

- `syncing` invalidates and reloads the session, its inbox and its messages, then ends the handoff. The data layer keeps the optimistic row, so the prompt stays visible.
- `issued` never resets, so a timer or sync from an earlier handoff cannot match a later one on the same session.
- `composer/submit.ts` settles or clears the handoff straight from `sendPrompt`'s settlement (`settle` when it resolves or `session.admitted(id)`, otherwise `clear`), so an aborted promotion still ends it.
- The timeline controller holds the handoff while the view is detached, like `pendingItems`.

## Deleted

- Module `createStore` `handoffs`, the `handoffOrder` LRU (`MAX = 40`), the per-closure `unsubscribe`.
- `setSessionMessageHandoff`, `getSessionMessageHandoff`, `clearSessionMessageHandoff`, `createSessionMessageHandoff`, and the `SessionStateKey` keying: handoffs key by session ID per server.
- `failSubmission`'s `handoff.clear`.

## Product calls and deviations from the design

- **No store-reconciliation effect.** The design also cleared from synced store state (queued, delivered, staged revert, missing). Every held entry is already bounded by a timer and ends in a sync, and a reactive revert check would wrongly clear a steer sent into a session that already has a staged revert (the steer commits it). Dropped for simplicity.
- **Signal, not store.** The machine state lives in one signal and is replaced whole, so no store merge can share objects between sessions. The timeline reads it through memos with value equality.
- **No `has` selector.** `timeline/model.ts` reads `!!handoff.get(id)`.
- `createActiveComposerAdapter` keeps its now-unused `sessionKey` input, to leave `session/composer/controller.ts` (in flight elsewhere) untouched.
- A first prompt that fails after an aborted promotion has no unit test: the abort path rethrows into an unhandled rejection by design. The `submit.test.ts` table covers settle on success, settle on a lost response after admission, and clear on failure, all now from `sendPrompt` directly.
- Off the hot path (one dispatch per submit and per inbox event), so no benchmark.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none">
  <style>
    .ghost{animation:ghost 4s ease-in-out infinite}
    .sync{animation:sync 4s linear infinite;transform-origin:44px 52px}
    @keyframes ghost{0%,35%{opacity:.55}55%,100%{opacity:0}}
    @keyframes sync{0%,30%{opacity:0;transform:rotate(0)}35%{opacity:.6}55%{opacity:.6;transform:rotate(360deg)}60%,100%{opacity:0;transform:rotate(360deg)}}
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ghost,.sync{animation:none}.ghost{opacity:0}.sync{opacity:0}}
  </style>
  <rect x="24" y="8" width="72" height="4" rx="2" fill="currentColor" opacity=".35"/>
  <rect x="24" y="18" width="104" height="4" rx="2" fill="currentColor" opacity=".35"/>
  <g class="ghost"><rect x="24" y="30" width="96" height="4" rx="2" fill="currentColor"/></g>
  <circle class="sync" cx="44" cy="52" r="6" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="20 18"/>
  <rect x="132" y="44" width="84" height="16" rx="8" fill="currentColor" opacity=".18"/>
  <rect x="142" y="50" width="56" height="4" rx="2" fill="currentColor" opacity=".7"/>
</svg>
```

prs.title: fix(app): drive the composer focus handoff with an explicit state machine
prs.body:
Focus moving from the pending session's composer to the created session's composer is now one explicit machine, `packages/app/src/session/composer/focus-machine.ts`. Before, two unrelated closures handled it: a one-frame `document.querySelector` in `PreparingComposer` and a one-shot `on(adapter.ready)` frame in the session composer controller. ### Bugs fixed - **Focus is taken back after the user leaves the pending composer.** 1. While the worktree is being created, the user clicks the user message or the status line (or uses another control that then unmounts). 2. `document.activeElement` is `body`. 3. The session is created. The new controller sees `body` and focuses the composer anyway. - Now: leaving the pending composer (`focusout` inside a focused window, not to a titlebar tab link) records `declined`. The composer that replaces it leaves focus alone. A later visit to the session focuses as usual. - **The session composer tries only once.** If the first frame after mount finds the composer hidden (request dock, `SessionLocationMissing`), a dialog open, or the editor not connected, focus is lost for good. Now the controller waits reactively until `adapter.ready() && editor() && editable() && !dialog.active`, for at most `FOCUS_HANDOFF_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s). A frame that finds it blocked again retries up to 3 times. - **A session created before the pending composer's first frame dropped the handoff.** The old check `document.activeElement !== element` ran before the `restoreFocus` frame had focused anything. `claiming` now counts as focused. - **The caret could lag behind a held key.** `ComposerEditor` stores the caret only on input, key up and pointer up. `PreparingComposer` now also syncs it on `selectionchange`, using the new `getCursorPosition` in `composer/editor/dom.ts`, which is the inverse of `setCursorPosition`. The handler returns at once unless the pending editor has focus, and allocates nothing. On unmount, the handoff reads the caret straight from the DOM, and that caret wins over the stored cursor. - **Frames and timers belonged to nobody.** The pending composer's frame was never cancelled and focused any `[data-component="composer-editor"]` in the document. The driver now owns every frame and timer, targets the registered editor ref, and cancels them on target change or disposal. ### State ```ts type ComposerFocusState = | { status: "idle"; target: string | undefined; attempt: number } | { status: "preparing"; target: string; attempt: number; focus: "claiming" | "focused" | "blurred" } | { status: "handoff"; target: string; attempt: number; cursor: number } | { status: "declined"; target: string; attempt: number } | { status: "pending-real"; target: string; attempt: number; cursor: number | undefined; retries: number } | { status: "focusing-real"; target: string; attempt: number; cursor: number; retries: number } | { status: "disposed" } ``` ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> idle: target.changed idle --> preparing: preparing.mounted (frame.preparing) preparing --> preparing: preparing.frame / focused / blurred preparing --> handoff: preparing.unmounted [claiming | focused] preparing --> declined: preparing.unmounted [blurred] idle --> pending_real: real.mounted (timer.start) handoff --> pending_real: real.mounted (cursor kept) declined --> idle: real.mounted (no focus) pending_real --> focusing_real: real.ready (frame.real) focusing_real --> idle: real.frame focused | claimed focusing_real --> pending_real: real.frame blocked [retries < 3] focusing_real --> idle: real.frame blocked [retries = 3] pending_real --> idle: timeout ``` - `target.changed` from any state goes to `idle` for the new session and cancels the old frame or timer. `disposed` is terminal. - Frame and timer results carry `attempt`; a stale one returns the same state object. - The driver (`session/composer/focus.tsx`) lives in `ComposerFocusProvider` around the pending/resolved `` in `session/route.tsx`, so it outlives the pending composer. It holds the state in a signal, not a store. Outside the route (stories), `useComposerFocus` creates a local driver, and the composer focuses on mount as before. - The selector `needsRealComposerFocus(state, sessionID)` drives the controller's readiness effect. ### Deleted - `PreparingComposer`: the `element` and `pathname` closures, the uncancelled `onCleanup` frame, `document.querySelector`, and `editor.restoreFocus(...)` on mount. - `createSessionComposerController`: the `on(adapter.ready)` one-shot frame and the non-reactive `editor` variable (now a signal). ### Deviations from the design - `target` is the session ID string. The provider sits under one keyed `ServerProvider`, so the server key adds nothing. - `real.mounted` replaces starting `pending-real` on `target.changed`. The controller is recreated whenever its session becomes visible (for example, the mobile changes view). Each new controller focuses as on `dev`, and a `declined` handoff is used up by the first one. - Cut: the `source` field, `preparing.cursor`, `dialogOpen`, `real.edited`, `real.unavailable` and the view selector. Nothing branched on `source`. The unmount event carries the DOM caret. The frame checks `dialog.active` itself. A frame that finds focus already in the composer settles without moving the caret, which covers `real.edited`. The timeout settles child and not-found routes. - No `maxCursor` clamp: `setCursorPosition` already falls back to the end. - The design's `
` mismatch does not apply: the editor renders line breaks as text in a `pre-wrap` element, so the old cursor already counted them. ### Product calls - Leaving the pending composer for a titlebar tab link does not count as declining, matching the existing tab-link rule in the old controller. - The pending composer's first focus now gives way to a control or dialog that already holds focus, like the session composer does. On `dev` it always took focus. - A session composer that is hidden by a request dock when it mounts takes focus once the dock clears, if that happens within 10 s and nothing else holds focus. ### Tests - `focus-machine.test.ts`: each bug sequence, stale frames and timers, the retry limit, the timeout, a target switch before and after unmount, and disposal. - `dom.test.ts`: `getCursorPosition` round-trips every caret row in the existing table, handles carets on and inside mentions, and returns `undefined` for ranges and outside selections. - `e2e/regression/new-session.spec.ts`: - The user leaves the pending composer, and focus stays out of the composer after the session is created. This test fails on `dev`. - A mid-draft caret (start of line 2) and focus survive the handoff. Typing goes to the focused element without focusing the editor again. Off the hot path: no per-frame work. Selection changes run one early return unless the pending editor has focus. I did not run a benchmark. ### Before / after The user clicked the "Creating worktree" status line, then the session was created. A blue outline marks the focused composer (added for the screenshot only). | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/111029da-3bb3-476c-9af4-ae07fcce3f0c) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ce512f1b-eae4-4be2-8d32-d364dbcbe8d6) | ### Visual ```svg ``` --- _Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._ Related: #57176

prs.title: fix(app): drive Home session list, search and row gestures with explicit state machines
prs.body:
Home's session list, its search panel and the row menu/rename each run on one explicit state machine now. Each machine has a pure `transition`, selectors for the UI, and a thin driver that fences results by attempt.

### Bugs fixed

- **The list loads forever while the server cannot answer.** The query was `enabled` only while connected, so a signed-out, unreachable, incompatible or stuck-connecting server stayed `isPending`. Home then showed placeholder rows and the search spinner forever. Now:
  - an unreachable server shows "Can't reach this server" with **Try again**;
  - a signed-out server shows "Signed out of this server";
  - an incompatible server shows "This server version isn't supported";
  - a connect that takes longer than 15 s ends as unreachable.
- **A failed load looked like an empty server.** A 500 left `isPending` false with no data, so Home showed "Nothing here yet / New session". It now shows "Couldn't load sessions", the error, and **Try again**. A list request that hangs times out after 30 s.
- **A failed delete hid the session until a refetch.** The cached index dropped the row before `DELETE` settled. The data layer already hides the row on `remove()` and shows it again on failure, so the cache now drops the row only after the server confirms the delete.
- **Placeholder rows faded over errors and server switches.** Two `setTimeout` effects drove the placeholder rows. The skeleton and reveal are now machine phases, so an error or a cached server shows at once.
- **Tabbing out of search left the results panel open** over the list until the next pointer press. Focus leaving the search control now closes the panel and keeps the text. Tabbing back reopens it.
- **A session ID found on one server stayed after you switched server or project.** Opening it then opened server A's session ID on server B. A scope change now drops the match and looks the ID up again. Lookups are abortable and time out after 10 s.
- **A rename save that hung left the row stuck.** The `disabled` input lost focus, and `closeEditor()` ignored Escape while saving. The input is now read-only while saving, so it keeps focus and Escape cancels the save (abort). A failed save returns to editing with the draft. A save that times out after 15 s does the same and shows a toast.
- **A row remount during a long press lost its click suppression.** The row kept its suppress-click and outside-dismiss flags in local `let` variables, so a session that moved to another date group mid-gesture lost them. The flags now live in the machine at the list root.

### State

```ts
// load-machine.ts: the phase only; the list stays in the shared ["home-sessions", conn] query cache
type HomeSessionsLoadState =
  | { status: "idle"; issued }
  | { status: "connecting"; issued; server; attempt; since; skeleton }
  | { status: "loading"; issued; server; attempt; since; skeleton; queued }
  | { status: "ready"; issued; server; reveal }
  | { status: "refreshing"; issued; server; attempt; reveal; queued }
  | { status: "unavailable"; issued; server; reason: "offline" | "auth" | "incompatible" }
  | { status: "error"; issued; server; failure: { type: "rejected"; message } | { type: "timeout" } }
  | { status: "disposed" }

// search-machine.ts
type HomeSessionSearchState =
  | (Fields & { status: "idle" })
  | (Fields & { status: "looking-up"; attempt; sessionID })
  | (Fields & { status: "found"; exact: HomeSessionRecord })
  | { status: "disposed" } // Fields = { scope, connected, issued, focused, value, highlighted }

// row-machine.ts
type HomeSessionRowState =
  | { status: "idle"; issued; suppressClick: string | undefined }
  | { status: "pressing"; issued; attempt; sessionID; x; y; menuX; menuY }
  | { status: "menu"; issued; sessionID; x; y; suppressClick; outside }
  | { status: "editing"; issued; sessionID; draft }
  | { status: "renaming"; issued; attempt; sessionID; draft }
  | { status: "disposed" }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> idle
  idle --> connecting: server connecting, no cache
  idle --> loading: connected, no cache
  idle --> ready: cached and fresh, or server away with a cache
  idle --> refreshing: connected, cached but stale
  idle --> unavailable: offline / auth / incompatible
  connecting --> loading: connected (keeps placeholder rows)
  connecting --> unavailable: 15 s connect timeout
  loading --> ready: fetch.succeeded (reveal if rows showed)
  loading --> error: fetch.failed / 30 s timeout
  error --> loading: Try again, invalidation
  unavailable --> connecting: Try again (probes servers)
  ready --> refreshing: invalidated, stale on reconnect
  refreshing --> ready: settles (a failure keeps the list)
```

| Row machine | Event | Next |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `idle` | touch `pointerdown` | `pressing` (500 ms timer) |
| `pressing` | move > 8 px / `pointerup` | `idle` |
| `pressing` | timer, or Android `contextmenu` | `menu { suppressClick: true }` |
| `menu` | close | `idle` (`suppressClick` carried until the release click), focus row unless dismissed outside |
| any | Rename | `editing` |
| `editing` | Enter (changed) | `renaming` (abortable save, 15 s) |
| `renaming` | Escape | `idle` + abort; blur is ignored |
| `renaming` | failed / timed out | `editing` with the draft |

### Kept from the query

- **Cache:** the list reads and writes `["home-sessions", conn]` with the same options as before: no retry (`retry: false`), 30 s stale time, and `gcTime: Infinity`, which keeps it across visits. Fetches go through `queryClient.fetchQuery`, so a fetch the sidebar already started is joined.
- **Refetch:** the list refetches on mount or retarget when stale, when the cached query is invalidated (any `invalidateQueries`, for example from side tabs), and when `onlineManager` reports online while the list is stale. A refresh asked for during a fetch runs once more after it.
- **Pointer events:** `pointermove` checks `selectLongPressMoved` before it builds an event, so a move allocates nothing unless it cancels a pending long press.

### Deleted

- `useQuery` in the controller, the `[placeholder, setPlaceholder]` signal and its two timers, and the pre-request `setQueryData` in `remove`.
- The search store `{ value, focused, highlighted, exact, lookingUp }` and its `let lookup` counter.
- The `rowUI` store and the four per-row `let` flags: `longPressTimer`, `longPressStart`, `suppressClick` and `menuInteractedOutside`.

### Product calls and deviations from the design

- **Placeholder rows while connecting:** connecting shows the same delayed placeholder rows and search spinner as loading, bounded by the 15 s connect timeout. This is closer to `dev` than a blank list, and the rows carry over into the first fetch.
- **Error over open-tab sessions:** a failed first load shows the error even when open-tab sessions exist. A partial list would hide the failure.
- **Errors and reconnects:** an error waits for **Try again** or an invalidation. When the server goes away, the error is replaced by the server's unavailable state.
- **Saves in the background:** a rename save is aborted only by Escape or by its timeout. Starting another gesture lets it finish in the background, because the server may already have it.
- **Row menu trigger:** the hidden menu trigger is `disabled`, so it takes no focus. Kobalte's `DropdownMenu` focuses its trigger on close unless the user interacted outside. That stole focus from the rename editor the Rename item had just focused.
- **Dropped from the design:** a window-level Escape fallback while saving. The read-only input keeps focus, so the fallback is not needed.
- **Benchmark:** the change is off the hot path, so it has no benchmark. Load, search and menu transitions are not per-frame work, and pointer moves allocate nothing.
- **Feature flag:** none. This is a bug fix.

prs.title: fix(app): model session fork, compact, export and the Cmd+W close guard as state machines
prs.body:
Session commands that start async work (`/fork`, `/compact`, `/export`) now claim their work synchronously in explicit state machines, and the ⌘W "panel just emptied" guard is one too.

### Bugs

| Trigger | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/fork`, then Enter twice (or double-click a row) before the fork returns | Two `POST /fork`, two forked sessions, two navigations, two un-keyed `dialog.close()` | One request; the picked row shows a `Loader`, rows are disabled, the search box is read-only |
| Pick a message in `/fork`, then Escape, click the backdrop, or switch session before it returns | The late result still navigates to the fork and restores its prompt | The fork request is aborted; nothing happens when it settles |
| "Fork from here" on message A, then on message B while A is pending; or a stalled `/fork` | Two forks race `navigate`; a stalled request never settles | One fork per controller; 30 s timeout aborts and toasts |
| `/export` twice on a large session, or leave the session screen mid-export | Two full-history inline-media fetch loops and two downloads or OS Save dialogs; fetching continues after unmount and pops a Save dialog later | One export per session; unmount aborts the fetch; each request is bounded by 60 s |
| `/fork` twice while the picker chunk loads; the chunk fails to load | `dialog.show` runs twice; an unhandled rejection | One load; a failed load toasts |
| ⌘W closes the side panel's last tab and focus moves out a microtask later | The `focusin` clears the guard, so an overshooting ⌘W closes the session tab | Focus during the arming frame does not disarm the guard |
| ⌘W closes the side panel's last tab with `side.opened()` updated in a batch | The `side.opened()` effect disarms the guard right after it arms | Same tab and a closed panel keep the guard armed |

### State

`packages/app/src/session/fork-machine.ts` (one per `/fork` dialog and one per timeline):

```ts
type SessionForkState =
  | { status: "idle"; surface: "dialog" | "inline"; attempt: number }
  | { status: "forking"; surface; attempt; sessionID; messageID; draft: SessionForkDraft }
  | { status: "closed"; surface; attempt } // dialog after success or close, so rows stay disabled through the exit animation
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  idle --> forking: fork.requested / fork.start
  forking --> forking: fork.requested (ignored)
  forking --> idle: fork.failed / toast
  forking --> idle: fork.timed-out / abort + toast
  forking --> closed: fork.succeeded [dialog] / open + dialog.close
  forking --> idle: fork.succeeded [inline] / open
  idle --> closed: disposed, session.changed [dialog]
  forking --> closed: disposed, session.changed [dialog] / abort
  forking --> idle: session.changed [inline] / abort
```

`packages/app/src/session/commands/machine.ts`:

```ts
type SessionCommandsState =
  | {
      status: "active"
      issued: number
      compacting: Record<sessionID, attempt>
      exporting: Record<sessionID, attempt>
      forkDialog: { status: "closed" } | { status: "loading"; attempt: number; sessionID: string }
    }
  | { status: "disposed" }

type CloseTabGuardState =
  | { status: "disarmed"; issued: number }
  | { status: "armed"; attempt: number; tabKey: string | undefined; settling: boolean }
  | { status: "disposed" }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  disarmed --> armed: close.completed [keybind, panel closed] / settle.schedule
  armed --> armed: focus.in [settling], modifier or ⌘W key, layout.synced [same tab, panel closed]
  armed --> armed: settle.completed [attempt] (settling = false)
  armed --> disarmed: pointer.down, window.blur, other key, focus.in [settled], layout.synced [other tab or panel open]
```

- Every result event carries its attempt; a stale or post-dispose result returns the same state and no effects.
- `DialogFork` closes itself through `useDialog().close()` and stops on `useDialog().closing`, so a late result never closes another layer (#61903).
- The forked draft targets `forked.location.directory`, not the route's current directory.
- `fetchSessionExport` takes an `AbortSignal` and bounds each request with `AbortSignal.timeout(60_000)`.
- The mock server gains `POST /api/session/:id/fork` (`onFork` hook).

### Deleted

- The unguarded `async` closure in `useSessionFork` and `.then((opened) => dialog.close())` in `DialogFork`.
- The `try`/`catch` `exportSession`, the `async` `compact`, and `openDialog(...)` for `/fork`.
- `emptied`/`setEmptied`/`resetEmptied` and their listeners.

### Product calls

- `/compact`, `/fork` and `/export` stay enabled while they run; a repeat is a no-op. Disabling them would drop them from the composer's slash list, and a second `/compact` + Enter would then send the literal text as a prompt.
- Switching session while `/fork` is open closes the picker, since it lists the previous session's prompts.
- A fork that timed out or was cancelled may still exist on the server; it shows up in the session list through sync, without navigation.
- `/compact` has no client timeout. The data layer already returns the in-flight admission for a repeat, so a timeout would only toast "Request failed" for a compaction that may still land.
- A save that finishes after the session screen unmounts shows no toast.

### Deviations from the design

- No `open` fork-dialog phase or `fork-dialog.close` effect: `DialogFork` owns its own close and session fence.
- No fetching/saving phase split and no whole-export timer: each request is bounded instead, so a long history with large media still exports.
- No `selectSessionCommandsView` and no in-flight `disabled` flags (see product calls).
- No compaction timeout (see product calls); the double failure toast the design lists was already collapsed by the toast key.

### Before / after

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf150bd8-c2c5-4bb7-a44a-7f66d81df50b) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dfd7382d-1e20-4ccd-82e4-7833d42e046a) |

Enter pressed twice on "Now add a backoff cap" with the fork held: before, no feedback and 2 requests; after, the row spins and 1 request.

### Visual


prs.title: fix(core): tell forked sessions they're forks so they stop waiting on the original's subagents
prs.body:
**A forked session now knows it's a fork, so it stops waiting on the original's subagents.**
Forking copies the history, including subagent launches. Those subagents still report to the original, so the fork used to wait for results that would never arrive.

❌ **Before**
1. A session starts a background subagent, then you fork it.
2. The fork sees the launch in its copied history and waits for the report. ❌ The report goes to the original, so it never arrives.
3. If the fork tries to continue that subagent, it gets "not a child of the current session", with no hint why.

✅ **After**
1. Every fork gets one message at the end: "This session is a fork of …", and the last copied message's time.
2. When the original has subagents the copied history can see that were still running or never reported back, the message lists them and tells the model not to wait for them; start a new subagent if the fork needs that work. A subagent started after the fork point isn't listed.
3. Continuing one of them from the fork fails with a clear reason: it belongs to the original, start a new subagent here instead.

The copied history isn't changed, so the prompt cache still hits. The notice waits for the fork's next turn and doesn't wake the fork by itself.

```diff
  fork: copy history up to the chosen message
+ scan the copied rows once: launches minus later reports, plus children with a running job
+ append one notice ("you are a fork of X, copied through <time>"), plus "don't wait for these: …" when any
```

📊 **Proof**

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Background subagent still running at fork | ❌ fork waits forever | ✅ listed, "don't wait" |
| Foreground subagent moved to the background before the fork | ❌ fork waits forever | ✅ listed |
| Subagent that already reported before the fork | ✅ not listed | ✅ not listed |
| Fork from an earlier message; subagent started after that point | ✅ not listed | ✅ not listed |
| Fork continues the original's subagent | ❌ "not a child" | ✅ "belongs to the original, start a new one" |
| Copied history bytes (prompt cache) | ✅ unchanged | ✅ unchanged |

The new tests fail without the change. 67 tests pass across the two touched files.

👀 **Read:** `session/fork-notice.ts`, `collect`. It reads the copied rows straight from the database in pages of 500 and loads only text and tool parts, so forking a long, screenshot-heavy session doesn't load its images. A launch counts as outstanding until a later `<subagent sessionID="…"` report shows up. The rest is routine.

<sub>🔍 Seen in real use: a fork waited on subagents that belonged to the original · reviewed before push</sub>

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

- `bun run test test/session-create.test.ts test/tool-subagent.test.ts` (packages/core): 67 pass, 0 fail
- `bun typecheck` (packages/core): no type errors

</details>

prs.title: fix(app): drive the connect-provider dialog and Console catalog wait with explicit state machines
prs.body:
## Summary

The connect-provider dialog decided its step from two stores, a mutable `back.current` ref, five child-to-parent mirror callbacks and the first matching branch of a 12-case `<Switch>`. The Console workspace wait was two copies of a `while` + 250 ms loop with no cancellation. This PR replaces both with explicit state machines and fixes the bugs that the implicit state caused.

- **Dialog**: one `ProviderDialogState` (`dialog-machine.ts`) composes the existing single-attempt `ProviderConnectState` from #61610 (`machine.ts` is unchanged). The dialog renders only from `selectProviderDialogView`.
- **Console wait**: one `ConsoleSettleState` (`catalog/settle-machine.ts`) and one driver (`catalog/console-settle.ts`), shared by the dialog and Settings account actions.

## Bugs fixed

| # | Sequence | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Picker → GitHub Copilot (one OAuth method) → sign-in starts → **Back** | The picker keeps `preventBackdropDismiss` on. A backdrop click does nothing until the dialog is reopened. | The flag comes from the current step, so the picker closes on a backdrop click. The OAuth attempt is cancelled. |
| 2 | Console sign-in → workspace has no models → **Back** (or Refresh fails → **Back**) | Stays on "connected, no models". **Refresh** does nothing because the sign-in is back at `choosing`. | Returns to the Console sign-in methods. |
| 3a | Connected Claude Agent → Add account → **Check again** → **Back** | Skips the accounts list and goes to the picker. In standalone mode the Back arrow is hidden. | Returns to the accounts list. |
| 3b | Claude check confirming → Back, or a new check | A late `sync` still shows the connected toast and closes the dialog, or moves the dialog to models on the wrong screen. | `claude.confirmed` carries `(session, check)`. A stale result is ignored and the 65 s timer stops. |
| 4 | Accounts → **Remove** → click Remove again, or Back while the last removal is in flight | Sends two `DELETE /api/credential/:id` requests. A late final removal closes the dialog from the picker. | The first click claims `removing(attempt)` synchronously. A late result for another session is ignored. |
| 5 | Switch or remove a Console OAuth account, then close Settings, or one catalog read fails | Polls for up to 10 s after unmount and shows a toast. A rejected read shows "Request failed" after a successful switch. | Unmount stops both timers and answers `cancelled`, so no toast. Read failures count as misses until the deadline. |

## State

```ts
type ProviderDialogState =
  | (Meta & { status: "picker" })
  | (Meta & { status: "provider"; provider: string; accounts: ProviderAccounts; step: ProviderDialogStep; closed: boolean })
  | (Meta & { status: "disposed" })

type ProviderDialogStep =
  | { kind: "accounts"; action: AccountStepAction; connect: ProviderConnectState }
  | { kind: "connect"; returnTo: "picker" | "accounts"; copy?: { attemptID: string; copied: boolean }; connect: ProviderConnectState }
  | { kind: "claude"; returnTo: "picker" | "accounts"; phase: ClaudeStepPhase; connect: ProviderConnectState }
  | { kind: "no-models"; returnTo: "picker" | "accounts"; catalogPending: boolean; connect: ProviderConnectState }
  | { kind: "models"; selectedModel: string; collapsed: Record<string, boolean> }

type AccountStepAction = idle | confirming(id) | renaming(id) | activating(attempt, id) | removing(attempt, id, final)
type ClaudeStepPhase = idle | starting(check, replacing) | checking(check) | confirming(check) | timed-out(check)

type ConsoleSettleState =
  | { status: "idle"; attempt: number }
  | { status: "waiting"; attempt: number; syncing: boolean }
  | { status: "disposed"; attempt: number }
```

`Meta` holds `session` (bumped for each provider change, and carried by every sign-in result), `attempt` (account actions and Claude checks), `standalone`, `completed` and `chatgptWelcome`.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> picker
  picker --> accounts: picked, has accounts
  picker --> connect: picked / opened for a provider
  picker --> claude: Claude Agent
  accounts --> connect: Add account
  accounts --> claude: Add account (Claude)
  connect --> models: connected, has models
  connect --> no_models: Console, no models / wait timed out
  connect --> closed: connected, no models
  claude --> models: check confirmed
  no_models --> models: Refresh finds models
  no_models --> connect: Back (methods)
  connect --> accounts: Back (returnTo accounts)
  claude --> accounts: Back (returnTo accounts)
  connect --> picker: Back
  claude --> picker: Back
  accounts --> picker: Back
  models --> closed: Continue
```

| Step | Back goes to |
| --- | --- |
| `accounts` | picker (none when standalone) |
| `claude` | `accounts` if entered from it and accounts remain, else picker |
| `no-models` | Console sign-in methods |
| `connect` | `accounts` if entered from it and (one method or still choosing). Else methods if a method is chosen and there are several (or Console). Else picker. |

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  idle --> waiting: started (not loaded) / deadline + poll
  idle --> idle: started (loaded) / settled loaded
  waiting --> waiting: poll.due / sync, sync.settled (miss) / poll
  waiting --> idle: loaded or catalog.loaded / settled loaded
  waiting --> idle: timed-out / settled timed-out
  waiting --> idle: cancelled (Back) / settled cancelled
  waiting --> disposed: disposed (unmount) / settled cancelled
```

## What was deleted

- Outer store `{ completed, modelProvider, authorization, chatgptWelcome, picked, stepBack, accounts, title }`, `back.current` / `setBack`, and the callbacks `onFirstConnection`, `onAuthorization`, `onStepBack`, `onAccounts` and `onTitle`.
- Inner store `{ models, noModels, catalogPending, selectedModel, collapsed, adding, direct, confirming, switching, activating, renaming, claudeAgent, replacing, copied, copyFailed }`, the `claudeAgent` effects and 65 s timer effect, `prepareConsoleCatalog`, `backToAccounts` and `backToMethods`.
- `createProviderConnectionController` and its `manual` / `prepare` options. `createProviderDialogController` drives the whole dialog through one queued `dispatch`, and each effect runs isolated with `Promise.try`.
- Both `while (Date.now() < deadline)` loops.

## Deviations from the design

- `direct` is not stored. It equals "entered from accounts with a lone method", which the machine derives from the catalog.
- `copy` stores the `attemptID` it was copied for, so a new authorization shows `idle` without a reset transition.
- The account count, active ID and problem flag live in `state.accounts` (`accounts.synced`). `back` and `account.remove.settled` therefore need no payload.
- Claude Agent with a sign-in problem, picked from the list, goes Back to the picker as on `dev`. The design suggested `accounts`, which would bounce straight back to the setup.
- Each Console wait settles through one `timers.stop` effect, not separate `poll.stop` and `deadline.stop` effects.

## Product calls

- After a credential change succeeds, a failed catalog refresh no longer shows "Request failed". The catalog catches up on the next sync. This also applies to rename.
- Settings now treats the Console workspace as loaded as soon as any workspace provider appears (`consoleCatalogLoaded`). Before, it waited for the root provider's name suffix. The dialog already used this rule.
- The key or sign-in step stays visible while the dialog animates closed (`closed: true`), and further input is ignored.

## Tests

- `connect/dialog-machine.test.ts` replays bugs 1 to 4, the late save across a provider switch, Console Refresh → models, ChatGPT welcome, standalone, link copy per attempt, and disposal.
- `catalog/settle-machine.test.ts` covers unmount and Back cancel, failed reads, the loaded fast path, the deadline, supersede and disposal.
- `e2e/regression/settings.spec.ts` adds keepers for bugs 1, 2 and 3a. Each one fails on `dev`. The mock server gains `DELETE …/connect/oauth/:attemptID` and `POST …/connect/external`.

Off the hot path (dialog steps and a 250 ms poll), so there is no benchmark.

## Screenshots

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |

prs.title: fix(app): keep a running rewind's echo through a commit
prs.body:
Follow-up to #61907, from the review thread on that PR: a commit during a running rewind made the **Rewound** toast disappear right after it appeared.

### Bug

`revert.committed` cleared every pending echo, on the assumption that a commit lands after every request sent before it. A rewind that is still in `interrupt`/`wait` has not sent its stage yet, so its echo was lost too:

1. `/undo` starts a rewind of `msg_3`. Pending echoes: `[msg_3]`.
2. `revert.committed` arrives, for example from a prompt sent while an earlier boundary was staged. Pending echoes: `[]`.
3. `rewind.succeeded` moves the state to `restored` and shows the Rewound toast.
4. `revert.staged(msg_3)` is our own echo, but it no longer matches anything. The state goes to `idle` with `toast.dismiss`.

### Fix

A commit keeps the running operation's own pending echo. Echoes drain in order, so a pending echo at the end of the list always belongs to the running operation.

```ts
const echoes =
  event.type !== "revert.committed"
    ? state.echoes
    : state.status === "running" && state.operation.type !== "withdraw"
      ? state.echoes.slice(-1)
      : []
```

- A withdraw sends no stage or clear, so a commit during a withdraw still clears every echo.
- A new transition test replays steps 1–4 and expects `restored` with no effects after step 4. The test fails on `dev`.

prs.title: fix(app): drive the sidebar hover peek with one explicit state machine
prs.body:
The collapsed sidebar's hover peek (`packages/app/src/shell/sidebar-peek.ts`) encoded its lifecycle in a `shown` signal, the spring's `target`, a `watch` interval used as a phase flag, `opening`/`closing` timers and a plain `let handedOff`. This moves it to one union in `sidebar-peek-machine.ts` with a pure transition, and leaves `sidebar-peek.ts` as a thin driver for timers, the spring and the DOM.

### Bugs fixed

- **Escape or a window blur did not cancel a pending dwell.** Rest on the collapsed toggle, press Escape (or Cmd+Tab) within 500 ms: the timer still fired and the peek opened, in a backgrounded window too. Both now cancel the dwell.
- **A press released outside the window held the peek open.** Press inside the peek, leave the window (or enter an iframe/native view), release there: `pressed` stayed `true`, so `held()` kept the peek open and `interrupted()` blocked later dwells. Leaving the window, `dragstart`, `dragend`, `contextmenu` and `blur` now release it.
- **The toggle reopened a peek it should not.** `pointerover` on the toggle called `show()` whenever `shown()` was true, ignoring `open` and `available`: during a dock it restarted the 150 ms watch, and after a reversed dock it reopened the peek over the still-closing docked sidebar. The toggle now only turns a slide-out around while a peek is available.
- **`handedOff` stayed `true` after the dock landed**, until the next close. It is now a selector over the state, so it ends with the hand-off.
- **A dock that never reports landing left the hand-off open.** `whenDocked` callbacks carried no attempt, and a dropped one had no fallback. Results are attempt-fenced, with a 1 s fallback (800 ms for the slide-out when frames stop).
- **Leaving vertical tabs while peeking leaked the peek.** Switching to horizontal tabs or a narrow window kept `sidebar.peek` set and the watch interval running. A new `enabled` input (`verticalTabs`) ends any peek at once.
- Global listeners re-registered on every `tabsAside` change; they now register once.

### State

```ts
type SidebarPeekState =
  | { status: "idle"; attempt: number }
  | { status: "dwelling"; from: "edge" | "toggle"; attempt: number }
  | { status: "peeking"; attempt: number }
  | { status: "grace"; attempt: number }
  | { status: "leaving"; attempt: number; restoreFocus: boolean }
  | { status: "handing-off"; attempt: number }
  | { status: "disposed" }
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  idle --> dwelling: edge sample / toggle.enter
  dwelling --> peeking: dwell.elapsed (ready)
  dwelling --> idle: left, press, Escape, blur, dock, !ready
  peeking --> grace: left corridor
  grace --> peeking: back in corridor / toggle / held
  grace --> leaving: grace.elapsed
  peeking --> leaving: Escape (restores focus), blur, focus left, dock closed
  leaving --> peeking: edge / toggle (if available)
  leaving --> idle: leave.settled (spring rest or 800 ms)
  peeking --> handing_off: dock opened
  grace --> handing_off: dock opened
  leaving --> handing_off: dock opened
  handing_off --> leaving: dock closed
  handing_off --> idle: dock.settled (whenDocked or 1 s)
```

`disabled` sends every phase to `idle`, `disposed` to `disposed`. Effects are derived from `(previous, next)` by `sidebarPeekEffects`: what the previous phase leaves (`dwell.clear`, `grace.clear`, `leave.clear`, `handoff.clear`, `watch.stop`, `peek.reset`) and what the next one starts.

### Hot path

- Pointer moves dispatch one of four frozen `pointer.sampled` events built from two booleans, and the pointer is kept as scalars (`pointerX`, `pointerY`, `hasPointer`) instead of a fresh `{ x, y }` per move.
- A sample that changes nothing returns the same state object, writes no signal and computes no effects.
- The driver reads only what the phase needs: edge hit-tests in `idle`/`dwelling`/`leaving`, corridor checks in `peeking`/`grace`, nothing while handing off. No per-frame work is added, so no benchmark was run.

### Deleted

- `shown` signal, `opening`, `closing`, `watch` as a phase guard, `motion.target` as a phase guard, `let handedOff`, `pointer: Point`, `show`/`hide`/`end`/`check`/`approach`/`start`.

### Product calls and deviations from the design

- Samples without a target (scroll, window exit, watch tick) never cancel an edge dwell, as on `dev`; only pointer moves and wheels aim at the edge. The design routed them all through one sample, which would cancel the edge dwell on every wheel-driven scroll.
- `pressed` follows `event.buttons` on wheel and `pointerover` too, so a drag that enters the toggle does not start a dwell.
- Escape while a menu or field holds the peek is still ignored, as on `dev`.

### Visual

Escape while the pointer rests on the collapsed toggle (e2e: `tabs.spec.ts`, "the collapsed sidebar peeks from a resting toggle…").

prs.title: fix(cli): rewrite noninteractive run lifecycle
prs.body:
Supersedes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61722 and https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61723: their behavior is folded in here, and the job-list regression from the first one is fixed. Fixes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/57678.

## Problem

`packages/cli/src/run/noninteractive.ts` mixed rendering with control flow spread across about 17 mutable flags. Bugs on `dev`:

1. **SIGTERM leaves the session running** (`timeout`, CI cancel, closing the terminal): run exits, the server keeps going, and the model takes its next step.
2. **Ctrl+C while waiting on a background job leaves the job running**, and the model replies again when it ends.
3. **`run --continue` hangs forever** if the session has any older running job (a dev server from an earlier turn).
4. **A background job that never exits hangs `run` forever**, with no output.
5. **Piped stdout is cut at 64 KiB**: `run ... | (sleep 6; cat) | wc -c` gives 65536. Cause: `process.exit` runs before the pipe write finishes.
6. **`run "hi"` started with spawn's default stdio blocks until stdin closes**, even though the message is an argument. Node and Bun give the child an open, silent stdin socket (bug-hunt repro: `sleep 15 | run "hi"`).
7. **Ctrl+C or SIGTERM in standalone prints `Error: Transport: ECONNRESET`** (or interrupted-step errors and a JSON `error`). Cause: the private server shuts down while requests are still open.
8. **Quoted messages are stored with literal quotes**: `run "say hello world"` stores `"say hello world"` (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/57678).
9. **SIGTERM exits 130 instead of 143.**
10. **A retried step prints `step_start` twice** for the same message.

From the two open PRs: a recovered step failure was fatal, retries were invisible, a prompt that failed before promotion could hang, and background state was read out of order. https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61722 also made every run exit 1 against servers built before the job list endpoint.

## Change

The renderer stays. The control part is rewritten as one explicit lifecycle:

```text
admitting → running → settling → waiting for this prompt's jobs → done(exit code)
any state + SIGINT/SIGTERM → cancelling → done(130 / 143)
```

- **Exit code**: decided in one function (`finalError`), from the first stored idle marker after this run's prompt. If the server stores no marker, the matching live terminal event is used. If neither exists, the run exits 1 with "no recorded outcome". A recovered step failure is not fatal. `session.retry.scheduled` becomes a non-fatal `retry` JSON event (one `!` line in text mode).
- **Cancel**: SIGINT/SIGTERM interrupt the `run` fiber, and that interruption now **waits** for the run to cancel (`Effect.callback` with a cleanup that awaits). The run interrupts the session, removes this prompt's background shells, and interrupts its subagents. It then interrupts any execution that starts until the tree is quiet, which covers the wake that each cancelled job queues. Only after that does the private server shut down. Errors during cancellation are ignored. `index.ts` reports SIGTERM as 143.
- **Waiting for jobs**: only jobs started at or after this prompt's admission count, so older jobs neither hold the run nor get cancelled. State is read in order (jobs → inbox → active), one read at a time, and a failed read is an error (from https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61722). A server without the job endpoint means "no jobs". While waiting, text mode prints `waiting for N background job(s) (stops after 10 minutes)` and JSON emits `{"type":"background_wait","jobs":[...],"limitMinutes":10}`.
- **Jobs that never exit**: the wait is capped at 10 minutes. After that, the run cancels this prompt's remaining jobs and exits 1 with one error. Tradeoff: a legitimate background job over 10 minutes gets cancelled, and the message says so. Waiting forever hung CI with no output. A flag can come later if someone needs a longer wait.
- **Output**: the runtime teardown ends stdout/stderr before `process.exit`, which waits for pending pipe writes. No sleeps.
- **Input**: argv parts are joined with spaces, as typed. With a message argument, a shell pipe (FIFO) or a redirected file is still read in full and merged, however slow its producer (`npm test 2>&1 | run "fix the failures"`). Any other stdin, such as the socket that spawn's default stdio gives a child, is read only if data or EOF arrives within 1 s, and otherwise closed unread. That means the literal `sleep 15 | run "hi"` still waits: from inside `run`, a silent shell pipe looks the same as a slow producer.
- **V1 compatibility**: its own small event loop (`consumeV1`) and its own SIGINT handling in `v1.ts`, so its frozen output is unchanged. The V1 tests pass unmodified.
- **JSON**: event names and shapes are unchanged. The only additions are `retry` and `background_wait`. A failure emits exactly one terminal `error`.

| Case | Before (`dev`) | After |
|---|---|---|
| SIGTERM during a tool, `--server` | exit 130; tool keeps running; model takes next step | exit 143; tool killed; session interrupted |
| Ctrl+C while waiting on a background job, `--server` | exit 130; job runs on; model replies later | exit 130; job removed; the wake it queues is interrupted, no reply stored |
| `--continue` with an older running job | hangs | exits 0; older job untouched |
| Background job that never exits | hangs, silent | one waiting line; after 10 min: jobs cancelled, exit 1, one error |
| 300 KB piped to a slow reader | 65536 bytes | 300013 bytes (text), 301023 (JSON) |
| Spawned with default stdio (open, silent socket) + message | blocks until stdin closes | prompt sent right away |
| `(sleep 4; echo ctx) \| run "review"` | waits, merges `ctx` | waits, merges `ctx` (unchanged) |
| Ctrl+C / SIGTERM in standalone | 130 + `ECONNRESET` / interrupted-step errors | 130 / 143, no error output |
| `run "say hello world" 'it'"'"'s "quoted"'` | stored with added quotes and escapes | stored as typed |
| Provider 500 once (JSON) | two `step_start`, same message | one `step_start`, one `retry` |
| Mid-stream cut, then recovery (JSON) | 2 × `error`, exit 1 | one `retry`, exit 0 |
| Old server without `/api/experimental/job` | exit 0 | exit 0 (with only https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61722: exit 1) |

`noninteractive.ts` goes from 953 to 975 lines, even with job cancellation, the bounded wait, retries and a separate V1 loop added.

Test fixture changes: two existing tests now include a stored idle marker in their projected messages, as in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61723. The old "Ctrl-C … exits 130" test is replaced by cancel tests, because the signal now arrives as an `AbortSignal` from the command boundary.

## Out of scope

- ANSI escapes in non-TTY stderr, and the missing blank lines between sections (`run/ui.ts`). Fixing these changes the frozen V1 output.
- A tool process left behind after the server is SIGKILLed (server-side cleanup).
- A cancelled job's notice still reaches the provider once before it is interrupted. Suppressing it needs a server API.
- Image jobs can't be cancelled through the API. Cancel doesn't wait on them.
- A mid-stream cut starts a new assistant message, so it shows as a second step. That part is unchanged.

## Verification

- `bun typecheck` (packages/cli): no errors.
- `bun test` (packages/cli): 387 pass, 0 fail. The new tests in `test/run/noninteractive.test.ts` and `test/run/process.test.ts` cover cancel (session, shells, subagents, ignored transport errors), older jobs, the missing job endpoint, retry and step dedupe, outcome from idle markers, the pre-promotion inbox, in-order state reads, stdin (spawn socket not awaited, slow shell pipe read in full), quoting, and SIGTERM → interrupt + 143 (that one is skipped on Windows, which has no SIGTERM delivery). With the source changes reverted, 11 of them fail; the missing-endpoint test passes on `dev`, which still swallows that error.
- `bunx prettier --check` and `bunx oxlint` on the changed files: clean.
- End to end with the mock provider, comparing `dev` (20c94b79f1) with this branch, in standalone and against an isolated `--server` on its own data directories. A proxy that 404s `/api/experimental/job` stood in for an old server. Every row of the table came from those runs, except the two stdin rows: those come from `test/run/process.test.ts`, with a real CLI process and a fake server. The never-exiting-job row used the limit temporarily lowered to 15 s. Regressions also checked: plain success, a background job that finishes (follow-up streamed, exit 0), a failing follow-up and a provider 400 (exactly one `error`, exit 1).


---

Closes #61899

### Type of change

### What does this PR do?

Windows processes can inherit an ignore-Ctrl+C console attribute from a detached OpenCode parent. The daemon now restores default Ctrl+C handling at startup, before creating any ConPTY shells, while preserving registered handlers.

### What do you want to change?

Add built-in providers for Volcengine Ark and BytePlus Ark, following the existing OpenAI-compatible provider pattern in packages/ai (same shape as the Kimi For Coding / MiniMax integrations).

### Why?

Ark  ([Volcengine Ark](https://www.volcengine.com/product/ark) in China, [BytePlus ModelArk](https://www.byteplus.com/en/product/modelark) internationally) is the only official API source for the Doubao Seed model family. 
[Seed 2.1](https://seed.bytedance.com/blog/seed2-1-officially-released-advancing-ai-productivity) is built for coding and agentic workloads, which makes it a natural fit for pi.

One Ark API key also gives access to DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM and other hosted models, so pi users get an OpenRouter-like gateway to the China/APAC model ecosystem — a developer audience pi's current providers don't reach.

Precedent: Kimi For Coding and MiniMax are already built-in providers. Ark's Coding Plan follows the same subscription model, so both the integration pattern and the user demand are already proven.

On a personal note: I build on pi myself — [phus](https://github.com/narcilee7/phus), a self-evolving agent runtime, wraps pi-agent-core as its LLM loop. This request started from wanting Doubao models in my own pi setup — being on the Ark team just means I can also do the integration work.

### How? (optional)

### How? (optional)

Two providers:

- ark — BytePlus Ark (international),
  base URL https://ark.ap-southeast.bytepluses.com/api/v3,
  API key via ARK_API_KEY
- ark-cn — Volcengine Ark (China),
  base URL https://ark.cn-beijing.volces.com/api/v3,
  API key via ARK_CN_API_KEY

Scope for the first PR: pay-as-you-go endpoints only, static model catalog following packages/ai/catalog conventions, tests per AGENTS.md, npm run check and ./test.sh passing. Coding Plan subscription endpoints can come as a follow-up.

I work on the Ark team and will implement and maintain this myself — happy to open the PR once approved via lgtm. I can provide test API keys for maintainers privately on Discord.

issues.title: No way to see a collapsed paste before sending it

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Pasting a long block into the editor collapses it to `[paste #1 +40 lines]`. The content is restored when the message is sent, but until then there is no way to see it or edit it — no key expands the marker in place.

I would like pasting the same content a second time to expand the marker into the full text, and a `paste again to expand` label near the editor while that offer stands.

### Why?

Collapse is the right default for a long paste, but right now it is one-way from the user's side. If you paste a stack trace and then want to check you grabbed the right one, or trim two lines off it, you have to clear the editor and start over. The editor already holds the content — it just will not show it to you.

The whole mechanism is already yours: the marker format, the `pastes` map, the id renumbering, and `expandPasteMarkers` on submit. The only missing piece is expanding one in the editor.

I have this working in my extension, pi-starline, but only by patching `insertTextAtCursorInternal`, `pastes` and `pasteCounter` on the editor instance. There is no supported API for it, and that kind of patching is exactly what broke for me on 0.84. It belongs in the editor rather than around it.

### How? (optional)

When a paste collapses, remember which marker it produced and what text is behind it. If the very next paste is that same text, replace the marker with the full text in place instead of inserting a second marker. Forget it on any other keystroke, or when the marker is deleted — the offer should not linger.

One thing to be careful about: deleting a marker renumbers the ones after it, so a remembered id can end up pointing at a different paste. Before expanding, check that the text behind the id is still the text that was collapsed, and do nothing if it is not. The cost of refusing is one extra marker on screen, which the user can see. The cost of guessing is sending the wrong content without anyone noticing.

The label needs somewhere to live. A small hint slot below the editor would be the natural home, and the pending-selection indicator discussed in #7720 would want the same thing, so it seems worth building once rather than twice. I would send the behaviour, the label and the slot as one PR.

Claude Code does this and it is the thing I miss most in the editor.

issues.body:
## Summary

The TUI crashes to the terminal with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'render')` / `... (reading 'invalidate')` when a tool's custom `renderCall`/`renderResult` returns `undefined`. The root cause is in `ToolExecutionComponent`, which wraps the renderer's return value in a `MouseRegion` without a null check.

## Environment

- pi version: `1.5.0` (also reproduced on `1.4.0`)
- Node: `v25.9.0` (Homebrew, arm64)
- OS: macOS 15.5 (arm64)
- Install: `npm install -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install an extension whose tool has a `renderResult` that can return `undefined` for some result. The shipped behavior that triggers it: when a tool call fails schema validation, pi records the result as `details: {}` (an empty object, `isError: true`).
2. In `renderResult`, code like this returns `undefined` because the `switch` has no `default` and `details.action` is undefined:

```ts
renderResult(result, { expanded }, theme) {
  const details = result.details;      // {} on validation failure -> truthy
  if (!details) { /* ... */ }            // skipped
  if (details.error) { /* ... */ }       // skipped
  switch (details.action) {              // undefined
    case "list": /* ... */
    case "add":  /* ... */
    /* no default -> falls through -> returns undefined */
  }
}
```

(For example: a tool with `action: StringEnum(["list","add","toggle","clear"])` called with an invalid `action` value.)

3. Resume / open a session that contains the resulting validation-failed tool result. pi exits with an uncaught exception.

## Stack trace

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'render')
    at MouseRegion.render (…/chunk-4EYXVSA5.js:107:6834)
    at Box.render (…/chunk-4EYXVSA5.js:71:53182)
    at ToolExecutionComponent.render (…/chunk-4EYXVSA5.js:71:30283)
    at ToolExecutionComponent.render (…/chunk-44DLKSKE.js:943:1664)
    at Container.render (…/chunk-4EYXVSA5.js:71:30283)
    at Container.render (…/chunk-4EYXVSA5.js:71:30283)
    at renderCached (…/chunk-4EYXVSA5.js:108:29865)
    at layoutComponent (…/chunk-4EYXVSA5.js:108:30633)
    ...
```

The same failure also surfaces on shutdown/mode-switch as `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'invalidate')` (via `MouseRegion.invalidate` → `_InteractiveMode.switchTuiMode`).

## Root cause

In `ToolExecutionComponent`:

```js
createResultRegion(component) {
  return new MouseRegion(component, event => { /* ... */ });
}
```

`updateDisplay()` does this for the call and result renderers without guarding the renderer's return value:

```js
let component = callRenderer(this.args, theme, this.getRenderContext(...));
this.callRendererComponent = component;
renderContainer.addChild(this.createResultRegion(component)); // component may be undefined
```

`MouseRegion` then dereferences `this.child` unconditionally:

```js
class MouseRegion {
  constructor(child, onMouse) { this.child = child; /* ... */ }
  render(width) { return this.child.render(width); }   // child === undefined -> crash
  invalidate() { this.child.invalidate(); }            // child === undefined -> crash
}
```

Note the asymmetry: the fallback path is already null-guarded (`component && renderContainer.addChild(...)`), but the custom-renderer path is not, and a thrown error is caught while an `undefined` return is not.

## Suggested fix

Guard renderer return values in `updateDisplay()` (treat `undefined`/`null` like a missing renderer and fall back to the default rendering), for example:

```js
let component = callRenderer(this.args, theme, this.getRenderContext(...));
if (component) {
  this.callRendererComponent = component;
  renderContainer.addChild(this.createResultRegion(component));
} else {
  renderContainer.addChild(this.createResultRegion(this.createCallFallback()));
}
```

and the equivalent for `resultRenderer`. This makes the TUI resilient to extension/custom renderers that return `undefined`.

## Workaround

Users who hit this today can make their custom `renderResult`/`renderCall` never return `undefined` (e.g. add a `default` branch returning a `Text`, and guard `details.action`). That stops the crash immediately.

issues.title: OSC 52 copy in fullscreen TUI is swallowed by tmux (no passthrough wrap)
issues.body:
### What happened?

Copy-on-select in the fullscreen TUI writes a raw OSC 52 (`\x1b]52;c;...`). When pi runs inside tmux, tmux consumes the incoming OSC 52 into its paste buffer and does not relay it to its client. pi flashes "Copied!" either way.

On a headless Linux host over SSH (no DISPLAY/WAYLAND), OSC 52 is the only clipboard route, so copying from the TUI silently does nothing.

### Steps to reproduce

1. tmux on a headless Linux host, SSH'd from another machine (`set-clipboard on`)
2. Run pi, drag-select text in the transcript, release
3. "Copied!" flashes but the client machine's clipboard is unchanged
4. `tmux show-buffer` on the pi host shows the selection: tmux ate it

Traced to core, not an extension. Both OSC 52 emit sites write the raw sequence: `copyToClipboard` in `packages/coding-agent/src/utils/clipboard.ts` and the TUI fallback in `packages/tui/src/tui-alt-screen.ts`.

### Expected behavior

The client terminal's clipboard updates. Wrapping the write in the tmux DCS passthrough (`\x1bPtmux;\x1b<seq>\x1b\\`) when `$TMUX` is set fixes it: tmux forwards the unwrapped sequence to its client, where a plain terminal sets the clipboard and an outer tmux picks it up. I have the change with tests ready and can send a PR.

### Version

1.0.0 (also present on current main)

---

Drafted with AI assistance (traced and verified with an agent; I did the diagnosis and reviewed the writeup).

issues.title: OAuth refresh token lost when an RPC process is stopped during the startup catalog refresh (invalid_grant)
issues.body:
### What happened?

My `openai` (Sign in with ChatGPT) login keeps dying with `OAuth refresh failed for openai: OpenAI OAuth token request failed (400): {"error": "invalid_grant"}`. `/login` fixes it until the token next expires while I'm not using it.

I run pi inside T3 Code, which starts `pi --mode rpc` every few minutes to check status and stops it as soon as it answers. In RPC mode pi starts the catalog refresh in the background at startup, and that also refreshes any expired OAuth credential, even though the catalog doesn't need it. If the process is stopped after the token request goes out but before the new token is written, OpenAI has already used up the old refresh token and auth.json keeps it. The SIGTERM shutdown doesn't wait for the refresh (on Windows it's a hard kill anyway). This may explain some of the "dies after idle" reports in #10377.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Let the `openai` access token in auth.json expire.
2. `pi -ne --mode rpc --no-session`, send `get_state`, then SIGTERM it 200–300 ms after it answers.
3. The next request fails with invalid_grant.

Against a local token endpoint with single-use refresh tokens and ~150 ms latency, this lost the token 30 of 30 times. Stopping within 150 ms or after 350 ms never did, and neither did `--offline`.

### Expected behavior

The catalog refresh shouldn't rotate credentials it doesn't use, and shutdown should wait (with a timeout) for a refresh already in flight. Using `--offline` as a workaround for now.

### Version

1.4.0 (macOS and Windows, Node 26)
