issues.title: Win11: uncaughtException spawn /bin/sh ENOENT when running pi self-update

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows 11, pi crashes on startup with an uncaught exception because something in pi's self-update path spawns `/bin/sh`, which does not exist on Windows.

## Crash

```
pi exiting due to uncaughtException:
Error: spawn /bin/sh ENOENT
    at ChildProcess._handle.onexit (node:internal/child_process:315:19)
    at onErrorNT (node:internal/child_process:553:16)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:90:21) {
  errno: -4058,
  code: 'ENOENT',
  syscall: 'spawn /bin/sh',
  path: '/bin/sh',
  spawnargs: [
    '-c',
    'node C:/Users/theap/.pi/agent/bin/pi-launcher.js update --all > /tmp/pi-update.log 2>&1'
  ]
}
```

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 (native, not WSL)
- pi: 1.5.0 (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`)
- Shell available: Git Bash/MSYS, PowerShell, cmd.exe. There is no `/bin/sh` and no `/tmp` on this host.

## Root cause

The update command is executed by spawning `/bin/sh` with a Unix shell redirection to `/tmp/pi-update.log`. Both are Unix-only assumptions that break on Windows:

- `/bin/sh` does not exist on Windows, so `spawn` throws `ENOENT` as an uncaught exception and tears down the process.
- `/tmp/pi-update.log` is not a valid path on Windows.

## Suggested fix

Make the spawn platform-aware:

- On Windows, use `process.env.ComSpec` (cmd.exe) or `powershell.exe` as the shell, or better, avoid shelling out entirely and spawn `node` directly with `stdio` redirected to a log file under `os.tmpdir()`.
- Use `os.tmpdir()` for the log path instead of the hardcoded `/tmp`.
- Wrap the spawn in a try/catch (or `.on('error')`) so a missing shell degrades gracefully instead of crashing pi.

## Impact

pi becomes unusable on Win11 whenever this update path triggers. Workaround is to avoid triggering it, but the crash is process-fatal.

Thanks!

issues.title: bash tool reports "Command timed out after N seconds" for a command that already exited with a real exit code
issues.body:
**What happened?**

When a bash command has already exited with a real exit code, but a descendant keeps the inherited stdout/stderr pipe busy, the tool reports:

```
Command timed out after N seconds
```

The command did not time out. Example measured here: the shell exited with code 1 after ~1.06s, the tool returned at 12.75s with `timeout: 3`, and the model was told `Command timed out after 3 seconds`. The real exit code 1 never reached the model, so it treats a finished-and-failed command as a slow one.

Root cause: `dist/core/tools/bash.js:107` only tests the `timedOut` flag:

```js
if (timedOut) throw new Error(`timeout:${timeout}`);
```

`waitForChildProcess` had already resolved with the real exit code (the child exited long before the deadline), and `killProcessTree` at the deadline is a no-op on a pid that no longer exists (`taskkill` exits 128), so nothing about that call is actually a timeout.

Related: #6787 asked for the timeout deadline to be enforced when descendants keep stdio active (auto-closed by the new-contributor gate). This report is narrower — I am not asking to change the wait, only to stop reporting a false `timed out` when the child already exited. That is a one-condition fix and it also preserves the wait behavior added for #5303.

**Steps to reproduce**

Windows 11, Git Bash, `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.4.0:

```bash
bash(command: "bash -c 'while true; do echo tick; sleep 0.05; done' & sleep 1; echo boom >&2; exit 1", timeout: 3)
```

Result: returns after 12.75s (varies: 5.1s, 12.0s, 22.7s in repeated runs) with output ending `Command timed out after 3 seconds`.

Control cases on the same machine:

| command | timeout | shell exited | tool returned |
|---|---|---|---|
| above (chatty descendant) | 3s | 1059ms, code 1 | 22744ms → `timed out` |
| same but descendant stdio redirected | 3s | 1050ms, code 1 | 1050ms → `Command exited with code 1` |
| `sleep 1; echo boom; sleep 300` | 3s | 3310ms (killed) | 3310ms → `timed out` (correct) |

**Expected behavior**

If the shell had already exited before the deadline, report its real exit code (the same `Command exited with code N` path), not `timed out`. Keep `timed out` for commands whose process was still alive at the deadline.

Suggested condition: record the exit timestamp, and in the `timedOut` branch throw only when the child had not exited before `start + timeoutMs`; otherwise return `{ exitCode }`.

**Version**

pi-coding-agent 1.4.0 (also present on `main`), Windows 11 + Git for Windows bash. Reached through pi-web-ui 0.113.1, which passes `timeout` through unchanged — reproduced directly against the SDK, no extension loaded.

---
_Filed by the reporter's coding agent; the measurements above were produced and re-run locally, not generated._

issues.title: read tool reads whole files even when one line is requested
issues.body:
### Problem

The `read` tool reads the whole file into memory before it uses `offset` or `limit`. Asking for one line from a very large file can therefore make Pi use a lot of memory and crash.

### Reproduction

Tested with `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.85.1`:

1. Create a 128 MiB file without filling the disk:

```sh
truncate -s 128M /tmp/pi-read-large.txt
printf 'first line\n' | dd of=/tmp/pi-read-large.txt conv=notrunc status=none
```

2. Run this Node.js code:

```ts
import { createReadTool } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";

const before = process.memoryUsage().rss;
const result = await createReadTool("/tmp").execute("repro", {
  path: "pi-read-large.txt",
  limit: 1,
});
const after = process.memoryUsage().rss;

console.log(result.content[0].text.length); // 61 characters
console.log((after - before) / 1024 / 1024); // about 259 MiB more memory
```

The result is only 61 characters long, but Pi uses about 259 MiB of extra memory, roughly twice the file size.

### Expected behavior

Pi should read only the requested lines. Its memory use should stay about the same even when the file is much larger.

issues.title: SIGILL (ILL_ILLOPN) in Worker thread at pi+0x2407064 (ud2 after a sigaction call), headless runs — 1.4.0 linux-x64

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

Two long headless task runs (`pi "<prompt>"`, tool use only) killed the process with SIGILL / ILL_ILLOPN, ~40 min apart (2026-11-03), on a thread named `Worker`. Both times the faulting instruction is the same: `pi + 0x2407064`, which gdb decodes as a deliberate trap:

```
0x260705c: mov    %rbx,%rsi
0x260705f: call   0x2634e80     ; tail-jumps to sigaction@plt
=> 0x2607064: ud2
0x2607066: int3  (padding)
```

`ud2` with int3 padding right after a `sigaction` wrapper is an assert/abort path, not a wild jump — pi trapped itself. Top frames identical across both crashes:

```
#0 pi + 0x2407064 (ud2)   #2 pi + 0x2404768   #4 pi + 0x36940f4   #8 libc start_thread
#1 pi + 0x2405266         #3 pi + 0x24046e9   #5-7 pi + 0x3693xxx
```

Ruled out: OOM (52 GiB free, no kernel OOM kills), hardware (same offset twice). `~/.pi/agent/crashes.json` has no entry — SIGILL bypasses the JS-level crash handler. No `.node` addons on the machine. Same faulting offset as #9500 (0.85.1, cause unconfirmed) — possibly the same trap site; this report adds two preserved cores and the disassembly.

### Steps to reproduce

Non-deterministic — two independent long-running headless sessions, heavy bash/read/edit/write tool use; not reproduced on demand. Honest gap per the template: these runs had extensions loaded (npm packages + local scripts in `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`), and **`pi -ne` validation is not satisfied** — a transient mid-session crash can't be bisected that way yet.

### Expected behavior

Worker threads should not hit a `ud2` trap; if an assertion fired, something on stderr first.

### Version

1.4.0 (bun-compiled linux-x64, via mise). Host: Arch, kernel 7.2.5, glibc 2.44, i7-8850H. Current 1.5.0 not yet tested. Cores preserved via systemd-coredump (PIDs 468627, 469347) and available for symbolization attempts.

issues.title: Preserve model selector selection after background refresh
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Prevent the interactive model selector (`ModelSelectorComponent`) from resetting the user's highlighted selection back to the default model when the asynchronous background catalog refresh completes.

### Why?

Opening the model selector triggers a background catalog refresh (`refreshModelCatalogs`)
If the user moves the cursor or filters the list while the request is in flight, the completion handler unconditionally resets `selectedIndex` back to the initial model, which may cause to select the wrong model.

### How? (optional)

Adopt the selection-preservation pattern already used in `ScopedModelsSelectorComponent`:
  - Snapshot the currently selected model before reloading catalog items and re-applying active search filters.
  - Restore `selectedIndex` to that model (by provider and ID) in the refreshed list.
  - Fall back to the session's active model only if the browsed model was removed.
  - Avoid redundant list rebuilds when the index did not change.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: inprogress
labels.description: Issue is being worked on

issues.body:
### What happened?

On startup pi opens the external editor. The prompt contains `;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000;1;rgb:d4d4/2c2c/3a3a;…`.
The query runs regardless of theme.

**Versions:** 0.99.x are affected. 0.87.1 is fine. Windows Terminal is fine.
**Terminal:** mintty on Windows, native node.exe, `TERM=xterm`, `EDITOR=vim` (I am using GitBash for Windows environment)

## Cause

0.87.1 sent a single `ESC]11;?BEL` query. 0.99.x sends OSC 10, OSC 11, OSC 4 for indices 0–15, and DA1 (`ESC[c`) as the end marker (`TERMINAL_COLOR_QUERY` in `packages/tui/src/tui.ts`). In this terminal:

1. The DA1 reply arrives first, before any color reply. `consumeTerminalColorResponse` then drops the pending query, so later replies are no longer consumed.
2. The OSC replies arrive without their `ESC]4` prefix, in fragments (`;0`, `;rgb:0000/0000/0000`, `BEL`, `;1`, …). The reply regex cannot match them anyway.
3. `StdinBuffer` splits non-escape input into single characters, so they land in the editor as text. Each stray BEL is Ctrl+G and opens the external editor.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run pi under GitBash (Windows).
2. The prompt contains `;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000;1;rgb:d4d4/2c2c/3a3a;…`.
3. External editor opens, containing the prompt.

### Expected behavior

Prompt is empty and external editor is not opened at the startup. Worked in 0.87.1.

### Version

0.99.0, 0.99.1, 0.99.2,
1.0.0 (tui-mode regular; see my comment below)

Termux/Android: findExecutableOnPath and commandExists spawn on the caller thread and can freeze an in-process host

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## What do you want to change?

Two helpers in `packages/coding-agent/src/utils` spawn a process to answer a question that needs no process:

- `findExecutableOnPath()` (`shell.ts`) runs `spawnSync("which", ...)` on POSIX.
- `commandExists()` (`tools-manager.ts`) runs `spawnSync(cmd, ["--version"])`, and it runs once per grep/glob tool call through `ensureTool("rg"/"fd")`.

I want both to scan `PATH` with `access(path, X_OK)` on POSIX, the same check `which` applies per entry, and keep the current spawn paths on win32. `findExecutableOnPath()` would keep `which` as a fallback when the scan finds nothing, so the current "trust which" behavior stays for unusual layouts.

## Why?

A `spawnSync` on the main thread of a multi-threaded process can freeze the whole process on Android/Termux. Concrete trace from pi-web-ui#78 (public, with thread dumps): every grep eventually froze the host; at hang time the parent sat in `pipe_read` and the forked child in `futex_wait` with the parent's cmdline, so the child never reached exec and libuv's `uv_spawn` kept waiting on the error pipe. Process alive, event loop dead, port no longer accepting connections. Eight hangs in two days, recovered only by restarting the process. That was this exact `ensureTool` -> `commandExists` path.

It hits any host that runs the agent in-process, not just us: the SDK is what forks. Standalone `pi` mostly escapes it because the CLI is not a multi-threaded server, which is also why CI can never reproduce it.

We work around it downstream today: pi-web-ui carries an in-memory load-time patch that rewrites both helpers on Android/Termux only (xing-shuyin/pi-web-ui#810, hardened in #815, `server/patch-executable-lookup.ts`). It exists solely because the SDK forks, and it is written to be thrown away once the SDK resolves executables from `PATH` itself. So this change deletes downstream code instead of adding any.

Second reason, platform independent: `commandExists()` spends one fork per grep/glob call. On Android that is measurable; everywhere else it is free to remove.

Still present on `main` today (1.5.0): both functions are unchanged.

## How?

I have the patch (two functions, plus one line in the existing test mock) and will open the PR once you approve. Verified on a real device (Termux, aarch64, Node 26.3.1): the PATH scan returns exactly what `which` returns for `bash`, `sh`, `rg`, `fd`, `git`, and for a name that does not exist.

The current comment says `which` "handles Termux and special filesystems"; that is the reason it stays as a fallback instead of being deleted. Both call sites are in core, no extension involved.

issues.title: grep: a glob with a folder in it silently matches nothing unless path is the cwd

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

grep's `glob` doesn't say what it's relative to, and in practice it's anchored to the process cwd, not to `path`. So `{ path: "repo", glob: "migrations/main/*.js" }` returns "No matches found" even though `repo/migrations/main/a.js` exists.

That's ripgrep's design (it roots `--glob` at its own cwd, `OverrideBuilder::new(&state.cwd)` in hiargs.rs), and `grep.ts` spawns rg without a cwd, so the anchor is a folder the model never sees. Meanwhile grep prints results relative to `path` (`migrations/main/a.js` in the example), so a glob written in that same frame finds nothing. `find` already handles this case, it prefixes `**/` to path globs.

It bit us in agents: the model got a false "no matches", decided the file didn't exist and gave up. The empty result looks exactly like a real negative.

I'd like to implement the fix myself, it's a three-line change plus a test.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/g/repo/migrations/main && echo hello > /tmp/g/repo/migrations/main/a.js
cd /tmp/g
rg -l --glob 'migrations/main/*.js' hello repo        # nothing
cd repo && rg -l --glob 'migrations/main/*.js' hello . # ./migrations/main/a.js
```

Same through the tool: from `/tmp/g`, `grep` with `path: "repo"`, `glob: "migrations/main/*.js"`, `pattern: "hello"` returns "No matches found". With `glob: "**/migrations/main/*.js"` it finds `migrations/main/a.js`.

### Expected behavior

The glob is relative to `path`, the same frame grep prints its results in, so it finds `a.js`.

Two ways to get there, either works for me:

1. Anchor the glob to `path`: spawn rg with `cwd` set to the search dir and search `.` instead of the absolute path, then resolve rg's relative paths against `searchPath` in `formatPath`. Searching `.` matters: rg resolves its cwd through symlinks, so only setting `cwd` still misses on paths like macOS `/tmp`. I patched it into 1.5.0's dist and the call above finds `a.js` (relative, absolute and symlinked `path`), a decoy at `repo/nested/migrations/main/b.js` correctly stays out, and output for every other case is unchanged.
2. If anchoring to the cwd is intended, say so in the `glob` description (folder globs need a leading `**/`) or prefix it like `find` does.

### Version

1.5.0

issues.title: insertThinkingLevelMessages can emit adjacent output_config directives → OpenRouter 400 "Two adjacent output_config directives are not allowed"

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
## Summary

`insertThinkingLevelMessages` (anthropic-messages provider, dist bundle chunk `anthropic-messages-BWGCKOF4.js`) emits one `{role:"system", content:[], output_config:{effort}}` directive before every assistant message that has a provider thinking level, plus a trailing directive for the active effort. If the **converted** message list ever contains two consecutive leveled assistant messages (which happens when an intermediate message is absent — e.g. an assistant message whose blocks were all dropped by a folding/compression proxy in front of OpenRouter), the result is **two adjacent output_config directives**, which OpenRouter rejects:

```
400 ... "path":["messages",2,"output_config"],
"message":"Two adjacent output_config directives are not allowed"
```

## Reproduced

- Two adjacent directives → OpenRouter 400 with the exact error above (minimal request).
- Full 197-message session history with all directives, sent direct to OpenRouter **without** the folding proxy → 200 OK.
- Same history **through** the folding proxy → 400. The proxy's fold reconstruction is what leaves two directives adjacent (client-side sequence itself is healthy — verified by simulating `convertMessages` + `insertThinkingLevelMessages` over the session file: no adjacency).

Session details (private content, sanitized): pi 1.5.0, `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5` via OpenRouter, thinkingLevel `max`, model compat `supportsMidConvoEffort: true`.

## Ask

`insertThinkingLevelMessages` should de-duplicate: when two leveled messages end up adjacent in `converted.messages` (or when the previous emitted message is already a directive), **skip the earlier directive and keep the latter** (later effort wins — same semantics as the trailing active directive). One-line defense that makes pi robust against any history reshaping between turns.

Related: #9165 (same directive pipeline, but a model-catalog fix — different failure mode; this one is about adjacency, not support).

## Workaround

`/thinking off` (or any non-effort level) stops directive emission entirely and unblocks the session; switching back to `max` re-triggers the 400 deterministically on the next request.

tui: split kitty CSI-u sequences are flushed into the composer as text, then glue to the next keypress (dead Enter/quit); report-event-types is requested but unused

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

Typing in the composer sometimes produces raw escape sequences as text instead of characters:

```
H^[[104;1:3uo^[[111;1:3uw^[[119;1:3u^[[0^[[I^[[<35;54;32M
```

After that, Enter, `/quit` and `/resume` stop responding — the session has to be killed. Seen in Ghostty 1.4.0 and Alacritty 0.16.1 (both implement the kitty keyboard protocol), in pi 1.5.0 and in pi-bolt 1.4.0. Started the day 1.5.0 was installed; more likely while the agent is streaming output.

Two causes in `StdinBuffer`, as far as I can tell:

1. An *incomplete* CSI fragment is flushed to the key parser when its bytes arrive more than 50 ms apart, so a split kitty CSI-u sequence gets typed as text; the half-sequence then stays buffered and swallows the next keypress (dead Enter). Same mechanism as #11172, but for CSI-u rather than SGR mouse.
2. pi requests kitty `report event types` (`DESIRED_KITTY_KEYBOARD_PROTOCOL_FLAGS = 7`), and nothing in pi reads keyboard release events, so releases arrive as noise that ends up in the composer — the `hello` output in #2484.

### Steps to reproduce

Feed `StdinBuffer` from the shipped 1.5.0 bundle two chunks 90 ms apart:

- `"\x1b[104;1:3"` then `"u"` → emits `["\x1b[104;1:3", "u"]` (expected: `["\x1b[104;1:3u"]`)
- `"\x1b[0"` then `"h\r"` → emits `["\x1b[0", "h", "\r"]`, i.e. the Enter is consumed as part of the pending fragment

A gap under the timeout (5 ms) reassembles correctly, which is why it looks intermittent.

### Expected behavior

An incomplete escape sequence must never reach the focused component as key input, and a pending fragment must not swallow the following keypress.

### Version

pi 1.5.0 / macOS 15.8.1 / Ghostty 1.4.0 and Alacritty 0.16.1

---

I can implement this (hold-then-drop instead of flush, and stop requesting event types). Waiting for `lgtm` per CONTRIBUTING before opening a PR.

issues.title: Extension loader fails to resolve declared dependencies of extensions installed with pnpm (jiti + isolated node_modules layout)
issues.body:
## What happened?

Context: I had my extensions configs with git installs, but since I set up [semver-calver-release](https://github.com/cad0p/semver-calver-release) I now have npm `@next` tags releases for each commit on main, so I tried porting my `settings.json` setup to npm installs, to more closely match what another user of my pi extensions would have in their setup. The following is what I discovered

---

pi fails to load extensions installed from npm when pnpm is configured as `npmCommand` in pi's settings (pi's managed install then uses pnpm's default isolated node_modules layout). Two real cases:

1. **`@cad0p/pi-napkin`** (pi extension) imports `@cad0p/napkin` — declared in its [`package.json`](https://github.com/cad0p/pi-napkin/blob/main/package.json#L74) `dependencies`. `@cad0p/napkin` is a plain TypeScript Node package (CLI library), not a pi extension. Boot fails:

   ```
   Failed to load extension: Cannot find module '@cad0p/napkin'
   Require stack:
   - .../node_modules/@cad0p/pi-napkin/extensions/napkin-context/index.ts
   ```

2. **`@cad0p/pi-steering`** (pi extension) imports `@cad0p/unbash-walker` — also declared in [`package.json`](https://github.com/cad0p/pi-steering/blob/main/package.json#L76) `dependencies`, a plain JavaScript package (`dist/index.js`). Same error: `Cannot find module '@cad0p/unbash-walker'`.

Both dependencies are declared correctly, and plain Node resolves them; pi's loader doesn't. The failure is layout-dependent, not package-dependent: it reproduces with any unrelated pair (`debug` → `ms` in the repro below). It's a three-way interaction:

1. **pnpm isolated layout**: `node_modules/<pkg>` is a symlink into `.pnpm/<pkg>@<ver>/node_modules/<pkg>`, and transitive deps exist only as siblings inside that store dir — not in the root `node_modules`.
2. **jiti's resolver doesn't realpath** the entry module before resolving its imports. Node's native loader does, which is why the same file resolves under plain Node.
3. **pi passes the symlink path as-is** to `jiti.import()` in `loadExtensionModule` (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/loader.ts`).

jiti's upward traversal walks the symlink path, misses the store-only sibling, and fails. The failing step is specifier resolution from the *entry's* location — the dependency's own language is irrelevant (case 2's dep is plain JS and fails identically). Affected are entries jiti transpiles itself: TypeScript, and JavaScript with ESM syntax. Entries jiti delegates to Node's native loader (`.cjs`, `.mjs`) get realpath'd and work — which is why pi extensions, whose entries are `.ts` or ESM `.js`, always hit this. A consumer-side workaround exists (`publicHoistPattern` in the managed `pnpm-workspace.yaml`) but is package-manager-specific, only covers the listed packages, and every consumer must configure it.

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/pi-repro && cd /tmp/pi-repro
echo '{"name":"t","private":true}' > package.json
pnpm add debug@4.4.1 jiti@2.7.0
printf 'import ms from "ms";\nexport default { found: typeof ms };\n' > node_modules/debug/probe.ts
```

Now load `node_modules/debug/probe.ts` with jiti the way pi does (pi 0.84.1 bundles jiti 2.7.0):

```js
import { createJiti } from "jiti/static";
const jiti = createJiti(import.meta.url, { moduleCache: false });
await jiti.import("./node_modules/debug/probe.ts", { default: true });
// -> Cannot find module 'ms'
// -> importing the realpath (node_modules/.pnpm/debug@4.4.1/node_modules/debug/probe.ts) works
```

Real-world case: `pi install npm:@cad0p/pi-napkin@next` with pnpm as `npmCommand`, start pi → the boot error above.

## Expected behavior

Declared dependencies of installed extension packages resolve regardless of the package manager's layout — the same way Node's native loader resolves them.

## Version

0.84.1 (Node dist)

## Suggested fix

Realpath the entry once at the load boundary in `loadExtensionModule` (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/loader.ts`) — one line using `canonicalizePath` (already exported from `utils/paths.ts`, realpath with fallback):

```diff
- const module = await jiti.import(extensionPath, { default: true });
+ const module = await jiti.import(canonicalizePath(extensionPath), { default: true });
```

(plus `canonicalizePath` in the existing `resolvePath` import from `../../utils/paths.ts`). I can open a PR.

issues.title: Load prebuilt ESM extensions without jiti when they import host packages

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

Pi loads every extension that imports a host package (`@earendil-works/*`, `typebox`) through jiti, even when the entry is a prebuilt ESM bundle. jiti transpiles the bundle and writes a copy to `$TMPDIR/jiti`.

With a cold jiti cache this adds about 1 to 4 s to startup. The cache is cold after every update of an extension package and in every new `TMPDIR` (new host, sandbox, container).

Extensions that import only `node:` modules load natively, with no jiti cache file. Adding a single host package import, for example `import { getAgentDir } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent"`, sends the same file through jiti.

Measurements (time to the first `get_state` reply in `pi --mode rpc --no-session -ne -e ...`, median of 4 to 8 runs, one host):

| Config | Cold cache | Warm cache |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No extensions | 625 ms | 590 ms |
| 7 extensions, `.ts` sources | 2255 ms | 725 ms |
| Same 7 extensions, bundled `.js` | 1766 ms | 712 ms |
| Full setup (~20 extensions) | ~6700 ms | ~2400 ms |

Bundling saves only ~0.5 s, because jiti still transpiles each bundle.

Also, pi never prunes the jiti cache: I had 25,631 files (235 MB) after ~3 months, about 95% of them copies of older versions of the same sources.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a minimal ESM extension that imports a host package:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p /tmp/esm-ext && cd /tmp/esm-ext
   cat > package.json <<'EOF'
   {"type": "module", "pi": {"extensions": ["./index.js"]}}
   EOF
   cat > index.js <<'EOF'
   import { getAgentDir } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";
   export default function () {
     getAgentDir();
   }
   EOF
   ```

2. Start pi with an empty `TMPDIR` and request the state:

   ```bash
   export TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
   echo '{"type":"get_state"}' | pi --mode rpc --no-session -ne -e /tmp/esm-ext/index.js
   ```

3. Check the jiti cache:

   ```bash
   ls -R "$TMPDIR/jiti"
   ```

   It contains a transpiled copy of `index.js`, although the file is already plain ESM.

4. For comparison, remove the `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` import (and the `getAgentDir()` call) and repeat steps 2–3 with a new `TMPDIR`. Pi now loads the file natively and `$TMPDIR/jiti` contains no copy of `index.js`.

### Expected behavior

Pi loads prebuilt ESM extensions natively, without jiti, even when they import host packages. Host packages still resolve to pi's own instances.

### Version

1.3.0

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): wait for a started OAuth refresh to be saved before exit
prs.body:
Fixes #11692.

## Problem

In RPC mode the startup catalog refresh runs in the background and also refreshes an expired OAuth credential. If pi exits after the token request went out but before the new token is written, the provider has already spent the old single-use refresh token and auth.json keeps only that one. The next request fails with `invalid_grant`.

Trace: `pi --mode rpc` starts, `get_state` is answered, catalog refresh sends the token request, the client sends SIGTERM (or closes stdin), `shutdown()` runs `runtimeHost.dispose()`, which does not know about the refresh, and the process exits. Same for print and interactive mode, and for a prompt-time refresh cut off by an exit.

## Fix

- `RuntimeCredentials.modify()` tracks every pending modification (same idiom as the MCP `track()` / `McpAuthProvider.settled()`).
- `RuntimeCredentials.settled()` / `ModelRuntime.settleCredentialWrites()` wait for them.
- `AgentSessionRuntime.dispose()` waits for them. All modes exit through `dispose()`. No extra timeout: the OAuth refresh (15 s) and the auth.json lock wait (30 s) are already bounded, and a second signal still exits at once.

Not changed: the catalog refresh still refreshes expired OAuth credentials, also for providers whose catalog does not use them (the pi.dev catalog for `openai`, `anthropic`, ...). Skipping that would need a per-provider "catalog needs auth" signal in pi-ai; it is optional now that exits wait.

`docs/rpc.md` now says that pi waits for pending work before exiting.

## Testing

- `test/runtime-credentials.test.ts`: `settled()` waits until a pending modification is written, and resolves after a failed one.
- `test/suite/regressions/11692-dispose-waits-for-oauth-refresh.test.ts`: `dispose()` waits until the token from a background catalog refresh is saved. Fails without the fix.
- Real process: `pi --mode rpc` with an extension OAuth provider (expired credential, 400 ms refresh), SIGTERM about 100 ms after the token request started. Without the wait: 3 of 3 runs kept the spent refresh token. With the fix: 3 of 3 saved the new one (exit 143). Closing stdin instead of SIGTERM: new token saved, exit 0.
- `npm run check`; `test/rpc*`, `test/print-mode`, `test/model-runtime*`, runtime and regression suites pass.

prs.body:
The edit tool rewrote the line endings of lines it did not touch. It could also run out of memory after the file was already written. Encoding handling (non-UTF-8, UTF-16) was split out into a separate PR.

## Line endings (#8544)

**Problem.** The edit tool looked for the first line ending in the file, normalized the whole file to LF for matching, and wrote the whole file back with that one ending:

```
a\nb\r\nX = 1\r\n   edit X = 1 -> X = 2   =>  a\nb\nX = 2\n    (both CRLF became LF)
a\r\nb\nc           edit c -> C           =>  a\r\nb\r\nC     (the LF became CRLF)
a\rb\nX = 1\n       edit X = 1 -> X = 2   =>  a\nb\nX = 2\n    (untouched lone CR became LF)
```

**Solution.** Matching still runs on the LF-normalized text, so matching itself is unchanged: exact and fuzzy matching, multiple edits, duplicates, overlaps and error messages. `applyEditsToNormalizedContent` now also returns the replacements it applied. `applyReplacementsToOriginal` maps each replacement back to the original text and splices it in there. Normalizing only shortens CRLF to LF, so the original offset is the normalized offset plus the number of CRLFs before it. A range that covers a normalized LF therefore covers the whole CRLF. Text outside the replaced ranges keeps its bytes.

Line breaks in the new text use the line ending of the line where the replaced range starts. For an unterminated last line, they use the ending of the line before. A lone CR is used only in files with no LF at all (classic Mac files). Elsewhere a lone CR is more likely a control character inside a line.

Fuzzy matches still rewrite the whole lines they touch, as before. They now return those lines as one replacement instead of rebuilding the file, so lines outside the replacement keep their endings.

A kept CR and an LF can meet at a splice seam and would then merge into one CRLF line break. For example, in `a\rb\nc` the edit `b -> \nB` would write `a\r\nB\nc` (normalized `a\nB\nc`) while the diff shows `a\n\nB\nc`. Deleting `b` would write `a\r\nc` while the diff shows `a\n\nc`. Whenever a piece ending in CR is followed by a piece starting with LF, an LF is added at the seam. This turns the CR into a CRLF of its own, so the written file normalizes to exactly the content the diff and patch describe. No kept byte is changed or removed; the one added byte sits where the replaced text was. For a pure deletion between a lone CR and an LF there is no other way to keep both line breaks. Writing the merged bytes and diffing them instead would silently join two lines the model meant to keep apart.

Pure LF and pure CRLF files produce the same output as before. For files without any CR, the normalized result is written directly, as before.

## Memory: diff before writing, notice for files larger than 5 MB

**Problem.** `execute` wrote the file and then ran `generateDiffString` and `generateUnifiedPatch`. Each of these diffs the whole file. A one-line edit of a 50 MB file under `--max-old-space-size=256` crashed with a heap out-of-memory error after the new content was already on disk. The TUI preview (`computeEditsDiff`) diffs the whole file a third time.

**Solution.**
- The diff and patch are now computed before the file is written. If they fail, the file is unchanged.
- For files larger than 5 MB (`EDIT_DIFF_MAX_FILE_BYTES`, measured on the file as read), both `details.diff` and the preview are the one-line notice `Diff not shown: the file is larger than 5 MB.` `details.patch` is `""` (documented on `EditToolDetails`), and `firstChangedLine` is unset.
- The built-in renderer shows lines that are not diff lines as context text, so the notice appears where the diff would be. No change was needed there. The `built-in-tool-renderer.ts` example counted `+`/`-` lines and showed `+0 / -0` for such edits. It now shows `Applied, diff not shown` when `details.patch` is empty.
- The model-visible result (`Successfully replaced N block(s) in <path>.`) is unchanged. Only `details` and the preview change.

**Threshold.** Diffing one file with `diffLines` used about 10 to 15 times the file size in heap (measured: 5 MB per side about +50 MB, 10 MB per side about +160 MB, 20 MB per side about +360 MB). 5 MB keeps the diff around 50 MB and 200 ms, and source files are far smaller. The limit applies to the file's byte size, not to old plus new content. An edit's new text is model output and small compared to such a file, and bytes are never fewer than the UTF-16 code units the diff works on, so this measure is conservative.

## Behavior differences

- Files with mixed line endings or lone CRs keep their bytes outside the edited text. Files that use only CR line endings now get CR in inserted lines; before, the whole file was converted to LF.
- Files larger than 5 MB: the TUI shows the notice instead of a diff, `details.patch` is empty, and `firstChangedLine` is unset.
- Not changed: matching still builds file-sized strings, mainly the fuzzy normalization used to count duplicates. With a 256 MB heap, a 50 MB edit running at the same time as the TUI preview can still run out of memory sometimes. That happens during matching, before anything is written.
- Removed unused internal helpers: `detectLineEnding`, `restoreLineEndings` and `applyReplacementsPreservingUnchangedLines`, which became the private `widenReplacementsToLines`. None of them were exported from the package. `packages/durable` has its own copy and is not changed.

## Testing

- `npm run check`: clean.
- `test/tools.test.ts`, `test/edit-tool-diff-before-write.test.ts`, `test/edit-tool-legacy-input.test.ts`, `test/edit-tool-no-full-redraw.test.ts`, `test/file-mutation-queue.test.ts`, `test/suite/regressions/8337-utf8-bom-parsing.test.ts`: 131 passed.
- New tests, all with `Buffer.equals` on the written bytes:
  - mixed endings with LF first and with CRLF first (#8544)
  - lone CR
  - pure CRLF and pure LF with inserted lines (unchanged behavior)
  - multiple edits in a mixed file, each new line getting its line's ending
  - fuzzy match widening in a mixed file
  - files larger than 5 MB: preview and `details` show the notice, the patch is empty, the result text is unchanged, and the file is correct
  - diff before write: `generateUnifiedPatch` is mocked to throw, and `writeFile` is never called
  - seams: insertion after a lone CR, deletion between a lone CR and an LF (written bytes checked, and the patch applied to the old content gives the intended content), and an inserted CR ending before a kept LF
  - random property test: 3000 random mixed `\n`/`\r\n`/`\r` files with random edits, checking that the written content normalized to LF equals the content that was diffed. It fails without the seam rule.
- On `origin/main`, all new tests fail except pure CRLF and pure LF, which pass there because that behavior is unchanged. Without the seam rule, the three seam tests fail.
- Ad-hoc random comparison against `origin/main`'s implementation, 40k random edits:
  - On pure LF and pure CRLF files, the written output and the error messages are identical.
  - On files mixing `\n`, `\r\n` and `\r`, the normalized result is identical.
- Memory, 50 MB file with a one-line edit in the middle, `node --max-old-space-size=256`:
  - before: heap out-of-memory crash, with the edit already written to the file
  - after, LF file: `execute` succeeds, the file is correct, sampled heap peak about 166 MB, about 2 s
  - after, CRLF file: same result, sampled heap peak about 210 MB
  - Running `execute` and the preview at the same time succeeded in most runs. One CRLF run ran out of memory during matching, before anything was written, and left the file untouched.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): read and edit handle UTF-16 and non-UTF-8 files without corrupting them
prs.body:
`read` and `edit` assumed every file is UTF-8. `edit` silently corrupted files that are not UTF-8, and `read` showed UTF-16 files as garbage. This PR adds one shared helper, `src/core/tools/file-encoding.ts`, that both tools use.

## Problem

**Not valid UTF-8 (#10349, #5797).** `edit` decoded the file with `buffer.toString("utf-8")`, so every invalid byte became U+FFFD and was written back as `ef bf bd`. For example, in the Windows-1252 file `caf\xe9\nTIMEOUT = 30\n`, the edit `TIMEOUT = 30 -> 60` turned the untouched `e9` into `ef bf bd`, and the tool reported success. A GBK comment from #10349 (`# 配置：超时时间（秒）`) became `# 锟斤拷...`.

**UTF-16 with BOM.** `read` showed UTF-16 files as NUL-interleaved garbage. A normal `oldText` in `edit` did not match. An `oldText` copied from that garbage, including its NUL characters, did match, and `edit` wrote the file back as UTF-8 with the BOM turned into U+FFFD.

## Solution

`file-encoding.ts`:
- `decodeFile(buffer, path)` is used by `edit` and round-trips exactly:
  - `FF FE` / `FE FF`: UTF-16LE/BE, decoded with Buffer's `utf16le` (byte-swapped for BE), which keeps lone surrogates. A file with such a byte order mark but an odd number of bytes is not valid UTF-16 and is refused: `Could not edit file: <path>. It starts with a UTF-16LE byte order mark but has an odd number of bytes, so it is not valid UTF-16. The file was left unchanged.`
  - Valid UTF-8 (`isUtf8`): exactly as before, `toString("utf-8")` plus `splitBom`.
  - Anything else is `bytes`: decoded as Latin-1, one character per byte, which is lossless.
- `encodeNonUtf8File(encoding, text)` encodes back, with the same BOM for UTF-16.
- `TextFileDecoder` is used by `read`, in both the streaming path (merged in #11750) and the whole-file fallback for custom operations without `createReadStream`. A UTF-16 BOM selects UTF-16 without the mark; characters split across chunks are decoded correctly. Everything else is decoded exactly like `Buffer.toString("utf-8")`, so invalid UTF-8 still shows U+FFFD and a UTF-8 BOM stays as U+FEFF, as on main.

`read.ts` changes only at the decode step (2 lines).

`edit`:
- The file is decoded with `decodeFile` and written back in the same encoding.
- UTF-8 files still go through `EditOperations.writeFile(string)`, unchanged.
- Other files go through a new optional `EditOperations.writeFileBytes(absolutePath, Buffer)`, which the default operations implement. `writeFile` takes a string and cannot reproduce these bytes. Custom operations without `writeFileBytes` get `Could not edit file: <path>. The file is not valid UTF-8|UTF-16LE|UTF-16BE, and the configured edit operations can only write UTF-8 text. The file was left unchanged.`
- For `bytes` files the original encoding is unknown, so an edit is only applied when it can splice exact bytes:
  - **`oldText` and `newText` must be ASCII.** Otherwise the edit is refused. The error says the file is not valid UTF-8 and that only ASCII edits are applied. It suggests anchoring on ASCII text, using bash (`iconv`, or a script that reads and writes the file in its encoding), or `write` if converting the file to UTF-8 is acceptable.
  - **Only exact matches, and only exact duplicates.** Fuzzy matching rewrites the touched lines from NFKC/whitespace-normalized text, which would change non-ASCII bytes in those lines. In Latin-1-decoded text, NFKC turns 0xB2 (`²`) into `2` and 0xBD (`½`) into `1⁄2`. 0xA0 becomes a space and is dropped at line ends, although 0xA0 can be a GBK trail byte. Duplicate counting in these files is exact too: `X = 1` and `X\xa0= 1` are different text there, not two occurrences.
  - **No change within 3 bytes after a non-ASCII byte.** In GBK, Big5 and Shift-JIS the second byte of a character can be ASCII; in GB18030 so can the fourth (U+20000 is `95 32 82 36`). Shift-JIS `表` is `95 5C`, which `read` shows as `\uFFFD\`. An edit is refused if any of the 3 bytes before its first changed position, after the unchanged prefix of `oldText`/`newText`, is non-ASCII.
    - Why this is enough: the edit is ASCII, so every byte between that position and any later changed byte is ASCII. If no non-ASCII byte is within 3 bytes before the first change, none is within 3 bytes before any change. A changed or inserted byte therefore cannot be a trail byte. EUC-JP and EUC-KR trail bytes are never ASCII.
    - Cost: some harmless edits in single-byte encodings are refused. For example, in Latin-1 `caf\xe9=1`, the edit `=1 -> :1` is refused. The error names the alternatives.

Why splice bytes rather than refuse all non-UTF-8 files, or guess the encoding:
- **Refusing every such file** would make the common case need bash: an ASCII change in a Windows-1252 or GBK source file.
- **Guessing the encoding (chardet-style)** is unreliable on short files, as noted in #5797. A wrong guess corrupts the whole file silently.

Splicing bytes needs no guess. Its only failure mode is a refusal with an explanation.

## Dependencies and overlaps

- **#11750 (read streaming)** is merged; this PR is rebased on it and wires `TextFileDecoder` into both read paths. A test reads UTF-16LE/BE through 1-byte and 3-byte streamed chunks and through the fallback path.
- **#11751 (edit line endings)** also changes `edit.ts` and `edit-diff.ts`. This PR keeps main's line-ending code, so whichever merges second rebases. The conflict is in the read, normalize and write lines of `execute` and in `computeEditsDiff`.
- **Line endings depend on #11751.** Here, UTF-16 and `bytes` files keep every byte except line endings. Those still go through main's normalize-and-restore: the whole file is written with its first line ending, so mixed CRLF/LF and lone CRs in untouched lines change, and the patch, built on normalized text, does not show it. #11751 makes untouched line endings survive for every encoding. Whichever of the two PRs merges second adds a combined test: a mixed-ending Latin-1 file and a mixed-ending UTF-16 file, edited with every other byte preserved.

## Behavior differences

- UTF-8 files, with or without BOM: unchanged in `read` and `edit`.
- Files that are not valid UTF-8: `read` is unchanged and still shows U+FFFD. `edit` applies ASCII edits keeping all other bytes except line endings (see #11751). It refuses non-ASCII edits, fuzzy-only matches, and changes within 3 bytes after a non-ASCII byte. Before, it corrupted the file.
- UTF-16 with BOM: `read` shows the decoded text, and `edit` edits it and writes UTF-16 with the same BOM. For an odd-length file, `read` shows the dangling byte as U+FFFD, and `edit` refuses the file.
- UTF-16 without a BOM is not detected. It is usually valid UTF-8 (ASCII plus NULs) and is handled as before.
- Custom `EditOperations` without `writeFileBytes`: non-UTF-8 and UTF-16 files are refused with the error above.
- The model learns that a file is not UTF-8 only through these errors. `read` still shows U+FFFD without a hint.

## Testing

- `npm run check`: clean.
- `test/file-encodings.test.ts` (new), `test/tools.test.ts`, `test/edit-tool-legacy-input.test.ts`, `test/edit-tool-no-full-redraw.test.ts`, `test/suite/regressions/8337-utf8-bom-parsing.test.ts` and `test/read-line-range-display.test.ts`: 127 passed.
- New tests, with byte-level `Buffer.equals` on written files:
  - Latin-1 ASCII edit applied byte-exactly (#10349, #5797)
  - non-ASCII edit refused, checking the full message and that the file is unchanged
  - fuzzy match refused
  - changes within 3 bytes after a non-ASCII byte refused: GB18030 `95 32 82 36` with `2 -> 2X`, and Shift-JIS `95 5C abc` with `\abc -> Xabc` and `\abc -> \Xbc`
  - an ASCII change 3 bytes away from non-ASCII bytes applied
  - Latin-1 `X = 1` next to `X\xa0= 1` not counted as a duplicate
  - UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE files with an odd number of bytes refused, file unchanged
  - UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE round trip with a non-BMP character
  - UTF-8 BOM bytes kept
  - custom operations without `writeFileBytes` give the error and nothing is written
  - `read` decodes UTF-16LE/BE without the mark
  - `read` output for UTF-8, a UTF-8 BOM and invalid UTF-8 equals `toString("utf-8")`
  - `TextFileDecoder` across 3-byte chunks, with a dangling odd byte at the end
- On `origin/main`, 10 of the 13 tests in `file-encodings.test.ts` fail. The UTF-8 BOM, `read` UTF-8 and decoder tests pass there, as expected.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): report the shell exit code when bash times out after the shell exited
prs.body:
Fixes #11613.

## Problem

The bash tool waits for stdout/stderr to close, not only for the shell to exit (#5303). A background process that inherited those pipes and keeps writing keeps the tool waiting after the shell exited. When the timeout then hits, the tool reported only `Command timed out after N seconds`.

Example, timeout 3s:

```bash
bash -c 'while true; do echo tick; sleep 0.05; done' & sleep 1; echo boom >&2; exit 1
```

The shell exits with code 1 after ~1s. The tool still times out at the deadline, because the loop is still writing to its output. Both facts are true: the command failed with code 1, and something it started was still running at the timeout. The old message dropped the first, so the model read a failed command as a slow one and retried with a longer timeout, which never helps here.

## Fix

The timeout stays a timeout, since the tool did hit its deadline while background processes were still writing. When the shell had already exited before the deadline, the message now also says so:

```
Command timed out after 3 seconds. The shell exited with code 1 after 1.1 seconds, but background processes it started kept writing output until the timeout.
```

A shell still running at the deadline keeps the plain `Command timed out after N seconds`.

The local backend throws a module-private `ShellTimeoutError` with the message `timeout:<seconds>` as before, so custom `BashOperations` that throw `timeout:N` are unaffected.

## Behavior per platform

- Linux and macOS: the shell runs in its own process group (`detached: true`). At the deadline `kill(-pgid)` still reaches the background processes after the shell exited, the pipes close, and the tool returns at the deadline. Tested on Linux; macOS uses the same mechanism and matches the macOS repros in the issue.
- Windows: still not fully solved. At the deadline `taskkill /T /PID <shell>` fails with `process not found`, because the shell pid is gone. Walking parent pids does not help: Git's `bin\bash.exe` is a launcher for `usr\bin\bash.exe`, and the orphaned loop's parent is that already-exited inner bash, not the pid pi holds. The tool keeps reading until the output pauses for 100ms. Measured with Git Bash: the message is now correct, but the tool returned after 14s instead of 3s; with a loop that never pauses it never returns. This PR only fixes the reporting.

## Same pattern elsewhere

- `packages/durable/src/env/node.ts` (`NodeExecutionEnv.exec`): same code, same false `timeout:N` after the shell exited. Same Windows limitation.
- `packages/coding-agent/src/core/exec.ts` (`pi.exec` for extensions): the timeout sends SIGTERM/SIGKILL to the direct child only, no process group. A descendant that keeps writing keeps the call waiting past the timeout on every platform, and the result has `killed: true` even when the child had already exited with its own code.
- `packages/coding-agent/src/core/package-manager.ts` (capture commands for git/npm): waits for `close` and kills only the direct child on timeout, so a descendant holding the pipes makes the timeout ineffective on every platform, even when the descendant writes nothing.
- `packages/mcp/src/transports/stdio.ts`: on Windows, closing a server that already exited skips taskkill, so children holding its pipes survive. The code documents this as a known limitation.

Possible follow-up for Windows and the cases above: once the deadline passed, stop waiting for the pipes (destroy our ends). On Windows this also ends most writers, which die from a broken pipe (tested with Git Bash).

## Tests

- `test/suite/regressions/11613-bash-timeout-after-shell-exit.test.ts` (Unix only; it would hang on Windows for the reason above): background writer after the shell exits with code 3, and a shell still running at the deadline. The first case fails without the fix.
- Checked manually on Windows 11 with Git Bash through the built bundle: both messages are as above.
- `npm run check`, `test/tools.test.ts`, the #5303 and #5208 regressions, `bash-close-hang-windows`, `powershell-tool`, `shell-kill-process-tree`.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): stream the read tool instead of loading whole files
prs.body:
## Problem

`read` loads the whole file before it applies `offset`/`limit`: `ops.readFile` -> `toString("utf-8")` -> `split("\n")`. A one-line read still holds the whole file three times: as a Buffer, as a string and as an array of lines.

Measured on main with a 200 MB log (2.36M lines):

- `offset: 1, limit: 1` peaks at 638 MB RSS. With `--max-old-space-size=256` it crashes in `Runtime_StringSplit` (OOM).
- Files over about 512 MB fail with `Cannot create a string longer than 0x1fffffe8 characters`. Files over 2 GB fail with `ERR_FS_FILE_TOO_LARGE`.
- Aborting only rejects the promise; the read keeps running in the background.

## Solution

- `ReadOperations` gets a new optional `createReadStream(absolutePath, { signal })`, which returns an `AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>` (a Node `Readable` works). The default local operations open the file once, `fstat` the handle, and stream from it. Like `fs.readFile`, they stop a regular file at its size when opened: text appended during the read is not counted, and a file that keeps growing still finishes. A file that reports size 0 (such as `/proc` files) and other file types (FIFOs, devices) are read until EOF, as `fs.readFile` reads them. No existing member changed.
- The text path decodes the chunks with a streaming UTF-8 `TextDecoder` (non-fatal, `ignoreBOM: true`). That matches `Buffer.toString("utf-8")`, including invalid bytes and a UTF-8 byte order mark kept as U+FEFF.
- It counts every line but stores only the selected lines `truncateHead` can show. Storing stops once the stored lines are past `DEFAULT_MAX_LINES` or `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES`, plus one more line, and the existing `truncateHead` runs on the stored lines. `totalLines`/`totalBytes` are then patched from the counts, as grep and find do on main.
- The extra line is needed because `truncateHead` drops a trailing empty line. Example: 2001 short lines, then an empty line, then more text. If storing stopped at the empty line, the stored text would end in `\n`. `truncateHead` would count 2000 lines and report "not truncated", but the full text is truncated by lines.
- A line over 50KB is never stored whole; only its size is tracked. A first line of 1 GB therefore still gives today's `[Line 1 is ..., exceeds 50.0KB limit ...]` notice.
- Abort: the signal is passed to the stream, and the loop also checks it between chunks. Leaving the loop closes the stream.
- The whole-file path stays unchanged for custom operations without `createReadStream`, and for fractional `offset`/`limit` or negative `limit`. Array slicing defines what those odd ranges select; for example, `limit: -1` selects all lines but the last.
- Images are unchanged.

Output is the same as main's, byte for byte, including line counts, notices, details (including key order) and errors. A file appended to during the read gives the same output too: both read a regular file up to its size when opened. Out of scope: the trailing-newline off-by-one in line counts from #7329 is kept as is.

## Testing

- `test/read-streaming.test.ts` keeps a copy of the old text algorithm as the reference. It compares the streaming path against it on text, details and error messages, with chunks of 1 and 4096 bytes and offsets and limits around the boundaries. The cases are: empty file, trailing newline or not, CRLF, multi-byte characters and a UTF-8 BOM, 2001 lines, and a first line over 50KB. There are also edge cases where the line or byte cap falls exactly on an empty line, and the 50KB + trailing newline case that `truncateHead` reports as `truncatedBy: "lines"`. Further tests:
  - details key order
  - multi-byte characters split across chunks, and invalid UTF-8
  - the `readFile` fallback, including fractional and negative ranges
  - local files through the default stream, including EISDIR
  - abort: the stream is closed and no more chunks are pulled
  - a local file appended to mid-read (a decode hook in the test appends after the first chunk): `limit: 1` still says `[1 more lines ...]`. This test fails with an unbounded `fs.createReadStream`.
  - bounded memory: a child process with `--max-old-space-size=64` reads a 200 MB single line, generated in memory as 64 KB chunks from a custom `createReadStream`, and must print the size notice. It takes about 0.8 s and uses 17 MB of heap. If over-long lines are stored whole, it runs out of memory. 64 KB chunks matter here: V8 keeps decoded strings of 1 MB outside the heap limit, so with 1 MB chunks the test would not catch that regression.
- With main's `read.ts`, 5 of the 8 tests fail: matrix, key order, chunked decoding, bounded memory and abort. The fallback, local-file and append tests pass on main because they check behavior that did not change. Removing the one-line-past-the-cap rule, or the trailing-empty-line adjustment of `totalLines`, makes the matrix fail.
- `test/tools.test.ts`, `read-line-range-display`, `tool-execution-component`, `block-images` and `image-resize-callers` pass. `npm run check` is clean.

Measured with an ad-hoc script on a 200 MB log. Baseline RSS after loading modules is about 121 MB.

| Case | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| offset 1, limit 1 | 1028 ms, 638 MB peak RSS | 478 ms, 131 MB |
| offset 2000000, limit 10 | 926 ms, 637 MB | 486 ms, 132 MB |
| no offset/limit (counts all lines) | 1561 ms, 1010 MB | 524 ms, 132 MB |
| offset 1, limit 1, 256 MB heap | OOM crash | 131 MB |
| 1.1 GB single-line file | string length error | 2.2 s, 130 MB, line-size notice |

Remaining difference: custom operations that only implement `readFile` keep the whole-file memory use, and their reads continue after an abort, as before.

prs.body:
Opening the selector starts a background catalog refresh. When it finished, the selection jumped back to the current model, or to the top row with a search query, discarding any browsing done in the meantime.

Pass the selected model into filterModels() so the refresh keeps it selected by provider and ID. If it is gone, the existing fallback applies. The index is chosen once and the list is rebuilt once.

Based on #11758.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): do not split surrogate pairs when truncating text
prs.body:
Several places truncate text by UTF-16 code units with `slice()`. When the cut lands between the two halves of a surrogate pair (an emoji or other character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane), the result keeps a lone high or low surrogate. That is invalid UTF-16.

Example: a grep match line with 499 ASCII characters followed by `😀` is cut at 500 units, so the output ends in `\uD83D... [truncated]`.

The bundled providers strip lone surrogates before sending (`sanitizeSurrogates` in pi-ai), so the usual effect is a dropped character. But the broken text still reaches the session file, RPC and JSON clients (strict UTF-8 encoders such as Rust's serde_json reject lone surrogates), extensions, and custom providers.

This adds `sliceHead(text, n)` and `sliceTail(text, n)` to `core/tools/truncate.ts`. They behave like `slice(0, n)` and `slice(-n)` but return one unit fewer when the cut would split a pair, and are used where truncated text reaches the model:
- `truncateLine` (grep match lines), the case reported in #7121
- codemode `truncateOutput` head and tail, and its argument and error previews
- compaction `truncateForSummary` (tool results sent to the summarizer)
- MCP server summaries in the system prompt and stderr tails in connection errors

The cost is two `charCodeAt` checks per truncation, and nothing on the untruncated path.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): fork-free executable lookup in findExecutableOnPath and commandExists
prs.body:
## Problem

`findExecutableOnPath()` (src/utils/shell.ts) spawns `which` on POSIX, and `commandExists()` (src/utils/tools-manager.ts) spawns `<cmd> --version` on every call. On hosts where these run on the main thread of a multi-threaded process, a `fork()` can deadlock the entire process on Android/Termux: the forked child stays stuck between fork and exec on an inherited lock, while libuv's `uv_spawn` blocks its caller reading the child's error pipe.

Concrete trace (pi-web-ui server, agent running in-process, Android 17/Pixel 10 Pro, Node 26.3.1): every grep/glob tool call goes through `ensureTool("rg"/"fd")` -> `commandExists("rg")` -> `spawnSync("rg", ["--version"])` on the server's main thread. During active websocket/snapshot traffic this fork intermittently deadlocked the server: process alive, event loop dead, port no longer accepting connections. Reproduced 8 times over two days; after removing the forks, 3+ days clean (pi-web-ui issue #78, fix PR #88 covers the pi-web-ui side; this PR covers the SDK hot paths).

## Solution

Both helpers scan `PATH` with `existsSync` on POSIX instead of spawning:

- `findExecutableOnPath()`: POSIX branch is a plain PATH scan. The win32 `where` branch is unchanged.
- `commandExists()`: PATH scan on POSIX; the win32 `--version` probe is unchanged. `cmd` containing a path separator short-circuits to `existsSync`.

This also removes a per-tool-call fork: `commandExists` runs via `ensureTool("rg"/"fd")` on every grep/glob invocation.

## Verification

- `npm run check:pinned-deps`, `check:runtime-deps`, `check:ts-imports`, `check:entry-graphs`, `check:shrinkwrap`, `check:install-lock:coding-agent` pass.
- `biome check` and `tsgo --noEmit` could not run on-device (no aarch64-android builds for the Biome CLI / tsgo); formatting follows the existing style, CI will confirm.
- `tools-manager.test.ts`: 7/8 on-device; the one failure (`surfaces the error cause chain when a download fails`) is host-dependent and fails identically on unpatched `main` — on Android, `os.platform()` is `android`, so `ensureTool` takes the `pkg install` branch instead of the download path the test asserts. Passes on Linux CI.

Prepared with the pi coding agent on-device; I reviewed and understand the changes.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): align manifest resource discovery
prs.body:
## Summary

Extension package manifests were resolved by two implementations that disagreed. Auto-discovered extension folders and `discoverAndLoadExtensions` treated `pi.extensions` globs as literal paths, so `["./extensions/*.ts", "!./extensions/*.test.ts"]` matched nothing and pi fell back to loading every file, including the excluded ones (#9788).

- Extension discovery lives in one module, `core/extensions/discovery.ts`, shared by the package manager and the extension loader.
- Manifest path handling lives in `core/pi-manifest.ts` for all resource types: `./` anchoring, package-relative `~/`, glob detection through minimatch (brackets, braces, extglobs), and backslash separators.
- A directory listed in `pi.extensions` resolves its own `pi.extensions`, then `package.json` `main`, then `index.ts`/`index.js`, before scanning its files. A `"."` entry loads the package's index instead of every file.
- A broken extension package no longer stops pi from launching. An invalid or unreadable `package.json`, an unreadable extension directory, or `pi.extensions` entries that lead back to the package skip that package and are reported with the extension errors. Before, a configured package with an invalid `package.json` crashed startup with a bare `SyntaxError` (from the #9863 host-dependency check), and the other cases were ignored silently.

## Behavior changes for package authors

- `package.json` `main` now takes precedence over `index.ts` for directory entries and auto-discovered subdirectories.
- A manifest whose patterns match nothing no longer falls back to `index.ts`.
- `PackageManager.resolve()` results gain an optional `resolutionErrors` field listing skipped packages.

## Tests

- Manifest pattern cases run through both auto-discovery and package-source resolution in one table.
- Regressions for invalid, unreadable and cyclic packages at the package manager, extension loader and resource loader boundaries.
- `npm run check` passes. Package manager, extension discovery and resource loader tests: 250 passed.

Fixes #9788

prs.title: fix(ai): allow prompt cache keys for compatible proxies
prs.body:
Chat Completions only sends `prompt_cache_key` to direct OpenAI URLs or when long retention is requested and supported. A compatible proxy therefore cannot receive pi's session key with default short retention, even if it accepts that field.

Add `compat.supportsPromptCacheKey` to opt in independently of long retention:

```json
"compat": {
  "supportsPromptCacheKey": true,
  "supportsLongCacheRetention": false
}
```

`false` explicitly suppresses the key; unset preserves existing behavior. `cacheRetention: "none"` still omits it. This does not change retention duration or session-affinity headers.

In a live test through [llm_proxy](https://github.com/elixir-vibe/llm_proxy) with a Codex backend, a follow-up without the key returned 0/1,931 cached input tokens; a separate pair with a stable key returned 1,792/1,931.

Related to #6654, but addresses the URL/retention gate that PR explicitly leaves unchanged, rather than adding a key-value override.

Validation: `npm run check`, `npm run build:offline`, and `./test.sh` pass. Added coverage for proxy opt-in, unchanged defaults, disabled caching, independent retention, missing session IDs, Unicode key clamping, and models.json provider/model overrides. A filesystem-watcher test timed out on the first full run, then passed individually and in the full rerun.

prs.title: fix(tui): prevent cursor marker leaks
prs.body:
## Summary

Fix cursor-marker leakage across the full-screen selection and terminal rendering paths.

- Treat APC cursor markers as positional metadata instead of persistent styling, so `sliceWithWidth()` does not replay them into later selection slices.
- Preserve the bottommost valid visible marker as the hardware-cursor position and remove duplicate markers from that cursor line.
- Enforce the output-boundary invariant by stripping all remaining cursor markers from every non-image rendered line, including other visible lines and scrollback lines written during a main-screen full render.

This combines the duplicate-marker cleanup reported in #9257 with the upstream selection-slicing cause identified in #9332. The `sliceWithWidth()` root cause and Ghostty behavior were identified by @Andy8647 in #9332. The duplicate-marker cleanup direction was also independently proposed by @bluefateludi in #9257.

Closes #9257
Closes #9332

## Test Plan

- Confirmed the `sliceWithWidth()` regression test fails before the fix because later slices contain `CURSOR_MARKER`.
- Confirmed APC cursor markers are not carried into later slices while persistent SGR styling still is.
- Confirmed the regular-screen duplicate-marker test preserves the first marker's cursor column and emits no marker bytes.
- Confirmed a 2-row main-screen render with markers above the viewport and on multiple visible lines preserves the content, uses the bottom visible marker for cursor positioning, and emits no marker bytes.
- Confirmed the full-screen regression starts with one caret marker, performs a real mouse drag after the caret, renders the selection highlight, and emits no marker bytes.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): make subagent progress and failures reliable
prs.body:
The shipped subagent example could say a child was done while it was still working, lose the useful part of process failures, and return a normal-looking tool result when the delegated work had actually failed. Single and chain output could also exceed the normal tool limit.

This also adds a dedicated regression suite covering progress state, cancellation, process failures, output limits, cwd-based agent selection, and persisted tool-result error state.

After this change:

- queued, running, completed, failed, and aborted work stay distinct throughout the run;
- interrupting the parent run preserves partial child results, stops queued work from starting, and escalates when a child ignores SIGTERM;
- signal exits, spawn failures, provider errors, stderr, and assistant output remain visible instead of collapsing to `(no output)`;
- failed subagents become failed tool results, so the parent model can react instead of treating them as successful calls;
- single and chain results stay within the normal 50 KB / 2,000-line limit;
- project agents are selected and confirmed from each task's actual working directory rather than the dispatcher's directory.

## Further potential improvements

These are useful follow-ups, but they are separate product and storage decisions rather than part of the failure-handling fixes in this PR.

<details>
<summary>Potential follow-ups</summary>

### Keep persisted transcripts bounded

Subagent tool results persist the full child message history in `details`, which can make parent session files large and slow to reload. A follow-up could compact that history or spill it to disk.

### Define an aggregate parallel-output budget

Parallel mode still gives every task its own 50 KB budget. A follow-up could keep every task represented while enforcing one overall tool-result limit.

### Report child usage to the calling session

Per-child token and cost usage is visible in result cards but is not added to the calling session's totals.

### Isolate malformed agent definitions

One malformed YAML agent can still break discovery for every valid agent in the same directory.

### Limit subagent recursion

A nesting limit would prevent accidental process and paid-request multiplication when subagents can invoke the subagent tool again.

* https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8195

### Add a configurable timeout

Unattended runs would benefit from a generous opt-in timeout for children that never complete.

</details>

## Related issues

### Spawn failures lose their diagnostics

This directly addresses the reported case where a nonexistent child working directory produces `(no output)` instead of the actual spawn error. The regression suite includes that same reproduction.

* https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/8129

### Persisted child history can bloat sessions

This PR intentionally keeps full child history in tool-result details, so session compaction or spill-to-disk remains follow-up work rather than something fixed here.

* https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7452

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): keep extension console output off the interactive TUI
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #10002.

Extensions run in-process, so `console.error()` / `console.warn()` / `console.log()` — and any direct `process.stdout` / `process.stderr` write — from extension code goes straight to the tty while the differential renderer owns it. The write lands raw between rendered frames and garbles the display. On 0.87.1, with the issue's minimal extension, the sentinel lands immediately after the renderer's cursor writes:

```
… \x1b[?2026l\x1b[3A\x1b[1G\x1b[?25l\x1b[1G\x1b[?25lEXTENSION_DIAGNOSTIC_SENTINEL\r\n
```

This change makes the terminal enforce its ownership of the terminal while it is started:

1. **`ProcessTerminal`** — while `start()`ed, writes to `process.stdout` / `process.stderr` that do not come from its own rendering are routed to a new `onCapturedOutput` sink instead of the terminal. Renderer writes are marked via `writeRaw()` and pass through untouched. `stop()` restores the stream writes, so suspend, external editor, uncaught-crash, and quit paths all return to plain output. Without a sink nothing is intercepted (unchanged behavior).
2. **`InteractiveMode`** — captured text is appended verbatim to `pi-captured-output.log` and shown as a chat entry (latest write, capture count, log path), keeping diagnostics available through the supported notification/log path. Consecutive captured writes coalesce into the previous entry, matching `showStatus` behavior.

With the fix the same repro renders the diagnostic inside a synchronized frame:

```
… \x1b[?25l\x1b[1G\x1b[?25l\x1b[?2026h\x1b[1A\r\x1b[2K \x1b[38;2;255;255;0mEXTENSION_DIAGNOSTIC_SENTINEL\x1b[39m … \x1b[2K \x1b[38;2;128;128;128mCaptured output ×1 · full log: …/pi-captured-output.log\x1b[39m
```

### Non-goals (explicit)

- Child processes spawned with inherited stdio write at the fd level and cannot be intercepted from JS; unchanged.
- Non-interactive modes (print, rpc) are unaffected; rpc's existing stdout takeover stands.

## Test plan

- [x] `packages/tui`: `node --test test/terminal-output-capture.test.ts` — 4 pass (issue repro via `console.error`, renderer pass-through, stream restore on stop, no sink = unchanged)
- [x] `packages/coding-agent`: `vitest --run test/suite/regressions/10002-captured-terminal-output.test.ts` — 4 pass (capture through `createInteractiveTui`, log + chat surfacing, coalescing, empty-write handling)
- [x] `npm run check`
- [x] `./test.sh`
- [ ] CI on this PR

## Notes

AI-assisted content (per CONTRIBUTING.md): code and this description drafted by an agent and posted from the agent account at the operator's request; the before/after repro traces above are captured from real PTY runs of the issue's minimal extension.

An RPC/SDK prompt can finish while tree navigation is awaiting a hook or summary, then disappear from active context when navigation completes. The inverse order also fails when navigation starts during async prompt preparation.

Extension commands and `agent_settled` navigation remain supported. Automatic compaction and public `isStreaming` behavior are unchanged; reload/preflight serialization is outside this PR. Related: #7751 addresses broader compaction/rewrite coordination.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): report settings save failures in interactive mode
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #10168.

`SettingsManager.enqueueWrite` catches write failures and only queues them for `drainErrors()`. Interactive mode drains that queue once at startup (`main.ts` -> `collectSettingsDiagnostics`), so a runtime save failure — read-only `settings.json` (`EROFS`/`EACCES`), e.g. a store-symlinked config — is never reported: the toggle shows success (`Thinking blocks: visible`), the change is lost on restart, and the only trace is the next startup's diagnostic.

This implements the hook proposed in the issue:

1. **`SettingsManager.onWriteError(listener)`** — save failures are delivered to registered listeners as they happen. While any listener is registered the failure is not queued for `drainErrors()`, so it is reported exactly once; with no listener, behavior is unchanged.
2. **Interactive mode** subscribes in `rebindCurrentSession` and shows each failure through the existing error entry: `Failed to save global settings to <path>: <message>. The change applies to this session only.`

### Non-goals (explicit)

- No new error surface; reuses `showError`.
- Startup diagnostics path (`collectSettingsDiagnostics` / `drainErrors`) unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] `packages/coding-agent`: `vitest --run test/settings-manager.test.ts` — 52 pass, including the new regression test (listener delivery instead of queueing; queueing resumes after unsubscribe)
- [x] `npm run check`
- [x] `./test.sh` — all pass except 2 pre-existing failures in `packages/ai/test/models-entry.test.ts` (`packages/ai/dist` build artifacts absent on a fresh checkout; reproduced on pristine main without this change)
- [ ] CI on this PR

## Notes

@ggbdpq volunteered on the issue; this implements the design already proposed there.

AI-assisted content (per CONTRIBUTING.md): code and this description drafted by an agent and posted from the agent account at the operator's request. `npm run check` and `./test.sh` ran in a fresh checkout after `npm run hydrate:model-data`.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): realpath extension entries before jiti import (closes #8092)
prs.body:
Closes #8092.

Extension entries are realpath'd before being handed to jiti. pnpm's isolated layout symlinks `node_modules/<pkg>` into `.pnpm/<pkg>@<ver>/node_modules/<pkg>`, and jiti's resolver (unlike Node's native loader) doesn't realpath the entry before resolving its imports — so upward traversal from the symlink path misses declared dependencies that only exist as store siblings, and loading fails with `Cannot find module '<dep>'`. Realpath'ing the entry once at the load boundary makes resolution start inside the store, where pnpm links all declared deps.

Verified: the regression test builds a fake pnpm isolated layout (symlinked entry + store-only sibling dep) and fails without the change (`Cannot find module '@test/dep'`), passes with it. `npm run check` is clean.

Note: this PR text was drafted with an AI assistant and reviewed/approved by me before filing. The analysis and the linked change are mine and I stand behind them.

prs.title: feat(ai): add promptCacheKey stream option to override the prompt cache key
prs.body:
Closes #6627

## Summary

Adds an opt-in `promptCacheKey?: string` to `StreamOptions`. When set, it replaces `sessionId` as the input to `clampOpenAIPromptCacheKey()` in the four providers that send `prompt_cache_key`:

- openai-responses
- openai-completions
- openai-codex-responses (covers both the SSE and websocket transports, they build the same request body)
- azure-openai-responses

When unset, it falls back to `sessionId` and behavior is unchanged.

Not changed

- retention `none` still omits the key on the responses path
- the completions baseUrl/retention gating is unchanged, the override only replaces the value
- the 64-char clamp still applies to the overridden value
- session-affinity headers stay tied to `sessionId`

The option is also forwarded where the other cache-related stream options already flow in `packages/agent`: the `Agent` config, the `streamProxy` serialized options, and `AgentHarnessStreamOptions` (so it's patchable per request via `before_provider_request`).

## Why

Without this there's no way to share the prompt cache between sessions that have a large identical prompt prefix, because the key is hardcoded to the per-session `sessionId` and identical prefixes end up routed to different cache shards. More details in #6627.

## Validation

- New assertions in the existing request-body test files: the override wins over `sessionId` and is clamped to 64 chars, retention `none` still omits it with the override set, and the codex and azure paths include it in the request body
- `npm run check` and `./test.sh` pass

prs.title: fix(plan-mode): make progress tracking robust and tolerant
prs.body:
## What

Hardens the plan-mode example extension's step-progress tracking. Previously, completion markers were only recognized in the exact `[DONE:n]` form inside visible text blocks, so steps frequently never got checked off during execution.

## Changes

- **`getTextContent`** now reads `thinking` blocks as well as text blocks, so `[DONE:n]` tags emitted during reasoning are honored.
- **Marker tolerance** (`extractDoneSteps`): accepts `[DONE: 1]`, `[DONE 1]`, `Done: n`, and prose phrasings like "Step n done / is complete / finished" — all adjacency-anchored so negations ("Step 9 is not done") never match.
- **Whole-plan fallback** (`allStepsComplete`): if the run's final message says the plan is done (e.g. "All steps complete"), all remaining steps are marked at `agent_end`.
- **Plan extraction dedup**: only the last `Plan:` section is extracted, so a plan drafted in a thinking block no longer duplicates the steps from the text block.
- **No more truncation**: step text is kept in full (previously cut at 50 chars); the widget truncates for display only. The execution prompt now shows the complete step text.
- **No more dropped steps**: steps whose text starts with a backtick (e.g. `1. \`index.ts\` — …`) are no longer skipped.
- **Widget refresh** happens on every turn instead of only when a marker matched.
- **Plan-complete card** is delivered with `nextTurn` instead of triggering an extra LLM turn.

## Tests

`packages/coding-agent/test/plan-mode-utils.test.ts` updated for the new behavior (truncation, backtick steps, marker-count semantics) and extended with coverage for the new cases (marker variants, prose phrasings, negation safety, thinking-draft dedup, markdown titles, whole-plan completion).

All 43 tests in `plan-mode-utils.test.ts` + `plan-mode-extension.test.ts` pass (`npx vitest run`).

Note: the repo-wide type-check currently fails on `main` with pre-existing `ModelCatalog`/`never` errors unrelated to this change; this branch adds none (same count with and without the diff).
