prs.body:
Adds native `longcat` provider support for LongCat-2.5 in pi-ai. Users can select it from the built-in provider directory and authenticate with `LONGCAT_API_KEY`, including in consumers such as DeepSeek Harness.

Reuses the OpenAI completions transport with binary thinking, text/image input, and tool-call reasoning replay. A narrowly scoped compatibility option sends an empty string for tool-only assistant content; other providers keep their current behavior. Catalog metadata follows the current official LongCat documentation because models.dev still lists older model IDs.

Supersedes #11776 using `feat/longcat-2.5-provider`, with upstream `main` merged through `b317575fd`. Related contribution proposal: #9308. This targets LongCat-2.5 and the current catalog layout, replacing the earlier LongCat-2.0 implementation. Maintainer contributor approval is still pending; this PR is a draft for review.

Validation:
- `npm run check` passes; focused provider/compatibility tests: 68 passed.
- After upstream synchronization, `npm run check` passed again and the newly merged terminal regression suite passed all 83 tests. Installed-package smoke tests below preceded the final upstream-only terminal/Azure/Windows/llama merges.
- `npm run build` passed. The pi-ai section of the isolated offline suite passed: 1,786 tests passed, 888 skipped.
- Packed and installed the changed packages locally. Real user flows passed in pi 1.5.0 interactive CLI and DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 UI: native model selection, thinking off/on, CSV read/write tools, image understanding, and follow-up recall using the real LongCat API.
- Rechecked on 2026-11-04 with a separate real validation API key: LongCat-2.5 model lookup returned HTTP 200, and the installed pi package read a CSV and wrote the correct total (`70`) using tools.
- The full monorepo offline suite is not green on this macOS environment: Chord reports Linux `/proc/self/fd` and path assumptions, coding-agent find tests lack `fd`, and pi-env requires its native daemon build. These failures are not represented as passing checks.

Official sources: [model parameters](https://longcat.chat/platform/docs/zh/api/model-params), [vision](https://longcat.chat/platform/docs/zh/image-video-understanding), [current promotional USD pricing](https://longcat.chat/platform/docs/zh/pricing/longcat-2.5).

prs.title: Send the session name as the OSC 7501 title
prs.body:
Pi sent the session name in OSC 7501 reports only as `msg`, and only in the `working` and `done` states. In the other states `msg` holds something else: the dialog title, the error line, "Compacting context", or nothing when idle. Dashboards that want a stable label for each session had no field they could rely on.

This change:
- `pi-tui`: adds `title` to `ProgramStatus`. `formatProgramStatus` encodes it like `msg`: control characters become spaces, the text is trimmed, cut at a UTF-8 boundary to the spec's 192-byte decoded limit (256 bytes encoded), and base64-encoded. It is emitted before `msg`.
- `coding-agent`: `ProgramStatusReporter` now sets `title` to the session name on every report. When the session has no name, `title` is left out. Nothing else changes: `msg` and the state mapping are the same as before.
- `docs/terminal-setup.md`: one sentence documenting the title.

The limits match Ghostty's parser (`max_title_bytes = 192`, `max_title_encoded_bytes = 256` in `src/terminal/osc/parsers/program_status.zig`).

Testing:
- New tests in `packages/tui/test/program-status.test.ts` cover title encoding, control-character replacement, and truncation. New tests in `packages/coding-agent/test/program-status-reporter.test.ts` check that the title is present in the idle, working/compacting, blocked, and error states. Both files fail without the source change and pass with it.
- `npm run check` and the `pi-tui` test suite pass.
- Ran `PI_PROGRAM_STATUS=1 pi --name "Fix login"` under `script`. The startup report is now `ESC]7501;state=idle:app=pi:title=Rml4IGxvZ2lu`; before this change it had no title.

Fixes #11670

Requested by @badlogic

prs.title: Fix the edit preview flicker on remote edits
prs.body:
pi got a flicker!

When the edit tool uses injected remote operations, the tool row briefly turns red with a local "Could not edit file" error before the remote operation replaces it with the correct diff.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b8c1dbf-3b9f-4243-944f-36717922b8d3

Preview and execution used different backends. Execution honored the operations injected into the edit tool, but the pre-execution preview always read the local filesystem. The renderer therefore reported a missing local file even though the target existed remotely. If the same path existed locally, it could instead show a diff for an unrelated file.

This change passes the edit definition's operations to its preview renderer, so preview and execution read from the same filesystem. Definitions without custom operations still use the local filesystem. The edit arguments, result shape, and factory signatures do not change.

A renderer without a bound backend now skips the speculative read and displays the result diff instead of assuming the file is local. This covers renderer inheritance, display-only clients, and tools built with `createEditTool()`, which intentionally omits renderer metadata. An extension whose reads must wait for authorization or execution-time setup can opt out by clearing `renderCall` while retaining the rest of the definition.

Extensions may replace `renderCall` and `renderResult` independently. The call renderer therefore marks the row settled when a final result is present instead of relying on the built-in result renderer. A late preview cannot overwrite a settled row. Preview work remains speculative: execution does not wait for it, mutation ordering is unchanged, and cancellation is unaffected.

The SSH and Gondolin examples now use the same backend and working directory for preview and execution. This preserves relative-path resolution when the session cwd differs from the mapping root. The extension docs state that `readFile` may run before `access`, `execute`, and `tool_call` hooks, may run concurrently with execution, and receives no abort signal.

prs.title: fix(ai): inline $ref tool schemas for NVIDIA NIM models
prs.body:
Fixes #10270.

`nemotron-3.5-super-vl-preview` and `qwen3.8-flash-next` return an object described only by a local `$ref` as a JSON string. `validateToolArguments` rejects that:

```
schema:  "settings": { "$ref": "#/$defs/Settings" }
model:   "settings": "{\"notifications\":false}"
```

With the definition inlined, both work. Kimi K2.6 on the same route works either way. Thanks @itayzit for the report, the reproduction, and the [first patch](https://github.com/itayzit/pi/tree/schema-ref-compat).

### Changes

- New `OpenAICompletionsCompat.inlineSchemaRefs`, wired like `supportsStrictMode`:
  - `detectCompat()` and `NVIDIA_OPENAI_COMPAT` default it to true for NVIDIA NIM; it is false everywhere else.
  - `models.json` can enable it for other endpoints, for example Qwen on vLLM.
  - When it is on, `convertTools` sends the inlined schema.
- Other providers are unchanged.
- New `packages/ai/src/utils/json-schema-refs.ts` does the inlining:
  - Expands local `#` and `#/...` references only.
  - Leaves recursive, external, and unresolved refs in place, along with refs that have non-annotation siblings, and keeps the root `$defs` they point into.
  - Sends the schema unchanged if a nested `$id` or anchor is present, or if inlining would add more than 1,000 nodes.
  - Never mutates the input, and caches the result per schema object.
- Argument coercion and optional-null cleanup in `validateToolArguments` now run against the inlined schema. Before, `{"notifications": "false"}` was coerced to `false` in an inline schema but rejected behind a `$ref`. `Check` still runs against the original schema. This applies to all providers and changes nothing that is sent.

Not included:

- Repairing stringified objects during validation, which was declined in #3336.
- Keeping `$defs` in Anthropic non-strict schemas, which is #9557.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance.

prs.title: fix(ai): coerce JSON-encoded object and array tool arguments
prs.body:
## Summary

`validateToolArguments` recovers a tool argument the model delivered as a JSON-encoded string, for `object` and `array` parameters.

`arguments` already travels as a JSON string, so a model that mixes up the two encoding levels quotes a nested value one time too many: the outer parse succeeds and the inner value stays a string. `coercePrimitiveByType` already recovers that for every scalar type, but not for structures, so a tool whose parameter is an object or an array cannot be called at all by such a model — validation fails before the tool runs, once per `oneOf` branch:

```
Validation failed for tool "configure":
  - target: must be object
  - target: must be object
  - target: must match exactly one schema in oneOf

Received arguments:
{
  "action": "inspect",
  "target": "{\"kind\": \"agent\", \"name\": \"researcher\"}"
}
```

Reproduced on openrouter with `qwen/qwen3.8-flash`, 3/3 on two different object parameters. The scalars beside it arrive natively.

`parseStructuredString` sits next to the structural coercion rather than in `coercePrimitiveByType` — it reshapes a value instead of converting a primitive — and runs before the per-property descent so the parsed structure still gets the existing item/property coercion. It takes a string only when the schema asks for `object` or `array`, the string parses, and the result matches a type the schema accepts; otherwise the value is returned untouched and the original type error is still reported. A schema that also accepts `string` is left alone, so a caller's literal JSON-looking text is never rewritten. For example, with `type: ["string", "object"]` a JSON-encoded object stays a string, because it already matches the `string` arm; this is deliberate, so a model that sends serialized objects there keeps the string.

JSON-encoded strings on plain `properties`/`items` are decoded while optional nulls are normalized, before `Value.Convert`. The decoded structure gets the same optional-null handling as a native one, and a native TypeBox `Type.Array` does not wrap the encoded string into a one-element array. Strings decoded later inside `anyOf`/`oneOf` branches are normalized against the branch schema before descending. A union without a direct `type`, such as a native `Type.Union([Type.Array(...), Type.Null()])`, is decoded through the member that accepts the parsed structure, unless a member already accepts the string.

Refs #5697, #8757.

## Testing

- `npx vitest --run test/validation.test.ts` in `packages/ai` — 16 passed; the coercion, TypeBox array/object, native nullable-array union, and native-vs-encoded optional-null tests fail without the change
- `npm run check` — passes, rebased on current `main`
- `npx vitest --run` in `packages/ai` — same pass/fail set as `main`, plus the 6 new tests
- `npx biome check` on both changed files
- `npx tsgo --noEmit` — no new errors

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): restore continuation after retry and compaction
prs.body:
I ran into an edge case with the recovery flow introduced in [`32850ef7`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/commit/32850ef7c5edff7a6eee0214516fbb7382bf292d).

Basically, if Pi hits a temporary error and the retry also gets cut short, it compacts the conversation but accidentally leaves the first error as the last message. When it tries to continue, it fails with:

>   Cannot continue from message role: assistant

I included a regression test that walks through the whole sequence, which should make the problem easier to see, but I'm happy to provide more details if anything is unclear.

I wasn't sure whether I needed to open an issue first since I'm already approved to send PRs, so I went ahead and sent the fix directly. If you'd prefer an issue too, please let me know.

(I used my clanker for the rest of this, but I vetted/edited myself)

 To reproduce, you need to:

 1. Enable automatic retry and compaction.
 2. Start a turn with enough history for compaction.
 3. Have the first attempt return a retryable error, such as server_error.
 4. Have the retry end with a recoverable length response.

 Pi then compacts the conversation and fails when it tries to continue the interrupted turn.

 This PR:

 - removes all failed attempts restored at the end of the active conversation before Pi continues
 - keeps those attempts in the saved session history
 - adds a faux-provider regression test covering the full error, retry, truncation, compaction, and resume sequence

prs.title: feat(coding-agent): dispatch hooks on every turn-start path (cancellable turn preflight)
prs.body:
## The bug

`sendCustomMessage(triggerTurn: true)` starts a turn without dispatching the `input` hook or `before_agent_start`.

`packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts`, current `main`:

```ts
async sendCustomMessage<T = unknown>(message, options?): Promise<void> {
  const appMessage = { role: "custom", ... };
  if (options?.deliverAs === "nextTurn") { ... }
  else if (this.isStreaming && options?.triggerTurn !== false) { ... }
  else if (options?.triggerTurn) {
    await this._runAgentPrompt(appMessage);   // <-- idle + triggerTurn
  }
  else { ... }
}
```

Every other turn-start path dispatches the hooks — a human-typed turn does, and a streaming turn queued via `steer`/`followUp` does. **Only the idle + `triggerTurn: true` branch calls `_runAgentPrompt` directly and skips them.**

## Why it matters

`sendCustomMessage(triggerTurn: true)` is how an extension starts a turn the human did not type: an incoming message from another process, an RPC-injected prompt, a scheduled or event-driven turn. Those are exactly the turns where an extension most needs the `input` hook, because that is where per-turn context gets applied.

The failure is silent and shaped badly:

- nothing throws, nothing logs, no capability reports missing;
- the turn runs and produces a perfectly reasonable answer;
- it just runs **without** whatever the `input` hook would have contributed.

So an extension that relies on `input` for correctness gets a turn that looks fine and is missing its context, with no signal at either end. **The defect is that two turn-start paths dispatch hooks differently and one does so silently** — not any specific thing a consumer wanted to inject.

`before_agent_start` matters in the other direction for the same reason: it is the documented place to *cancel* a turn, and a turn that cannot be cancelled by policy is a turn that runs whatever arrives.

## The change

A shared preflight that both turn-start paths run, so hooks fire uniformly and a hook can refuse the turn.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `_applyAgentStartPreflight()` | one hook-dispatch path, used by both branches |
| `ExtensionCapabilities.turnPreflight` | lets an extension detect the capability instead of assuming it |
| `TurnPreflightCancellationEntryData` | a persisted entry, so a cancellation is auditable rather than a silent no-op |
| `turnPreflight.cancelled` → `preflightResult?.(true)` | cancellation is reported, not swallowed |

Cancellation carries provenance (which extension refused, and why), and delivery is recorded separately from execution so "the message arrived" and "the turn ran" stay distinguishable.

```text
10 files changed, 595 insertions(+), 47 deletions(-)

src/core/agent-session.ts                     134   the fix
src/core/extensions/types.ts                   39   capability + entry type
src/core/extensions/runner.ts                  21
src/core/extensions/{loader,index}.ts          11
src/index.ts                                    4
docs/extensions.md                             29   documented
CHANGELOG.md                                    1
test/suite/agent-session-preflight.test.ts    303   tested
test/extensions-runner.test.ts                100   tested
```

**403 of the 595 insertions are tests and docs.** No public API change except by addition.

## Verification

Ran `vitest --run` for `packages/coding-agent` on this branch and on `upstream/main` as a control:

```text
upstream/main (control):  18 failed | 1905 passed | 49 skipped
this branch:              18 failed | 1913 passed | 49 skipped
```

The set of failing test names is **identical** between the two — those 18 are pre-existing on `main` and unrelated to this change. The branch adds 8 passing tests and no new failures. The patch's own two files pass 46/46 in isolation.

Note for anyone reproducing: `packages/ai` needs `npm run generate-models` before the suite can load, otherwise every file fails to import on a missing `./data/amazon-bedrock.json`.

This has run in production continuously since 2026-07-24 in a downstream fork across four agent processes, with a consumer-side conformance gate asserting the capability is present. The branch here is `upstream/main` + exactly one commit; no fork-specific changes are included.

prs.title: fix(ai): map models.dev cost tiers for every provider
prs.body:
Fixes #7912.

## Problem

`getModelsDevCost` (generate-models.ts) already maps models.dev's `cost.tiers[].tier{type,size}` onto `cost.tiers[].inputTokensAbove`. It had exactly one call site: the github-copilot block. Every other provider built cost inline from the four scalar rates:

```ts
cost: {
  input: m.cost?.input || 0,
  output: m.cost?.output || 0,
  cacheRead: m.cost?.cache_read || 0,
  cacheWrite: m.cost?.cache_write || 0,
},
```

`m` is the models.dev model, tiers included; they were simply never copied. Anything over a provider's threshold was then priced at the short-context rate.

Concretely, models.dev has carried xAI's grok-4.5 long-context tier since 2026-07-31:

```json
"tiers": [{"input": 4, "output": 12, "cache_read": 0.6, "tier": {"type": "context", "size": 200000}}]
```

0.84.1 ships `{"input": 2, "output": 6, "cacheRead": 0.3, "cacheWrite": 0}` with no tiers. Measured over 10,119 grok-4.5 requests through our gateway, 244 (2.4%) exceeded 200k prompt tokens; catalog rates priced them at $270.83 against $302.35 on xAI's published card, 10.4% under.

`gpt-5.6-luna` looked correct only because `withOpenAiLongContextPricing` synthesizes its tier from a hardcoded allowlist, so the generic path was serving one provider out of roughly twenty-three.

## Change

Route the remaining models.dev-sourced providers through `getModelsDevCost`. For providers without tiers in models.dev the output is identical, since the helper computes the same four fields with the same `|| 0` fallbacks and only adds `tiers` when non-empty.

Four blocks have deliberate cost logic and keep it by spreading over the helper's result rather than replacing it:

- `google-vertex` keeps the `gemini-2.5-flash` cacheRead override and `cacheWrite: 0`, and zeroes `cacheWrite` on its tiers too, for the same reason it is zeroed on the base rates (pi only accounts `cachedContentTokenCount`, as cacheRead). This is the one judgement call in the diff.
- `mistral` keeps the `cache_read ?? input * 0.1` fallback.
- `kimi-for-coding` keeps its implied subscription costs.
- `moonshotai` keeps the `KIMI_K3_COST` fallbacks.

Providers priced from their own APIs (OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway) and the hardcoded model lists are untouched.

## Effect

Generating the catalog before and after and diffing all 1223 models:

```
models with tiers:  21 -> 56  (+35)
total models:     1223 -> 1223
base rates changed:  0
```

Zero base-rate changes: the change is purely additive. Tiers gained by provider: opencode 9, google 6, opencode-go 5, cloudflare-ai-gateway 4, amazon-bedrock 3, xai 3, google-vertex 3, minimax 1, minimax-cn 1.

`xai/grok-4.5` now generates as:

```json
{"input": 2, "output": 6, "cacheRead": 0.3, "cacheWrite": 0,
 "tiers": [{"inputTokensAbove": 200000, "input": 4, "output": 12, "cacheRead": 0.6, "cacheWrite": 0}]}
```

`src/providers/data/` is gitignored and `models.generated.ts` is unchanged, since no models were added or removed, so the diff is the generator plus one test.

## Tests

`packages/ai/test/model-cost-tiers.test.ts` pins grok-4.5's 200k tier and adds a catalog-wide invariant that no tier is priced below the rate it steps up from. Verified it fails against the pre-change catalog and passes after.

`npm run check` clean. `./test.sh` green (216 passed in coding-agent, 23 in ai, 132 in agent, all other packages passing).

Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code). Reviewed and verified by me before submitting.

issues.title: Web Shell: show notification setup instructions only for the user's current OS

labels.name: priority/P3
labels.description: Low - Minor, cosmetic, nice-to-fix issues

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/ui
labels.description: User interface and display

labels.name: status/ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified; an AFK coding agent can pick this up with no human context

issues.body:
### What happened?

WebShell's **Task notifications** popover shows both macOS and Windows system notification setup instructions, without filtering them by the operating system of the user's current device.

When a user opens this popover on macOS, the Windows heading is still visible, and the user can expand the Windows setup steps. This adds irrelevant information and can lead users to instructions that do not apply to their device.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a WebShell session in a browser on macOS.
2. Open the **Task notifications** popover.
3. Locate the section that asks users to check system notification settings if they have not received notifications.
4. Observe that both macOS and Windows instructions are available as expandable sections.

This behavior was reported in a user-provided screenshot. It was not independently reproduced in a browser for this report.

### What did you expect to happen?

Show only the system notification setup instructions that match **the operating system of the user's device running the current browser**:

- On macOS, show only the macOS instructions; do not show the Windows heading or content.
- On Windows, show only the Windows instructions; do not show the macOS heading or content.

Detect the client OS, rather than the OS of the remote daemon, container, or server. For other or unrecognized platforms, generic guidance can be retained to avoid showing misleading platform-specific steps.

### Client information

- UI: WebShell, Chinese locale, **Task notifications** popover.
- User-reported platform: macOS.
- Browser version and WebShell artifact version of the reported instance: not provided.

### Source confirmation

The current main-branch source was checked: [BrowserNotificationControl.tsx](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/92bed7eeae9eae77fe2bf2a0249bda705d7379d1/packages/web-shell/client/components/messages/BrowserNotificationControl.tsx). Both the macOS and Windows `<details>` blocks are rendered unconditionally, consistent with the screenshot report.

### Acceptance criteria

- Opening the Task notifications popover in a macOS browser shows only the macOS system instructions.
- Opening the same popover in a Windows browser shows only the Windows system instructions.
- Both Chinese and English locales follow the same OS-filtering behavior.

labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/core
labels.description: Core engine and logic

labels.name: status/ready-for-human
labels.description: Specified but requires human judgment to implement; not suitable for an autonomous agent

issues.body:
### What happened?

The main session tells the model the date in two places:

1. The startup context at the top of the history (`getEnvironmentContext`, `core/environmentContext.ts`) says `Today's date is <date>.`
2. On a UserQuery turn, `LlmClient.sendMessageStream` (`core/client.ts`, added in #4798) prepends a reminder when the date differs from `lastInjectedDate`:

   ```
   The current date is: <date>. Note: This is the authoritative current date — it may differ from the "Today's date" mentioned earlier in the conversation startup context.
   ```

`lastInjectedDate` lives in memory and is not derived from the history the model actually sees. That causes three problems:

- **A. Every session's first turn repeats the date.** `startChat` resets `lastInjectedDate` to `undefined`, but the startup context it builds already carries today's date. So the first user turn of every new session, resume, `/clear` and manual `/compress` gets the same date a second time, with a note that tells the model the two "may differ" when they do not. A captured first request of `qwen -p` shows both: the startup reminder, then the date reminder in front of the user's text.
- **B. A rewind can leave the model with a stale date.** In a session that crossed midnight, the next user turn gets the new date and `lastInjectedDate` is set to it. If the user then rewinds to before that turn, `truncateHistory` drops the reminder but leaves `lastInjectedDate` unchanged, so no reminder follows. The only date left in the history is the previous day's, in the startup context.
- **C. Cron turns never refresh the date.** The check runs only on `SendMessageType.UserQuery`. A headless session whose cron prompts run past midnight keeps the previous day's date.

### What did you expect to happen?

The model sees the current date exactly once, and again only when it changes:

- The first turn adds nothing when the startup context already has today's date.
- After the date changes, the next user or cron turn adds one reminder that says the date has changed, without suggesting a conflict that does not exist.
- The decision comes from the history itself: the last date the history announces, from the startup context or an earlier date reminder, compared with today. Rewind, resume, compaction and `/clear` then need no extra state to stay correct.

Proposed fix:

- Replace `lastInjectedDate` with a helper that scans the history backwards for the last announced date. It reads only system-generated text: the startup context (including the legacy pre-reminder prelude) and `<system-reminder>` date parts in either wording. It never reads user-written text.
- Run the check on UserQuery and Cron turns.
- Reword the reminder to say the date has changed and that the change need not be pointed out to the user.

### Client information

<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

Read from source on `main` at 92bed7eeae (Linux). The behavior does not depend on the platform or the auth type.

</details>

### Login information

Any. The date reminder is built in core before the request reaches a content generator.

### Anything else we need to know?

- Out of scope: the date that the memory extraction agent carries, subagents, and moving the date out of the startup context.
- Test plan: unit tests for each case above, using `vi.setSystemTime` for the midnight cases and `truncateHistory` for the rewind case. Plus a request capture showing that the first request carries the date once.

**State at head `6fb4559be2`** (frozen; no commits from the author since):
- `mergeable: true`, `mergeStateStatus: blocked`, `reviewDecision: REVIEW_REQUIRED`
- approvals: 0 of 2 required — `main` ruleset wants 2 approving reviews, and `dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push: true`
- the only required status check, `Lint & Static (ubuntu-latest, Node 22.x)`, is green
- the red checks are infrastructure, not this diff: `review-pr` timed out at its 360-minute cap (run `41278942716`; the logs show 429 rpm backoff and repeated agent timeouts, no review was produced), and the `Managed Agent` / `SDK Java` lanes are the repository's known flakes
- no reviewer or assignee is requested on the PR, so it does not surface in a review queue on its own; the author cannot add one (fork author, `pull:true` only — `requested_reviewers` returns 404)

**Why the approvals went away:** the PR had two approvals (`wenshao`, `yiliang114`) before main advanced and the branch went `CONFLICTING`. The author resolved the conflict with merge commit `6fb4559be2` (merges `origin/main` `beaa46b172`, a fast-forward from `b67d229cc1`), and the repository's stale-approval setting dismissed both. The production diff vs `origin/main` is unchanged (18 files: docs, tests, and the `QQChannel.ts` / `ChannelBase.ts` hooks); validation on the merged tree: typecheck clean, `events.test.ts` 168/168, `loop.test.ts` + `loop-store.test.ts` 24/24, `loop-runtime.test.ts` 2/2, `ChannelBase` hook tests 3/3.

**Ask:** @wenshao @yiliang114 — add yourselves as reviewers and submit the two approvals on the frozen head `6fb4559be2` (or merge it directly). Nothing else is outstanding from the author side.

**Same blocker affects the sibling PRs**, whose heads are also frozen and both also at 0/2 approvals after their own conflict-resolution pushes: [#15634](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15634) at `9ea0c9d27f` (code-side signed off by @wenshao, no changes needed) and [#15450](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15450) at `54281ae8` (round-2 merge-ready verification recorded at that head). They will hit the same escalation window in about two days if the approvals do not land.

issues.title: perf(memory): move the main session's auto-memory guidance into a bundled skill

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: type/feature-request
labels.description: New feature or enhancement request

labels.name: category/performance
labels.description: Performance and optimization

labels.name: scope/token-management
labels.description: Token handling and limits

labels.name: scope/memory
labels.description: Memory and context management

labels.name: roadmap/context-performance
labels.description: Roadmap: Context and performance

labels.name: status/ready-for-human
labels.description: Specified but requires human judgment to implement; not suitable for an autonomous agent

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Split the main session's `# auto memory` system-prompt section into a short resident part and a bundled `auto-memory` skill that the model loads when it decides to save or reorganize a memory.

**Resident part (every request, about 3.5k characters).** It keeps what a session needs to save correctly without loading anything:

- the catalog note, and the memory directories with their tiers (USER, PROJECT, and TEAM when enabled);
- when to save: immediately when the user asks to remember something, and remove when asked to forget;
- the four types, one line each, with the scope that decides the directory, plus the **Why:** / **How to apply:** body rule for `feedback` and `project`;
- what not to save, in one sentence, including the rule that this holds even when the user asks;
- the two save steps, the frontmatter template and the fixed category list;
- update instead of duplicating, and remove memories that turn out to be wrong;
- using memory: when to read it, honoring "ignore memory", and verifying that a named file, function or flag still exists before recommending it;
- when TEAM memory is on, three lines: what belongs there, never `user` memories or secrets, and never hand-editing the team `MEMORY.md`;
- a pointer to the `auto-memory` skill.

**Skill body (paid only when loaded, about 15.5k characters).** It holds the current full guidance: the `Types of memory` block with its examples, the category explanation, the full "What NOT to save" list, the keyword and usage-scenario rules, the team-memory section, "Before recommending from memory", and "Memory and other forms of persistence".

**Delivery.** Reuse the routing in `skills/bundled-reference.ts`, which already serves `workflow-authoring` and `agent-delegation` (#12323):

| Route | Main-session memory section |
| --- | --- |
| `skill` | resident part + pointer |
| `skill-via-tool-search` | resident part + pointer + bridge sentence |
| `inline` (no route to any skill) | resident part + the full reference, as today |
| `withheld` (the user disabled the skill or the bundled level) | resident part only |

**Scope.**

- Only the main-session prompt that `Config.refreshHierarchicalMemory` builds changes, together with the `autoMemory` layer that subagents inherit from it.
- The extraction, Dream, User Dream, `/remember` and import agents keep the full constants (`TYPES_SECTION_INDIVIDUAL` and the others). `buildManagedAutoMemoryPrompt` keeps its full output for those callers.
- Structured recall (`buildStructuredAutoMemoryPrompt`) and the request-tail catalog (#13521) are unchanged.
- The TS constants stay the single source. A two-way anchor test pins them into `SKILL.md` and keeps them out of the resident prompt, as #12323 does.

### Why is this needed?

With the defaults (`memory.enableManagedAutoMemory: true`), the `# auto memory` section is the largest part of the main-session system prompt. I measured it on main (2026-11-04) by capturing a `qwen -p` request against a local OpenAI-compatible stub:

| | characters |
| --- | --- |
| whole system prompt | 35,792 |
| `# auto memory` section | 16,140 (45%) |
| of which `## Types of memory` | 7,939 |
| system prompt with `enableManagedAutoMemory: false` | 19,653 |

This section is sent on every request of every surface (Ink, OpenTUI, headless/SDK, ACP) and is inherited by subagents. Yet the main model writes memories in only a few turns, mostly when the user explicitly asks to remember or forget something; the background extractor writes the rest, with its own full prompt. The detailed type guidance and examples are needed on those few turns, not on every request.

With the draft resident text, the section goes from 15,867 to 3,551 characters (both normalized to typical directory paths). That saves about 12.3k characters, or roughly 3k tokens, per request, for every session that has auto memory on.

The trade-off is the same one #12323 measured for the Agent tool:

- The skill adds one `<available_skills>` entry, about 350 characters.
- A session that loads the skill carries its body in history from then on, until compaction.
- A session that never saves a memory pays nothing extra.

### Additional context

**Evaluation plan.**

1. Size, with no model involved:
   - Budget-test rows for each route, read from a real `Config`.
   - Before/after wire captures of `-p` requests, where everything outside the memory section must be byte-identical.
2. Behavior: a before/after run with real models, using at least two model tiers, five runs per scenario and arm, headless `--yolo`, an isolated HOME with a seeded corpus, and the background extractor kept out of the measurement.

| # | Scenario | Pass when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | "Remember: I use pnpm, not npm" | `feedback` file in USER; frontmatter parses with a valid type and category and 2–6 keywords; one pointer line added to the same directory's `MEMORY.md` |
| 2 | "Remember: merge freeze from Thursday for the mobile release" | `project` file in PROJECT, with an absolute date |
| 3 | "Remember: pipeline bugs are tracked in Linear project INGEST" | `reference` file in PROJECT |
| 4 | "Remember this project's directory layout" | not saved as is; the model asks what was non-obvious |
| 5 | Same topic already saved, user gives an update | existing file updated, no duplicate |
| 6 | "Forget what you know about pnpm" | file and pointer removed |
| 7 | A seeded memory names a flag that no longer exists; user asks how to enable the feature | the model checks the code before recommending |
| 8 | "Don't use memory for this" | the answer does not draw on memory |
| 9 | An ordinary task unrelated to memory | the skill is not loaded and nothing is written |

Metrics:

- the pass rate per scenario;
- the skill load rate in scenarios 1–6 and the false loads in scenario 9;
- main-model input tokens and the request count.

The change should not lower the pass rate of any scenario beyond run-to-run noise.

**Known limits.**

- A save made without loading the skill may get weaker metadata, such as keyword choice or body shape. The background extractor and Dream keep the full rules.
- The route resolver reads the tool registry, not a subagent's tool policy. So a custom subagent that cannot call `skill` would get a pointer it cannot follow. This is the existing #12424 gap; the resident part alone still saves correctly.

**Related.**

- #12028: token governance.
- #12781: system prompt simplification.
- #12947: the structured recall rollout. It is independent, because this change targets the default legacy path.
- #12323 and #11013: the bundled-reference precedent.

I plan to send the PR, with a design note in English and Chinese.

prs.title: fix(managed-agent): let --check read the configuration the server reads
prs.body:
## What this PR does

`qwen-managed-agent-server --check` now reads the configuration the server reads.

**Before.** The preflight built its environment with a loader of its own. It read the file that `SPRING_CONFIG_ADDITIONAL_LOCATION` (or `--spring.config.additional-location`) names, plus the packaged `application.yml`, and nothing else.

**Now.** It prepares the environment the way `SpringApplication` does, through a `ServerEnvironment` it now shares with `ResolvedConfiguration` (the upgrade command's resolver). Everything the server reads therefore counts, in the process's working directory as the server reads it:
- `application.yml` and `config/application.yml` at Spring Boot's default locations;
- imports and profile files;
- `.properties` files;
- `spring.config.name`;
- `SPRING_APPLICATION_JSON`.

**The `config` rows** now mean "the files the server reads". There is one row per file, each checked, as before, for the service account's access and for the secret-file mode. A row fails exactly where Spring would refuse to start:
- **A named file that does not exist:** the row prints its path.
- **A file this process cannot read:** the row names the file and the account.
- **A YAML error:** the row names the file, line and column. Spring's own message names neither the file nor the location, so the preflight looks for the file that does not parse among those named and those at the default locations.

When Spring refuses, the other rows still run, against the packaged defaults and the environment, as they ran before over a missing file. When the server reads only the packaged defaults, a WARN says so.

**Docs.**
- `systemd/README.md`'s hand-run `--check` now passes `--working-directory=/opt/qwen-managed-agent`, the unit's `WorkingDirectory`, and says why.
- The deployment guide (EN and ZH) says `--check` reads what the server reads and should run from the distribution root.

## Why it's needed

The issue's case is the reference systemd layout:
- `server.env` names `/etc/qwen-managed-agent/application.yml`;
- the unit's `WorkingDirectory` is the distribution root;
- the distribution's own `config/application.yml` holds a setting, such as `server.port`.

The server reads that file through Spring's default `./config/` location, and `--check` did not. As a result:
- **The `server-port` row** checked 8080, and the `session-store` row derived `http://127.0.0.1:8080`, while the server listened elsewhere.
- **The upgrade command's `verify`** failed its preflight row against a healthy server.
- **A syntax error in that file** passed `--check` and then stopped the server at start.

The same cause hid imports, profile files, `.properties` files and `SPRING_APPLICATION_JSON` from `--check`.

The two design points triage left for a decision were settled:
- **Working directory:** the process's own, as the server's, so the config rows print absolute paths, and the README and guide say where to run it.
- **The `config` row:** "the files the server reads", failing where Spring would.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

```bash
cd packages/managed-agent-server
mvn -pl verification -am test -Dtest='ServerEnvironmentTest,ManagedAgentPreflightTest,ResolvedConfigurationTest,ExternalRuntimeConfigurationTest' -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false
mvn -pl server,verification checkstyle:check
```

`ServerEnvironmentTest` covers, case by case:
- the issue's layout: a named file plus a `config/` directory, an import and a profile file;
- a file reached through two locations, which is listed once;
- location precedence;
- the argument over the variable;
- a missing named file, a missing import and a YAML error in a named file;
- a YAML error inside an imported file;
- an unreadable file, both through a readability seam and for real when not run as root;
- a wrapped cause, said once;
- the WARN when only the packaged defaults are read;
- an end-to-end `checks()` whose `server-port` row checks the port from the file beside the named one.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Everything below ran on a real systemd host with MySQL 8.4, a real Hosted Harness and a scripted model:
- **`prev`** is the reference distribution 0.1.0-alpha.104, built from `main` before this change.
- **`head`** is this branch, as 0.1.0-alpha.105/106.

Every `--check` ran as the unit runs it: as the service account, with its `EnvironmentFile`, in its `WorkingDirectory`. `server.env` names `etc/application.yml`.

| Case | `prev` | `head` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `server.port` only in the distribution's `config/application.yml`, server stopped | `config PASS etc/application.yml`; `session-store http://127.0.0.1:8080`; `server-port 127.0.0.1:8080 is free` | two `config PASS` rows (etc and `…/config/application.yml`); `session-store http://127.0.0.1:45335`; `server-port 127.0.0.1:45335 is free` |
| the same, server running on 45335, `--check --online` | `FAIL server-port nothing listens on 127.0.0.1:8080` | `PASS server-port 127.0.0.1:45335 is listening (online)` |
| the same, upgrade command `verify` | `FAIL preflight --check --online failed`, then `PASS health … 45335 … is UP` | `PASS preflight --check --online passed` (fresh alpha.105 install, port 58591), then `health`, `turn` PASS |
| a YAML error in the distribution's `config/application.yml` | `config PASS etc/application.yml`, all rows pass; the server then fails to start (`while parsing a flow node`) | `FAIL config …/config/application.yml, line 3, column 1: expected the node content, but found '<stream end>'`, fix `fix the YAML syntax` |
| that file unreadable by the service account | `config PASS etc/application.yml` | `FAIL config …/config/application.yml is not readable by qmae2e`, with the chown/chmod fix; run as root, the same FAIL through the service-user access check |
| `server.env` names a file that does not exist | two FAIL rows: `does not exist` and a spurious `is not readable` | one FAIL row: `…/etc/missing.yml does not exist`, fix `create it, or correct the location that names it` |
| `--check` by hand without the unit's working directory (cwd `/`) | — | reads only the named file and checks 8080, which is why the README now passes `--working-directory` |

**Upgrade path.** The upgrade from alpha.104 to alpha.105 was refused at `check`, as it should be: `main` rewrote `V1__managed_schema.sql` in place after alpha.104, and #16175's database row reports exactly that. So alpha.105 was installed fresh on a recreated database. With the configuration restored, `start` plus `verify --tenant e2e --turn` pass end to end.

**Mutation sweep.** 17 single-point mutants. Each one runs against the unmodified suites in a separate copy of the module, and the source is restored with a fresh mtime afterwards. They cover:
- **`ServerEnvironment.files()`:** without unwrapping `OriginTrackedResource`; keeping class path resources; without the named files that hold no setting; without deduplication.
- **`failure()`:**
  - a missing file shown as Spring's reference;
  - a YAML error without its line;
  - no candidates at all;
  - no named, default-location or `config/*/` candidates;
  - an unreadable candidate ignored;
  - a wrapped cause said twice;
  - a multi-line message kept.
- **`ManagedAgentPreflight`:**
  - the fallback without the packaged defaults;
  - the old loader in place of `ServerEnvironment`, which is the fix itself;
  - the "no configuration file" WARN turned PASS.
- **`ResolvedConfiguration`:** without the shared preparation.

The final sweep is still running and its result follows in an update.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ |

### Environment (optional)

- **Tests:** Linux x86_64 (Debian 13), OpenJDK 21, Maven offline.
- **Real host:** systemd 257 with MySQL 8.4 in Docker, running the reference distribution.

## Risk & Scope

- **Main risk or tradeoff.**
  - `--check` now depends on its working directory, as the server does. Run from another directory, it reads what a server started there would read, not what the unit's server reads.
    - The config rows print absolute paths, so a wrong directory shows.
    - The upgrade command already runs it in the unit's `WorkingDirectory`.
    - The README's hand-run command now passes it, and the deployment guide says to run from the distribution root.
  - Finding the file behind a YAML error is best effort. A file imported from inside another is not among the candidates, so its row says "a configuration file" with Spring's line and column.
  - A file at a default location that holds no setting is not listed, because Spring adds no property source for it. A named one is listed.
- **Not validated / out of scope.**
  - macOS and Windows: the preflight targets the reference systemd layout.
  - The pre-existing log lines (`Standard Commons Logging discovery…`, the `BrokerSecurity` INFO line) print before the rows, as they did before.
- **Breaking changes / migration notes.**
  - The config row's texts change: one row per file read, a WARN that says "no configuration file; packaged defaults and the environment only", and new FAIL texts.
  - A deployment that relied on `--check` ignoring a broken file at a default location now gets a FAIL. The server already refused to start on that file.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #16057

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

`qwen-managed-agent-server --check` 现在读取的配置与服务端一致。

**原来。** preflight 用自己的加载器构建环境，只读取 `SPRING_CONFIG_ADDITIONAL_LOCATION`（或 `--spring.config.additional-location`）指定的文件和打包的 `application.yml`。

**现在。** 它按 `SpringApplication` 的方式准备环境，所用的 `ServerEnvironment` 与 `ResolvedConfiguration`（升级命令的解析器）共用。服务端读的所有内容都会计入，并且像服务端一样在进程的工作目录下解析：
- Spring Boot 默认位置下的 `application.yml` 和 `config/application.yml`；
- import 和 profile 文件；
- `.properties` 文件；
- `spring.config.name`；
- `SPRING_APPLICATION_JSON`。

**`config` 行**的含义改为"服务端实际读取的文件"。每个文件一行，仍像原来一样检查服务账号能否读取、以及密钥文件的权限。只在 Spring 自己会拒绝启动的地方判失败：
- **指定的文件不存在：** 该行写出文件路径。
- **本进程读不了某个文件：** 该行写明文件和账号。
- **YAML 错误：** 该行写明文件、行号和列号。Spring 自己的报错既不写文件也不写位置，所以 preflight 会在被指定的文件和默认位置的文件中找出解析失败的那个。

Spring 拒绝时，其余检查行照常运行，改用打包默认值和环境变量，与原来遇到文件缺失时一样。服务端只读到打包默认值时，以 WARN 提示。

**文档。**
- `systemd/README.md` 中手动运行 `--check` 的命令加上了 `--working-directory=/opt/qwen-managed-agent`，即 unit 的 `WorkingDirectory`，并说明原因。
- 部署指南（中英文）说明 `--check` 读取服务端读取的内容，应在发行包根目录下运行。

## 为什么需要

issue 里的场景就是 reference 的 systemd 布局：
- `server.env` 指定 `/etc/qwen-managed-agent/application.yml`；
- unit 的 `WorkingDirectory` 是发行包根目录；
- 发行包自带的 `config/application.yml` 里写了某项设置，例如 `server.port`。

服务端会经 Spring 的默认位置 `./config/` 读到这个文件，`--check` 却读不到。结果是：
- **`server-port` 行**检查 8080，`session-store` 行推导出 `http://127.0.0.1:8080`，而服务端实际监听的是另一个端口。
- **升级命令的 `verify`** 在服务端健康的情况下，preflight 行判失败。
- **这个文件里的语法错误**能通过 `--check`，之后让服务端启动失败。

出于同一原因，import、profile 文件、`.properties` 文件和 `SPRING_APPLICATION_JSON` 也都被 `--check` 忽略了。

triage 留待决定的两个设计点已经定下：
- **工作目录：** 用进程自身的，与服务端一致；config 行打印绝对路径，README 和部署指南写明在哪里运行。
- **`config` 行：** 表示"服务端读取的文件"，在 Spring 会拒绝启动的地方判失败。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

```bash
cd packages/managed-agent-server
mvn -pl verification -am test -Dtest='ServerEnvironmentTest,ManagedAgentPreflightTest,ResolvedConfigurationTest,ExternalRuntimeConfigurationTest' -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false
mvn -pl server,verification checkstyle:check
```

`ServerEnvironmentTest` 覆盖以下情况：
- issue 中的布局：一个被指定的文件，加上 `config/` 目录、一个 import 和一个 profile 文件；
- 经两个位置读到的同一个文件，只列一次；
- 位置的优先级；
- 参数优先于环境变量；
- 指定的文件缺失、import 缺失、被指定文件中的 YAML 错误；
- 被导入文件中的 YAML 错误；
- 读不了的文件：通过可注入的可读性判断覆盖，非 root 运行时也会真实覆盖；
- 包装异常的原因只说一次；
- 只读到打包默认值时的 WARN；
- 端到端的 `checks()`：其 `server-port` 行检查的是被指定文件旁边那个文件里的端口。

### 证据（修改前后）

以下都在真实 systemd 主机上运行，使用 MySQL 8.4、真实 Hosted Harness 和脚本模型：
- **`prev`**：从修改前的 `main` 构建的 reference 发行包 0.1.0-alpha.104。
- **`head`**：本分支构建的 0.1.0-alpha.105/106。

每次 `--check` 都按 unit 的方式运行：服务账号、unit 的 `EnvironmentFile`、unit 的 `WorkingDirectory`。`server.env` 指定的是 `etc/application.yml`。

| 场景 | `prev` | `head` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `server.port` 只写在发行包的 `config/application.yml`，服务停止 | 只有 `config PASS etc/application.yml`；`session-store` 推导出 8080；`server-port` 检查 8080 | 两行 `config PASS`；`session-store` 为 45335；`server-port` 检查 45335 |
| 同上，服务运行在 45335，`--check --online` | `FAIL server-port nothing listens on 127.0.0.1:8080` | `PASS server-port 127.0.0.1:45335 is listening` |
| 同上，升级命令 `verify` | `FAIL preflight`，但 `health … 45335 … is UP` | `PASS preflight`（全新安装 alpha.105，端口 58591），health、turn 均 PASS |
| 发行包 `config/application.yml` 中有 YAML 错误 | 所有行都 PASS，随后服务端启动失败 | `FAIL config …/config/application.yml, line 3, column 1: …`，修复提示 `fix the YAML syntax` |
| 该文件服务账号读不了 | 只有 `config PASS etc/application.yml` | `FAIL config … is not readable by qmae2e`，附 chown/chmod 修法；以 root 运行时，经服务账号访问检查同样 FAIL |
| `server.env` 指定的文件不存在 | 两行 FAIL：`does not exist`，外加一行错误的 `is not readable` | 一行 FAIL：`… does not exist`，修复提示 `create it, or correct the location that names it` |
| 不按 unit 的工作目录手动运行 `--check`（cwd 为 `/`） | — | 只读到被指定的文件，检查的是 8080，这正是 README 现在要加 `--working-directory` 的原因 |

**升级路径。** 从 alpha.104 升级到 alpha.105 在 `check` 处被拒绝，这是正确的：alpha.104 之后 `main` 原地改写了 `V1__managed_schema.sql`，#16175 的 database 行报告的正是这一点。因此 alpha.105 是在重建后的数据库上全新安装的。还原配置后，`start` 加 `verify --tenant e2e --turn` 端到端通过。

**变异测试。** 17 个单点变异。每个变异都在模块的独立副本中、对未修改的测试套件运行，之后还原源码并刷新 mtime。覆盖：
- **`ServerEnvironment.files()`：** 不拆开 `OriginTrackedResource`；保留 classpath 资源；不列出被指定但不含设置的文件；不去重。
- **`failure()`：**
  - 把缺失的文件报成 Spring 的引用描述；
  - YAML 错误不带行号；
  - 完全没有候选；
  - 去掉被指定位置、默认位置或 `config/*/` 中的候选；
  - 忽略读不了的候选；
  - 包装异常的原因重复两次；
  - 保留多行消息。
- **`ManagedAgentPreflight`：**
  - 回退时不加载打包默认值；
  - 用旧加载器代替 `ServerEnvironment`，即撤掉修复本身；
  - "no configuration file" 的 WARN 改成 PASS。
- **`ResolvedConfiguration`：** 不走共用的环境准备。

最终一轮变异测试仍在运行，结果稍后补充。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ |

### 环境（可选）

- **测试：** Linux x86_64（Debian 13）、OpenJDK 21、离线 Maven。
- **真机：** systemd 257，MySQL 8.4 运行在 Docker 中，运行 reference 发行包。

## 风险与范围

- **主要风险或权衡。**
  - `--check` 现在和服务端一样依赖工作目录。在别的目录下运行时，它读到的是"在那里启动的服务端"会读的内容，而不是 unit 的服务端会读的内容。
    - config 行打印绝对路径，目录不对一眼可见。
    - 升级命令本来就在 unit 的 `WorkingDirectory` 下运行它。
    - README 的手动命令现在带上了这个参数，部署指南也写明要在发行包根目录下运行。
  - 定位 YAML 错误所在的文件是尽力而为。从另一个文件内部导入的文件不在候选范围内，这时该行写作"a configuration file"，附 Spring 给出的行号和列号。
  - 默认位置上不含任何设置的文件不会被列出，因为 Spring 不会为它创建 property source；被直接指定的这类文件仍会列出。
- **未验证 / 不在范围内。**
  - macOS 和 Windows：preflight 面向 reference 的 systemd 布局。
  - 检查行之前原本就会打印的日志行（`Standard Commons Logging discovery…`、`BrokerSecurity` 的 INFO 行）保持原样。
- **破坏性变更 / 迁移说明。**
  - config 行的文本有变化：读到几个文件就有几行；WARN 改为 "no configuration file; packaged defaults and the environment only"；FAIL 的文本也是新的。
  - 依赖 `--check` 忽略默认位置上损坏文件的部署，现在会得到 FAIL；而服务端本来就会因为这个文件拒绝启动。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #16057

</details>

prs.title: feat(core): add local notes compaction with a strategy selector
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds an opt-in local notes compaction strategy. Users can select **Summary** or **Notes and History** under **Chat Compression Strategy** in `/settings`, or set `model.chatCompression.strategy` to `summary` or `notes` in `settings.json`. Summary remains the default; changing the selection requires restarting Qwen Code.

Eligible main sessions gain `session_notes`, `session_history`, `get_context_remaining`, and `new_context`. The model can persist a bounded working checkpoint, start a smaller context from that checkpoint and the latest consumed user request, and recover omitted evidence from the active branch of its local session log. Successful notes rollovers make no summarization request. Notes revisions live in the existing JSONL transcript, with a generated Markdown projection for inspection; checkpoint persistence must succeed before active history changes. Resume, fork, rewind, archive, and deletion handle the matching notes state.

Missing, stale, or unusable notes fall back to summary for automatic and ordinary manual compression. An explicit `new_context` requires a fresh revision and reports an error if it cannot commit. `/compress <instructions>` continues to summarize, and `/compress-fast` keeps its existing behavior. The notes tool bundle respects recording availability and tool policy and is excluded from subagents, teammates, and nested code-mode calls. Ink and OpenTUI display a notes-specific transition notice.

## Why it's needed

Repeated full-history summaries can lose constraints, decisions, and tool evidence that a long task needs later. A local working checkpoint plus bounded history retrieval gives the model a way to carry forward its current state and recover details on demand. Storage and retrieval use the existing session log and require no additional memory backend. Selected notes and retrieved history still go to the configured model provider as normal inference input. Real-model quality, total token cost, and latency remain to be measured before considering a default change.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Start the local build with no strategy configured and confirm summary behavior. Open `/settings`, search for `compression`, switch to **Notes and History**, and confirm the saved value is `model.chatCompression.strategy: "notes"` and the restart notice appears. Restart and check that the four notes tools are available. Repeat with `summary`, including activation through `settings.json`.
2. In an isolated recorded session, have the model write notes and request a new context in separate tool-only responses using the returned revision. Repeat three times. Each new context should retain the checkpoint and current user constraints, with no summarizer request. Deliberately omit an earlier identifier from the notes, then recover it through history search/read. Resume the session and check that its latest notes revision and old history reference still work.
3. Check that missing/stale revisions, oversized notes, and notes/reset calls mixed with ordinary text or tools cannot install a new context. Disabling recording or denying a required notes tool should disable the complete bundle. After switching to a smaller model window, existing bounded notes should remain readable, while an oversized checkpoint must be shortened before it can authorize a reset.
4. Compare compression commands: `/compress` with fresh notes should use notes; missing/stale notes should fall back to summary; `/compress <instructions>` should forward those instructions to the summarizer even with fresh notes; `/compress-fast` should retain its current tool-output clearing behavior. Check that the next model request uses the committed context and that notes transitions show the notes-specific notice.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Actual tmux captures of `/settings`, with the search set to `compression`:

**Before — global `qwen` `0.23.3-nightly.20260913.faa395885e`:**

```text
No settings match your search.
```

**After — local bundle `0.24.1`:**

```text
Chat Compression Strategy                                                   Notes and History*
Choose summary compression or local notes with history recovery. Restart Qwen Code to apply.
To see changes, Qwen Code must be restarted. Press r to exit and apply changes now.
```

The fresh-notes `/compress` case displayed `Started a new context from local notes` in the actual TUI. The complete deterministic headless/tmux run passed settings persistence, tool availability, history recovery/resume, six rejection cases, and all six manual-compression cases. After the final fixes, the rebuilt handoff rerun again committed **three distinct notes windows in 15 main requests with zero summarizer requests**; resume took three requests and restored the same notes revision and historical reference.

`npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, and `npm run bundle` passed. Relevant core, ACP, settings/schema/i18n, and Ink/OpenTUI regression tests passed. The final focused rerun passed 23 core tests and 54 event-adapter tests; the commit hook also passed formatting and ESLint. A separate comment contains the E2E matrix and coverage limits.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested locally |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ Not tested locally |

### Environment (optional)

macOS arm64, Node.js `v26.8.2`; local bundled CLI `0.24.1`; isolated temporary settings and runtime directories; deterministic localhost OpenAI-compatible provider; headless CLI and real tmux interaction. The user's normal settings and sessions were not modified by the tests.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: This changes core recording, compaction, and replay paths. Correctness depends on fresh notes, successful checkpoint persistence, and branch-correct recovery; note completeness still depends on the model. The Markdown file is a generated view, so editing it directly does not update canonical notes.
- Not validated / out of scope: Real-model task quality, token/cost/latency comparisons, full ACP/Web Shell E2E, other provider wire protocols, process-crash/disk/lease fault injection, and Windows/Linux execution. The deterministic E2E suite does not cover automatic/hard-overflow triggers, nested code mode, or fork/rewind/archive lifecycle operations; focused regression tests cover relevant runtime paths, without claiming end-to-end coverage. Cross-session memory, multi-file notes, and a notes editor are out of scope.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: No settings migration is required. `summary` remains the default, existing transcripts remain supported, and enabling or disabling `notes` requires a restart. Ordinary compression can use summary fallback; an explicit `new_context` never silently summarizes.

Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/158a0511ddcdd465e14083c56d0f9c7cc8ac629a/docs/design/2026-09-19-local-notes-compaction.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/158a0511ddcdd465e14083c56d0f9c7cc8ac629a/docs/design/2026-09-19-local-notes-compaction.zh-CN.md). Both versions are complete and synchronized, including decisions, constraints, acceptance criteria, and follow-up validation.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #12257

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的内容

增加可选的本地 notes 压缩策略。用户可以在 `/settings` 的 **上下文压缩方式** 中选择 **摘要** 或 **笔记与历史**，也可以在 `settings.json` 中把 `model.chatCompression.strategy` 设为 `summary` 或 `notes`。默认仍为摘要；修改选项后需要重启 Qwen Code。

符合条件的主会话获得 `session_notes`、`session_history`、`get_context_remaining` 和 `new_context` 四个工具。模型可以保存有大小限制的工作笔记，从笔记和最近已消费的用户请求启动更小的上下文，再从本地 session log 的有效分支找回遗漏证据。成功的 notes 换窗口不发起摘要请求。笔记版本保存在现有 JSONL transcript 中，并生成方便查看的 Markdown 文件；只有恢复 checkpoint 持久化成功后才替换当前历史。恢复、分叉、回退、归档和删除操作会处理对应的笔记状态。

自动压缩和普通手动压缩在笔记缺失、过期或不可用时回退到摘要。显式调用 `new_context` 必须提供新鲜的笔记版本，无法提交时返回错误。`/compress <instructions>` 继续生成摘要，`/compress-fast` 保持现有行为。笔记工具组遵循录制可用性及工具策略，并对 subagent、teammate 和嵌套 code-mode 调用关闭。Ink 和 OpenTUI 会显示专门的 notes 换窗口提示。

## 为什么需要

反复生成全历史摘要可能丢失长任务后续需要的约束、决策和工具证据。本地工作笔记加上有界历史检索，使模型能够保留当前工作状态并按需找回细节。存储和检索复用现有 session log，不需要新增 memory 后端。选中的笔记和检索出的历史仍会作为正常推理输入发送给配置的模型 provider。在考虑修改默认策略前，仍需评估真实模型的任务质量、总 token 成本和延迟。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 使用本地构建启动，不配置策略时确认仍使用摘要。打开 `/settings`，搜索 `compression`，切换到 **Notes and History**，确认保存的值为 `model.chatCompression.strategy: "notes"` 并显示重启提示。重启后检查四个笔记工具可用。再切回 `summary`，并验证通过 `settings.json` 启用的行为一致。
2. 在隔离且开启录制的会话中，让模型先写笔记，再用返回的 revision 请求新上下文；两次调用分别放在独立且只含该工具的回复中。重复三次。每个新上下文都应保留 checkpoint 和当前用户约束，且不发起摘要请求。故意不把某个早期标识符写入笔记，再通过历史搜索和读取找回。恢复会话后，检查最新笔记版本和旧历史引用仍可用。
3. 检查缺失或过期的 revision、超限笔记，以及混入普通文本或其他工具的笔记/换窗口调用，都不能安装新上下文。关闭录制或拒绝任一必需工具后，整个笔记工具组应被关闭。切换到窗口更小的模型后，已有且满足固定大小上限的笔记仍应可读，但超过当前模型预算的 checkpoint 必须缩短后才能用于换窗口。
4. 对比压缩命令：笔记新鲜时 `/compress` 应使用笔记；笔记缺失或过期时应回退到摘要；即使有新鲜笔记，`/compress <instructions>` 也应把指定要求转交摘要模型；`/compress-fast` 应保留现有清理工具输出的行为。检查下一次模型请求使用已提交的上下文，且 notes 换窗口显示对应提示。

### 证据（前后对比）

以下为真实 tmux 捕获的 `/settings` 画面节选，搜索词为 `compression`：

**修改前：全局 `qwen` `0.23.3-nightly.20260913.faa395885e`：**

```text
No settings match your search.
```

**修改后：本地 bundle `0.24.1`：**

```text
Chat Compression Strategy                                                   Notes and History*
Choose summary compression or local notes with history recovery. Restart Qwen Code to apply.
To see changes, Qwen Code must be restarted. Press r to exit and apply changes now.
```

使用新鲜笔记执行 `/compress` 时，真实 TUI 显示 `Started a new context from local notes`。完整的确定性 headless/tmux 测试通过了设置持久化、工具可用性、历史找回与会话恢复、六项拒绝场景以及全部六项手动压缩场景。最终修复后重新构建并复测交接，再次在 **15 次主模型请求中提交了三个不同的 notes 窗口，摘要请求为零**；恢复过程使用三次请求，恢复了相同的笔记版本和历史引用。

`npm run build`、`npm run typecheck` 和 `npm run bundle` 均通过。相关 core、ACP、设置/schema/国际化、Ink/OpenTUI 回归测试均通过。最后的针对性复测通过了 23 个 core 测试和 54 个 event-adapter 测试；提交钩子的格式和 ESLint 检查也通过。另附评论列出 E2E 场景矩阵和覆盖范围。

### 测试平台

| 平台 | 状态 |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未在本地测试 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 未在本地测试 |

### 环境（可选）

macOS arm64、Node.js `v26.8.2`、本地 CLI bundle `0.24.1`；使用隔离的临时设置和 runtime 目录、确定性的 localhost OpenAI 兼容模型服务、headless CLI 和真实 tmux 交互。测试未修改用户日常使用的设置和会话。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：涉及 core 的录制、压缩和回放路径。正确性依赖笔记新鲜度、checkpoint 成功持久化以及有效分支恢复；笔记内容是否完整仍依赖模型。Markdown 文件只是生成视图，直接编辑不会更新权威笔记。
- 未验证或不在范围内：真实模型任务质量、token/成本/延迟对比、完整 ACP/Web Shell E2E、其他 provider 的通信协议、进程崩溃/磁盘/写入租约故障注入，以及 Windows/Linux 运行。确定性 E2E 未覆盖自动/硬溢出触发、嵌套 code mode 或分叉/回退/归档生命周期操作；针对性回归测试覆盖了相关运行时路径，但不代表完成了这些场景的端到端验证。跨会话记忆、多文件笔记和笔记编辑器不在本次范围内。
- 破坏性变更或迁移说明：无需迁移设置。默认仍为 `summary`，继续支持已有 transcript；开启或关闭 `notes` 需要重启。普通压缩可以回退到摘要；显式 `new_context` 绝不会悄悄改用摘要。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/158a0511ddcdd465e14083c56d0f9c7cc8ac629a/docs/design/2026-09-19-local-notes-compaction.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/158a0511ddcdd465e14083c56d0f9c7cc8ac629a/docs/design/2026-09-19-local-notes-compaction.zh-CN.md)。两个版本完整同步，包括决策、约束、验收标准和后续验证。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #12257

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): keep the user's instruction last in the model request
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Keeps the user's own instruction as the last content the model reads on a fresh turn. Injected context that currently trails the prompt — hook and Mod context, plus the memory catalog snapshot — is moved ahead of it in the outgoing request, at the single point where every main-turn request is assembled. Stored history is left exactly as it is; only the request copy is reordered.

Leading tool results keep their position, an entry whose tool result is not in the leading run is left untouched, and the volatile reattach tail stays last so the provider cache breakpoint keeps its anchor. A reminder the caller placed between two of its own parts bounds the movable run and stays where the caller put it.

## Why it's needed

A user submitted one complete 2461-character task with seven numbered steps. The model replied "I have not received a specific task yet", and its reasoning read "The user only provided a system reminder about available skills ... no specific task."

The instruction reached the provider intact — its position did not survive assembly. A fresh turn's user entry is built from four independent sources: per-turn reminders prepended ahead of the prompt, the user's own parts, the hook/Mod context block appended behind them, and the memory catalog appended after that. The real task therefore sits mid-entry with injected context on both sides. Three independent caps (8000 characters for the skills listing, 25000 per memory index with two indexes injected, and unbounded hook context) let those surrounding blocks reach tens of kilobytes, at which point a flash-class model reads the envelopes and misses the task.

Moving the instruction to the tail addresses the reported symptom without touching any budget.

The reordering is deliberately request-only. The trailing position of the hook block is load-bearing for stored history: the transcript display projection treats a complete final tagged part as pairing evidence for the display text, and resume re-stamps its delivery receipt only on the final part. Reordering the stored entry would break the display projection and re-deliver already-delivered hook context on every turn.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Start a session with auto-memory enabled and a `UserPromptSubmit` hook that returns `additionalContext`, then submit a long multi-part instruction (several separate text blocks, as an ACP client sends them). Inspect the outgoing request in the debug API log: the reminders, hook block and catalog should precede the instruction, and the instruction's own blocks should close the user entry in their original order. Inspect the session transcript afterwards: the stored entry must still end with the hook block, and a resumed session must not re-deliver that hook context.

Also worth confirming on a tool-result turn: the tool result stays first, and a session that reattaches earlier images keeps its reattach region (marker, label, image) contiguous and last, so prompt caching still hits.

Targeted unit run: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/llm-chat.test.ts` — 716 passed. Two assertions that pinned the old order were updated: the pending-turn check now asserts the catalog is present and the user text is last, and the durable-recovery check now asserts the request holds the same entries and parts as history with the catalog moved ahead of the recovery prompt. Four regression cases were added for the placement itself, the tool-result and volatile-tail ordering, an untouched prompt, and a caller-interleaved reminder.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — request-shape change, covered by the unit assertions above. No TUI surface changes.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Package-local unit tests only (`packages/core`, vitest). No real-model or daemon run.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the model now sees injected context ahead of the instruction rather than split around it. Providers that cache on a stable prefix are unaffected because stored history and the volatile tail keep their order, but a provider sensitive to intra-message ordering would see a different block sequence than before.
- Not validated / out of scope: no real-model reproduction of the original session, and no Windows or Linux run. The aggregate budget across per-turn injected blocks, moving the catalog off the user entry entirely, and the CJK token undercount in the always-on-context warning are separate work (#16184, #14976) and are not addressed here.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No setting, protocol field, or storage format changes; existing transcripts replay unchanged.

<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

让用户自己的指令成为新轮次中模型最后读到的内容。目前尾随在正文之后的注入上下文——hook 与 Mod 上下文，加上记忆目录快照——会在外发请求中被移到正文之前，改动落在每轮主请求组装的唯一位置。已存历史完全不动，只重排请求副本。

前导工具结果保持原位；工具结果不在前导区段的条目原样返回；易变的 reattach 尾部仍在最后，让服务商缓存断点保有其锚点。调用方放在自己两个分片之间的提醒会成为可移动区段的边界，保持原位。

## 为什么需要

用户提交了一条完整的 2461 字符任务，含 7 个编号步骤。模型回复"目前还没有收到具体任务"，其 thinking 原文是"The user only provided a system reminder about available skills ... no specific task."

指令完整送达了服务商，但它的位置在组装过程中没有保住。一次新轮次的 user 条目由四个独立来源拼成：前置在正文之前的每轮提醒、用户自己的分片、追加在其后的 hook/Mod 上下文块，以及再追加在后的记忆目录。真实任务因此落在条目中段，两侧都是注入上下文。三个各自独立的上限（skills 列表 8000 字符、每个记忆索引 25000 且会注入两个索引、无上限的 hook 上下文）让包围它的块可达几十 KB，此时 flash 级别的模型只读到这些信封，漏掉了任务。

把指令移到尾部即可消除本次报告的现象，且无需改动任何预算。

重排刻意只作用于请求。hook 块位于尾部这一点对已存历史是有承载作用的：transcript 展示投影把完整的末尾 tagged 分片当作展示文本的配对证据，resume 也只对最后一个分片重新盖上投递回执。重排已存条目会破坏展示投影，并让已投递的 hook 上下文每轮重复投递。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

开启 auto-memory，并配置一个返回 `additionalContext` 的 `UserPromptSubmit` hook，然后提交一条长的多分片指令（多个独立文本块，如 ACP 客户端的发送方式）。在 debug API 日志中检查外发请求：提醒、hook 块和目录应排在指令之前，指令自己的分片应按原顺序收尾该 user 条目。随后检查会话 transcript：已存条目必须仍以 hook 块结尾，且 resume 后的会话不应重复投递该 hook 上下文。

工具结果轮次也值得确认：工具结果仍在最前；回放了早前图片的会话，其 reattach 区域（标记、标签、图片）保持连续且位于最后，从而 prompt 缓存仍能命中。

定向单测：`cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/llm-chat.test.ts` —— 716 项通过。两处固定旧顺序的断言已更新：待发送轮次的检查改为断言目录存在且用户正文在最后；持久化恢复的检查改为断言请求与历史持有相同的条目和分片，只是目录被移到了恢复提示词之前。新增 4 个回归用例，覆盖位置本身、工具结果与易变尾部的顺序、未被改动的提示词，以及调用方自行交错的提醒。

### 证据（Before & After）

N/A —— 请求形状变更，由上述单测断言覆盖，TUI 界面无变化。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 环境（可选）

仅包内单测（`packages/core`，vitest）。未做真实模型或 daemon 运行。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：模型现在看到注入上下文排在指令之前，而不是分布在其两侧。基于稳定前缀做缓存的服务商不受影响，因为已存历史和易变尾部都保持原顺序；但对消息内部块顺序敏感的服务商会看到与之前不同的块序列。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：没有对原始会话做真实模型复现，也没有 Windows 与 Linux 运行。跨每轮注入块的总量预算、把目录彻底移出 user 条目，以及 always-on-context 告警对中文 token 的低估，都是独立工作（#16184、#14976），本 PR 不处理。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。没有设置、协议字段或存储格式变更；既有 transcript 回放不变。

prs.title: refactor(web-shell): share session view reset state
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This PR consolidates the shared transcript-view reset used by session changes and `/clear`. It also makes the component contract explicit: when a consumer keeps the same transcript component mounted across a session-key change, a reading pause from the previous session is cleared. A reconnect within the same session continues to preserve that pause.

## Why it's needed

The two reset paths maintained overlapping state independently. Sharing their common reset keeps those paths consistent and covers the component's mount-stable session-switch contract. The shipped routes already remount the transcript or render an empty transcript when switching sessions, so this is component-level hardening, not a demonstrated user-visible fix on those routes.

The main-CI failure tracked in #15038 is an unhandled rejection in the hosted workspace tool-turn tests. This Web Shell change does not fix that failure and must not close its tracker.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Keep one transcript component mounted, pause following, and change its session key while supplying the next session's non-empty transcript. Following should resume, both with and without a replay transition.
- Reconnect within the same session after pausing. The reading position should remain paused.
- Clear the transcript within the same session. The existing clear/reset behavior should remain intact.
- Treat the session-switch DOM cases as component-contract coverage; the shipped routes' remount/empty-first behavior is not a before/after reproduction of this change.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Earlier review reports establish that the added DOM cases fail without the session-switch pause reset and pass with it. The same reports establish that shipped-route-shaped cases already pass on the base. Those historical results support the component contract only; they are not new validation of the current head.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| macOS | No local checks run in this closeout |
| Windows | No local checks run in this closeout |
| Linux | Earlier DOM evidence is recorded in the PR discussion; the previous head's smoke check failed and checks for this closeout are pending |

## Risk & Scope

- The shared reset clears reading-pause, pagination-snapshot and expansion state. Each caller retains its additional resets; the settled-stale latch is cleared by `/clear`, not by the render-phase session switch.
- This PR changes no shipped route's mounting or empty-transcript behavior and does not repair the hosted workspace tool-turn failure.
- No local tests, build, lint or typecheck were run during this closeout, as requested. The previous smoke failure is reported separately and checks for the new head are pending; no passing browser result is claimed.
- No public API or migration change.

## Linked Issues

Refs #15038; this PR does not resolve it.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

合并会话切换与 `/clear` 共用的视图重置逻辑，并明确组件契约：调用方若在切换 session key 时保留同一个消息列表实例，上一会话的阅读暂停状态会被清除。同一会话重连仍保留阅读暂停。

## 为什么需要

两条路径原先分别维护重叠的重置状态。共用重置逻辑可以保持行为一致，并补全不重建组件时的会话切换契约。当前已发布页面在切换会话时会重建消息列表，或先渲染空记录，因此本 PR 是组件层加固，不是已证实的现有页面可见缺陷修复。

#15038 跟踪的是 hosted workspace tool-turn 测试中的未处理拒绝。该 Web Shell 改动不能修复此 CI 故障，也不应自动关闭它。

## Reviewer 测试计划

- 保持消息列表实例不变，暂停跟随后，改变 session key 并传入下一会话的非空记录。有回放与无回放两种情况下都应恢复跟随。
- 同一会话暂停后重连，应继续保持阅读位置。
- 在同一会话清空记录，原有清空和重置行为应保持。
- 新增 DOM 用例验证组件契约；已发布页面重建组件或先清空记录的路径不能作为本改动的前后对照复现。

## 已有证据与验证边界

此前评审记录表明，移除会话切换时的暂停重置会使新增 DOM 用例失败，保留时通过；按已发布页面形态编写的对照用例在 base 上原本就通过。这些历史结果只支撑组件契约，不代表本轮重新验证了当前 head。

本轮按用户要求未运行本地测试、构建、lint 或 typecheck。上一 head 的 Web Shell smoke 失败另行记录，新 head 的检查尚未完成；未声称浏览器验证通过。macOS 与 Windows 本轮均未验证，Linux 既有 DOM 证据见 PR 讨论。

## 风险与范围

公共重置处理阅读暂停、分页快照和展开状态；调用方保留各自额外的重置。settled-stale 状态只在 `/clear` 路径清除，不在渲染期会话切换路径清除。本 PR 不改变页面挂载方式，也不修复 hosted workspace tool-turn 故障。无公共 API 或迁移变更。

## 关联 Issue

Refs #15038；本 PR 不解决该 issue。

</details>


### Latest repair

The latest repair also cancels old-session follow/animation callbacks and strengthens continued-follow assertions. It carries the two smoke selector corrections already landed in #15860. These new cases were not run locally; current-head CI remains pending.

auto_merge.commit_message:
* fix(web-shell): reset follow pause when the session changes (#15038)

Preserving a reading pause across reconnects also preserved it across a
session switch, because the pause lives in a ref that outlives the
displayed transcript. Switching sessions while paused then left the new
transcript stranded above the latest content even though the reader never
paused it. Drop the pause in the existing session-scoped reset.

Add a DOM test that pauses session A, switches to session B mid-replay,
and asserts B lands at the bottom once catch-up completes.

* test(web-shell): pin the no-replay session switch and share the reset (#15038)

prs.title: fix(ci): preserve Maven suite results across cache write-back failures
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This PR hardens the SDK Java Maven cache path after the suite/write-back lock split. Failed MySQL integration suites can still publish downloaded artifacts while preserving the original suite status, cache setup failures preserve the already-known suite result, and the final error annotation identifies the failed Maven stage. Cache seeds report copy failures, tolerate an unavailable cache or failed best-effort prune, and detach mutable resolver metadata before Maven runs — including single-link resolver state inherited from a previous job, since RUNNER_TEMP persists across jobs on the self-hosted pool. Write-back excludes the same metadata and partial-download files.

## Why it's needed

The lock relocation associated with #15262 already landed on main through #15128 and #15254. This branch is the remaining hardening delta: a failed suite should not throw away reusable downloads, a best-effort cache operation should not replace the suite result, and mutable resolver state should not be published as an immutable shared artifact. The test repair in 11c0f4b2fb12c also includes the deferred-status reporter in extracted shell snippets so those tests can exercise their intended paths.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Fail either Maven stage in the self-hosted MySQL integration lane. Reusable downloaded artifacts should reach write-back, later suites should not run, and the step should retain the failed stage's status and annotation.
- Run a green and a failed suite with an unusable cache or missing job-local repository. The cache fault should produce a warning and preserve the suite result.
- Seed a warm cache containing resolver markers and version metadata. Mutable hardlinks should be detached before Maven runs; write-back should publish artifacts while excluding resolver markers, metadata and partial-download files.
- Exercise a cold cache and a seed prune failure. Both should still reach Maven; an actual copy failure should remain visible in the log.
- Plant a plain single-link `resolver-status.properties` / `x.jar.lastUpdated` directly in `${RUNNER_TEMP}/m2-repo` before the seed body runs. The seed prune must delete both while the host-cache peers stay intact. Restoring `-links +1` to the seed prunes must red the `clears inherited single-link resolver state from the job-local repository` witness.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Head `26960a72d1` merges main `a5fec03684` into `89d3898f4d`; the PR delta is unchanged (the same seven files, 1116 insertions / 198 deletions), and the merged workflow's `.size-baseline` entry is re-recorded to 162545. Earlier measurements below are labeled with the commit they were taken at; the four required suites were re-run after this merge. Prior heads: `a0d162dbcc` (main `90eb13e4c6`), `d0f6312b82` (main `91a6274075`), `7618d49a` (main `fe30b5daaa`).

| Check | Result | Measured at |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| sdk-java-workflow + sdk-java-lock + workflow-size + main-ci-failure-issue-workflow | 505 passed \| 47 skipped (552), re-run after the latest merge | 26960a72d1, local macOS (a0d162dbcc: 502/47) |
| Wider set: six other sdk-java.yml parsers + qwen-triage-workflow | 241 passed \| 0 skipped; 191 passed \| 10 skipped (triage's pre-existing 5 s subprocess timeouts on a tmux-less Mac pass with `--testTimeout=30000`; no test modified) | 26960a72d1, local macOS (a0d162dbcc ten-suite set: 743/47 + 191/10) |
| Maintainer Linux verification: 34 replay cells + author guard suite + 18-row mutation matrix | 61/61 assertions; guard suite 142/142 on Linux; 18/18 mutations killed, no survivors — verdict **merge-ready** (report in the PR thread) | 7618d49a, Linux node:22-bookworm non-root, 2026-10-31 |
| SDK Java (fast) / ubuntu-latest / Java 21 — real self-hosted pool lane | pass, 30m25s | 7618d49a CI |
| SDK Java (full) tier on the real pool — Runtime Broker and Managed Agent MySQL (1h13m), Hosted process fault (1h54m), EventTransport broker / multi-node, Java 11/17/21, Real daemon E2E, Flyway | all pass | 7618d49a CI |
| Six other suites parsing sdk-java.yml (spotbugs-gate, hosted-process-ci, managed-agent-gate-workflow, managed-agent-server-e2e, event-transport-multi-node-ci, event-transport-broker-ci) | 236 passed \| 0 skipped | c7746613ec, local macOS; PR delta unchanged since |
| Mutation: restore `-links +1` at the four seed prunes | Witness red, vitest exit 1 (`inherited single-link marker survived the seed prune: expected true to be false`); fix restored, green. Re-killed on Linux as row m5b at 7618d49a | c7746613ec local macOS; 7618d49a Linux |
| `.size-baseline` sdk-java.yml entry | 162545 = exact `git show HEAD:.github/workflows/sdk-java.yml \| wc -c` (159271 at a0d162dbcc) | 26960a72d1 |
