prs.title: fix(core): headless project-hook trust requires the folder-trust feature
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Unifies settings-file project hooks on a single rule: **they load only with explicit folder trust, in every mode** — interactive TUI, headless one-shot runs, and ACP/SDK embeddings alike. This removes the non-interactive exemption introduced with the first gate, which left the reported proof of concept (a headless one-shot invocation) executable on a fresh default environment. The rule is one predicate at the single load point; the CLI settings layer already drops workspace settings for an undecided folder once the trust feature is enabled, so no separate headless branch is needed. Documentation and integration coverage state the unified contract. The web-shell workspace overview also surfaces trust-withheld hooks: the ACP status serializer now carries the listing's disabled reason, and the overview flags the hooks facet and names the remedy in its tooltip, so the withheld state is visible outside the TUI as well.

## ⚠️ Breaking change

Project hooks declared in a repository's `.qwen/settings.json` no longer execute on a default installation. Previously they ran unconditionally (the reported vulnerability); now every caller must opt in:

- **Interactive users**: enable `security.folderTrust.enabled` and trust the folder (trust dialog / trust store), or grant IDE workspace trust. A startup warning names the remedy when hooks are withheld.
- **Headless / CI**: same requirement; there is no implicit-trust exemption. Automation that legitimately uses repository hooks enables the feature and pre-trusts the directory in its managed home.
- **Embedding platforms (ACP/daemon)**: enable the feature in the platform-managed home settings and record managed directories in the trust store; one `TRUST_PARENT` entry can cover a whole workspace tree. Without this migration, repository-declared hooks stop loading after upgrade — intentionally fail-closed, and the reason this must be called out in release notes.

User-level and system-level hooks are unaffected. `--safe-mode` / `--bare` behavior is unchanged.

## Why it's needed

The external report's proof of concept runs headless (a one-shot prompt with structured output), which fell inside the previous unconditional headless exemption — so on a fresh default environment the reported repository-hook execution still reproduced after the first fix. The unified explicit-trust rule closes that path with the smallest possible surface: one predicate, no mode-specific branches, no dead exemption code. Both Claude Code and Codex gate repository-supplied executables behind an affirmative user decision; Codex additionally exposes an explicit, danger-marked automation bypass flag rather than an implicit exemption — a follow-up direction tracked with the approval-dialog work, not silently built in here.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Reproduce the reporter scenario locally: in a fresh home (no trust file, feature off), run a repository whose settings declare a SessionStart marker hook via a one-shot headless prompt. Before this change the marker is written; after, it is absent. Then enable the folder-trust feature in the home settings and grant the directory in the trust store: the marker is written again, confirming the embedder path. Interactive behavior is unchanged from the previous gate.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — non-UI. Verified locally on this branch's bundle with the reporter's exact invocation (stream-json one-shot): default fresh home → marker absent; feature on + trust-store grant → marker written. Core config suite 1002 passed; tool-hook CLI/ACP integration 14 passed; ACP parity model-error cases passed. The earlier intermediate revision (feature-gated headless exemption) was verified equivalent on all reachable paths before being simplified away.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Local `npm run build && npm run bundle`; vitest for the core config suite and the tool-hook/ACP-parity integration tests against the bundle; the reporter's exact local invocation (stream-json one-shot) as the decisive probe.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: this is a deliberate breaking change (see above). Headless users and embedding platforms must enable the feature and record trust; the reporter-facing default is fail-closed in every mode.
- Not validated / out of scope: Windows/Linux local runs (CI covers them); the approval dialog remains in #14748.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: repository project hooks no longer load without explicit trust in any mode. Migration: set `security.folderTrust.enabled: true` in user/home settings and record the workspace in the trust store (`TRUST_FOLDER`, or one `TRUST_PARENT` for a managed tree). Release notes must carry this prominently.

## Linked Issues

Refs #14746
Follow-up to #16196 and #16182.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

将设置文件项目 hooks 统一为单一规则：**所有模式（交互 TUI、headless 一次性运行、ACP/SDK 嵌入）都只在显式目录授信后加载**。移除了第一轮门引入的非交互豁免——它使报告 PoC（headless 一次性调用）在全新默认环境仍可执行。统一后只有一个谓词、一个加载点，无模式分支；CLI settings 层在功能开启且目录未决定时本就不贡献 workspace settings，无需单独 headless 分支。web-shell 工作区概览同步透出被信任门扣留的 hooks：ACP 状态序列化透传 disabledReason，概览标记 hooks facet 并在 tooltip 指明补救方法，TUI 之外也能看到扣留状态。

## ⚠️ 破坏性变更

默认安装下仓库 `.qwen/settings.json` 的项目 hooks 不再执行（旧行为即漏洞）。所有调用方需显式 opt-in：交互式用户启用 `security.folderTrust.enabled` 并信任目录（或 IDE 授信）；headless/CI 同样要求，无隐式豁免；嵌入平台在其管理的 home settings 启用功能并在信任表记录目录（一条 `TRUST_PARENT` 可覆盖整棵 workspace 树）。不迁移则升级后仓库 hooks 停载——有意 fail-closed，release notes 必须醒目标注。用户级/系统级 hooks 不受影响。

## 为什么需要

外部报告的 PoC 走 headless，落在上一版无条件豁免内——第一轮修复后默认环境仍可复现。统一显式授信规则以最小面堵死该路径：一个谓词、无模式分支、无死代码。Claude Code 与 Codex 均以用户主动决策门控仓库可执行内容；Codex 另提供显式危险标记的自动化 bypass flag 而非隐式豁免——该方向随审批对话框工作跟进，不在本 PR 静默引入。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

本地复刻报告场景：全新 home（无信任文件、功能关），以一次性 headless prompt 运行声明了 SessionStart 标记 hook 的仓库。改动前标记写入；改动后不写入。再在 home settings 启用功能并在信任表授信目录：标记恢复写入，确认嵌入方路径。交互式行为与上一版门一致。

### 证据

N/A —— 非 UI。以报告者原始调用方式（stream-json 一次性）在本分支 bundle 验证：默认全新 home → 无标记；功能开 + 信任表授信 → 写入。core config 1002 通过；tool-hook CLI/ACP 集成 14 通过；ACP parity model-error 通过。中间版本（功能门控的 headless 豁免）已在全部可达路径验证等价后简化删除。

### 测试平台

macOS ✅；Windows/Linux ⚠️（CI 覆盖）。

## 风险与范围

prs.title: fix(web-shell): defer rewind capacity-latch re-open publish past the rebuild commit (#16347)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Defers the capacity-latch re-open React state publish for a rewind (`evictedOldest === false`) by one microtask, so the publish lands after the rewind rebuild has committed instead of inside the truncation callback. The latch's ref fields (`rejectedPage`, `hasMore`, `capacityReached`) still update synchronously, so `loadMore()` gating and other synchronous readers see the reopened latch immediately; only the `setTranscriptHistoryState` publish is deferred. Oldest-first trims keep the fully synchronous path.

## Why it's needed

Main CI failed once on macOS in `daemon/session/DaemonSessionProvider.test.tsx > DaemonSessionProvider > reopens a rejected history page after authoritative rewind with same anchor` (#16347): the reopened latch raced the rewind rebuild, and the transcript came back as `[root-user, root-answer, target-user, target-answer]` instead of `[root-user, root-answer]`. A rewind drops the NEWEST blocks and the rebuild that follows replays the surviving prefix synchronously, so a synchronous publish inside the truncation callback let a concurrently batched same-anchor page append land before the rebuild's prefix on a slow runner.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The failure was a single slow-runner flake, so the strongest local evidence is that the full `DaemonSessionProvider.test.tsx` suite stays green deterministically and the latch re-open contract is preserved. Run from `packages/web-shell`:

```
npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts client/daemon/session/DaemonSessionProvider.test.tsx
```

Expected: 523 passed / 0 failed, including both `reopens a rejected history page after authoritative rewind ...` variants and `drops an in-flight history page when a trim re-anchors pagination mid-fetch`. Reviewers can also inspect the diff: the only behavioral change is the rewind branch's state publish moving to `queueMicrotask`, with ref updates unchanged.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (non-UI change; the observable contract is the test assertion, covered by the run above).

| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   N/A  |

N/A — unit tests only (`vitest` under `packages/web-shell`).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the rewind latch re-open is now visible to React one microtask later; synchronous readers and `loadMore()` gating are unaffected because the ref updates stay synchronous.
- Not validated / out of scope: cannot conclusively prove the once-ever CI flake is eliminated by local green runs alone; the fix targets the specific ordering the flake violated.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #16347

prs.title: fix(managed-agent): prove A3 rewritten command recovery without Hook rerun
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Completes the remaining A3 rewritten-input / Hook-no-rerun half of the G3 Step 3 recovery matrix. It proves that a command input rewritten by a Hook is treated as a new, independently approved step rather than inheriting the previous step's Allow; that completed Hook occurrences and completed command steps replay durable results after restart without physical re-execution; and that an outer skill expanding into two command steps survives a crash between the steps while preserving the second Action's identity and deadline. It adds a packaged failover arm, durable evidence collection, focused regression witnesses, and synchronized English/Chinese design documentation.

## Why it's needed

Issue #14481 tracks recovery gaps where restart could reuse an approval for a different final command input, rerun already-completed Hooks or command effects, or lose the identity of a later command step. These behaviors are safety- and correctness-critical for managed command execution: a rewritten input must not ride on a stale Allow, and durable receipts must be the source of truth for replay. This change closes the A3 gap with real packaged evidence rather than only unit-level assertions.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the new packaged command-rewrite failover arm in the managed-agent harness. The expected observation is a three-generation sequence: generation 1 waits for the first command approval; generation 2 allows the first step, completes it and its PostToolUse occurrence, then crashes when the second approval is requested; generation 3 replays the first step and completed Hook occurrences from durable results without physical rerun, preserves the second Action's ID, creation time, expiry, and input reference, and requires a separate Allow for the second step. The final evidence must show two distinct Actions, one physical execution for each command stage and each completed Hook occurrence, settled command receipts, recorded model traffic, a completed relief Turn, terminal count 2, and reliable close. A focused TypeScript regression can be run with `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/hosted-command-step-hook-recovery.test.ts`. The merged branch passes local TypeScript build/typecheck and contract/meta suites; full Java and Hosted CI gates are pending on this PR.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — non-UI recovery and evidence changes. A separate PR comment contains the packaged run report, evidence hashes, local gate results, and CI-pending caveats.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local macOS TypeScript tests, build, and typecheck; real packaged managed-agent harness on Linux with Temurin 21, MySQL 8.4, registered storage, and delegated cgroup. Acceptance remains pending until the required CI gates pass on the merged revision.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Recovery now distinguishes extension-owned Hook/command replay from native approval continuation; incorrect gating could either re-execute durable effects or block legitimate recovery. The added packaged arm and regression witnesses pin both sides.
- Not validated / out of scope: Full post-merge Java/Hosted CI suites are not yet green. Local full ESLint was OOM-limited on this host, so lint was run partitioned with generated build outputs ignored. R2 remains out of scope.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: No public API migration. Action ID validation now accepts the command-step Action grammar alongside the legacy tool approval grammar; stored development catalogs should follow the module's baseline schema policy.

Design documentation: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/14481-a3-rewritten-hook/docs/design/2026-11-01-hosted-a3-rewritten-hook.md) / [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/14481-a3-rewritten-hook/docs/design/2026-11-01-hosted-a3-rewritten-hook.zh-CN.md). Both versions are complete and synchronized, including decisions, constraints, acceptance criteria, and follow-up work.

## Linked Issues

Refs #14481 (G3 Step 3 A3 rewritten-input / Hook-no-rerun recovery). This PR does not auto-close the tracker.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

完成 G3 Step 3 恢复矩阵中剩余的 A3「改写输入 / Hook 不重跑」半边。它证明：被 Hook 改写后的命令输入会作为新的、需要独立批准的步骤处理，而不是继承上一步的 Allow；已完成的 Hook occurrence 和已完成的命令步骤在重启后通过持久化结果重放，不会物理重跑；外层 skill 展开成两个命令步骤时，在两步之间崩溃仍能保留第二个 Action 的身份和截止时间。它新增了一个打包故障支路、持久化证据采集、聚焦回归见证，以及同步的英文/中文设计文档。

## 为什么需要它

Issue #14481 跟踪了一些恢复缺口：重启后可能把批准复用于不同的最终命令输入、重跑已经完成的 Hook 或命令副作用，或者丢失后续命令步骤的身份。这些行为对受管命令执行的安全性和正确性至关重要：改写后的输入不能搭上旧的 Allow，持久化回执必须作为重放的唯一事实来源。这个变更用真实打包证据关闭 A3 缺口，而不仅依赖单元级断言。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

### 证据（Before & After）

N/A — 非 UI 的恢复与证据变更。单独的 PR 评论包含打包运行报告、证据哈希、本地门禁结果和 CI 待通过说明。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### 环境（可选）

本地 macOS TypeScript 测试、构建和类型检查；Linux 上的真实打包 managed-agent harness，使用 Temurin 21、MySQL 8.4、注册存储和委托 cgroup。在所需 CI 门禁于合并修订上通过之前，验收仍为 pending。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：恢复逻辑现在区分扩展拥有的 Hook/命令重放与原生批准 continuation；错误门控可能导致重跑持久化副作用，或阻塞合法恢复。新增打包支路和回归见证钉住了两侧。

prs.title: fix(sdk): resolve tool name from _meta.toolLifecycle so web-shell stops showing unknown Tool
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The daemon UI normalizer now treats `_meta.toolLifecycle.toolName` as the last source when it resolves a tool call's name. The chain stays ordered — an explicit `title`, a top-level `toolName`/`name`, and `_meta.toolName`/`_meta.name` all still win; the lifecycle name is only consulted when none of them is present.

## Why it's needed

In the web-shell session view, every tool call made by a foreground subagent is labelled "unknown Tool". The frames that carry those calls name the tool in exactly one place: `_meta.toolLifecycle.toolName` (emitted by `createTranscriptToolLifecycleUpdate` in `packages/acp-bridge/src/transcript-replay.ts`). The normalizer never read that field, so the projected block had no `toolName` and fell back to the generic `'Tool'` title, and the web-shell adapter's `resolveToolCallName(block.toolName, block.rawInput) || 'unknown'` rendered the pair as "unknown Tool". The tools themselves ran correctly — only the labels were lost.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the SDK tests for the projection path:

```
cd packages/sdk-typescript
npx vitest run test/daemon-ui-transcript.test.ts test/tool-lifecycle.test.ts \
  test/unit/daemon-transcript-projection.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false
```

The new case feeds one `tool_call_update` whose only name carrier is `_meta.toolLifecycle.toolName: 'read_file'`, projects it into the transcript, and asserts the resulting block matches `{ kind: 'tool', toolName: 'read_file', title: 'Tool' }` — the name lands on `toolName` only; the human-readable title is deliberately left untouched. Before the change that block was `{ kind: 'tool', title: 'Tool' }` with no name, i.e. exactly the input that produces "unknown Tool" downstream. A second case pins the precedence: an explicit `title` and `_meta.toolName` still beat the lifecycle name.

The existing case `tool lifecycle > does not create or overwrite Chat cards for metadata-only updates` was rewritten for this behaviour: pure `_meta.toolLifecycle` frames (no status/content/title/kind) are now forwarded as `nameOnly` events, so the reducer can name an existing block by `toolCallId` and never creates a card from them. Every tool call therefore contributes two extra events (started/ended) to the shared daemon stream, and consumers that render `tool.update` must ignore `nameOnly` events. The silent-shell heartbeat drop for `shellProgress`/`subagentProgress` frames is unchanged.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before (reproduced on the base commit with the new test in place):

```
FAIL  test/daemon-ui-transcript.test.ts > tool name carried only by the lifecycle metadata > names the tool block from _meta.toolLifecycle.toolName
AssertionError: expected { id: 'tool-1', kind: 'tool', …(8) } to match object { kind: 'tool', …(2) }
  {
    "kind": "tool",
-   "title": "read_file",
-   "toolName": "read_file",
+   "title": "Tool",
  }
```

After:

```
 ✓ test/daemon-ui-transcript.test.ts (38 tests) 70ms
 ✓ test/tool-lifecycle.test.ts (5 tests) 29ms
 ✓ test/unit/daemon-transcript-projection.test.ts (23 tests) 71ms
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  66 passed (66)
```

Browser screenshot: N/A. This is a label/projection defect, and the two visual paths to it are both closed on this machine — the repo pins a Playwright browser revision that the local install cannot provision, and there is no live `qwen serve` session with a foreground subagent to attach to. The evidence above is the assertion the browser would render from: `toolName === 'read_file'` instead of `'unknown'`.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

Linux: unit tests listed above. macOS/Windows: not run locally; this is a pure projection change with no platform-specific code, so CI covers it.

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit tests only.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a false tool name could be picked up if some other producer stuffed an unrelated string into `_meta.toolLifecycle.toolName`. The field is only written by the replay/emitter pair that uses it as the canonical tool name, and the fallback sits last in the chain, so explicit values always win.
- Not validated / out of scope: a browser-level screenshot (see the Evidence note for why). The projection that produces the label is covered by the tests above: a frame named only by its lifecycle metadata now projects the real tool name instead of `'Tool'`.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #16301

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

daemon UI normalizer 解析工具调用名字时，把 `_meta.toolLifecycle.toolName` 追加为最后一个来源。优先级不变：显式 `title`、顶层 `toolName`/`name`、`_meta.toolName`/`_meta.name` 仍然优先，只有它们都缺失时才读生命周期里的名字。

## 为什么需要

web-shell 会话视图里，前台 subagent 发起的每一个工具调用都显示为 "unknown Tool"。这类调用帧只在 `_meta.toolLifecycle.toolName` 带名字（由 `packages/acp-bridge/src/transcript-replay.ts` 的 `createTranscriptToolLifecycleUpdate` 产出），而 normalizer 从不读这个字段，于是投影出的 block 没有 `toolName`，title 兜底成 `'Tool'`，web-shell 适配层 `resolveToolCallName(...) || 'unknown'` 就渲染成 "unknown Tool"。工具本身执行是正常的，只是标签丢了。

## 复核方式

跑 `packages/sdk-typescript` 下三个测试文件（命令见上方）。新增用例构造一个只靠 `_meta.toolLifecycle.toolName: 'read_file'` 带名字的 `tool_call_update`，断言投影出的 block 是 `{ kind: 'tool', toolName: 'read_file', title: 'Tool' }` —— 名字只写进 `toolName`，人类可读的 title 刻意不动；修复前该 block 是 `{ kind: 'tool', title: 'Tool' }`（没有名字）。另外，纯 `_meta.toolLifecycle` 帧现在被转发成 `nameOnly` 事件，不再丢弃。第二个用例钉住优先级：显式 `title` 与 `_meta.toolName` 仍然压过生命周期名字。

原有 `tool lifecycle > does not create or overwrite Chat cards for metadata-only updates` 未改动且仍通过：纯 `_meta.toolLifecycle` 帧（无 status/content/title/kind）继续被丢弃，silent-shell 心跳行为不变，丢弃守卫没有被放宽。

## 风险

只在解析链尾部追加一个名字来源；显式值优先级不变；没有平台相关代码。UI 截图 N/A：本机 Playwright 浏览器修订被 pin 住无法安装，也没有可挂接的 `qwen serve` 前台 subagent 会话，证据以投影层红/绿断言为主。

Fixes #16301

prs.title: feat(mods): let a Mod submit a prompt of its own in headless runs
prs.body:
## What this PR does

In headless runs, a Mod can now submit a prompt of its own with `$.prompt.submit({ text, asUser? })`. The prompt starts a turn of its own once the run is idle, after the turn that is running.

- **The hooks hear it first.** The call raises `prompt.submit` through every hook except the caller and the hooks it runs beneath, with `origin` `{ kind: 'plugin', name }`. They can rewrite it, attach context or drop it, as for a typed prompt. The call resolves once the hooks have answered and the prompt is queued, to `{ text, context?, origin }` or `{ drop }`.
- **The model is told who sent it.** Unless the Mod passes `asUser: true`, the text goes inside a `<qwen:mod-prompt mod="…">` block, followed by a line saying the Mod sent it while the session was idle and the person did not type it. A closing marker inside the text cannot end the block.
- **It is a prompt like any other.** UserPromptSubmit hears it, its turn raises `turn.start` and `turn.complete`, and it counts toward the session turn limit. `@` references in it are not read.
- **The transcript says it is the Mod's.** It is recorded with a provenance of its own, `mod_prompt`, and the Mod's name, so Goal evidence and the session-agent view never take it for the person's words.
- **Loops stop.** The Mods' prompts start at most 8 turns before the person sends a prompt; past that a call resolves to a drop and a line says why.
- **Other hosts.** The Ink and OpenTUI terminals do not run these prompts yet. There, `$.session.version()` does not list the method, and a call resolves to a drop without any hook hearing it. They come in the next two steps.

The user guide and the design document (English and Chinese, §9 and its decisions) describe the call, the frame, the record and the limit.

## Why it's needed

`$.prompt.submit` is how a Mod wakes a quiet session: a follow-up after a turn, a reminder, a check a background job asks for. Qwen Code rejected the call with `Mod API not supported: $.prompt.submit`, so the hook that made it failed and the follow-up never ran.

The call resolves when its prompt is queued rather than when its turn starts. The Mod worker runs one dispatch at a time and waits for a dispatch's calls before ending it, so a call that waited for its turn would hold up the very hook dispatch that keeps the session from being idle. Resolving once the hooks have answered matches what `next(e)` already does for a typed prompt; the user guide lists this as a difference.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Install a Mod whose `turn.complete` hook calls `await $.prompt.submit({ text: 'List the TODOs you just mentioned.' })` once and logs the result, with a `prompt.submit` hook that attaches the context `Mod context: from <origin.kind>`. Run `qwen -p "Look for TODOs" --output-format json` against a model.
  - Expected: two turns. The second request's last user message is the framed prompt, followed by the hidden context block with `Mod context: from plugin`. The log shows the call resolving to `{text, context, origin: {kind: 'plugin', name}}`.
  - On `main`, the run has one turn and the Mod's hook fails on `$.prompt.submit`.
- A Mod that submits at every `turn.complete` stops after 8 Mod turns, with the line `$.prompt.submit refused: the Mods have started 8 turns since the last prompt from the person`.
- With `asUser: true`, the second request's last user message is the bare text.
- `npx vitest run src/mods/ src/services/chatRecordingService.test.ts` in `packages/core`; `npx vitest run src/nonInteractiveCli.test.ts src/services/` in `packages/cli`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Headless JSON runs against a loopback OpenAI-compatible fixture, with the Mods above installed through `qwen extensions install`. Before is `main` at `776331b1f9`, After is this PR. Both bundles were built locally.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$.session.version().qwen.methods` lists `prompt.submit` | no | yes |
| A `turn.complete` hook submits once: turns | 1 (the hook fails on `$.prompt.submit`) | 2 |
| Second request's last user message | none | `<qwen:mod-prompt mod="followup-mod">` … `</qwen:mod-prompt>` with the line naming the Mod, then `<qwen:user-prompt-submit-context>Mod context: from plugin</qwen:user-prompt-submit-context>` |
| What the call resolved to | — | `{"text":"List the TODOs you just mentioned.","context":["Mod context: from plugin"],"origin":{"kind":"plugin","name":"followup-mod"}}` |
| `turn.start` heard | `Look for TODOs` | `Look for TODOs`, `List the TODOs you just mentioned.` |
| Transcript records | `real_user` | `real_user` for the person's prompt; `mod_prompt` with `"mod": "followup-mod"` for the Mod's |
| A hook submits at every `turn.complete` | 1 turn | 9 turns (the person's and 8 of the Mod's), then `$.prompt.submit refused: the Mods have started 8 turns since the last prompt from the person` |
| `asUser: true` | 1 turn | 2 turns; the second request's last user message is `Say done` |

Automated checks:

- `packages/core`: `src/mods/` 393 tests (1 skipped); `client.test.ts`, `chatRecordingService.test.ts`, `src/goals/` and `src/agents/session-agents/` pass, 21 files, 1361 tests.
- `packages/cli`: `nonInteractiveCli.test.ts`, `src/services/` and `src/nonInteractive/` pass, 56 files, 1584 tests (1 skipped).
- 23 targeted mutants of the change are all caught: the host gate, the queueing and its refusal, `asUser`, the call's shape, the method listing, the limit and its reset, the session check, the frame and its escape, the headless options, both loops' turn events, the batching, the record's provenance and the Mod's name.
- `tsc --noEmit` for core and cli, ESLint and Prettier pass on the changed files.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Linux, Node 24.21.0, bundles built with `npm run bundle`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a Mod can now start turns, which costs requests. The 8-turn limit bounds a runaway hook, and the person's next prompt resets it. A headless run that used to end after its prompt now also runs the turns its Mods queue.
- Not validated / out of scope: the Ink and OpenTUI terminals, which come next, including how they show a Mod's prompt and how a resumed session shows its record. `attachments` are not taken. A stream-json session was covered by unit tests only.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. A transcript record gains the provenance value `mod_prompt` and the payload field `mod`; readers that look for `real_user` treat it as not the person's.

Design document: [English](docs/design/2026-10-30-mod-prompt-submit.md) · [简体中文](docs/design/2026-10-30-mod-prompt-submit.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Part of #13749.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

在 headless 运行中，Mod 现在可以用 `$.prompt.submit({ text, asUser? })` 提交自己的提示。这条提示会在运行空闲后、正在运行的回合之后，作为独立的回合运行。

- **hook 先听到它。** 调用以 `origin` `{ kind: 'plugin', name }` 触发 `prompt.submit`，经过除调用者及其外层 hook 之外的全部 hook。它们可以像对待用户输入的提示一样改写、附加上下文或丢弃。hook 答复、提示排队后调用返回 `{ text, context?, origin }` 或 `{ drop }`。
- **模型会被告知是谁发的。** 除非 Mod 传了 `asUser: true`，文本会放进 `<qwen:mod-prompt mod="…">` 块，块后有一行说明：该 Mod 在会话空闲时发来这条消息，用户没有输入它。文本里的闭合标记无法提前结束这个块。
- **它和其他提示一样。** UserPromptSubmit 会听到它，它的回合会触发 `turn.start` 和 `turn.complete`，并计入会话回合上限。其中的 `@` 引用不会被读取。
- **transcript 标明它属于 Mod。** 它以单独的来源 `mod_prompt` 记录，并带上 Mod 的名字，因此 Goal 证据和会话代理视图都不会把它当成用户本人的话。
- **循环会停下。** 在用户发送提示之前，Mod 的提示最多启动 8 个回合；超过之后调用返回 drop，并有一行说明原因。
- **其他宿主。** Ink 和 OpenTUI 终端暂不运行这类提示。在那里 `$.session.version()` 不列出该方法，调用直接返回 drop，不经过任何 hook。它们在接下来的两步中实现。

用户指南和设计文档（中英文 §9 及其设计决策）说明了调用方式、框文、记录方式和上限。

## 为什么需要

`$.prompt.submit` 是 Mod 唤醒空闲会话的方式：回合结束后的跟进、提醒、后台任务要求的检查。此前 Qwen Code 以 `Mod API not supported: $.prompt.submit` 拒绝这个调用，发起调用的 hook 失败，跟进也就不会运行。

调用在提示排队时返回，而不是在回合开始时返回。Mod worker 一次只运行一个分发，并在分发结束前等待其中的调用；如果调用等到回合开始才返回，它就会拖住正让会话无法空闲的那个 hook 分发。在 hook 答复之后返回，与 `next(e)` 对用户输入的提示已有的行为一致；用户指南把这一点列为差异。

## 验证方式

- 安装一个 Mod：它的 `turn.complete` hook 调用一次 `await $.prompt.submit({ text: 'List the TODOs you just mentioned.' })` 并记录结果，另有一个 `prompt.submit` hook 附加上下文 `Mod context: from <origin.kind>`。对模型运行 `qwen -p "Look for TODOs" --output-format json`。
  - 预期：两个回合。第二个请求的最后一条用户消息是带框文的提示，后面是含 `Mod context: from plugin` 的隐藏上下文块。日志显示调用返回 `{text, context, origin: {kind: 'plugin', name}}`。
  - 在 `main` 上只有一个回合，Mod 的 hook 在 `$.prompt.submit` 处失败。
- 每次 `turn.complete` 都提交的 Mod 在启动 8 个 Mod 回合后停止，并显示 `$.prompt.submit refused: the Mods have started 8 turns since the last prompt from the person`。
- 带 `asUser: true` 时，第二个请求的最后一条用户消息是原文。
- 在 `packages/core` 中运行 `npx vitest run src/mods/ src/services/chatRecordingService.test.ts`；在 `packages/cli` 中运行 `npx vitest run src/nonInteractiveCli.test.ts src/services/`。

## 前后对比

对回环的 OpenAI 兼容 fixture 跑 headless JSON，上述 Mod 通过 `qwen extensions install` 安装。Before 是 `main` 的 `776331b1f9`，After 是本 PR，两个 bundle 都在本地构建。

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$.session.version().qwen.methods` 是否列出 `prompt.submit` | 否 | 是 |
| `turn.complete` hook 提交一次：回合数 | 1（hook 在 `$.prompt.submit` 处失败） | 2 |
| 第二个请求的最后一条用户消息 | 无 | `<qwen:mod-prompt mod="followup-mod">` … `</qwen:mod-prompt>` 加上写明 Mod 的说明行，之后是 `<qwen:user-prompt-submit-context>Mod context: from plugin</qwen:user-prompt-submit-context>` |
| 调用的返回值 | — | `{"text":"List the TODOs you just mentioned.","context":["Mod context: from plugin"],"origin":{"kind":"plugin","name":"followup-mod"}}` |
| `turn.start` 听到的 | `Look for TODOs` | `Look for TODOs`、`List the TODOs you just mentioned.` |
| transcript 记录 | `real_user` | 用户的提示为 `real_user`；Mod 的提示为 `mod_prompt`，带 `"mod": "followup-mod"` |
| 每次 `turn.complete` 都提交的 hook | 1 个回合 | 9 个回合（用户的 1 个加 Mod 的 8 个），之后显示 `$.prompt.submit refused: the Mods have started 8 turns since the last prompt from the person` |
| `asUser: true` | 1 个回合 | 2 个回合；第二个请求的最后一条用户消息是 `Say done` |

自动化检查：

- `packages/core`：`src/mods/` 393 个测试（1 个跳过）；`client.test.ts`、`chatRecordingService.test.ts`、`src/goals/` 和 `src/agents/session-agents/` 通过，21 个文件 1361 个测试。
- `packages/cli`：`nonInteractiveCli.test.ts`、`src/services/` 和 `src/nonInteractive/` 通过，56 个文件 1584 个测试（1 个跳过）。
- 针对本改动的 23 个变异全部被捕获：宿主开关、排队及其拒绝、`asUser`、调用形状、方法列表、上限及其重置、会话检查、框文及其转义、headless 选项、两条循环的回合事件、批处理、记录的来源和 Mod 名字。
- core 和 cli 的 `tsc --noEmit`，以及改动文件的 ESLint 和 Prettier 均通过。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：Mod 现在可以启动回合，这会消耗请求。8 个回合的上限限制了失控的 hook，用户的下一条提示会重新计数。以前在提示结束后就退出的 headless 运行，现在还会运行 Mod 排队的回合。

- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。transcript 记录新增来源值 `mod_prompt` 和负载字段 `mod`；查找 `real_user` 的读取方会把它当作不是用户本人的。

prs.title: feat(managed-agent): enable external workspace execution
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Builds the external Workspace execution slice on top of the materialization prerequisite in #15654. The branch now includes live `hosted-workspace-external-files/1` admission, bounded and single-query Workspace discovery, authoritative registration checks, stable lifecycle refusal classification, and receipt-backed release for external Runtime bindings. The separate materialization operation still creates metadata only; it does not allocate storage or start a worker.

This revision closes the remaining review gaps in that execution slice: registration decode failures, including field-type failures, now resolve to a permanent `409 workspace_unavailable`; a malformed registration disables only its own Workspace during batch discovery; saved-provider shutdown is classified as retryable `503`; attachment actor lookup fails closed on zero, multiple, or null rows; and external lifecycle authorization preserves the exact permanent fence response.

## Why it's needed

#15512 needs a durable link from registered external storage to a Workspace that can be discovered and used safely. A Session must not become executable through a partially wired path, and one corrupt storage row must not hide every healthy Workspace on the page. The same branch also needs terminal close and recovery paths to distinguish permanent identity failures from provider availability failures.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

On an isolated fresh catalog, register external storage using the loopback operator credential, materialize its alias with an owner, and verify that only the owner can discover it. Exercise Session creation after the external-files gates and a Harness lifecycle capability are available. Confirm that prompts can run, file tools remain within the external profile, and close/recovery uses the receipt-backed ownership transition without destroying a shared placement.

For the query and failure paths, corrupt one registration and confirm only that Workspace loses Session-creation eligibility while another Workspace remains visible. Confirm that an admission attempt against the corrupted Workspace returns `409 workspace_unavailable` with `retryable=false`. Shut down the saved external provider during drain-capability checks and confirm a retryable `503`. Submit a non-current lifecycle authority to the external attachment path and confirm `409 workspace_lifecycle_claim_fenced` with `retryable=false`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before this revision, a field-type error while decoding an opaque-persisted registration could escape as a mapper failure, batch discovery could fail as a whole when one row was malformed, and a shut-down saved provider was conflated with a permanent binding conflict. The candidate maps these cases explicitly, uses one registration batch read rather than per-row JDBC work inside a mapper, and keeps external lifecycle fences non-retryable.

Earlier evidence in this stack covered materialization, registration replay, and isolated MySQL validation. The newest commit was checked statically and through the repository's CI gates; no local test, build, or typecheck was run under the requested execution policy.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--- | :---: |
| macOS | ✅ static review and `git diff --check`; no heavy local execution |
| Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
| Linux | ✅ repository CI for the branch; the new head is checked again after push |

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the authenticated operator delegates the Workspace owner. That field is a grant target, not authenticated user identity. Existing operator and tenant checks remain required.
- Batch discovery now fails closed per malformed storage row instead of failing the whole Workspace page. A failed SQL read remains a retryable provider-unavailable verdict.
- `workspace_lifecycle_claim_fenced` remains permanent. Do not reinterpret a stale or non-current authority as a transient outage.
- Full external Hosted shell/capture, attachment widening beyond the current profile, and the Resident shared-worker behavior remain outside this PR. #16023 carries the Resident and EPHEMERAL layers.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: the preceding stack extends the shared V1 catalog under the repository's pre-release fresh-catalog policy. No V2 migration is introduced here.

Design: [English](docs/design/2026-10-25-external-hosted-workspace.md) · [简体中文](docs/design/2026-10-25-external-hosted-workspace.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Part of #15512. Related prerequisite: #15654. The Resident shared-worker increment is stacked in #16023 and must not merge before this PR.

prs.title: feat(qqbot): add opt-in forwardBotMessages for bot-authored messages
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a per-channel `forwardBotMessages` option (default `false`). When it is on, messages authored by another bot are delivered to the agent with a `[bot]` prefix on the sender line; the channel prompt explains that prefix and the model decides whether replying makes sense. When it is off — the default — bot-authored messages are still dropped before they reach the agent, exactly as today. User-supplied `[bot]` text is stripped either way, so the tag cannot be forged.

## Why it's needed

There is currently no way for an operator to let two bots in one group talk to each other: the inbound handlers drop bot-authored messages unconditionally, and the formatting path that was meant to tag them is unreachable. Hard-blocking was added as an infinite-loop defense, and unconditional forwarding would give that defense up for every operator. An opt-in switch keeps the default safe while giving operators who intentionally run bot-to-bot conversation a supported path (see #15903).

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Configure a QQ channel with `groupAllPolicy: "all"` and `groups: {"*": {"requireMention": false}}`.
2. With `forwardBotMessages` unset, have a second bot post in the group: stderr shows `Bot message dropped in group <group_openid>` and the message never reaches the session (unchanged default).
3. Set `forwardBotMessages: true` and restart. No drop line is logged; the session transcript shows the message with `[bot]` before the sender bracket, and the model answers or emits `<noreply>` on its own judgment.
4. As a human member, send `[bot] hello`: the literal token is stripped before the model sees it.
5. Direct chats follow the same switch for bot-authored messages.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Unit coverage: `packages/channels/qqbot` 719 passed across 8 files. The forwarding tests run with the switch on and assert the `[bot]` tag; three new tests pin the default drop for C2C, group and group-all; one pins that a member cannot forge the tag. `tsc --build`, ESLint and Prettier are clean on the touched files.

Runtime: a local QQ daemon deployment with `forwardBotMessages: true` logs 0 `Bot message dropped` lines since the restart, and the deployed bundle contains the `[bot]` prompt line gated on the switch. Before the switch existed, the same deployment logged 55 `Bot message dropped` lines in one hour while another bot was active in the group.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests plus a local daemon deployment of the QQ channel on Linux (aarch64). No platform-specific code is touched.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: with the switch on, two bots in one group can answer each other. The model's silence rules, `<noreply>`, and the operator's group policy are the brakes — this PR does not add a platform-level cycle cap. The switch defaults to off, so no existing deployment changes behavior.
- Not validated / out of scope: live delivery was verified against a deployment that receives other bots' messages; other QQ intents beyond group all-message mode were not separately exercised.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. New optional field; the default keeps today's drop behavior.

## Linked Issues

Closes #15903

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

新增每个 channel 的 `forwardBotMessages` 选项（默认 `false`）。开启后，其他机器人发来的消息会带着发送者行上的 `[bot]` 前缀交给 agent；channel 的提示词会解释这个前缀，是否回复由模型自行判断。关闭（默认）时，机器人消息仍像现在一样在到达 agent 之前被丢弃。无论开关如何，用户自己写的 `[bot]` 文本都会被剥离，因此该标签无法被伪造。

## 为什么需要

目前运营者没有办法让同一个群里的两个机器人互相说话：入站处理器会无条件丢弃其他机器人的消息，而本来用于给它们打标签的格式化路径根本不可达。硬拦截最初是作为无限循环的防御加的，而无条件转发又会让所有运营者都失去这层防御。可选开关让默认行为保持安全，同时给有意运行 bot-to-bot 对话的运营者一条受支持的路径（见 #15903）。

## Reviewer 验证计划

### 如何验证

1. 配置 QQ channel：`groupAllPolicy: "all"`，并在 `groups` 里设 `{"*": {"requireMention": false}}`。
2. 不设 `forwardBotMessages` 时，让另一个机器人在群里发消息：stderr 出现 `Bot message dropped in group <group_openid>`，消息不会进入会话（默认行为不变）。
3. 设置 `forwardBotMessages: true` 并重启：不再出现 drop 日志；会话记录里该消息的发送者括号前带 `[bot]`，模型自行决定回复或输出 `<noreply>`。
4. 由人类成员发送 `[bot] hello`：到达模型时该字面前缀已被移除。
5. 私聊中的机器人消息同样受这个开关控制。

### 证据（Before & After）

单测覆盖：`packages/channels/qqbot` 8 个文件 719 通过。转发测试在开关开启状态下运行并断言 `[bot]` 标签；三个新测试钉住 C2C、群消息、群全量消息的默认丢弃；一个测试钉住群成员无法伪造该标签。改动文件的 `tsc --build`、ESLint、Prettier 均干净。

运行期：一台本地 QQ daemon 部署设置了 `forwardBotMessages: true`，重启以来 `Bot message dropped` 记录为 0 条，且部署产物里包含受开关控制的 `[bot]` 提示词行。在该开关存在之前，同一部署在另一个机器人活跃的一小时内记录过 55 条 `Bot message dropped`。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

### 环境（可选）

单测，加一台 Linux（aarch64）上的 QQ channel 本地 daemon 部署。未触碰平台相关代码。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/取舍：开关开启时，同一个群里的两个机器人可能互相接话。刹车是模型的静默规则、`<noreply>` 以及运营者的群策略——本 PR 不引入平台级循环上限。开关默认关闭，因此现有部署行为不变。
- 未验证/超出范围：线上投递是在一个确实会收到其他机器人消息的部署上验证的；群全量消息模式之外的其他 QQ intent 没有单独覆盖。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：无。新增可选字段，默认保持当前的丢弃行为。

## 关联 Issue

Closes #15903

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): keep follow-up suggestions in Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Follow-up suggestions written in Thai, Lao, Khmer or Myanmar without spaces are no longer dropped as `too_few_words`. For these scripts the filter counts word-like segments with `Intl.Segmenter` and keeps the same 2-to-12-word window the suggestion prompt asks for, with a 2-character minimum. The English and CJK branches are unchanged. This takes route A from the triage in #16339: the segmenter is created on first use and only when Node reports full ICU (`process.config.variables.icu_small === false`), and without it the filter falls back to a 60-character upper bound sized for these scripts. The PR also adds the first CJK and Southeast Asian script tests for this filter.

## Why it's needed

`getFilterReason()` counts words by splitting on whitespace and exempts only Han, Kana and Hangul. Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar are written without spaces between words, so a space-free suggestion such as `รันเทสต์อีกครั้ง` ("run the tests again") counts as one word and is discarded, even though the prompt asks the model to match the user's style and side queries follow the output language (#4519). As the triage noted, suggestions that contain a space or a Latin token already pass, so the affected case is space-free suggestions in these scripts. For those, the existing `> 12 words` check can never fire either, so the segment count also supplies the missing upper bound.

I chose the segmenter over a plain character bound because Thai words are several characters long and vary a lot in length: a bound tuned for Han would reject normal 7-word Thai suggestions of 31 to 40 characters. The ICU guard follows the triage: this filter is exported from core and runs on daemon, SDK and non-interactive paths that the CLI's `icu-check.ts` probe never covers, and a small-icu build can crash in `segment()` (#11747). Checking `icu_small` avoids calling the segmenter at all on such builds, rather than relying on a try/catch that cannot catch a native crash. A host that repairs small-icu with `--icu-data-dir` uses the character fallback, which is the conservative choice.

## Reviewer Test Plan

prs.title: fix(channels): keep GitHub notifications unread on transient thread errors
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When the GitHub channel reads a notification's thread — its comments, its issue events, or the issue/PR itself for a first-contact body — and GitHub fails transiently (a 5xx, a network error, or a rate limit), the channel now leaves the notification unread and keeps the poll cursor where it was, so the next poll reads that thread again. A permanent answer, such as a 404 for a deleted issue or a 403 from a SAML-protected organization, still skips the thread immediately. A rate limit or a credential failure stops that poll and holds the window until GitHub answers again. A held window is read again from the start on every poll, as before. A notification listed again at or before the cursor (its mark-as-read did not apply) belongs to a window that already committed, so a 5xx reading it neither holds the window nor spends the budget. The hold for 5xx failures is bounded per window: on the 30th poll of a window that sees one (about 30 minutes at the default interval, plus the in-call retries), the threads that still fail are skipped and the window is marked read, so threads that keep failing — alone or in turn — cannot hold back mark-as-read indefinitely. These failures are now recorded in the Channel event timeline: a failed row when a thread starts failing and on every tenth failing poll, and a skipped row when the channel gives up; a failure while one of the thread's own tasks is unfinished is a failed row too, since that task holds the window and the thread is read again. Because a held window re-reads every thread on each poll, rows that would only repeat — a permanent failure, a rate limit, the `duplicate` or `mention_required` skip of a re-read comment — are written once per window (a rate limit on its first and every tenth poll). The first-contact path, which used to swallow its own fetch failures, follows the same rule. A secondary rate limit that arrives as a bare 403 (no `retry-after`, quota left) is recognised by GitHub's message, so it holds the window rather than being skipped; the PR watch pass recognises it the same way and stops, instead of sending one rejected request per watched PR.

## Why it's needed

The poll loop caught a per-thread error, logged "skipping", and moved on — but the same poll then marked every listed notification read and advanced the cursor past it. Because comments are only read inside the cursor window, a GitHub hiccup of about three seconds on one thread (three failed in-call attempts) lost that thread's @mention permanently: no reply, no retry, no dead-letter, and no timeline row. This was found while driving the real daemon through a set of GitHub scenarios, and reproduces there (below).

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Make one thread's comment listing fail with a 5xx for all three in-call attempts and then recover: the mention should be answered on the next poll, and the notification should stay unread (no mark-as-read, cursor unchanged) until then.
- Make a thread fail with a 404, or with a 403 from an organization's SAML enforcement: the poll should still mark notifications read and advance, with a skipped `github_api_error` row in the Channel event timeline.
- Keep one thread failing with a 5xx: other threads keep being answered meanwhile, and on the 30th poll the failing thread is skipped and the window is marked read. The same holds when two threads fail on alternate polls.
- A first-contact issue whose body mentions the bot, with the issue fetch failing transiently once, should be answered on the next poll.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Unit: `packages/channels/github` 516/516 (476 in `GithubAdapter.test.ts`), with 45 cases in the new `transient per-thread GitHub errors` group, a PR watch case, and three updated ones (the old "marks everything read even on failure" contract now applies to permanent failures only; two existing cases relied on an unmocked comment listing whose error used to be swallowed and now give it an empty answer). Each of these mutants is killed:

- dropping the cursor hold, or the shared-failure stop;
- budgeting per thread instead of per window, never spending the budget, not resetting it at commit, or letting rate-limited polls spend it;
- treating every error or every 403 as transient, or dropping either secondary-limit wording;
- swallowing first-contact errors;
- journaling every poll, or never reporting the shared counter;
- not deduplicating the `duplicate` / `mention_required` / skip rows, or not clearing them at commit;
- removing the bound on the once-per-window keys, storing every failure count past its bound, or reporting a thread whose count does not fit on every poll;
- carrying the hold count across a restart, or dropping its initial value;
- dropping the secondary-limit wording from the PR watch pass;
- reporting a failure `skipped` while the thread's own task holds the window, or `failed` when only another thread's task, a settled task or one out of attempts is left, or under the skip row's key;
- skipping a thread on a held poll after it read cleanly, failed with a 404, or failed while stale (a first-contact body, a same-second comment, a momentary 404 and a late notification would each be lost);
- letting a stale notification hold the window, spending the budget without a window to commit, or resetting it before mark-as-read succeeds;
- dropping the repository from the thread key.

E2E on a real `qwen serve` daemon with its channel worker and Octokit, pointed at a local GitHub REST fake (notifications with unread/`last_read_at` semantics, second-precision timestamps, fault injection) and a scripted model. Scenario: an allowlisted user @mentions the bot on a thread whose comment listing returns 500 three times in one poll; a control thread fails twice.

Before (main at `f217a8e5d9`; its channel code is identical to this PR's base):

```
faulted thread: bot replies 0, notification unread=false (marked read), timeline rows 0
stderr: [Channel:gh-main] API error processing issue:5, skipping: fault
control thread (2 failures, recovered by the in-call retry): bot replies 1
```

After (this branch, re-run on `fbf47f9186`):

```
faulted thread: bot replies 1, timeline rows 5
stderr: [Channel:gh-main] API error processing issue:6 (1/30), keeping it unread for the next poll: fault
control thread: bot replies 1
```

The other reliability scenarios (rate-limited reply persisted as pending and posted once after restart, ambiguous 502 not re-posted, notifications outage catch-up, asynchronous 202 mark-as-read, SIGKILL mid-turn recovery) and the basic dispatch scenarios (mention, first contact, review request, assignment, aggregation with `<no-reply/>`, sender/repository/mention gates, reason filter) give the same results as on main.

### Tested on

|     OS     |    Status     |
| :--------: | :-----------: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅ tested   |

macOS and Windows are covered by CI only.

### Environment (optional)

Built worktree (`npm run build && npm run bundle`); daemon started as `node dist/cli.js serve --channel …` with an isolated `QWEN_HOME`, a stub `gh` on `PATH`, a local GitHub REST fake, and a scripted OpenAI-compatible model.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: while a thread is being retried the whole poll window is held, the same mechanism a recoverable task already uses, so each poll re-lists the unread notifications since the held cursor and re-reads their comments; comments already handled are deduplicated as before. The 30-poll budget bounds how long 5xx failures can hold a window; a thread whose first failure lands on that 30th poll is skipped after one failing poll. Rate limits and credential failures hold the window until GitHub answers, since they block every read anyway. The counts are kept in memory, so a restart starts them again. Writing repeated skip rows once per window also applies to the existing hold while a failed task is retryable.
- Cost while held: every poll re-reads the threads of the window, as the existing task hold already does, so one thread failing for the full 30 polls costs about 30 reads of the window. Skipping threads on a held poll was tried and lost items main delivers: GitHub's one-second timestamps and late notifications make an unchanged notification timestamp no proof that a thread has nothing new, a first-contact body waits for the re-read, and even a 404 can be momentary right after an issue is created.
- Not validated / out of scope: the same-second cursor boundary (#16227), how a secondary rate limit on the final reply is classified, and the per-thread cursor discussed in the design review.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Operators may see new `github_api_error` rows in the Channel event timeline.

## Linked Issues

Related to #16227 (another way a comment can be lost inside the same comment window; not fixed here).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

GitHub channel 读取某条通知对应的线程时——读评论、读 issue 事件，或在首次接触时读 issue/PR 本身——如果 GitHub 返回临时性失败（5xx、网络错误或限流），现在会保持这条通知未读、轮询游标不前进，下一轮重新读取该线程。永久性错误照旧立即跳过，例如 issue 已删除返回 404、组织开启 SAML 强制返回 403。限流或凭据失败会停下本轮，并保持窗口直到 GitHub 恢复应答。被保持的窗口每轮仍会从头重读。重新列出的、时间不晚于游标的通知（它的标已读没有生效）属于一个已经提交的窗口，读它时的 5xx 既不保持窗口，也不消耗预算。5xx 造成的保持按窗口设上限：一个窗口里第 30 次遇到 5xx 的那一轮（默认间隔下约 30 分钟，另加单次调用内的重试），仍在失败的线程被跳过、窗口被标为已读，因此无论是单个线程持续失败还是多个线程轮流失败，都不能无限期卡住标已读。这类失败现在会记入 Channel 事件时间线：线程开始失败时和每第十个失败轮次记一条 failed，放弃时记一条 skipped；该线程自己的任务尚未完成时出现的失败也记为 failed，因为这个任务保持着窗口，线程会被重读。由于被保持的窗口每轮都会重读所有线程，只会重复的记录——永久性失败、限流、重读到的评论的 `duplicate` 或 `mention_required` 跳过——每个窗口只写一次（限流在第一轮和每第十轮写）。首次接触路径以前会吞掉自己的读取失败，现在遵循同一规则。以裸 403 形式出现的二级限流（没有 `retry-after`、配额还有剩余）按 GitHub 的报错文案识别，会保持窗口而不是被跳过；PR watch 也以同样方式识别它并停下，不再对每个被 watch 的 PR 各发一次注定被拒的请求。

## 为什么需要

轮询循环捕获单线程错误后只打印 "skipping" 就继续，但同一轮随后把列出的所有通知都标为已读，游标也越过了它。由于只在游标窗口内读评论，某个线程上约 3 秒的 GitHub 抖动（单次调用内 3 次尝试都失败）就会让这条 @mention 永久丢失：不回复、不重试、不进死信，时间线上也没有记录。这是在用真实 daemon 跑一组 GitHub 场景时发现的，在那里可以复现（见下文）。

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- 让某个线程的评论列表在单次调用的 3 次尝试中都返回 5xx，随后恢复：这条 @ 应在下一轮被回复；在此之前通知保持未读（不标已读、游标不变）。
- 让某个线程返回 404，或返回组织 SAML 强制的 403：本轮照常标已读并推进游标，Channel 事件时间线出现一条 skipped 的 `github_api_error`。
- 让某个线程持续返回 5xx：期间其它线程照常被回复；到第 30 轮该线程被跳过，窗口被标为已读。两个线程隔轮交替失败时也一样。
- 正文 @ 了 bot 的新 issue（首次接触）在读取 issue 时临时失败一次：应在下一轮被回复。

### Evidence (Before & After)

单测：`packages/channels/github` 516/516（其中 `GithubAdapter.test.ts` 476 个），新的 `transient per-thread GitHub errors` 组共 45 个用例，另有 1 个 PR watch 用例，并调整 3 个（旧的"失败也全部标已读"契约现在只适用于永久性失败；两个已有用例依赖未打桩的评论列表，其报错以前被吞掉，现在给出空结果）。以下变异各被杀死：

- 去掉游标保留，或去掉 shared 失败时的停止；
- 按线程而不是按窗口计预算、从不消耗预算、提交时不重置，或让限流轮次消耗预算；
- 所有错误或所有 403 都当临时，或去掉任一种二级限流文案；
- 吞掉首次接触错误；
- 每轮都写日志，或从不累加 shared 计数；
- 不对 `duplicate` / `mention_required` / 跳过记录去重，或提交时不清除；
- 去掉每窗口键集合的上限、超出上限后仍存下所有失败计数，或让计数存不下的线程每轮都记录；
- 保持计数跨重启保留，或去掉它的初始值；
- 从 PR watch 的判定里去掉二级限流文案；
- 线程自己的任务保持着窗口时把失败记为 `skipped`，或在只剩其它线程的任务、已完成的任务或已用完重试次数的任务时记为 `failed`，或让它与跳过记录共用键；
- 在保持期间跳过读取成功、返回 404 或陈旧时失败的线程（首次接触正文、同一秒的评论、短暂的 404 和迟到的通知都会因此丢失）；
- 让陈旧通知保持窗口、在没有可提交窗口时消耗预算，或在标已读成功前重置预算；
- 线程键里去掉仓库名。

E2E：真实 `qwen serve` daemon + channel worker + Octokit，指向本地假 GitHub REST（通知有未读与 `last_read_at` 语义、时间戳精确到秒、可注入故障），模型为脚本化假模型。场景：白名单用户在某线程 @ bot，该线程的评论列表在一轮内连续返回 3 次 500；对照线程只失败 2 次。

修复前（main 的 `f217a8e5d9`，其 channel 代码与本 PR 的基点相同）：

```
faulted thread: bot replies 0, notification unread=false (marked read), timeline rows 0
stderr: [Channel:gh-main] API error processing issue:5, skipping: fault
control thread (2 failures, recovered by the in-call retry): bot replies 1
```

修复后（本分支，在 `fbf47f9186` 上重跑）：

```
faulted thread: bot replies 1, timeline rows 5
stderr: [Channel:gh-main] API error processing issue:6 (1/30), keeping it unread for the next poll: fault
control thread: bot replies 1
```

其余可靠性场景结果与 main 相同：限流回复存为待发并在重启后只发一次、歧义 502 不重发、通知接口故障后追上、202 异步标已读、SIGKILL 中断后恢复。基础派发场景也相同：@mention、首次接触、请求 review、assign、聚合与 `<no-reply/>`、发送者/仓库/mention 门禁、reason 过滤。

### Tested on

|     OS     |    Status     |
| :--------: | :-----------: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅ tested   |

macOS 和 Windows 仅由 CI 覆盖。

### Environment (optional)

已构建的 worktree（`npm run build && npm run bundle`）；daemon 以 `node dist/cli.js serve --channel …` 启动，`QWEN_HOME` 隔离，`PATH` 上放 `gh` 桩，本地假 GitHub REST，脚本化 OpenAI 兼容模型。

## Risk & Scope

- 主要风险或取舍：线程重试期间整个轮询窗口被保留，这和可恢复任务现有的机制相同，因此每轮都会重新列出被保留游标之后的未读通知并重读其评论；已处理的评论照旧去重。30 轮预算限定了 5xx 能保持一个窗口多久；如果某个线程的第一次失败恰好落在第 30 轮，它失败一轮就会被跳过。限流和凭据失败会一直保持窗口直到 GitHub 恢复应答，因为它们本来就会让所有读取失败。计数只在内存里，重启后重新计数。重复的跳过记录每窗口只写一次，这一点同样作用于已有的"失败任务仍可重试"时的保持。
- 保持期间的成本：每轮都会重读窗口里的线程（已有的任务保持也是如此），所以一个线程持续失败满 30 轮，约等于把窗口读 30 遍。曾尝试在保持期间跳过部分线程，结果会丢掉 main 能投递的内容：GitHub 的时间戳只精确到秒、通知也可能迟到，通知时间不变并不能说明线程没有新内容；首次接触的正文要靠重读才会补发；刚创建的 issue 也可能短暂返回 404。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：同一秒的游标边界（#16227）、最终回复遇到二级限流时的判定，以及设计评审里讨论的逐线程游标。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。运维人员可能会在 Channel 事件时间线里看到新的 `github_api_error` 行。

## Linked Issues

Related to #16227（同一评论窗口里另一种丢评论的方式，本 PR 不修）。

</details>

prs.title: feat(cli): run the Ink TUI's tool batches on the shared loop's batch
prs.body:
## What this PR does

With `experimental.unifiedAgentLoop` on, the tool calls of each Ink TUI model round run as one batch of the shared loop, `runToolBatch`. This is PR 3b-1 of #15327, the second step of the Ink TUI after #16206.

The batch runs on an executor over the TUI's own scheduler. The scheduler takes the batch as before, so the tool group, its approvals, Esc and the Mod tool middleware are unchanged. What changes is where the batch's completion goes: back to the executor, instead of the scheduler's completion callback. The TUI's completion step, `handleCompletedTools`, then runs as today with the batch's results, and continues the turn with a `ToolResult` round as today.

The batch does the part the loop already owns:

| The TUI today | With the setting on |
| --- | --- |
| the stream processor answers a provider replay and holds it until the batch completes | the batch answers it in place |
| the completion step orders, finalizes and records the results | the batch orders and finalizes them; the completion step records the ones it sends, after its session check, with the batch's recording |
| the completion step counts each completed call toward the session's tool calls | the batch counts them, except the calls the Mod tool middleware counted per attempt and the skipped siblings of a plan-mode entry |
| a batch that completes during a model stream waits for it to end | the same: it is handled when the stream ends, against history as it is then, in one continuation with the other waiting batches |

A response made only of provider replays keeps the current path, since it runs nothing.

The pieces:

- `useReactToolScheduler`'s `schedule` takes an optional `onBatchComplete`. The completion of that batch goes to it in place of the hook's `onComplete`; other batches are unchanged.
- `createInkToolExecutor` (new, `packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/ink-tool-executor.ts`) implements the loop's `AgentLoopToolExecutor` with it. It marks the calls the Mod tool middleware already counted, through a new optional `recorded` on the loop's settled call, so the batch does not count them twice.
- `runToolBatch` also returns its finalized parts by call, `responses`, and with the new optional `deferRecording` leaves each result unrecorded and returns its recording as `record`. The completion step uses them to leave out the results it does not send (a call whose result history already has, or a call of another interaction owner) and records only the ones it sends, after its session check.
- In `use-llm-stream.ts`, the scheduler's completion handling moved into `commitCompletedToolBatch`, which the scheduler's callback and the shared batch both call. `handleCompletedTools` takes the shared batch's results and skips the steps the batch did. With the setting on, the TUI logs each tool batch it runs on the shared loop to the debug log.

Both additions to the loop are optional, so headless and ACP are unchanged.

The Ink parity suite counts the shared tool batches through the debug log, as it counts the shared rounds. It adds three scenarios:

- a replayed call next to a fresh one;
- an approved write, then a declined one, in the default approval mode;
- a shell command cancelled with Esc while it runs.

The setting's description now says the Ink TUI also runs its tool batches through the shared loop. The design doc splits 3b into 3b-1 and 3b-2, describes 3b-1, and lists its intended difference.

## Why it's needed

The Ink TUI is the next surface in #15327. 3b-1 puts its tool batches on the shared batch while the TUI's completion step still continues the turn. 3b-2 then makes the TUI's own steps host hooks, and has the turn await the batch.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Run `npm run bundle`, then `cd integration-tests && QWEN_E2E_RENDERER=ink npx vitest run interactive/ink-agent-loop-parity.test.ts`. Fourteen scenarios must pass, each with the shared rounds and tool batches it expects on the run with the setting on and none on the other.
- Unit tests:
  - `packages/core` `agent-loop.test.ts`: a call the executor recorded is not counted again; the batch returns its parts by call; with `deferRecording` it records nothing and returns each recording.
  - `packages/cli` `use-llm-stream.test.tsx`, "shared agent loop round": the calls run as one shared batch and their results go out as the next round; a call the Mod tool middleware counted is not counted again; a replayed call is answered and only the others run; a result history already has is neither sent nor recorded, and is counted once; a result that replaces a placeholder is recorded once; replay answers keep the turn going when every executed call was cancelled; a batch that completes during another model stream is handled when it ends, against history as it is then.
  - `packages/cli` `useToolScheduler.test.ts`: a batch's completion goes to its own callback, and later batches go back to `onComplete`; a schedule that fails without completing releases the callback.
  - `packages/cli` `ink-tool-executor.test.ts`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A: the change is behind an off-by-default setting, and the parity suite compares both loops.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local results on Linux:

- the Ink parity suite: 14/14, from a fresh `npm run bundle`;
- `agent-loop.test.ts` 30 passed; `use-llm-stream.test.tsx` and `useToolScheduler.test.ts` 429 passed; `ink-tool-executor.test.ts` passed; `acp-tool-batch.test.ts` and `nonInteractiveCli.test.ts` 265 passed;
- root `npm run typecheck` passes; eslint and prettier are clean on the changed files.

Mutation checks:

- When the executor stops marking the Mod middleware's calls, the executor test and the hook's no-double-count test fail.
- When `schedule` ignores `onBatchComplete`, the scheduler test fails, and the shared batch never completes.
- When the shared batch drops its results on a cancel (`keepCancelledResults: false`), the parity suite's Esc scenario fails on the session records.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the scheduler's completion handling moved into a function that both paths call, and `handleCompletedTools` has a branch for the shared batch's results. With the setting off, the scheduler's callback reaches the same code as today.
- Not validated / out of scope:
  - The TUI's own steps as hooks, awaiting the batch, and a tool that ends the turn (3b-2); input at a tool boundary and other turn kinds (3c).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

Design: [docs/design/2026-10-23-unified-agent-loop.md](docs/design/2026-10-23-unified-agent-loop.md) and [docs/design/2026-10-23-unified-agent-loop.zh-CN.md](docs/design/2026-10-23-unified-agent-loop.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Part of #15327.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

开启 `experimental.unifiedAgentLoop` 后，Ink TUI 每个模型轮的工具调用作为共享 loop 的一个工具批（`runToolBatch`）运行。这是 #15327 的 PR 3b-1，也是 Ink TUI 继 #16206 之后的第二步。

工具批运行在一个 executor 上，底层是 TUI 自己的 scheduler。scheduler 和以前一样接收这一批，因此工具组、审批、Esc 和 Mod 工具中间件都不变。变化的是这一批完成结果的去向：交回 executor，而不是 scheduler 的完成回调。随后 TUI 的完成步骤 `handleCompletedTools` 用这一批的结果照常运行，并和现在一样以 `ToolResult` 轮次续发。

工具批负责 loop 本来就负责的那部分：

| TUI 现在 | 开启设置后 |
| --- | --- |
| 流处理器应答 provider 重放，并暂存到这一批完成 | 由工具批就地应答 |
| 完成步骤给结果排序、收尾并记录 | 由工具批排序和收尾；完成步骤在会话检查之后，用工具批的记录方式记录它发送的结果 |
| 完成步骤把每个完成的调用计入会话的工具调用数 | 由工具批计入，但 Mod 工具中间件已按尝试计入的调用、plan mode 入口被跳过的同批调用除外 |
| 在模型流进行中完成的工具批等待它结束 | 相同：流结束时按当时的历史处理，并和其他等待中的工具批合并为一次续发 |

只由 provider 重放组成的响应不运行任何调用，因此保留现有路径。

具体改动：

- `useReactToolScheduler` 的 `schedule` 新增可选参数 `onBatchComplete`。这一批的完成结果交给它，而不是 hook 的 `onComplete`；其他批次不变。
- 新增 `createInkToolExecutor`（`packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/ink-tool-executor.ts`），用它实现 loop 的 `AgentLoopToolExecutor`。它通过 loop 已完成调用上新增的可选字段 `recorded`，标记 Mod 工具中间件已经计入的调用，避免工具批重复计数。
- `runToolBatch` 另外按调用返回收尾后的结果（`responses`）；新增可选项 `deferRecording` 时不记录结果，而是把每条结果的记录方式作为 `record` 返回。完成步骤用它们排除不发送的结果（历史中已有结果的调用，或属于其他交互 owner 的调用），并在会话检查之后只记录它发送的结果。
- `use-llm-stream.ts` 中，scheduler 完成后的处理搬进了 `commitCompletedToolBatch`，scheduler 的回调和共享工具批都调用它。`handleCompletedTools` 接收共享工具批的结果，并跳过工具批已经做过的步骤。开启设置后，TUI 会把它在共享 loop 上运行的每个工具批写入 debug 日志。

loop 的两处新增都是可选的，因此 headless 和 ACP 不受影响。

Ink 对拍测试像统计共享模型轮那样，通过 debug 日志统计共享工具批，并新增三个场景：

- 重放的调用和一个新调用在同一批；
- 默认审批模式下，先批准一次写入，再拒绝一次；
- 运行中按 Esc 取消的 shell 命令。

设置的描述改为：Ink TUI 的工具批也经由共享 loop 运行。设计文档把 3b 拆成 3b-1 和 3b-2，描述了 3b-1，并列出它的预期差异。

## 为什么需要

Ink TUI 是 #15327 的下一个入口。3b-1 先把它的工具批放到共享工具批上，轮次仍由 TUI 的完成步骤续发。3b-2 再把 TUI 自己的步骤改为宿主钩子，并让轮次等待工具批完成。

## 验证方法

- 运行 `npm run bundle`，然后 `cd integration-tests && QWEN_E2E_RENDERER=ink npx vitest run interactive/ink-agent-loop-parity.test.ts`。十四个场景必须通过；开启设置的那次运行，共享模型轮数和工具批数都要等于场景规定的数目，另一次运行两者都为零。
- 本地（Linux）：Ink 对拍 14/14（重新 `npm run bundle` 后）；相关单测全部通过；根目录 `npm run typecheck` 通过；改动文件的 eslint 和 prettier 都干净。三组变异（executor 不再标记 Mod 中间件的调用、`schedule` 忽略 `onBatchComplete`、取消时丢弃结果）都会让对应测试失败。
- 单元测试：
  - `packages/core` 的 `agent-loop.test.ts`：executor 已记录的调用不重复计数；工具批按调用返回结果。
  - `packages/cli` 的 `use-llm-stream.test.tsx`，"shared agent loop round"：调用作为一个共享工具批运行，结果作为下一轮发出；Mod 工具中间件已计入的调用不重复计数；重放的调用被应答，只运行其他调用。
  - `packages/cli` 的 `useToolScheduler.test.ts`：一批的完成结果交给它自己的回调，之后的批次回到 `onComplete`。
  - `packages/cli` 的 `ink-tool-executor.test.ts`。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：scheduler 完成后的处理搬进了两条路径共用的函数，`handleCompletedTools` 多了处理共享工具批结果的分支。设置关闭时，scheduler 的回调走到的代码和现在相同。
- 未验证/不在范围内：
  - TUI 自己的步骤改为钩子、等待工具批完成、结束轮次的工具（3b-2）；工具边界的输入和其他轮次类型（3c）。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：无。

</details>

auto_merge.commit_title: feat(cli): run the Ink TUI's tool batches on the shared loop's batch (#16304)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* feat(cli): run the Ink TUI's tool batches on the shared loop's batch

With experimental.unifiedAgentLoop on, the tool calls of each Ink TUI model
round run as one batch of the shared loop, runToolBatch, on an executor over
the TUI's own scheduler. The tool group, approvals, Esc and the Mod tool
middleware are unchanged; the batch's completion goes back to the executor,
and the TUI's completion step continues the turn with the batch's results.

- useReactToolScheduler's schedule takes an optional onBatchComplete that
  receives that batch's completion in place of onComplete.
- createInkToolExecutor implements AgentLoopToolExecutor over it and marks
  the calls the Mod tool middleware already counted, through a new optional
  `recorded` on the loop's settled call.
- runToolBatch also returns its finalized parts by call, `responses`, so the
  completion step can leave out results it does not send.
- The scheduler's completion handling moved into commitCompletedToolBatch,
  which both paths call; handleCompletedTools skips the steps the shared
  batch did. A response made only of provider replays keeps the current path.
- The Ink parity suite counts shared tool batches through the debug log and
  adds a replayed call next to a fresh one, an approved then declined write,
  and a shell command cancelled with Esc.
- The setting's description and the design doc (3b split into 3b-1 and 3b-2,
  with 3b-1's intended difference) are updated in both languages.

* fix(cli): send and record only the shared tool batch results the TUI keeps

- runToolBatch takes `deferRecording` and returns each result's recording,
  so the Ink TUI records only what it sends, after its session check; a
  result that replaces a placeholder is recorded once, and dropped or
  secondary-owner results are not recorded.
- A shared batch that completes during a model stream is queued like the
  current path's batches and handled when the streams end, against history
  as it is then, in one continuation with the other waiting batches.
- Calls the shared batch ran are not counted again by the history-dedup and
  secondary-owner steps.
- The batch's replay answers keep the continuation going when every
  executed call was cancelled.
- A failed shared batch falls back to the current completion path for its
  settled calls; a schedule that ends without completing releases the
  batch's callback.
- Provider call fingerprints are recorded when the batch is scheduled.

* fix(cli): keep a shared tool batch in the session and render it completed in

- Take the session and chat when the scheduler completes the batch, before
  it is finalized, so a /clear or /resume while a large result is persisted
  no longer sends or records that result in the new session.
- Commit the tool group inside the scheduler's completion callback, in the
  render that clears its display list, instead of after the finalize.
- Leave cancelled calls to the TUI to count, so a cancelled call whose id
  history already answered is not counted.
- Merge queued shared batches' results one per call id.
- When the batch throws, drop the replay ids it marked as answered but
  never sent.

* fix(cli): continue a shared tool batch with the TUI's current state and settle it when its completion throws

- runSharedToolBatch commits through commitCompletedToolBatchRef and reads the
  chat from the client the TUI holds now, so a batch that waited on approvals
  or long tools continues with the current handleCompletedTools, submitQuery,
  quota fallback and client, as the scheduler's onComplete ref does.
- The Ink executor resolves the batch in a finally block, and the session
  capture in onSettled no longer throws: a chat that cannot be read (a reset
  under way) ends the batch without a continuation and releases the turn's
  activity instead of leaving it Responding.

prs.title: perf(core): defer workflow tool schemas by default
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Workflow now uses the existing deferred-tool discovery and invocation bridge. Fresh requests carry a short catalog entry; the full description and parameter schema are returned on demand. Explicit workflow requests and Workflow mode follow the same discovery path, with reminders that correctly explain how to reach the hidden tool. Searching does not add its definition back to the standing tool declarations.

## Why it's needed

With workflows enabled, ordinary requests currently pay for the full Workflow definition even when no workflow is used. Comparing captured requests from the same base and changed build removes roughly 2,000 estimated input tokens while preserving the existing execution and approval paths.

Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e18b041b3634ebd0998d33694a4a9c8e3c8546b1/docs/design/deferred-workflow-tool.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e18b041b3634ebd0998d33694a4a9c8e3c8546b1/docs/design/deferred-workflow-tool.zh-CN.md).

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Enable workflows in Direct mode with the default preload budget and send an ordinary prompt. The request should contain a short Workflow catalog entry and no full Workflow function declaration.
2. Search for Workflow by exact name or orchestration keywords, then invoke a minimal deterministic workflow through the bridge. The complete schema should be returned, execution should succeed, and subsequent requests should retain the same standing declarations. Calling before schema discovery should still be refused.
3. Enable Workflow mode and verify that the reminder directs the model through discovery without preloading the definition. In CodeMode, discovery should lead to execution through exec instead of the Direct-mode bridge.
4. Verify explicit visibility, budget preload and incomplete-bridge fallback; verify that deny rules, disabled tools and named-only restrictions still hold. Existing history restoration, reset and mid-session review activation behavior should remain intact.

### Evidence (Before & After)

No TUI layout change. Actual headless CLI request capture against an isolated local mock provider, comparing base `ed6760aa2c30b1d48c368822b7cd061e7e2711b7` with this change:

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full Workflow declaration characters | 8,726 | 0 |
| Tool-array proxy BPE tokens | 6,485 | 4,474 |
| Normalized complete-request proxy BPE tokens | 13,651 | 11,659 |
| Minimal workflow invocation | Direct call | Search, then bridge call |

The added catalog line measures 17 proxy tokens independently; tokenizer boundaries mean component counts are not strictly additive. Only isolated run-directory names were normalized, other tool definitions were identical, and the remaining message difference was the new catalog line. These are fixed public Qwen3.5 tokenizer estimates, not provider billing. Mock usage is synthetic.

Validation: build, typecheck (including integration types), bundle, changed-file ESLint/Prettier, bilingual design links, 2,150 passing regression tests across 11 core test files, and 13 passing CLI scenarios. The CI follow-up additionally verifies 77 Mod-permission tests and rechecks the 12 deferred-Workflow tests, plus three CLI startup cases with incomplete discovery bridges and Workflow mode enabled. A global CLI dry-run established the procedure before the same-base comparison. Detailed E2E results are posted separately.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :---: |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested locally |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ not tested locally |

### Environment

Node.js 26.7.0, pnpm 11.24.0, locally built CLI, isolated configuration/runtime directories, local OpenAI-compatible mock provider, and deterministic workflows that dispatch no agents.

## Risk & Scope

- Main tradeoff: using Workflow adds a discovery round trip when its schema is absent from context. Explicit visibility, budget preload and the existing incomplete-bridge fallback remain available.
- Not validated / out of scope: live-provider billing, production deployment, other tools, context-usage accounting, and UI changes.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: no API, parameter or persistence changes. As with other natively deferred tools, an eager allowlist does not force Workflow visible; use explicit visibility when that is intended.

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 此 PR 的改动

Workflow 现在复用已有的延迟工具发现及调用桥。新请求仅携带简短目录条目，完整描述和参数 schema 按需返回。明确的 workflow 请求与 Workflow 模式也走相同的发现路径，提示词会正确说明如何访问隐藏工具。搜索不会将完整定义重新加入常驻工具声明。

## 为什么需要

当前启用 workflow 后，即使普通请求不使用 workflow，也会携带完整定义。同一基线与修改版的实际请求对比显示，输入可减少约 2,000 个估算 token，现有执行和审批路径保持不变。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e18b041b3634ebd0998d33694a4a9c8e3c8546b1/docs/design/deferred-workflow-tool.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e18b041b3634ebd0998d33694a4a9c8e3c8546b1/docs/design/deferred-workflow-tool.zh-CN.md)。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 在 Direct 模式启用 workflow，并使用默认预加载预算，发送普通问题。请求应仅包含简短的 Workflow 目录条目，不包含完整的 Workflow 函数声明。
2. 使用精确名称或编排关键词搜索 Workflow，再通过桥调用最小确定性 workflow。应返回完整 schema、执行成功，后续请求的常驻声明保持一致。未经 schema 查阅的调用仍应被拒绝。
3. 开启 Workflow 模式，确认提示词引导模型先发现工具，且不会预加载完整定义。在 CodeMode 中，发现后应通过 exec 执行，而非 Direct 模式的桥。
4. 验证显式展示、预算预加载和桥接缺失时的兜底；确认 deny 规则、工具禁用和 name-only 限制仍有效。历史恢复、重置以及会话中途 review 激活应保持原有行为。

### 改动前后证据

无 TUI 布局变化。使用隔离的本地 mock provider 捕获真实无界面 CLI 请求，对比基线 `ed6760aa2c30b1d48c368822b7cd061e7e2711b7` 与本次改动：

| 测量项 | 改动前 | 改动后 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 完整 Workflow 声明字符数 | 8,726 | 0 |
| 工具数组 proxy BPE token | 6,485 | 4,474 |
| 归一化完整请求 proxy BPE token | 13,651 | 11,659 |
| 最小 workflow 调用 | 直接调用 | 搜索后桥接调用 |

新增目录行独立测得 17 个 proxy token；tokenizer 边界意味着分项不能严格相加。仅归一化隔离运行目录名，其余工具定义一致，消息差异仅为新增的目录行。以上使用固定的公开 Qwen3.5 tokenizer 估算，不是 Provider 计费用量。Mock usage 为合成值。
