issues.body:
**Bug type:** Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

**Beta release blocker:** No

**Summary**
In an always-on Telegram group with `unmentionedInbound: "room_event"`, follow-up queue overflow (default `cap: 20`, `drop: "summarize"`) evicted a direct mention that was queued behind a long turn, because victims are chosen by age only, and the mention was later replayed as a context-free `[Queue overflow] Dropped 1 message due to cap.` turn.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Run OpenClaw 2026.10.5 with an agent on the `claude-cli` runtime (`anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`), a Telegram supergroup with `requireMention: false`, `agents.entries.<agent>.groupChat.unmentionedInbound: "room_event"`, `messages.queue` unset (defaults: `steer`, cap 20, `summarize`) and `messages.visibleReplies: "automatic"`.
2. Mention the bot with a request that keeps one turn busy for several minutes (multi-step tool use; ours ran 4 min 53 s).
3. During that turn, send one direct mention with a question, then let other members post 20+ unmentioned messages.
4. The mention fails to steer (`steering rejected; applying follow-up policy`, `reason: injection_unavailable`) and enters the follow-up queue. The unmentioned messages enter the same queue, because room events never steer.
5. After the long turn ends, inspect the session transcript.

On current `main`, where the Claude CLI backend can accept text steering, set `messages.queue: { mode: "followup", cap: 3 }` so that the mention deterministically enters the follow-up queue; room events go there in every mode. Unit-level: `applyQueueDropPolicy` (`src/utils/queue-helpers.ts`) with `cap: 20`, items `[userRequest, ...19 roomEvents]` and the same `isProtected` as `applyFollowupQueueOverflow` drops `userRequest` when one more room event arrives.

**Expected behavior**
`docs/channels/ambient-room-events.md` says unmentioned messages become quiet room events while "mentioned messages stay user requests". Under queue pressure, overflow should evict ambient room events before user requests, the same way `enqueue.ts` already keeps automatic Goal continuations from consuming "the last slot needed by real input". The group history window already keeps the evicted room events as context. A user request that still has to be summarized should keep its sender, message id and context.

**Actual behavior**
- One burst produced 30 synthetic user turns `[Queue overflow] Dropped 1 message due to cap.\nSummary:\n- <text>`, one per evicted entry: 28 ambient room events, 1 direct mention, and 1 internal exec-completion notice that was queued in the same session (tracked separately).
- Based on arrival order (no eviction is logged), the mention was evicted about 2.5 minutes after it was sent, while the original turn was still running. It was replayed 6.5 minutes after it was sent as an 84-character prompt with no sender, message id, reply or conversation context. The preceding normal user-request prompt in this session was about 11.7k characters and included a "Conversation info"/"Conversation context" block. The model had to call `sessions_history` to work out who had asked what.
- Evicted room events were replayed as separate turns without the `[OpenClaw room event] … not a request` framing. For one of them, a question between members that was not addressed to the bot, the agent posted a visible reply via `message(action=send)` more than 10 minutes after it was written, and members asked what it was replying to.
- The cap did not shed load. Every evicted entry still cost a full model turn, and those turns run first, so after the long turn ended the pending queue stayed at 20 for another ~9.5 minutes and every message that arrived in that phase evicted another entry. A direct mention sent during that phase waited 9 min 47 s for its turn. The model also told one requester that their still-queued message had been dropped.
- At the default log level nothing records the evictions, and the sender of the evicted mention is not notified.

**OpenClaw version:** 2026.10.5 (source checked: the overflow path is unchanged in 2026.10.6, release/2026.10.7, release/2026.10.10 and `main` at c055a496)

**Operating system:** macOS 27.0.1

**Install method:** npm global

**Model:** anthropic/claude-opus-5-5

**Provider / routing chain:** openclaw -> claude-cli (Claude Code CLI 2.1.30x, local login) -> Anthropic

**Additional provider/model setup details**
`agents.defaults.models["anthropic/*"].agentRuntime.id = "claude-cli"`; the agent has no model fallbacks. On 2026.10.5–10.7 the Claude CLI runtime does not register message injection, so default `steer` falls back to follow-up. 2026.10.10 and `main` add `registerMessageInjection` in `extensions/anthropic/cli.runtime.ts`, which changes how mentions reach the queue but not the overflow policy.

**Logs**
```shell
# gateway log, UTC+3, identifiers redacted
04:33:56.044 cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 promptChars=11754 trigger=user ...   # long turn starts
04:34:03.320 Inbound message telegram:group:<group> -> @<bot> (group, 26 chars)                        # the direct mention
04:34:03.388 steering rejected; applying follow-up policy {"reason":"injection_unavailable","disposition":"followup-policy","channel":"telegram"}
# 35 more inbound group messages after the mention until 04:38:33; none attempts steering (room events)
04:38:49.522 cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=293478 outBytes=8
04:38:49.991 cli exec: provider=claude-cli ... promptChars=72 trigger=user ...   # first "[Queue overflow] Dropped 1 message due to cap." turn
04:40:36.816 cli exec: provider=claude-cli ... promptChars=84 trigger=user ...   # the evicted mention, replayed as a summary
# 28 x "recorded message-tool-only run outcome" (room-event summary turns) between 04:40:25 and 04:48:26
```
Session transcript: 30 user rows between 04:38:49 and 04:48:24, each with text `[Queue overflow] Dropped 1 message due to cap.\nSummary:\n- …` and an `idempotencyKey` starting with `followup-overflow:`. Their metadata holds only `senderIsOwner`, while normal rows carry sender identity and the transport message id. The Claude CLI session log for the mention's replay shows the 84-character summary as the entire user prompt.

**Screenshots, recordings, and evidence**
Code path on `main` (c055a496):
- `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run-admission.ts:148-151, 484-494`: room events never steer and are forced into follow-up while a run is active.
- `src/sessions/session-controller.mailbox.ts:81-101`: one mailbox per session, pending items in arrival order, defaults cap 20 / summarize.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/enqueue.ts:242-283`: `applyFollowupQueueOverflow`; the only protection is `protectFromQueueOverflow` (`:282`). Compare the goal-continuation supersession at `:121-125`.
- `src/utils/queue-helpers.ts:52-91`: victims are the oldest pending, unprotected entries; summary lines are cut to 160 characters.
- `src/sessions/session-controller.mailbox-dispatch.ts:56-61, 101-110` and `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/envelope.ts:259-268`: evicted room events drain one per turn, ahead of newer entries.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/drain.ts:151-155, 184-191`: the replay prompt is only the summary and `currentInboundContext` is cleared, which removes the sender/context block and the room-event framing built in `get-reply-run-context.ts:509-512, 563-581`.

**Impact and severity**
- Affected: always-on group rooms using ambient room events (observed on Telegram; the queue code is channel-agnostic) whenever a turn runs long and a user request cannot be steered: Claude CLI runtime before 2026.10.10, `followup`/`collect` modes, messages with media, runtimes without injection.
- Severity: direct questions are answered late and without their context; the bot posts replies to chatter nobody addressed to it; evicted entries still cost a model turn each.
- Frequency: 30 of about 50 inputs received during one long turn and the replay phase that followed (about 15 minutes). These are the only queue-overflow rows in this agent's stored history, all inside the ambient-mode window.
- Consequence: confusing answers in the group, extra model usage, and no visible signal that a message was summarized.

**Additional information**
Related: #99142 / #99145 kept the `room_event` kind on overflow summaries (delivery only, not eviction order or prompt context); #97320 (busy-group backlog delivered late); #121204 (Discord ingress-layer stale ambient backlog); #160405 (opt-in receipts for summarized/dropped steers); #142268 (queued follow-ups lose the reply target); #160740 (mailbox refactor kept cap/drop semantics). Possible fix: rank overflow victims by reply expectation (optional room events first, `isRequiredReplyExpectation` entries last); drop room-event victims without a replay turn, since the group history window already carries them; keep `currentInboundContext` (or at least sender, time and message id) for a single-source summary; log evictions.

issues.body:
Summary
Discord GPT-Live voice previously worked on OpenClaw 2026.9.9. Following an upgrade to 2026.10.9, voice startup fails with:
Failed to start Discord realtime voice: OpenAI GPT-Live authentication failed
An upgrade regression is a hypothesis, not a confirmed cause. Discord text messaging continues to work normally.
Environment and working baseline
Ubuntu 24.04 VPS, Gateway running as a systemd user service.
Current OpenClaw and official @openclaw/discord plugin versions: 2026.10.9. The plugin declares openclaw >=2026.10.9; no version mismatch is apparent.
Discord voice: effective mode agent-proxy (voice.mode unset), agent main, provider openai, model gpt-live-1-codex, voice cove.
Discord GPT-Live/Cove worked during the October 17, 2026 tests on OpenClaw 2026.9.9, using ChatGPT subscription authentication. The user confirmed audible responses around 2–3 seconds after speaking.
An ElevenLabs stt-tts trial was rolled back by unsetting channels.discord.voice.mode; GPT-Live worked afterward. ElevenLabs TTS settings remain saved, but stt-tts is not the selected conversation mode.
The host was upgraded to 2026.10.9 on October 30. No retained evidence establishes a successful Discord GPT-Live connection after that upgrade.
Current failure and rollback comparison
A persona-instruction trial added instructions to browser Talk and Discord realtime configuration. Those additions were subsequently removed, preserving Discord’s pre-existing pronunciation instructions exactly.
The rollback hot reload completed at 2026-11-03 02:26:42 UTC, and config revision acceptance was logged at 02:26:43. A fresh Discord /vc join failed about nine minutes later:
02:36:13.954 UTC: Discord join selected Main / OpenAI / gpt-live-1-codex / Cove.
02:36:14.005 UTC: Gateway logged realtime bridge startup.
Discord displayed the exact authentication error quoted above.
Gateway PID and restart count remained unchanged during the rollback. Reverting the persona additions did not restore voice startup.
Evidence distinction: the authentication error was visible in Discord. The retained Gateway logs contain bridge startup but no corresponding underlying auth exception, HTTP status, provider error code, or selected credential type.
Authentication-path inspection
Installed-source inspection indicates that Discord’s GPT-Live bridge and browser GPT-Live sessions share resolveOpenAIQuicksilverBridgeAuth. For this subscription model, it tries ChatGPT OAuth first and considers Platform API-key authentication if OAuth resolution returns none.
Current metadata shows an OAuth profile and a configured Platform-key input, but no per-attempt record proves which credential route was selected or whether OAuth refresh occurred. No credential values were exposed or changed.
Both paths share account-header construction and upstream call-building logic. Their WebRTC peer ownership and offer lifecycle differ.
Control UI comparison limit
The user reports that Control UI voice connected, though it introduced itself as ChatGPT rather than the configured agent persona. Retained talk.client.create successes at 02:07:22.890 and 02:08:01.746 UTC establish broker-session creation only: they omit the selected model/auth type and do not establish the completed upstream SDP exchange. They therefore cannot serve as a proven equivalent GPT-Live authentication comparison.
Diagnostic gap
Installed code maps auth-resolution exceptions and provider fatal-auth events to generic errors. Existing debug/trace logging and the inspected diagnostic-flags catalog do not expose a verified way to recover the selected auth route, refresh outcome, or sanitized upstream status/error code.
Release notes mention Discord realtime initialization/configured-agent-model changes and shared OAuth-refresh work around 2026.10.8. These are investigation leads, not evidence that those changes caused this failure.
Requested help
Is this a known Discord GPT-Live startup/authentication issue between 2026.9.9 and 2026.10.9?
Is there a supported diagnostic method to distinguish credential resolution/refresh failure from upstream rejection?
Can startup diagnostics preserve the failing stage, auth type, and allowlisted HTTP status/error code without exposing credentials, account identifiers, response bodies, SDP, audio, or transcripts?
We have not established a credential defect or a confirmed upgrade regression. No custom patch has been applied for this failure.
Submission scope: publish this report only. Do not change local code, configuration, credentials, services, or sessions, and do not run another voice test.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Active Memory's trigger recall (the step that injects `MEMORY.md` entries whose `<!-- trigger: ... -->` words appear in the user's message) matches a Chinese, Japanese, or Korean trigger only when spaces or punctuation separate it from the rest of the message, so in ordinary Chinese or Japanese text it almost never matches. The message is split into words at non-letter characters, so an unspaced sentence such as `明天的会议几点开始？` is one long word, and a trigger such as `会议` (meeting) never equals a whole word of it. Korean triggers miss the same way when a particle is attached (`절차를` does not equal `절차`).

Dreaming promotion writes trigger tags from its concept vocabulary, which segments CJK text on purpose, so promoted CJK entries carry triggers that recall almost never matches.

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191603 fixed the same mismatch for standing intents: a CJK term matches by substring. Trigger recall still compares whole words only.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable the Active Memory plugin for agent `main` with `allowedChatTypes: ["direct"]` and `logging: true`.
2. Put this in the workspace `MEMORY.md`:
   ```markdown
   - The weekly team meeting is in Room 7B on Thursdays at 15:00. <!-- trigger: 会议 --> <!-- importance: 8 -->
   - The deploy checklist lives in docs/deploy.md. <!-- trigger: deploy --> <!-- importance: 8 -->
   ```
3. In a direct chat, send `hello` (so the memory index builds), then `明天的会议几点开始？` ("When does tomorrow's meeting start?"), then `how do I deploy?`.

### Expected behavior

The Chinese turn carries the meeting entry in its `<active_memory_plugin>` block, the same way the English turn carries the deploy entry.

### Actual behavior

The Chinese turn reaches the model with only the skip notice:

```text
<active_memory_plugin>
Active Memory intentionally skipped deep recall because this turn did not ask for past context.
</active_memory_plugin>

明天的会议几点开始？
```

The English turn works:

```text
<active_memory_plugin>
- - The deploy checklist lives in docs/deploy.md. (Source: MEMORY.md#L4)
</active_memory_plugin>

how do I deploy?
```

The Gateway logs `active-memory: lane-1 injected 1 trigger-matched entries` once, for the English turn only.

### OpenClaw version

main @ 1ecd3a9d12974528f299ab885fa43009cb150c29

### Operating system

Linux (Ubuntu, kernel 6.8)

### Install method

Source checkout, built with pnpm

### Model

A local OpenAI-compatible fixture model that records the request and answers with a fixed text

### Provider / routing chain

Custom `openai-completions` provider pointing at the local fixture

### Additional provider/model setup details

An isolated Gateway (its own state directory and loopback port, synthetic token), `memory.search.provider: "none"`. Turns were sent with `openclaw gateway call chat.send` to `agent:main:main`.

### Logs

The blocks under Actual behavior are the current user turn as the fixture model received it.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

See Actual behavior.

### Impact and severity

A trigger written in Chinese or Japanese matches only when spaces or punctuation separate it in the message, so in ordinary Chinese or Japanese text those entries are almost never recalled by their trigger, including the ones dreaming promotes on its own. A Korean trigger misses whenever the message attaches a particle to it. English and other spaced-script triggers are unaffected.

### Additional information

The word splitting is in `extensions/active-memory/trigger-recall.ts` (`normalizeWords` and the whole-word lookups in `prepareTriggerScorer`).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After the 2026.9.x→2026.10.10 upgrade, cron jobs created before the scheduled-tool-policy era (no `payload.toolsAllow`) cannot perform delegated channel reads; the only signal is `Delegated discord:read requires current provider and account context.`, which names no remedy.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On 2026.10.10, run a pre-2026.07 cron job (created before `scheduledToolPolicy` existed, `payload.toolsAllow` absent, job prompt asks the agent to read a Discord channel).
2. Observe the isolated run fail: agent tool calls rejected with `Delegated discord:read requires current provider and account context.`
3. Stamp a finite tool cap: `openclaw automations edit <jobId> --tools message` (job gains `scheduledToolPolicy: {"version":1,"mode":"trusted"}`).
4. Re-run the job — reads succeed.

### Expected behavior

Per `docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md` ("With `message` in the tool cap, scheduled agent turns can read messages and channel information") and #150166, scheduled turns with `message` in the tool cap can read channels. Jobs predating the policy system get no migration path, doctor check, or error pointing at the documented recovery; the failure is silent until you read gateway logs.

### Actual behavior

Every delegated read in the cron-isolated session throws; the job fails with `⚠️ Message failed` and no actionable hint. Reproduced on two agents' jobs (ops watcher + alerts sweep), both fixed by step 3 and verified `ok` by forced runs.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 (production gateway host)

### Install method

npm global

### Model

any — failure is model-independent (gateway-side rejection)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw → api.z.ai coding endpoint

### Logs

Redacted, from one failing run:
```shell
[tools] message failed: Error: Delegated discord:read requires current provider and account context. raw_params={"action":"read","limit":30,"target":"discord:<channelId>"}
[tools] dispatch_action failed: Unknown account "discord" for channel discord.
cron: job run returned error status
```
After `automations edit --tools message` + forced re-run: `ok`.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: operators running pre-2026.07 cron automations that read channels (alert sweeps, ops watchers)
- Severity: High — the monitoring jobs fail permanently with no surfaced reason
- Frequency: every scheduled occurrence, 100%
- Consequence: alerting lanes silently dark until manual log inspection

### Additional information

Related, not duplicates: #154801 (same error signature, stale-closed unfixed; maintainer note confirms legacy jobs still fail), #126634 (open, toolsAllow coupling), #150166 (restored reads for jobs that *have* a tool cap — jobs with none are not covered), #150221 (authority restoration requires an existing policy). Suggested direction consistent with the documented recovery: doctor detection/repair for policy-less jobs and/or an error hint naming `automations edit <jobId> --tools message`, mirroring `resolveCronToolsAllowExecTargetRecoveryError`'s embedded-command style. Happy to contribute the fix.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
When a provider returns HTTP 403 for an upstream outage (`"Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable."`), OpenClaw classifies it as an auth failure, shows "Couldn't sign in to the AI service. Sign in again…", and puts the provider's whole auth profile on cooldown. Every other model on that provider is then skipped with `Provider opencode-go has auth issue (skipping all models)`, even though the API key is valid and those models work.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Configure the `opencode-go` provider with a valid API key and at least two models (here `deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `gemini-4-argon`).
2. While OpenCode Go's Gemini 4 Argon backend is down, send any request to `opencode-go/gemini-4-argon` (for example `openclaw agent --agent <id> --model opencode-go/gemini-4-argon --message "Reply OK."`). The provider answers 403 with `{"error":{"code":403,"status":"UNKNOWN","message":"Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable."}}`.
3. Send a request to `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`.

### Expected behavior
The 403 with "Endpoint is unavailable" is treated as a model/endpoint availability failure: that one model fails (and its fallback chain moves on), the error says the endpoint is unavailable, and other models on the same provider keep working. The user is not told to sign in again.

### Actual behavior
- The Argon request surfaces "⚠️ Couldn't sign in to the AI service. Sign in again under Models in the Control UI or run `openclaw configure`. | 403".
- The auth profile is marked `reason=auth window=cooldown`, and the fallback decision is `reason=auth`.
- The DeepSeek request on the same provider then fails without being sent: `All models failed (1): opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash: Provider opencode-go has auth issue (skipping all models) (auth) | MODEL_FALLBACK_SKIPPED`.
- Each further Argon request renews the cooldown, so any agent whose chain includes the down model keeps blocking every model on the provider. Restarting the Gateway cleared it.
- The same key worked for DeepSeek on opencode-go right before the Argon 403, and the provider's dashboard showed no account problem.

### OpenClaw version
2026.10.10 (7dc3350)

### Operating system
openSUSE Tumbleweed (Linux 7.3), Node v26.12.1

### Install method
npm global (`~/.local/lib/node_modules/openclaw`), Gateway as a systemd user service

### Model
opencode-go/gemini-4-argon (failing endpoint); opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash (collateral)

### Provider / routing chain
opencode-go (built-in provider, one API-key auth profile) → gemini-4-argon / deepseek-v4.1-flash; agents also have muse-code, openai and anthropic models in their fallback chains.

### Logs
```
[provider-error] Model request failed ... provider=opencode-go model=gemini-4-argon status=403 message="{\"error\":{\"code\":403,\"status\":\"UNKNOWN\",\"message\":\"Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable.\"}}"
[agent/embedded] Assistant attempt failed provider=opencode-go model=gemini-4-argon code=403 message="403: {...\"Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable.\"}}"
[agent/embedded] auth profile failure state updated: ... provider=opencode-go reason=auth window=cooldown reused=false
[agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: stage=assistant decision=surface_error reason=auth attempt=1 retry=0 rotations=0 from=opencode-go/gemini-4-argon
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=opencode-go/gemini-4-argon candidate=opencode-go/gemini-4-argon reason=auth next=none detail=Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable.
[model-fallback/decision] decision=skip_candidate requested=opencode-go/gemini-4-argon candidate=opencode-go/gemini-4-argon reason=auth   (x12 over the following hour)
```
Suggested fix: classify a 403 as auth only when the body indicates an auth/permission problem; treat upstream/endpoint-unavailable bodies as a per-model availability failure, and scope any cooldown to the model rather than the whole auth profile.

issues.body:
## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (7dc3350), Linux arm64 (Raspberry Pi 5), Node v24.22.1
- `/tmp` is a 1 GiB tmpfs (`tmp_size=1073741824`); the host has 16 GB RAM and 6 GB swap
- Single gateway, ~500 archived session transcripts (`.jsonl.zst`)

## Observed

After the 2026.10.10 upgrade, the gateway materialized the entire compressed session archive into `/tmp/openclaw/session-archive-read-cache`:

```
$ du -sm /tmp/openclaw/session-archive-read-cache
623     /tmp/openclaw/session-archive-read-cache
$ ls /tmp/openclaw/session-archive-read-cache | wc -l
495
$ ls -lS /tmp/openclaw/session-archive-read-cache | head -1
-rw------- 1 sxr sxr 81677322 ... cb221a94...-14781566-1793242040676.jsonl
```

That is 495 decompressed copies (largest ~78 MiB) — 62 % of the whole tmpfs for one cache directory. `/tmp` reached 77 % (821 MB) and stayed there; any other writer on `/tmp` would start failing. Clearing the directory by hand freed 619 MB, and the same 495 files were regenerated about 18 minutes later by the next archive-reading pass.

## Mechanism

`src/config/sessions/archive-compression.ts`:

- `materializeSessionArchiveForRead()` writes each `.zst` archive as plain JSONL under `path.join(resolvePreferredOpenClawTmpDir(), "session-archive-read-cache")`.
- `resolvePreferredOpenClawTmpDir()` hardcodes `/tmp/openclaw` on POSIX; there is no config/env override to move the cache to a disk-backed path.
- `MATERIALIZED_ARCHIVE_CACHE_TTL_MS = 864e5` (24 h). `sweepMaterializedArchiveCache()` runs at most once per hour and only unlinks entries whose mtime is older than 24 h — there is no total-size or entry-count cap.

So peak usage scales with the total size of all compressed transcripts, and persists for a day. On a small tmpfs this is enough to take down unrelated writers (session saves, update staging, screenshots).

## Expected

At minimum, the cache should not be able to consume most of `/tmp`:

1. A size/entry budget with LRU eviction (e.g. keep the most recently read N archives or ≤ X MB).
2. A configurable cache root, so deployments with a small tmpfs can point it at disk (`OPENCLAW_CACHE_DIR`-style), instead of the hardcoded `/tmp/openclaw`.
3. Or materialize only the byte range/page being read instead of the full decompressed archive.

A startup warning when `/tmp` free space is below the projected cache size would also help operators plan.

## Notes

- The 24 h TTL is also unnecessarily long for a read cache; the same archives are rarely re-read.
- Reproduced twice today (12:30 and 12:48 local) on a clean 1 GiB tmpfs.

I can test a patch on this host if useful.

issues.body:
### Summary Add a native, conversation-scoped collection for finding, previewing, and saving files shared in an iOS chat. ### Problem to solve While using the iOS app, I wanted to return to files shared in a conversation without finding each original message again. **Pages → Files** opens the agent's workspace, which answers a different question: what is in the agent's working directory, rather than what was shared in this conversation. Individual attachment downloads already exist; the missing piece is a place to find those files together. Concrete examples where this would help: - Return to a PDF brief after a long exchange of messages without remembering where it appeared. - Find a task's available documents and reference images in one collection, using their names or types instead of the surrounding conversation text. - Preview a result, save it to iOS Files or share it with another app, then return to the same conversation. The conversation already supplies useful context. A collection would make its available outputs and uploads easier to retrieve without requiring users to export and organize every file immediately. This is about reducing retrieval friction, not replacing the workspace or reorganizing files on disk. ### Proposed solution Provide a **files shared in this conversation** view for the current chat, including the main session: - List available attachments from both the user and assistant, with names, types, and sizes when known. - Search the returned collection by name and filter by type; keep distinct files with the same name separate. - Preview supported text, images, and PDFs, with the system Share / Save to Files flow for supported downloads. - Return to the same chat without changing its draft. Keep the collection bound to that conversation and Gateway. **Attachment scope:** The proposal includes supported assistant files and user uploads returned by the catalog. These have different native baselines: [current iOS documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6d08b6c7f0127937e6307a48ee4e47b9ef34433a/docs/platforms/ios.md#L35) describes assistant-file downloads but says inbound uploads cannot yet be downloaded from native history. Retrieving user uploads is therefore an additional part of the proposed scope. A separate local validation on November 5 found and addressed a Gateway catalog gap for canonical inbound attachments; the end-to-end results are below. This extension is not shipped upstream. I have a local native prototype with a direct toolbar button beside the chat-actions menu. Files are conversation content that users may revisit, so direct access seems easier to discover than placing them among configuration and export actions. The prototype calls the view **Artifacts** and uses a `tray.full` symbol to suggest a collection. The name, icon, and placement are proposals, open to the project's design direction. **Product decision requested:** Should native iOS include this conversation-scoped collection? For an initial version, I propose the direct chat-toolbar entry shown below, with text/image/PDF previews and system sharing, using the existing artifact catalog and download contracts. Naming and placement remain open to the native app’s design direction; the prototype is a concrete option to evaluate, not a settled design. ### Alternatives considered - **Scroll or search the chat:** useful for the surrounding discussion, but requires locating messages to retrieve individual files. - **Use Workspace Files:** valuable for working-directory access, but not a list of attachments from a particular conversation. - **Save everything to iOS Files immediately:** useful for long-term organization, but requires manual export before knowing which results will be needed later. - **Use the web Files experience:** useful existing functionality and design reference; this proposal brings a focused retrieval flow into the native app. ### Impact Affected: iOS users returning to attachments in ongoing conversations, especially longer chats or tasks with several files. This is a usability improvement, not a data-loss report or a release blocker. The practical cost is repeated scrolling and manual file organization; I have not measured population-wide frequency or time savings. ### Evidence/examples **Current integration gap — source checked at `6d08b6c7f012`:** - **The conversation catalog already exists.** The [Gateway artifact contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6d08b6c7f0127937e6307a48ee4e47b9ef34433a/docs/gateway/protocol/rpc-talk-config-and-agents.md#L87) supports session-scoped discovery and downloads, with current session-access checks. - **The web client consumes that catalog.** Its [Files data owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6d08b6c7f0127937e6307a48ee4e47b9ef34433a/ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-session-workspace-state.ts#L138) requests `artifacts.list` with the conversation’s `sessionKey` and `agentId`. - **Native Workspace Files serves a different purpose.** Its [request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6d08b6c7f0127937e6307a48ee4e47b9ef34433a/apps/ios/Sources/Design/AgentWorkspaceFilesScreen.swift#L188) uses `agents.workspace.list` with an agent and directory path, not the conversation’s attachment catalog. - **Native chat has individual downloads, but no collection entry in these controls.** The [chat toolbar](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6d08b6c7f0127937e6307a48ee4e47b9ef34433a/apps/ios/Sources/Design/ChatProTab.swift#L113) and [complete chat-actions menu](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6d08b6c7f0127937e6307a48ee4e47b9ef34433a/apps/ios/Sources/Design/ChatProTab.swift#L448) do not expose a conversation file collection. The existing [native download transport](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6d08b6c7f0127937e6307a48ee4e47b9ef34433a/apps/ios/Sources/Chat/IOSGatewayChatTransport.swift#L565) already scopes downloads to the conversation and rejects results after a Gateway-route change. These sources were rechecked at `4a43644e7a7b`. A fresh simulator run on that native baseline also confirmed the retrieval gap: an assistant file downloaded successfully from its message, but neither the chat controls nor Workspace Files offered a conversation collection. This is a missing retrieval flow, not a claim that a previously supported collection regressed. The screenshots below show the earlier physical-device prototype. Original, unannotated captures of the local native Debug prototype, in English and Light mode, on a physical iPhone 17 / iOS 27.0.1. The files are synthetic. These are working app screens, not mockups or App Store screenshots. The first screen shows the proposed Artifacts button: the tray icon immediately left of the three-dot chat-actions menu.
Chat entry point Conversation collection Native PDF preview
The prototype is based on upstream `8ac9810c6eaff05ce4f7e5f38a3f714638674562`, built as iOS Debug 2026.10.10 (970). I checked the collection, search/filtering, text/PDF previews, system sharing, and return to the chat on the physical iPhone against an isolated TLS Gateway 2026.10.9. Image preview was also checked separately. No model generated these fixture files. This is a local product prototype, not a claim of full platform/CI qualification. Its code is not published yet, so the screenshots and the self-reported results below do not provide independent verification of the implementation.
Prototype validation — executed November 4, 2026 - **Real isolated Gateway:** seven synthetic files downloaded through both inline RPC and HTTPS with matching bytes/hashes; empty and secondary conversations checked; an artifact ID requested from the wrong conversation was rejected. This used `operator.read/write`, not a test of `operator.sessions.read` alone. Synthetic transcript fixtures do not establish the complete user-upload flow from the iOS picker through history reload. - **Native contracts:** transport, media-loader, and collection suites passed, including retired-route rejection, cancellation, duplicate filenames, unsupported previews, and retry behavior. These controlled tests are separate from the real-Gateway checks above. - **Physical UI:** the collection → search/filter → text/PDF preview → system Share → return-to-chat test passed, including draft preservation. The toolbar revision passed the same flow in 55.806 seconds. - **Typography:** the initial combined device run failed on 13 source-reading checks because Mac source paths were unavailable on the iPhone. The typography suite subsequently passed all 23 tests on the simulator. The original combined run was not green. These are results from the prototype environment identified above, not a fresh run against current upstream or a public CI result.
Follow-up validation — executed November 5, 2026 Native baseline and prototype were built from upstream `4a43644e7a7b` using Xcode 27.1, iPhone 17 Simulator / iOS 27.0, Debug 2026.10.10 (1193). The screenshots above remain from the earlier physical-device build. The isolated Gateway initially ran 2026.10.9; the upload fix was tested on source version 2026.10.10. The picker, app, network, persistence, preview, and iOS export were real; only the model reply was supplied by a local synthetic responder. - **Baseline control:** the existing chat download returned the original 197-byte assistant file. Chat toolbar/actions had no collection, and Workspace Files showed its separate workspace scope. The prototype made that same file retrievable from the collection. - **Actual upload exposed a catalog gap:** a file selected and sent through the iOS picker survived history reload but was absent from the catalog. The local Gateway extension projects canonical inbound attachment facts through the existing artifact owner and download authorization, without a new RPC or filesystem index. Restoring the previous owner makes the inbound discovery test fail while inline/managed controls still pass, with the same pinned dependencies. - **Complete upload/export flow:** after the fix, both the earlier upload and a fresh picker upload were retrievable. The fresh file survived app relaunch, appeared in the collection and native preview, and was saved through Share → Save to Files. The input and saved copy were byte-identical; the export remained after dismissal, the temporary file was removed, and a nonempty chat draft stayed intact. - **Isolation and regressions:** real Gateway requests from another conversation were rejected, and an empty conversation showed no foreign files. Controlled tests cover route changes, cancellation, access revocation, changed bytes, removed transcript membership, missing/oversized files, and unsupported paths. Review also found repeated artifact identities; the native collection now deduplicates by ID while preserving distinct files with the same name. - **Checks:** 78 native tests, 9 shared tests, the UI flow (61.658 s), and 78 Gateway/media-store tests passed. Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, documentation, and test-line-budget checks passed. The UI test uses seeded fixtures; the separate picker/export run above supplies ingestion evidence. These are self-reported local results for the unpublished code, not public CI or independent upstream approval. Product/design agreement and external code review are still needed.
### Do you plan to open a PR for this? This proposal is open for a contributor interested in implementing it. The user flows, scope, and prototype screenshots are included above; the initial scope and entry point remain open for maintainer agreement. ### Additional information This builds on the existing workspace browser (#100705 / #100767), native document download/export work (#155195), and mobile web Files browsing (#176329). Those provide useful foundations; the proposed addition is a native collection scoped to the conversation. The prototype reuses the existing artifact list/download contracts and authorization. Recovering canonical inbound uploads also requires the bounded Gateway catalog extension described above. Neither part introduces a new filesystem index or model tool. Workspace browsing remains separate. The collection follows the existing artifact catalog, not every path mentioned in chat or a permanent offline archive. Some images linked only in Markdown are not included and remain accessible in the conversation. Editing, deleting, moving files, and revision history are outside this proposal. ### Acceptance criteria for an implementation - Retrieve a cataloged file without locating its original message; search/filter the returned collection and keep same-name files distinct. Show empty, partial, and failed loads accurately. - Keep listing, preview, and export bound to the originating conversation and Gateway. Switching either must discard stale results; unauthorized, missing, or expired artifacts must not yield file bytes. - Preserve the chat draft when entering and leaving the collection. Keep exported bytes available throughout the system sharing activity, then clean up temporary files through the existing owner. - Validate assistant outputs and user uploads separately. For uploads, exercise the native picker/send → history reload → collection → download path, not only a seeded transcript. Preview only supported types within existing limits; do not execute active document content. These criteria describe what an implementation must demonstrate; they are not claims that every scenario has already been validated by the private prototype.

### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary
Memory Wiki ChatGPT re-import retains an older transcript when it contains a literal Notes start marker inside Markdown code.

### Reproduction
1. Enable Memory Wiki with an isolated vault and bridge disabled.
2. Import a supported synthetic conversations.json containing the following assistant message:

````markdown
~~~html
<!-- openclaw:human:start -->
CODE_v1
<!-- openclaw:human:end -->
~~~
````

3. Add a handwritten note inside the generated page's actual final Notes slot.
4. Change CODE_v1 to CODE_v2 in the export and re-import it.
5. Independently read the generated source page.

Expected: CODE_v2 replaces CODE_v1 and handwritten Notes remain exact.
Observed on main 982f3b1ee2b668afafe69c352d48baef470d2d20: command exits 0 while CODE_v1 remains and CODE_v2 is absent. Ordinary transcript and end-only-marker controls refresh correctly.

### Environment and evidence
Source build 2026.10.10; Debian trixie Linux arm64 Docker; Node 24.22.1; independent pnpm 12.15.0 frozen installation and official sourcePerformance runtime build. Actual dist/entry.js CLI processes, temporary home/state/vault, synthetic supported export data, network disabled for behavioral proof, no ChatGPT account or model calls.

Default Notes lookup scans unmasked source. Existing dollar-replacement and malformed-real-Notes fixes are adjacent. Preserve the strict refusal to overwrite Notes with missing opening/closing/both markers; do not enable markerless legacy acceptance for ChatGPT pages.

issues.body:
## Environment

OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (npm global install), Windows host, a fleet of roughly thirty scheduled automations with agentTurn payloads, all created before 2026.10.10.

## Observed

After updating to 2026.10.10, scheduled automations stopped running with: "Automation has no recorded inference account. Explicitly select its account with a model@profile update before running it."

The failure hit the whole fleet, not one job: a 30-minute job showed five consecutive errors, an hourly job four, and every job I sampled carried the identical error text. The impact window ran from the update (the gateway restarted into 2026.10.10 at about 15:46 local) until each job's model field was re-bound with an @profile suffix. Nothing at update time migrated the bindings or warned about the requirement; the only signal was the per-run error, and on a channel-less gateway the failure alerts could not deliver either.

## Expected

An update that changes the inference-account requirement should migrate existing automations, or fail visibly at update time. At minimum, the release notes should name the re-binding step and the platform should list unbound jobs in a health check.

## Suggested fix

1. Migrate existing jobs' account binding during the update, or default them to the gateway's primary profile.
2. Surface unbound automations in doctor or status output, with the exact re-binding instruction (the run error already contains it).
3. Call out the requirement in the release notes whenever the account model changes.

## Related

#158819 (failure-alert and one-shot delivery visibility, the reason the fleet breakage stayed silent), #128140 (a separate concurrent memory-subsystem problem, not the cause here).

## `update repair` / `doctor --fix` permanently refused on macOS 15.x — new service-membership check requires `ps -o "resource coalition="` which old macOS `ps` does not support

### Summary

Since OpenClaw 2026.10.10, `openclaw update repair` and `openclaw doctor --fix` can never enter maintenance on macOS < 14 (e.g. macOS 15.7.5 / macOS 12–13 era `ps`). Every attempt fails with:

```
Doctor could not enter maintenance. Error: Process ancestry could not be fully inspected.
Use the Gateway update action for a managed handoff, or retry from an independent terminal
without inherited service markers. Stop the Gateway service and other OpenClaw processes
using this state, then run openclaw doctor --fix from an independent shell.
```

This did **not** happen before 2026.10.10 — `update repair` worked fine on the same machine with earlier versions (10.2 … 10.6). Each failed attempt also leaves a new `update_runs` row (`reason=repair-failed` / `abandoned`), so retrying accumulates bad records.

### Root cause (code-level)

New file in 2026.10.10: `src/daemon/service-process-membership.ts` (dist: `service-process-membership-*.mjs`).

`inspectLaunchdMembership(gatewayPid)` first compares process groups:

```ts
if (groups.get(process.pid) === groups.get(gatewayPid)) return "inside";
const caller  = readResourceCoalition(process.pid);
const gateway = readResourceCoalition(gatewayPid);
if (caller === void 0 || gateway === void 0) return "unknown";   // <-- always hits here on macOS 15.x
```

`readResourceCoalition` (via `@openclaw/proc-safe/darwin`) runs `ps -o "resource coalition=" -p <pid>`. On macOS 15.7.5 this fails:

```
$ ps -o "resource coalition=" -p 1234
ps: resource: keyword not found
ps: coalition: keyword not found
```

So `readResourceCoalition` returns `undefined` (the "feature unsupported" case, distinct from `null` = "no coalition"), membership becomes `"unknown"`, and the admission gate:

```ts
function resolveServiceProcessMembershipBlock(membership, ancestryComplete, platform = process.platform) {
  if (membership === "inside") return "inside-gateway-service";
  if (membership === "unknown") return "service-membership-unverified";
  return !ancestryComplete && (platform !== "darwin" || membership !== "outside")
    ? "service-ancestry-unverified"
    : void 0;
}
```

refuses the maintenance entry. On darwin the only pass condition is `membership === "outside"`, which is **unreachable** when the `ps` feature is missing — regardless of whether the Gateway is stopped, and regardless of process ancestry.

### Why this is a regression, not intended behavior

- On macOS 14+, `ps -o "resource coalition="` works, and the design intent is clear from the gate: when coalition proves `outside`, ancestry completeness is not required.
- On older macOS the same "outside" proof is equally strong via the pgid/sess check that runs *before* the coalition lookup (distinct process groups + sessions already prove the CLI is not in the Gateway's launchd service group). The coalition lookup should be an *enhancement*, not a hard requirement.

### Suggested fix

In `inspectLaunchdMembership`, when the coalition feature is unavailable for **both** pids (`caller === undefined && gateway === undefined`), fall through to `"outside"` instead of `"unknown"` — the preceding pgid comparison already established distinct process groups. Minimal diff (verified locally):

```ts
const caller = readResourceCoalition(process.pid);
const gateway = readResourceCoalition(gatewayPid);
// ps without "resource coalition" support (macOS 15.x) returns undefined for BOTH pids;
// the pgid check above already proved distinct session groups, so treat as outside.
if (caller === undefined && gateway === undefined) return "outside";
if (caller === undefined || gateway === undefined) return "unknown";
```

Alternative: probe `ps` capabilities once at startup and skip the coalition path on older macOS.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (7dc3350), Node v26.12.1
- macOS 15.7.5 (x86_64, Intel), `ps` from /bin/ps
- Gateway installed via npm global (`/usr/local/lib/node_modules/openclaw`), launchd service
- `openclaw update repair --yes` (independent Terminal, Gateway stopped or running — same result)

### Local workaround applied

Patched dist locally (backup `service-process-membership-OOxxz7LH.mjs.bak-20261105-ps-coalition`) with the diff above; `node --check` passes. Will be lost on next upgrade.

### Verification on 15.x

```
$ ps -o "resource coalition=" -p $$
ps: resource: keyword not found
ps: coalition: keyword not found
```

## Summary

`openclaw update` (both in-gateway `/update` and CLI `openclaw update`) fails on macOS 26.3.1 (arm64) with a **false** `global-install-permission-denied`: the validator reports EACCES on `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules` although the directory is fully writable by the invoking user. The same run shows the updater's process-inspection/sandbox layer failing repeatedly, and state capture refuses to export because the capture walker hits a root-owned `.fseventsd` inside a mounted volume under the state dir.

## Environment

- macOS 26.3.1 (arm64), node v24.22.1
- openclaw 2026.10.10-beta.5 (npm global install in /opt/homebrew), updating to 2026.10.10
- Install mode: npm; LaunchAgent gateway

## Evidence

1. In-gateway `/update` (2026-11-03 12:23): admission checks all pass (config, database-schema, node-runtime, plugin-availability); staging OK; fails in **validating** with:
```
Failed: package-update — Exit code: 1; Package update cannot write /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules (EACCES; owner UID 501, GID 80)
Failing check package-install (global-install-permission-denied)
```
2. CLI `openclaw update` from Terminal fails **identically** — so this is not gateway-specific.
3. Filesystem is proven writable: prefix is `drwxr-xr-x alex:admin`, no ACLs/flags (`ls -leO`), live `touch` write tests succeed at the prefix, in a leftover updater stage dir, and inside the package dir. The suggested `chmod u+rwx` is a no-op.
4. Plain `npm install -g openclaw@2026.10.10` succeeds in 25s and the new version runs fine — only the updater's validating phase is broken.
5. Same failed run logs the updater's process-inspection failing 7× with:
```
[infra:temp-artifacts] Runtime retained at /opt/homebrew/lib/openclaw-update-runtime-*: Could not inspect OpenClaw processes: ProcSafeError: incomplete: unterminated Darwin environment
```
   (each failure also retained a ~0.5–1.6 GB runtime copy — ~4.6 GB accumulated across 2 failed attempts on one machine)
6. State capture refused:
```
Private update capture marker is unreadable; export refused. | EACCES: permission denied,
lstat '$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/workspace/state/polycs-local/store/.fseventsd/.openclaw-private-update-capture' | EACCES
```
   `.fseventsd` inside that mounted APFS volume is `drwx------ root` (macOS creates it on mount). The capture walker treats an unreadable directory as grounds to abort the **entire** state-capture export instead of skipping the foreign/system dir.

## Actual vs expected

- Actual: update blocked for npm-prefix users on macOS 26.3 with a mounted volume under the state dir; recovery advice (chmod) does not apply; each failed attempt leaves a retained updater runtime (no visible cap).
- Expected: the permission probe should reflect real filesystem access (or clearly attribute sandbox-internal failures), the capture walker should skip unreadable/system dirs and still export, and retained debug runtimes need a retention cap.

## Workaround

`npm install -g openclaw@<version>` + gateway restart; then manually delete `/opt/homebrew/lib/openclaw-update-runtime-*`.

Related: #135299 (upgrade permission failures family), #186650 (update-capture scan fragility). Happy to provide the full update-reports (19426995…, ff70482e…) and the diagnostic JSON if useful.

issues.body:
### Summary

On macOS (Intel x64), `openclaw gateway stop` and `openclaw gateway stop --force` both fail with:

```
Gateway stop failed: ServiceInspectionError: Process ancestry could not be fully inspected.
Use the Gateway update action for a managed handoff, or retry from an independent terminal
without inherited service markers.
```

The command is run from a **standalone Terminal.app login shell** (not spawned by the Gateway, no inherited service markers), so the suggested remedy cannot be followed. `--force` — documented as "Allow stop from a non-interactive shell" — does not bypass the check either.

### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| OpenClaw | 2026.10.10 (7dc3350) |
| Install | npm global, launchd LaunchAgent (macOS) |
| OS | macOS 15.8.1, x86_64 (Intel) |
| Node | v26.12.1 |
| Shell | zsh login shell in Terminal.app (ttys000) |

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch the macOS Terminal app from Spotlight (independent shell, no gateway ancestry).
2. Run `openclaw gateway stop` → fails with `ServiceInspectionError: Process ancestry could not be fully inspected`.
3. Run `openclaw gateway stop --force` → fails with the identical error.

### Expected

`gateway stop` either succeeds, or at minimum `--force` overrides the ancestry heuristic as documented.

### Actual

Both variants refuse to act. The only working path is bypassing the CLI and driving launchd directly:

```
launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/<gateway-label>
# run offline maintenance (e.g. openclaw doctor --fix)
launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/<gateway-label>.plist
```

### Related symptom (possibly same root cause)

`openclaw doctor --fix` also reports process-inspection failures and therefore retains temporary updater runtimes:

```
[infra:temp-artifacts] Runtime retained at <path>: Could not inspect OpenClaw processes:
ProcSafeError: layout-mismatch: invalid Darwin argument alignment
```

Three retained runtime directories (~1.8 GiB total) had to be cleaned manually.

### Analysis

Both failures point at the native process inspection layer (`proc-safe`) rather than the service itself: the ancestry check cannot complete, and the same layer reports a sysctl/kernel-struct layout mismatch on Darwin x86_64. This suggests the process inspection helper mis-parses Darwin process arguments on this platform/build.

### Impact

- Cannot stop the Gateway through the documented CLI path.

issues.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw --help` costs about **36 ms** with no config file, but about **1274 ms** as soon as the config file contains a `plugins` key — for **byte-identical** help output. That is a ~35x slowdown on the most common entry point into the CLI, and it happens on every invocation.

The cost is not the `plugins` value being meaningful. A `plugins` key that does not affect help at all is enough to trigger it.

## Reproduction

Release build, Node v22.23.1, config at `$HOME/.openclaw/openclaw.json`, fresh `HOME` per run, 5 runs per case, `md5` of raw stdout:

| config file | `--help` p50 | mean | stdout md5 | bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| *(none)* | 36 ms | 37.2 ms | `b46e2268ed` | 7126 |
| `{"gateway":{"port":1234}}` | 36 ms | 36.0 ms | `b46e2268ed` | 7126 |
| `{"plugins":{}}` | **1274 ms** | **1281.8 ms** | `b46e2268ed` | 7126 |
| `{"plugins":{"entries":{"a":{"enabled":true}}}}` | 2014 ms | 2011.6 ms | `b46e2268ed` | 7126 |
| `{"plugins":{"enabled":false}}` | 1819 ms | 1814.4 ms | `250658844f` | 7061 |

The third row is the bug: identical bytes to the no-config case, ~1238 ms more work.

The last row is **not** a bug — `plugins.enabled: false` legitimately changes the output (65 fewer bytes, bundled plugins stripped), so it must keep loading the config.

## Where it comes from

`loadRootHelpRenderOptionsForConfigSensitivePlugins` in `src/cli/root-help-live-config.ts` unconditionally does:

```ts
const configModule = await import("../config/config.js");
const snapshot = await configModule.readConfigFileSnapshot({ observe: false, skipPluginValidation: true });
```

…and only afterwards decides whether anything about `plugins` actually affects help. When the answer is "no", the whole config load is discarded and `outputPrecomputedRootHelpText()` prints the same bytes it would have printed anyway.

## Why it has not shown up in the startup bench

`scripts/bench-cli-startup.ts` has a `--help` case, but `buildConfigFixture` returns `null` for every case except `configGetGatewayPort`, `gatewayHealthJson`, `health` and `healthJson` — and those four write only a `gateway` key. So the benched `--help` runs with **no config file at all**, and the four cases that do get a config get a gateway-only one, which measures the same as no config (36 ms above).

The harness and its regression budget therefore cannot observe this path. That is an honest gap in fixture coverage, not a mistake by anyone.

## Prior art

[#85396](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/85396) by @FelixIsaac proposed a fast path for this and was closed stale on 2026-07-22 after review raised compatibility concerns around the dotenv probe paths — specifically the legacy `~/.config/openclaw/gateway.env` route and a `.env` sitting beside an explicit `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. Those concerns were valid: reading the config has the side effect of loading those dotenv files, so any fast path has to account for them before it can skip the read.

I am opening a PR against this issue that keeps those two routes on the slow path explicitly, with tests for both.

## Environment

- Node v22.23.1, Linux x64
- Release build (`pnpm build`, `node openclaw.mjs --help`)
- Reproduced on `main` at `417bd3c88a33e1fb823c279ac8017be4effdd384`

*Investigated with AI assistance.*

issues.body:
## Problem
During 2026.11.5-beta.1, GitHub created duplicate "ghost" queued jobs in rerun attempts of FRV children, which made the children unsealable and killed two whole FRVs (~7.5 h).

- FRV 41641584200: `frv continue --failed` reran two normalCi jobs in one request; normalCi 41642643158 attempt 3 held ~40 phantom queued `checks-node-core-src-security-3` jobs.
- FRV 41667384444: **single-job** `frv rerun --job` attempts 5–7 also showed 25–31 duplicates; attempt-6 seal failed with `Child evidence publisher is not in the current active workflow attempt`.
- One batched rerun per child on FRV 41732921061 produced clean attempts.

Related tooling gaps seen in the same release:
- `frv continue --failed` reruns each child once per invocation, then idles silently (npm attempt 2 failed 10:42Z, loop idle until 11:06Z).
- `frv rerun --job` blocks until unrelated active children settle (~40 min lost).

## Proposed
- After submitting a rerun, `scripts/frv.mjs` checks the new attempt for duplicate same-name queued jobs and reports "ghost jobs detected; recommend fresh FRV" instead of continuing.
- `continue --failed`: honor a per-signature budget, or exit with "child X failed again; budget N" instead of idling; add `--wait-for-seal`.
- `rerun` returns once the new attempt is observed.
- release-openclaw-ci skill: ghosts can follow any rerun; prefer one batched rerun per child.

Source: 2026.11.5-beta.1 retrospective (openclaw/maintainers release/retrospectives/2026.11.5-beta.1.md, findings 1 and 4).

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
With Claude Code signed in and `claude-cli/*` allowed, `models.list` lists no `claude-cli/*` models and `sessions.create` rejects `claude-cli/<model>` with "Unknown provider", even though Claude CLI model discovery succeeds and its catalog outcome is `ready`.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Sign in to Claude Code (`claude auth status` reports `loggedIn: true`, `authMethod: claude.ai`).
2. Start a Gateway with an Anthropic API key in `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and this config:
   ```json
   {
     "agents": {
       "defaults": {
         "model": { "primary": "anthropic/claude-opus-5" },
         "models": { "anthropic/claude-opus-5": { "agentRuntime": { "id": "openclaw" } } },
         "modelPolicy": { "allow": ["anthropic/*", "claude-cli/*"] }
       }
     }
   }
   ```
3. Run `openclaw gateway call models.list --params '{"view":"all"}' --json`.
4. Run `openclaw gateway call sessions.create --params '{"agentId":"main","model":"claude-cli/claude-opus-5"}' --json`.

### Expected behavior
The Claude Code model list appears as `claude-cli/*` rows next to the `anthropic/*` rows, and `sessions.create` accepts `claude-cli/claude-opus-5`.

### Actual behavior
`models.list` has 0 `claude-cli` rows while `providerOutcomes` reports `claude-cli: ready`. `sessions.create` fails with `INVALID_REQUEST: Unknown provider "claude-cli". Use /models to list providers.` Adding an empty `models.providers["claude-cli"]` entry (`baseUrl` and `api` only) makes all 12 Claude Code models appear and `sessions.create` succeed.

### OpenClaw version
main at fc6dff488ce, built from source

### Operating system
macOS 27.2 (arm64)

### Install method
pnpm build from source

### Model
claude-cli/claude-opus-5 (requested); anthropic/claude-opus-5 (primary)

### Provider / routing chain
openclaw -> claude-cli runtime (Claude Code native login) for claude-cli/*; openclaw -> openclaw runtime -> Anthropic API for anthropic/*

### Additional provider/model setup details
Claude Code 2.1.296 signed in with a claude.ai subscription; its model discovery returns 12 models. Placeholder Anthropic API key. No `models.providers` entries. The discovered `claude-cli` catalog is published by the anthropic plugin, which registers `claude-cli` as a CLI backend rather than as a model provider; the generated plugin catalog filter keeps only providers whose owner plugin it can resolve, and its owner lookup does not consider CLI backends.

### Logs
```text
[ws] res x sessions.create errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=Unknown provider "claude-cli". Use /models to list providers.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
```text
$ claude --version; claude auth status
2.1.296 (Claude Code)  "loggedIn": true  "authMethod": "claude.ai"

Same build of main, same Gateway config except for one line:
                                      claude-cli rows   claude-cli outcome   sessions.create claude-cli/claude-opus-5
no models.providers entry             0                 ready                Unknown provider "claude-cli"
models.providers["claude-cli"] = {}   12 (available)    ready                accepted
```
(`{}` here means `baseUrl` and `api` only, no `models`.)

### Impact and severity
Affected: users who keep `anthropic/*` on the API and want Claude Code models as `claude-cli/*` in the same agent. Severity: blocks the subscription route for that setup. Frequency: every run of the reproduction above. Consequence: the only working options are pinning `anthropic/*` to `claude-cli` (removes the API route) or hand-writing a `models.providers["claude-cli"]` block.

### Additional information
Related: #158922 (claude-cli models report available false after restart), #182467 (spawn validation vs models.list). PR intent: No, proposing the idea only.

issues.body:
## Summary

Managed Claude CLI sessions still change their advertised tools and tool-derived system instructions for a verified message-owned child completion, then change again for an internal `sessions_send` update. This is a remaining explicit-cap case after #176892 and #172026, rather than a request to grant the completion broader execution permissions.

Related: #155868 (agent-sourced roster changes), #167710 (message-only stranded retry), #143017 (broader cache-prefix producers).

## What Problem This Solves

Keep the normal session tool definitions stable while retaining the completion's strict execution rule: only sending the result to its verified source is allowed. Every other action must be refused before argument hooks, tool execution, configured MCP calls or descendant authority export.

## Observed sequence

On OpenClaw 2026.10.5, a managed local Claude CLI conversation went through:

1. Ordinary owner turn: 61 tools.
2. Verified child completion with `message_tool_only`: only `message`, and memory recall guidance omitted.
3. An independent scheduled agent sent an internal `sessions_send` update: 60 tools, with memory guidance restored.

The completion changed its system input from 24,395 to 14,542 encoded bytes; the internal update then used 24,548 bytes. Between the latter two turns workspace/bootstrap inputs and the 44 selected skills were unchanged, as were provider authentication identities. The first internal-update request reported zero cache-read tokens and 84,921 cache-write tokens. A real skill was added before the completion, so this observation alone does not isolate every cause of native process replacement or provider cache invalidation. The provider did not report an exact miss reason for that request.

## Remaining source path after the merged fixes

At #172026 merge `77d9f42c86bf42ee05f997ec5f838ad95d268a0a`:

- `resolveCompletionToolPolicy` still returns `["message"]` for the verified message-owned Claude completion.
- `resolveCliRuntimeToolPolicy` and `prepareCliMcpToolProjection` pass that explicit cap into the MCP projection.
- `constructMcpLoopbackTools` applies `applyPolicyToolsAllow` before serializing the advertised definitions.
- CLI preparation derives exact availability and prompt tools from the filtered result, so memory guidance also changes.

The inherited-requester stable-catalog fix does not undo this explicit filtering. Independently, the `codex_plugins` and `whatsapp_login` factories return no definition for non-owner internal turns; native question mode can add `ask_user`.

## Expected behavior and constraints

- Stable ordered full tool names, descriptions and schemas, plus stable tool-derived guidance, across ordinary owner → verified message-owned completion → internal agent update → ordinary owner, with fixed configuration/skills/inventory.
- The message-owned completion can execute only one source-bound result delivery. Non-message tool calls remain denied before hooks or effects.
- Owner-only actions remain denied to internal non-owner turns; unsupported question actions remain unsupported.
- Revoked/reassigned/replayed completion authority fails closed. Displayed-but-denied tools never become child/cron permissions.
- Preserve one-shot recovery and delivery ownership, avoiding duplicate sends or a completion being recovered as a new human task.
- Real skill/config/schema changes remain truthful; do not ignore fingerprints or freeze authorization.

## Proposed direction

Extend the existing stable-definition / call-time-gating mechanism to the verified message-owned path. Reuse the host's source-reply-only semantics and verified completion capability independently of the presented catalog. Normalize the known route-dependent tool producers through permission-denying executors rather than removing definitions. This is a design direction, not a request to remove `["message"]` enforcement or enable native Claude tools.

## Reproduction and validation

A new local regression on exact merge `77d9f42c86bf42ee05f997ec5f838ad95d268a0a` reaches the production `runAgentAttempt` → CLI preparation → MCP `tools/list` owners. Native provider execution is mocked; policy/preparation/MCP owners are real. On the unchanged product source, the four original tests pass and this new test fails:

```text
Normal tools/list: message, sessions_spawn, read, exec
Verified message-owned completion tools/list: message
Expected: equality of full ordered names, descriptions and schemas
Actual: completion definitions omit sessions_spawn, read and exec
Tests: 1 failed | 4 passed
```

The new test is currently local/uncommitted in `src/agents/command/attempt-execution.cli-mcp.test.ts`, named `keeps the production owner/completion/brain/owner catalog while completion calls stay message-only`. It is not claimed to exist upstream yet. Runner:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/command/attempt-execution.cli-mcp.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The initial control uses four tools to isolate the explicit-cap defect. It is not proof of the complete production catalog, configured MCP, owner-only factory or question-tool invariants. A narrow candidate and those broader permission controls are in progress; passing candidate tests are not claimed here. No provider request or actual channel send was made.

## Original safeguard

#112534 prevented restart recovery from treating a child-completion notification as an interrupted human task, which could repeat work and cascade. #117148 and #162374 later restored verified continuation authority for selected routes. This report preserves that safeguard; catalog presentation and permission to execute should be checked separately.

## Local candidate validation update — 21 October

A local candidate now exercises the complete ordinary-owner → verified message-owned completion → actual `sessions_send` internal/webchat turn → ordinary-owner sequence through command preparation, the production attempt/CLI preparation, real Anthropic argument preparation, MCP list/call, and the actual live-process fingerprint owner. Native/provider execution and external sends are mocked; this is not a live provider-cache result.

- All four turns retain the same 50 ordered tool definitions, the same complete 17,808-byte prepared system instructions, and the same live-process fingerprint. The brain turn still carries its real internal route and absent delivery account.
- The focused batch passed 154 tests, including source-bound delivery, revoked/reassigned completion lineage, native tool restrictions, and authorized-only child exports. A restriction-only tool marker must survive SDK wrappers; retaining a gated executor alone was insufficient for descendant export.
- After stabilizing definitions and instructions, a separate remaining restart came from `agentAccountId` in the process fingerprint: command preparation populates it from the current delivery account, which changed from `default` to absent on the internal turn. Changing only that component made the actual fingerprint match. The candidate uses the exact target session's saved account only for eligible managed-process identity; the current execution account still governs MCP, hooks and event routing. Authentication, credentials, environment, model and workspace invalidators remain intact.

The candidate has independent source review. Its regression is still local and is not yet present in the upstream test tree. The compatible installed-runtime port and rollout checks are separate work. This does not establish provider cache savings, and it does not claim to repair inherited schema-only native refresh behavior. No broader tool grant or persistent context snapshot is required.

issues.body:
## Summary

When a `before_agent_run` hook blocks a run, any message that was **steered** into that run while it was being prepared is never committed to the transcript. The queue then waits the full `DEFAULT_QUEUE_TRANSCRIPT_COMMIT_TIMEOUT_MS` (120 s) for it. Until that timer runs out, the block reply is held back and later messages in the same session queue behind it.

Version: `openclaw@2026.7.1-2`, Telegram channel, `dmScope: "per-peer"`.

## Why it matters

`before_agent_run` is the natural place to enforce a policy on every channel, and a block is the expected outcome there, not an error. We use it in [Pinchy](https://github.com/heypinchy/pinchy) to enforce monthly cost budgets (heypinchy/pinchy#1228): when an agent's budget is used up, the plugin returns `{ outcome: "block", reason: "budget_exhausted", message }`, and the sender should get "Your message could not be sent: …" right away.

A user who gets no answer tends to send a second message ("hello?"). If that second message lands while the first run is still being prepared, it is steered into that run, and the refusal then shows up two minutes late. The block itself still works; the delay makes the agent look broken rather than paused.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Register a plugin with `before_agent_run` that returns `{ outcome: "block", reason: "test", message: "blocked" }`. Set `plugins.entries.<id>.hooks.allowConversationAccess: true`.
2. Send a Telegram DM to the agent, then send a second DM within the short window before the hook has answered. Slowing the hook down by about 1 s makes the window easy to hit.
3. Observe:
   - **Expected:** both messages are refused at once, each with the block reply.
   - **Actual:** the gateway log shows `before_agent_run hook blocked by <plugin>` immediately, but the refusal reaches Telegram only about 120 s later. Messages sent in between wait behind it.

## Where it seems to come from

In `dist/selection-*.js`, `steerActiveSessionWithOptionalDeliveryWait` calls `steerAndWaitForTranscriptCommit(activeSession, text, options.deliveryTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_QUEUE_TRANSCRIPT_COMMIT_TIMEOUT_MS, …)`, which resolves only on the queued user message's end event (`isQueuedUserMessageEnd`). When the active run is blocked before model input, the steered message never produces that event, so the wait runs out instead of resolving.

## Possible fix

When a run ends with a `before_agent_run` block, settle any steered messages that are waiting on its transcript commit right away. Either run each one through the gate as its own turn, or refuse it with the same block decision. Either way the queue would not have to wait out the timeout.

Related, but a different question: #78830 (a `before_steering` hook).

## Problem
2026.11.5-beta.1 publishes 41757100833 and 41759831231 failed before publishing anything. `@openclaw/openshell-sandbox` reported "unreviewed critical findings in exact npm artifact": `dist/.setup/worker-cli-*.mjs` hashed to `c5050d40…`, not the reviewed `799a34cf…` in `REVIEWED_CRITICAL_FINDING_CONTENT_SHA256`.

The normal publish route repacks plugins with the publisher tooling's (P) toolchain. Main moved to tsdown 0.23.2 / rolldown 1.2.15 in #188576, so main's own build had failed this scan since 10-30 without anything noticing. The FRV tarball, built with the candidate's toolchain, still hashed to `799a`. #192489 updated the hash after review; the diff was cosmetic (chunk name and region comments). Cost: about 50 min plus an extra approval.

## Proposed
- Run `scripts/plugin-npm-security-scan.mts` against main-built packs in main CI, so a toolchain bump that changes a reviewed hash fails on main.
- In `release:candidate` / publish preflight, pack and scan with P's toolchain, not only the FRV tarball.
- In `publication-recovery.md`: on a reviewed-hash mismatch, reproduce under P's `.release-tooling` before any redispatch.

Source: 2026.11.5-beta.1 retrospective, finding 7.
