issues.body:
**Scope**

This only affects sessions that run on the Codex harness (`extensions/codex`). Other agents build their own system prompt and already report it fully.

**What happens**

On Codex sessions, the Dashboard's context panel shows "—" for **Workspace files**, **System instructions** and **Messages**. Only Tools and Skills get numbers.

**Why**

1. **AGENTS.md is never confirmed.** Codex loads `AGENTS.md` itself and injects it into the model's context. OpenClaw never sees that happen, so `buildCodexSystemPromptReport` marks the file `injectionStatus: "native_unverified"` with `injectedChars: null`.
   - That one unknown file makes the files total unknown.
   - System instructions and messages are both worked out by subtracting the files total, so they become unknown too.
2. **Codex's base instructions are missing.** The report's `systemPrompt.chars` counts only OpenClaw's developer instructions. Codex also sends base instructions on every request (about 10–17k chars, depending on the model and on who sets them). Today they don't appear anywhere in the breakdown.

On a real Codex session:

| | Messages | Files | Tools | Skills | System |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shown today | — | — | 4,869 | 1,642 | — |

Codex's own record for that session shows 11,481 chars of base instructions and a 6,549-char AGENTS.md fragment. Neither is reflected in the report.

**Why OpenClaw can't simply ask Codex**

Codex has no API for the instructions it loaded into a thread yet:
- The app-server accepts `baseInstructions` and `developerInstructions` on `thread/start`, `thread/resume` and `thread/fork`, but never returns them.
- `thread/read` hides the AGENTS.md block Codex injects.

The only place Codex records either value is its local rollout file (the session's JSONL transcript in the Codex home):
- `session_meta.base_instructions` holds the base instructions.
- The `agents_md` entry in `world_state` records holds the AGENTS.md text the model currently sees. This entry is updated by full snapshots and partial updates, and reset by compaction.

**Proposed fix (Codex harness only)**

After each turn, read Codex's local rollout file and use it to fill in the report:
- Count the base instructions and the rendered AGENTS.md fragment in the system prompt.
- Mark AGENTS.md as confirmed when Codex's recorded text contains the workspace file.

The read follows compaction the same way Codex rebuilds its own context, and only reads what was added since the last read. It applies only when Codex runs locally against OpenClaw's own Codex home. Remote app-servers, unreadable files and changed or truncated content keep today's `native_unverified` status, and a failed read never fails the turn.

**Tradeoff**

This depends on Codex's on-disk rollout format, because Codex has no API for this yet. The plugin already reads `session_meta` from the rollout for its native tool catalog. When Codex adds an app-server method that returns a thread's loaded instructions, this reader should be replaced with it.

**Expected result on the same session**

| | Messages | Files | Tools | Skills | System |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| With the fix | 21,908 | 2,642 | 4,869 | 1,642 | 4,967 |

**Known remaining gap (follow-up)**

Codex also injects context this fix doesn't count, so it still lands in Messages. Messages is still overstated by roughly 12k tokens on this session:
- About 4,300 chars of its own developer messages (permissions, collaboration mode, multi-agent, environment).
- A 45,956-char `additional_tools` item. Its overlap with the tool schemas already counted hasn't been checked.

issues.body:
## Summary

A supported Git install detached at a release tag can successfully fetch the selected remote's `refs/heads/main` but still skip an implicit `--channel dev` update with `no-upstream`. This occurs when `remote.origin.fetch` only maps tags and there is no configured local `main` upstream. A single-branch release-tag clone is a normal way to reach this configuration.

## Reproduction

In an otherwise working Git install cloned with `git clone --single-branch --branch <release-tag> <repository> <directory>`:

1. Confirm HEAD is detached, no local `main` upstream is configured, and `git config --get-all remote.origin.fetch` maps only the release tag.
2. Run the normal `openclaw update --channel dev` command without an explicit detached target.
3. The selected `main` fetch succeeds, but the update returns `skipped` / `no-upstream`.

The private regression uses task-owned synthetic commits, a temporary bare remote, a real tag-only clone, and actual Git execution through the shipped `updateGitCheckout` owner. It verifies the fresh fetched commit before checking the update outcome. No real user repository or running Gateway is updated.

## Expected behavior

Use the commit verified from the successful selected-source fetch, without requiring a remote-tracking mapping. Leave user fetch refspecs/configuration and unrelated remote/local state unchanged, and continue honoring explicit negative exclusions.

## Cause

The fetch owner verifies `FETCH_HEAD^{commit}` but discards that revision. Preflight then requires `main@{upstream}`, which cannot be resolved through a tag-only fetch mapping. The fetched source revision and optional symbolic cache-ref identity must be handled separately.

## Source evidence

Reproduced against admitted base `d3b571f8163c658feafb327d8699d3485ae1680d`. The implicated metadata and preflight files match the supplied `4129e21215e7a6963bf34dc4bf2aad28b1543b95` evidence; the target file differs only in the import owner of `compareSemverStrings`, not the implicated behavior. The same implicated fetch/preflight behavior is still present on main aa401d8fbdd5ac7eb2755022744f33e996fae85b (read-only inspection). The runtime reproduction was performed on the admitted base.

## Credit and disclosure

Reported and scoped by @ooiuuii. Reproduction, implementation, and tests were prepared with AI assistance using OpenClaw (Roboclaw).

prs.title: fix(ui): Control UI checks flake on slow CI shards
prs.body:
Related: #190824 (CI run 41451247788, jobs 125297564171 and 125297564323) ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Control UI checks fail intermittently on contended CI runners when a test's real-time wait also pays for loading a lazy module or for opening dozens of unrelated sections of the complete Settings form. ## User Impact No user-visible change. PRs stop picking up these unrelated `checks-ui` and `checks-ui-e2e` failures, and a future test that hides the same costs fails deterministically on a fast machine instead of only on a slow CI shard. ## Why This Change Was Made All three failures on #190824's head are timing contracts, not leaked state. Each test's real-time budget included work the assertion is not about: - **`chat-details-session.test.ts`, "groups every direct subagent…"** polled for the lazy live-activity element inside `waitForSolid`'s 1 s budget, so the first, cold import of `chat-subagent-activity-live.tsx` counted against it. The test now settles that import with `vi.dynamicImportSettled()` (the file already does this at three other lazy boundaries) and asserts synchronously, leaving no import-speed-dependent wait. - **`config-form-integrity.e2e.test.ts`, "round-trips Agent List model overrides…"** used `revealControl`, which opened closed config sections in document order until the target rendered. Against the complete Gateway schema that meant 48 unrelated sections before reaching the agent's `Tools` section. Callers now name the closed sections that hold a nested control, and the helper fails with that instruction if the control is not rendered. The two other callers never opened a section. - **`plugins-page.test.ts`** failed on that head only because the head predates #191157, which already preloads `settings-view.tsx` before the fake-timer test. Test 2's failure was a cascade from test 1's still-pending import. Main needs no change here.
Why not change waitForSolid itself Settling imports inside the shared helper would add a real macrotask to ~4,000 waits, and it would deadlock tests such as `chat-question-card-loading.test.ts` that deliberately hold a lazy import pending with `vi.doMock` to assert loading states.
## Evidence Reconstructed from the failing job's `[vitest:module]` records: one Bun fork (concurrency slot 2, one environment batch) ran `app-sidebar-rail` → `agents/view` → `session-hovercard` → `widget-card` → `desktop-panel` → **`plugins-page`** → `session-pull-requests` → **`chat-details-session`**. I replayed that exact order in a single Bun fork (`unit` project, `isolate: false` with the cleanup runner) through a scratch sequencer: - On a fast Mac without emulation it passes, matching the green single-file controls. - With cold lazy modules emulated by a 2.5 s real-time top-level await in `settings-view.tsx` and `chat-subagent-activity-live.tsx`, **before** reproduces exactly the three CI unit failures: plugins tests 1 and 2 with `No plugin action matching …`, and the subagent test with `expected null not to be null`. 219 other tests pass. **After** (main with this PR): 222/222. - Without the new settle line, the subagent test now fails 3/3 locally with the CI message (56–74 ms), not just under load. - E2E under 20x Chromium CPU throttle (`Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate`): **before** times out at 120 000 ms, the CI error, with 73.5 s spent in the section walk. **After** it passes in 94.3 s with a 9.3 s reveal. Unthrottled locally, the reveal drops from 5.1 s to 0.8 s and the test from 14.7–17.2 s to 11.0–15.0 s. - The original unnamed `revealControl(rawOnly)` call fails under the new helper with `Pass the closed sections that hold this control`. - `check:changed` passes. The test-line ratchet net delta is 0. The three `revealControl` e2e files pass 7/7. - Cost (`--maxWorkers=1`, local): `chat-details-session.test.ts` 18/18 in 8.6 s wall (tests ≈0.7 s); `config-form-integrity.e2e.test.ts` 3/3 in 22.1 s test time (69 s wall with bundled-UI setup). CI seconds will follow from this PR's run.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): reduce cold concurrent worktree CPU
prs.body:
Related: #192963

## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent worktree creation after #192963 spends extra CPU starting shared-state readers while sandbox preparation loads unrelated command handlers. Five fresh A/A pairs bounded CPU variation to ±1.5%; five A/B pairs reproduced a 14.5% cold-process CPU increase.

## User Impact

Cold sandbox/worktree preparation uses less CPU while unrelated creation keeps its short capacity wait. The fix is 6.9% below the pre-#192963 CPU baseline in the final comparison. Capacity, mutation custody, live-authority checks, and reader-pool limits are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Sandbox registry reads fell through to the aggregate read-handler module. Profiles show that cold import overlapping the independent creator and starting another reader, whose thread and associated internal worker account for about 3 seconds of CPU. The four sandbox reads now use their existing kernel through the existing lazy domain registry. All callers move together; the old fallback dispatch, manual command types, and one-use wrappers are removed. Production code shrinks by 25 lines, with no schema, configuration, cache, or dependency change.

## Evidence

Five counterbalanced triplets on the same frozen synthetic fixture, with only the custody change and this scoped patch varied:

| Measure | Before #192963 | #192963 | This fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Cold Node-process CPU median | 22.280 s | 25.067 s | **20.740 s** |
| Combined-completion p95 | 25.495 s | 24.798 s | **23.214 s** |
| Independent creation median | 16.965 s | 3.993 s | **2.270 s** |
| Capacity wait median | 14,871.7 ms | 15.54 ms | **16.23 ms** |
| Main-isolate allocation median | 392.917 MB | 382.820 MB | **373.089 MB** |

Fixed CPU range is 18.344–21.003 s, below every baseline sample (21.879–22.621 s). The initial block reproduced the completion-p95 increase, but that increase was not stable across blocks; n=5 nearest-rank p95 is the maximum. All completed samples are retained.

Separate recursive diagnostic profiles confirm the targeted import disappears: fixed sandbox-domain preparation takes 20.5 ms, and that run reuses the first reader for the creator's queries. Captured JavaScript allocation drops 260 MB versus custody. One-reader reuse is scheduling-dependent, not a new serialization guarantee. Diagnostic timings include profiler overhead and are excluded from the table.

Fixture: the retained source-run harness (`--import ./scripts/tsx.mjs`), fresh processes/state, Node 26.12.1, pnpm 12.15.0, real rootless Podman installation, Btrfs, 62,018 files / 1.10 GB, 10,001 synthetic sessions. The agent database is 8 MB; **35-GiB database scale is not qualified**. CPU includes Node workers, not container/subprocess CPU. Packaged-CLI cold timing is not measured. No real user data or services were used.

The added startup case fails on the parent specifically because unrelated handlers load, and passes with the fix. **86 focused tests passed** across reader startup/dispatch, registry reads/ordering, authority, preparation/retirement, and allocation/heartbeat loss. UI import search found no affected browser module.

Codex autoreview of the full change against `ffbbb514ba3b7d06d59ca8dd11521e100335da4d`: **scoped-clean through P2**, no accepted/actionable findings. Full `pnpm build` passed, including runtime bundles, declarations, public SDK verification and Control UI. `pnpm check:changed --staged --base ffbbb514ba3b7d06d59ca8dd11521e100335da4d --timed` passed in full, including all 29 affected test typecheck graphs, changed-file lint, export scans and import/schema/authority guards.

The initial CI run (41972591016) failed the test-line budget: the five-line regression met 23 lines of existing main debt. Consolidating the neighboring equivalent absent-publication case into the same startup table preserves its request, result/admission and lazy-import assertions, and database cleanup; total test delta is now −10 lines. No baseline or allocation was raised. The existing debt traces to #185636 (+33 unallocated lines), partially offset by test deletions and a #193183 reconciliation measured before that commit. It is recorded for follow-up; the unchanged-tree exemption means this was not classified as an inherited CI failure.

After the consolidation, all 22 worker-file cases, the affected state-logging typecheck, formatting, and the test-line guard pass. Fresh full-diff Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2.

prs.title: fix(onboarding): keep npx Gateway services running after cache cleanup
prs.body:
Fixes #192328

## What Problem This Solves

Quick start skips background-service setup for npx/dlx users, so closing the terminal stops the Gateway. A manually installed service can also depend on files that disappear when the runner cache is cleared.

## Solution

On supported hosts, Quick start offers background operation. A service installed from npx, pnpm/Yarn dlx or bunx runs the same OpenClaw version from a durable npm copy under the profile's state directory (`<state>/npm`). This applies to `openclaw gateway install`, onboarding/configure/Doctor setup and `openclaw node install`.

- **Planning decides, and never installs.** The runtime and wrapper are validated first, including generated macOS/Windows wrappers, which planning clears. The service entrypoint is planned from the running copy (same version, same layout), so the argument builder never probes a copy that may not exist yet. Repair and Doctor planning reuse an existing copy only when it matches this version and passes integrity checks, and otherwise report an explicit reinstall command instead of installing.
- **The swap happens inside the service install.** Under the package lock, the install checks the durable copy and reuses it when it still matches this version and passes integrity checks. Otherwise npm stages and verifies the copy while any existing service keeps serving the old one. The staged copy must contain the planned entrypoint. The package updater's activation gate releases the swap from `service.install`'s mutation hook, under the service operation lock. The updater's transaction keeps the previous copy until the install settles:
  - if the install fails, the previous copy is restored. When native activation fails, the systemd, launchd and Scheduled Task installers restart the previous definition as part of their recovery. A new optional, internal `beforeRecovery` hook on `GatewayServiceInstallArgs`, run by `withGatewayServiceInstallationRecovery` before the native restore, puts the previous copy back first. Installs that pass no hook behave as before;
  - a failed first install keeps its new copy;
  - after a successful install, the backup is retired once the service is verified loaded.
- **One package lock.** Gateway and node services share the durable copy but not a service lock, so one file lock on the durable npm prefix covers the check, staging and settlement, including a reuse. A failed install's restore therefore cannot undo another install's swap, or the copy another install's service now runs. Only a dead holder's lock is reclaimed. **`openclaw update` does not take this lock.** It updates the copy in place under its own ownership, so an update running at the same moment as a Gateway or node install from npx is not serialized with it. A failed install therefore restores the previous copy only while the live copy is still the one it published (same directory identity, read from the validated candidate the swap renames into place). It passes that check to the package rollback as its authority, which the rollback runs synchronously right before each rename, after its backup verification. If an update has replaced the copy at any point before the restore's renames, the install keeps it, keeps its own backup and warns.
- **PATH and lifecycle.** The service PATH gets the durable launcher folder and excludes disposable runner paths. npm lifecycle scripts run with the current Node. Standalone runtimes and genuine wrappers don't use a durable copy.

## Evidence

- **Targeted tests:** the affected daemon, setup, planning, Gateway-install and node-install test files pass with `--maxWorkers=1`. `tsgo:core`, the affected test-typecheck shards, lint, format and the test-lines ratchet pass.
- **Regressions:** each was red on the commit before its fix and is green now. They cover:
  - an unsupported `--runtime bun` rejected before any package work;
  - generated-wrapper planning;
  - swap, restore and backup retirement around the service install;
  - first Gateway and node installs through the real argument builder;
  - a staged copy missing the planned entry;
  - a failed Gateway install's restore racing a node install that either replaces or reuses the shared copy;
  - the previous copy being in place when native recovery restarts the old service (through the real recovery wrapper), and the systemd installer running the hook before its rollback restart;
  - through the real package swap and rollback, a failed node install restoring the previous copy, and not restoring over a copy that `openclaw update` published while the install's own updater was finishing, before the restore started, or while the rollback verified its backup.
- **Live Linux proof (`7c54aca2d47`):** this proof predates the current planning and locking code. It used a fresh npx Quick start in a throwaway user with its own systemd manager.
  - The Gateway survived closing the terminal, deleting the `_npx` cache and restarting the service.
  - The service ran from `<state>/npm/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js`, with the durable `npm/bin` and no `_npx` on its PATH.
  - An npx reinstall/upgrade from published `2026.10.10` kept settings and an existing session.
  - Model responses were mocked; install, migration, storage and systemd were real.
- **Not verified:** standalone installs end to end, macOS/Windows hosts, real-model inference, an `openclaw update` run of the durable copy, and a live repeat of the install/upgrade proof on the current head.

## Hosted CI

The branch includes main's fix for the Bun Codex worker-fixture assertion, which failed `checks-node-changed-10` on an earlier head. CI for the current head has not been checked here.

## What Problem This Solves

The Windows repair package-owner test fixture shells out to system tar for every synthetic archive. Its existing "without system tar" test restricts PATH only after archive creation, hiding that dependency.

## User Impact

The fixture creates fresh gzip archives through the existing tar dependency and waits for archive closure before removing the lifecycle marker. The no-system-tools check now covers fixture creation too. Production behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Source review: 23 fixture archive calls per complete 24-case file; external fixture tar launches become zero. This is a source-derived process count, not a timing or billing measurement.
- Fresh files and archives remain independent per case. Real Node loader/import-hook processes, package-member authentication, tamper, symlink, missing-member, oversized and compressible-member coverage stay intact.
- The separate real npm pack and offline install case is unchanged.
- Independent source review and local autoreview: no actionable findings. Awaited tar.create completion matches the installed dependency contract.
- Current head passes all 24 cases on explicitly selected Node. Baseline-red/candidate-green no-tools controls pass on Node and pinned Bun. Earlier tooling checks passed; the one-line PATH follow-up has fresh independent source review and formatting proof. Local empty-PATH behavior was traced to Bun host-tool fallback, so the case uses a fresh empty directory. Performance qualification below holds promotion.

Production LOC delta: 0. Tests: +5/-8 (net -3). No new helper, dependency, cache, fixture reuse, timeout or retry.

## Prospective Performance Rule

Record this rule before any timed run. Compare the complete committed baseline and candidate 24-case file on the same Mac host, Node version, frozen dependencies and environment, using the repository test wrapper with one worker and OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node explicitly selected on both sides. Run one untimed warm-up per side, then five serial alternating A/B pairs. Report every pair plus wall time, user CPU, system CPU and peak RSS median, empirical nearest-rank p95, and min/max spread; verify both sides pass the same 24 cases. Do not run other task-owned checks concurrently with timing.

Every measured surface must hold or improve. A regression of 20% or more stops promotion; smaller adverse results hold this draft for explanation rather than being rounded away. prs.title: fix(release): preserve checkout history for SDK review
prs.body:
## Summary

- stop limiting the explicit predecessor-tag fetch to depth 1
- retain `--no-tags`, `--filter=blob:none`, and the exact tag refspec
- add a real-Git regression proving a full checkout stays non-shallow and older changelog provenance ancestry remains valid on rerun

## Cause

`git fetch --depth=1` updates the repository's shallow boundary even when fetching one explicit predecessor tag. In a previously full checkout, the early Plugin SDK API review could therefore turn the repository shallow; a later rerun could then reject an older valid changelog provenance base because the required ancestry was no longer available.

## Recovery for affected checkouts

Restore full history before rerunning the release candidate checks:

```sh
git fetch --unshallow origin
```

## Verification

- focused release-candidate checklist suite: 148 passed
- touched type/lint/format/diff checks passed
- independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: fix(skills): republish a discovery read retired by a config refresh
prs.body:
Closes #189735

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: skills reads can fail with “Skills discovery was retired before publication” when a config refresh commits during their discovery scan. This can lose a `skills.status` refetch or a cron run preparing skills.

## User Impact

An overlapping skills read can return the refreshed publication. Shutdown still rejects the read, and repeated refreshes cannot cause an unbounded retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

The discovery owner records whether refresh or shutdown retired a registration. Publication re-registers the same selection and watch intent once after refresh; normal registration waits for the reset to finish. This keeps recovery at the existing owner instead of adding retries to every caller.

Production delta: +14 lines. The growth records the retirement reason and implements the bounded retry; changing reset ordering would entangle in-flight scans and shutdown. Test delta: +46 lines for the refresh race and distinct shutdown guard. No new configuration, persistent state, or public API.

## Evidence

Independent secretless Linux verification on Node 24.22.1:

- With `refresh.ts` from main `2270152d224ae48de9a10f3fe26b4c594ac9e87d`, the refresh regression fails with the reported retirement error; the shutdown guard passes.
- With this fix, `pnpm test src/skills/runtime/discovery.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes all 19 tests on the contributor head. After merging current main, the exact integrated tree passes all 20 tests (47.10 s suite; 53.78 s runner). The suite covers refresh, shutdown, source environments, watch intent, and worker sharing.

The contributor also ran real isolated Windows Gateway comparisons. When a read started before the config write, main failed 39/40 rounds; this fix failed 0/40, with 39 retries observed. The ordinary write-then-read loop failed 2/200 on main and 0/100 on the final contributor head. This pass did not rerun the live Gateway comparison; it independently reproduced the race at the production discovery boundary.

The current main revision `3cd454f949f1466692261a8615fcc38199027a98` is integrated without changing the fix. Targeted oxlint, oxfmt, and diff checks pass. Independent diff-scoped Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 issue.

Thanks @wr-web for the fix, regression coverage, and original Gateway proof.

prs.title: fix(macos): retain Codex code-mode host JIT entitlements
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #192851. The macOS app signer treats the bundled Codex V8 code-mode host as a plain hardened-runtime executable, dropping its required JIT entitlements. The issue reports that Codex tool calls then crash with V8 CodeRange allocation failure.

## User Impact

The candidate routes only the exact Darwin arm64/x64 Codex code-mode host paths through the existing JIT entitlement set. Ordinary executables, the Rust Codex command, Linux paths, and library-kind entries remain plain. Bun’s separate addon exception and library validation are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fix the existing runtime signing owner rather than disabling hardened runtime or expanding all Codex payload permissions. Cover platform alias packages and the legacy vendor layout. No signing identity, certificate, configuration, protocol or release change.

## Evidence

- Focused regression executes the **actual production runtime inventory/signing loop and entitlement plist**, stubbing signing I/O only. The base fails at the intended host plain-vs-JIT assertion; the candidate passes all four host cases, ordinary negative paths, Bun/Claude controls, both required JIT keys, and an exact-host library-kind negative.
- `python3 scripts/codesign-codex-host.test.py` passed; `bash -n scripts/codesign-mac-app.sh` and `git diff --check` passed. No real app is signed and no candidate runtime/tool is executed by that test.
- Added `test/scripts/codesign-codex-host.test.ts` for ordinary Linux/macOS Vitest discovery with a matching 16-line allocation. **The Vitest wrapper is not yet executed in this worktree; PR CI is pending.** Windows intentionally skips this POSIX signing fixture.
- Independent source assessment found no actionable P0–P2 under the supplied package-layout contract; actual package layout and native signed-app behavior are not certified by that review.

## Remaining Proof — Keep Draft

**Do not merge yet.** Physical packaged-host path qualification, exact-head CI, and a successful Codex tool call from an isolated signed macOS app remain UNRUN. The Linux dispatch regression is not signed-app proof. Read-only Crabbox AWS macOS readiness was refused because the current brokered selection has `capacity.market=spot`, while macOS requires on-demand. No lease was created, no paid-host allocation was requested, no credentials/configuration were changed, and this is not a claim that all Mac providers are unavailable.

No release, notarization, certificate import, Gateway deployment/restart or production signing operation was performed.

prs.title: fix(plugins): preserve environment references when updates migrate settings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw plugins update` replacing an authored environment reference with its resolved value when a replacement plugin moves the setting and core migration changes the plugin allowlist.

## User Impact

Moved settings retain references such as `${LISTENER_HOST}` in root config and single-owner `$include` files. Existing plugin config and installed-index records remain readable and updateable. Previously flattened literals stay literals because their original reference cannot safely be reconstructed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The replacement plugin's selected manifest registry and IDs now accompany both authored/resolved replay views. Replay therefore uses the same candidate migration that moved the setting, even while the old package generation is still the persisted owner. Existing fingerprint checks, deferred-owner selection, backups, guarded publication, completion, and rollback remain in force. There is no new config option, schema, or cache.

The compatibility assertion now checks exact invocation count and selected config/plugin IDs without depending on absent optional fields. The existing include scenario exercises the moved reference too. Current main was merged without rebasing; its #193097 repair also resolves the original unrelated `check-lint-core-2` Promise-executor errors.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `7075e19cff8e3b02264dce5f3c14dbcec3c61caf` reproduces the exact raw-file `${LISTENER_HOST}` → `127.0.0.1` failure at the production update-command boundary on Node 26.12.1 and pinned Bun. Package acquisition and Gateway transport are fixtures in this regression; persistence and migration are real. The affected owners/test are unchanged between that main and merged base `3816bcb3dea1879d055853fc070af78bc7737ab0`.
- **After:** all 46 tests pass on both runtimes across `plugins-update-command.migrations.integration.test.ts`, `channel-legacy-config-migrate.test.ts`, and `config-flow-steps.references.test.ts`, covering the original regression, include ownership, selected/non-channel owners, replacement installs, disabled/pending migrations, completion, and rollback. Node migration-file Vitest duration: 410.34s; two smaller files: 32.27s; total wrapper wall 575.64s. Bun: 226.80s and 29.50s; total wrapper wall 425.26s. The existing SQLite/publication matrix dominates runtime; no new cases were added.
- **Stored-data / real CLI:** a local synthetic npm registry supplied plugin 1.0.0 and 2.0.0. The built `plugins install`, `config validate`, `plugins update`, and `config get` commands loaded old `oldPort`/`oldHost` settings, migrated them, and returned `127.0.0.1` while raw root/include files retained `${LISTENER_HOST}`. Both the ordinary update/retry control (75.16s) and unmarked nonempty allowlist cases (54.58s) passed, preserving the include pointer, unrelated label, and authored policy. Restoring the synthetic state copy emitted a conservative source-snapshot cleanup warning; update/validation succeeded and no deletion bypass was used.
- **Live model:** the built `openclaw infer model run --local --model ollama/qwen2.5:7b` command loaded the updated included config and returned `listener-update-ok` via the shared local Ollama server (18.80s). This is direct CLI/provider proof, not a Gateway/agent-turn claim.
- **Review:** Codex branch autoreview against the pinned merged base, P0–P2, is scoped-clean on `9fcb3e85c450c0984f26b4b8c2ea04a4de3df272`.
- **Ratchets:** `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base 3816bcb3dea1879d055853fc070af78bc7737ab0` and separate line-cap pass. Scoped format/lint, core types, Doctor and CLI test types, and `pnpm build` pass. The build took 931.31s on macOS, including full package declarations and UI assets; lint/type wall times include waiting for its artifact lock.
- **Size:** production +35/-5 (net +30), tests +6/-7 (net -1), docs +14. The production growth is the typed candidate selection forwarded through existing owners. No baseline/ceiling, allocation, dependency, or changelog changes.

Update behavior: the candidate plugin-update command needs the fix; older installed updaters need no new marker or protocol. Existing state is input to the same repair/publication owners; unresolved data migrations retain their inputs and existing Doctor guidance.

Platform limit: local proof ran on macOS. No published-core stable-to-candidate updater run is claimed; the data compatibility proof upgrades an installed synthetic plugin and its existing config/index through the real CLI.

prs.title: perf(cron): avoid duplicate schedule events after completion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Completed recurring cron runs notify clients of the same next-run schedule twice: in `finished`, then in an identical `scheduled` event.

## User Impact

Cron views receive fewer event frames with the same run result and next-run time. Quiet trigger evaluations still publish schedule changes, and historical completions can still be followed by a correction to a different resident schedule. No configuration, schema, authorization, or audience change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record the terminal event's next-run time in the scheduler's existing publication map before invoking callbacks. The schedule publisher then emits only a different fact. This removes duplicate projection, serialization, plugin-hook preparation, and socket delivery without adding a cache or subscription protocol.

Runtime production delta: **+3 lines** (one map update and its ownership comment); proof scripts: +612 lines. The requested non-test/non-doc diff is +615 lines because it includes those scripts. That bookkeeping preserves the existing publisher for quiet evaluations and historical-row corrections. Usage lives in each script's header; the shared perf README is unchanged.

## Evidence

Base: `11c8f236b330e8f51c03331dcd6ae0c661080e7b`. The owner benchmark exercises real CronService admission and worker persistence with 200 jobs and a cheap runner. Five alternating pairs, 500 measured completions per arm per pair, 200 warmups; timing and collected-object allocation sampling are separate passes.

| Measurement | Base | Candidate | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Owner sampled allocation/completion (2,500/side) | 598,579 B | 587,665 B | −1.82% |
| Owner main-thread CPU/completion (2,500/side) | 3.226 ms | 3.332 ms | +3.27% |
| Events/normal completion | 3 | 2 | −33.3% |
| Mixed Gateway emits/min | 32 | 24 | −25% |
| Mixed Gateway delivered frames/min, six clients | 192 | 144 | −25% |
| Duplicate completion schedules/min | 8 | 0 | removed |
| Successful finishes / quiet schedules | 8 / 4 | 8 / 4 | preserved |

The allocation gain is small. CPU pair deltas range from −5.3% to +10.0%; no CPU improvement is claimed. Every run's client runtime projection matches `cron.list`.

The real built-Gateway proof uses 200 synthetic jobs, six Control UI protocol clients, four active command jobs, and two quiet trigger jobs over 60 seconds. Main-thread CPU was 2.054→1.874%; RSS/heap 1146.3/436.2→1057.8/410.9 MiB; loop p99 36.73→26.08 ms (2,681/2,734 samples). GC rose 360.7→470.7 ms/min while host load rose 110→158. These short-run resource numbers are context, not a claimed Gateway speedup. Four predeclared same-code A/A pairs test that GC uncertainty; their full results, per-kind counts, and maxima are below. Identical code itself trips the GC noise thresholds, so the short-run GC comparison is inconclusive.

The existing trigger-error regression fails on the base with the extra `scheduled` event; with the fix it receives `started, finished` and retains the persisted next-run time. **52 focused tests pass** across trigger evaluation, batch finalization, runtime publication, and mutation operations, including quiet-trigger and same-ID replacement behavior. Root script typecheck, cron test typecheck, changed-file format/lint, and both runtime builds pass. Lint used the supported skip-prepare mode after a separate SDK-declaration preparation timeout; no lint finding was bypassed. Initial probe setup/assertion errors were corrected before the reported runs. An initial owner series mixed loaders and was excluded in full; both arms in the reported series use identical native TypeScript loading.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): autoreview's configuration preflight refused the selected provider. The authorized fresh-context fallback found one benchmark assertion error, corrected before measurement; follow-up reviews, including loader parity, have no accepted findings.

No cron tick heartbeat or per-token progress emitter was found. Sidebar consumers use runtime events outside the cron page, so audience scoping would require a separate protocol design. This bounded proof follows the authorized duplicate-work fast path: it is not the full 10,000-session/40-plugin concurrent-turn stress campaign or a browser-render test. No sessions.list/server-handler latency claim is made. CI on the final pushed head remains the broad validation gate.

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): stable active transcript reload [do not merge]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Investigates cached transcript movement when a signed-in operator reloads an active conversation and live history includes new rows. The campaign's original reload census recorded fourteen presentation states; this experiment addresses the transcript replacement step only. This draft experiment must not be merged.

## Why This Change Was Made

End-follow can choose a target from provisional row heights, then correct backward when the appended rows are measured. The candidate measures mounted rows and commits the native range in the existing transcript presentation owner before evaluating the end anchor. It removes the former host callback. No protocol, server record, schema, config, or cache format changes.

## User Impact

The intended result is an unchanged cached reader position, or one direct update to the final end for a following reader. The shared synthetic fixture includes a bounded long Markdown reply recovered through the native full-message path, an incomplete tool group that completes, and newly appended turns. The benchmark retains the existing Team-scale sidebar settings and native snapshot persistence.

## Evidence

Initial native Chromium diagnostic: the retained long-reply height stayed at 3326.65625 px. Baseline scroll sequence: 5095 → 5335 → 5263 px; candidate: 5095 → 5263 px. The baseline overshoots by 72 px and corrects backward. These are geometry observations on a loaded development host, not performance timing results.

The faithful active-history fixture keeps the retained reader row at the same screen position through live replacement. Native Chromium regression: 3/3 pass (66.42 s including production bundle preparation). The pre-fix end-follow case fails the one-step assertion. A scroll-offset adjustment that preserves the visible row is allowed for readers; end-follow must have exactly the cached and final offsets.

Preregistered acceptance: eleven interleaved baseline/candidate pairs plus A/A on one quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge lease, active reader/end views, archived-chat and dashboard secondaries, live-like latency, no CPU profiling. Report anchored-row movement, CLS, hello-handled, FCP, first/final rows, Long Animation Frame blocking, snapshot bytes, medians/IQRs and all paired deltas. Primary improvement requires at least 9/11 better pairs; the campaign's paired secondary regression rules apply.

Pending: quiet-host measurements, full UI e2e, changed checks, exact-head CI and inspected synthetic before/after strips. The current isolated review is clean through P2; this does not establish a performance pass.

Shipping runtime delta: +21 lines (25 added in the existing presentation owner; 4 added/8 removed in the virtualizer host). The required ordering is measurement and native range commit before end-anchor evaluation. Proof tooling shares one fixture and one per-frame probe between the existing benchmark and native regression. Exact test allocation: +164 lines, justified by reader geometry and one-step end-follow regressions; no slack.

Release-note context: keep an active conversation's cached transcript stable when history catches up after reloading.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Templates detail view mixing agent documents with fixtures, schemas, and other supporting files in the main Workspace files list.

## User Impact

Users see named agent documents first and can open every available file through a “View all” row in the same card. Both named rows and “View all” use the existing shared file previewer. Packaging, installation, and Add behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Match exact root workspace destinations using the existing template bootstrap-name contract, with the other supported agent documents explicitly included. Nested lookalikes stay in the complete preview inventory rather than appearing as named agent documents. Reuse the current preview and read owner; no new viewer, cache, endpoint, or install path. Preserve the navigation-chevron lane on the Templates route and the approved 72px “View all” row. Keep descriptions to one line with ellipsis across Workspace files, Skills, Integrations, and Automations.

## Evidence

- 36 focused UI tests passed, including root-only classification, supporting-only lists, named-file selection, complete-file inventory, and navigation across supporting files. Regression assertions fail on the base and pass with the fix.
- UI typecheck and production build passed on `40251226238ae405368ab157153f0de3698e01db`; touched-source formatting and stylesheet checks passed.
- Real isolated Gateway/UI proof against a published workflow-operator template release: named-file preview, all ten inventory entries, and server-backed reads of all eight supporting files passed. Geometry checked at 400, 820, and 1280px; before/after screenshots are attached in the proof comment. Production Gateway was not modified or restarted.
- Fresh independent reviews of the behavior change and final geometry reported no concrete findings. The attempted local ClawSweeper run failed and is not claimed as clean; hosted review remains pending after publication.
- Aggregate local test-line gate has 93 lines of inherited debt, established on the comparison base. This change’s net 34 added test lines have an exact 34-line allocation; no inherited allowance or assertion was weakened.
- Simplification pass: removed supporting-file inline presentation and its daily-memory role special case; retained existing preview/read ownership. Necessary growth is the document projection, “View all” row, and fixed action-lane styling.

Visual proof uses the actual UI and isolated Gateway with the published release; it is not a production deployment or an installation attestation.

[Inspected before/after screenshots and shared previewer proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193215#issuecomment-6650408747).

### One-line subtext correction

At `51e301e838e4fb3d81dbd36c2c4b7e544d16a924`, the 12-test template browser suite passed against a freshly built production browser bundle. The four responsive regressions fail without the one-line rule and pass after restoration, covering long workspace and skill excerpts. Formatting, stylesheet lint, and diff checks passed. [Inspected before/after one-line subtext screenshots, including Skills](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193215#issuecomment-6650597875). Previous auto-merge request was retired before updating this head; current-head native gates are being reconciled.

prs.title: fix: repeated inline-code paragraphs no longer stall the Gateway
prs.body:
Fixes #186598. Credited replacement for the author's withdrawn #186600.

**Not ready to land: the Control UI bundle budgets require an owner decision.** No budget baseline has been changed. Land #186605 first; this is the second step.

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated paragraphs containing inline code can make a streamed answer repeatedly parse the whole reply and stall the Gateway.

## User Impact

Repeated inline-code paragraphs collapse promptly while preserving meaningful whitespace inside code. `a  b`, `a b`, `a b` retains two distinct paragraphs. Fenced and indented code stays protected, and later reference definitions retain canonical correction behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Paragraph identity preserves canonical inline-code bytes and recomputes its comparison when append validation says code ownership can change, including split backticks and GFM table delimiters. Ordinary continuation bytes keep the incremental comparator. Block-ambiguous and nonlocal Markdown retain canonical protection; code-free links stay inexpensive.

The original branch already carried the shared Markdown resolver prerequisite. This refresh merges current main and the refreshed #186605 branch, preserving both contributor history and the two-step dependency. Thanks @JasonBuildAI for the report and original investigation; the original `Co-authored-by: JasonBuildAI <jasonbuildai@gmail.com>` credit is retained.

## Evidence

Current head: `690a950a34e20b02561a695a539f4bcd536b496e`. Main merge base: `bca996c12f5568a125d2159fc87186213f1a705c`. Prerequisite head: `67618a3d03406cb5e0da894cd3d008c433765777`.

The duplicate projector remains byte-identical to the previously reviewed second-PR owner. The shared scanner files match the freshly reviewed first PR. The pending-header conflict was resolved at that owner, retaining its code-region protection. Both unquoted multiline headers and quoted unfinished markers now have regression coverage.

- Current-main reproduction through `createAssistantVisibleStreamText("final_answer")`, four-character deltas: the 8 KiB repeated-inline-code fixture still parses 6,621,260 characters. The committed work regression fails at 9,621,042 against a 325,888 budget while final bytes remain correct.
- Candidate 8/16/32 KiB runs parse 55,596 / 111,036 / 222,522 characters, matching the previous proof and preserving canonical output and delta reconstruction. These are deterministic work counts; the refresh timings are not a new paired benchmark.
- All 526 focused/consumer tests pass on this merge (52.70 s command wall time), including the transcript and duplicate work regressions, inline whitespace identity, quoted incomplete headers, and current XML siblings. Scoped lint, formatting, core types and all ten baseline ratchets pass; the combined test delta is negative.
- Codex review covers the second owner and the shared correction through P2. A prior local finding about no-duplicate link/code replies was disproven through the real entry point: zero parsed characters at 8/16/32 KiB, with exact output. The full-source review then passed; the final integration preserves those reviewed owners.
- The qualified UI comparison fails with the same result as the refreshed first PR: new-session JS 799,817 B gzip versus base 799,089 B (+728 B, with 192 B allowed variance), and chat boot 1,286,619 B versus its 1,286,062 B ceiling. The complete metrics and emitted hashed-asset names are identical to the first PR, so the second step adds zero UI bytes after that prerequisite. The shared differential failure is not an inherited-main CI result.

Prior isolated built-Gateway evidence is retained: repeated-inline-code fixtures at 8/16/32 KiB delivered exact streaming and final text, and a real shared Ollama `qwen2.5:7b` turn collapsed three outside-code repetitions to one 95-character paragraph. That is historical proof, not a new live run of this final merge. A new full build/live run was stopped when the fresh review found the pending-state issue; qualification stops at the remaining UI-budget decision. No operator Gateway or shared model service was changed.

After #186605, this PR adds 40/removes 8 production lines (net +32) and adds 84/removes 85 test lines (net -1). Before the prerequisite lands, its complete diff against main is production +246/-72 (net +174), tests +127/-129 (net -2). The remaining growth preserves code-aware identity and canonical ownership correction without a second parser or cache owner. No configuration, schema, dependency, or changelog change. Validation is local macOS.

prs.title: fix(llama-cpp): restore managed Windows runtime downloads
prs.body:
Fixes #192366.

## What Problem This Solves

Managed llama.cpp setup fails on Windows because the pinned b10809 CPU archives and CUDA runtime dependency are served with different, much shorter bytes than their published SHA-256 digests describe.

## User Impact

This proposes restoring managed Windows downloads by refreshing the runtime from **b10809 to b11977**. **Draft: the runtime refresh still requires explicit maintainer approval.** Native Windows setup has not been exercised on this Mac.

## Why This Change Was Made

b11977 is the newest complete binary release that had seven days of soak at the selection cutoff (2026-11-05 04:47:32 UTC). The newer `v0.9.0` release contains a nightly-tag marker, not the platform archives; upstream still publishes binaries under `b` tags.

Refresh the build/commit, published hashes and sizes, and authenticated library aliases together. Increase only the CUDA archive's extraction budgets to fit its measured 657,155,869-byte expanded contents and 594,121,728-byte largest DLL. SHA-256 enforcement, CUDA driver requirements, and installed-runtime validation remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Complete GETs and the production installer reproduce the b10809 failures:

| Archive | Published bytes | Served bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Windows CPU x64 | 18,407,457 | 507 |
| Windows CPU arm64 | 11,974,499 | 371 |
| CUDA 12.4 runtime | 391,443,627 | 6,491 |

All eight selected b11977 release archives were fully downloaded and matched the upstream published sizes and SHA-256 digests. Both unchanged Visual C++ redistributables also matched their pinned sizes and hashes. All manifest aliases and CUDA extraction budgets match the inspected archive members. The macOS 13.3 and Linux glibc 2.34/x64 and 2.38/arm64 floors are unchanged. The actual executable reports `build 11977, commit 7ac5727d6`.

The Mac managed installer completed in 6.1 seconds. CLI embedding-only onboarding completed in 28.3 seconds. A real `openclaw agent --local` turn using Qwen 2.5 7B returned exactly `PIN_REFRESH_OK` (20.4 seconds in the agent, 46.4 seconds wall time). Local memory indexing completed in 11.3 seconds, and a real embedding-backed search returned the synthetic note with vector score 0.635 in 7.4 seconds. These ran in isolated state on port 20447; no operator Gateway was used.

prs.title: perf(agents): reuse kill snapshots and attribute lifecycle waits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Subagent cancellation repeatedly copies prepared descendant snapshots, while slow-lifecycle warnings leave the awaited work inside preparation and execution opaque.

## User Impact

Cancellation performs less allocation during descendant discovery. Diagnostics identify awaited discovery, kill-intent, admission-drain, caller-stop, and registry-settlement costs. Kill authority, cascade ordering, process cleanup, and persisted state contracts remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The controller selector only reads its input, so it can consume the existing read-only snapshot directly. The resident snapshot remains necessary because synchronous scheduler callbacks can mutate the registry during capture. Bounded subphase timings augment the existing slow warning; they do not add a queue, cache, schema, or configuration option.

This is a small absolute owner improvement. It does not establish a fix for the reported multi-second cancellation delay; the diagnostic breakdown is intended to distinguish that residual cost.

## Evidence

Owner benchmark: 10,000 synthetic retained runs across 40 controllers; 250 rows in each prepared read scope; 3,000 iterations per arm in each of two AB/BA pairs. Timing and collected-object allocation sampling are separate passes. Outputs preserve selected row identity and order.

| Metric | Base | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU, 3,000 discoveries (paired mean) | 62.737 ms | 15.580 ms | -75.2% |
| Sampled allocation per discovery (paired mean) | 49,738.8 bytes | 9,490.7 bytes | -80.9% |

Host load was 124.6 for timing and 135.7–136.6 for allocation; wall time is not a reliable throughput claim. This measures the removed adapter around the real selector, not full cancellation or Gateway performance.

Commands: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/subagent-kill-discovery-measure.ts --mode timing --iterations 3000` and the same with `--mode allocation`.

The regression on production base `11c8f236b330` failed after the existing discovery/outcome assertions: five redundant snapshot iterations, expected zero. The fix is exercised through the real `withSubagentKillScope` refresh path, including late descendants and rejected refreshes.

Isolated built-dist Gateways ran a root, child, and grandchild through native `sessions_spawn`, each holding an actual awaited tool process. In both arms all three processes exited before teardown, all `agent.wait` results were terminal cancellations, and the registry was killed-terminal or retired with no pending kill intent before shutdown.

| Targeted Gateway smoke | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `sessions.abort` RPC | 3,588.9 ms | 1,272.5 ms |
| Child processes verified stopped before teardown | 3/3 | 3/3 |

These single runs establish behavior, not a speedup or reproduction of the reported production median. The base logged one slow mutation (prepare 1,945 ms; run 507 ms); the candidate had no mutation above the slow-log threshold. The Gateway runs preceded a mechanical extraction of the timing recorder and kill parameter type into their existing owners; focused tests cover that final extraction. No Team load was started. The pure-deletion fast-path protocol applies; no broad 10-minute stress result is claimed.

Source attribution: sibling cancellation already uses `Promise.allSettled`; descendant levels wait for parent cleanup. Preparation includes caller facts, descendant refresh, durable intent, caller Stop hooks and admission draining. Execution includes refresh, runtime load, abort and registry/session settlement. Raw source and child-process cleanup joins occur outside the logged mutation. Required registry writes were retained because completion can update metadata while cleanup yields. The added bounded fields expose these awaited costs without changing kill authority or cleanup ordering.

Production runtime delta: +76 lines, solely for explicitly requested bounded subphase diagnostics; the performance change replaces two expressions and removes one redundant allocation without a new path or cache. The requested non-test/non-doc count is +196 lines including the 118-line reproducible benchmark and two-line regression allocation record. Existing test extensions add 32 net lines, allocated for the work-count and diagnostic boundary regressions.

Autoreview's configured-route preflight is unavailable because the requested provider does not match the operator config. Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable) found no actionable P0–P2 findings, including a follow-up review of the final extraction. No provider configuration was changed.

Validation: built baseline/candidate runtime and real nested-process Gateway smoke passed; scoped source/script lint, strict `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, matching agents-sessions and other core-test typechecks, and export-name collision guard passed. Focused validation passed 50 tests across `subagent-control.refresh`, `subagent-control.accounting`, `subagent-control.accepted-stop`, and `session-controller.lifecycle-diagnostics`; import-closure guards passed 40 tests. Docs MDX and formatting checks passed. A final type-export cleanup during one test invocation triggered the source-integrity guard before two files ran; those two files were rerun unchanged and passed (31 tests). Exact-head PR CI will supply broad proof.

Rebased without conflicts onto current main `1e101d06645b30edfc0c686813de5c795acea2d4`; every task file is byte-identical to the locally validated/reviewed version. Head: `eb95168948db6d5f23a60ada1d483ba4c02f854a`.

prs.title: fix: memory status says embeddings are pending when the index is complete
prs.body:
Closes #192756

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `memory.status` reports degraded / “Memory embeddings are pending” after a successful embedding probe and semantic search, even when the stored vector index is clean and complete.

## User Impact

Complete and empty indexes no longer appear degraded merely because the manager answering the request has not initialized embeddings. Dirty sources, failed syncs, unknown/incomplete/unverified vectors, actual provider degradation, and keyword fallback retain their warnings. Coverage health does not claim live connectivity; use `doctor.memory.status` with `probe: true` for that check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared coverage adapter now distinguishes stored vector completeness from manager initialization. This applies to both transient status managers and long-lived managers: the same persisted coverage facts have the same meaning. It avoids initializing a provider just to answer status and adds no configuration or persistence changes.

Preserves @Yun-0000’s original fix and commit, restores the independent unknown-state regression, and strengthens the existing table with pending complete/empty indexes and complete-index degradation/dirty controls.

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateway on macOS, native Ollama adapter, shared `nomic-embed-text`, one newly indexed synthetic note. A task-owned loopback relay forwards to the real model and allows an outage control without changing the shared server. Separate CLI calls exercise `doctor.memory.status` → v2 `memory.search` → `memory.status`.

On current main `2270152d224ae48de9a10f3fe26b4c594ac9e87d`: indexing succeeded (64.675s), probe returned `embedding.ok: true` (27.127s), search returned the exact note with `coverage: complete` (13.854s), then status returned `degraded` with the pending warning despite `dirty: false` and a complete 768-dimensional index (17.760s). Timings include CLI startup. A separate premature startup attempt received connection refused and was excluded from product evidence.

On fixed head `87e16bed4d6a1ee31a96d55ae2b52af88b18f841`, from a fresh isolated state directory:

| Step | Result | Wall time |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Index synthetic note | 1 file indexed through real Ollama embeddings | 10.709s |
| Explicit probe | `embedding.ok: true` | 7.786s |
| v2 search | Exact synthetic excerpt, score 0.6725831398, `coverage: complete` | 7.252s |
| Separate status | `status: ready`, `dirty: false`, complete 768-dimensional index, manager still `pending` | 2.646s |
| Inject HTTP 503 on embedding calls | v2 search returns `UNAVAILABLE`, explicit error, CLI exit 1 | 5.539s |
| Explicit probe during outage | `embedding.ok: false` with the injected provider error | 5.476s |

The synthetic excerpt was: “The lighthouse kestrel project keeps its violet emergency compass in the cedar cabinet.” The live fault control proves failures remain visible; the independent adapter regression specifically proves a known degraded provider still warns even with complete stored vectors.

Regression: the final test table against the original pending condition fails exactly the complete and empty pending-index cases (2 failed, 9 controls passed, 30 skipped; 173.02s wall). The fixed focused suites passed all 88 tests across the adapter, Gateway memory-provider, and Doctor files. Most wall time is worker compilation; individual adapter cases take milliseconds.

Validation: `pnpm build` passed (935.73s wall; included unrelated advisory UI size-budget output). The focused four-file command passed 88 tests in 294.24s wall (Gateway shard 183.98s; adapter shard 50.86s). `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base c7b7c79ef4e681c5b60873d28d2b61616a5e2501` passed (276.96s); the separate line-cap check passed (6.72s). Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Scoped oxlint and the plugin test typecheck passed; their wall times included waiting for the build-owned artifact lock (1070.69s and 1071.57s). Production core typecheck also passed (7.19s).

Codex autoreview of `c7b7c79ef4e681c5b60873d28d2b61616a5e2501...87e16bed4d6a1ee31a96d55ae2b52af88b18f841`: **scoped-clean**, no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings.

The earlier CI run [41846736834](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41846736834) failed on unrelated UI inputs: duplicate `closeSessionTitle` (TS1117 / no-dupe-keys) and a missing mock-export preservation in `sessions-page-cloud-stop.test.ts`. The memory change touches none of those inputs. Current-head CI is checked separately; no branch refresh was made for those unrelated failures.

Diff versus merge base: production +9/-2 (net +7), tests +13/-13 (net 0), docs +5/-0. The explicit completeness condition stays readable; no unrelated code was removed to offset it. No test ceiling or baseline was raised.

Platform limit: live proof is macOS with Ollama; the reporter’s Linux managed llama.cpp deployment was not reproduced. No schema/config migration is introduced.

prs.title: feat(sessions): list and read session workspace files from the CLI
prs.body:
Closes #193221

## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway knows every file in a session's workspace — the Control UI file view renders that inventory — but the terminal could not read it. An operator on a headless host had to hand-call `gateway call sessions.files.list` with raw JSON parameters.

## User Impact

`openclaw sessions files <sessionKey> [path]` lists the workspace files (name, kind, size, update time) with `--search` name filtering; `--get` prints one file's content; `--output` writes it to disk. `--json` returns the raw `sessions.files.list` / `sessions.files.get` response.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The command forwards the canonical owners and only shapes output: blank selectors and `--output` without `--get` are rejected before dispatch, transport failures exit non-zero, and the transport keeps its default timeout when `--timeout` is omitted.
- Registered beside the other gateway-backed session verbs; the parent `sessions` list selectors stay rejected.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/sessions-files.test.ts src/cli/program/register.status-health-sessions.test.ts` → 27/27 passed locally.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` → clean; `oxfmt --check` → clean.
- **Real behavior proof**: the branch was built through the shipped `build-all` (after refreshing the pinned `@openclaw/fs-safe` dependency the moved `main` requires) and exercised against a real Gateway booted from this checkout (isolated state dir, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`):

```text
$ openclaw sessions files "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000 --json
{ "sessionKey": "agent:main:main", "files": [] }        (exit 0 — real sessions.files.list round-trip)

$ openclaw sessions files "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000
Session files agent:main:main
No files in this session workspace.                       (exit 0 — empty-inventory rendering)

$ openclaw sessions files x --output f.txt                (exit 1 — --output requires --get)
$ openclaw sessions files "   "                           (exit 1 — blank key rejected)
```

The fresh session workspace has no files, so the populated table rendering is covered by the unit tests; the live evidence covers the RPC path, empty-state rendering, and argument rejection in both modes.

## Risks

- None beyond the new verbs: no RPC, workspace, or config changes.

prs.title: fix(cron): command jobs fail with spawn sh ENOENT on Windows Gateways
prs.body:
Closes #141038

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Windows Gateway cron `--command` jobs always fail with `spawn sh ENOENT` when `sh` is not installed.

## User Impact

`cron add` and `cron edit` use the Gateway host's shell: `cmd.exe /d /s /c` on Windows and `sh -lc` on macOS/Linux. This also handles a CLI running on a different platform from its Gateway. Explicit `--command-argv` stays exact.

Existing Windows jobs retain their stored arguments. Repair an old shell job with `openclaw cron edit <job-id> --command <shell>`. If Gateway platform metadata is unavailable, the CLI explains how to use `--command-argv` instead of guessing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI reads the existing `system.info` surface; Doctor uses the platform of the host whose cron store it repairs. Cron and node-host execution share the existing Windows verbatim-quoting implementation in `infra/node-shell.ts`, and its previous private implementation is removed.

The cron-only agent-runtime scope exception does not pass through this CLI: it requires a signed runtime identity that the CLI transport neither accepts nor forwards. Runtime automation tools call the cron RPC directly. A direct human caller needs `operator.write` to change a host-command job, which already includes `operator.read`. No authorization scopes are widened. `system.info` has existed since at least 2026.7; unsupported or incomplete responses give the explicit-argv next step.

Main was merged to resolve the command-edit conflict, preserving its newer environment-replacement diagnostics. Shell, migration, and process tests share existing fixtures and parameter tables to retain coverage without growing the test-line budget. Thanks @nobrainer-tech for the original fix and Windows proof.

## Evidence

The contributor's [native Windows base/fix and stable-upgrade run](https://github.com/nobrainer-tech/openclaw/actions/runs/41064923463) demonstrates:

- Base jobs store `sh -lc` and fail without `sh`; fixed plain and quoted Windows commands succeed.
- Upgrade from stable 2026.10.9 converts a legacy command prompt using the Windows shell, preserves explicit argv/environment/timeout, and successfully repairs an existing shell job using the documented edit command.
- The native Windows cron quoting regression passes with the fix and fails with the base runner.

Current maintainer validation on macOS:

- Seven focused files: 284 tests pass; four platform-specific cases skipped. The cold run took 450.71 s, mostly worker compilation/imports.
- Red on pinned main `2270152d224`, green with this fix: Windows Doctor conversion and CLI add/edit/missing-platform regressions. Base: one Doctor failure plus four CLI failures at the expected argv/guidance assertions (178.40 s and 90.27 s). Fixed: all six selected cases pass (152.92 s).
- Cron-scoped runtime callers: both `operator.cron` and `operator.write` cases pass through the production authorization/cron-owner composition (410.96 s including the cold worker build).
- Core and focused test typechecks pass. Scoped lint/format pass after completing the frozen development dependencies. All baseline ratchets and the separate line-cap check pass; test-line delta is exactly zero.
- Codex branch autoreview of `4142f39e8d646be4383b5b9e2c5f7f22bf5f2171` against `2270152d224ae48de9a10f3fe26b4c594ac9e87d`: no actionable P0–P2 findings.

Built CLI / Gateway proof on the final head:

- Remote `win32` WebSocket fixture: add and edit store `cmd.exe /d /s /c`; explicit argv remains exact; unknown `system.info` and absent platform both fail before a write with `--command-argv` guidance (17.83 s total CLI time).
- Real isolated macOS Gateway: add, run, edit, run, explicit-argv edit, run, remove all pass (45.08 s CLI time). Saved POSIX argv stays `sh -lc`; the three summaries are `live-add`, `live-edit`, and `live-argv`. The test job and Gateway were cleaned up.
- `pnpm build` passes (599.2 s). It emits non-fatal UI bundle-budget warnings; this PR changes no UI source, build configuration, or dependency lockfile.

This maintainer validation does not claim a new native Windows run. Command jobs execute directly and do not invoke a model.

Whole PR line delta: production +88/-35 (**+53**), tests +193/-193 (**0**), docs +2/-2 (**0**). Production growth is the remote-platform discovery and its explicit failure path; the Windows launch policy is moved and shared, with its old implementation deleted.

prs.title: fix(state): reduce lease heartbeat write contention
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long-lived state leases perform unnecessary synchronous commits, making foreground state writers more likely to wait behind slow storage.

## User Impact

Five-minute leases, including the Gateway SQL owner, renew every 100 seconds instead of every 30 seconds. Short leases retain their existing cadence. A single commit already in progress can still delay another SQLite writer; this reduces how often that happens.

## Why This Change Was Made

Renew at TTL/3 without the fixed cap, preserving the existing retry margin and shared heartbeat batching. The Gateway's old 90-second heartbeat-age scheduling dependency became obsolete when #178076 required process/namespace evidence for recovery. Its separate filesystem heartbeat is unchanged. A source audit of the latest published tag, `v2026.10.10`, found that older cross-namespace admission still checks that filesystem heartbeat and refuses a fresh foreign owner before reaching SQL lease takeover; same-namespace ownership uses process identity. This change does not relax that boundary.

The existing scheduler already prevents overlapping renewal batches. FULL lease durability, conditional owner/expiry checks, closure-bound authority, failed-renewal handling, and writer ordering are unchanged. No new database, schema, config, or cache. Runtime production delta: -3 lines.

## Evidence

Acceptance: fewer renewal commits and lower cumulative foreground-writer wait for the same offered writes, with no material CPU/allocation regression; retain expiry/owner rejection and no overlapping renewal. Compare A/A controls and five interleaved A/B pairs using the production scheduler, real SQLite, and a native WAL-fsync delay. This is an owner-level experiment, not Gateway RPC or btrfs latency evidence.

The persisted long-TTL cadence regression fails on the unchanged parent. Focused tests cover renewal, contention, expiry/replacement, in-flight settlement, and Gateway ownership. The 18-line test allocation extends the existing native SQLite regression fixture and Gateway heartbeat boundary.

The fixture contains 10,002 lease rows and 1,075,920,896 bytes of synthetic state. Five warm A/B pairs each offered 240 foreground writes; time was scaled 50x (300s TTL → 6s, 30s → 600ms, 100s → 2s), with a 400ms native WAL-fsync delay (20s equivalent). All writes and lease renewals completed without terminal failure or expiry.

| Metric (median of five arms) | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Renewal WAL syncs | 19 | 5 |
| Cumulative foreground write time, including native lock waits | 8,275 ms | 2,257 ms |
| Per-arm foreground write p95 | 391.38 ms | 2.15 ms |
| Renewal execution median | 405.97 ms | 406.39 ms |
| Renewal CPU | 31.83 ms | 10.96 ms |
| Main + renewal CPU | 81.41 ms | 59.94 ms |
| Main + renewal sampled JS allocation | 2,201,040 B | 1,186,072 B |

Worst individual foreground write across all five samples remained essentially unchanged: **494.35 → 495.92 ms**, one injected commit plus native busy-polling/scheduling overhead. Cumulative-wait ranges were 7,741–8,491 → 2,110–2,560 ms; total CPU ranges 75.74–89.14 → 58.28–65.59 ms. Two A/A controls produced 19 syncs each, cumulative waits 8,843/8,936 ms, CPU 102.50/96.28 ms and sampled allocation 2.216/2.282 MB. CPU is host-load-sensitive; the sync-count reduction is stable.

Run: `node scripts/perf/state-lease-commit-measure.mjs --out .local/lease-commit-proof --samples 5 --mib 1024 --delay-ms 400 --duration-ms 12000` (Node 26, macOS or Linux with `cc`). The experiment holds the scheduler constant and changes cadence inputs; the regression tests cover production-owner wiring. prs.title: fix(mac): keep JIT entitlements on the Codex code-mode host
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #192851: Codex tool calls in the signed macOS app fail when the bundled code-mode host starts V8.

## User Impact

The bundled Codex host can execute code after OpenClaw re-signs it. Other native helpers keep their existing permissions, and the Codex host retains library validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The macOS signer was replacing the Codex host's upstream JIT entitlements with a plain hardened-runtime signature. Extend its existing Claude SDK JIT branch to the exact arm64 and x64 Codex package paths, including nested dependencies. Update the signing documentation and existing architecture/elevation regression matrix.

The dependency contract was personally checked at [Codex 529d965d](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/529d965d80a36f7b5d9d9ab218d88daf41106748/.github/scripts/macos-signing/codex-code-mode-host.entitlements.plist#L5): both `allow-jit` and `allow-unsigned-executable-memory` are required. Its [package signer](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/529d965d80a36f7b5d9d9ab218d88daf41106748/.github/scripts/macos-signing/sign_macos_cli_package.py#L36) applies those entitlements with hardened runtime.

Thanks @SebTardif for the fix and @h6y3 for the report. Contributor commits are preserved; current main was merged without rebasing. Release-note context stays here because OpenClaw's changelog is release-owned.

## Evidence

On macOS 27.0.1 arm64, tested the **actual host from `@openai/codex@0.164.0-darwin-arm64`**, with the registry tarball's SHA-512 verified against the lockfile. Two private minimal app fixtures used the same real host and OpenClaw Foundation Developer ID. The fixture app's main executable was a stand-in; the Codex host was not. Both runs used the production signing script with hardened runtime enabled and timestamps disabled for local proof.

- **Main signer:** `codesign -d --entitlements :-` shows no entitlements. The real host completes the protocol handshake and opens a session, then the first `session/execute` crashes with SIGTRAP and `Fatal process out of memory: Failed to reserve virtual memory for CodeRange` (0.966 s).
- **Fixed signer:** `codesign -d --entitlements :-` shows exactly the two JIT keys. `codesign -dv --verbose=4` confirms `flags=0x10000(runtime)` and `TeamIdentifier=FWJYW4S8P8`. The same `session/execute` evaluates `text("CODEX_SIGNED_V8_OK " + (6 * 7))`, returns `CODEX_SIGNED_V8_OK 42`, closes its session, and exits 0 (0.667 s).
- **Negative control:** the actual host copied to an unrelated `node_modules/other/bin/codex-code-mode-host` path remains plain hardened-runtime signed with no entitlements.

This is direct signed-host/V8 proof, not a full native app launch or model-driven Gateway turn. No operator app, Gateway, saved authentication, LaunchAgent, notarization, or publication was involved. x64 path selection is regression-tested; x64 execution was not run.

Validation on `41e7468d72f60d57d4ce07987c5c7e2047b70884`:

- The four architecture/elevation regression cases fail on main `2270152d224ae48de9a10f3fe26b4c594ac9e87d` for the missing JIT keys (31.65 s). All 71 signing tests pass with the fix (73.01 s command wall time; 65.23 s Vitest time).
- `node scripts/worktree-setup.mjs gateway` completed; runtime build phases took 10m 17s.
- Scoped tooling typecheck passed (379.46 s including build preparation), scoped lint passed (124.06 s including preparation), format passed (0.15 s), and Bash syntax, ShellCheck, and `git diff --check` passed. The gateway-only dependency setup initially omitted the lint plugin; installing the already-declared `@openclaw/solid-lint` workspace dependencies fixed that setup failure without a lockfile change.
- `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base 2270152d224ae48de9a10f3fe26b4c594ac9e87d` passed all ten checks (491.44 s), including line-cap, assertion-safety, test-lines, config docs, and plugin inventory.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the complete base-to-head diff is **scoped-clean at P0–P2**, with no findings. Reviewed base: `2270152d224ae48de9a10f3fe26b4c594ac9e87d`; head: `41e7468d72f60d57d4ce07987c5c7e2047b70884`.

Exact-head [CI run 41972700549](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41972700549) and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. [ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192867#issuecomment-6635811776) of this exact head found no actionable issues or before-merge items and rated the real-host proof sufficient. The full-app/model-driven and x64 execution limits above remain explicit.

Production: +4/-2 (net +2: the two package-specific cases); tests: +5/-11 (net -6); docs: +2/-2. The removed test inspected obsolete internal variable names; executable temp-allocation and signing-boundary coverage remain.
