prs.title: fix: long streamed replies that quote tool-call transcripts no longer stall the Gateway
prs.body:
Fixes #186601

**Not ready to land: a Control UI bundle-budget decision is required.** The streaming checks pass, but this revision exceeds the differential UI budgets below. No budget baseline has been changed.

## What Problem This Solves

Long streamed answers quoting legacy `[TOOL_CALL]`, downgraded `[Tool Call: ...]`, or historical transcript markers repeatedly parse the whole reply and can stall the Gateway.

## User Impact

Quoted examples stay visible and stream promptly. Unquoted scaffolding is removed, including after a fenced block leaves a list or blockquote. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each canonical removal pass uses the existing container-aware Markdown checkpoint owner because removing one marker can expose a fence for the next pass. Incomplete candidates remain pending; settled text stops participating in subsequent scans. The separate resolver was removed, preserving existing trim and correction semantics.

The refresh also fixes a previously missed checkpoint case: an unquoted legacy header split across blank lines must stay pending before its closing bracket arrives. Quoted incomplete headers use canonical code protection and continue settling incrementally. The same protected-region rule is applied independently in each downgraded removal pass. The existing regression suites cover all marker families without adding test lines.

Thanks @JasonBuildAI for the report, original implementation, and reproduction workloads. All contributor commits and credit are preserved through merges; no rebase or force-push.

## Evidence

Current head: `67618a3d03406cb5e0da894cd3d008c433765777`. Main merge base: `bca996c12f5568a125d2159fc87186213f1a705c`.

- Current-main reproduction through `createAssistantVisibleStreamText("final_answer")`, four-character deltas, still parses 16,785,006 legacy / 33,568,848 downgraded characters at 8 KiB. Both committed work regressions fail on main for their scan budget, with correct output.
- Refreshed 8/16/32 KiB runs parse 348 legacy / 1,239 downgraded characters at every size, with exact canonical output and reconstructed deltas.
- The blank-line header regression fails before the correction and passes after it. The quoted incomplete-header work regression also fails before the refinement and passes after it; a 5,657-character literal probe falls from 1,464,945 to 30,794 parsed characters with identical output.
- All 524 focused and consumer tests pass (48.63 s command wall time). Scoped type-aware lint, formatting, and core types pass. Fresh Codex review is scoped-clean through P2; all ten baseline ratchets pass without raising a baseline.
- Qualified UI comparison against the same base and Vite/Pako toolchain fails: new-session JS is 799,817 B gzip versus base 799,089 B (+728 B; only 192 B variance allowed). Chat boot is 1,286,619 B versus the 1,286,062 B ceiling. These are new differential failures, distinct from the known runner/device-copy failure in the earlier refresh CI.

Prior isolated built-Gateway evidence is retained: nine synthetic WebSocket responses had exact streaming/final text, and a real shared Ollama `qwen2.5:7b` turn completed in 3.24 s with 566 canonical final characters. That is historical proof, not a new live run of this corrective head. Further live qualification stops at the new budget decision; the checkpoint correction is covered at its owning projection boundary.

Production +206/-64 (net +142); tests +71/-72 (net -1). Remaining source growth carries checkpoint/candidate state and canonical pass composition. There is one Markdown ownership implementation. Validation is local macOS. #186667 remains the second step and must follow this PR.

prs.body:
Related: #167266. Parent: #171666; followed by #168399. UI #171710 is a sibling.

## What Problem This Solves

A committed answer needs one continuation after restart without repeating an uncertain admitted execution.

## User Impact

Answers resume under the original caller’s current authority. Interrupted or failed attempts remain visible and are not automatically replayed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Claim custody at native admission and retain original physical-source authority through execution. Adapt question-specific restart recovery to main’s current ordinary-input admission owner; do not restore the retired generic recovery subsystem. Nonthrowing error/timeout finals retain interrupted receipts. A structured startup-unavailable rejection before any native claim stays owed for the existing scheduler; generic failures and post-claim failures remain terminal.

## Evidence

Continuation/recovery cases, core/Gateway types, scoped lint, formatting and independent P0–P2 review pass. The startup repair passes all 37 owning cases, including a failing-before/passing-after regression and generic-unavailable/post-claim controls. All three native queued-input metadata cases pass, including two independently admitted senders under genuine question custody: FIFO principals/message bytes, no generic question resume, and idempotent second startup. The five remaining owning continuation/recovery files pass all 56 cases. Fresh native crash/lost-ACK and original-member allowed/revoked proofs all pass on matching production builds; details are linked below.

Rebased on main `4a43644e7a7b455d6e257f1ab62fe00e74156a5f`. Each slice credits only its exact added native test lines. The pinned main already exceeds the repository test-line ceiling by 86 lines; this refresh does not raise that baseline. Hosted CI must be assessed on the published head. Ready for review; no merge is authorized.

prs.title: fix(fetch): retain response metadata when releasing request ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: official plugins lose a fetched response's URL, redirect status, and response type when `responseWithRelease` retains request ownership, including when cloning that response.

## User Impact

Official plugin consumers can inspect the actual final URL and redirect status while retaining the existing body-release behavior. `fetch-runtime` is a private-local JavaScript host export for official plugins, as documented in the SDK subpath catalog. This is a response-metadata correction with no API, configuration, or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the metadata/recursive-clone handling already used by the abort wrapper. Keep the release wrapper's copied Headers and native clone isolation; preserve the abort wrapper's existing header behavior. Body ownership, cancellation, and exactly-once release remain with the existing owner.

This is the same boundary/lifecycle defect class as the externally contributed, maintainer-merged #181655; it fixes a separate metadata-loss bug.

## Evidence

- Real loopback HTTP server, native `fetch`, and built `openclaw/plugin-sdk/fetch-runtime`, without mocked responses: a 302 to `/final` originally gives the native response a final URL, `redirected=true`, and `type=basic`. Before the fix, the release wrapper, its clone, and its clone-of-clone report `url=""`, `redirected=false`, and `type=default`. After the fix, all three retain the native metadata. Direct responses are also checked; every payload stays `complete`, and each request releases exactly once.
- Red regression: six existing SDK checks pass; both new HTTP metadata cases fail on the base. Final focused tests at `81e393e872429d0c737fc6a83e62046a87d0cd62`: **16 pass on Node; 15 pass and 1 existing Node-specific test skips on the pinned Bun**. Both direct/redirected HTTP cases and mutable-header isolation pass in each runtime.
- Canonical `tsdown-build.mts` SDK/runtime compilation, owner and changed-test typechecks, targeted lint and format check passed. The sparse working-tree test-line check passed, but a subsequent full-index check exposes pre-existing aggregate baseline debt (described below). The broader `cliStartup` build compiled successfully but its subsequent plugin-assets stage stopped at an absent unrelated `@discord/embedded-app-sdk`; no full startup-build pass is claimed. The built SDK HTTP reproduction passed again after this build. All repository execution used an isolated, secretless container with independent dependencies and the pinned Node/pnpm toolchain. Typechecking used the lock-integrity-verified musl build of the same pinned tsrs version through its supported binary override to accommodate the container libc.
- Simplification: one existing metadata/clone decorator now serves both wrappers; no new exported abstraction or finalizer. Production delta +32/-20; tests +66 lines. Those lines cover real direct/redirected HTTP and the distinct mutable-header compatibility boundary (explicit test allocation: 66).
- Independent full-diff review found and resolved an initial header-sharing regression, then passed the final three-file change at `bbb49031459ee4fae4086baf39b873d79de59d4a`. After the CI portability repair, the complete three-file diff was independently reviewed again at `81e393e872429d0c737fc6a83e62046a87d0cd62`. Local `autoreview` could not start because the configured provider contains unsupported `stream_max_retries`; no autoreview pass is claimed.

- **CI runtime repair:** pinned Bun returns native `Response.type="default"`, while Node returns `"basic"`. The test now compares with `original.type`, preserving the metadata invariant rather than hardcoding Node semantics. The production fix is unchanged. Native HTTP assertions through the owner supplement the earlier unchanged built-SDK proof on both runtimes; this test-only repair does not claim a new whole-SDK build.
- **Baseline-ratchet attribution:** prior exact-head CI reports total 6,479,261 / ceiling 6,479,169, over by 92, with net +66 test lines and exactly +66 allocation. The common pinned base `ffbbb514` independently reports 6,478,490 / 6,478,404, over by 86 at net delta zero, using the canonical full-index check. These are upstream aggregate gaps, retained rather than covered with unrelated allocation. CI may remain blocked by this baseline condition.

Scope: this proves the built SDK runtime boundary and lifecycle on Linux/Node, with current native-owner and committed-regression validation on the repository-pinned Bun; it does not claim full release, other-platform, or live-provider validation. Broader coverage is left to PR CI.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the observable boundary</summary>

After installing and building the checkout, run:

```sh
pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/fetch-runtime.test.ts src/infra/net/guarded-body-stream.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The committed regression uses a real HTTP redirect and direct response. The independent built-SDK check imports `openclaw/plugin-sdk/fetch-runtime`, fetches a loopback `/redirect` → `/final`, calls `responseWithRelease`, then clones twice and drains all bodies. Its observed output was:

```text
Before: native   /final  redirected=true   type=basic
        wrapped  ""      redirected=false  type=default
        clone    ""      redirected=false  type=default
        grandclone ""    redirected=false  type=default
After:  native, wrapped, clone, grandclone all /final redirected=true type=basic
Both:   bodies=[complete,complete,complete]; release=1
PASS: shipped SDK preserves fetched metadata, cloned payloads, and exactly-once release
```

</details>

prs.title: perf(gateway): skip unchanged participant notifications
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated contributions by an existing session participant send `sessions.changed` notices even when the public participant row has not changed.

## User Impact

Clients receive fewer redundant participant updates. Participant identities, ordering, contribution history, and all actual participant changes remain available as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The participant writer already reports whether its public projection changed. Native writes and host commit publication now use that fact, and the resident count-only worker no longer schedules a redundant lifecycle callback. Committed actor and cache receipts still carry the exact contribution counters and timestamps. No new cache, schema, configuration, or authority change.

Runtime source is net **8 lines smaller**. The separate benchmark supplies reproducible owner measurements; the existing three-socket test gains 15 lines to protect legacy/delta client equivalence without another Gateway fixture.

## Evidence

The two owner regressions fail on the baseline with **2 notifications instead of 1**; the other 43 tests pass. They preserve exact aggregate/version facts and final committed participant state, including rollback behavior. The real three-socket regression additionally checks that the repeated contribution adds no frame, the public row stays equal, and legacy and delta clients decode equivalent state.

Measurement workload: `scripts/perf/session-participant-emission-measure.ts`, 10,000 synthetic sessions, ten hot rows, 100 warmup contributions, 3,000 measured writes per process. Timing and sampled-allocation passes are separate and counterbalanced. Baseline uses `--owner-file` with the original native writer. Setup and final assertions are outside the measurement window; every arm verifies exact aggregate counts/timestamps and the same public-row digest. Acceptance was fewer redundant notices, unchanged public state, and no material CPU/allocation regression.

| Owner metric | Baseline | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Count-only notices / 3,000 writes | 3,000 | 0 | −100% |
| Thread CPU / 3,000 writes, mean of 3 pairs | 317.58 ms | 289.10 ms | −8.97% |
| Sampled allocation / write, mean of 2 pairs | 55,638.5 B | 54,294.9 B | −2.41% |
| Public-row digest and exact aggregates | Verified | Identical / verified | Preserved |

Timing pairs (baseline → candidate CPU ms): 376.068 → 302.579; 274.736 → 308.375; 301.941 → 256.333. The first two had opposite signs, so one additional pair was predeclared and all samples retained. One-minute host loads per timing arm were 115.4 → 112.6, 109.7 → 108.3, and 119.4 → 111.8. Allocation pairs were 167.135 → 162.535 MB and 166.696 → 163.234 MB per 3,000 writes; arm loads 139.1 → 151.6 and 132.7 → 148.2. Timing work: 9,000 writes per side; allocation work: 6,000 per side.

This is a small owner-level improvement. CPU estimates are sensitive to the loaded host; no whole-Gateway CPU, latency, emissions/minute, or fan-out reduction is inferred. The lane's bounded-deletion proof exception applies; a 10-minute Gateway stress campaign was not run.

Validation: targeted formatting/lint passed; `pnpm tsgo:test:root` and the agents-sessions and gateway-server test typecheck leaves passed; export-name collision guard passed. All 52 tests across the native participant, worker sharing-store, and memory collaboration files passed. The closure files finished with 39 passing tests and one timeout in the unchanged `retains Darwin inputs inside excluded namespaces` traversal (149.7 s against its existing 120 s limit); no timeout was changed.

The local test-line guard found existing base debt: before this change, 6,478,970 test lines versus a 6,478,876 effective ceiling (94 over). This PR adds 15 regression lines and a matching 15-line allowance: 6,478,985 versus 6,478,891, still 94 over. The shared baseline is unchanged. CI on `0094568c52a88c8b5152900246f43f6c968dc7cb` later reported 6,479,273 lines against a 6,479,249 ceiling, still +15 lines matched by +15 allowance; its newer merge context has 24 inherited excess lines ([ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41972345113/job/127063945331)). Both local socket attempts (default runtime and the supported Node runtime) timed out during the original initial `sessions.create`, before the new assertions. No timeout was relaxed. The three-real-socket client-equivalence regression subsequently passed in CI in 7.9 s on `0094568c52a88c8b5152900246f43f6c968dc7cb` ([passing job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41972345113/job/127063946084)); the local setup timeouts are retained as failures, not claimed as fixes.

CI also caught a stale capacity-conformance expectation for count-only updates. It now expects no notice while retaining exact counter/timestamp and capacity-rejection assertions. Both SQLite cases passed locally; the two PostgreSQL variants were skipped without a local service. The infra test-typecheck, focused formatting, and lint passed.

Review: **independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable)**, fresh isolated context, P2+, no actionable findings across native/worker/incognito publication, projection, socket regression, and benchmark; the capacity-test follow-up also received a clean independent review. Autoreview preflight refused the requested provider because it did not match operator configuration; no configuration was changed.

prs.title: fix(cron): announce jobs without an account deliver to a nonexistent "default" Discord account
prs.body:
Related: #186043

## What Problem This Solves

Accountless scheduled announcements can be recorded under the nonexistent `default` account when a channel is configured only with a named account such as `main`. Subsequent replies can then fail because the stored conversation belongs to the wrong account.

## User Impact

Scheduled delivery uses the channel's configured default account after explicit, remembered, and bound account choices are exhausted. Existing invalid conversation records and the separate event-loop stall reported in #186043 remain outside this fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the account before route construction and delivery persistence. The channel helper owns default-account selection; cron owns the order in which its account sources are considered. The two adjacent fallback blocks are combined without changing that precedence, and an unnamed `default` remains implicit.

Original fix and regression by @yousan.

## Evidence

- Secretless Linux verification: `pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-target.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 24/24 tests (61.88s including compilation). Replacing only the target resolver with main's version produced exactly the intended failure (1 failed, 23 passed; 47.95s): the account remained undefined instead of `main`.
- Targeted oxlint passed on all three TypeScript files (4.50s). The exercised resolver, runtime helper, and regression file hashes are retained with the isolated run.
- Formatting and an independent P0–P2 review passed with no actionable findings. Production: +14 net lines (reduced from +25 by combining the fallback branches); tests: +20 net lines, funded by an exact dedicated allocation. The remaining production growth connects the existing channel-default owner before route construction; further deletion would expand the scope. The shared test-line baseline is unchanged.

No fresh Discord round-trip was attempted because the required channel credentials are unavailable. The contributor's earlier CLI/Gateway comparison on `69f1cf3` reported a real delivered message stored under `default` on base and `main` on the fix, including a release upgrade. That evidence reproduced the wrong identity, not the missing-token error; this PR therefore leaves #186043 open.

prs.title: fix: reject channel names without message destinations
prs.body:
Related: #91372

## What Problem This Solves

When the outbound channel is inferred, its bare ID, alias, or target prefix can be mistaken for a recipient. Namespace-only inputs must not silently select a native destination.

## User Impact

Ambiguous channel-only targets fail with destination guidance. Explicit native destinations, provider-qualified targets, and unique exact-directory matches remain supported. Existing allowlists and direct-message policy remain authoritative; ordinary destinations retain the current main flow.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve only channel-namespace collisions before the existing outbound-policy call, and preserve restrictive channel-selection provenance through Gateway delegation. Cron keeps the canonical resolved recipient and conversation identity; proactive delivery still applies direct-message blocking after a namespace recipient is rewritten.

This cleanup removes the general post-resolution policy pass, recipient-kind classifier, result-wrapper module, and proactive tuple pipeline. Against the selected main baseline, the complete feature is 24 files: runtime **+296/-58**, tests/support **+593/-8**, generated validator **+4/-1**, and one test-allocation line: **+894/-67 overall**, previously **+1897/-159**. Runtime additions were **643** before cleanup; the retained growth covers the collision guard, provenance, and affected delivery boundaries.

## Evidence

- The actual message-action boundary regression fails on the unpatched main baseline by sending to the channel name, then passes with the fix. Added cron-identity, preferred-kind, and provider-qualified policy-rewrite regressions also failed before their repairs.
- Final focused routing replay: **120 tests passed in six files**. The preceding structural candidate also passed **57 Gateway/runner checks**; unchanged protocol validation passed **16 tests**. These are focused checks, not a full-suite or live-transport claim.
- Independent local ClawSweeper review covered the full reduced candidate and final corrective delta. Both actionable routing findings were reproduced and fixed; the final delta has no remaining code findings. The final publication tree is compared with the reviewed tree.
- The full changed-file gate passes: production typing, all 29 core test-type shards, lint/format, dead-export scans, and static guards. Gateway generated validators and normal protocol/native-model commit hooks also pass.
- Test-budget hold is retained: the untouched baseline has **6,478,899 test lines / 6,478,805 ceiling**, already **94 over**. This feature adds exactly **558 counted LF lines** and grants exactly **558**; it does not raise a baseline scalar or absorb inherited debt. The positive-growth gate therefore remains held by those 94 lines.
- Published signed head [`5c608d91d9c4`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5c608d91d9c48848278adc3e93d54246badb92aa) has the reviewed tree `62467f1002d9fdc5212be479a161ecb2aa9c2083`. The hosted PR head and source ref match; GitHub verifies the signature and reports no conflicts. [Current-head GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41974915747) is running and is not yet qualified. ## What Problem This Solves

A native ask_user turn currently retains a live answer waiter that cannot survive restart.

## User Impact

Supported native questions commit custody and hand off the turn. Answers resume the original conversation under current authority; uncertain execution is visible and never automatically repeated. Detached, incognito, secret, MCP and unsupported presentations remain transient.

## Why This Change Was Made

Activate the separately reviewed storage, RPC and continuation prerequisites. Require canonical admission custody; older conversations establish it with a new/reset session. Use main’s existing trusted terminal receipt so accepted durable handoff stops later tools; recording a yield alone no longer terminates the native turn. prs.title: test: derive package-root launcher fixtures from their import closure
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: CI integration shards break with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` when a package-root launcher module (`cli-invocation.mjs`, `node-runtime-env.mjs`, ...) gains a new sibling import. About ten test fixtures copied these modules from independent, hand-maintained lists. On 2026-10-24 that broke CI twice: #182306 (fixed by #182464) and #182856 (fixed by #182990).

## User Impact

User impact: no user-visible change. Contributors who add a sibling import between package-root `.mjs` modules no longer break unrelated integration shards. A fast unit test names the missing file instead.

## Why This Change Was Made

`scripts/lib/package-root-modules.mts` exports `collectPackageRootModules(entries)`. It closes entry modules over their `./<name>.mjs` sibling imports: static, re-export, side-effect, and dynamic. Every fixture now names only its entry modules:

- the Vitest worker runtime assets and their 6 consumers
- the launcher fixture and run-node-lifecycle
- the node-compile-cache, sqlite-capabilities, docker-entrypoint, docker-packaging harness, bun-standalone-support, and node-bootstrap-artifact fixtures

The computed sets equal the previous hand lists (16 launcher files, 5 worker assets). There are no production code changes. `vitestWorkerRuntimeAssets` moved from `vitest-worker-declarations.mts` into the new module, so the declarations file stays pure metadata and the trusted PR-wrapper inventory is unchanged.

`test/scripts/package-root-modules.test.ts` replaces the single-list check from #182464 and checks three things:

- For every package-root `.mjs`, the scanner matches an acorn parse.
- `package.json` `files` contains every sibling import of each packaged module, failing as `a.mjs -> b.mjs`.
- On a temporary fixture, the closure follows each import form, and a missing sibling names its importer.

## Evidence

- Mutation: adding `import("./docker-entrypoint.mjs")` to `cli-invocation.mjs` fails the packaging test with `cli-invocation.mjs -> docker-entrypoint.mjs`.
- Converted consumers pass locally:
  - tooling launcher, run-node-lifecycle, and bun-standalone tests
  - 7 gateway node-bootstrap-artifact tests
  - infra compile-cache and sqlite tests
  - 4 cli-process candidate-authority tests through the prepared worker runtime
  - launcher-version e2e
  - the docker packaging harness test
- After the first CI round, eager-import-closure, test-projects, pr-wrapper-source-closure, and package-root-modules (253 tests) pass locally.
- Docker packaging harness: `scripts/lib/check-limits.mts` now imports `release-context.mjs` (#192806), so the harness also stages `release-context.mjs` and `release-version.mjs`. The trusted-harness test passes locally.

### Test-line budget

The test-line ceiling is raised manually by exactly 74 lines (6479235 to 6479309, slack 0):

- +25 net lines in this PR: the new closure, parity, and packaging test, net of the deleted single-list test and the shrunken fixtures.
- 49 lines of inherited debt already on main at the base.

An allocation file can't cover this, because a combined allocation and scalar change exceeds the per-PR credit cap.

prs.title: fix: leftover SQLite snapshot copies from Doctor and triage are never reclaimed
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193174

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: SQLite snapshot copies that Doctor or `openclaw triage` fail to remove are never reclaimed. On top of that, every run leaves a new empty `~/Library/Caches/openclaw/sqlite-<hash>/` directory.

On one Mac host, 49 GB of leftover copies from two triage runs sat in `sqlite-0e5d8581…` and `sqlite-ac549b06…`. The installation's own namespace (`sqlite-9565507d…`, the one its Gateway sweeps) was empty.

## User Impact

Snapshot copies taken during Doctor and triage now live in the installation's own namespace. If one is left behind by a crash, a kill or a failed cleanup, the Gateway's existing snapshot reclamation removes it after its usual grace period. Runs no longer add an empty namespace directory each time.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor lint inspects a private copy of the state directory. That copy is a snapshot staged inside the installation's namespace, and Doctor points `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` at it. The snapshot namespace is a hash of the resolved state directory, so every snapshot taken in that context went into a namespace hashed from the throwaway path. That's a new one per run, and the Gateway's sweep (`reclaimAbandonedSqliteSnapshots`) only looks in the installation's namespace.

`resolveSnapshotStagingRoot` now reuses the enclosing namespace when the resolved state directory is strictly inside an existing `sqlite-<24 hex>` namespace under the admitted cache root. Any other state directory, including a different installation sharing the cache, keeps its own hashed namespace. Reclamation still takes each snapshot's lifetime token before deleting it, so copies that are in use stay fenced.

This is independent of PR #193174, which fixes the cleanup failure when an inspection task is cancelled. This PR makes sure anything that still escapes cleanup can be reclaimed.

## Evidence

Head `a8f78d51296a`, which contains `origin/main` `94bea34ae991`.

Reproduction in a disposable HOME and state dir, logging every `sqlite-<hash>` namespace created and the `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` at that moment:
- Base: each triage or Doctor run created a fresh namespace (`ca81928c…`, `5c9aaece…`, `afc816a0…`, `b976225e…` across runs). Its `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` was `…/sqlite-<install>/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-*/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-*/openclaw-state`.
- This branch: two `triage --run` runs left only the installation's namespace.

Regression test: an extended case in `src/infra/sqlite-private-directory.test.ts`, "isolates installations sharing a cache and keeps each namespace stable". A private state copy inside the first installation's namespace resolves to that namespace, and the cache root holds only the two installations' namespaces. The existing assertions that two installations get separate, stable namespaces remain as the negative control.
- base: fails (`Received: …/sqlite-57ec9c87a7d6e09de39115ad`)
- this branch: passes

Commands:
- `pnpm test` on the 31 files touching the staging root, reclamation, retirement, read-only location cleanup, update-candidate state and Doctor lint state: 220 passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: lint, format and import-cycle guards pass. Madge: 0 cycles. The local tsgo typecheck can't run on this machine because the checkout uses the shared pnpm store, which its graph boundary refuses. CI's typecheck is the gate for that.
- Test-lines ratchet: net growth +9, recorded exactly in `config/test-lines-allocations/sqlite-snapshot-private-state-namespace.txt`. The check still reports main's own overage.
- Autoreview (Codex, branch mode against `origin/main`, P0–P2): scoped-clean.

Test file audit (`src/infra/sqlite-private-directory.test.ts`, read in full): the new assertions reuse the existing temp-dir tracker and environment. No other case changed, and nothing was pruned.

prs.title: fix(oc-path): reject the redaction sentinel used as an object key
prs.body:
## 问题原因

`oc-path` 的红字哨兵守卫只覆盖「值」，不覆盖「对象的键」：

- `jsonc/edit.ts` 的 `jsoncValueToJson()` 递归时先 `guardSentinel(entry.value)`，再以 `entry.key` 直接拼 `Object.fromEntries`。
- `jsonl/edit.ts` 的 `renderJsoncValue()` 同样只对 `e.value` 递归守卫，`JSON.stringify(e.key)` 直接落到输出。

YAML 分支不同：值最终走 `formatFrontmatterValue` / yaml 序列化，键被当作标量一并检查，所以同一个对象插进 YAML 序列会抛 `OC_EMIT_SENTINEL`。结果是文档承诺的「所有 kind 一致」在 JSONC / JSONL 上不成立，`oc://data.jsonc/items/+`、`oc://data.jsonl/+` 会把 `__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__` 当作键写进文件并返回 exit 0。

## 修改机制

- `jsonc/edit.ts`：在 `Object.fromEntries` 的 map 回调里先 `guardSentinel(entry.key, \`${guardPath}/${entry.key}\`)`，键与值共用同一指针前缀。
- `jsonl/edit.ts`：键在 `entries.map` 中单独检查，命中时抛 `OcEmitSentinelError(\`${guardPath}/${walked.join("/")}/${e.key}\`)`，与现有嵌套值报错路径风格一致（`oc://file/L2/<key>`）。

两处都是 fail-closed：抛出发生在 `applyEdits` / 行拼接之前，文件内容不变。守卫仍是子串匹配，`prefix__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__suffix` 这类键同样会被拒绝。

## 验证与证据

隔离 harness（`jsonc-parser` + 本目录源码闭包，vitest）里跑 `extensions/oc-path/src/oc-path/tests/` 全量：

| 阶段 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| 修复前，新用例 | 红：`setJsoncOcPath` 与 `appendJsonlOcPath` 均未抛错，返回值正常（`expected [Function] to throw an error`） |
| 修复后，新用例 | 绿：jsonc 抛 `sentinel literal at oc://config/x/__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__`，jsonl 抛 `OcEmitSentinelError`，两次都断言 `ast.raw` 未变 |
| 修复后，全量 | 33 个测试文件 / 404 条用例全绿（含 `sentinel-cross-kind.test.ts` 原有 3 条） |
| 反证 | 回退两个源文件、保留新测试：仅新用例 1 条失败，其余 3 条仍绿 — 说明用例测的就是这个缺口 |

`oxfmt --check`（仓库 `.oxfmtrc.jsonc`，printWidth 100）对 3 个改动文件均通过。

## 证据边界（未验证项）

- 没有跑完整 `openclaw` CLI 端到端（本机 `git fetch` 不通，只有 Oct 30 的镜像），因此「`openclaw path set ... --json` 返回 exit 1」这一层是靠单元级 `OcEmitSentinelError` + 未改动文件断言推导，未直接在进程里复现 issue 的第 3 步。
- 只覆盖 `jsonc` / `jsonl` 两条写入渲染路径；`md` / `yaml` 未改（它们本来就拒绝）。
- 测试行净增 18 行，已在 `config/test-lines-allocations/oc-path-sentinel-object-keys.txt` 申请等额额度。

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): guide recovery from ambiguous connection locks
prs.body:
Related: #192981. Related investigation: #192989.

## What Problem This Solves

A crash during WhatsApp lock creation can leave an empty sidecar. Startup then reports that another process owns the connection, even when the creator is gone, and gives no recovery steps.

## User Impact

The busy error now points to Doctor. Doctor identifies configured accounts' locks without a valid owner PID, names the exact sidecar, and explains how to recover offline while preserving the credentials. It also reports unreadable lock files.

Doctor deliberately retains ambiguous files, including under `--fix`. Stop every process sharing the auth directory, including suspended processes and owners on other hosts, before moving the reported sidecar aside and restarting one Gateway. The WhatsApp troubleshooting guide documents that procedure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Exclusive acquisition remains unchanged. An aged empty lock can still belong to a suspended live creator, so age is not evidence that it is safe to reclaim. The pinned fs-safe dependency owns the create-then-write publication window; closing that window requires a separate provider change. This PR provides guided recovery, not automatic crash prevention, and does not change the dependency.

The existing account-path resolver now accepts Doctor's environment so an isolated profile is inspected correctly. Thanks @chrislro for the report and @xiaopan-xydt for the related investigation.

## Evidence

- On the base, a child paused after exclusive creation and before payload publication leaves a zero-byte sidecar. Real WhatsApp connection-owner acquisition retains the same inode while the child is suspended (606 ms), and after it is killed (508 ms). Doctor provides no guidance.
- With this change, both safety controls still retain the same inode (505/487 ms); the busy error and Doctor provide recovery guidance. After removing only the orphan with the creator confirmed dead, acquisition succeeds and a competing owner is rejected.
- The new regression fails on the base for missing guidance (6 failed / 3 passed, 9.50 s). Focused stale-owner and file-lock suites pass (24 tests); the final WhatsApp ownership, account, and Doctor suites pass (48 tests, 260.89 s including a cold worker compilation; summed test-case timings were 1.04 s).
- Real CLI: `openclaw doctor --lint --only core/doctor/channel-preview-warnings` reports the exact ambiguous lock and retains its bytes. After the documented offline move to a backup, the same command reports one check run, no findings, and exits successfully.
- `pnpm build` passes (17m 19.4s). Scoped WhatsApp typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, all baseline ratchets, and line-cap checks pass. The cold WhatsApp import-memory check is qualified at 113.9 MiB, +62.6 MiB above the baseline.

- Production: +42 net lines; tests: -8 net lines; docs: +15 lines. Duplicate fixture setup was consolidated without removing the ownership, handoff, cancellation, or account-inheritance contracts.

Limitations: local proof is on macOS and exercises real filesystem/connection ownership. Real WhatsApp network reconnection was not exercised. Full prevention remains an fs-safe follow-up; this PR must not be presented as automatic orphan reclamation. The selected Doctor check is proven; unfiltered Doctor lint exited without JSON on the fresh fixture, so no claim is made about the full diagnostic run.

prs.title: fix(gateway): reserve the A2A namespace from the Control UI SPA
prs.body:
Fixes #193086

## What Problem This Solves

`GET /a2a/v1/agent-card` answered **200 `text/html`** with the Control UI document (~47 kB of `<!doctype html>…`). A client probing the A2A prefix for an agent card parsed a successful HTML page instead of learning that the route does not exist.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `a2a` plugin registered `/a2a/v1` with `match: "exact"` (`extensions/a2a/src/channel.ts`), so a descendant never reached the plugin handler and the Control UI SPA fallback claimed it. The handler already answers unclaimed descendants with `{"error":"Not found"}` — it just never saw them.

The JSON-RPC path now registers in the existing `prefix` mode; the two discovery documents stay `exact`. Namespace and lifecycle ownership stay with the plugin: there is no core classifier change.

## Evidence

**Before** (Gateway on pre-fix source, `channels.a2a` enabled):

```text
$ curl -s -o body -w '%{http_code} %{content_type} %{size_download}B' http://127.0.0.1:18795/a2a/v1/agent-card
200 text/html; charset=utf-8 47200B
$ head -c 60 body
<!doctype html>
<html data-openclaw-control-ui-base-path=""
```

**After** (built Gateway from this head, `channels.a2a` enabled, Control UI served by the same Gateway):

```text
$ curl -s -w '%{http_code} %{content_type}' http://127.0.0.1:18797/a2a/v1/agent-card
404 application/json; charset=utf-8
{"error":"Not found"}

$ curl -s -w '%{http_code} %{content_type}' http://127.0.0.1:18797/.well-known/agent-card.json
200 application/json; charset=utf-8
{"name":"OpenClaw","description":"OpenClaw agent gateway using the Agent2Agent protocol.",...

$ curl -s -X POST -H 'authorization: Bearer <peer token>' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","method":"GetTask","params":{"id":"nope"}}' \
  -w '%{http_code} %{content_type}' http://127.0.0.1:18797/a2a/v1
200 application/json; charset=utf-8
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"1","error":{"code":-32001,"message":"Task not found"}}
```

Discovery and the JSON-RPC endpoint still answer as before; only the unclaimed descendant changed from SPA HTML to the plugin's JSON 404.

Tests:

- `extensions/a2a/src/gateway.test.ts` — `/a2a/v1` registers with `match: "prefix"`, both `/.well-known/agent*` stay `exact` (4 passed).
- `extensions/a2a/src/http.test.ts` — new case drives the registered handler with `GET /a2a/v1/agent-card` and gets `404 {"error":"Not found"}`.

prs.title: fix(plugins): expose verified Control UI requester identity to tools
prs.body:
### Exact-head CI result

Run [41972784926](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41972784926) completed on `dbe22b7be800`: all applicable test/type/build jobs passed. The only failing root job is `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`: 6,480,148 test lines versus ceiling 6,480,128 (20 inherited main lines on the tested merge; own +893 exactly allocated). The aggregate CI gate follows that failure. No further baseline increase was made.

Related: #166721

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin tools being unable to identify a verified Control UI requester even though the Gateway has authenticated that person. Tools requiring both a person and owner permission fail closed because operator UI turns intentionally have no transport sender ID.

## User Impact

Plugins can opt into a separate, live `context.requesterProfile` (`{ id, assertCurrent }`) for a proven single-person Control UI turn. `requesterSenderId`, `senderIsOwner`, and resource policies retain their meanings. Existing plugins need not change; new consumers must fail closed on older hosts or unsupported/unproven turns.

**Maintainer product/SDK and security decision requested:** please assess the optional public shape, initial Control UI-only scope, and rejection once multiple people steer a turn. This proposal is for review, not an accepted contract. Maintainers can request changes or close it if another direction is preferred. No merge, deployment, or production-state change is requested or performed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the private profile, reply snapshot, participant, admitted-run and plugin-lifetime owners. Match the exact agent/session/run and host-issued operator authority. Recheck identity and invocation in the final synchronous effect admission after awaits; resource/owner policy remains independent. Preserve synthetic-ingress rejection and original-client liveness without restoring ingress execution context around plugins. Steerers never replace the requester; ambiguous turns fail closed. No new store, config, protocol or OAuth mapping. Already-dispatched work cannot be retracted.

### Related identity work and dependencies

Pinned main `a5b6c876b9c5d806a7808a970333d3aba609b8a6` retains the gap. Bounded searches and patch comparisons found no duplicate factory fix:

- #187952 `f9ed2281`: hook/memory observation, not factory authority. Shared `requester-profile.ts` needs reconciliation; this fixes source liveness rather than adding a context snapshot.
- #177356 `4780daa5` and #188164 `6e19a644`: overlapping MCP alternatives, not factory fixes. No OAuth/store dependency; single-participant semantics align with #188164. Do not combine both wholesale.
- #164607 `28be4999`: channel-link Profile UI, not external-account verification. No link-management or sender-ID promotion here.
- #164825 `0421a29e`: optional setup display name; presentation remains distinct from authentication.
- #163765 `4f0365c1` / #162164: native personal sign-in/Dashboard work. This consumes admitted identity; device admission and Shared owner fallback are unchanged.
- Landed #159850 / #164593: preserve participant/steering and Shared owner naming semantics.

No hard dependency on these open PRs; shared requester/caller owners may need textual reconciliation. No new native, MCP or profile-UI qualification is claimed. Trusted-plugin contract, not in-process isolation; JSON/prompt/client claims, names or pairing confer no personal authority.
## Evidence

### New protected-effect runtime qualification

The current E2E launches the **built Gateway through its real CLI as a separate owned process**. Public `system.info.pid` must equal the child PID and differ from the test process. A real TLS proxy forwards WebSocket traffic to the Gateway; trusted-proxy authentication/device admission remain separate from profile roles. Public `chat.send` drives the native agent and disk-loaded V2 plugin. No client object, profile binding or run/participant authority is fabricated. Model transport remains a deterministic HTTP fixture, not live-provider inference.

| Case | Observed effect boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Personal administrator | Three model requests drive read → consume result/draft → completion. One real HTTP read and one draft POST. Service persists `.eml` with `X-Unsent: 1` and verified profile ID; sender absent, independent owner true. |
| Personal non-admin | Public `users.setRole`, then a fresh connection: neither protected tool exposed; explicit allowlist fails closed before model/protected HTTP dispatch. Artifact unchanged. |
| Role revoked during preparation | After read, plugin awaits unprotected preparation. Public `users.setRole` commits revocation. Release reaches explicit final-guard refusal: no draft POST, artifact unchanged. Preparation does not consume cancellation in place of the guard. |
| Disconnect during preparation | Presence first confirms live connection, then server-observed retirement. Release reaches final-guard refusal: no draft POST, artifact unchanged. |
| Profile merge during preparation | Public `users.merge` returns a different canonical profile. Final guard refuses: no draft POST, artifact unchanged. |
| Second participant during preparation | Second human `chat.send` steers a shared session. Test-plugin RPC probes the original captured guard and confirms the existing several-participants error without reading process-private maps. Final guard refuses: no draft POST, artifact unchanged. |

All data/services are synthetic and owned; no peer-send operation exists. Assertions inspect actual request counts and persisted bytes, not merely a post-return error. Fixture closes Gateway, clients and servers.

- Standalone E2E passed: **8.865s tests / 15.72s Vitest** with built runtime. Owning gateway-other types, type-aware lint, format, whitespace and line/test budgets pass. Full `pnpm build` exits 0; its unrelated CSS-budget diagnostic is retained, not suppressed.
- Fresh full-candidate Auto Review (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2): **scoped-clean**, no findings; not independent test execution or maintainer approval.
- Production unchanged from `ba43c981`, whose [canonical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41224971308) and [CI/security gates](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41225661116) passed. New-head CI/seconds remain separate.
- Earlier **19 factory**, **93 V1/V2/optional**, **10 profile-authority** cases, authenticated chat E2E, steering/participant/prefix checks, core/test types and focused lint passed. Factory success regression is red on pinned main: missing tools.

Type repair: reproduced CI’s `Duplex`/`Socket` mismatch, used the actual `Duplex` contract, and passed the owning gateway-other typecheck (gateway-root excluded this file). Runtime logic unchanged.

**Historical CI at the original head:** `1da24df421a0591b42398d52228afca92d761078` passes [canonical CI 41243692223](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41243692223), including the owning test types and selected runtime checks, plus [CI/security gates](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41244386624). GitHub reports mergeable/clean; the PR remains open and unmerged.

Earlier `3971b5a` CI passed requester proof but timed out in untouched restart/resume (180s, classification unknown). Exact local shard-order replay passed all 13 cases; that is not a causal fix or proof of inheritance. The later type-only fixture correction is independently reproduced red/green. No CI rerun, timeout increase or guard change. ClawSweeper rated the standalone proof **diamond 5/6**, with no findings or before-merge items, at pre-type-correction `b316ade8`; runtime logic is unchanged.

**Limits:** no live-provider inference: no isolated model credential, and configured remote-proof doctor failed before allocation because Blacksmith CLI is unavailable. No paid provider/new credential selected. New full-E2E baseline attempt hit a 240s command bound during compiled-subprocess preparation: no product verdict, not red proof. Factory regression retains its red comparison. Codex app-server, native-device, peer-send and rollout proof remain outside scope.

No new production logic in this update. Production remains **+124 net lines** using existing owners. The 403-line boundary and 490-line standalone fixtures cover distinct authority risks with exact allocations; shared budget unchanged.
## Focus-week conflict and CI repair

Current repair head: `dbe22b7be800ef631a8311e69030be39fc11f2bf`. Integrated main through `6f975afb9213581bc225dba2417f638c49c828e2`, including the separately approved inherited test-budget correction in #193183. The PR remains open and unmerged; this repair does not approve its product/SDK contract or security design.

- Resolved the original `gateway-personal-caller.ts` conflict by preserving both the requester's source/ambient synthetic-caller checks and main's attended-session creator semantics. No product or public-contract expansion was introduced by the repair.
- Repair head `279ada00da472fca109787e1c39e6cff81bb653c` passed **70 focused tests**: requester-profile/prompt-prefix (33) and account-authority (37), plus core typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and whitespace checks. Full-candidate P0–P2 AutoReview was scoped-clean. These are prior-head results, not a claim that current-head CI has passed.
- The subsequent main integration was conflict-free. All 16 PR-specific files remain byte-for-byte identical to that reviewed repair; the candidate remains +1,078/-8 against integrated main. Ordinary commit hooks and whitespace checks passed. No runtime or standalone E2E rerun is claimed for this mechanical integration.
- **Remaining inherited CI issue:** the canonical test-line ratchet reports 6,480,151 lines against a 6,480,127 ceiling, 24 over. This PR adds exactly 893 test lines with matching 893 allocations; the remaining 24-line debt is inherited from the integrated main baseline. No scalar or allocation was increased by this repair, and the failure is not relabeled green.
- Fresh GitHub CI must qualify `dbe22b7be800ef631a8311e69030be39fc11f2bf`; older successful CI and runtime evidence above remain historical. No merge, CI bypass, or security approval was performed.

### Credit

Thanks to @PollyBot13 for the report/causal investigation, @jonathanlindsay for the concrete contract/use case, @Canvinus and @apps3000 for related MCP/hook work, and @TheAngryPit for the profile/native-identity work. Credit is for context and design constraints, not approval of this proposal.

prs.title: fix(a2a): return JSON 404 for unsupported /a2a/v1 paths
prs.body:
Fixes #193086

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a GET to `/a2a/v1/agent-card` returned HTTP 200 and the Control UI HTML document. Documented discovery and JSON-RPC routes already behaved correctly: `GET /a2a/v1` is a JSON 404, `/.well-known/agent-card.json` and `/.well-known/agent.json` return agent cards, and `POST /a2a/v1` is JSON-RPC.

## Why This Change Was Made

The configured A2A plugin now claims `/a2a/v1` through the existing prefix registration contract. Unsupported descendants reach the plugin's existing JSON 404. The well-known discovery routes stay exact matches. The generic Control UI router is unchanged.

## User Impact

While the A2A account is running, unsupported paths under `/a2a/v1` — including `GET /a2a/v1/agent-card` — return `application/json` with HTTP 404 and `{ "error": "Not found" }`, for missing and wildcard `Accept` headers. Neighboring paths such as `/a2a/v10` and ordinary Control UI routes still serve the SPA. After the account stops, the namespace is released.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, `pnpm test src/gateway/server-http.a2a-namespace.test.ts` failed with Control UI enabled and a real `index.html`: `GET /a2a/v1/agent-card` (absent `Accept`) expected 404 and received 200.
- After the fix, that Gateway regression passed. It covers absent and `*/*` `Accept` headers, exact `GET /a2a/v1` JSON 404, both well-known agent cards, `GET /a2a/v1/.well-known/agent-card.json` JSON 404, unauthenticated `POST /a2a/v1`, SPA responses for `/chat` and `/a2a/v10`, and the descendant returning the SPA again after the account stops.
- `pnpm test extensions/a2a/src/gateway.test.ts extensions/a2a/src/http.test.ts` passed (45 tests).

## Live Gateway proof (Linux, isolated)

Built this branch (`OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (ce3e7d9)`), ran Gateway on loopback port `18991` with an isolated state directory, `gateway.auth.mode=none`, Control UI enabled, and the A2A plugin started (`http server listening (1 plugin: a2a`; `[a2a] [default] starting account (reason: startup)`). Synthetic/local only; no provider keys or non-public endpoints.

While A2A was running:

| Request | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /a2a/v1/agent-card` (no `Accept`, and `Accept: */*`) | `404` `application/json; charset=utf-8` `{"error":"Not found"}` |
| `GET /a2a/v1` | same JSON `404` |
| `GET /a2a/v1/.well-known/agent-card.json` | same JSON `404` |
| `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` and `GET /.well-known/agent.json` | `200` JSON agent cards; interface URL ends in `/a2a/v1` |
| `POST /a2a/v1` with no bearer | `401` JSON |
| `GET /chat` and `GET /a2a/v10` | `200` `text/html` Control UI (`<!doctype html>…`) |

After `channels.stop` for `a2a` / `default` (`{"stopped":true}`):

- `GET /a2a/v1/agent-card` → `200` `text/html` (namespace released to Control UI)
- `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` → `404` `text/plain` `Not Found`
- `GET /chat` stayed HTML

After `channels.start` (`{"started":true}`), `GET /a2a/v1/agent-card` was JSON `404` again. Gateway stopped afterward.

prs.title: fix(sessions): bound the plaintext archive read cache by size and entries
prs.body:
## 问题原因

`materializeSessionArchiveForRead()` 会把每个 `.jsonl.zst` 归档解压成明文副本，落在
`/tmp/openclaw/session-archive-read-cache`。这个目录只有一条清理路径：`sweepMaterializedArchiveCache()`
每小时最多跑一次，且只删 `mtime` 超过 24 小时的条目。没有字节上限，也没有条目数上限。

结果就是缓存目录的大小等于「全部归档解压后的总和」，并且要停留一天。报告里 495 个文件 / 623 MB 直接吃掉
1 GiB tmpfs 的 62%，之后读写 `/tmp` 的会话保存、更新暂存、截图都可能失败。值得注意的是 `archive-compression.ts`
里两处注释已经写着 "budget eviction"（"archives deleted by budget eviction"、"cache itself cannot outgrow
the archives"），但代码里并没有预算逻辑——这次把注释说的东西补上。

## 修改机制

新增 `src/config/sessions/archive-cache-budget.ts`：

- `MATERIALIZED_ARCHIVE_CACHE_MAX_BYTES = 128 MiB`、`MATERIALIZED_ARCHIVE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 64`。
- `evictMaterializedArchiveCacheOverBudget(cacheDir, budget?)`：读目录（`readdirSync` + `statSync`，跳过
  非普通文件），按 `mtime` 升序删到同时满足字节与条目上限；上限可注入，便于测试用小夹具。
- 跳过 `.tmp`：并发写入者的临时文件名是唯一后缀，删掉它们会打断正在进行的物化。
- 目录不存在、条目在扫描与删除之间消失、平台拒绝 unlink 打开中的文件，都只是跳过，不抛错。

`archive-compression.ts` 侧两处改动：

1. 首次写入前调用一次 `evictMaterializedArchiveCacheOverBudget(cacheDir)`（在 `mkdirSync` 之后），
   保证新增副本落地时目录已经在预算内，而不是等下一次每小时清扫。
2. 命中缓存时 `utimesSync` 刷新 mtime。这就是「最近使用」能成立的前提：不刷新的话，热归档在预算看来
   仍是最旧的一份。副作用是 24 小时 TTL 从「物化后 24 小时」变成「闲置 24 小时」，与预算配合更合理。

## 验证与证据

新模块的 6 条单测（`archive-cache-budget.test.ts`，node 环境，临时目录夹具）：

| 用例 | 断言 |
| --- | --- |
| 目录在预算内 | 不删任何条目 |
| 字节超限 | 删最旧一条，中间与最新保留 |
| 条目数超限（都很小） | 只留最新一条 |
| 存在 `.tmp` 写入者 | `.tmp` 保留，普通条目按预算清掉 |
| 目录不存在 | 不抛错 |
| 默认常量 | 条目上限为 64 |

`oxfmt --check`（仓库配置，printWidth 100）对 3 个改动文件通过。

## 证据边界（未验证项）

- 没有跑端到端物化：该路径需要 sealed temp-root runtime 才能解析 `/tmp/openclaw`，本机 sandbox 起不来。
  因此「495 个归档只保留 ≤64 份」这个整体效果是策略层面的推论，不是实测。
- 128 MiB / 64 条是我选的默认值（1 GiB tmpfs 下约 12%），不是维护者给过的数字；如果需要按部署调，
  更合适的后续是把它们做成配置项（issue 里的建议 2），本次没做配置层。
- 只按 mtime 做 LRU，`relatime` 挂载下 atime 不可信，所以没用 atime。
- 测试行净增 84 行，已申请 `config/test-lines-allocations/session-archive-cache-budget.txt` 等额额度。

prs.title: fix(media): byte streams return corrupted content when producers reuse buffers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: bounded byte-stream reads silently corrupt content when an async producer reuses its binary read buffer.

## User Impact

Callers receive the original bytes even when successive chunks share backing storage. For example, reading a real file containing `abcd` through a reusable two-byte buffer currently returns `cdcd`. The same corruption affects Buffer, Uint8Array, DataView, and ArrayBuffer chunks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Snapshot accepted binary bytes before requesting another chunk, at the existing media-core owner. Strings already have owned conversion buffers. Byte limits, supported input types, errors, and overflow cleanup remain unchanged. The extra linear copy is limited to admitted binary bytes; there is no upfront allocation based on the configured limit.

This is a separate boundary/code-fault fix in the same class as externally contributed #188681 (anmol0b), merged by RomneyDa on November 5. No API, configuration, dependency, or lockfile changes.

## Evidence

- **CI attribution:** all test shards and other substantive checks pass; the [baseline-ratchets job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41973424444/job/127067208418) and downstream CI gate fail on inherited test-line debt. Its merge snapshot reports `6479330` lines / `6479310` ceiling, over by **20**, net delta **+46**. An independent full-index count of the exact CI base `3cd454f949f1466692261a8615fcc38199027a98` reports `6479284` / `6479264`, also **20** over at delta zero. This PR adds 46 lines and 46 allocation, leaving the inherited gap unchanged. No unrelated baseline or allocation padding. The local sparse-tree check is not claimed as full-tree evidence.
- **Before/after through the actual built package export:** created a temporary file with `abcd`, independently read its expected bytes, and fed native file-handle reads into `@openclaw/media-core/read-byte-stream-with-limit`. For Buffer and offset Uint8Array/DataView views, plus ArrayBuffer backing storage, the producer reused one two-byte buffer. All four returned `cdcd` on the base and `abcd` after rebuilding the fix. Exact-four-byte acceptance and three-byte overflow both close the file descriptor; the overflow message remains unchanged. No mocked I/O or copied implementation.
- The committed real-file regression failed in all four new cases before the fix; the two existing cases passed. All **six tests pass on both Node and the repository-pinned Bun**, using the native test-projects runner. Reproduce with `pnpm test packages/media-core/src/read-byte-stream-with-limit.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (select `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` or `bun`).
- Repository-supported `pnpm --filter @openclaw/media-core build` passed, including runtime and declaration outputs. Focused production/test typechecks, scoped lint, and format checks passed. Execution used separate physical dependencies in a secretless Linux x64 container, Node 24.22.2 and pinned pnpm 12.15.0. The locked static musl tsrs binary was integrity-verified and selected via its supported override for container libc compatibility.
- Simplification: one ownership fix, no new abstraction or cleanup mechanism; production +2/-1 and tests +46 lines, with an explicit 46-line allocation. Independent full-diff review passed at `5e216e3217abaf3362008a98441b554fa6d258e5`. The configured local autoreview provider could not start safely; no autoreview pass is claimed.

Scope: the runtime proof uses the canonical built media-core package entry that core consumers import. It does not establish that Node stdin/HTTP producers themselves reuse buffers. The whole-root SDK build exceeded the container memory limit; no complete SDK/Gateway/live-provider build or execution is claimed. Broader validation is left to PR CI.

<details>
<summary>Observed real-file output</summary>

```text
Chunk type   File   Before   After   Descriptor closed
Buffer       abcd   cdcd     abcd    true
Uint8Array   abcd   cdcd     abcd    true
DataView     abcd   cdcd     abcd    true
ArrayBuffer  abcd   cdcd     abcd    true
Overflow at 3 bytes: rejects at 4 bytes and closes the descriptor for all four shapes.
```

</details>

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #193175. `openclaw path set` could persist `__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__` inside JSONC/JSONL object keys, while YAML already refused the same new content.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared object-entry emitter now checks each new key using the existing sentinel guard. Both JSON serializers delegate entry emission to this owner, retaining their existing value guards and serialization behavior. This does not scan or reject untouched source containing a pre-existing marker. HeMiaolin's original commit is retained; the repair consolidates its duplicated guards and regression coverage.

## User Impact

New sentinel-bearing keys (including nested keys and substring matches) fail with the existing `OC_EMIT_SENTINEL` error before a write. YAML behavior and ordinary content remain unchanged. No new error text, SDK export, migration, or test-growth allocation.

## Evidence

Built Linux CLI, Node 24.22.1, secretless Docker: frozen main `4a6ca3afd549af75ab68636d4b8a62ae3c16cbfa` twice and candidate `57bb55b2131f` twice, through the installed oc-path plugin's `path set` command. Sixty observations cover exact/nested sentinel keys plus YAML, normal keys/values, sentinel values, and unrelated pre-existing marker controls.

- Main JSONC/JSONL writes sentinel keys; candidate refuses them with exit 1 / `OC_EMIT_SENTINEL`. Every refusal retains the file's exact SHA256.
- YAML refuses on both refs. Sentinel values remain refused on both. Ordinary writes and writes alongside pre-existing markers have byte-identical output files across refs; response fields agree apart from each isolated profile's filesystem path.
- Focused regression: 132 tests passed, five files; lint passed. On frozen main, four key cases fail while four existing-value/YAML controls pass.
- Consolidated existing tests instead of adding duplicate test blocks: test source net −19 lines, no allocation.

## AI Assistance

AI assisted the original contribution and the shared-owner repair/proof.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores prior behavior without a migration. Blast radius is new structured object emission through oc-path JSONC/JSONL set/insert/append; untouched source is preserved.

prs.title: perf(sessions): avoid rereading locked transcript prefixes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Appending to a long transcript while carrying a current snapshot reads and decompresses the entire existing history twice inside the agent database write transaction, delaying other writes.

## User Impact

Prepared transcript appends spend less CPU and allocation on existing history and hold the writer for less time. Stored transcript bytes, conflict detection, ordering, durability, and public behavior are unchanged; no schema or configuration changes are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the full snapshot comparison inside the transaction, then reuse that verified prefix and read only newly appended rows for the returned snapshot. Opaque native callbacks retain their existing refresh path because they can rewrite earlier rows. Runtime production delta is **+8 lines**: the tail bound and prefix reuse preserve the existing exact conflict contract while removing the second full read.

## Evidence

Real worker-owner benchmark with synthetic 1 KiB messages, 1,000 background sessions, and carried snapshots. Five counterbalanced timing pairs, 100 appends per history size per arm per pair (**500 per size per side**); two separate collected-allocation pairs (**200 per size per side**). Timing runs have allocation sampling disabled. Base owner source is from main at `11c8f236b330e8f51c03331dcd6ae0c661080e7b`; the relevant owner code remained unchanged when rebasing for publication.

| Existing messages | CPU ms/append, base → fix | Sampled MiB/append, base → fix | Mean transaction-callback median ms, base → fix | Total GC ms/append, base → fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 100 | 5.08 → 3.79 (−25.4%) | 1.54 → 1.14 (−25.7%) | 3.01 → 2.05 | 1.66 → 0.95 |
| 1,000 | 15.49 → 9.80 (−36.8%) | 8.77 → 5.46 (−37.7%) | 28.90 → 7.79 | 11.70 → 6.77 |
| 10,000 | 148.40 → 83.84 (−43.5%) | 81.75 → 48.68 (−40.5%) | 514.50 → 304.95 | 137.64 → 84.45 |

This is a smaller history-dependent hold, not a constant-time append: the exact comparison and returned snapshot still scale with history. Canonical stored/returned row SHA-256 digests match between arms at every size. A separately traced append at 10,000 messages reads **20,005 → 10,003 payload rows**, eliminating one complete prefix decode. The regression is red on the original owner (**9 rows read, expected 5**) and green with the fix; it also checks the returned snapshot, stored prefix, and idempotent replay.

Validation: 17 focused tests passed across `session-message-rewrite.test.ts` and `session-accessor.reply-init-concurrency.test.ts`; `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, the script typecheck, the agents/sessions test typecheck, changed-file lint/format, and export-name collision guard passed. Independent review is clean: **independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable)**. The route preflight rejected a provider/config mismatch; no operator configuration was changed. The baseline regression run additionally reported source-fingerprint cleanup drift after the expected assertion failure; the fresh candidate run completed with source verification intact.

Closure checks: 39/40 passed; the unchanged Darwin input-closure check hit its 120-second timeout on this heavily contended host. It is recorded as unresolved local evidence, not claimed to be a fixed or proven inherited failure. The isolated recheck also timed out (3/4 passed); no timeout was changed. Exact-head PR CI is pending.

Measurement limits: host load was roughly 100–148; per-run latency tails have only 100 samples and are context, not gates. Short-history maximum GC pauses were noisy despite lower total GC and fewer collections; four identical-code control pairs reproduced mixed-sign total-GC changes and one maximum-pause safeguard crossing (117 → 235 ms at 1,000 messages), so short-run GC diagnostics are inconclusive on this host. At 10,000 messages, end-of-run RSS/heap snapshots were 1,135/257 → 1,411/314 MiB; these are uncollected instantaneous snapshots, not retained-heap measurements, and identical-code controls at that size ranged from 980 to 1,550 MiB RSS. A separate two-pair post-collection diagnostic at 10,000 messages (100 appends per arm, collection after timing) measured retained heap 111.15 → 111.23 MiB and 111.23 → 111.22 MiB; RSS 1,542 → 1,536 MiB and 1,565 → 1,523 MiB. The earlier instantaneous heap difference did not persist after collection. No whole-Gateway latency or retained-memory improvement is claimed. No Gateway stress campaign was run for this narrowly scoped duplicate-read deletion.

The companion investigation found `sessions.transcript-maintenance` uses a read snapshot, so it is not a writer-lock holder; its measured `version` operation and ordinary `append-turn` queries are bounded. This change does not claim to explain all reported multisecond transaction durations. SQL statement IDs/text and counts are emitted by the benchmark; production statement sampling is not enabled for these labels, so absent production IDs cannot be reconstructed.

Reproduction and flags are documented in the header of `scripts/perf/transcript-locked-write-measure.ts`; the shared performance README is unchanged.

Initial CI caught an unavailable Node GC diagnostic type export under the script tsconfig; that benchmark-only issue is corrected and independently reviewed. The test-line ratchet also reported an inherited 92-line deficit: total 6,479,293 vs ceiling 6,479,201, with exactly +98 test lines and +98 allocation in this PR. No unrelated budget increase or timeout relaxation was made. [Initial CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41971234948) remains prior-head evidence.

<details>
<summary>Timing-arm GC and host diagnostics</summary>

Each arm has 100 appends; latency p95/p99 do not gate with that per-run sample count. Columns list base → candidate, in pair order.

| History | Pair | GC collections | Maximum GC pause ms | Host load (1 min) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 100 | 1 | 6 → 4 | 22.9 → 54.2 | 108.6 → 124.6 |
| 100 | 2 | 6 → 4 | 196.5 → 38.3 | 124.1 → 148.2 |
| 100 | 3 | 6 → 4 | 120.5 → 26.2 | 115.2 → 110.3 |
| 100 | 4 | 6 → 4 | 121.1 → 33.2 | 105.3 → 107.8 |
| 100 | 5 | 6 → 4 | 5.3 → 109.8 | 100.2 → 119.8 |
| 1000 | 1 | 37 → 21 | 112.6 → 224.9 | 113.3 → 123.2 |
| 1000 | 2 | 35 → 23 | 230.8 → 120.5 | 124.9 → 144.7 |
| 1000 | 3 | 35 → 21 | 223.0 → 173.0 | 110.8 → 110.3 |
| 1000 | 4 | 37 → 21 | 184.8 → 98.2 | 102.8 → 104.6 |
| 1000 | 5 | 35 → 21 | 137.3 → 74.7 | 100.2 → 121.8 |
| 10000 | 1 | 391 → 236 | 623.5 → 493.4 | 108.3 → 144.4 |
| 10000 | 2 | 398 → 237 | 636.5 → 369.9 | 115.0 → 141.6 |

Per-kind diagnostics were added for timing pair 5 (earlier pairs record total/count/max). At 10,000 messages: minor 379 → 224 collections, 13,865 → 5,140 ms total; major 9 → 7, 311 → 345 ms; incremental 10 → 7, 15.8 → 7.9 ms. Major counts are below 50, so those per-kind comparisons are context. Mean instantaneous RSS/heap MiB at 100, 1,000, 10,000 messages: 573/132 → 542/123; 602/247 → 566/229; 1,135/257 → 1,411/314. These are not collected retained-heap estimates.

A/A controls use the same untraced workload, 100 appends per size, four counterbalanced pairs. At 10,000 messages each arm includes several natural major GCs. GC deltas (B−A, ms/append): 100 messages +0.13, −1.47, +1.04, −0.91; 1,000 messages +4.75, +0.30, −3.21, −1.06; 10,000 messages −24.09, +47.81, −123.18, −45.34. No pauses or maintenance windows were trimmed.
</details>

Current head: `56b36fde214bbea6c082e7fb3f91e2a5fcadf433`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41972735607) is pending; this PR is intentionally left unmerged for maintainer review.

prs.title: fix(ios): reuse Mermaid initialization across canceled requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat's initial layout cancels a Mermaid request while WebKit is still loading, discards that initialization, and immediately creates another document. Both the successful and failed screenshot runs do this. The failed run then stalls before document commit, before any Mermaid JavaScript starts.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41958326550

## User Impact

Canceled requests stop receiving results, while their replacement can reuse initialization that has not executed request-specific JavaScript. Rendering and snapshot cancellation still retire the document to keep canceled scripts isolated.

This removes a redundant initialization, but does not establish a latency improvement or prove the intermittent screenshot failure fixed. Assertions, watchdogs, capture deadlines, simulator lifecycle, and release behavior stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The loading phase cannot have injected a diagram. Reusing that document avoids restarting WebKit during initial layout. Temporary Debug screenshot tracing also correlates document lifecycle events with bundled-resource delivery using document-owned identifiers, fixed resource categories, byte counts, and timestamps. It excludes diagram text, SVG, URLs, arbitrary paths, response contents, and error descriptions. Remove this instrumentation with the existing incident traces after diagnosis.

If the final loading subscriber cancels without a replacement, initialization may remain pending without a job watchdog. A later request still gets its own existing watchdog; idle memory-warning cleanup still retires the document. This accepts idle initialization retention rather than adding another timer owner.

## Evidence

- Local simulator build passed with the pinned SwiftFormat/SwiftLint checks. Focused `ChatMermaidRendererTests`: all four cancellation, coalescing, ordering, and recovery tests passed (3.8 seconds of test execution; 25.3 seconds for XCTest).
- Actual Agent and Chat screenshot XCTest entry points passed in all three local comparisons:

  | Case | Documents created | Replacement request to Mermaid image | Chat test |
  | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
  | Baseline, immediately after fresh boot | 2 | 3.51 s | 22.09 s |
  | Baseline, after measured CPU headroom | 2 | 2.62 s | 19.52 s |
  | Candidate, immediately after fresh boot | 1 | 8.23 s | 21.27 s |

- The headroom check added 70 seconds, so this change does not add a post-boot wait. The candidate delivered the index resource in under 1 ms, followed by a 4.8-second gap before WebKit commit; resource tracing now separates delivery from that wait.
- Local proof uses Xcode 27.2, whereas the incident used 27.1. Chat PNGs are byte-identical across all three local cases. These samples prove reuse and matching capture output, not an intermittent-failure fix.
- Fresh independent review of the complete diff found no actionable P1/P2 findings. Local ClawSweeper completed review of `f21943152ad4..545330fb2559` with no actionable correctness or security findings. The full hosted screenshot-only validation is pending.
- SwiftFormat, documentation formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. No tests were weakened or new test-only production seams added.

prs.title: feat: let the memory slot owner report its own dreaming status
prs.body: Related: #138366 ## What Problem This Solves A memory plugin that owns the memory slot and does its own consolidation has no way to describe its dreaming on the Memory page. The page reports dreaming as disabled or unscheduled while it in fact runs every night. Two host assumptions cause this: - `resolveMemoryDreamingConfig` gives all three phases the same expression, so a plugin whose REM and deep passes run on separate schedules, or whose light pass is event-driven, cannot say so. - The promotion counters come from memory-core's own store, which stops advancing once another plugin takes over consolidation. The workaround is worse than the symptom. Setting `dreaming.enabled: true` on the slot owner makes memory-core create its managed promotion cron at the same frequency, so the same workspace gets two consolidation passes in the same minute. ## Why This Change Was Made `MemoryPluginCapability` already has this shape once. `publicArtifacts` lets a non-`memory-core` slot owner contribute data through an optional provider, while the host keeps ownership of semantics. This PR applies the same pattern to dreaming: ```ts export type MemoryPluginCapability = { publicArtifacts?: MemoryPluginPublicArtifactsProvider; dreaming?: MemoryPluginDreamingProvider; // added // … }; ``` The contract is reporting-only. Lifecycle, memory-core's managed sweep cron and the dream actions stay with memory-core. The full rules are in `docs/plugins/sdk-overview/memory-and-context.md`: - **Overlay.** `doctor.memory.status` overlays the report field by field on the host resolution. Without a provider the response is unchanged. - **Every status path.** The provider is consulted with a search runtime, without one, and when the plugin answers through its own `providerRuntime` (new in this revision, see below). - **Owner lock.** Any report arrives as `reportedByProvider: true`. That locks the page's switch against turning the host sweep on, since both would dream at once. A running host sweep can still be turned off. The Off confirmation then says that a promotion job memory-core already scheduled survives until #156667's orphan cleanup or manual removal. - **Switch and scene.** Reported `enabled` arrives as `reportedEnabled`. The Dreams scene lights while the owner reports running, or while a phase is enabled and scheduled. - **Counters.** Reported counters arrive as `reportedStats` next to memory-core's figures, not in their place. The Dreaming status line and Settings > Memory › Activity show the owner's counters, with n/a for any it omits. The Review lists keep memory-core's figures, entries and actions, together with a note that says so. - **Schedule rows.** Settings > Memory › Sleep schedule takes each phase's state from its own `enabled` and `scheduled` flags while an owner reports. ## Revision on current `main` This revision merges current main and resolves the two P2 findings of the last review: - **Provider-runtime slot owners.** A plugin that registers both `providerRuntime` and `dreaming.getStatus` took the provider-runtime branch, which returned before the dreaming lookup. Both runs use the same `doctor.memory.status` fixture: slot owner `acme-memory` reports REM/deep schedules, an event-driven light phase and `promotedToday: 4`, while memory-core's own count is 2 and the host switch is off. | | Before (main) | After (this PR) | |---|---|---| | Overview: phases and counters | | | | Dreams: scene and switch | | | **Live.** The previous revision of this change, on a 2026.10.10 build, has been running in a production installation since 2026-11-05 with a third-party memory slot owner that dreams on its own schedule. No real timers, sleeps or Gateway boots in the new tests. **Plugin SDK surface.** The budget comment adds +3 type-only exports (`MemoryPluginDreaming{Provider,Status,PhaseStatus}`). `plugin-sdk:surface:check` already fails on `main` itself (3862 > 3859 exports, 2233 > 2232 callable).
