prs.title: perf(state): avoid redundant workspace sweep digests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workspace manifest cleanup returns each traversed pack's digest even though the lookup batch already contains those keys, converts those bytes back to strings, and maintains separate roots, pending, and visited Sets. That repeats work while walking shared manifests.

## User Impact

Workspace cleanup allocates less memory. Candidate selection, checkpoint/root retention, missing-pack errors, the read snapshot, and epoch-protected deletion stay unchanged. There is no schema, index, retention, configuration, or permission change.

This is a bounded allocation improvement. It does **not** remove large-payload SQLite I/O or shorten the lifetime of the sweep's read snapshot.

## Why This Change Was Made

One growing Set now represents queued and visited digests. A persistent iterator consumes only the Set's currently known entries in each batch, so discovering children after a partial batch cannot strand them behind an exhausted iterator. Unique keys and the existing row-count check retain missing-pack detection; traversal queries return only child links.

Runtime code shrinks by six lines. The existing retention regression gains nine lines to verify returned digest bytes, with a scoped test-line allocation. Benchmark-only growth adds historical sweep epochs, sorted candidate digests, and the warmup its header already promised. No second implementation or cache is retained. The broader non-test/non-doc diff filter is +20 lines because it includes +24 benchmark lines and two test-budget metadata lines; runtime code itself is net negative.

## Evidence

The regression fails on the base with **19,712 returned digest bytes instead of 9,920**, then passes with the same retained/deleted content and reuse-after-selection checks. All **35 focused tests** in the CAS, store, and manifest-tree files pass. Wrapper wall time was 317.36 s, dominated by cold transformation; Vitest reports 90% transform and 6% test execution.

Synthetic owner measurements use a 1.228 GB SQLite database, 10,000 projection rows, 37 distinct 80,000-file manifests, and 29,674 packs. Live-heavy retains all trees; history-heavy retains one (802 reachable packs and 28,872 orphan candidates). Stored epoch is 2 and sweep epoch 4: SQLite's zero-byte encodings for 0/1 would understate reads behind large payloads. Five counterbalanced pairs per shape, one complete sweep per side per pair, with separate untraced timing and 32 KiB sampled allocation including collected objects. Each process has an excluded warmup. Values below are arithmetic means.

| Workload / metric | Base | Candidate | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| live-heavy: untraced CPU | 915.88 ms | 903.49 ms | -1.35% |
| live-heavy: untraced wall (context) | 3,699.72 ms | 3,153.98 ms | -14.75% |
| live-heavy: sampled allocation | 80.96 MB | 64.04 MB | -20.91% |
| history-heavy: untraced CPU | 474.95 ms | 438.68 ms | -7.64% |
| history-heavy: untraced wall (context) | 982.79 ms | 1,098.29 ms | +11.75% |
| history-heavy: sampled allocation | 32.81 MB | 32.79 MB | -0.07% |

Every arm has the same sorted candidate digest and count: zero candidates in live-heavy, 28,872 in history-heavy. Path sets are empty in these performance fixtures; the existing correctness test covers live, orphan, and reused path sets. CPU and wall measurements come from a heavily loaded shared host; wall time is context, not a claimed latency improvement. live-heavy untraced 1-minute host load: base 124.3–154.0, candidate 129.6–156.9. history-heavy untraced 1-minute host load: base 109.7–134.4, candidate 103.9–129.7.

Reproduction uses `scripts/perf/local-workspace-manifest-read.ts` and its sparse baseline overlay support:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/local-workspace-manifest-read.ts \
  80000 1 timing <synthetic-db> --reuse --sweep --sweep-epoch=4
# Repeat with allocation; alternate baseline/candidate source overlays.
```

Fixture preparation (new synthetic database only, outside measured windows):

```sh
mkdir -p .local/sweep-proof
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/local-workspace-manifest-read.ts \
  80000 1 timing .local/sweep-proof/synthetic.sqlite --target-bytes=1200000000 --sweep
node --input-type=module -e '
  import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite";
  const db = new DatabaseSync(process.argv[1]);
  db.exec("UPDATE local_workspace_tree_packs SET sweep_epoch = 2");
  db.close();
' .local/sweep-proof/synthetic.sqlite
```

Measure the all-live shape first. To create the history-heavy shape, clear `tree_root_digest` on every projection except `worktree_id = 'synthetic-manifest'` in this synthetic fixture, then measure again. The SQL changes only the fixture. Baseline source is `11c8f236b330e8f51c03331dcd6ae0c661080e7b`; extract its `src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-cas.kernel.ts` into a matching sparse directory and set `OPENCLAW_BENCH_BASELINE_DIR` to that absolute directory for baseline arms. Candidate arms use the checkout normally. No production data or production load is used. This follows the pure-deletion fast path: no whole-Gateway CPU/GC/latency improvement is claimed, and no Gateway stress campaign was run.

Formatting, focused core/script lint, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, the matching gateway-other test typecheck, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex subagent review through P2 is **scoped-clean** (autoreview route unavailable: its configured-provider preflight was refused; no operator config changed). The reviewer saw the frozen complete diff and relevant source context only. No accepted findings remain.

Exact-head CI completed on `17910aef316556f62a65937d8bd33d9f5da12ffd`: all test, typecheck, lint, build, and security jobs passed. The only underlying failure is the [test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41972731066/job/127065182703), which also makes the aggregate CI gate fail. CI reports 6,479,267 test lines against a 6,479,244 ceiling: 23 over, with this PR adding nine lines and allocating exactly nine. A direct LF-byte count of tracked test blobs and allocation scalars at CI's base `f21943152ad460bc2df25c3a518a8d999f087b93` confirms 6,479,258 against 6,479,235: the same inherited 23-line debt. Current main `1e101d06645b30edfc0c686813de5c795acea2d4` still has 20 lines of debt (6,479,284 against 6,479,264), so a rebase would not clear this gate. The ratchet permits non-growing changes on an over-budget tree; green main runs therefore do not disprove this debt. No baseline was raised, test proof removed, CI rerun, or merge attempted. Ready for TS review; exact-head green remains blocked on the shared test-budget debt.

prs.body:
Closes #168200
Related: #167873; runtime recovery subsequently landed in #189900.

## Problem and user impact

Unrecoverable conversation startup and code-workspace preparation failures still need an understandable explanation and next step instead of generic errors or internal identifiers. Messaging-channel users must be able to recover in their current channel.

## Relevance against current main (2026-11-04)

Main now includes #189900 (`e515a095c5b5`): missing unused Codex threads can reach lifecycle recovery instead of failing in inference preflight. Recovery refuses to discard acknowledged native history. This PR is **fallback presentation, not that runtime fix**. Missing-thread guidance remains for failures that reach the user, and lost workspace leases remain a separate case. Main does not yet provide this curated startup copy or the certified startup diagnostic projection.

## Changes

- Specific UI and channel copy; no Control UI prerequisite in channel replies.
- Preserve certified, bounded, redacted diagnostics in reopened history; unrelated diagnostic payloads remain excluded.
- Keep recovery guidance visible outside collapsed Details and main's new diagnostic popover. Preserve main's separate detail payloads, host-authored notice precedence, archived-child behavior, and retry eligibility.
- Recognize main's parenthesized lease-loss diagnostics. A regression invokes the real state-lease error producer; it failed before the matcher adjustment and passes afterward.
- Update the two existing browser selectors to main's renamed composer Stop control.

### User-facing copy (unchanged)

| Failure | Control UI | Messaging channels |
|---|---|---|
| Missing saved thread | **OpenClaw couldn't find the saved conversation data needed to continue.** Start a new conversation and send your request again. | **OpenClaw couldn't find the saved conversation data needed to continue.** Send /new to start a new conversation, then send your request again. |
| Lost/expired workspace allocation lease | **Couldn't finish preparing the code workspace.** Send your request again to retry workspace setup. | Same as Control UI. |

Presentation only: no automatic retry/replay, lease repair, rebinding, or reconstruction of conversation state. A missing backend thread does not establish that the visible OpenClaw transcript was deleted.

## Validation (2026-11-04)

Four conflicts resolved against main `3cd454f949f1`; later observed main `1e101d06645b` also merges cleanly locally.

- 135 focused runtime/history tests passed across four files.
- 44 UI/component tests passed across three files, including real-browser popover behavior.

- Independent Codex AutoReview: scoped-clean at P0–P2 against snapshot `5e58e984fe71`; its tree matches repair commit `cdb1ccb89dfd`. Unchanged implementation context was not supplied to the reviewer; production-path tests above provide execution proof.
- Synthetic Gateway/browser fixtures and isolated frozen dependencies; no live Gateway or channel delivery was exercised.

An initial runtime compilation was invalidated by formatting during artifact capture; the settled-source run passed. The first broad browser run exposed obsolete Stop selectors; the corrected run passed all eight scenarios. Earlier attempts are not counted as passing proof.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): resolve bundled channel in sandbox explain (companion to #189343)
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/51245 (partial: this fixes the `sandbox explain` diagnostic only; the live Telegram elevated-execution denial steipete kept open in that issue is not addressed here, so the issue should stay open).

Builds on #189343 by @nikolas-sapa. Their commit is cherry-picked unchanged with authorship kept; this PR adds the test change and Linux proof that ClawSweeper asked for on #189343. Credit for the fix goes to @nikolas-sapa. If #189343 lands instead, this can be closed.

## What Problem This Solves
`openclaw sandbox explain --session telegram:slash:<id>` reports `channel: (unknown)` and `allowedByConfig: false` when the CLI's plugin registry has no channel plugins (the sandbox-backends scope is empty for stock docker/podman configs), even with `tools.elevated.allowFrom.telegram` configured.

## User Impact
User impact: `openclaw sandbox explain` shows the right channel and `allowedByConfig: true` for telegram sessions on stock docker/podman setups, so elevated-tool allow lists can be checked without confusing `(unknown)` output.

## Why
- Original fix (@nikolas-sapa, 4e58d9b): fall back to the static bundled channel catalog after the runtime registry misses, for both the stored-delivery and the parsed-key paths.
- Added here: the stored-delivery regression test now uses a session key with no channel (`agent:builder:main`), so only the stored delivery context supplies telegram. It now fails if the stored-delivery fallback is removed (it previously passed because the key also resolved telegram).

## Evidence
Setup: Linux, built CLI, isolated HOME.

Config: `{"tools":{"elevated":{"enabled":true,"allowFrom":{"telegram":["123456"]}}}}`

Before (main 88217c925; `sandbox-explain.ts` and `channels/registry.ts` are unchanged from there to base 43a3abe0595):
```
Elevated:
  enabled: true
  channel: (unknown)
  allowedByConfig: false
```
After (this branch 46de5b0c90f):
```
Elevated:
  enabled: true
  channel: telegram
  allowedByConfig: true
```
`--json` before/after: before `"allowedByConfig": false` (no `channel` field); after `"channel": "telegram", "allowedByConfig": true`

### Tests
- Red (fix reverted): `Tests  2 failed | 18 skipped (20) (exit 1)`, both tests fail
- Red (stored-delivery fallback only reverted): `Tests  1 failed | 1 passed | 18 skipped (20) (exit 1)`, the stored-delivery test fails
- Green (branch): `Tests  2 passed | 18 skipped (20) (exit 0)`; whole file: `Tests  20 passed (20) (exit 0)`
- oxlint exit 0, format check exit 0, check:test-mock-exports exit 0, git diff --check exit 0

AI-assisted; all output above is from real runs.

### Live elevated gate (second half of #51245)

Commit 553345060b6 adds regression tests for the runtime gate (`resolveElevatedPermissions`, used by `get-reply-directives` for live Telegram turns). I checked the live path on current main: Telegram native slash turns reach the gate with `Provider: "telegram"`, and `tools.elevated.allowFrom.telegram` is looked up by that provider. With **no channel plugin registered**, a Telegram slash context (`SessionKey: telegram:slash:123456`, `SenderId: 123456`) is authorized for `["123456"]`, `[123456]` and `["telegram:123456"]`, and a different sender is still denied. So no runtime code change is needed on main. The tests keep it that way. The `sandbox explain` fix above was the remaining part of the issue.

```
$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/reply-elevated.test.ts src/commands/sandbox-explain.test.ts
```

prs.title: fix(ui): dashboard widget links do nothing in the macOS app
prs.body:
<!-- focus-week-repair:start -->
## Focus-week conflict and CI repair — November 4, 2026

- Integrated main and resolved only the wrapper output fixture conflict. Preserved both main's `data.query` bridge output and this PR's captured pristine `MessageEvent.data` getter; no link authorization or activation logic was removed.
- The combined wrapper fixture is 17,967 bytes, SHA-256 `c7d26e46938bab7e73a1902c863092740b44f6a72b7837033e386549abc84d6e`. It was independently reconstructed from the trusted main generator plus the reviewed PR's emitted-string changes. This static byte-composition check is not execution of the contributor test suite.
- Whole-candidate independent AutoReview through P2 was scoped-clean; diff checks passed. Exact allocation of 531 own net regression-test lines covers the distinct wrapper port, sandbox activation and retirement boundaries. No shared scalar or checker change belongs to this PR.
- Runtime checks use secretless hosted CI, not execution of fork code on the maintainer host. Existing native app receipts below remain prior-head evidence, not a new native run.
- Current-revision maintainer/security approval is still required. The WebKit activation-consumption tradeoff and bounded native/browser proof gaps remain explicit; conflict repair is not security approval.
- Incorporated the separately approved shared baseline correction from #193183 at main `6f975afb9213`; published repair head `6bb46f292b3a1d63b9cd19f64a9d11ae1a5c4b9d`. Prior repaired-head UI/Node checks passed except the inherited test-budget debt. Hosted CI run 41972707178 completed: all applicable test/type/build checks passed; the only failing root job is `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (6,479,789 test lines vs 6,479,766 ceiling, inherited 23-line debt after current-main changes; own +531 is exactly allocated). The aggregate CI check follows that failure. The separate PR-context job was cancelled, not a test failure. Current-revision maintainer/security approval remains pending; no extra baseline raise or security approval is included in this repair.
<!-- focus-week-repair:end -->

Related: #142606

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: clicking an `https` `target="_blank"` link inside a dashboard HTML widget does nothing in the macOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: in the macOS app, a deliberate click on a widget link opens the destination in the default browser, the same place other external Dashboard links already go. Every click opens, including two clicks in quick succession. Browsers keep their current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI opens widget links with `window.open` from the `host.open` MessagePort task. WebKit's popup blocker does not carry the click's gesture across a MessagePort, so the dashboard web view drops the open before the app's existing new-window handoff runs.

`host.open` now offers the URL to the app's existing `openclawLink` owner first (`postNativeExternalLink`) and keeps `openExternalUrlSafe` for browsers, the pattern the browser-tab card and browser panel already use. The native receiver accepts `openclawLink` only from the Control UI main frame and calls the same `ControlUIDocumentHost.openExternal`. The native route stays per caller rather than inside `openExternalUrlSafe`, because moving it there would change the destination for every caller and would hand `blob:` URLs to a native handler that cannot open them.

The native route skips the popup blocker, so it applies that blocker's rules itself: the gesture must be in this widget, and each open spends it. An open goes native only when all of these hold (`ui/src/lib/board/widget-bridge.ts` `openNativeLink`):

1. **The dashboard has live activation** (`navigator.userActivation.isActive`).
2. **The gesture was in this widget.** The board host asks the widget's own sandbox proxy frame for its `navigator.userActivation.isActive` (`ui/notifications/sandbox-activation-query` with a random id, `ui/src/lib/board/widget-sandbox-host.ts`). The answer counts only from `frame.contentWindow` at `sandboxOrigin`. No answer within 250 ms means refuse. The proxy answers in `src/agents/sandbox-host.ts` and never relays `sandbox-` notifications from its inner frame, so the widget cannot forge the answer. Activation reaches the proxy frame only from input inside its own widget (WebKit probe below). The proxy is served fresh by the Gateway, so this also covers stored widgets that keep their approved wrapper bytes.
3. **The request is still current after that await.** Widget retirement, a Gateway disconnect or reconnect, and a document reset bump the request generation, so `isCurrent()` returns false. In that case `host.open` throws `widget link request is no longer current` before both the native opener and the `window.open` fallback. The same lifecycle paths settle every pending activation query as inactive and drop its id (`cancelActivationQueries`), so a late proxy answer finds nothing to resolve. The native receiver gets no widget lifecycle identity, so the bridge enforces retirement before it posts.
4. **Each open spends the gesture.** Before posting, the bridge consumes the page's transient activation the way an opened popup does: `document.createElement("input").showPicker()` runs WebKit's consume-user-activation (`HTMLInputElement::showPicker` calls `LocalDOMWindow::consumeTransientActivation`, which clears activation in every frame of the page). A detached text input has nothing to show. The bridge then checks that `isActive` really went false, and refuses otherwise (fail closed). One real click or key in a widget yields at most one open. The next open needs new input, and a new click opens at once. There is no rate limit or time budget.

Browsers without `openclawLink` (`hasNativeExternalLink()` is false) skip all of this and keep the old path.

New wrappers also read bridge and prompt port messages through a `MessageEvent.prototype.data` getter captured before widget code runs (`src/canvas/wrap.ts`), the same approach the shortcut bridge uses. That closes the port theft itself for new documents. The proxy binding and per-open consumption cover stored widgets.

Widget-side gates are unchanged: trusted click, adopted view ticket, `http(s)` only, private port. No popup permission, sandbox attribute, or Swift change.

**Why not `document.activeElement`:** a WKWebView probe with real HID input and the dashboard's 3-level nesting showed that a cross-origin widget with no activation of its own can focus itself (`input.focus()`, `link.focus()`, `window.focus()`). The parent's `activeElement` then becomes that widget's frame while activation from a click elsewhere is still live, so it does not prove a gesture in that widget.

<details>
<summary>Root cause trace (main 5291a06cc263)</summary>

| Hop | Code | Result in WebKit |
|---|---|---|
| Trusted widget click to `host.open` | `src/canvas/wrap.ts:147-154` | reaches the host |
| Proxy port hand-off and request dispatch | `src/agents/sandbox-host.ts:393-404`, `ui/src/lib/board/widget-sandbox-host.ts:178-191, 260` | synchronous into `BoardWidgetBridgeOwner.handle` |
| `host.open` | `ui/src/lib/board/widget-bridge.ts:129-137` | calls the opener |
| Opener | `ui/src/lib/open-external-url.ts:73` | `window.open` returns `null` |
| WebKit popup gate (`ControlUIDocumentHost.swift:56`) | | blocked: no `decidePolicyFor`, no `createWebViewWith` |
| Native handoff | `DashboardWindowController.swift:312-340`, `ControlUIDocumentHost+NavigationPolicy.swift:375-378`, `AppActivation.swift:62-65` | never reached |

A `null` result from `window.open` is not the failure signal: with `noopener` WebKit returns `null` even for opens it performs.
</details>

### Risk

- In the macOS app, widget links go to the default browser through `openclawLink` (`target: "external"`). That is the destination the app's new-window delegate already uses for Dashboard `window.open` requests.
- The popup blocker no longer runs on the native route. Its rules are applied by the four checks above. A widget gets at most one open per real gesture inside it, the same as a popup.
- A native open spends the page's activation, as an opened popup does. Another activation-gated action on the same gesture afterwards needs new input.
- A slow proxy answer (over 250 ms) refuses the open. The user can click again.
- Any other host that installs `openclawLink` gets the same route. Only the macOS dashboard does today.

## Security boundary

The native route skips WebKit's popup gate, so the remaining guards are pinned by tests, WebKit probes, and the app runs below:

- **Port theft.** Widget code can redefine `MessageEvent.prototype.data` and read the wrapper's private port and ticket when host-init arrives. On 98f66694ae2 a stored widget with old wrapper bytes that steals its port opens nothing after a click outside it, and one click inside it opens exactly once while it keeps sending through the stolen port (app run below). New wrappers no longer leak the port (captured getter). The `wrap.test.ts` case runs the real wrapper with a `data` override and goes red without the getter.
- **Retirement during the activation query.** `host.open` rechecks `isCurrent` after the query and rejects before either opener. Pending queries are settled as inactive on retirement, disconnect, reconnect and reset. Tests: `widget-bridge.test.ts` (retired during a pending query, for both a positive and a negative answer) and `widget-sandbox-host.test.ts` (retired, reconnected, disconnected while the query is pending: no `openclawLink`, no `window.open`, activation untouched, query timer released at once). App run below: with the query held, killing the Gateway opens nothing on 98f66694ae2 and opened the link on 2031987bfa4.
- **Native receiver.** `openclawLink` is accepted only from the dashboard web view's main frame (`DashboardWindowController.swift:546-556`) and receives no widget lifecycle identity. Retirement is therefore enforced in the bridge before posting (above).
- **Proxy activation answer.** Only the widget's own proxy window at the sandbox origin, with the query's random id, can answer. Answers from another frame, another origin, a wrong id, or no answer within 250 ms refuse (`widget-sandbox-host.test.ts`). The proxy answers from its own activation and never relays a widget-sent `sandbox-activation` (`mcp-app-sandbox-http.test.ts`).
- **Gesture spent per open.** One gesture opens one link even when requests race the query (`widget-bridge.test.ts`). An engine whose `showPicker()` leaves activation live, or throws, gets no native open.
- **Wrapper** (`src/canvas/wrap.ts:147-154`): forwards only `isTrusted` primary `target=_blank` clicks or middle clicks. On the real wrapper, scripted `click()` and synthetic `click`/`auxclick` on https, `javascript:` and `data:` anchors post no `host.open`.
- **Host and owner:** `host.open` from the window channel, another frame, another origin, a second port offer, or a forged or retired ticket never reaches `openclawLink`. The forged-port test now waits on the host closing the forged port, not on a sleep. 11 non-HTTP(S) URLs reach neither `openclawLink` nor `window.open`. The host-realm `^https?://` check is the binding scheme gate.

## Real behavior proof

Shipped macOS app built from the exact source, real HID pointer clicks, before and after, plus stolen-port and retire-during-query legs on the new head and on the previous head.

- Environment: MacBook Pro, Apple silicon (arm64), macOS 27.2 (26B123), Xcode 27.1, default browser Google Chrome 156.0.8078.74. App built with `scripts/package-mac-app.sh` (debug, ad-hoc signed, `ai.openclaw.mac.debug`, app version 2026.10.7) from 98f66694ae2. Each run's `identity.txt` records `source_sha` = `expected_sha` (98f66694ae2, 2031987bfa4 or 5291a06cc263).
- Harness: fork `etzelm/openclaw` branch `mac/proof-6b` commit `4cedbb52eba` (`scripts/mac-proof/6.sh`, `6s.sh`, `6r.sh`, driver and instrumentation in `scripts/mac-proof/local-185433-r8/`) on lib `mac/proof-5` `f354d51cefd`. It runs locally (`PP_LOCAL=1`, isolated state dir and app profile) with a loopback Gateway on 28789, the MCP App sandbox on 28790, and a fixture on 127.0.0.1:38790 that records each hit with its User-Agent. A fixture hit from Chrome is the final effect, whichever opener caused it.
- Targeted tests on the same build tree: `widget-bridge` + `widget-sandbox-host` 63/63.

### After, head `98f66694ae2dde1a19db163a2688db9b6c96beb4`: PASS, and two quick clicks both open

```
14:44:11 HID click 1 posted at the link's AX center
14:44:12 allowed open via: HID pointer click 1
14:44:16 double click: mouse-ups at 1793483055815 and 1793483056323 ms, 508 ms apart (app re-activated between them)
14:44:17 after-double: probe v1 moves:6 down:trusted-b0 click:trusted-d1-act-yes dbl:2
14:44:17 double click hits /double = 2 at 21:44:15.885Z 21:44:16.392Z
14:45:56 final-effect hits /synthetic = 0
14:45:56 final-effect hits /forged-open = 0
14:45:56 final-effect hits /forged-request = 0
14:45:56 allowed hit opener: {"at":"2026-10-31T21:44:11.451Z","port":38790,"path":"/widget","ua":"... Chrome/156.0.0.0 Safari/537.36"}
14:45:56 PASS 6 (HID pointer click 1): the click opened the default browser; two clicks under a second apart opened twice; ...
```

One real click opened `/widget` in Chrome. Then two real clicks on a second link, 508 ms apart, opened it twice (fixture hits 507 ms apart). The widget recorded both trusted clicks (`dbl:2`). Chrome takes the front after the first open and covers the app here, so the harness brings the app back between the clicks, as a user would. A first attempt without that step sent click 2 into Chrome and opened once. The previous head's shared 1 s budget refused any second open inside a second (its own unit test pinned that), so this step would lose the second open there.

- Widget in the dashboard panel before the click: 

  ![after-12-before-click.jpg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/86f36bad11592d926802838a23c431c36a0e6e3d/mac-item-6-widget-links/proof-r8/after-12-before-click.jpg)
- Default browser after the two clicks (tab strip, bookmarks, icons and banner blacked out): 

  ![after-20-default-browser.jpg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/86f36bad11592d926802838a23c431c36a0e6e3d/mac-item-6-widget-links/proof-r8/after-20-default-browser.jpg)
- Recording (app window only): [after-recording.mp4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/86f36bad11592d926802838a23c431c36a0e6e3d/mac-item-6-widget-links/proof-r8/after-recording.mp4)

### Before, base `5291a06cc263f0815fa087fd02bbdb29c3839089`: FAIL

```
14:47:07 HID click 1 posted at the link's AX center
14:47:28 after-hid-1: probe v1 moves:2 down:trusted-b0 click:trusted-d1-act-yes dbl:0
14:47:31 HID click 2 posted at the link's AX center
14:47:52 after-hid-2: probe v1 moves:3 down:trusted-b0 click:trusted-d1-act-yes dbl:0
14:47:55 no default browser open after the HID clicks; activating the link with AXPress
14:48:25 FAIL: no default browser hit on /widget after pointer clicks and AXPress
```

The widget's probe shows the trusted click with user activation, and the fixture logged no request: 

  ![before-13-no-pointer-open.jpg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/86f36bad11592d926802838a23c431c36a0e6e3d/mac-item-6-widget-links/proof-r8/before-13-no-pointer-open.jpg)

### Stolen port: outside click opens nothing, one inside click opens once

The `6s` widget overrides `MessageEvent.prototype.data`, keeps the wrapper's port and ticket, and sends `host.open` for `/stolen` through it every 300 ms for the whole run. The harness stores it with a Gateway on 7bdf01c0b32 (old wrapper bytes that leak the port) and serves it from the source under test. It clicks chat text outside the widget, sends a keystroke, and then clicks plain text (not a link) inside the widget once.

New head 98f66694ae2:

```
14:50:29 seed source 7bdf01c0b323cfc4fcf0d2c1b7d32c4a4feaba3c; serving source 98f66694ae2dde1a19db163a2688db9b6c96beb4
14:51:15 stolen port armed: yes
14:51:45 after-outside-click: probe s1 moves:0 down:none port:yes ticket:yes sent:57 oks:0 last:err:widget link could not be opened
14:51:45 RESULT 6s: no open: stolen-port requests after a click outside the widget were refused
14:51:49 inside click posted on the widget's plain text (not a link)
14:51:57 after-inside-click: probe s1 moves:2 down:trusted-b0 port:yes ticket:yes sent:97 oks:1 last:err:widget link could not be opened
14:51:58 final-effect hits /stolen after the inside click = 1 (at 21:51:49.236Z )
14:51:58 RESULT 6s-inside: 1 open(s) from one click inside the widget while it kept sending
```

The one inside click opened once. Between the two probe reads the widget sent 40 more requests through the stolen port (`sent:57` to `sent:97`), and only that one was accepted (`oks:1`). Previous head 2031987bfa4, same harness: outside click 0 opens, and the one inside click gave **3** opens (`21:53:37.850Z 21:53:39.911Z 21:53:41.892Z`), the reusable window the budget allowed.

- Dashboard after the inside click (probe: `sent:98 oks:1`): 

  ![stolen-new-43-after-inside-click.jpg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/86f36bad11592d926802838a23c431c36a0e6e3d/mac-item-6-widget-links/proof-r8/stolen-new-43-after-inside-click.jpg)

### Retire during the activation query: no open on the new head, opened on the previous head

The production query window is a few milliseconds (immediate proxy answer, 250 ms timeout), too short to retire the widget inside it from outside the app. For this leg only, the driver applies timing instrumentation to the served build and restores it afterwards (`local-185433-r8/instrument.mjs`). The proxy sends its usual answer, read at answer time, 2500 ms late. The dashboard waits up to 10 s for it instead of 250 ms. No check in the path changes.

`6r.sh` first clicks a control link with the Gateway up. The held answer must still open it, which shows the instrumented path works. Then it clicks the retire link and kills the Gateway (`kill -9`) right after the click, inside the hold. The Gateway disconnect is the retirement the review describes: the frame stays rendered, the host goes inactive and `connected: false`, and the proxy is still alive to answer.

New head 98f66694ae2:

```
15:00:48 timing instrumentation: proxy holds activation answers 2500 ms; dashboard query timeout 10000 ms
15:01:08 control: click helper ran 1793484064709..1793484065527; hits /control = 1; browser hit 2489 ms after the click returned
15:01:14 retire: click helper ran 1793484073904..1793484074273; Gateway pid 79050 killed at 1793484074290 (17 ms after the click returned; the proxy answers ~2500 ms after the click)
15:01:15 after-retire: probe r1 moves:4 down:trusted-b0 control:trusted-act-yes retire:trusted-act-yes
15:01:24 final-effect hits /retire = 0 (any opener: native link owner or window.open fallback)
15:01:24 RESULT 6r: no open: the widget link pending when the Gateway dropped was refused
```

Previous head 2031987bfa4, same harness and instrumentation:

```
14:58:10 control: click helper ran 1793483886789..1793483887630; hits /control = 1; browser hit 2499 ms after the click returned
14:58:16 retire: click helper ran 1793483895968..1793483896346; Gateway pid 76799 killed at 1793483896364 (18 ms after the click returned; the proxy answers ~2500 ms after the click)
14:58:17 after-retire: probe r1 moves:7 down:trusted-b0 control:trusted-act-yes retire:trusted-act-yes
14:58:26 final-effect hits /retire = 1 (any opener: native link owner or window.open fallback)
14:58:26 RESULT 6r: OPENED: the widget link pending when the Gateway dropped reached the default browser (1 hit)
```

The leg is armed. On the previous head the same trusted click with activation opened `/retire` in Chrome at 21:58:18.832Z, 2.5 s after the Gateway was killed. On the new head nothing reached the browser. The fixture count covers any opener. WebKit would also block a `window.open` from this task, so the unit tests pin separately that the fallback is never called (`window.open` spy, `widget-sandbox-host.test.ts`).

- New head after the retire click (probe shows the trusted click with activation; no browser open): 

  ![retire-new-51-after-retire.jpg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/86f36bad11592d926802838a23c431c36a0e6e3d/mac-item-6-widget-links/proof-r8/retire-new-51-after-retire.jpg)
- Previous head: Chrome opened the retired link: 

  ![retire-r7-52-default-browser.jpg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/86f36bad11592d926802838a23c431c36a0e6e3d/mac-item-6-widget-links/proof-r8/retire-r7-52-default-browser.jpg)
- Recording, new head (app window only): [retire-new-recording.mp4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/86f36bad11592d926802838a23c431c36a0e6e3d/mac-item-6-widget-links/proof-r8/retire-new-recording.mp4)

The app's session list is blacked out in every shot and recording. No tokens appear (the Gateway token lives only in the temp state dir).

## Evidence

- **WebKit consumption probe** (MacBook, macOS 27.2, WKWebView, real HID clicks, dashboard-like parent, proxy-like frame and opaque-origin widget, two widgets). The parent uses this PR's sequence: own activation, proxy activation, then `document.createElement("input").showPicker()`. Results: after one open, the parent, both proxies and both widget frames report `isActive=false`. Two real link clicks about 625 ms apart both opened. A burst from one trusted click (+300 ms, +900 ms, no new gesture) opened once. After an outside click the reuse was still refused because the proxy reported false. A link click in A and then in B about 480 ms later both opened.
- **WebKit focus/activation probe** (round 7): the proxy frame's activation is set only by a click or key inside its own widget. It stays false after parent clicks and keys, after clicks in a sibling widget, and after focus theft.
- **Red/green** (Studio): the new tests against 2031987bfa4 production code: 10 fail. Single-check mutations of this patch: no `isCurrent` recheck 4 fail, no query cancellation 3 fail, no consumption 4 fail, no consumption check 1 fail. Full patch: `widget-bridge` + `widget-sandbox-host` 63/63. Wider UI (`lib/board`, `native-link-routing`, `components/board`, `canvas-widget-view-owner`) 272/272.
- `tsgo:ui` exit 0. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 2031987bfa4`: every check ok (format, lint, UI and core-test typecheck, guards) except the dead export scan (`BrowserGraphicsDevice`, `resolveGatewayRecoverySchemaPaths`), which flags files this PR does not touch and fails the same way on 2031987bfa4 and on main.
- Gaps: middle click (`auxclick`) is unproven in the app, because the harness produced no `auxclick` in the widget (both click kinds share `host.open`). Chromium behavior is from the live proof in #128125 and was not re-run for this head. One browser-mode test file could not start on the test host (Playwright Chromium not installed). The retire app leg uses the timing instrumentation above, and the unit tests cover the retire paths at production timing. Widget link routing to the reading tab or the Gateway browser preference is out of scope: the destination stays the default browser, as for Dashboard `window.open` today.

prs.title: experiment(control-ui): composer controls final at pane mount [do not merge]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes composer controls changing width during a warm reload of a signed-in chat deep link. The campaign's original signed-in dashboard reload passed through 14 visual states before settling around 15 seconds; this experiment targets the remaining composer handoff.

## User Impact

The selected context-window badge and last run action restore with the cached pane. Stop keeps its settled appearance but remains disabled until live permission and target ownership are available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing scoped snapshot retained the model and effort but omitted the selected context-window display inputs. Replacing that incomplete display with live settings inserted a badge and pushed neighboring controls left. The same snapshot now retains those bounded inputs. The session display snapshot also retains the run-action presentation; the live action owner still admits every mutation.

This is an experiment draft pending the required quiet-host proof. Do not merge.

## Evidence

The focused native-browser regression reproduced a 51.5 px model/control/ring movement on the original code and passes with 0 px movement with the candidate. It also covers unchanged labels, cached Stop colors, offline mutation blocking, and legitimate changed live settings. The final local invocation passed in 60.55 seconds including its bundle build (7.615 seconds test time). These are behavioral counts and test costs, not performance timing results.

Acceptance rule, declared before remote measurement: 11 interleaved baseline/candidate pairs plus active-chat A/A on one quiet AWS c7a.4xlarge. Composer movement must be at most 1 px in at least 10/11 candidate pairs. Archived chat and dashboard are secondaries. Report per-pair deltas and median/IQR for hello-handled, FCP, first painted rows, final rows, LoAF blocking, CLS, and snapshot growth. Also run the Team-scale bench with the live-fast latency profile, focused consumers, changed checks, and the full UI e2e suite on the final head.

Remote proof, inspected synthetic before/after captures, production LOC delta, and exact-head CI will be added before marking ready. The browser regression adds exactly 85 test lines, allocated in its own ratchet record because existing snapshot assertions did not exercise first-frame-to-live geometry. Independent local autoreview is required clean through P2 before each substantive commit.

Current requested production diff stat: +86/−9 = +77 lines, including proof tooling, its Markdown guide, and the exact test allocation. UI production files account for +24 net lines (+18 runtime/schema lines and +6 type lines). Growth carries already-loaded display facts through the existing cache rather than adding a store or placeholder width. The old handler-dependent Stop visibility path is removed; the live callback now controls whether the preserved Stop button can execute.

prs.title: fix(plugins): keep adopted tools and hooks on one service owner
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Prepared agent registries can borrow a live Gateway's tool factories while retaining hooks from a different `register()` invocation. A hook that records per-registration state then writes to a different closure from the executor, so valid calls fail despite matching parameters and caller identity.

The selected-tool follow-up also needs to tolerate registrations that exist only in the donor. In particular, a donor containing `[owner_tool, unnamed factory]` must be able to serve a prepared consumer containing only `[owner_tool]`. Rejecting that donor group leaves the selected tool on its discovery instance, where its service has not started.

## User Impact

Stateful, service-backed plugins keep their hooks and selected tools on the admitting Gateway's service instance. Donor-only named or unnamed factories are not exposed to the prepared consumer. Selected unnamed or unmatched registrations still retain their local owner. Retained hook callbacks reject access after either owner retires.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing adoption owner matches every selected registration by identity, multiplicity and declared contract. Source digests, plugin configuration and hook policies must also match. It copies all three hook planes together and binds them to the prepared consumer's lifetime; other provider and capability adoption is unchanged.

The latest repair skips unnamed registrations only while collecting donor identity groups. It preserves the stricter selected-registration check and does not add shared state, a cache, permissions or a fallback.

## Evidence

The donor-only unnamed regression uses the real registrar, `acquireAgentRuntimePluginRegistry`, and an actually started service. The initial run at prior PR head `a73130fce56fc5853db93330c45503694007730e` has 1 failure and 22 passing cases; the affected selected tool throws `service is not started`. This red run preceded a test-only correction to the unused donor factory's returned label/result shape. Registration and grouping do not call that factory, and the failure trace enters only the selected named tool, so the correction does not affect the demonstrated cause. With the final valid fixture and two-file repair, all 23 cases pass, including named and unnamed donor extras, selected-unnamed rejection, contract checks and both owner-retirement paths. The native wrapper and final source verification completed with exit 0.

Final scoped validation passed: 23 owner cases, typed lint for both changed files, relevant core and test type checks, formatting, native commit hooks and the final source verification. The production file did not change during the test-only return-shape correction, so its already-passing core type check was reused.

A fresh canonical Codex review of the final two-file scope completed on the same Windows host with `scoped-clean`, no actionable P0–P2 findings, and successful final source verification. The reviewer assessed the supplied source; the test executions above are separate evidence.

This PR is open for review. Current-candidate Gateway agent-entry proof of allowed storage, forbidden peer-session effects and retained tool-callback retirement is still pending. The owner suite directly tests hook-callback retirement, not every retained tool executor after either owner closes. An isolated Gateway attempt timed out before producing an effect receipt and is not counted as a pass. The owner-suite results above do not claim a complete Gateway/model/channel run, repository-wide suite or hosted CI result.

## Additional published-stable adoption probe — 2026-11-05

An isolated Node probe now exercises the actual OpenClaw **2026.10.10** adoption function, `PluginInstance`, runtime store, and hook runner with per-registration proof state. The baseline selects the donor tool but retains the local hook, so the donor tool returns `accepted: false`. The implementation from exact head **609d86a8183bc905788d8fd9f7cb6379c274f785**, substituted only into the adoption module for this process, returns `accepted: true`. Hooks reject calls after either the local or donor instance retires; the baseline fails to reject after donor retirement. All three candidate scenarios pass.

The probe exposes the existing private adoption function for testing and initializes the runtime store under each real instance. It does not start the real service manager, registrar/discovery loader, or Gateway. This supplements the historical 23-case owner suite and does not close the Gateway agent-entry, storage-effect, or retained tool-executor acceptance gaps described above. A newer-main Vitest attempt produced no case report and is not counted as a pass. Marked ready for review at the author's request; the acceptance gaps remain open.

prs.title: fix(agents): stop provider fallback for unavailable transcript projections
prs.body:
Related: #153976.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes provider fallback attempts and failure attribution when a local session transcript projection is rebuilding.

## User Impact

The original storage error stops the turn without consuming another configured provider candidate. There is no configuration or stored-data change. This does not wait for rebuilding, retry the user's message, or improve rebuild speed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add the existing projection exception to the existing runtime-coordination classification. That owner already stops fallback for local failures, including errors preserved through provider-looking wrappers. The change leaves failure wording, visibility and recovery ownership in place.

The hydration recovery proposed in #164843 addresses a separate wait/retry boundary. This change only prevents a storage error that reaches fallback from being treated as a provider failure.

## Evidence

A direct Node 26.5.0 probe calls the real `runWithModelFallback` owner with two synthetic candidates and the actual storage exception, in isolated state with no provider transport. On both unpatched main `38c85c2fe23` and the real published OpenClaw 2026.10.5 package, the direct exception and a provider-looking `503` wrapper execute two candidates and report a provider failure. With this fix, each executes once, reports no provider failure or fallback step, and preserves the identical original error. The wrapper previously lost that error in aggregate fallback failure.

No live provider request or production transcript is used or claimed. No new state, policy, configuration, retry owner or recovery path was added; the production delta is one error-classification entry. No Gateway or channel E2E acceptance is claimed.

## Additional current-stable owner probe — 2026-11-05

Repeated against the actual published OpenClaw **2026.10.10** fallback runner in isolated state. The direct `SessionTranscriptProjectionUnavailableError` and the same exception wrapped by a provider-looking 503 error each execute **two candidates before the fix**, and **one candidate after it**, propagating the identical original error. An ordinary provider 503 still executes the backup candidate, and the existing `ActiveTurnClaimError` still stops after one.

The candidate probe loads the same single classification-name addition through a process-local module load hook; the installed package on disk remains unchanged. All four candidate scenarios pass. An initial probe used an incorrect shortened exception name and failed; that probe was corrected against the actual public diff before the passing run. prs.title: fix(gateway): keep systemd service recoverable when state is busy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a systemd Gateway starts on state that needs migration while another OpenClaw process holds that state, startup exits `78`. `RestartPreventExitStatus=78` then leaves the Gateway down until someone runs `openclaw gateway start`. A short-lived CLI or Doctor run during the first start after a package swap is enough to take the service down.

Seen once in a fleet lane, then reproduced deterministically below.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareSystemdGatewayActivation` wraps every failure as `StartupMaintenanceRequiredError`, including `GatewayStateOwnerContentionError` from Doctor's maintenance admission. That catch exists so a failed repair does not loop under `Restart=always`, but contention means the repair never ran and nothing is wrong with the state.

Two repair paths also reduced `SQLITE_BUSY` to warning text, so a blocked migration could not be told apart from a failed one.

Activation treats state contention as transient:

- Maintenance admission uses Doctor's existing wait for a recorded holder, with progress logging, and retries unidentified holders for the Gateway's existing five-minute lifecycle budget.
- If contention persists, or a repair is blocked by an SQLite lock, startup exits `1` so `Restart=always` retries. Five-minute waits keep it under the unit's `StartLimitBurst=10` in 300 s; a blocked repair repeats at most within that limit.
- Schema repair results now carry `failure`, so `doctor-schema-migrations` keeps the cause and activation can classify a blocked repair.

Genuine repair failures and `data-at-risk` refusals still exit `78`. `RestartPreventExitStatus=78` is unchanged: it protects low-resource hosts from config restart storms.

Activation only runs on Linux under systemd; launchd and Windows have no equivalent path.

## User Impact

User impact: a first start after a package swap survives a concurrent `openclaw` command, instead of leaving a `failed` unit that needs a manual start.

Accepted edge cases:

- A recorded holder can hold startup for up to Doctor's 20-minute wait. Progress is logged and starts do not count against the limit.
- A legacy pre-v17 agent database blocked by an SQLite lock during its legacy media upgrade still parks with `78`, because that owner reports only warning text. It needs a very old database plus a lock at that moment, and `openclaw doctor --fix` recovers it.

## Evidence

Regression tests in `src/cli/gateway-cli/systemd-activation.test.ts` fail on base (`expected 78 to be 1`) and pass with the fix. They cover waiting then entering maintenance, persistent contention past the budget, a blocked repair, a blocked full repair, a failed repair, and contention behind a data-at-risk refusal.

Native proof on Crabbox AWS Linux: published 2026.10.10 systemd install and state, `ExecStart` pointed at the build, and a separate real process holding Gateway state ownership.

| Build | Holder | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Base `49f8a60f227` | `sqlite-maintenance`, 40 s | Unit `failed` in 2 s, `status=78/CONFIG`, stays down after the holder releases |
| Fix `35ac0e33478` | `sqlite-maintenance`, 40 s | Waits 39 s, healthy at 46 s, 0 restarts |
| Fix `35ac0e33478` | `gateway`, 330 s | `status=1` at about 300 s, restarts, healthy at 340 s, 1 restart |
| Fix `35ac0e33478` | Released before start | Healthy at 7 s |

Gaps: the native runs predate the final commit, which only adds the blocked full-repair rethrow, so that and the blocked-repair path are proven by tests only. A reader holding a read transaction did not block migration in this snapshot on base or fix. The holder is a proof-only script calling the shipped `acquireGatewayLock`, not a stock CLI command.

`$autoreview` is scoped-clean. Independent Codex review found three issues: the scoped repair cause (fixed), the full-repair cause (fixed), and the legacy media path (declined above as an accepted edge case). It also flagged the 20-minute wait, which is deliberate.

prs.title: fix(plugins): record inference ownership for service-created cron jobs
prs.body:
Fixes #192327

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway-hosted plugin service that creates an agent-turn job with `ctx.getCron().add(input)` records no inference account, so every run is refused before the model:

```text
Automation has no recorded inference account. Explicitly select its account with a model@profile update before running it.
```

The Gateway's own `cron.add` method captures one for its callers (`captureCronCreatorSession` → `captureCronInferenceForCaller`); the plugin service handle forwarded none (`src/plugins/service-cron.ts` called `cron.add(normalized, { commitGuard })`).

## Why This Change Was Made

The service handle gains a creation-time capture callback, supplied by the host that owns the config:

- `service-cron.ts`: `add()` awaits `captureInference(normalized)` and forwards the result into `cron.add(normalized, { commitGuard, ...binding })`, after a lifecycle re-check.
- `service-automation-capabilities.ts`: passes the callback through.
- `services.ts`: resolves the binding with the existing owner, `captureCronInferenceBinding({ cfg, agentId, model })`, for `agentTurn` jobs whose `sessionTarget` is not `main` — the same eligibility the Gateway applies. The capture is best-effort: an unresolvable account logs a warning and leaves the job unbound, preserving the pre-change behavior instead of failing plugin creates.

## Evidence

Regression (`src/plugins/services.cron-inference.test.ts`) creates a stored-account agent turn through the real service handle and reads the recorded binding back.

Red on the base (the three capture files reverted to `HEAD~1`, test unchanged):

```text
AssertionError: expected undefined to match object { Object (version, provider, ...) }
Tests  1 failed (1)
```

Green on this head:

```text
✓ src/plugins/services.cron-inference.test.ts > records the inference account for a service-created agent turn
Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Existing plugin-cron coverage stays green (`src/plugins/services.cron.test.ts`, 5 passed). Test lines are covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/plugin-cron-inference-binding.txt`; `check:test-lines-ratchet` reports `slack: 80`.

Note: the unit test needs `--pool=forks` because shared-state admission is host-thread only (`npm test` projects select their pool; this does not change production behavior).

prs.title: fix: tool_call rejects quoted numbers and booleans that direct calls accept
prs.body:
Related: #166133

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a deferred tool call fails with `limit: expected integer; received "3" (string)` when the model quotes a number or boolean inside `tool_call` args, even though the same quoted value works when that tool is called directly.

## User Impact

User impact: models that quote scalars inside `tool_call` args now reach the tool instead of failing the call. One #166133 reporter logged this with MiniMax on `web_fetch`, `exec` and plugin tools. Numbers and booleans that were already typed correctly behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Direct tool calls go through `validateToolArguments` in the agent loop, which coerces `"3"` to `3` and `"true"` to `true` against the tool's schema. `tool_call` declares its nested `args` as `Record<string, Unknown>`, so that same step only sees an opaque object and never coerces the fields inside. The catalog validator then rejects them with no coercion step of its own. The nested args also give the model no type to anchor on, which is probably why quoting shows up here specifically.

This runs the existing coercion for `tool_call` targets too, before the `before_tool_call` hook and before catalog validation. If coercion can't satisfy the schema, the original input goes on to the catalog validator, so the error text from #172453 doesn't change.

A few choices worth checking:

- Only the `tool_call` control opts in. Code Mode and other `runtime.call` users stay strict, because guests there get typed signatures, and the #172453 test that pins `"10"` as rejected on `runtime.call` still passes untouched. #172453 said strict rejection stays, and that was about its diagnostics scope, so I'd rather you weigh in on this than assume. If you want strictness on `tool_call` too, this is easy to close.
- It reuses the direct-path rules on purpose rather than adding a narrower set, so `tool_call` now matches them exactly. That includes the odd ones: `null` and `false` become `0` for a numeric field unless the schema rejects `0`.
- #172329 fixed this for one tool's limits (`maxFires` on standing intents). This covers the rest of `tool_call`. I left that normalization alone.

I used `Related` rather than `Closes` because #166133 also reports MCP servers receiving strings. This coerces MCP targets called through `tool_call` as well, but nobody has shown whether every report there has this cause.

## Evidence

Reproduced on main at 5bb4dfda334 through the real `Agent` loop, with a scripted model emitting `{ limit: "3", recursive: "true" }` for a tool with `integer` and `boolean` fields:

| route | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| direct tool call | tool runs with `{"limit":3,"recursive":true}` | unchanged |
| `tool_call` | tool never runs | tool runs with `{"limit":3,"recursive":true}` |

- The new test in `tool-search.agent-loop.test.ts` fails on main (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times`) and passes here.
- Passing: `tool-search.agent-loop`, `tool-search`, `tool-search-runtime` (plus `.output-variants` and `.refusal`), `tool-search.mcp-error`, `tool-search.discovery`, `tool-search.metadata`, `code-mode.mcp`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean.

This adds 18 net test lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/tool-call-quoted-scalars.txt`. I kept the test because this was a silent mismatch between two routes in a shared entry point, and it runs through the real agent loop so it checks what the tool actually receives.

Not run: a live MiniMax turn, since I don't have those credentials. The scripted model stands in for the provider, so this proves what happens once quoted values arrive, not why a given provider quotes them. @miluo-star's transcript on #166133 shows the same call succeeding unquoted and failing quoted, but it isn't the raw provider capture steipete asked for. The test typecheck lane (`tsgo:core:test`) wasn't run locally either, and I didn't measure the new test's `--maxWorkers=1` wall time or CI seconds. The second commit (replacing a cast with a type guard, plus the allocation record) wasn't re-tested locally because this machine is low on disk, so CI is the check on that one.

---
I'm a college freshman and I worked on this with Claude Code. I read the code paths, ran the repro and checked the results myself, but tell me if I missed something about why this is strict.

Update helper processes load recovery, post-core and Doctor code even when their selected mode does not need it. This candidate narrows that eager work without changing the update protocol.

## Evidence

Before first measurement: existing worker tests 33/33 and diagnostic tests 2/2 pass on pinned Bun. Two isolated Codex reviews are scoped-clean (P0–P2). Compiled candidate build passed. Typed lint preparation is currently blocked by the mandated external virtual-store path failing the existing declaration containment rule; no bypass used. prs.title: fix: keep ambient chatter from evicting user requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #182176. Follow-up to #187833: optional room events must not evict or delay explicit user requests when the follow-up queue reaches capacity.

## User Impact

Requests retain their place ahead of optional room events. Under the default `summarize` policy, overflow ambient text is compacted into bounded background context on an eligible pending turn, rather than always discarded or replayed as extra turns. Explicit `old` and `new` policies still discard ambient overflow without previews.

## Behavior and limits

- Shed optional ambient work first, preserving survivor FIFO. Active turns, protected recovery work, and required replies are not ambient eviction candidates.
- A pending recipient in the same channel, account, room, thread, and Gateway retains the newest `min(cap, 20)` previews, ordered by mailbox arrival. Each message body is capped at 160 characters; sender and message ID fields at 80 each.
- Previews are conversation data, not instructions or sender authority. Approved input text wins over raw text. If an input write hook has not approved the body, retain an omission notice instead of bypassing that hook.
- Context attaches once, survives preparation retries without duplicate growth, and never creates another runnable queue or independent replay turn. It expires with its recipient; no eligible recipient means no preview. Recipient cancellation or discard may lose the context. This is bounded, best-effort preservation—not lossless history.
- Source custody still settles as intentional non-delivery without opening execution delivery scopes. QA-channel's existing disposition callback releases its receipt; active delivery tracking stays intact. Discard logs include `contextPreserved` without message content.
- Channel history retention and request-versus-request overflow remain unchanged. No new configuration or storage.

## Evidence

- Added preservation assertions fail on published head `6275c329bf19`: ambient overflow has no context under `summarize`.
- Revised candidate: **119 focused tests pass** across overflow context, collection, pending inputs, and steering (four files, two Vitest shards, 65.14s wall time). Covers cross-sender attribution without authority transfer, thread/account/Gateway isolation, approved versus unstaged content, preview truncation/count limits, retry nonduplication, cancellation expiry, request priority, and existing receipt/delivery regressions.
- Core and messaging-test typechecks, touched-file type-aware lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, line-cap ratchet, and staged test-line ratchet pass.
- Fresh independent static review of the revised candidate found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Local ClawSweeper completed a full read-only review of `65181e714709..06a8405bf219` (high reasoning effort), finding no actionable correctness or security issues; no review findings remain. It did not execute tests or mutate GitHub.
- Live Telegram/channel proof remains **unverified**. The earlier isolated Gateway attempt could not classify ambient QA-channel inputs. These queue-boundary tests are not presented as live channel evidence.
- Previous-head CI failure was attributed to inherited test-budget debt: exact CI merge `2241d0d4d086` was 8 lines over its ceiling, and unchanged base `232327e0239a` was already 8 over. The PR allocated its own complete test growth. Revised-head CI must be assessed separately.

## Scope and review

The revised design replaces unconditional default-policy content loss with context owned by an existing pending turn. `pr-simplify` avoided a mailbox-wide buffer, cleanup state machine, new configuration, and independent replay work. Compared with the original merge base: production +172 net lines, tests +191, docs +28. The dedicated allocation covers exactly the PR's 191 net test lines; the shared scalar is unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

Tool Search still allocates a temporary `Object.values()` array for every decoded object while freezing a tool result. Cron's headless Code Mode calls take this path even though those arrays are immediately discarded.

## User Impact

A small reduction in allocation while processing object-heavy tool results. Tool Search results, cron outcomes, JSON normalization, schema checks, detached immutable snapshots, and internal result metadata remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enumerate each decoded object's own keys directly while keeping the existing array iteration path. The full JSON snapshot remains necessary: it normalizes values before output validation and isolates data across delayed consumers. Snapshot reuse from #135220 and array traversal from #186935 are already present in the evidence build; this addresses their residual object traversal cost.

Production LOC: +9. The separate array/object loops preserve the existing fast array traversal and own-property semantics while removing the per-object temporary array. No cache, new configuration, schema change, or caller branch is introduced.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: identical result bytes and immutability, zero object-value scratch-array slots per cron result, a repeatable allocation or CPU improvement without a material adverse owner result. Separate untraced timing and collected-inclusive allocation passes, 2,000 snapshots per arm, counterbalanced order. Five pairs for 400 synthetic file descriptions, two pairs for each array-heavy, large-text, and small-result control. Host load is reported as context; CPU measurements use `process.threadCpuUsage()`.

Reproduction: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/trigger-script.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'snapshots a cron tool result'` fails on the original owner with **80 temporary array slots instead of 0**, after the cron result assertion succeeds. |---|---:|---:|---:|
| files | 5 × 2,000 | 607,637.43 → 577,981.97 (-4.88%) | 356.76 → 356.16 (-0.17%) |
| table | 2 × 2,000 | 455,020.61 → 455,659.92 (+0.14%) | 477.14 → 475.38 (-0.37%) |

Host one-minute load ranged from 88.1 to 133.9. Figures are arithmetic means; all five file-workload allocation pairs improved. Final focused command wall time: 363.14 s, dominated by worker preparation and transforms; the new test itself took 297 ms. Local proof preceded a conflict-free rebase onto `3816bcb3dea1`; the snapshot, runtime, JSON conversion, MCP metadata and cron owner/test files were unchanged between those bases. Pushed head: `1c859922691737d16b5ee13d1d6786b90f387b5a`. [Exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41972226072) completed: build, production/test types, lint, source/architecture/prompt checks, security, and selected tests passed. The only substantive failure is `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (and its aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`), caused by inherited test-line debt. prs.title: fix(ui): catalog dashboard e2e stalls in reconnect on loaded runners
prs.body:
Related: openclaw/openclaw#190824 (CI run 41404623180, job `checks-ui-e2e` 6/7, failed on an unrelated head)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI model catalog dashboard e2e test (`ui/src/e2e/model-catalog-dashboard.e2e.test.ts`) intermittently times out in its `reconnect` step on loaded CI runners, with the UI stuck in `reconnecting`, failing unrelated PRs.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The test no longer flakes in its reconnect step, so unrelated PRs stop failing `checks-ui-e2e` on it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The compact replay pauses Playwright's virtual clock and drives each action by polling `page.clock.runFor(50)` inside a 15 s real-time `expect.poll` budget. The `reconnect` step calls `reconnectMockGateway`, whose offline → new socket attempt → online → connected transitions are awaited in real time with `page.waitForFunction`. That couples two clocks:

- The step needs about 1 s of virtual time, the transport's first reconnect delay (800–960 ms), so about 20 polls. When polls are slow, the 15 s budget runs out first and the UI is left in `reconnecting`, which is the CI signature.
- When polls are fast and the host lags, virtual time passes the browser socket's 30 s opening deadline. The offline attempt closes and backoff grows (observed: a second attempt after a 1.4–1.6 s backoff).

The reconnect step now runs with the clock ticking, the way boot already does, then pauses it again. That matches the other suites, which call `page.clock.resume()` before `reconnectMockGateway`. The helper now documents that it expects a ticking clock. Assertions, timeouts, and row attribution are unchanged; the reconnect row still waits for its post-reconnect catalog read.

## Evidence

- **Mechanism, instrumented locally:** a probe logged virtual time, socket states and `connect` counts on every poll.
  - Normal run: the new socket appears after ~0.9–1.0 s virtual (~20 polls). The offline socket stays CONNECTING (the mock never fails it), so backoff does not grow in normal timing.
  - Host held 30 s before `setOnline(true)`: the offline socket closed at ~31 s virtual, and the next attempt came after the grown backoff.
  - No local timing reproduced the CI failure unthrottled: 6 parallel copies, 6× page CPU throttle, and 8 s host lag all passed.
- **Throttled variant (900 ms real host delay per virtual-time poll), same harness applied to both:**
  - base `0809cf31e693`: 2/2 failed at `reconnect` with `expected false to deeply equal true`, readiness `{gatewayPhase: "reconnecting", rosterReady: false, ready: true}` (identical to the CI dump).
  - this branch: 2/2 passed all 24 rows.
- **Bounded loop, 20 runs each of base and this branch, unthrottled, two parallel workers on a host at load average 110–143:**
  - base: 19/20. The failure was organic: it stopped at `reconnect` with the CI signature above, after the 15 s poll budget.
  - this branch: 20/20.
- **Checks:** `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` clean on the changed files. The local oxlint wrapper timed out preparing plugin-sdk boundary types under host load; CI lint covers it.
- **Review:** Codex autoreview (local diff vs `0809cf31e693`, P0–P1): scoped-clean, no findings.

Gap: the CI failure dump has no transport state, so which of the two modes the CI runner hit is not proven. The fix removes the coupling behind both.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Filtered Knowledge searches repeatedly scan the complete keyword corpus while preparing their ranking subset.

## User Impact

Filtered keyword searches use less CPU while preserving the same results, ranking, snippets, pagination and scope checks. No schema, index, stored-data or configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The FTS record ID is unindexed. Copying each selected row with `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE id=?` therefore scans the corpus once per selected record. Search already holds the validated records used to reconcile that exact corpus. Populate the temporary FTS table from those same values and retain the subset-specific BM25 calculation.

## Evidence

Acceptance: identical result digests (excluding query/index timestamps), eliminated persistent-corpus reads, lower owner CPU and no demonstrated adverse allocation/GC result. Synthetic fixture: 5,000 valid pages with approximately 1 KiB bodies, 100 selected by tag. This is an explicit size assumption, not a measured production row count.

The regression counts SQLite read authorizations on the persistent FTS corpus: 13 on the baseline, zero with this change. All 18 retrieval tests pass, including scope isolation, invalid/duplicate exclusion, withdrawals, edits and projection rebuilds. The test file took 497 seconds wall time on the loaded host (most time was worker preparation); the added regression took 0.66 seconds. Its 42 net test lines are recorded in a dedicated allocation file.

Production LOC delta: **0** (three lines replaced). The temporary corpus remains necessary for the existing subset-specific BM25 contract; no parallel implementation or cache was added.

Formatting, targeted lint, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, the final strict scripts leaf, and the export-name collision guard passed. Both closure guard files passed (40 tests, 558 seconds wall time on the loaded host). Exact-head CI is pending.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable), P0–P2: no actionable findings. Autoreview refused the requested provider because it did not match the operator configuration; the configured route was not changed. The isolated reviewer received only the diff and relevant source/docs. No Gateway load test was run: this is a deletion of redundant reads within the same synchronous search owner, with no scheduling, authority, transaction or storage changes.


Five alternating untraced pairs, 200 searches per arm (1,000 per revision), on the synthetic 5,000-record/100-selected fixture:

| Owner metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Process CPU / search | 301.52 ms | 5.71 ms (−98.1%) |
| Wall time / search | 941.31 ms | 22.43 ms |
| Total GC / search | 0.687 ms | 0.747 ms (+0.061 ms) |
| Endpoint RSS, mean | 288.09 MiB | 322.67 MiB |
| Endpoint heap used, mean | 83.96 MiB | 65.81 MiB |
| Sampled JS allocation / search, first 500-call pair | 5.520 MiB | 5.462 MiB |

The first sampled allocation pair is separate from the timing runs; collected objects are included, native SQLite allocations are excluded. A second 500-call pair and four identical-candidate A/A controls are still running and will be added before handoff. RSS is reported as measured: it rose 34.59 MiB at the endpoint while heap use fell 18.14 MiB; this is not a retained-memory claim. Host one-minute load ranged 98–131 during the timing starts.

All completed arms share result digest `36ba8ab6b673405f0cf869ea4227e7bd67785542ea5a159ad14311b192a7a40f` (only query/index timestamps omitted). The GC absolute mean increase is below 1 ms/operation; individual max-pause excursions require the pending identical-build controls before an adverse conclusion. Baseline/candidate maxima by timing pair: 249.66/20.93, 42.44/53.72, 4.21/108.68, 54.72/124.59, 4.53/18.38 ms. Each timing arm recorded 14 minor collections and no major collections.

Reproduce with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/knowledge-filtered-search.ts --iterations 200`; use `--source .local/retrieval-baseline.ts` for the baseline owner snapshot and `--sample --iterations 500` for separate allocation passes. The script header documents the fixture and scope. Measurements began on `11c8f236b330e8f51c03331dcd6ae0c661080e7b`; the reviewed patch is byte-equivalent after rebase onto `4a6ca3afd549af75ab68636d4b8a62ae3c16cbfa`, and the baseline search owner is unchanged there.

## What Problem This Solves

Normal embedded-web picker/keyboard and credential-retirement proof, baseline reproduction, and inspected before/after captures remain outstanding.**

The native picker and Gateway app-menu shortcuts previously called the generic Gateway open action, which correctly reuses a window belonging to the destination Gateway but cannot switch the originating window. Inactive Gateway content stays owned by that window until it closes or the Gateway's ownership is retired.
