prs.title: fix: allow large Linux host builds to use the shared memory allowance
prs.body:
Closes #191975

## What Problem This Solves

Large Linux host builds are killed at a per-command quarter-RAM limit despite unused capacity, while concurrent commands each receive a separate allowance.

## User Impact

Foreground, PTY, background, and durable host commands can use the unused shared RAM/swap allowance automatically, with reserves for the host and Gateway. No new configuration is required. Existing execution policy, service hierarchy, and I/O isolation remain in effect.

Sampling can overshoot and shared pages can be overcounted. Cache-heavy commands can slow under kernel reclaim; ordinary cache protection requires writable delegation. Separate Gateways retain separate budgets.

**Validation status:** the exact-head public Gateway build passed above the former cutoff on Ubuntu 24.04 with the 6.8 AWS kernel. Standard review, focused checks, build-artifacts, repaired agents-core-tools, and dependencies passed. Bounded CI attribution completed 20 full-file invocations on quiet AWS: all 10 candidate invocations passed; exact base reproduced the extra CLI-launch signature. Broad CI completed with 234 passing, 17 failed (16 lanes plus the aggregate gate), 1 cancelled, and 11 skipped jobs; iOS tests passed. The cancelled QA shard exhausted its two-hour outer budget during active Bun progress. Remaining failures and proof limits are recorded below. No merge, release, or deployment is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

One sampler accounts for combined RAM and swap, includes inherited cgroup limits, and cancels one large contributor through its existing cleanup owner. Ordinary commands remain inside their delegated hierarchy and receive a full-budget soft cache limit. Durable units join sampled accounting and retain individual hard RAM/swap backstops across restart/adoption. Commands are never automatically replayed.

Memory-limit failures remain eligible for notification after durable recovery; only an explicit manual stop suppresses that notification. A crash before persistence can still recover the system manager's observed exit instead of the exact cancellation reason.

The smallest coherent stage is one shared budget across ordinary and durable callers. Superseded per-command memory arguments/watch exports and caller plumbing are removed; existing owners retain cancellation, cleanup, persistence, and I/O sizing. Production grows by 331 lines; tests/support by 451 lines for inherited capacity, aggregate RAM/swap, durable recovery, and distinct lifecycle regressions. No schema, public config, hierarchy relocation, or dependency change.

## Evidence

- The [real Gateway build](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_167b4f32efd60d53a5486c1fa1a0194c) passed on quiet AWS Crabbox `cbx_af642c4488d7`: Ubuntu 24.04, actual `6.8.0-1067-aws`, four CPUs, and a 20 GiB service RAM / 6 GiB swap envelope. A real model generated one approved foreground `pnpm build` with ordinary defaults in an independent cold checkout. Its original exec owner returned exit 0 in **380.5 seconds**. Build-tree RSS reached **7.28 GiB**, including one compiler at **6.27 GiB**, above the former **5 GiB** cutoff and within the **13.66 GiB** shared allowance. No command was replayed.
- The compiler's exact PID/starttime remained active during public cancellation of a concurrent 64 MiB peer. Committed abort and physical extinction settled within **0.392 seconds**. All **9,780** health/readiness/session-write requests succeeded; session-write p95/max were 20.1/431.3 ms, and independent readback matched the final acknowledged write. Across 3,934 process samples and 1,523 kernel samples, no sampled budget violations or read/listener/max/OOM errors occurred; aggregate/session I/O policy stayed unchanged. All 195 recorded process incarnations exited; service, cgroup, port, task swap, and owned AWS lease cleanup were verified.
- Both independent checkouts stayed at `a12314606f5e93cb0ec34510155d8cfcfada9d73`, with all 63,492 tracked source hashes identical before/after. All 26,293 prepared runtime-dist entries remained unchanged; the cold build produced 26,684 independent dist entries including the runtime entry. An independent receipt audit confirmed these outcomes. **Limits:** no swap, parallel JavaScript build workers, or native reclaim stack was observed. This run does not qualify parallel-worker contention, natural reclaim, performance parity, or an iOS compiler. The observer used 18.9 MiB peak RSS and 103.3 CPU-seconds over 393.2 seconds on four CPUs (about 6.6% of total CPU capacity); these are measurement overhead, not product sampler cost. Maximum polling gap was 139.5 ms.
- The [PTY cached-budget diagnostic](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_e308a1a87515dc1aafb98a1860e9d424) confirmed a test-composition defect exposed by Node CI: an earlier shared-worker consumer could cache the real budget before the scaled fixture. The diagnostic matched the timeout signature; assigning the unchanged suite to the existing isolated owner passed all six cases under Node and pinned Bun. The [routing consumer/lint check](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_93e70ea2850ecd34c9f3e794ccd2651c) passed all 22 existing config tests and lint; format, diff and test-line gates also passed. This final one-line repair changes no production code or assertions.
- [Current-head broad CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41940301325) verifies exact candidate `a12314606f5e93cb0ec34510155d8cfcfada9d73` and base `2dbd7f79bbf1fc49b38049429cb9e55b5437f0be`, with distinct trusted harness `4129e21215e7a6963bf34dc4bf2aad28b1543b95`. Build-artifacts, types/lint, repaired agents-core-tools, and dependencies passed. The run completed with failure: **234 passed, 17 failed, 1 cancelled, 11 skipped**, with no active jobs. The 17 failures comprise the 16 inspected lanes and the final aggregate gate, whose log only propagates selected-lane failures. iOS tests passed. Private-QA shard 17 exceeded its two-hour job limit; its Node half passed 873 tests and its Bun half was still passing cases 3.5 seconds before cancellation. Incomplete Bun coverage and the cause of the long total runtime remain unresolved. All current failed job logs were inspected. No CI redispatch or rerun was used to chase green.
- The [bounded CI attribution campaign](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_f6b79dc3a25ed705fba637349e15d4f1) ran complete failing files once per selected runtime on quiet AWS Crabbox `cbx_0b1182459499` (Ubuntu 24.04, four observed CPUs, about 32 GiB RAM, Node 24.22.1, pinned Bun). Independent exact-base/candidate frozen installs and original assertions/deadlines were used. **All 10 candidate invocations passed.** Exact base passed nine and reproduced the CI extra CLI launch after credential revocation (9 vs 8 at `server.chat-cli-auth.test.ts:364`). The preceding 502/ok:false assertion passed; the later provider-request-count assertion did not execute, so unauthorized provider access is unproved. This establishes inherited presence, not a candidate repair. Gateway creation, hooks (Node/Bun), approval forwarding, reload continuations, CLI resume, native runtime selection, auth timers, and isolated completion passed their paired replays. No candidate-only defect was demonstrated, and no source or test assertion was changed. **Limit:** these replays do not reproduce full-shard predecessor/concurrency state; the original failures remain unresolved where not independently attributed. The 36,178-byte evidence archive matched the guest SHA256 `d0be2c652186915f096f3b36a55d7da0d7e5c83a9aea372d13a86b25a8195d8c`; all 20 command source-cleanliness checks passed.
- The [earlier fitting Gateway acceptance](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_5a46371e6780ac992e1ef0ea9affd5b6) passed with a real model, 9.62 GiB allocation, one scoped 1 GiB reclaim, full byte/hash readback in 33.15 seconds, actual swap-in faults, public abort, acknowledged writes, controlled restart persistence, and physical cleanup. All 1,896 public probes succeeded. This was controlled-reclaim fitting-workload evidence on the 6.17 kernel, not natural-pressure or performance-parity proof. A separate pinned-Bun small-command smoke passed; Bun did not repeat heavy pressure.
- [Affected-contract validation](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_b98699babb6c56e3d858f6540cd4fa15) passed 99 tests, targeted checks, a full build and CLI smoke. [Pending-write tests](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_35ab5eab9a664e9fa275b40862f4130c) proved cancellation and authority revocation prevent late launch with intended negative controls. [Durable restart/adoption](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_5307a201580a8ddba870a121221a5b66) retained one native start/handle, canceled one aggregate-budget victim and let its sibling complete without replay. The recovered-notification regression has intended [red](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_f658a09564290ca307489a07bb834044) and [green/full-build](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_4adb3546763294d9d4d13d3883348e1e) proof.
- Standard shared Codex review of the full committed repaired range returned scoped-clean with no P0–P2 findings. The final one-line owner change received another clean selected-helper review; direct inspection covered the owner/config/classifier consumers outside that narrow review sandbox. Reviewers did not run tests. Simplification retained the shared owner and existing lifecycle mechanisms, with no new production mechanism in the subsequent CI repairs.

<details>
<summary>Preserved failures, source bindings, and remaining limits</summary>


Current CI failure attribution (source identity alone is not runtime inheritance):

| Failed job | Finding / proof limit |
| --- | --- |
| Locale | Same catalog fallback drift runtime-reproduced on clean exact base; prior receipts reused. |
| UI E2E 4/6/7/10 | Unchanged label/password-control, retired Secrets markup, copy/gutter, and capitalization expectations; no exact-base browser replay. |
| Real-Gateway UI | Device summary has two actual matches; existing-key Set vs Replace action mismatch is source-supported. Prefix-input poll remains unresolved. |
| UI 3 | Bun-only introduced-read counter 0 vs 1 in a mocked-Gateway fixture; actual counter location omitted; unresolved. |
| Release-packed 18 | Real Gateway captured-creating-reference rejection during setup, not a package-content assertion. Full-file Node base/candidate pass; original shard failure unresolved. |
| CLI-process 7 | Three Doctor advisory exit-124 results within the fixture subprocess budget. All 11 cases pass on Node base/candidate; original shard failure unresolved. |
| Core-tooling 11 | Direct spawnSync copied-Node status null; missing error/signal metadata. All 3 cases pass on Node base/candidate; original failure unresolved. |
| HTTP-plugin-WS | Deferred hooks event missing during polling and reload wrapper outer deadline. Full files pass in affected runtimes on base/candidate; original shard failures unresolved. All three nested reload scenarios complete, including failed-reload cleanup. |
| Agent runtime | Mocked locked-quota output-rejected vs runtime-unavailable; deadline causality unproved. All 47 cases pass on Bun base/candidate; original failure unresolved. |
| Runtime-state | Approval false-vs-true; shifted frame cannot identify which boolean. Full-file Bun base/candidate pass; original failure unresolved. |
| Isolated-server 5 | Exact-base reproduction of extra CLI launch 9 vs 8; candidate 4/4 pass. Underlying cause/security impact unresolved. |
| Private-QA 26 | Successful mocked auth leaves fake-timer count 1 vs 0; timer identity unknown. All 39 cases pass on Node base/candidate; original failure unresolved. |
| macOS Swift | Full native artifact identifies interrupted-download represented URL /archive.bin vs actual WebKit /article at DashboardNativeBrowserTests.swift:753. Rollback vs queued projection ordering unresolved; unchanged native owners, no Gateway/Node/host-exec path; no base native replay. |
| Private-QA 17 (cancelled) | GitHub explicitly reports the two-hour job limit. Node completed 62 passing files/873 passing tests (2 skipped); the subsequent Bun half continued passing cases until cancellation. No reported assertion or memory-budget failure. Outer budget exhaustion is proved; inherited timing/performance parity and unfinished Bun cases are not. |
| Final aggregate CI gate | Propagates the previously inspected selected-lane failures; no new product test or failure signature. |

The attribution setup first failed before tests because the copied Git seed lacked a base blob. Preserved failure evidence was followed by supported exact-SHA fetches into empty independent repositories and frozen installs; source and assertions were unchanged. No product verdict is assigned to that setup failure.

The first [real-build prelaunch attempt](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_8d1365f9b9e13bf203002039a4f12743) failed because the harness required explicit optional `background:false`; `awaitResults:true` already disables backgrounding. Zero approvals were released, all native workload PID counts stayed zero, and build dist remained empty. The failed results, Gateway state and manifest were preserved. Only that documented-default comparison was corrected before fresh isolated state continued the unexecuted workload. Explicit true/null and all other differing/unknown arguments still fail. Source, resources, deadlines and ordinary build concurrency stayed fixed. The actual build ran once.

Earlier over-budget pressure attempts remain failed evidence. The [earlier Gateway pressure attempt](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_836a330eff24b9d0ef9334b0a5ec8a9a) did not reach abort or full readback; it is not relabeled by the later successes. The [direct native proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ecd6272329b61b91449fe987c00a8d12) qualified discrete exact reclaim witnesses during a long nonblocking write and verified all original payload; it does not establish continuous reclaim or public Gateway behavior during it. An original native qualification missed full-readback bounds and remains failed. The storage comparison stopped at a baseline OOM after four candidate successes, so it does not establish performance parity. Earlier paired older-kernel work did not overlap reclaim and flagged latency changes.

Current head has 27 changed files. Earlier fitting evidence binds `a4889ff` through source manifest SHA256 `596d005019baa631725e261d9095bcd19820a47bb03cc0528b63a0ceb1937780`; production bytes are unchanged by the final test-routing commit. The exact-head real-build harness manifest is `71371a8b4654bb0539a4b51f16abb9415041e0e46468b9eb70009a87adf74f3d`; the failed prelaunch manifest/evidence remain separate. Export hashes for all 107 final evidence files were verified.

Separate test-line records retain the 304-line shared-owner grant and add exactly 85 lines for pending-write cancellation/authority regression coverage and necessary fixture corrections. The shared scalar is unchanged. Subsequent fixture/getter repairs and the isolated-owner assignment fit the existing ceiling, with one counted line of slack.

No latest-stable upgrade, iOS/macOS compiler, latency-parity, saturated-I/O-throughput, or zero-regression claim. No release, deployment, or production-service change.

prs.title: fix(gateway): report retryable session work-start conflicts from OpenAI-compatible endpoints
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `/v1/responses` and the other OpenAI-compatible endpoints report `SessionWorkStartChangedError` ("changed while starting work. Retry.") as a generic HTTP 500 / `response.failed` with type `api_error` and message `internal error`, so clients cannot tell the request is safe to retry.

Closes #192465.

## User Impact

User impact: a client that overlaps two requests on the same session key now receives a 409 with a stable `code` (`SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED` / `SESSION_WORK_START_INVALIDATED`) and the original "Retry." message instead of a hard 500 internal error, so retry logic can act on it exactly like the archived-session case.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveOpenAiCompatError` in `src/gateway/openai-compat-errors.ts` handles `SessionWorkStartError` with reason `archived` (409, added in #170029) and failover reasons, but has no branch for `SessionWorkStartChangedError` / `SessionWorkStartInvalidatedError` from `src/config/sessions/work-start-error.ts`. Those fall through to `describeFailoverError`, stay unclassified, and the caller (`openai-compatible-agent-run.ts`) emits the fallback 500 `internal error`. Both error classes carry stable `code` fields specifically so wrappers can classify them, and both are retryable conflicts like the archived case.

The fix adds one branch that maps `isSessionWorkStartInvalidatedError(err)` (which recognizes both classes and wrapped errors carrying the stable codes) to 409 `invalid_request_error` with the error's own message and stable code — mirroring the #170029 precedent.

## What Was Changed

- `src/gateway/openai-compat-errors.ts`: new branch mapping session work-start changed/invalidated errors (including wrapped errors that only carry the stable code) to 409 + stable code.
- `src/gateway/openai-http.test.ts`: three regression cases in a self-contained describe — changed error, invalidated error, and a wrapped error carrying only the stable code.

Not changed: the archived-session branch, tool-authorization and failover mappings, retry behavior inside the gateway, and the error classes themselves.

## Evidence

Real before/after through `resolveOpenAiCompatError` (the exact production mapping for these endpoints), run as part of the registered `openai-http.test.ts` suite:

```text
before (fix stashed): Tests 3 failed | 112 skipped — the mapping returns
  undefined, so the caller emits 500 {"type":"api_error","message":"internal error"}
  (matches the issue's production log)
after:                Tests 3 passed | 112 skipped — each error maps to
  409 invalid_request_error with its stable code and "Retry." message
```

- Focused suite: `scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-server.config.ts src/gateway/openai-http.test.ts -t "session work-start conflicts"` — 3/3 passed.
- Full-file run for reference: 111/115 passed; the 4 failures are pre-existing environment-sensitive SSE/disconnect e2e tests in this heavy suite (15s streaming timeouts on a loaded local Windows machine), unrelated to this change and not touched by it.
- Format check (after formatter write) and scoped oxlint on both changed files: pass.
- Latest-main re-check at `3816bcb3dea1`: `openai-compat-errors.ts` still has no work-start-conflict branch, so the fix is not already upstream.
- Local full-repo typecheck was not runnable in this environment (it needs the generated `packages/plugin-sdk/dist` declarations, which the local build pipeline does not emit on Windows); the change reuses the existing error-class guards and mapping shape, and CI type coverage applies.

## Risks / Notes for Reviewers

- Status/type choice follows the archived precedent (409 + `invalid_request_error`); the stable `code` field lets clients branch precisely.
- Wrappers that only forward the stable `code` are recognized by the same guard the sessions layer already ships.

prs.title: test(ci): reuse fixtures and join hook admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three test owners repeat expensive fixture construction or observe the wrong completion signal:

- macOS distribution cases recompile identical debug executables and complete dSYMs.
- locale-finalizer fixtures pack and push the initial warm corpus before exercising real finalizer publication; four initial setup pushes previously timed out.
- Gateway hook cases poll after HTTP admission, which precedes the real deferred-wake receipt.

The existing Darwin workflow also omitted the distribution owner. Qualification exposed two inherited test-only Promise-executor lint errors in the MCP fullscreen E2E setup and teardown.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. Packaging, real finalizer publication, routing, refusal, replay and queue assertions remain intact. Existing Decision and Baseten diagnostics expose unavailable outcomes without changing caller deadlines or claiming to repair those outcomes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep one lazy, complete distribution seed per architecture. Privately copy its executable and entire dSYM after compilation, symbol generation and UUID inspection succeed. The first existing packaging case proves cold arm64 preparation, cold x86_64 preparation, reuse, in-place executable/DWARF corruption, borrower deletion and fresh UUID arrays. One complete byte/tree snapshot covers both surviving and fresh borrowers; this consolidation removes six test lines and strengthens the surviving-borrower topology check.

Construct the initial bare locale origin with Git's local `clone --bare --no-hardlinks`, preserving configuration, ancestry and tracking refs and proving private objects/corruption isolation once. Later catch-up and publication pushes remain real. The internal cause of the initial setup-push timeout remains unknown; no timeout, compression or pack setting changes.

Join the real deferred-wake receipt through the existing canonical hook helper, retaining its observer chaining, queued/coalesced assertion and cancellation-safe cleanup. Direct wake endpoints already await admission and use immediate queue assertions. Replay, refusal, now, fanout and dispatch-only contracts remain unchanged.

Add the complete distribution owner and four direct input paths to the existing PR-only Darwin workflow. Retain its five TypeScript owners, Python coverage, exact-head checkout, read-only permissions, disabled caches, Node 24.22.1/arm64 admission and 20-minute budget. This adds native coverage; it does not itself reduce work.

Use statement-bodied Promise executors for the existing sandbox `listen` and `close` calls. Completion still belongs to their original callbacks, with the same teardown order and assertions. No lint rule is disabled.

Qualification on current main also exposed a shallow-history fixture copying only two checker files after the checker gained more static imports. Reuse the existing canonical runtime-import closure at the fixture producer. Real Git history, negative budget refusal, workflow admission and positive allocation assertions remain intact.

The signed integration retains frozen main `bae191254328d6a032052cd705a05e21f75bc025`, including the canonical hook helper from [#190788](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190788) and intentional locale glossary removal/metadata controls from [#193067](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193067).

Runtime production LOC: 0. Workflow/tooling: +7. Tests: +160 net against frozen baseline `bae191254328d6a032052cd705a05e21f75bc025`. The normal allocation is 156 against the current CI comparison base: four identical UI callback lines already exist on main and earn no additional credit. The separate allocation record covers seed isolation, cancellation/workflow controls, diagnostics and ratchet fixture imports; the shared scalar is unchanged. Existing distribution-consumer setup calls decrease from 45 to 6 by source count. This is not a measured whole-module duration or billing saving. Locale construction replaces nine initial pushes with 23 setup/proof Git launches, so no subprocess-count reduction is claimed.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(doctor): prepare plugin contracts off the main thread
prs.body:
**Owner accepted the measured tradeoff on 2026-10-31: Peter answered “Land it” to the coordinator’s acceptance question.** The realistic ~6,500-file workload improved median elapsed by 14.3%, total CPU by 14.7%, main-thread CPU by 90.9%, and maximum timer delay by 92.5%; the accepted loss is first-phase p95 +36.6% (the slowest of seven runs on a loaded host). The small 131-file fixture regressed elapsed +16.5%, CPU +15.8%, and first-phase median +24.3%, reflecting a fixed roughly 90 ms worker cold start plus the retained tail outliers. This is not an overall speedup at every scale.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can block its main event loop while capturing an external plugin's setup-contract source. This uses the existing plugin-generation preparation pool, retains one unexecuted source seed, and creates independent artifacts and fresh callbacks for each phase. It preserves source/admission validation, receipts, authority rechecks after awaited work, native custody, and cleanup before retirement. Metadata-only declarations remain metadata-only.

## User Impact

The isolated source-preparation workload is substantially more responsive at both scales, with the small-workload overhead and retained tails explicitly accepted by the owner. This does not establish that the reported Windows duration or separate `--fix` hang is fixed. Integrated current main at `f77032845236b5f6093c81b12be9bc4bbf69c3da`, including snapshot publication (#189624). Final integrated-head proof and CI attribution are recorded below. No release or fs-safe pin change is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Current bootstrap investigation

Moved the existing snapshot-cleanup error class to the small lifecycle-errors owner and migrated every internal caller; the class identity and behavior are preserved. Plugin install roots now import the existing narrow state/config path owners directly. The preparation-worker bootstrap drops **304 → 299 local TypeScript modules**, **1,904,355 → 1,859,621 source bytes** (44,734 bytes, 2.35%). This census excludes built-ins and external package source.

Seven-per-arm alternating, uninstrumented cold-import probes measured import wall median/p95 **76.3/90.9 → 79.8/86.8 ms**, and thread CPU **75.6/84.2 → 79.4/84.2 ms**. Fewer imports did **not** demonstrate a cold-time improvement. The roughly 80–90 ms bootstrap remains. The 131-file runtime trace makes zero Jiti factory/transform calls; there is no further compiler initialization to remove from that source-preparation path. Transformation remains lazy for modules that require it.

A proposed heap-diagnostics deferral was discarded: every pool task already requests sampling, so it relocated the same work and complicated child-worker observation. It is absent from this head. No extra worker pool, unconditional warmup, persistent snapshot or cache was added.

There is no exact admitted external-setup capture signal before `doctor.config-flow`. Startup reads source config; database preflight validates core-only schemas. Exact manifest, source, contract and cache selection occurs inside config-flow. Starting earlier would add discovery/admission work to zero-capture runs, so early warming is skipped. Persistent plugin snapshots are not assumed as a Doctor fix.

The retained earlier optimizations keep source inspection's resolver lazy, preserve supported read-only native `import.meta.url` parsing, and use the originally admitted artifact as the pristine seed instead of making an unused extra copy. Each consumer still gets independent custody and validates its receipt.

## Evidence

### Rule fixed before these runs

Apply independently to both scales: elapsed and total-process-CPU medians within A/A noise or better; **no median/p95 cell may regress by 20% or more**; retain main-thread responsiveness. Seven samples per arm, all retained. The rule was published before these comparative runs. The tables remain complete below; on 2026-10-31 Peter explicitly accepted the worse metrics described above. Before landing, the integrated head receives three alternating samples per arm at the same large scale: stop if median elapsed or total CPU is at least 20% worse than baseline, or if the responsiveness win is lost. Smaller changes/noise do not reopen the accepted decision.

The same committed `scripts/perf/doctor-setup-preparation-measure.ts` and two test-support helpers were byte-identical on both arms. Baseline `4d2a9f8bb4c47da0daae7fd820cab33fa450ef7b` uses `--route legacy`; candidate uses `--route prepared`. Default pinned Bun 1.4.4; `--files 128 --phases 3`; fresh processes in order **A,A,B,A,B,A,B,A,B,A,B,A,B,B**. This is the same historical baseline as the earlier comparison, so overall deltas include the integrated prerequisites and earlier worker changes; the cold-import probe isolates the new bootstrap delta.

Fixture generation/imports and post-run source verification are outside the timed interval. Worker creation/imports, callback execution and awaited phase/final cleanup are inside. Total process CPU includes workers; main-thread CPU overlaps it. With seven samples, nearest-rank p95 is the observed maximum. No task-owned build, review, test or cleanup job ran during timing.

### Small: 131 files / 597,689 bytes

The original fixture's source bytes and expected payload hash are unchanged. One-minute host load: **13.12–17.76**. Initial A/A elapsed/CPU changed **−15.9%/−7.8%**; final B/B **+1.4%/+1.7%**.

| Metric, ms | Baseline median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 | Median / p95 change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Three-phase elapsed | 545.7 / 648.8 | 635.6 / 1753.5 | +16.5% / +170.3% |
| Total process CPU | 613.7 / 665.5 | 710.7 / 1685.8 | +15.8% / +153.3% |
| Main-thread CPU | 426.5 / 490.1 | 177.7 / 503.4 | -58.3% / +2.7% |
| Maximum phase timer delay | 267.1 / 370.2 | 62.7 / 236.1 | -76.5% / -36.2% |
| First phase elapsed | 274.0 / 382.4 | 340.6 / 1472.9 | +24.3% / +285.2% |
| Second phase elapsed | 98.3 / 100.9 | 104.8 / 310.5 | +6.7% / +207.8% |
| Third phase elapsed | 94.2 / 102.7 | 96.4 / 283.3 | +2.3% / +175.9% |
| Second phase timer delay | 91.4 / 93.4 | 44.7 / 236.1 | -51.1% / +152.6% |
| Third phase timer delay | 86.5 / 93.9 | 42.6 / 215.3 | -50.7% / +129.2% |

**Historical gate failed; owner accepted this tradeoff.** Elapsed +16.5% and CPU +15.8% exceed their A/A controls; first-phase median +24.3% and multiple p95 cells independently fail the 20% rule. The first candidate sample has a large cold-worker tail; another has elevated warm phases and main-thread CPU. They are retained, not discarded as host noise. The median gap is roughly 90 ms elapsed / 97 ms CPU, but this is **not a fixed-cost-only failure**.

### Large: 6,503 files / 26,423,397 bytes

`--fixture large` generates 26 synthetic ESM dependencies, each with 248 4,096-byte assets, equivalent in scale to the earlier ~6,500-file closure. All 26 dependency callbacks execute; every asset contributes to a fixed checksum. Assertions check private dependency URLs, unchanged original source bytes, fresh phase callbacks, matching receipts and completed worker cleanup. One-minute host load: **12.34–34.80**. Initial A/A elapsed/CPU **−27.9%/−26.4%**; final B/B **−2.7%/−2.5%**.

| Metric, ms | Baseline median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 | Median / p95 change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Three-phase elapsed | 16443.9 / 28899.3 | 14100.3 / 33230.4 | -14.3% / +15.0% |
| Total process CPU | 17099.4 / 26248.6 | 14592.8 / 28609.5 | -14.7% / +9.0% |
| Main-thread CPU | 12648.6 / 22170.9 | 1147.0 / 1391.8 | -90.9% / -93.7% |
| Maximum phase timer delay | 7636.7 / 16391.2 | 570.3 / 841.7 | -92.5% / -94.9% |
| First phase elapsed | 8012.5 / 16974.9 | 7492.0 / 23180.1 | -6.5% / +36.6% |
| Second phase elapsed | 4729.0 / 12535.2 | 3331.3 / 5271.0 | -29.6% / -58.0% |
| Third phase elapsed | 3643.5 / 7241.1 | 3388.5 / 5254.8 | -7.0% / -27.4% |
| Second phase timer delay | 2480.3 / 12078.7 | 373.0 / 521.8 | -85.0% / -95.7% |
| Third phase timer delay | 3107.9 / 5722.6 | 328.7 / 432.5 | -89.4% / -92.4% |

**Historical gate failed; owner accepted this tradeoff.** Elapsed and CPU medians improve (−14.3%/−14.7%) and responsiveness is retained, but first-phase p95 **+36.6%** independently fails the rule. Load rose sharply during the window. That limits causal timing claims; it does not waive the retained tail. The first-phase p95 regression and retained loaded-host tails are part of Peter’s explicit acceptance, not dismissed as noise.

### Stable work counts

All seven samples in each arm have identical JavaScript filesystem and logical generation counts.

| Scale | Baseline main / worker sync calls | Candidate main / worker sync calls | Total call change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Small | 33,595 / 0 | 15,221 / 17,592 | −2.33% |
| Large | 943,000 / 0 | 34,262 / 868,993 | −4.21% |

Both candidate scales perform four captures, three source reuses and four receipt passes. Small: 524 receipt file reads / 2,390,756 bytes; large: 26,012 reads / 105,693,588 bytes. Original bytes are acquired once, with independent consumer copies retained. Counts are JavaScript/logical work, not kernel syscalls or physical-storage traffic.

### Historical validation

The seven-per-arm tables above are the accepted pre-integration measurements, retained in full. The original worker change passed its focused capture/cleanup tests, build, typecheck and independent review. The integrated cutover additionally preserves installed-source snapshot publication from #189624 and its independent runtime generations. Current-head validation is recorded below; historical draft-skipped CI is not used as landing proof.

Further bootstrap separation and profiling of retained cold/warm tails may be useful follow-up work. They are not prerequisites to the owner-accepted cutover.

## Integrated-head landing evidence (2026-11-04)

Final head: `c4dabe4361e5bb45a456de52fb4cac2452c1d90a`. Integrated main `f77032845236b5f6093c81b12be9bc4bbf69c3da`, including #189624. The cutover preserves installed-source snapshot publication, independent frozen runtime generations, Doctor's unexecuted worker seed, source receipts/native admission, post-await authority checks and awaited cleanup. The old synchronous source-custody wrapper is removed.

CI exposed two ownership issues that are repaired here. Raw invalid configuration now resumes the original diagnostic read after preparing precisely the requested source, without treating unvalidated input as typed config. Collected migration resource facts retain the caller's authority; temporary setup/read-scope authority stays around executable preparation and does not escape into those facts. Closing the inner read scope therefore permits unchanged-capture reuse, while caller revocation still rejects access. Test callers explicitly own and dispose their transferred plugin caches before broker cleanup. Existing byte-equality, one-capture and broker-empty assertions remain intact.

The original seven-per-arm tables above remain the owner-accepted tradeoff. The final required sanity check used the same byte-identical harness on both arms, historical baseline `4d2a9f8bb4c47da0daae7fd820cab33fa450ef7b`, and checksum-verified pinned Bun 1.4.4. Three samples per arm ran serially in A/B/A/B/A/B order, with no local build, test or review alongside timing. All source/runtime stamps, callback/receipt assertions and cleanup passed. One-minute load was 21.89–27.66. Median elapsed **−9.8%**, total CPU **−9.3%**, main-thread CPU **−92.0%**, maximum timer delay **−94.3%**: the integration stop rule passes. Three-sample maxima below are observations, not a new tail-distribution estimate.

| Metric, ms | Baseline median / p95 | Candidate median / p95 | Median / p95 change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Three-phase elapsed | 20605.1 / 26389.1 | 18591.2 / 19353.9 | -9.8% / -26.7% |
| Total process CPU | 19608.0 / 21187.9 | 17776.7 / 17974.1 | -9.3% / -15.2% |
| Main-thread CPU | 16262.0 / 18655.8 | 1301.2 / 1317.6 | -92.0% / -92.9% |
| Maximum phase timer delay | 9955.1 / 10221.3 | 565.2 / 626.0 | -94.3% / -93.9% |
| First phase elapsed | 10302.1 / 10663.7 | 9142.7 / 9603.3 | -11.3% / -9.9% |
| Second phase elapsed | 4432.2 / 10284.6 | 4392.7 / 4400.1 | -0.9% / -57.2% |
| Third phase elapsed | 4960.7 / 5409.3 | 4874.3 / 6274.6 | -1.7% / +16.0% |
| Second phase timer delay | 2988.1 / 9851.8 | 388.0 / 480.7 | -87.0% / -95.1% |
| Third phase timer delay | 4592.7 / 4969.0 | 400.3 / 439.2 | -91.3% / -91.2% |

All 3 samples per arm retained. This is a sanity check, not a new tail estimate; p95 shown is the observed maximum.

| Sample | Arm | Elapsed ms | CPU ms | Main CPU ms | Maximum delay ms |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | A | 26389.1 | 21187.9 | 18655.8 | 10221.3 |
| 2 | B | 17732.9 | 16457.2 | 1087.3 | 400.6 |
| 3 | A | 20605.1 | 19608.0 | 16262.0 | 9955.1 |
| 4 | B | 19353.9 | 17974.1 | 1301.2 | 565.2 |
| 5 | A | 17268.2 | 16966.2 | 14334.0 | 9821.3 |
| 6 | B | 18591.2 | 17776.7 | 1317.6 | 626.0 |

Validation: the earlier integrated proof passed 396 focused cases. The baseline rendezvous failed first with zero progress ticks and watchdog release; all five integrated outcomes recorded three ticks without host blocking or watchdog release. The snapshot-custody negative control failed collection, and the restored path passed. Current CI repairs pass the original 14 cleanup cases, 37 auto-enable cases, 17 raw-diagnostic/snapshot cases, 16 security/responsiveness/authority cases, and the final 22-case resource/authority/capture run (overlapping suites, not an additive unique count). The unchanged five-repair capture test passes. The new resource-lifetime assertion failed first on normal inner-scope drainage and passes with caller revocation still enforced.

Core/scripts types, all 29 affected test type graphs and targeted lint pass. Final owner changes were rechecked in core and affected test graphs. Full integration and final repair deltas independently reviewed with Codex at P0–P2: scoped-clean. The simplification pass retains existing owners and removes eager raw-config coercion; the additional preparation guard is temporary and introduces no cache or fallback.

The PR's 1,213 net test lines are exactly funded (1,097 original + 116 integration/regression lines). The local test-line guard remains red by **93 inherited lines** (6,480,182 total; 6,480,089 ceiling); exact main baseline independently reproduces the same 93-line debt. This is not claimed as a passing guard.

Exact-head broad CI: [41973518283](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41973518283), currently running. The earlier failed run revealed the PR-caused issues above and also four baseline failures: UI runner/device wording, trusted-package harness omitting `release-context.mjs`, listener environment-reference writeback, and the 93-line test-line debt. Final-run attribution is pending; unknown failures will not be waived.

No release, tag or fs-safe pin change (`0.27.1`). The reported Windows duration and separate `--fix` hang remain unverified; #166526 stays open.

prs.title: improve(backup): omit Codex diagnostics from restart checkpoints
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Local-companion restart checkpoints unnecessarily capture Codex’s changing diagnostic SQLite log database and its companions.

## User Impact

Local-companion capture omits only the activated Codex plugin’s managed agent-home `logs_2.sqlite` and `-wal`/`-shm`/`-journal`. Full backups and unrelated same-name files remain unchanged. Codex state, credentials, session rollouts, and other databases remain preserved. Omitted diagnostic history is not recovered; Codex recreates the log store.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep vendor policy in Codex manifest `backupResources` and add an optional generic `local-companion` profile selector to the existing planner. No global filename exclusion, extra policy owner, schema/version change, or template-exclusion option is introduced. Native backup safety and source-preservation behavior remain intact.

The native contract was inspected in [Codex 8f73cde](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/8f73cdee456b6c46b791780d40cadf9d556d22a4): `codex-rs/state/src/sqlite.rs:29,59-65,146-148,297-310` separates logs from durable databases and recreates missing stores with WAL; `codex-rs/state/src/runtime/logs.rs:3-57` records bounded diagnostic/feedback history. OpenClaw’s managed-home owner is `extensions/codex/src/app-server/auth-start-options.ts:7-42`. Custom external Codex/sqlite homes are intentionally not inferred.

## Evidence

- Standalone head: `379cf56d5cca739bb94ce6678e46847c2edf48fa`, directly parented by baseline `4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914`. Mechanically separated from `1346e4f6f80911f634b77a212aead087089e1143`; no dependency on template-option commit `84f84f4e818851746b93a78e0a29bcf5b652bc8d`. Eleven files have byte-identical added/deleted lines; the remaining archive-create call only expands the baseline formatting to pass `localCompanion`.
- Fresh standalone proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/backup-local-companion.test.ts src/plugins/manifest-backup-resources.test.ts src/commands/backup-resource-inventory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` with a unique filesystem cache: **27 passed**, three files, **44.74s** including compiler preparation. Companion create/verify/restore test **237ms** (runner **7.67s**); plugin declaration runner **3.04s**; inventory runner **1.14s**. CI seconds unavailable.
- Real archive creation, verification, and restore preserve diagnostic source bytes, state/auth/rollout bytes, a similarly named sibling, unrelated same-name database, client credentials, and PostgreSQL anchors while omitting declared diagnostics. Full-archive resource selection retains the diagnostics.
- Targeted `run-tsgo` passed for all eight changed TypeScript files and their import closure; `run-oxlint` passed all eight; formatter check passed eight TypeScript files and two docs; both docs passed MDX validation; Codex manifest JSON parsed and formatter stdin output was byte-identical; `git diff --check` passed.
- Reused original red proof: the same companion regression reached real restore and failed because `logs_2.sqlite` existed instead of returning `ENOENT`. Reused broader original lane proof: **73 passed, 1 Windows-only skipped**, **131.44s**. These are original reviewed-lane results, not new-head broad-suite results.
- Reused canonical autoreview: P0–P3, complete original local candidate against `4221b02f6e4a08ab0d73646f7e3eb4834f6c8914`, scoped-clean with no actionable findings. That review included both independent original changes; this separation changes only context and removes the unrelated template change, so no substantive re-review was required. No claim of a new standalone autoreview run.
- Simplify: one profile conditional in the existing resource planner; no new vendor code in core or duplicate exclusion owner. Production TypeScript **+34/-6**, manifest **+24**, tests **+72/-3**, docs **+13**, allocation **+2**. The 69-line test allocation covers one archive/restore regression and independent metadata-profile admission/deduplication contracts.
- Earlier harness proof used a PostgreSQL discovery fixture. The additional exact-head compiled-CLI proof below uses real PostgreSQL and actual plugin discovery. No real-agent inference, upgrade, Windows or PostgreSQL-disconnection scenario is claimed.

## Main integration and refreshed validation

Integrated official main `2777468d26e5f21455b67591a045a40c770aee13` with an ordinary merge, preserving the original Codex head `379cf56d5cca739bb94ce6678e46847c2edf48fa`. New head: `c5a610763a84ad8e11f42af69e0a7422febb0796`.

The two conflicts were additive option forwarding in `backup-shared.ts` and `backup-create.ts`. Both `localCompanion` and `excludeWorktreeTemplates` remain supported together. Registered template selection still belongs to the native registry, and exclusion precedence still belongs to the existing resource planner. No new policy owner, schema, version, or configuration option was introduced by this integration.

Fresh proof on the exact committed tree:

- **32 tests passed across four files**: combined companion/template archive creation, verification and restore; compiled CLI template/full backup behavior; native resource inventory; manifest admission and deduplication. Runner wall time **71.00s**, including worker preparation; shard wall times **29.62s / 1.17s / 3.26s**. The existing template CLI case took **5.411s**, and the companion case **0.246s**. CI seconds for this head are not yet available.
- Real lower-level planning discovers activated Codex metadata and registered templates together, omits both regenerable resources, and retains nested agent/credential owners. The archive-level test drives both options through real traversal/verification/restore and checks original source bytes. Its PostgreSQL discovery remains the existing explicit synthetic boundary; it is not fresh live-PostgreSQL proof.
- Two existing cases were extended, with no extra test case or product boot. A separate **36-line allocation** accounts exactly for this composition regression coverage; the original 69-line allocation and shared baseline remain unchanged.
- Targeted commands and infra typecheck leaves, lint, formatting, test-line ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent **P0–P3 review** of the complete candidate against the pinned main base completed **scoped-clean**, with no actionable findings. The committed tree exactly matches the reviewed tree.

### Prior runtime proof remains correctly scoped

The real compiled-CLI/PostgreSQL 17.11 run remains evidence for original head `379cf56d5cca739bb94ce6678e46847c2edf48fa`: all eight CLI invocations passed; ordinary full archives retained all four diagnostics, companion archives omitted them, and companion restore preserved durable Codex content, local credential data, and PostgreSQL anchor identity. This was not relabeled as a new-head execution.

The Codex manifest, manifest parser, activated-plugin discovery, PostgreSQL discovery adapter, archive verifier entrypoint, and restore module are byte-unchanged from that run. Incoming main adds template registry/resource plumbing and a template manifest option, plus an equivalent manifest-path expression and a remote-namespace error import relocation. This is not a claim that the whole runtime dependency closure is identical. Fresh combined tests cover the changed option/planning and archive/manifest surfaces. Existing runtime-proof limits remain: synthetic Codex payloads, no live Codex conversation or restored Gateway activation, and no separately severed-PostgreSQL test.

## Credits

Requested by @galiniliev; adapted from the release-branch work with native OpenClaw owners. All commits retain Galin’s co-author credit.

## Additional runtime evidence

Exact candidate `379cf56d5cca739bb94ce6678e46847c2edf48fa`: compiled CLI plus real PostgreSQL 17.11 completed eight CLI invocations, all exit 0, including Doctor, native database port, ordinary full backup, local-companion create, verification, and staged restore. Actual activated Codex manifest discovery omitted `logs_2.sqlite` and its WAL/SHM/journal companions from the companion archive; the ordinary full archive retained all four.

Restoration preserved Codex state, synthetic credentials and rollout bytes, a similarly named backup and an unrelated same-name file. PostgreSQL anchor/store/namespace, metadata and sentinel data were preserved. One E2E passed; fixture lint passed. Task containers and snapshot were positively confirmed absent. No production change.

Limits: synthetic Codex payloads, not a live Codex conversation. Shared PostgreSQL state was populated; other portable families were selected but unused. Full archive was inspected/verified, not restored. No restored Gateway activation or separately disconnected-PostgreSQL verification.

### Captured CLI output

Actual output with only fixture paths redacted; omitted fields marked.

— backup create --local-companion --verify (exit 0)
```text
  "localCompanion": true,
  "verified": true,
... (other fields omitted)
    {
      "kind": "plugin resource",
      "sourcePath": "<state-fixture>/agents/main/agent/codex-home/logs_2.sqlite",

```

## Investigated UI CI failure and bounded replay

The original [UI E2E failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41422704713/job/125202451410) remains unresolved: Chromium reported `keyboard.press: Target crashed` in `new-session-page.responsive-welcome.e2e.test.ts:165`, “keeps phone setup compact with 2 agents.” The job displayed 5/7, but its recorded command executed shard **5/6 with four workers**. Its executed merge was `acc670a76cf53736398652c6314380472de9427a` (main parent `419d0c53118045c5a48e80c6743454f2726c67fd`, this PR head `c5a610763a84ad8e11f42af69e0a7422febb0796`). Retained original artifacts contained only progress metadata, not a renderer crash dump. Zero recorded cgroup OOM events do not identify another cause.

After the earlier four-file Node 26 replay passed, a bounded [full historical-shard diagnostic replay](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41554166719) on November 3 used **Node 24.22.1**, pinned pnpm 12.15.0 / Vitest 5.0.5 / Playwright 1.64.1 / Chromium 156.0.8078.4, four actual CPUs, and the native sequencer's exact **138 original project/file members from 834 include patterns**. Historical application/test inputs and assertions were preserved; a reviewed task-only context-lifecycle/CDP observer overlay was added.

- **138 files and 537 tests passed**, zero unhandled errors, **467.59s**. The former failing two-agent case passed in 5.665s; all seven responsive-welcome cases passed.
- Verified replay source tree: `65e183652ffd319ad7802d6958ce8166384d87b7`; transport carrier: `b9442fbd081b934b18bd72e90813a9abb3f5ea9f`. These identify the instrumented historical merge, not a new PR commit.
- The observer armed before application execution, recorded 1,602 target-created and 1,602 target-destroyed events, and recorded **zero renderer-crash events**. No crash status/error code exists to infer. The flush barrier completed; observer and browser exited 0; the journal closed.
- Test, payload and wrapper exits were 0. Artifacts were downloaded and hash-verified before exact lease teardown; final remote settlement is complete. The backing Actions run's cancellation is normal one-shot Testbox cleanup, not the test result.
- Retained private evidence archive SHA-256: `10ab66b6143954501e591e132a9a11017963561203e8dab0780145b73c6ae2e9`; 40-file evidence manifest SHA-256: `ba49cfb5ecfc3fc9448ee1b38be8dd4fac5818a5fc4e64ad420e7647b15097fe`.

**Interpretation:** the original renderer failure was not reproduced, not fixed or classified as infrastructure/inherited. Original cache contents, concurrent interleaving, cgroup scope and the diagnostic overlay differ. This replay does **not** replace current-head PR CI or clear its failed gate. No product repair, CI rerun, weakened assertion, timeout extension or repeated replay is claimed.

## Native renderer diagnostics — requested follow-up

Diagnostic commit: `28909ec0e209c8242d14e6b225ae6de3ff82a39c`, parent `c5a610763a84ad8e11f42af69e0a7422febb0796`, with Galin’s co-author credit.

The original renderer crash still has no attributable native cause. This follow-up adds the missing evidence for a future occurrence; it does not claim to repair that crash or authorize rerunning its old CI job.

The existing invocation-owned shared Chromium setup now arms one browser-level `Target.targetCrashed` observer before lending its endpoint to tests. It captures at most 32 timestamp/target/status/error-code records through the existing `failure-*/failure.public.json` artifact upload path, with a numeric overflow count. It includes no page URLs, titles, content, or connection endpoints. Artifact publication happens when the native event arrives, without evaluating the dead page, retrying a test, or relaunching Chromium. Existing browser ownership closes the observer.

### Focused evidence

- Real Chromium through the actual global setup: native termination capture, target-ID match, public-data exclusions, surviving sibling-page evaluation, and normal shared-browser shutdown passed. A subsequent connection to the closed endpoint was rejected.
- The identical native capture oracle against the original `c5a61076` setup failed because the crash-artifact directory was absent, after the real native crash event and normal browser shutdown. This is the red/green diagnostic contract, not reproduction of the historical CI failure.
- Captured fixed-run output (only the private artifact path omitted):

```text
[ui-e2e] Chromium target crashed {"at":"2026-11-04T13:13:27.211Z","targetId":"FBF65150C2DC91F0833EC8C251DAB271","status":"crashed","errorCode":133}
NATIVE_CRASH_CAPTURE_PASS {"kind":"chromium-target-crashes","crashes":[{"at":"2026-11-04T13:13:27.211Z","targetId":"FBF65150C2DC91F0833EC8C251DAB271","status":"crashed","errorCode":133}],"dropped":0}

SHARED_BROWSER_SHUTDOWN_PASS
```

- Targeted TypeScript, lint, formatting and whitespace checks passed.
- The existing shared-browser regression adds 30 justified lines with a matching separate allocation, retaining prior assertions, cleanup ownership and deadlines. The crash trigger waits for the actual page-crash event, closes that target and settles its raw CDP command, which otherwise can remain pending. The one-shot nested projects disable persistent filesystem module caching: installed Vitest's server cache reader returns a Buffer where Vite's source-map reader requires text. No dependency bytes or repository-wide cache settings changed.
- Final canonical autoreview of the complete local diagnostic delta against `c5a61076` completed **scoped-clean P0–P2**, with no actionable findings, including crash-command settlement and the scoped cache setting. It is a code review, not another runtime execution; unchanged context was unavailable in that final bundle. The earlier independent full-source review separately covered the setup, artifact-directory owner, regression and allocation with no consequential findings. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable because its checkout held unrelated changes; this uses the documented autoreview-plus-hosted-review route.
- The complete shared-browser regression passes after the fixture-only cache correction: **1 test passed**, pinned-Bun test time **5.766s**, runner wall time **7.00s**; supported Node control **1 passed**, test time **13.790s**, runner wall time **17.93s**. - Simplification: the invocation's existing browser owner also owns the single diagnostic connection; publication reuses the existing artifact-directory/upload owner. No new runtime manager, retry, page-content capture or CI workflow. Incremental setup delta **+73/-3**; regression **+30/-0**.


## Approved Vitest cache repair

The cache-enabled UI startup failure is separate from the historical renderer crash. Vitest 5.0.5's server module runner read a cached source file as a Buffer and supplied it as Vite's `code`; stack/source-map processing calls `code.charCodeAt` and requires text. The approved one-line repair uses `readFile(result.tmp, "utf-8")` in the existing dependency patch. pnpm's patch workflow regenerated the patch and lockfile binding without dependency-version changes. Its generated lockfile also normalizes existing optional metadata for escape-string-regexp 4.0.0.

The temporary `--no-fsModuleCache` workaround is removed. The existing native shared-browser regression now explicitly enables filesystem caching. No assertions, crash trigger, cleanup owner, browser flags or deadlines were weakened, and the exact test-line allocation shrinks by two lines.

- After repair, pinned Bun passes the complete regression: **1/1**, **2.37s** runner. Supported Node with explicit cache enabled passes **1/1**, **2.09s** runner. This covers the actual global setup, native renderer crash artifact/privacy, sibling survival, custom launch, next-project reuse and shutdown.

The reviewer inspected the change with the real global setup and native shutdown helper as context; test execution and generated hash verification are parent-owned evidence. The original renderer-crash cause remains unknown. Existing earlier runs retain their original scope and outcome; these results prove the separately reproduced cached-source startup fix.


## Integrated CI repairs and smaller manifest coverage

Local integrated candidate `42a360417abfa023ff1d47f841c2a6f998b7ba86` (tree `9d9fcc1f7ef9488c2b9e13148adf2ded0a790d0e`) combines reviewed cache repair `64e1fd4ba682999793b1ceff77863dc47a8b236f` with main `77c263b9fa112ce0e1657f6cbf56016092cd1077`, without merge conflicts. - Complete shared-browser resource-ownership module passes **15/15**; Vitest **75.73s**, wrapper **87.13s**. Its new-main clipboard scheduling case is retained.
- Manifest consolidation plus companion archive/database and inventory privacy checks pass **27/27** across four files and three runner configurations; wrapper **99.73s**, including a **75.784s** cold worker build. The manifest module is **23/23**, **3.12s** Vitest. This is not a full-archive CLI or Gateway-authentication run.
- Targeted manifest typecheck, lint, formatting and final source review pass. Canonical isolated autoreview of the complete main-relative candidate is **scoped-clean P0–P2**, zero findings, exit0. The reviewer assessed supplied source/execution evidence, not an independent execution.

The standalone profile-identity test is folded into existing activated-owner and disabled-plugin cases. Enabled expectations retain identical-path unprofiled and companion-only resources plus duplicate filtering; disabled expectations retain the original durable non-database resource and both regenerable profile variants, while requiring database-only output. Invalid-profile and profile-limited-durable rejection rows stay intact. This removes **one case, one fixture tree, two inventory resolutions and three formatted test lines**; the corresponding allocation shrinks **69→66**. No new helper or production seam is introduced. It preserves all 15 ownership cases and changes no scalar ceiling or allocations.

Intermediate published candidate: `b99bcba5cb7260d0c72df7bd895ff907f699f4a0`, tree `ed15c27e1bfa28604ee676c0a649a74364adea2f`, an ordinary conflict-free merge of reviewed candidate `42a360417abfa023ff1d47f841c2a6f998b7ba86` with the actual supporting-cleanup landing `d755a99495e79c0b98ae1ad612511889097b259f`. Galin's co-author credit is preserved.

All 18 substantive candidate files, including the Vitest UTF-8 patch, renderer observer, native crash regression, backup implementation, manifest consolidation and allocations, are byte-identical to the prior independently reviewed candidate. The only changed candidate files are the lockfile and the shared ownership test: the lock preserves the same approved Vitest patch binding while integrating upstream dependency changes; the ownership test preserves the reviewed five-line fake-browser repair while incorporating upstream file membership and the landed seven-line simplification. prs.title: perf(ui): reduce Sessions first-visit network rounds
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sessions first visits spend an extra network round trip fetching small helper chunks on the Gateway's HTTP/1.1 connection pool. Follow-up to #192075.

## User Impact

Sessions loads about one RTT sooner on slower connections: 837 → 734 ms at 100 ms RTT and 1,893 → 1,637 ms at 250 ms RTT in the qualified workload. Cron fetches two fewer assets but has no material latency improvement; it still needs five request waves. Local route medians hold within the acceptance band.

## Why This Change Was Made

Group five small navigation helpers in the existing build chunk owner. The group has no page renderers or styles and remains outside startup, New Session, and Chat boot. Pages and independent panels retain the lazy boundaries and foreground-first scheduling from #183042 and #189015. Less-common helper consumers can fetch the other small helper definitions; this bounded tradeoff replaces several requests with one. Cron's encoded body grows 324 B while its requests fall 30 → 28; Sessions falls 39 → 35 and saves 561 B.

Both direct Gateway HTTP and HTTPS listeners use HTTP/1.1. All initial route asset requests are initiated within 2–4 ms: Vite already modulepreloads the known static graph together, so another hint layer would not remove queueing. The measured Sessions waterfall falls from seven six-connection waves to six. Cron stays at five waves. Native HTTP/2 would need request lifecycle, shutdown, and WebSocket work; no transport or proxy configuration changed.

## Evidence

Twenty interleaved base/head pairs plus unchanged A/A per local, 100 ms, and 250 ms profile (180 samples total). Base `4a43644e7a7`, head `2cbb1afc2c3`; frozen committed readiness harness `74563362e8ee`. Synthetic Team fixture, desktop, production HTTP asset handler, fresh document/cold client/cache per sample; ten base/control/head triplets then ten head/control/base triplets. One browser per block. One-minute host load: 11.78–59.84.

Acceptance set before measurement: local median ≤5% regression and p95 holds; assess noisy tails using A/A, script/task CPU, and work counts. Keep startup and cache behavior, lazy boundaries, and scheduling. No warm/cold mixing or timing samples dropped.

Full navigation includes drawer preparation; values are median / p95 ms:

| RTT | Page | Base | A/A | Head |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 ms | Sessions | 143.7 / 164.7 | 147.0 / 194.6 | 146.1 / 156.0 |
| 0 ms | Cron | 234.2 / 259.2 | 225.8 / 261.7 | 234.6 / 316.7 |
| 100 ms | Sessions | 836.6 / 879.3 | 834.3 / 849.3 | 734.0 / 748.3 |
| 100 ms | Cron | 917.6 / 974.4 | 919.2 / 1004.6 | 922.1 / 965.5 |
| 250 ms | Sessions | 1893.0 / 1921.8 | 1888.9 / 1898.6 | 1636.6 / 1660.4 |
| 250 ms | Cron | 1807.4 / 1878.0 | 1814.4 / 1839.7 | 1823.2 / 1877.5 |

Sessions' full-navigation gain is 1.03×RTT at both remote profiles. The click-to-ready slope between 100 and 250 ms is 7.046×RTT +116 ms on base and 6.049×RTT +113 ms on head. Cron stays near 5.1×RTT +155–158 ms. The 100 ms screening waterfall's last asset arrives 774 → 679 ms after click, while last-asset → ready stays 45–46 ms. Cron's last asset moves only 587 → 575 ms, with five waves retained. This is an attributed remaining cost under the preserved shared-component boundaries, not a claim that Cron reached day-start performance.

Timing qualifications: local Cron full-navigation p95 is 259 → 317 ms, chiefly in pre-click drawer preparation; click-to-ready p95 is 118.5 → 119.0 ms. Local cold-Chat p95 is 404 → 507 ms, with first-build visits split unequally between base/control labels; whole-scenario task CPU p95 improves 1,470 → 1,456 ms and script p95 rises 4.7%. Cold-Chat medians change +2.8% / +0.4% / +0.3% at local / 100 / 250 ms. Do not read these as all-tail improvements.

Cron's 100 ms task p95 is 384 → 478 ms (A/A 404), with isolated TaskOther spikes also on base/control. Paired median change is +2.4 ms versus base and −5.6 ms versus A/A. Six separate fresh-process diagnostic traces alternating base/head did not reproduce the large bursts: TaskOther was 142–150 ms on base and 138–157 ms on head, with only 2–4 ms MinorGC and no MajorGC. This does not explain the original bursts or exclude a reused-browser lifetime effect. The paired CPU medians and bounded diagnostic show no sustained regression; the unresolved tails remain disclosed, not counted as passing guards.

Paired strict performance check: no relative violations or warnings. Existing absolute baseline overruns are not increased; no budget edits.

| Surface | Base gzip bytes | Head gzip bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS | 92,457 | 92,456 |
| Chat JS | 1,286,432 | 1,286,462 |
| New Session JS | 799,708 | 799,652 |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 |

Chat's +30 B is within 64 B build variance. An isolated warm HTTP-cache probe, using the production asset handler and complete route inventories, made zero asset requests to the server and transferred zero asset bytes on repeated fresh-document visits for both routes on both builds. Responses retain `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`; Chromium reports `http/1.1`. This is HTTP asset-cache evidence, not a service-worker or full warm-app navigation claim.

UI typecheck, nine chunk-boundary tests, scoped lint, format, and diff checks passed. Production Knip fails identically on head and the exact base (`scripts/perf/tokenjuice-rule-cache-measure.ts`: unlisted `tokenjuice` dependency); no new dead-code or dependency finding. Independent Codex autoreview of this exact scope found no actionable P0–P2 finding. Simplification retained only seven production lines (720 → 727), no test lines or new abstraction.

Load-order audit covered Sessions startup-roster/page-query ordering, Cron busy/input/RPC waits, and immediate route-CSS assertions. No inspected E2E test depends on these asset names/counts. Full UI CI is requested with `ci:full`; no local full E2E run. No markup/style change, so before/after UI screenshots are not applicable.

Reproduction uses `scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts` at the frozen harness commit with `--gateway-http --first-load --cold-http-cache --untraced --thread-cpu-time --face chat --boot-route chat --critical-path --critical-path-route sessions --critical-path-route cron --no-owner-probes --viewport desktop --fixture-now-ms 1793013547604`. Set both `--network-latency-ms` and `--latency-ms` to the profile, download to 10,000 Kbps remotely / unlimited locally, and rotate immutable bundles through the native comparison slots for 30 samples in each ordering. Instrumented attribution runs are separate from timing evidence.

Limitations: synthetic readiness proves asset delivery and rendering, not live remote Gateway/provider latency. Settings timing was not remeasured because its frozen harness entry no longer matches current UI. New/Chat boot graphs are preserved; the accepted composer tradeoffs remain untouched. Reports and raw artifacts stay outside committed source.

prs.title: fix(ui): use host zoom for desktop content sizing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Mac app lacks familiar content-zoom shortcuts, and its new page zoom would otherwise compound with the Control UI’s older Text size preference.

## User Impact

- **Mac app:** View → Zoom In / Zoom Out / Actual Size and Cmd-+ / Cmd-=, Cmd--, Cmd-0 resize the Dashboard and full Native chat web transcript, bounded to 50–200%. New windows restore the app profile’s last zoom; existing windows retain their reading size. Native sidebar, Connection window, Quick Chat, and offline native fallback do not scale.
- **Desktop browsers on macOS, Windows, and Linux:** use browser-owned Cmd/Ctrl +/-/0 zoom. The old Text size control and search target are retired without intercepting keys or adding another scaling layer. Its saved value is retained; a page cannot convert it into browser-owned zoom, so choose browser zoom once after upgrading.
- **Accessibility and unqualified hosts:** touch-capable browsers (including mouse-attached tablets), mobile embeds, and native hosts without an explicit zoom capability retain Text size. Unqualified Tauri and WebView2 embeds do not lose their control. This is a supported-host cutover, **not universal Windows native-app parity**; Windows Hub’s separate native renderer is outside this repository’s implementation.

**Draft — not ready for merge. Browser runtime verification and inspected browser before/after captures are now complete. New native migration tests still require a disposable macOS runner. Real-app Native-chat readiness/zoom, full-window native-app visuals, and the earlier product-harness cleanup failure remain unresolved.**

## Why This Change Was Made

One scaling owner—native WKWebView page zoom or the desktop browser—replaces compounded CSS text scaling on supported hosts. Theme/preference refreshes keep their CSS text multiplier at 1. The existing document/device-settings bridge offers only the canonical local legacy value to the native owner; no direct localStorage reader, second zoom manager, new Gateway configuration, migration store, or server preference mutation is added.

On Mac, existing native zoom wins. Otherwise the first foreground document adopts its saved local text size once; background preloads cannot choose the profile default, and an early shortcut/reset wins. A legacy 125% text preference becomes 125% whole-page zoom, deliberately affecting layout and fonts. Cmd-0 means 100%. Legacy and unrelated preferences remain saved. Native chrome insets compensate for page zoom.

## Evidence

Current candidate: 805e4d5a4a4c3f7fe39ffa08e96456e6ef42f50f. A real GitHub merge conflict was resolved by integrating main at c1e6a094ec0e689f00faa9f40cd0629ef87c303f, preserving its shared theme-test fixture and observation-helper refactor. Focused tests, lint, localization, and whole-candidate P2 review were repeated against that exact refreshed base. Older fork results are **not exact-source proof for the new retirement/migration changes**.

- **Current UI checks:** 5 suites / 113 tests passed (19.33 s Vitest; 23.34 s shard): scaling ownership across native/browser/touch/mobile/unqualified hosts, mouse-attached touch preservation, optional native importer, theme refresh and preference preservation, actual Appearance conditional rendering, search retirement, and conversation bridge isolation. Initial native/browser CSS assertions were red before implementation. The component fixture emits Solid strict-read warnings from existing rendering paths; this is not layout/native proof.
- **Static checks:** targeted UI/script lint, formatting, native localization verification, and diff checks passed. UI typecheck still fails with 11 diagnostics in untouched files. An immutable UI/config snapshot from baseline c1e6a094, sharing only unchanged source/dependencies/generated declarations and native fixture assets, reproduced the exact same 11 normalized diagnostics. prs.title: fix(doctor): API and Claude CLI routes for the same model collapse onto Claude CLI after an update
prs.body:
Related: #191149

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after an update, an agent that runs one Claude model both through the API and through a legacy `claude-cli/<model>` ref (as primary plus fallback, or as primary plus heartbeat/subagent model) is moved entirely onto Claude CLI, and its fallback disappears.

Reported on r/openclaw after 2026.9.7 → 2026.10.10: "The migration rewrote my claude-cli model refs to anthropic refs. One agent had an API primary with a Claude CLI fallback on purpose. After the update it was pinned to the CLI and the fallback was gone."

## User Impact

User impact: Doctor and `openclaw update` no longer change which route (API or Claude CLI) a configured selection runs on. When an agent runs the same model both ways, Doctor keeps the `claude-cli/*` (or `google-gemini-cli/*`) refs as written, reports a warning, and both routes keep working.

Configs that a release before this fix already migrated are not repaired automatically. Doctor cannot tell from `primary: anthropic/X, fallbacks: [anthropic/X]` which entry used to be the API route. Affected users can restore the selection from `openclaw.json.pre-update` or the `.bak` ring, or re-add the `claude-cli/<model>` fallback by hand.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor rewrites `claude-cli/<model>` to `anthropic/<model>` and pins `agentRuntime: claude-cli` on that model in the scope's `models` map. The runtime is chosen per model, so the pin also moves every direct `anthropic/<model>` selection that the pin reaches. Fallback dedupe (`model-fallback-candidates.ts` keys on provider/model) then drops the now-identical fallback.

The collapse is not new in 2026.10.10. It has been in the core migration since #85341 (May), and the published 2026.9.7 Doctor produces the same result for the same config (table below). a5d10f965731 fixed the case where a single `model` or `subagents.model` selection contains both spellings. This PR replaces that check with one that covers every ref whose runtime the pin decides:

- the scope's primary, fallbacks, heartbeat, and subagent selections;
- selections the agent inherits from `agents.defaults`;
- defaults selections, whose pin reaches every agent;
- an allowlist that names both spellings, or a model map that does when the scope also selects or allows the canonical ref (a canonical map key alone is metadata).

A canonical ref that already resolves to the CLI runtime (exact pin, `anthropic/*` wildcard, provider pin) still migrates. Sign-in-seeded maps that contain only legacy keys also still migrate (the #124952 test is unchanged). Retention errs toward keeping refs: retained legacy refs still run, while a wrong rewrite changes billing.

The Anthropic plugin's `anthropic/*` wildcard repair (#168074) keys on a CLI-pinned default primary. On affected configs, the collapse in the same Doctor pass created that pin, so the wildcard followed. With the collapse fixed, the wildcard repair no longer fires on these configs (table, `candidate` column).

## Evidence

**Failing-first class test.** The retained-ref cases now share one table in `legacy-model-reference-migration.test.ts`; 8 new cases in `legacy-model-reference-migration.test.ts` fail on `origin/main` 11c8f236b330 and pass here: subagent/heartbeat CLI model beside an API primary, agent heartbeat beside its own or an inherited API primary, defaults CLI heartbeat beside an agent API primary, model map and allowlist with both spellings, and the Gemini CLI equivalent. 3 controls migrate both before and after: different model, canonical already CLI-pinned, separate agents. Related files (`legacy-config-migrate{,.e2e}`, `legacy-config-compat`, `runtime.models`, `runtime.cli-backends`, `legacy-runtime-model-policy.wildcards`, `legacy-runtime-session-migration`, `extensions/anthropic/{cli-migration,doctor-contract-api}`, `doctor-legacy-config.migrations`) pass. The first CI run caught a canonical model-map key with no direct use being treated as a second route; fixed in d751f239. The PR adds no net test lines. `tsgo:core`, oxlint, and format pass.

**Doctor `--fix` on 2026.9.7-authored configs** (isolated HOME/state, published npm packages; candidate via `pnpm openclaw`):

| Config (same model on both routes) | 2026.9.7 | 2026.10.10 | 2026.11.5-beta.1 | candidate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| defaults: API primary + `claude-cli` fallback | collapsed | collapsed + `anthropic/*`→CLI | collapsed + wildcard | kept, warning |
| agent: API primary + `claude-cli` fallback | collapsed | collapsed | collapsed | kept, warning |
| API primary + `claude-cli` subagents model | collapsed | collapsed + wildcard | collapsed + wildcard | kept, warning |
| API primary + `claude-cli` heartbeat model | — | collapsed + wildcard | collapsed + wildcard | kept (moved verbatim into the heartbeat automation), warning |
| allowlist with both spellings | — | collapsed + wildcard | unchanged; Doctor exited 1 (cause not investigated) | kept, warning |
| model map with both spellings | — | aliases merged, CLI pin + wildcard | same | kept, warning |
| docs example: different CLI fallback model | migrated | migrated | migrated | migrated (unchanged) |
| separate agents per route | — | migrated | migrated | migrated (unchanged) |

(2026.11.5-beta.1 predates a5d10f965731; "—" = not run on that version.)

**Live turn** (`pnpm openclaw agent exec --config <migrated config> --json`, invalid `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, real Claude Code login, isolated state):

- Candidate-migrated config: `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 status=401` → `decision=fallback_model reason=auth` → `candidate=claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5` → `candidate_succeeded`, final `ROUTE-OK`.
- 2026.10.10-migrated config: no API attempt; the primary runs on `claude-cli` directly.

**Review.** autoreview (branch vs `origin/main`, P2) on Claude Fable 5, because the Codex route failed live auth: scoped-clean, no findings. Two residual over-retention risks were noted, both on the safe side.

**Gaps.** I did not run a full `openclaw update --tag file:<candidate.tgz>` cell from published 2026.9.7. The table uses the same Doctor `--fix` path the update's fresh-Doctor phase runs. Hosted CI pending.

prs.title: fix(dns): dns setup prints only "The CLI command failed." when no domain is configured
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw dns setup` prints only "The CLI command failed. For help, run `openclaw doctor`." when no discovery domain is configured, when `--domain` is not a valid DNS name, and when `--apply` runs off macOS or without a tailnet IP. Doctor can't fix any of these; the command already has a message that says what to do, but it never reaches the terminal.

## User Impact

User impact: those four refusals now print their existing reason, for example "No wide-area domain configured. Set discovery.wideArea.domain or pass --domain." Exit status stays 1, the wording is unchanged, and successful plans and `--apply` runs behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The checks throw plain `Error`s, which the root renderer treats as unexpected and hides. They now go through the existing `throwExpectedCliError`, the same classification used for the proxy, transcripts and pairing refusals in #191295 and #189993. The invalid-domain error comes from `normalizeWideAreaDomain`, so `dns setup` catches it at the call that already exists to surface it and rethrows the same message. Subprocess failures during `--apply` (brew, sudo) are left as they are.

## Evidence

Ran from source (`pnpm openclaw`, which builds first) on macOS, Node 26.7.0, with a fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and no discovery domain configured.

Before (`main` at ad5218d25d):
```
$ openclaw dns setup
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
$ openclaw dns setup --domain bad..name
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
```

After (this branch):
```
$ openclaw dns setup
No wide-area domain configured. Set discovery.wideArea.domain or pass --domain.
$ openclaw dns setup --domain bad..name
wide-area discovery domain must be a valid DNS name
```
With the fix both exit 1. I didn't run the two `--apply` refusals against the real CLI, since on a Mac with a domain set `--apply` goes on to brew and sudo; the tests below cover them.

Tests:
A new `dns setup refusals` case in `src/cli/dns-cli.test.ts` runs each refusal through `registerDnsCli` and the real `formatCliFailureLines`, and checks the output is exactly the existing message and that no subprocess starts. The `widearea-dns` mock now spreads the real module, so domain validation runs for real; zone paths, zone writes and tailnet addresses stay synthetic.

- `pnpm test src/cli/dns-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` with the fix: 10 passed. On `main` the four new refusal cases fail (4 failed, 6 passed): each error is a plain `Error` and renders as the generic failure.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on the changed files: clean.



- Test-line budget: the regression tests add 69 net lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/dns-setup-reasons.txt`. Rebased on current `main`.
