prs.title: fix(macos): onboarding "Set up later" takes down a Gateway installed outside the app
prs.body:
Closes #187841

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS app's onboarding deletes `gateway.mode` from `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` when the user clicks **Set up later** on "Where should your assistant live?", and a Gateway that was installed outside the app (CLI LaunchAgent) restarts on the change and then refuses to start ("Gateway start blocked: existing config is missing gateway.mode", EX_CONFIG loop) until someone sets the mode back by hand.

## User Impact

User impact: "Set up later" no longer edits `openclaw.json`. A Gateway already running from that file keeps running, and the app still comes back with no primary Gateway on the next launch until the user picks one, as #141872 intended. If the file's gateway section is later changed by another writer (CLI `onboard`, `config set gateway.mode …`), the file wins again. The page caption now says that a Gateway installed outside the app keeps running (the app still stops its own Gateway on that click, as before). `openclaw-mac primary clear` is unchanged: it is an explicit operator command and still removes the mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

The app and the Gateway read a missing `gateway.mode` in opposite ways. The app wrote it to mean "no primary chosen yet", because `ConnectionModeResolver` lets the file's mode outrank the app's own stored mode on launch, so deleting the line was the only way the choice survived a relaunch (#141872). The Gateway treats the same missing line as a clobbered config and refuses to start. The app's stop path already leaves an external Gateway alone (`GatewayProcessManager.stop()` returns early for `Installation.external`); the write path had no such check.

The deferred choice now lives in the app's defaults (`openclaw.primaryGatewayDeferredFingerprint`), bound to a SHA-256 digest of the file's `gateway` section (a digest, not the JSON: that section carries Gateway credentials, and the record must not). `ConnectionModeResolver` consults it before the file, `AppState.syncedGatewayRoot` leaves the file untouched for an unconfigured primary, and the re-read after a save honours the record instead of snapping the app back to the file's mode. Any change to the gateway section retires the record, and so does an explicit selection through the control CLI (`primary set` / `primary clear`) even when it leaves the file as it is. Stored data is unchanged: the record is one new additive defaults key (`Data`, 32 bytes); no existing key, file or Keychain item changes meaning or shape, and an app without the record resolves exactly as before (`ConnectionModeResolverDeferralTests › without a deferral the file mode wins…`). The live run below launched this build over defaults, config file and Keychain items written by the previous build on the same Mac. The release-to-fix upgrade run below launched this branch, packaged under the release bundle id, over the state the official 2026.10.10 app and CLI had written: settings, config and agent database carried over. The `removesGatewayMode` result of the onboarding sync is gone; the saver's `allowGatewayModeRemoval` stays for the CLI clear path.

## Evidence

### Full-product repro on main

`main` 7511f52280e, app and CLI built from source on an isolated Mac (Apple M4, macOS 27): `openclaw gateway install` (LaunchAgent, `gateway.mode: "local"`, loopback, token auth), app onboarding unseen, config file hashed every second. Page shows "On this Mac — Existing gateway detected (node pid 42297). Will attach.". **Set up later** at 23:06:30 IST (3 Nov):

```
# config watcher (hash, gateway.mode), the only write is the app's
230634  e3d22137ecab2089764e1a2a399d641d  mode=None      <- 23:06:34, Set up later
# ~/.openclaw/logs/config-audit.jsonl (the app's own write audit)
2026-11-03T17:36:33Z config.write success gatewayModeBefore=local gatewayModeAfter=null argv=[.../apps/macos/.build/debug/OpenClaw]
# Gateway log
[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (gateway.mode)
Gateway start blocked: existing config is missing gateway.mode. Treat this as suspicious or clobbered config. ...
# launchctl print gui/501/ai.openclaw.gateway
	state = spawn scheduled
	last exit code = 78: EX_CONFIG
```

![main: the page with "Existing gateway detected … Will attach."](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sukhdeepjohar/openclaw/proof-assets/187841/main-page-will-attach.png)
![main: after Set up later, old caption, Gateway already restarting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sukhdeepjohar/openclaw/proof-assets/187841/main-after-set-up-later.png)

`openclaw.json.clobbered.<ts>` vs `openclaw.json.last-good`: only `gateway.mode` gone plus the app's `meta.lastTouchedVersion` stamp. Every other control on the page (Next with On this Mac through a verified model to Finish, both remote editors cancelled, window close; plain token and store SecretRef) left the file alone. Recovery as in the report: `openclaw config set gateway.mode local` + kickstart.

### Live run, with this change (same rig, same LaunchAgent, Gateway pid 3383 throughout)

Fixed app built from this branch's patch on the same tree; Gateway untouched; app state read with the app's own control CLI.

```
15:33:08  Set up later
  cfgwatch: 121201 ab30ca9474bce9a15a54611a4b5c6e3b mode=local      <- hash unchanged since 12:12
  launchctl: state = running; pid = 3383; last exit code = 0
  config-audit.jsonl: no new config.write line
  defaults: openclaw.connectionMode = unconfigured; openclaw.primaryGatewayDeferredFingerprint = <152 bytes>
15:33:51  quit + relaunch
  cfgwatch: unchanged; launchctl: pid = 3383
  openclaw-mac primary show --json --no-launch
  {"connection":{"state":"disconnected"},"mode":"unconfigured","transport":null,"tunnel":{"running":false},"url":""}
15:38:44  openclaw config set gateway.reload.mode hybrid      <- another writer edits the gateway section
  Updated gateway.reload.mode. No gateway restart needed.
  cfgwatch: 153844 1ac8109de5e91ae6eacce38b6a27b7c8 mode=local; launchctl: pid = 3383
  defaults: openclaw.connectionMode = local; deferral record removed
  openclaw-mac primary show --json --no-launch
  {"connection":{"gatewayVersion":"2026.10.10","state":"connected"},"mode":"local","transport":null,"tunnel":{"running":false},"url":"ws://127.0.0.1:18789"}
```

Fix reverted (the same binary with the old behaviour, 3 Nov table above): the click deletes the mode and the Gateway loops on EX_CONFIG.

![fix: the same page before the click](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sukhdeepjohar/openclaw/proof-assets/187841/fix-page-before-click.png)
![fix: after Set up later, new caption (an earlier wording of it; the final caption says "a Gateway installed outside the app keeps running", because the app still stops its own), Gateway pid 3383 still running](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sukhdeepjohar/openclaw/proof-assets/187841/fix-after-set-up-later-caption.png)
![fix: wizard after relaunch, app unconfigured per the control CLI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sukhdeepjohar/openclaw/proof-assets/187841/fix-relaunch.png) Note: after a relaunch the wizard pre-highlights "On this Mac" whenever the app is undecided, on `main` and here alike, so the app's control CLI is the signal for the deferred state, not the page.

### Upgrade from the latest release (2026.10.10) to this build, settings intact

Same Mac. The official `OpenClaw-2026.10.10-arm64.dmg` (bundle id `ai.openclaw.mac`, Developer ID) installed to `~/Applications`, with the published `openclaw@2026.10.10` CLI's own LaunchAgent on a fresh state directory (`gateway.mode: "local"`, port 18789, token auth, Ollama model). The release app's wizard was completed (On this Mac → model verified → Finish), so the "existing state" is the release's own: defaults under `ai.openclaw.mac`, the config file, the agent database at schema 27, the Keychain registries. Then the upgrade: the Gateway side moved to this tree's build (`openclaw doctor --fix` migrated the agent database 27 → 40), and the app bundle was replaced by this branch packaged with `scripts/package-mac-app.sh` under the same bundle id (ad-hoc signed; a release build is Developer ID signed).

```
##### before (release app 2026.10.10, pid 75184)
config: c0ab56485032455a2bcce119c9e2ce14  mode=local port=18789 model=ollama/qwen2.5:0.5b
gateway: state = running; pid = 74946 (openclaw@2026.10.10 LaunchAgent)
defaults(ai.openclaw.mac): openclaw.lastLaunchedAppVersion = "2026.10.10"; openclaw.onboardingSeen = 1; openclaw.onboardingVersion = 8
openclaw-mac status: {"app":{"version":"2026.10.10"},"primary":{"connection":{"gatewayVersion":"2026.10.10","state":"connected"},"mode":"local","url":"ws://127.0.0.1:18789"}}

##### after swap: this branch packaged as ai.openclaw.mac (Signature=adhoc), Gateway from this tree on the same state dir (pid 87602)
17:56:06  no wizard shown; same defaults: onboardingSeen = 1; onboardingVersion = 8; lastLaunchedAppVersion = "2026.10.10"
config: 45efd6277461db7bdd99f5e4c11e7781  mode=local port=18789 model=ollama/qwen2.5:0.5b   (hash differs only by doctor's wizard.lastRun* stamp and plugins.entries.ollama.enabled; no app write: config-audit.jsonl empty)
openclaw-mac status: {"primary":{"connection":{"gatewayVersion":"2026.10.10","state":"connected"},"mode":"local","url":"ws://127.0.0.1:18789"}}

##### onboarding re-entered (defaults onboardingSeen/onboardingVersion removed, relaunch) → Set up later  17:57:56
config: 45efd6277461db7bdd99f5e4c11e7781 (unchanged)   gateway: pid = 87602 running
defaults: openclaw.connectionMode = unconfigured; openclaw.primaryGatewayDeferredFingerprint = <32 bytes>
openclaw-mac status: {"primary":{"connection":{"state":"disconnected"},"mode":"unconfigured"}}

##### relaunch  17:58:46
config unchanged; gateway pid = 87602; openclaw-mac status: "mode":"unconfigured"; deferral record still 32 bytes
```

![release 2026.10.10: gateway page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sukhdeepjohar/openclaw/proof-assets/187841/upgrade-0-release-2026.10.10-gateway-page.png)
![release 2026.10.10: onboarding finished, dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sukhdeepjohar/openclaw/proof-assets/187841/upgrade-1-release-2026.10.10-onboarded.png)
![this build over the release's state: after Set up later, new caption, Gateway alive](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sukhdeepjohar/openclaw/proof-assets/187841/upgrade-2-fixed-build-after-set-up-later.png)
![this build: relaunch, app undecided, file untouched](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sukhdeepjohar/openclaw/proof-assets/187841/upgrade-3-fixed-build-relaunch.png)

Two harness notes. The ad-hoc signature of the test bundle differs from the release's Developer ID, so macOS re-prompts for the release app's Keychain registries (`ai.openclaw.gateway-profiles`, `ai.openclaw.onboarding-route-binding`); they were removed and recreated by the new build. And the new app refused to start until the Gateway on the same state directory was upgraded too ("OpenClaw client credentials need recovery", resolved by `openclaw doctor --fix` with the matching CLI), which is the documented upgrade order and unrelated to this change. A real Sparkle upgrade keeps the signature and updates both sides together.

### Tests (`swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter …`)

- `AppStateRemoteConfigTests` › `set up later leaves the config file untouched and holds across re-reads` (file mode local / remote): no saver call, file byte-identical, app stays unconfigured through a same-file re-read, follows the file after a gateway-section edit. The historical implementation calls the saver with `allowGatewayModeRemoval: true` and removes the mode. See the red-run limitation below; this was not executed on the unchanged base.
- `AppStateRemoteConfigTests` › `explicit primary selection retires a deferral without a file change`: after "Set up later", `setPrimaryGateway(.local)` on a file that already says local writes nothing, sets local, and a re-read keeps it.
- `ConnectionModeResolverDeferralTests` › `the deferral record is a digest and carries no credential bytes`: 32-byte digest, no token bytes, changes when a token rotates.
- `ConnectionModeResolverDeferralTests` (3 more): a matching record resolves to unconfigured with source `.deferredPrimary`; meta-only changes do not retire it; a gateway-section edit does; without a record the file mode wins over a stored unconfigured mode (unchanged behaviour). The first two depend on the new deferral API and cannot be run unchanged on base.
- `AppStateGatewaySyncDraftTests` › `unconfigured draft keeps gateway.mode and gateway.remote` replaces #141872's `unconfigured draft authorizes only an owned mode removal`; `configured drafts write their mode` replaces `configured drafts never authorize mode removal`. `CLI primary saves authorize removal only for an explicit clear` keeps the CLI arms of #141872's permission test.
- Focused run with the change: `AppStateRemoteConfigTests`, `AppStateGatewaySyncDraftTests`, `ConnectionModeResolverDeferralTests`, `OnboardingViewSmokeTests`, `GatewayEndpointStoreTests`, `OnboardingFirstRunTests`, `PrimaryGatewayControlConfigurationTests`, `OpenClawConfigFileTests` (the CLI clear path, unchanged): 183 of 183 pass in 8 suites. Red run (the new test file does not compile on the untouched base, so the old behaviour was stubbed back in behind the new API (resolver ignores the record, sync removes the mode and remote, re-read ignores the record): `set up later leaves the config file untouched…` (both arms), `unconfigured draft keeps gateway.mode and gateway.remote` (all four arms) and `deferred primary outranks the file…` fail, 14 issues; the other tests in those suites still pass).

Checks: `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --product OpenClaw` clean; `scripts/format-swift.sh macos`: 0 files need formatting; `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos`: 2 violations, both pre-existing file-length limits in untouched files (`DashboardManager.swift`, `GatewayConnection.swift`); `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` regenerated `apps/.i18n/native-source.json` for the one changed string and `verify` passes.

Not in this PR: **On another computer → Save** also rewrites the file (`gateway.mode: "remote"`), and a Gateway running from it dies the same way; that write is the app's intended meaning ("this Mac is a client") and is noted on the issue for a product decision.

Proof artifice: isolated Mac, test token, LaunchAgent from a source checkout; a local Ollama model only to reach Finish on the repro side.



## Preparation review and limitations

The existing no-primary contract survives relaunch. Merely omitting the configuration write is incomplete: ConnectionModeResolver gives the file mode precedence, so a reread or relaunch selects that Gateway again. The proposed app-local digest preserves deferral without clearing another process's configuration, and retires it after a changed Gateway section or explicit primary selection. This is the recommended shape if the added persisted preference is retained. Preparation also repaired a reconciliation bug: an unchanged file must not acknowledge the app-only deferral before the existing primary-window cleanup runs. The existing regression now checks that pending mode intent survives a file reread until sync. Net diff: production +74 lines, generated native inventory +1 line, tests +134 lines. The growth implements durable app-only intent and reconciliation; removing it requires changing the existing relaunch behavior.

PROOF GAP: the reported red run restored historical behavior behind new APIs; it was not an execution of the unchanged base. The added behavior needs a base-compatible red regression before treating that claim as verified. The reported 183 passing native tests and live/upgrade traces are contributor evidence. No native code was executed during this preparation because contributor execution on the maintainer Mac is outside this lane's boundary. The upgrade exercise recreated Keychain registries under an ad-hoc signature; it does not prove signature-preserving upgrade behavior.

The original head’s CI [41839278352](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41839278352) succeeded; its native Swift matrix was skipped, so it is not a fresh execution of the added native tests. The shown screenshots were inspected; they illustrate the behavior, with an earlier wording of the new caption. Contributor: @sukhdeepjohar.

Open design question for landing: retain the new app-local persisted deferral record, or intentionally change the previously supported relaunch behavior? Keeping the record is recommended; dropping only the write is incomplete. Before landing, establish a true base-red run with a base-compatible `AppStateGatewaySyncDraftTests` case.

Preparation review: the full six-file candidate against main `3816bcb3dea1` passed independent P0–P2 review after the reconciliation repair. The review also caught and corrected the new assertion to use the existing string-valued helper. The contributor commit is retained; main was merged without conflicts. Native tests remain delegated to CI.

Prepared head: `31a421637d6c08cb0c6d226bda3f3f2ecf17cc41`. The reconciliation repair and its assertion have not been executed natively during preparation; the previous contributor green run predates these additions. New exact-head CI [41972415539](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41972415539) succeeded. Native i18n passed; both Swift jobs were skipped, so this does not establish native compilation or execution of the added assertions. The original untouched-base red-run gap remains explicit above.

Related: #193195

## What Problem This Solves

Generated release notes can mistakenly thank the known automation account `tideclaw-bot` as a human contributor.

## User Impact

Release notes omit that automation identity while preserving verified human credit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add the identity to the existing exclusion set shared by author, coauthor and recorded-credit paths. Extend the existing regression without broad suffix-based filtering or another policy owner. Production grows by one line; tests have zero net line growth. Provenance and publication rules are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact base: `dd327c741ebf1b054137d570eeac087b1b5684a8`; reviewed head: `ca24da23de6c557e73861012761f6c50db02c196`. Regression before fix fails as intended: expected false, received true.
- All 129 verifier tests pass after the fix; independently rerun by the parent reviewer.
- Focused type-aware lint, scripts-test typecheck, two-file formatting and whitespace checks pass. Private checkout used a physical frozen-lockfile install.
- Local autoreview attempted with both complete changed files and P0–P2 scope; preparation completed but the Codex executable was unavailable. No successful helper review is claimed. Independent P0–P2 source review found no findings after inspecting eligibility and its author, coauthor, reporter and historical-credit consumers.
- Earlier release-target regeneration evidence is not presented as an exact-main CLI run. No generated notes, security provenance or publication state changed here.

Arbitrary `-bot` handles remain unaffected. Release-note regeneration remains owned by the release workflow.

prs.title: perf(sessions): reuse stored reference facts during deletion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session deletion repeats JSON validation and optional-reference checks while finding surviving owners of retained transcript generations.

## User Impact

This modest optimization reduces SQLite CPU work during deletion without changing which sessions or transcript generations survive. There are no schema, index, retention, or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The canonical entry writer and migration already maintain `has_optional_references` alongside the stored entry. Consume that fact instead of re-deriving it. Plain IDs avoid JSON validation; optional-reference rows skip the unsuccessful plain-row checks before using the existing parser/projection. Raw-ID, malformed-reference, timestamp, encoding, and deterministic owner-selection behavior remain intact.

Runtime source shrinks by two lines. The 147-line benchmark and two-line test allocation record account for the net +147 non-test lines; they make the synthetic measurement and remaining-row digest reproducible; the regression protects the eliminated JSON work. No cache or alternate owner was introduced.

## Evidence

The slow statement fingerprint `5274521810ae205f` maps exactly to `readSessionReferenceOwners`. EXPLAIN shows a `session_nodes` scan, two materialized CTEs, and a sort. The scan remains; this PR removes repeated parsing within it. Removing materialization or introducing a JSONB input stage used more CPU in exploratory measurements, so neither is included.

Synthetic owner workload: 10,000 sessions, 16 KiB entry payloads, 10% optional references, 100-deep parent chains, and 79,920 transcript events. It measures absent-owner lookups; optional rows benefit from skipping redundant plain-row checks. The regression separately covers the plain-row shortcut.

| Measurement | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Untraced CPU/read, AB pair (1,000 per side) | 53.67 ms | 52.16 ms (-2.8%) |
| Untraced CPU/read, BA pair (1,000 per side) | 53.42 ms | 53.11 ms (-0.6%) |
| Mean untraced CPU/read (2,000 per side) | 53.55 ms | 52.64 ms (-1.7%) |
| Sampled V8 allocation/read, 100 iterations per side | 3,086,776 B | 3,088,960 B (+0.07%, effectively flat) |
| Plain-row JSON validation calls | 1 | 0 |

Allocation sampling includes collected objects and excludes SQLite native allocation. Traced CPU is not used as a timing gate. Host load varied heavily (first CPU arm started at 97.5; second at 148.2), so elapsed time is not a latency claim. The reverse pair started at load 111.5 (candidate) and 131.3 (base). Both CPU pairs favor the candidate; wall time remains host-load context.

After actual `deleteSessionEntryRows` calls, including shared-generation rehoming, both revisions leave 9,997 nodes, 9,998 windows, and 77,916 transcript events. Remaining-row SHA-256 is identical: `f45bfc839ce858d4b6c1cf559dddd89e7d5d2b8f4c994237617dfceb349ad4c6`.

Reproduce with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-lifecycle-delete-measure.ts --output .local/delete-proof --iterations 1000`; use a fresh output directory and `--allocation --iterations 100` for the separate allocation pass.

Validation: the new regression fails on base (one validation instead of zero) and passes on candidate. Focused exact-read and deletion-receipt tests: 46 passed, one inherited local Bun UTF-16 exclusion failure also reproduced on unchanged production source. Scoped lint, formatting, root-script and session-test typechecks, and export-collision guard passed. The eager-import closure guard passed. The unchanged Darwin-input case in the PR-wrapper closure file timed out at 120 seconds both in the combined run (39 passed, one timed out) and a focused replay (three passed, one timed out); no assertion or timeout was weakened.

Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): clean P0–P2 review of the complete diff and predicate/writer/deletion contracts. The helper refused the requested provider route because it does not match operator configuration; configuration was left unchanged.

Measurements used base `11c8f236b330e8f51c03331dcd6ae0c661080e7b` and the reviewed patch; the subsequent main rebase did not change the predicate, reference query, or agent schema.

This is a synchronous worker query simplification. No full Gateway stress was run under the scoped redundant-work-deletion proof rule; no claim is made about Gateway tail latency, main-thread CPU, or audit-writer latency.

Exact-head CI: [run 41970529244](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41970529244) is blocked by [checks-fast-baseline-ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41970529244/job/127058138239), specifically the inherited test-line ceiling debt. The PR adds 29 test lines and exactly 29 lines of allocation. CI reports 6,479,225 lines against a 6,479,132 ceiling, still 93 over. Re-running the guard against the unchanged parent test tree (`2270152d224ae48de9a10f3fe26b4c594ac9e87d`) reports 6,479,093 lines against 6,479,000, also 93 over, with net delta zero. No shared ceiling was raised. The exact-head production/test typechecks, lint, and config-boundary review passed; downstream test jobs are skipped behind the failing gate. PostgreSQL conformance is still running. This PR remains ready and unmerged; CI is not green.

prs.title: fix(doctor): 2026.10.10 update refuses when an imported audit archive lost its sanitized companion (backport #186998)
prs.body:
Related: #186974
Backport of #186998 (`4a0ab0928cc`) to `release/2026.10.10`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on 2026.10.10 betas, `openclaw doctor --fix`, and so an update, refuses at the `audit-logs` migration and blocks every later repair when an already-imported legacy config-audit archive is re-detected and its sanitized companion is gone.

## User Impact

User impact: a 2026.10.10 update on a host in that state finishes instead of refusing and rolling back. Real unimported records still refuse with the backup-restoration guidance, as on main.

## Why This Change Was Made

#186998 fixed this on main on 10-28, after `release/2026.10.10` was cut. It is not in beta.4, beta.5 or the branch tip `1cdcfc00d84`, by ancestry and by subject. The production change and docs here have the same patch-id as main's (`051fd155b6deec28`), and the release branch's two audit source files are identical to beta.4's, so they apply as is.

main refactored both audit test files after the cut. This keeps the release branch's `state-migrations.audit-logs.test.ts` and adds main's two missing-companion cases to `state-migrations.audit-skips.test.ts`. It also adds a case for the shape I hit (same bytes, size and mtime under a new file identity), and a Doctor-runner case for the other half of the rule: an unimported record with the companion gone still refuses.

## Evidence

- **Hit on a real 2026.10.10-beta.4 update on one of my macOS gateways (2026-10-31 04:07Z).** Doctor ran 434 s and exited 1:
  ```
  Failing check audit-logs (step-refused): Skipped config audit log recovery because its sanitized archive is missing or truncated
  Failing check managed-outgoing-images (blocked-by-prior-refusal): Migration step "managed-outgoing-images" was not run because prior step "audit-logs" refused execution.
  ```
  `apns-registrations`, `exec-approvals` and `mcp-oauth` were blocked the same way, and the update rolled back.
- **Cause, read-only on that host's state.** The raw-archive checkpoint (`migration.legacy-audit-raw`) records `dev 16777231, ino 19235396, size 478022, recordCount 0`. The file now reads `dev 16777230` with the same inode, size and mtime, and `config-audit.jsonl.migrated.sanitized` does not exist. Only the device number moved, so detection stopped matching and the step refused although nothing remained to import.
- The same production change on the same data: with #186998 carried onto beta.4 (same patch-id as this PR), doctor on that host logged `Skipped config audit log recovery because its sanitized companion is missing and no records remain to import; left ~/.openclaw/logs/config-audit.jsonl.migrated.raw in place.`, ran every later step, and the update finished with rc 0 at 07:30Z.
- Installed-package upgrade, latest stable (npm `openclaw@2026.10.9`, `8b18b55`) to this branch's build at `23e85739821`. Run with an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `--profile upgradeproof` and port 29789, and `doctor --fix --non-interactive` each time. No launchd label or LaunchAgent was added on the host.
  1. 2026.10.9 on a seeded legacy `logs/config-audit.jsonl` of 3 `config.write` records: exit 0, `Migrated config audit log -> shared SQLite state (3 new row(s))`. Afterwards the raw archive's sha256 is `f6cc44861440c55a…`, the checkpoint reads `ino 185071743, size 423, recordCount 0`, the `config-audit` history holds 5 rows (the 3 legacy rows hash to `ab40ca823113eea8…`), and `openclaw.json` hashes to `2ccd48ad6b26cc54…`.
  2. The raw archive is copied beside itself and renamed over (ino `185071743` -> `185071842`, same size and mtime_ns), and the sanitized companion is removed.
  3. 2026.10.9 again: exit 1. `audit-logs (step-refused): Skipped config audit log recovery because its sanitized archive is missing or truncated`, and `managed-outgoing-images`, `apns-registrations`, `exec-approvals` and `mcp-oauth` are blocked by the prior refusal.
  4. This branch on the same state: exit 0, `Skipped config audit log recovery because its sanitized companion is missing and no records remain to import; left <state>/logs/config-audit.jsonl.migrated.raw in place.`, and `Doctor complete.` A second run: exit 0, the same skip.
  5. After steps 3, 4 and 5, every value from step 1 is unchanged: the raw sha256, the checkpoint row, the 5 history rows with the same legacy hash, and the `openclaw.json` hash.
  6. This branch's `doctor --lint` over that state ran 39 checks. Its 3 findings are environment warnings (browser cookie import, a Codex route for the default model, no gateway auth token); none concern state or migrations.
- Tests on this branch at `23e85739821` (Node 26.12.1):
  - `pnpm test src/infra/state-migrations.audit-skips.test.ts src/infra/state-migrations.audit-logs.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 52 passed, 0 failed.
  - Control: with `state-migrations.audit-logs.ts` and `state-migrations.audit-sanitized.ts` reverted to the branch tip, 4 failed and 10 passed in `audit-skips`. The three skip cases get `outcome: "refused"` with `Skipped config audit log recovery because its sanitized archive is missing or truncated`, the message from the real host. The refusal case gets that same undifferentiated message instead of `the raw archive contains unimported records`.
  - The refusal case also checks that nothing is imported and that the raw bytes and checkpoint are unchanged.
  - `pnpm tsgo:all` exited 0. oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the changed files.
- Gap: a unit test cannot move `st_dev`, so the moved-file case changes the inode instead. The copy is written beside the original and renamed over it, so it cannot reuse the inode. The test asserts the premise: a different inode with the same size and mtime.

prs.title: fix(update): update replaces a still-serving install, then rolls back, when PostgreSQL backup cannot run
prs.body:
Related: #193163

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update` replaces the install of a Gateway that is still serving, then fails the database backup and rolls back, when the state stores use PostgreSQL and the Gateway runs under a service the updater does not stop (for example a custom system LaunchDaemon).

## User Impact

User impact: with PostgreSQL state stores and a Gateway the updater cannot stop, the update now refuses before it changes anything. The install stays as it was, the Gateway keeps serving, and the message says to stop the Gateway through its service owner and rerun the update. Before this change, each attempt swapped the checkout under the running Gateway, failed, rolled back, and caused two unclean Gateway restarts.

Updates where the updater stops the Gateway itself, or where no PostgreSQL family is configured, behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The pre-migration database backup runs after activation has replaced the install. For PostgreSQL families that backup needs exclusive state ownership and deliberately refuses without it (`PostgreSQL update capture requires exclusive ownership`). With a Gateway still serving, that refusal was certain, but it was only discovered after the swap. The failure report showed it as `State schema inspection failed (exit): [redacted-diagnostic]` because the plain message carries no diagnostic code.

The update now checks the same ownership in the shared pre-activation step, right after the service stop and the post-stop checks, and refuses with `database-engine-preflight` while nothing has changed. The backup and the new check share one ownership probe, so the two cannot drift apart. The backup worker keeps its own refusal as the backstop. A Gateway that starts between the check and the backup still hits that later refusal, which is the existing behavior. This change does not try to close that window.

This change covers part (a) of the issue. Part (b), Gateway shutdown loading hashed chunks after an in-place swap, is not addressed here.

<details><summary>Root cause details</summary>

- Git updates call `onTransaction` (database capture) after `git-checkout` and `git-runtime-activation` in `src/infra/update-runner-git.ts`.
- `captureUpdateDatabases` tries the `sqlite-maintenance` gateway lock. While a Gateway holds state ownership, the lock is unavailable, so `postgresOffline` is false.
- `createUpdateDatabaseBackupInProcess` then throws the exclusive-ownership refusal for any PostgreSQL source. An existing test in `update-database-backup-engine.test.ts` pins that refusal.
- The `readGeneration()` path mentioned in the issue is not what fails. The stopped path also spawns the inspection worker after the swap and succeeds, so the worker's module resolution is not the cause either.

</details>

## Evidence

- New test in `update-command-execution.test.ts` covers Git and package installs, with state ownership held by a serving Gateway and free.
  - On `main` with only the test added, both "held" cases fail: the install is replaced (`expected [ 'install-replaced' ] to deeply equal []`). Both "free" cases pass.
  - With the fix, all four pass. The "held" cases end with `mutationStarted: false` and reason `database-engine-preflight`, and the install is never replaced.
- Consumer tests for the touched modules pass: 13 files (update execution, database rollback and retention, package, Git snapshot, foreground, admission, maintenance contention, original service, initial admission, failure report, client credential update, Doctor maintenance database writes), 225 passed, 5 skipped.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck (core and core tests), lint, import cycles, dead exports and the database ratchets pass. The format lane flagged one import order, which is fixed, and the format check passes on all changed files.
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`: this PR adds 78 test lines with a matching 78-line allocation. The check still reports the tree over its ceiling because `main` is already 93 lines over (on `main` it passes only because the net delta is 0).
- Not run: an end-to-end update of a real Gateway on PostgreSQL. The original failure reproduced on 3 of 3 attempts with a Git install, the dev channel, and a custom system LaunchDaemon; this change has not been re-run against that setup.

prs.title: chore: update mature dependencies and oxlint
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw misses maintained dependency, toolchain, and linter releases until each upgrade is qualified, and oxlint 1.89 reports new errors that the pinned Bun analyzer does not, failing CI lint parity.

## User Impact

User impact: no configuration migration or user action. Refreshes MCP, ACP, Mistral, Matrix, IMAP auth, QA, media, native, and tooling dependencies and moves oxlint to 1.89.0, keeping ACP wire behavior and Matrix crypto routing unchanged. Holds below; not a vulnerability-free-graph claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

Audit **2026-10-31T16:54:00Z**; inclusive cutoff **2026-10-24T16:54:00Z** for every introduced version, including transitives. No new release-age exception, override, patch, cast, lint disable, weakened test, or removed feature; locks come from pnpm, cargo and bundler. #187578 (undici) and #189308 (node-domexception) are not duplicated.

**oxlint 1.88.0 → 1.89.0** ([release](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/releases/tag/oxlint_v1.89.0)): standalone oxlint reported 31 source errors (23 core/UI, 8 extensions) and 59 generated-validator errors that Bun did not. Fixed at the source:

- `/=+$/` → equivalent `/[=]+$/`; `else { if }` → `else if`; statement-bodied setters; a local request key instead of a parameter write.
- `workspace.ts` calls `Minimatch#match`, not `String#match`: it passes `partial = false` explicitly (the matcher's existing default) instead of a `RegExp#test` rewrite.
- TypeBox counting reducers (`oneOf`, `minContains`/`maxContains`, bundled `Counted`) returned `++result`, a dead write to the callback parameter. The generator now emits the equivalent `result + 1`, including esbuild-renamed nested accumulators (`result2`), and rejects any other increment; outputs are regenerated. Codex validators drop their `no-param-reassign` disable.

**Migrations** (consumers adapted):

- **@agentclientprotocol/sdk 1.9.0 → 2.0.2** ([2.0.0](https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/typescript-sdk/releases/tag/v2.0.0), [migration](https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/typescript-sdk/blob/main/MIGRATION_STABLE_UNSTABLE.md)): removed connection classes; `openclaw acp` builds an `agent()` app with the same methods, the client a `client()` app; stable v1 import retained.
- **@mistralai/mistralai 2.7.0 → 3.2.0** ([3.0.0](https://github.com/mistralai/client-ts/releases/tag/v3.0.0)): breaks only workflow/beta APIs and built-in tool unions; function-tool use unchanged.
- **mailauth 7.3.1 → 8.0.4** ([changelog](https://github.com/postalsys/mailauth/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md)): ESM/TS rebuild, linear multi-signature DKIM. Its exact pins move undici 8.11.2 → 7.30.1 (Node 20 support; includes October undici fixes).
- **matrix-js-sdk 43 → 44** ([release](https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-js-sdk/releases/tag/v44.0.0)): MatrixRTC-only breaks (unused); the existing crypto patch applies unchanged and is still needed.
- **@openclaw/crabline 0.1.31 → 0.2.0** ([release](https://github.com/openclaw/crabline/releases/tag/v0.2.0)): CLI `--version`; existing patch carried unchanged.

**Highlights:** MCP 2.4.0/1.32.2 ([notes](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/releases/tag/v2.4.0); no upgrade-note patterns used); proxyline 0.4.1 keeps socket/pipe requests off network proxies; music-metadata 12.3.0 bounds parser resources; rastermill 0.4.1 recovers after WASM traps; tao 0.37.2/wry 0.57.1 Linux crash fixes; ICU 2.4; fastimage 2.4.3; TypeScript 7.1 nightly 20261024; tsrs 0.18; ignore 7.0.14; werift 0.25.2; Muse 1.4.13; testing-library 1.0.0-rc.2; Vercel CLI 65.2.0 ([changelog](https://github.com/vercel/vercel/blob/main/packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md); only 65.0 break is `traces inspect --json`; our `vcr login` flags still parse); docs plugin snippet typebox 1.4.3 (matches the repo); `@aws-sdk/core` override 3.978.5 (matches the clients' `^3.978.5`). 

**npm 12.2.1** joins the exact bundled-dependency policy: brace-expansion 5.0.12 now meets the override; bundled ip-address 10.7.2 (12.2.0 had 10.5.0) is approved only at that exact path, still below the 10.7.4 override.

### Holds

- **@tanstack/virtual-core stays 3.19.2:** 3.19.7 sizes viewports from the client box. A Logs fixture fixed its 16 Logs cases, but [CI 41239333177](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41239333177) then showed ~130 model-picker failures, including real Chromium (`chat-model-picker.browser.test.tsx`, rows missing after reopen) and composition e2e; main passes. Reproduced locally (9/12 failed); reverted with the fixture.
- tauri-plugin-deep-link 2.6.3 / single-instance 2.5.5: published 2026-10-28, after the cutoff; 2.6.2/2.5.4 stay deferred (2.6.3 fixes a rust-ini compile error).
- Sibling lanes: Anthropic/Vertex 1.x, OpenTelemetry 3 (incl. api 1.10), MXC 1.x, Copilot 1.0.26.
- Swift (transitive; unresolvable until parents release): AXorcist 0.2.3 — Peekaboo 4.9.6 and 4.9.7 both pin `exact: "0.2.2"`; swift-crypto 5 — swift-transformers 1.3.5 and swift-huggingface 0.13 cap `<5.0.0`; swift-huggingface 1.0 — mlx-audio-swift 0.1.6 caps `upToNextMajor(0.8.1)`; yyjson 0.13 — swift-transformers pins `exact: "0.12.0"`. Peekaboo/mlx-audio: Dependabot #188049/#187506.
- convex 1.48 (broker review route), path-to-regexp 9 (outside Express 5), Actions (Dependabot), Go (only post-cutoff releases), parent-constrained Cargo pins.
- joi 18.3.0 under mailauth (fix 18.3.1 is after the cutoff); prod audit high findings drop 9 → 5, none new.

## Evidence

Heads `aeb236d0` and follow-up `f9d52dc7` on main `1df551011c87`; main merge `b96cd1d6` (only conflict: generated gateway predicates, regenerated): frozen install, `tsgo:prod`, validators, decisions/TypeBox tests, CI-mode lint parity on 810 main-changed files (2 inherited `max-lines`) pass.

- **Lint parity:** baseline CI-mode run reproduced the failure (extensions 84 vs 23 diagnostics, core 258 vs 229; extras all new 1.89 errors). After fixes, CI-mode `run-oxlint.mjs` (core, extensions, scripts) on every changed file: 0 errors, parity passed.
- **Typecheck:** `tsgo:prod`, `tsgo:scripts`, `tsgo:test:root|src|packages`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, tooling leaf: passed.
- **Generated:** codex/gateway/UI/static `validators:check` passed (unchanged after the accumulator fix). New generator test covers `oneOf`, bounded `contains`, nested counting and the unsupported-increment refusal; it failed on the first head (nested `result2` rejected) and on main (dead write emitted).
- **Tests** (`run-vitest --maxWorkers=1`): typebox/Vercel/docs 3/45; final-tree UI picker/Logs/smoke 5/38; extension lint-fix consumers 10/280; migration consumers (all `src/acp` units, acpx, Mistral, IMAP, Matrix, patch guard, desktop prune) 41/480; root consumers 16 files, 427 passed, 9 failed in `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts` from this host's loopback `HTTP(S)_PROXY` (`UND_ERR_SOCKET`); with proxy variables unset it passes 51/51. ACP real-Gateway e2e and crabline Discord tests are likewise proxy-sensitive (same on old versions).
- **Supply chain:** lock audit: new identities ≤ cutoff, no unapproved downgrade (undici 8.11.2 → 7.30.1 is mailauth's exact pin); npm-lock (110 scopes), patch and pin checks pass.
- **Vercel CLI:** lock regenerated with pinned npm 12.2.1 `--before` the cutoff (35 identities, all ≤ cutoff, no downgrade); `materialize-vercel-cli.sh` installs it, `vercel --version` = 65.2.0, `vcr login --help` lists `--project`/`--scope`; existing overrides still bind.
- **Native:** `cargo metadata --locked` x3; Rust 148 + Watch RTC 13 tests pass; Ruby frozen bundles load. App builds: platform CI.
- **Review:** Codex autoreview at P0–P2, full candidate and follow-up commit: scoped-clean.

Not run locally: full suites, live IMAP/Matrix/Mistral, app builds.

Requested and guided by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @steipete](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/f22d8bdb-5b30-435f-b808-30f9c6f82102)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/40ba5652-76b8-4959-b97f-76f85794ee9f)

## Worked on by

- @steipete

prs.title: fix(agents): keep a local Codex owner refusal from cooling the shared credential
prs.body:
Closes #191473

## Needs from a maintainer (nothing is waiting on the author)

Two one-line actions, neither of which CODEOWNERS routes to anybody — which is the mechanical reason they have been waiting since Nov 3:

1. **`/allow-security-sensitive-change`** for head `e960518954b`. This is maintainer-tier, not SecOps: matched against the repo's own security policy, the gate covers **one** non-test production file (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts`) and **3 lines** in it. The gate is live and correctly keyed, verified from the shipped logic: `scripts/github/security-review-rollout.mjs` returns mode `enforced` for this PR (rollout pull 152415 merged 2026-09-19, this PR created 2026-11-03), and `.github/workflows/security-review.yml` triggers on `issue_comment` created/edited plus a ten-minute reconcile schedule — so posting the command is picked up on its own, with no push or re-run needed from anyone.
2. **A yes/no on the `Decision needed`**: whether `session_authority` joins the closed failover vocabulary. The review's own recommendation is to approve it; the measured alternative is that a refused scheduled run's cause is dropped to `undefined` by the run-history reader's own enum (`z.enum(FAILOVER_REASONS)`), because the writer already emits the value. Who can answer: the repo requires explicit approval for protocol changes (`AGENTS.md` — “Protocol/version bumps … need explicit approval; fix/ship authority ≠ release authority”) but names no owner for them — `CODEOWNERS` is 23 lines covering only `openclaw-secops` and `openclaw-release-managers`, has no catch-all, and lists nothing for `packages/gateway-protocol/**`; searching `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/` for a protocol/vocabulary owner returns nothing. So this is waiting for any maintainer, not for a specific team that has been silent. Measured so the decision is framed correctly: `packages/gateway-protocol/src/failover-reasons.ts` has **exactly two commits in its entire history** — created whole by #121334 (2026-08-10, `3d5f916523d`) after duplicated reason lists had drifted and worker live events were rejecting `tls_certificate` payloads, and touched once since by #158222 (2026-09-26, `3c449bd35be`), a refactor that preserves the contract. **No member has ever been added to the canonical list.** So a yes here is the *first* expansion, not a routine continuation — which is precisely why the reviewer logged it as an owner decision instead of a schema detail; stated plainly so nobody has to guess the size of the yes.

Head moved twice since the last review: `main` regenerated the one colliding generated path, first in 513c12703ad and again in d0e78b07144, each time flipping this PR to CONFLICTING and stopping CI, so the branch was re-integrated and the predicate regenerated — `e960518954b` (main `9cb29007ed1`, 56 commits) is now the head to approve; `a58d99c1fbc` is one merge behind it, the durable review quotes `83e1c7e1d1b`, two merges behind, and the historical notes below still name `23ba4def295`. Re-verified on the newest merge: all five validator checks; the protocol registry, generation, native `--check` and since guards; the core test typecheck; the seven touched suites (45, 25, 13 and 72 passed across four shards); and the test-line ratchet with 15 lines of slack. On the previous merge the same set passed with the touched suites at 72, 13, 42 and 25. One environment caveat carried forward: `codex-app-server:protocol:check` cannot run here because it wants a sibling `openai/codex` checkout at `rust-v0.164.0`, and no workflow references it, so it is a dev-time sync check rather than a gate. One measured caveat: on that earlier merge `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` reported the tree 7 lines over the ceiling, and the identical 7 is `main`’s own overage (same checker, same throwaway-index method: `Test lines: 6467640; ceiling: 6467633; over by: 7; net delta: 0`), while this change still contributes exactly its allocated 292. Nothing was trimmed to hide it; the shared scalar is untouched.

Current state: no merge conflict, proof confidence 🦞 5/6, patch quality 🦞 5/6, zero open findings, no remaining rank-up moves. CI on the previous head `83e1c7e1d1b` ran 90 succeeded / 51 skipped with four red rows, none of them from this diff — each is inherited, and named here rather than drive-by fixed inside a credential-health PR:

- `checks-ui-e2e (1/4)`, `(2/4)`, `(3/4)` — Control UI copy assertions broken by upstream `f1a317d4674` ("chore(ui): refresh control ui locales", landed 17:50Z, i.e. after this branch's previous integration). All seven failing spec files (`cron-search`, `cron-filters`, `cron-run-completion`, `cron-run-suppression`, `boot-module-boundaries`, `settings-layout`, `new-session-page.workspace-memory`) are byte-identical to `main` here — `git diff 77c263b9fa1 HEAD -- <file>` is empty for each — and none is in this change's surface.
- `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` — the tree is 7 lines over the test-line ceiling, and `main`'s own tree is over by the same 7 under the same checker and method (`Test lines: 6467640; ceiling: 6467633; over by: 7; net delta: 0`); this change still contributes exactly its allocated 292.

Head `a58d99c1fbc` then merged main past `9938e65a609`, the upstream commit that realigned those e2e expectations with the refreshed locales, and past the test-line reconciliation: on this merge the ratchet measures 25 lines of slack rather than 7 over, and the seven UI spec files are byte-identical to a `main` that contains its own repair. Measured on this merge: `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` and `checks-ui-e2e (3/4)` turned green, exactly as those two upstream reconciliations predict. Two lanes stayed red there for a **different** copy drift that the e2e-alignment commit did not cover: `ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.device-dispatch.e2e.test.ts` still expects `No worker slots are available` while the UI renders `No session slots are available. Wait for a slot or pick another device.`, and `boot-module-boundaries` / `cron-filters` still expect `to the selected runner` where the UI now renders `to the selected device`. Concretely, on this tree `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-new-session-setup.ts:243` renders `deviceNoSlots: "No session slots are available…"` and `:96` renders `placementSyncsFolder: "Syncs {folder} to the selected device"`, while `ui/src/e2e` still holds 3 expectations for the retired `No worker slots are available` and 1 for `… selected runner`. The paired unit tests already assert the new wording (`ui/src/pages/new-session/device-placement.test.ts:43`, `checkout-chip.test.ts:245`), so the rename was deliberate and only the browser layer lags — a one-line alignment in those specs, not a product change. 
All three spec files are byte-identical to `main` on this branch (`git diff a58d99c1fbc^2 -- <file>` is empty for each), none is in this change's surface, and the alignment belongs to whoever owns that rename — not patched quietly inside a credential-health PR. Re-measured on the newest head rather than assumed: `main` has since narrowed the first drift from three expectations to one (`ui/src/e2e/session-placement.move.e2e.test.ts:173`) and left the second in place (`ui/src/e2e/session-placement-module-boundaries.test-support.ts:250`), so the owner-side alignment is still outstanding.

Mergeability, stated plainly so nobody re-derives it: `main` regenerated that same generated predicate **again** at 00:44:29Z (`730b60991ee`, #186073), which is twenty minutes after the head above, so this PR reads `CONFLICTING` once more. The collision is one generated file and the resolution is mechanical — measured at 05:16:00Z against main `3816bcb3de`: 300 files changed on `main` since this branch's merge base, and exactly **one** of them intersects this PR's 21-file surface (the generated predicate; the intersection is empty for every source and test file, so no hand resolution of any reviewed line is needed) — take main's version of `packages/gateway-protocol/src/compiled/protocol.generated/predicates.js`, run `pnpm gateway:validators:gen`, commit the generator output (then re-`git add` it, because a merge commit records the index) — and it recurs on roughly every protocol-touching merge. That is why the branch is deliberately **not** being re-pushed on a clock: every push re-keys `/allow-security-sensitive-change` to a fresh SHA and re-runs ~30 minutes of shared CI while changing no verdict. The order of operations that actually ends this is *final integration first, then the approval on whatever head lands*. Two artifacts can mislead whoever picks this up, so both are named rather than left to be rediscovered:

- The hosted review's `Before merge` checkbox still asks for `/allow-security-sensitive-change` for `83e1c7e1d1b`, which is **two merges dead**. Approving a stale SHA does not clear the gate. The artifact that does track the live head is the pinned `openclaw:security-sensitive-guard` comment — it re-keyed itself to `e960518954b` at 00:37:32Z and re-lists the same single sensitive file, which is also the whole scope of what is being approved.
- The two inherited reds are not stale bookkeeping. Re-checked against `main` at 01:08:28Z: `ui/src/e2e/session-placement-module-boundaries.test-support.ts:250` still expects `Syncs target-repo to the selected runner` (while `:262` in the same file already uses the new `… to the selected device` wording), and `ui/src/e2e/chat-mcp-app-fullscreen.e2e.test.ts:26`/`:29` still return from inside a promise executor (`await new Promise<void>((resolve) => sandbox.listen(claim.port, "127.0.0.1", resolve))`). Each is a one-line change by the owner of that rename or that spec; they are listed here instead of folded in because a credential-health PR is the wrong place to edit unrelated browser specs.

**CI on `e960518954b`** — complete, 100 succeeded / 64 skipped / 4 red, and none of the four comes from this diff. Recorded here so the next reader does not re-derive it:

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a local Codex owner refusal (HTTP 403 produced by the in-process inference relay, before any provider request) was classified as a provider authentication failure, which cooled down the shared OpenAI OAuth profile and interrupted every other agent using that credential.

## User Impact

User impact: one refused run no longer logs an entire profile out. Sibling agents on the same credential keep working, the model fallback chain is not consumed for a refusal that says nothing about the model, API clients receive a permission rejection instead of a retryable server error, and the message no longer tells operators to sign in again — it tells them to start a fresh request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refusal is generated locally, so the credential answered nothing; the 401/403 rule in `src/agents/failover/classification-rules.ts` could not tell the two apart. The fix preserves the local refusal's identity instead of exempting HTTP 403 or the `model_permission_denied` code globally, so genuine provider permission errors keep their exact current handling.

- The local relay's own refusal copy is the identity carrier. Codex's transport drops the relay's JSON body and renders only `error.message` as `unexpected status {status}: {message}, url: {url}` (`codex-rs/protocol/src/error.rs`, `UnexpectedResponseError::display_body` / `Display`), so the copy is the part that survives to the runner.
- A new run-scoped `session_authority` failover reason carries it: `src/agents/auth-profiles` and `run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` record profile health only for `auth`, `auth_permanent`, and `billing`, so the shared credential is never cooled.
- The reason resolves to `coordination` in `resolveModelFallbackError`, the owner that already stops the chain when "changing models cannot repair" the failure. Another model cannot re-establish the refused run's owner, so the chain surfaces the refusal instead of blaming a candidate, which is what the issue's "should not consume the model fallback chain" requirement asks for.
- `FAILOVER_STATUS` projects the reason as `403` with `permission_error`, so OpenAI-compatible clients stop seeing an unmapped reason fall through to a retryable `500`.
- Operator-facing copy for the reason avoids sign-in advice on both the assistant and auth-profile surfaces.

Currency check, re-run on the tip this branch now carries: `main` @ `be881a7f8b1` still has no competing repair — `session_authority` appears 0 times there, `message-patterns.ts`, `packages/gateway-protocol/src/failover-reasons.ts` and `run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` carry no local-refusal handling, and the only occurrence of the refusal copy on `main` is the relay that emits it (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-dispatch.ts`), which is exactly the side core misreads. So the misclassification was still live on `main` up to the commit this branch merged, and this PR remains the only fix.

Hook integrity was checked pre-merge against `df9d3240e52` because CI could not run while the branch was unmerged; the merge makes that reasoning moot and the live code is now the evidence. Between the old base and `be881a7f8b1` exactly one commit touched the classifier files this repair hangs off (`7e4bdf2f607`, provider deadline timeouts reported as auth failures), and after the merge the classification still resolves the refusal prose to `session_authority` (`classify.test.ts`), the profile policy still skips the health write (`run.harness-auth-failover.test.ts`), and the Gateway proof still shows the shared profile serving the next turn.

The one stronger form not reproducible on this host:

- **Latest-stable upgrade with existing state** — `pnpm test:docker:published-upgrade-survivor` with `OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_SURVIVOR_BASELINE_SPECS="openclaw@2026.10.10 openclaw@2026.9.36"` (current `latest` and `extended-stable` from the registry) against this PR's candidate package; Package Acceptance resolves the same lane from `source=ref`, and the QA Lab scenario id is `docker-upgrade-survivor` (`qa/scenarios/runtime/docker-upgrade-survivor.yaml`, script `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/docker-e2e-lane.ts`). Checked before writing this: every existing-state upgrade scenario the repo ships (`docker-upgrade-survivor`, `docker-release-upgrade-user-journey`, `docker-update-channel-switch`, `docker-update-migration`, `docker-update-restart-auth`) routes through `docker-e2e-lane.ts`, so there is no host-runner equivalent to substitute — this is the one gate that genuinely needs a container or a runner rather than more local evidence. That is the check that a pre-existing install still loads its stored cron, auth-profile and session state after moving onto this build. The additive-vocabulary probe above shows existing reason values still validate, but it is not the upgrade run the review asked for.

Correction worth recording: the Gateway-turn gate did **not** need a container. It runs on the host through the shipped QA product harness (`test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts`, `--runner host` semantics), and the earlier claim that this sandbox could not exercise a Gateway turn was wrong. The survivor lane genuinely is container-only (`scripts/e2e/upgrade-survivor-docker.sh` hands off to `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/run.sh` inside the harness image) and this machine has no running Docker daemon; starting one, or using a credentialed remote runner, is a host-level action that needs the operator's go-ahead, and remote execution is maintainer-authorized. I still tried the host route today, and it stops on a guard that should not be bypassed: published `openclaw@2026.10.10`, run in an isolated `HOME` on its own port, created real durable state (a seeded cron row, canonical `state/openclaw.sqlite`, per-agent SQLite, config journal), and this branch's CLI then refuses to load it with `UpdatePreMutationError: Runtime artifacts changed, but the affected Gateway is running or its offline state could not be verified`, because the machine has a LaunchAgent-managed Gateway. That refusal is correct behavior on a live install, so the existing-state upgrade check needs a container or a runner without a live service rather than a workaround. One ordering detail matters for whoever runs it: until `main` is integrated, this branch's own version reads `2026.10.9`, which predates the `2026.10.10` stable baseline, so a meaningful upgrade run has to follow the merge rather than precede it. Integration is complete, and the blocker was local configuration rather than the link: this machine's global `http.lowSpeedLimit=1` aborted the fetch during the v0 full-ref advertisement ("expected flush after ref listing"), which is what the earlier failures looked like. `git -c protocol.version=2 -c http.lowSpeedLimit=0 fetch` pulled the whole pack at 9-11 MB/s. The merge itself was one generated file plus `pnpm gateway:validators:gen`, and the branch version now reads `2026.10.10`, so a survivor run pairs a published `openclaw@2026.9.36` baseline against this build rather than treating `2026.10.10` as the newer side.

prs.title: feat(pairing): pair a browser with a short code approved on the host
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A browser with no Gateway credential has no way to ask for one. It needs a pasted token, or a one-time link from `openclaw dashboard` carried over from the host. On a headless Gateway reached over SSH, both mean moving a secret by hand.

## User Impact

- A browser can pair with no token, link or host browser.
- New CLI command `openclaw pair <code>` and a new public route, both documented in `/cli/pair` and `/web/control-ui/connect-and-pair`.
- When `gateway.roles` is configured, bootstrap connections need a verified identity, so code pairing is refused there the same way `openclaw dashboard` links are.
- **Known low-impact limit:** a network client rotating its source address can keep the 32-row pending table full, so other browsers see "Too many pairing requests". One address holds only about half the table under the default rate limit; holding it full takes two or three. State stays bounded, nobody can replace or remove another browser's request, no credential is exposed, and token and `openclaw dashboard` sign-in keep working. A per-source allowance would raise the cost if this ever matters in practice.
- On a plain `http://` address, anyone on that network can read Gateway traffic after pairing, as with any plain-HTTP Control UI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Device-code pairing for the Control UI:

1. The login gate's sign-in card gains a **Pair with a code instead** link. It opens a second card that holds only pairing: **Get a code** shows the command `openclaw pair ABCD-EFGH` and a Browser ID while the browser waits, and **Sign in with URL and secret** goes back. The URL and secret sign-in is unchanged.

   ![Sign-in card with code pairing link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0598b57-272f-4ea4-9d85-4c476a42c6e4)

   ![Pairing card waiting with command and Browser ID](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f421e08d-c6a2-4cb1-807c-b0885c26c1aa)

   ![Pairing card waiting at phone width](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d572f64c-71da-4a82-891a-edd473332bf0)

2. On the host, over SSH if needed, `openclaw pair` shows who is asking and waits for an answer.

   ```text
   A browser is asking for full administrator access to this Gateway.

     Code                34EL-ZNRU
     Browser (reported)  Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7) ... Safari/605.1.15
     Address             127.0.0.1
     Page (reported)     http://127.0.0.1:18789
     Browser ID          e2de4320
     Requested           just now

   Approve only if you opened this page yourself and it shows this code and Browser ID.
   If someone sent you this code or command, answer no: approving gives their browser full control of this Gateway.
   Approve this browser? [y/N]
   ```

3. The waiting browser connects by itself.

   ![Control UI connected with full access after approval](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6952e4cd-4691-4d4f-81c0-fe40e85439ac)

### How it works

- `POST <base>/__openclaw__/browser-pair/start` is public, same-origin and rate limited. It takes a signature from the browser's device key and files one row in a new `device_pairing_browser_requests` table, returning a request ID and an eight-character code.
- `device.pair.code` requires `operator.admin`. With `code` it returns the request. With `requestId` and `decision` it settles exactly that request. Approval issues the existing Control UI owner bootstrap token, pre-bound to the request's key.
- `POST .../collect` returns the decision only to a signature from the requesting key. The browser then connects through the existing bootstrap path, which creates the paired device with `approvedVia: bootstrap`.
- Each attempt belongs to the Gateway it started on. Going back to the sign-in card or a changed Gateway target ends the attempt, and an approval is only ever connected to the Gateway that issued it.

### Security properties

- The code names a request and is not a bearer secret.
- The collected token only works with the requesting key. A stranger presenting it is refused.
- Requests expire after ten minutes. At most 32 are pending, and each source's filing is limited by the Gateway's auth rate limit.
- The route uses the Gateway's browser origin policy, including the check that a loopback page came from a loopback socket. This stops other sites filing requests from a visitor's browser. It is not a network boundary: authority comes from host approval and the key proof.
- `Browser` and `Page` are marked `(reported)` in the prompt because the requester chooses them. `Address` is what the Gateway saw, and the code and Browser ID are what the operator matches against the page.
- The token column is covered by the secret-table policy, so redacted backups omit the table.
- Without a terminal the CLI approves nothing unless `--yes` is passed. The page never suggests `--yes`.

### Decisions for review

- **Separate table, not the pending-device list.** The route is unauthenticated, so its input stays out of the list operators approve from, including `openclaw devices approve --latest`. These requests therefore do not appear in `openclaw devices list` or the Devices page.
- **Approval grants the owner profile.** It matches `openclaw dashboard`, and it is why the method needs `operator.admin` rather than `operator.pairing`.
- **One additive protocol method and one additive lazy table.** No protocol version change.
- **Test-line allocation.** `config/test-lines-allocations/browser-pair-code.txt` covers the 778 net test lines this PR adds. The tests were consolidated first, from 1,076 lines; each remaining case fails when the check it guards is disabled, so cutting further would remove coverage.

## Evidence

Tests: 25 new gateway, worker and CLI cases plus 14 UI cases pass, with consumer suites for login gate, secret tables, method registry, CLI registration, Git backup and the Postgres schema generators. Full suite not run locally. Each security check was disabled in turn (key binding, collect key match, signature, origin, loopback socket check, inspect and approve expiry, inspected-request match, rate limit) and a test failed every time.

Independent review: a separate reviewer attacked the route, the approval method and the token binding with nine probes against a real Gateway, and found no way to obtain a credential without host access or `operator.admin`.

Authority at the final effect, checked against the request row and the bootstrap token table on a real Gateway:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Caller with `operator.pairing`, `operator.read` or `operator.write` | Refused, nothing issued, request still pending |
| Administrator revoked while the approval is queued | Refused, nothing issued; with the request authority removed, the same test issues a token |
| Authority lost at any check inside the approval | Transaction rolled back, nothing issued, no paired device |
| Revoked bootstrap credential presented with the right key | Connection refused, no paired device; without the revocation, the same test connects |

Live run: packaged build installed in a clean macOS VM, Safari in the guest, `openclaw pair` over SSH from outside the guest.

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Wrong code | Refused: `No browser is waiting for this code.` |
| Code after its real ten minutes | Refused: `This code has expired.` |
| No terminal | Details printed, nothing approved |
| Answered no | Browser shows it was declined |
| Answered yes | Browser connects, stays connected after reload |
| Plain `http://` LAN address | Browser connects |

Not covered: a browser on a different machine from the Gateway, trusted-proxy and Tailscale Serve deployments, the Postgres state engine, an upgrade from the latest stable release, and translated strings, which `control-ui-locale-refresh` adds. The `(reported)` labels, the loopback socket check and Gateway target handling have test coverage but were not part of the live run.

Related: #159660, #120768

## Additional validation

On Linux with Node 24.22.1, build `559f82070f2` ran in a throwaway Gateway with a scratch profile, mock model and separate port. A headless browser rendered the signed-out screen and lazy pairing card. Starting an attempt returned HTTP 200 and began collection polling; Back restored sign-in and stopped pairing traffic for 5.5 seconds, exceeding the two-second poll interval. Each step was captured. The browser, Gateway, mock and scratch profile were cleaned up. This checks card loading and cancellation, not host approval or a complete pairing exchange on `72db66c`.

[CI for `72db66c`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41858549852) passes `control-ui-performance`. UI and type checks also fail in [main's run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41857633230); some individual UI failures differ between runs. The baseline ratchet also reports two mock-export violations present on main. The shared OpenClawKit dead-code check fails separately; its cause has not been attributed here. Maintainer security approval is required for this head.

The test-line failure comes from shared baseline debt. Main `7c2ff8f` has 6,466,021 test lines against a 6,465,830 ceiling, already 191 lines over. This PR's 778-line allocation matches its own growth exactly. The fix is a maintainer reconciliation commit on main, following #192519, rather than an extra allocation in this PR.

prs.title: fix(security): isolate install-policy tests from host temp permissions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes 18 install-policy test failures when `TMPDIR` has a non-sticky, group-writable ancestor. Found while validating #186817.

## User Impact

No product behavior change. Developers can run the install-policy suite when their checkout or temp directory lives below a 0775 volume or directory; policy commands under writable parents remain rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture at `src/security/install-policy.test.ts:119` on base `2270152d224ae48de9a10f3fe26b4c594ac9e87d` called `tempDirs.make()` without an explicit root. `test/helpers/temp-dir.ts:14` selects `os.tmpdir()`, so even a private 0700 fixture inherited unsafe ancestors. The production guard correctly rejects these at `src/security/install-policy.ts:178`, before the command can run.

Create each POSIX fixture under canonical `/tmp`, whose root-owned sticky directory is accepted by the existing policy. The shared tracker still creates private 0700 directories and owns cleanup. Windows retains the existing temp-directory selection. Reuse the per-test fixture for the writable-parent and symlink cases instead of allocating redundant roots; the explicit 0777 child and all assertions remain intact. Production delta: 0 lines; test delta: -1 line. Completed the pr-simplify pass; no new helpers or policy exceptions are needed.

## Evidence

Reproduced before any source edit on unmodified `origin/main` at `2270152d224ae48de9a10f3fe26b4c594ac9e87d` after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`:

```sh
mkdir -p .artifacts/install-policy-proof/group-writable
chmod 775 .artifacts/install-policy-proof/group-writable
TMPDIR="$PWD/.artifacts/install-policy-proof/group-writable" node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/security/install-policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Before (exit 1; absolute fixture path abbreviated):

```text
AssertionError: expected { blocked: { …(2) } } to deeply equal {}
"reason": "install policy failed closed: security.installPolicy.exec.command parent directory permissions are too open: <worktree>/.artifacts/install-policy-proof/group-writable"
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  18 failed | 8 passed (26)
Duration 268.43s
[test] failed 1 Vitest shard in 286.05s
```

After, the identical command and 0775 parent (exit 0):

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  26 passed (26)
Duration 34.83s
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 48.69s
```

This includes the writable-parent negative controls and the real forked-child timeout test. The first run built the repository's compiled-worker artifacts; the second reused them. CI timing is pending; CI was not waited for.

Validation:

```sh
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.config-cli.json --incremental
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/security/install-policy.test.ts
pnpm format:check src/security/install-policy.test.ts
git diff --check
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main
```

Ratchet (exit 0):

```text
Test lines: 6479092; ceiling: 6479000; over by: 92; net delta: -1. Tree is over the ceiling; this change does not add test lines.
```

All validation commands above passed. Independent Codex autoreview covered the complete local diff against `2270152d224ae48de9a10f3fe26b4c594ac9e87d` at P2 coverage and returned `scoped-clean`, with no accepted/actionable findings. It also inspected the unchanged production policy and temp-dir tracker. The measured post-fix case durations total 2.379 seconds; the longer command wall time includes worker preparation and cleanup.
