prs.title: fix: interrupted triage leaves full-size SQLite snapshot copies in the cache
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: interrupting `openclaw triage` (Ctrl-C, SIGTERM, a closed terminal) while Doctor's database inspection is copying a database leaves the full-size read-only copy under `~/Library/Caches/openclaw/sqlite-<hash>/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-*/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-*/database.sqlite` after the process exits.

On one Mac host, two triage runs left four nested copies of the agent and state databases (13, 15, 6.2 and 15 GB), and free disk fell from 87 GiB to 38 GiB. Every leftover `owner.sqlite` was empty with a 512-byte `-journal`, and no process held the files afterwards. Those two runs were not interrupted: one was refused late for an oversized `--update-result` file, the other was a non-TTY `--run` refusal, and both exited 1. This PR fixes the leak mechanism I can reproduce, which is cancellation of the inspection task while it holds a copy. I have not reproduced that host's exact trigger; see Evidence.

## User Impact

An interrupted triage or Doctor inspection now removes its private snapshot copy before it exits. A copy that a live reader still holds is kept until that reader releases it, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor's database-engine inspection runs as a served worker task. When triage is interrupted, the task is cancelled, and its cleanup does start. But each SQLite statement on the private staging token, and the retirement of the copy's admission facts, goes through the worker's admission-facts exchange. That exchange checks the task's cancellation first. So cleanup failed with `SQLite admission facts exchange cancelled by its caller`, and the worker thread was torn down with the copy still on disk.

This adds `withSqliteDatabaseAdmissionSettlement` to the admission-wait scope. The scope now lives in a leaf module, `sqlite-database-admission-wait.ts`, so the staging token and the admission store can import it without a madge cycle through the worker relay; the relay re-exports the helpers its existing importers use. The settlement scope stops outer cancellation from failing the exchange but keeps outer deadlines. Two cleanup primitives use it: the staging token's open, release and retirement, and `retireSqliteDatabaseAdmissionForPath`. Every retirement path goes through those two. Live readers still fence retirement with their own disk tokens, and cancelled admission waits outside these two primitives behave as before. Each half alone still leaks; both are required.

Ruled out:
- **Reclamation skips the nested layout.** Once the holders were dead, `beginSqliteSnapshotRetirement` with the gateway sweep's cutoff removed both nested and flat leftovers, including the stale `-journal`.
- **The owner record never commits.** An empty `owner.sqlite` with a 512-byte `-journal` is what a creator token holding `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` leaves when its process ends without releasing. It's a live lock, not a failed commit.
- **A normal run leaks.** Uninterrupted triage runs, with and without a live Gateway owning the database, left nothing.
- **A non-zero CLI exit leaks.** On base, with a 12.6 GB live-owned state DB, `triage --json --update-result <9 KB file>` (refused with `File exceeds 8192 bytes` after 237 s) removed every copy before it exited 1. Head behaves the same, as does the non-TTY `triage --run` refusal (exit 1 after writing the bundle).
- **The Gateway's side of triage's RPCs leaks.** An instrumented Gateway created no snapshot copies while serving triage's `health` and `diagnostics.capabilities` calls.

Not fixed here: when the host dies, the spawn broker's SQLite native resource deliberately keeps creator custody of its own session-allocated snapshot (covered by the existing "refuses cleanup after losing its host fence port" test). The orphaned broker then keeps one flat copy alive. That fail-closed behaviour needs a maintainer decision, so it belongs in a separate PR.

## Evidence

Head `2d64b108fc71`, which contains `origin/main` `f21943152ad4`. The red reproduction ran on `ffbbb514ba3b`. Later main commits touch only release, UI, template, Android, openclaw-id, process-ancestry and test-line allocation code, not these paths; the focused tests and the madge check were rerun after merging main.

Reproduction, in a disposable HOME and state dir with a 3.1 GB state database owned by a disposable Gateway, then SIGINT to the `openclaw triage --non-interactive --json` process group as soon as the nested copy appears:

| Build | Runs | Nested copy left after exit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| base | 9 | 9 (3 GB each, empty `owner.sqlite` with a 512-byte `-journal`) |
| this branch | 3 | 0 |

Instrumenting base showed the worker calling `removeTempDirectoryAsync` 10 ms after cancellation, then failing at `BEGIN` on the staging token (`getSqliteDatabaseSchemaRevision` → admission exchange → `worker task cancelled`). With only the token change, it failed next at `retireSqliteDatabaseAdmissionForPath`.

Regression test in `src/infra/worker-task-server.test.ts`: "retires a cancelled task's snapshot copy unless a live reader still holds it". It drives the real task server, cancellation word, admission relay, staging tokens and a real SQLite copy:
- base: fails (the idle copy survives)
- token-only change: fails
- admission-retirement-only change: fails
- this branch: passes

The same test is the negative control: while a live read token holds one copy, removal returns `false` and the copy and payload stay. After the reader releases, the same removal succeeds.

Commands:
- `pnpm test src/infra/worker-task-server.test.ts`: 7 passed.
- `pnpm test` on 38 affected files (admission relay and records, staging token, snapshot, read-only location, native resource, worker task server, cron cold cleanup): 348 passed, 3 skipped, 3 failed. The 3 failures are in `src/infra/sqlite-snapshot-cow.test.ts` (APFS clone-ID comparison). They fail identically on unmodified base on the same Mac.
- `pnpm check:changed`: lint, format, import-cycle and boundary guards pass. The local tsgo typecheck can't run on this machine because the checkout uses the shared pnpm store, which its graph boundary refuses. CI's typecheck is the gate for that.
- Autoreview (Codex, branch mode against `origin/main`, P0–P2): scoped-clean on both commits.
- `scripts/check-madge-import-cycles.ts`: 0 cycles (the first push had 1, fixed by the leaf module). Runtime import cycles: 0.
- Test-lines ratchet: this PR's net growth is +49, recorded exactly in `config/test-lines-allocations/sqlite-snapshot-cancelled-retirement.txt`. The check still reports main's own overage (23 lines after merging `f21943152ad4`); this PR adds none on top.

Test file audit (`src/infra/worker-task-server.test.ts`, read in full): the fixture's synthetic `node:worker_threads` mock now reports a worker `threadId`, so fact retirement takes the cross-thread path a real served worker takes. The other six tests pass unchanged. The new `nativeSections` fixture parameter and the temp-dir tracker are used only by the new test, which owns and removes its temp root. Nothing was pruned: every existing case covers distinct behaviour.

prs.title: perf(plugins): reuse tokenjuice rules across ignored cwd changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tokenjuice discards and recompiles unchanged rules when session or metadata directories change even though an explicit command workdir still selects the same rules.

## User Impact

Less compaction bookkeeping during directory churn, with the same tool-result content and metadata. The 128-directory retention bound remains; no dependency, configuration, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Track the directory Tokenjuice actually selects, preserving its precedence and untrimmed strings, instead of serializing all possible directory sources into a tuple. Fill missing status on the metadata copy the adapter already owns. Keep lazy loading and cleanup after rejected reducers.

Production change: **14 added / 17 removed, net −3 lines**. The larger command-parsing and grapheme-allocation costs are inside Tokenjuice 0.10.0 and are outside this patch.

## Evidence

Acceptance: unchanged fixture output; preserve rule reuse through ignored-cwd churn and eviction after 128 real directories; lower owner CPU/allocation for redundant bookkeeping. No whole-Gateway improvement is claimed.

- The owner regression fails against unchanged main `11c8f236b330e8f51c03331dcd6ae0c661080e7b`: 256 ignored fallback changes replace the selected directory's compiled rules. It preserves the same rules with this patch. The existing integration test also checks actual-directory eviction and exact CRLF file-read/compacted output.
- Strict `pnpm tsgo:test:root` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: passed. Changed-file oxfmt and direct oxlint: passed. The local extension-aware lint wrapper hit its declaration-preparation timeout; exact-head CI passed lint and the boundary gates.
- Focused Tokenjuice proof: **8 tests passed across both files**. The final simplified retention file passed both tests on the stable corrected head; the unchanged index file passed all six tests. The final negative-control replay failed only the intended baseline cache-identity assertion (candidate 2/2 pass, baseline 1 expected failure and 1 pass). The closure checks passed 39/40 tests; `pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts` / `retains Darwin inputs inside excluded namespaces` hit its 120s timeout on this shared host. The export-name collision guard passed. The committed regression replayed against the unchanged baseline fails at the expected compiled-rule identity assertion (1 failed, 1 passed).
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): final diff clean at P0/P1/P2. The helper refused a provider-route mismatch before inference; operator configuration was unchanged. Review prompted retaining the existing lazy dependency import.
- Committed benchmark: `scripts/perf/tokenjuice-tool-result-measure.ts`; usage is in its header. **Five alternating pairs completed**, with 2,000 measured results per arm/case per pair (160 for real-cwd churn): **10,000 results per side/case, 800 for real-cwd churn**. Each case has 40 warmups. CPU is untraced process CPU; allocation is a separate 64 KiB sampling pass including collected objects. Full-result hashes match across all 160 prepared events per case, all five pairs, and both instrumentation modes.

| Workload | CPU µs/result base → candidate | Δ | Sampled bytes/result base → candidate | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| small | 141.19 → 142.59 | +1.0% | 192,977 → 189,913 | -1.6% |
| small-no-status | 105.69 → 96.38 | -8.8% | 188,353 → 190,287 | +1.0% |
| large | 1852.65 → 1842.26 | -0.6% | 3,612,900 → 3,626,984 | +0.4% |
| non-matching | 2174.36 → 2078.50 | -4.4% | 4,322,325 → 4,329,912 | +0.2% |
| file-read | 5.42 → 4.98 | -8.3% | 11,831 → 11,817 | -0.1% |
| non-exec-churn | 116.60 → 1.06 | -99.1% | 11,996 → 1,516 | -87.4% |
| shadowed-cwd-churn | 540.34 → 113.54 | -79.0% | 214,014 → 190,741 | -10.9% |
| real-cwd-churn | 30942.42 → 31538.34 | +1.9% | 2,195,653 → 2,320,720 | +5.7% |

Host 1-min load range: 91.6–153.4.

The primary scoped gain is ignored-cwd churn: **CPU −79.0%, allocation −10.9%**. Non-exec fallback churn also stops falsely evicting rules. Ordinary compaction remains dominated by the unchanged dependency; its small differences are not claimed as wins.

Cases run in the same fixed sequence within each fresh arm. Genuine-cwd churn can include the candidate's first lazy root-barrel import, while the baseline already paid it during false eviction. Its +1.9% CPU / +5.7% allocation is reported as that workload's result, not a steady-state rule-loading regression. The main-thread-only breakdown for this case is 3.982 → 5.053 ms/result (+26.9%), so matched A/A and warm-barrel controls were run before drawing a conclusion. The shared host load was 91.6–153.4, so wall time is not used to claim an improvement.

The explicit redundant-work fast path uses owner proof here; no Gateway load test was run and no whole-Gateway CPU, GC, event-loop or latency claim is made. The retention fixture now calls the middleware directly while sibling tests retain registration coverage: **net −3 test lines**, with every assertion preserved. The first CI run exposed 93 inherited lines above the global ceiling despite our scoped +15 allocation; simplifying the fixture removed the allocation and passes the ratchet without changing its baseline. Corrected head: `74e9cd16e7de37de18d95bec5397c06b4685c38d`; [exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41970522370), including `openclaw/ci-gate`.


Control follow-up for the main-thread signal: four identical-source A/A pairs on the genuine-cwd workload gave **+1.21%, +3.08%, −2.68%, −0.51%** main-thread deltas. With the dependency root barrel preloaded in both arms, two swapped base/candidate pairs gave **−2.52% main-thread CPU** (4.020 → 3.919 ms/result) and **+1.03% allocation** (2,208,578 → 2,231,219 bytes/result). That removes the original +26.9% main-thread signal and supports one-time import displacement, not a steady-state regression. Across the entire original eight-case sequence, main-thread CPU is **9.408 → 9.071 seconds (−3.58%)**; this is a synthetic mix, not an estimate of production traffic.

The controls use the same committed script with `--iterations 1` (the genuine-cwd case remains 160 measured calls plus 40 warmups), and add `--import ./extensions/tokenjuice/node_modules/tokenjuice/dist/index.js` before the script to preload the barrel in both arms. CPU controls are untraced; allocation is a separate pass. All control output hashes match. No dependency code was modified.

prs.body: Related: `pickerRuntimes` (2026.9.5 release notes, `docs/concepts/models.md` › "Choose the same model with different runtimes") ## What Problem This Solves In the Telegram `/model` picker, a model with several configured runtimes (`agents.defaults.models["/"].pickerRuntimes`, for example API and Claude CLI) appears as a single button, and that button carries only the default route label. The Control UI and the Discord picker already offer each runtime as its own choice. On Telegram, the other runtime is only reachable by typing `/model --runtime `. ## User Impact Telegram shows one button per offered runtime, labelled with the existing route prefix (`API · Claude Opus 5.5`, `Claude CLI · Claude Opus 5.5`). Tapping one selects the model and pins that runtime for the session, and ✓ marks the active model/runtime pair. Models with a single runtime look exactly as before. Picking the configured runtime of the agent's default model still resets the session to its default. ## Why This Change Was Made The picker data already carries `runtimeChoicesByModel`; the Telegram list did not use it. - `model-buttons.ts` expands a model into one entry per runtime variant. The new callback is `mdl_rt_{runtime}_{provider/model}`. When that does not fit Telegram's 64 bytes, an opaque `mdl1~r:{sha256}` is used instead. Runtime selections resolve only against the variants the picker offered. - `model-runtime-variants.ts` (new) builds the variants per model, with the configured runtime first. - `bot-handlers.callback-router.ts`: pagination counts entries, and a runtime button applies `applySessionModelSelection` with `runtime: { kind: "set" }`. - `commands-models-catalog.ts` exposes `modelRuntimeIds`. This is the runtime each multi-runtime model uses with no session pin, resolved from config and auth for any provider. It is optional and absent for single-runtime models. - `commands-models.ts` / `command-ui.ts`: the direct `/models ` reply pages over the same runtime rows as the callbacks. - `ChannelCommandAdapter.buildModelsListChannelData` gains five optional inputs. Adapters that ignore them keep one row per model. No config, storage or protocol changes, and existing `mdl_sel_*` / `mdl1~m:` callbacks keep working. ## Revision on current `main` This revision merges current main. The one real conflict is main's role-policy filter for CLI alias twins in `loadModelsProviderData`. It now runs after `modelRuntimeIds` is filled and also drops the runtime id of a model it filters out. Behaviour and callbacks are otherwise unchanged from the last reviewed head `abb6c39d7bb`. ## Evidence **Before / after (live Telegram, `pickerRuntimes` set on the Anthropic models):** | Before | After | |---|---| | | | **Real behavior proof.** ClawSweeper asked for this as "Add real behavior proof". Since 2026-10-18 the change has been running in a production installation: first on a 2026.10.4 build, and since 2026-11-05 on a 2026.10.10 build with this exact port. It serves three daily-use Telegram bots, and selecting a runtime from the picker moves subsequent turns to that runtime. A logged CLI↔API switch is shown below. ``` cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 trigger=user useResume=false cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=17379 cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 trigger=user useResume=true session=present [model-fetch] response provider=anthropic api=anthropic-messages model=claude-opus-5-5 status=200 ``` Session entry afterwards: `modelOverride: "claude-opus-5-5"`, `agentRuntimeOverride: "openclaw"`. Still open from the review: Telegram **Test Server userbot** evidence via the repository `telegram-e2e-userbot` skill, covering revised selection, the configured-default reset, and direct-reply/callback pagination. It needs Convex-leased team credentials that I do not have. If a maintainer can run that lane, or lease me the credentials, I'll add the recording. **Owner decision.** The five optional `ChannelCommandAdapter` inputs are additive, and adapters that ignore them are unaffected. They still need a maintainer's yes or no. **Tests** (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1`, merged base `d189a554154`, wall time on a shared host): - `extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts`: 13 passed (11 s); `model-runtime-variants.test.ts`: 5 passed (9 s); `command-ui.test.ts`: 5 passed (64 s) - `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-models.test.ts`: 19 passed (70 s, includes "reports each model's configured runtime regardless of the session runtime pin"); `commands-models-order.test.ts`: 1 passed; `commands-models.catalog-recovery.test.ts`: 6 passed - `extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts -t model`: 5 passed - `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`: clean. `oxlint` (core + extensions tsconfig) and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files: clean. prs.title: fix(openai): let fast voice answers skip acknowledgments
prs.body:
Related: #175603.

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway-controlled OpenAI Talk acknowledges every delegated request immediately, even when the answer is ready fast enough to speak directly. Repeated acknowledgments make short conversations feel repetitive and add unnecessary speech before the result.

## User Impact

Work starts immediately. An answer or failure arriving within 1.5 seconds skips filler. Slower requests receive at most one short acknowledgment using the existing caller-language, naturally varied wording from #175603. Wording variation remains model-directed, not guaranteed.

Spoken updates, follow-ups, controls, and call shutdown cancel an unsent acknowledgment. Status, cancellation, final results, and failure delivery retain their existing ownership. No new configuration or client changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Race the existing consult against a short acknowledgment timer in its existing controller. This avoids a separate predictive model call or delaying the actual work. The timer is canceled when the consult settles or its presentation becomes obsolete, and uses the original socket's delivery checks.

The 1.5-second window is an initial UX choice, not a measured latency improvement. An answer arriving just after that window can still follow an acknowledgment already submitted to the provider.

## Evidence

- Baseline regression: 12 failures / 20 passes against the unmodified controller, including the new fast-answer, slow-answer, and cancellation cases failing on its immediate append.
- All 89 focused tests pass across delegation (32), public delegation (8), Gateway bridge and browser session (36 combined), and agent-tool prompt stability (13). Two old consumer expectations of immediate filler were updated and their 40-test subset rerun successfully.
- Changed delegation/public-delegation suites: 25.43 seconds including compilation; 28.19 seconds including runner cleanup. Earlier four-suite voice run: 6.52 seconds with cached compilation. Hosted CI timing pending.
- OpenAI package typecheck, type-aware lint of all four touched TypeScript files, formatting, and whitespace checks pass.
- Independent autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings in the diff. Review was limited to supplied changes; focused execution provides the runtime proof above.
- Graphify AST-only refresh completed for the OpenAI package. Generated graph files are not part of this PR.

No live provider/audio or physical-device acceptance test was run. The running Gateway and native app were not changed.

The simplification pass retains one timer in the existing controller and no new policy owner, queue, config surface, or predictive classifier. Production delta: +30/-2 lines; tests: +113/-17; docs: +5/-2.

prs.title: fix(zalouser): sanitize outbound tool traces
prs.body:
## Merge Brief

- **Problem / value:** Zalo Personal's custom monitor callback bypasses its standard adapter, so a `message_sending` hook can reintroduce internal tool traces immediately before transport. This patch keeps recipient text and captions clean while preserving configured Markdown-table rendering.
- **Relevance:** Independent P1/security report #90684 tracks this leakage class. Merged #112621 sanitizes the standard adapter only; current `main` still leaves this distinct callback seam open.
- **Smallest complete fix / review map:** Keep configured table conversion in `delivery.preparePayload`, where durable final delivery sees it, and sanitize only the effective post-hook payload in the custom callback. Scope is 4 files, `+76/-20`: two small helpers, two focused regressions, and the boundary wiring.
- **Risk / proof:** Risk is limited to ordering between two existing transforms. Exact head `b012137ca6889eab50e9474c9d34497b2e4752e3`; full Zalouser `221/221`; changed-file format/lint, extension production/test types, branch ratchets, and all 36 non-skipped hosted checks pass. The exact deterministic wrapper has only untouched frozen-base Codex/dead-export debt.
- **External proof limit:** Authenticated recipient-visible transport is `blocked_external` because no safe configured account/recipient route exists. Exact-head tests reach both lifecycle boundaries; no live send is claimed.
- **Non-goals:** Standard adapter, sanitizer parser dialects, Zalo Bot, authentication, configuration schema, and protocol changes.
- **Maintainer ask:** Please apply `no-stale` while authenticated recipient proof is coordinated; the assigned-PR age clock otherwise ignores substantive updates.

## What Problem This Solves

Zalo Personal's custom inbound-reply path in `monitor.ts` can deliver a post-hook payload without passing through the standard outbound adapter. That leaves one route for compact tool-failure lines or tool XML to reach recipients. The repair must also preserve `channels.zalouser.markdown.tables` for final replies handled by durable delivery. Related: #90684.

## User Impact

Recipients get intended assistant text and media without internal tool-trace scaffolding, while existing table preferences such as `markdown.tables: "bullets"` continue to apply to durable final replies. Ordinary prose, captions, chunking, and media delivery remain unchanged; users have no migration step.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `delivery.preparePayload` owns configured table conversion before the lifecycle can return through durable delivery.
- The private custom callback owns sanitization after `message_sending`, so a supported hook cannot reintroduce internal traces.
- Merged #112621 covers the standard adapter only; this remains a narrow, distinct callback repair.

## Evidence

- Exact signed candidate head: `41e305a4a4f4fd73973bac5858b07766db1791f9` on frozen maintenance base `b464d49019995ec229595bdcbba9d3b61ff035f7`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/zalouser`: `33` files and `317/317` tests passing, including configured bullet-table preparation before durable delivery and post-hook trace sanitization at custom delivery.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: passing.
- Changed Zalouser scope passes type-aware Oxlint, Oxfmt, and `git diff --check`. Repository-wide extension lint's only failure is unchanged frozen-base debt in `extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.test.ts` (`max-lines`).
- Deterministic `openclaw-pre-pr.sh` gate: passed for frozen base `b464d49019995ec229595bdcbba9d3b61ff035f7`, exact head `41e305a4a4f4fd73973bac5858b07766db1791f9`, and merge tree `1d2e0ad6dc09fd07dfa21423c38602b80e92ae9d`.
- Current-`main` negative control: the custom monitor callback still resolves and delivers the post-hook payload directly. This head restores pre-durable table preparation and sanitizes immediately before custom text/caption resolution.
- Remaining proof state is `blocked_external`, not a claimed live pass: authenticated recipient-visible proof still requires a safe Zalo Personal account and recipient route.

AI-assisted change, manually reviewed and validated.
## Exact-head refresh (2026-10-26)

<!-- clawsean-head-refresh-2026-10-26 -->
The current signed PR head is `b012137ca6889eab50e9474c9d34497b2e4752e3`, rebuilt on frozen base `f4a0d4875912103be54dd672e32db17064d003db` with a four-file patch and clean merge tree `f44ddf096cf52e14aadcf50b892f2ea4b8765eee`.

- Disposable Linux/arm64 proof used Node 24.22.1 and a fresh frozen-lockfile install; the full Zalouser suite passed `221/221` across 30 files.
- Changed-file format/lint, production and test extension typechecks, conflict/line-cap/assertion/SQLite/plugin-boundary ratchets, doctor-contract tests, media/runtime guards, and import-cycle checks passed.
- Independent exact-diff review found no P0-P2 findings. GitHub and the fork ref read back this exact head, and all 36 non-skipped hosted checks pass with none pending or failed.
- Authenticated recipient-visible Zalo proof remains externally blocked: no consented safe recipient route is available, so no private recipient was used and no live-send claim is made. The deterministic negative path, exact-head full suite, and hosted execution are the strongest contributor-safe evidence currently possible.

prs.title: fix(memory): dreaming keeps running after Memory Core opt-out when another plugin owns the memory slot
prs.body:
Related: #156666, #156667

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: managed Memory Dreaming keeps running and writing diaries despite the documented opt-out when a third-party plugin without dreaming settings owns the memory slot.

## User Impact

User impact: `plugins.entries.memory-core.config.dreaming.enabled: false` disables dreaming for that configuration. An explicit dreaming configuration on the selected slot owner still takes precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared resolver previously read only the slot owner's configuration, so an owner without a dreaming field silently defaulted to enabled. It now falls back to Memory Core's entry. Startup, managed-cron reconciliation, the cron hook and Doctor consume the same decision.

This complements #156667, which removes jobs after the sidecar unloads; it makes the opt-out reach that unloading decision.

Thanks to @etzelm for the fix and lifecycle reproduction. The diff-scoped simplification pass retained the fallback in the existing owner. Production +8 lines net is the explicit-owner/fallback decision; tests +20.

## Evidence

- Contributor regression: base plus the new test gives one failure/12 passes; head gives 13 passes. Sixteen affected resolver, loader, lifecycle and Doctor suites pass 329 tests.
- Contributor targeted checks and core/core-test typechecks pass.
- Contributor isolated real Gateway proof: released 2026.10.9 and current main create a managed dreaming job despite the opt-out; forcing it writes diaries. Upgrading the same state to main plus this fix removes the job and sidecar while preserving authored settings and memory/diary hashes.
- Contributor restart and hot-reload proof: current main retains the job; main plus this fix removes it. Explicit selected-owner dreaming=true still creates it; switching back to an owner without dreaming settings removes it. Fresh corrected state starts with zero jobs.
- Exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41157613621.
- Independent full-diff review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Trusted-tooling oxfmt and static oxlint pass on both changed source blobs. Full-graph proof remains the contributor checks and CI above.

Live Gateway lifecycle was not rerun in this lane; the existing contributor runs are retained as prior proof. The original PR head predates #156667: removal of an inherited job on plain restart depends on that now-merged companion fix, which the main-plus-PR proof includes.

Final ClawSweeper review found no code issues. Its latest-stable upgrade request remains a proof gap: the retained upgrade starts at 2026.10.9, and a 2026.10.10 upgrade was not rerun under the best-effort live-proof scope. The separate generic data-model concern does not warrant a code change: this patch changes only selection of existing configuration, introduces no schema or persisted fields, and the retained upgrade proof verifies authored settings and unchanged memory/diary hashes.


<details>
<summary>Contributor's original proof record</summary>

## Real behavior proof

Environment: Mac Studio (macOS, arm64, Node 24.22.2), real `openclaw gateway run` processes from built trees, each arm in its own `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` on loopback. Job state read with `openclaw automations list --all --json` (summarized to the dreaming row).

Builds:
- `v2026.10.9` from npm (`OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (8b18b55)`)
- current main `9f14244a6067` (parent of the merge ref, already includes #156667)
- main + this PR: `refs/pull/188950/merge` = `aebf4bba7848` (merges head `b242bf0f10907a1c20147b831c0c05dc7dff9397`)
- this PR head `b242bf0f1090` alone

Config in every arm (the same shape as the live report): the memory slot is owned by a local third-party plugin `acme-memory` (`kind: "memory"`, `configSchema.additionalProperties: false`, no `dreaming` key), and

```json
"memory-core": { "config": { "dreaming": { "enabled": false, "frequency": "0 4 * * *", "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles" } } }
```

The frequency and timezone make it easy to tell which entry a job was built from.

**1. Before: v2026.10.9, fresh state.** Memory Core starts as the sidecar and creates the job from defaults (`0 3`, no tz, `minRecallCount=3`), not from Memory Core's entry. `openclaw memory status` says `Dreaming: off` at the same time.

```
[plugins] memory-core: created managed dreaming cron job.
dreaming jobs: 1
  key=memory-core:memory-dreaming-promotion enabled=True schedule=0 3 * * * tz=None
```

Forcing that job (`openclaw automations run <id>`) writes dreaming output to the workspace:

```
[plugins] memory-core: dreaming promotion complete (workspaces=1, candidates=0, applied=0, failed=0, degraded=0, narrativesPending=2).
+ workspace/DREAMS.md
+ workspace/memory/dreaming/deep/2026-10-30.md
+ workspace/memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-30.md
+ workspace/memory/dreaming/rem/2026-10-30.md
```

**2. Upgrade v2026.10.9 -> main + this PR, same state dir.** The new build asks for `openclaw doctor --fix` (agent DB schema v25 -> v38, the normal upgrade step). Doctor, using the shared resolver, now sees the opt-out:

```
Retired 1 managed dreaming cron row(s) because dreaming is disabled.
Dreaming: disabled (cadence 0 4 * * *).
Next scheduled run: dreaming disabled.
```

Then on Gateway start: `dreaming jobs: 0`, and Memory Core no longer loads as a sidecar. Settings and data were kept: all 14 authored config keys keep their values (doctor only added `meta.*`, `wizard.*`, default `skills.entries.*` and `plugins.entries.memory-core.enabled`). The sha256 hashes of `MEMORY.md`, `memory/2026-10-29.md` and the earlier `DREAMS.md` are the same before and after. A later hot reload (`config set plugins.entries.acme-memory.config.endpoint ...`, `config hot reload applied`) still leaves 0 dreaming jobs.

For comparison, current main's doctor on the same config keeps the job:

```
Dreaming: enabled (cadence 0 3 * * *).
Next scheduled run: 2026-10-31T10:00:00.000Z.
dreaming jobs: 1  enabled=True schedule=0 3 * * *
```

**3. Restart, no doctor: current main -> main + this PR.** On current main with a fresh state you get `memory-core: created managed dreaming cron job.` and 1 job, so the bug is still on main even with #156667. Restarting the same state dir on main + this PR gives `dreaming jobs: 0 (total jobs 0)`.

**4. Hot reload, plus the explicit-owner control (main + this PR, one running Gateway):**
- `config set --batch-json` switches the slot to the bundled `memory-lancedb` with its own `dreaming.enabled: true`, while memory-core still says false. Hot reload logs `memory-core: created managed dreaming cron job.` and you get `dreaming jobs: 1`. The slot owner's explicit setting still wins.
- `config set plugins.slots.memory acme-memory` switches back to the owner without dreaming settings. Hot reload gives `dreaming jobs: 0`: the existing canonical row is removed without a restart.

**5. Fresh config on main + this PR:** 0 dreaming jobs and no sidecar from the first start.

**No later diary writes:** with the fix, no managed dreaming job exists and Memory Core is not loaded as a sidecar, so nothing is left to run the sweep or the `before_agent_reply` dreaming hook. In arm 2 `DREAMS.md` keeps its pre-upgrade hash.

**PR head alone (`b242bf0`, branched before #156667 landed):** a fresh config never creates the job, and `doctor --fix` retires an inherited one (`Retired 1 managed dreaming cron row(s) because dreaming is disabled`, then 0 jobs). A plain restart on the head alone keeps an inherited row, because removing a row after the sidecar unloads is #156667's job. The merge ref above shows the two together.

Behavior that did not change: when another owner has its own dreaming turned off, `openclaw memory` was already unavailable on current main, because Memory Core is not loaded. The same now applies to this configuration.

## Evidence (tests)

- Live observation (git install of main ac2c420): slot `hindsight-openclaw`, `plugins.entries.memory-core.config.dreaming.enabled=false` since 10-29, restart 10-29 12:11. On 10-30 at 03:01 the managed job ran: `memory-core: dreaming promotion complete (workspaces=8, candidates=0, applied=0, ...)` plus 5 `dream diary entry written for rem phase` lines, and DREAMS.md plus memory/dreaming/{light,rem}/2026-10-30.md were written.
- Red/green (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/memory-host-sdk/dreaming.test.ts`): base + new test only: 1 failed / 12 passed (`expected { apiUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:9077' } to deeply equal { dreaming: { enabled: false, …(1) } }`); with fix: 13 passed.
- Targeted suites with the fix, 16 files (resolver, plugin loader/startup plan/activation, dreaming reload, doctor, memory-core dreaming lifecycle and hook): 329 passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all lanes ok through `typecheck core`; `pnpm tsgo:core:test` run on its own: 29/29 shards passed.

</details>

prs.title: fix: resume conversations after a shared connection is retired
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a shared connection is retired, one conversation can stop responding even though its unsubscribe succeeded: cleanup waits for the whole connection to close while an unrelated conversation still uses it. Model fallback then repeats the same blocked startup.

## Evidence

The existing [retained-client release](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/adca087e79d1e9a342b0f3c150bd182144b16274/extensions/codex/src/app-server/shared-client-lifecycle.ts#L351-L359) waits for a retired connection's exit without distinguishing remote sockets from process-owned writers. The [thread handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/adca087e79d1e9a342b0f3c150bd182144b16274/extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle-warm.ts#L158-L177) enters that wait even after unsubscribe has completed. Another conversation's lease can keep the connection alive indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Allow a confirmed WebSocket or Unix-socket unsubscribe to finish that conversation's handoff independently. Process-owned writers, closed transports, and unconfirmed releases retain their shutdown fences. Startup cancellation also reports a harness failure so changing models does not repeat the same startup wait. This repair targets the release branch only.

The two focused suites passed 172 tests in 24.48 seconds with one worker. Hosted CI time is pending.

prs.title: fix(android): make sidebar session parentage explicit
prs.body:
Related: #150054 — Android-specific context: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150054#issuecomment-5848447065

## What Problem This Solves

Android needs an unambiguous choice between starting a new root chat and creating a child of the selected chat. Previously, implicit Gateway parentage could make a supposedly independent chat a child, while explicit children and grandchildren could appear at root in Threads.

## User Impact

- The sidebar header **+** starts an independent root session. There is no second, competing independent-session button.
- The selected eligible session's overflow menu offers **New child session**. Children and grandchildren retain their hierarchy in Threads.
- Existing sessions are not migrated or reparented. Connection, busy-state, write-access, and selected-parent guards remain.
- These creation actions require a Gateway supporting the new intent fields. An older Gateway gets an update-required error; the app does not silently fall back to different parentage.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair carries explicit child intent through creation, persisted session metadata, reset preservation, list/describe/event projection, and Android rendering. Ordinary New sends `independent: true`; child creation sends `explicitChild: true` with the selected parent. Existing upstream standalone/direct-chat behavior and visibility admission remain intact.

The public API rejects conflicting independent/parent intent and adoption of existing keys. A review-discovered edge case is also fixed: explicit child creation without a key cannot take the main-session reset shortcut and reset its parent.

This is an Android proposal, not a web Control UI `/new` change. **Maintainer acceptance of the public `sessions.create` fields and Android product behavior remains separate from this repair.** No upstream merge is requested by this update.

## Evidence

### Final conflict refresh — October 31

Latest head: `83a24f9b7ac18ea4c62e5b94a2404c22023a5c87`, integrating upstream `20cdaea4bb5fc2035949a39643ae2df413ed9f3b` with published `edd05d65883acfcadf20f7b7ba8ecadf9563a321` as first parent. Normal fast-forward publication, no force push.

Upstream advanced during the preceding validation. The only new conflict was the generated Gateway predicate output: canonical regeneration preserves upstream's optional publication-review URL field alongside this PR's session intent fields. Main inspected the incremental generated diff; no handwritten repair was needed. **36 affected schema/compiled-validator tests passed**, canonical freshness and native merge hooks passed, and the exact tree/parents were verified. Prior session lifecycle, inheritance, projection, catalog, lint/types/format and Android evidence remains scoped evidence for unchanged PR-owned inputs. Earlier UI build proof is not exact-current-head clearance because upstream also changed unrelated UI files. Hosted CI remains separate.

### Preceding repair and integration — October 31

Preceding repair head: `edd05d65883acfcadf20f7b7ba8ecadf9563a321`, integrating upstream `bf56514c98ecb628b406889e6d573d0485bfd53e` while preserving published `7e886928692e6897289bf66af707fb86646b0609` as its first parent. No force push.

The earlier Build dist failure was caused by a stale Control UI history-state validator after the session-row schema gained `explicitChild`. Canonical regeneration and a schema/standalone parity regression fixed it in `7e886928`: the regression failed before regeneration and passed afterward; all 29 validator tests, UI production build, scoped lint and test typechecking passed on that head.

The integration resolves the generated Gateway predicate conflict through canonical generation, preserves upstream session-creation authority and cancellation changes, and reuses the existing error-response helper to satisfy the session-creation file's line limit without changing error behavior.

- Integration validation: 17 Gateway lifecycle tests, 2 inheritance tests and 13 session-entry projection tests passed on the integration candidate. The only subsequent source edit was the equivalent catalog error-response simplification; 2 selected public-handler catalog rejection tests passed afterward (22 unrelated cases were intentionally not selected).
- Scoped Gateway lint, Gateway-server typechecking, formatting and diff whitespace checks passed on the final tree. Gateway and UI generated-output freshness checks remain applicable: generator inputs and outputs did not change after those checks.
- Main independently inspected the integration's three handwritten merge owners, the final error-response change, generated-validator parity and proof applicability; no actionable integration finding remained. Earlier full-feature independent review is described below. The standalone autoreview authentication gap remains; this is not a claim of an autoreview or ClawSweeper pass on the new head.
- Earlier UI and Android build/test evidence below is scoped prior-head evidence, not a fresh full-suite run on this integration. No new APK or live-device test was performed. Hosted CI and maintainer product/API acceptance remain separate gates.

### Earlier feature repair evidence

Repair commit: `6a07b12ac85ece37ddaf80a002266969ddcd29eb`.
Integrated upstream: `54c3474691a6adc971056be145135d9146289394`. The update preserves the previously published head as its first parent; it is not a force push.

### Fresh focused validation

- **17 Gateway lifecycle tests passed**, including independent roots, explicit child/grandchild persistence and projection, reset retention, conflicting intent, and existing-key rejection. The new no-key child regression failed before the reset fix and passed afterward; it verifies a distinct child, unchanged parent entry, child metadata, and no parent-end hook.
- **2 inheritance-owner tests and 13 session-entry projection contract tests passed.**
- **69 Android tests passed**: controller creation (5), sidebar/Threads UI (2), grouping (24), and command controls (38). Production/test compilation and `:app:ktlintCheck` passed.
- Targeted TypeScript lint, Gateway-server typecheck, formatting, native-string inventory, canonical Gateway validator regeneration, and whitespace checks passed.
- Independent read-only code review covered the complete candidate. Its one actionable finding—the no-key child reset path—was fixed, regression-tested, and reviewed again. The standalone autoreview CLI could not authenticate; the independent review ran through the connected coding-agent session instead. No standalone-autoreview success is claimed.
- A normal hook-enabled merge commit was created in a secretless container, with exact tree and both parents verified. Merge-mode hook behavior is not a claim that all ordinary-commit checks ran.

Gateway checks used isolated repository harnesses and the repository-supported Node/oxlint fallback because the pinned Bun runtime could not be staged in the offline proof environment. Android dependency hydration/build used a task-owned secretless container. Full hosted CI is separate; earlier failed checks belong to the old head and are not represented as cleared by these local results.

### Before / after

Inspected synthetic Compose test renders, not connected-device screenshots. The historical before image shows the redundant root action and inline child action. The repaired sidebar uses one header New action plus the selected row's overflow menu. Minor speckling in the sidebar render is a test-raster artifact; incidental navigation ordering is not the claimed change.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: redundant independent action and inline child action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/0e0a214538c4414432318b4ec46e251964e14696/20261031-before.png) | ![After: one header New action and selected-row overflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/0e0a214538c4414432318b4ec46e251964e14696/20261031-after.png) |

![Selected-row menu: New child session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/0e0a214538c4414432318b4ec46e251964e14696/20261031-child-menu.png)

![Threads: Project, Child, and Grandchild remain nested; Ordinary New is a separate root](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/0e0a214538c4414432318b4ec46e251964e14696/20261031-threads.png)

### Scope and remaining limits

No new APK installation or live Android-to-Gateway device test was performed. Public-handler and rendering tests prove the scoped boundaries, not a full deployed-version upgrade matrix. [Earlier contributor-reported device evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159159#issuecomment-5901361888) predates this candidate and is not exact-head proof. The full cross-platform suite was not rerun locally; current-head CI and maintainer review remain merge gates.

The repair uses the existing creation, lineage, projection, and reset owners rather than adding a parallel hierarchy manager. Its necessary growth is the explicit intent contract and boundary regressions; most generated-code churn is canonical predicate renumbering.

#192806 (4a43644e7a7b) made `scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts` import `./lib/check-limits.mts`, which in turn imports `release-context.mjs` and `release-version.mjs`. Copy the ratchet's full relative import set into the fixture.

prs.title: perf(ui): share overlapping model catalog refreshes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Withdrawn: the attempted reduction of overlapping `models.list` requests violates catalog-publication freshness. This PR must not land.

## User Impact

The candidate can retain stale model choices or an authentication failure after a newer publication. The original cancellation behavior is required by current consumers.

## Why This Change Was Made

The proposed reorder acquired a replacement subscriber before aborting the old one. A synthetic browser probe showed four overlapping catalog-event reads becoming one, but those events invalidate the previous intent. The replacement reader then accepts a request started before the change. The reduced count is not a valid performance improvement.

The separate native/placement producer audit found that prepared native ownership and worker inference already reach the existing `sessionModelRevision`. The raw row builder's undefined inference argument is replaced by the final placement-aware facts. No producer fix was justified by the synthetic omission probe.

## Evidence

CI run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41970820303

Three existing consumer regressions reproduced locally on the candidate (79 passed, 3 failed across 82 tests):

- `ui/src/components/command-palette.test.ts`: publication replacement must fence the old catalog.
- `ui/src/pages/agents/agents-page.test.ts`: a newer publication must reject the old model read.
- `ui/src/pages/new-session/model-control.metadata-lifecycle.test.ts`: a successful auth refresh must clear the previous auth failure.

Running the identical 82 tests with the original reader restored passed all 82 (22.05 seconds wall time; candidate 36.97 seconds). These are candidate-caused regressions, not inherited CI failures.

The independent reviewer withdrew the initial clean verdict and accepted the freshness issue as P1. The new request-count regression had encoded the wrong sharing assumption. No clean review or green CI is claimed for this candidate.

CI additionally reported 31 new test lines against the test-line budget and 248 bytes of new-route gzip growth against an already-over-budget base (192-byte build-variance allowance). Neither baseline was changed.

Unchanged producer proof: 27 focused tests passed; a direct placement-owner probe matched the worker-inference catalog revision and invalidated on worker attachment change. Synthetic Control UI checks retained zero additional reads for certified native patches and one refresh for each changed model/account/placement/auth revision. These checks do not attribute production session-scoped traffic.

prs.title: fix(telegram): drop native commands from DM senders dmPolicy does not admit
prs.body:
Closes #181955

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: with `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`, a stranger's ordinary DM is dropped silently, but their builtin native command (`/think`, `/login`, ...) gets the reply `You are not authorized to use this command.` — confirming to an unknown sender that a bot is listening. Scoped direct-chat allowlists could still reach an earlier refusal even after the first repair.

## User Impact
Unadmitted DM senders, including senders excluded by a scoped direct-chat allowlist, are now ignored for native commands exactly as they are for ordinary messages. Senders admitted by dmPolicy but denied by `commands.allowFrom` keep the deliberate refusal; explicit command grants, owners, and group-command behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made
Native dispatch has more than one visible authorization-refusal boundary. A scoped direct `allowFrom` rejection happens during base-access evaluation, before final command authorization, so a final-only silence check left that path visible. The shared refusal path now applies the same DM-admission decision at every visible boundary. The final gate uses the latest owner result, while earlier boundaries preserve their existing explicit-grant and scoped-restriction semantics.

## Evidence
- Registered Bot pipeline with an owned loopback Bot API fixture: on the previous head, scoped-direct `/think` still produced the refusal (base-red). After the repair, account-level and scoped excluded senders produce no outbound reply and start no turn. An admitted command-denied sender still receives the refusal, an explicitly authorized sender retains the `/think` argument menu, and the existing group refusal regression stays green.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` against `bot-native-command-dispatch.routing.test.ts`, `.delivery.test.ts`, and `.concurrency.test.ts`: 38/38 passed. `bot-native-commands.registry.test.ts`: 8/8 passed, including `requireAuth:false` plugin commands. Node 24.22.1.
- Both extension production and extension-test tsgo lanes passed. Targeted extension lint completed with 0 warnings/errors across 292 rules, oxfmt passed, the SQLite worker ratchet passed against the PR merge base, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Broader local coverage is not claimed green: `pnpm test:extension telegram` timed out after 30 minutes with the first 11 files passing and no observed test failure; it did not finish. The full changed-check also reports existing dead-export findings outside this diff.
- Live Telegram Test Server proof was not run: the standalone doctor found no authenticated Convex launcher or broker environment pair, so no live trace or live cleanup is claimed. Independent `autoreview` produced no verdict because Codex returned HTTP 403.

prs.title: fix(telegram): ignore native commands from senders the DM policy rejects
prs.body:
Closes #181955

## What Problem This Solves

With `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`, a normal message from a sender who is not on the list is dropped. The same sender's native command (`/status` and the rest of the menu) got the reply "You are not authorized to use this command." That tells a stranger a bot is listening.

## User Impact

Senders the DM policy does not admit get no reply to native commands, the same as for ordinary messages. A sender who is admitted but is not allowed to run the command still gets the refusal. Pairing still replies, so a first contact can finish the challenge. `commands.allowFrom` denials are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

#131408 made the refusal text deliberate for a channel-admitted sender who lacks command permission. This path was also used when `dmPolicy` itself rejected the sender. The command authorization result now carries that distinction, and the native-command dispatch returns without sending when the denial is `dm_policy_not_allowlisted` or `dm_policy_disabled`.

## Evidence

Regression in `src/channels/message-access/telegram-native-owner.test.ts`: a native command as sender 300 with `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` and `allowFrom: ["999999"]` must not call the handler and must not send a message. The existing owner-admission cases still expect the refusal text.

I could not run the OpenClaw suite on this machine. CI is the run that counts.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

prs.title: fix(codex): hold a finished child's completion while a sibling protects the parent
prs.body:
Related: #188422 ## What Problem This Solves A Codex-harness parent that yields after spawning several native children keeps its native parent subscription alive while any child is still running (`releaseParentThreadIfChildrenSettled` returns early for a non-terminal sibling — intentional, `native-subagent-monitor.parent-retention.test.ts` pins it). A _finished_ child's announce cannot always reuse that subscription: `tryReuseCodexLiveThread` only continues an idle retained thread, so a parent that has nothing idle to continue falls through to `releaseCodexBoundLiveThread`, which refuses while that same retention is held. So a finished child whose sibling is still running was treated as deliverable, the announce was refused with `Codex thread

is claimed by active work; stop it first.`, and the refusal was charged against the completion retry budget. On 2026.10.9 the first refused announce was read back by the core reconcile step as a recovery receipt (`recoveryBlocked`), which abandoned the result immediately: `Native subagent completion retired without delivery`. A successful child's result was lost, and the parent stayed unusable for ordinary turns until the sibling settled. Retention alone does not mean the announce must release the parent: protected warm-parent continuation (the merged #174900 path) still reaches a retained thread through `tryReuseCodexLiveThread`. So this change holds a completion back only when the retention leaves the parent **no announce route but that release**, and it announces otherwise: - `native-parent-thread-announce.ts` answers that question from live-thread ownership: a protected parent can still be announced when it holds an idle subscription (warm continuation), and cannot when the only ownership left is the claim retention is parking. - `CodexNativeSubagentCompletionDelivery` defers only for that case (`mustWaitForSiblingRelease`), without spending a retry attempt, mirroring the existing deferral for a foreground-owned parent. The execution custody root is kept for the same reason: no attempt was made, so nothing is settled. - `releaseParentThreadIfChildrenSettled` re-drives held completions (`deliverDetached`) after the release it performs, which is the exact moment the announce path can succeed. Scope is limited to delivery timing. Parent retention, entry predicates, write admission, revocation and the retry schedule are untouched; a completion that is attempted and fails still retries and is still bounded, and an announce that a retained parent can already carry is never delayed. ## Evidence Red first, on the previous head, with the existing integration case that a blanket hold regressed — a settled child's result is expected while its sibling still runs: ```text $ node scripts/test-projects.mts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.native-followup-custody.test.ts × reports an earlier turn's unsettled native child to a later turn's sessions_yield AssertionError: expected spy to have been called with ... "Settled result" Tests 1 failed | 5 passed (6) ``` Red for the new warm case on the same head, and green after the change: ```text × announces a finished child through the parent's idle subscription while a sibling still runs AssertionError: expected [] to deeply equal [ 'first result' ] Tests 1 failed | 3 passed (4) # before ✓ keeps an interrupted assignment resumable without pinning its restored parent ✓ announces a finished child through the parent's idle subscription while a sibling still runs ✓ holds a finished child's completion when the blocked release is its only route to the parent ✓ permits parent cold resume once every child is terminal, while preserving undelivered results Tests 4 passed (4) # after ``` The two new cases split the behaviour the review asked for. The warm case keeps the parent's idle subscription while a sibling runs and asserts the finished child is announced immediately, then again from the sibling release. The refused-delivery case keeps no idle subscription, asserts no attempt and nothing charged over 10 minutes of retry-schedule time, then asserts both results arrive in order from the sibling release. The custody case above, plus the delivery and monitor suites, on the same head — no expectation edited: ```text run-attempt.native-followup-custody.test.ts 6 passed native-subagent-monitor.parent-retention.test.ts 4 passed native-subagent-monitor.completion-delivery.test.ts 17 passed monitor + custody + direct-authority + release-retry + parent-retention + custody-run (7 files, one batch) 96 passed (34 + 62) ``` Static checks on this head: ```text ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <6 touched files> Found 0 warnings and 0 errors. node scripts/run-format.mts --check All matched files use the correct format. node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts Test lines OK: 6390157; ceiling: 6401632. ``` `run-oxlint.mjs` / `run-tsgo.mjs` cannot run on this host right now: after the tree moved, `node_modules/@openclaw/fs-safe` no longer matches the checked-out commit, so their boundary/type steps fail on pre-existing errors in `src/agents/host-file-write.ts`, `src/infra/private-dir-mode.ts`, `src/config/io.audit.ts` and `extensions/memory-core`. None of them is in a touched file; running `tsgo -p tsconfig.extensions.json` and filtering the output for `subagent`/`app-server`/`native-parent` returns nothing. The same fallback (`./node_modules/.bin/oxlint`) is what the earlier revision used for lint. CI will type-check with matching dependencies. Test-line allocation: `config/test-lines-allocations/codex-native-completion-sibling-hold.txt` = 41 net added test lines (counted after `run-format`). Not demonstrated here: an end-to-end run against an independently started Gateway with the real Codex app-server. This host cannot build the shipped gateway (`dist`), so the only trace I can produce is the unit/integration-harness one above; the integration lane will have to confirm it.

## What Problem This Solves The Android chat screen shows "Could not refresh models. Tap Refresh to try again." when `chat.metadata` fails. In that case `models.list` never runs. A transient metadata read race, for example the Gateway `UNAVAILABLE` "Session changed while preparing its metadata. Retry the request.", looks like a model catalog outage. After this change, a `chat.metadata` failure shows "Could not refresh chat metadata. Tap Refresh to try again." A `models.list` failure or a `refreshFailed` catalog still shows the models notice. The accepted model choices stay in the picker in both cases. The existing Refresh action clears both notices. ## Why This Change Was Made - `fetchChatMetadata` records when `chat.metadata` succeeds. The failure handler uses that flag to select the metadata notice or the models notice. - `isChatMetadataNotice` treats both notices as one group. `refresh()` keeps either notice, a `refreshFailed` catalog replaces either notice, and a clean refresh clears either notice. - The new string goes through `pnpm native:i18n:baseline`. prs.title: fix(exec): successful commands reported as failed when they start a detached daemon on macOS
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on macOS, `exec` reports a command that succeeded as `failed` (`runtime-error`, exit code lost) when the command starts a daemon that detaches from its process group, for example `tmux new -d` starting a tmux server.

## User Impact

User impact: agents see the command's real exit code and output instead of a cryptic "service child cleanup did not complete before its hard deadline" failure, plus a short note that a detached process may still be running and that long-lived services belong in `background: true`. Agents stop retrying or second-guessing commands that already did their job. Failed and canceled commands, request Stop, and Gateway shutdown keep reporting the cleanup failure exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #150750, exec stops and joins a completed command's process tree before reporting. On macOS the owner is the process group, so a descendant that calls `setsid` (a tmux server) escapes it and keeps the inherited lineage pipe open. The supervisor correctly cannot confirm extinction and rejects at its cleanup deadline, but exec then rewrote the already observed, successful outcome into a runtime error. The relay host already states the intended rule ("Authority loss cannot erase an already observed root result"); exec now follows it.

For a completed, non-canceled command, exec keeps the observed outcome, marks the session's cleanup as uncertain (so request owners and one-shot cleanup scopes still report it), logs the redacted diagnostic, and appends one actionable note. The supervisor's own accounting is untouched: scope retirement and `supervisor.shutdown()` still reject with the cleanup failure. Windows `uncertain` extinction results keep their existing silent handling. Linux is unaffected in practice because its subreaper adopts and stops such daemons.

## Evidence

- Real macOS reproduction through `createExecTool` with a real supervisor and real tmux (`tmux -S <sock> new -d -s work; tmux -S <sock> new-window -d -P -F '#{window_id}'`), run as a local scratch test in the database-worker lane:
  - before: `status: "failed"`, `exitCode: null`, output `@1` followed by the deadline error, after ~8.9 s
  - after: `status: "completed"`, `exitCode: 0`, output `@1` plus the note; `supervisor.shutdown()` still rejects with "did not complete before its hard deadline"
- Same failure shape observed on a real macOS Gateway session that ran `tmux new -d`: `failed`/`runtime-error` although the window existed and the next command used it.
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.cleanup.test.ts`: new cases for exit 0 and exit 3 (completed outcome and its "(Command exited with code 3)" text preserved, note appended) are red on the base and green with the fix; the exit 127 case guards that failed commands still report the cleanup failure. Whole file: 21 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, type-aware oxlint on the touched files, and `format:check`: clean.

Gaps: the ~9 s wait for the cleanup deadline before the result returns is unchanged. The tmux reproduction is not committed because it needs tmux on the runner and spends the full cleanup deadline; the unit cases cover the exec mapping.

Closes #186721

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: finished Run history rows show a relative `Next in` or `Due ... ago` label that changes with the clock.

## User Impact

User impact: each Run history row shows the next run time that the job had at the end of that run, as a fixed date and time.

## Why This Change Was Made

The row now formats `nextRunAtMs` with the same timestamp formatter as the other times in the row. This removes `formatRunNextLabel` and the unused `cron.runEntry.due` string.

## Evidence

Real Gateway on Linux, main `01d66c79` against this branch, built Control UI. One job that runs every 2 minutes, with its run history open about 40 minutes later.

| | Main | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Newest row | `Next in 42m` | `Next 10/28/2026, 9:46 AM` |
| Older rows | `Due 18m ago`, `Due 33m ago`, `Due 39m ago` | `Next 10/28/2026, 8:45 AM`, `8:30 AM`, `8:25 AM` |

| Before | After |

| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jondihaynes/openclaw/proof-bug-fixes-6-7-8/proof-bug-fixes-6-7-8/8-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jondihaynes/openclaw/proof-bug-fixes-6-7-8/proof-bug-fixes-6-7-8/8-after.png) |

prs.title: fix(wiki): refresh ChatGPT transcripts containing Notes markers
prs.body:
Fixes #193161

## What Problem This Solves

Re-importing a ChatGPT conversation whose transcript contains a literal Notes opening marker inside Markdown code can silently retain the old transcript. The shared Notes parser pairs that example marker with the real final closing marker and preserves too much of the old page.

## User Impact

Updated transcript text is refreshed while handwritten Notes remain byte-exact. Malformed real Notes slots still refuse updates rather than overwrite handwritten content. No new format, retention policy or configuration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing length-preserving `maskMarkdownCode` owner before selecting Notes markers, retaining the existing Content boundary and original byte offsets. Only `producerMarkdown` continues to allow markerless producer documents; ChatGPT does not enable that mode. The preservation splice still copies original Notes bytes, not masked text.

Original fix and report by @KhanCold; contributor commit retained unchanged. The existing ChatGPT fixture factory replaces duplicate setup, and existing regression cases now cover fenced transcript markers, strict malformed-slot rejection and an unchanged next import. Net test lines are zero, with no allocation file.

## Evidence

[Independent exact-head built Linux CLI proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193173#issuecomment-6650058142): main `bca996c12f5568a125d2159fc87186213f1a705c` versus candidate `9b37d380ddbc0afa09b3b2f7cd2cbaa1e7f954ad`, **twice each** in isolated Node 24.22.1 Docker.

- Fenced marker transcript: main exits 0 but keeps CODE_v1; candidate writes CODE_v2. Handwritten final Notes remain byte-exact, including Unicode, whitespace, dollar sequences and a marker example.
- Normal re-import refreshes on both refs. An unchanged next import leaves the whole page byte-identical.
- Missing opening, closing or both real Notes markers remain refused with unchanged page bytes on both refs.
- The consolidated regression fails on main with zero updates/one skip instead of one update. Candidate: **83 tests pass across seven focused files**, plus changed-file lint/format checks. Harness setup corrections are disclosed in the evidence.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the old marker selection without migrations or a new published contract. Blast radius is code-aware marker selection in shared Memory Wiki Notes preservation/extraction, including ChatGPT, ingest, source synchronization and OKF. Strict default refusal and OKF's existing producer-mode distinction remain unchanged.

prs.title: fix: retry model listing when a remote catalog replaces its snapshot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `models.list` can return retryable `UNAVAILABLE` when a remote catalog publication replaces the snapshot between acquisition and projection, even though a replacement is ready and clients do not retry.

## User Impact

Model listing uses the current replacement without asking the client to retry. Account unlink and other authority changes retain their existing rejection behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The remote publication owner records the exact retired-to-replacement generation. Catalog acquisition rereads published facts once only while that replacement remains current, before capturing private account facts. It does not replay discovery or introduce a generic retry for supersession errors.

This is intentionally bounded to published-catalog acquisition. It does not retry later account-preparation failures or independently cached/preloaded chat-metadata failures. The acquisition operation lives in a focused sibling module to preserve the listing owner's enforced line cap.

## Evidence

- Real `models.list` handler plus remote publication owner regression: fails against base production code (the handler returns failure), passes with the fix and replacement rows.
- Remote publication followed by retirement of its replacement still rejects without rereading.
- Focused tests: 47 passed across `prepared-model-runtime.remote-publication.test.ts`, `models-list-result.plugin-runtime.test.ts`, `models-list-result.configured-static.test.ts`, and `model-account-catalog-authority.integration.test.ts`, including unlink during auth and DNS. All 47 also passed after extraction.
- Final extracted remote suite: 10 passed, 18.30 seconds suite duration. Other three suites: 37 passed, 118.34 seconds. The combined command completed in 184.03 seconds including worker preparation. These are local durations; hosted CI timing is pending. Fixtures isolate provider I/O; this is not a live-provider claim.
- Original-head formatting, diff checks, and staged line-cap ratchet passed. Original core typecheck/lint bootstrap was blocked by inherited MCP declaration errors; see the current-head validation below.
- Independent review: no actionable P0–P3 findings; fresh extraction-only review also found no actionable issues. Local ClawSweeper review complete for `34007820fa2c..19c133d7d247`: no actionable correctness or security findings.
- Simplification retains every existing authority predicate and introduces no handler-wide retry. Net production growth is 47 lines; 38 net test lines cover successful replacement and revoked-replacement rejection, with a separate allocation record.

## RFR follow-up

Rebased without conflicts onto main `982f3b1ee2b668afafe69c352d48baef470d2d20` because [#192387](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192387) has now merged the stale Goal assertion correction. Current head: `7a93c35617dd4da2c456fb7144c3b0a144d16ed5`.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes overlapping session avatars showing through the front face when the owner is not viewing the conversation.

## User Impact

The owner keeps the same dimmed, mostly grayscale “not viewing” appearance, while the participant behind it stays properly occluded. Avatar identities, presence semantics, run indicators, and geometry are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the stack’s existing right-hand cutout as an opaque, row-composited backing beneath the dimmed face. Clip the row-tint layer inside the border to avoid applying translucent selected/hover colors twice. Preserve the higher counter layer for participant overflow. The occlusion repair stays in scoped CSS; no new component wrappers or presence state. A follow-up removes redundant sidebar-agent image loading while preserving canonical URL admission, authentication gating, and the inner avatar’s resource ownership. The overflow cutout selects its existing higher stack layer through a custom property, avoiding a separate selector override.

## Evidence

Before and after were captured from the full built Control UI with synthetic users and mocked Gateway responses. The before capture applies the original stylesheet from base commit c8094c112b45a3b7ab378af7668be0f60cafd0cd over the same app; the after uses the candidate stylesheet. No live production state was changed.

After:

prs.body:
Closes #190719

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a saved `openclaw memory forget --json` report does not disclose that another plugin's memories were outside the deletion's coverage.

## User Impact

User impact: when another plugin owns the memory slot, JSON includes `provider` and `memoryCore: "consolidation-sidecar"`, matching `memory status --json`. Memory Core-owned JSON, human output and stderr notices remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The coverage notice already goes to stderr, which scripts may discard. The JSON renderer now records that existing fact using the existing status fields. Deletion behavior stays with its current owner; selected-plugin deletion is the separate feature in #190720.

Thanks to @etzelm for the fix and built-CLI reproduction. The diff-scoped simplification pass retained the small conditional at the output boundary and the documentation. Production +5 lines net; tests +26; docs +2.

## Evidence

- Contributor regression on base 3259404694b: one failed/nine passed. With the fix, the slot and CLI suites pass all 68 tests.
- Contributor built CLI on isolated macOS state with no Gateway or credentials: `openclaw memory forget --agent main --session proof-forget-session --dry-run --json`, capturing stdout and stderr separately.
- With a foreign slot owner, base omits coverage from stdout and head adds exactly the two fields. With Memory Core selected, stdout is byte-identical between refs. The stderr notice is preserved.
- Contributor changed-file checks passed except an unrelated dead-export report for `ui/src/components/image-lightbox.tsx: ImageLightbox`.
- Exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41368861093.
- Independent full-diff review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Trusted-tooling oxfmt passes all three changed files and static oxlint passes the TypeScript blobs. Full-graph proof remains the contributor checks and CI above.

Live CLI proof was not rerun in this lane; the contributor's existing isolated run is retained as prior proof.


<details>
<summary>Contributor's original proof record</summary>

## Evidence

Built CLI (`pnpm build:runtime`, run as `node openclaw.mjs`) on macOS. Each run used its own `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, with no Gateway running and no credentials. One owner session was seeded into that state.

Command for every case: `openclaw memory forget --agent main --session proof-forget-session --dry-run --json`, with stdout and stderr captured separately.

**Memory Core as sidecar** (`plugins.slots.memory = "memory-lancedb"`, dreaming enabled):

- **Before, merge base 3259404694b:** stdout ends at `"refusals": []`, and nothing in the JSON names the selected plugin. stderr has the notice:

```text
Memory Core is running as the consolidation sidecar; plugins.slots.memory selects "memory-lancedb". This command acts on Memory Core's sidecar index, not the agent's selected memory.
```

- **After, c435743ec7a:** same session resolution and counts. The report gains the two fields:

```text
  "refusals": [],
  "provider": "memory-lancedb",
  "memoryCore": "consolidation-sidecar"
}
```

  stderr has the same notice as before.

**Memory Core selected** (`plugins.slots.memory = "memory-core"`), after c435743ec7a: stdout is the same report as on the merge base, ending at `"refusals": []` with no added fields. stderr has no notice, only the plugin loader lines that both refs print, for example `[plugins] loading memory-core from <repo>/dist/extensions/memory-core/cli-metadata.js`.

Diffing stdout between the two refs: the Memory Core case has no differences, and the sidecar case differs only by the two added fields.

<details><summary>Full CLI captures (redacted)</summary>
