prs.title: fix(plugins): every Codex turn fails when a left-behind Codex plugin predates 2026.11.5
prs.body:
Closes #192759

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex turns fail with a missing SDK export when current OpenClaw runs with a left-behind Codex plugin from 2026.9.7 through 2026.10.10.

## User Impact

User impact: the Gateway refuses the incompatible plugin at startup with the existing guidance to run `openclaw update repair` or `openclaw plugins update codex`, then restart. Codex remains unavailable until the plugin is repaired.

## Why This Change Was Made

#180106 removed `HEARTBEAT_RESPONSE_TOOL_NAME` from the SDK surface. The published 2026.10.10 Codex package still imports it; 2026.11.5-beta.1 is the first compatible published runtime. Raising the existing compatibility floor rejects the bad runtime before activation and keeps version policy with its current owner.

Thanks to @sukhdeepjohar for the fix and isolated reproduction. Independent inspection confirmed the removal commit and the differing public package contents. The existing version comparator handles prerelease ordering. The diff-scoped simplification pass retained the one-line floor change and updated six-row test; production and test LOC are both net zero.

## Evidence

- Contributor loader regression: base with the updated table gives one failure/five passes; head gives six passes. Neighboring install/update suites pass 11 and four tests respectively. Targeted lint, format and core/core-test typechecks pass.
- Contributor isolated packaged-Gateway proof: old plugin loads on base but the first turn fails importing the removed export. Head refuses it with repair guidance; the compatible plugin reaches the provider (expected 401 from a dummy key).
- Contributor repair proof on a beta-labelled host: `openclaw plugins update codex` updates 2026.10.10 to 2026.11.5-beta.1; after restart the turn reaches the provider. Doctor also updates it, but exits 1 on a separate migration-authority refusal.
- Independent public-package inspection found the obsolete import in 2026.10.10 and none in 2026.11.5-beta.1. Contributor import audit resolved all 500 named SDK imports in the compatible package.
- Exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41823462504.
- Independent diff review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Trusted-tooling oxfmt and static oxlint pass on the two exact-head source blobs; full-graph type proof remains the contributor checks and CI above.

Live Gateway/repair was not rerun in this lane. The contributor set the host label to 2026.11.5-beta.1 because main still carries 2026.10.10. Plain stable-channel repair on that main label, `openclaw update repair`, and a real model reply were not live-tested.


<details>
<summary>Contributor's original proof record</summary>

## Evidence

### Full-product repro on main (live run)

Isolated Gateway from a real npm package built from `main` `4b13fade1e6`, `@openclaw/codex@2026.10.10` installed from npm, one Codex turn (dummy model key; the failure happens before any model request):

```text
plugins list: codex 2026.10.10 loaded
[agents/harness] Codex agent harness failed; not falling back to embedded OpenClaw backend harnessId=codex provider=openai modelId=gpt-5.6-sol error="The requested module 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime' does not provide an export named 'HEARTBEAT_RESPONSE_TOOL_NAME'"
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ agent errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=The requested module 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime' does not provide an export named 'HEARTBEAT_RESPONSE_TOOL_NAME'
```

The published `2026.11.5-beta.1` shows the same failure, both with the plugin installed directly and after a plain `npm i -g openclaw@2026.11.5-beta.1` over a stable 2026.10.10 install (the plugin stays at 2026.10.10).

### With this change (same setup, package built from this branch)

| Codex plugin | Result |
|---|---|
| 2026.10.10 (left behind) | refused at startup: `Official runtime plugin codex 2026.10.10 is incompatible with OpenClaw 2026.11.5-beta.1 (minimum compatible plugin version is 2026.11.5-beta.1); it is unavailable until repaired. Run openclaw update repair or openclaw plugins update codex, then restart the Gateway.` The turn reports `Agent harness runtime "codex" is unavailable … Owner plugin "codex" failed during validation` |
| 2026.11.5-beta.1 | loads; the turn reaches the provider (401 on the dummy key), no import error |
| 2026.10.10, then `openclaw plugins update codex` (the command the refusal names) | `Updated codex: 2026.10.10 -> 2026.11.5-beta.1.`; after restart the turn reaches the provider |
| 2026.10.10, then `openclaw doctor --fix` | Doctor also updated codex to 2026.11.5-beta.1 and the turn then reaches the provider, but Doctor exited 1 on a separate check (`plugin-doctor-state (step-refused): Refused plugin migrations that do not match the immutable action order and authority declared by codex`); not investigated here |

Import check: all named `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` imports in the installed `@openclaw/codex@2026.11.5-beta.1` (179 built files, 97 subpaths, 500 names) exist in the package built from this branch: 0 missing.

Checks on this branch (isolated Linux test machine, Node 26, targeted):
- `loader.runtime-version.test.ts` on `main` with the updated table: the left-behind row fails (`expected 'loaded' to be 'error'`), the other five pass; with this change 6/6 pass.
- Neighbours that install or update codex: `missing-configured-plugin-install.version-drift.test.ts` and `.availability.test.ts` 11 passed; `plugins-update-command.generation.integration.test.ts` 4 passed.
- Core and core-test typecheck, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files: clean.

Proof artifice: dummy model key (every result is decided before a model request); host version label set to `2026.11.5-beta.1` (`OPENCLAW_COMPATIBILITY_HOST_VERSION` for the messages, and the package version for the repair rows) because `main` still carries the `2026.10.10` label; packages built with the repo's Docker packer and installed with `npm i -g`.

Test lines are net 0 against `main`: the six-row table changes values only.

Not tested: `openclaw update repair` (it updates core from the registry; the beta's core has no floor fix yet), and a real model reply.

</details>

prs.title: fix(daemon): Gateway repair stops the Gateway and fails when macOS denies the Trash
prs.body:
Related: #188563

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: macOS Gateway removal and repair stop after bootout when moving the LaunchAgent plist into Trash fails with EPERM or EACCES.

## User Impact

User impact: removal can finish without Full Disk Access. A timestamped Trash destination preserves earlier items; if Trash access is denied, the already-unloaded plist is deleted so reinstall can proceed.

If deleting the plist also fails, that failure still propagates and the service stays unloaded. Restoring the previous service in that case is outside this fix, so this PR does not close the whole issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared plist owner now handles disposal for both uninstall and Doctor's legacy cleanup. Both callers unload the service first. Only EPERM/EACCES trigger deletion; other errors preserve their existing handling.

Thanks to @sukhdeepjohar for the fix and detailed macOS reproduction. The diff-scoped simplification pass retained one shared disposal owner for the two callers. Production +21 lines net is the common fallback plus timestamped destination; tests +33 and test allocation +2.

## Evidence

- Contributor red/green: `src/daemon/launchd.test.ts` rejects on base when Trash is denied, then passes all 74 tests with the fix. The two Doctor suites pass 65 tests, including denied-Trash cleanup.
- Contributor checks: changed-file formatting/lint plus core and core-test typechecks pass.
- Contributor live proof on isolated AWS Macs, macOS 26.5 and 27: released app reproduces EPERM with a pre-existing same-name Trash item. Applying the removal logic allows uninstall; restoring release code restores the failure. The existing Trash item keeps its hash.
- The final branch-built release-tag-plus-patch cycle uses the timestamped destination, removes the service, allows app takeover, then reinstalls successfully with HTTP 200 and unchanged config hash. An earlier branch-built fixed-name cycle separately exercises EPERM → unlink successfully.
- Exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41258932756.
- Independent whole-diff review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Trusted-tooling oxfmt and static oxlint pass on all five changed TypeScript blobs. Full type-aware proof remains the contributor checks and CI above; loose blobs do not reproduce the project import graph.

Live macOS removal was not rerun in this lane; these are contributor-provided runs. Current-main app builds, Doctor's legacy cleanup live, the reporter's exact 26.5.1 build and restoration after unlink failure were not live-tested.


<details>
<summary>Contributor's original proof record</summary>

## Evidence

Runs on an AWS EC2 Mac (macOS 27.0, Node 24), this branch on main `82c8ad576b3`.

**Regression test** (`src/daemon/launchd.test.ts`, `removes the booted-out plist when Trash mkdir/rename is denied without Full Disk Access`): the real `uninstallLaunchAgent` with the launchd and file-system fixtures, where creating or renaming into `~/.Trash` fails with `EPERM`.

```
# main (test only)
× launchd uninstall > removes the booted-out plist when Trash mkdir is denied without Full Disk Access
  → promise rejected "Error: LaunchAgent removal failed (EPERM)…" instead of resolving
# with the fix
src/daemon/launchd.test.ts                 Tests 74 passed (74)
src/commands/doctor-gateway-legacy-services.test.ts + src/commands/doctor-gateway-services.test.ts
                                           Tests 65 passed (65), combined across both files
```

Doctor's legacy LaunchAgent cleanup is covered by a new row in its existing table (`doctor-gateway-legacy-services.test.ts`, `settles legacy macOS cleanup for Trash-denied plist`): the Trash move fails with `EPERM`, the plist is deleted, cleanup reports it removed, and the note names no Trash destination.

Format and lint pass on the changed files (pre-commit). `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass.

### Live run

We now reproduce the permission failure through the app. Applying the removal fix makes uninstall succeed while preserving the existing Trash file; restoring the release code makes the failure return. The hosting cycle below (uninstall under the denial, app takeover, reinstall, reconnect) passes with a branch-built CLI.

Setup on two AWS EC2 Macs: Apple M1 on macOS 27.0, and Apple M4 on macOS 26.5 (25F71), the closest AWS image to the reporter's 26.5.1. Each runs the notarized 2026.10.9 app (Developer ID: OpenClaw Foundation) from `/Applications`, set up "On this Mac", with OpenClaw listed in Full Disk Access and its switch off. Each run turns "Keep OpenClaw running when the app is closed" on (installs the LaunchAgent), then off, which runs the app's own `gateway uninstall` through its bundled Bun CLI. Before the failing runs, Finder moved a same-name `ai.openclaw.gateway.plist` into `~/.Trash`.

| Mac | CLI code | `~/.Trash` before uninstall | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1, macOS 27.0 | release | Finder-placed same-name plist | `LaunchAgent removal failed (EPERM)` (2 runs; each logged twice, uninstall then the app's recovery) |
| M1 | release | no same-name file | Removed; plist moved to Trash |
| M1 | this PR's removal logic | Finder-placed same-name plist | Removed; plist deleted, service gone, no error; Finder's Trash file unchanged (same SHA-256) |
| M1 | release, restored right after | Finder-placed same-name plist | `LaunchAgent removal failed (EPERM)` again |
| M4, macOS 26.5 | release | Finder-placed same-name plist | `LaunchAgent removal failed (EPERM)` (one uninstall attempt plus one recovery attempt) |
| M4 | this PR's removal logic | Finder-placed same-name plist | Removed; Finder's Trash file unchanged (same SHA-256) |
| M4 | release | no same-name file | Removed; plist moved to Trash |
| M4 | release | same-name plist created and moved into the Trash from a shell (no Finder) | `LaunchAgent removal failed (EPERM)` |
| M4 | release | same-name plist the app itself trashed in the previous run | Removed; the earlier Trash file is replaced |

Creating the existing Trash directory returned EEXIST; the subsequent rename failed with EPERM, matching a TCC denial for the app's Bun helper:

```
# release CLI, M1 (fs_usage, bun; errno 17 = EEXIST, 1 = EPERM)
13:21:23.510452 mkdir  [17] ~/.Trash
13:21:23.544012 rename [ 1] ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist
# TCC, same moment (one request)
13:21:23.510 AUTHREQ_CTX    msgID=164.128 service=kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAllFiles
13:21:23.510 AUTHREQ_ATTRIBUTION responsible=ai.openclaw.mac (/Applications/OpenClaw.app) accessing=bun (~/.openclaw/runtime/2026.10.9-release-…/bin/bun)
13:21:23.541 AUTHREQ_RESULT msgID=164.128 authValue=0
# app log
13:21:23.577 [gateway.launchd] Gateway daemon command failed (exit 1): Gateway uninstall failed: Error: LaunchAgent removal failed (EPERM). Check permissions and retry.
13:21:24.959 (same, the app's recovery attempt)

# removal fix, M1: rename denied, unlink succeeds, plist absent
13:32:17.381920 mkdir  [17] ~/.Trash
13:32:17.382024 rename [ 1] ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist
13:32:17.382157 unlink      ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist
13:32:17.382243 openat [ 2] ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist

# macOS 26.5, M4: the same sequence
13:52:57.534581 mkdir  [17] ~/.Trash
13:52:57.537 AUTHREQ_CTX msgID=137.80 service=kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAllFiles, responsible=ai.openclaw.mac, accessing=bun
13:52:57.570 AUTHREQ_RESULT msgID=137.80 authValue=0
13:52:57.570194 rename [ 1] ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist
# removal fix, M4
13:54:24.110721 rename [ 1] ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist
13:54:24.110798 unlink      ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.openclaw.gateway.plist
```

**Final change, branch-built** (M4, macOS 26.5): the release tag `v2026.10.9` plus this PR's production changes (Trash fallback, `hasErrnoCode`, timestamped Trash name), built with `pnpm build` and placed as the app's runtime `dist`. `~/.Trash` held a same-name `ai.openclaw.gateway.plist` created and moved there from a shell, the case the release refuses.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| "Keep OpenClaw running" on | LaunchAgent installed from the branch-built runtime, `state = running`, Gateway HTTP 200 |
| off (uninstall) | `mkdir [17]` → `rename` succeeds into `~/.Trash/ai.openclaw.gateway-1793494086095.plist`; no `EPERM`, no TCC denial, no daemon-command failure; the delete fallback is not reached; the earlier Trash file unchanged (same SHA-256); the app takes over hosting, HTTP 200 |
| on again (reinstall) | LaunchAgent reinstalled and running, HTTP 200 |
| settings | `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` SHA-256 identical before and after the cycle |

The fallback path was exercised the same way earlier with the fixed name (M4, branch-built `v2026.10.9` + `d29a399f43a`): `mkdir [17]` → `rename [1]` → `unlink`, no daemon-command failure, plist removed, Gateway healthy after reinstall, settings unchanged.

| Build | Same-name item already in `~/.Trash` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Released app (fixed name, no fallback) | yes | `EPERM`, Gateway left unloaded |
| This PR before the timestamped name (fixed name + delete fallback) | yes | uninstall succeeds by deleting the plist; no Trash copy |
| This PR (timestamped name + delete fallback) | yes | uninstall succeeds; plist kept in the Trash under a new name |

The reporter confirmed on the issue: macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), OpenClaw listed in Full Disk Access with its switch off, and `ls ~/.Trash` denied in Terminal, the same permission state as these runs. They then confirmed in Finder that their Trash contains `ai.openclaw.gateway.plist`, the same-name file that triggers the denial here.

Proof artifice: the same-name Trash file was created by hand and moved into the Trash with Finder (AppleScript `delete`), and the Full Disk Access entry was added with its switch off by hand. The M1 fixed runs applied this PR's removal logic to the release bundle's CLI file. For the M4 cycle, the app accepts only a runtime whose `dist/build-info.json` matches its own build stamp, so the release's `build-info.json` and its unchanged `control-ui` assets were kept in the branch-built `dist`.

Not tested: the reporter's exact 26.5.1 build and their 2026.10.3 to 2026.10.7 upgrade path; the doctor legacy-cleanup path live; a build of current `main` with this branch (the cycles used the release tag plus this PR's production changes); and restoring the previous service when deleting the plist also fails, which this PR does not change.

Test lines are net +33 against `main`, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/launchagent-trash-denied.txt`: one case that an earlier same-name Trash item is never overwritten, one parameterized case in the existing uninstall suite (its neighbouring tables assert rejection or idempotent removal and cannot express a denied Trash that must still remove the plist) and one row in doctor's existing legacy-cleanup table.

No stored data, config or plist format changes: the plist written by install is unchanged, only where uninstall puts the old one differs.

prs.title: fix(install): browser extension setup fails under Ubuntu's default umask 0002
prs.body:
Related: #179493, #179538

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: browser extension setup refuses the installed package after installation under a default umask of 0002, as on Ubuntu and Fedora.

## User Impact

User impact: fresh installs and installer-driven upgrades produce package paths that pass the existing ownership check, with settings and workspace data preserved. The invoking shell's umask is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The earlier private-directory repair covered mkdir calls, but npm still inherited the caller's mask and created group-writable package contents. Both standalone installers now remove group/world write permission from their process-local mask. Stricter inherited permissions stay strict; the browser's owned-path check remains intact.

Thanks to @javiermv for the fix and reproduction. The diff-scoped simplification pass retained the two small installer blocks: sharing them would compromise the standalone installer contract. Production +8 lines (two executable lines plus comments/spacing); tests +11 net.

## Evidence

- Contributor regression: the shared installer contract fails on base with four group-writable fixture paths per installer, then passes with the fix. Both installer suites report 290 passed and two Darwin-only skips.
- Contributor real CLI proof: non-root Node 24 container, umask 0002, real npm install followed by `openclaw browser extension setup --action inspect --json --wait-ms 1000`. Base refuses the group-writable extension; head reports `nextAction: install`.
- Contributor upgrade proof: 2026.10.7 to 2026.10.8 through `install-cli.sh` removes unsafe package modes while preserving gateway.port, config and workspace hashes.
- Source review confirms the rejection is the owned-path check in the browser extension owner and no installer step depends on inherited group-write access.
- Exact-head CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40698308949.
- Independent full-diff review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Trusted-tooling oxfmt and static oxlint pass on the changed shared test. Runtime and full-graph proof remains the contributor runs and exact-head CI above.

Live install/upgrade was not rerun in this lane; the contributor's existing isolated runs above are retained as prior proof. The `install.sh` path has shared regression coverage; the real upgrade run exercised `install-cli.sh`.

The retained upgrade predates stable 2026.10.10; an upgrade from that latest stable version was not rerun. The patch is unchanged, and the original non-root installation/upgrade output below exercises the same package-permission boundary.


<details>
<summary>Contributor's original proof record</summary>

## Evidence

- New shared contract case in `test/scripts/install-test-contract.ts`, run by both `install-cli.test.ts` and `install-sh.test.ts`: install under a 0002 caller umask, then assert that no package path is group- or world-writable. It fails on `origin/main` (4 group-writable paths in each installer) and passes with the fix.
- `vitest run test/scripts/install-cli.test.ts test/scripts/install-sh.test.ts`: 290 passed, 2 skipped (Darwin-only re-exec tests).
- Real install in a clean `node:24.22.1` container as a non-root user with `umask 002`, using `install-cli.sh --prefix <tmp> --runtime-only --no-onboard` (installs OpenClaw 2026.10.8), then `openclaw browser extension setup --action inspect --json --wait-ms 1000`:

| | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| group/world-writable paths under the prefix | 46161 of 52050 | 0 of 52050 |
| `browser extension setup --action inspect` | `Refusing group/world-writable path at …/openclaw/dist/extensions/browser/chrome-extension` | `"nextAction": "install"` |

- Existing-install upgrade, as a non-root user with `umask 0002` and a throwaway `HOME` (default prefix and state dir `~/.openclaw`): install 2026.10.7 with `origin/main`'s `install-cli.sh --version 2026.10.7 --runtime-only --no-onboard`, set `gateway.port 18790` and write `~/.openclaw/workspace/NOTES.md`, then upgrade to latest (2026.10.8) with `install-cli.sh --runtime-only --no-onboard` from each side. Writable counts exclude symlinks, whose mode is always 0777 and unused on Linux.

| | before upgrade (2026.10.7) | upgraded with `origin/main` | upgraded with this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `openclaw --version` | 2026.10.7 (157d8c2) | 2026.10.8 (dc2523e) | 2026.10.8 (dc2523e) |
| `config get gateway.port` | 18790 | 18790 | 18790 |

prs.title: fix: long streamed lists and quotes slow down when inline code meets a comparison
prs.body:
Closes #187400

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: long streamed lists and blockquotes slow the Gateway when they mix
inline code with a `<` comparison, the remaining case after #187433.

## User Impact

User impact: these replies stream faster without changing their visible text. No settings,
stored-data format, delivery policy or plugin interface changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing scanner treated ordinary list/quote text as possible block code,
forcing repeated parsing of the growing reply. Keep its conservative paragraph
handling, but mark block-code ambiguity only when indentation could require it.
Fence and uncertain-Markdown fallbacks remain unchanged.

## Evidence

The two added rows in the existing work-count test each make main re-read
2,979,000 characters for a 17,757-character reply, against the test's existing
35,514-character work budget (about 84 times over). Both pass with the fix.
This is a regression-test measurement, not a runtime message-size limit.

### Full-product repro on main — real Gateway runtime proof

Built Gateway on main `b6287c8675cf14ef42e7385130fc4f8fff32fc2d`, real HTTP
client and provider transports, local scripted Responses provider declaring
`final_answer` and emitting four-character deltas. Five samples per case,
alternating main/fix. Median time from provider request to completed stream:

| Reply | Size | Main | Fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Plain prose (control) | 16 KiB | 835 ms | 734 ms |
| Flat inline comparison (control) | 16 KiB | 804 ms | 753 ms |
| List | 8 KiB | 881 ms | 482 ms |
| List | 16 KiB | 2022 ms | 809 ms |
| Blockquote | 8 KiB | 770 ms | 424 ms |
| Blockquote | 16 KiB | 1498 ms | 792 ms |

The controls do not exercise the changed branch; their differences are
run-to-run variation, not an improvement attributed to this fix.

<details>
<summary>Captured Gateway result excerpt: first 16 KiB list sample</summary>

Main:

```json
{
  "shape": "list",
  "requestedBytes": 16384,
  "afterProviderStartMs": 1740.6842140000008,
  "matchesExpected": true
}
```

Fix:

```json
{
  "shape": "list",
  "requestedBytes": 16384,
  "afterProviderStartMs": 705.0464620000021,
  "matchesExpected": true
}
```

</details>

All 80 comparison replies and eight markup controls match the expected visible
text, including reconstruction from streamed deltas. Actual tool scaffolding
stays hidden; fenced and indented examples stay visible.

Parser/projection tests: 260 passed. Agent-consumer tests: 178
passed. Type checks, targeted lint, formatting parity and diff checks pass.
Test lines are net 0 against `main`: the two new rows are offset by fitting the
shared sample sentence on one line.

Proof artifice: fixed synthetic provider responses, not real model timing;
Linux, Node 26, not a Windows-device run. The completions-provider control
buffered this text and did not reproduce the slowdown. Uncertain indentation
and container fences deliberately retain the canonical-parser fallback.


### Independent verification

The list and quote regressions were rerun in a secretless Linux environment with Node 24.22.1. With the current-main scanner, each fails at 2,979,000 parsed characters against the existing 35,514-character budget. With this patch, all 178 tests across `tool-call-xml.streaming-work.test.ts`, `tool-call-xml.streaming-parity.test.ts`, and `protection-fast-path.test.ts` pass (11.89 s wall time). The work suite takes 4.65 s, including the existing exhaustive chunk-boundary parity test. Indented code, tabs, nested containers, and fences retain their canonical-parser checks.

Production delta: +1 line; test delta: 0. The extra assignment separates paragraph uncertainty from possible block-code ownership using the existing state. The prior Gateway timing evidence above was not independently rerun; this pass focused on the regression and indentation/parity contracts.

CI run [41955883572](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41955883572) on `1f275e2812d2cf8f0e53d186635da1dcf5c70bff` passes the affected test, type, lint, and security checks. Its failed `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` job expects “Syncs target-repo to the selected runner” but receives “Syncs target-repo to the selected device.” Scheduled main run [41961707257](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41961707257/job/127029590062) fails the same `boot-module-boundaries.e2e.test.ts` case with the same assertion; this is inherited, not a scanner regression.

Thanks @sukhdeepjohar for the fix and original Gateway measurements.

Integrated current main without conflicts at `18c7fcd4aa3640b85cbdf053e611324f80342e9c`; the reviewed two-file fix is unchanged. Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Exact-head CI [41969879519](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41969879519) has completed: the affected tests, types, lint, and security checks pass. The only failed test job is `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` (job `127056015497`), with the same runner/device assertion as scheduled main above; `openclaw/ci-gate` reflects that failure.

prs.body:
**Draft — local Mac-runner qualification handoff only. Do not mark ready or merge until the outstanding native acceptance checks are completed.**

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native chat audio and video repeatedly becoming unavailable when the Gateway publishes an attachment while its playback inspector is busy and omits optional playback metadata.

## User Impact

Native iOS and Mac chat can ask the Gateway to prepare playback instead of repeatedly fetching an unsupported original. Explicit native playback and image/document downloads retain their original-byte routes. No configuration, schema, dependency, or permission changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared native attachment row treats missing audio/video metadata as a request for the existing lazy playback route, not an affirmative native-codec decision. The Gateway still owns inspection, conversion, native passthrough, access checks, and limits; neither platform gets a second codec policy.

## Evidence

- Original reviewed media-fix checks remain valid: Gateway file **46 passed**; final focused recovery regression **1 passed / 45 skipped**; Gateway-root test typecheck, touched-file lint/format, docs MDX, whitespace, and the 57-line allocation passed. Gateway JavaScript inputs are unchanged by this follow-up and were not unnecessarily rerun.
- The held-inspector regression uses real publication, persisted membership, scoped tickets, original-byte HTTP, HTTP 202 preparation, and the playback owner, but **fixed ffprobe/ffmpeg I/O—not real-codec HTTP playback proof**.
- [Earlier runner qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191517#issuecomment-6591304369) separately reports real synthetic one-second PCM CAF conversion through `resolvePlaybackTranscode` to AAC `audio/mp4` M4A; ffprobe reported AAC/1.000 seconds and macOS AudioToolbox decoded the rendition into a 92,296-byte WAV, exit 0. This is codec/AudioToolbox evidence, not iOS player, shared macOS chat-consumer, or real-ticket HTTP acceptance.
- The [complete source-repair attachment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191517#issuecomment-6608858835) is now incorporated in [`0cb80db5e18e`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0cb80db5e18eb83a83e7c4a7381ddf49cee39ede), directly after `d56977e94c9cdb6158ac41a6c5717c5656fe8b4f`. Three parts, archive checksum, and all 13 declared member hashes/lengths were independently verified. Both supplied patch forms reconstruct the exact declared tested source tree **`07735da8d2ffeb583a4366026ad3b68e5ae44106`**, matching the published commit. The two-file follow-up only extracts unchanged demo seed arrays into private helpers and removes unused `throws`; routing assertions and media/auth owners are unchanged.
- [Native simulator results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191517#issuecomment-6606241324) are **runner-reported and source-equivalent to that published tree, not a fresh run of the published commit or hosted CI**: **12 SwiftUIRenderSmokeTests declarations / 18 parameterized executions, zero failures/skips**, including all **seven managed-media route cases**, plus a normal app/Share/Watch graph build. Focused strict SwiftLint, SwiftFormat, and diff checks passed on the runner's repaired checkout. Those source repairs are now public; normal full CI and a new local Mac run are not claimed. Generated build inputs were captured at attachment time, without an independent historical-byte receipt.
- The hosted audio/video callbacks return **nil**: route/render passes are **not decoding or playback acceptance**. No physical-device/live-Gateway success is claimed. Earlier pre-repair build/hosted attempts exited 65 at the inherited function-length gate; an earlier zero-test exit 0 and skipped/permission-blocked hosted checks are **not passes**. Raw native logs/result bundles and media were not independently replayed or inspected here; they remain runner-local, not downloadable attachments.
- The actual published tree passed canonical identity, whitespace, and test-line-ratchet checks. Fresh **whole six-file P0–P2 independent review** of this candidate found no actionable findings; native Swift/Xcode/lint/format tools are unavailable in this environment.
- **Remaining acceptance — keep Draft, not qualified:** published-source native qualification beyond source equivalence; hosted caller base-red/fix-green; actual iOS-player and shared macOS-consumer recovery; real scoped-ticket HTTP with real codec output; retry authorization and Gateway-switch rejection; and native runtime/visual acceptance. No layout/style/asset/string changes or new native screenshots are claimed.

- @jjjhenriksen

prs.title: fix(cli): compare gateway state dirs case-insensitively on Windows
prs.body:
Closes #185913

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Windows configure falsely refuses to run, and Doctor reports a state-directory mismatch, when the CLI and installed Gateway use case-only spellings of the same directory.

## User Impact

User impact: setup accepts equivalent Windows state/config paths even before their trailing directories exist. Genuinely different paths still refuse; POSIX comparisons remain case-sensitive.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing ancestor resolver preserves the spelling of missing path components. Comparing its results byte-for-byte therefore split one Windows directory into two identities. Native `path.relative` supplies the platform's equality semantics without another path-policy helper. The same comparison owner serves configure and Doctor. The docs now describe the Windows behavior.

Thanks to @YangManBOBO for the fix, regression, and Windows reproduction. Contributor commits are preserved.

## Evidence

- Contributor Windows 11 proof at `22dc6841c212`: the regression fails on base (1 failed, 6 passed), then passes with the fix (7 passed). The built CLI proceeds past the configure state-store guard for a case-only alias recorded in a Scheduled Task, while `.OTHER` still refuses. Doctor shares that comparison. Original captures: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185917#issuecomment-6445306689.
- Independent secretless AWS run on original head `6492fad98e6b`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/state-dir-gateway-check.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 6 tests and skipped the Windows-only regression on Linux (50.04 seconds including cold worker preparation). This is sibling-boundary proof, not native Windows proof.
- Simplification replaces the local equality helper with native `path.relative`; targeted oxlint and oxfmt pass. Isolated review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- The existing regression is now included in the native Windows CI target list for subsequent native runs. CI run 41969684256 selects its platform scope from the trusted base inventory, so its Windows lane is skipped; this run does not provide native Windows proof for the revised implementation.
- Production LOC: +2/−2 (net 0). Tests: +18/−0. Docs: +2. The separate 18-line test allocation preserves the regression without changing the shared baseline.
- Final-head CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41969684256 completed with two inherited failures. The test-line job reports 93 lines over budget despite this PR adding exactly 18 test lines and 18 credits. Scheduled main run 41967849929, job 127049160103, explicitly reports the same 93-line debt and passes only because its delta is zero. No baseline ceiling was changed here.
- The other CI failure is the Docker packaging fixture's missing `scripts/lib/release-context.mjs` import. Scheduled main run 41967849929 fails the same test at the same assertion in Windows job 127049160705. The relevant fixture and importing module blobs are identical on main, the tested merge base, and this PR's merge. This is recorded for the maintainer's inherited-failure decision; CI is red, not green.
- A separate built-in Node path contract check confirms Windows case-only state/config aliases compare equal through `path.win32.relative`, genuinely different Windows paths stay unequal, and POSIX case remains distinct. This checks the selected library semantics, not the full native Windows regression.

Not live-tested again in this lane: Windows Scheduled Task/configure interactions; the available secretless box was Linux. The contributor's native captures above are retained as prior live evidence.

prs.title: fix(ios): recover QR camera access and clear canceled scanner status
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes iPhone QR pairing getting stuck without actionable camera-permission guidance, and leaving ‘Opening QR scanner…’ visible after canceling the camera.

## User Impact

Users get the native camera prompt on first scan, an Open Settings recovery path after denial, and restriction-specific guidance. Cancel returns to a neutral onboarding screen. No Gateway or pairing-credential changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared QR view now resolves camera authorization before constructing VisionKit’s scanner and refreshes authorization when the app becomes active. This also covers Settings and ESP QR scanning. Onboarding no longer writes a transient opening message to its persistent status line; queued QR results, actual errors, and reconnect suppression keep their existing lifecycle.

## Evidence

### Reconciled physical-device build and manual proof

- [Chris’s device report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192118#issuecomment-6613230664): iPhone 16, iOS 27.2, Xcode 27.2, based on `595322e4dc38c5f886ada0efb2365e680295afd7` with identified local fixture and selector changes. App and test targets built; SwiftFormat/SwiftLint passed across 509 files with that refactor.
- The [complete single-file fixture patch supplied by @ceckert](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192118#issuecomment-6614232297) is now incorporated, as is the exact `.firstMatch` correction used for the device-built cancellation test. The fixture blob is `ef75abe3752922495ce0cdaa7abe79f51ca161d9`, matching the supplied patch. Personal signing/bundle settings and generated personal Info.plist changes are excluded. The only additional follow-up is the canonical source inventory. This reconciles the reported build inputs; it does not claim a new full native run at this commit.
- Chris manually confirmed Camera permission recovery works. [Inspected after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192118#issuecomment-6613821821) show denied-access guidance with Open Settings and onboarding after cancellation without stale status. These captures contain no pairing codes or private Gateway details.
- `QRScannerResultHandoffTests` passed on device. The cancellation UI case passed with the selector correction. Typography source-fixture tests could not run meaningfully on the device and still need a source-accessible test environment.

### Review repairs and checks

- Regenerated the native text inventory: exactly five scanner-source rows. On Node 26.12.1, native i18n verification failed before regeneration and passes afterward (4,626 entries). No translation/provider calls were made.
- Independent full-patch review and the local equivalence check found the two fixture extractions behavior-preserving: identical ordered messages, payloads, IDs and timestamps; reversing the extractions restores the entire original file byte-for-byte. Both correctly retain the existing `now` value.
- The UI test now differs from its original source only by Chris’s device-built `.firstMatch` fix. No production permission/foreground behavior was changed in these follow-ups, and no untested diagnostic assertion was retained.
- Fresh independent source review found no P1/P2 findings. `git diff --check` passes. Earlier local autoreview was P0-only; its interrupted final attempt is not represented as a clean full review of the current head.

### Remaining review and merge evidence

- The denied-access automation reached Settings and attempted to enable Camera, but its guidance-disappearance assertion failed on return. It did not independently verify the post-tap switch state. That automated result remains failed/uncertain; manual functional success is separate evidence, not a claimed automated pass.
- Current-head CI and iOS maintainer review are still required. Before screenshots, a separately recorded successful scan/pairing, and shared-caller checks remain unrecorded. The two posted images are after screenshots, not a fabricated before/after pair.
- This is submitted for review, not asserted to be fully validated, approved, or ready to merge.

## Focus Week Credit

Reported and verified by [Chris Eckert (@ceckert)](https://github.com/ceckert) during Team Server’s **Mobile Apps focus week**. Chris identified both user-visible issues and verified that enabling Camera restored pairing. [Canonical Team Server discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/33257e49-0012-426e-80ab-6ba8f8eb881f).

Co-authored-by: ceckert <779559+ceckert@users.noreply.github.com>

## Worked on by

- @ceckert

prs.title: fix: reject unbridgeable update compatibility inventories
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: update compatibility inventory checks accept recorded updater exports that the candidate cannot bridge, leaving the failure to surface later during runtime postbuild (including macOS builds).

## User Impact

Release maintainers get the bridge failure when checking the inventory. Run `pnpm build` first, then `pnpm update:compat:check`; validation does not modify `dist`. No installed updater behavior or compatibility window changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The check reuses the existing bridge writer in dry-run mode, so inventory validation and postbuild use one mapping/validation owner. Explicit release inputs still check regeneration without consulting live dist-tags. Release guidance now distinguishes tag coverage from a supported, bridgeable source window: do not add a newer-line extended-stable artifact merely to satisfy coverage; report the unsupported source and missing proof instead.

Simplification review retained one optional dry-run flag rather than a second bridge planner. Production delta: +20/-1 lines; regression delta: +28 net lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/update-compat-inventory-bridge.txt` for real CLI failure/non-mutation contracts.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the real inventory CLI returned exit 0 for an inventory referencing an unavailable export. Both new CLI regressions failed on base `34007820fa2c` (unbridgeable inventory and missing build).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/runtime-postbuild.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **115 passed**, including bridge writing, old updater importability, explicit offline input, tag coverage, bridge rejection, and non-mutation checks. Test time 16.45s; wrapper wall time 99.27s including cold compilation. CI timing pending.
- Formatting, native Node syntax checks for both changed scripts, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Scripts and tooling TypeScript checks attempted; both fail in unchanged MCP metadata/materialization files on the base (`McpCatalogTool` missing export and optional-field type mismatches). Targeted lint stops during declaration preparation on the same errors. These checks are **not passing**; no full package build or platform release qualification is claimed.
- Fresh independent source review: no actionable P0–P3 findings.
- Local ClawSweeper committed-range review of `34007820fa2c..6cc95f320846`: complete, no actionable correctness or security findings; source-only review, not execution proof.
- Historical initial-head CI: [run 41741188034](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41741188034); superseded by the updated-head run below. The initial draft-open run was skipped.

### CI follow-up

Initial-head CI failed on inherited MCP metadata type errors and 47 lines of pre-existing test-budget debt. After integration: 115 runtime-postbuild tests passed; tooling typecheck and targeted lint passed. Updated-head CI completed with the unrelated failures detailed below; the initial-head MCP failures are historical evidence only.

The previously reviewed feature diff remains unchanged against the updated main base; original review scope and hashes above remain historical evidence.

## Latest CI attribution

Rechecked for head `770464d6381dde1b8ac1d66518054a03688118e4` on 2026-11-04. GitHub reports the PR mergeable; no source update or main integration was needed for conflicts. CI remains failed, not waived or relabeled green.

The log reports **6,446,024 test lines; ceiling 6,445,978; over by 46; PR net delta +28**. The PR adds exactly 28 literal LF test lines and an allocation of 28. prs.title: docs(sessions): distinguish run accounting from context usage
prs.body:
Closes #160863

## What Problem This Solves

Session JSON documentation does not distinguish recorded run accounting from context occupancy, so consumers can mistake an idle session's old input-token count for current context pressure.

## User Impact

Readers can choose the context snapshot and its validity flag for pressure monitoring, handle unknown capacity, and check activity separately. This documents the existing JSON behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explain `inputTokens`/`outputTokens`, `totalTokens`, `totalTokensFresh`, and `contextTokens` in the sessions CLI reference and session-store field reference. The guidance distinguishes current-version snapshot validity from wall-clock freshness and links the two references.

## Evidence

- [Existing contract tests and explicit-base documentation checks](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/41679122353): **49 existing tests pass** across session JSON, usage persistence, and context-token provenance. Explicit-base glossary coverage also passes. No tests or runtime code were changed.
- [Documentation validation](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/41677991772): canonical formatting, Markdown/template lint, MDX, internal routes, configuration examples, and changelog checks pass. Its extra whole-repository anchor scan reports two existing findings; the successful follow-up above preserves both original exit codes and confirms byte-identical findings on unchanged base and this candidate, with both new links checked and no additional errors. No suppressions or unrelated pages were changed.
- Independent **Codex autoreview, P0–P3**, completed on `7584bf5b758e4477b54a8698c50fd1ac9cbb6dbf` against `64b00dd6dd9d9a156f2c11049822c3884bd3b25d`, with five complete original source modules supplied as context: **no actionable findings**. The review confirms snapshot validity is distinct from wall-clock activity.
- Downloaded artifacts' hashes for both formatted pages match the committed files; the executed patch reverse-checks against this head. Validation ran in the contributor's secretless fork Actions.

<details>
<summary>Scope and inherited anchor findings</summary>

Only two existing English documentation pages change: +34/-1 lines. Production and test deltas are zero. The change adds no new field or calculation; the existing usage projection and CLI validity checks remain authoritative.

The full anchor scan exits 1 on both base and candidate for the same two unrelated findings:

- `/tools/acp-agents-setup#agent-process-environment`: duplicate authored/canonical ID.
- `releases/2026.10.1.md` → `/providers/openai/runtimes#agents-api-mvp`: missing fragment.

The comparison keeps the raw outputs and exit statuses and ignores only the checked-link counter, which increases by two. ClawHub mirrored fragments are outside this checkout; both new links target local core documentation and are checked.

No live-pressure measurement or runtime behavior change is claimed.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ui): surface bounded cron run diagnostics on summary pages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI cron run history requests `view: "summary"` (since #173965), and summary projection deleted `diagnostics` entirely. Warn-level operator notes (for example delivery destination owned by another chat) never reach the Runs list, while full-view pages still carry diagnostic entries. Operators cannot tell why a delivered run looks odd without opening a full transcript.

## User Impact

On the cron Runs list, a delivered run with warn-level diagnostics shows only status/facts. After this change it also shows a muted `Diagnostics: …` note under the header. Execution/delivery failures still use `RunError` and still mark the run as failed; a diagnostics note never overrides `OK` / `Delivered`.

## Why

Issue #168687 (P2, assigned obviyus). Summary pages exist to bound payload size (#173965 stripped `diagnostics`/`delivery`/`failureNotificationDelivery`), but the bounded `diagnostics.summary` string is operator-facing and small. Entries (16KB payloads) stay full-view only. Keeping summary only—without delivery traces—preserves the size gate while restoring the note.

## Evidence

Red on base / green with fix:

1. **Summary projection** — `src/gateway/server-methods/cron.runs.test.ts`: base red missing `entries.0.diagnostics.summary` on the summary page. Fix green (14/14): summary keeps `diagnostics` as `{ summary: "Diagnostic-only search", entries: [] }`, and both `delivery` / `failureNotificationDelivery` are still absent on `summary` while present on `full`.
2. **Size gate** — `src/cron/run-history.test.ts`: summary page keeps `diagnostics.summary`, ships no `diagnostics.entries` and no `delivery` trace, and `diagnostic-payload:` stays absent from summary JSON; full view still contains it. Green (11/11).
3. **Rendered note** — proven end to end below against a shipped Control UI build and an isolated Gateway (Playwright `cron-run-diagnostic-note` `noteCount: 0` → `1`). The note is display-only and never rewrites status.

Local checks:

- `oxfmt --check` on all 7 files: clean.
- `check:test-lines-ratchet`: this change adds no test lines (gateway paging assertions folded into the existing case, net delta ≤ 0), so it stays green even while `main` itself sits over the ceiling. No allocation file required.
- Typecheck: `tsconfig.core.json` and `tsconfig.ui.json` pass under `OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo`, including the UI test shards.
- Targeted suites green: `cron.runs.test.ts` 14/14, `run-history.test.ts` 11/11.

**Shipped Control UI + isolated Gateway before/after** (source `startGatewayServer`, token auth, built Control UI root, Playwright chromium, synthetic OK+Delivered run with `diagnostics.summary` + entries + delivery trace):

- **Before** (base UI): Runs activity shows `OK` + `Delivered`, **no** `cron-run-diagnostic-note` (`noteCount: 0`).
- **After** (head UI): same row still `OK` + `Delivered`, muted note `Diagnostics: Provider returned a bounded advisory note without failing delivery.` (`noteCount: 1`).
- **Response output** (`cron.runs` `view: "summary"` from the browser WS join and Node admin client): `diagnostics.summary` retained; `diagnostics.entries` is `[]`; `delivery` trace absent; `status: ok`, `deliveryStatus: delivered`.

Before:

![before cron summary](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8168904b-d71d-4e49-aee3-b6baf3246642)

After:

![after cron summary](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad4f8766-9112-41d9-a4c2-b5f645c70b79)

Local proof artifacts (not committed): `/tmp/cron-diag-proof/{before,after}-evidence.json` + PNGs from `scripts/capture-cron-diag-proof.mts`.

## Merge Danger

- **Payload size:** summary still cannot ship `diagnostics.entries` or `delivery` traces; SQL `jsonRemovePaths` strips entries before the page crosses the driver, and the size gate still forbids `diagnostic-payload:`.
- **Status semantics:** note is display-only; `completionStatus` / `RunError` path unchanged.
- **Search:** still runs on the full record before prune (`SEARCH_KEYS` unchanged).
- **Scope:** 7 files; no config/schema/durability changes. Protocol comment only documents existing summary behavior.

Closes #168687

prs.title: fix(process): macOS Terminal commands refuse when process ancestry stops at root-owned login
prs.body:
Related: #191944, #191855, #192882

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `gateway stop`, `doctor --fix` and `update repair` refuse with "Process ancestry could not be fully inspected" from an ordinary macOS Terminal, and updates keep their retained runtimes while a Gateway runs on macOS releases before 27.

## User Impact

User impact: from an independent macOS Terminal, those commands no longer hit this refusal. A process inside the Gateway tree is still refused. A running Gateway no longer pins every update's retained runtime on affected macOS releases. Other JS runtimes with an unreadable environment, and PIDs with an unreadable argument image, still keep the runtime with a warning naming the PID.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Ancestry.** Terminal shells descend from root-owned `/usr/bin/login`, and the native identity read is denied for it. The walk now resumes with `ps -o ppid=,lstart=`, keeping start ordering at one-second resolution. A recycled or unreadable parent still leaves it incomplete, and a completed walk that finds the Gateway still refuses.
- **Unreadable environment.** A JS runtime whose Darwin environment reports `incomplete` kept no argv, including a title-erased `openclaw-gateway`. It now keeps argv, and only a decision that needs the service marker stays unknown, matching the Linux path.
- **`layout-mismatch`.** This error aborted the whole census. It now leaves only that PID unknown, like `incomplete`.

Accepted edge case: a PID recycled within the same second as its child can pass the `ps` start ordering. It would have to happen to a root-owned ancestor during a one-shot walk.

`config/test-lines-allocations/darwin-process-inspection.txt` covers this PR's 75 added test lines: new contracts for the three fixes, and an existing case moved out of a file at its line cap.

## Evidence

- New census and ancestry tests fail on base and pass with the fix. The reader's expectation changed from a throw to argv plus the flag.
- Focused suites pass: restart-stale-pids, its ancestry test, the census and its native test, the Darwin command reader and its native test, service membership, and launchd current-service.
- Live on macOS 27 with the real exported walk, for a Ghostty shell under root-owned `login`: native result `complete: false, stoppedBy: unreadable-parent`; resumed result `complete: true` through login, Ghostty and launchd.
- Autoreview scoped-clean; independent Codex review found nothing.

Gaps:

- No Intel macOS 15 host was available, so the failing commands were not rerun there. The absent coalition on those hosts is inferred from the refusal text and is unexplained; the fix does not depend on it.
- `incomplete: unterminated Darwin environment` and `layout-mismatch` were exercised through fixtures, because macOS 27 does not produce them.
- #192882 attributes this to `ps -o "resource coalition="`. Current source reads `launchctl print pid/<pid>` and the native coalition API, so its suggested patch was not used.
- #191855's false `EACCES` and `.fseventsd` capture refusal are not touched and stay open.

prs.title: fix(read): accept optional false without schema rejection
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `read` tool input schema typed `optional` as `Literal(true)`. When a model sent `optional: false` (meaning required), argument validation rejected the call with `optional: must be equal to constant` before the tool ran.

## Fix

Widen `readToolInputSchema.optional` to `boolean`. Execution already treats only `optional === true` as missing-file suppression (`optional !== true` keeps ENOENT/ENOTDIR as errors), so `false` now validates and behaves as required.

## Evidence

### Local createReadToolDefinition proof on head `9b7d6de6a0`

Ran schema validation + the shipped read tool definition (not a mocked schema-only check):

```text
date 2026-11-04T01:17:01.681Z
head 9b7d6de6a0ee4b65ec838d1c08f8e0e8b4b1ed37

=== schema validation ===
{"path":"present.txt","optional":false} => true
{"path":"present.txt","optional":true} => true
{"path":"present.txt"} => true
{"path":"present.txt","optional":"yes"} => false

=== execute optional:false on present file ===
{
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "hello"
    }
  ],
  "details": {
    "kind": "text",
    "content": "hello"
  }
}

=== execute optional:false on missing file ===
throws: File not found: /tmp/openclaw-read-optional-qC4cdq/missing.txt.
code: ENOENT

=== execute optional:true on missing file ===
{
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "Optional file not found: missing.txt."
    }
  ],
  "details": {
    "kind": "not_found",
    "status": "not_found",
    "path": "missing.txt",
    "optional": true
  }
}
```

Focused Vitest:

```text
pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/sessions/tools/read.test.ts -t "optional false"
# accepts optional false and keeps missing required paths as errors — passed
```

### Gap

No full Gateway agent-turn transcript on this box (no configured Gateway session). The proof above is the production read tool owner used by agent turns; a Gateway RPC/trace can be attached if maintainers still require that layer.

prs.title: improve(ui): open large completed chat runs faster
prs.body:
## Current refresh (2026-11-04) — do not merge

Pushed head: `12793987a60f320024d3941e26b44ba7c520640e`, merged with main `4a43644e7a7b455d6e257f1ab62fe00e74156a5f`. Auto-merge remains off; Peter’s decision is pending. Full CI [41968001269](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41968001269) is running on this head. Historical sections below describe their named older heads until this refresh finishes.

The main-integration regressions are repaired: run frames alone own their inline previews; saved composer widths remeasure when layout inputs refresh; reader compensation retains the offset before a shrinking extent clamps it; and an armed history gesture recreates its observer after a geometry correction. The four previously failing targeted browser cases pass, as do the affected history and projection unit tests. Independent repair review is complete with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Exact committed UI typecheck and production build pass. Three-traversal memory replays and 20-triplet/A-A scroll, mixed-local streaming, fork and edit comparisons are running serially on this committed bundle.

**Additional open blocker:** strict asset comparison against the same main bundle fails Chat boot **+6,416 B gzip** and New Session boot **+318 B**, on surfaces already over cap. Startup is **+2 B**, CSS **−171 B**. No caps were raised. Source-map audit attributes the route growth to the bounded-preparation/windowing owners, without duplicated libraries or accidental heavy imports. These bytes are separate from the historical streaming tradeoff; neither has maintainer acceptance.

---

## What Problem This Solves

Completed runs with thousands of rich messages materialized their entire subtree when opened. This fragments eligible large completed runs, budgets preparation ahead of the viewport, preserves measured geometry, and bounds row/Markdown retention. Medium runs retain the cheaper whole-run path. Existing owners keep sanitization, media custody and session state; tags, selectors and lazy boundaries remain unchanged.

## Open tradeoff for maintainer acceptance

**Do not merge. Auto-merge is off. Peter’s decision is pending; no acceptance is claimed.** Final pushed head: `cccd12de54a580639adea26f6790ae609aaf2aed`, integrated with main `49df70b5caf137f92583346bf6b452e0db3aac83`. The final repairs inline private CSS constants without changing selectors or computed values, and replace one equivalent mapped object copy in a test fixture.

Remaining measured regressions in the preceding 20-triplet runtime matrix:

- **Mixed localhost streaming Task: +10.36% median versus base, +10.92% versus A/A; +4.68% p95.** This is approximately 405 ms over 645 deltas. Script is flat and Style improves 1.6%. The remaining increase is not fully attributed to one writer: outer virtual-height updates and extra prepaint/layerization remain. The measured Task minus Script/Layout/Style residual grows 18.96%; it is not an independently measured phase.
- **Six streaming-onset tasks are 51–54 ms.** Base had 17 tasks above 50 ms, maximum 60 ms. Splitting these was optional for this preparation round and was not attempted.
- **Search Task p95 +4.44%**, despite median −8.17% and Search Script p95 −0.30%. Search wall p95 +30.35%, with noisy A/A +9.68%; the prior source-mapped audit and flat Script tail do not establish a corresponding CPU regression. No head search RPCs occurred.
- **Switch-out Task median +2.47%; p95 −2.04%.** This remains inside the median band.

The trade under consideration is approximately **7.4× faster direct-run readiness and 2.9× less heap**, with vastly fewer retained transcript elements. Fresh exact-head replay preserves these gains: direct readiness 3,687 → 508 ms (one replay sample, not a new timing distribution), retained heap 191.60 → 66.99 MiB, and transcript elements 44,265 → 680. Mixed retention is below current main.

## Evidence

### Exact pushed head: retention and functional replay

Clean committed production bundles, headless Chromium, synthetic 2,000-message fixtures, localhost. Base and head each traverse end-to-end **three times**. No missing loaded messages or memory metrics. These are bounded-retention/functional replays; their single-pair wall times are not timing acceptance distributions.

| Scenario, after traversal 3 | Current main | Pushed head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Mixed retained heap | 78.95 MiB | 78.91 MiB |
| Mixed all DOM nodes | 10,069 | 9,272 |
| Mixed transcript elements | 542 | 415 |
| Mixed detached nodes, C1 / C2 / C3 | 1,442 / 1,433 / 1,433 | 940 / 940 / 940 |
| Direct-run retained heap | 191.60 MiB | 66.99 MiB |
| Direct-run all DOM nodes | 111,277 | 8,303 |
| Direct-run transcript elements | 44,265 | 680 |
| Direct-run detached nodes, C1 / C2 / C3 | 577 / 577 / 577 | 893 / 926 / 894 |

Direct detached counts fluctuate but do not accumulate over traversals (C3 is one above C1); they are not identically flat. Functional replay covers opening, switch out/in, search/clear, scrolling end-to-end and returning to the bottom. Final mixed captures were inspected: matching layout/content, synthetic data only.

### Exact pushed head: scroll gate

Twenty serial base/base/head triplets (60 complete observations) on the final committed production build; 2,000 mixed messages, localhost, headless Chromium, 1719×1179 viewport. A/A uses the identical current-main bundle; every run loaded all messages and retained actual sample boundaries. Host one-minute load ranged 13.35–29.77. This replay measures scroll only; it does not replace the preceding streaming matrix.

| Scroll metric (ms; per-run median / p95) | Current main | A/A | Final head |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Up frame-tail p95 | 66.61 / 66.70 | 66.60 / 66.70 | 33.31 / 33.40 |
| Down frame-tail p95 | 66.60 / 66.70 | 66.60 / 66.70 | 16.80 / 33.30 |
| Up Task CPU | 2789.35 / 2905.14 | 2808.60 / 2912.54 | 1070.08 / 1139.43 |
| Down Task CPU | 2942.26 / 3066.95 | 2938.43 / 3047.37 | 938.22 / 984.58 |
| Up Script CPU | 1638.59 / 1722.59 | 1657.93 / 1724.91 | 561.42 / 594.44 |
| Down Script CPU | 1574.39 / 1665.96 | 1577.84 / 1640.71 | 446.32 / 476.49 |

Both directions pass the fixed 40.08 ms frame-tail gate. Final head has **zero tasks over 50 ms** during setup, scrolling or settling, zero full/substantial partial blank frames, zero corrective scrolls and zero endpoint misses. CPU Script/Task, Layout and Style medians and p95 all improve versus both controls. The absolute gate is checked against the original 33.4 ms predecessor, not relaxed to the slower current-main measurements.

### Previous full mixed-local timing matrix

Twenty serial base/base/head triplets on the same host, 645 deltas at 30/s, renderer-thread CPU. Host one-minute load 10.52–49.54; A/A retained. All 60 observations and loaded-message counts complete. Base `be8eca7f92b2d7c9acb4043debef785906af6188`; measured runtime head `1882116dac73ebf28f8ade09bf22542d11f37078`. These results establish the open trade, not a claim of a new full streaming matrix after the CSS-only integration repair.

| Metric (ms) | Base median / p95 | A/A median / p95 | Head median / p95 | Head/base median / p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Readiness wall | 1465.65 / 1675.12 | 1513.10 / 1591.89 | 1572.85 / 1624.74 | +7.31% / -3.01% |
| Open Task | 1610.69 / 1697.77 | 1595.22 / 1660.49 | 1546.27 / 1638.27 | -4.00% / -3.50% |
| Search Task | 137.91 / 145.26 | 141.48 / 146.32 | 126.64 / 151.71 | -8.17% / +4.44% |
| Search Script | 66.27 / 72.65 | 67.59 / 70.30 | 64.26 / 72.44 | -3.04% / -0.30% |
| Clear-search Task | 163.38 / 178.96 | 165.36 / 176.40 | 137.40 / 178.21 | -15.90% / -0.42% |
| Switch into session Task | 495.32 / 550.89 | 488.37 / 535.06 | 337.27 / 359.05 | -31.91% / -34.82% |
| Switch out Task | 469.45 / 517.32 | 465.64 / 492.85 | 481.06 / 506.78 | +2.47% / -2.04% |
| Scroll up Task | 2746.99 / 2876.31 | 2751.50 / 2999.54 | 1093.50 / 1146.37 | -60.19% / -60.14% |
| Scroll down Task | 2875.10 / 3055.35 | 2907.61 / 3049.41 | 956.14 / 1053.30 | -66.74% / -65.53% |
| Streaming Task | 3909.78 / 4255.84 | 3889.95 / 4239.22 | 4314.83 / 4455.15 | +10.36% / +4.68% |
| Streaming Script | 1256.85 / 1290.90 | 1245.63 / 1291.56 | 1258.38 / 1300.21 | +0.12% / +0.72% |
| Streaming Style | 348.58 / 381.81 | 344.36 / 375.06 | 343.04 / 355.03 | -1.59% / -7.01% |
| Streaming Layout | 188.16 / 195.45 | 186.85 / 193.76 | 195.26 / 202.74 | +3.77% / +3.73% |
| Streaming residual (not an independent phase) | 2104.10 / 2439.11 | 2102.22 / 2442.77 | 2503.07 / 2621.85 | +18.96% / +7.49% |
| Streaming frame-tail p95 | 33.40 / 50.00 | 33.40 / 50.00 | 16.75 / 16.80 | -49.86% / -66.40% |
| Streaming native blocking | 4.30 / 9.01 | 5.15 / 7.78 | 0.40 / 3.67 | -90.70% / -59.27% |

The traced live row’s `contain-intrinsic-block-size` writes fell from 245 on base / 251 on the prior head to **zero**. Matching style-triggered layout feedback also fell to zero. Outer `.chat-thread-inner--virtual` height writes remain (245/251/253), owned by `TranscriptLayoutOwner.commitRange`; geometry reads reach `maxTranscriptScrollOffset`/native `clientHeight`. No recurring ancestor class/custom-property or layer-promotion toggles were found. Base already had this feedback loop; removing it does not fully explain the remaining Task difference. Diagnostic traces are not acceptance timings.

## Validation and CI

Full CI [41210520819](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41210520819) **completed successfully on final pushed head `cccd12de54a580639adea26f6790ae609aaf2aed`**: 50 successful jobs, 23 skipped, zero failures. All three UI unit jobs, seven Control UI E2E shards, both real-Gateway E2E shards, performance and i18n passed. PR remains open and mergeable; auto-merge is off. Native `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency review and security-sensitive review also report success. Separate PR context/evidence and advisory ClawSweeper checks are cancelled; none is a failed product test. No inherited-failure waiver was needed.

The integrated runtime passes UI typechecking, scoped lint and both resize tests. Final head passes production Knip, the repaired geometry case, a clean production build, and strict assets. All 62 responsive-layout checks passed on its production-identical parent. Independent reviews of the geometry/anchor repair, fixture lint correction, final CSS patch, and mapped-copy fixture fix found no actionable P0–P2 defects. Earlier targeted repairs passed Markdown (17), responsive (62), geometry (26), and the prepend-anchor contraction/streaming/navigation case.

Full CI on the production-identical parent [41209458082](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41209458082) passed every UI, Control UI E2E, real-Gateway, and performance job. Its sole failing lint diagnostic was the mapped copy in a test fixture, now fixed and independently reviewed. No inherited waiver was used.

Earlier repairs address the 13 UI failures and lint failure from [41202622021](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41202622021), whose failing names did not match scheduled main. No inherited waiver was used for those failures.

| Final asset proof | Current main | Final head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS gzip | 89,379 B | 89,372 B |
| Startup JS / CSS requests | 3 / 1 | 3 / 1 |
| Startup CSS gzip | 33,572 B | 33,593 B |
| Chat boot JS gzip | 1,268,202 B | 1,270,702 B |
| New Session boot JS gzip | 781,995 B | 778,854 B |
| Total CSS gzip | 309,487 B | 309,276 B |
| Total CSS raw | 1,599,922 B | 1,598,466 B |

Final head is under all existing caps; none were raised. Chat boot grows 2,500 B gzip (+0.20%) for the bounded-fragment/preparation path; startup JS decreases 7 B and New Session boot decreases 3,141 B. Request counts are unchanged. This small route cost is retained for the measured long-session readiness and memory gains. Current main itself exceeds both total-CSS caps, while this PR reduces both totals and fits them. Entire PR: 179 changed paths, 80,929 → 88,059 lines (+7,130), including the synthetic workload and proof harness. Final CSS repair: 20 insertions / 32 deletions. Reports/traces are uncommitted.

## Before / after

Existing inspected synthetic captures: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183800#issuecomment-6540934463. Fresh final-head mixed-session captures were inspected locally and show matching content, layout and composer; no new media upload was made.

![Before: large completed run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6be788ad-b73b-4c9f-823b-f4d94024d9dc)
![After: bounded completed run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe93de9d-69d4-4eff-90ce-4e6bac38c54d)

## Effect on queued transcript items

Frozen current main `8b47948c8d3c5a1150516aa7e250a8d2d6c91085` versus this PR's unchanged head `cccd12de54a580639adea26f6790ae609aaf2aed`. Headless production bundles, Chromium 156 / WebKit 27.2, localhost, desktop; **20 interleaved main/head/main-control triplets per action/profile**. All **900 engine observations passed their scripted functional assertions**; this is not acceptance of every timing delta. The main control uses identical bytes. The recorded one-minute host load ranged from 4.48 to 22.05 across the engine matrix; CPU counters and the A/A control accompany wall/frame timings. These are complete-version comparisons: newer main contains other changes, so the deltas are not isolated estimates of windowing alone.

The table reports **main → PR**, in milliseconds. Action rows use longest native task **median / p95** for Chromium and application-span **median / p95** for WebKit. Scroll uses the per-run frame-tail p95 distribution. The two diagnostic rows are single source-mapped 4× CPU samples, not acceptance timings. `none ≥50` means no Long Task entry, not zero CPU. WebKit has no native Task CPU/Long Task metric and no 4× throttle.

| Queued item / workload | Chromium 1× | Chromium 4× | WebKit 1× |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Mixed streaming, including publication and scroll | none ≥50 → none ≥50 | 125.5 / 222 → 111.5 / 138 | 4912 / 5006 → 4882 / 4920 |
| Fork destination, 398 retained messages | <50 / 51 → 54 / 57 | 232 / 256 → 274 / 298 | 563 / 599 → 575 / 600 |
| Edit/resubmit | none ≥50 → none ≥50 | 144 / 153 → 159 / 181 | 859.5 / 880 → 862 / 879 |
| Split-view open + close, 400 messages | 81.5 / 85 → 79 / 84 | 403 / 437 → 382 / 436 | 1291 / 1314 → 868 / 921 |
| Fast scroll, 2,000 simple-text messages | 16.75 / 16.8 → 16.7 / 16.8 | 83.4 / 83.4 → 50 / 50.1 | 34 / 39 → 24 / 26 |
| Structural publication CPU (diagnostic) | — | 151.7 → 114.8 | — |
| In-stream scroll CPU (diagnostic) | — | 175.8 → 123.1 | — |

The engine fast-scroll fixture is simple text, with zero blank/endpoint failures on every engine and profile and mounted rows 13 → 6. It does not collect native Long Tasks; the separate rich-scroll gate below does. The mixed-stream fixture is 400 prior messages plus 645 deltas at 150 Hz, reasoning, 24 tool results, an image and concurrent input. Its **4× head maximum was 191 ms**, below 200 ms in all 20 samples (main maximum 259 ms, control 229 ms). Whole-action Task CPU median/p95 improves **1613.47/1692.26 → 1493.30/1565.74 ms at 1×** and is flat at 4× (**5223.89/5704.55 → 5193.20/5648.17 ms**). This workload does **not** replace the still-open 2,000-message/30 Hz streaming trade above.

Single-pair, source-mapped 4× traces separate the two historical streaming handoff items: the largest structural tool-publication task is **151.7 → 114.8 ms CPU**, still in `projectChatTranscript` / `createTranscriptStreamSource` / `buildCachedChatItems`; the largest scroll task is **175.8 → 123.1 ms CPU**. Forced geometry remains: the PR has a 35.4 ms style/layout pair beneath TanStack's `getMaxScrollOffset` native `scrollHeight` read, plus a separate 34.5 ms initial-range row measurement. Explicit start marks select the measured streaming interval. Traces are attribution, not timing acceptance samples.

Fork is the clearest follow-up: its 4× longest-task median/p95 regresses **18.1% / 16.4%**, and 1× Task CPU median/p95 rises **7.4% / 8.0%**. The diagnostic destination task has **10.0 → 67.9 ms layout CPU**, with forced reads in `TranscriptLayoutOwner.sync` and `completeLayout`. Edit stays below 200 ms at 4× but its task tail worsens; 1× Task CPU rises **5.7% / 5.3%**. Against A/A, the 1× fork/edit Task CPU median increases are 4.9%/4.0%; the 4× fork longest-task control is 235/256 ms, confirming the blocking regression. Split Task CPU improves about 6% on both Chromium profiles, but its blocking tail largely remains. Its longest trace task still mounts the second pane; the original pane's rows survive. **WebKit's split value measures the compound open/close span, including driver gaps, not isolated mount latency.**

The **rich 2,000-message scroll gate** also completed all 120 observations (20 main/control/head triplets at each Chromium throttle), with verified bundle identities and all 2,000 messages loaded. Frame-tail values below are the median / p95 distribution of each run’s adjacent-rAF p95.

| Rich scroll direction | Chromium 1×, main → PR | Chromium 4×, main → PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Up | 50.10 / 50.10 → 33.20 / 33.31 | 234.23 / 300.00 → 108.77 / 117.53 |
| Down | 50.10 / 50.14 → 16.80 / 16.84 | 250.00 / 301.66 → 83.40 / 85.01 |

All variants had **zero full or substantial partial blank samples, zero corrections and zero endpoint misses**; maximum mounted rows fell **14 → 5**. At 1× the head had **zero native tasks over 50 ms** across setup, traversal and settling, and passed the fixed 40.08 ms frame/50 ms task gates. At 4× the largest head task was **136 ms** (main **390 ms**, A/A **453 ms**): below the 200 ms throttled task goal, but the fixed normal-speed gates correctly report a miss at 4× and are not claimed as passed. Whole-scroll Task CPU median fell **63.5% up / 67.5% down at 1×**, and **60.8% up / 68.8% down at 4×**; the full A/A tables remain in the lane report. One equal-timestamp pair in head run 15’s settling callbacks is retained unchanged; all trajectory timestamps are strictly increasing. The rich gate is Chromium-only; WebKit scroll coverage above uses the existing simple-text engine scenario.

Prepared, unpushed follow-up: first test for duplicate initial geometry reads and remove confirmed duplicates at the transcript layout/virtualizer owner, prove fork and split together, then revisit structural publication and edit only where duplicate work remains. Target a measured ≥5% affected CPU win and the existing 50/200 ms task targets; these are experiment goals, not promised savings. No code, commits or pushes were made for this measurement round; auto-merge remains off and no merge is requested.
