prs.title: fix(auto-reply): honor send policy for agent database refusal replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refs #192021. When an agent's database admission is refused, `gatherDispatchRequest` replies with the raw refusal reason and the `openclaw doctor --fix` hint before `session.sendPolicy` is resolved. A `deny` rule cannot stop a reply from this branch. The report describes 33 of these messages reaching third-party WhatsApp chats on 2026.10.9. **I could not reach this branch from any real channel entry on current main; see "Reachability" below.**

## User Impact

Any caller that does reach this branch no longer sends this internal error to a chat whose configured send policy resolves to `deny`. The turn is still recorded as an error with the refusal code, and the reply resolver still does not run. Chats where the policy allows sending get the same reply as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refusal branch now evaluates `resolveSendPolicy` before sending, using the same target session key the later dispatch path prefers, plus the channel and chat type from the inbound context.

The session entry is not passed, because the refused database cannot be relied on to supply it. A per-session `/send off` override is therefore not honored in this state; only configured rules are.

This restores existing deny semantics only. It does not restrict the diagnostic to owners in chats that allow sending, or forward it to the owner. The review on the issue raises that as a maintainer decision, so I left it out.

## Evidence

![Refusal reply A/B](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/192021/proof-192021.png)

Real `dispatchInboundMessage` and real reply dispatcher, using the config from the issue and a WhatsApp-shaped inbound context. The refusal is recorded through `recordAgentDatabaseAdmissions`. Only `gather.ts` differs between the two columns.

| `session.sendPolicy` | Before (f5c23834340) | After (946245c9731) |
|---|---|---|
| Issue config: deny `keyPrefix: agent:reader:` | delivered 1 | **delivered 0** |
| Deny `channel: whatsapp`, `chatType: direct` | delivered 1 | **delivered 0** |
| Deny rule for another agent only | delivered 1 | delivered 1 |
| No send policy | delivered 1 | delivered 1 |

`dispatch-from-config.test.ts -t "reports agent refusal"`: with the source change 3 passed; without it the new `denied` case fails with `expected true to be false`.

Passed locally: oxfmt, oxlint, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:test-lines-ratchet` (net 0 test lines), `check:assertion-safety`.

**Reachability: I could not produce the transport proof the review asks for**

I tried to drive the refused state from real channel entries to a recorded transport call. None of them reached this branch, with or without the fix:

| Entry | Transport recorded at | Sends with refusal, before | After | What happened |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Telegram DM, real Gateway | fake Bot API `sendMessage` | 0 | 0 | spooled update failed, kept for retry |
| Synology Chat DM, real Gateway | fake incoming webhook | 0 | 0 | spooled update failed, kept for retry |
| Signal DM, real Gateway | fake signal-cli `send` RPC | 0 | 0 | debounce flush failed with `AgentDatabaseAdmissionError` |
| Signal group, real Gateway | fake signal-cli `send` RPC | 0 | 0 | same |
| Telegram `/status` command, real Gateway | fake Bot API `sendMessage` | 0 | 0 | `dispatch failed: AgentDatabaseAdmissionError`, kept for retry |
| WhatsApp, real `processMessage` in a test | `msg.platform.reply` | not run | 0 | rejected with `AgentDatabaseAdmissionError` before any reply |

The WhatsApp rejection comes from `getOpenClawAgentDatabaseIfOpen`, under the session writer. `agent-database-inspection-failed` refuses reads as well as writes, so the turn fails before dispatch. I did not identify which WhatsApp call issues that write, and I ran that case on the fix commit only; the frames are outside the changed file.

In all of these the refusal was injected with the same shape `createAgentDatabaseInspectionRefusal` produces, because I could not trigger a real `session reclamation commit checkpoint expired`. No real WhatsApp account was used.

So on current main a deny-listed chat received nothing in these runs, but neither did allowed chats. The reported delivery was on 2026.10.9 and I have not reproduced it on any version through a channel entry. I did not test `chat.send` or Discord and Slack slash commands, which may still reach the branch. I am stopping the channel-by-channel search here, because each entry costs a full rig and this is waiting on the maintainer decision.

**For maintainers:** this patch is now a guard on a branch I can only demonstrate through `dispatchInboundMessage`. Please decide whether that is worth keeping, or whether #192021 should be handled by confirming the earlier channel failure is the real fix. The "allowed recipient keeps its reply" half of the requested proof does not hold through these channels, because they currently send nothing at all during a refusal. That silence may itself deserve a look.

`get-reply.ts:172` has a similar refusal return that I did not change, and I did not establish whether any caller reaches it without passing a send-policy check.

prs.title: fix(devices): avoid stale-request errors when clearing pending repairs
prs.body:
Closes #127622

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw devices clear --yes --pending` empties the pairing table but reports `unknown requestId` when a paired device also has a pending repair request.

## User Impact

Clear succeeds for paired repairs and reports the exact committed device/request IDs in one JSON document. Device-token callers retain their existing self-only and role restrictions. A transaction failure leaves pairing and bootstrap state unchanged.

The CLI requires a Gateway supporting `device.pair.clear`. Its handshake capability check refuses an older Gateway before sending any deletion, with an actionable update/restart message. There is no sequential legacy fallback. If post-commit worker cleanup fails, the result retains the committed IDs, includes `cleanupFailedDevices`, and exits 1 so operators can inspect Gateway logs.

**Maintainer decisions still required:** accept this new RPC/Gateway-upgrade compatibility requirement and provide the security-sensitive review for the current head. This PR does not claim either approval.

## Why This Change Was Made

The former CLI loop read a snapshot, removed a paired device (also deleting its repair), then tried to reject the stale request ID. The new RPC selects and clears through the existing SQLite worker transaction, capturing repair IDs before cascading removal. It preserves bootstrap/APNS cleanup, notifications, live authority checks, and credential revocation. Default clear also revokes the bootstrap credentials of repairs removed with their paired device, while leaving unrelated pending requests and credentials intact. The caller receives its final result before its removed connection closes; no database schema or permission expansion is required.

## Evidence

Current repair: head `c2eca741fbcc0ec2b14aec4d71b6d0afa80372a8`, merged with main `78e97d169703a32ee97221f91593ab20200bc05f`. Environment: macOS arm64, Node 24.19.0, pinned pnpm 12.12.1; local Vitest uses the documented `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` option.

- Resolved both merge conflicts using main's current Gateway capability-test table and consolidated device-handler mocks. Retained the PR's capability refusal, response-before-close behavior, and main's newer lifecycle cleanup. A merge simulation against subsequently advanced main `45c780ab54` was clean.
- Reproduced and fixed a credential-revocation bug: default clear (`pending=false`) cascaded paired repair requests but left their bound bootstrap credentials valid. The regression issues and verifies real bootstrap credentials through the production owner. Before the fix, the removed repair's credential still returned `ok: true`; after the fix it returns `bootstrap_token_invalid`, while an unrelated pending device's credential remains valid. prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): add the tunnel transport, OpenClaw ID sign-in and relayed-device Gateway auth
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A linked claw must be reachable from an owner's or member's browser through the OpenClaw ID relay, and the Gateway must authenticate those relayed devices by their membership, not by headers or other credentials. This draft adds the tunnel transport, OpenClaw ID sign-in for the Control UI, and the Gateway auth changes that admit relayed devices.

## User Impact

No user-visible change while the `gateway.openclawId.enabled` Labs switch is off (the default): no tunnel child, no ingress listener and no tunnel principal resolver exist, and every auth path behaves as on `main`.

With the switch on and the services configured, the Gateway runs a supervised tunnel child, the local operator can sign in with OpenClaw ID and link the claw, and admitted devices reach the Gateway through the relay with their owner, operator or viewer role.

**Security-relevant:** this PR changes Gateway authentication, ingress attribution, the browser-origin check and the plugin cookie handoff. Those changes are listed separately below.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stacked on #192335 (Gateway membership authority). It also needs the iroh Node binding, #191470: the tunnel child loads `@openclaw/iroh-node` at runtime and reports the transport unavailable (and keeps the Gateway running) when it cannot.

**Tunnel transport** (`src/gateway/openclaw-id/`):

- `tunnel-child/**`: a separate child process that owns the iroh endpoint. It authenticates each device key W in the QUIC handshake, refuses keys that are not admitted before any stream, and proxies HTTP and WebSocket streams to the Gateway over a private Unix socket with a per-boot proxy token. Client-supplied ingress and identity headers are replaced with authenticated facts.
- `tunnel-supervisor.ts`, `tunnel-ipc.ts`, `tunnel-runtime.ts`: start, health-ping, RSS-limit, backoff and stop the child (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL); push membership changes to it; report `running`, `unavailable`, `relay denied` or `crash looping`.
- `ingress-listener.ts`, `tunnel-api.ts`: the private listener marks each request as `openclaw-id-tunnel` with W and a synthetic per-device address, and serves the small tunnel API that owner devices use behind the loader.
- `remote-signout.ts`: signs out one relayed browser (closes its connections and revokes its tokens) without removing the device.
- `service.ts`: starts the tunnel runtime when the switch is on, publishes the tunnel principal, device-token binding and claw-origin resolvers, and requires the running endpoint key for linking.

**OpenClaw ID sign-in** (`account-sign-in.ts`, `openclawId.authority` `account_*` actions): an OIDC authorization-code flow with PKCE for the Control UI's account menu, direct loopback only. The Gateway holds the verifier and redeems the code; it keeps only display claims (`sub`, name, email) in the claw record.

**Gateway auth changes (security boundary):**

- `auth.ts`: a request the tunnel listener attributed to W authenticates as a `trusted-proxy` principal in every auth mode: owner devices act as the Gateway owner, members carry `openclaw-id:<account_id>` as the user. A key the authority no longer admits is refused (`openclaw_id_not_admitted`), and a tunnel request never falls back to the Gateway's other credentials.
- `ingress-attribution.ts`: adds the `openclaw-id-tunnel` transport (never direct loopback, rate-limited per device key). While the switch is on, identity headers (Cloudflare Access, `Remote-User`, `X-Remote-User`, the configured `userHeader`/`requiredHeaders`) also disqualify loopback locality, so a proxy that omits client-address headers cannot reach the local-only link ceremony. With the switch off this rule does not apply and attribution is unchanged.
- `ws-connection/*`, `operator-role-policy.ts`, `http-auth-user-profile.ts`: members are capped by their role's operator policy (operator: read, write, approvals, questions, talk; viewer: read only) on WebSocket and HTTP. Pairing within that ceiling is approved automatically for relayed browsers; owner devices pair with what they request.
- `device-token-binding.ts` users (`connect-auth.ts`, `connect-device-pairing.ts`, `http-auth-utils.ts`): a device token issued over the tunnel is bound to the W that obtained it; presenting it from another W, or from ordinary ingress, is refused and logged.
- `origin-check.ts`: a relayed WebSocket may also use the linked claw's own origin (`https://<claw hostname>`), read from the current owner-signed binding.
- `http-auth-plugin-cookie.ts`, `control-ui-plugin-auth-cookie.ts`: a signed plugin cookie cannot replace a relayed device's current membership, and none is issued to a tunnel request (it could be replayed on ordinary ingress).
- `gateway-owner-profile.ts`, `connect-device-pairing.ts`: an owner device acts as the Gateway owner when named `gateway.roles` are configured, like a token or password client.

Docs: `docs/gateway/remote.md` (OpenClaw ID alongside Tailscale, Cloudflare Access and Gateway credentials) and `docs/gateway/trusted-proxy-auth.md` (identity headers deny loopback locality).

## Review

An independent review (GPT-6 Astra) of this PR found four issues; three are fixed here with tests, one is narrowed:

- Fixed: plugin read cookies were issued to tunnel requests and could be replayed on ordinary ingress for their five-minute life. Tunnel requests no longer get them.
- Fixed: owner devices were refused when named `gateway.roles` were configured, because they carry no user. They now take the owner path.
- Fixed: the identity-header locality rule applied even with the switch off. It now applies only while OpenClaw ID is on.
- Fixed (decision in #192335): device tokens issued over the tunnel stay bound to their device key across a Gateway restart with the switch off. #192335 reads the saved bindings at Gateway start; here both ingress checks (`connect-auth.ts`, `http-operator-device-token.ts`) await that read. `http-auth-utils.paired-device.test.ts` saves a binding in the real claw store, starts a fresh service with the switch off, and shows the token refused on HTTP, including for a request that arrives before the read finishes. The test fails without the Gateway-start read.

**ClawSweeper's review of `9049570`: a removed owner could still invoke tools (P1), fixed here.** An HTTP request kept only the role it was admitted with. A `POST /tools/invoke` waiting in a before-tool-call hook therefore still ran its tool after its device was removed: closing the tunnel connection does not stop a request the Gateway already holds. Every authority check on a relayed HTTP request now also asks the membership authority whether the device is still admitted with the same kind, account and role (`isOpenClawIdTunnelPrincipalCurrent`, read from the claw record already loaded, in `http-auth-user-profile.ts`). If the device is removed, its role changes, or OpenClaw ID turns off, the request's next check fails. That includes the last check before the tool runs, which answers 403 "Gateway requester authority changed". `http-auth-utils.openclaw-id-tunnel.test.ts` drives the real HTTP authorization path and fails without the fix. The same review's P2, four test fixtures missing `getGatewayServer`, was fixed earlier.

ClawSweeper's review of `e164242` raised the same restart gap (now fixed, see above) and one doc finding, fixed here: `docs/gateway/trusted-proxy-auth.md` now says the Cloudflare Access, `Remote-User`, `X-Remote-User` and configured-header locality rule applies only while OpenClaw ID is on, and the Tailscale rule always applies.

Rebased onto #192335 at `9269511` and `main` at `06acff14158`. `service.publication-refresh.test.ts` now waits for startup publication, which #192335 moved beside the lifecycle queue.

Rebased with #192335 onto `main` at `0809cf31e69` (#193146 merged), without conflicts.

Rebased onto `main` at `49f8a60f227` (after #192859). Two files this PR touches had gone over the 700-line lint cap, so two self-contained pieces moved out, unchanged:

- `verifyHttpOperatorDeviceToken`, the HTTP device-token fallback that holds the tunnel-binding check, moved from `http-auth-utils.ts` to `http-operator-device-token.ts`.
- The config-derived settings helpers moved from `openclaw-id/service.ts` to `openclaw-id/service-settings.ts`.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test` over `src/gateway/openclaw-id`, the two `server.*openclaw-id*` integration suites, `auth.test.ts`, `control-ui-plugin-auth-cookie.test.ts`, `http-auth-utils.paired-device.test.ts`, `auth-context.test.ts` and the `hello` test: 44 files, 291 tests passed (plus 13 in the sign-in suite), 8 skipped (the tunnel-child tests, which need the native binding). This also includes `gateway-owner-profile.test.ts`, `user-profiles-http.auth.test.ts` and `server.auth.identity-network.test.ts`.
- With the iroh binding from #191470 present (built from its head `a66ec81`), the tunnel child and supervisor suites pass end to end: 5 files, 28 tests, including admission refusal before any stream, HTTP and WebSocket proxying, header replacement, the 64-stream limit, malformed HEAD reset and closing a live connection when membership drops its key. Without the binding the 8 tunnel-child tests skip, as they do in CI until #191470 lands.
- **Labs switch off:** the PR 1 off-state tests still pass here, and `coexistence.test.ts` shows Access, Serve and tailnet users are admitted with their existing permissions but get no People, link ceremony or sign-in.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and the core test typecheck shards passed. `pnpm check:changed`: see the comment below for the run on the published head.
- Test-line ratchet: `config/test-lines-allocations/openclaw-id-tunnel-signin.txt` allocates exactly the 3,248 test lines this PR adds (new tests for new surface). `main` itself is currently over its test-line ceiling by 94 lines, which is inherited and unrelated to this PR.
- Staging: the lab Gateways run this code (openclaw `1bc84010c2e`). The gates recorded in #191469 went through this tunnel: removed browsers reconnecting through the relay were refused at connection setup with no HTTP or WebSocket line logged; the removed owner device's open Control UI session was closed with `1008 removed from this claw`, and its operator tokens were revoked.

## What Problem This Solves
Dashboards whose primary content is a session:website widget appear as empty boards in the Dashboards gallery with the message 'A clear board, ready for work'. This occurs because session:website is registered with previewSafe: false to prevent passive code execution, causing board-document.tsx to filter out the widget and leaving BoardView with zero active rectangles (view().empty === true).

## Solution
Rather than changing previewSafe: true (which would allow unisolated iframes in gallery thumbnails), this change computes a safe websiteIdentity from authorized snapshot metadata during passive rendering. When BoardView detects an empty layout rectangle set, it inspects websiteIdentity and renders a recognizable website preview card featuring the built-in globe icon, saved title, and localized Website badge.

## Invariants & Security
- previewSafe: false is strictly retained in CORE_BOARD_WIDGET_ELEMENTS.
- Exactly 0 iframes or executable website widgets are mounted in passive mode.
- 0 network requests are initiated.
- Truly empty boards continue to display the standard empty-board prompt.
- Other unsafe widgets (agent:node-browser, mcp-app) remain isolated and do not display a website card.
- Mixed boards with preview-safe widgets (HTML) continue to render normal widget previews.

## Evidence
- Focused unit & integration regression tests: 27/27 pass.
  - ui/src/components/board/board-document.test.ts (14/14 pass).
  - ui/src/pages/dashboards/dashboards-page.test.tsx (6/6 pass).
  - ui/src/lib/board/widgets/website.test.ts (5/5 pass).
  - ui/src/lib/board/widgets/index.test.ts (2/2 pass).
- TypeScript check: pnpm tsgo:ui (0 errors).
- Linter checks: pnpm lint:ui:styles and pnpm lint:ui:no-raw-window-open (0 errors, 0 warnings across 6091 files).
- Build check: pnpm --dir ui build (clean build of 6325 modules in 1m 19s).
- Visual evidence: Playwright browser verification with system Chrome confirming recognizable card rendering with globe icon and widget title, and 0 iframes mounted.

Fixes #178467

prs.title: fix(cron): restore automation run history for administrator chats
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes administrator chats being able to inspect an existing automation while reading its run history fails with `Automation not found`, including managed dreaming jobs.

## User Impact

Administrators can read an existing automation's run history using their admitted management authority, including selecting a specific run. No permission changes or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the existing management grant to `cron.runs`, as already happens for `cron.get`. Keep the management and recovery tool schemas and descriptions consistent with that capability. Existing caller restrictions, grant validation, and current-job restrictions still apply.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through a real authenticated administrator chat: `get` succeeded while `runs` failed. After deploying the fix, both succeeded and the native tool returned all eight retained dreaming runs.
- Added a regression using the real automation tool, grant binding, Gateway handlers, and persisted SQLite history. It fails before the fix, passes afterward, and verifies that a call without the management grant is still denied.
- All 89 focused tests passed, covering run visibility, grant/context handling, management and recovery schemas, requester authority, and tool-prefix stability.
- Production typecheck, targeted lint/format, documentation validation, and runtime build passed.
- Independent autoreview completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The isolated PR checkout matches the tested and deployed source byte for byte.

<details>
<summary>Validation scope and timing</summary>

Focused suites: `cron.runs.test.ts`, `cron-tool.management.test.ts`, `cron-creator-authority-context.test.ts`, `cron-creator-authority-grant.test.ts`, `requester-cron-authority.integration.test.ts`, and `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts`, with `--maxWorkers=1`.

The new regression took 2.165 seconds. The run-history suite took about 26 seconds of test execution and 159.34 seconds wall time; the remaining focused suites took 327.82 seconds wall time, largely compilation. The integration test crosses the grant-forwarding boundary that isolated handler tests missed. CI timing is pending.

Additional checks: `pnpm tsgo:core`, targeted `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `pnpm format:check`, `scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs`, `git diff --check`, and `pnpm build:runtime` (2 minutes 45.6 seconds).

</details>

prs.title: fix: bound Codex catalog startup and client cleanup
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/152886

## What Problem This Solves

Codex catalog startup can load the agent runtime prematurely and retain client work after its owner closes, while competing health refreshes can consume catalog admission during Gateway startup.

## User Impact

Catalog and client work keeps its existing owner, cancellation and cleanup boundaries. A canonically bundled Codex plugin can use the host's state APIs without mislabeling a locally patched archive as an official npm installation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the catalog factory available when the harness loads while deferring heavyweight authentication code and actual client/catalog requests. Close owned transport work, fence native catalog walks, and align the bundled harness with native Codex 0.159.3.

This branch also includes its inherited Gateway health ownership, catalog admission, fleet metadata and serialized build fixes. It contains six commits and 39 changed files relative to the release branch's common ancestor; the final Codex commit changes 24 files. It preserves installed-plugin provenance and the existing local-archive trust refusal. Host bundling uses the canonical package composer.

## Evidence

- 45 focused tests passed on the final source in 27.37 seconds; native version and npm lock checks also passed.
- The canonical Core build completed successfully, with source/dependency and process-closure checks preserved.
- The canonical bundled archive installed into an isolated private prefix. Its content inventory, bundled metadata and native 0.159.3 producer matched the packaged inputs.
- A real installed-loader check passed all three storage cells in 19.91 seconds: honest local archive refused; host bundle opened synchronous and asynchronous keyed stores; host-bundle selection with an unchanged global archive record opened both stores.
- A real isolated installed-CLI model turn passed in 17.05 seconds. It observed the pinned native app-server process and exact response marker, then closed its unit and removed private runtime state. It used a maintenance account, so it does not certify service-account credentials or production review jobs.

The full Core test/check suites and upstream CI have not run for this head. Fresh isolated nine-agent startup qualification is pending. This draft does not claim production release or review-job acceptance.

prs.title: feat(media): optional silent delivery for audio transcript echo
prs.body:
Closes #187243

## What Problem This Solves

With `tools.media.audio.echoTranscript` enabled, every voice note produces two notifications on Telegram: one for the transcript echo and one for the agent reply that follows, so the confirmation-only echo becomes notification noise.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can set `tools.media.audio.echoSilent: true` to deliver the transcript echo silently (Telegram `disable_notification`: the notification still appears, but without sound) while the agent reply keeps notifying normally. Default is `false`, so existing behavior is unchanged; channels without silent delivery keep sending the echo as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`sendTranscriptEcho` is the single owner of echo delivery for the media-understanding path, audio preflight, and the plugin-SDK preflight runtime, and it already receives the effective config. It now forwards `silent: true` to the durable outbound send when `echoSilent` is set. The outbound path already carries `silent` end to end (delivery params, durable queue persistence, Telegram adapter mapping to `disable_notification`, the same route `channels.telegram.silentErrorReplies` uses), so no channel code changes are needed. Config schema, field help/label, docs, the generated config-doc baseline hashes, and the common-tier snapshot are updated.

## Evidence

- New integration test in `src/media-understanding/echo-transcript.integration.test.ts` drives the real durable SQLite queue with a fake Telegram outbound adapter: the default echo reaches the adapter without `silent`, and with `echoSilent: true` the adapter receives `silent: true`. Red on base (`upstream/main` f03f131: test fails), green with this change.
- `pnpm test src/media-understanding/echo-transcript.integration.test.ts src/media-understanding/echo-transcript.test.ts src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts src/config/schema.tiers.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/media-understanding-runtime.test.ts src/media-understanding/audio-preflight.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: all passed.
- `pnpm config:docs:gen` / `pnpm config:schema:gen` run; `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files.
- `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main`: every lane green (typecheck core + core tests, lint core, format, config docs baseline, bundled channel config metadata, plugin boundaries, import cycles, ratchets) except the dead-export scan, which fails only on pre-existing unused exports elsewhere in `src/` on `main`; none are in files touched here and this change adds no exports.
- Live Telegram end-to-end run completed on a real Gateway, as [reported by the PR author](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187312#issuecomment-6527766230): with `tools.media.audio.echoSilent: true`, the transcript echo arrives without sound, while the agent reply notifies normally. No recording or request/output logs are attached for independent verification; a screenshot would not show the difference between a muted and a normal notification. The Telegram `silent` → `disable_notification` mapping itself is existing, covered code.

prs.title: fix(codex): doctor --fix removes an appServer.command that points into a missing plugin generation
prs.body:
Related: #181037
Complementary prevention (merged): #191693

## What Problem This Solves

Recovery only: older cleanup versions may already have deleted the managed Codex generation referenced by `plugins.entries.codex.config.appServer.command`. The merged prevention fix #191693 keeps configured generations on disk, but cannot restore files already deleted.

## User Impact

Run `openclaw doctor --fix`, then restart the Gateway. Doctor removes only the stale command override so normal managed binary selection resumes (or `OPENCLAW_CODEX_APP_SERVER_BIN` applies). This may select a newer Codex binary. Other app-server settings, including arguments, remain unchanged. Plain Doctor previews the repair through its existing normalization flow.

Existing generation pins, unrelated custom executables, and non-missing filesystem errors remain untouched. No runtime fallback or cleanup changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the repair with the Codex plugin's existing Doctor normalizer. Recognize only the historical `openclaw-codex-8902d781d4__openclaw-generation__g-<16 lowercase hex>` directory layout beneath the state directory's `npm/projects`, and remove the override only when the generation stat returns `ENOENT` or `ENOTDIR`.

The historical name is deliberately frozen recovery data, not a second implementation of future install naming. This removes the hash-helper dependency, duplicate containment check, and nested exception scaffolding without adding SDK surface or state. Tests use an independent historical fixture and consolidate repeated setup and assertions.

Limits: no recovery of arbitrary custom paths, pinned non-default npm roots, relative command paths, external state-directory symlink aliases, or missing binaries inside an otherwise existing generation. No claim that updating alone applies this unpublished plugin repair; direct Doctor recovery is the supported scope.

## Current Validation

- Simplified head: `090cc4fea9b5`; original contributor head: `5e9100d477b2`.
- Credential-free Linux ARM64 container, Node 24.22.1, frozen dependency install; no host state or credentials mounted. Tests ran with networking disconnected.
- Focused recovery and sibling Doctor suites: **60/60 passed**, two Vitest shards in 129.43s. After cleaning leftover source files from the reused image, the recovery suite was rerun: **21/21 passed**, 66.96s wrapper / 61.51s Vitest, dominated by compilation. The subsequent final change only adds required braces to a test conditional and adjusts its line allocation.
- Both primary recovery cases fail on pre-fix `c147613091ca` because the command remains configured; they pass with the repair.
- Targeted production/test TypeScript check passed using the repository test config with the two touched files as roots. Targeted source-backed lint: zero warnings/errors (23.4s). Pinned formatting, pre-commit checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent source review: no P0–P2 findings. Local ClawSweeper completed the full `c147613091ca..be697c268f72` range: no correctness/security findings. Final delta since that review is only the test braces and 122→124 line allocation; no production changes.
- Initial package-boundary validation encountered stale source files in the reused image; these were removed before the final focused checks. No successful full repository build is claimed.
- No new live Doctor/Gateway/model/channel or latest-stable updater run was performed. The contributor's earlier live evidence below is prior-head evidence, not a claim of current-head execution. Hosted CI is pending the push.

Compared with the original revision: production additions 62 → 44; regression test lines 394 → 124. The 124-line test allocation covers missing-generation recovery, managed selection, idempotency, preservation of settings and working pins, custom-path boundaries, symlinks, and filesystem-error distinctions.

Original contribution and live proof by @Satoshi-Kusumoto are retained below. The follow-up preserves the contributor's commit ancestry.

<details>
<summary>Original contributor evidence at 5e9100d477b2 (prior revision, not current-head proof)</summary>

The following is the contributor's original evidence and limitations. References to "this head" below mean `5e9100d477b2`, not the simplified revision. The new scope is complementary recovery; prevention is now supplied separately by #191693.


**Live run: stable 2026.10.8 writes the state, this head repairs it** (2026-10-30; head `5e9100d477b2`, Linux x64, Node 24.22.1). One isolated `HOME`, so the state directory is `<home>/.openclaw`; the Gateway listened on loopback with token auth; one real OpenAI OAuth sign-in (device code); the Telegram turns came from a self-created test bot in a private chat. The steps follow an update that leaves the old generation on disk until a later cleanup; the generation directory was created and removed by hand (see **Live proof** under **Not covered**). Redacted output is in the collapsed block below.

- **Stable writes the state.** `npm install -g --prefix <prefix> openclaw@2026.10.8 --allow-scripts=openclaw` into an isolated prefix (`OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (dc2523e)`), then `openclaw plugins install @openclaw/codex@2026.10.8`, which installed a flat managed project with no generation directory. The stable CLI then set `appServer.command` to `<home>/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-codex-8902d781d4__openclaw-generation__g-115fa95f6ea65a40/node_modules/@openai/codex-linux-x64/vendor/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex`. The path was written by hand, not left behind by an update, and no directory existed at it while the stable build ran. The stable CLI also wrote the `appServer` keys `transport: "stdio"`, `homeScope: "agent"`, `mode: "guardian"`, `sandbox: "read-only"`, `approvalPolicy: "on-request"`, `requestTimeoutMs`, and `args`, plus Gateway, Telegram, tool-policy, and agent-runtime settings.
- **Before (stable 2026.10.8).** `openclaw doctor` and `openclaw doctor --fix --yes` keep the command: the preview listed no removal and left the config file byte-identical, and both runs printed core Doctor's existing custom-command warning (`Custom Codex app-server command bypasses OpenClaw's managed exact-version binary.`); `--fix` wrote stable Doctor's own updates (an empty `agents.entries.main`, `meta.migrations.webhookListeners`, `plugins.entries.openai.enabled`, 30 `skills.entries.*.enabled: false` entries, and `wizard` run metadata) and left every `plugins.entries.codex` key, including `appServer.command`, unchanged. With the stable Gateway running, `openclaw agent` (through the Gateway, not `--local`) exits 1 with `Codex catalog updater cannot run: <home>/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-codex-8902d781d4__openclaw-generation__g-115fa95f6ea65a40/…/bin/codex or its working directory was not found`. A Telegram message got no reply within 3 minutes, and the Gateway logged `[telegram] dispatch failed: CodexAppServerSpawnError: Codex catalog updater cannot run: <home>/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-codex-8902d781d4__openclaw-generation__g-115fa95f6ea65a40/…` (the same error as the CLI turn) and `spooled update <id> failed; keeping for retry`.
- **After (this head, same state).** The stable Gateway was stopped, an empty directory was created at the seeded generation path, and the same `HOME` was handed to a build of this head (`OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (5e9100d)`). Doctor ran the Codex plugin bundled with this build (see **Live proof** under **Not covered**).
  - First repair, generation present: `openclaw doctor --fix --yes` ran this build's pending state migration (`Doctor: database migrations`, with pre-migration SQLite backups saved under `<home>/.openclaw/state/` and `<home>/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/`) and kept `appServer.command`, since the generation directory existed; the other `appServer` keys were unchanged. Config changes in this run: `messages` added (Doctor's existing default, `Set messages.queue.allowCollaborativeSteering to false (default).`), `meta.lastTouchedVersion` 2026.10.8 → 2026.10.7, and `wizard.lastRunAt` / `wizard.lastRunVersion` (the latter 2026.10.8 → 2026.10.7) from Doctor's run metadata. On a separate stable-written state with the same kind of command and no directory, the same first `doctor --fix --yes` removed the command.
  - Cleanup: the empty generation directory was removed.
  - Preview: `openclaw doctor` lists `Removed plugins.entries.codex.config.appServer.command; it pointed into an OpenClaw-managed Codex plugin generation that no longer exists. …` as a pending change and leaves the config file byte-identical.
  - Repair: `openclaw doctor --fix --yes` writes it. The only `appServer` change is the removed `command`; all config changes in this run: `plugins.entries.codex.config.appServer.command` removed, and `wizard.lastRunAt` updated by Doctor's run metadata.
  - Restart: the Gateway started on this build, and the Codex app-server log line was `Codex app-server: using bundled 0.164.0 (no codex on PATH)`.
  - Turns: `openclaw agent` exits 0 with `CLI-CANDIDATE-OK`, and the Telegram message was answered with `CANDIDATE-OK` (about 8 s after the Gateway received the message; no spawn error was logged after it). The stable-phase Telegram message, which the stable Gateway had kept for retry, was answered with `STABLE-OK` about 13 s after this head's Gateway logged `http server listening`.
- **Version order.** This head identifies as 2026.10.7, older than the 2026.10.8 release that wrote the config (main's version string lags the release branch). Its first commands printed `Your OpenClaw config was written by version 2026.10.8, but this command is running 2026.10.7.` No command refused to run, and `OPENCLAW_ALLOW_OLDER_BINARY_DESTRUCTIVE_ACTIONS` was not set. The `meta.lastTouchedVersion` change in the config diffs is the normal config-write stamp.
- **Existing data still works.** This head used the stable-written OAuth profile, Telegram pairing, and Gateway token as they were: no new sign-in, no new pairing code, and the CLI connected with the stored token. After the Gateway stopped, this head's `openclaw models auth list --json` showed the one stable-written OpenAI profile (OAuth, not expired), `openclaw pairing list telegram` showed no pending request, and `openclaw sessions --json` listed the CLI session from the stable phase and the Telegram session. The Telegram update that the stable Gateway had kept for retry was replayed and answered by this head.
- **Other commands are kept.** The same stable-then-this-head sequence, Doctor only, on two more states written by the stable CLI, each with one command outside the managed root: an existing executable (`<iso>/custom-bin/codex`) and a missing path (`<iso>/missing/codex`). On each, this head's first `doctor --fix --yes` left the command and the other `appServer` keys unchanged, and a following `doctor` listed no removal: on both, the `appServer` subtree was byte-identical before and after the first repair and the config diff had no `REMOVED` entry (run on 2026-10-29 in the same isolated setup, without credentials). A command inside a generation directory that still exists is covered by the first repair above.

prs.title: fix(cli): invalidate Gateway-cached MCP runtimes on mcp reload
prs.body:
Closes #164642

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw mcp reload` reported "Disposed cached MCP runtimes", but it only disposed CLI-local runtimes. The Gateway process owns its own cached session MCP runtimes, and the CLI command could not reach across the process boundary — so the Gateway's stdio MCP server kept serving the stale runtime and subsequent agent turns never saw the new MCP config.

## What Changed

- New gateway method `mcp.reloadRuntimes` (`mcp-app` family, `operator.write`): disposes the Gateway-side session MCP runtimes via the existing `disposeAllSessionMcpRuntimes` owner.
- The CLI's `mcp reload` dispatches the method before the local dispose and degrades gracefully when no Gateway is reachable (the CLI-local dispose always runs; the log states which side was disposed).

## Evidence

- Handler regression (`mcp.reload-runtimes.test.ts`): the method disposes all session MCP runtimes and acknowledges `{ ok: true }`. Red on `origin/main` (no such method).
- Suites: recovery 222/222, `session-accessor.readonly` 26/26, `server-startup-post-attach` 115/115; `tsc` core clean in all touched files.
- The reporter's source inspection (CLI-local dispose only) matches the pre-fix behavior; the gateway-side dispose reuses the same owner the server-close path already calls.


## Update — 2026-10-04 (Rev 3 rework)

- **Lease-preserving reload**: the handler now runs the Gateway's own config-reload path (`reloadSessionMcpRuntimes`, the same one the hot-reload flow uses) instead of the shutdown-grade `disposeAllSessionMcpRuntimes` — admitted calls keep their runtimes; only stale ones rebuild on the next turn. The manager's `reloadConfig` propagates per-runtime reload failures (no swallowed errors).
- **Authority revalidation**: the handler reads the request's mutation authority and asserts it current immediately before the reload — a caller revoked during the acquisition wait can no longer trigger it.
- **CLI output**: the failure branch now states which side was disposed and that the Gateway-side reload was **not confirmed** (no more misleading "active agents use new config" assurance when the reload did not run); the no-Gateway case is labeled explicitly. The import-boundary assertion follows.
- Handler tests: reload shape (`reloadPlugins: false`), authority revalidation observed, and the failure path responding with an error shape.

Still open: the authority-chain live evidence (allowed reload, read-only rejection, queued revocation preventing closure, discovery/active-call survival) and the command-scope framing — the reload semantics now match the Gateway's own hot-reload behavior rather than a Gateway-wide teardown.

prs.title: fix(auth): stop automatic session accounts from vetoing strict CLI routes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A session's machine-chosen model-account binding (`authProfileOverrideSource: "auto"`) was fed into the CLI runtime auth evaluation as if the user had selected that account. `evaluateCliRuntimeModelAuthAvailability` collapsed both fields into one value:

```ts
const selectedProfileId = ref.pinnedProfileId?.trim() || ref.preferredProfileId?.trim();
```

and then, for a backend declaring `strictSelectedProfile` (`claude-cli`, `nativeAuthProfileIds: ["anthropic:claude-cli"]`), the non-pinned branch returned the untouched provider-only `evaluation`:

```ts
return ref.pinnedProfileId
  ? evaluateProviderAuth(provider, { modelId: ref.modelId, requiredProfileId: selectedProfileId })
  : evaluation;
```

For Anthropic through `claude-cli` that provider-only evaluation has no credential evidence, so every Anthropic row came back `available: false` / `unavailableReason: "missing-auth"` whenever the session's automatic account happened to belong to another provider (OpenAI in the report). The credential was never missing: the CLI's own login is prepared on the route (`preparedRuntimeAuthModes["claude-cli"]`), and the executor already agrees that an automatic preference is a preference, not a constraint — `resolveCliExecutionAuthProfileId` deliberately ignores a selection whose `authProfileIdSource` is `"auto"` (`src/agents/cli-execution-auth.ts:60-92`).

Only an explicit pin is a selection now; an automatic preference falls through to the prepared native-runtime result for the route, which is the fact the UI needs to stop disabling every Claude row.

### Changes

- `src/agents/model-auth-availability.ts` — the `strictSelectedProfile` veto requires `ref.pinnedProfileId`, and the non-pinned fall-through that returned the provider-only evaluation is gone. Pinned-profile and `requiredProfileId` behavior is unchanged.
- `src/agents/model-auth-availability.test.ts` — regression coverage: an automatic account owned by another provider keeps the native CLI route `available: true` (`evidence: "runtime"`), while an explicit pin of that same account is still refused.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(codex): cold web-search support verdicts no longer rotate bound threads
prs.body:
Closes #174676

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: a Codex conversation's native thread is replaced — re-sending its full selected history — on the second turn after a Gateway cold start, because turn 1 recorded the web-search policy from a cold capability probe.

## User Impact
Conversations that start right after a Gateway start keep their native thread and prompt context. A cold "unsupported" capability read no longer forces a full history re-send once the provider's web-search support resolves (the issue measured ~1.2M characters re-injected on a lossless session).

## Why This Change Was Made
A cold app-server can answer `modelProvider/capabilities/read` before its model metadata hydrates, producing a definitive-looking "unsupported" verdict. The lifecycle persisted that verdict's disabled thread config as the binding's authoritative web-search fingerprint, so the first informed turn counted the change as a persistent policy change and rotated the thread.

The preflight now also computes the fingerprint an uninformed ("unknown") plan produces under the same config. When a binding's stored fingerprint equals that uninformed shape and the current plan is informed, the lifecycle adopts the informed fingerprint on the existing thread instead of replacing it. Genuine policy edits (allowed domains, provider opt-outs, persistent denial) move the plan away from the uninformed shape and still rotate as before; a first turn under an "unknown" verdict already keeps a provisional binding and is untouched.

## Evidence
- Regression in `thread-lifecycle-web-search.test-support.ts` (registered from the binding suite): turn 1 under `nativeProviderWebSearchSupport: "unsupported"` persists the disabled fingerprint; turn 2 under `"supported"` keeps `thread-1` with exactly one `thread/start`. Fails on base — the thread is replaced via the "web search config changed" rotation named in the issue — and passes with this change.
- Neighbors stay green: 5/5 `search`-filtered cases in `thread-lifecycle.binding.test.ts` (including the existing unknown-support preservation case) and 8/8 in `thread-lifecycle.assignment-rotation.test.ts`, run with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on Node 24.19.
- Not run locally: full extension suite and project typecheck (CI covers).

prs.title: fix(release): exit FRV continue on repeat child failure and flag ghost jobs
prs.body:
## Problem

During 2026.11.5-beta.1, GitHub ghost jobs (runnerless queued copies of a job name) appeared in FRV child rerun attempts. They made two FRVs unsealable and cost about 7.5 hours. Two controller gaps made it worse:

- `pnpm frv continue --failed` reruns each child once per invocation. When a child it reran failed again, the loop filtered the child out (`!ownedAttempts.has(child.runId)`) and sat idle until every unrelated sibling settled. Only then did it throw `failed child reruns did not produce a complete green composite`. In the release, the npm attempt-2 failure at 10:42Z went unreported until 11:06Z. The follow mode of `rerun --job` behaved the same way.
- Duplicate-job detection already existed: `verifyRerunAttemptJobs` after a rerun POST, `readChildAttemptEvidence` with its 60s materialization window, and the watch scan. None of their errors said what to do next. The policy error (`is unsealable due to duplicate job identity`) and the watch message gave no recommendation, so operators kept rerunning.

## Solution

- `continueFailed`: when no new rerun is ready and a child that this invocation reran is terminal-failed, throw at once: `child <key> failed again on attempt N; rerun budget remaining M; rerun pnpm frv continue --failed --run <id> to retry a confirmed flake, otherwise start a fresh all-group FRV`. M is derived from the exact attempts and the existing `DEFAULT_CHILD_MAX_ATTEMPTS`. No new persisted state; the controller stays stateless. First-time failures of other children in the same loop are still rerun before this exit.
- One shared `GHOST_JOBS_ADVICE` string, owned by the policy module, is appended to all three existing duplicate-job reports: the policy's duplicate-identity error (used by `status`, `continue` and verification), `verifyRerunAttemptJobs`, and the `watch` duplicate event. No second detector was added; the existing 60s reconciliation still owns timing.
- Skill (`release-openclaw-ci`): ghost jobs can follow any rerun, single-job or batched. Send at most one rerun request per child, only after it is terminal. Duplicate or ghost reports mean a fresh all-group FRV. The skill also documents the new repeat-failure exit and `rerun --job --no-follow`.
- `docs/reference/full-release-validation/continuation.md`: describes the repeat-failure exit and the ghost-attempt outcome.

### Deliberately not done

- **`rerun --job` returning once the new attempt is observed:** `--no-follow` (#188020) already does exactly this. Making it the default would drop the parent reseal that follow mode performs and change the CLI contract, so I left it. With this PR, follow mode also exits immediately when the targeted child fails again instead of waiting on siblings. The skill now points to `--no-follow`.
- **Per-signature rerun budget, or allowing batched multi-job reruns:** the planner deliberately refuses multi-job reruns (#187996). Changing that, or adding budget state, is a recovery-policy decision for maintainers. The skill wording "one batched rerun per child" here means one request per child, not lifting that refusal.
- **Ghosts that appear after the first clean post-rerun read:** `verifyRerunAttemptJobs` returns on its first clean, non-empty job list. A ghost that materializes later is still caught by the next `continue` inspection, which re-reads every attempt each poll and fails after the 60s window with the new advice, and by `watch`. Holding every rerun for the full window was not worth the added latency without a live reproduction showing late ghosts.
- `--wait-for-seal` already exists (#181909); untouched.

## Impact

Release tooling only (`scripts/frv.mjs`, policy message, skill, continuation doc). Operators now get an immediate, actionable exit when a rerun child fails again, and every duplicate-job report names the fresh-FRV recovery. There is no change to which reruns are sent.

## Evidence

- New regression `exits when a rerun child fails again instead of idling on an active sibling`: on base it times out against the 2s operation deadline (red, 2003ms). With the fix it passes.
- Updated expectations, all red on base and green with the fix: targeted `rerun --job` repeat failure now reports `failed again on attempt 3; rerun budget remaining 0`. The persistent-duplicate materialization test and the post-POST duplicate test now assert the `GitHub ghost jobs detected` advice.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/frv.test.ts test/scripts/full-release-validation-state.test.ts test/scripts/full-release-child-evidence.test.ts test/scripts/frv.release.test.ts`: 402 passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json --incremental`: clean. `run-oxlint` on changed scripts and tests: clean. `oxfmt --check`: clean. `git diff --check`: clean.

Fixes #192561

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): add Gateway membership authority and publication behind the Labs flag
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw ID remote access needs a Gateway-side owner for each claw's membership: who the owner devices and members are, how signed changes from them are accepted, and how the claw is published to Discovery. This draft adds that owner, without any transport, sign-in or UI, so it can be reviewed on its own.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Everything here sits behind the `gateway.openclawId.enabled` Labs switch, which is off by default. With the switch off the Gateway starts nothing, opens no sockets, makes no OpenClaw ID, Discovery or relay calls, hides the `openclawId.*` methods and events from `hello`, and answers every `openclawId.*` call with "off" or a refusal.

With the switch on, a claw still cannot be linked from this PR alone: linking needs the tunnel endpoint key, and the tunnel lands in the next PR. Linking is refused with `tunnel_not_running` until then.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the third PR of the OpenClaw ID stack. It builds on the protocol package (#191469, merged) and on #193146 (merged), which makes revocations replay-safe and bounds invites. The next PRs are:

- the tunnel transport, OpenClaw ID sign-in and the Gateway auth changes for relayed devices (stacked on this branch; it also needs the iroh binding, #191470);
- the Control UI and the People plugin.

What this PR adds, all in `src/gateway/openclaw-id/` unless noted:

- **Membership authority** (`authority.ts`, `claw-store.ts`, `binding-check.ts`, `claw-migration.ts`): the durable claw record in the shared state database. It applies owner-signed statements through the protocol package's authority rules, keeps invite reports and device-token bindings (in a second row, so each row fits the plugin-state value limit at every cap), deletes spent invites with their reports before each write, and runs the link ceremony (`prepareLink`/`commitLink`). A claw's root never changes: there is no owner reset (it was removed from the protocol package and is redesigned separately).
- **Admission and classification** (`channel.ts`, `connection-identity.ts`, `tunnel-principal.ts` types, `device-token-binding.ts`): a client is `local_operator` only when the handshake attested direct loopback, and `tunnel` only when it carries a relayed device key (set by the next PR). People, owner devices and invites are disclosed only to the local operator or an active owner device.
- **Publication** (`publisher.ts`, `publication-retry.ts`, `registration-recovery.ts`, `discovery-client.ts`, `gateway-key.ts`, `stale-seq.ts`): publishes the descriptor and a K_gw-signed membership snapshot to Discovery, retries failures with backoff, refreshes before the snapshot ages out, and recovers a registration that Discovery lost.
- **Mailbox and notices** (`mailbox-reader.ts`, `owner-notices.ts`, `device-mail-relay.ts`): reads the claw's Discovery mailbox (invite redemptions and owner-signed changes) and mails owner notices.
- **Removal effects and People events** (`removal-effects.ts`, `member-activity.ts`, `tunnel-connections.ts`, `people-events.ts`, `owner-expiry.ts`, `owner-lifecycle.ts`, `invite-expiry.ts`): removing a device closes its connections, cancels its runs and revokes its tokens; owners get a keyless `openclawId.people.changed` invalidation.
- **Service and RPC** (`service.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/openclaw-id*.ts`): `openclawId.status`, `openclawId.people` (owner only) and `openclawId.authority` (`check_name`, `prepare`, `commit`, `publish`, `submit`, `register_invite`, `device_mail`).
- **Gateway wiring**: the service is created in kernel state, reconciled after ready and on config reload (`gateway.openclawId` is hot-reloadable), and stopped with the Gateway. `GatewayClientRegistry` gains `subscribeChanges` so People events can observe connections without replacing another owner.
- **Config**: `gateway.openclawId` (`enabled`, `issuerUrl`, `clientId`, `discoveryUrl`, `relayUrl`, `loaderDomain`, `ownerDeviceInactivityDays`, `memberDeviceInactivityDays`) with schema, labels, help and docs.

<details><summary>Notes for review</summary>

- `core-descriptors.ts` was at the 700-line `max-lines` limit, and the protocol-since check needs new methods inline in that table. To fit the three `openclawId.*` rows, the `cron.status` share policy object is now written on one line. Formatting only.
- Exports that only the next PR consumes in production (`device-token-binding.ts`, `tunnel-child/keyfile.ts`) have Knip production-scan entries with a note to drop them with that importer. Focused tests cover them here.
- `tunnel-child/keyfile.ts` is in this PR because K_gw (`gateway-key.ts`) uses the same 0600 key-file loader; the tunnel child itself is in the next PR.
- The `openclawId.people.changed` event is allowlisted for iOS and Android: the People page is Control UI only.

</details>

## Review

An independent review (GPT-6 Astra) found four issues in the code carried over from the staging branch. All are fixed here, with regression tests:

- Two concurrent first loads of the claw record could each read it; a late read could replace a committed change (for example restore a removed owner device). The first read is now shared.
- Turning the switch off did not cancel a mailbox long-poll already in flight; its response could still be applied. The request now carries the stop signal, and a stopped reader applies nothing more.
- `openclawId.authority` `publish` did not check ownership, and its result names the owner account. It now requires a current owner, checked before and after publishing.
- A config reload while running ignored changes to `discoveryUrl`, `loaderDomain` and the inactivity windows. A change now restarts the service.

ClawSweeper's review of `fbdae28` found three more; all are fixed in `e9522d1`, each with a regression test:

- **Token restriction kept until revocation is confirmed.** A removal used to delete a tunnel token's device-key binding before revoking the token, so a failed revocation left a valid, unbound token that ordinary ingress would accept. Now the token is revoked first and only confirmed revocations (or already-absent tokens) drop their binding. A token whose revocation failed stays bound to its removed key, so every ingress keeps refusing it, and the next start retries it (`orphanedTokens`: bindings whose key is no longer in the membership).
- **Each mailbox statement settles before the next.** A `root_statement` message with several statements now applies each committed statement's effects (close connections, cancel runs, revoke tokens) before the next is submitted, so a later failure cannot discard an earlier removal's effects.
- **Stop cancels Discovery.** Every Discovery request carries the service's lifecycle signal, which stopping remote access aborts, and a 30-second deadline that also covers reading the body (long polls get their wait plus 30 seconds). Startup publication no longer holds the reconcile queue, so turning the switch off or stopping the Gateway is never queued behind a stalled publication.

A second ClawSweeper pass (on `e9522d1`) found two more, fixed in `9269511` with tests:

- **Device mail rechecks authority at the network boundary.** The relay now rechecks the caller and the exact owner-device certificate it signed with immediately before the request leaves for Discovery, not only after the response. A device removed (or the switch turned off) during signature verification sends nothing.
- **A stopped mailbox reader submits nothing more.** Within one `root_statement` message, the reader's stop signal is checked before each statement; a statement already committed still gets its effects.

**Fixed, maintainer decision (2026-11-04): read saved token bindings at Gateway start even with the switch off.** A token whose revocation failed, or any token issued over the tunnel, stays bound to its device key across a restart with the Labs switch off:

- `service-token-bindings.ts` reads the local claw record once at Gateway start (`server-runtime-state-prepare.ts`, before any listener admits a connection). It publishes the binding owner only when saved bindings exist, so a Gateway without them behaves exactly as `main`. No process, socket or remote service is touched; `service.inert.test.ts` gains a case for this read.
- `checkDeviceTokenPeer` is now async and waits for that read, so a connection that arrives during boot cannot slip past it.
- Fail closed: if the claw record cannot be read, every device token is refused (`device-token-bindings-unreadable`) until the switch turns on or the Gateway restarts, and a security warning is logged. Shared-token and password auth are unaffected, so the owner keeps a way in.
- This replaces the earlier "switch off reads nothing" contract with "switch off reads only the local claw record".
- Tests: `service.token-bindings-start.test.ts` (restart with the switch off, a check that arrives mid-read, no saved bindings, unreadable record) and `device-token-binding.test.ts` (the read gate, unreadable refusal). The ingress callers arrive in #192345, which adds an HTTP test against the real claw store.


**ClawSweeper's review of `08d444e`: replayed mailbox revocations (P1), fixed by #193146.** A captured revocation replayed through the mailbox after an owner approved the device again removed it again. The repair is in the protocol package (#193146, credited to @SebTardif's #192230): a revocation now names its claw and the seq its signer saw, and removes only keys listed at or before that seq. This PR adds the Gateway side:

- `mailbox-reader.test.ts` drives the real authority through `applyMailboxMessage`: revoke, approve again, replay. The replay is refused with `seq_conflict`, the device stays admitted, and no removal effects run. The test fails when the protocol's seq check is removed.
- Invites stay bounded: the sweep that expires pending redemptions now also deletes spent invite records (cap expired, nothing pending) with their reports (`service.invites.test.ts`).
- **Claw record size.** At every protocol cap (20 owner devices, 256 members with 10 browsers each, 100 invites) and with a token binding for every browser, the record as one value would be about 1.3 MiB, past the 1 MiB plugin-state value limit, so every write would fail. Token bindings now live in their own row of the same namespace. `claw-store.test.ts` builds that claw with every text field at its longest: the record row is 809,134 bytes and the bindings row 563,060 bytes, each under the 1,048,576-byte limit; the single value would be 1,372,193 bytes. A record written before keeps its bindings until the next write moves them into the row.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/openclaw-id`: 25 files, 125 tests passed on `49f5c8357f9`, including the review regressions. `service.stall.test.ts` runs the real service and Discovery client against a Discovery that never answers: turning the switch off completes and aborts the publication and mailbox requests, well inside the request deadline (it times out against the previous head). The config schema, `hello`, method, broadcast-scope, config-reload and client-registry suites also pass.
- **Labs switch off** (new `labs-off.test.ts`, plus `service.inert.test.ts` and the `hello` test): with the switch absent or `false`, even with a linked claw record and every service URL configured, the service spawns no child, opens no `net`/`dgram` socket and calls no `fetch`; every `openclawId.authority` action and `openclawId.people` is refused for the loopback operator; `openclawId.status` reports `off` and no link; `hello` advertises no `openclawId.*` methods or events.
- Rebased onto `main` at `0809cf31e69` (#193146 merged) without conflicts. `pnpm tsgo:core` and the core test typecheck shards passed. `pnpm check:changed --base HEAD~1`: see the comment below for the run on the published head. Known inherited failures on `main`: `ui/src/pages/systems/systems-sidebar.tsx: systemKind` in the Knip scan, and `max-lines` warnings in four files this PR does not touch.
- Test-line ratchet: `config/test-lines-allocations/openclaw-id-gateway-core.txt` allocates the 3,886 test lines this PR adds; the ratchet's net delta equals the allocation. `main` itself is currently over its ceiling by 94 lines, which is inherited and unrelated. They are new tests for new surface; no existing tests were replaced.
- **Stored data:** token bindings move from the claw record into their own row; a record written before keeps its bindings until the next write moves them (`claw-store.test.ts`). The protocol's new listing seqs and invite creators are optional, so staging records load unchanged. `claw-migration.test.ts` loads pre-allowlist records and rewrites them once. No released OpenClaw version has OpenClaw ID state, so there is nothing to upgrade from a stable release.
- The staging lab Gateways run this code (openclaw `1bc84010c2e`, whose Gateway and UI sources match this stack before the rebase fixes). The staging gates recorded in #191469 exercise this authority through the tunnel: removing an owner device also removes the device it approved, the next published snapshot lists neither, and the 21st owner device is refused with `limit_reached`.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): add the Control UI account menu, linking dialogs and the People plugin
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With the Gateway parts in place, an owner still needs a way to use OpenClaw ID from the Control UI: sign in, turn on remote access for a claw, keep the recovery kit, approve their other browsers, and invite and manage people. This draft adds those Control UI surfaces and the bundled People plugin.

## User Impact

No user-visible change while the `gateway.openclawId.enabled` Labs switch is off (the default): the account menu, dialogs, the Labs entry's dependent surfaces, the `gateway.openclawId` settings, the People page and its plugin catalog entry, grants and asset routes are all absent.

With the switch on, owners get:

- **Account menu** (sidebar avatar): Sign in with OpenClaw ID, Turn on remote access, Your devices, Copy claw link, Sign out of OpenClaw ID, depending on the connection and setup state. Members see their own account and role, and no People or setup actions.
- **Turn on remote access**: choose a claw name, create and save the recovery kit (download, print, or save to 1Password), then link. Each linking step reports its own progress and failure.
- **Owner approval**: approve a new owner browser from an existing one with a short authentication string (SAS) check.
- **Your devices**: list approved owner browsers and remove one; the confirmation names any devices removed with it.
- **People** page (bundled `openclaw-id-access` plugin, under Pages): invite by email, approve or deny requests, see members' devices and activity, and remove members.

There is no owner reset in this version; the docs say so.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stacked on the tunnel and sign-in PR (#192345), which is stacked on the Gateway core PR (#192335). It is the last PR of the Gateway split of the OpenClaw ID stack.

- `ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/**`: browser-side account storage and sign-in popup, link ceremony steps, recovery-kit export, owner device keys (non-extractable WebCrypto Ed25519 in IndexedDB), owner-approval SAS, device mail and remote sign-out.
- Your devices signs each revocation with the claw id and the seq it last read (#193146), so it covers only the listing on screen; a device approved again since is refused as a concurrent change, and the dialog refreshes.
- `ui/src/components/openclaw-id/**`: the account menu, Make reachable, recovery kit, owner approval and Your devices dialogs, with the Control UI's existing menu and modal components.
- Sidebar and settings: an optional, feature-owned extension of the identity menu (`app-sidebar-identity-menu.tsx`), the Labs registry entry, and `gateway.openclawId` hidden from settings search and the config form while the switch is off.
- `extensions/openclaw-id-access/**`: the People page, a bundled plugin enabled by default whose Control UI module loads only while the switch is on.
- Gateway: the Control UI document carries a public `data-openclaw-id-enabled` attribute only when the switch is on; the plugin catalog, tab grants, asset routes and managed-plugin list hide `openclaw-id-access` while it is off, and a switch change broadcasts `plugins.controlUi.changed`.
- New dependency: `@1password/save-button` 1.3.0 in `ui` (the recovery kit's Save in 1Password button).
- Config surface: the plugin config baseline grows from 4,940 to 4,961 entries and core from 2,586 to 2,595, for the new bundled plugin and the `gateway.openclawId` keys from the earlier PRs (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json`).
- Docs: `docs/concepts/experimental-features.md` (OpenClaw ID remote access) and the plugin reference and inventory.

<details><summary>Notes for review</summary>

- The account menu conflicted with `main`'s fix that keeps the profile avatar element stable (#189747). The OpenClaw ID initial is rendered inside that stable avatar instead of replacing it.
- Type assertions in the new browser code either carry `// SAFETY:` comments or were removed (`stepOfKind` in the Make reachable dialog, the role select in People).
- Exports that focused tests use but production does not import have Knip production-scan entries; the full-tree scan still checks them.

</details>

## Review

An independent review (GPT-6 Astra) found three issues; all are fixed here:

- Two overlapping "Create recovery kit" requests could show one kit while another root signed the link, leaving a kit that cannot recover the claw. Overlapping requests now share one kit (regression test in `link.test.ts`).
- The config editor removed the `gateway.openclawId` settings even with the switch on, because it filtered the schema a second time without the flag.
- The owner-approval toast could open its dialog after the switch turned off. It now checks whether the feature is still on.

Later changes on this branch:

- `people-error.test.ts` builds its credentialed-URL fixture at runtime (`new URL` with `username`/`password`), so the diff holds no `user:password@` literal for secret scanners. The test still checks that such a URL is stripped from diagnostics.
- `docs/concepts/experimental-features.md`: `clientId` is listed with the settings needed to turn on remote access, not as optional. The account menu offers Turn on remote access only after OpenClaw ID sign-in, which needs `clientId` (ClawSweeper P3).
- People actions reach the Gateway authority from #192335, which decides access; the page grants nothing itself. Invites must be signed by a current owner device (`service.invites.test.ts`: registration is refused over the mailbox or from an unidentified client); `openclawId.people` and the authority actions refuse viewers, operators, LAN clients and expired owner devices (`people-access.test.ts`).
- Rebased onto #192345 and `main` at `258d034391a`. `main` dropped per-row Documentation links from Labs (#191418), so the OpenClaw ID Labs row no longer has one and the off-state e2e no longer expects it.

- Rebased onto `main` at `49f8a60f227`. `main` now requires an explicit toast `severity` (#192453), so the OpenClaw ID toasts set one: errors are `error`, sign-in and link copy are `success`, the reachability offer and approval notice are `info`, and partial sign-out is `warning`. Labs labels follow `main`'s renames.
- The raw config editor's schema filter is now a named helper, `omitEditorOwnedConfigLeaves`, so `config/view.tsx` stays within the 700-line cap.


## Evidence

- `pnpm test` over the 34 test files this PR adds or changes (UI unit, browser and e2e suites, the People plugin, and the Gateway Control UI bootstrap, document and plugin-asset tests): 37 files, 316 tests passed (with `management-service.test.ts`).
- **Labs switch off:** `openclaw-id-off.e2e.test.ts` drives the built Control UI in Chromium with the switch absent and with it `false`. Across the shell, Pages, the account menu, Settings, Labs and the command palette it finds no OpenClaw ID copy or elements, loads no OpenClaw ID, recovery-kit or 1Password assets, and sends no config writes or chat requests; an unsent draft survives; `control-ui-plugin-assets.test.ts` checks that the plugin catalog, grants and asset routes disappear at once when the switch turns off; the bootstrap tests check the document attribute is absent.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` passed. `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` passed after regenerating the raw-copy baseline (two recovery-kit strings). `pnpm check:changed`: see the comment below for the run on the published head.
- Test-line ratchet: `config/test-lines-allocations/openclaw-id-ui-people.txt` allocates exactly the 3,470 test lines this PR adds (new tests for new surface).
- Staging: the lab Gateways serve this Control UI (openclaw `1bc84010c2e`). The gates recorded in #191469 used it: an owner enrolled browser A with the recovery kit, approved browser B from A over SAS, and removed A from Your devices, whose confirmation named B as removed with it.

Screenshots: not attached to this draft. The UI is new and appears only with the Labs switch on; screenshots will be added before it is marked ready.
