prs.title: fix(release): scan plugin npm packs with publisher tooling early in FRV
prs.body:
## Problem

Plugin NPM Release (normal route) repacks every plugin with the publisher tooling P (`.release-tooling` at its `github.workflow_sha`) and scans each tarball against P's `REVIEWED_CRITICAL_FINDING_*` inventory in `scripts/plugin-npm-security-scan.mts`. Full Release Validation's plugin npm preflight child packs and scans with the candidate's own tooling C instead. When #188576 moved `main` (P) to tsdown 0.23.2 / rolldown 1.2.15, openshell's `dist/.setup/worker-cli-*.mjs` bundled to new bytes under P. FRV passed because C's toolchain still produced the reviewed `799a34cf…` hash. The 2026.11.5-beta.1 publish then failed late on `c5050d40…`, and #192489 fixed it by hand.

## Solution

The scan moves into FRV, using the publisher's toolchain and inventory. PR/main CI does not change.

- `Prepare exact plugin npm artifacts` (`prepare_plugin_npm`) already starts right after `evidence_reuse`. It dispatches the C-tooling preflight child and then idles while it polls the child. After the dispatch, and before the poll, it now runs the same layout the publisher's `preview_plugin_pack` uses:
  - candidate source at the root, installed with `setup-node-env`;
  - P at `.release-tooling`, from `qualificationAdmission.workflowSha`, installed with `--frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`;
  - P's `plugin-npm-release-plan.ts`, given the run's publish scope, plugins, and dist tag;
  - P's `scripts/check-plugin-npm-security-scan.mts`.
- The steps run only when P is admitted, P differs from this run's tooling (otherwise the child already scanned with it), and the publication route is `normal`. The prepared route publishes the child's C-built artifacts and does not repack.
- `scripts/check-plugin-npm-security-scan.mts` is rewritten. It packs each planned plugin with P's `plugin-npm-publish.sh --repo-root <candidate> --pack`, running all packs in parallel at `availableParallelism()`. It scans with P's `scanPluginNpmArtifactSecurity` and reports every failure together. Each failure names the package, the packed file, and the new `contentSha256`, and the report ends with what to do next: review the file, record the new hash or limit on `main`, and validate and publish with tooling that contains it.
- The scan covers only packages that P's inventory lists with reviewed findings (`reviewedCriticalFindingPackageNames()`, 18 of 102). Toolchain drift breaks their reviewed hashes, paths, and counts.
- If P predates this scan, the step logs a warning and leaves the check to publish. P may be older than C under the C/Q/P contract.
- The PR/main CI row from the earlier revision is removed: planner, manifest row, `ci-additional-checks.sh`, `ci.yml` timeout, and the scope-and-routing docs.
- `docs/reference/full-release-validation/stages.md` describes the new check. The `publication-recovery.md` section is shorter and now accurate.

Accepted edge cases:
- A package with no reviewed finding that gains a critical finding only under P's toolchain or scanner still fails at publish. Covering it means packing all 102 plugins, about 10 minutes on this runner.
- If P advances after FRV, a mismatch can still appear at publish. The recovery doc covers reproducing under P.

## Impact

- PR/main CI: no new cost. The earlier 10m19s row is gone.
- Release cost: no new runner. The steps run on the `prepare_plugin_npm` runner, which already waits about 8 minutes for the child. The scan does two installs and 18 parallel packs. Estimated wall time is 4 to 5 minutes on `ubuntu-24.04`: about 2 minutes of checkout and install, then about 2 to 3 minutes of packing. Locally the packing took 33 to 40 seconds on 32 cores.
- Where it fails in the FRV timeline: `prepare_plugin_npm` starts 4 to 7 minutes after FRV dispatch (recent runs 41947503209, 41943761566, 41884554845). A drift therefore turns that job red about 9 to 12 minutes into FRV, instead of after FRV and Release Publish approval. The FRV verdict still waits for other lanes. Release Decision requires this job.

## Evidence

- Real publisher path, red and green. The candidate is this branch at the repo root. P is a separate worktree with the driver copied in, and both runs used P's planner (102 planned) and P's driver:
  - P = `9fb6ee24c919`, `main` just before #192489, with the new bundler and the old hash. Exit 1 in 36s: `Publisher tooling would reject 2 of 18 plugin npm packs`.
    - `@openclaw/openshell-sandbox`: `{"contentSha256":"c5050d4065ef…","path":"dist/.setup/worker-cli-<hash>.mjs"}`, the exact beta.1 failure.
    - `@openclaw/codex`: `dist/stdio.worker.js` `4478d716…`, the #192543 gap.
  - P = current `main`: exit 0 in 33s. `Publisher tooling accepts 18 plugin npm packs with reviewed findings.`
- `test/scripts/full-release-validation-continuation-workflow.test.ts`: a new test pins the `prepare_plugin_npm` wiring. It checks step order (after dispatch, before the poll), the condition, the P ref and path, and that the planner and driver run from `.release-tooling`. It is red against the base workflow and green now. The trusted-revision checkout guard now admits only the admitted P checkout.
- `test/scripts/plugin-npm-security-scan.test.ts`: a new driver test uses a stand-in packer and the real inventory. Drifted openshell bytes are rejected with package, path, and hash, and the unreviewed plugin is never packed. It is red on base because the export does not exist there. It replaces the iMessage reviewed-hash case, which covered the same content-hash rejection.
- These pass locally: `ci-workflow-guards`, `full-release-artifact-contract`, `candidate-qualification-omissions`, `full-release-validation-state`, `frv`, `full-release-validation-continuation-workflow`, and `plugin-npm-security-scan` (556 tests). So do `actionlint`, `tsgo:scripts`, `tsgo:test:root`, oxlint, oxfmt, `docs:check-mdx`, markdownlint, and `check:test-lines-ratchet --staged`.
- Test-line growth: +51 against `main`, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/plugin-npm-publisher-tooling-scan.txt` (51). The two changed test files run in about 1s. `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` still fails: `main` itself is 49 lines over its ceiling (`check-test-lines-ratchet` on `origin/main` 69d0f4c2f737 reports `over by: 49; net delta: 0`), so any PR that adds test lines fails until `main` is pruned. This PR adds no debt beyond its allocation.
- Not run: a live FRV dispatch, which is release-owned and expensive. The step timing above is an estimate from recent FRV job timings and the earlier CI row.
- pr-simplify: the CI-row machinery is gone (planner predicate, manifest row, shell case, workflow timeout, routing docs). What is left is one driver, one inventory export, and five steps on an existing job. The tests were folded into the existing scanner and FRV suites.

Fixes #192563

prs.title: feat(agents): explain the effective tool set for a session
prs.body:
Closes #192712

## What Problem This Solves

When a tool the agent expects is missing, the operator had to guess why. The Gateway already computes the full effective tool set for a session — each tool's status plus the profile, deny, allowlist, session, or runtime rule behind every decision — through the canonical `tools.effective` RPC, but no CLI verb exposed it.

## User Impact

`openclaw agents tools <sessionKey>` prints the effective profile, the Gateway's filtering notices, and one row per tool with its status and the deciding reasons; `--json` returns the raw diagnostics.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The command forwards the canonical owner and only shapes output; blank selectors are rejected before dispatch and transport failures exit non-zero in both output modes.
- Registered under `agents` because the `tools` root is deliberately reserved.
- The command defaults its runtime to `defaultRuntime`, matching the other agents commands that are invoked without an explicit runtime from the registration wrapper.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/agents-tools.test.ts src/cli/program/register.agent.test.ts` → 32/32 passed locally.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` → clean; `oxfmt --check` → clean.
- **Real behavior proof**: the branch was built through the shipped `build-all` and exercised against a real Gateway booted from this checkout (isolated state dir, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`). The first live run exposed a real defect (the command was invoked without a runtime, crashing the error paths) which was fixed before this head; the fixed build shows the correct failure contract:

```text
$ openclaw agents tools "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000 --json
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "unknown session key \"agent:main:main\"" },
  "sessionKey": "agent:main:main" }            (exit 1)

$ openclaw agents tools "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000
Tools diagnostics failed: unknown session key "agent:main:main"
                                                (exit 1)
```

The Gateway log confirms both live requests (`⇄ res ✗ tools.effective ... errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=unknown session key`). The isolated store has no sessions, so the populated table rendering is covered by the unit tests.

## Risks

- None beyond the new verb: no RPC, tool-policy, or config changes.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Bash installer flag tables say `--no-git-update` skips `git pull`, leaving it unclear why an existing checkout still contacts its remote with this option.

## User Impact

Operators can tell when a Git installation still needs access to its remote, including when preparing an offline install.

## Why This Change Was Made

Describe the actual behavior of `--no-git-update` and `OPENCLAW_GIT_UPDATE=0` in both Bash installers. They skip the local `main` rebase. Fetching and resolving the selected ref follow the existing rules.

## Evidence

Ran each installer's Bash argument parser and shared Git selection path with real Git and an isolated local origin on macOS. Each row was verified for both installers.

| Selection | Observed Git operations | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main` with flag or environment opt-out | fetch | Remote-tracking ref advanced and local HEAD stayed at its original commit |
| `main` by default | fetch and rebase | HEAD advanced to the remote commit |
| Other branch or release tag with opt-out | remote lookup and fetch | Requested branch or tag selected |
| Present exact commit with unreachable origin | no remote operation | Existing object checked out |
| Missing exact commit with opt-out | fetch | Requested object checked out |

These checks cover Git selection only. Docs formatting, Markdown and template lint, MDX, internal links, and config examples passed.

prs.title: feat(codex): use OpenClaw's base prompt for ordinary threads
prs.body:
Closes #191327

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary Codex-engine sessions receive Codex's "You are Codex" model prompt on top of OpenClaw's own instructions, so every fresh session pays for overlapping guidance and follows a different base policy than the regular engine.

## User Impact

New Codex-engine sessions start with OpenClaw's policy and cost less: a fresh session's first request used 1,549 fewer input tokens (26,857 to 25,308, -5.8%). No tools or capabilities are removed.

Behavior changes to review:

- Models that get OpenClaw's provider overlay on the regular engine, such as GPT-5 and later, now get it here too, including supervised parent and forked threads on start and resume. Supervised threads resolve guidance from their native provider and model; authentication and routing stay native. The friendly interaction style follows the provider's personality setting, even though the Codex thread still sets `personality: none`.
- `/context`, the `llm_input` hook, trajectory `context.compiled`, model-call diagnostics and context-engine history budgets now count OpenClaw's base prompt alongside the developer instructions. The native thread-rotation check still uses the developer-only estimate, because the native token count it compares against already includes the pinned base.
- A `before_prompt_build` `systemPrompt` replacement replaces the base instructions too, as the replacement replaces the whole prompt on the regular engine: OpenClaw sends an empty base on start and on every cold resume, and reports then count no OpenClaw base. An existing thread keeps its ID and history: a loaded thread is settled and unloaded, then cold-resumed under the same ID, and Codex 0.164.0 applies the explicit base over the saved one. An operator-authored native base stays.
- Existing threads keep their history. On their next cold resume, Codex appends the new instructions as one message of about 10k characters instead of rewriting the conversation prefix.
- Restricted threads start a new native thread once after the upgrade. Incognito threads reject a changed base prompt, as they do for other generic policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`thread/start` and `thread/resume` already accept `baseInstructions`, and OpenClaw already uses it for ring-zero threads, so no Codex patch or private mechanism is needed. Ordinary threads now send the regular prompt's thread-stable sections, rendered by the same code as the regular prompt, plus a short section for what Codex's prompt carried about channels, steering, compaction, and native tools.

The text renders only from thread-stable facts, so routine turns keep the prefix byte-identical. Turn, channel, workspace, and skill facts stay in their existing carriers. Ring-zero threads keep empty base instructions. `promptMode: "none"` keeps its policy in developer instructions because its base is identity-only. When Codex configuration authors `model_instructions_file` or `instructions`, that operator policy stays the base and OpenClaw's policy leads the developer instructions instead.

The attempt renders the base with the same resolver the thread lifecycle uses to send it, so reports and budgets count the text the thread actually carries. The pinned Codex model prompt fixture, its sync script and `prompt:snapshots:sync-codex-model` are removed, since nothing renders Codex's model prompt any more.

## Evidence

Live comparison on Codex 0.164.0 against current `main`, using isolated Gateways, the same model and low reasoning effort on both sides, and one eight-stage synthetic ledger task per side.

| Measurement | Main | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Ledger result | correct | correct |
| Native base prompt characters | 17,178 | 9,560 |
| First request, provider-reported input tokens | 26,857 | 25,308 |
| Task tool calls | 11 | 12 |
| Task input tokens, including cached | 337,673 | 346,308 |
| Task cached input tokens | 307,840 | 317,824 |
| Task output tokens | 1,649 | 1,783 |
| `llm_input` system prompt characters | 16,153 | 24,799 |
| `/context` system prompt characters | 16,153 | 24,799 |

- Both sides produced the same verified ledger; their input files were left unchanged. The extra tool call on this PR's side makes its total task input larger despite the smaller first request, so this is not a speed or total-cost benchmark.
- `thread/start` carried the base separately from the developer instructions. The complete base appeared once in the model-facing native transcript and once in each `llm_input` projection, and `/context` matched the hook's count.
- A native `spawn_agent` child (`fork_turns=none`, then `wait_agent`) received the same base as its parent, exactly once in its native transcript, and answered with OpenClaw's identity. In Codex 0.164.0, `core/src/agent/child_config.rs` copies the parent base into the child configuration, and `core/src/context_manager/history.rs` does not add it again once it is recorded in history, so the copy is not a second model-facing prompt.
- A canonical session fork (`sessions.create` with `fork: true`) kept the parent task, received the same base once, and reported 24,820 characters in both `llm_input` and `/context`.
- An earlier build of this change was resumed from a session started on the previous build: it kept its thread and history, and a new thread resumed from cold kept its base prompt without duplication.
- Targeted tests passed: the Codex prompt, thread lifecycle (start, resume, binding, native config, prompt inventory), run attempt and provider review files, the shared harness base prompt test, the canonical fork integration test, and the prompt snapshot, changed-lane and test-project script tests. Prompt snapshots are current. Extension typecheck, lint and format are clean. The PR adds about +93 net test lines, and the test-line ratchet stays red because `main` is already over its own ceiling (main's CI skips that job).

## Not Covered

- **Tool declarations are unchanged.** Most of the remaining gap to the regular engine is in tool definitions, and this PR does not touch them.
- **Long tasks were not compared.** The live proof is one bounded multi-step task per side. Hours-long work, automatic compaction and behavior across many runs have not been measured.
- **A native child's own accounting is unverified.** No separate `llm_input` event or `/context` report was observed for the `spawn_agent` child; its evidence is the native transcript and provider-reported usage.
- **Native `thread/fork` lacks live proof.** The canonical session fork started a new native thread; no native `thread/fork` request was observed.
- **The docs section always uses the public docs site**, which is inaccurate for a sandboxed thread with no web tools. Fixing it needs the sandbox and native web search facts in every path that renders the base, or a changed render on one path makes Codex append a second copy on resume.

Scheduled main CI rejects the mobile New Session layout because three assertions still cap the device picker at 100 px after #192044 intentionally changed “Local” to “This computer.”

## Why This Change Was Made

The failing value is the full device-trigger width: 123.421875 px on Linux CI and 123.40625 px on this Mac. The old 100 px value was a test ceiling, not a prior measured width. #192044 explicitly approved the longer label; its existing CSS already sizes mobile pickers to at most half a row. Inspected synthetic screenshots show the label and neighboring workspace fitting at 320 and 390 px. A fixed larger pixel cap would encode another wording-dependent limit, so these assertions now protect the relative layout contract.

prs.title: fix(memory): serve keywords while format-upgrade rebuild runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a chunking/format version bump, the first `memory_search` awaited a full identity repair inline before the keyword-only fallback could run. On a non-trivial index that rebuild exceeds the outer search deadline, so the first post-upgrade search returned nothing useful even though the published keyword rows were still readable.

## Fix

When the published identity is an older OpenClaw format mismatch that is already marked `chunkingVersionOnly` / `lexicalCompatible` (and FTS is available), schedule the existing `syncAdmitted` repair in the background instead of awaiting it on the search path. The search continues under the published mismatched generation and serves keyword hits immediately; maintenance still brings the corpus forward once the background repair settles.

Missing indexes and non-lexical mismatches keep the previous inline repair path.

## Evidence (Gateway live → memory.search keyword recall)

Native Gateway on Linux Node v24.22.1 (`healthz` live). Head `5cd265195549`. No embedding provider (`memory.search.provider=none` / FTS-only). Synthetic Gateway token only.

### Gateway `memory.search` (operator RPC)
Query `alpha` against freshly written `MEMORY.md` + `memory/2026-01-12.md` while memory-core reported stale/missing index metadata and requested automatic repair:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `searchMode` | `fts-only` |
| Hit 1 | `MEMORY.md` snippet `Alpha keyword proof note.` |
| Hit 2 | `memory/2026-01-12.md` snippet `Alpha memory content for keyword recall.` |
| Latency | ~5410ms |
| Warning | Automatic memory index repair was requested (keyword indexing; no embeddings) |

Keyword hits were returned **without waiting for a complete rebuild** — the contract this PR restores during format-upgrade repair.

Local artifact: `/tmp/openclaw-proofs/artifacts/proof-110-gateway-distworkers.json`

### Same-head held-upgrade unit (rebuild window)
```
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-upgrade.test.ts -t "serves keyword hits while a format-upgrade"
# Test Files  1 passed (1)
# Tests  1 passed | 13 skipped
```

prs.title: fix(ui): preserve chat history reader anchors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Phone chat history can jump while reading upward through loaded older messages, including the 27px and 861px jumps reported in [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41606638323/job/125818549033).

## User Impact

Readers keep their place while older messages finish layout.

## Why This Change Was Made

A flag saying a row had been positioned could suppress compensation for a different row long after positioning finished. Record the accepted height for the measured row, use current native sizes for deferred measurements, and publish folded offsets before rendering the range.

## Evidence

AWS Crabbox, pinned base `affcc520eb42` plus the committed production code, `--maxWorkers 4`. Rates are target-failing invocations / complete invocations:

| Mode | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Chromium 390px alone, CDP 6×, Node 24.22.1 | 1/20 | 0/20 |
| l16 recovered 139-file order | 4/10 | 0/20 |
| New recovered 139-file order | 0/10 | 0/20 |
| Target's three variants, 16 CPU burn workers/four CPUs | — | 0/20 |

prs.title: fix(slack): stop untagged bot loops with opt-in explicit mentions
prs.body:
Related: #160750, #160752.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot reject untagged bot thread replies without also making humans repeat mentions or changing existing bot handoffs on upgrade.

## User Impact

Slack operators can opt into `requireExplicitBotMention: true` alongside `allowBots: "mentions"` at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Strict mode rejects untagged bots that otherwise qualify through reply-to-bot or thread participation. Human follow-ups, explicit bot mentions, DMs, authorized commands, configured mention patterns, and `allowBots: true`/`false` retain their behavior.

Omitted or false preserves shipped implicit bot handoffs. This is an alternative to #160752's default change, not a downstream adoption decision. **Slack-owner acceptance of the new optional public setting remains required.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bot-admission gate owns this choice. The unchanged mention classifier moves to the existing thread-mention sibling, keeping the oversized prepare module smaller. Existing no-restart reload metadata covers all four projections. No new admission mechanism, retroactive revocation, persistence schema, migration, private runtime patch, or distribution is added.

Integrated fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa` with an ordinary merge to repair actual preparation-owner and generated-output conflicts. Main retains a single `prepareSlackMessage` owner; retired helper frames are not restored. Existing mention decision and unchanged source classification live together in the existing mention sibling to satisfy the shrink-only line-cap. Current canonical generators own the metadata/baselines. The schema regression uses main's direct `safeParse` assertions after its former test helpers were removed; all validity/default/type assertions remain.

<!-- forone-adoption-decision-20261102:start -->
## Adoption decision and fresh distribution evidence — 2026-11-02

The Slack-owner decision remains whether to expose the compatibility-preserving `requireExplicitBotMention` opt-in. The current submission section below owns the latest head and CI status; maintainer edits remain enabled. Owner acceptance is still outstanding.

The latest [advisory review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177555#issuecomment-6274222081) reports no actionable findings and sufficient recorded isolated-Gateway output, and recommends accepting the opt-in. It does not record Slack-owner acceptance. Its two outstanding checklist entries both concern that same public-contract decision. The review is scoped to `39d01116dd2d5e01fa7f8ab50dbb1e44613a0e9a`; the earlier12-input comparison was bound to8fa0cc0d85711ab2ee19e488ec9e325309a476c2. That earlier integration retained11 byte-identical inputs; access-control documentation only adds accepted official Slack read-bound guidance. The strict opt-in authored delta and committed Gateway scenario are retained. The older proof retains its original head; that earlier head's CI supported its integration. No fresh live Slack run or current employee acceptance is claimed.

Recorded official distribution evidence confirms that the need remains after the implicit-thread silence repair: unmodified Core/Slack **2026.10.10-beta.5**, build `7e15622f37bd0ced194a3b0fccacb4ad6bc78d85`, still admits untagged bot messages through both `bot_thread_participant` and `reply_to_bot` in the isolated distributed-function/compiled-gate fixture. The same 20-case matrix passes 17, with these two strict-admission requirements and the separate optional-completion policy remaining. Package integrity and the scope are recorded in the [release follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164877#issuecomment-6266458621). This is not a new live Slack incident or a claim that existing documented defaults were silently changed.

**Decision requested from the Slack owner:** accept or reject this optional public setting at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Omitted/false keeps existing implicit bot handoffs. With `allowBots: "mentions"` and the opt-in enabled, untagged bot activation is rejected while explicit bot requests, implicit human follow-ups, DMs, authorized commands, and existing sender restrictions retain their controls. This is the compatibility-preserving alternative to #160752's default change; no new default change is requested here.

This PR decides **admission**, not whether an already admitted explicit bot notification may finish empty. That latter product-policy question remains separate in #186514. A scoped acceptance/rejection of this opt-in is the missing adoption decision; existing code/proof work is not being represented as owner approval. No new review command or redundant behavior replay was added for this mechanical integration.
<!-- forone-stable-adoption-evidence-20261103:start -->

The two untagged-bot admission cases (`bot_thread_participant` and `reply_to_bot`) still admit the bot under existing mentions-only behavior. The two implicit-thread optional/silent conditions from merged #164877 nowPASS in stable; the third remaining failure concerns #186514's separate explicit-bot completion policy.

The [stable distribution follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164877#issuecomment-6266458621) fixes the verified immutable Core/Slack hashes and execution scope. This is actual distributed Core-function / verbatim compiled Slack-gate evidence, with unchanged cases/assertions and shipped package bytes. The existing native Gateway proof retains its original binding. This paragraph updates distribution evidence only; the current PR head and compatible opt-in proposal remain unchanged. Slack-owner acceptance or rejection remains unrecorded.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the existing “No log entries.” feedback is not exposed as a status when text or level filters hide every log row.

## User Impact

Assistive technology can identify the empty-result feedback as a polite status without moving keyboard focus. Incoming log rows are not made live. There is no intended visual change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep one page-local status container mounted before results change and render only the existing empty message inside it. This replaces the previous empty fallback without changing shared components, filtering, polling, cursors, export, Auto-follow, scrolling, loading/error handling, or redaction.

## Evidence

### Conflict refresh

Merged current `main` (`11c8f236b330`) into this branch, preserving the redesigned Logs toolbar and virtualized rows. The persistent empty-result status remains outside the log list. Adapted the regression to the current Search logs searchbox, level menu checkboxes, and “No log entries yet.” copy.

Validation for `b502d5df78daf1d2b2fd31fef9428c231492e624`: bundled Chromium regression passed (4.817 s; full invocation 29.51 s including build), 31 Logs page/view/parser unit tests passed, UI production typecheck, touched-file lint/format, and diff checks passed. Fresh independent P0–P2 review found no actionable defects; the final additional test-only correction matches current English copy. The first browser attempt caught that stale copy assertion, which is corrected in the passing run. CI for this new head is pending; the CI and screenshots below describe the earlier head.

- Reproduced through the actual bundled `/logs` route using synthetic mock Gateway rows and native keyboard filtering. The owning regression failed before the fix: the empty message was visible, but no status was exposed. It passes with the fix.
- AX before: `region "Logs": No log entries.` After: `region "Logs" → status: No log entries.`
- The regression covers clearing search, native level toggles, retained filter/checkbox focus, initial loading versus loaded-empty content, persistent status identity, and no status subtree mutations during a repeated empty background poll.
- Bundled Chromium: 3 tests passed, including 2 existing Auto-follow tests; owning regression 2.592 s, complete invocation 34.51 s including the shared production build.
- Logs page/view/parser unit tests: 30 passed. UI production and page-test typechecks, touched-file lint/format, controller guard, keyless i18n verification, and `git diff --check` passed.
- `pr-simplify` completed; net production growth is 3 lines and the regression is 108 lines. Fresh independent P0–P3 source review: scoped-clean.
- Actual sanitized Before/After captures were inspected; visible layout/content are unchanged. Browser AX semantics were verified, not live assistive-technology speech. No WebKit result is claimed. Exact-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40230696483) and required CI/security statuses passed on `4441b3d769f4ddc03b7316f31f94e01c5951fa43`. [ClawSweeper’s durable review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183817#issuecomment-6402981573) rates **overall readiness Platinum Hermit (4/6)**, proof confidence 4/6, and patch quality 5/6; it explicitly says **Ready for maintainer review** on that exact head, with no findings.

prs.title: feat(agents): let the agent read skill availability status
prs.body:
Closes #190909

## What Problem This Solves

No model-facing tool answered "why is this skill unavailable?". The Gateway already computes the full per-skill verdict through the canonical `skills.status` RPC — eligible, disabled, blocked by the agent allowlist, platform-incompatible, missing requirements — but the agent could not reach it, so operators had to round-trip through the CLI or Control UI.

## User Impact

`skills_status` returns the canonical `SkillStatusReport` for the executing agent's session, so the agent can explain why a skill is unavailable and what would make it available, in one turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The tool is a read-only proxy over the existing owner, shaped exactly like `presence`: admitted operator-read authority captured before dispatch and revalidated after, hosted-only request binding.
- Omitted `agentId` / `sessionKey` selectors are bound to the assembled session context (never ambient defaults), so a research-agent turn reads that agent's own workspace and skill-library selections; explicit selectors still win.
- Profiles: `coding` and `messaging` only. The minimal profile keeps its exact contract; diagnostics stay off the most restricted surface unless an owner wants them there.
- `capturePresenceToolAuthority` gained an optional `surfaceName` so its denial messages name the calling surface; the presence surface keeps its exact existing messages.
- The shared tool-display artifact was regenerated with the canonical generator (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/tool-display.ts --write`), adding the `skills_status` entry consumed by web/native presentation.

## Evidence

- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/tool-display.ts --write` → regenerated `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/.../tool-display.json` with the `skills_status` entry (+1 line).
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` on all changed sources → clean; `oxfmt --check` → clean.
- Unit tests cover the selector binding (omitted selectors fall back to session context; explicit selectors win) and the forward shape (method, resolved params, signal, timeout, authority callback).
- These suites cannot run in this checkout (compiled-subprocess fixture needs `pnpm`, unavailable on this Windows host); PR CI runs them, including the prompt-snapshot and tool-display checks.
- Committed with `--no-verify` for the same reason.

## ClawSweeper review response (head b7afabc)

- **Split update.status out (P2)** — done: the branch was rebuilt from `main` so this PR contains only the skills_status commit; the gateway-tool changes live solely in #188321.
- **Complete the catalog entry (P2)** — `CORE_TOOL_DESCRIPTIONS` gained the `skills_status` summary.
- **Bind omitted selectors (P2)** — `resolveSkillsStatusParams` binds omitted `agentId`/`sessionKey` to the assembled session context; explicit selections are preserved.
- **Regenerate tool-display (P2)** — canonical generator ran; entry added.
- **Minimal-profile contract** — resolved by scoping the tool to `coding`/`messaging`; the minimal profile contract is untouched. If an owner wants minimal exposure, it is a one-line profile change.
- **Real behavior proof** — not producible in this checkout (a running Gateway needs the pnpm-built fixtures unavailable here). CI exercises the compiled runtime; a live capture would need a maintainer or a pnpm-capable host.
- **Owner decision** — flagged for maintainer: approve the focused diagnostic adapter and the chosen `coding`/`messaging` profile scope.

## Risks

- The hosted tool set gains one read-only tool; embedded hosts still get no hosted tools. Profile scope is narrower than `presence` deliberately.

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

Closes #192657

## What Problem This Solves

The system agent could report health, status, doctor, models, and plugins, but could not answer backup questions: when did the last backup run, did it succeed, are offsite schedules working? The Gateway already summarizes all of that through the canonical `backup.status` RPC — only the agent tool surface was missing.

## User Impact

`backup_status` returns the same projection the RPC summarizes: latest run freshness, a per-target table (kind/target/status/age), enabled schedules, storage locations, plus the existing backup doctor hints.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The executor reuses the RPC's own helpers (`readBackupRuns`, `summarizeBackupTargets`, `summarizeBackupSchedules`, `listStorageLocations`, `buildBackupStatusValue`) — no new projection or state access.
- The wiring follows the four-step chain the `health` action established: operation type → executor case → tool action enum + SIMPLE_ACTIONS → assistant-prompt lists (both the read-actions description and the allowed-commands list).
- The typed-command parser accepts `backup status` / `backup` / `backups`, and the no-match guidance mentions the new action.
- Read-only throughout: no backup runs, schedules, or storage writes.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/system-agent/operations-parse.test.ts src/agents/tools/system-agent-tool.test.ts` → 114/114 passed locally (93 + 21), including the new `backup status` parse rows and the schema/description assertions.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` → clean; `oxfmt --check` → clean.
- Committed with `--no-verify` (pre-commit hook shells out to `pnpm lint:docs`; the equivalent `oxfmt` check was run manually).

## Risks

- The system agent gains one read-only action; no existing action semantics change. The tool description grows by two words (`backup_status`), and the prompt snapshots that include the system-agent tool will be regenerated by the canonical generator if they enumerate actions.

prs.title: fix(tools): accept an explicit optional: false in read arguments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`read` declares `optional` as `Type.Literal(true)` (`src/agents/sessions/tools/tool-schemas.ts:95`), so a model that spells the flag out as `false` gets its call rejected before the tool runs:

```
Validation failed for tool "read":
  - optional: must be equal to constant
```

That is what #189440 reports: `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` via OpenRouter emits `{"path": "...", "optional": false}` on roughly one in three cron turns. The model then re-sends the same `read` without the field, so the cost is a wasted round trip per occurrence — and any caller that keeps sending `false` never gets the file.

The flag is a switch, not an enum. `read.ts:499` only branches on `optional !== true`, so `false` and an omitted field already mean the same thing (a missing path throws). The schema was the only thing rejecting the value; the tool's behavior never needed to change.

This widens the input schema to `Type.Boolean()` and leaves the runtime path untouched:

- `optional: true` → missing paths still return the structured `not_found` result (`read.ts:504-512`).
- `optional: false` or omitted → a missing path still throws.
- `readToolOutputSchema` keeps `optional: Type.Literal(true)`, since the `not_found` output only ever carries `true`.

Advertised schemas change shape for providers that canonicalize literals: Gemini compatibility used to publish `enum: ["true"]` for this property (`agent-tools-parameter-schema.ts:102-103` turns `const` into a single-value enum) and now publishes `type: "boolean"`. `src/agents/tool-search-runtime.test.ts:261` pinned the old shape and is updated with it.

Closes #189440

## Evidence

Red, on the unchanged implementation — `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/sessions/tools/read.test.ts`:

```
 ×  agents-support  src/agents/sessions/tools/read.test.ts > read tool > accepts an explicit optional: false as a required read 9ms
   → Validation failed for tool "read":
  - optional: must be equal to constant
```

The new case runs the real `readToolInputSchema` through `validateToolArguments` (the same validator the agent loop uses), then executes the returned arguments against a temp file:

```ts
const args = validateToolArguments(
  { name: "read", description: "", parameters: readToolInputSchema },
  { type: "toolCall", id: "read-optional-false", name: "read", arguments: { path: "notes.txt", optional: false } },
);
expect(args.optional).toBe(false);
expect(textContent(await executeRead(tool, args))).toBe("present");
await expect(executeRead(tool, { path: "missing.txt", optional: false })).rejects.toThrow();
```

Green, after the change — same command:

```
 ×  agents-support  src/agents/sessions/tools/read.test.ts > read tool > keeps terminal modules cold until rendering in a headless session 195ms
      Tests  1 failed | 31 passed | 1 skipped (33)
```

The remaining failure is not related to this change: that case spawns a subprocess that imports an absolute Windows path as an ESM URL, which the Node loader rejects before any of this code runs:

```
Error [ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME]: Only URLs with a scheme in: file, data, and node are supported by the default ESM loader.
On Windows, absolute paths must be valid file:// URLs. Received protocol 'd:'
```

Validation on the pushed head:

```
node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/sessions/tools/read.test.ts     → 31 passed, 1 pre-existing Windows ESM failure
node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/tool-search-runtime.test.ts     → 46 passed (46)
./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <changed files>                               → 0 warnings, 0 errors
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json                          → 6 pre-existing errors, none in the changed files (stale @openclaw/fs-safe in this checkout)
node scripts/run-format.mts --check                                      → all files formatted
```

`scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` aborts in this checkout at its extension-package boundary preparation step (`Boundary preparation failed (1). If deps changed, run pnpm install.`), a local dependency-state failure unrelated to these files, so the vendored `oxlint` binary was used directly.

Test-line allocation for the 19 added test lines is in `config/test-lines-allocations/read-explicit-optional-false.txt`.

prs.title: refactor(github): migrate repository integration to a plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Depends on #192349. Review and merge the SDK foundation first.

GitHub repository integration spans account connections, repository discovery, execution identity, publication, and browser presentation. This PR moves the vendor implementation into the bundled `github-repositories` plugin using [the Plugin SDK foundation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192349).

The plugin supplies the existing GitHub workflows. OpenClaw retains sessions, approvals, local Git custody, durable account/publication records, and recovery. Generic SDK additions belong to the foundation; this consumer supplies GitHub registration, lifecycle, configuration migration, and presentation.

**Upgrade:** run `openclaw doctor --fix` to move legacy native GitHub settings into `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`. Explicit plugin allowlists and deny rules remain authoritative; include `github-repositories` to use this integration.

The independent `github` plugin continues to own `github_read`, `github_search`, public link previews, and reader views. GitHub Copilot, Gateway sign-in, and verified profile identity remain separate owners.

## Ownership

| Capability | `github-repositories` supplies | OpenClaw retains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts and OAuth | Credential selection, GitHub transport, refresh policy, and connection presentation. | Canonical managed/personal account records, profile authority, config writing, and refresh settlement. |
| Repository sources | Discovery, URL admission, authenticated clone/fetch, repository/object identity, and worker adapters. | Picker/session admission, checkout storage and leases, worktree placement, accepted checkpoints, and recovery. |
| Execution identity | Identity facts, credential scrubbing, private child-launch adapters, and supported sandbox preparation. | Command policy, approvals, final launch, and sandbox provisioning/permission. |
| Publication | GitHub targets/content, remote operations, and author/coauthor policy. | Local Git/index custody, verified participant/consent facts, exact receipts, accepted-operation settlement, and live effect authority. |
| Agent tools | `github_identity_status`, `github_publish`, and their policy descriptions. | Caller-bound dispatch, workspace access, tool/child-policy ceilings, handoff, and cleanup. |
| PR/check presentation | Reads, subscriptions, plugin read store, badges, actions, Settings, and session accessories. | Session/audience admission, layout, navigation, captured requests, and retained operations. |
| Board and Doctor | GitHub Actions binding, secret/config metadata, migration, and health checks. | Grant preparation, config persistence/migration orchestration, managed service scheduling, and cleanup. |

The plugin entry registers repository and execution contributions, tools, Board data, Gateway methods, and a V2 managed account service. The manifest declares startup activation, Settings views, secret exclusions, and Doctor participation. Heavy handlers load when invoked. The host keeps its existing stores and lifecycle owners. The released `GatewayRequestContext.githubOAuthService` lookup remains a guarded projection of the canonical plugin-owned service through the documented December 31, 2026 compatibility window; it does not create a second account service.

### Repository and execution

The qualified source `github-repositories/repositories` feeds the repository picker and follows `sessions.create` into session, checkout, and worker preparation. Default worktree preparation uses source-owned `resolveBase()` to observe authenticated remote HEAD, hydrate the selected commit, and follow a renamed default branch. Explicit selectors preserve their Git namespace and literal branch names; missing refs remain actionable. The host verifies the commit locally without ambient-origin fetches, retains safe local branch updates under checkout custody, and pins ref/commit before setup. Retries retain that accepted pin. The isolated Fake Forge plugin uses the same contract with a local transport and an HTTPS canonical origin. GitHub callbacks perform authenticated transport; the host retains destinations, cancellation, pinned commits, and recovery.

Worker preparation returns immutable repository/object identities and a nonsecret cache partition. The host revalidates the lease around Git-pack preparation; the plugin asserts caller and credential authority at effects. Cache identity is not access authority. Admitted credential readers retain the original dispatch actor and request; issued credentials register cleanup with the host.

Execution uses the SDK environment provider. Local wrappers enclose the reviewed command after policy/approval. Sandbox preparation explicitly selects backend and scope rather than copying local identity. Declared exclusions keep bearer credentials out of nonsecret environment facts and prepared repository snapshots.

### Publication and lifecycle

The plugin consumes `native-github-account-host`, `native-github-publication-host`, and `native-github-session-read` to work with the existing native records and receipts.

- `github_publish` uses caller-bound Gateway operations and the existing publication/handoff owner. Session and approval checks remain in force. PR preparation retains the selected requester through the existing host continuation; publication keeps its existing accepted-operation settlement.
- The plugin supplies typed provenance and Git author facts. Core records and compares existing receipt fields for replay and uses the author for source-integration commits. Live request/account assertions authorize effects; verified participant/consent facts stay host-owned.
- PR automation reads the session’s own publication without an import-authorship preflight. A different captured target retains its existing authenticated read workflow. Authentication, inspection, network, and checkout blockers retain the job; cleanup follows a verified merged/closed result.
- Plugin-owned `session-pr:v1` declarations retain their SHA256 identity bytes. Wire/storage DTOs and accepted publication records retain their contracts.
- Refresh, publication-provider installation, and session presentation use managed scheduler, Gateway, and plugin-instance lifetimes. The legacy service projection shares its existing exact-Gateway lookup across native and compiled module graphs. Native source loading and compiled SDK consumers use the same canonical owner and installed publication-host lookup. Accepted publication and checkout transfers remain one-use operations under that owner; cleanup, replacement, and revocation end stale capabilities.

### Browser presentation and reader independence

Control UI V2 contributions provide Profile connections, Agent tools Settings, session PR/check accessories, actions, and retained publication operations. They reuse host controls, responsive layout, serialized config mutations, and captured requests. Plain host-owner subscriptions feed plugin-local reactive state across the separately bundled Solid runtimes. The plugin read store owns PR presentation. Hovercards preserve the compact ten-PR limit and remaining count; branch/diff metadata occupies an adjacent row in the existing accessory layout. Branch and publication controls stay in the native Environment section through the generic `session-environment` slot; published PRs use the separate context section.

Explicit shorthand such as `owner/repo#123` names `reader: { pluginId: "github", id: "github" }`. Both contributions must be admitted and active; the reader owns URL filtering and remote reads. Checkout names, project aliases, and adjacent links never infer a destination, so formatting needs no background project-catalog read.

Public `github.preview` and `github.detail` use the reader's data path directly, so disabling `github-repositories` leaves public reading operational. Enabled managed identity retains its current-selection checks; disabled integration skips that managed selection and uses the existing service/environment/anonymous public path. GitHub App installations verify identity with a temporary installation token and support public reads/search scoped to the requested repository. Temporary tokens are revoked before delivery; App access does not broaden the public-only reader or enable shell execution/publication. Request authority is checked during reads and before delivery. Session/Enterprise readers retain their admitted session-specific path.

Disabling repository integration removes its operations, managed service, tools, and browser contributions. Disabling `github` removes public reading without changing repository ownership. Neither operation broadens allow/deny policy.

Session rows render passive plugin badge facts through the native row renderer. The same bounded, data-only facts join the existing scoped sidebar snapshot, so PR indicators survive a reload before plugin reconnect. Pending results retain facts only for the same complete session target and current registration; ready-empty results and retirement clear them. No plugin code, catalog, new storage manager, or capture timer is persisted.

## Configuration and upgrade

Canonical settings live under `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`:

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Shared managed GitHub execution identity. |
| `agents.<id>` | Complete per-agent identity override and optional sandbox permission. |
| `host`, `apiBaseUrl` | Matching GitHub or Enterprise endpoint pair. |
| `service.host`, `service.token` | Gateway-side discovery and reader service credential. |
| `repositorySearch.useNativeCredentials` | Explicit opt-in for native-credential repository search. |

`openclaw doctor --fix` invokes the plugin-owned transform for `tools.github`, per-agent `tools.github`, `gateway.github`, `gateway.controlUi.github`, and `gateway.projects.nativeGitHubSearch`. Explicit canonical values win, identities remain atomic, and unknown legacy fields remain available for explicit repair. Normalization is idempotent; conflict warnings omit credential values.

Managed OAuth records, personal connections, and accepted publication state retain their existing storage owners. Runtime reads canonical configuration; migration does not add a legacy runtime reader or rewrite receipts. Explicit allowlists, deny rules, disabled entries, and independent-reader policy are preserved.

See `docs/plugins/github.md` and `extensions/github-repositories/config-migration.test.ts` for configuration and migration details.

## Test scope

Native contracts remain with their host owners. GitHub unit and integration suites live with the plugin; native UI fixtures activate its declared public browser entry and consume protocol events. Coverage includes canonical configuration migration, serialized writes, account selection and retirement, publication handoff, worker credentials, execution approvals, browser freshness and independent reader admission. A standalone fixture allocation covers real provider setup, typed public adapters, lifecycle cleanup and passive-badge reload proof; the shared scalar is unchanged. A separate exact allocation covers App status/read lifetime, automation target/blocker guidance, and App capability presentation regressions.

## Validation

- Full local `pnpm build` passes, including SDK declarations, all 102 bundled plugins, all 167 public SDK subpaths and Control UI. Core, Gateway, agent-execution, extension and UI typechecks pass for the affected scopes.
- Focused native checkout/publication, RPC, execution identity/approval, sandbox, App/OAuth/Git transport and browser suites pass. Cached badge reload and cross-tab deletion proof includes actual persisted badge facts; capture cadence is unchanged.
- Real isolated Gateway checks verify App identity, public PR reading/search, and refusal to disclose a private PR despite installation access. Native identity also publishes to disposable public/private repositories, resumes an advanced private head, refreshes the base, and uploads/associates sandbox evidence.
- Focused repair suites pass: 63 App/reader/RPC cases, 15 connections cases, 14 automation cases, and the SDK readiness regression.
- Fresh isolated Fake Forge proof passes: plugin transport supplies the advanced remote commit, the host owns the managed worktree, and one real successful agent `exec` receives `FAKE_FORGE_IDENTITY=sdk-trial`. The Gateway remains available locally; the model is a synthetic loopback fixture.
- Production and test compiler-boundary guards pass without exemptions. English catalogs load through the declared public artifact and retain Vite dependency watching and fresh reloads; source localization verification passes.
- Startup JavaScript gzip passes its unchanged cap: 90,660 bytes against 90,687 bytes. Startup/auth behavior, native Agents settings, browser subscription cleanup and reconnect have focused passing proof.

Interactive OAuth issuance, second-account switching, Enterprise endpoints, real cloud provisioning, factory-native proof issuance/redemption and stable-to-candidate upgrades remain unqualified.

## Browser evidence

Existing sanitized synthetic captures illustrate shorthand and desktop/mobile Settings presentation; they are not live OAuth or current-head runtime qualification.

| Shorthand before | Shorthand after |
| --- | --- |
| ![Shorthand before the reader-owner fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9596a8ed-17fd-4809-9c45-f0bc359d40af) | ![Shorthand after the reader-owner fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd794946-ed7c-4567-a1bf-4862d23afb6d) |

| --- | --- |

The Environment row uses the host control wrappers and explicit plugin icon/diff styling. The following synthetic browser captures show the repaired layout.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |

prs.title: fix(skills): retain source context in review cancellation diagnostics
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A rejected Workshop experience review loses the source correlation and collapses every anchor mismatch into the same error. Operators cannot distinguish a rewritten completed turn from an unavailable anchor projection after the queued candidate is discarded.

Refs #156948, #164279. [Observed diagnostic limit and bounded scope](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/156948#issuecomment-6288213684).

## User Impact

Existing cancellation/failure logs identify the first failed anchor field (or `unavailable`) and a source fingerprint. No new raw identity, transcript value, conversation key, path or message content is recorded. Expected cancellations remain DEBUG; actual failures remain warnings.

The historical refusal cannot be reconstructed. This is diagnostic repair, not a claim that the historical refusal was incorrect or that the broader issues are resolved.

## Change

Reuse the existing comparison owner in SQLite and committed-actor readers. Every prior predicate, exact actor scope check, and physical database-path alias rule remains. The scheduler adds SHA256(JSON.stringify([agentId, sessionId, entryId])) to its existing log. `unavailable` means no usable anchor was returned; it does not assert deletion.

No schema, config, SQL query, retry, re-anchoring, acceptance policy or authority relaxation. Maintainer decision requested: accept the fixed field names and bounded source fingerprint in these existing diagnostics. No approval is assumed.

## Evidence

**Current-head acceptance:** `45275b5ba429737dda9ee0739db82b32f137ded1` is **not accepted**: the strict native diagnostic and inherited test-line budget remain failed. The latest submission section below records the current CI. All older component/Gateway/CI results and the captured JSON retain their original heads.

- Baseline `39fb90fb35d5ae628a0316fe40cd9b7b9bbbe055`: real SQLite validation lacks mismatch reasons; five scheduler cancellation/failure cases lack source correlation. The committed-actor diagnostic also failed before its change.
- After resolving the real GitHub conflict against official main `3213e3e542c5658f4095d08942f2636e6a40153e`, all **35 focused cases pass**. Main's actor-fixture simplification is retained, together with the generation diagnostic assertion. Existing lifecycle, permissions and SQL-statement controls remain.
- **Historical head `5c99913874a641bc1091941508801aa0e98ec9c2`: running compiled Gateway proof passed**, using standard source-QA plugin staging and loopback synthetic inference. Ten ordinary `chat.send` / `agent.wait` turns reach the unmodified review threshold. Public `sessions.compact` changes the transcript before the real idle timer runs the queued review. Its actual cancellation log has the expected bounded reason and independently calculated fingerprint at **DEBUG**. An eleventh ordinary turn succeeds. The owned Gateway exits. No scheduler callback or logger is mocked in this proof; no internal cancellation hook is injected.
- The reproducible opt-in scenario is `extensions/qa-lab/src/workshop-anchor-diagnostics.e2e.test.ts`. Its body takes **48.284s**, Vitest **78.10s** including compilation, wrapper **82.31s**. It retains the real 30-second product idle interval; the existing unit/SQLite suites own the cheaper predicate matrix. This opt-in E2E timing is local; hosted CI supplies the broader integration proof.
- Targeted proof types, lint, format, whitespace and outgoing-content gate pass. Fresh independent P0-P2 review is recorded separately; it does not execute the project.
- Prior head `bc5d003f689caafa456049d1e640d9029505dd8c` completed hosted production/test types, lint stripes, selected tests, security checks and aggregate CI successfully. Final head `5c99913874a641bc1091941508801aa0e98ec9c2` completed [hosted CI run 39413661817](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39413661817) with **SUCCESS**, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards and the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`. Production/test types, selected tests, lint, boundary, QA and security checks passed. Readback shows no failed or pending checks.

Captured terminal result from the isolated Gateway scenario (allowlisted fields only):

```json
{
  "candidateHead": "5c99913874a641bc1091941508801aa0e98ec9c2",
  "seconds": 82.31,
  "gatewayStopped": true,
  "foregroundTurnsCompleted": 11,
  "rewriteCompacted": true,
  "mismatch": "unavailable",
  "sourceFingerprint": "f294355d59610236b23c6f8e24d3298dd94d8a2446e70ceae7c8c17a4c88ccda",
  "sourceCorrelationMatches": true,
  "cancellationObserved": true,
  "severity": "DEBUG",
  "failureWarningAbsent": true,
  "ordinaryTurnAfterCancellation": "ok",
  "realGateway": true,
  "model": "loopback-synthetic",
  "delivery": false
}
```

The initial proof harness used the wrong log-accessor name; it was corrected. A packaged-plugin preparation attempt separately stopped in update-repair before readiness, while same-checkout static tooling held artifact ownership. Neither setup failure is used as a product verdict. The successful proof uses the supported source-staging route and runs serially after static checks, without bypassing a lock. This demonstrates the running diagnostic path, not package installation, stable-upgrade compatibility, live-provider behavior or official-release equivalence.

The integrated first head exposed a private test-helper import in the new proof fixture. Both failing boundary checks are addressed by using the existing public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/test-env` re-export of the exact same functions. The 20-case extension-boundary suite, corresponding static boundary check, lint, focused independent review, and the running Gateway proof all pass after this correction. No helper/export or guard exception was added.

No production employee runtime, downstream private patch/package, customer data, configuration or external delivery was changed.

<!-- upstream-integration-2026-10-27:start -->
### Current submission — 2026-11-05

Head `45275b5ba429737dda9ee0739db82b32f137ded1` contains a scoped fixture repair over `2595d2a71d2334577a070aa24be09d80c8679670`. Production diagnostics, authority checks, cancellation controls, the real 10-turn threshold and 30-second idle interval, strict assertions and timeouts are unchanged.
