prs.title: fix(agents): resolve scheduled account policy in the caller registry
prs.body:
Related: #150278, #178677.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled jobs reporting an available named account as unavailable when their channel plugin exists only in the current runtime registry scope.

## User Impact

Scheduled account checks and group tool policy use the current channel implementation. A scoped account removal continues to deny the run even if the process-root implementation still lists that account. No configuration, stored-job or credential migration is added. Legacy jobs without authenticated creator origin still require native reauthorization; this does not repair their missing provenance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing channel registration resolver with `loadedOnly: true` instead of the process-root lookup. This retains loaded-only behavior and the existing account guard without adding a registry, cache or fallback. Distinct native registry owners cover the policy regression, and three additional isolated product cases exercise the scheduler through actual message execution and cancellation.

## Evidence

The existing policy suite has 17 passing tests: the two registry regressions fail on base `925d43df5722e6f3aa2abdce4912042b2753f3eb` while the 15 existing tests pass. Those policy tests remain unchanged in this follow-up.

The added product suite passes all three cases through the real Gateway, admitted local automation creation, scheduler, embedded agent and Discord message-action path:

- With the account available in both the prepared scoped registry and the Gateway registry, the scheduled tool reads the expected synthetic message through metadata and `/messages` GETs.
- With the scoped Discord registration retained but its account roster missing `work`, while root still lists it, the scheduler rejects before any model or provider request.
- Holding the metadata GET response, disabling the active job through native `cron.update`, then releasing the response ends the occurrence as disabled by operator. No `/messages` request is sent.

The test hooks select the prepared runtime registry and supply account rosters; this does not validate production prepared-registry acquisition itself. The model HTTP endpoint and Discord HTTP responses are also synthetic. Policy decisions, registration custody/read authority, occurrence admission, agent execution and dispatch are native. The local creator is a harness-admitted principal, not a live human channel session. Discord credential-only reads delegate to the Gateway, so successful execution also requires the account in the Gateway owner. These cases do not claim that a scoped-only account bypasses that second owner.

This is provider read-effect evidence, not live Discord, send/write, notification, production-deployment or hosted-CI proof. The earlier isolated published-2026.10.7 policy/cron probes remain separate pre-execution evidence and are not substituted for these source product tests. Normal current-head maintainer/security review is still required before landing.

Validation of this follow-up on commit `0ced7be2a363c7ed259929f43146d594e1fa10f1`:

- Native Gateway product suite: 3/3 passed; the wrapper and final source verification completed successfully.
- Native formatting, typed lint for both added files, and the gateway-server TypeScript project check passed.
- Independent local canonical review of the full candidate against `925d43df5722e6f3aa2abdce4912042b2753f3eb` completed through P2 with no actionable findings; its final source verification passed. This was a static review, separate from the executed tests above.


## Recorded runtime output

The [three recorded scenario traces and complete redacted terminal log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184164#issuecomment-6413402588) show the authorized metadata/message GETs, the scoped-account rejection with zero recorded model/provider requests, and active disablement before the message-list request. The attachment preserves observed event order and native completion fields, separately labels assertion explanations, and binds the original artifact hashes and five source-file hashes to this published content.

This is the existing execution of the frozen staged candidate subsequently committed unchanged as `0ced7be2a363c7ed259929f43146d594e1fa10f1`, not a post-commit rerun. Synthetic endpoints, identities, credentials and private local paths are redacted. The original retained-namespace warning is included; the log is not presented as a blanket descendant-cleanup guarantee. Maintainer security authorization is still required before landing.


## CI repair follow-up

The incremental test-only correction is committed as `46cbc61b97ef5669fa71c6a4f197c7ab6ef7805b`, directly on the previously published head above.

- Use the existing cancellation-aware `withinTest` / `awaitGateBeforeSettlement` helpers and Vitest's native `it.for` test signal, retaining the existing assertions and 300-second case timeout.
- Preserve the original `node-exec-availability` exports in the partial mock.
- Remove exactly one obsolete mock-baseline tuple identified by the ratchet; no baseline allowance is added.
- Re-executed all three product cases under the repository's supported `CI=1` mode with an isolated Node 24.22.1 toolchain: **3/3 passed**, including scoped-account removal and active revocation. Endpoint/principal limitations above still apply.
- Timeout-race ratchet passed. The mock-export ratchet passed with 6,882 grandfathered factories against exact published head `0ced7be2a363c7ed259929f43146d594e1fa10f1` (`--no-merge-base`). This is validation of the incremental repair, not a current-main merge or hosted-CI result.

Independent read-only P0–P3 review of this exact incremental commit found no actionable defects; it did not rerun tests or grant security-policy approval.

Production code is unchanged by this follow-up. Current-head maintainer/security authorization is still required before landing.

## Test-line allocation and current CI limits

The native scheduled-account acceptance adds 577 test/support lines in total. The current trusted CI checker supports per-change allocations under `config/test-lines-allocations`; this PR requests exactly 577 lines there. The global baseline and checker remain unchanged. This allocation retains the real Gateway/SQLite success, scoped-account removal and active-revocation cases rather than replacing the owning runtime with mocks. The three product cases passed on the previously published test revision; their code and assertions are unchanged by the allocation.

The latest run of that published revision passed the mock-export and timeout-race ratchets but failed the separate test-line ceiling (556 over the merged-tree ceiling, net +577). The allocation addresses that accounting failure only. A separate Darwin tooling workflow checked out this older PR branch and requested `test/scripts/pr-dependency-cache.test.ts`, which does not exist on that branch. That workflow failure and the required maintainer/security approval are not reported as green.

## Additional current-stable policy-owner probe — 2026-11-05

Executed the real published OpenClaw **2026.10.10** group-policy function with native registry scopes, without starting jobs or sending channel traffic. The baseline rejects an account available only in the scoped channel, accepts a root account removed from the scoped channel, and returns the root policy instead of the scoped policy. Substituting the exact two-line resolver change fixes all three scenarios: the scoped account is accepted, the removed account is rejected, and the scoped `deny: [exec]` policy is returned.

The candidate probe uses a process-local module load hook; the installed package remains unchanged. An initial strict assertion incorrectly treated an explicit `allow: undefined` property as a policy difference; assertions were corrected to check both policy fields, and both baseline and candidate runs then completed. This is policy-owner execution with synthetic channel registrations, not a repeat of the product Gateway suite or a live scheduled-channel acceptance.

Hosted status remains separate: Darwin is still failed at **Test dependency cache lifetime**, ci-gate still reports failure, and security-sensitive review is pending. The current job metadata confirms the failed step; the CLI returned no retained log lines for that job in this check, so that absence is not evidence of a passing run. No hosted green, production deployment, or maintainer authorization is claimed.

prs.title: fix(android): match Control UI page scheme to the gateway socket
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A discovered gateway on a non-loopback address opens a TLS socket even when its Bonjour record omits `gatewayTls`. The Android Control UI page did not use that decision. It chose `http` or `https` only from `endpoint.tlsEnabled`, so the page stayed on cleartext while the socket was TLS.

The Terminal, dashboard, and desktop screens load that page after the operator session connects. The page origin is where the signing bridge answers a challenge. A cleartext page is the wrong origin for a connection the socket policy already refused to leave on cleartext.

Manual LAN cleartext is unchanged. A stored pin still does not upgrade that page to HTTPS, matching the socket. A manual remote host whose cleartext toggle is off stays on HTTPS, also matching the socket.

## Evidence

API 34 emulator, play debug build, head `8f4143070ae`. The production `ControlUiWebView` loaded a page on the emulator's private LAN address `10.0.2.15`. The discovered endpoint had `tlsEnabled` false and no advertised fingerprint. The manual endpoint used the cleartext toggle.

```console
$ adb -s emulator-5554 shell am instrument -w -r -e class ai.openclaw.app.ui.ControlUiSchemeDeviceTest ai.openclaw.app.debug.test/androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner
OK (2 tests)

url=https://10.0.2.15:36997
page=https://10.0.2.15:36997/ wss://10.0.2.15:36997 NATIVE_AUTH

url=http://10.0.2.15:34079
page=http://10.0.2.15:34079/ ws://10.0.2.15:34079 NATIVE_AUTH
```

![Discovered LAN page loaded over HTTPS and installed native auth](https://github.com/SebTardif/openclaw/raw/8f4143070ae6055df10f80e3928f0451d0d38978/apps/android/app/src/androidTest/proof/https-discovered.png)

![Manual LAN cleartext page stayed on HTTP](https://github.com/SebTardif/openclaw/raw/8f4143070ae6055df10f80e3928f0451d0d38978/apps/android/app/src/androidTest/proof/http-manual-lan.png)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** The Control UI WebView origin follows the socket. A discovered private-LAN host with no gatewayTls advertisement loads HTTPS, and the native auth bridge publishes a wss gateway URL. Manual private-LAN cleartext stays HTTP and publishes a ws URL.
- **Real environment tested:** Android emulator API 34 google_apis arm64, play debug app `ai.openclaw.app.debug`, head `8f4143070ae`. The page host is the emulator guest address 10.0.2.15.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Installed the play debug apk and ran `adb -s emulator-5554 shell am instrument -w -r -e class ai.openclaw.app.ui.ControlUiSchemeDeviceTest ai.openclaw.app.debug.test/androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner`.
- **Evidence after fix:** The WebView document and the screenshots above. Discovered LAN showed `https://10.0.2.15:36997/` plus `wss://10.0.2.15:36997` and `NATIVE_AUTH`. Manual LAN showed `http://10.0.2.15:34079/` plus `ws://10.0.2.15:34079` and `NATIVE_AUTH`.
- **Observed result after fix:** The production WebView loaded the HTTPS page for the discovered case and the HTTP page for manual cleartext. Both documents received the native auth payload for that origin.
- **What was not tested:** A physical phone. This was not a full OpenClaw gateway login. The page is a local document served to the production WebView so the loaded scheme and the installed auth bridge are visible.

## Summary

The page URL is built from the same TLS decision as the gateway socket. No changelog entry.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): exec completions keep the requester's current sender and DM tool policy
prs.body:
Closes #177510

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a background command's completion turn loses `exec` and `process` when the sender who started it is allowed only by their own `toolsBySender` entry and the `"*"` entry denies those tools.

## User Impact

User impact: with a `toolsBySender` wildcard deny, a sender allowed by their own entry can let a background command finish its task on the completion turn, without sending another message. Guests stay denied, and changing that sender's entry, or denying the tool for the conversation they wrote in (a Telegram DM entry under `channels.telegram.direct.<chat>`, including `toolsBySender` keyed on their id, username or name, or a Discord guild or channel entry under `channels.discord.guilds.<guild>`), before the completion runs takes the tool away.

## Why This Change Was Made

A completion turn is built without a sender, so requester policy fell to the `"*"` entry. #185476 restored the sender only for command owners (`commands.ownerAllowFrom`); a sender allowed only through `toolsBySender` was never restored.

My first revisions restored too little. Review found four real gaps, all fixed:

- Without the conversation id, `resolveRequesterConversationToolPolicy` skips the channel's `security.resolveDirectToolPolicy`, so an unchanged sender entry escaped a DM-level deny. #185476's owner completions had the same gap.
- Without the sender's username and name, Telegram's `resolveTelegramDirectToolPolicy` missed a DM `toolsBySender` entry keyed `username:` or `name:`, fell back to the DM's unrestricted tools, and the requester's global id entry then allowed exec.
- Without the requester's group space and channel name, a completion in a Discord guild channel resolved group policy with no guild, so `resolveDiscordGuildKey` found no guild entry, a guild or channel deny added after launch was missed, and the requester's global id entry allowed exec.
- `combineSessionEventTargetsForHost` compared only command-owner requesters, so targets from two `toolsBySender`-only requesters could share a batch that restores only the first one.

What the PR does now:

- The session-event target keeps the requester's channel, account, sender id, E164, username, display name, group space (a Discord guild), group channel name, chat type and conversation id, taken from the host-owned tool caller. The group id comes from the completion's own route, which is the requester's conversation.
- The completion turn restores `SenderId`, `SenderE164`, `SenderUsername`, `SenderName`, `GroupSpace`, `GroupChannel` and `ChatId`, but only on the requester's own channel account and only when the turn has the requester's conversation type. A completion routed to another chat stays senderless and gets the `"*"` policy.
- The restore grants nothing by itself: a non-owner's `senderIsOwner` stays `false`, and owner-only effects still recheck at use.
- A batch refuses targets whose retained requester differs in any of those fields.
- Only exec completions and node `system.run` events retain a requester. Subagent announces, cron, heartbeats, session-state notices and adopted durable processes do not, so their authority is unchanged.
- Behavior change for #185476: an owner's sender is restored only when the chat types match; before, a matching channel and account was enough. Where they differ, the owner-effect check now fails closed.

## Evidence

Head `6fbcf9eae1e` (main `586f576` merged in), macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1.

Real Gateway (QA Lab flow `exec-completion-requester-sender-policy`: Gateway child, qa-channel, real `exec` and `config.patch`; only the model is scripted). `node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario exec-completion-requester-sender-policy --concurrency 1 --fast`, run at `58bf6c5`:

- This branch: pass. The allowed sender's completion runs `exec` and writes its marker. The guest gets `exec is not available in this turn. Do not retry exec.` at launch. Revoking the third sender's entry after launch (same Gateway pid) leaves its completion with `Unknown tool id: exec` and no marker.
- Same flow with main's `session-event-target.ts` and `session-event-context.ts`: fail, `allowed requester's completion did not run exec: {"launched":true,"ran":false,..."completionOutput":"exec is not available in this turn. Do not retry exec."}`.
- #185476's `exec-completion-owner-authority` still passes in the same run.

Completion-side exec through the real Telegram and Discord plugins (`session-event-completion-reauthorize.test.ts`): the managed tool host has shell tools; DM policy resolves through `telegramPlugin.security` (`resolveTelegramDirectToolPolicy`) and guild policy through `discordPlugin.groups.resolveToolPolicy` (`resolveDiscordGroupToolPolicy`). The completion runs `printf ran > <marker>` through `exec`. 13/13 pass.
- Telegram DM rows: allowed; guest; sender revoked before admission; DM `.tools` revoked; DM `toolsBySender["username:alice"]` revoked; DM `toolsBySender["name:Alice"]` revoked; command owner with DM revoked; DM revoked with the completion routed to another chat; sender or DM revoked after admission (the tool host is retired before the call: `agent harness host capability is no longer active`).
- Discord guild channel rows (guild `200001`, channel `ops`): allowed; `guilds["200001"].tools.deny` added after launch; `guilds["200001"].channels.ops.tools.deny` added after launch.
- Source of `c4925913532`: both Discord revocation rows fail, with exec offered and run. With `GroupSpace` restored but not `GroupChannel`, the channel row still fails.
- Source of `176614364929`: the username and name rows fail. Source of my first revision: the three DM rows that existed then failed. Main's source: the allowed row fails (exec not offered), which is #177510.

Batching (`session-event-handoff.test.ts`): `otherGuest`, `ownerElsewhere`, a same-id requester with another username (`renamed`) and the same requester in another guild (`otherGuild`) combined before; now they are refused. The file passes 24/24.

Also on this head:
- Related suites: 16 files, 250 tests pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:all` exit 0 (33 stages, 0 `error TS`); oxlint and oxfmt clean.
- Ratchets OK against `586f576`: line-cap, max-lines, assertion-safety, mock-exports, test-lines, timeout-race.
- Cost: `--maxWorkers=1` gives 37.5 s for the new file (rows 1.1 to 5.2 s). Net test lines +301, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/completion-requester-policy.txt`.
- CI on `176614364929` ([run 41584998941](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41584998941/job/125748700908)): `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` reported `Test lines: 6421452; ceiling: 6420618; over by: 834; net delta: +236.` The 834 was main's own overage at the time (main went over at `2a32ab046f2`, #191638; #191696 later raised the baseline by 834, and main was 10 over at `f5f27c3ef6e`). This PR's growth is allocated exactly.

Not shown end to end:

- A live Telegram or Discord transport. The DM and guild rows use the real plugins' policy code in process, with real admission and a real `exec`, but no Bot API traffic.
- On a live Gateway, a `channels.telegram.direct` change made while a background exec runs is deferred until that exec completes (the Gateway logs `deferring until 1 background exec session(s) complete`), so a DM deny added mid-run does not reach that run's completion turn. This is existing reload behavior (`src/gateway/server-reload-active-work.ts`), which this PR does not change; the DM rows are proven by the unit test. I did not measure whether a `channels.discord.guilds` change is deferred the same way.
- Batching through a product path. The only caller, session-state notices, does not retain a requester, so the batch check is proven by the unit test only.

## What Problem This Solves

`redactSnapshot` was masking every `storage.encryption` string that looked sensitive, even when the value is ordinary encryption configuration rather than a credential. That hid useful diagnostics in config snapshots and made support harder.

This patch only redacts a candidate string when the value is concrete-sensitive **and** the key is either marked sensitive by a hint or sits on a sensitive path, so genuine credentials stay masked while harmless configuration remains readable. Ref #176229.

## Evidence

- Traced `redactValue()` through the config snapshot path: `storage.encryption` values without a sensitive hint or sensitive path now pass through unchanged, while hint-marked values still resolve to `[REDACTED]`.
- The existing config tests and lint/typecheck jobs pass on this revision; the change is limited to the redaction predicate.

prs.body:
Supersedes #171738 and links the closed replay #112375. ## What Problem This Solves Scheduled jobs that poll for work still start a model turn when the inbox, queue, or watch target is empty. This supersedes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171738 and replaces the closed replay of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/112375. Those branches targeted the previous cron store and could not be applied to current main. This branch is based on current `openclaw/openclaw` main (`7559fb21a57059bd7483fb8c0a7117aff9794f92`). ## User Impact User impact: an operator can attach a host shell precheck to an `at`, `every`, or `cron` job. Exit code 0 continues into the trigger and payload. Exit code 2 records a skipped run with summary `precheck-no-work` and does not start the model turn. Denied, unapproved, timed out, or unexpected results fail closed and skip the payload. Agent turns cannot create or edit the command. Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/schedules#shell-precheck ## Why This Change Was Made Current cron jobs live in SQLite `job_json`, with validation in the cron service and execution in `executeJobCore`. The precheck is an optional field on that job, not a new config key or schema version. The probe runs through `createExecTool` with `nonInteractiveApproval` and no host-approval bypass, then the existing gateway allowlist and approval floors. `cron.triggers.enabled: false` disables it. Forced manual runs still run the probe; they do not skip it the way they skip a condition script. ## Evidence Local validation on `7712f5df3648054ff2bd2ecdd0c90d96b73d71c5`: - `pnpm test src/cron/job-precheck.test.ts src/cron/job-precheck-run.test.ts src/cron/service/timer-execution.precheck.test.ts src/cron/service/timer-execution.occurrence.test.ts src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-precheck.test.ts` — passed. Cron shard: 4 files, 86 tests. CLI shard: 1 file, 3 tests. The exec-policy file proves a marker file is not created when security is deny, ask is always, the job pin requires ask always, `toolsAllow` excludes exec, or run authority is rejected. An allowed `full`/`off` policy covers exit 2 (no work) and exit 0 (work). - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the changed TypeScript files — passed. - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check` on the 29 changed files — all matched files use the correct format. - `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed. - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test-services-cron.tsbuildinfo` — passed. ## Security review ### Threat model A precheck is an unattended host command. The realistic attackers are a model turn that tries to persist one, an operator who saved a command and later tightened exec policy, and a forced or restarted run that might otherwise skip the gate. The command can do anything the exec tool would allow, including reading or writing files on the gateway host. The feature must not add a second spawn path with weaker defaults. ### How approvals are enforced - The runner calls `createExecTool` with the resolved `tools.exec` host, mode, security, and ask, plus the live exec-approvals file that the tool already re-reads. It does not pass `bypassHostApprovalFloors`. - `nonInteractiveApproval: true` makes approval-requiring commands return `approval_required` before spawn. `ask: "always"`, an allowlist miss, and `security: "deny"` therefore do not run the command. - A stored `toolsAllowExecTarget` pin is applied with `pinExecToolTarget`, so a creator floor of `ask: "always"` still denies a headless run when global policy is `full`/`off`. - A defined `toolsAllow` that does not include `exec` denies the probe before the tool is built. - `assertRunCurrent` is awaited in `executeJobCore` and again inside the runner immediately before `tool.execute`. A rejected run does not spawn. - If the gateway does not wire `runJobPrecheck`, or `cron.triggers.enabled` is false, the job errors and the payload does not start. - Agent creates and patches that set a non-null `precheck` are rejected in the automations tool and again in `assertCronModelJobAllowed`. Clearing the field is allowed. `cron.run` of an existing job is not treated as authoring. - Invalid persisted prechecks quarantine the row instead of being dropped, so a bad write cannot fall open into an unguarded payload. - Each run re-reads current policy. A command saved under a looser policy is denied after the operator tightens it. ### Residual risks - Command payloads (`runCronCommandJob`) still spawn from their own runner and do not use this exec-tool gate. That path is unchanged. - Operators who can already persist command jobs can persist a precheck through the CLI or Gateway API. The protection is the run-time policy check, not a second save-time approval dialog. Reusing the stream approval dialog would describe the wrong effect. - `mode: "auto"` remains the existing exec auto-review path. With `nonInteractiveApproval`, a reviewer that approves can still allow a spawn. Tests pin `mode: "full"` so they do not depend on a reviewer. This change does not weaken or special-case auto-review. - When config omits security, the exec tool keeps its own non-sandbox default and the approvals file still applies its floors. That is the same default as other exec callers. - Exit codes are the only work signal. A command that prints a success banner and exits 2 is no-work. A command that exits 0 after doing nothing is work. Overlapping codes are rejected. - The probe runs on the exec host selected by `tools.exec` unless a gateway pin forces the gateway host. It cannot target a node or sandbox that the exec tool itself would refuse.
  
--- > [!NOTE] > **High Risk** > Introduces unattended host command execution on the gateway before scheduled agent turns, gated by exec policy but still a security-sensitive automation surface. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 7712f5df3648054ff2bd2ecdd0c90d96b73d71c5. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). Updated by merging current upstream main (merge commit `ce9c3641f4`); the precheck, occurrence and CLI cron tests (89 tests) and `pnpm tsgo:core` pass on the merged head.

prs.title: fix(agents): subagent results never reach the parent while a sibling waits for its reply
prs.body:
Closes #164334
Related: #164241, #158603, #161114

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a finished subagent's result never reaches its parent when another child in the same yielded batch has paused with `sessions_yield` `waitFor: "message"` and its pause notice was already delivered.

## User Impact

A parent that receives a child's "paused awaiting continuation" notice now still gets its other children's results as they finish, whether or not it has sent that continuation yet. The paused child's own result arrives separately after it resumes. Previously the parent stayed idle with zero wake attempts, even though `sessions_yield` had just told it the sibling's completion "will arrive as a later turn". In the reported case, that lasted about six hours until a human sent a message.

Plain `sessions_yield` pauses without a notice keep their existing one-combined-delivery behavior. There is no config, schema or migration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

A consumed pause notice hands the paused child's continuation to its requester. The child still sat in its frozen yield batch, and the batch waits for every member. The paused child was waiting for its requester, and the requester was waiting for the batch.

Consuming the notice now detaches that child into its own completion wave (`batchRunIds: [self]`), keeping its own completion custody. Frozen batch membership is mutual: wave selection, the wave's descendant scope and kernel outcome settlement skip a member whose own batch no longer lists the settling run.

Requester cron/operator authority follows the split. A yield authority still covers only its original cohort, requester session, operator and rearm generation, but each detached wave of that cohort can use it. It is narrowed as waves settle and released after the last one. Settled operator rows keep their binding, so a stray retry fails closed exactly as `discard()` already requires. The cohort rules and frozen-wave selection moved into small sibling modules to stay within the line caps.

Known limit, unchanged by this PR: the in-memory requester final attachment is keyed by the cohort's original run IDs and is never remapped. Resuming a paused child already created a new run ID, so a cohort containing a message-wait pause could not match it before this change either.

## Hardening and authority boundaries

- Each detached wave retains the original operator, requester incarnation and frozen cohort generation; no newer authority is borrowed.
- Admitted turns retain their own lifecycle while earlier waves settle. Custody releases only after both scoped work and admitted delivery acknowledgements finish; original-source revocation still cuts it off immediately.
- Exact admitted-wave retries may retrieve the Gateway's cached result, but cannot create new input/execution if the cached outcome is missing.
- Operators without Cron-management entitlement receive lifecycle-only acceptance tracking, never a Cron capability or new permission.
- No persisted schema, config option, orchestration registry or live Gateway change.

## Evidence

Raw red/green excerpts, reproducible commands, SHA-256 bindings, postcommit build metadata, and proof limitations: [proof behind the proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164366#issuecomment-5974580321).

Reviewable immutable source: [Gateway admission regressions](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/gateway/server.requester-pause-authority.test.ts), [receipt/lifecycle tests](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/agents/subagents/requester-cron-authority-cohort.test.ts), and [actual acceptance boundary](https://github.com/stackingrockss/openclaw/blob/a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8/src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-admission-phase.ts).

Exact candidate: `a7002f214bdc174b73c86559f9f3fb1c33a856e8`.

- **Real Gateway admission + SQLite proof:** `server.requester-pause-authority.test.ts` runs the public `agent` method through the actual Gateway handler, admission/actor identity and runtime stores. Original operator revocation, expired authority, requester reset, late retirement, cached retry, cache eviction and a retired delivery claim are exercised. The agent-command/provider bridge is synthetic; this is not a live model or ordinary outside-harness UI demonstration.
- **Non-Cron negative control:** an `operator.write` client with no admin override and no Cron entitlement originally reached execution/input staging twice after cache eviction. The repaired code replays without changing transcript/admission count, rejects cache-missing retry, and still delivers the next detached completion. Cron authority stays undefined.
- **Original-source liveness:** cached retries and their captured dispatch assertion reject independently revoked channel-owner grants and registry lifecycle rotation while the operator profile and requester session remain unchanged. The after-await case is owner-level assertion proof on a genuinely admitted/cached wave, not a raced public transport request.
- **Timing reproductions:** late-wave retirement, ambiguous sibling/final acknowledgements, and zero-scoped-turn unsettled receipts failed before their repairs. Immediate revocation remains covered. Prior fixture-reference errors are not counted as bug reproductions.
- **Coverage retained:** 18 Gateway cases and 37 authority/cohort cases pass; retirement tests were moved intact into a coherent sibling module to meet the line-cap ratchet. Existing registry/lifecycle/completion/outbox/codec cases remain.
- **Validation:** full `pnpm check:changed` passed including production/test types, lint, dead exports, runtime cycles and line caps. `git diff --check` and six-file format validation passed.
- **Independent review:** final full-delta autoreview through P2 is scoped-clean for this exact head. Earlier actionable findings were reproduced and repaired, not waived. The reviewer assessed supplied source/test evidence; its isolated sandbox did not independently execute the repository.
- **Build:** postcommit `pnpm build` passed in 378.64s; `dist/build-info.json.commit` matches this exact head. An earlier build was invalidated by removal of temporary review inputs during compilation; it was not credited, and the stable-namespace rerun passed.
- **CI/security:** current-head CI/ClawSweeper reconciliation and authorized upstream security approval remain pending. No merge/deployment has been performed.


---
[View the OpenClaw team session](https://claw.seelig.dev/chat/main/dashboard/d32aa602-6464-4f30-80da-8bccb0bd2f3a)

prs.title: fix(test): retain selected Bun through isolation
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

A launcher selects the pinned absolute Bun executable before isolating test HOME/cache. `pinnedBunEnv` carries only PATH, so a nested formatter resolves a new empty cache and stages the same runtime again. This was observed while qualifying https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186469: its existing dirty-to-formatted fixture entered the Bun stager and downloaded a second executable archive.

## Canonical fix

Carry the already-selected absolute executable in the existing `OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH` provision. Keep relative CI `bun` PATH-only. The resolver, checksum/revision admission, explicit-override behavior, isolated HOME/cache and formatter policy remain owned by their existing modules. `test-live` already binds the selected local executable before changing child CI defaults; this applies the same ownership invariant to all callers of the shared provision.

Production +11/-6 (net +5), justified by preserving runtime identity across the child-environment ownership boundary; tests +25/-1 (net +24). Reuse existing cache-resolution cases and the two-route launcher proof; no extra child or test matrix. The cache case resolves under a different HOME/cache with only the provision and requires the original executable, no second stage and no isolated cache creation. The launcher child also retains its cache/exit/argument assertions. It already inherits an explicit path, so it is supporting integration proof rather than the discriminating regression.

## Prospective qualification rule — recorded before benchmark execution

- Real flow: reuse the committed `changed-lanes.test.ts` dirty-file to formatted-file check and its actual changed-plan → package script → `run-format` → formatter chain. Two formatter invocations per body; identical diagnostics, file selection and source bytes; dirty exits 1, formatted exits 0.
- Counts first: after local selection of a verified absolute Bun and before HOME/cache isolation, carry only the shared provision. Candidate must use that selected executable and perform zero additional staging/downloads against an empty isolated Bun cache. The existing injectable resolver fixture establishes the baseline extra-stage red case without a network download. Mock staging counts are resolver evidence, not formatter timing.
- Comparable timing: preseed both isolated caches from identical already-verified Bun bytes/stamps outside measurement. Warmup separately; five serial alternating baseline/candidate pairs on the same host. Cold empty-cache behavior is reported separately, not timed as a failed baseline versus successful candidate.
- Record host load, wall/user/system CPU/peak RSS, median/p95/spread and exact output parity. Every measured metric must hold or improve; a 20% adverse move is an immediate stop, and smaller regressions require explicit acceptance. Otherwise retain the draft.
- Use only committed workloads, existing focused runner and existing dependency ownership. No new cache, fixture framework, benchmark service or paid box allocation.

## Observed qualification

At exact head `a94d7d5b31adddda7f496a708cb82b636e58235a`, the native physical checkout passed the frozen install and 114 tests across pinned-Bun, launcher, and dev-tool suites. The tooling-test typecheck, production and changed-test lint, targeted formatting, and the committed real dirty-to-formatted case also passed. That last run executed one selected test; 67 other tests were intentionally skipped.

A separate before/after resolver probe used the complete production owner with the existing injectable synthetic stager. Baseline selected a different executable and staged again after HOME/cache isolation; candidate retained the selected executable, performed zero additional stages, created no isolated cache, and left the parent environment unchanged. These are resolver work-count results, not network-download or formatter timing measurements.

Independent review of all five callers and local autoreview found no actionable code issue. The latest exact-head ClawSweeper review requested the formal qualification above and real-flow/performance evidence; performance evidence remains open.

The draft is retained because the promised alternating A/B performance comparison has not run. The unchanged committed case creates an unpredictable worker HOME and resets XDG_CACHE_HOME inside test setup. There is no existing independent Bun-cache selector or preseed seam, so outer-cache preparation cannot satisfy the prospective requirement to preseed both actual isolated caches outside timing. An independently owned baseline checkout can solve dependency availability, but cannot solve that cache-preparation constraint. No setup hook, runtime override after isolation, or fixture change will be introduced to manufacture a passing comparison.

No benchmark has run for this candidate. No ordinary Actions billing reduction is claimed: the relative workflow-provisioned `bun` path stays unchanged. Release-owned changelog; this is development/test runtime ownership.

prs.title: fix: Template details take too long to load
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: opening a Template’s details leaves its workspace-file and content rows loading while independent registry requests run one after another.

## User Impact

Template details load faster without changing their contents, exact-release selection, visibility checks, artifact integrity, or preview/apply behavior. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read package metadata, exact-release metadata, and the archive concurrently, then reuse the release’s artifact metadata instead of making a redundant artifact-resolution request. Archive content is not consumed before the existing identity and integrity checks pass. A request-owned abort cancels unfinished speculative downloads on metadata failure, and staged downloads are always cleaned up.

The parser and integrity helpers move unchanged to the existing artifact owner to keep the source module within its line limit. No cache, endpoint, dependency, or configuration surface is added.

## Evidence

- Isolated real OpenClaw Gateways against the same local ClawHub installation and hash-verified published Research monitor 0.1.2 archive: five interleaved fresh-connection loads per arm. Average **1012.94 → 331.52 ms (67.27% lower; 3.06× faster)**; median 954.20 → 307.49 ms; p95 1179.77 → 459.37 ms. Every complete JSON response was deeply equal. This success-path measurement predates the failure-path cancellation repair and helper relocation; final-code browser/production evidence is recorded separately below.
- Rerunnable real-Gateway benchmark: `scripts/bench-template-detail.mts` (at least five samples, response parity, per-run host load, no credential output). It measures authenticated connection plus full verified detail response, not CLI startup or browser INP.
- Focused source/artifact/Gateway tests pass. Source suite includes concurrency/no-consumption-before-validation, redundant-request removal, failure cleanup, and genuinely pending-download cancellation. Three new regression cases fail on unchanged baseline (3 failed, 34 passed); baseline checkout restored afterward.
- Final-code real-browser baseline/candidate flows render identical Research monitor workspace files and nonempty SOUL.md previews. Detail RPC: 669.57 → 249.52 ms in these single illustrative captures (not a multi-run latency claim); preview RPC succeeds on both. Automation-to-visible-detail wall time: 1011.71 → 507.30 ms. No browser page errors. The synthetic empty session produces an unrelated `mcp.app.discover` access refusal; all Template RPCs succeed. Before/after screenshots are attached below.
- Targeted template and scripts typechecks, four-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent read-only review of exact commit `7e0d2c402e6f182402e8c027d9315fb42721d7d8` confirms both cancellation and benchmark-token typing findings resolved, with no remaining blockers in the four-file scope. The reviewer did not rerun checks. Local ClawSweeper completed the entire committed range `c8094c112b45a3b7ab378af7668be0f60cafd0cd..7e0d2c402e6f182402e8c027d9315fb42721d7d8` (high reasoning, read-only source correctness/security scope): no actionable findings; no tests or runtime benchmarks were run by that review.
- Author simplify pass removes one redundant primary registry lookup and the serial critical path without adding cache/configuration ownership. Whole-change delta: production +81 net lines, tests +72, benchmark +91; runtime growth is parallel coordination and explicit download lifecycle ownership.
- UI proof reused generated production UI assets; no production UI source changed. The isolated UI build emitted assets but reported startup-size budget violations outside the touched source scope; it is not claimed as a green full UI build.

No production OpenClaw Gateway was rebuilt or restarted. This is an OpenClaw-side optimization; it does not itself deploy new Gateway code.

![Before - complete Template details on baseline Gateway](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b647ebb9-c80b-44d0-a887-7f81741256b7)

![After - equivalent Template details on candidate Gateway](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ab1e794-3305-45f7-a143-18ebb79daa7e)

![Before - SOUL.md preview on baseline Gateway](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/befd2f5c-aaff-4483-96c8-ad35a4eac142)

![After - SOUL.md preview on candidate Gateway](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/483f9449-329d-4feb-9f38-01bf8634abb6)

### Current-production final-code benchmark

Final commit `7e0d2c402e6f182402e8c027d9315fb42721d7d8` versus unchanged baseline `c8094c112b45a3b7ab378af7668be0f60cafd0cd`, using already-running isolated real Gateways on ports 19561/19562. Both processes were verified bound to `OPENCLAW_CLAWHUB_URL=https://clawhub.ai`. Workload: exact published `@openclaw/research-monitor@0.1.2`; five serial ABAB pairs, each over a fresh authenticated Gateway connection through the full verified archive/extraction/detail path. Process/module startup is excluded. The >=2x average speedup target passes; full JSON deep equality passes for all ten responses.

| Metric (ms) | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Average | 3620.30 | 1049.26 |
| Median | 3343.90 | 988.84 |
| p95 (5 samples/arm) | 5042.19 | 1199.79 |
| Min-max | 3100.07-5042.19 | 973.29-1199.79 |

Average **3.45x faster / 71.02% lower**. Per-sample 1/5/15-minute host load was recorded; observed 1-minute load 9.62-10.55. Initial slower baseline sample is retained, not discarded. Source-owned primary registry reads fall from four to three, with the three remaining independent reads concurrent; archive-internal HTTP work is not included in that count. No cache is added.

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-template-detail.mts   --baseline-config /path/to/baseline/openclaw.json   --candidate-config /path/to/candidate/openclaw.json   --output /path/to/current-production-gateway-ab.json
```

This measures current production ClawHub, **not** a new shared backend deployment. Shared backend PR openclaw/clawhub#4443 merged as `923099b7bb4fa9de01fe157722403434af139ab6`; its exact-SHA Deploy Test passed, but production Deploy [41951554456](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/actions/runs/41951554456) refused unrelated large-index deletion. That guard was not bypassed. Post-shared-deployment validation remains blocked. This PR remains an OpenClaw-only proposal and does not update or restart the user's production Gateway.

All four attached before/after PNGs were subsequently loaded and decoded from the rendered PR (1440x1050 each).


### CI fixture repair

The original exact-head CI [checks-node-changed job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41951469660/job/126996802638) failed in `server-templates-add-authority.e2e.test.ts` with `Downloaded Template package manifest is invalid.` The CI classifier marked attribution unknown (no matching main job and annotation-only discovery); the completed job log was subsequently inspected directly.

The fixture and manifest reader were both byte-identical to baseline `c8094c112b45a3b7ab378af7668be0f60cafd0cd`: the fixture declared the retired `openclaw.template: template.json`, while the reader accepts only package-relative `CLAW.md` with frontmatter. A bounded owning-reader reproduction on baseline and candidate, for both allowed/revoked fixture shapes, rejects the old selector with `invalid_package_metadata` and admits the canonical manifest with package dependencies and cron declarations intact. This establishes the inherited fixture defect, not a passing full Gateway replay.

The follow-up changes only that existing E2E fixture: point the package selector at `CLAW.md`, move the unchanged manifest JSON into its frontmatter, retain the original heading, and remove the obsolete JSON artifact. All authorization, revoked-admin, persistence, and effect assertions remain unchanged. Production source is unchanged from measured/reviewed `7e0d2c402e6f182402e8c027d9315fb42721d7d8`, so the benchmark and screenshots above remain applicable.

Changed-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Local full E2E preparation refused because managed-Gateway artifact separation could not be verified; no artifacts were rebuilt and that guard was not bypassed. The supported isolated runner requires Linux and is unavailable on this Mac. Full real-Gateway confirmation subsequently passed on fixture commit `665fab132433ca7563f14c1b19669dd86ae0a54a`: [checks-node-changed job 127001030795](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41952682969/job/127001030795). The original authority test passed in 14.77 seconds (53.15 seconds for its full isolated invocation), and the trusted-plugin sibling passed in that job. This supersedes the local E2E verification gap; overall CI is not yet claimed green.

Published fixture-only follow-up: `665fab132433ca7563f14c1b19669dd86ae0a54a`. Independent read-only review reports no findings or boundary weakening: manifest declarations are preserved and all authentication, consent, revocation, before-effect gating, settlement, and installed-state assertions remain unchanged. The reviewer did not execute tests.


### Scoped test-line allocation

CI on `665fab132433ca7563f14c1b19669dd86ae0a54a` then failed only the completed baseline-ratchet job's test-line check: 6,477,280 lines versus ceiling 6,477,260; this change has +71 net test LF lines. Preserve the regression tests rather than deleting unrelated coverage or weakening assertions. Per the repository's comparison-aware test-budget policy, commit `5316e2f03939a1fc72f2a11f3dd3dc3c7ec3633e` adds the separate `config/test-lines-allocations/templates-detail-parallel-artifact.txt` record for exactly those **71 net lines** (+72 source regression lines and -1 canonical authority-fixture line). It covers concurrent-read admission without early extraction, elimination of the redundant artifact lookup, completed-download cleanup on metadata/integrity failure, and genuinely pending-download cancellation. The shared scalar is unchanged.

The staged checker passes against both original base `c8094c112b45a3b7ab378af7668be0f60cafd0cd` and CI's observed comparison base `8526701724c109fd911837ba0fe4585b42fa50a5`: local tree 6,473,470; effective ceiling 6,473,499; slack 29. The new record is bounded to actual owned growth; no inherited debt or blanket allowance is added. `git diff --check` passes. No production or test behavior changed after the passing real-Gateway replay. Replacement exact-head CI remains the final broad verification gate.


### Exact-head CI: attributed inherited test-budget debt

At head `5316e2f03939a1fc72f2a11f3dd3dc3c7ec3633e`, [checks-node-changed passed again](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41954663511/job/127007610835), including the real-Gateway authorization tests. prs.title: fix(macos): app quits with a generic credential alert when a separately managed Gateway blocks migration after an update
prs.body:
Related: #187000

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after an in-place app update, the macOS app shows the generic "client credentials need recovery" alert and quits when a local Gateway it does not manage (extended-stable channel, a channel install policy, or an independently managed or write-disabled service) is still running and blocks the required credential migration.

## User Impact

User impact: the app now explains which owner keeps that Gateway's version and reports the known credential-maintenance conflict, with **Retry** / **Quit OpenClaw**. It does not infer version incompatibility from contention or unconditionally recommend an upgrade/downgrade. Resolve the reported conflict through the Gateway's management tool; change versions only if recovery identifies incompatibility. It still never stops, replaces, or migrates under such a Gateway. Credential preparation failures with any other cause keep the existing generic alert. Background (`--background-only`) launches print the same guidance and quit, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the credential migration owner knows why preparation failed, so it now marks the one case this alert explains. When a required migration's maintenance admission is refused because a process with lock role `gateway` holds the state, `prepareStartupClientCredentials` throws `ClientCredentialGatewayHeldError`, and `openclaw doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive --json` reports `error.code: "client_credentials_gateway_held"`. The app runs that command with `--json` and shows the Gateway-owner alert only for that code **and** an excluded local Gateway service. Everything else, including invalid config and the runtime-pin conflicts proposed in #191436, keeps the generic recovery alert. Legacy preparation before admission is validate-only, so the alert can accurately report stopping before the required maintenance. The earlier draft's "nothing was changed" claim for every failure is gone.

The stale-service detection from #190162 (remote primaries hosting a local Gateway) now returns one pure `admission` decision (`notHosted`, `excluded(reason)`, `admitted`), and `managedRepairGatesOpen` is derived from the new `managedRepairExclusion`, so existing gate callers behave the same.

Overlap: #191468 (merged) touches only `GatewayEndpointStore`. #191436 (open) edits `startup-client-credentials.ts` and the same docs paragraph. The overlap is textual only: its pin-migration failures are not Gateway-held, so they correctly keep the generic alert.

## Evidence

**Real CLI against a real isolated Gateway.** Private `HOME`/state/config, named profile `mgre2e`, port 34781, never the operator's Gateway:
- With `pnpm openclaw gateway run` holding state (pid 19622, role `gateway`) and a required migration (receipt device mismatch, the remount case), `doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive --json` exited 2 with `"code": "client_credentials_gateway_held"` and the contention message naming that holder.
- Same running Gateway, unrelated failure (invalid config): exit 2, **no** code (`Cannot prepare client credentials with invalid config …`).
- After stopping that Gateway, the same command exited 0 with `{"ok": true}`, and the receipt returned to `complete` with the original device. This is the CLI side of **Retry**.

**Original-head regression evidence** (`c7e792e3b2d3`), red on the base and green with the fix:
- `startup-client-credentials.test.ts`: "attributes a required migration refusal to the Gateway only when a gateway holds state" uses a real state-owner lock. The `gateway` case fails without the fix, and the `agent-embedded` case proves non-Gateway holders are not attributed. Suite: 22/22.
- `register.maintenance.test.ts`: the coded JSON failure envelope and exit 2. Suite: 39/39.
- Swift, private `HOME`/state/`TMPDIR`: `ClientCredentialStartupTests` (`--json` arguments, only the Gateway-held code yields `GatewayHeldError`, owner-specific recovery text) and `StaleGatewayServiceReplacementTests` (the #190162 hosting matrix plus owner exclusions): 11/11.

**Original-head gates** (`c7e792e3b2d3`):
- `swift build` for the app product and the test targets passed.
- `scripts/format-swift.sh macos`, `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, oxfmt, oxlint and `pnpm tsgo:core` / `tsgo:core:test` all pass.
- `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` reports only 2 existing file-length violations in untouched files (`DashboardManager.swift`, `GatewayConnection.swift`).

**Original-head review:** local autoreview (Codex), committed range `d894035c7829..c7e792e3b2d3`, `--max-priority P2` with the owning sources as context: `scoped-clean`, no P0–P2 findings (0.88). An earlier P0-only pass was also clean.

**ClawSweeper finding follow-up** (`dddadc75e57f`):
- Removed the unsupported incompatibility diagnosis and unconditional version-change advice from the alert and docs. Receipt reconciliation after a remount can require exclusive maintenance without changing the credential layout.
- Removed the unused app-version argument and the wording-only helper test; error attribution, cancellation, and bundled-owner tests remain. No detection or service-lifecycle behavior changed.
- Current checks passed: `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` (app and test targets), targeted SwiftFormat, `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, docs oxfmt, and `git diff --check`.
- Native tests were not rerun on the operator desktop; the macOS guide requires OS-level isolation or a disposable runner. The earlier 11-test result above is prior-head evidence and includes the now-removed wording test. Subsequent explicitly authorized isolated native proof is recorded below.

**Native app validation on a prior head (`dddadc75e57f`):**

Performed natively with explicit operator authorization, in a fresh OCM environment: separate HOME/CFFIXED_USER_HOME, state/config/profile, bundle identity, test LaunchAgent, and port 34781. No copied operator credentials or channels. A sandbox guard denied app access to the operator state and writes to operator preferences/LaunchAgents, and blocked connections to the live Gateway ports. App metadata pins the tested commit.

- Stable `2026.10.10` service: the actual app showed the owner-preserving maintenance alert with Retry / Quit. Retrying while the service held state returned to the alert without migration. After stopping only the test service, Retry completed migration; the native credential socket returned the original synthetic device ID, public/private keys, and creation time. Test config remained unchanged.
- Compatible runtime: the test service ran the PR app's bundled runtime. A synthetic receipt device mismatch represented remount maintenance (not a real filesystem remount). The real app showed the same corrected maintenance alert without asserting version incompatibility. Retry while held returned to the alert. After stopping only this test service, Retry repaired the receipt; native credential admission preserved the original identity/keys and config.
- Operator config and Gateway LaunchAgent hashes remained equal to their pre-test values. The live Gateway restarted independently during the interrupted agent run, so continuous PID preservation is not claimed; no test command stopped or modified that service.

**Merged head (`58359d17191c`):** merged current `main` and fixed the Quit hang.

- Conflict resolution: `doctor --client-credentials` keeps both `prepareRuntimePins: true` from `main` and this PR's coded failure. The docs text moved to the new **Credential recovery** section.
- Quit fix: both credential-startup alert paths now use `AppDelegate.requestTermination()` instead of calling `terminate` on the main dispatch task.
- Isolated OCM run, same guards, app metadata pinned to this commit: with the test Gateway holding state and a synthetic receipt device mismatch, process sampling shows the app in `retryAfterExcludedGatewayFailure` → `NSAlert.runModal`. The bundled CLI exits 2 with `client_credentials_gateway_held`.
- Passing: `startup-client-credentials.test.ts` and `register.maintenance.test.ts` (64/64), app packaging, oxfmt, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, `git diff --check`.
- `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` reports 5 violations, all in files this PR does not touch.
- Native test targets do not compile on `main`: `GatewayEndpointStoreTests.swift` calls the now-throwing `_testLocalConfig` without `try`. This PR does not touch that file. With a temporary local `try!` patch, not committed, the test targets built.

- Real alert clicks, same isolated OCM run on `58359d17191c`, pressed through the Accessibility API with the alert's actual text and controls read back:
  - **Retry** while the test Gateway held state: the alert returned and no migration ran.
  - **Quit OpenClaw**: the app exited in about 2 seconds. This is the path that hung on `dddadc75e57f`.
  - **Retry** after stopping only the test Gateway: the receipt returned to `complete` with the real device, and the native credential socket returned the original device ID, public/private keys, and creation time. Test config unchanged.
- Operator config and Gateway LaunchAgent hashes matched before and after.

**Remaining gaps:**

- **Visual screenshots remain missing.** `AppActivation.presentAlert` sets `alert.window.sharingType = .none`, so captures of the real alert are blank. No mockup or blank image is offered as proof.
- The alert's **Details** line uses `detail.suffix(300)`, so it can start mid-word (observed: "e directory."). The actionable end of the message is intact.
- Successful Retry is proved at the real app credential socket, not full chat/model connectivity. The full native suite remains CI-owned.

prs.title: feat(sessions): show per-session token and cost usage from the CLI
prs.body:
Closes #192616

## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway records per-session token and cost attribution and the Control UI shows it, but the terminal could not: `openclaw gateway usage-cost` prints one aggregate number, so a headless operator could not see which session, agent, or model burned the tokens.

## User Impact

`openclaw sessions usage [sessionKey]` prints one row per session (label, agent, model, messages, tokens, cost) plus range totals, with `--agent`, `--all`, `--range`, `--start/--end`, `--max-rows`, and `--group-family` selectors. `--json` returns the raw `sessions.usage` response.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The command forwards the canonical `sessions.usage` owner and only shapes output: conflicting selectors are rejected before dispatch, and the report's `partial` status is printed instead of hidden, so a time-budgeted answer is never mistaken for "no usage".
- The row cap flag is `--max-rows` rather than `--limit`, because the parent `sessions --limit` list-row cap owns that name (the sibling search command follows the same naming after review feedback).
- Registration rejects the parent list selectors, matching the other gateway-backed verbs.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/sessions-usage.test.ts src/cli/program/register.status-health-sessions.test.ts` → 27/27 passed locally.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` → clean; `oxfmt --check` → clean.
- **Real behavior proof**: the branch was built through the shipped `build-all` and run against a real Gateway booted from this checkout (isolated state dir, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`):

```text
$ openclaw sessions usage --timeout 120000 --json
{ ..., "startDate": "2026-10-06", "endDate": "2026-11-04", "cacheStatus": {"status": "partial"},
  "partial": { "reason": "time-budget", "message": "Usage request exceeded its 15-second budget; ..." } }

$ openclaw sessions usage --timeout 120000
Session usage (2026-10-06 → 2026-11-04)
No session usage recorded in this range.
Totals: $0.0000 · 0 tokens · in 0 / out 0
Partial report: Usage request exceeded its 15-second budget; narrow the date range or select a session.

$ openclaw sessions usage --agent x --all          → exit 1 (conflict)
$ openclaw sessions usage --end 2026-10-31         → exit 1 (missing --start)
$ openclaw sessions usage --max-rows 500           → exit 1 (cap exceeded)
```

The live response's `partial` reason surfacing in text mode is the behavior the review asked to prove: an incomplete answer is labeled, never silent.

## Risks

- None beyond the new verb: no RPC, ledger, or config changes.

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

prs.title: fix(android): preserve accepted work when ending Talk
prs.body:
Closes #188134

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes accepted agent work being canceled when an Android phone user taps End Talk.

## User Impact

End Talk stops listening and playback while accepted work continues and its answer remains available in chat. To cancel work instead, say “cancel” before ending the call or use the chat run’s existing Stop control.

Realtime detachment requires a Gateway advertising `talk-session-close-disposition`; older Gateways retain their legacy aborting close. Other clients’ Stop behavior is unchanged. No new setting, permission, protocol field, or UI control is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ending an audio conversation should not silently discard work the agent already accepted. Reuse the phone’s existing capture-cleanup path, which already detaches during backgrounding and mode changes, rather than maintain a separate abort override for End Talk. Native Talk keeps its existing accepted-work behavior.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the actual Android `NodeRuntime` and relay WebSocket boundary on base `563ba501dced074d9d282fb3a4cb48cfc31bcf9e`: the updated regression failed with **expected detach, observed abort** specifically for End Talk.
- With the fix, `:app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest` passed **131 tests**: all **112 TalkModeManagerTest** cases and **19 RealtimeAgentCoordinatorTest** cases, with zero failures, errors, or skips. These include End Talk/mode-change close requests, capture retirement, native accepted-work preservation, explicit abort, legacy capability behavior, and voice cancellation. Gradle completed in **47 seconds**.
- Gateway `server.talk-consult-history.test.ts -t "settles close disposition"` passed **9 selected scenarios** in **84.75 seconds** overall. This exercises the real close/admission/history owners with fixed inference/provider fixtures: detach leaves accepted work running and publishes its answer; explicit/default abort cancels it. It also covers work completed before close, spoken replacement, a second consult, and uncertain transcript append outcomes. The 13 unrelated cases were filtered, not claimed passing.
- Android `:app:ktlintCheck` passed (**17 seconds**); production and test Kotlin compiled as part of the focused Gradle run. Both changed docs passed MDX and formatting checks; `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent **AutoReview**, Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium reasoning, **P0–P2**, reviewed the complete local candidate against the pinned base with relevant unchanged lifecycle/cancellation context: **scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. Only an American English spelling correction followed. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable within this task’s permitted source/skill scope, so the documented fallback route was used; hosted ClawSweeper has acknowledged the PR for review; its review is pending.
- Simplification: removes the phone-only close-disposition override and its unused plumbing. Production Kotlin **+2/-8**; regression test **+4/-4**. No new state or parallel lifecycle owner.

**Proof limits:** this is Android runtime/WebSocket and isolated Gateway boundary proof, not a newly installed physical-phone call or live-provider audio test. No rendered UI changes are included. Broad PR CI is separate from these focused passing checks.

Reported by @jeffjhunter in #188134. Prepared at the request of @RomneyDa.

prs.title: fix(openclaw-id): replayed revocation removes a device that was approved again
prs.body:
Related: #192230 (closed in favor of this PR), #192335

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a captured OpenClaw ID revocation, submitted again through the Discovery mailbox, removes an owner device or member browser that an owner approved again after the revocation was signed. Invite records also pile up with no limit, so a stolen owner device could grow the claw record until the Gateway can no longer save it.

## User Impact

- A replayed revocation no longer removes a device that was approved again. A revocation signed after the re-approval still removes it.
- An invite lasts at most a week, a claw keeps at most 100 invites, and expired invites are deleted. Removing an owner device also deletes the open invites it created.
- Signed format change (draft protocol): a Revocation must now carry `claw_id` and `seq`, and the old form is refused as `malformed`. Gateways run none of this code until the OpenClaw ID Gateway stack (#192335) merges.

## Why This Change Was Made

@SebTardif found the replay in #192230 and fixed it by keeping every applied revocation signature. That list only grows. The claw stopped keeping history on 2026-11-02 because its earlier revoked list outgrew the 256-entry statement limit, so this PR fixes the replay without a list.

A revocation now covers only what its signer saw. It names the claw and the membership `seq` the signer last read. Every listed key records the seq at which it was listed, and listing a key that is still listed anywhere keeps its earliest seq. A revocation removes a key only if it was listed at or before that seq, together with every device the key approved. A re-approval is a new listing the old signature never covered, so the replay is refused with `seq_conflict` and changes nothing. Invites get the same treatment: each one expires within a week, so the claw no longer has to remember used invites forever.

Tradeoff: a revocation signed from a view older than the key's re-approval is refused (`seq_conflict`). The signer has to sign it again at the current seq.

## Evidence

- `vitest` over `packages/openclaw-id-protocol`: 21 files, 141 tests passed. New tests are in `revocation-scope.test.ts` (6) and `invite-retention.test.ts` (4).
- The replay regressions fail without the fix: with the seq check removed, the three replay tests fail and the other two pass. The removed-device invite test fails without the cleanup.
- Type checks (`pnpm tsgo:core`, package tests) report no errors. `oxlint` finds no problems in the 16 changed files, and the max-lines ratchet passes.
- Test-lines ratchet passes: 279 new test lines, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/openclaw-id-bounded-authority-state.txt` (slack 76 against `main` `658e3db2a46`).

prs.title: test(openai): GPT-Live RTP test needs no LAN or public STUN path
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the GPT-Live audio-worker RTP tests time out when the test host has no reachable LAN path or public STUN, for example in a network-restricted agent sandbox.


The two `keeps RTP and media delivery running during a blocked Gateway` cases in `extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver-peer-worker.test.ts` (direct sink false/true) timed out 3/3 on clean `main` for the lane landing openclaw/openclaw#180100. SDP negotiation completed, but the receiver never saw RTP. On a normal developer Mac the same file passes 5/5, both at the lane's baseline `2b18fc8e` and at current `main`. This is not a product or dependency regression.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Developers and CI lanes in network-restricted environments get a hermetic loopback RTP test instead of 30 s timeouts.

## Why This Change Was Made


The test is meant to send media over loopback between the product audio worker and a werift receiver worker in the same process. werift does not do that by default:

- Host-candidate gathering skips `internal` (loopback) interfaces and VPN-style `utun*`/`tun*`/`tap*`/`ipsec*` interfaces.
- `iceServers: []` does not disable STUN. The ICE layer falls back to `stun.l.google.com:19302` whenever no STUN server is configured, and waits up to 5 s per side when it is unreachable.

As a result, the test only connected through a reachable LAN address or a STUN server-reflexive candidate via NAT hairpin. In a network-restricted sandbox (for example a Codex worker), or on a host whose only routable interfaces are VPN tunnels, no candidate pair connects. Signaling still succeeds because it runs over worker messages, but no RTP flows.

**Fix.** 
The test-owned receiver advertises an explicit `127.0.0.1` host candidate (`iceAdditionalHostAddresses`). The audio worker's sockets are bound to the wildcard address, so it reaches that candidate over loopback whatever the host's real interfaces look like. Assertions, thresholds, and timeouts are unchanged, and no product code changes. Production GPT-Live peers talk to OpenAI's media servers and never use this path.

Accepted edge case: the product peer still uses werift's default public STUN server, so a fully offline host adds up to about 10 s of bounded gather time per case (measured about 12 s per case, inside the existing budgets). Removing it would need a product-side ICE option that only tests use, which isn't worth it.

## Evidence

Reproduction harness (local only, not committed): a `--require` preload replaces `os.networkInterfaces()` with `lo0` plus an unreachable TEST-NET host (`192.0.2.10`), handed to both the receiver and the audio worker. The run uses a Seatbelt profile that denies non-loopback outbound IP (STUN unreachable), similar to a restricted sandbox.

| Revision | Result under the harness |
|---|---|
| `main` (`176c9c74`) | both cases fail: `expected 0 to be greater than or equal to 5` (zero RTP) after about 20–22 s |
| this PR | 5/5 pass (about 12 s per RTP case) |

A standalone werift probe under the same conditions stays in `connecting` without the loopback candidate. With it, ICE nominates `192.0.2.10 → 127.0.0.1` and connects.

Normal environment on this PR: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver-peer-worker.test.ts` passes 5/5 twice on Node and 5/5 on Bun (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun`). Codex autoreview (P0–P2) was scoped-clean. oxfmt, oxlint, and `git diff --check` are clean.

Release-note context: test-only change, no user-visible behavior.
