Original implementation by @VACInc. Delivery-owner repair and additional verification by RoboClaw.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/49d142f3-696c-4b7e-95a2-161ba913bcb3)

<details>
<summary>Original design contract and author-reported verification</summary>

## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Today every automation either names its own chat route or follows the conversation that created it. An operator who wants all results in one place (for example topic 1 of a Telegram forum) has to pin `channel`/`to`/`threadId` on every job, and agent-created jobs pin whatever chat they were made in. Failure alerts have a Gateway-wide route but no per-agent or per-person one.

This adds configurable default destinations at three layers, for both primary results and failure alerts:

- `cron.delivery` (and the existing `cron.failureAlert`): Gateway-wide defaults.
- `cron.agents.<agentId>.delivery` and `.failureAlert`: defaults for the agent that owns the job.
- `cron.creators.<profileId>.delivery` and `.failureAlert`: defaults for the human who created the job, keyed by Gateway profile id.

Defaults resolve at run time. Stored jobs are never rewritten, and a job that names its own route keeps it.

```json5
{
  cron: {
    delivery: { channel: "telegram", to: "-100123456789", threadId: 1 },
    failureAlert: { channel: "telegram", to: "-100123456789:topic:1" },
    agents: {
      ops: { delivery: { channel: "slack", to: "channel:C123" } },
    },
    creators: {
      "profile-id": {
        delivery: { channel: "telegram", to: "-100123456789", threadId: 2 },
        failureAlert: { channel: "telegram", to: "-100123456789:topic:2" },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

### Contract

- **Owner.** The job's `agentId`, else the agent in its session key, else the default agent.
- **Creator.** The trusted creation seam already stamps `createdActor` on every job it stores (`cron-creator-session.ts`, `cron-input-validation.ts`), and run-time execution context already reads its profile id. The creator layer reads the same stamp through the canonical `sessionCreatorProfileId` helper. It applies when the creator is a human with a Gateway profile, or a human profile that delegated creation to an agent (`delegatedBy`). Legacy jobs with no `createdActor`, and channel-only, unknown, agent-without-a-human, and system creators have no creator default. Profile keys match exactly; they are opaque ids, so they are not case-folded like agent ids.
- **One shared helper.** `resolveCronDeliveryDefaultsScope` derives both the owner and the creator for every path: preview, isolated run delivery, command/script completion, run-queue check, failure alerts, and create/update validation. `cron.add` passes the stamped creator into its validation and preview so the add result already shows the creator default.
- **Precedence.** The job's own route, then the creator-profile default, then the owner-agent default, then the Gateway-wide default, then today's behavior. "Own route" means a `channel` other than `last`, `to`, `threadId`, `accountId`, or `target: "owner"`.
- **Why this order.**
  - The job's own route is explicit intent for that one job, so nothing overrides it.
  - The creator is the person who set the job up, the most specific "who". Their chosen inbox should follow them across whichever agent they used.
  - An agent is a shared runtime that can serve several people, so its default is broader than one person's.
  - The Gateway default is the catch-all, and with nothing configured behavior is unchanged. "Routing fields" means a `channel` other than `last`, `to`, `threadId`, `accountId`, or `target: "owner"`.
- **Most specific default wins whole.** No field merging, because recipient, thread, and account belong to the channel that supplied them.
- **Eligibility.** Only a resolved `announce` mode with no routing field gets a default. This holds for every session target, including `current` and `main`, where the default replaces the creating-conversation route.
- **`mode: "none"` and `"webhook"` never gain a chat destination.** That includes `message`-tool context. Failure alerts for `none` jobs still use configured failure routes, as today.
- **Failure route.** `cron.creators.<profileId>.failureAlert` and `cron.agents.<id>.failureAlert` set `mode`, `channel`, `to`, and `accountId`, in the same creator-then-agent order, replacing the global route fields whole. `enabled`, `after`, `cooldownMs`, and `includeSkipped` stay Gateway-wide, so `cron.failureAlert.enabled: false` still disables inherited alerts. Like a `cron.failureAlert` object, a scoped route activates the alert policy. Precedence: per-job `failureAlert` route, then `delivery.failureDestination` layered over the creator route, else the agent route, else the global route, then the primary announce route. That last step now includes a primary default, and its `threadId` is kept.
- **Agent-created jobs.** When the cron tool creates a route-less job and a default applies to the job's agent or to the requesting human profile, it no longer pins the creating chat route. Otherwise the inferred route would become an explicit per-job route and hide the default. The tool reads the requester profile from the authenticated requester origin, the same source the Gateway uses to stamp `delegatedBy`.
- **Validation.** Config load rejects a default whose `channel` names no installed channel plugin (`cron.delivery` and the `cron.agents`/`cron.creators` `delivery` and `failureAlert` routes; built-in aliases such as `gchat` pass). An unknown `cron.failureAlert.channel` only warns, so existing configs keep loading. `cron.agents` keys that resolve to the same agent id (`ops` and `OPS`) are rejected with the same check `agents.entries` uses. `openclaw doctor`'s delivery-target advisory also lists defaults whose channel plugin is not active.
- **Compatibility.**
  - With no defaults configured, nothing changes.
  - Existing jobs that already store a route, including routes pinned at creation by earlier releases, keep it.
  - The new keys are optional and the `cron` block stays strict.

### Behavior matrix (tested)

| Config | Job delivery | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| global only | announce, no route | global default |
| agent only (owner matches) | announce, no route | agent default |
| global + agent | announce, no route, owner has entry | agent default, whole (no global field merge) |
| global + agent | announce, no route, other owner | global default |
| any | names channel / to / threadId / accountId / owner target | job's own route |
| any | `none` / `webhook` | unchanged |
| none configured, or only another agent's entry | announce, no route | unchanged (creating chat / remembered route) |
| creator + agent + global | announce, no route, human profile creator | creator default, whole |
| creator only | announce, no route, human profile creator | creator default |
| creator + agent + global | announce, no route, agent creator with delegating human profile | creator default |
| creator + agent + global | announce, no route; creator legacy (no `createdActor`), channel-only, unknown, agent, system, other profile, or case-different id | agent default (no creator default) |
| creator + agent + global | names a route, owner target, `none`, `webhook` | unchanged by the creator default |
| global failureAlert + agent failureAlert | any | agent route fields, global tuning |
| global + agent + creator failureAlert | human profile creator | creator route fields, global tuning |
| creator with only `delivery` | failure alert | agent failure route |
| global `enabled: false` + agent failureAlert | no job failureAlert | no alert |
| per-job failureAlert | any | per-job route |
| primary default, no failure route | announce | alert to primary default (thread kept) |
| primary default and agent failure route | announce | primary to default, failures to agent route, independently |
| owner only in session key | route-less | session-key agent's defaults in preview, completion, and alerts |

### Docs

- `docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md`: new "Default destinations" section with the precedence table, the `none` decision, the session-route decision, and failure-route layering.
- `docs/gateway/config-automation.md`: `cron.delivery`, `cron.agents`, and `cron.creators` reference, plus the updated failure precedence.
- Configuration reference index, schema help and labels, and the generated config baseline.

## Verification

- Typecheck:
  - `pnpm tsgo:core`: pass.
  - `pnpm tsgo:test:src`: all shards pass.
  - `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: pass.
- Lint and format: `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on touched files are clean.
- Schema and docs generation:
  - `pnpm check:base-config-schema`: ok.
  - `pnpm config:docs:check`: ok, after `config:docs:gen`.
  - `pnpm format:docs:check`: clean.
  - `pnpm docs:check-links`: 0 broken.
  - `docs:check-links:anchors`: 6 misses, all in pre-existing release notes and none in touched pages.
  - `git diff --check`: clean.
- Focused tests (`pnpm test <files>`), all passing. New tests:
  - `src/cron/delivery-defaults.test.ts`: the matrix above, including every non-creator actor shape, legacy jobs with no `createdActor`, the `none`/`webhook` interaction, and failure vs primary resolved independently.
  - `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`: no route pinning when a Gateway, agent, or creator default applies (requesting or delegating profile); still pins for another agent's default, another profile's default, or a requester without a profile.
  - `src/cron/delivery-preview.test.ts`: real `resolveDeliveryTarget`. A route-less `current` job previews to the default; an explicit `to` still wins; another agent's default is ignored; a human-profile creator's default beats the agent default.
  - `src/gateway/server-cron-completion.test.ts`: completion uses the session-key owner's default rather than the resolver fallback agent.
- Existing suites rerun, all passing:
  - delivery-plan, failure-alerts (account routing, outcome, persistence), service failure-alert and delivery-plan;
  - isolated delivery-target, session-run, server-cron-completion;
  - gateway cron validation, request-validation, webchat-delivery, caller-scope, ownership-matrix;
  - config schema, metadata, hints, control-ui contract, zod agents and core;
  - run-recovery, run-finalization and scheduler-actor workers;
  - after the creator layer: delivery-plan, failure-alerts (account routing, outcome, persistence), gateway cron validation, request-validation, webchat-delivery, caller-scope, ownership-matrix, delegated-creator and creator-transports integration, server-cron-completion, isolated delivery-target, and config schema, help quality, hints, field metadata, control-ui contract, zod core, base generated schema (22 files, all passing).
- Mutation checks:
  - The cron-tool tests fail against the base `cron-tool.ts`.
  - Creator mutants each killed by the new tests: dropping the creator from the scope, swapping creator and agent order, dropping the creator failure route, attributing any actor id as a creator, and case-folding creator keys.
  - The completion owner test fails when the session-key owner resolution is removed.
- Independent review: three structured review passes (P0 to P2). The first raised two findings:
  - Missing `defaultAgentId` on finalization and skip snapshots: verified false, the snapshots already carry it.
  - Completion owner taken from `job.agentId` only: valid, fixed by the shared scope helper.
  - The second pass on the agent/global diff was clean.
  - The third pass on the final diff, including the creator layer, was clean. Its one open doubt (whether worker-loaded jobs carry `createdActor`) checks out: failure-alert workers load jobs through the same row decoder (`loadedCronStoreFromRows`) whose `createdActor` the run-time execution context already reads.
- Validation follow-up (head after `7d661bba`):
  - Lint fix: the create-time default check no longer casts raw cron tool input to `CronDelivery`; `check:assertion-safety-ratchet` (`src/cron/delivery-context.ts: 2 > 1`) now passes.
  - `pnpm check:changed --base 5c410ef4eb5`: all lanes pass except the dead-export scan, whose entries are all in files this PR does not touch (same list on the base).
  - New `src/config/config.cron-default-destinations.test.ts`: unknown channel rejected at each of the five default paths, global `cron.failureAlert` only warns, known channels and built-in aliases pass, `last`/webhook routes skipped, `cron.agents` keys differing by case rejected.
  - `src/commands/doctor/cron/warnings.test.ts`: defaults on inactive channels are listed; active defaults stay quiet.
  - Mutation checks: dropping the load-time issue, the `cron.agents` duplicate check, or the doctor default scan each fails the new tests.
- Micro-benchmark of `resolveCronDeliveryPlan`. Node 24.22, 64-job mix, 20k-iteration warmup, 15 samples of 5k iterations, median ns per call, base (`5c410ef4`) vs head, three runs:
  - no defaults argument: about 24.5 → 30.5;
  - defaults scope with nothing configured: about 33;
  - defaults configured: about 178. That path resolves and normalizes the default route and scans agent keys.
  - Plan resolution happens a few times per run, so this is negligible next to run cost. I moved the default lookup before the eligibility normalization so unconfigured Gateways pay only the lookup.

### What was not tested

- No live channel send. Proof is through the real target resolution and completion paths with synthetic channel I/O.
- `openclaw doctor` does not flag an unknown agent id under `cron.agents`.
- Config-load validation checks that a default's channel plugin is installed, not that the channel is configured or the recipient exists; doctor covers inactive plugins, and a wrong recipient still surfaces at send time.
- No Control UI changes or checks beyond the generated schema metadata.

### Open questions

- **Opting a job back into creating-chat routing.** Once a default is configured, a route-less job cannot return to the creating conversation, because `channel: "last"` is also the stored CLI default. Should there be an explicit opt-out, such as `delivery.target: "source"`? Today such a job must name its `channel`/`to`.
- **Failure routes have no `threadId`.** Telegram topics use the `-100…:topic:N` form, matching the existing `cron.failureAlert` shape. Should failure routes get a `threadId` field for parity?

prs.title: docs(release): keep blocked release work moving
prs.body:
## Problem

Release owners can idle for hours while one long validation lane or operator decision is pending, repeatedly re-arming an unchanged watcher instead of preparing the next eligible validation or proving independent lanes. Guidance also needs to preserve the one-active-parent rule and avoid dispatching immediately before an approved port is about to land.

## Solution

Add one focused blocked-state rule to the release-owner lifecycle:

- keep either the active FRV or a named blocker/proof lane in flight;
- pre-stage the next eligible FRV inputs and run independent proofs without dispatching a duplicate parent;
- wait for an approved port expected within about 15 minutes before dispatching;
- ask decisions non-blockingly with a recommended reversible default while independent work continues;
- send one notification for an unanswered question and avoid watcher re-arms with no new transition or work.

## Evidence

- `pnpm format:docs:check` — passed (1,413 files clean)
- `pnpm docs:check-links` — passed (16,398 internal links, 0 broken)

No runtime code or release behavior was executed or changed.

prs.title: fix(runtime): expire discovery and room caches on elapsed time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two process-local cache windows use wall time. A backward clock correction keeps an expired Mantle discovery catalog or Nextcloud Talk room kind fresh longer than its defined lifetime.

## User Impact

Use native elapsed time for Mantle's one-hour discovery cache and Nextcloud Talk's room-kind cache. Existing TTLs, credential/account scopes, payloads and policies stay unchanged. IAM-token expiry and pricing dates remain wall-clock/epoch operations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both owners are extensions, so their existing private caches now use `performance.now()` for recording and checking elapsed windows. No new timers, managers, SDK exports, configuration or migrations are needed.

Credits @wangmiao0668000666. Original commits from #193066 (`7c4c1b8e`, `c45cc5cd`) and #193082 (`f3ea8175`, `61e29e17`) are retained via cherry-picks. This sweep supersedes those two fixes; the lead decides their closure after landing. Conditional UI proposal #193070 by the same author is **not included**: this sweep makes no built-UI, screenshot or gzip-size claim.

The allocation was removed. Mantle expiry coverage now extends existing strict-refresh/recovery cases; room expiry extends credential-scope cases with paired wall/elapsed clock mocks. Existing response fixtures were consolidated without weakening failure/release assertions, and the durable inbound retry consumer also fakes performance alongside Date. Whole patch: production +4/-4 (8 gross lines); tests +24/-24 (net 0).

## Evidence

Built Linux Node 24.22.1 Gateways, task-owned profiles/state, synthetic credentials and faithful local services. Only process-local `Date.now()` was stepped. **No system-clock change, performance acceleration or TTL modification.**

Detailed receipts: [Mantle real-TTL Gateway proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193147#issuecomment-6648315225) · [Nextcloud Talk authenticated room-cache proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193147#issuecomment-6648315575).

### Mantle discovery

- Two immediate authenticated `models.list` refresh RPCs reuse one real HTTPS discovery request, proving the shipped Gateway path reaches the cache.
- After **3,605,120.823 ms of real elapsed time**, the fixture adds a model and the stepped Gateways' Date.now moves backward two hours.
- Main keeps the stale catalog (1 total discovery GET); candidate refreshes and lists the new model (2 GETs).
- No-step main and candidate controls both refresh normally (2 GETs each).
- The real registered provider uses its guarded HTTPS transport through the documented operator proxy with task-owned CA trust. No fetch/SDK mock or TLS/auth/SSRF bypass.

Mantle was exercised at `34c5fe53e37400893d03e19c7fc279bdf28a5691`. Its entire extension tree and the complete Gateway/SDK `src/` and `packages/` trees are identical in the final combined candidate `10c1f02a981d2d0b196d391dec4d62349292e2f6`; only disabled-in-those-lanes Nextcloud source/tests were subsequently added. That unchanged-input proof is retained honestly, not relabeled as a different executed artifact.

### Nextcloud Talk

- Own built-Gateway proof at the final combined candidate, normally installed development plugin, real HMAC-authenticated webhooks, Basic-authenticated OCS room lookups and verified signed bot replies.
- Two initial direct-room messages reuse one room GET per Gateway and produce two replies.
- After **305,155.867 ms of real elapsed time**, the fixture supplies a type-3 room snapshot and only stepped Gateway Date.now moves backward ten minutes.
- Main-step retains stale direct classification (1 room GET, 3 replies); candidate-step refreshes and applies the existing disabled-group policy (2 GETs, 2 replies).
- Both no-step controls also refresh and terminate with `group_policy_disabled` (2 GETs, 2 replies each). All 12 actual message webhooks have durable acceptance markers; every Basic/HMAC check matches.

This is catalog/room-cache behavior against local protocol fixtures, not live AWS/Nextcloud operation or paid inference. No UI behavior is claimed.

Both builds, targeted format/lint and 47 focused tests passed. Pre-fix witnesses fail as intended: Mantle serves stale data instead of attempting the expired refresh (2 cases); all three room credential-scope cases skip the required refetch. The original #193082 `prefer-const` red was its own code and its contributor correction is retained; fresh sweep lint passes.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous timing without persisted-state or configuration changes. Blast radius is the elapsed validity of these two extension caches. Credential scopes, epoch expiries, channel policies, UI recovery windows and other providers are unchanged.

prs.title: feat(sandbox): add lightweight local SRT backend
prs.body:
Related: #163540

## What Problem This Solves

Adds an optional Docker-free sandbox backend that confines local command and file writes to admitted writable roots while keeping managed skills and readonly resources protected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SRT plugin uses the existing sandbox SDK and one filesystem policy for command and file tools. Host-owned custody contains command descendants; the backend retains the host authority callback and checks it before new effects. Cleanup remains available after revocation. Windows execution stays disabled before provisioning because the pinned runtime cannot establish safe shared-account ownership and rollback.

This update replaces an argv-shape assertion with launched exec-spec effects, adds a regression for a failed exec-spec build releasing its own custody lease, and makes qualified live runs fail when SRT is unavailable. It also records representative installed macOS workflow results. No host runtime logic changed in this update; installed proof therefore uses a compatible released host rather than a locally built host.

## User Impact

Operators can select the optional `srt` backend on macOS or Linux. This is write-focused confinement: host reads remain broad except explicitly hidden workspace paths. External npm/ClawHub distribution is configured, but sponsorship/distribution and security-owner acceptance remain maintainer decisions.

macOS custody necessarily denies `setsid`, `setpgid`, and `posix_spawn`. In the installed qualification, shell pipelines, an existing Git repository's status/diff/empty commit, Node itself, ripgrep and tar/gzip worked. Node child-process APIs failed with `EPERM`; npm/pnpm scripts, the system Python launcher, a make/cc build, and Git initialization with default hook templates failed. A successful version command does not qualify a build workflow. Maintainers still need to accept these restrictions or narrow initial platform support. Windows execution is not qualified or enabled. No merge, platform-acceptance, or product-direction decision is made here.

## Evidence

Candidate: `0c0704c303ede0a8f4ca97c9f2fd4ba659ae2ed3` (proposal3 delta above `119c99b81b9974c6c297d1f130c96fd5ecd4474c`).

Real installed proof ran on macOS 15.3.1 arm64 / Node 26.5.0 with released **OpenClaw 2026.10.3 (59cb447)** and the final **@openclaw/srt-sandbox 2026.10.3**, packed through `scripts/plugin-npm-publish.sh --pack`. The host was installed into an isolated prefix, the plugin through the installed CLI, and real Gateway `/v1/responses` turns selected real exec/write tools. A scripted model fixture supplied tool requests; it did not replace admission, sandboxing, execution, filesystem operations, or cancellation.

| Installed check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Allowed exec and file writes | Both exact contents landed in the workspace |
| Exec and file writes to managed skills / outside writable roots | Denied; files absent; existing outside file unchanged |
| Deny-policy network | Connection to a host-reachable fixture endpoint rejected |
| Allow-policy network | Same final artifact returned HTTP 200 through SRT's proxy with ambient `NO_PROXY` bypass cleared |
| Real Gateway-owned HTTP disconnect during a running deferred command | Two processes existed before cancellation; none remained after 21 ms; releasing the flag produced neither main nor descendant write |
| Disconnect after sandbox preparation while model response was held | Held request included sandbox context; after release, neither requested exec nor file write occurred and no corresponding tool result was emitted |
| Shutdown | No retained pin-owner or proof-root processes remained |

The HTTP request's owner abort signal cancels the admitted run. An exploratory `chat.abort` returned `aborted:false` for this HTTP flow and is **not** claimed as revocation proof. This evidence does not claim a direct replay of an exported retained bridge after owner retirement.

Artifact SHA256:

```text

openclaw-srt-sandbox-2026.10.3.tgz
90bd5ba600a61b80a2d49767987afebc9c1b0fd780a932e7867eea92d28a43bf
```

Focused validation:

- Removing only `custody.release()` made exactly the new lease-directory assertion fail (8 other tests passed); restoring the production bytes returned all 9 tests to green. No mutation remains.

The availability helper and network test bytes match this candidate. The historical 168-pass/15-skip suite is not installed-artifact evidence.

prs.title: fix(secrets): file references lose whitespace in JSON Pointer keys
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

File SecretRefs with whitespace at the end of a JSON Pointer select the wrong key through config builders, or fail resolution when supplied directly.

## User Impact

`/token ` selects the literal `"token "` key and remains distinct from `/token`. Missing references retain the correct failure classification and runtime owner. Existing env, store, and exec ID trimming is preserved. No schema, provider permissions, public SDK, or credential-redaction policy changes.

IDs still follow the documented grammar: the single-value ID is exactly `value`, and JSON Pointers start with `/`. Whitespace inside a pointer is literal key data; padded malformed IDs are rejected rather than silently repaired.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing reference-contract owner for source-aware normalization in CLI inputs, resolver grouping, missing-ref matching, and runtime attribution. This is the same input-preservation defect class as recently merged external contribution #192796. Four callers consume that one rule; no new state or fallback is introduced.

## Evidence

Real source CLI on Linux/Node 24, in a secretless container with isolated state and a synthetic private JSON vault; no mocked resolver, live credentials, remote provider, or model calls:

- Persist `config set gateway.auth.token --ref-source file --ref-provider vault --ref-id '/token '`: the original base saves `/token`; the fix saves `/token `.
- With only `{"token ":"SYNTHETIC_SELECTED"}`, `config set ... --dry-run --json` through builder flags and strict JSON SecretRefs: the original base fails; the fix succeeds with one reference checked.
- With only `{"token":"SYNTHETIC_NEIGHBOR"}`, the trailing-space reference: the original builder incorrectly succeeds; fixed builder and raw JSON both fail. Ordinary `/token` succeeds as a control.

The original real-CLI reproduction failed with four violations. The current committed HEAD replay passes all six behavior/control checks with zero violations. Regressions cover all three CLI input modes (flags, batch, patch), distinct batched file resolution, exact missing-ref identity, runtime attribution, and non-file compatibility.

Current HEAD validation: 151 focused tests across seven files, touched format, typed lint, core types, and touched-test types passed. Command: `pnpm test src/cli/config-cli-input.test.ts src/secrets/resolve.test.ts src/secrets/runtime-degradation-attribution.test.ts src/secrets/ref-contract.test.ts src/secrets/exec-secret-ref-id-parity.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.secrets.integration.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.reference-values.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Independent static review covered the complete final base-to-HEAD diff and affected consumers, with no actionable findings. Linux/POSIX proof does not establish Windows end-to-end behavior or live model/provider behavior.

## CI Repair and Remaining Gates

The original [CI run 41880488067](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41880488067) failed the test-line ratchet and six UI E2E shards. Production types, changed lint, core lint stripes, touched-test types, and npm/config checks passed.

The original fix is rebased, without conflicts or patch changes (`git range-diff`: equivalent), onto fixed main `54c9f7afe4236814ad8d43fe5d5a3ec2121eb762`. That base includes the maintainer's budget reconciliation #192905 and relevant UI repairs #192885, #192907, #192913, #192914, #192966, #192993, and #193026. Exact old failed assertions were matched to 39 changed assertion records across the six shards. These incorporated repairs do not resolve every upstream CI failure; the current-head results follow below.

**The real local test-line ratchet still fails.** On this fixed base/HEAD it reports 6,477,587 lines against ceiling 6,477,536, a 51-line deficit. The base alone has 6,477,519 lines against ceiling 6,477,468, the same deficit. This patch adds exactly 68 regression lines and a separate allocation of exactly 68. It does not change the shared scalar or add unallocated debt. The failed command and exact attribution are retained; successful focused checks do not waive this gate. No extra allocation, unrelated test deletion, or shared budget increase is included.

### Current-head hosted outcome

[CI run 41958528726](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41958528726) completed for `b653fc1f020fd8da09ac87d3b4123e37cfe4874a`: 48 jobs passed, 28 skipped, and 7 failed (the ratchet, five UI shards, and the aggregate gate). Production types, all selected test-type/lint stripes, and the selected Node test lanes passed. UI shards 4/7 and 7/7 passed. This is **not CI-green**.

- **Hosted budget:** [the actual failing job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41958528726/job/127019479036) reports 6,478,220 lines against ceiling 6,478,171: a 49-line deficit and net test delta +68. Its merge checkout is `2fc3272a944f0df78e5b94ada9d70efcd445e67b`, based on newer main `69d0f4c2f73761fa04cf61068b8bccc70bb98d49`. The exact merge diff is still the same nine-file patch, with +68 tests and +68 allocation. That main tree therefore has 6,478,152 lines against ceiling 6,478,103, also a 49-line deficit. The local 51 and hosted 49 are different base snapshots. A scheduled main ratchet can pass via the checker's nonpositive-delta rule despite existing debt; that does not make this PR's failed ratchet green. Shared budget reconciliation requires maintainer action.
- **UI attribution:** all eight distinct assertion/wait signatures from the five failed PR shards also occur in the completed UI jobs of [scheduled main run 41955318723](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41955318723), head `79d467a82ca886ee9a9051b8cb155d401ef134c0`. Comparison uses file plus exact expected/received values or waiting locator, rather than shard number. The CI-generated report uses older completed main run 41948437406 and job names only; it calls PR shard 5 "new", but the identical mobile geometry failure occurs in newer main shard 6. No PR-only assertion signature was found in these captured logs. This is observed matching-main evidence, not an exact-base replay or a waiver of the failing checks.

Some case titles are redacted in the hosted logs. In particular, two responsive-welcome failures share the same redacted title and geometry error; they count as two failed cases but one distinct signature. prs.title: fix(oc-path): find rejects quoted filenames containing question marks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw path resolve` can read a quoted literal filename such as `report?.jsonc`, but `path find` rejects the same parsed filename as a wildcard and exits 2. The parser has already separated the query string; a remaining `?` in `pattern.file` is literal filename data.

## Change and user impact

Keep the existing post-parse file-slot `*` refusal, but stop misclassifying literal `?` as a wildcard. No parser/query grammar, filesystem resolution, input ceiling, public API, SDK, config or permission change. The CLI guide adds one quoted-filename example.

Both zhangguiping-xydt contributor commits are preserved. Production remains **+3/−2**, five changed lines including explanatory comments.

## Regression consolidation

Removed the standalone 47-line regression file and its allocation. The literal-filename case is now part of the existing CLI find/resolve matrix, sharing its already-loaded Commander harness and fixtures. It checks two values, query-suffix preservation, successful resolve round-trips and unchanged source bytes. The no-match case is retained as a matrix row across the file variants, and the existing `*` refusal case remains.

Whole-PR tests are **+21/−26, net −5**, with no added test file, import suite, allocation, baseline increase or lint exception. Equivalent related outcome assertions are grouped to keep the existing suite within its unchanged line cap. The literal `?` file case retains its non-Windows applicability boundary.

## Evidence

**New exact-head Linux proof:** frozen installs and full builds of main **f6428243dcf677bf9f7d479f74aa68a77579ed3b** and candidate **1bd6f8f62e97be7246190f2429cdc898edae3004**, run through the actual public `openclaw.mjs --profile … path find` / `path resolve` CLI in secretless Linux/arm64 Docker, Node **24.22.1**.

- `report?.jsonc`: main resolve works, but find refuses with `OC_PATH_FILE_WILDCARD_UNSUPPORTED` / exit 2. Candidate find returns **first and second**, count **2**, exit **0**.
- `nested?/batch?.jsonc`: same baseline refusal; candidate returns both distinct expected values.
- Every returned path retains `?session=literal-proof` and resolves back to identical match data.
- Ordinary-file find/resolve is unchanged. A file-slot `*.jsonc` wildcard still returns the explicit refusal and exit 2, not an ENOENT failure.
- All three input files are SHA-256 hashed before/after every command, with identical bytes throughout. The CLI uses normal working-directory resolution, not a file override or parser patch.

The committed existing-suite filename case fails on main for the intended status/count mismatch and passes on the candidate. **76/76** CLI suite tests pass; repository lint passes for both changed TypeScript files, and formatting passes for those files plus the documentation.

Detailed native CLI results, commands, session-scoped round-trips and hashes: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193123#issuecomment-6648529261.

This is Linux/POSIX filename evidence, not a Windows claim; literal question marks are not valid Windows filenames. No model, provider, channel or real credentials are needed.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the incorrect `path find` refusal without migrations or stored-data changes. Blast radius is read-only searches of quoted literal-question-mark filenames; file-slot `*` refusal, query parsing, path resolution and file protections retain their existing behavior.

prs.body:
## Repair and validation update — November 4, 2026

Current head: `8149b98130829cb7d83ec153c9bc9355bcc7cc64`. Validation completed November 5 UTC (November 4 Pacific).

The follow-up fixes Core secret preparation: a remote-client token no longer deactivates the local password SecretRef. Local-token suppression and remote fallback rules remain intact. Original contributor history is preserved.

[Successful exact-candidate validation run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41944079495) (proof harness `41fd6f3290417aa078a1de9cbfc4114d247c389f`):

- Original-Core regression remains red; repaired Core tests, focused native tests, actual app build, scoped lint and both typechecks passed.
- All eight app phases passed: four fresh candidate credential scenarios, both v2026.10.9 baselines, and both dollar/braced-shorthand candidate upgrades. Independent inspection of retained Gateway logs confirms expected authentication and successful protected `config.get` on the same native UI connection in every phase.
- Authored auth, environment, named preferences and user document preservation assertions passed in all eight phases. Both manual upgrades completed Doctor-owned credential migration and retained auth/workspace through service replacement. All six scenario cleanups passed.
- This proves attach-only app launches against a ready service. The harness applies the existing readiness gate before each app launch, including after upgrade; authentication/preservation assertions and timeouts were not weakened.
- **Unresolved startup-recovery limitation:** in [prior run 41933671638](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41933671638), the braced-shorthand candidate exhausted initial control operations while the replacement Gateway was starting, then authenticated without issuing protected `config.get`. The ready-service replay does not demonstrate a fix for that behavior.
- PR CI test checks and the CI workflow's `openclaw/ci-gate` check run passed. The separate current `openclaw/ci-gate` status is **failure**, with `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` pending: “A maintainer must approve the current PR revision.” Thus the aggregate gate is not green. Fresh independent source review and local ClawSweeper review of `3481ca33..8149b981` previously found no actionable correctness/security findings; those reviews do not satisfy the outstanding maintainer approval.

**Requested native/upgrade proof complete; maintainer security approval remains outstanding.** No merge performed. Historical evidence below retains its original revision and limitations; historical pending proof statements are superseded only by the exact-candidate evidence above.

---

Closes #128171

## What Problem This Solves

The macOS app could not authenticate to a local Gateway when `gateway.auth.token` or `gateway.auth.password` used a typed env SecretRef. The Gateway supports those inputs, but the native endpoint store previously handled only strings.

## What Changed

- Resolve supported typed env SecretRefs from the actual Gateway LaunchAgent environment, with the app environment as fallback.
- Enforce the configured env provider and allowlist; malformed, unsupported, denied, or unresolved refs fail closed.
- Keep configured refs authoritative over same-surface ambient fallbacks.
- Match Core's implicit-mode behavior: two configured token/password inputs remain ambiguous; a concrete opposite-side fallback suppresses typed-ref materialization; after materialization, password is inferred before token.
- Match Core startup when a typed local password coexists with `gateway.remote.token`: the local password wins unless an ambient Gateway token causes Core to leave that password ref inactive; when token auth is active, preserve LaunchAgent-token precedence before the remote-token fallback.
- Pass only the selected credential into the native Gateway handshake.

## User Impact

Users can keep local Gateway credentials in supported typed environment SecretRefs without breaking the macOS app connection. Invalid or disallowed references remain fail-closed, and the native app follows the same token/password selection behavior as Core.

## Evidence

### Current evidence refresh, 2026-10-28

Current public head is `3481ca33a1bf69a445814f0c620e12719c78f947` (tree `f9061f44fb6a5815d8ab0e0f3a5391a9cac3a758`). Its merge preserves `c17b72d3538f81e934caaa4d5c373cf90e90c513` and integrates main `9a5581b4ce230381e3f200a62be4cdbe78e41c19`. GitHub blob identities confirm that both PR-owned Swift files are unchanged from `c17b72d353`. Contributor credit and the prior source and native evidence below remain attached to their stated revisions.

[Canonical CI run 40678248294](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40678248294) and its CI gate succeeded for head `3481ca33a1bf69a445814f0c620e12719c78f947`. This run contains 5 successful and 38 skipped jobs. Both macOS Swift phases and the iOS build phase were skipped. [macOS and shared Periphery run 40678248230](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40678248230) completed seven selected jobs successfully, including both shared-kit producers and the intersection; the iOS dead-code scan was skipped. Skipped native tests and successful static scans do not establish packaged-app authentication.

No new native run or fresh ClawSweeper verdict is claimed. The durable review below remains bound to `ff41c754`, and the shorthand correction at `c17b72d353` remains a source disposition. Exact-current-head focused tests, packaged-app coverage of the later remote-fallback combinations, and a stable-release upgrade retaining existing shorthand settings remain required. Historical native runs, the beta2 port, and earlier CI are preserved below and are not relabeled as current-head proof.

### Historical evidence status refresh, 2026-10-27

At that refresh, the public head was `c17b72d3538f81e934caaa4d5c373cf90e90c513`. The [completed CI run 39411875583](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39411875583) succeeded on tested merge `44577cf085aada61cbbfb40cbbd236c63a28518a`, combining this head with main `d8c96213c5cf40295863fb5fb6d347e1f9caf6b7`. Its unique job inventory contains **5 successful and 37 skipped jobs**, with no failures or pending jobs. These are this run's jobs, not a sum of duplicate check/status surfaces; skipped jobs are not passing runtime proof.

The [exact delta since reviewed head ff41c754](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/ff41c754d9d4aa8a70bf2da9422ade5047d11c9c...c17b72d3538f81e934caaa4d5c373cf90e90c513) changes only the endpoint source and its test file. `configuredInput` now classifies trimmed shorthand through `envSecretRefName` before auth-surface selection, and the existing handshake matrix adds both `$GW_PASSWORD` and `${GW_PASSWORD}` with the available service token. This addresses the source change requested by the earlier P1 finding and preserves the original shorthand/fallback intent. It is a source disposition, not a new exact-head ClawSweeper verdict or packaged-app result.

The [durable review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/128175#issuecomment-5385443900) explicitly says maintaining Swift/Core parity alone does not require another product decision. Earlier parity-approval language below records historical status and is superseded on that point. Maintainer acceptance remains outstanding. **Packaged-app proof for the later remote-fallback combinations and a stable-release upgrade retaining existing shorthand settings remain unproven.** The beta2-port test evidence below is not relabeled as current-head packaged-app proof. Earlier pending-CI statements are historical and superseded only by the completed run identified here. No new runtime test, whole-current-tree review, or upgrade demonstration is claimed by this refresh.


### Historical follow-up, 2026-10-20

Follow-up head: [c17b72d353](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c17b72d3538f81e934caaa4d5c373cf90e90c513).

- Classify the existing `$NAME` and `${NAME}` shorthand forms as references before implicit auth-mode selection. A missing password reference no longer suppresses an available service token. Explicit modes and malformed or literal values keep their existing paths.
- The two-file follow-up passed scoped P0–P3 Codex review with no actionable findings. This is source review, not runtime proof.
- The equivalent fix was compiled in the beta2 native integration. Its 13 credential-test functions passed in a deny-default OS sandbox, including the handshake matrix with both new shorthand cases. Strict SwiftLint, SwiftFormat, native i18n verification, and `git diff --check` passed. This is synthetic proof of the beta2 port, not an exact-head packaged-app run or real Keychain, GUI, identity, or upgrade proof.
- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39411875583) started automatically after the push; no completed verdict is claimed here. Maintainer parity and acceptance decisions remain open.

### Historical candidate evidence

Current PR candidate: `1ad4bcb852b2266950eea45c077ee023e1a42358`, merged with current `openclaw/openclaw:main` at `1e13fc8abcd942ca398a89ca5560da11a1d46c41`. GitHub confirms the PR is OPEN and the head/base match those revisions. The branch is `MERGEABLE` (no content conflict), but the merge state is BLOCKED by required CI. The PR delta against current main is limited to `GatewayEndpointStore.swift` and `GatewayEndpointStoreTests.swift` (+118/-8 production, +477/-1 tests).

- The prior exact-head CI run found a SwiftFormat `conditionalAssignment` style error before compilation. The follow-up changes only the expression form and is being validated in current-head CI.
- Scoped Codex autoreview on this exact head returned `scoped-clean` at P2 with no findings (confidence 0.76). Its report used the selected diff and supplied Core auth sources; it does not claim runtime verification. The report is preserved in the task-local review artifacts.
- ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head and reported no actionable code or security findings. It marked merge blocked pending the macOS auth owner's decision on the ongoing Swift/Core credential-selection parity contract, and notes there is no fresh packaged-app runtime demonstration for the remote-token fallback.
- Exact-head GitHub CI run [36282160728](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36282160728) completed with the `macos-swift (tests)` job cancelled while its Swift test step was running; no Swift test result is available. The aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` failed solely because the selected `macos-swift` check was cancelled. Preflight, `security-fast`, `native-i18n`, all three macOS Node shards, Swift lint, `macos-swift (packages)`, shared OpenClawKit scans, macOS Periphery, OpenGrep, actionlint, changed-path scan, and security review passed. The iOS Periphery scan was skipped by scope.
- A rerun was requested for the cancelled job, but GitHub refused it with `Must have admin rights to Repository`. The Swift test verdict and aggregate CI gate therefore require a repository admin to rerun.
- `git diff --check` passes. This Windows host has no Swift toolchain, so native Swift execution relies on exact-head GitHub CI.
- The app-to-Gateway runtime proof below was performed on the earlier candidate `23b805fa3821e06e882d846843d96da2252a91bd`. It is historical evidence and does not demonstrate the added remote-token fallback cases on the current candidate.

Native validation on 2026-09-04:

Validated candidate: `23b805fa3821e06e882d846843d96da2252a91bd`.

The main refresh preserves @TheAngryPit's original repair, @CassieMei's carried
auth-mode and precedence corrections, and all five contributor commits. Its sole
content conflict was two independent insertions in the endpoint store; both the
typed-reference resolver and main's source-snapshot helper are retained.

### Before

[Native baseline run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33910257814)
used unchanged production main `606d9ab82afdb28ebaad33896e41811b96ad87c7`.
The actual ad-hoc packaged app sent no token for a supported typed custom env
reference that the healthy managed local Gateway could resolve. It received
`token_missing`. A fresh literal-token control authenticated as `openclaw-macos`
and completed `config.get`.

### After

[Exact-candidate native run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33916513675)
reconstructed and checked the exact candidate tree/commit, verified its signature,
built the real app through the normal package script, and installed each real
local service through `gateway install --wrapper`. The wrapper supplied normal
diagnostics and, only in the app-env fallback cases, the service's synthetic env
value. Every case used fresh synthetic profile/pairing state.

| Cases | Native result |
| --- | --- |
| Service-only typed token and password | Shared authentication and completed `config.get` |
| Different app/service values for one ref, both modes | Service value selected; completed `config.get` |
| Supported app-env fallback, both modes | Service snapshot lacks the ref value; completed `config.get` |
| Explicit modes with inactive opposite refs | Correct active credential; completed `config.get` |
| Typed token + ambient password; typed password + ambient token | Same password/token selection as Core; completed `config.get` |
| Denied and unresolved active refs, both modes | No credential sent despite a valid ambient fallback; no protected request completed |
| All four rejected setups corrected and relaunched | Shared authentication and completed `config.get` |

The protocol evidence correlates `openclaw-macos`, mode `ui`, to successful
protected responses on the same connections. Separate Control UI traffic is not
used as a substitute. Rejected-ref probes kept the server healthy with the
existing reload-off option; no auth or pairing policy was relaxed. The corrected
setups connect normally.

- `GatewayEndpointStoreTests`: 83 tests passed on the exact candidate, including
  provider/allowlist rules, handshake auth, legacy strings and lifecycle siblings.
- All 14 managed services were uninstalled/unloaded, all app phases stopped, and
  all synthetic Keychains were deleted successfully.
- The earlier obscured screenshots are not counted as visual auth evidence.
- Native proof does not replace the fresh independent review or required PR CI.

### Prior ClawSweeper finding and current scope

The fresh ClawSweeper finding was checked against Gateway startup at the exact
Core revision it reviewed. Startup's `hasGatewayTokenCandidate` excludes
`gateway.remote.token`, so a typed local password ref is materialized when no
ambient/local token candidate suppresses it; after materialization Core infers
password mode before token. The native selector and connect-frame regression
now preserve that password. If an ambient Gateway token is present, Core leaves
the password ref inactive and the native selector uses the token surface.

Against current main, the production delta is +118/-8 and the test delta is
+477/-1. The added native code
implements the existing typed-env contract; it adds no configuration option,
policy, schema, remote-auth behavior, or file/exec/store-ref support. Keep the
native/Core parity cases aligned when the shared auth contract changes.

The material below is retained contributor history at its stated inputs, not a
replacement for this current baseline and exact-candidate proof.

## Historical contributor evidence

Historical contributor head: `4e35b1caf03687853b8cc9dd47f8d5c6ea81bb93`

The native proof was built from the exact two-file PR patch (`patch-id 7040be749e604bbda4f9be0b44ed15605a058bd9`) over frozen base `9d79bf3f8c5f18f7c35d028d57402f5085659640`.

- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter GatewayEndpointStoreTests` — 75/75 passed on Apple Silicon macOS.
- SwiftFormat with `config/swiftformat` — 0/2 files require formatting.
- SwiftLint 0.65.1 with `config/swiftlint.yml` — 0 violations.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Full ad-hoc `OpenClaw.app` package build completed; `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passed.
- Real isolated app-to-Gateway proof passed on port 19791: the Gateway service and app process received different synthetic values for the same typed token ref; the app selected the Gateway service value, authenticated, and completed a real `config.get` response.
- Both isolated proof PIDs stopped afterward; the installed app remained running and no operator Gateway, config, Keychain, or PortGuardian state was changed.

### Review finding and vanilla verification

ClawSweeper correctly identified that the previous selector returned no credential for mixed typed-ref/ambient cases. Before changing it, the current Core Gateway was exercised directly in two isolated profiles:

- typed token ref + ambient password: Core marked the typed token surface inactive and started with password auth;
- typed password ref + ambient token: Core marked the typed password surface inactive and started with token auth.

The native selector and regression expectations now reproduce those observed Core outcomes rather than introducing an independent token/password policy.

### Fail-before evidence

- The original typed-ref handshake cases failed before the SecretRef implementation.
- Active-mode regression cases failed before mode filtering.
- The service-vs-app conflict initially selected the stale app value before LaunchAgent precedence was corrected.
- The two mixed inferred-mode cases returned no credential before `4e35b1caf03`; both now match the isolated Core runtime outcomes.

## Historical current-main revalidation (2026-09-03)

- Current `openclaw/openclaw:main`: `9d6f5d218884b00a50746353c40170f5ab46e4db`.
- Exact PR head preserved: `4e35b1caf03687853b8cc9dd47f8d5c6ea81bb93`.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main refs/remotes/audit/pr128175` completed cleanly.
- The change is not superseded: current main resolves literal strings and legacy `$ENV`/`${ENV}` string forms, but still lacks the typed SecretRef object flow and matching credential-selection semantics covered by this PR.
- Current product checks are complete. The earlier red `PR context and evidence` result was caused by malformed heading presentation; this body restores the authored sections explicitly.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, test, and review this change. The final diff and proof were inspected against current Core behavior.

prs.title: fix(logging): mask credentials carried in a nested URL
prs.body:
## Evidence

### Rebase and fresh local validation (2026-11-05)

Head `686df1b5e533143844a3c677a9dc080f1032851a` rebases the three authored commits onto upstream `982f3b1ee2b668afafe69c352d48baef470d2d20`. The seven core redaction files are byte-identical to the previous PR head `487d593cbea`. All upstream support-file changes are retained; the only support-file diff remains the encoded-redactor entry in the wrapper inventory and the recovery fixture's real-module list. The PR remains nine files, 219 additions and 11 deletions.

Fresh checks on this rebased head, using a private frozen-lockfile install and the repository's canonical wrappers/configurations:

- `pnpm test src/logging/redact.test.ts src/logging/redact-byte-identity.test.ts src/logging/redact-large-text-security.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 63 passed.
- `pnpm test test/scripts/pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts test/scripts/update-restart-module-outcome.test.ts test/scripts/pr-git-invocation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 8 passed, 13 existing platform/runtime skips. The recovery wrapper also verifies its 19 native cases pass with no failures or skips.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the seven changed TypeScript/JavaScript files: exit 0.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` on the changed supported files: exit 0.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit` and `git diff --check`: exit 0.

These fresh local results supersede the older local lint/typecheck gaps below for the stated checks. They do not establish a full-repository CI pass. The UI E2E failures on `487d593cbea` remain older-head evidence; no same-base baseline established their cause, and they must be assessed again from fresh-head CI. The previously repaired Darwin mismatch and its older-head pass remain documented below. Maintainer security approval is still required.

### Darwin workflow/source synchronization (2026-11-03)

Head `487d593cbeac56c914d71a943499a92b5bb346de` integrates upstream `031604b4e836ffa0be30fd8d1740ef699eb345f9`, the upstream parent used by the failing Darwin workflow revision. The old PR head lacked `test/scripts/pr-git-invocation.test.ts`; both that test and `pr-tooling-darwin.yml` were introduced by upstream `39b3d94413b`. The Darwin job failed before executing the test, with `explicit test/source file(s) not found`. The integration brings the matching workflow, test and tooling source together without manually changing the logging fix.

After synchronization, the redaction, byte-identity and large-text security files pass 63 tests. Wrapper source-closure and Git-invocation tests pass 7 tests, with 13 existing platform/runtime skips on this Linux host. These targeted runs use the real workspace sources through the previously documented isolated config, the repository's canonical 120-second test timeout, and the declared dependencies installed privately for this task. The initial local source-closure replay used Vitest's default 5-second timeout and timed out; rerunning with the repository's actual timeout passes. No product test timeouts or assertions were changed. Commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.

[PR tooling Darwin now passes on head `487d593cbea`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41689707049/job/126104760194), including the previously missing Git-invocation test. This confirms the workflow/source mismatch is repaired. Full lint/typecheck remains unverified locally. Four UI E2E shards still fail on this head (1/7, 2/7, 3/7 and 5/7). Their logs contain UI assertion and browser-locator failures. The PR diff against the synchronized upstream parent changes no UI files, but attribution of these failures to an upstream baseline has not been established. They remain CI gaps, and no all-green result is claimed. Earlier CI results below are evidence for their stated older heads. Maintainer security approval is still required.

### CI integration follow-up (2026-11-02)

CI on `dffbb6741e85a2551cd98376ff698c0f7ffd7d18` exposed two missing consumers of the extracted encoded-query module: the explicit PR-wrapper source inventory and the recovery test VM's list of real modules. Both now include `redact-encoded-url`, so copied wrappers retain the import and recovery tests load the actual factory rather than an external-dependency stub. The authored evidence also now uses the template's required `## Evidence` heading.

The wrapper source-closure tests pass 3/3, and the update/restart module-outcome tests pass 19/19. These checks use the exact declared TypeScript, fs-safe and proc-safe versions installed in a task-private dependency directory; the shared installation and dependency pins are unchanged. The body passes the repository's external-PR context/evidence evaluator. On exact head `13a1f2ef0d27ffd987ee71a94db64a15e65b24df`, [CI job checks-node-changed-1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41575096698/job/125717118397) passes, including `pr-worktree-provision.test.ts` with 16 passed and 2 existing skips. The duplicate local provisioning run was stopped after that exact-head CI result became available; it is not counted as a local pass. The previously failing `checks-node-compact-small-2` also passes on that head. New CI remains required; this is not a claim that all repository gates pass.

### Whole-text follow-up (2026-11-02)

The previously documented encoded-URL gap in `redactSensitiveText` is now closed. Whole-text redaction reuses the same encoded-query matcher as line and record redaction. The default prefilter admits `%3D`, including when the credential name is entirely percent-encoded. The matcher follows non-credential callback values up to the existing nested-query depth bound, with offsets kept in the original input.

The regression covers ordinary and fully encoded credential names, one and two levels of callbacks, whole text, tool output, log lines, and log records. It also checks that disabling redaction leaves the text alone and that a non-credential query remains readable. Restoring the original production files makes it fail by exposing the synthetic credential.

`redact.test.ts` and `redact-byte-identity.test.ts` pass 59 tests in 2.53 seconds; the large-text security file passes another 4 tests. All 250 byte-identity samples and 468 recorded hash cases pass without modifying either fixture. Formatting and commit freshness checks pass. Tests ran through the repository wrapper with an isolated config that maps workspace imports to their actual source files, because the full repository config cannot load missing local dependencies. There are no parser/redactor stand-ins in this run.

Full repository lint/typecheck and a fresh real CLI run remain unverified. The lint wrapper fails while preparing package-boundary artifacts, and the full lint configuration cannot load `eslint-plugin-solid` from this machine's dependency install. A correctness-only Oxlint check passes, but is not presented as the full lint gate. CI and maintainer security approval are still required.

The shipped CLI traces below are historical evidence from the earlier revision. The new whole-text behavior is demonstrated through the public redaction APIs and regression tests above.

## What Problem This Solves

A credential inside a **nested** URL survives logging redaction. `URL_QUERY_VALUE` is `[^&#\s<>]*`, so in

```
https://x.test/?cb=https://y.test/?token=<secret>
```

the value of `cb` runs to the end of the string. `cb` is not a credential name, the nested `?token=` sits inside that value, and the `g` scan has already consumed past it. A direct `?token=<secret>` is masked correctly today — only the nested shape leaks.

The same leak has a percent-encoded form, the OAuth `redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp%2Fcb%3Faccess_token%3D<secret>` shape, where the separators are `%3F`/`%26` and the `=` is `%3D`. No assignment grammar matches that, and net-policy's URL redactor (which *does* decode nested URLs) is not on this path.

Measured on `main` with a neutral sentinel — one that no value-shape rule recognises on its own:

```
redactSensitiveText("https://x.test/?cb=https://y.test/?token=<secret>")   -> secret in full
redactSensitiveLines(["GET https://x.test/?next=%3Ftoken%3D<secret>"])      -> secret in full
redactLogRecordForTransport({message: <same>})                             -> secret in full
```

## How It Was Found

A sentinel-secret fuzz over the production redaction entry points: credential-named assignments in 33 base names × 16 spelling mutations × 15 contexts, asserting the sentinel never survives, and only demanding redaction where the shared classifier itself calls the name a credential.

A methodology note, since it bit me: the first run used an `sk-`-prefixed sentinel, which openclaw's own value-shape rules mask on their own, hiding this gap. The numbers above use a neutral sentinel.

## Fix

Nesting is handled in the scanner, not in the grammar. `visitPair()` recurses into a value **only when that value's own name is not a credential**:

```ts
if (!isSensitiveBodyKey(key)) {
  if (kind !== "url" || depth >= MAX_NESTED_URL_QUERY_DEPTH || !token.includes("?")) {
    return;
  }
  const nested = new RegExp(URL_QUERY_PAIR, "gu");
  for (let match = nested.exec(token); match; match = nested.exec(token)) {
    const nestedPrefix = match[1] ?? "";
    const nestedKey = match[2] ?? "";
    visitPair(
      nestedKey,
      match[3] ?? "",
      valueOffset + match.index + nestedPrefix.length + nestedKey.length + 1,
      depth + 1,
    );
  }
  return;
}
```

A sensitive value still reaches `splitSecretValueForMask` + `maskToken` untouched, so the mask boundary of an actual credential is never recomputed. Only `?` can open a nested assignment, because `&` cannot appear inside a value. The depth bound mirrors net-policy's `MAX_NESTED_URL_REDACTION_DEPTH`, a fresh regex per level keeps `lastIndex` out of the recursion, and offsets are threaded through so existing original-offset coverage still lines up.

**`URL_QUERY_VALUE` is byte-identical to `main`.** An earlier revision of this PR narrowed it to end at `?`; that truncated the mask of a sensitive value that legitimately contains a raw `?` (`password=***?bravo`) and was correctly caught in review. The character classes are not touched any more, which is what makes this change strictly additive: every assignment `main` masks is still masked identically, because that branch is untouched.

One preparation rule covers the encoded form on the record and line paths, masking the value of an encoded assignment whose decoded name is a credential (reusing `isSensitiveBodyKey`). Both grammars are tempered rather than greedy, so the scan stays linear — 48 KB of back-to-back encoded pairs costs **10.6 ms**.

### Keeping a serialized edit inside its scalar

A log record is redacted by scanning its *serialized JSON*, and `URL_QUERY_VALUE` admits `"`, `:`, `,` and `}`. With no trailing `&` to stop it, a value runs past the closing quote of its own scalar, and the capture was applied to every token it overlapped:

```
{"message":"https://x.test/?cb=https://y.test/?token=<secret>","level":"info"}
  ->  {"message":"https://x.test/?cb=https://y.test/?token=***","***":"***"}
```

`level` is destroyed, key and value both. `src/logging/redact-json.ts` now clamps a serialized capture to the scalar it starts in:

```ts
const firstIndex = firstIntersectingToken(tokens, capture.start);
for (let index = firstIndex; index < tokens.length; index += 1) {
  …
  if (!batch && index > firstIndex) {
    break;
  }
```

The `","` between two scalars belongs to the JSON, not to any URL or form body. Line **batches** are excluded, because there the tokens are lines of one text and a capture legitimately spans several.

**This defect is not introduced by the nested scan — `main` has it today.** A top-level credential that ends the message is enough (`{"message":"https://x.test/?token=opaque-short","level":"info"}` → `"***":"***"` on `main`), and the repo's own baseline records it: 2 of the 250 log-record entries in `redact-byte-identity-fixture.json` store `"***":"***"` where `"level":"info"` belongs, both from the *encoded form* grammar (`client%5Fsecret=`). What the nested scan changes is the reach — on `main` nested callbacks are skipped entirely, which is the leak this PR fixes — so the fix belongs on the path, not on the symptom.

## Historical evidence — shipped entry points

The real CLI, built from the earlier revision and run as a process with stdout piped. The *before* column is the same CLI with `src/logging/redact.ts` replaced by `upstream/main`'s copy and a forced rebuild; nothing else differs. Synthetic credential `nested-sentinel-0123456789abcdefghij`, hosts under the reserved `.test` TLD.

**Gateway log tail** (`openclaw logs --limit 200 --plain`, reading the configured file log):

```
# main
info gateway oauth callback …?redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?access_token=nested-sentinel-0123456789abcdefghij&page=2
warn gateway retry         …?redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.test%2Fcb%3Faccess_token%3Dnested-sentinel-0123456789abcdefghij&page=2
info gateway top-level control …?access_token=***
info gateway no credential nested …?redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?page=2

# this head
info gateway oauth callback …?redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?access_token=***&page=2
warn gateway retry         …?redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.test%2Fcb%3Faccess_token%3D***&page=2
info gateway top-level control …?access_token=***
info gateway no credential nested …?redirect_uri=https://app.test/cb?page=2
```

**Plain console output** (`openclaw config validate` echoes a rejected value as `got: "<value>"` through `console.error` → `redactSensitiveText`):

| case | `main` | this head |
|---|---|---|
| nested, plain | `?cb=https://y.test/?access_token=nested-sentinel-0123456789abcdefghij` | `?cb=https://y.test/?access_token=nested…ghij` |
| nested, percent-encoded | leaks | **unchanged — still leaks** |
| top level | `?access_token=nested…ghij` | `?access_token=nested…ghij` |

The top-level row is the control: `main` already masks it, so redaction was running over these lines before this PR. The only thing that changes is nesting. The masked nested value takes `maskToken`'s own partial `nested…ghij` shape, identical to the top-level shape for the same value.

## Encoded whole-text gap

The gap described in the earlier console table is fixed by the follow-up above. That table remains historical evidence of the previous revision rather than a result from the current head.

## Earlier checks (Node 24)

```
src/logging/redact.test.ts                 -> 58 passed
src/logging/redact-byte-identity.test.ts   -> 3 passed
src/logging (whole directory, 64 files)    -> 716 of 716 passed, 0 failures
oxlint, oxfmt --check on the changed files -> clean
run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json         -> exit 0
```

**Recorded-corpus changes, stated explicitly:** 2 of the 250 log-record entries in `redact-byte-identity-fixture.json` are re-recorded, because they had stored `"***":"***"` in place of `"level":"info"` — the corruption described above. Their masked `message` bytes are **byte-identical**; only the clobbered sibling field is restored. The other 248 entries and all 468 `redact-prefilter-fixture.json` hashes are untouched, verified by replaying all 250 samples and confirming exactly 2 differ and both only in that field. The reason is recorded in a comment in the test file so the deviation from "byte-identical to the pre-fix implementation" is not silent.

New cases: the two `?password=alpha?bravo` regressions, a top-level/nested mask-parity assertion, the plain nested URL through the whole-text path, a nested URL with no credential staying byte-for-byte readable, the percent-encoded nested query through the line-batch path, and a record-path case asserting that a mask with no trailing `&` leaves its sibling fields intact (red on base: `expected undefined to be 'info'`).

Companion PR: #176526 fixes the same class of leak in `packages/net-policy` (URL redactor, nested URL behind leading text). The two are independent — this path does not call that redactor.

This touches a security-sensitive file, so it will need a maintainer `/allow-security-sensitive-change`.

prs.title: fix(process): forward-port startup cleanup and shared lineage fixes
prs.body:
## Problem

Process startup failures discovered during the 2026.10.10 stable release cycle could be hidden by cleanup errors, or cleanup could be declared uncertain before a loaded native process tree had time to settle. A source-host/dist-plugin combination could also load separate inherited-lineage bindings.

This is the process-only split of #191830. It targets `main` directly and does not depend on the other split PRs.

## Solution

- Preserve the bounded five-second startup cleanup window, keeping the original startup failure when cleanup succeeds.
- Keep the startup failure first when cleanup also fails, retaining cleanup uncertainty and its restart guidance as secondary evidence. The refused-launch hard-deadline test now expects an AggregateError; the cleanup fence is unchanged.
- Share inherited process lineage through the existing global-singleton owner across module copies.

The original commit attribution and release references are preserved: `ba42adbc70`, `e51fa6420f`, and `7dc3350cb9` from `release/2026.10.10`.

## Scope and regression budget

The simplify pass retains the existing process/relay owners and distinct tests for delayed cleanup, startup-vs-cleanup error precedence, and duplicate-module lineage. There is no new manager or alternate cleanup path. Product delta is +62/-24 lines; net test growth is 92 lines. A dedicated 92-line test allocation covers exactly this split's net regression growth; the original aggregate allocation is not copied.

## Evidence

- Focused process suites: 42/42 tests passed across three files (147.51s wall including a 115s cold worker compilation).
- After the review-driven fake-clock correction, `owned-stdio.test.ts`: 4/4 passed in 2.45s wall (5ms tests).
- Scoped oxfmt check and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Core typecheck attempted; fails in untouched `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts` and `mcp-metadata.ts` (missing exported McpCatalogTool and optional UI metadata versus required Pick). Scoped lint is blocked by the same declaration-emitter prerequisite. These files are unchanged from the pinned main base.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed base `34007820fa2c` through `c838f5525d7f`: no production or security defects; its exact test-budget allocation and deterministic-clock findings are addressed. The later changes only add the scoped allocation and replace real waits with fake-clock advancement.
- CI duration: pending.

Original #191830 recorded failing-without-fix regression evidence for these process changes. This split preserves the production hunks unchanged; the mocked timing regression now advances a fake clock rather than waiting in real time. Native Linux/Windows live-process lanes have not been rerun locally; broad/platform coverage remains PR CI work.


## Split CI status

- [Observed CI failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41740474504/job/126282035331) is inherited from main `34007820fa2c`: missing `McpCatalogTool` export in `mcp-metadata.ts` and consequent optional UI metadata errors. That file and `agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts` / `agent-bundle-mcp-types.ts` are byte-identical to the base; SDK declaration preparation propagates the same error into build/boundary/lint lanes.
- [Test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41740474504/job/126281223136) retains the pre-split 47-line deficit: baseline total 6,444,916 versus ceiling 6,444,869. This split’s dedicated allocation covers its exact positive test-line delta; inflating it would violate the allocation checker.
- Ready for review does not mean green CI or ready to merge. Remaining broad checks are still running; no merge requested.

## Exact-head CI attribution audit

Audited 2026-11-04 at `82fcb528584d78b1d31687fc6f6153a0db0a5a2e`. Failed job logs were inspected individually, not inferred from their names.

The MCP failures are inherited from base `34007820fa2c`: `src/agents/mcp-metadata.ts`, `agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts`, and `agent-bundle-mcp-types.ts` have identical Git blob IDs at base and PR head. The missing `McpCatalogTool` export and consequent optional-property errors propagate through SDK declarations into boundary/build/lint/type lanes.

The test-line ratchet is also inherited: this PR offsets its exact positive test-line delta, and its job still exceeds the adjusted ceiling by the same **47 lines** already present at base (6,444,916 vs 6,444,869). No baseline increase or unrelated repair is included.

| Failed check | Attribution |
|---|---|
| [checks-fast-baseline-ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41740474504/job/126281223136) | Inherited 47-line test-budget deficit |

prs.title: fix(exec-host): allow macOS exec requests up to 1 MiB
prs.body:
Related: #188681

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: macOS companion execution rejects larger commands when their signed requests exceed the previous 256,000-byte limit.

## User Impact

User impact: users can submit signed exec requests up to 1 MiB (1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes, excluding the trailing newline). Larger requests still fail before sending with `INVALID_REQUEST` and reason `too-large`.

Update the macOS app and node host together. Older apps retain the 256,000-byte limit, so larger requests sent to them can still report an unknown execution outcome. This version mismatch is accepted; there is no compatibility negotiation. For larger scripts or data, put them in a file on the execution host and run that instead.

## Why This Change Was Made

Raises both the node-host sender limit and macOS socket receiver limit to 1 MiB while preserving the pre-send rejection introduced in #188681. Adds exact-byte boundary coverage and documents the limit and upgrade requirement.

## Evidence

Previously completed validation for this unchanged patch:

- 87 focused TypeScript tests passed, including exactly 1 MiB accepted and one byte over rejected at the socket boundary.
- TypeScript typecheck, lint, and formatting passed.
- macOS app and test bundle compiled; Swift lint and formatting passed.
- Fresh local ClawSweeper review found no production issues. Its test-line ratchet bookkeeping correction is committed: 39 ratcheted lines, excluding Swift lines.

Native runtime tests were **not executed**; native runtime verification remains an explicit CI gap. No validation was rerun for this publication-only recovery.
