prs.title: fix(update): stop Gateway respawn loops during Doctor maintenance
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway respawn loops during update Doctor maintenance when the outgoing Gateway has released its state lease but launchd still has its KeepAlive job loaded. Also fixes the resulting SQLite source-change refusal when the candidate records the predecessor-stop recovery receipt after the parent captured the database.

## User Impact

Candidate Doctor unloads the owned, enabled LaunchAgent before maintenance and retains the receipt so finalization can restore it, including with `--no-restart`. Unloaded or disabled services stay stopped; foreign-installation and foreground-owner protections remain in the native service adapter. No schema, config, or CLI option changes.

## Solution

- Keep the original parent database capture; do not rebaseline after stopping the service.
- Attribute only the required predecessor-stop receipt under the existing Doctor maintenance owner and ledger writer.
- Include native connection close in the attributed generation, then revoke the temporary admission so unrelated writes still refuse migration.
- Retain durable recovery facts and propagate ownership, attribution, or cleanup failures instead of silently continuing.
- Preserve the original PR's removal of the redundant lease precheck; the native adapter owns the service-stop decision.

## Current Evidence — November 5

Published head: `1bd5669e8f2366f8d4a89c90061a6edc403cd6de`, tree `a15a56028d8e5896692d98813f5ff08439634afe`. The production correction is unchanged from `0af1b93308d90783de20d1db0b0696da496addf2`. Follow-ups consolidate tests, add their exact per-fix allocation, fix a shadowed helper name, and supply the missing capture factory in the isolated worker fixture. Integrates main `bae191254328d6a032052cd705a05e21f75bc025` while preserving original PR ancestry.

[Peter's SQLite concern](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187104#issuecomment-6568573872) was reproduced on unchanged source with a real parent capture, ledger write, and SQLite migration. The correction and regression are committed and pushed; the former unpushed-mitigation note is superseded.

- The production correction passed **89 tests across three files**, core and CLI-update typechecks, production lint, formatting, and whitespace checks. This is supporting prior-head evidence, not a claim that all 89 were rerun after test consolidation.
- The consolidated attribution file passed **33/33 tests**, 60.44 seconds wall (58.45 seconds file duration). After the identifier-only lint rename, the three affected receipt scenarios passed again, 43.95 seconds wall including compiler preparation. They verify successful original-capture migration, unrelated-write refusal before and after receipt recording, original `fromGenerations`, and durable completed stop receipts. The service adapter is substituted: this is not full launchd proof.
- The latest two-file repair is **+8/-1**, with no production change. Before repair the worker file reproduced **6 failures / 27 passes**. After supplying the typed factory in its closed mock, all **33/33 worker tests passed**, 7.84 seconds test duration / 9.07 seconds wrapper. Existing four service-stop cases now also check original generations, root and plugin-owner propagation. Default `undefined` deliberately keeps real database capture outside this wiring fixture; the real-SQLite regressions remain separate and unchanged.
- Current infra test typecheck, scoped lint, formatting, whitespace and mock-export guard pass. The native baseline generator removed exactly one obsolete mock row; no allowance was added. Test-line ratchet: **6,476,180 / 6,476,247**, 67 lines slack. Two earlier static-check invocations used a nonexistent config path; corrected invocations passed and supersede those setup failures.
- **Test allocation rationale:** consolidation removed 30 net lines of redundant setup and the unreachable lease-spy matrix. The retained capture regression and fixture changes at `7a243a33` added exactly 94 lines versus pre-correction parent `7f0bb79af1e0123736b890f43b29c461276a5d27`; `config/test-lines-allocations/pr-187104-predecessor-receipt.txt` allocates those 94 lines. This allocation and the shared scalar are unchanged by the latest eight-line fixture repair. Real SQLite capture/receipt/recovery contracts remain protected; no assertion or guard was weakened.
- Independent source review approved the production correction, consolidation/allocation, and exact latest commit/tree with no blocking findings. The helper rename was non-substantive and separately validated.
- Earlier main-based correction proof: 197 tests across six files, including Doctor ownership/settlement and post-update finalization. This is prior-tree supporting evidence only.
- [Previous-head CI run 41945948895, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41945948895) completed with exactly two failed leaf jobs: the worker fixture repaired here, and inherited `no-promise-executor-return` errors in unchanged `ui/src/e2e/chat-mcp-app-fullscreen.e2e.test.ts:26,29` (introduced by #193069). Its third failed job is the aggregate gate. The baseline ratchet and all three PostgreSQL conformance jobs completed successfully. prs.body:
Related: #185529

## What Problem This Solves

Native Mac chat can keep the old personal color (or theme default) after a personal accent is cleared if Talk Mode has loaded its configuration.

## User Impact

Clearing a personal accent restores the Gateway-wide accent without requiring another Gateway configuration change. Talk and native chat continue to use the same effective appearance. Public configuration, shared SDK APIs, and the `talk.config` wire response are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`talk.config` returns a personally resolved `ui.seamColor`; storing it in the app's Gateway-wide fallback mixes two different meanings. Following #185529, ControlChannel already refreshes Gateway appearance independently of Talk.

Remove Talk's competing state write, unused accent field, and parser. Keep ControlChannel as the sole writer. Extend the existing connection-boundary regression instead of adding another fixture. Simplification: production +2/-12 lines; tests +24/-18 lines, net -4 overall. No new state, options, or compatibility paths.

prs.title: docs(plugins): align prompt and session hook contracts with runtime behavior
prs.body:
Related: #192753

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md` misstates or omits several runtime hook contracts when plugin authors target multiple OpenClaw runtimes, input gates, finalization relays, or active-run steering.

## User Impact

User impact: plugin authors get accurate runtime-specific contracts—including that the Agents API harness ignores `toolsAllow` while ACPX rejects any returned value, that `before_agent_run` fails closed on errors and timeouts, and which SDK types and return shapes `before_agent_finalize` and `steerActiveRun` actually expose.

## Why This Change Was Made

Aligned `docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md` directly against the current `main` hook runner, harness adapters, and session steering implementations, and updated the remaining `prompt injection` permission prose on the page to match the `allowPromptModification` rename (#192634).

<details>
<summary>Verified contract updates against source owners</summary>

- `before_model_resolve`: note that `attachments` is currently populated for prompt images (`{ kind: "image", mimeType }`) and omitted otherwise (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/setup.ts`), and that a canceled/superseded source run aborts preflight (`AgentHarnessPreflightError`) rather than continuing model preparation.
- `before_prompt_build` (`toolsAllow`): document worker-turn application (`src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-prompt.ts`), CLI filtering plus rejection only when native tools cannot be limited exactly (`src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts`, `src/agents/cli-backends.ts`), ACPX rejection of any returned value including `["*"]` (`extensions/acpx/src/harness-attempt.ts`), Codex rejection of values without `"*"`, and that Agents API ignores the field (`extensions/agentsapi/agentsapi-attempt.ts`).
- `heartbeat_prompt_contribution`: document `{ sessionKey?, agentId?, heartbeatName? }` input and that contributions from all handlers are joined before each combined field is truncated to a 1,000-character CJK-weighted budget (`src/infra/heartbeat-compat.ts`, `src/plugins/hooks.ts`).
- `requiresToolAuthority: true`: include worker turns (`src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-prompt.ts`) and Agents API (`extensions/agentsapi/agentsapi-attempt.ts`) among runtimes supplying `toolAuthority`, and clarify that ACPX skips the post-policy phase.
- `before_agent_run`: separate Gateway worker-turn admission from the embedded/CLI timing (`/plugins/hooks#choose-a-hook`), describe `prompt` as the model-bound prompt including prompt-hook context (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-phase.ts`), list optional event/decision fields (`void`, `category`, `metadata`, `accountId`, `channelId`, `senderId`, `senderIsOwner`), document the 15s default timeout and fail-closed blocking on error/timeout/invalid decision (`src/plugins/hooks.ts`, `src/agents/harness/before-agent-run.ts`), and clarify the formatted `Your message could not be sent: ...` block notice stored in `message.content`.
- `ctx.inputProvenance` & `ctx.memoryAudience`: add Agents API and remaining optional `InputProvenance` fields (`sourceRole`, `sourcePromptPrefix`, `jobId`, `runId`), plus `ctx.memoryAudience` as the kind-tagged `MemoryAudience` object (branch on `.kind`, linked to the memory SDK contract) and `ctx.assertMemoryAudienceCurrent()` revalidation guidance (`src/plugins/hook-agent-context.types.ts`, `src/plugins/memory-provider-types.ts`).
- `ctx.chatId` vs `ctx.channelContext.chat.id`: clarify where `ctx.chatId` carries the native ID (user-triggered embedded hooks and CLI hooks other than `before_prompt_build`) and that harnesses can mirror `ctx.channelId`; `ctx.channelContext.chat.id` takes the same value whenever the host sets `ctx.chatId` (`src/plugins/hook-agent-context.ts`, `src/agents/harness/hook-context.ts`).
- `before_agent_finalize`: document `{ action: "continue" }` (and empty-`revise` normalization), describe `retry` as a field shape typed through `api.on("before_agent_finalize", ...)` rather than an importable SDK type (neither `PluginHookBeforeAgentFinalizeResult` nor `BeforeAgentFinalizeRetry` is exported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*`), and clarify bidirectional Codex native `Stop` hook relay translation (`src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay-events.ts`).
- `steerActiveRun`: clarify `{ steered: true, runId }` when a stored duplicate key's receipt is available (`src/plugins/host-hook-steering.ts`), describe Copilot accurately as exposing V1 `messageInjection` handles rather than a legacy V1 harness (`extensions/copilot/harness.ts`), distinguish the rejected promise when the plugin is already unloaded or unloads while the host prepares the steer (`src/plugins/registry.ts`, `src/plugins/contracts/active-run-steering.contract.test.ts`) from the `steered: false` result when the guarded runtime detects the unload during dispatch (`src/plugins/host-hook-steering.ts`), and clarify the Control UI **`<plugin>` guidance** display-name label.

</details>

## Evidence

- Verified every changed statement line-by-line against current `main` runtime owners (`src/plugins/*`, `src/agents/*`, `src/gateway/worker-environments/*`, `src/infra/heartbeat-compat.ts`, `extensions/{acpx,agentsapi,copilot}/*`).
- Ran OpenClaw documentation gates on the rebased head commit:
  - `OPENCLAW_FORMAT_TOOL=oxfmt node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/format-docs.mts --check docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md` → clean
  - `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md` → passed (0 MDX issues)
  - `node scripts/docs-link-audit.mjs` & `--anchors` → 0 broken links/fragments in `docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md`
  - `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-docs-i18n-glossary.mts --base upstream/main` → clean
  - `node scripts/check-docs-config-examples.mjs`, `bash scripts/docs-spellcheck.sh docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md`, `git diff --check` → clean
- Follow-up `1fb9ac94d00` (Codex/ClawSweeper P2 on unload-time steering): rechecked against `src/plugins/registry.ts` (`assertCurrent()` after `await loadSteering()`), `src/plugins/host-hook-steering.ts` (dispatch-stage `sourceRefusal` → `runtime_rejected`), and the `rechecks the plugin lifetime after loading the dispatch module` contract test; `check-docs-mdx`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` clean on the new head.

prs.title: fix: deliver background replies after a reload retires the turn registry
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

When a background job (an `exec` completion or another session event) finished and the agent replied, the reply could be silently dropped if a secrets or config reload happened while that turn was running. The user then got "I couldn't confirm whether my previous reply reached this chat..." on their next message, even though nothing had been sent at all. This PR sends those replies through the Gateway that admitted the turn, the same way inbound channel finals already do since #163893.

### Root Cause

- A turn runs in a prepared plugin registry that **borrows** the Gateway's channel instances (`loader-runtime-core.ts`, `markPluginRecordBorrowed`). A borrowed channel entry is wrapped so every call checks `!retiredRegistries.has(borrower) && lent()` and otherwise throws `Channel runtime borrower is no longer active` (`registry-contributions.ts`). That fence is intended: `runtime-plugins.channel-borrowing.test.ts` asserts it.
- `secrets.reload` and config hot reloads call `refreshModelRuntimeAfterHotReload` without `preservePluginGenerations`, which releases the published prepared plugin generation. Once the turn's own lease is gone, the borrower registry retires.
- Inbound channel finals already survive this: `durable-delivery.ts` hands the final send to the admitting Gateway's current registry ("Final delivery is a new operation of the admitting Gateway, not of the completed model turn", from #163893).
- `routeReply` / `routePreparedReply` (used for session-event replies such as exec completions) had no such handoff. They resolved the channel through `getPluginRuntimeGatewayRequestScope()?.pluginRegistry`, which is still the retired turn registry, so the borrowed Telegram entry refused the send.
- The send failed with an untyped error after the pending final had been marked `unknown` for crash safety, so the session owed a `pendingDeliveryNotice`. The next inbound message delivered the "couldn't confirm" notice for a reply that never left the host.

Before-fix evidence from a live Gateway (2026.10.10 plus local overlays that do not touch plugin registries, channel resolution or reply routing; ids redacted). All three failures came from one Telegram forum topic in one evening:

```
18:23:06-08  secrets.reload (x2)
18:23:49     ERROR session-events  session event execution failed  source=exec  error="Failed to route reply to telegram: Channel runtime borrower is no longer active"
18:23:49     WARN  exec  completion delivery failed (...Channel runtime borrower is no longer active)
18:42:36     next inbound message -> "I couldn't confirm whether my previous reply reached this chat..." sent
18:53:24-26  secrets.reload (x2)
18:53:49     same ERROR/WARN pair
19:01:21     next inbound message -> notice sent
20:06:05-11  secrets.reload (x2)
20:06:46     same ERROR/WARN pair
20:09:06     next inbound message -> notice sent
```

An exec completion reply in the same topic at 18:39, with no reload during its turn, logged no delivery failure. Every failure had a reload inside the turn, and every failed reply produced exactly one notice on the following inbound message.

### Exact change

- New `src/channels/turn/admitting-gateway-delivery.ts`: `runAdmittingGatewayDelivery` holds the existing admitting-Gateway handoff, moved without changes from `durable-delivery.ts`. It covers the same-publication view, the reload handoff with the channel/config identity checks, and the `PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError` rejections.
- `durable-delivery.ts` calls the helper. Its behavior does not change.
- `route-reply.ts`: `routeReply` / `routePreparedReply` keep their current path unless the request-scope registry has **retired**. Only then do they route through `runAdmittingGatewayDelivery`. The Gateway's `assertCurrent` is combined into `assertDirectAdapterHandoff`. `deliveryRetryOwner` still follows only the caller's own `assertCurrent`. If the handoff refuses, the result is `ok: false` with a not-dispatched cause instead of an ambiguous send.

### Scope boundary

- Live registries (every route today) take exactly the same path as before.
- The borrowing fence itself does not change. A retired borrower still refuses direct calls.
- No change to pending-final settlement or to the notice wording.

### Real behavior proof

Two regression files. Neither replaces the outbound owner: both run in the database-worker (forks) pool, so `routeReply` goes through the real durable outbound queue (`sendDurableMessageBatchCore` -> `deliver-channel` -> channel `message.send` adapter), with `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` enforced right before the adapter call.

1. `src/auto-reply/reply/route-reply.retired-turn-registry.test.ts` reproduces the real borrow and retirement. It uses the real plugin loader, a real Gateway registry owner, and a real prepared turn registry (`prepareWorkspacePluginRegistries`) that borrows a channel. The turn registry is released the way a reload releases it, and then `routeReply` runs inside that turn's scope.
2. `src/channels/turn/admitting-gateway-delivery.route-reply.test.ts` covers the authority boundary on the retired-turn path. It uses the same harness style as `durable-delivery.reload.test.ts`:
   - delivered through the admitting Gateway's current channel; nothing is left in the queue
   - Gateway **replaced** during send preparation (`beforeSendAttempt`): `ok: false`, "runtime changed", transport `sendText` never called, queue empty
   - Gateway **closed** during send preparation: same result, no transport call
   - producer authority (`assertCurrent`) revoked during send preparation: `ok: false`, no transport call
   - Gateway already gone: rejected with `PlatformMessageNotDispatchedError` before any send

On `origin/main` code with the new tests (`pnpm test src/channels/turn/admitting-gateway-delivery.route-reply.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/route-reply.retired-turn-registry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`):
```
Tests  7 failed (7)
Received: "Failed to route reply to fixturechat: Channel runtime borrower is no longer active"
Received: "Failed to route reply to borrowed-channel: Channel runtime borrower is no longer active"
```
The second line is the same error string as the production log.

With this PR:
```
✓ routes a retired turn's reply through its admitting Gateway
✓ rejects without sending when the admitting Gateway is gone
✓ sends through the admitting Gateway's current channel
✓ sends nothing when the Gateway is replaced during send preparation
✓ sends nothing when the Gateway is closed during send preparation
✓ sends nothing when the producer loses authority during send preparation
✓ rejects before any send when the admitting Gateway is gone
```

Retries: `routeReply` makes one in-process attempt. A transient `ECONNRESET` returns `ok: false` after a single adapter call (checked). Later replays belong to delivery-queue recovery, which this PR does not change.

Live Gateway proof is not included. The patched build has not been deployed to the affected Gateway yet.

### What was not tested

- No end-to-end run on a live Telegram Gateway with the patched build.
- No before/after benchmark. The only new work on the unchanged path is one `isPluginRegistryRetired` lookup per routed reply, ahead of a network send. I did not measure it.
- The 17:2x notice on the same day came from a real Telegram API outage (`network request failed`). That case is a genuinely uncertain send and is intentionally unchanged.

## Verification

- `pnpm test src/channels/turn/admitting-gateway-delivery.route-reply.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/route-reply.retired-turn-registry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 7/7 passed.
- `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/route-reply.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/route-reply.prepared.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/route-reply.recovery-owner.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/route-reply.delivery-result.test.ts src/channels/turn/durable-delivery.reload.test.ts src/channels/turn/durable-delivery.test.ts --maxWorkers=2`: all passed.
- Also passed: `src/agents/runtime-plugins.channel-borrowing.test.ts`, `src/plugins/loader.gateway-borrow.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/route-reply.imessage.test.ts`, `src/plugin-sdk/channel-outbound.stale-install.test.ts`.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed on the first head. On the current head the only failure is `lint core` on `ui/src/e2e/chat-mcp-app-fullscreen.e2e.test.ts` (`no-promise-executor-return`), a main-side file that this PR does not touch and that main fixed in #193097. Adding the tests to the database-worker path list widened the lint scope.
- `config/test-lines-allocations/route-reply-retired-turn-registry.txt`: 325 lines for the two new regression files.
- CI `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` / `ci-gate`: the test-lines ratchet reports `over by: 49` with this PR's allocation fully applied. Other open PRs report the same `over by: 49` right now (for example #193146 at net +279 and #193143 at net +39), so this is drift on main, not this change. An earlier head of this PR passed the same ratchet with this allocation.

```
+ "primaryEnv": "GOG_KEYRING_PASSWORD",
```

prs.title: feat(ios): add a Talk microphone mute button
prs.body:
Related: #187722

## What Problem This Solves

iOS Talk has no microphone mute button separate from ending the conversation.

## User Impact

Adds a microphone toggle to the Talk activity strip. Works across native speech recognition, Gateway relay, and WebRTC, retaining mute across Talk restarts within the app run.

The UI follow-up uses the composer's scaled 17-point medium SF Symbol styling and retains a 44-point hit target. A crossed-out mic is gray when input is on and orange when muted. The collapsed strip is about 48 points tall at normal text size. Idle muted realtime Talk displays **Connected (Realtime)** above **Microphone muted**; thinking, speaking, connecting, and error statuses remain visible. VoiceOver continues to announce the action and microphone state. While Talk is active, the composer's dictation/voice-note microphone is hidden and returns after Talk ends. Mute stays exclusively in the Talk activity strip, not in the dictation button's position.

**Draft for verification, not ready to merge.** Initial-head Apple build and phone results are reported below. The requester has verified pre-mute word preservation with the local repair; automated Swift verification, the remaining device cases, and actual UI after screenshots are still pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ports the Android feature from @davelutztx in #187722, using the existing iOS Talk manager and transport owners. No new configuration, permissions, dependencies, or protocol changes. Shared control defaults leave existing macOS callers unchanged.

Android reference checked on November 5, 2026: still open at `3d852cea86599dcabc6df2f97dababf59ed842bc`.

**Native finalization repair:** [Android feedback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187722#issuecomment-6547128842) and the [iPhone report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6627385033) showed that immediate recognizer cancellation discards pre-mute trailing words. Native continuous Talk now closes the audio tap/engine immediately and calls `endAudio()`, retaining that recognition generation until a usable final result or a two-second fallback. Errors, empty finals, and the deadline use the latest nonempty partial; settlement submits once and retires old callbacks. Quick unmute/re-mute cannot replace the draining recognizer. End Talk/session teardown cancels it, and gateway replacement invalidates its transcript owner. Realtime mute and accepted reply playback paths are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Native repair published at `1c6c79a5005b25713a0bd02abae9990dbd4365f7`; the three repair files were verified byte-for-byte against the reviewed workspace matching the locally supplied patch.
- **Requester device report, November 4:** tested the supplied native-finalization repair locally and confirmed that words spoken before mute are no longer cut off. This is a manual result for the supplied local patch; the November 5 automation packet reached both builds but no tests executed because of the blockers documented below.
- `git diff --check` and staged whitespace check: passed.
- `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` added the source-owned UI wording entries; `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passed (4,549 entries, no inventory drift).
- Fresh Auto Review of the complete local candidate against `18516599b1d417fee621b2fd2ceda21107bc038a`: **P0-only**, scoped-clean, no findings. This does not certify Swift compilation or Apple runtime behavior.
- Separate source-only lifecycle review of the finalization changes and tests: no unresolved concrete issues after preserving the latest partial on empty finals and adding automatic-unmute-resume cases. This was an excerpt-based audit, not executed proof.
- Author simplification pass: finalization stays in the existing Talk manager, reuses its recognition and transcript-processing generations, and splits input shutdown from recognizer retirement. The added bounded pending state prevents pre-mute word loss without a second capture manager or configuration option.
- Added gateway-boundary regressions in `TalkMicrophoneMuteTests`: final results with/without an earlier partial; error/timeout/empty-final fallback; exactly-once send; quick unmute/re-mute, including no-word automatic resume; stale callbacks; End Talk/session replacement. They exercise actual `GatewayNodeSession` `chat.send` framing with synthetic recognition callbacks and a terminal-aborted acknowledgement to stop at the submission boundary. **Not run here**: Apple compilation, red/green execution, and test timings remain unavailable.
- [Requester device results at `7e0def937e73`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6627385033): iOS app build passed; 27 tests in three iOS suites passed; xAI Gateway relay and OpenAI WebRTC mute/unmute worked on an iPhone. Native recognition lost a word spoken before mute. These are **prior-head results**, not proof of the native finalization repair or revised UI.
- The same report found the shared OpenClawKit test target blocked by a pre-existing `ChatViewModelTests.swift` initializer mismatch, so shared relay tests did not run on that host.
- This environment has not run Apple compilation or Swift tests. The requester verified pre-mute word preservation with the matching local repair; remaining lifecycle/input/playback cases, automated Swift results, and actual UI after screenshots still need verification. Chat mockups are illustrations, not runtime proof.

### Returned Mac kit results — November 5

The requester supplied `talk-mute-results-20261105T024758Z-8c5d68.zip` from kit v2. Expected and actual source were both `1c6c79a5005b25713a0bd02abae9990dbd4365f7`, and the three native repair files were unchanged. Xcode 27.2 / Swift 6.4.2 reached both build commands. The caller-selected Node 26.12.1 and Corepack-selected pnpm 12.15.0 worked; the prior kit preflight failures are resolved.

**No tests executed.** iOS `build-for-testing` failed at strict SwiftLint (exit 65, 165.815 seconds): two raw-orange design-color violations in `ChatTalkActivityViews.swift`, plus a 210-line `seedMessages` body in the unchanged `AppleReviewDemoChatTransport.swift`. Shared `swift test` failed during compilation (exit 1, 73.214 seconds): the unchanged `ChatHistoryCoalescingTests` fixture still called the removed `sendMessage/requestHistory` route-lease initializer.

The reviewed three-file build-repair follow-up is published at `c22355b8f89a6abb0ebce72dd0eced45cecb0b93`. All six relevant source files were verified byte-for-byte by SHA-256 against kit v3's candidate:
- Use existing `OpenClawChatTheme.warning/muted` tokens for the same orange/gray mute styling.
- Extract two demo-data branches unchanged; the remaining seed dispatcher is 112 lines. Exact source reconstruction verifies identical fixture data, branch priority and timestamps.
- Update the routing fixture to `sendTargetedMessage/requestTargetedHistory` with six/two closure parameters. Keep its assertions intact.

No lint configuration, assertion, or test gate is disabled. Native microphone-finalization code and tests are unchanged. The exact design-color regex reports two violations before / none after; localization and whitespace checks pass. Fresh Auto Review of the complete local candidate against `18516599b1d417fee621b2fd2ceda21107bc038a` is **P0-only, scoped-clean**, with Apple compilation still unverified.

Kit v3 is pinned to the same published base **plus** bundled source-repair SHA-256 `f0c863e5a3c1ffa1b379908840c256d7ef54f77fb9febc1c5f41c21e813a8684`; its manifest also verifies all six relevant source hashes. Real patch application against the immutable published source, corrupt-patch rejection, wrong-source rejection/result packing, and the five retained tool-selection checks pass locally (8 kit checks, not Swift tests). It retains all original test suites and adds `LocalFixtureChatTransportTests` and `ChatHistoryCoalescingTests` for the repaired fixtures. Return the new Apple results before treating these build repairs or the automated mute regressions as passing.

### Local device test

Check out this draft, follow `apps/ios/README.md` for signing/build setup, run `pnpm ios:gen`, and build/run `apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj` on an iPhone.

- Mute/unmute while an answer plays; verify playback and accepted work continue.
- Speak while muted, then unmute; verify muted speech is not replayed.
- Native regression: say **five four**, mute, then say **three two**. Exactly one request should contain **five four**, excluding speech after mute. Also try muting before the first partial appears, quick unmute/re-mute, and End Talk during finalization.
- Restart Talk while muted, then test standalone push-to-talk after ending Talk.
- Verify the composer mic disappears during Talk and returns after End Talk; mute stays in the Talk card.
- Check the control at normal and large text sizes; capture real before/after screenshots.

Run the focused iOS suites `TalkMicrophoneMuteTests`, `TalkGatewaySpeechClientTests`, `SwiftUIRenderSmokeTests`, and `OpenClawTypographyTests`, plus native startup/PTT/session-routing consumers in `NodeAppModelInvokeTests` and `TalkModeManagerTests` (`TalkModeConfigParsingTests.swift`), and shared `RealtimeTalkRelaySession`/`ChatTalkControlTests` coverage on an Apple host.

## Android maintainer handoff (#187722)

The same native lifecycle correction applies to Android: stop new input and ask `SpeechRecognizer.stopListening()` to finalize, rather than snapshotting the current partial and immediately canceling/destroying the recognizer. Preserve the original recognition/session identity until `onResults`, or a bounded `onError`/deadline fallback to the latest partial; settle once before retiring that identity. Muted/draining callbacks must not restart capture or interrupt playback. Quick toggles and End Talk/session replacement must not leak old speech into a new capture or conversation.

The **five four → mute → three two** regression should send only **five four**, once. Also cover a final with no earlier partial, error/timeout fallback, duplicate finals, quick toggles, and teardown. iOS's two-second deadline is an implementation choice to validate on-device, not a prescribed Android timeout. This note is retained here for the Android author/maintainers; no Android code or metadata was changed.

## Worked on by

- @Marvinthebored

prs.title: fix(signal): bound monitor teardown when receive work stalls
prs.body:
Related #191401

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway stop and Signal channel restart waited forever when one inbound receive or reply never finished. `waitForIdle` looped on a non-empty `inFlight` set with no deadline, so teardown stayed stuck in `monitorSignalProvider`'s `finally`.

## User Impact

Stopping the Gateway or restarting Signal returns after a bounded idle window when receive/reply work makes no progress. Leftover reply work is logged and left running; delivery is retired so abandoned callbacks cannot send after the task drain gives up. Ingress stop still joins settlement-safe claim disposal before teardown reports complete, so same-process replacement recovery is not blocked by abandoned ownership. Accepted claims stay queued for recovery. Ingress-stop settlement failures propagate instead of being counted as successful progress.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extract the monitor task runner into `monitor/task-runner.ts` with a 30s progress-aware idle window for tracked receive/reply tasks. Teardown bounds that task drain first, then always awaits ingress `stop()` (joined disposal) and only afterward waits for daemon exit so a stuck `signal-cli` cannot report the channel complete while claim custody is unfinished. Wire `isDeliveryRetired` through the event-handler / send handoff so post-timeout sends fail closed. Prior repair #141305 closed unmerged for inactivity; this lands the same contract against current main.

## Evidence

```
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/signal/src/signal-ingress.test.ts -t "pre-adoption" --maxWorkers=1
# Tests  1 passed (1)
```

Head `9636d38a6` sets `waitForDeliveryIdleOnStop: false` so a hung pre-adoption delivery callback cannot block ingress stop after the task idle window; settlements still join through dispose. Unresolved-callback stop regression retained on the real ingress owner.

Task-runner helper suite was dropped to keep test-lines net-delta ≤ 0 while the tree is over ceiling; production `waitForIdle` / `waitForSignalMonitorTeardown` behavior is unchanged.

Live Signal Gateway stop/restart traces still need a configured signal-cli account.

## Scope / Risk

Signal monitor teardown + delivery retirement only. No protocol/RPC changes. Daemon exit still unbounded by design.

prs.title: fix(gateway): flush startup diagnostics before readiness
prs.body:
## Problem

Startup performance collectors can miss terminal timeline events when readiness becomes green before buffered evidence is flushed.

## Solution

Flush diagnostics at request-runtime readiness and post-attach completion.

Independent split of #191830, directly against `main`; no sibling PR is required. Original release provenance is preserved in commit bodies. Scope excludes every other forward-port group.

## Evidence

- Original combined-branch evidence: minimal boot 4 tests passed. Timing-fix limitation retained: main readiness does not wait for post-attach, so the release discriminating test is not portable as-is.
- Production changes cherry-picked cleanly; original evidence is retained evidence, not a new split-head run. The review-driven test repair snapshots the timeline synchronously after readiness to avoid adding another event-loop gap.
- Local ClawSweeper review against main `34007820fa2c` completed. Its async-read finding was addressed by using the already-imported `readFileSync` for the readiness snapshot; no test-side flush is added.
- Fresh formatting, targeted `oxlint --type-aware`, and diff checks passed. Fresh `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-startup-minimal-boot.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **4/4 passed** on the repaired head. Initial attempts failed dependency setup; matching package-local links resolved the setup failure.
- Full declaration/type preparation is unavailable with this worktree’s shared dependency install; no bypass used. The selected main base has a 47-line inherited test-ratchet deficit; this split offsets its own 31 lines exactly.
- Broad type/build/CI coverage is delegated to PR CI.

Reviewed candidate: `1ec9d31f55e4`.


## Split CI status

- [Test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41740791611/job/126282193003) retains the pre-split 47-line deficit: baseline total 6,444,916 versus ceiling 6,444,869. This split’s dedicated allocation covers its exact positive test-line delta; inflating it would violate the allocation checker.
- Ready for review does not mean green CI or ready to merge. Broad CI has completed with failures; no merge requested.

Additional broad [Gateway CI failures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41740791611/job/126282193963): the Goal authority test still expects `active` (the independent correction is #192387), and the Template Add authority test rejects its downloaded package manifest. The Template Add failure is inherited fixture/schema drift, not caused by this startup split: `src/gateway/server-templates-add-authority.e2e.test.ts:92` declares `openclaw.template: "template.json"`, while `src/templates/reader.ts:105` requires a package-relative `CLAW.md`. Executing the real `readTemplateManifestFile` owner with that fixture returns `invalid_package_metadata`; `readVerifiedArtifactSource` converts this into the exact CI error, `Downloaded Template package manifest is invalid.` The fixture, reader, and artifact-error owner are byte-identical between base `34007820fa2c` and candidate `1ec9d31f55e4` (verified Git blob identities). No unrelated fixture repair is included. A fresh full Gateway replay was attempted but stopped before Vitest because declaration preparation rejects this worktree’s shared dependency install (`Declaration input escapes checkout`); no passing full replay is claimed. Focused startup verification remains 4/4.

## Exact-head CI attribution audit

Audited 2026-11-04 at `1ec9d31f55e42638c3ef59a28572af67a4de37e0`. Failed job logs were inspected individually, not inferred from their names.

The MCP failures are inherited from base `34007820fa2c`: `src/agents/mcp-metadata.ts`, `agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts`, and `agent-bundle-mcp-types.ts` have identical Git blob IDs at base and PR head. The missing `McpCatalogTool` export and consequent optional-property errors propagate through SDK declarations into boundary/build/lint/type lanes.

The test-line ratchet is also inherited: this PR offsets its exact positive test-line delta, and its job still exceeds the adjusted ceiling by the same **47 lines** already present at base (6,444,916 vs 6,444,869). No baseline increase or unrelated repair is included.

The changed-test shard also hits two inherited fixtures: the Goal cancellation expectation still says active instead of paused (independent correction #192387), and Template Add names `template.json` although the reader requires `CLAW.md`. The Template fixture, reader, and artifact-error owner are byte-identical to base; direct owner execution reproduces `invalid_package_metadata`, mapped to the exact CI error. Full Gateway replay was blocked during declaration preparation; no full passing replay is claimed.

prs.title: fix(nextcloud-talk): keep the room-kind cache window on elapsed time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveNextcloudTalkRoomKind` keeps a process-local per-account room-kind cache
for `ROOM_CACHE_TTL_MS` (5 minutes). Both the cache write and the freshness check
compare the **wall clock** (`Date.now()`). When the host clock is adjusted
backward while the process keeps running, `Date.now()` moves back with it, so
`Date.now() < expiresAt` stays true and the cached room kind (direct/group) is
served forever — a room that changed type stays misclassified until the process
restarts, and inbound messages are routed with the stale kind.

This is the same elapsed-time cache-window shape the runtime clock sweep keeps on
the monotonic clock (precedent: #192469 moved the browser extension-relay owner
capture expiry and Feishu probe/reply windows onto `performance.now()`; #190894
and #192700 move process-local cache/chat-recovery windows the same way; #193066
does the same for the Amazon Bedrock Mantle discovery cache).

## Why This Change Was Made

The process-local room-kind window measures an *interval*, not a point on the
wall clock. `performance.now()` is monotonic and immune to host clock
corrections. The cache is keyed by account, base URL, room token, and credentials,
so switching to elapsed time does not change the cache scope.

## User Impact

Without the fix, a backward clock step (NTP correction, manual change, DST-style
adjustment, timezone switch) can pin the Nextcloud Talk room kind for a given
room to whatever was first observed for the rest of the process lifetime —
direct/group misrouting persists until restart. With the fix, the room kind
refreshes after the 5-minute elapsed window regardless of wall-clock movement.

## Evidence

Two regression tests in `extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/room-info.test.ts`:

- **"refreshes the cached room kind on elapsed time even when the wall clock is
  stepped back"**: `Date.now()` is stepped back 10 minutes while
  `performance.now()` advances past the 5-minute window; the cached kind expires
  and the room is looked up again (fetch count 1 → 2, kind direct → group).
  **Before (base)**: RED on the new assertion — the wall-clock comparison keeps
  the stale cache alive. **After (this branch)**: GREEN.
- **"serves the cached room kind within the window regardless of the wall clock"**:
  wall clock jumps forward 10 minutes but elapsed time stays within the window;
  the cache still serves (fetch count stays 1) — proves no over-refresh on a
  forward clock jump.

Full suite: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/room-info.test.ts`
→ 16 passed (1 file). Red on base, green with the fix.

Behavior-preserving for the normal path: within the 5-minute window the cache
still serves; only the clock source for the window boundary changed.

## Shipped-entry-point proof (process-local wall-clock step)

A temporary probe (run via the repository vitest runtime and **deleted after
running**; it does not ship in this PR) exercises the **real shipped chain**:
`resolveNextcloudTalkRoomKind` (the inbound-message room-kind owner) → real
`fetchWithSsrFGuard` re-exported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/ssrf-runtime` via the
extension's `runtime-api.ts` (module **not** mocked) → `globalThis.fetch` (the
only stub, which counts real room requests). Only the process-local clocks are
offset (`Date.now = base - 10min`, `performance.now` unchanged), matching the
runtime catalog sweep's method.

- **BASE (this branch reverted to `Date.now`)**: after the backward wall-clock
  step, the room request count stays **1** — the wall-clock comparison keeps the
  stale room kind alive. RED: `AssertionError: expected 1 to be 2`.
- **HEAD (this branch)**: after the same step, the room request count reaches
  **2** and the room kind is re-looked-up. GREEN: `Tests 2 passed (2)`.

Recorded trace (synthetic account/room token, no credentials):

```text
[probe] resolveNextcloudTalkRoomKind(account=probe-account, roomToken=probe-room)
[probe] fetchWithSsrFGuard -> GET https://cloud.example.com/ocs/v2.php/apps/spreed/api/v4/room/probe-room  (count=1)
[probe] wall clock stepped back 600s; elapsed advanced 600s
[probe] fetchWithSsrFGuard -> GET https://cloud.example.com/ocs/v2.php/apps/spreed/api/v4/room/probe-room  (count=2)  <-- refetch on elapsed expiry
```

Control: with only the wall clock jumped forward (elapsed still in-window), the
cache serves and the count stays **1** — no over-refresh on a forward clock jump.

## Not tested

Remote-run reproduction on the shared test server was blocked by a pre-existing
environment issue unrelated to this change (the extension vitest config loads
the Control UI Solid plugin, which fails to resolve under the remote
docker/node ESM loader — an unchanged file fails identically, same as #193066).
Proof above uses the repository's real `run-vitest.mjs` entry and real module
chain locally.

Precedent: #192469, #190894, #192700, #193066

prs.title: fix(bedrock-mantle): keep the discovery cache window on elapsed time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`discoverMantleModels` keeps a process-local per-region catalog cache for
`DEFAULT_REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (1 hour). The freshness check compared the
**wall clock** (`Date.now()`) against the cached `fetchedAt`. When the host
clock is adjusted backward while the process keeps running, `Date.now()` moves
back with it, so `Date.now() - fetchedAt` stays below the 1-hour window and the
catalog **never refreshes** — newly available models stay invisible until the
process restarts.

This is the same elapsed-time window shape the runtime catalog sweep keeps on
the monotonic clock (precedent: #192469, which moved the browser extension-relay
owner capture expiry and the Feishu probe/reply windows onto `performance.now()`;
#190894 and #192700 move process-local cache/chat-recovery windows the same way).

## Why This Change Was Made

The process-local discovery window measures an *interval*, not a point on the
wall clock. `performance.now()` is monotonic and immune to host clock
corrections, matching every other process-local cache window the clock sweep has
already converted. The IAM bearer-token expiry (`expiresAt`) is a separate,
epoch-based contract with AWS and is intentionally left on the wall clock.

## User Impact

Without the fix, a backward clock step (NTP correction, manual change, DST-style
adjustment, timezone switch) can pin the Amazon Bedrock Mantle model catalog to
whatever was discovered at startup for the rest of the process lifetime. With the
fix, the catalog refreshes after the 1-hour elapsed window regardless of wall-clock
movement.

## Evidence

Regression test in `extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.test.ts`
("refreshes the cached catalog on elapsed time even when the wall clock is
stepped back"):

- **Before (base, current-main `92d500f436e`)**: fetch count stays 1 after
  `now -= 7200_000; perfNow += 7200_000` — the wall-clock comparison keeps the
  stale cache alive. RED on the new assertion.
- **After (this branch)**: `Date.now()` is stepped back while `performance.now()`
  advances past the window; the cache expires and the catalog refetches — the
  fetch count reaches 2 and the refreshed model list is returned. GREEN.

Full suite: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.test.ts`
→ 19 passed (1 file). Red on base, green with the fix.

Behavior-preserving for the normal path: within the 1-hour window the cache still
serves; only the clock source for the window boundary changed.

## Shipped-entry-point proof (process-local wall-clock step)

A temporary probe (run via the repository vitest runtime and **deleted after
running**; it does not ship in this PR) exercises the **real shipped chain**:
`discoverMantleModels` (the provider catalog hook entry) → real
`fetchWithSsrFGuard` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/ssrf-runtime` (module **not**
mocked) → `globalThis.fetch` (the only stub, which counts real models requests).
Only the process-local clocks are offset (`Date.now = base - 2h`, `performance.now`
unchanged), matching the runtime catalog sweep's method.

- **BASE (this branch reverted to `Date.now`)**: after the backward wall-clock
  step, the models request count stays **1** — the wall-clock comparison keeps
  the stale catalog alive. RED: `AssertionError: expected 1 to be 2`.
- **HEAD (this branch)**: after the same step, the models request count reaches
  **2** and the refreshed catalog is returned. GREEN: `Tests 2 passed (2)`.

Recorded trace (synthetic token/endpoint, no credentials):

```text
[probe] discoverMantleModels(region=probe-region, bearerToken=synthetic-probe-token)
[probe] fetchWithSsrFGuard -> GET https://bedrock-mantle.probe-region.api.aws/v1/models  (count=1)
[probe] wall clock stepped back 7200s; elapsed advanced 7200s
[probe] fetchWithSsrFGuard -> GET https://bedrock-mantle.probe-region.api.aws/v1/models  (count=2)  <-- refetch on elapsed expiry
```

Control: with only the wall clock jumped forward (elapsed still in-window), the
cache serves and the count stays **1** — no over-refresh on a forward clock jump.

## Not tested

Remote-run reproduction on the shared test server was blocked by a pre-existing
environment issue unrelated to this change (the `extension-providers` vitest
config loads the Control UI Solid plugin, which fails to resolve under the remote
docker/node ESM loader — an unchanged file fails identically). Proof above uses
the repository's real `run-vitest.mjs` entry and real module chain locally.

Precedent: #192469, #190894, #192700

prs.title: fix(deepinfra): honor thinking off for Nemotron 3.5 Super VL
prs.body:
Closes #192978

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: explicit thinking off omits a disabled-reasoning selector when using DeepInfra Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on the OpenAI-compatible chat route.

## User Impact
User impact: choosing off for this model now sends an explicit request to disable its default-on reasoning; enabled levels and unset/provider-default behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made
Use DeepInfra's documented reasoning.enabled false control in its existing provider wrapper, scoped to the exact model and completions API because off support is not universal across DeepInfra reasoning models.

## Evidence

### Shipped CLI entrypoint (2026-11-05)

On the unchanged accepted tree, the actual `openclaw.mjs agent exec` entrypoint selected `deepinfra/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL` with `--thinking off`, a task-private pinned config and the real DeepInfra extension. The actual CLI process ran from 02:44:48 to 02:44:56 UTC and exited 0. The real client made one local HTTP POST containing `reasoning: { enabled: false }` and no scalar `reasoning_effort`. A compatible synthetic SSE response reached the CLI's final JSON output.

```text
HTTP requests: 1; synthetic SSE responses: 1
request.model: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL
request.reasoning.enabled: false
request.reasoning_effort: absent
CLI: ok=true, status=ok, provider=deepinfra, exit=0
CLI final: SYNTHETIC_LOOPBACK_RESPONSE_REQUEST04
```

The marker retains the previous fixture's name because that response helper was reused; the new process timestamps and request receipts identify this successful run. The prior attempt failed before HTTP dispatch because it combined mutually exclusive `--config` and `--auth-env-only`; it remains recorded separately. The corrected run removed only `--auth-env-only`, retaining the normal CLI attribution and admission checks. The listener closed, its thread joined, and no observed descendants or unknown operations remained.

The existing staged build identifies `79914df148bc963162e9fa0258c223817955a821`. Its tracked runtime source is byte-equivalent to the accepted tree; the sole source-tree difference is the test allocation. This is not a fresh current-commit build. The configured DeepInfra artifact was hashed before and after, with identity tied to the normal loader declaration and observed provider behavior; no low-level import trace was collected. This proves local shipped-entrypoint serialization and response consumption, not real DeepInfra inference, vendor interpretation, shared Gateway execution or maintainer acceptance. The original tests and reviews were not rerun.

### Test-line ratchet follow-up

- Preserves the real [checks-fast-baseline-ratchets failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41902050581/job/126827466961). Reproduction at the retained CI merge context: 6,472,219 test lines, ceiling 6,472,129, over by 90, net delta +106. This was a budget failure, not a runtime/environment failure.
- Adds only config/test-lines-allocations/deepinfra-nemotron-thinking-off.txt = 106 under the documented change-owned regression allocation policy. That equals this PR's entire net new test-file LF count. The shared scalar and accepted product/test/doc bytes stay unchanged; no unrelated test removal or shared-scalar adjustment. The effective ceiling increases only through this permitted, scoped 106-line grant.
- Necessity: registered-provider plus actual serialized-request capture proves the missing off selector at the owning boundary. The same file retains five distinct enabled/default, DeepSeek, Anthropic and always-on GLM controls. A helper-only test could pass while the provider's final request stays broken, and moving setup to test-support still counts. Reclaiming 90 of the 106 lines would remove most of the required fixture/assertions rather than provide a small consolidation.
- Local ratchet after allocation, same historical CI merge context: Test lines OK: 6472219; ceiling: 6472235; slack: 16. Refreshed-main merge probe at cd4cd6b4168b61c7cb6a949a3bb44e885a2d6da0: Test lines OK: 6473328; ceiling: 6473353; slack: 25. These are isolated local merge-tree probes, not branch integration or a claim that GitHub CI has rerun.
- Cost check: OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2 pnpm test extensions/deepinfra/reasoning.test.ts --maxWorkers=1: six tests passed, command wall 11.606s; Vitest reports 8.72s. Actual Vitest child is the supported pinned OpenClaw Bun fork (executable SHA-256 0cef667e2f3fd465b6429904ed074381a679be379ec44fa42b5f460ed118b2b8); the Node launcher version is not used as runtime evidence. Separately attributable per-file CI seconds are not available in the retained CI material and are not invented.
- Functional proof reused without relabeling: accepted packet 02's 139-test fast lane, 122 compatibility guards and supported guarded typecheck apply because all product/test bytes are unchanged. The six-case cost check is a subset, not an additional unique-test count. Two fresh independent native autoreview invocations at high effort covering P0-P3 are scoped-clean with zero findings on final candidate 650f36697fef550ee2077a3a21fa60f474ca9b71, tree acf3f8555c7a854f5ccf6b666bade67985437a06. The earlier accepted functional reviews are preserved; these are separate new reviews of the allocation update.


- Registered-provider synthetic capture through the real OpenAI-completions client: exact baseline 6efce589ab1a0e93e1d338e7d2d0925ced9e5a71 and refreshed main base e629e2a6eaceb7b62fa935177967687847b5d669 omit both off selectors. Candidate 79914df148bc963162e9fa0258c223817955a821 serializes reasoning: { enabled: false } and no scalar reasoning_effort.
- Supported pinned-Bun rerun on the identical candidate: pnpm test:extension deepinfra passes 139 tests, and all 122 shared OpenRouter/reasoning/completions guards are rerun and pass. Guarded typecheck passes under the pinned Bun launcher with the native compiler directly observed. The earlier four-file 41-test result and six-case capture proof remain preserved separately; their actual historical child runtime is undetermined and is not relabeled.
- Preservation controls cover enabled nested effort, unset/default behavior, DeepSeek disabled thinking, Anthropic cache markers, and no new off selector for always-on GLM. No shared OpenRouter normalizer was changed.
- Scoped guarded typecheck, targeted lint, Markdown lint (1,403 files), formatting and git diff checks passed. Two independent native high-effort P0-P3 reviews are scoped-clean on the exact candidate, with no findings.
- Actual supported test runtime: pinned OpenClaw Bun 1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1, SHA-256 0cef667e2f3fd465b6429904ed074381a679be379ec44fa42b5f460ed118b2b8, verified from observed Vitest/worker executable paths and bytes. The ordinary pnpm/runner launcher remains Node v24.20.0 (below the current source-checkout Node floor); its version is not used as child-runtime evidence or claimed to meet that floor. pnpm 12.15.0, Linux x64. No shared installation change or admission bypass was used. These remain local captured-request results, not live vendor inference or service-side success evidence.

Reproduction command (copy only the supplied regression test to the baseline for the red run):

    OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2 pnpm test:extension deepinfra

Contract: https://docs.deepinfra.com/chat/reasoning and https://deepinfra.com/blog/nvidia-nemotron-3-5-super-vl-release. Nested reasoning.effort remains supported; this fix makes no universal off claim.

AI assistance: implementation, tests, evidence and this draft were prepared with Roboclaw/OpenClaw AI assistance; the two native review reports are retained separately from the implementation.

Runtime supplement is hash-bound to original packet SHA-256 806f788d18a38870f5455d4479777d020b3a52a8dca8441980152205c2d88160. Candidate 79914df148bc963162e9fa0258c223817955a821/tree 746dcd41ad36f82ef9dd0837ece05df08742f344 and all three source blobs are unchanged; both existing native reviews remain bound and were not rerun.

Transport note: published commit 48483a20ca34450765bbe6b6918293d02abcc5f5 has the same tree acf3f8555c7a854f5ccf6b666bade67985437a06 and parent as the reviewed private candidate; only Git commit metadata differs. The shipped CLI local-HTTP proof is recorded above; shared Gateway and live-vendor execution were not performed.

prs.title: fix(agent): --config-override errors show a blank path when a top-level key is wrong
prs.body:
Related: #191974

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw agent --config-override` errors show a blank path when the bad key is at the top level, so `{"sessions":{"allowThreadTargets":true}}` gives `Invalid --config-override: : Unrecognized key: "sessions"`.

## User Impact

User impact: that error now reads `<root>: Unrecognized key: "sessions"`, so a key put at the top level by mistake says where it is. Paths into arrays change too, from `agents.list.0.id` to `agents.list[0].id`, which is how the reload log and the other config errors already print them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Same gap #191974 closed for the reload log. The message goes through the shared issue formatter with the root label on, rather than building each line itself.

## Evidence

The new row in the rejected-override table in `agent-exec.test.ts` fails on `main` (it gets `: Unrecognized key`) and passes with the change. That's from verbatim copies of the formatter and the message line, since I couldn't install the workspace, so the real suite hasn't run it yet. Autoreview and ClawSweeper weren't available, so I had Codex look over the final diff instead and it found nothing to change.

---

`/config set` builds the same line by hand in `config-mutations.ts`, so a top-level typo there probably shows the blank path as well. I haven't tried it, so it's not in here.

prs.title: fix(copilot): discover models with usable saved sign-ins
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/issues/1870

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: GitHub Copilot model discovery returns no usable models when an inactive setup replacement or expired token is the first saved profile, even though a later saved sign-in works.

## User Impact

Users can discover Copilot models using an eligible saved sign-in without adding a manual auth order or repeating device login. Explicitly selected profiles, configured account order (including an empty order), and direct/environment credential priority are unchanged.

This is a partial repair related to the Store onboarding report. It does not establish or claim to fix its separate runtime SecretRef error, the rejected profile's HTTP 401, or Windows issue #1761's browser callback failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Automatic discovery bypassed the shared credential eligibility owner and selected the first stored profile. The existing explicit-order path already used the canonical resolver. Both unpinned paths now use that resolver, removing the separate first-profile policy. Explicit profile requests remain pinned.

Simplification: production +7/-13 lines, tests +27, docs +3/-1. No new state, configuration, migration, retry, or credential fallback mechanism.

## Evidence

- Base-red registered-provider regression: both inactive and expired first-profile cases return an empty model list instead of the usable later account's model. Two failures, 39 skipped; 126.62s wrapper wall with cold compiled-worker setup.
- After repair: all 41 registered-provider tests and all 14 auth-resolution tests pass. Two shards, 65.40s wrapper wall; registered-provider file 45.84s including compilation (test execution about 10s), auth file 15.32s.
- The regression uses the registered provider catalog and real isolated auth-profile storage. Copilot token exchange and model HTTP responses are synthetic. It observes the model list exposed to the caller and ensures exactly one exchange, not a retry loop.
- Extension production and test TypeScript checks pass. Focused type-aware lint, formatting and git diff checks pass.
- Fresh shared Codex autoreview through P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Review scope was the three-file patch plus supplied owner/issue context; unchanged source was unavailable to the reviewer.
- Separate existing real-WebSocket first-signin integration passed (one scenario, 38.7s test / 345.3s wrapper including a cold runtime build). This exercises sign-in reuse, protected tokenRef activation, ownership and revocation with synthetic provider HTTP. It is not a reproduction of the reported Windows Current model verification failure.

Not verified: authenticated Microsoft Store/Windows UI flow, live provider account, update/reboot scenario. [Required CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40438130948) and its [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40439243860) passed for head `25042ab6d7fcb0d5454b4608644a323c49d9b958`. [Exact-head ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185328#issuecomment-6432400928) completed with no findings or before-merge requests. Shipped CLI/upgrade proof remains an optional improvement, not executed evidence. No merge requested.

prs.title: fix(apple): New Chat starts an independent conversation like the web UI; /new keeps inheriting
prs.body:
Related: #189467

## What Problem This Solves

Restores contextual native `/new` inheritance affected by #189467, while preserving the landed behavior where sidebar/global New Chat starts independently with Gateway defaults.

## User Impact

New Chat starts an independent conversation with Gateway defaults. In-chat `/new` again creates a child and inherits the current conversation's settings. Agent selection, worktree options, creation guards, and unsupported-transport behavior are preserved.

A Gateway may group an independent conversation under Home; that implicit association is separate from explicitly requesting a parent and inheriting its settings.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared native producer handles two different intents. This change defaults it to independent creation and opts only in-chat `/new` into inheritance, on both the direct transport and captured-route paths.

Now that #189467 has landed, this preserves its independent sidebar/global creation while restoring contextual `/new` inheritance to match the web UI. Web references at base `d921a2bfcc4`:

- Sidebar navigation: [app-sidebar-base.ts:327–333](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d921a2bfcc4/ui/src/components/app-sidebar-base.ts#L327-L333).
- Global New Session builds [draft parameters without a parent](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d921a2bfcc4/ui/src/pages/new-session/draft-create-params.ts#L17) and [submits them](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d921a2bfcc4/ui/src/pages/new-session/draft-submission-flow.ts#L496-L568).
- In-chat `/new` uses [createSession](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d921a2bfcc4/ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-session-creation.ts#L144-L170) and [resolveSessionCreateParams](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d921a2bfcc4/ui/src/lib/sessions/session-create-params.ts#L1-L14), including the parent.
- Gateway [root grouping and parent inheritance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d921a2bfcc4/src/gateway/session-create-inheritance.ts#L36-L62) remain unchanged.

## Evidence

### Original contributor evidence (historical)

- Stock source plus regression tests: **46 tests, five expected assertion failures** (0.197 seconds). All ordinary/Home × direct/captured sidebar cases incorrectly supplied a parent; the `/new` parent assertion already passed.
- Patched: **47 tests passed** (0.201 seconds), including sidebar parent absence, in-chat parent inheritance, and same-/cross-agent ownership guards.
- Command: `DEVELOPER_DIR=<Xcode 27.1> nice -n 15 swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit -j 2 --filter ChatViewModelSessionActionTests`, after `node scripts/prepare-apple-mermaid.mjs`.
- Final formatted commit plus agent-navigation boundaries: **65 tests passed** in two suites (0.198 seconds). Scoped SwiftFormat passed; SwiftLint exited zero with four pre-existing long-line warnings outside the diff.
- Local review: Codex and cross-family passes both clean.
- Real native simulator proof: sidebar New Chat emitted a fresh key without a parent or settings overrides and persisted the agent default model; in-chat `/new` emitted the parent and persisted its nondefault model. Independently checked through session metadata and inspected screenshots. Native build and XCUITest driver both passed; all owned sessions, simulator, and paired device cleaned up. No model turns required.

### Maintainer repair and native proof (2026-11-05)

- Preserves all 46 baseline session-action test functions and adds four functions covering nine parameterized cases. Explicit direct/captured fixtures prevent a reset fallback from standing in for creation.
- Native before/after comparison: before, 47 tests / 52 cases with exactly two expected `/new` inheritance assertion failures; after, 50 tests / 59 cases passing, zero issues or skips.
- Supplied native execution used Xcode 27.2 / Swift 6.4.2 on macOS 27.0. Checksums, source trees, commands and logs were independently verified; this was not a Linux-native run.
- The supplied Mac runs tested commit `bc07858757938fffff1a0ed28374f0fd6c44affc` / tree `b967b9597d92433072ec7ca8df9a013e41735a4f`, using the same disclosed test-only helper overlay in both lanes. The enclosing verbosity test was compiled but not selected.
- Refreshed candidate `8658e01b86de3faa57b552e1f2ae5cc1c5c9eba3` retains byte-identical behavior changes and session-action tests. It resolves the newer-main helper overlap by keeping #193084: `loadAndWaitBootstrap` awaits the owning task and asserts `!isLoading`, so the redundant additional wait is removed. The helper file is byte-identical to current baseline. The earlier Mac results are not claimed as execution of this new whole tree; fresh exact-head native CI remains required.
- Refreshed diff against baseline `982f3b1ee2b668afafe69c352d48baef470d2d20`: production +14/-7 (net +7); tests +53/-0 (net +53). No new config/protocol surface. Focused proof does not replace required hosted CI or claim live Gateway/device validation.

### Separate follow-up

Preexisting native command-hook, main-session reset and `/new <model>` parity gaps are not expanded into this inheritance repair.

AI-assisted implementation and review. [Sanitized working log and native screenshots](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/tree/7543a4dd082dd670b62db17caf19f9d8c6202313).

prs.title: fix(gateway): record visible activity on chat setup failures
prs.body:
Related: #160003

## What Problem This Solves

When an accepted chat fails during setup or dispatch before its run starts, the terminal failure can be recorded without advancing session activity. A user who has already marked the session read can therefore miss that failure.

The restart-safe recovery path originally addressed by this PR was removed by #185730. This revision targets the remaining setup and dispatch failure paths in the current architecture. It does not claim that the removed mechanism still exists or that every symptom in #160003 is resolved.

## Change

Carry the existing run and RPC-source visibility into terminal lifecycle persistence. Visible failures advance activity; hidden work remains quiet. Lifecycle ownership and the unread predicate are unchanged.

Thanks @wangmiao0668000666 for the original investigation in #159285.

## Evidence

- On upstream main `4e472c7eda03fe91631ee666ca79e08b40206ae7`, the new isolated SQLite regressions fail for visible setup and unstarted dispatch failures because `lastActivityAt` does not advance. The hidden setup control passes.
- On the candidate, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-dispatch-errors.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 25/25 on Windows with Node 24.22.1 using isolated SQLite state. Targeted lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and the test-line ratchet against that upstream snapshot passed. The separate allocation covers 61 net regression-test lines for both terminal paths and hidden controls.
- Independent source review found no actionable defects. This exercises the lifecycle owner, not a browser-rendering or live Gateway flow.
- The updated head `278ccf6b9159efcdcb8d8c08e187cd82538857a8` has a successful `openclaw/ci-gate` status. Consult its checks for details.

The prior PR evidence and old-head CI concerned the removed recovery path and are not validation of this revision.

prs.title: fix(feishu): keep ordinary inline quotes out of topics
prs.body:
Closes #193140

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary Feishu group quotes carrying `root_id` without `thread_id` are incorrectly classified as topic messages. This forces `reply_in_thread: true` despite default or disabled `replyInThread`, for both ordinary replies and streaming-card startup.

## User Impact

Ordinary root-only quotes stay inline. Actual thread IDs, topic-group root fallback and explicitly enabled topics retain their behavior. Quote ancestry, triggering-message reply targets, session keys and mention admission are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Classify topic membership at the inbound producer using `thread_id`, with the existing `topic_group` root fallback. Keep `root_id` available as reply ancestry. The repair changes one predicate and its explanatory comment, updates existing consumer expectations, and adds a regression through the actual handler, dispatcher, send owner and Lark SDK serializer.

## Evidence

| Check | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ordinary root-only quotes: two scopes × two configurations × ordinary/streaming send | 8 assertion failures | 8 passed |
| Actual thread/topic-group/enabled controls | 6 passed | 6 passed |
| Existing handler suite | — | 60 passed |
| Mention/thread/dispatcher coverage | — | 102 passed |

- The regression checks the final serialized `message.reply` body, including CardKit-reference streaming replies. Synthetic inference and isolated external HTTP I/O are the fixture boundaries; there is **no live Feishu or model/Gateway proof**.

prs.title: fix(voice-call): resolve model aliases for responseModel (#191631)
prs.body:
Closes #191631

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where configuring a model alias in `voiceConfig.responseModel` (such as `responseModel: "medium"` or `responseModel: "support-model"`) causes voice-call text response generation and realtime consults to treat the alias as a literal model ID on the runtime default provider (e.g. `together/medium`) instead of resolving it against configured model aliases in `coreConfig` (e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`).

## Why This Change Was Made

In `extensions/voice-call/src/response-model.ts`, `resolveVoiceResponseModel` now accepts optional `coreConfig` and `agentId`. When `coreConfig` and `responseModel` are supplied, it resolves aliases using `buildModelAliasIndex` and `resolveModelRefFromString` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-runtime`. If resolved, the alias's canonical `provider` and `model` are returned. When unmapped or when `coreConfig` is omitted, it preserves existing single-segment fallback on the runtime default provider for full backwards compatibility. Both classic response generation (`generateVoiceResponse`) and realtime consultation (`createVoiceCallRuntime`) now forward `coreConfig` and `agentId` to `resolveVoiceResponseModel`.

## User Impact

Users and operators can now configure friendly model aliases (both global defaults and agent-scoped models) in voice-call `responseModel` settings. Classic response generation and realtime agent consults will reliably resolve and dispatch to the alias's underlying provider/model without requiring raw provider-qualified strings.

## Evidence

1. **Reproduction & Regression Unit Tests**:
   Added tests in `extensions/voice-call/src/response-model.test.ts`:
   - `resolves model aliases configured in coreConfig`
   - `resolves agent-scoped model aliases when agentId is provided`
   Added tests in `extensions/voice-call/src/response-generator.test.ts`:
   - `resolves model aliases configured in coreConfig when responseModel is set`
   Added tests in `extensions/voice-call/src/runtime.test.ts`:

2. **Test Suite Verification**:
