prs.title: fix(cli): load Unicode PowerShell completion files on Windows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes PowerShell completion installation failing to load when the Windows state directory contains non-ASCII characters, and cached completion corrupting Unicode command choices in Windows PowerShell.

## User Impact

Windows PowerShell users can reload installed completion from Unicode paths and receive the original Unicode choices. Re-run the existing completion installation command to repair a previous profile. No configuration or migration is required. Existing UTF-16 profiles keep their encoding; ASCII and non-Windows output remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Windows PowerShell reads BOM-less script files as ANSI. Declare UTF-8 only when the existing profile/cache writer emits non-ASCII text. Keep profile preservation, atomic publication, and stdout generation with their existing owners.

## Evidence

Native Windows, Node 24.22.1, actual `powershell.exe` 5. The command-entry reproduction used `registerCompletionCli` with `completion --shell powershell --install --yes`, a real cache under a task-only `state ü 空` directory, and then dot-sourced the resulting profile. Paths below are redacted; no platform or filesystem mocks.

```text
BEFORE
profilePrefix: 23204f (no BOM)
powershell.exe: exit 1
CommandNotFoundException: the cache path is decoded incorrectly

AFTER
profilePrefix: efbbbf
powershell.exe: exit 0
{"major":5,"loaded":true}
stderr: ""
```

The committed regressions exercise actual PS5 file decoding for new/existing profiles and the real CLI cache writer with a bounded fixture command registry, then request completion through `CommandCompletion.CompleteInput`. Existing tests evaluated script strings directly and therefore missed file decoding.

- Unmodified owner: **3 failed, 16 passed, 3 existing POSIX-only skips**; the two Unicode-path cases fail on profile reload, and the cached choice is decoded incorrectly.
- Repaired owner: **19 passed, 3 unchanged skips** across both files; 12.10 s wall time, about 7.6 s native profile test time. Native PS5 processes are necessary to test its file decoder. GitHub’s incremental CI matrix skipped the Windows job; the native Windows/PowerShell results above are local.
- Targeted maintained production/test types, typed lint (four files), formatting and whitespace checks passed. Independent manual review and canonical complete five-file P0–P3 review: scoped-clean, zero findings; all six file/context hashes unchanged. The compatibility consumer suite had 19 passed, 1 failed, 10 skipped: its untouched Windows Bash/MSYS fixture fails identically on the clean base, with no added skip or weakened assertion. Full exact-head CI passed on `4088c2c3d5cc8c2ee08cf025999f14811cf30181` (run 40628894530). Native Windows timings above are local; GitHub CI timing is not presented as a measured before/after test-cost comparison.

<details>
<summary>Scope and simplification</summary>

The two existing file producers remain the owners. No new API, setting, dependency, shell invocation in production, or wrapper is introduced. One existing profile table gains two concrete filesystem-decoding cases; one CLI-writer regression protects Unicode cache contents. Distinct open completion PRs #173223 (quote escaping) and #162918 (option terminators) were inspected and do not repair file encoding.

</details>


<!-- unicode-production-proof-20261104 -->
## November 4 production repair and shipped Windows PowerShell 5 proof

Verified head: **38dff0100f57c8656433d3dc24ef628f2e966cb1**. Main **8c411658c18b2787937e75db8c56faad10532590** was merged normally, retaining upstream native profile-removal tests. Before push, live main **d1d350f5f2a8dcbb53a39b0b9954159e225347b5** was inspected: its five newer commits do not change the completion owners. No force push, PR merge, or review bypass.

### Additional production upgrade bug reproduced and fixed

Stable BOM-less Unicode cache files survive ordinary completion --install because that command reuses cached plugin registrations. Fixing only newly generated files did not repair this upgrade: Windows PowerShell 5 still returned mojibake. Installation now validates existing BOM-less Unicode cache bytes as UTF-8 and atomically prefixes their exact payload with the BOM. It does not regenerate the cache, lose plugin commands, or rewrite configuration. Existing BOM-marked UTF-8/UTF-16 and ASCII caches stay unchanged.

Regression red: **1 failed, 16 skipped** expecting the BOM on the preexisting cache. Green: **19 passed, 3 existing platform skips** including native Unicode completion. No new test file.

### Actual shipped CLI -> native Windows PowerShell 5

On Windows with Node 24.22.1, the real built shipping launcher ran:

    node openclaw.mjs completion --shell powershell --write-state --install --yes

A harmless task-local plugin registered the command **openclaw unicode-proof café空** through the normal plugin CLI API. Synthetic home/config/state paths contained **ü 空**. A separate **powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive** process explicitly dot-sourced only the synthetic profile and called:

    $line='openclaw unicode-proof caf'
    [System.Management.Automation.CommandCompletion]::CompleteInput($line,$line.Length,$null).CompletionMatches

Native choice strings were UTF-8/base64 encoded inside PowerShell to avoid terminal-codepage ambiguity. Raw output:

    {"major":5,"choices":["Y2Fmw6nnqbo="]}

CLI exit **0**, PowerShell exit **0**, stderr empty, profile prefix **efbbbf**, cache prefix **efbbbf**. The choice decodes to exactly **café空**. No PowerShell 7 substitution; no registerCompletionCli harness in this proof.

### Actual published stable 2026.10.8 -> candidate compatibility

The npm openclaw@2026.10.8 archive was extracted task-locally and its own production dependencies installed there (ignore-workspace, scripts disabled). Its real openclaw.mjs generated/installed the plugin cache into an existing synthetic UTF-16LE/BOM profile containing CRLF user code and an imported custom completion script. Existing config enabled the fixture plugin. Candidate ran only:

    node openclaw.mjs completion --shell powershell --install --yes

Raw stable native output (mojibake choice):

    {"choices":["Y2Fmw4PCqcOnwqnCug=="],"greeting":"Y2Fmw6kg56m6","imported":"ZMOpasOgIOepug==","major":5}

Raw upgraded native output:

    {"choices":["Y2Fmw6nnqbo="],"greeting":"Y2Fmw6kg56m6","imported":"ZMOpasOgIOepug==","major":5}

Stable CLI, candidate CLI, both native invocations, and a second candidate reinstall all exit **0**. Passed assertions: **profile byte-exact**, **config byte-exact**, **cached plugin payload byte-exact after removing the newly added BOM**, imported completion/user greeting unchanged, upgraded choice exactly **café空**, reinstall idempotent. Operator shell profiles/rc/config, live Gateway, installed OpenClaw, and credentials were untouched. Every native shell used -NoProfile and loaded only the synthetic profile; no real accounts or non-public endpoints were involved.

### Exact-head validation receipts

All nine steps returned actual exit **0** at the verified head:

1. Bounded shipping cliStartup build, 4,608 MB heap/two Rayon threads.
2. Shipped CLI -> PowerShell 5 Unicode fixture.
3. Published stable -> candidate compatibility/idempotence fixture.
4. Native/cache regressions **19 passed, 3 skipped** plus doctor consumers **8 passed**; two shards, maximum one test worker.
5. Maintained formatting.
6. Allocation ratchet: total **6,476,665**, ceiling **6,476,749**, slack **84**, narrowly justified allocation **54**.
7. Maintained focused production types.

Both failures were separately reproduced with integrated-main production completion files, then candidate files restored byte-for-byte. They are not counted as passes or repaired here.

Canonical independent autoreview: **scoped-clean at P3, no actionable findings**, limited to supplied patch, not project execution. A separate independent read-only reviewer checked the final line-limit simplification and production/test diff: **no actionable findings**; exhaustive comparison of all **16,843,009** byte buffers of lengths 0-3 found **zero BOM-predicate mismatches**. prs.title: docs(sessions): say archived delete is scope-based, not creator-based
prs.body:
Fixes #191949

## What Problem This Solves

`docs/concepts/multi-user.md` states the archive/restore creator rule, and `docs/gateway/operator-scopes.md` lists the `sessions.delete` scopes, but neither says whether deleting an archived session inherits that creator rule. A reader cannot tell whether an `operator.write` caller who did not create the session may delete it once it is archived.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deletion is scope-based, not creator-based. `sessions.delete` is a dynamic-scope method (`src/gateway/methods/core-descriptors.ts`): `operator.write` may delete an already-archived session with the supported fields, `operator.admin` keeps unrestricted delete, and the handler rechecks the archived requirement (`src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-delete.ts`). There is no creator gate on that path, unlike archive and restore.

Both pages now say so next to the existing rules:

- `multi-user.md`: the archive paragraph states the creator rule, then notes that deleting an archived session is not creator-limited.
- `operator-scopes.md`: the `sessions.delete` bullet adds the same clarification for the archived-only path.

## Evidence

- Behavior: `src/gateway/methods/core-descriptors.ts` ("State-aware: write scope may delete already-archived sessions") and `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-delete.ts` (archived-only recheck; the delete path has no creator comparison).
- Docs: `oxfmt --check` clean on both files; `git diff --check` clean.

prs.title: fix: ignore a captured revocation after the same key is approved again
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A captured OpenClaw ID revocation can delete a device again after an owner approves that same key back. Membership changes carry a sequence number, so a second submit fails. A revocation does not, and the mailbox accepts it.

## User Impact

Submitting the same signed revocation again does not remove an owner device or browser that was approved after that signature was captured. A new signature still revokes, including when the signer's clock is behind the certificate. A revocation for a key the claw no longer lists stays a no-op.

## Why This Change Was Made

`applyRevocation` used to delete whatever fingerprint was listed, so the old signature removed a later approval. Comparing `issued_at` with the certificate clock was the wrong guard: a certificate may be up to five minutes ahead of Gateway time, and a fresh revocation then looked older than the certificate. The signature that actually removed a key is remembered instead. The same bytes are a no-op. A different signature still revokes, and a revocable owner still takes every device it currently approved.

## Evidence

Terminal output from the identity protocol package at `ec20db33baa1`, through `submitStatement`:

```
revocation > keeps a newer approval when an older revocation is submitted again
revocation > still removes every device a revocable owner approved
revocation > honours a revocation that is newer on the signer's clock than the add
revocation > removes a device with every device it approved, transitively, and disconnects them
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Submitting a previously accepted revocation through the mailbox removed an owner device, or a member browser, that had been approved again after that revocation was signed.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node, packages/openclaw-id-protocol at ec20db33baa1. The reference membership model is the owner of this rule. The Gateway does not call it yet.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** From the package, ran the allowlist suite. One case replays the same signed revocation after a newer certificate and expects no events. One revokes an owner by peer key while a descendant certificate is 120 seconds ahead, and expects every device removed. One revokes a browser at WORLD_NOW + 1 while Gateway now is WORLD_NOW + 120, and expects the browser peer keys cleared.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from that run:

```
revocation > keeps a newer approval when an older revocation is submitted again
revocation > still removes every device a revocable owner approved
revocation > honours a revocation that is newer on the signer's clock than the add
revocation > removes a device with every device it approved, transitively, and disconnects them
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The replay returns no events and leaves the re-approved device listed. A new signature still removes the owner and every device it approved, even when a descendant certificate is two minutes ahead. A browser revocation still clears that browser when the Gateway clock is ahead of the signer. A second submit while the key is already gone still changes nothing.
- **What was not tested:** A live Gateway or Discovery mailbox. No route calls `submitStatement` yet.

prs.title: fix(plugins): reject duplicate tool-name registration instead of silently shadowing
prs.body:
## Summary

`registerTool` appended entries to `registry.tools` **without checking whether a tool with the same name already existed**. Downstream resolution does a first-match name lookup (e.g. `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/prompt-cache-observability.ts:655` `previous.tools.find(c => c.name === tool.name)`), so a later registration with an already-taken name was **silently shadowed** — no error, no warning.

This mirrors `registerHook`, which already rejects duplicate hook names:

```ts
const existingHook = registry.hooks.find((e) => e.entry.hook.name === hookName);
if (existingHook) { reportRegistrationError(record, `hook already registered: ${hookName} (${existingHook.pluginId})`); return; }
```

## Change

In `src/plugins/registry-registrars.ts`, before `registry.tools.push(...)`, bail out with a registration error when any of the new `normalized` names collides with an existing entry's `names`:

```
tool already registered: <name> (<pluginId>)
```

The check is case-sensitive, matching the existing `normalizePluginToolNames` semantics (so `Alpha` and `alpha` remain distinct).

## Tests

`src/plugins/tool-factory-context.test.ts`:
- rejects duplicate tool names within a plugin
- rejects cross-plugin tool name collisions

All plugin tool-registry tests pass (18 in this file + 82 across `registry-registrars.*` and `tools.optional`).

## Impact

Plugins that accidentally register the same tool name twice now surface a clear registration error instead of producing a dead/shadowed tool. Correctly-named registrations are unaffected.

prs.body:
Related: #190258, #79252

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with rolling loop detection enabled, an agent can indefinitely repeat a stable Code Mode `exec` → `read` → `write` workflow because each signature occupies only a third of the history window.

## User Impact

Stable three-tool rotations now reach the existing critical recovery path. Progressing workflows and separate runs in the same conversation remain allowed. Rolling detection remains opt-in.

## Why This Change Was Made

The global breaker previously reused a per-signature streak. The existing no-progress owner now also aggregates repeated stable outcomes across different tools in the current run. Changed outcomes end that shared tail, and pending calls or unanchored vetoes cannot establish repetition. Only continuing participants inherit the shared breaker, so a new tool or arguments can execute during recovery. Typed terminal failures reuse their stable failure identity. The bounded 30-record history and single-tool argument-churn policy remain unchanged.

The regression table covers stable rotation, progress, pending results and unanchored vetoes. Consolidating existing veto-test setup preserves its assertions while reducing total test lines by one; no baseline or allocation changes are needed.

prs.title: fix(goals): retain admitted continuation custody across restart
prs.body:
Related: #192988. Depends on #193103 and #193024.

## What Problem This Solves

An accepted Goal continuation can disappear during a Gateway restart, leaving an active Goal with no execution owner.

## User Impact

Admitted Goal work can resume after restart using its original operator permissions and tool/delivery restrictions. Earlier accepted human input keeps priority, and Stop, Pause, clear, or replacement cancels stale pursuit.

This dependent draft is not live-qualified or ready to merge. Recovery refuses unavailable original authority, source-bound capabilities, and required workers rather than broadening permissions. Unanswered human-decision durability and Codex autonomous pursuit are not implemented by this slice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing session store records the accepted continuation before its predecessor releases it. Startup and child settlement use the ordinary input/execution owners to recover that exact receipt. Writer cleanup preserves pursuit custody, while explicit Stop and Goal/session changes invalidate it. A narrowly guarded adoption transition permits a restart-interrupted execution to reacquire its Goal without weakening the native owner check.

Storage, publication, restoration, acquisition, and final delivery ship together: splitting these would leave a stored receipt without a safe consumer. No new scheduler, queue, timer, or state store is introduced. This branch includes the unchanged prerequisites; [the stage-only comparison](https://github.com/GoatInAHat/openclaw/compare/c0286528d78be1de21d309ae45203a31f81bbcde...41f1d1aab017a0ec0268621ec01d11d873347ee1) isolates this change.

## Evidence

Checked recovery commit: `41f1d1aab017a0ec0268621ec01d11d873347ee1`.

- Final owning/consumer batch: 594 passing tests across 29 files.
- Eight canonical production/test type projects pass. Scoped lint, formatting, MDX and exact incremental test allocation (1,690 LF) pass.
- All 49 committed paths match the independently reviewed final source and index hashes.

- Original production reproduces writer receipt loss and interrupted execution rejection before any model call. Five cancellation controls pass on that baseline.
- Corrected running and already-killed recovery cases pass. A second interrupted recovery completes through a fresh Gateway context over the same store; expired occurrence authority remains expired. All eleven execution scenarios have passing results across full and focused runs.
- Independent source review resolves both production findings; final fixture-delta review is clear.
- Physical two-process restart, real provider inference and final external delivery remain unqualified. Mocked provider and same-process restart tests are not presented as live proof.

prs.title: fix(update): updates fail when another connection opens the state database during a generation read
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: updates fail with "SQLite WAL commit publication could not be verified" when anything opens or closes the state database during a generation read, even without writing.

## User Impact

User impact: an update no longer fails, or loses automatic database restoration, just because another connection briefly opened or closed the state database without writing. Real writes during the read still fail the same way they do now.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readUpdateDatabaseGeneration` and `readUnchangedUpdateDatabaseGeneration` compare the WAL index header before and after reading, and refuse when it appears or disappears. A connection that opens a closed WAL database without writing creates an empty `-wal` and a `-shm` whose change counter, commit checksum and frame count are all zero. When the last connection closes, both files go away. Neither publishes a commit. `sameSqliteFileGeneration` already treats that empty-WAL churn as unchanged, but the header check didn't.

The read now accepts that one transition: from no index to a zero-commit index, or back, with no rollback journal and no WAL frames. Two different headers still refuse. So does a header that carries commit evidence and then disappears, and so does any real commit, which fails earlier with "SQLite file generation changed while reading". Fingerprints, `emptyReaderAlternate` and receipt reuse are unchanged. A receipt simply isn't reused across the transition, and the caller reads again.

## Evidence

On one Mac, four updates hit this error on `state/openclaw.sqlite` (Oct 26 twice, Nov 2, Nov 4). On Nov 4 the Gateway had already stopped. The pre-migration backup first lost its write generation ("Database changed during capture"). Then the parent's ledger observation before Doctor failed after 2.2 seconds, and the run ended `post-update-failed` even though the new Gateway verified healthy.

Real SQLite probes against an unchanged 615 MB WAL database, with a separate process acting during the read:

- A read-write or read-only connection opening mid-read, with no writes, gives this error.
- A connection closing mid-read, with no writes, gives the same error.
- A real commit mid-read gives "SQLite file generation changed while reading".

New cases in `src/infra/update-database-generations.test.ts` open or close a real `node:sqlite` connection at the final stable read:

- Red on base `a1f99240c836` (branch now rebased on `e531410a397e`; the intervening commits touch macOS, UI, templates, Gateway logs and release code only): the open, close and receipt-reuse cases fail with this error.
- Green on head: the reads return the closed database's generation, or its empty-reader alternate, with source bytes unchanged.
- A commit during the read, and a committed writer retiring its index, still refuse on base and head.
- The whole file passes: 46 tests. Eight generation consumer test files in the infra project pass (177 tests), plus `update-command-migrated-schema` (21). `doctor-maintenance.settlement.test.ts` has one failure, "settles interrupted original-state capture (restart fails: false)", and it fails the same way on base.

Format check passes, `lint:core` has no findings in the touched files, and `tsrs` on core and the infra test shard shows only the existing `packages/ai` error that base also has.

This PR doesn't identify which process opened the database on that machine. The read now tolerates any opener that doesn't write. The stuck-run repair from that failure is #193132.

prs.title: fix(update): repair refuses forever after a verified update fails a later step
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update repair` refuses forever when an update activated a candidate that then verified healthy, but a later update step failed.

## User Impact

User impact: repair now settles that run forward and moves on, so the next update is no longer blocked. A rollback that has real reason to refuse still refuses with the same message.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the updater fails after activation, its plugin cohort stays pending. Repair always rolled a pending cohort back. By then the candidate's Doctor had already completed the plugin obligations the update reopened, so `restorePluginCohortMigrationRowsInDatabase` refused with "Plugin migration obligation changed after update publication". Repair had already recorded the `rollback` disposition before refusing, so every later repair took the same path. Doctor and triage kept pointing back to `update repair`, and nothing native could close the run.

That refusal exists to protect the original core from candidate plugin state. Once the original core is gone, rollback only gets converged forward again by finalization, and its refusal blocks that. `settleInterruptedUpdatePluginCohort` now commits the cohort only when all of these hold:

- no rollback publication has settled yet
- the installed core is provably not the original: a readable different version, or a readable build ID that differs from the original's
- the installation has no package activation anchor, control or journal, and the dry-run pending check passes, so package recovery can't restore the original core afterwards
- the run ledger recorded the candidate serving (service running, version match, same version and build)

The gate checks for the original core's absence instead of the exact candidate build on purpose. An install that is already stuck has to receive this fix as a new build, so its build ID no longer matches the reservation's candidate.

`settleUpdatePluginCohort` accepts commit over a recorded rollback only in that case, through an explicit option. Every other caller keeps its current behavior.

## Evidence

Seen on a Git source install: run `d2e3d44f` activated and verified the candidate, failed in a later database step, and now stays `running` / `activating`. Its cohort holds disposition `rollback` with `settledPublications: 0`, and `update repair` refuses in about 4 seconds with the discord obligation message.

New `src/cli/update-cli/update-plugin-cohort-settlement.test.ts` builds that state with real SQLite: a cohort reservation, an obligation the updater reopened, and a later completion by the candidate's Doctor.

- Red on base: the three forward cases fail with `Plugin migration obligation changed after update publication: discord`. Those cases are a pending cohort, the recorded refused rollback, and the refused rollback under a later repair build.
- Green on head: all three settle, the cohort recovery is gone, recovery admission is clear, and the later decision row is unchanged.
- Refusal still holds on base and head when the original core is installed, when the original version has no readable build ID, when the candidate never recorded serving, when a package activation record remains, and when a rollback publication has already settled. The package-record case fails if its guard is removed.
- `node scripts/test-projects.mts` across `src/plugins/update-cohort-recovery.test.ts`, `src/plugins/update-cohort.test.ts`, `src/infra/update-plugin-cohort-recovery.test.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-repair-command.test.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-repair-handoff.test.ts`, `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-plugin-cohort-handoff.test.ts` and `src/infra/update-plugin-cohort-commit.process.test.ts` passed before the gate revisions. After merging current main, the new file, `update-cohort-recovery`, `update-plugin-cohort-recovery` and `update-repair-command` pass again (95 tests).
- Format check passes, and `lint:core` has no findings in the touched files. Locally, `tsrs` on `tsconfig.core.json` and the cli-update test shard shows only the existing `packages/ai` error that base also has. I couldn't run the `tsgo` wrapper here because it refuses shared pnpm links, so CI owns that check.
- The test-line allocation covers the 205 added lines. `src/cli/plugins-update-command.migrations.integration.test.ts` ("preserves listener settings and completion authority: env-reference") fails on CI, and it fails the same way on base locally.

The WAL generation false failure that made this run fail is fixed separately in #193134.

Related: #178719

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Messages Automation send failures leave the iMessage account green, with no recovery guidance, when a Gateway reply uses AppleScript text, attachment delivery, or the auto fallback.

## User Impact

Failed sends report the affected account and Messages Automation recovery steps. A successful send clears that warning; a successful read probe does not. Delivery error identity and classification are preserved.

**Limitations:** This does not preserve TCC grants across upgrades. Signed macOS upgrade testing was not available.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ordinary sends and native attachment actions now share the existing account-warning publisher. The RPC-only publication and duplicated RPC error-message augmentation were removed. Successful ordinary and native message completion clear only a matching Automation warning, not unrelated watcher errors. No options, permissions, runtime identities, or automatic resend behavior changed.

## Evidence

### User-friendly wording update — November 4

The warnings now lead with plain-language explanations and concrete steps: open Messages, approve any permission prompt, and quit/reopen the app if frozen. Permission-denied errors explain that OpenClaw needs permission to control Messages. Both retain Automation settings guidance, the current `bun` entry for app-managed Gateways, and the reminder to check delivery and queued replies before retrying. The original AppleScript diagnostic is retained at the end so successful-send warning clearing remains unchanged.

Copy-only follow-up: 8 lines added / 8 removed in `process-diagnostics.ts`; no changes to matching, sending, or retry behavior. Checked both generated messages, re-recognition of each normalized warning, unrelated-error rejection, and the error-code boundary with a focused Node check of the source function. Formatting and `git diff --check` pass. The targeted lint wrapper could not start its package-boundary preparation because this older checkout expects a `typescript/fs` export absent from the available dependency installation. Full plugin and live macOS tests were not rerun for this copy-only update; the captures below remain evidence from the explicitly named earlier heads.

**Fault-injected imsg on Linux:** real shipped Gateway, real iMessage plugin, and real process spawn. The executable emits the exact imsg v0.17.0 Automation diagnostic and exits non-zero. This is not real Messages/TCC testing. RED and GREEN used fresh isolated HOME/state/config paths, separate free ports, and identical stand-in/media bytes. The live Gateway was not touched.

Server and client entry points (targets, paths, ports, and hosts redacted):

```sh

# Attachment case: message="", mediaUrl="<isolated-workspace>/proof.pdf"; sendTransport=applescript.

```

The following are recorded account-status projections from CLI JSON; `probeOk` is the returned probe's `ok` field. Long recovery text is explicitly truncated after the System Settings destination. Full captured responses remain in the proof folders.

Captured recovery guidance (identical on both GREEN paths):

On the Messages Mac, open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Automation and allow Messages for the process running imsg. prs.title: fix(cli): do not re-publish a binding cleared mid-turn
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`persistCliSessionBindingResult` rewrote the native CLI session binding on every non-`preserveBinding` settle. `agent_end` (and other writers) can clear that binding **before** settle. The settle path then resurrected the retired id, so the next turn resumed a process the clear had already retired (`useResume=true resumeSession=<old>`).

## Fix

- `withAdmittedCliCandidate` captures the in-lane resumed native session id.
- `persistCliSessionBindingResult` skips applying a settle result that would only re-publish that same resumed id when the store no longer names it.
- Explicit clears and newly minted native ids still publish.

## Evidence

```
pnpm test src/agents/cli-session-store.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# Test Files  1 passed (1)
# Tests  32 passed (32)
```

New coverage:
- `does not re-publish a resumed binding another writer cleared mid-turn`
- `still publishes a newly minted native id after a mid-turn clear`

Closes #186613

prs.title: fix(sandbox): treat dash missing-parent cd errors as ENOENT
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`SandboxFsBridgeImpl.stat()` only treated GNU/BusyBox `No such file or directory` as a missing path. On Debian/Ubuntu sandbox containers where `/bin/sh` is dash, stating a path whose **parent directory does not exist** fails at `cd -- "$1"` with `can't cd to …`, and the bridge threw an uncategorized `stat failed …` error instead of returning `null` (`ENOENT`). That broke `optional: true` / path-variant fallbacks in sandboxed `read`.

## Fix

- Before `cd`, the container script now checks `[ -d "$1" ]` and emits a C-locale `No such file or directory` when the parent is missing.
- `isSandboxStatMissingPathError()` also accepts dash's `can't cd to ` wording so historical/edge failure shapes still map to `null`.
- Non-missing failures (e.g. `Permission denied`) still throw.

## Evidence

### Local dash (/bin/sh) behavior on head `4cac7473877e`

Host Linux with `/bin/sh -> dash`. Exercised the exact fs-bridge stat script and the shipped sandboxed read tool through the local remote-shell backend (argv `sh -c`, so dash).

=== Head script: present file succeeds ===

prs.title: fix(storage): forward-port SQLite admission and lease cleanup fixes
prs.body:
## Problem

Cold SQLite opens can deadlock behind the shared open queue, and an offline maintenance collision can leave a released lease blocking later acquirers.

## Solution

Take the database admission turn before the per-carrier open queue; retain cleanup ownership and retry maintenance contention until lease expiry. No schema or stored-data format changes.

Independent split of #191830, directly against `main`; no sibling PR is required. Original release provenance is preserved in commit bodies. Scope excludes every other forward-port group.

Local review found two additional cleanup defects: a synchronous filesystem admission failure left an outstanding reservation, and cleanup used the original acquisition expiry after automatic renewal. Both were reproduced before repair. The admission owner now settles its reservation in `finally`; lease cleanup uses the existing heartbeat's committed expiry observation. The shared heartbeat-state module owns buffer construction and expiry reading; no second lifecycle owner or new queue was added. Final review also caught a native startup regression in the repair: preallocating an observation changed who published startup renewals. The native lease now retains the heartbeat's own observation after construction, leaving its startup publication intact. A real delayed-worker startup regression reproduces the original-expiry failure before this correction.

The exact scoped allocation is **152 net regression-test lines**, covering cold admission ordering, physical-owner reuse, failed admission drainage, offline-maintenance release, and cleanup after renewal. Production delta is +95/-38 lines against the base; tests are +162/-10. Necessary growth retains bounded cleanup under the existing owner.

## Evidence

- Fresh six-suite validation passed **74/74 tests**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.capacity.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-lease-async.maintenance.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-lease-async.timer.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-lease-contention.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-lease-native-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Includes broker capacity/drainage, lease lifecycle, and real cross-process offline-maintenance contention.
- Red proofs: `settles cold admission filesystem failures before draining the broker` failed on the unrepaired source; `retries contended cleanup through the committed automatic renewal expiry` failed because release was called once instead of twice. Both pass after repair.
- Final helper-extraction replay passed **14/14** (6 timer tests and 8 real contention tests). Native startup/heartbeat plus startup, async timer, and maintenance validation passed **33/33** after the native-startup correction; the typed maintenance fixture was replayed afterward (**8/8**).
- Native-startup red proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/state/openclaw-state-lease-heartbeat.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'preserves native startup renewals'` failed at the original ~1-second startup expiry. The same real lease / delayed real worker path passes after repair, without changing the existing startup cap.
- `git diff --check`, targeted oxfmt, and commit-hook line-cap checks passed.
- Targeted TypeScript validation is blocked by unchanged base MCP errors: `src/agents/mcp-metadata.ts` imports a missing `McpCatalogTool` export, with consequent optional-property errors in `agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts`. These source files are unchanged by this split. Broad CI remains separate; this is not a green-CI claim.
- Final local ClawSweeper reviewed the committed range `34007820fa2c..8405968e8578`: no actionable correctness or security findings; all previous findings resolved.
- Original combined-branch evidence: SQLite worker 384 tests and lease 26 files passed; deadlock regression failed on the original base. This is retained evidence, not a new split-head run.

Reviewed candidate: `8405968e8578`; base `34007820fa2c`. No live production or authenticated Gateway verification is claimed.

## Related CI repairs

Follow-up commit `ce08ea219f28` fixes both split-introduced CI failures from head `8405968e8578`:

- Use `throw` in the async admission function, retaining rejected-Promise behavior while satisfying `unicorn/no-useless-promise-resolve-reject`.
- Supply the heartbeat-owned shared expiry observation in the existing failed-startup mock using `createLeaseHeartbeatState()`. The scoped allocation grows by exactly two fixture lines, to 152.
- Fresh `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/gateway-owner-lease.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.capacity.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **67/67 passed**, including failed heartbeat startup custody and broker admission/capacity/drainage.
- Targeted `run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` on both changed TypeScript files, targeted format check, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.infra.json --noEmit`: the introduced missing-expiryObservation error is gone; only unchanged base MCP export/optional-property errors remain.
- Test-line checker: net +152 matches the allocation; inherited deficit remains 47 lines (6,445,063 versus 6,445,016). No baseline relaxation.

These are mechanical lint/fixture corrections following the prior clean local review; new-head CI is separate and not claimed green.

## Current-main conflict repair and CI audit

Merge commit `d98fcc967e0e` integrates main `cc595f5c0f6b` directly (not a sibling PR), resolving all three conflicts in `sqlite-worker-input-admission.ts`, `sqlite-worker-broker.test.ts`, and `sqlite-worker-broker.capacity.test.ts`. Main independently landed the synchronous admission settlement and cold-open regression coverage in #192586. The resolution keeps that production owner and main's tests, preserves the remaining lease-cleanup fixes, and combines the required filesystem imports. The admission implementation and broker test file now have no diff against the integrated main.

The remaining exact net test delta is **111 lines**, reduced from 152 because main now carries overlapping coverage. The allocation was reduced accordingly. Earlier diff counts and base-specific validation above describe the pre-integration revision.

Fresh validation on the merge candidate:

- Broker, broker capacity, async lease timer, and heartbeat suites: **68/68 passed** across four files and two Vitest shards (6 + 62). Includes main's real ELOOP/capacity regression and the split's startup-renewal regression.

prs.title: fix(codex): forward-port 2026.10.10 thread ownership and cleanup fixes
prs.body:
## Problem

The 2026.10.10 stable release fixed Codex thread ownership and native follow-up failures that were missing from main. A freshly forked child could fail its first turn with an active-writer error; a resumed thread could race its previous owner; a later parent turn could no longer resolve a native child by task name. Short shutdown budgets also converted healthy loaded cleanup into failure.

## Solution

Keep this existing PR for the Codex portion of the original forward-port batch. All sibling splits target main independently; this is not a stack.

- Unload a canonical fork before its child turn connection resumes it.
- Wait for a live previous owner's unload before another client resumes the same thread.
- Preserve bounded loaded one-shot cleanup and match Codex's 10-second unload confirmation window.
- Retain canonical native child paths across parent registrations and name usable agent IDs for unidentified targets.

Preserves the six original Codex forward-port commits and release references. Fresh local review also caught a defect in the inherited one-shot change: shared retirement started shutdown before its longer grace options were applied. The repair now applies those options at the first close; the operation lives with the existing shared-client lifecycle owner. A deterministic fake-clock regression fails before this repair because containment starts before the delayed clean exit. The exact scoped test-line allocation is 295 lines for fork handoff, native targeting, previous-owner handoff, and shutdown-budget regressions. Simplification review kept these ownership fixes together; unrelated Matrix, process, storage, cron, config, startup, and file-transfer changes moved out.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` and targeted oxfmt checks passed.
- Red proof for shared cleanup: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/client-shutdown.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — the new grace regression failed as expected; 3 existing tests passed.
- Fresh targeted lint and extension typecheck were attempted after a successful isolated frozen install. Both are blocked by an unchanged main error: `src/agents/mcp-metadata.ts:5` imports `McpCatalogTool` from a module that does not export it, with consequent optional-property errors in `agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.ts`. All three source files are byte-identical to base 34007820fa2cc4b5a7a9b9bdc2047aafed41ab1c.
- Fresh cleanup validation: shared-client/client-shutdown 162/162 and one-shot cleanup 11/11 passed. Final local ClawSweeper reviewed `34007820fa2c..f00f4d2e7b58`: no actionable correctness or security findings; prior shutdown-grace finding resolved.
- Fresh focused validation: all 336 tests passed across 6 files / 3 Vitest shards (814.57s including worker compilation): native-subagent inventory, native thread handoff, thread binding, run-attempt, canonical-descendant integration, and Gateway Codex failure recovery.

Prior combined-PR evidence: canonical-descendant 65/65; native-subagent 141; binding 100/100; codex-failure-recovery 7/7; handoff.native 2/2. The original regressions were confirmed failing without the corresponding changes, except the one-shot cleanup budget (the delayed-exit fixture was flaky and nondiscriminating, so no such test is claimed).

Codex shutdown contract checked against sibling source commit 092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d; the per-thread unload-delay override was also verified against pinned rust-v0.164.0 (6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9): `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_lifecycle.rs` waits for shutdown and only emits `thread/closed` after cleanup, reporting shutdown as slow after 10 seconds.

Known limitation retained from the original PR: the retired native child-path index is not pruned. Broad CI and live authenticated Codex/MCP qualification are not claimed by local fixture tests.

All eight target `main` directly, not one another.

prs.title: fix(sessions): title pasted paths and non-control leading-slash text
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session title derivation treated any first message that starts with `/` as a slash command and skipped it. Pasted absolute paths (`/Users/…/handover.md read this`) therefore stayed untitled (`New conversation`) and worktree sessions fell back to random crustacean branch names.

## Fix

- In `resolveSessionTitleSource`, keep skill-command arg extraction. For other leading-slash text, accept only **path-like** forms (`//…` or a second `/` in the string) as title source. Unregistered `/command` tokens stay untitled so we do not need the heavy `command-detection` wrapper import.
- In `prepareDashboardSessionTitle`, prepare skill commands whenever the trimmed draft starts with `/` so registered skills stay skill-aware before the empty-command fast path.

## Evidence

### Live Gateway proof (Linux Node v24.22.1, synthetic model over loopback)

Built/started real `startGatewayServer` on loopback with a synthetic OpenAI-compatible title utility (API key `synthetic-key-not-real`, no vendor account). Health `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`.

```
chat.send sessionKey=agent:main:dashboard:path-title-proof
message='/tmp/openclaw-path-proof-notes.md read this handover'
→ sessions.displayName='Summarise the notes file'
builderPath='/tmp/openclaw-path-proof-notes.md read this handover'
resolveSessionTitleSource='/tmp/openclaw-path-proof-notes.md read this handover'
attachment-first /explain → 'Explain DNS resolution'
fakeModelRequests=1
```

Artifact: `/tmp/openclaw-proofs/artifacts/proof-043-113.json` (case pr=192043). Head `aee4a653f`.


## Notes

Does not add a post-reply title retry; this PR only corrects the leading-slash skip so the existing first-message path can name path-like sessions.

Closes #192031

prs.title: fix(matrix): message bursts become separate turns despite messages.inbound debounce
prs.body:
Closes #165823 Related: #161505 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Matrix turns every line of a quick text burst into separate agent turns, even when `messages.inbound.debounceMs` or `byChannel.matrix` is configured. ## User Impact With `messages.inbound.byChannel.matrix` (or the global `debounceMs`) set, a burst of Matrix messages from one sender gets one reply. The Matrix default stays 0, so nothing is delayed unless the operator opts in. ## Why This Change Was Made Rebuilt on the durable Matrix ingress (the earlier head targeted the replay-claim API that main has since removed). It follows the Mattermost fan-in debouncer from #166499: - Ingress `dispatch` hands each event and its claim lifecycle to a room-keyed `createChannelInboundDebouncer` and returns `{ kind: "deferred" }`. `canAppend` only merges contiguous text from the same sender and thread root, and `serializeImmediate` keeps everything in room order, so a burst never jumps ahead of another sender's message. - A flush fans the batched claims into one lifecycle (`fanInChannelIngressLifecycles`). Adopting the merged turn completes every claim; a gated turn settles them; a handler failure fails each claim so the drain's retry policy applies; shutdown or an aborted claim cancels them back to the queue. - The merged event keeps the latest event id (reply threading), joins bodies with newlines, keeps each event's HTML in `formatted_body` (escaped plain text otherwise, joined with `
`) so the handler's matrix.to pill check still validates mentions, and merges `m.mentions`. - Media, voice notes, edits, real replies (not thread fallbacks), the bot's own events, and control commands dispatch alone. Command bypass strips the mention prefix the way the handler does (bot MXID, room display name, every agent's mention patterns), so `@Bot: /stop` is never delayed. Prefix lookup is async, so it is chained per room. - Pre-startup history and E2EE decryption are now handled by ingress before delivery, so the old pre-startup predicate and repeat-emit filter are gone. - Monitor shutdown closes the debouncer with task admission: pending batches and late deliveries return to the durable queue instead of being dropped. - The delay is read from live config.
Test-only changes - `index.test-helpers.ts`: the fake ingress passes a full claim lifecycle and records it; the fake runtime gains a `messagesConfig` knob and a `mock-isolation` note (`config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt` drops that entry). - `index.test.ts`: handler failures and late post-shutdown events are now asserted on the claim lifecycle (`onFailed` / `onCancelled`) rather than as a rejected delivery; the shutdown-order test waits for the handler to start before aborting.
## Evidence - Original defect: the new `index.test.ts` case "merges a Matrix text burst when messages.inbound.byChannel.matrix is set" fails with `index.ts` reverted to main (handler called 2 times, no batching) and passes with the fix. - `inbound-debounce.test.ts` (16 tests): merge on latest event, single adoption per claim, gated-turn settle, failure fans out `onFailed`, immediate dispatch for edits/replies/commands (MXID, display-name pill, mention pattern)/images, arrival order under async prefix lookup, room order across senders and threads, HTML and mention merge, own messages, shutdown cancellation. - `index.test.ts`: burst merge through the monitor wiring and a debounce delay committed after startup. - Local gates on this head: `pnpm test:extension matrix` pass; `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main` typecheck-all, format, mock-export ratchet, dead-export scan, plugin boundaries pass; oxlint on `extensions/matrix` clean; `pnpm format:docs:check` clean. - Earlier live run (2026.9.8 Gateway, previous implementation, `byChannel.matrix: 3000`): a five-line Element burst produced one user-triggered agent turn. Not re-run on this head.

prs.title: feat(control-ui): show worker lifecycle and telemetry
prs.body:
Closes #163982

## What Problem This Solves

The Systems page hides worker lifecycle history, can leave a reclaimed worker shown as `Attached` until reload, and does not connect live dedicated workers to the CPU, memory, and disk telemetry their enrolled nodes already report.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish active workers from recent destroyed or failed workers, inspect lifecycle/provider/profile/lease/error details, see terminal state changes without reloading, and troubleshoot or right-size live dedicated workers from the same resource graphs used for base systems.

Workers without dedicated node telemetry show an explicit not-reported state. Shared-host workers do not expose whole-host statistics as if those measurements belonged to one worker.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Systems inventory now retains terminal worker records, groups active and historical workers separately, and refreshes canonical `environments.list` data when durable `sessions.changed` events or worker placement changes arrive.

For dedicated workers, the Gateway additionally projects the enrolled node identity. The Systems inventory joins that exact identity to `node.list`, reuses the existing host-stat history and graphs, and continues polling while the worker is selected. No provider shell probe, SSH command, or second telemetry poller is introduced.

## Evidence

### October27 identification repair

Short worker IDs now remain visible beside lifecycle status. [Exact-head regression results and before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163995#issuecomment-6456168501). This fixes the same-profile identification finding; history-policy acceptance and main integration remain pending.

### Earlier lifecycle and telemetry evidence

The following results document earlier tested revisions; they are not a new full-suite or live-runtime qualification of the October27 head.

Live Apple Container lifecycle, captured from the same Systems page without a reload:

**Before reclaim — worker is Attached**

![Systems sidebar showing an attached worker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff22cbbe-35d0-4d25-a08c-6799626eb040)

**After reclaim — worker moved to Recent worker history as Destroyed**

![Systems sidebar showing the reclaimed worker as destroyed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee681765-dd7b-4cad-adf6-0708837275eb)

- Live transition observed in about one second and repeated twice without reloading.
- Disposable live telemetry proof: an Apple Container worker reached `ready`, published a dedicated node identity, and reported Linux host stats with 5 CPUs, load averages, 4.26 GB memory capacity, and 541.13 GB disk capacity through `node.list`. The worker was reclaimed; provider and Apple Container inventories were empty afterward.
- Focused validation:
  - Gateway environment projection: 20/20 pass.
  - Gateway protocol schema: 22/22 pass.
  - Systems telemetry/UI: 36/36 pass, including distinct session and telemetry-node names.
  - Changed-file formatting and lint: pass.
  - Core and UI typechecks: pass.
  - Production Control UI build: pass.
- Earlier branch-wide validation:
  - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main`: pass (335.15 s).
  - `pnpm test:changed`: 20,926 pass / 3 skip; one unrelated `shell-viewport.test.ts` RAF-coalescing assertion failed under the full parallel lane, then passed 3/3 isolated reruns (11/11 each).
  - Upstream `control-ui-performance`: pass. The local check showed a nondeterministic gzip edge 24–30 B over the 373,454 B startup limit while raw startup JS stayed exactly 1,208,683 B with and without the Systems reconciliation helper, confirming this patch does not change the startup asset set.
  - Repo autoreview helper was attempted but unavailable because its local Codex credential returned HTTP 401; no review verdict was produced.

The two older `Destroying` rows visible in the screenshots predate this worker and are a separate provider-history cleanup issue.

prs.title: chore(codex): test warm claim settlement and scope revocation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Tests-only regression coverage; no runtime source change or production fix in this PR.** The proof target here is that a failed owner leaves no orphan native-thread claim and a later attempt can reuse that thread.

A Codex-backed conversation can reject the next turn as “claimed by active work” after failed ownership settlement, even though the failed attempt is no longer running. The existing cleanup lacks targeted coverage at the warm-claim cleanup and monitor-setup revocation seams.

Related: karmaterminal/openclaw#1431 (the queue-behind-*genuinely active* work request is separate and remains open).

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. These tests protect the existing claim-release behavior against regressions that could strand subsequent Codex attempts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inject a lease-settlement failure after proving warm claim transfer (without a cold resume), and separately revoke session binding authority during monitor setup. Assert cleanup clears each claim and the same native thread can be claimed by a follow-up attempt. The latter is **scope revocation, not a simulated binding-store lease expiry**. The tests complement the existing lifecycle cleanup; they do not implement queueing behind active work.

## Evidence

- Based on upstream `main` `6ba6ad224ae` (2026-10-25); two Codex app-server test files only.
- Focused Codex app-server suites: 2 files, 21/21 tests passed on upstream base.
- Exact PR head 14bf56f9ea33: [GitHub Actions changed-extensions-config](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40253224772/job/121349722824) ran both changed test files, 21/21 passed. Its log includes the warm lifecycle injected-failure test and the monitor-failure binding-scope revocation test; the latter asserts a completed follow-up turn on the same native thread with the claim cleared. [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40253224772/job/121351049271) passed. These are fixture-driven in-repo assertions, **not** a shipped Gateway/CLI lease-loss trace.
- Extension test typecheck, targeted format and lint pass; line-cap ratchet passes against `upstream/main` for the two changed files. (The default local ratchet base is `origin/main`, a divergent fork, and falsely flags unrelated upstream files.)
- No live service change or end-to-end field reproduction claimed.

**Follow-up proof correction (2026-10-27):** A Claude source review found the monitor case calls `releaseBindingAuthority()` (binding scope, not simulated lease expiry); the warm case now asserts ownership is held at the injected settlement fault and no cold `thread/resume` occurs before it. Updated head `71d416664521dc5f51bf3e6ac2a435786f91f07c`: focused Vitest 21/21, extension-test tsgo, targeted oxfmt/oxlint and diff check passed locally. Hosted CI is pending; no live lease-expiry or production fix is claimed.

prs.title: fix(telegram): route bound conversations when agent selection is ambiguous
prs.body:
Closes #159334

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Telegram conversation with an active session binding fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError` on a multi-agent install that has no channel-wide Telegram route, so its messages are never processed.

## User Impact

User impact: runtime-bound Telegram conversations reach their bound agent regardless of how many agents are configured. Conversations without a binding, or whose binding names no agent, keep today's behavior — including still requiring an explicit channel owner. A binding revoked or replaced while a message is being routed no longer leaves the former owner selected.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareTelegramConversationRoute` asked ordinary agent selection for a route before looking at the binding, and ordinary selection refuses an ambiguous roster. It now selects the base route inside the SDK's `resolveRuntimeConversationBindingRouteAsync({ resolveRoute })` (and `inspectRuntimeConversationBindingRoute({ inspection, resolveRoute })` for route-owner inspection): the binding owner's canonically classified `boundAgentId` arrives before ordinary selection, and when it is set the base route is derived from session-only config with that agent as the default. This is the shared binding-owner selection Slack, Discord and iMessage use, so Telegram no longer re-implements the session-key/metadata classification. Topic overrides, configured bindings, and the runtime-binding step that follows are unchanged.

### Binding changes during resolution (review follow-up)

An earlier revision chose the agent from a synchronous binding read and then let `resolveRuntimeConversationBindingRouteAsync` read the binding again after an `await`, so a binding revoked in between could leave the former owner selected; that revision guarded it with a re-prepare/retry loop.

Since merging current `main` (`4ee4606`), agent selection runs inside the `resolveRoute` callback of the single awaited inspection, so the agent and the binding facts come from the same read. There is no second read to diverge from, and the retry loop is gone. The same applies to `prepareTelegramConversationRouteInspection` (new on `main`), whose `resolve(inspection)` now selects the agent from the inspection it is handed. `inspectTelegramConversationRouteAsync` shares the inbound path with `touchBinding: false`.

## Evidence

New cases in `conversation-route-owner.test.ts`, all on a two-agent config with no route bindings:

- inbound `resolveTelegramConversationRoute` selects the bound agent and session, reports `runtime-bound`, and touches the binding once;
- `inspectTelegramConversationRouteAsync` selects the bound agent without touching liveness;
- a sentinel `global` session with `metadata.agentId` selects that agent;
- a binding that names no agent still rejects with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED`;
- a binding revoked just before the awaited inspection rejects with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` instead of routing to the former owner;
- a binding replaced just before the awaited inspection routes to the new owner and its new binding.

Negative controls: with `main`'s `conversation-route.ts` (`4ee4606`), 4 of these 6 fail with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` (the bound-agent, inspection, sentinel-metadata and replacement cases); the no-agent and revocation cases pass there, as intended, since both assert that rejection.

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/conversation-route-owner.test.ts
19 passed (19)
$ pnpm test extensions/telegram
passed 63 Vitest shards
$ pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
0 errors
```

Focused regression cost: `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/conversation-route-owner.test.ts` — 19 tests, 16.4 s Vitest duration / 20.8 s wall time locally. `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` and the assertion SAFETY ratchet are clean on the changed files. The test fixture uses `agents.entries` (the authored shape since `agents.list` was retired on `main`).

**Live Telegram proof:** not included. The `telegram-e2e-userbot` harness needs Convex-leased team credentials, which I don't have as an outside contributor. The evidence above is unit-level through the real binding-routing SDK with a test adapter.

AI-assisted. I reviewed the change and ran the tests and negative controls above locally.

## What Problem This Solves

prs.title: fix(doctor): refresh SQLite planner stats after migration
prs.body:
Related: #119884
Related: #119720
Related: #119739
Supersedes #119901

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who ran `openclaw doctor --fix` could finish an agent SQLite schema migration without persisted planner statistics. Large migrated stores could then choose poor query plans, including after the original migration had already completed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair lives in the normal Doctor-owned agent database migration path. Before releasing each database, Doctor runs `ANALYZE main` under an explicit 1,000-row-per-index analysis limit. This repairs already-current databases as well as newly upgraded ones without adding runtime maintenance, configuration, or an OpenClaw schema change.

Explicit `ANALYZE` is required for the supported SQLite 3.44.x floor. In that lineage, `PRAGMA optimize=0x10002` ignores the later all-table bit and skips tables that the short-lived Doctor connection has not queried. The older #119901 patch instead placed full `ANALYZE` in explicit offline compaction, which does not own the normal migration path and could perform unbounded work on large stores. #119739 remains a related, distinct post-compaction proposal, while #133925 covers runtime bulk cleanup.

## User Impact

Running `openclaw doctor --fix` now restores planner statistics for affected agent databases. Existing and newly migrated stores can use their indexes with current approximate statistics. Work is bounded to roughly 1,000 visited rows per index and runs only inside Doctor's explicit repair window; there is no new setting or runtime hot-path maintenance.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix regression: both the v14-to-current migration and an already-current database failed with `no such table: sqlite_stat1`.
- Minimum-runtime contract: official SQLite 3.44.6 source at check-in `863c171b76cd36e0` requires `TF_StatsUsed` for `PRAGMA optimize` and has no `0x10000` all-table behavior; SQLite documents that behavior as new in 3.46.0.
- Executable minimum-runtime proof: a source-built SQLite 3.44.6 at that exact check-in honored `analysis_limit=1000`; bounded `ANALYZE main` populated two `sqlite_stat1` rows for 100,000 indexed records.
- Executable compatibility A/B: official SQLite 3.44.2 left `sqlite_stat1` absent after `PRAGMA analysis_limit=1000; PRAGMA optimize=0x10002;`; the repaired `ANALYZE main` sequence populated indexed tables.
- Regression coverage requires named statistics for `idx_agent_transcript_event_sequence` after v14 migration and for a populated `session_suggestions` index that the migration never queries.
- Owner/sibling migration coverage: 26 tests passed across current, v0/v14/v15, additive-schema, target-resolution, and lifecycle-recovery paths.
- Doctor orchestration coverage: 97 tests passed in `src/commands/doctor-state-migrations.test.ts`.
- Final focused coverage after test-lifecycle cleanup: 15/15 tests passed.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/infra/state-migrations.media-persistence.ts src/infra/state-migrations.media-persistence.test.ts` passed, including formatting, production/test types, lint, database-first, schema, and import-cycle guards.
- Fresh isolated autoreview: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings (0.98 confidence).
- Production source: +8/-0. The helper has two owner-path call sites and avoids duplicate maintenance policy.
- Tests: +65/-16, including migration/current-store regressions and conversion of the touched suite to automatic temp cleanup.

- @VACInc

prs.title: fix(macos): chat accent updates after Control UI changes

Related: #128922 ## What Problem This Solves The Mac chat window's native conversation does not refresh the Gateway-wide saved accent (`ui.prefs.accent`) when only chat is open. The existing per-profile accent path already updates separately; Gateway-wide changes can leave chat on its old color. ## Why This Change Was Made The long-lived Mac control connection reads Gateway config on connection and `config.changed`, resolving the saved Gateway preference before `ui.seamColor`. The Talk Mode config reader uses the same precedence so it cannot overwrite the chat color. Profile appearance retains separate inherit, theme, and color states, so an explicit theme choice cannot fall through to a Gateway color. The shared hex decoder used by iOS remains available with its prior result. Superseded reads and replaced Gateway leases remain fenced. ## User Impact Native chat can pick up a Gateway-wide saved accent without opening Mac Settings or Talk Mode, while a personal profile accent continues to win. Normal shared-token Control UI connections receive an owner profile and save Appearance changes through `users.prefs.set`; this PR does not claim that those edits exercise the Gateway-wide path. Real-app verification narrows the visible repro to native conversation mode (`openclaw.chat.useNativeConversation`). The default embedded web conversation already follows Gateway-wide accent changes in both the baseline and patched builds; this PR repairs the native `AppState.effectiveAccentHex` path. ## Evidence Independent real-app verification reported by @holgergruenhagen on November 1, 2026 ([original evidence comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185529#issuecomment-6563459034)): merge base vs. exact PR head, chat window only. Gateway-wide accent changed with `config.patch` (`ui.prefs.accent`), personal accent with `users.prefs.set` (`ui.accent`), both from the CLI against the test Gateway. - One user message in `main` gives a fixed probe: the native user bubble is canvas + 15 % accent (`desktopUserBubble`). Each value is the median of a 5×5 patch, converted to sRGB; "≈" is the accent recovered as (bubble − 0.85·canvas)/0.15 (canvas `#0e0f15`). Built-in default accent (dark) is `#ff5c5c`, which shows up as bubble `#321c20` (≈ `#fe665e`). **Where the bug is visible.** With default settings the chat window renders the conversation through the embedded web conversation, which already follows `ui.prefs.accent` live in both builds (web "Retry" button `#aa0000` → `#00bb00` before and after, image below). The native accent this PR fixes (`AppState.effectiveAccentHex`) is what the conversation shows with the debug toggle `openclaw.chat.useNativeConversation` on, so cases 1–5 were run with that toggle set in the test profile. **Results (native conversation, chat window only)** | Case | Before `1299676` | After `b34033c` | |---|---|---| | 1. Chat only, gw `#aa0000` → `#00bb00` | `#321c20` (≈ default) at start, +10 s and +40 s: gw color never shown | `#260e12` (≈ `#ae0801`) → `#0d2a12` (≈ `#07c301`) within 10 s | | 2. Test Gateway restart, reconnect, then gw → `#00bb00` | `#321c20` throughout | `#260e12` before restart and after reconnect, `#0d2a12` 10 s after the change | | 3a. Personal `#0000cc`, then gw → `#00bb00` | `#0d0e31` (≈ `#0708d0`), stays | `#0d0e31` (≈ `#0708d0`), stays | | 3b. prs.title: fix(ios): keep main session discoverable after switching chats
prs.body:
Related: #192203

## What Problem This Solves

The native iOS main conversation appears to disappear after switching chats because Sessions and All Sessions omit it, while its existing shortcut is named Home.

## User Impact

- The current agent's existing conversation is recognizable as **Main Session** in Pages, Sessions, All Sessions, Overview, and current-session accessibility text.
- Both sidebar shortcuts share selection while Main Session is open; selecting another chat or page clears that selection.
- History and session identity are reused. Existing main-session delete, archive, and snooze protections remain in place.
- The optional blue selection redesign is deliberately excluded.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the shared session projection and alias resolver rather than creating a second conversation or changing session lifecycle policy. All Sessions includes the resolved current-agent main row; Overview still keeps its main shortcut separate from recent conversations. Native localization artifacts and the iOS navigation documentation are updated.

Related work was checked: #191729 changes New Chat creation, #167173 concerns group controls, and #165515 concerns last-chat restoration and voice routing. This change does not replace those behaviors.

## Evidence

- Original implementation base: `f9ca54aefc19109ebc52873d3dd29f2541a04f57`. Repair baseline: published head `66435a92b1ca1148e14e58f198b776cc97fb364d`.
- Verified the three hosted-review defects against their source owners: the old recent-row prefix omitted main behind 25 newer conversations; the old cron assertion contradicted the helper/status-scope contract; and Rename was still offered for fixed-title main rows. The repair reserves one main row plus the existing 20-row ordinary budget, preserves automation scope semantics, and omits ineffective Rename in the shared iOS action owner. No persisted pin or shared/global ordering policy changed.
- Native regressions now exercise the actual rendered-row projection with custom main names, groups, pins, multiple agents, descendants/collapse, and uncapped search. Automation assertions exercise `SessionStatusScope`, including its selected-session exception.
- Extended the existing synthetic-Gateway `SessionSnoozeUITests` flow (no extra app launch) to check both rendered selected shortcuts, other-chat/page transitions, retained main history, main menus in sidebar and All Sessions, ordinary Rename, and snooze. Removed the added source-string action guard and direct Boolean selection restatement.
- **Native red/green execution remains unverified:** Xcode preflight still fails with `xcodebuild: not found`. The previous six textual wiring checks did not establish behavior and are not counted as runtime proof. The native regressions still need execution on Xcode; inspected before/after UI artifacts must also be captured there.
- Passed after repairs: `pnpm native:i18n:sync`, `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, `pnpm apple:i18n:check`, `pnpm exec oxfmt --check docs/platforms/ios.md`, and `git diff --check`.
- Final independent review of the complete diff through **P2** found no actionable defects; this is source review, not native compilation or UI validation.

**Pending native proof:** actual attempts at `xcodebuild -version`, `swift --version`, `xcrun simctl list devices available`, and `xcrun devicectl list devices` all returned command-not-found in the current Linux environment. Remote execution supports an explicit node identifier, but no authorized Mac node/runner or node-discovery tool is available to this session. The missing requirement is an authorized Mac with Xcode and an iOS simulator/device, using isolated baseline and patched source snapshots. SwiftFormat preflight also reports the pinned formatter is unavailable. Native build/typecheck, the new tests and affected sidebar/session/typography suites, navigation/VoiceOver checks, and inspected native before/after screenshots remain pending. Donnie is arranging Xcode access; these checks and native proof remain required before merge. Ready-for-review does not mean this validation has passed. No screenshots from the issue's separate prototype are presented as proof of this patch.

## What Problem This Solves

`plugins init Invalid_ID --type feature` creates a partial target directory before rejecting the feature ID. Correcting the ID and retrying in that same directory then fails with “Refusing to overwrite existing path.” The initial rejection also hides the existing ID requirements behind a generic CLI error.

## User Impact

Rejected feature IDs leave the target untouched and display the existing validator error. Plugin authors can correct the ID and retry immediately. This also preserves existing entries and marker bytes when the invalid attempt uses `--force`. Accepted tool, provider and feature scaffolds are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing feature validator in the feature writer, and create its source directory only after validation succeeds. The command's earlier mkdir remains for tool/provider scaffolds only. Route the existing feature error through `throwExpectedCliError`; no new validation rule, message, API or configuration.

Original fix by @zhangguiping-xydt; original commit retained. Consolidated the regression and neighboring metadata coverage to net -2 test lines, with no allocation file. Necessary production growth is +4 lines (8 gross changed lines).

## Evidence

[Final-head built Linux CLI proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193100#issuecomment-6647797271), main `658e3db2a464336f399704c201dda521ed4fac33` versus candidate `163e683b8610c90edeb6b2349bd782a997f06147`, once each in isolated Node 24.22.1 Docker:

- Main leaves `src` after the invalid ID and blocks the corrected retry. Candidate creates nothing, shows the existing ID requirements, and the corrected retry succeeds.
- Invalid `--force` attempt leaves candidate directory entries and marker bytes unchanged.
- Accepted feature, tool and provider scaffolds all succeed, with identical recursive file inventories and generated-file hashes across refs.
- Consolidated regression fails on main at the leftover-directory assertion. Candidate: 34 tests across the two focused files pass; changed-file lint and formatting pass. Setup corrections are disclosed in the evidence.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the earlier behavior; no migration or persisted contract changes. Blast radius is feature scaffold rejection and directory creation ordering. Valid scaffold contents, overwrite policy, tool/provider generation and credential handling are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(fal): reject unsupported music durations and FLUX edit geometry
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes fal requests that send unsupported MiniMax Music 2.6 duration or FLUX dev edit geometry, and Stable Audio 2.5 durations beyond its native 190-second limit.

Related source contracts: https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/587 and https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/588.

## User Impact

MiniMax Music 2.6 rejects explicit duration. Stable Audio accepts integer durations from 1 through 190 seconds. FLUX dev edits reject size, aspect-ratio, and resolution overrides before submission. ACE-Step retains fractional durations from 5 through 240 seconds.

Release note: reject unsupported fal music durations and FLUX dev edit geometry before a paid request. No production deployment or provider activation is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native schemas differ by model. Typed, opt-in capability constraints let the actual music and image runtimes reject invalid values before normalization can hide them. Direct provider calls enforce the same limits; inferred image resolution never becomes unsupported FLUX edit geometry. Models without these declarations keep their existing normalization behavior.

Primary contracts:
- [MiniMax Music 2.6 schema](https://fal.ai/api/openapi/queue/openapi.json?endpoint_id=fal-ai/minimax-music/v2.6): no duration input.
- [Stable Audio 2.5 schema](https://fal.ai/api/openapi/queue/openapi.json?endpoint_id=fal-ai/stable-audio-25/text-to-audio): integer seconds_total, minimum 1, maximum 190.
- [FLUX dev image-to-image schema](https://fal.ai/api/openapi/queue/openapi.json?endpoint_id=fal-ai/flux/dev/image-to-image): no image_size field.

## Evidence

Exact candidate `a194e367b2cdea63169e05736030262aa7a9637f`: [CI run 41668554264](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41668554264), in progress. The workflow reference SHA is not source proof; checkout/build evidence remains required.

- Cached checksum-qualified repository formatter, Node syntax checks on all 11 changed TypeScript files, diff whitespace checks, and added-line privacy scrub pass.
- Focused regression fixtures cover native request bodies, rejection before network I/O, actual image-runtime geometry handling, and music-runtime duration handling. Semantic execution and before/after regression proof are **pending**.
- Required focused commands: `pnpm test:extension fal`; `pnpm test src/music-generation/runtime.test.ts src/image-generation/runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Required SDK/build/type proof remains pending exact-head CI. Per-file runtime measurements are unavailable until those tests execute.
- Local dependencies are unqualified: managed dependency admission refused a broken/escaping nested workspace link. No installation or borrowed runtime dependencies were used. No remote lease was started; publication follows the documented draft/CI proof policy.
- **Test-line gate blocked by exact-base debt:** frozen base `6daa81f3576e8084155d63e4bae9383b1ec524c2` has 6,436,839 lines against 6,436,686 (153 over, delta 0). This branch has 6,436,944 against 6,436,791 (153 over, delta +105). The allocation is exactly 105; the shared scalar is unchanged. Base comparison used a disposable Git index with the same native checker.
- This is native OpenClaw source coverage, not actual ClawRouter Worker integration or live provider parity. No manifests, Worker codecs, credentials, pricing, or routes changed.
- Independent review was explicitly waived by the maintainer. Required CI and native landing gates remain in force; no failed gate is bypassed.

prs.title: fix(tailscale): managed Serve recovery skips sudo for "must be root"
prs.body:
Closes #190772

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: managed Tailscale Serve recovery fails after a daemon restart when Tailscale returns `401 Unauthorized: must be root...`, because the permission classifier never recognizes that wording and skips the existing noninteractive sudo fallback.

## User Impact

User impact: an unprivileged Linux Gateway can reclaim its managed Serve route through the existing `sudo -n` path after `tailscaled` restarts, instead of looping on unrecognized permission denials. Route-conflict and password-required sudo failures keep their current diagnostics. This change was verified through the production claim path with fixtures, not a live Tailscale daemon handover.

## Why This Change Was Made

Teach `isPermissionDeniedError` to match Tailscale's `must be root` denial so `claimTailscaleRoute` enters its existing sudo fallback. Extend the existing sudo fixture with a `must-be-root` mode that emits the observed stderr on the first claim attempt.

## Evidence

- Base tip `6daa81f357`; Node 24.22.1; Linux.
- Red without the classifier line: `preserves must-be-root diagnostics` failed with the raw `401 Unauthorized: must be root...` error (sudo fallback never attempted).
- Green with the fix: `pnpm test src/infra/tailscale.test.ts src/infra/tailscale.claim.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 56/56 passed, including `preserves must-be-root diagnostics` (expects the sudo password diagnostic after fallback).
- Password and conflict fixture rows unchanged.
- Limit: no live unprivileged host with passwordless sudo and a real Tailscale daemon was available, so live ownership handover after `tailscaled` restart is not claimed.
