prs.title: feat: watch a running command automation's output live in the Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long-running command automation shows nothing in Automations, Run history until it finishes, so an operator cannot tell what a multi-hour job is doing. Only Settings, Logs is live, and it does not contain the script's output.

## User Impact

User impact: while a command automation runs, its Run history shows a **Live output** panel that follows the combined stdout and stderr like `tail -f`. It auto-scrolls, pauses when you scroll up (with a **Jump to latest** button), and stops polling while the browser tab is hidden. When the run ends the panel goes away and the recorded run appears in the list as before. Gateway clients can read the same tail with `cron.liveOutput`.

Risks and limits:
- Live text is redacted with the tool-payload policy, so it can be masked more strictly than the recorded summary of the same run. The recorded summary is unchanged. A private key is masked across polls; one whose start was already dropped from a full tail is masked only while its end line is still held.
- Only the most recent output is kept: at most 256 KiB, or `payload.outputMaxBytes` when that is smaller. The panel keeps the last 2000 lines.
- Agent-turn runs have no live panel. Their transcript is still available only after the run is recorded (see Evidence).

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway keeps a fixed-size in-memory ring for the active run. The command runner owns it and discards it in its existing `finally`, so exit, timeout, abort and spawn failure all clean up through one path. `cron.liveOutput` (`operator.read`, same job visibility checks as `cron.get`) returns complete lines from a byte cursor, so a reconnect neither loses nor repeats lines. The panel reuses the existing visible-poll and stream-auto-follow helpers. Cursor polling, like `logs.tail`, keeps the Gateway free of timers and per-chunk broadcasts when nobody is watching. No config key, schema or migration; `cron.history` and `cron.runs` are unchanged.

Size: about 360 lines of new production code across 3 modules, about 560 lines of tests, small edits to existing files, plus regenerated validator files.

## Evidence

Before and after screenshots (Run history of a running command job; Live output panel; paused with **Jump to latest**; hand-off when the run ends) are in the first comment below. The extra Error row in the before shot is from restarting the throwaway Gateway while testing.


- Throwaway Gateway (own state dir, port 28789, loopback, throwaway token) and a real headless Chrome against the built Control UI. A command job printed a line per second for 60 to 90 s. Follow reads returned only new lines, replaying a cursor was idempotent, stderr was interleaved in order, a fake `token=sk-...` was masked, and `active` flipped to `false` exactly when `state.runningAtMs` cleared, including after a job timeout. The recorded run was unchanged.
- Tests: buffer bounds and fixed memory, cursor, drop-oldest, UTF-8 safety, redaction (including a private key across polls) and escape stripping, cleanup on exit, timeout, abort and spawn failure; the gateway method (follow, inactive, validation, visibility, access closed mid-read); the UI line bound and panel (follow, hidden tab, hand-off, still polling before the command starts, jump to latest).
- Review round: fixes covered by focused tests and typecheck only; the throwaway Gateway run above predates them. `check:changed` passes except the dead export scan, which flags `flattenRun` in `scripts/lib/catalog-compare-released-diff.mts` (already on main, not in this PR).
- Checks run: `pnpm gateway:validators:check`, `pnpm protocol-registry:check`, the protocol since-guard (new method vintage `2026.10`), the native protocol check, scoped core and UI tests (including the existing `command-runner`, `cron.history` and `cron.runs` suites), `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, and `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` (all lanes passed). I re-ran the validators, registry and new tests after the work finished.
- Agent-turn runs: not changed. Run history rows, including the transcript binding `cron.history` needs, are written when the run completes, so an in-flight run has no row and **View transcript** is unavailable. Live agent transcripts need an early binding row from the run owner and a follow protocol for transcript pages, which is a separate change.
- Local review: autoreview and local ClawSweeper were not run. The author read the full diff against the simplify checklist before opening.
- Not covered: hidden-tab pause in a real browser (unit-tested with a mocked `visibilityState`), narrow layout, dark theme and RTL screenshots, Windows and macOS, WebKit, the full test suite.

Follow-ups: `openclaw automations runs <id> --follow` (needs a polling loop, abort handling and a `--json` decision); live agent-turn transcripts; `public-schema.ts` is at its line cap, so the new live-output schema types are not re-exported there and a maintainer may prefer a sibling file.

prs.title: fix(vydra): require distinct Kling motion references
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The native Vydra Kling adapter rejected video references and sent its image URL as both `image_url` and `video_url`. Motion control requires a character image and a distinct motion video.

## User Impact

Use the existing typed `inputImages` and `inputVideos`: exactly one remote HTTPS image and one distinct remote HTTPS motion video. Missing, buffered, duplicate, extra, credential-bearing and unsupported audio references fail before upstream I/O. The existing Models create and original-job GET flow stay intact. Veo3 remains text-only.

Kling advertises motion support with model-specific image/video limits, while image-only generation is disabled. The shared video runtime already supports mixed references through its typed video-to-video capabilities; no SDK input type or model family is invented.

## Why This Change Was Made

This corrects the frozen and current native client against the [primary Kling schema](https://www.vydra.ai/docs/models/kling) and the published contract in https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/586 (landed3b75c3a9eaabaf927314ec9cf35c3164e4528de6). No Worker, manifest, pricing, credentials or controller changes are included. ClawRouter `vydra.model_video_create` activation still requires qualified schema/runtime support on the existing `vydra.jobs` lifecycle, preserving the original model/create route and GET-only controls.

Release-note context: Vydra Kling motion control uses the supplied motion video instead of reusing its image reference, with truthful per-model capabilities and early unsupported-input errors. CHANGELOG.md is release-owned; user docs and the plugin README are updated here.

## Evidence and remaining gates

- Frozen task base:21d44cf768fe94ec1d502bf4a88aadd1ae054a4f. Exact candidate:7c25de1886304bceda3dd6ab1cfa3ea3001ddbe3. Native maintainer/testing instructions are unchanged from the previously qualified revision.

prs.title: fix(macos): session previews stay loading or stale after reopening the menu
prs.body:
Closes #187603

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: recent-message previews in the macOS menu stay on “Loading preview…” or show old messages when a session submenu is reused.

## User Impact

User impact: reopening can retry a cancelled preview without reconnecting the Gateway. Fresh cached messages are projected immediately; expired previews show Loading while the existing asynchronous load refreshes both retained views. **Open for maintainer review; current-head native compilation and all 20 focused tests passed. New supplied interactive proof shows cancellation/reopen recovery and expired-cache Loading → recovery in the unmodified final-head debug app, including compact and expanded previews.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the submenu, hosted views, existing cache, and one cancellable load per submenu. The latest supplied candidate makes the existing UI-only cache/loader main-actor owned so configuration can synchronously project fresh cached content or Loading before menu tracking. Network requests remain asynchronous; the existing limiter, timeout, cancellation checks, and Gateway/session ownership remain intact. No polling or additional cache implementation.

## Evidence

### Current candidate

- Published head: `0fb8f65de80660a12516a24f1376438908159234`; complete tree: `ee8be264e612f0e10c6737b157947fa27aa8271d`. The published tree matches the reviewed local candidate `33fd9fb02dd19e3c427844fd68b997d14ae4af53`.

Official completed-job logs show `Linking OpenClawPackageTests` followed by `Build complete! (713.47s)` at 2026-11-01 09:08:35 UTC. The job and full Periphery workflow completed successfully. At 09:28 UTC the current head had 20 successful checks and 59 skipped checks, with no failures or pending checks. These are CI-check counts, **not a report of executed native tests**. prs.title: fix(macos): Mac tab reloads forever when its page keeps crashing
prs.body:
Related: #183928
Depends on: #185432 (this branch is stacked on it; the diff shows both until that PR merges)

Depends on the Mac tab load-failure change for #183927 (branch `mac/5a-tab-load-error`); this branch is stacked on it and reuses its failure view and Reload retry.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Mac tab reloads in an endless loop when its page's web content process keeps quitting.

## User Impact

User impact: a page whose web content quits is still reloaded automatically, up to twice. If it quits again before the user navigates or reloads, the tab stops reloading and shows "This page stopped repeatedly" with Reload. Reload, a toolbar navigation, Back/Forward (Browser panel buttons, or Navigate > Back/Forward and their Command-[ / Command-] shortcuts), or a pointer click on a link starts a fresh budget. Each tab counts on its own.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every WebContent termination of a reading tab ran `webView.reload()` with no limit (`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardWindowController.swift:1493-1494` on `70c70646d86`), so a page that crashes on load keeps reloading, using CPU and network, and never becomes usable.

The tab now owns a small budget (`DashboardBrowserTab.automaticReloadLimit = 2`). `DashboardNativeBrowserHost.webContentProcessDidTerminate(_:)` spends one automatic reload per termination; once spent, it shows the shared failure state from #183927 instead of reloading. The budget is not restored when a load finishes, because in the reported loop each termination follows a reload that finished successfully. It is restored only by user intent: Reload, toolbar navigation, Back/Forward, and main-frame link activations with a physical pointer button (which page script cannot synthesize). Back/Forward from the Browser panel (`perform(.back/.forward)`) and from the Navigate menu and its shortcuts (`DashboardWindowController.navigateBack()`/`navigateForward()`) go through the same `DashboardNativeBrowserHost.goBack(in:)`/`goForward(in:)`, so every Back/Forward command the app provides resets the budget. There is no new setting and no time window: two unrelated exits over a long session (for example under memory pressure) also spend the budget, and the cost of that is one Reload click, which restores it. The dashboard's own web view keeps its existing failure page from #183280.

## Real behavior proof

The PR build, packaged and launched through its normal entry point, with a page whose content process keeps quitting.

- Run: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/41208243695 (`proof 5b`, success; artifact `mac-proof-5b`).
- Environment: GitHub-hosted `macos-26` runner, macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Xcode 26.6. The app is packaged from this PR's head `c1160a13e196` (`identity.txt`: `source_sha = expected_sha = c1160a13e196e65f204d3bb15515abc1ae8aba73`) with `scripts/package-mac-app.sh` (debug, ad-hoc signed, `ai.openclaw.mac.debug` 2026.10.9). It talks to a job-owned loopback Gateway and a loopback HTTP fixture that logs every page load (`logs/fixture-hits.jsonl`).
- Harness: `scripts/mac-proof/5b.sh` on `etzelm/openclaw` branch `mac/proof-5b-raise` (`ec76014ea5f`). Crashes are induced by SIGKILL of the tab's WebContent process. Only processes whose kernel responsibility record names the PR build are killed. The native failure view is read from the window with Vision OCR (`logs/settled-view-*.txt`), because WebKit keeps AppKit subviews of a `WKWebView` out of the accessibility tree. Navigate > Back/Forward are clicked in the menu bar.
- Scenario and result (`scenario.log`; the counts are fixture loads of that path):
  1. A new tab opens `/page/crash`. After three terminations the loads go 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 3: two automatic reloads, then no third. OCR: "This page stopped repeatedly / Choose Reload to try loading it again." with Reload.
  2. Toolbar Reload: load 4, the failure view is gone. The next termination reloads automatically (load 5).
  3. Link to `/page/b`. Its terminations take its loads 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 3, settling on the failure view. Navigate > Back loads `/page/crash` (load 6), and its next termination reloads automatically (load 7).
  4. Navigate > Forward loads `/page/b` (load 4). Two further terminations both reload (loads 5, 6) with no failure view.

```
14:29:25 termination 1: loads of /page/crash = 2
14:29:30 termination 2: loads of /page/crash = 3
14:29:38 termination 3: loads of /page/crash = 3
14:30:01 termination after Reload: loads of /page/crash = 5
14:30:29 page b termination 3: loads of /page/b = 3
clicked Navigate > Back
14:30:41 termination after Back: loads of /page/crash = 7
clicked Navigate > Forward
14:30:51 termination 1 after Forward: loads of /page/b = 5
14:30:56 termination 2 after Forward: loads of /page/b = 6
14:30:58 PASS 5b: bounded reloads, settled view, Reload and menu Back/Forward reset
```

The dialog over the chat pane in every shot is the runner's own local network prompt, for its `hosted-compute-` agent, not for the app. It does not cover the Browser panel.

![11-settled-failure-view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/053e715b926a22d3f18cadea10ffc6d2d369d4d3/mac-item-5-tab-failures/proof-run-41208243695/11-settled-failure-view.png)
(After three terminations, the tab stops on "This page stopped repeatedly" with Reload and keeps the address `/page/crash`.)

![12-reload-recovered](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/053e715b926a22d3f18cadea10ffc6d2d369d4d3/mac-item-5-tab-failures/proof-run-41208243695/12-reload-recovered.png)
(Reload loads the page again; the next termination reloads automatically.)

![20-page-b-settled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/053e715b926a22d3f18cadea10ffc6d2d369d4d3/mac-item-5-tab-failures/proof-run-41208243695/20-page-b-settled.png)
(`/page/b` has spent its own budget. The next step is Navigate > Back, after which `/page/crash` reloads automatically after a termination.)

![31-forward-budget-restored](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/053e715b926a22d3f18cadea10ffc6d2d369d4d3/mac-item-5-tab-failures/proof-run-41208243695/31-forward-budget-restored.png)
(After Navigate > Forward, two terminations reloaded `/page/b` and no failure view is shown.)

Recording (app window only, 132 s): [recording.mov](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/053e715b926a22d3f18cadea10ffc6d2d369d4d3/mac-item-5-tab-failures/proof-run-41208243695/recording.mov)

## Evidence

Offscreen renders from the real controller in the regression harness; the grey band is a test harness readout of the published tab state and the fixture's page-load count, not app UI.

![b-before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/8741e3612b3ea2b8c0cfb96990e57865054ebdae/mac-item-5-tab-failures/b-before.png)
(Before, on main: after three content-process exits the page has been reloaded three times, 4 loads in total, and it keeps reloading on every further exit.)

![b-after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/8741e3612b3ea2b8c0cfb96990e57865054ebdae/mac-item-5-tab-failures/b-after.png)
(After: the first two exits reload, the third leaves the tab on the native failure view with Reload: 3 loads in total.)

Focused real-WKWebView regression in `DashboardNativeBrowserFailureTests` that SIGKILLs only the WebContent process WebKit reports for a task-owned tab (`_webProcessIdentifier`), against a loopback `DashboardHTTPFixture` that counts page loads:

- the first two terminations reload; the third shows the failure, is not loading, and keeps the tab URL;
- a second tab on another host still reloads after its own termination;
- Reload loads the page, clears the failure, and the next termination reloads automatically again.
- after a load that is not a user action (`WKWebView.load` called directly, so no reset) moves the tab to a second page, Navigate > Back (`DashboardWindowController.navigateBack()`, the command behind Command-[) and then Forward each restore the full budget: on each history entry two terminations reload and no failure view appears.

Results on macOS 27.0.1 arm64, Swift 6.4 (Command Line Tools), on top of `mac/5a-tab-load-error` before it gained `e164e6e589e`. The suites were not re-run after merging #185432's current head and main into this branch (`c1160a13e19`, both merges clean except the appended test suite); the running-app proof above is on that merged head.

Earlier results:

- `swift test --filter DashboardNativeBrowserFailureTests` on this branch: 4 tests passed (the 3 from #183927 plus this one).
- The extended test with only the Navigate menu change reverted (sources at `1853bd4e7da`): fails at `browser.failureView == nil` with "exit 2 at /crashing after menu history"; menu Back left the budget spent, so the second termination showed the failure view.
- The budget test before the Navigate menu leg was added, with all of this branch's sources reverted (A sources; test loop bound written as `2` because `automaticReloadLimit` does not exist there): fails at `browser.failureView != nil` and `!crashing.isLoading`; the third exit reloads again.
- Siblings `DashboardNativeBrowser|DashboardHTTPFixtureTests|DashboardBrowserDownloadTests|DashboardBrowserCookieBoundaryTests|DashboardCloseShortcutTests`: 39 tests in 8 suites passed.
- `swift build --build-tests`, `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` (0 files need formatting), `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` (only the existing `DashboardManager.swift` file_length violation, also on base), `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, `git diff --check`: clean.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base <current main>` on this branch (the stack head, so it also covers #183927's files): every guard passed except `lint apps` (the existing `DashboardManager.swift` file_length violation) and `macOS app CI tests` (1 failed, 607 passed), whose one failure is the tooling test `test/scripts/generate-gateway-protocol-plugin.test.ts`, which builds a fixture Swift package and fails on this machine because the shim it probes forwards to the test runner's own Node (v26.3.0 here, below the required >=26.12.1), so the protocol plugin rejects every candidate; it does not touch the files in this change. The lint result is identical on base and head (`scripts/lint-swift.sh macos`: 1 violation, the same `DashboardManager.swift` file_length).

## Related work

- #152668 (open, prepare integrated tab logins before opening links) touches `DashboardNativeBrowserHost.swift`, `DashboardWindowController.swift` and `apps/.i18n/native-source.json`. No shared lines: its host change removes `self.onOpen?()` in `open` (line 160 on `70c70646d86`), a few lines above this stack's `navigate`/`perform` changes; its controller hunks are in lines 99-559, ours at 1331-1496. It already conflicts with current main on its own. Whichever lands second regenerates the i18n inventory with `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` (the inventory records source line sites).
- No open PR covers #183927 or #183928 (searched by symptom and by the owner file names).

## Gaps

- The reporter's loop was induced by killing the content process; a page that naturally crashes on every load was not available, so the regression induces terminations the same way (SIGKILL of only the test tab's own WebContent process).
- The two images under Evidence are offscreen renders from the regression harness; the running app is shown under Real behavior proof.
- Budget reset by toolbar navigation and physical link clicks is covered by code review only; the regression test calls the Navigate commands directly, and the running-app proof clicks Navigate > Back/Forward in the menu bar (not their key shortcuts). Browser panel Back/Forward shares the same `goBack(in:)`/`goForward(in:)` helpers but is not exercised by the test.
- WebKit's default right-click menu in a reading tab (Back, Forward, Reload) calls WebKit directly and does not reset the budget, as before this change; filtering or rerouting those items is left for a follow-up.
- The `macos-swift` CI job is skipped for this PR, so the Swift suites last ran locally with the Command Line Tools (same local stand-ins as #183927) before the merges that produced `c1160a13e19`.
- There is no running-app "before" run. The behavior on main (unbounded reloads) is shown by the offscreen renders under Evidence and by the regression test with this branch's sources reverted.

prs.body:
Closes #193126

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes eligible IMAP mail being dropped when a trusted receiving MTA includes valid comments around its Authentication-Results identifier.

## User Impact

User impact: operators who explicitly enable trusted assertions at an asserted floor can receive mail with correctly commented identifiers. Verified remains the default; existing sender, freshness, token and authentication checks remain in place. The receiving MTA must still strip or overwrite forged Authentication-Results headers.

## Why This Change Was Made

The parser split at the first semicolon and checked the unprocessed prefix. Normalizing nested and escaped comments as whitespace preserves token boundaries. Quoted contents cannot supply result clauses, and malformed syntax and misleading result suffixes are rejected.

prs.title: fix(macos): exec host returns empty output for invalid UTF-8
prs.body:
Closes #187601

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS app exec host returns empty `stdout`/`stderr` when a command's output contains any invalid or incomplete UTF-8 sequence, while still reporting `success: true`. A command killed at its timeout right after printing half of a multibyte character (spinners, box drawing, emoji) comes back with `timedOut: true` and no output at all.

## User Impact

Agents running `host=node` commands on a Mac now get the valid part of the output, with `U+FFFD` in place of the bad bytes, instead of an empty result.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ShellExecutor`'s file-backed capture decoded each whole buffer with `String(bytes:encoding:) ?? ""`. That decode fails for the entire buffer when any one byte sequence is invalid. It now uses `String(decoding:as: UTF8.self)`, which `runStreamingDetailed` in the same file already uses through swift-subprocess. Process, timeout, and capture behavior are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and other readers</summary>

- `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/ShellExecutor.swift:45-46` is the only failable decode of captured command output. The pattern has been there since the file-backed capture in #104827, which kept the earlier pipe-based decode.
- `PortGuardian.swift:461` decodes `ShellExecutor.run`'s payload, which is now always valid UTF-8, so its fallback can no longer trigger.
- `GatewayProcessManager.swift:1403` reads the Gateway log file. That's a different owner, outside this bug.
- The issue's related note about signal-terminated children being reported as `exit N` is a separate behavior change and is not part of this PR.
</details>

## Evidence

I packaged main (`c32556b0cea`) and this branch as ad-hoc macOS apps. Each ran under a named profile in remote mode against an isolated Gateway (private state and config, loopback port) started from that app's bundled runtime. Each case is a Gateway `node.invoke` `system.run` call to the paired app, the node command that `exec host=node` forwards and that runs `ShellExecutor.runDetailed`.

Main:
```
## control-ascii: /bin/sh -c "printf 'plain-ascii'; printf 'err-ascii' 1>&2"
{"success":true,"exitCode":0,"timedOut":false,"stdout":"plain-ascii","stderr":"err-ascii"}
## invalid-byte: /bin/sh -c "printf 'abc\377'; printf 'abc\377' 1>&2"
{"success":true,"exitCode":0,"timedOut":false,"stdout":"","stderr":""}
## split-multibyte: /bin/sh -c "printf 'abc\342\234'; printf 'abc\342\234' 1>&2"
{"success":true,"exitCode":0,"timedOut":false,"stdout":"","stderr":""}
## timeout-split: /bin/sh -c "printf 'building \342\234'; sleep 5" (timeoutMs=1000)
{"success":false,"exitCode":null,"timedOut":true,"stdout":"","stderr":""}
```

This branch:
```
## control-ascii
{"success":true,"exitCode":0,"timedOut":false,"stdout":"plain-ascii","stderr":"err-ascii"}
## invalid-byte
{"success":true,"exitCode":0,"timedOut":false,"stdout":"abc�","stderr":"abc�"}
## split-multibyte
{"success":true,"exitCode":0,"timedOut":false,"stdout":"abc�","stderr":"abc�"}
## timeout-split
{"success":false,"exitCode":null,"timedOut":true,"stdout":"building �","stderr":""}
```

Tests: two new `LowCoverageHelperTests` cases (both streams for `\377` and a truncated `\342\234`, plus the timeout case) fail on main with empty output and pass here. `LowCoverageHelperTests` and `ShellExecutorTimeoutTests`: 26 passed. Run locally with `swift test --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --filter 'LowCoverageHelperTests|ShellExecutorTimeoutTests'`. The timeout test's budget went from 0.5 s to 1 s after the app capture; production code is unchanged since.

Not run locally: `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` and `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` (pinned tools not installed); CI covers them.

Production delta +2/-2; test delta +22/-0.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the previous decode with no state or config migration. Blast radius is output captured by `ShellExecutor.runDetailed` on macOS.

## What Problem This Solves

Two leftovers from the Skill Workshop off-state audit (#192931), both approved by the maintainer:

- With `plugins.enabled: false`, the Workshop page offered **Turn on Skill Workshop**. The button always failed, because turning on one plugin can't override the global switch. `plugins.list` doesn't report that switch, and the Control UI has no setting for it.

## User Impact

- Non-admins see "Skill Workshop is off" with only "An admin can turn it on from Plugins."
- Admins with plugins on are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The off panel now loads the runtime config, the same owner the Workshop already reads for its learning mode. `arePluginsDisabled` in `mode.ts` returns true only when the loaded config sets `plugins.enabled: false`. If the config is unknown or still loading, the page keeps offering the button, so a slow read never hides a working action.

prs.title: fix(exec): dollar amounts in agent messages are corrupted when exec text uses $<digit> in double quotes
prs.body:
Closes #179890

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: dollar amounts in agent-sent messages are silently corrupted ("$900" becomes "00") when an `exec` command passes the text in double quotes.

## User Impact

User impact: exec commands that would deliver a corrupted dollar amount are refused before they run. The refusal shows the text as written next to what the shell would deliver, and how to fix it (single quotes, `\$`, or a quoted heredoc), so the agent retries correctly instead of sending the wrong amount to a customer. It can be disabled with `OPENCLAW_EXEC_DOLLAR_GUARD=off`.

**Open question for maintainers:** this is default-on and uses an environment switch. If you'd prefer it opt-in, or shipped as a plugin on the existing `before_tool_call` hook instead of in core, I'm happy to rework it that way. Tell me which shape you want.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runBeforeToolCallHook` checks `exec` command text for a `$<digit>` that the shell would expand, before any plugin or approval policy runs. Codex-native shell commands reach the same policy through the PreToolUse native hook relay. Relay planning now counts the guard as a before-tool-call policy and keeps `exec` in the PreToolUse matcher, so native commands are covered even with no other policy installed.

The scanner is deliberately conservative. It only flags an expansion it can show would be empty:
- It honours single quotes, `\$`, `$'...'`, quoted heredoc delimiters, `${...}`, `$((...))` and comments.
- It recurses into `$(...)`, including substitutions inside unquoted heredoc bodies, with their own quoting.
- It ignores `$0` (the shell or script name) unless it reads as money (`$0.50`).
- It stays out of commands that define functions or set positional parameters (`set --`, `shift`, `getopts`), where `$1.00` may be intended.
- It fails open on anything it cannot parse.

Code-mode `exec` (JavaScript) is excluded.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/shell-dollar-expansion-guard.test.ts` (35 tests): the hazard shapes, every safe quoting form, `$0`, populated positional parameters, heredoc command substitution, `bash -lc` unwrapping, fail-open, and the `runBeforeToolCallHook` veto, allow and disable cases. The `$0`, positional-parameter and heredoc-substitution cases fail on the previous revision and pass now.
- `src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.dollar-guard.test.ts` (6 tests): Codex `Bash` and `exec_command` are denied and single-quoted amounts pass. Relay planning enables PreToolUse for `exec` with no other policy and keeps it in a relay scoped to other tools; these planning cases fail without the relay change.
- The existing `agent-tools.before-tool-call*` and `native-hook-relay*` unit suites pass. `native-hook-relay.participants` and `native-hook-relay.remote-http` fail identically on `main` without this change in my environment.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- Replayed against 391 unique `$`-bearing exec commands from a production deployment: 18 were flagged, all genuine expansion bugs, with no false positives.
- Still to add: a gateway trace of a real agent refusing and retrying. I'll attach it before asking for re-review.

prs.title: fix(gateway): label root config issues in reload logs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway reload warning prints an empty path for root-level config issues:

```
[reload] config reload skipped (invalid config): : Unrecognized key: "sessions"
```

Refs #191869. That report reads this line as a rejection of `tools.sessions`, but the empty path means a root-level `sessions` key. The missing `<root>` label is what makes the two hard to tell apart.

## User Impact

Operators who mistype a top-level key now see `<root>: Unrecognized key: "sessions"`, so the log says where the bad key lives. The config audit record already used this label. Accepted configs and nested issue paths log the same as before.

This does not change validation. `tools.sessions.allowThreadTargets` was already accepted, and this PR does not add `tools.sessions` to `agents.defaults` or agent entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

The invalid-config branch formatted the same issues twice: once with `normalizeRoot: true` for the audit record and once without it for the log. It now formats them once and uses the result for both, which also removes two lines from a file held by the line-cap ratchet.

## Evidence

![Reload log and sessions_send proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/191869/proof-191869.png)

Local Gateway on Windows with isolated state on port 28793. Each row is a hot edit to the config file while the Gateway was running.

| Config written | 2026.10.10 reload log | This branch (16055383409) |
|---|---|---|

prs.title: fix(agents): a quota-class failure should prefer the model chain over a same-profile auth rotation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a quota-class provider failure (HTTP 429 with a usage/plan-limit body), the embedded agent rotates the auth profile and re-runs the **same** model before the configured model-fallback chain is consulted. When the provider has exactly one usable profile - or when the rotation re-selects the profile that just failed - that rotation is a no-op: it spends a provider attempt against the same exhausted plan and delays the chain that could have recovered the run.

The `rate_limit` path already has a rotation cap that escalates to the model chain (`MAX_RATE_LIMIT_PROFILE_ROTATIONS`), and the `overloaded` path escalates through `overloadProfileRotationLimit`. What is missing is the rule that **a rotation which lands on the same profile is not a rotation at all**.

## User Impact

A quota-class failure now advances the model chain in the same failure instead of burning an attempt on the exhausted profile first. A run that has a working fallback chain configured recovers on the first quota error rather than the second.

## Why This Change Was Made

`advanceAuthProfileCandidate` advances by **index** over the prepared auth attempts. When two prepared attempts carry the same profile id (an OAuth attempt and an inline attempt for the same profile, or two routes for one profile), the "rotation" re-selects the profile that just failed and still reports success. The caller then retries the same model against the same exhausted plan.

The fix keeps profile rotation useful whenever it can actually change the credentials:

- The rotation is reported as a rotation only when the active profile changes.
- When the rotation re-selects the failed profile and a model chain is configured, the controller reports "no rotation", so the failover policy resolves to `fallback_model` and the chain advances immediately.
- Without a configured chain the existing same-profile retry is preserved, so a single-model deployment loses nothing.

Scope notes:

- The `overloaded` path is untouched.
- The session/request model-pin contract (#151980) is untouched; this change is about auth profiles, not model pins.
- The failed profile is still marked in cooldown exactly as before; only the decision to *retry* the same profile changes.

Related: #141115 (a 429 must consult the chain - this PR is the ordering half of that class), #151980 (session model pins stay strict; this change touches auth profiles, not model pins), #186418 (the request-level ladder half, carried by #186420).

## Evidence

Focused test run on this branch (rebased onto main at `fdeb8f7e`):

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-embedded-agent-run.config.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-retry-controller.test.ts
    -> Test Files  1 passed (1), Tests  42 passed (42)

New coverage in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-retry-controller.test.ts`:

- a quota-class rotation that re-selects the failed profile reports no rotation, so the caller advances the model chain;
- a quota-class rotation that moves to a different profile still reports a rotation and still counts toward the rotation cap;
- without a configured model chain the same-profile rotation still retries, so single-model deployments keep their existing recovery.

One existing fixture was updated: "waits for the provider floor before exhausting recovery and rotating credentials" used an `advanceAttemptAuthProfile` stub that returned `true` without moving the active profile. A successful rotation moves the active profile, so the stub now does the same; the assertions are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(acp): a failed identity save leaves a new backend session on every request
prs.body:
Closes #127371

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an ACP request succeeds on a backend identity that was never saved when the identity write fails, and the next request opens yet another backend session.

## User Impact

User impact: a failed identity save now fails the request and closes the new handle, instead of silently opening a new backend session on every call.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ensure write is now strict like session init: it must return the stored ACP entry before the handle is cached. Init and ensure share the close and persisted-entry helpers. Control and refused publications keep their handle open, as before.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof: isolated Gateway with the `acpx` backend. The backend is a tiny ACP agent I wrote over stdio (official SDK, no session resume), not a real harness. The storage failure is injected: a SQLite trigger aborts `acp_sessions` updates that store a new backend session id for session A (`database or disk is full`). Sessions A and B were created with `/acp spawn toy --mode persistent --thread off`, then the Gateway was restarted:

```text
main (74f111a):
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 1"   exit=0  pong   # opened toy-1351073-1, prompt sent, identity never saved
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 2"   exit=0  pong   # closed toy-1351073-1, opened toy-1351194-1, prompt sent
gateway log: acp-manager: failed persisting ACP metadata for <A>: Error: database or disk is full

PR (5059270):
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 1"   exit=1  OpenClaw couldn't save your conversation because the disk is full. ...
                                                                    # opened toy-1349192-1, closed it, no prompt sent
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 2"   exit=1  (same)   # opened toy-1349284-1, closed it, no prompt sent
$ openclaw agent --session-key <B> --message "B request 2"   exit=0  pong     # prompt to B's own toy-1349059-1, untouched
-- trigger dropped, storage restored --
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 3"   exit=0  pong     # opened toy-1349394-1, prompt sent
$ openclaw agent --session-key <A> --message "A request 4"   exit=0  pong     # same toy-1349394-1, no new backend session
```

prs.title: feat(release): allow approved tiny emergency patches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Urgent security patches currently wait through full release-validation cycles even when the complete change is tiny and a release manager accepts the validation risk.

## User Impact

Release managers gain an exceptional stable/latest fast track, bounded to the complete baseline-to-candidate delta: **3 commits, 20 files, 500 added/deleted lines, no binary changes**. Ordinary releases keep their current gates. This PR authorizes no actual release.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `emergency-patch-v1` to the existing shared publisher, independently of the historical beta-focused shortcut and retrospective waivers. A reviewed, release-manager-owned policy pins exact signed base/candidate tags and SHAs plus the emergency rationale; its default approval list is empty. The baseline must be current npm latest (or the exact candidate for already-published recovery). Environment approval/authenticated human receipt, npm preflight, SDK acknowledgement, exact-tarball/provenance verification and publication authority remain mandatory.

Full release validation, source CI, cross-OS/live-provider/soak/performance cycles are deliberately omitted, never reported as passing. An attached evidence asset identifies the approved full delta and skipped coverage. The hard limits are conservative ceilings, not a claim that small patches are inherently safe.

Simplification: one admission owner and existing publication/recovery owners, rather than a second pipeline or beta-promotion adapter. Necessary growth is the policy/admission module, workflow wiring and boundary regressions (583 additions, 10 deletions; 193 added test lines).

## Evidence

- Actual pre-change npm workflow guard rejects `emergency-patch-v1`; updated actual guard accepts its approved-parent shape and rejects missing parent/mixed validation inputs.
- 82 tests passed across emergency admission, historical focused evidence, approval workflows and parent publication. Real Git fixtures cover complete diff, over-budget/binary rejection, signatures/identity/baseline checks, depth-one checkout and exact already-published recovery.
- 39 additional existing tests passed: release finalization, draft/evidence handling and npm publish wrapper. The 28 draft/finalization tests were rerun after the final evidence-rendering adjustment.
- Targeted oxlint and tooling TypeScript project passed; formatter, shell syntax, test-line ratchet and `git diff --check` passed.
- Workflow owner-generation, composite-input and conflict-marker guards passed. Local full `check-workflows` lacked actionlint/Go/pre-commit and Python venv ensurepip; **hosted actionlint passed on the current head**. Remaining broad CI is not claimed complete.
- Fresh independent review found two P1s (shallow checkout and postpublication recovery); both fixed with regressions. Follow-up full-diff review found no remaining P0–P2 findings.
- **Canonical autoreview completed scoped-clean at P0–P2**, OpenClaw engine with effective model `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, base `8c411658c18b2787937e75db8c56faad10532590` to head `2fc1647c95a901583888a1635341942e9da6c71a`. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable, so the supported OpenClaw-engine autoreview route was used. Hosted ClawSweeper has acknowledged intake, not completed review.

prs.body:
Related: #127613

## What Problem This Solves

Launch at Login could report success after launchctl failed, while waiting inside the settings queue prevented a newer Off choice from superseding an unfinished enable.

## User Impact

Failed changes reconcile the native switch and display actionable Login Items guidance. Normal retry can settle On with a registered job; normal Off removes future autostart. Enabling no longer forces an extra restart after bootstrap.

## Why This Change Was Made

LaunchAgentManager remains the serialized mutation owner: it checks required command results, rolls back failed activation, verifies loaded state, and publishes only the current intent. Validated FIFO admission is separate from reply completion, preserving #145451 intent ordering and existing consent/cancellation behavior. The distinct enqueueAdmission API preserves legacy enqueue callers.

The plist already has [RunAtLoad:true](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/launchd/blob/main/man/launchd.plist.5), so bootstrap starts the job. The repair removes the redundant forced kickstart from enable, retains final verification/rollback/generation guards, and keeps kickstart in explicit restart(). ## What Problem This Solves

A provider outage diagnosed after Full Release Validation currently requires another validation cycle just to apply an approved waiver.

## User Impact

Release managers can land an exact retrospective waiver in trusted release tooling, then reuse the original completed candidate validation without rerunning its tests. No active retrospective grants are included in this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse the existing waiver evaluator and strict publication verifier. Bind each new grant to the parent run, attempt, candidate SHA, version, child role, and exact supported provider/Telegram job.
- Retain the immutable attempt-specific manifest before the final policy verdict, **after** sealed-candidate integrity verification. Never rewrite the original manifest, failures, or admission records.
- Emit a separate verified policy evaluation with the new tooling SHA. Checklist and publication preflight consume that same verdict.
- Preserve hard gates: complete authenticated child evidence, exact aggregate failure causes, successful diagnostics and candidate integrity, and independently successful npm/Docker artifact producers. Only direct all-group candidate-owned evidence qualifies; old failures without the retained snapshot and evidence-reuse chains do not.

Updated the release contract and release-maintainer instructions. This adds no workflow, runtime waiver flag, state store, or competing validation pipeline. Net change: +206 production/workflow/declaration lines and +132 test lines; the rest is documentation and the explicit test allocation.

## Evidence

- Final committed release consumer suites: 6 files, 454 passed and 2 existing skips; 11.99 seconds wall time.
- Regression coverage exercises retrospective publication authentication and npm lineage with the original failing parent/child conclusions and unchanged manifest. Rejects wrong attempts/targets, Gateway E2E grants, package failures, and skipped candidate integrity verification.
- Base/fixed workflow comparison: the original manifest upload followed the failing verdict; the new snapshot precedes that verdict and follows candidate integrity verification. The ordering is covered by a committed workflow test.
- Scripts typecheck and tooling-test typecheck passed. Focused script/test lint, formatting, documentation formatting/content, test-line ratchet, and diff checks passed.
- Fresh independent read-only review found two hard-gate issues; both were repaired and independently re-reviewed clean. Local canonical autoreview (OpenClaw engine, P0–P2, final staged snapshot against base 8c411658c18b2787937e75db8c56faad10532590) completed scoped-clean. Its supplied-diff assessment did not execute code; independent review traced the unchanged owners too.

**Validation gaps:** no live release workflow or publication was dispatched. Local full workflow lint could not start because the host lacks pinned actionlint/Go and Python venv/pre-commit support. An additional package-acceptance subset had 34 passing tests and one setup failure because zip is unavailable; it did not establish a product failure. CI and release-manager review remain required before landing.

prs.title: fix(release): retry EPIPE readbacks and reject gated ClawHub children on cleanup
prs.body:
## Problem

Publish parent 41764249210 (2026.11.5-beta.1) hit two recovery gaps from #192564.

1. **`fetch failed: write EPIPE` failed the parent after a good publication.** The issue blamed `openclaw-npm-postpublish-verify`, but the job log and the uploaded `release-postpublish-diagnostics.json` show that verifier passed: signature, provenance, fresh-exact and install paths all printed OK. The failing stage was `pluginNpm`, at its first package (`@openclaw/abliteration-provider`), with `command-failure`. That stage reads the npm registry through `fetchNpmRegistryWithRetry` (`scripts/lib/npm-publish-plan.mjs`) and downloads Actions artifacts through `runBoundedRetry` (`scripts/lib/actions-artifact-archive.mjs`). Each loop kept its own copy of the transient socket-code list, and neither copy had `EPIPE`. So undici's `TypeError("fetch failed", { cause: { code: "EPIPE" } })` was rethrown on the first attempt. The two copies had also drifted: only one had `ENETUNREACH`. The postpublish verifier's own reads already retry on `fetch failed`, so this PR leaves it unchanged.
2. **A gated bootstrap child outlived its failed parent.** `cleanup_clawhub_children` (job "Preserve ClawHub recovery evidence before cleanup") already targets the exact recorded `CHILD_PLUGIN_CLAWHUB_BOOTSTRAP_RUN_ID`. It ran `gh run cancel 41765136531` at 04:04:51Z and GitHub accepted the request. The run still sat on its `clawhub-plugin-bootstrap` gate ("Validate immutable bootstrap handoff") until a maintainer rejected the gate by hand at 04:11:10Z. A cancel request alone does not end a job waiting on an environment gate.

## Solution

1. Add `EPIPE` to both existing transient socket-code lists. Nothing else changes in either retry loop. HTTP status handling, integrity checks, identity checks and conflict checks stay outside the classifiers, so a real verification mismatch is still never retried. The existing `CERT_HAS_EXPIRED` no-retry test still covers that. A first revision moved the two lists into one new shared module, but these files are copied by fixed release-tooling closures and sparse workflow checkouts (`release-plan-producer` reported "tooling import is outside the fixed closure", and package-acceptance fixtures failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`). A new import edge would have to be added to every closure, so this PR keeps the two lists separate and records the drift as a follow-up.
2. `cleanup_clawhub_children` now calls the existing `reject_pending_deployments` on each recorded, unfinished child before it cancels the child. This is the same reject-then-cancel order the superseded-child sweep already uses. A 403 on the reject call still warns and writes the reviewer reject/cancel commands to the step summary, and cancellation goes ahead anyway. Run IDs still come only from the parent's recorded outputs; there is no title search.

The release-CI skill's publish-children notes now describe this cleanup behavior.

Not done here: items 3 to 5 of #192564 (checklist resume command, publish watcher, `release:candidate` single pass) belong to a separate lane.

## Impact

Release tooling only. Production delta: +5 lines (two list entries plus the gate rejection call). A transient EPIPE on a plugin npm readback or an artifact download now retries within the existing bounded budgets (3 attempts, 1s/2s backoff, 180s deadline for npm; 5 attempts with jittered backoff for artifacts). It no longer forces a parent resume. A failed parent now clears its recorded bootstrap child's gate, so the resume checklist is no longer blocked by `FAIL concurrency.plugin-clawhub-new.yml.<run>`.

## Evidence

- Root cause from run 41764249210: job 126360277873 log (`verified published npm install paths` printed, then `fetch failed` / `Caused by: write EPIPE` from `release-verify-publish`), the diagnostics artifact (`currentStage: pluginNpm`, `postpublish: success`), and job 126380086087 log (`Request to cancel workflow 41765136531 submitted` at 04:04:51Z, while the child's approvals API shows a manual rejection at 04:11:10Z).
- Red on base, green with the fix:
  - `test/npm-publish-plan.test.ts` › "retries a request write EPIPE before any registry response". On base it fails with `promise rejected "TypeError: fetch failed"`.
  - `test/scripts/release-publish-parent.test.ts` › "cleans up recorded ClawHub children after a later dispatch fails" now asserts that the child's gate is rejected before the cancel. It fails on base.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/plugin-publication-artifact.test.ts test/npm-publish-plan.test.ts test/scripts/release-publish-parent.test.ts`: 3 files, 132 tests passed.
- `config/test-lines-allocations/release-publish-transient-recovery.txt` allocates the 16 added regression-test lines. `check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main` passes.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json --incremental`: clean. oxlint and oxfmt on changed files: clean. `git diff --check`: clean.

Refs #192564 (items 1 and 2; items 3 to 5 are tracked in a separate PR).

prs.title: fix(release): print core npm resume and report required candidate flags together
prs.body:
## Problem

Recovering 2026.11.5-beta.1 (#192564, items 3 and 5):

- `pnpm release:candidate` printed a fresh-publish command for a tag whose core npm child had already published. The retained evidence shows `npm.package.openclaw: not published; beta publication planned` with `npm.preflight` PASS. Preflight decided resume from `observeReleaseNpmState().corePublished`. With current FRV manifests that value comes from the sealed FRV npm decisions, which were recorded before publication. So the `core-npm.resume` discovery (npm provenance -> original publisher run) never ran.
- The `release.tag` row always warned `Candidate tag has not been published yet`, because the checklist always passed `allowPlannedTag: true`. It did this even though `assertReleaseCandidateTag` had already read the remote tag with `git ls-remote`.
- The checklist took three passes: the missing SDK acknowledgement, then `npm.preflight` failing with a 404 on a `release-publish/<sha12>-*` ref, then `--workflow-sha`. With no P pinned, preflight swapped in a *proposed*, nonexistent tooling tag and then verified npm lineage against it. So an unpinned run could never complete, and each pass reported only one missing flag.

## Solution

- **Resume:** `release-publish-preflight` reads the live core version from the `openclaw` packument it already fetches for the selector, using an `exactVersion` probe. Resume discovery runs on that live state. The command it prints now includes `-f openclaw_npm_resume_run_id=<original publisher>`. This uses the same provenance-based identification the publisher uses in `resolve_openclaw_npm_publish_state` / `openclaw-npm-resume-run.mts`. The now-unused `corePublished` projection is removed from `observeReleaseNpmState`.
- **Remote tag:** `assertReleaseCandidateTag` returns whether the remote tag exists at the target, and the checklist passes `allowPlannedTag: !tagPublished`. A pushed tag now resolves through GitHub as a PASS row.
- **One-pass flags:** right after any FRV dispatch, before waiting, the checklist gathers every missing flag into one failure with one exact rerun command. Today that means `--workflow-sha <trusted tooling SHA>` when neither `--workflow-sha` nor `--publish-workflow-ref` is set, plus the early SDK acknowledgement digest. The late SDK acknowledgement failure uses the same formatter.
- **Unpinned P:** the checklist prints the exact flag; it does not mint a tag on its own. The regular-release reference says a prepare-only request does not authorize pushing publication tags, so tag creation stays behind the explicit `--workflow-sha` (or an existing `--publish-workflow-ref`). This change makes preflight's "planned tooling tag" WARN branch unreachable, so it is removed. A `main` workflow ref now always fails with the existing remediation.
- Docs: regular-release and publication-recovery references describe the required P flag, the single failure, and resume discovery.

Scope: items 3–5 of #192564. The publish watcher (item 4) is split into a follow-up PR. Postpublish verifier retries and bootstrap-child cleanup (items 1–2) are handled in a separate lane.

## Impact

Release tooling only. A resumed direct publication gets the correct resume command on the first pass. Operators see every missing checklist flag at once, while FRV keeps running. A pushed release tag no longer shows a misleading WARN. A checklist without a P pin now stops right after dispatch instead of failing hours later at `npm.preflight`.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/release-publish-preflight.test.ts test/scripts/release-publish-state.test.ts test/scripts/release-candidate-checklist.test.ts`: 171 passed.
- New `release-publish-preflight.test.ts` (sealed decision says planned, live registry has the version: the command carries the resume run; when unpublished it does not). Red on base: the published case fails without the fix.
- Checklist coordinator case: unpinned P plus a required SDK acknowledgement produces one failure whose decoded rerun command adds exactly both flags, before any FRV wait or preflight. A pushed tag produces `allowPlannedTag: false`. `assertReleaseCandidateTag` returns false for absent and true for published lightweight/annotated tags.
- Test-line budget: net +103 regression lines, which `config/test-lines-allocations/release-candidate-resume-flags.txt` records. These are the two red-on-base regressions (live-registry resume at the preflight boundary, and one-pass flags in the coordinator). The cases were consolidated first: the checklist cases are merged into existing table rows, and the preflight test is compacted.
- `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json`, targeted `run-oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` are clean.
- Not proven locally: a hosted release resume. The incident evidence bundle (`release-candidate-evidence.md` for v2026.11.5-beta.1) shows the sealed `plan` row next to a passing `npm.preflight`, which is the condition the new test reproduces.

Refs #192564 (items 3 and 5; item 4 follows in a separate PR; items 1–2 are in another lane, so this PR does not close the issue)

prs.title: fix: show Gateway names for linked Slack mentions in Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI message bodies can show raw Slack mention IDs even after the referenced person has a verified Gateway profile link. Correct sender labels do not resolve inline references, and bot mentions must not be mistaken for the sender.

## User Impact

- Linked human references show the current Gateway display name using the existing viewer/session visibility policy.
- Unlinked people and bots use the Slack name already recorded in the message; unknown IDs, code, and messages without original account scope remain literal.
- Stored/model text, provider IDs, routing, authorization, and mention notifications are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep native syntax and ID normalization in Slack’s pure mention adapter. The Gateway resolves the canonical channel/account/sender tuple and enriches only the admitted display copy. Native pages are enriched before final byte budgeting/encoding, preserving pagination and the webchat fast path. Live fanout asks each reader to reload its canonical view rather than broadcasting a shared person-name projection.

The existing Slack stripping behavior is moved unchanged into the same sibling adapter to satisfy the channel module’s line-cap ratchet. No new persistence, configuration option, or permission is introduced.

Reported by @Patrick-Erichsen; human co-author credit is retained in the commit. **Patrick requested landing this PR on 2026-11-04. Landing remains subject to the applicable review/proof gates and supported inherited-CI policy. No deployment is requested.**

## Evidence

**Red:** On baseline `57405d6f170a905c1056ae755ec20e259f893abf`, the linked-state RPC and real Gateway/Control UI browser regressions fail on the expected Gateway-name assertion. The serialized-page contract also fails because the original encoder discards the object graph before display enrichment. Setup failures were not counted as regression proof.

**Green:** Real Gateway + native WebSocket Control UI proof passes for initial subscription history and committed live append/publication. Focused Gateway suites passed 155 tests; live-publication/availability/guest suites passed 54. The full touched history/serialization pair was rerun after isolating its adapter fixture from extension runtime graphs. Slack channel and agent-tool prefix-stability suites pass. Core/extension/changed-test type checks, targeted lint, formatting, whitespace, and the line-cap ratchet pass.

Primary reproduction command (run unchanged on baseline and candidate):

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/slack-inline-identity.e2e.test.ts
```

Deterministic linked-state regression:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-handler.test.ts -t "projects manually linked Slack"
```

Coverage includes different/missing account scope, unverified viewers, self references, unknown IDs, source fallbacks, code, escaping, expansion, unchanged stored content, and no inbox effects. Fresh independent local P0–P2 autoreview completed with no accepted findings; its chunked/cross-file-context limitations are not treated as runtime proof.

### Browser proof

The attached **baseline → candidate** captures are inspected, cropped, synthetic fixtures through a real Gateway and Control UI (not mocked transport). The sender fixture is Patrick; the separate human target is `Gateway Alice`, the bot fallback is `Roboclaw`, and unknown/code IDs remain visible. Slack accounts are disabled in the fixture; no live Slack API or inference turn is exercised.

### CI follow-up and test cost

The first CI run caught a one-second functional-readiness poll and unattributed test growth. Commit `c8bb79b1cde857f0fd19b1d8c20666e78a042836` waits for the exact initial/live history result with an explicit setup deadline; it does not change production timeouts or performance budgets. Commit `2690183c4fc67f40d813065a3518f4e76314fc25` registers the fixture with the real-Gateway inventory. The correctly routed **ui-e2e-serial** proof passes: **1 test, 70.23 seconds Vitest wall time** after private-QA preparation. The real-Gateway skip flag correctly excludes it from collection.

The separate `config/test-lines-allocations/slack-linked-mention-display-192473.txt` record attributes **432 new test lines** to the account/viewer, serializer, and real native startup/live-path contracts. The shared test-line scalar is unchanged. The pinned CI main base `f38495f7` independently has a **20-line preexisting ceiling gap** at net delta zero; the fully allocated PR preserves that gap. The separate CI admission assertion remains under investigation; isolated passing baseline/feature replays and the failed same-head CI replay are not claimed as a fix. Broad CI is not green.

Delivery is checked against GitHub’s rendered body image elements, and both actual published proof asset URLs load and decode correctly.

### Bounds

Gateway-link reads are bounded to 20 distinct identities per response; remaining references retain their recorded fallback/raw form. Historical messages without captured channel/account provenance are not guessed from text or the session’s current reply route. Broad PR CI remains separate proof.

![Before — raw Slack mention IDs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fca96dae-3c29-49d4-be4a-fcdedd63c0cc)

prs.title: feat(sessions): add creator-only and named-audience confidentiality
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Personal chats and closed working groups on multi-user Gateways need a read/write audience that is independent of visual Draft status and participation membership.

## User Impact

Operators can configure creator/admin-only conversations or exact named audiences without using Draft as the confidentiality mechanism. The policy applies to discovery, reading, events and mutation admission, while existing agent restrictions and incognito behavior remain in force.

This is an opt-in permission-model change. Enabling the source policy also restricts existing sessions without an explicit access override. Explicit per-session overrides remain authoritative. Restrictive access prevents public-share disclosure. Older binaries ignore the new access metadata, so staged adoption and rollback containment are required; this PR is not a production deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add a separate session access policy with creator-only, named-audience, source-bound and explicit unrestricted modes. Only direct-human creator/admin authority can manage access; existing-session changes are identity-fenced.
- Resolve source-bound audiences from exact agent/channel/account/chat rules and explicit migration aliases. Numeric Telegram topics inherit the exact chat audience; ambiguous or unknown routes fail closed. Audiences are trusted canonical profile IDs supplied by the operator, never inferred from display names, chat categories or participation members.
- Persist source access before the first publication of inbound, web and child sessions. Private or unknown sources do not inherit a shared parent's audience.
- Reuse one access decision across existing read, sharing, storage and transport owners. Recheck current access for revocation, retained mutation/media authority and cached discovery; stale bookkeeping cannot restore revoked access.
- Keep visual creation defaults, Draft, incognito and role/agent ceilings separate. No existing live configuration or session migration is included.

The smallest coherent stage is the access boundary plus atomic creation: exposing the setting without covering its read/write consumers would leave confidentiality incomplete. Canonical validator regeneration accounts for most changed-line churn; no unrelated refactor or dependency changes are included.

## Evidence and current status

**Current source head:** 23055baf8b1a6084c63706cd6bc29e14cc0c1a5d. The branch contains normal main merge commits; no force-push or production change.

- At the pre-integration feature head d6382f25, 274 unique targeted relevant tests passed across recorded suites. Core/extensions/UI typechecks, changed-file types, lint (89 core + 3 tooling files), formatting (95 files), and both validator checks passed. These are historical gates, **not** runtime results for the merged head.
- On the integrated source, canonical Gateway/UI validator generation and checks, and production core/extensions/UI typechecks (3/3) passed. The latest incremental merge passed syntax checks for 94 changed files, formatting for its four touched files, and diff integrity checks. Independent scoped source reviews found no unresolved P0–P2 issue in paths reviewed. These static gates are **not** full CI.
- Prior ClawSweeper findings on cron disclosure, opt-in Shared children, and creator access mutation were addressed in source and targeted regressions before integration with main; integrated runtime requalification remains pending.
- On earlier head 1e24780, an isolated notebook pilot with synthetic admin/Alice/Bob and a mock model verified authenticated browser/API visibility 5/2/2, permitted and denied group histories, and a spoofed identity-header negative. [Redacted screenshots and scope limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187836#issuecomment-6635034742). This is historical proof, **not** runtime proof for the current merged head or real staff.

**Pending checks:** Targeted runtime/security assertions on this merged head, changed-test typecheck, type-aware lint, and full local build have not completed. Local attempts were stopped by the host execution memory guard, not by failed assertions; none are counted as passes. Upstream PR CI was skipped while Draft. prs.title: fix(gmail): keep watcher tokens out of process arguments [AI]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Starting the Gmail watcher currently puts its push token and OpenClaw hook token in the Gog child process arguments, where other local users may be able to read them.

## User Impact

A Gog build supporting both environment-source flags receives these tokens through its child-only environment automatically. Older Gog requires a default-No, one-run foreground confirmation or explicit `hooks.gmail.allowInsecureTokenArgs: true`; that exception still exposes both tokens in process arguments. The Gateway never prompts. Failed or inconclusive compatibility checks stop Gmail startup without falling back.

This depends on [Gog PR #1292](https://github.com/openclaw/gogcli/pull/1292), which adds `--token-env` and `--hook-token-env`. Verify availability in the installed Gog build before deployment; no supporting release version is assumed. Dependency release availability remains a prerequisite for landing/shipping. Restart the watcher after upgrading Gog, and rotate previously exposed tokens. Existing token overrides on the parent CLI and the separate gcloud setup command remain outside this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared watcher service selects the credential transport before watch registration or Tailscale setup, so foreground and Gateway-managed starts follow the same policy. Supporting Gog always uses environment sources, including when legacy permission is enabled. Serve usage/configuration failures stop Gmail serving and renewal without downgrading the transport; foreground fatal failures terminate after cleanup. Configuration help, warnings, audit coverage, and lifecycle regressions accompany the change.

## Evidence

Implementation validation retained for commit `d03cab71aed295473500d6b878a26d50e097fc3a`; source and evidence hashes verified during PR preparation:

- 312 tests across 13 focused and sibling suites passed, with final affected-file reruns of 22 foreground tests and 112 Gateway reload tests.
- The process integration regression failed on the base and passed after the change, checking child credential receipt and absence from child arguments.
- Core and affected test typechecks, targeted lint/format checks, documentation/config metadata checks, and the full build passed.
- `pnpm check:env-var-count` remains red because the budget grows from 459 to 461 for the two child credential names; measured usage matches 461. This is a review gate, not a passing check.

Cross-user process inspection with actual Gog and isolated OpenClaw hook authentication, CI, and independent review are pending. Test fixtures and source checks do not establish that end-to-end proof.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep catalog and stale-chunk recovery windows on monotonic time
prs.body:
Precedent: #192700

## What problem this solves

#192700 moved process-local chat-history recovery windows onto monotonic time so host wall-clock adjustments cannot prematurely end them. Two Control UI recovery paths were left on wall time and still suffer the same failure: the Talk catalog warming retry window (`requestTalkCatalog`) and the stale-chunk reachability wait (`waitForReachableControlUiDocument`). A forward wall-clock step (NTP correction, manual clock set, tab-suspended device waking with the clock advanced) shortens both deadlines, so recovery is abandoned before its elapsed-time budget expires: Talk catalog warming stops retrying after one `UNAVAILABLE`, and stale-chunk recovery stops probing the gateway, leaving the user on a broken document that a reload would have fixed.

## Why this change was made

Both windows are process-local: they compare a deadline against the current time within one execution, never across restarts, and never persist the deadline. `Date.now()` is the wrong clock for them — only `performance.now()` is guaranteed to advance at a constant rate. The shared `monotonic-time.ts` owner already exposes `monotonicDeadlineAfter` / `remainingMonotonicMs`, the same helpers #192700 landed for the chat-history windows.

`behavior-completing`: extends the already-approved monotonic-recovery shape (merged as #192700) to the two remaining Control UI recovery windows that share it.

## User impact

- A host clock step during a Talk catalog warm-up no longer abandons the catalog retry; the conversation still becomes available once the gateway finishes warming.
- A host clock step during stale-chunk recovery no longer stops probing the gateway; the Control UI still reloads to the fresh build instead of leaving a broken document behind.
- No persisted data, configuration, protocol, or public contract changes. Epoch timestamps and user-facing dates are unchanged.

## Evidence

**Remote red/green (10.54.159.54, docker node 24.22.1, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run`).**

Base = `origin/main` (`6e24d6fa240`); candidate = this branch (`fce496eeedb`). Same tree, only the two production files differ.

| File | Base (Date.now) | Candidate (monotonic) |
|---|---|---|
| `ui/src/api/gateway-talk-catalog.node.test.ts` | **1 red** (`keeps retrying warming while a host clock step advances`), 11 green | 12 green |
| `ui/src/app/stale-chunk-reload.test.ts` | **2 red** (`keeps probing when a host clock step advances during recovery`, `keeps probing past a wall-clock step before the wait deadline`), 48 green | 50 green |

The three red tests each step the wall clock forward (`vi.setSystemTime(Date.now() + 120_000)`) inside the recovery window and assert the retry/probe continues. On `Date.now` they fail because the deadline advances with the clock and recovery is abandoned early; with the fix they pass because `performance.now()` is unaffected.

Discriminant tests are committed with the fix; red on base, green with the change.

**Formatting:** `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` passes.

## Not tested

- No real Chromium/Gateway e2e was run for these two paths. #192700 already established the same mechanism end-to-end with a built Control UI and real Gateway (its #192529 evidence: a browser-local +120 s `Date.now` step abandons chat-history/subscription recovery after one request on main, retries to completion on the fix). These two windows are the same shape at different call sites; the discriminant unit tests prove the per-site behavior.

## Risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous wall-time window behavior. Blast radius is limited to the Talk catalog warming retry loop and the stale-chunk reachability probe — both best-effort recovery paths that already tolerate early abandonment (they degrade to a failed request / a manual Retry), so the change only makes the existing recovery complete when the clock steps.

prs.title: feat(plugins): force reloads without stranding active conversations
prs.body:
Requested by @jacobtomlinson.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jacobtomlinson](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/85b7d33e-fd16-4ea2-85ee-46951f9ab0e2)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/7f95fa70-c4ab-4275-9766-c09eae3e53c1)

## What Problem This Solves

Waiting for a plugin reload from an agent turn can deadlock on that same turn's retained runtime, requiring fragile detached-exec and manual wake-up choreography.

## User Impact

Developers can use `openclaw plugins reload <id> --force --wait --accept-capabilities --json` to interrupt supported blocking native runs, reload safely, and automatically continue their conversations. The Gateway owns the durable operation independently of the calling exec or socket; `--operation-id` lets a later CLI invocation observe the same operation without submitting another reload.

Existing reload behavior without `--force` is unchanged. Forced continuation is limited to supported native conversations with durable input custody; other runtime owners follow the documented refusal or safe-drain behavior. Force never permits unloading code underneath live plugin work.

## Why This Change Was Made

A persisted operation and continuation journal bridges interruption, normal cleanup, reload publication or recovery, and fresh session admission. Queue ownership survives restart, aliases/shared physical stores, and stale concurrent journal writers. Continuations retain prior tool results, respect current destination authority and explicit Stop, and do not replay completed external actions. The operation has a bounded ten-minute drain; disconnecting a forced-reload observer does not cancel an accepted operation.

## Evidence

- Isolated native exec and code-mode-to-exec flows both loaded edited plugin version 2 and automatically continued the same conversation. Each completed external append occurred once, with three model requests.
- Initial regression suite: 155 passing tests across 13 files. Targeted recovery, physical-store custody, stale-writer and late-transfer regressions were observed red before their fixes and green afterward; latest owning consumer run: 34 passing tests across five files.
- Lifecycle-mapping extraction: 32 passing plan tests; staged line-cap checks passed.
- Core and affected test types, targeted production/test lint, formatting, validator generation and runtime build passed. Documentation validation checked 1,404 files with zero issues; glossary check passed.
- Independent local source review and renewed owning-delta reviews completed with zero P0/P1 findings on the final 56-file staged candidate. All reported recovery-custody defects were fixed and covered by regression tests.

Known validation limits: one broader readiness test observed this host's egress-proxy HTTP 502 instead of connection refusal; a direct-loopback diagnostic passed, and the original test was restored without relaxing assertions. The complete live multi-session/crash/reset matrix and a raw-cleanup-delay-specific live qualification were not run. Broad PR CI remains separate from these focused checks.

## Worked on by

- @jacobtomlinson

prs.title: fix(plugins): plugins pack prints only "The CLI command failed." when it refuses to pack
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw plugins pack` prints only "The CLI command failed. For help, run `openclaw doctor`." whenever it refuses to produce an artifact: the root has no `openclaw.plugin.json`, validation fails, package metadata is missing, the `--out` file already exists, or `--root` doesn't exist. Authors can't tell what to fix.

## User Impact

User impact: the command now prints the reason, for example `plugin manifest not found: <root>/openclaw.plugin.json` or `Refusing to overwrite existing plugin artifact: <path>. Pass a new --out path.` Existing artifacts are still never overwritten, exit codes are unchanged, and a successful pack is unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

`packFeaturePlugin` threw plain `Error` for each refusal, and the exclusive `wx` write and the root `realpath` surfaced raw `EEXIST`/`ENOENT`, all of which the root failure renderer replaces with the generic line. The refusals now use the existing `throwExpectedCliError` helper; `EEXIST` on the output and `ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR` on the root are mapped to explicit messages, and other filesystem errors still propagate. The existing messages are unchanged.

## Evidence

Built from `main` at b01845283f on Linux, Node 24.22.2, fresh state directory. `<draft-review>` is a feature plugin from `openclaw plugins init draft-review --type feature`, compiled and built (paths shortened).

Before:
```
$ openclaw plugins pack --root <draft-review> --out <draft-review>/review.tgz   # review.tgz already exists
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
$ openclaw plugins pack --root <dir with only package.json>
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
$ openclaw plugins pack --root <missing dir>
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
```

After:
```
$ openclaw plugins pack --root <draft-review> --out <draft-review>/review.tgz
Refusing to overwrite existing plugin artifact: <draft-review>/review.tgz. Pass a new --out path.
$ openclaw plugins pack --root <dir with only package.json>
plugin manifest not found: <dir>/openclaw.plugin.json
$ openclaw plugins pack --root <missing dir>
Plugin root not found: <missing dir>
```
All exit 1, as before; the existing `review.tgz` is unchanged.

Tests:
- `pnpm test src/cli/plugins-feature-artifact.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: passes (18 native subtests, 0 failed).
- New subtest "explains why a missing root or a directory without a plugin manifest cannot be packed", and the existing never-overwrite subtest now checks for `ExpectedCliError` with the message instead of a raw `EEXIST`. Both fail on `main` and pass with the fix.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on both files: clean.


- Test-line budget: the regression tests add 28 net lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/plugins-pack-reason.txt`. Rebased on current `main`.
