prs.title: improve(ci): speed up transform cache key preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

CI spends time inspecting unrelated source files while preparing the Vitest transform cache key. A completed [Node test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41942039134/job/126965975934) spent 2.055 seconds in that step.

## User Impact

Developers should get the same cached transforms with less setup work. This changes CI preparation only; there is no product behavior, cache namespace, dependency, or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing setup action now walks directory entries and hashes only the existing transform inputs. It avoids a separate status lookup for every unrelated file and skips only already-excluded subtrees. Both cache readers and the protected warmer still use the same action and generation.

The action-level fixture replaces two pattern simulations while retaining their inclusion, harness exclusion, and invalidation contracts. It also covers empty input, matching-directory descendants, file aliases, directory links, and a selected broken link.

## Evidence

- Untimed comparison against the [observed runner 2.338.2 bundle](https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/v2.338.2/src/Misc/layoutbin/hashFiles/index.js) matches ordered membership, digests, and selected broken-link failure in synthetic fixtures.
- Complete frozen source at `64402fd6bdda4db11b891cd92c9baeebfbdfe137`: both hash the same 676 files, producing `57486074bf763ca206244bd7d0f432028f5179bc77a0d74ab753e9f321d1e3b6`. Baseline: 66,281 `lstat`, 677 `statSync`, 2,294 directory reads, 676 file streams. Candidate: 2,294 Dirent reads, 676 file reads, zero path status calls. Local Node 26/macOS; these are work counts, not a timing result.
- Independent source review: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Local ClawSweeper reviewed `64402fd6bdda4db11b891cd92c9baeebfbdfe137..219f7cff9d480c48aa10a333d95de589e329650d` and found one P2: declare the new shell-launched helper as an exact executable root. Fixed alongside the existing setup helpers in `config/knip.config.ts`; final local ClawSweeper review completed for `64402fd6bdda4db11b891cd92c9baeebfbdfe137..3b5199e8373e9f1697cb1574470c988a92925e15`: no findings, patch correct (0.84 correctness confidence; medium decision confidence). Runtime tests and timing were outside that review. No ignore or baseline exception was added. The unused-file audit remains pending.
- `git diff --check`, JavaScript/Python syntax, matching pinned oxfmt checks pass. Source checkout has no qualified workspace dependencies. Both task-owned Blacksmith Testbox allocations queued and were stopped (the second followed a fresh empty live inventory), so focused tests, targeted typecheck/lint, workflow checks and Linux timing remain pending. This draft uses the repository's documented CI-proof route; it must not merge with those gaps. The [first manual dispatch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41947896863) stopped in manifest creation because `validation_tier=main` requires matching workflow/source revisions; no functional tests ran. The corrected [exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41948730956) was admitted by native `scripts/pr ci-dispatch 193107` for `3b5199e8373e9f1697cb1574470c988a92925e15`; preflight passed and functional checks are running.

### Performance acceptance rule — published before timing

Run the committed workload on Linux with Node 24 and the SHA-256-verified runner 2.338.2 bundle:

```sh
python3 scripts/perf/ci-transform-fingerprint-measure.py \
  --runner-bundle /tmp/runner-v2.338.2-hashFiles.cjs \
  --node node --samples 5 --output /tmp/transform-fingerprint-result.json
```

The workload exports committed source before dependency restoration, with no hydrated `node_modules` or Git metadata; both arms use identical files. One excluded warm-up per arm, then five serial AB pairs, fresh Node processes and a warm filesystem. Record raw wall time, CPU, peak RSS, load, actual CPUs/affinity, RAM and cgroup limits; report median, p95 and range separately for each arm. Every pair must produce the identical generation.

Accept only at least 5% lower median fingerprint wall time with wall p95, CPU and peak RSS holding or improving. Keep cache membership, file ordering, symlink behavior and input failures unchanged. Reject or revert if the rule fails. Profile separately from timing. This proves the fingerprint workload, not overall workflow duration, queue delay, or billing savings.

Focused proof: `pnpm test test/scripts/setup-node-env-transform-cache.test.ts test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, targeted tooling-test typecheck/lint and `pnpm check:workflows`. Record changed-file wall/test time. Net test-line count decreases; no allocation or baseline increase is requested.

prs.title: feat(ci): skip qualified unchanged Markdown tests
prs.body:
Related: #191191

## What Problem This Solves

A small Markdown source edit currently schedules every test in its directory, including tests whose complete reviewed inputs have not changed.

## User Impact

Eligible canonical pull requests now skip unchanged qualified Markdown tests. A frontmatter-only edit selects 33 files instead of 42, omitting nine Markdown files (149 test cases). Scheduled/main/release coverage stays unchanged. No runtime product behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Filter only the existing conventional-directory fallback using reviewed source/test and shared configuration fingerprints. Changed, missing, symlinked, or unqualified inputs keep their tests. Explicit owners, import consumers, policy checks, and smoke selection remain independent. The stateful table suite is deliberately unqualified.

The pilot is deliberately narrow: current canonical aggressive PRs containing only flat Markdown source changes. `OPENCLAW_CI_NODE_SELECTION=full` is the existing rollback. Qualification expires conservatively when shared inputs change; refresh requires reviewing and rerunning full/selected proof. This does not enable historical/model-driven skipping. Shared-process equivalence is backed by the bounded experiment below, not a general guarantee for unrelated suites.

## Evidence

- Native planner/manifest validation: 705 tests passed, including six new fingerprint/fallback tests (805 ms test time). The existing manifest suite took approximately 385 s; the new tests do not add that suite cost.
- Real CI manifest: eligible PR emits 33 files and exactly nine omissions; rollback emits 2,945 files with no pilot omissions; release gate emits the prior 42 with no pilot omissions.
- Real repository wrappers, Node and pinned Bun: full Markdown family 196 tests / 11 files passed; selected family 47 tests / 2 files passed. Single paired local wrapper samples: Node 5.384 → 3.392 s; Bun 4.668 → 2.975 s. These are local measurements, not hosted CI savings.
- Injected real frontmatter regression (empty parsed metadata): full and selected execution both caught the same six failures under both runtimes. Original source restored byte-for-byte.
- Targeted tooling/scripts typechecks, lint, final formatting and frozen-base test-line budget passed (607 lines slack). Production Knip scan passed with zero entries. The six new tests also passed on Node at the final head (769 ms test time, 4.15 s wrapper). The final commit only formats three files.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed the complete implementation range and found no actionable correctness/security issue. The final delta only formats three files.

The 85-line test allocation covers the new independent filesystem/fingerprint and fallback contracts; no shared baseline is raised.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep background work visible while chat waits
prs.body:
Related: #182684

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the missing work signal when a chat is waiting on subagents or still has task-owned background commands running.

## User Impact

The existing compact footer keeps its claw, elapsed time, and separate subagent/command counts visible, including in bubble mode. Counts open the existing Subagents and Processes panels. Detached services do not keep an idle conversation looking busy, and unavailable command observations are labeled rather than presented as zero.

## Why This Change Was Made

Implements the selected minimal-footer design without restoring the removed delegation tracker or per-worker narration. Command classification comes from the execution owner's retained request ownership, not command-name or output heuristics. The visible conversation shares the existing process observation with the panels.

Counts cover reconnectable background exec processes, not every foreground tool or OS process. Truncated inventories show a lower bound with "+". Older workers lacking ownership metadata remain inspectable in Processes but do not acquire an inferred busy signal. No execution, cancellation, retention, or permission behavior changes.

## Evidence

- Missing-claw regression fails on the original in flat and bubble modes and passes with the fix.
- Producer regression fails on the original and passes with task-owned, explicitly detached, unknown-owner, and terminal command cases.
- 60 focused UI tests and 7 producer tests pass. Production UI and affected chat-test typechecks pass; scoped lint, styles, controller guards, and formatting pass.
- Five browser flows pass, covering subagent waiting/resumption, one and 12 workers, command-only work, detached services, unavailable reads, reconnect, completion, and existing panel navigation. Deterministic Gateway fixtures exercise the actual running Control UI; the producer regression exercises real ownership with external process I/O fixed.

prs.title: fix(gateway): agent.run can carry a fallback ladder so a pinned model no longer dead-ends on a quota 429
prs.body:
Closes #186418
Related: #151980, #141115, #181981

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an automation caller that pins a model on the WebSocket agent.run request loses the agent's configured model-fallback ladder, so a quota-class 429 ends the run instead of advancing to the next candidate.

The request schema had no way to express a chain, so the only lever an automation caller had was to pin a model - which silently suppresses the configured ladder. Operators who configured a working fallback chain for the agent had no caller-side way to keep it alive.

## User Impact

User impact: automation callers can now send an explicit fallback ladder with their agent.run request, so a provider quota window on the pinned model no longer ends the run - the run advances to the next candidate the caller named.

This is opt-in and additive. A request that pins a model and sends no ladder behaves exactly as before: the pin stays strict and the configured chain stays suppressed, which is the contract #151980 asks to keep.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway already had the pieces to carry a run-scoped chain, but the wire protocol could not express one. Rather than relax the strict-pin contract, this change adds an explicit field so the caller states the chain it wants:

- agent.run accepts an optional fallbacks array of provider/model refs. Entries are trimmed, de-duplicated, and bounded to 16.
- The ladder is authorized exactly like a model override: a caller without the model-override scope is rejected with INVALID_REQUEST and a clear message.
- Every named model is checked against the agent's visible model set and the caller's operator authority before the run starts, so a caller cannot widen model access by naming extra chain entries.
- The chain travels with the run as a request-scoped override, so it is used for this run only and does not become session state.

The request-level pin remains the primary model; the ladder only adds candidates behind it.

## Evidence

Focused test runs, both green on this branch (rebased onto main at d2491817):

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-request-preflight.test.ts
    -> Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 33 passed (33)

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts
    -> Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 44 passed (44)

Typecheck:

    pnpm tsgo:test:root -> exit 0 (all root shards)
    pnpm tsgo:test:packages -> exit 0

New coverage:

- src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-request-preflight.test.ts - a request that carries both a pinned model and a ladder keeps the ladder and reports it as request-scoped; a request with a ladder but no model-override scope is rejected; a request with no ladder leaves the override unset.
- src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts - a request-supplied ladder survives a pinned model during model selection, and a request-supplied chain that names a model the agent cannot use is rejected before the run starts.

Behavior with no fallbacks in the request is unchanged, so existing agent.run callers are unaffected.

prs.title: fix(codex): clarify executable launch failures
prs.body:
Closes #191912
Related: #177742
Related: #181037

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a misleading catalog-updater diagnosis when a Codex executable cannot be launched for an agent turn.

## User Impact

Users see `Codex cannot run` with the executable and specific failure reason, rather than an assertion that the catalog updater failed. This only corrects the diagnostic: the executable or working-directory problem still needs repair, and the underlying launch failures reported in the related issues are not fixed here.

## Why This Change Was Made

prs.title: docs: minimize downtime between full release validation cycles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release owners waste validation wall time by waiting for diagnostics to finish before repairing failures, serializing optional local checks ahead of remote validation, or restarting with another known deterministic failure still unfixed.

## User Impact

Release operators get explicit guidance to prioritize time to the next passing Full Release Validation (FRV), with fixes ready by diagnostic-drain completion whenever possible. No runtime or workflow implementation changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Start remote FRV promptly after required preflight and known non-flake repairs; overlap useful local proof instead of putting redundant checks on the critical path.
- Diagnose and repair failures as they arrive, including focused proof, review, and required landings/backports while other diagnostics drain.
- Fix **every known non-flake failure affecting the next run** before dispatch. Never knowingly spend a full cycle fixing one failure while carrying another forward.
- Use bounded, targeted retries strategically and retain valid green evidence. Preserve candidate identity, mandatory gates, release scope, and cancellation/settlement rules.

This is scheduling guidance, not a new checklist, approval step, or demand for certainty before dispatch. Being ready by drain completion is an overlap goal, not a deadline. The known-failure rule does not require ruling out undiscovered failures or resolving unrelated issues.

The CI skill owns the detailed loop; maintainer and owner guidance link to it. Validation guidance now permits useful local diagnosis before a remote failure, without delaying dispatch for optional confidence.

## Evidence

- Documentation-only: four files; full diff reviewed and simplified.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- All four new policy links verified against existing files and heading anchors.
- Commit hook formatting passed for all four files using the checkout-pinned formatter after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in the isolated worktree.
- No release workflows dispatched; no production or test changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use workspace-relative `.cache/` roots for both restore and save, and configure each runtime with the corresponding absolute workspace path. Bump only those two archive namespaces so older host-dependent archives are not selected. Existing generation invalidation, worker isolation, and warmer ownership remain intact.

## Evidence

- Real tar/configure reproduction: both original cache archives failed to restore across different workspace depths; both corrected archives restored their bytes and configured environment successfully.
- Regression executes the shipped configuration scripts and real tar save/restore for both cache families. The existing generation-retention cases remain.
- `git diff --check` passed. The 56-line test allocation covers the cross-layout regression.

Dependency-backed tests, full changed-file runtime measurement, format, type/lint, and workflow validation are pending native PR qualification; the source worktree is code-only.
- This fixes the observed cache extraction failure. It does not claim to resolve the separate Git capability, installer, service, or Gateway failures, and no replacement live run has been started.

prs.title: feat(knowledge): warn in doctor when the saving model's output limit is low
prs.body:
## Summary

Knowledge scribes save with each agent's default model, and one save can write several full pages in a single reply. A custom provider model without `maxTokens` gets the 8,192-token output default, so long saves get cut off quietly.

This adds a Knowledge Doctor check, `knowledge/model-output-limit`. It warns when an agent's default model allows fewer than 65,536 output tokens, and names the exact setting to raise.

## High Level TLDR

- Knowledge ships `doctor-health-api.ts`, using the same bundled health bridge as Skill Workshop.
- Core registers it only while Knowledge holds the memory slot, and passes in a small resolver, `resolveAgentModelOutputLimit`. The effective limit is the lower of the model ceiling (config defaults: model, then provider, then catalog, then 8192) and any request budget from agent or model `params` (any `maxTokens` alias), since transports clamp a larger budget to the ceiling. The finding points at the setting that actually caps that agent.
- Catalog-only models are skipped, because their limit is not ours to judge. The check also stays quiet when Knowledge `writesEnabled` is `false`.
- The warning is grouped per model, not per agent. Category `fix-now` so plain `openclaw doctor` lists it (wired via `doctor:knowledge-model-output-limit`); report only, no repair.
- The core `isMemoryCoreActive` gate is generalized to `isMemorySlotPluginActive(cfg, pluginId)`, so Knowledge reuses it. The memory-core behavior is unchanged.
- Docs: one Limits bullet in `docs/plugins/knowledge/scribes.md`.

Example finding:

> Knowledge saves with local/small, which can write only 8192 tokens per reply. Long saves can get cut off.
> Fix: Set models.providers.local.maxTokens (or that model's maxTokens) to 65536 or more, if the model supports it.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/doctor-model-output-limit.test.ts extensions/knowledge/doctor-health-api.test.ts`: 9/9 pass, including a plain-doctor rendering test.
- `pnpm check:changed`: pass.
- Autoreview (codex gpt-6-luna, P0-P2): scoped-clean.
- Test-lines allocation: `config/test-lines-allocations/knowledge-output-limit-doctor.txt` (+74).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI table-copy regression test added in #192752 asserts the success feedback label is `Copied!`, but every copy control in the product reports `common.copied` = `"Copied"` (no exclamation mark). The test is therefore red on current main, failing `checks-ui (2/3)` for every UI PR based on main — currently blocking #193070 and #193067 (an unrelated PR fails identically).

## User Impact

User impact: no user-visible change. This is a test-only correction — the product behavior already matches the fixed expectation; the PR aligns the test assertion with the shipped `Copied` copy label so the CI gate stops failing.

## Why This Change Was Made

`Copied!` exists nowhere in the production code:

- `ui/src/components/markdown-tables.ts:373,378` set the success `aria-label` from `t(copied ? "common.copied" : "common.copyFailed")`.
- `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts:421` defines `copied: "Copied"`.
- All other copy controls (code blocks, sidebar, link reader, browser panel, file tooltip, mermaid) use the same `common.copied` key.
- `git grep "Copied!" origin/main` matches only `ui/src/components/markdown-tables.test.ts:130`.

The fix changes the test expectation from `Copied!` to `Copied` (one line). Production behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

Red on main, green with the fix, via the real vitest entry point on the remote tree (docker, node v24.22.1, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/components/markdown-tables.test.ts`):

prs.title: feat: follow active goals with Claude Code
prs.body:
Related: #192988. Depends on #193024.

## What Problem This Solves

Active OpenClaw Goals do not drive Claude Code's native pursuit loop, and a real Goal-tool terminal verdict must stop that loop without discarding the current answer.

## User Impact

An admitted Claude turn can pursue its active Goal natively while Stop, Pause, objective edits and revoked execution authority retain control. A committed complete/blocked tool verdict preserves the final reply and prevents another pursuit iteration.

This draft is not live-qualified or ready to merge. It requires Claude Code 2.1.318 or newer; exact token budgets and unrepresentable or mismatched native objectives are rejected explicitly. Durable restart recovery and Codex autonomous pursuit are separate follow-ups.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing execution owner lends a versioned Goal capability to the Claude plugin. Real managed tool calls use that same terminal transaction. Claude's native Stop callback reads the committed verdict at the transport write boundary; normal final-response and process cleanup still finish before status reconciliation.

The generic capability ships with its first working consumer. No timer, second continuation queue or provider-specific policy is added to core. The owner and its consumer stay together because splitting them would leave an unused or incomplete interface.

This branch includes the unchanged prerequisite commit from #193024. GitHub does not support native stacks across forks; [the stage-only comparison](https://github.com/GoatInAHat/openclaw/compare/e36a626b668bc1ced850f14a8b0a5c4e03d36f83...c0286528d78be1de21d309ae45203a31f81bbcde) isolates these changes. The prerequisite can be removed from the upstream diff after it lands.

## Evidence

- Real managed HTTP MCP transaction and owned stdio fixture: 13/13 cases pass. Complete/blocked successor-effect regressions fail on the pre-repair production files (one extra effect versus zero expected) and pass with the repair.
- Affected native runtime, host capability, CLI policy/steering, Goal tools and session publication consumers: 278/278 tests pass across 13 files. Ordinary no-Goal Claude execution remains a sibling control.
- Independent Codex source review covered the selective stage and terminal-Stop repair. Its production finding and two invalid fixture transitions were corrected; no actionable findings remain in that reviewed snapshot. The subsequent mechanical prompt-response extraction into the existing input helper preserves statement order and cancellation guards and has dedicated affected-check reruns. The installed native Stop contract was independently inspected, not inferred from the fixture.
- Scoped formatting, SDK export and plugin-boundary checks, changed MDX documents, and the exact test-line ratchet pass. The separate allocation is 980 net regression lines against the prerequisite, covering native transport, real MCP terminal/cancellation and independent host ownership. The shared scalar and prerequisite's 338-line allocation are unchanged.
- Published handoff behavior remains green: 102/102 tests across four inherited suites. In total, 393 tests pass across 18 files, with affected tests rerun after the final mechanical prompt-helper extraction. All six owning production/test type projects pass. The extraction also preserves the runtime line budget without a suppression.
- Scoped type-aware lint passes for 14 core/registration files, nine plugin files and the managed-MCP integration test. Exact head: `c0286528d78be1de21d309ae45203a31f81bbcde`.

Live vendor MCP transport, real native inference/Stop evaluation, final response and external cancellation still require the isolated authenticated Gateway run. Synthetic subprocess results and native-source inspection are not presented as that live proof. A full distribution build has not been run for this stage.

`automations list --query` already finds an automation across NFC/NFD spellings, but `automations show` cannot open the same result by its equivalent name. When equivalent names coexist, detail lookup can omit a matching choice and return an arbitrary-looking unique result.

prs.title: fix(cli): escape trajectory export summary values
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A valid trajectory export directory containing a newline, ANSI escape or other terminal control is printed verbatim in the success summary. The report can gain forged lines or clear/hide terminal text even though the bundle was exported correctly.

## User Impact

Human-readable export reports display paths safely. Actual directory names, exported transcript contents and decoded JSON paths retain their original bytes; normal report layout stays readable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing terminalText formatter at the complete CLI summary boundary, as adjacent session CLI owners do. JSON returns before this presentation step, and the slash-command chat response has a different nonterminal renderer. No custom sanitizer or file-path normalization is introduced.

No new configuration/default, protocol, permission, schema, dependency or migration. No generated changelog change.

## Evidence

### Current verification — November 4, 2026

Exact source/build head: `1421339200fc85c93eb4777cfbd501aa4edbe889`. Normal merge of upstream `258d034391ac03a8ee3530ba33552a5cbf2062fc`; reviewed production and regression files are byte-identical to the previous PR head. The unrelated toast mock-export and shared test-budget repairs come from upstream; this PR retains only its own exact test allocation relative to that main. No shared baseline adjustment was authored here.

- 17/17 focused tests pass, plus scoped source types, typed lint, formatting, whitespace and test-line/mock-export/timeout-race ratchets. Effective budget retains42lines of inherited main slack.
- Exact-head sourcePerformance build passes. The unchanged native driver passes: The real PTY summary contains no injected terminal controls; the on-disk manifest/events and JSON retain the original path bytes. Ordinary export and traversal-refusal controls pass.
- Author simplify/test-value audit complete; no independent model review is claimed. Hosted CI for this new head is reported separately; local proof does not claim a hosted pass.

Commands: `bash maintenance-validate-20261104.sh trajectory` runs the same explicit test files documented below; `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts sourcePerformance`; `node refill-three-trajectory-native-20261103.mjs <built-checkout> green <receipt.json>`.

      assert(reportText.includes('📦 Bundle: .openclaw/trajectory-exports/' + expectedDisplay + '\n'));
      assert.equal(reportText.includes('\u0007') || reportText.includes('\u001b[2J') || reportText.includes('\u0085') || reportText.includes('\u202e'), label === 'control-human' && expectation === 'red');

  }
  const refused = cli('escape-control', [...base, '--output', '../../../outside', '--json']);
  assert.equal(refused.code, 1); assert.equal(JSON.parse(refused.stdout).ok, false); assert(!fs.existsSync(path.join(root, 'outside')));
  assert.equal(fs.readFileSync(configPath, 'utf8'), config);
  report.configUnchanged = true; report.status = expectation === 'red' ? 'PASS_RED' : 'PASS_GREEN';
} catch (error) { report.status = 'FAIL'; report.error = String(error.stack ?? error); process.exitCode = 1; }
finally {
  socket?.close(); for (const handler of pending.values()) handler.reject(new Error('proof stopped'));
  if (gateway.exitCode === null && gateway.signalCode === null) { try { process.kill(-gateway.pid, 'SIGTERM'); } catch {} const deadline = performance.now() + 5000; while (gateway.exitCode === null && gateway.signalCode === null && performance.now() < deadline) await pause(); if (gateway.exitCode === null && gateway.signalCode === null) { try { process.kill(-gateway.pid, 'SIGKILL'); } catch {} await once(gateway, 'exit'); } }

prs.title: fix(sandbox): resolve literal remote-shell file paths without trimming
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `RemoteShellSandboxFsBridge.resolveTarget` trimmed the tool-supplied `filePath` (`.trim()`), so a literal file whose name starts or ends with whitespace (e.g. `" x.txt"`) was silently resolved as its trimmed sibling `x.txt`. A sandboxed agent reading or writing `" x.txt"` touched the decoy file instead of the one the model chose.
- Solution: Use the caller's literal `filePath` in `resolveTarget` instead of trimming it. Containment guards operate on the literal-resolved path, so safety is unchanged.
- What changed: `src/agents/sandbox/remote-fs-bridge.ts` (removed the `filePath.trim()` in `resolveTarget`), plus a regression test in `src/agents/sandbox/remote-fs-bridge.test.ts` (Linux-only GNU shell lane, per the platform separation in #131339) and a test-line allocation in `config/test-lines-allocations/remote-shell-literal-path-192041.txt`.
- What did NOT change: No changes to mount resolution, containment guards, read/write semantics, or the local sandbox bridge. No other components were affected.

Fixes #192041

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A file whose name starts with whitespace is a distinct filesystem entry from its trimmed sibling. Before this fix, the remote-shell bridge addressed the trimmed sibling, so literal paths were unreachable and writes could clobber the wrong file.
- **Real environment tested:** `/home/0668000889/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/issue-192041` with vitest, exercising the real `RemoteShellSandboxFsBridge` through the local remote-shell script runner (the same harness the suite uses for all remote-fs operations).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/sandbox/remote-fs-bridge.test.ts -t "literal whitespace"
  ```
- **Evidence after fix (current head d904f8fb):** The regression test passes: `readFile({ filePath: " x.txt" })` returns `Buffer.from("literal bytes")` (not the decoy `x.txt`), `readFile({ filePath: "x.txt" })` returns the decoy bytes, and `writeFile({ filePath: " y.txt", data: "literal write" })` creates `" y.txt"` while leaving `y.txt` intact. Focused test: 1 passed.
- **Behavior proof on base vs head (A/B):** The same regression test was run against the base source (`origin/main` still trimming, `const input = params.filePath.trim()`). On base it FAILS with the defect visible: `readFile({ filePath: " x.txt" })` resolves to the decoy `x.txt` (`Buffer[100,101,99,111,121,...]` = "decoy bytes" instead of "literal bytes"). On head (this PR) the identical test PASSES. This directly demonstrates the regression failing on base and passing on head through the real bridge.
- **Observed result after fix:** Literal whitespace-prefixed file names are now resolved as their own entries, matching how the runtime skill catalog and other literal-path fixes (#187554, #187777, #187766) treat them.
- **What was not tested:** A live remote SSH host was not exercised; the suite's local remote-shell script runner executes the same bridge scripts, and the 4 failures in this file are pre-existing local-environment guards failures (confirmed identical on pristine main).

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: `src/agents/sandbox/remote-fs-bridge.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: Reading and writing a file whose name starts with a space resolves the literal entry, not its trimmed sibling; the sibling remains untouched.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: It pins the exact defect (trimmed path addressing the sibling) through the production bridge for both read and write paths.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: `resolveTarget` in `src/agents/sandbox/remote-fs-bridge.ts` applied `.trim()` to the caller's `filePath`, so whitespace-prefixed/suffixed file names could not be addressed and always resolved to their trimmed sibling.
- Missing detection / guardrail: The bridge did not preserve the literal path supplied by the tool, unlike the local bridge and the already-merged literal-path fixes for extraDirs/OpenShell mirror/mxc.

## Review follow-up (d904f8fb)

- The regression test now lives inside the existing Linux-only GNU-shell `describe` block (per the deliberate platform separation established in #131339), so it cannot fail on Windows or stock macOS where GNU `readlink`/`stat` options are unavailable.
- Added `config/test-lines-allocations/remote-shell-literal-path-192041.txt` (18 lines) covering the regression's test-line growth so the shared test-lines baseline stays unchanged.
- A/B behavior proof above: regression fails on base (trim), passes on head (literal).

prs.title: fix(agents): preserve bounded operator authority across restart continuations
prs.body:
## Summary

Preserve bounded operator authority through principal-based ingress, Gateway restart recovery, and scheduled continuations without treating a system turn as a new human owner input.

## Problem

A valid live principal could lack durable recovery custody. A resumed task could then create a source-less continuation, and protected tools would later deny an operation that was originally authorized. A separate model-facing owner-tool gate also ignored a restored live admin grant. Temporary recovery-owner/store outages could terminally disable a one-shot before execution.

## Changes

- Add an optional ingress-owner recovery hook and an explicit principal source. The bundled MCP relay reconstructs the exact original audience and grant issuance from canonical RelayState.
- Preserve recorded original custody only for actual restart admission, intersecting original/current scope and model restrictions while checking both original consent/access and current principal authority.
- Keep transient source-restoration outages on the existing typed, pre-execution retry path for the same one-shot job.
- Project current admitted admin eligibility into control-plane tool admission without changing sender attribution. Preserve taint, policy, live receipt fences, independently scoped sessions/portal/automations, and explicit-owner standing intents.
- Report unsupported durable custody rather than silently implying retained operator capability. Do not upgrade existing source-less jobs or relax automation self-scope.

## Validation

- Real Gateway + real model: active user task, native SIGTERM shutdown, cold process replacement, automatic marked-session recovery with no new human ingress, protected read, and FIRST recurring automation created by the resumed user task.
- The same automation completed its protected read; revoking the exact original grant blocked its next occurrence, with zero successful protected reads after revocation. All isolated services stopped.
- Final assembled owner-tool and prompt-prefix tests: 23 passed.
- Principal/restart/temporary-owner-store/revocation matrix: 10 passed. Ingress composition: 9 passed. Relay/state and affected sibling checks also passed.
- Scoped production/test types, type-aware lint, format, and whitespace checks passed on the qualified source. The exact committed core production typecheck passed again.
- One additional broad changed-check attempt exited 139 in the core-test type graph; scoped affected test graphs had passed, and PR CI must supply broad proof.
- Fresh independent reviews resolved the restart-ordering, transient settlement, and scoped-tool findings. Official local ClawSweeper reviewed committed range 77c263b9fa112ce0e1657f6cbf56016092cd1077..864e6958b67da3410d5714aa051ddc841313de81. Its proposed TS2454 finding is rejected: the awaited return type already includes undefined, and the exact-head production compiler check passes.

## Scope and risk

The optional SDK hook is an explicit owner-held recovery contract, not a fabricated handshake or a new authorization owner. Identity, role/model, exact ingress issuance, and Gateway access-grant owners retain their checks. The native SIGTERM/cold-start route was qualified; restart-RPC/service-manager admission, external UI consent, and a deployed Team ingress were not exercised. This PR does not deploy or change live permissions.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): reuse restored workspace input admission
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Restored sandbox workspaces rebuild their admitted path inventory on the Gateway main thread after command finalization and filesystem mutations, although restoration has already persisted those inputs.

## User Impact

Workspace checkpoints avoid redundant main-thread Git enumeration and allocation. Host-index authority, admitted untracked paths, archived inputs, and ignore-rule boundaries remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restoration remains the owner of archive input admission. Checkpoints consume its persisted admission through the existing worker scan. The remaining inventory preparation passes decoded admission forward and avoids intermediate collections. The existing linear ancestor expansion is unchanged. No cross-operation cache, config, or schema change.

## Evidence

Predeclared measurement rule: use 62,000 real synthetic indexed files (1.143 GB logical sparse contents), compare frozen parent and candidate owner implementations in five interleaved pairs, plus A/A controls, separate uninstrumented CPU/wall and collected-object allocation passes. Record first calls separately from warm calls, compare output digests and retention writes. A win removes the restored checkpoint's entire main-thread preparation and lowers remaining per-call CPU/allocation without a material regression beyond control spread. This owner does not access agent databases; no database-scale, btrfs, full-Gateway latency, or production measurement claim.

Measured warm owner costs (median of five process samples, ten calls per sample):

| 62,000-file fixture / operation | Main-thread CPU before → after | V8 allocation before → after | Wall before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2,000 build-cache inputs / live | 36.17 → 30.07 ms | 49.14 → 42.19 MB | 46.83 → 40.35 ms |
| 2,000 build-cache inputs / snapshot | 46.20 → 41.75 ms | 65.34 → 56.14 MB | 111.76 → 110.86 ms |
| No build-cache inputs / live | 33.14 → 25.03 ms | 45.95 → 36.12 MB | 43.43 → 35.10 ms |
| No build-cache inputs / snapshot | 41.49 → 33.39 ms | 58.67 → 46.31 MB | 106.75 → 97.74 ms |

These are the remaining initialization/restore/full-inventory calls. A restored command checkpoint now performs **zero main-thread preparations instead of one**, removing its additional `ls-files` and `ls-tree`; the worker still performs its authoritative index selection. Successful unchanged turn preparation remains zero main preparations and two worker probes. Every command finalization checkpoints, even if it made no edits; filesystem mutations also checkpoint. Thus counts depend on tools used, not a fixed per-turn timer.

Separate collected-object sampling confirms live allocation 42.74 → 35.89 MB and snapshot allocation 61.39 → 54.35 MB. A/A sampled controls were 42.689/42.694 MB and 61.560/61.507 MB. Prepared selection is neutral (warm CPU 4.421 → 4.399 ms). An attempted parent-prefix optimization raised prepared CPU about 60% against stable A/A controls and was removed.

Cached live wall ranges were 43.80–47.17 → 38.64–41.50 ms; snapshot ranges were 109.61–139.11 → 106.26–113.70 ms. With five process samples, p95 is the sample maximum, not individual-call tail latency. A first prepared-call sample median moved about +0.5 ms despite identical prepared code; warm and no-cache controls remain neutral. CPU excludes Git children. This is macOS owner-level proof with sparse synthetic file contents, not btrfs or full-Gateway latency evidence.

Reproduce with `node scripts/perf/local-workspace-inventory-measure.ts`: `--prepare <proof> --base-ref 44eaed3d95d734509d4ac4de5b9076183ea76424`, `--fixture <workspace>`, then `--compare <proof> --fixture <workspace>`; repeat with `--control` and separately `--allocation`. Use another fixture with `--cache-files 0` for the no-cache case. The script verifies inventory/admission digests and zero repeated custody writes.

Focused proof: 90 tests passed, two existing skips (opt-in real Podman and filesystem-invalid UTF-8 fixture). Consumer suite: 118.62 s; the extracted archive regression passed again in 3.2 s of test execution. The regression fails on the exact parent because it performs the two redundant main-thread commands, and passes with archived inputs preserved outside the live index and newly generated siblings excluded. The complete scenario moved into the existing retention helper to honor the test-file line cap. Net test growth is 24 lines with a scoped allocation record.

Final Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2. Production delta is +7 lines: explicit insertion/retention loops replace allocating expressions; no cache or additional authority guard is introduced. The full `pnpm check:changed --staged` run completed with one benchmark-only TypeScript error; after repair, the identical scripts typechecker and comparator smoke passed. Every other selected check passed. Exact-head PR CI will gate landing.

prs.title: fix(gateway): scope image capability discovery
prs.body:
## Summary

- scope attachment image-capability fallback to the selected provider instead of rebuilding every provider catalog
- keep runtime-only models by using the existing request-scoped live catalog path
- retry the complete Gateway projection when its published runtime owner is replaced during scoped discovery

## Root cause and owner

Attachment admission first reads the lifecycle-published catalog. When a selected runtime-only model is absent or has provisional text-only metadata, current main falls back to `readOnly: false`, which rebuilds the full cross-provider catalog inside the request. The provider-scoped catalog machinery exists, but this Gateway caller did not use it.

The canonical owner is the Gateway catalog projection. The second read now carries the selected provider into the existing prepared request-scoped live catalog. The projection checks the published owner before and after the asynchronous scoped read and reacquires the full owner on replacement, so catalog, config, agent identity, and auth projection never mix generations.

## ClawSweeper findings

- Early owner replacement: fixed by retrying at the Gateway projection boundary; the regression replaces the owner during scoped discovery and proves only the replacement catalog returns.
- Final provider I/O fence: the old branch tried to turn generation liveness into a public provider-auth revocation contract, but that was incomplete and added a large cross-plugin surface. This port removes that contract. Published-generation liveness governs whether results may publish; it does not retroactively revoke already-started provider requests. Results from a retired generation are discarded and the owner is reacquired.
- Runtime-only models: retained. An independent P1 review caught and rejected an intermediate static-only rewrite; the final branch uses the existing scoped live mode.
- Test-cost evidence: recorded below for the new image-capability file and the combined focused Gateway set.

## Scope

Seven Gateway files changed against integrated main: 222 insertions and 60 deletions. Reuses the existing scoped catalog owner; no provider/plugin implementation changes, new configuration, or cache.

## Validation

- Integrated main: `1f01f4944d45eb265081f8bfbf8d3e8e54ff4266`; resolved conflicts while retaining current static-capability and projection owners.
- Three focused Gateway suites: 86 tests passed (image capability, catalog projection, session utilities).
- Core production typecheck and targeted lint passed; `git diff --check` clean.
- Fresh autoreview against integrated main, P0–P2: no actionable findings in the seven-file candidate diff. Surrounding loader implementations were not included in the isolated reviewer bundle; integration assurance also relies on focused tests and source inspection.
- Previous validation counts and hosted evidence were for the old head and are not current-head proof.
- No new real-channel/live-provider proof was run.
- CI follow-up: the new catalog mock now accepts the loader's optional argument. The affected Gateway-server test-type leaf passed; 16 catalog tests passed. Current head: `8a7567d2df5d`. Replacement exact-head CI is pending, not claimed green.

Agent transcript omitted.

## What

Russian docs localization is wired up but nearly empty: `docs/.i18n/glossary.ru.json` was 21 entries (1.2 KB) against 107 KB for `zh-CN`, and `ru-navigation.json` did not exist at all, so the Russian sidebar fell back to English while the pages themselves were already 75% translated.

This PR fills in the two files that drive the Russian locale:

- `glossary.ru.json`: **21 → 250 entries** (1.2 KB → 18.6 KB). Existing entries and their order are preserved; 6 target terms were corrected for consistency with the pages: Compaction → Сжатие контекста, Gateway → Шлюз, Node → Нода, Plugin → Плагин, Skills → Скиллы, Webhook → Вебхук. Deliberately kept in English: Active Memory, Cron, Dreaming, Heartbeat, Loopback, Markdown, Self-hosted.
- `ru-navigation.json`: **created from scratch — 12 tabs, 55 groups** (8.6 KB), mirroring the English navigation structure.

No page content, no build scripts, no English strings touched: two data files only.

## Verification

- Every path in `ru-navigation.json` was checked against the repository tree (1,385 `.md` files): 0 broken links, 55 unique anchors.
- Rendered through the real `composeDocsConfig()` from `scripts/docs-sync-publish.mjs`: 12/12 Russian tabs, 55/55 groups, pages resolve as `ru/index…`.
- `glossary.ru.json` parses as valid JSON and keeps the original key order (`json.load` round-trip diff on the untouched prefix).
- Note: `check-docs-i18n-glossary.mts` only validates `zh-CN` today, so this file is not CI-gated — I verified it manually as described above.

## Why

The Russian locale is the largest non-English audience for OpenClaw docs and currently has English headings over Russian text. These two files are the smallest, highest-leverage change: no translation work, but the sidebar and the inline glossary switch to Russian immediately.

## Visual proof

Rendered through the real `composeDocsConfig()` from `scripts/docs-sync-publish.mjs`, locale `ru`, same tree, only `docs/.i18n/ru-navigation.json` added.

| Before (`main` — no ru overlay) | After (this PR) |

prs.title: ci(i18n): add non-publishing native locale refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where maintainers cannot refresh secret-backed native translations for review without also creating and arming an auto-merge generated PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an explicit non-publishing dispatch mode that runs the existing bounded locale matrix and validation, then uploads an allowlisted binary patch artifact. The default publishing path remains unchanged.

Secret-backed non-publishing runs execute only from the trusted `main` workflow. The operator supplies an exact source SHA; that SHA must be the current head of one open, non-draft PR targeting `main` with GitHub's current review decision `APPROVED`. Each locale worker revalidates the exact PR head and current approval immediately before the translation-secret step. Branch-selected preflight support was removed: guards inside branch-controlled YAML cannot independently guarantee secret isolation. Manual runs use the trusted main workflow definition.

## User Impact

No direct user-facing change. Maintainers gain a review-only native translation refresh path that cannot push, open a PR, or enable auto-merge, while non-publishing source selection requires current exact-head review approval.

## Evidence

### November 2 review-readiness repair

- Removed the branch-selected preflight mode and restored the main-only dispatch contract, addressing the P1 workflow-boundary finding without adding another execution path.
- Focused workflow contract regression: fails on the previous head at the branch-admission condition; passes after the repair (1 test, 4.97s runner wall).

### CI integration repair

prs.title: fix(codex): retain native thread reasoning effort
prs.body:
## Summary

- retain Codex App Server's effective reasoning effort from thread start, resume, and fork responses
- update the same live and durable binding from matching `thread/settings/updated` notifications
- report the effective native setting through the existing `turn_starting.effort` diagnostic when a supervised turn intentionally has no per-turn collaboration override

## Root cause and canonical fix

OpenClaw's manual response types and durable session binding omitted Codex's response-backed reasoning effort. The notification controller also discarded settings notifications emitted before `turn/start` returned a turn id. Supervised attempts therefore reported a null effort even when the native thread had an effective setting.

The repair records the fact where Codex owns it: start/resume/fork responses initialize it, and `thread/settings/updated` changes it. All binding writers carry the same nullable field. Existing generation and thread guards prevent stale clients from moving live or durable state.

This current-main rewrite does not add `thread_ready.reasoningEffort` or another event field. It fills the long-standing `turn_starting.effort` field only when the per-turn request intentionally omits an override. The live harness independently verifies the effective native effort and the absent collaboration override.

## Dependency contract

The integrated plugin pins `@openai/codex` 0.164.0. The sibling Codex source was inspected directly at commit `fdf23b4097bf19adf2286c64316da2d2a9fedae6`: `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs` defines response-backed nullable `reasoning_effort` for thread start/resume and `ThreadSettings.effort` for settings updates. Native thread facts remain separate from per-turn overrides.

## Coverage and change shape

Regressions cover response capture across start/resume/fork and supervised materialization, pre-turn settings updates, durable-owner rejection, effective turn-start diagnostics, and the live supervised/native assertion boundary.

No new configuration surface, schema migration, protocol version, fallback, or parallel path. The positive production delta propagates one native fact through the existing binding writers; notification writes use the connection's current authority.

## Validation

- Current head: `ae1b83e6b0bd`; integrated main: `1f01f4944d45`.
- 89 tests passed across three affected files during conflict repair.
- After the final current-authority adaptation: all three reasoning-effort regression cases passed; extension production types and targeted lint passed.
- Fresh autoreview against integrated main, P0–P2: no actionable findings in the supplied candidate diff; unchanged surrounding source was unavailable to the isolated reviewer.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- No fresh credentialed live Codex run. Historical CI and hosted review are not current-head evidence.
- Exact-head CI pending after publication; not claimed green.

prs.title: fix: exclude fenced dreaming ranges from memory indexing and recall signal
prs.body:
Closes #172547

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: managed dreaming output written into daily memory notes under `openclaw:dreaming` fences is embedded, returned by memory search, and staged into short-term recall, even though it is scratchwork that can never be promoted.

Scope confirmation: this branch implements the scope Peter Steinberger set on #172547 on 2026-10-27: "Managed inline dreaming fences should be excluded from default memory retrieval, before chunking." and "@CloudCorpRecords, please go ahead with your branch on that scope."

## User Impact

User impact: memory search and recall signals no longer surface fenced dreaming scratchwork, while ordinary note content keeps its exact citation line numbers and the note files themselves are never modified. Indexes built by earlier versions rebuild once through the existing chunking generation, so already-indexed fenced chunks are reconciled away, and already-staged fenced candidates stay unpromotable through the existing rehydration owner. No new config option.

## Why This Change Was Made

Index preparation now blanks managed fenced ranges (blank lines, never deletions, so line numbers stay exact) before chunking, for memory sources only. The fence policy lives in one new owner, `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/dreaming-fences.ts`, exported through the host internals and the `memory-core-host-engine-indexing` plugin SDK surface. Promotion rehydration imports the same helpers and its private copy of the fence regexes and overlap logic is deleted, so indexing and promotion cannot drift on what a fence is. `MEMORY_CHUNKING_VERSION` moves from 6 to 7 so the existing reindex owner rebuilds stored indexes instead of a parallel migration.

## Evidence

- New unit tests for the shared module: 12/12 pass (closed, unclosed, mixed, stray-marker, and CRLF cases).
- Index-preparation tests, including two new fence cases (mixed note excluded with original line numbers; fence-only note produces no chunks): 9/9 pass.
- Differential fuzz of the shared overlap helper against the pre-cutover rehydration implementation, transcribed verbatim: 72,871 cases, 0 mismatches (an earlier run of the same comparison covered 235,839 cases, also 0 mismatches).
- Acceptance scenario from the issue thread, exercised at the preparation and promotion-guard boundaries: a synthetic daily note with ordinary facts before and after a managed fence produces no chunk containing fenced text or markers, chunk texts and start/end lines are identical to a pre-blanked control (the after-fence fact still ends at its original line), the source string is unchanged, and the promotion guard refuses the fenced range and both marker lines while admitting the ordinary lines.
- Red/green check: the pre-change path (strip annotation carriers, then chunk) leaks the fenced text into chunks; the new path does not, and keeps the ordinary facts.
- `tsc --strict` on the new module: clean.

Honest limits: the local runs above used a vitest-shim harness because this sandbox cannot install the repo toolchain (pnpm self-install fails here), so the repo's own test suite, typecheck, and lint are CI's to confirm. The full end-to-end pass from the issue (real memory index, search, and promote paths with isolated state and a real local embedding model) was not run locally because no local embedding model is available in this environment; it is a reviewer or CI step, not something claimed here. The branch was brought current with main by a merge commit; conflicts were resolved by reapplying the branch changes at their current locations, and the resulting diff against main is exactly the 8 intended files.

prs.title: feat(release): add read-only release:watch for any publish parent
prs.body:
## Problem

#192564 item 4: there is no supported watcher for a publish parent outside `release:stable`'s retained state. That watcher accepts only final stable versions, so beta and resumed parents were not covered. It also reports only run conclusions. During 2026.11.5-beta.1, hand-rolled monitors missed a child's environment gate and a failed `continue-on-error` child job (the core npm child's "Notify Windows of published Gateway packages") for about 20 minutes.

## Solution

- New read-only `pnpm release:watch --run <publish-parent-run>` (`scripts/release-watch.mts`). It shares the existing `release:stable --watch` owner, `scripts/lib/release-publication-watch.mts`, which now takes an explicit watch target instead of release-stable state:
  - **Parent identity:** the run must be an `openclaw-release-publish.yml` `workflow_dispatch` run on a protected `release-publish/<sha12>-<n>` tag whose prefix matches its head SHA. `release:stable` still pins the tag, SHA, release tag and source SHA from retained state.
  - **Children:** ClawHub, ClawHub bootstrap, and core npm are bound by the exact `parent=<run>/<attempt>` tuple each child's run-name records from its `release_publish_run_id` / `release_publish_run_attempt` inputs. They must also match the tooling identity, except bootstrap, which uses its own admitted ref. Plugin npm has no parent tuple, so it is bound by tooling tag/SHA, its exact title, and a creation time inside a completed parent's lifetime. That last bound keeps a resumed parent's plugin npm run (same tooling and source) out of the earlier parent. Inventories are per child workflow, so unrelated dispatches cannot truncate them.
  - **Reports:** pending environment approvals on the parent and every child; failed runs; and failed jobs from the current attempt's paged job list (`failure`, `timed_out`, `cancelled`, `startup_failure`, `action_required`), including jobs a green run hides. The JSON snapshot keeps `contractVersion: 1` and adds `failedJobs`.
  - **Polling:** the default is 120 s for `release:watch`; `release:stable` stays at 60 s. On a GitHub rate-limit error the watch backs off from 2× the poll interval, doubling up to 15 minutes, instead of exiting. The existing per-call `gh` GET retries are unchanged.
- Exit contract unchanged: 0 success, 1 attention (now also a failed job), 2 usage/identity/transport failure.
- Docs: RELEASING "Watch publication" and the release-ci skill's Publish children section.

Discovery uses each child's recorded parent tuple rather than the parent's `dispatch.json` artifact. That artifact records only the normal ClawHub run ID, and the parent's "Dispatched … : <url>" log lines can only be read once the long-running dispatch job finishes. Neither can find every child while the publish is still in flight.

## Impact

Release tooling only, read-only GitHub API calls. Operators get one supported watcher for every publish parent: beta, stable, or resume. It exits on the first child gate or failed job instead of relying on hand-rolled monitors. `release:stable --watch` gains the same failed-job reporting, rate-limit backoff and parent-lifetime bound.

## Evidence

- Live, read-only, against the 2026.11.5-beta.1 incident:
  - `pnpm release:watch --run 41764249210 --once` found exactly the four children the parent dispatched: plugin npm 41765128775, ClawHub 41765132948, bootstrap 41765136531, and core npm 41767438818. It ignored the resume parent's plugin npm 41773155605. It reported the failed parent job, the failed ClawHub matrix job (200-job inventory, paged), and the bootstrap child's failed and cancelled jobs, and exited 1. The core npm Windows notify failure was on attempt 1; attempt 2 later reran it to success, so the current attempt correctly reports nothing for it.
  - `--run 41772282891` (resume parent) returned `success` with its three children.
- `test/scripts/release-watch.test.ts` (new): one fixture tree with decoys (prior parent attempt, artifact-preflight title, other tooling SHA, a later resume parent's plugin npm). It asserts the owned children, the bootstrap child's pending `clawhub-plugin-bootstrap` gate, the Windows notify failed job on a green core child, and GET-only calls.
- `test/scripts/release-stable.test.ts` watch cases are updated for per-workflow inventories and job reads: 29 passed together with the new file.
- `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, the tooling test tsgo leaf, targeted `run-oxlint` and `oxfmt` are clean.
- Test-line budget: net +131 lines for the new command's fixture test, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/release-watch-publish-parent.txt`.

### CI failures not caused by this PR

This PR touches `package.json` and adds `config/test-lines-allocations/…`. Both are outside the release-tooling fast-lane scope in `scripts/ci-changed-scope.mjs`, so CI runs at full scope. Earlier heads failed on suites this PR does not touch, all of them stale on `main` at the time and since fixed there: prompt snapshots (#192628), the hooks JSON e2e (#192621), the qa-lab kill-restart e2e (#192996), UI test types and mock exports (#192850), and `main` being over the test-line ceiling (it is back under). Current head `de1356e37bc7` merges `origin/main` with those fixes; the test-line ratchet passes locally with this PR's +131 allocation.

Refs #192564 (item 4; items 3 and 5 are in #192590, items 1–2 in another lane)

prs.title: feat(clawrouter): generate Lyria music through qualified proxy offers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw cannot consume qualified ClawRouter Lyria music offers, and its music fallback loop can buy another provider attempt after an unusable dispatched response. Automatic downstream gzip also conflicts with the proxy client's strict complete-response validation.

## User Impact

The existing `music_generate` path consumes the two frozen Lyria models only when the current proxy-key catalog grants the exact native or manifest transport. Caller cancellation reaches generation, response reading and delivery; an uncertain dispatched attempt stops automatic fallback. Music POSTs explicitly request identity encoding. Complete unencoded MP3/WAV results succeed, while forced compressed responses still fail without saving partial audio or buying an alternate attempt.

This does not establish live availability or refund a completed upstream operation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native Google prompt/lyrics/inline-image serializer and asset conversion are shared through the existing music-generation SDK barrel. Direct Google keeps its credential resolution, base64 normalization and retry behavior, except that an abort prevents retry. The proxy uses only its selected ClawRouter credential, bounded complete JSON/audio, and the existing fallback-stop marker.

The music transport correction adds `Accept-Encoding: identity` to the existing guarded music POST. Encoding, byte-length, EOF, decoded-size, cancellation and no-replay guards are unchanged. It does not erase response headers, install a fetch shim or change Worker responses.

Parent https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192052 landed as `d65390bcf36b818b5018029cc00951799bebf0ed`. Router contracts are https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/665, https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/686 and the separate composed integration https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/716.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `32930bd62b1b8da8a185eaee67449b3e475e5a80`, tree `bd6af37f75047e172eb6d31954545715c944a18d`. The native artifact remains **NEEDS WORK**. This successor keeps the qualified `b905d0c2` source/dependency parent and music wire behavior. It corrects the actual Knip classification of a plugin-anchored Tokenjuice resolver, without adding a root dependency or excluding the script.

The repeated hosted catalog failure still has no established cause. Three private control-plane modules now attach a bounded `catalog_budget_origin_v1` cause at the existing pre-GET deadline rejection. It identifies the actual inherited budget, child clock, producing cache load and acquisition/guard clocks. Pending joins preserve producer identity. It contains no credentials, URLs, providers or cache keys; it does not change the timeout, retry, cache or error-message policy. This diagnostic is not a claimed timeout fix.

- Exact successor: **13/13 Node and 13/13 pinned Bun** origin/cancellation/cache regressions pass; **9/9 Node and 9/9 Bun** actual registered ClawRouter catalog cases pass. The six origin cases also pass after the owned lint correction. A disposable expected-failure test verified the actual native formatter displays the bounded cause, then was removed before commit. Local Node 26 passes are not hosted Node 24 cause evidence.
- Full `pnpm build` passes in 3m59.6s. Core production/source test types, scoped lint, format, privacy/whitespace, normal hooks and both production/all-export Knip scans pass. Physical checkout-owned frozen dependencies remain qualified: Node 26.13.0, pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`, pnpm 12.15.0, Darwin arm64.
- Ratchet passes: **6,474,528 <= 6,474,552**, slack **24**. The existing **637** music allocation is unchanged; the diagnostic's **177** real regression-test lines have their own exact allocation. No scalar or inherited-debt padding.
- Predecessor `b905d0c2dd255eb56e8217baf53c090e456d3f12` has **55/55 Node and 55/55 Bun** music proof: 26 registered ClawRouter tool cases, 18 direct Google cases and 11 runtime cases. Native/manifest identity headers, complete MP3/WAV bytes, forced-gzip denial, cancellation and zero paid fallback pass. These remain explicitly predecessor proof.
- [SDK artifact 13377882363](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41939774919/artifacts/13377882363) is sealed for **b905**, with both renders (1,206,742 / 1,186,730 ms), archive digest and actual merge `9c5efc4dce5df683cd6ab3456a6abc90121c4359` ordered parents verified. It is not successor SDK proof.

**Remaining:** exact successor normal CI/SDK and native landing gates. The single SDK slot stays behind [image run 41946417465](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41946417465). Prior b905 CI failed its hosted Node 24 catalog acquisition at **−556.872671 ms before GET**, five UI jobs, and the startup asset comparison. The latter measured **92,696 versus 92,380 gzip bytes**: +316, exceeding the 192-byte variance by 124. Source attribution remains unresolved; nonadditive module gzip and inherited raw-file deltas do not justify a budget increase or blanket baseline exception. Actual composed workerd proof remains separately owned by integration716.

prs.body:
Related: #192990

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex exposes only V1 computer actions when a paired node already advertises V2 capabilities before the first tool call.

## User Impact

User impact: new Codex tool surfaces include advertised paired computer actions. Policy, model vision, session-owned desktop and live execution authorization boundaries remain intact. German keyboard corruption is separate and remains unverified.

## Why This Change Was Made

The common async construction owner now reuses host-owned paired capability preparation before assembly, preserving prepared facts, combined cancellation and stable initial definitions. No SDK surface, discovery cache or dependency is added.

The review repair keeps the extension regression on the existing SDK-backed production-host fixture and exercises discovery over loopback Gateway protocol responses. Session-transport exclusions are tested in the owning core assembly suite. Cron fixtures still record every RPC; only `node.list` and `computer.status` are excluded from action assertions, so forbidden cron actions and unexpected methods still fail non-dispatch checks.

## Evidence

- **Committed regression, red/green:** the identical SDK-backed regression file ran on unchanged base `0af3fea539816c517ec8e595905ba1991dee6407` in a separate worktree. Its V2 case failed because the first serialized computer schema lacked `list_windows` (one failed, five unselected; exit 1). On the fix, all six extension cases passed (exit 0). Two core cases separately verify available/unavailable session-owned transport without paired discovery. No private extension-to-core imports or mocks remain; `lint:plugins:no-extension-test-core-imports` passes.
- **Consumer repair:** all 25 cron policy cases pass, including the six reproduced failures. Forbidden own/sibling automation mutations remain checked before dispatch, including revocation during an awaited call. No RPC history is cleared to obtain a pass.
- **Local acceptance:** 208 cases passed across eight files. After replacing raw WebSocket data stringification with the plugin's existing decoder, the affected six-case SDK fixture was rerun and passed. Core agent-test, cron-test and extension-test typechecks, affected lint/format, line-cap and test-line ratchets, whitespace and pre-commit checks pass. The allocation exactly covers 254 net regression lines. CI time is unmeasured.
- **Actual product proof retained:** an isolated Gateway and subscription-backed Codex app-server 0.166.0 used the same normally paired synthetic node advertising `screenshot` and `list_windows`. Baseline first `thread/start` omitted `list_windows`; the model replied `V2_UNAVAILABLE` without a computer call. The fixed snapshot included it before any computer action, invoked `computer.act` with `action: list_windows`, and produced a successful computer receipt and reply `COMPUTER_V2_192990`. Both live phases passed. The snapshot preceded mechanical preparation extraction/test relocation; equivalent inputs/order and subsequent tests/build support reuse. It is not literal final-head live proof, a physical Windows driver test, a keyboard fix, or blanket V2 exposure. This review follow-up changes tests only.
- **Review:** fresh local autoreview of the test repairs and supplied owner context found no actionable P0–P2 defects; the reviewer did not execute tests. `pr-simplify` removed private test wiring while preserving production behavior. prs.title: fix: resolve native Windows Git plugin paths
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes local Git plugin installs rejecting native Windows relative, parent-relative, and absolute paths. Also preserves an explicit `release.git` ref when a relative path is normalized and parsed again.

## User Impact

Windows users can install local Git plugins using normal native path syntax. Paths containing spaces, Unicode, and `@` ancestors are retained. No settings or migration are required. Existing absolute `.git` repository names retain their interpretation; use the already-supported `#ref` form when a literal absolute path and a ref would otherwise be ambiguous.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one existing local-path classification owner for ref admission and local resolution. Normalized Windows local refs use the unambiguous `#` selector, so a ref ending in `.git` cannot turn into part of the repository path. This addresses the review’s normalized-spec round-trip finding without changing remote Git transport, consent, policy, or publication transactions.

## Evidence

Native Windows / Node 24.22.1, real `runPluginInstallCommand`, Git, filesystem and safe npm install; activation disabled and all state/config task-isolated. The local fixture contains distinct `main` and `release.git` commits. Exact terminal result fields:

```text
requestedRef: release.git
mainCommit: 96d550607741acd090566d89e7cba75e2cae36b5
requestedCommit: 81a4fbe1eaa66524688a31cbad7d197e75f4e0ff
exit: 0
errors: []
installedArtifacts: 1
```

The proof asserts that the installed repository HEAD equals the requested commit, differs from main, and the installed JavaScript exactly equals the ref-specific bytes. The command wrote its isolated config. Native proof does not independently assert durable install-record serialization or update replay; those consumers were reviewed from source. No live Gateway or personal configuration changed.

- Original native-path cases reproduced the unsupported-spec failure before repair.
- Review finding reproduced before correction: parsing a relative `@release.git` succeeds, but parsing its normalized spec loses the ref and appends it to the repository path.
- Final complete installer owner suite: **34 passed** (29.77 s wall time; about 3 s test time). A new real CLI reproduction also exposed literal `@` path data being mistaken for a ref after file-URL transport; encoding that path data in the existing source planner fixes the full user flow. Two existing staging-path assertions now use the native separator instead of a hard-coded POSIX separator, resolving their five Windows failures without weakening the expected staging basename. Native timings are local; no CI before/after test-cost comparison is claimed.
- Complete CLI preflight suite: **22 passed**, including red/green native-path → encoded file-URL → Git parser round-trip. Actual CLI fixtures additionally install `@acme/plugin`, `team@acme/plugin.git`, and a literal `repo@release.git` repository, asserting exact installed commit and JavaScript bytes.
- Earlier broad update-consumer suite: **82 passed, 3 failed, 1 skipped**; all three Windows EPERM cleanup failures reproduced on its exact base. That suite mocks the Git installer; no unrelated cleanup change is included.
- Final targeted production/test types, typed lint (four files), format and whitespace: passed. Independent manual review plus canonical full four-file P0–P3 review: scoped-clean, both passes zero findings, all five source/context SHA-256 hashes unchanged. Full exact-head CI passed on `ca46f803ad1817d5a79913e3e806c34ae64cd721` (run 40625843299); both required ci-gates passed.

<details>
<summary>Scope and ownership</summary>

The Git parser, its existing owner test, the existing local-source transport adapter and its existing preflight test change. One private classifier replaces two duplicated path predicates; a ref guard retains legacy ancestor interpretation, and canonical Windows local refs remain unambiguous. No new API, dependency, platform mock, fallback, or additional feature. Distinct from #185333’s file-URL decoder. Inspected competing Git-install diffs do not implement this parser repair.

</details>


### November 4 conflict repair — current evidence

- Safely merged upstream `6e24d6fa240eef7ad3e8e4794b0e9256b6f55f85` without rewriting existing branch history. The only conflict was the preflight test import block: retained all upstream file-URL/temp-dir imports plus the existing parser/planner regression imports. No upstream behavior was discarded. Production delta remains the same two owners; added a dedicated 77-line test allocation, not the shared scalar.
- Fresh native Windows / Node 24.22.1 real CLI-command install fixtures, with isolated homes/config/database and activation disabled: relative Unicode/spaced native path plus `@release.git` installed the exact requested commit and ref-specific JavaScript bytes; absolute literal `repo@release.git` installed the exact default-branch commit/bytes, different from the deliberately distinct `release.git` branch. Real Git clone and npm dependency installation ran; no live Gateway or personal configuration touched. These fixtures do not independently prove durable update replay.
- Complete focused owner suites: **35 installer + 24 CLI-preflight tests passed** (`--maxWorkers=1`). Local wall times 61.82s / 232.43s respectively, including cold compilation; wrapper 374.28s. Git update consumer: **1 passed, 84 deliberately filtered** by `-t git`, shard 31.40s. No current CI timing claim.
- Targeted production + touched-test typechecks passed; typed core lint passed (293 rules, zero warnings/errors); four-file format and whitespace passed; test-line ratchet passed. An earlier custom lint tsconfig accidentally selected unrelated SDK boundary compilation and hit its 300s tooling timeout; the supported source-backed core lint configuration completed without disabling guards.
- Fresh independent full captured-source review raised one ambiguous spelling (`C:/repos/team@acme/plugin`, no `.git`). Retained existing `@<ref>` grammar because that spelling is also repository `C:/repos/team` plus valid slash-containing ref `acme/plugin`; do not reinterpret it using filesystem-dependent guesses. Use native backslashes for literal ancestors, a `.git` repository suffix, or an encoded file URL. Other targeted Windows/ref/transport cases were coherent on inspection. The shared local autoreview preparation was stopped before engine launch after 465s fingerprinting this 60k-file tree; no new canonical scoped-clean result is claimed.
- The older green CI/review evidence above remains explicitly bound to `ca46f80`; it is not current-head CI. Current-head checks and hosted rereview must be observed separately.

- Fresh real CLI negative control with exact main owner bytes: literal absolute `repo@release.git` is incorrectly split to nonexistent repository `repo`; actual Git clone fails and CLI exits 1. Candidate fixture installs correct default-branch commit and exact bytes, exits 0. This is the production-route red/green; the relative `@release.git` fixture is a separate passing selector control, not a baseline failure.

- Exact-main direct owner negative control completed: **10 regression failures, 2 passes, 23 filtered**, expected failure exit 1; candidate complete owner suite previously **35/35 green**. Temporary base owners restored byte-for-byte to candidate backups before committing.

Repair merge commit: `5584783ba6ec6e4e21b59bd769627c92e9b686a5` (parents retain prior PR head and pinned upstream).


### Exact-head verification completed — November 4

For 5584783ba6ec6e4e21b59bd769627c92e9b686a5, substantive CI run **41934231858 succeeded** (37 successful / 31 skipped / zero failed jobs); openclaw/ci-gate succeeded. Supported watcher completed GREEN with zero pending checks. Codex exact-head review completed at 23:38:35 UTC with **no findings or unresolved findings** (receipt comment 6645268413). ClawSweeper’s November 1 summary is stale, not a current-head verdict. PR is mergeable; GitHub aggregate remains UNSTABLE from cancelled auxiliary Auto response / older context checks, while replacement context evidence succeeded. No formal human approval or merge is claimed.
