prs.title: fix(whatsapp): retry inbound DMs with transiently unresolvable LID identity
prs.body:
Part of #119475

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: inbound WhatsApp direct messages (DMs) whose LID→phone mapping is not resolvable at admission time are treated as non-messages and permanently dropped, silently.

This is the retryable half of openclaw/openclaw#119475 (P1, `impact:message-loss`). When a DM arrives from a `@lid`/`@hosted.lid` chat, the normalizer calls `resolveInboundJid(remoteJid)`; if it returns `null` (LID mapping lookup not yet hydrated, or the lookup fails transiently), the normalizer returns `null`, the durable ingress drain completes the claim, and the message is gone — with only a verbose-gated log line.

Production reports confirm a large share of these losses is a **race, not a permanent absence**: the mapping files (`lid-mapping-<lid>_reverse.json`) are written within the same second as the drop, so a short retry/re-resolve delivers the message (see the 2026-09-02 production analysis in #119475: "the mapping is not missing, it is late … a meaningful share of CTWA losses can be fixed without promoting unmapped LIDs to peers").

## User Impact

User impact: operators running WhatsApp no longer silently lose first-contact DMs (CTWA ad leads, @username senders) when the LID mapping is briefly unavailable; the message now waits in the durable drain and is delivered as soon as the mapping resolves, exactly like any other transiently deferred inbound.

No breaking change, no config change, no security-sensitive identity promotion: this fix only changes *when* an already-retryable message is re-normalized. The separate permanent-`sender_pn`-absent case (which requires admitting an opaque LID as a peer, pending the maintainer product/security decision in #119475) is intentionally out of scope here.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveJidToE164` intentionally returns `null` on a LID lookup miss or failure — that contract is locked by `text-runtime.test.ts` (`returns null when lidLookup throws`). The drop happens one layer up, in the direct-message normalizer, which converted that `null` into "this is not a message" (`return null`). The drain then treats a `null` preparation as terminal (`prepared === null → return "completed"`), permanently discarding the claim.

The fix routes the unresolvable-identity case into the existing "durable drain will normalize again" retry path instead of the terminal path:

- `message-normalization.ts`: for a direct DM, an unresolvable sender identity now throws `WhatsAppIngressIdentityUnavailableError` instead of returning `null`. The error is raised *before* `checkInboundAccessControl`, so it has no pairing-reply side effects and can be retried freely. Groups are unaffected (they don't resolve the peer).
- `message-delivery.ts`: the completed-drain read-receipt branch guards normalization with try/catch so an unresolvable identity only skips the read receipt and cannot abort the rest of the batch. The already-existing `accepted` branch already catches normalize errors and calls `finishPreparation(undefined)`, which is what lets the drain re-normalize.

The durable ingress monitor releases the claim on dispatch failure and retries with backoff (base 1s, cap 3m, 8 attempts, 24h dead-letter floor), which is ample time for the same-second mapping write to land. `resolveJidToE164` keeps its contract unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused regression test added in `monitor-inbox.reply-context.test.ts` — `retries a direct DM whose LID identity is transiently unresolvable instead of dropping it`:

- Drives the real `messages.upsert` → admission → durable drain flow through `startInboxMonitor`.
- Mocks `getPNForLID` to fail once (transient lookup failure), then succeed.
- Asserts the lookup is retried (`toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)`), the message is delivered with the correct conversation id (`+999`), and the body round-trips.

Test + related suites all green (WhatsApp extension shard):
- `monitor-inbox.reply-context.test.ts`: 10 passed
- `monitor-inbox.delivery-and-dedupe.test.ts`, `monitor-inbox.access-and-echo.test.ts`, `inbound.test.ts`, `text-runtime.test.ts`: 128 passed
- `approval-reactions.test.ts`, `monitor-inbox.policy.test.ts`: 29 passed

Verification commands run:
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-whatsapp.config.ts <files>` — all passed
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/whatsapp/tsconfig.json` — clean (production source typecheck)
- Direct `oxlint` on all three changed files — clean
- `git diff --check` — clean

Notes on scope of evidence: this is a behavior fix on the channel boundary proven through the real mocked-Gateway ingress flow (the standard for this extension's inbound tests). Live WhatsApp proof for this exact race is documented by production reporters in #119475; a live account was not available in this environment.

### Focused one-worker run (measured)

The regression test was also run alone with `--maxWorkers=1` (real `startInboxMonitor` → `messages.upsert` → durable admission → drain retry → delivery flow, mocked socket + LID lookup):

```
✓ ... monitor inbox reply context > retries a direct DM whose LID identity is transiently unresolvable instead of dropping it 60063ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed | 9 skipped (10)
```

Measured one-worker wall time for the focused run: **380s** (dominated by first-run vitest worker compile + transform on this cold Windows host; the test itself reports 60s and 335ms when run warm alongside the rest of the file).

**AI assistance disclosure:** This PR was authored with AI assistance (CoMind), including the reproduction analysis, the fix, and the regression test. The human maintainer should review the identity-contract reasoning against the #119475 maintainer decision before extending this beyond the retryable share.

prs.title: fix(release): verify post-publication container registry readback
prs.body:
## Problem

RRI-352 identified that release verification could treat successful publication workflows as sufficient evidence without reading the published container manifests back from every registry. Missing architecture tags, stale moving aliases, or cross-registry descriptor drift could therefore escape verification.

## Solution

- add a bounded, retrying registry-v2 readback verifier for GHCR, Docker Hub, and Vercel Container Registry
- verify immutable default/slim/browser indexes and amd64/arm64 tags, cross-registry digests and descriptor sets, and policy-owned moving aliases
- run readback after Vercel mirroring and include its outcome in the workflow summary
- update release verification guidance for regular and extended-stable releases

## Tests

- add focused tests for missing immutable tags, stale aliases, missing Vercel variants, and beta's intentional zero-moving-alias policy
- update Vercel publication workflow contract tests to cover advisory mirroring and blocking recovery readback

## Limitations

This repair verifies published manifests and alias/descriptor consistency. It does not replace the separate attestation checks. Live reads of a private Vercel registry require existing Docker credential state; when unavailable, release verification must report that live-readback gap explicitly rather than infer success from the workflow conclusion.

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: fix(macos): first dashboard open is slow in remote mode
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS app never preloads the dashboard in remote connection mode, so the first open after launch waits for a cold web load.

## User Impact

User impact: in remote mode the dashboard loads hidden once the Gateway connection is authenticated, so the first open can show an already-loaded dashboard, as in local mode. Remote identity dashboards still resolve their sign-in address after hello and never receive pre-hello native credentials. At most one extra hidden load per app launch.

## Why This Change Was Made

The launch preload from #106997 uses the synchronous `immediateWindowConfiguration()`, which #137933 deliberately limited to local mode (`DashboardManager.swift:436-437` on main: "Remote dashboards must resolve the server's sign-in route before any document receives native credentials, including the synchronous fast path."). That guard stays. Remote mode now arms a one-shot preload at launch and starts it when the control channel reports connected, resolving the route through the same `windowConfiguration(for: .primary)` path a visible open uses, then presenting hidden.

<details>
<summary>Root cause and change details</summary>

Root cause on main 939750da217:
- `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/MenuBar.swift:464-468`: one `preloadIfConfigured()` call 2 s after launch.
- `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardManager.swift:460-464`: preload requires `immediateWindowConfiguration()`.
- `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardManager+Routes.swift:131-136`: `guard mode == .local`, added in 0d2bc80eee0 (#137933).

Change:
- `preloadIfConfigured()`: when the immediate config is unavailable in remote mode, arm the remote preload; start it at once if the control channel is already connected. It returns the started task (`@discardableResult`) so callers can join it. Its only caller is the launch hook in `MenuBar.swift` on `DashboardManager.shared`, which always observes gateway changes, so the former `observesGatewayChanges` term in the arming expression was redundant.
- `handleControlChannelStateChange(.connected)`: after reconciling existing documents, start the armed preload.
- `DashboardRemotePreloadDecision` (new, pure logic): `start` only when armed, remote, primary target, no main controller, no presentation or main-window open in flight, and connected; `wait` while not connected; otherwise `discard`. It is spent when it starts; reconnects never re-arm it, and a failed lookup is not retried until the next launch.
- `openWindow(for:reuseExisting:)` counts main-window opens while they await their lookup (`mainOpensInFlight`). The preload checks that count when it starts and again after its own lookup, together with the live channel state and the window lifetime, so an explicit open on either side of the lookup keeps the first document. Signed-out or credential-less configurations are skipped.
- It presents through `presentDashboard(..., source: nil, present: false)`, which records the presented endpoint. A newly created main controller now honors `present`; the default stays `true`, and only this call passes `false`.
- The hidden controller is retained before its document loads: `DashboardWindowController.retainHidden()` marks the never-shown window experience-hidden, the same lifetime `hideForExperience()` uses. So `hasRetainedWindow` is true, `documentHost.isNativeAuthAvailable()` answers native sign-in challenges, and `dashboardControllers()` includes it, so `handleEndpointState` reconciles reconnects and route changes before the first open. `show()` and `windowWillClose` clear the flag as before, so closed-window and stale-credential rejection is unchanged.
- The window also records that it was never shown (`DashboardWindow.isUnshownPreload`, cleared by `show()`). `openWindowCount(for:)`, which the Gateways menu card displays, skips it, so a hidden preload does not read as "1 window". The flag lives on the window, so it survives an endpoint change that replaces the controller.
- Reuse on the first visible open: `showResolvedPrimaryDashboard` resolves again and keeps the document unless `requiresIsolatedDashboardDocument` (`DashboardManager+Construction.swift:299-312`) sees a TLS, auth, browser-session or route change. Native-device auth compares URL, token, password and the legacy credential map. The token comes from the live hello snapshot or config (`GatewayConnection.swift:1300-1310`) and the legacy map holds only a token or password from the same binding (`GatewayConnection+ControlUIAuth.swift:24-27`), so the two lookups match while the same hello snapshot is live. After a reconnect that reissues a device token or bumps the route revision, the first open replaces the document, which is no worse than main. `openOrFocusDashboard(.primary)` sees the experience-hidden preload, resolves the route again for the user gesture and presents through the same reuse check, so the document is kept when nothing changed. `DashboardRemotePreloadTests` cover the reuse through `show()` and both open orderings (see Evidence).
- Test seam, DEBUG only: `testControlChannelConnected` overrides the live control channel state the preload reads (`ControlChannel.shared.state` is socket-driven). Tests arm the preload through `preloadIfConfigured()` itself, with remote mode and onboarding set as at launch.
- The hidden load runs `update(url:auth:)` like the existing local preload, including its guarded browser-profile import offer check (`DashboardWindowController.swift:497-502` on main), so remote mode gains no new UI path.

</details>

## Evidence

Built and tested locally on macOS 27.0.1 with Command Line Tools only (no Xcode.app), using host-side workarounds that change nothing in the repository; CI `macos-swift` remains the authority.

<details>
<summary>Build host workarounds and test isolation</summary>

A copy of the CLT PackageDescription/PackagePlugin modules without their stale `.private.swiftinterface` (`SWIFTPM_CUSTOM_LIBS_DIR`), stand-in `SwiftUIMacros`/`PreviewsMacros` compiler plugins (`-load-plugin-executable`; CLT ships neither), `-F`/`-rpath` to the CLT Testing framework, `node scripts/prepare-apple-mermaid.mjs`, and the two XCTest-only test files (`MacNodeLocationServiceTests`, `SimpleTaskSupportTests`) left out of the build because CLT has no XCTest. Tests ran with `--skip-build` under `sandbox-exec` with a private `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `TMPDIR`, a named test profile, and no access to the operator's `~/.openclaw`, Keychains or non-loopback network.

</details>

- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --product OpenClaw`: `Build of product 'OpenClaw' complete!`, no warnings from the changed files.
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests`: `Build complete!`.
- Native sign-in on the hidden preload (head `c05592db154`, test-only follow-up): new `DashboardRemotePreloadTests` case `hidden remote preload answers native challenges only while its document is current` sends a real `OpenClawNativeGatewayAuth` WK challenge from the hidden preloaded document through the production `ControlUINativeGatewayAuthMessageHandler` (only the native provider is a gated stub, as in `DashboardNativeGatewayAuthBridgeTests`). Cases: `current` gets the reply; `socket` (the provider's response is no longer current), `document` (the WebView commits a new document) and `browser-identity-pending` (the document switches to a browser identity while the challenge waits) get an error and no credentials; `browser-identity` (a browser identity document) is rejected without the provider being called. The preload stays hidden in every case.
  - `swift test --filter DashboardRemotePreloadTests`: `Test run with 5 tests in 1 suite passed` (the four earlier tests plus the new one, which runs 5 cases).
  - Red, retention: without `controller.retainHidden()` in `presentDashboard`, `current`, `socket`, `document` and `browser-identity-pending` time out waiting for a challenge the handler never forwards (the hidden document is not native-auth available), plus the earlier retention assertions: `Test run with 5 tests in 1 suite failed ... with 8 issues`.
  - Red, reply guard: without the post-provider `canUseNativeGatewayAuth` / revision / `isCurrent()` guard in `ControlUINativeGatewayAuthMessageHandler`, `socket`, `document` and `browser-identity-pending` receive the credential reply: `... failed ... with 6 issues`.
  - `DashboardRemotePreloadDecisionTests` (it mirrored the decision enum's guards) is removed; the manager suite covers the observable preload, reuse, ordering and reconciliation behavior.
  - Dashboard suites plus `DashboardNativeGatewayAuthBridgeTests`: `Test run with 69 tests in 10 suites failed with 6 issues`, the same 6 environment issues listed below; the bridge suite passes. `scripts/format-swift.sh macos`: `0/417` and `0/33 files require formatting.`; lint with CI semantics exits 0.
- Earlier head `62766ffc00a`: `swift test --filter DashboardRemotePreload`: `Test run with 9 tests in 2 suites passed` (including the since-removed decision tests).
  - `DashboardRemotePreloadTests` (real `DashboardManager` with a loopback HTTP fixture and gated endpoint lookups; every test arms through `preloadIfConfigured()` with remote mode and onboarding set): `first open reuses the hidden remote preload document` (the preloaded controller is hidden, has a retained window, answers native sign-in and is not counted by `openWindowCount(for: .primary)`; after `show()` it is the same instance, now visible and counted once); `open in flight before authentication owns the first document`; `open that starts during the preload lookup owns the first document` (the preload resumes and finishes first and installs nothing; the open's window is the one shown); `hidden remote preload follows an endpoint change before the first open` (after `handleEndpointState(.ready(...))` with a new URL and token, the same hidden window carries the new token, stays retained and is still not counted).
  - `open in flight before authentication owns the first document` alone: `Test run with 1 test in 1 suite passed`.
  - Red check, retention: without the `retainHidden()` call, `Test run with 9 tests in 2 suites failed ... with 4 issues` (`preloaded.hasRetainedWindow`, `preloaded.documentHost.isNativeAuthAvailable()`, `reconciled.auth.token == "rotated-primary-token"`, `reconciled.hasRetainedWindow`).
  - Red check, launch arming: without the `remotePreloadPending` assignment in `preloadIfConfigured()`, `Test run with 9 tests in 2 suites failed ... with 3 issues` (the reuse, preload-lookup and endpoint-change tests find no preload).
  - Red check, window count: without the unshown-preload filter in `openWindowCount(for:)`, `Test run with 9 tests in 2 suites failed ... with 2 issues` (`manager.openWindowCount(for: .primary) == 0` in the reuse and endpoint-change tests).
  - Earlier round: with `mainOpensInFlight` removed from the preload decision, both ordering tests fail.
- Existing dashboard suites, `swift test --filter "DashboardReconnectTests|DashboardWindowOwnershipTests|DashboardTokenlessRouteTests|DashboardGatewaySelectionTests|DashboardGatewaysTests"`: `Test run with 67 tests in 9 suites failed with 6 issues`, and the same filter on unmodified main 939750da217 fails with the identical 6 issues (same tests, cases and assertions). Four are `Caught error: .keychain(-61)` because the sandbox denies Keychain writes. The other two are `configured presentation uses its owned health probe` (mode .local, `controller.currentURL`) and `superseded primary presentation preserves the selected profile` (initial-command, `showConfiguredWindowIfPossible()`). This change adds no failures.
- `scripts/format-swift.sh macos`: `0/33 files require formatting.`
- `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` with the pinned tools from `scripts/install-swift-tools.sh`: one violation, `file_length` on `DashboardManager.swift` (1561 > 1500). Unmodified main already fails the same rule at 1505. With CI semantics (`GITHUB_ACTIONS=true`, limit rules advisory per `scripts/lib/check-limits.mts:11-13`) it exits 0.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 939750da217`: 11 lanes ok (including `format changed files` and `native state schema version guard`). Two failed, neither from this diff:
  - `lint apps`: the local strict run of the same `file_length` rule above (base already over the limit).
  - `macOS app CI tests` (Vitest for macOS tooling scripts): `Tests 1 failed | 607 passed (608)`. The failure is `test/scripts/generate-gateway-protocol-plugin.test.ts > resolves supported Node shims and reports failed probe reasons`, which shells out to `swift build` and hits this host's Command Line Tools manifest link error (`Undefined symbols ... PackageDescription.Package.__allocating_init`). This change touches neither that script nor its test.
- Gaps:
  - The full native suite and the XCTest-based files did not run here; CI's `macos-swift` job is the authority (`docs/platforms/mac/dev-setup.md`).
  - The packaged-app run below is on a GitHub-hosted runner with a job-owned loopback Gateway, not a real remote host; the base comparison stops before the first open (see Real behavior proof).
  - The live run shows the hidden document's native challenge being answered; the refusal cases (browser identity, socket or document retirement while a challenge waits) are shown on the hidden preload by the test above, not in the packaged app.

## Real behavior proof

Packaged app (ad-hoc signed debug build, `ai.openclaw.mac.debug`, app 2026.10.7) built from this PR head `c05592db15442a5dda82477da1ff64f7bbe2fb49`, on a GitHub-hosted macOS 26.6.2 arm64 runner. Run: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/41188038343 (job `proof 4a-head`, artifact `mac-proof-4a-head`, `identity.txt`: `source_sha=c05592db15442a5dda82477da1ff64f7bbe2fb49`). The same scenario also passed on the previous head `62766ffc00a` (identical app sources; run https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/41182007510).

Setup: a job-owned `openclaw gateway` on loopback with token auth and a placeholder default model (no model is called). The app runs in remote mode (`gateway.mode=remote`, direct transport) against a loopback logging proxy in front of that Gateway, so every HTTP request and WebSocket upgrade from the app and its dashboard WebView is timestamped (query values are not logged). The dashboard document is the request with `Sec-Fetch-Dest: document`. The app is launched normally (no `--dashboard`), then opened once with `openclaw://dashboard`, the same action as the menu item. The full CoreGraphics window list (on and off screen) is read before and after the open.

Result (`summary.md`):

| moment | dashboard document requests | dashboard window |
|---|---|---|
| launch to first open | 1 | on screen: none, off screen: 39 |
| first open to settled shot (~47 s: 16-frame burst, ~26 s on the runner, then 20 s settle) | 0 | on screen: 39 (same window as before open: yes) |

```
09:53:25 app launched: OpenClaw.app args:
09:53:36 document requests before any open: 1 (first seen 11.0 s after launch)
09:53:49 local network alert: pressed Allow in UserNotificationCenter
09:53:49 windows before-open: 0 on screen, 6 off screen
09:53:49 dashboard window before open: on screen=[] off screen=[39]
09:54:15 first-open frame burst done (16 frames, 250 ms apart)
09:54:36 windows after-open: 1 on screen, 5 off screen
09:54:36 dashboard documents: before open=1, open..+20s=0; window on screen after open=[39] same as preloaded=yes; page socket none s after open
09:54:36 PASS 4a: hidden remote preload loaded the dashboard document off screen; the first open showed that window without a new document load
```

The proxy log shows the hidden page's document at 09:53:34.993 and its Gateway WebSocket (the only upgrade with an `Origin` header) at 09:53:47.169, both before the open; nothing new after it. The Gateway log shows that page socket authenticating (the app's native control channel, no `Origin`, connected separately at 09:53:30):
```
09:53:47.330 [ws] client connected conn=3f7fcc67-... client=openclaw-macos mode=ui role=operator auth=token build=2026.10.7-c05592db1544-...
09:53:47.344 [ws] res ✓ connect 53ms
09:53:47.356 [ws] → hello-ok
```
That connect is the native challenge path: the page takes its `client` from the app's `nativeConnectAuth` reply only (`ui/src/api/gateway-connect-plan.ts:135-152`), and the app signs it as `client.id = "openclaw-macos"`, `mode = "ui"` (`apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/DashboardNativeGatewayAuth.swift:50`); a page without native auth connects as `openclaw-control-ui`. The connect carries the page's own build id (the app's native channel reports `build=legacy`). So the hidden preloaded document asked for and received a native challenge reply before the first open.

The review's other two boundary cases (a browser identity document gets no native credentials; a retired socket or document gets no pending reply) are shown on the hidden preload by the new test in Evidence, through the production message handler. A browser identity route needs a Gateway that advertises an https sign-in origin (trusted-proxy or Tailscale Serve, `src/gateway/control-ui-identity.ts:17-28`), which this loopback job does not have.

Once its document has loaded, the hidden page may open its own Gateway socket before any open (as here; in an earlier run, 40542122063, it waited until shown), so a remote launch can hold that one page connection; it is the connection the first open shows.

Before the open, nothing on screen; the 1240x860 dashboard window 39 exists off screen:

![before open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2f74c6ff4dc42389639b99c2a3a125d0983a5b44/mac-item-4a-preload-r5/10-screen-before-open.png)

The first frame right after the open shows the already-loaded dashboard shell while the chat pane repaints; the next captured frame (the 16-frame burst took ~26 s on this runner, so ~1.6 s later) is fully rendered, still with no new document request or socket:

![first open frame 00](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2f74c6ff4dc42389639b99c2a3a125d0983a5b44/mac-item-4a-preload-r5/20-first-open-frame-00.png)
![first open frame 01](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etzelm/openclaw/2f74c6ff4dc42389639b99c2a3a125d0983a5b44/mac-item-4a-preload-r5/20-first-open-frame-01.png)

Before (current PR base `3d064947c6b`; the root-cause line numbers above are from main `939750da217`, where this branch started; previous harness revision `3b74ff0466f` with the same launch-to-open checks, run https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/41178439473, job `proof 4a-base`, `identity.txt` `source_sha=3d064947c6bb6d6c1bda930c67ec8672f56dbbc0`): no hidden load at all.
```
07:22:42 document requests before any open: 0
07:22:54 windows before-open: 0 on screen, 4 off screen   (four 1024x30 windows, no dashboard window)
```
That base job then stopped on a harness bug (fixed in the runs above) before the first open, so it shows only the launch-to-open half: no dashboard document in 109 s after launch and no dashboard window at 121 s.

Harness: `scripts/mac-proof/4a.sh` on fork branch `mac/proof-4` (`64506d45e0a`). Logs contain no tokens, keys or non-loopback addresses.

Related: #185430

prs.title: feat(notion): add shared memory and Skills integration
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw users need a supported connection to Notion’s announced shared-memory and native Skills workflow, without building a second memory backend or treating remote setup instructions as permission to import their data.

Context: [requested integration](https://x.com/heyneighbor/status/2118138957229891670). The announcement’s short link resolves to its video; implementation requirements come from the [official setup guide](https://developers.notion.com/prompts/setup) (reviewed version 0.0.6, October 30, 2026), [MCP connection documentation](https://developers.notion.com/guides/mcp/get-started-with-mcp), and [technical memory/Skills reference](https://developers.notion.com/guides/mcp/tools-skills-agents-reference).

## User Impact

Adds a disabled-by-default Notion plugin contributing the official hosted OAuth MCP connection and a `notion-shared-brain` workflow skill. Users explicitly enable it, sign in, and approve their import sources and destinations. No live installation, production configuration change, automatic import, remote Skill installation, or scheduled synchronization is performed.

The guide explains provenance, corrections and forget requests, native Skill package preservation, and remote-content/prompt-injection boundaries. Notion-managed memory is private to the connected user; the default OpenClaw MCP credential is shared with callers allowed to invoke it on that Gateway. This is not automatic multi-user identity isolation or a guarantee of permanent/cross-agent erasure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing owners: Notion owns remote memory and native Skills; OpenClaw owns MCP OAuth, discovery, transport, tool policy, and cleanup. The plugin has no custom client, credential store, memory database, hooks, or background service, and does not replace OpenClaw’s selected memory plugin. Explicit operator MCP overrides and disables retain precedence.

## Evidence

- **4 new production-boundary tests passed:** actual bundled manifest discovery, hosted OAuth configuration and attribution, real published workflow Skill, disabled-by-default/explicitly-disabled behavior, and operator replacement/disable precedence without duplicate connections. No owner-loader mocks.
- **9 existing MCP contribution tests passed**, plus **410 plugin packaging/dependency contract checks**.
- Scoped entrypoint and integration-test typechecks passed using the repository compiler runner and independently owned frozen-lockfile dependencies. Focused lint/format checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- Docs formatting (1,413 files), targeted MDX checks, internal-link audit (zero broken links), and documented configuration schema checks passed.
- Final local **autoreview/Codex**, full eight-file uncommitted snapshot on base `c3cdd6bc2d79efdfc177d3049f0072c6a1eae0b2`, P0–P2 coverage: completed, scoped-clean, no actionable findings. This was static independent review, not authenticated product execution.
- The official hosted endpoint returned **401 with an OAuth protected-resource challenge**, as expected without credentials.

**Proof gaps:** no authorized Notion test account/workspace was supplied, so authenticated CRUD, forget behavior, native Skill transfer, and second-agent recall are not claimed as verified. The isolated source-CLI smoke attempt was blocked by the managed host’s runtime-artifact publication guard/host-environment permission check; the guard was not bypassed and the live Gateway was not changed or restarted. The docs include an explicit account-authorized verification checklist. PR CI remains the broad integration gate.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): retry DMs while LID identity is unavailable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: WhatsApp DMs are silently lost when their LID-to-phone mapping becomes available after intake.

Supersedes #158140, thanks @YangManBOBO.

Part of #119475

## User Impact

DMs from `@lid` and `@hosted.lid` remain eligible for delivery while their phone mapping is temporarily unavailable. The mapped phone still goes through the existing sender authorization policy. Group handling is unchanged.

Permanently unresolved messages use the existing shared retry policy: exponential backoff capped at three minutes, dead-lettering after both the eight-attempt floor and 24-hour minimum age. A pending message can hold its conversation lane.

## Why This Change Was Made

Throwing for an unresolved direct LID lets the existing durable ingress owner retry instead of completing a non-message. Completed-message receipt preparation catches normalization failures per message so a lost mapping cannot abort later messages in the same batch. Deduplication uses the existing transport-key completion tombstone.

Open overlap #106998 (`c281acb789bec20665a9d9bd395e22be00606372`) changes group classification and quoted-message identity metadata. Its resolver retains the unresolved-mapping `null` contract. It neither covers nor conflicts with this retry behavior; this fix works independently.

## Evidence

- **Red:** [PR-scoped CI 41934554000](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41934554000/job/126940438284), regression-only `495e731ad8c6e7e2c6f9728a0d90b2579618b979` on main `8c9310ee36391c657104e2bb3f5cd17c7154e49c`: Node and Bun each **5 failed / 17 passed**. Every new case found an empty queue instead of a retained retry through `messages.upsert` and the real durable monitor.
- **Green:** `15728d5dd790e464fcf5b3c126668fd7c9028ee7`; [exact-head WhatsApp job 126959246973](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41940098616/job/126959246973) passes **22/22 touched-file cases on both Node and Bun**, including permanently unresolved identities across eight persisted failures and the 24-hour bound. The containing worker shard passes **48/48 tests on both runtimes**; affected sibling shards pass **48, 81, and 1 cases per runtime**. Production/test types, lint, documentation/format, baseline ratchets, and UI performance checks also pass. The later [ordinary PR CI 41943175069](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41943175069), event `pull_request`, completed **SUCCESS** at this exact head: all 60 jobs completed success/skipped, zero failures. Combined dependency/security/ci-gate status is also **SUCCESS**. The earlier workflow-dispatch run 41940098616 separately has a verified inherited `tokenjuice` dependency failure; [scheduled main job 126937006082](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41933643248/job/126937006082) records the identical failure on the unchanged perf file. That historical failure is retained as evidence and is not the later successful ordinary CI. No rerun or admin exception is used.
- Coverage: both LID domains, mapped-phone allowlist acceptance/rejection, no read/pairing side effects before resolution, single delivery after recovery and completed redelivery, batch continuation, and the shared retry bound across restarts. Transport and identities are synthetic; the authorization fixture calls the real stable ingress resolver.
- Independent **Codex autoreview**, full diff from integrated main `2d0e42c125057af4321fe1c67ebea0282a886620`, candidate tree `8b002f1c9df85ef0e3d287b2cfa0f139ffd9e75c`: **P0–P2 scoped-clean**, static review with no test execution. ClawSweeper’s earlier finding on test-only head `495e731` (missing runtime repair) is addressed by the production hunks and green proof. Main was integrated for a named failing UI-size comparison gate; WhatsApp/ingress owners were unchanged and the PR still contains only four intended files.
- Production: **+11/-1, net +10**, needed for retry classification and completed-receipt recovery; there is no equivalent dead code to remove within this owner change. Tests: **+102 LF**, with an exact separate allocation. `git diff --check` passes.
- Named command: `pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/monitor-inbox.delivery-and-dedupe.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Local execution was avoided because cold worker preparation compiles a broad graph on this production host. Standalone one-worker wall time is unmeasured; the red single-file CI shard measured **109.08s Node / 29.73s Bun**, including transforms. The final five-file worker shard measured **102.65s Node / 40.68s Bun**. Testbox was queued and its owned lease stopped; PR CI supplies broad proof.
- Both original commits are unique to the PR and share one human author. Each replacement commit carries exactly one `Co-authored-by: 潘晓波0668000512 <pan.xiaobo@xydigit.com>`. Contributor code was read only with `gh pr view/diff`, never checked out or run.
- No live WhatsApp/Gateway roundtrip was exercised; real-client recovery remains unverified. No inherited-failure waiver is claimed. This addresses only the transient direct-message mapping subset of #119475; group and other LID symptoms remain outside scope. This same-repository branch is writable by repository maintainers; GitHub rejects the fork-only collaboration toggle for it.

prs.title: fix(auth): inline API-key failures break on PostgreSQL agent stores
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Gateway using PostgreSQL agent storage cannot record an authentication failure for a config-backed API key and instead reports “PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker.”

## User Impact

User impact: inline API-key failure bookkeeping completes on PostgreSQL without a spurious database-thread error. The caller keeps its normal provider sign-in error, and SQLite keeps its existing behavior. No schema, configuration, public API, or migration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The operation already captures the agent database execution before asynchronous preparation. Pass that execution to the existing worker store instead of acquiring a second, native database handle on the Gateway thread. Write ordering, live-owner checks, transaction/publication handling, and cleanup remain with their existing owners.

The simplification removes nine net production lines (mostly wrapper removal; the larger displayed diff is indentation). The regression reuses the existing Gateway-thread subprocess harness and production retry controller. Its 138 new test/support lines have a separate test-line allocation; the shared budget is unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Before:** on base `975e68cf820a536e068a3c04fdc511ac28005693`, the PostgreSQL 17.6 Gateway-role probe exits 1 at `withOpenClawAgentDatabaseRuntime` with the main-thread guard error. The same probe succeeds on SQLite.
- **After:** the PostgreSQL probe succeeds and both caller-visible and persisted failure counters equal 1. Unrelated main-thread PostgreSQL SQL still refuses before and after the operation.
- **Focused conformance:** 15/15 tests pass: the new PostgreSQL/SQLite subprocess regression (2 tests, 3.92 s file duration) plus the existing inline-auth worker suite (13 tests, 10.90 s). The complete focused invocation, including preparation, took 50.62 s. CI timings are not yet available.
- **Static checks:** core typecheck, state/logging test typecheck, lint and formatting on all four TypeScript files, staged whitespace check, and test-line ratchet pass.
- **Independent review:** bound Auto Review, OpenClaw engine / `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, local candidate against the exact base above, P0–P2 coverage: `scoped-clean` with no findings. The reviewer inspected source and supplied results; it did not independently rerun tests.

### Full built-Gateway before/after proof

Ran on 2026-11-01 at 01:28 UTC with real PostgreSQL 17.6 and isolated state. Both source snapshots were built through the supported `sourcePerformance` build profile: baseline `975e68cf820a536e068a3c04fdc511ac28005693` and this exact PR head `1c4c86387d86ed90417d22776034807461026cca`. The PR source tree was verified as `3c41427fbe1ce1c3318095f9dd3f0a7939c9356f`.

Each case launched its own **actual built Gateway process**, connected an authenticated normal test client, then executed `sessions.create → chat.send → agent.wait → chat.history`. A loopback OpenAI-compatible provider fixture received the real configured API-key request and returned HTTP 401 with `authentication_error / invalid_api_key`. Gateway execution, model routing, the retry controller, transcript persistence, and database writes were real—not mocked or called directly by the fixture.

| Built revision | Agent engine | Provider requests | Persisted inline errorCount | Forbidden native-open diagnostic | Public terminal/history |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| baseline `975e68c` | PostgreSQL | 1 | 0 | Present | Normal sign-in error; 2 history messages |
| PR `1c4c863` | PostgreSQL | 1 | 1 | Absent | Same sign-in error; 2 history messages |
| baseline `975e68c` | SQLite | 1 | 1 | Absent | Same sign-in error; 2 history messages |
| PR `1c4c863` | SQLite | 1 | 1 | Absent | Same sign-in error; 2 history messages |

Every request's Authorization header matched the synthetic config-backed key. The terminal status is intentionally `error` because the provider returns 401; the public error remains “Couldn't sign in to the AI service.” This fix repairs the missing durable bookkeeping and spurious internal database error, **not** the provider's authentication failure. Counters were read from the actual agent store after each Gateway stopped; no expected counter was seeded.

The live WebSocket hello reported the expected build identity in each case:

- Baseline: `2026.10.9-975e68cf820a-2026-11-01T01-07-49.804Z`
- PR: `2026.10.9-1c4c86387d86-2026-11-01T01-09-15.610Z`

The repository E2E runner completed all four arms successfully: one fixture test, **32.36 s** of test time, **80.25 s** file duration / **91.44 s** complete successful invocation including compiled-process preparation. Temporary fixture SHA-256: `f76e215c18c96949a8943597c5b9fd373a9c6abcce31e08e7bb18e4b22859151`; inspected result JSON SHA-256: `6474feafe5a94de5af25491bffe45b555818e2b2dd0b349b1db4d7cb66c6128e`. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter web_search cannot consume an admitted native xAI Responses search offer.

## User Impact

The actual web_search consumer can use the frozen grok-4.7 model through a qualified native or manifest ClawRouter offer. It resolves only ClawRouter credentials and refreshes admission for each invocation. No route, model, tariff, or dedicated x_search tool is activated by this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native xAI tools and ClawRouter now share one Responses request/text/citation codec. Model-specific native xAI reasoning policy stays in the native plugin. The client requires matching endpoint formats, supported low effort, declared web_search, and versioned hosted-tool admission. It sends one search tool with store:false, refuses POST redirects, bounds and wraps answer text, drops credential-bearing citation URLs, and does not expose unqualified inline offsets. Incomplete and failed responses remain errors; neither errors nor citation counts establish cost.

This consumes the source contract in https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/559 (landed f62fa89aef9a3ae74362d15f0ec86120d78692f2). Worker dispatch/accounting and catalog activation remain their respective owners' prerequisites; actual Worker-to-consumer acceptance remains pending.

## Evidence

- Frozen base: cafb1d2080edb528442e7a3107f6378202d32a71. Candidate: 68537623bd672f194d1722398587e036532314cc. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41654635488) selected that exact checkout (preflight125981589903); workflow SHA is not the tested source SHA.

These fixtures are source, not yet passing runtime proof. Existing native xAI web/x/code tests and the relocated parser tests remain required.
- Production types125982832813 and test types125982831985/125982832026/125982832597 passed. [Build125982825829](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41654635488/job/125982825829) passed with checkout/artifact revision68537623bd672f194d1722398587e036532314cc; public SDK declaration graph5010853 bytes is below its qualified5315536-byte limit. - [SDK API report125982827770](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41654635488/job/125982827770) exceeded its30-minute job limit and was cancelled. No completed API difference report is claimed.
- Actual-consumer coverage remains unproven in this manual run. Preflight selected candidate68537623bd672f194d1722398587e036532314cc and workflowce6257dd8bb62b78d443d8d9135a1c4ffa5821a9. The frozen-target branch in the workflow's `scripts/ci-build-manifest.mjs` imports the trusted harness planner. Its static `test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs` lacks `src/agents/tools/web-search.clawrouter.test.ts`; this candidate adds that required host-SQLite registration. No matching consumer result was found in the inspected agent-tools/infra jobs. A candidate-aware focused native test result remains necessary; neither removing SQLite ownership nor a green unrelated shard substitutes for it.
- Current failed surfaces include UI config runtime.subscribe, UI auth no-shadow, control-ui fallback-catalog drift, Brave/Firecrawl settings-editor timeouts, Knip unused exports, deferred OpenResponses SSE terminal, Discord identity pending state, hooks allowedAgentIds event timing, and update-resume plugin completion. These are not declared upstream solely because the named files are unchanged. Existing baseline CI41650742758 stopped at security-fast and did not qualify these semantic surfaces. The full run remains in progress; no completed semantic suite was retried and no failed gate was bypassed.
- Native test-line checker: exact base has 6,433,127 lines / 6,432,733 ceiling (394 inherited debt; delta 0). This branch has 6,433,480 / 6,433,086 (same 394 debt; delta +353). The separate 353-line allocation exactly covers the actual consumer regression fixture and parser security assertion; the shared scalar is unchanged. prs.title: fix(macos): New Thread exhausts memory during session creation
prs.body:
Closes #186215

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native macOS New Thread hanging and allocating unbounded memory when creating a conversation.

## User Impact

Native Mac users can create a thread through the sidebar or keyboard shortcut without entering recursive session creation. A missing or retired Gateway connection is rejected rather than silently retargeted. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mac transport now routes ordinary creation through its existing captured new-session lease. This replaces the recursive default-dispatch path without introducing another request builder or changing generic transports and iOS.

## Evidence

Product head: `2b916adf3896eb18fb11d7702c9dd203fa1aaecf` (unchanged).

- **Native regression/build:** [baseline red 40568043055](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40568043055); [exact-head native build and 35/35 mapping tests 40577761227](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/40577761227). SwiftFormat required changes in 0/416 source and 0/33 test files. Lint passed with one nonblocking `file_length` advisory in untouched `DashboardManager.swift:1642` (1505/1500), covered by `LIMIT_RULES`; not zero warnings.
- **Shared consumer validation: PASS.** Canonical [run 41741119844](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/41741119844) succeeded on the exact product checkout above, using fork workflow SHA `d8aaa1f4648d6a7375c20760baaa7bdd794f42e0`. Swift Testing executed **104 tests in 4 suites**, all passed after **1.000 seconds** (compilation: 1483.64 seconds). All three requested suites explicitly passed: `ChatViewModelSessionActionTests` (0.855s), `ChatGatewayTransportTests` (0.006s), and `ChatGatewayRequestTests` (0.111s); additional `ChatGatewayPayloadCodecTests` passed (0.024s). These are suite durations, not invented per-suite test counts. The XCTest bootstrap's zero-test message is not the selected Swift Testing result.
- **Inspectable shared artifact:** [13282253631](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/41741119844/artifacts/13282253631), GitHub SHA-256 `4e365458a53eef598c352ec68a930d9b3dc7d3243755a9a0eed018c19e1aeb8a`. @harjothkhara downloaded and read `source-and-toolchain.log` and `shared-consumer-tests.log`; public run success/workflow identity and artifact digest were verified here. Hosted `macos-26-intel`, Xcode 26.6 (17F113), Swift 6.3.3, Node 24.22.1; normal `setup-node-env` and `node scripts/prepare-apple-mermaid.mjs`, no source/test edits or full app build. Initial focused run 41739785982 was canceled before tests; 41740028156 failed missing generated Mermaid resources before tests. Those setup outcomes are not product defects; 41741119844 is the canonical executed result.
- **Actual native flow, full observer INCOMPLETE:** [run 41724743098](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/41724743098), [artifact 13279006255](https://github.com/harjothkhara/openclaw/actions/runs/41724743098/artifacts/13279006255), proof SHA `277557c120bea8530cfb2cb4b3ea6b2cbc9375cd`, targeted the same product head. Coordinator-inspected artifact records exactly one verified native New Thread AXPress and exactly one native `openclaw-macos` / `operator` `sessions.create`, succeeded for `agent:main:ios-2195ed8d-9dc4-4f7b-9243-95f0e69875a3`, followed by successful `sessions.messages.subscribe` and `chat.history` for that key. The main parent was initialized through the public Gateway first. RSS: 57 samples / 6.178 seconds; first 177428 KiB, last/peak 181316 KiB, no observed runaway, normal cleanup. The workflow nevertheless failed in phase `stability`: post-action `ax-copy-key` hit `TargetedMenu.deadline` at ~3032 ms. No after screenshot or post-inventory exists; this is **not a full harness pass**.
- **Relevant upstream workflows succeeded:** [CI 41738331438](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41738331438), [Security 41738331887](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41738331887), [OpenGrep 41738331471](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41738331471), and [Periphery 41738331200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41738331200), including macOS/iOS consumer reports. Ordinary-PR native Swift jobs were intentionally skipped; the standalone artifact above supplies the shared-suite execution, not ordinary PR CI.

### Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Native macOS New Thread must avoid recursive creation defaults and unbounded allocation and reach normal Gateway creation/error handling.
- **Real environment tested:** The exact-head native app plus isolated public Gateway on hosted Mac infrastructure; shared suites on the exact same product source with the toolchain above.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Connect the native app with an existing public-API-initialized main parent and invoke native Thread → New Thread once, recording RPCs/RSS. Shared validation: `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --scratch-path "$RUNNER_TEMP/session-test-build" --disable-index-store -Xswiftc -gline-tables-only --no-parallel --filter 'ChatViewModelSessionActionTests|ChatGatewayTransportTests|ChatGatewayRequestTests'`.
- **Evidence after fix:** Baseline regression red; exact-head native build and 35/35 mapping tests; successful actual native create → subscribe → history; standalone Swift Testing **104 tests in 4 suites passed**, with all three requested suites explicitly successful.
- **Observed result after fix:** The native action crossed the transport boundary once, created the new session and subscribed/loaded history for its key, without runaway allocation in the sampled interval. Shared consumer validation passed. The later copy-key observer timed out, so the full app-proof verdict remains incomplete.
- **What was not tested:** No after image/rendered success-or-error proof, completed clipboard active-key/stability check, or post-action durable-ID inventory is available. The short RSS sample is not long-duration memory proof. A second complete baseline-app build is not supplied; parent-selection PR #189467 and other PRs remain separate scope.

The PR remains open and ready for maintainer review, not merged. The former shared-suite evidence gap is now supplied by the canonical standalone result; no additional tests, harness changes, or duplicate runs were made. Fresh review is requested against this updated evidence; its acceptance/completion must be read separately.

Contributor: @harjothkhara.

prs.title: fix(macos): avoid startup crashes from invalid custom Gateway hosts
prs.body:
Closes #187602

## What Problem This Solves

Invalid saved custom Gateway hosts can crash the macOS app at startup or endpoint refresh. Configuration errors can also become stuck as ownership failures after the host is corrected.

## User Impact

The app displays an actionable IPv4 configuration error and recovers after host-only correction without silently choosing another Gateway, rewriting settings, or enabling unsupported IPv6 binding. Genuine ownership conflicts remain blocked. No new configuration, dependency, database schema or state owner is introduced.

Scope decision, 1 November: keep this PR focused on endpoint crash safety and configuration recovery. The first-launch updater/runtime-pin ordering failure discovered during validation is a separate repair task; it is not claimed fixed by this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing endpoint owner validates custom IPv4 binding before URL construction and publishes failures through its unavailable state. The process manager distinguishes retained ownership conflicts from recoverable configuration errors, preserving background activation intent.

The latest commit repairs only regression-test actor isolation and uses existing AppState owner APIs for the companion control; no production API or test-only production hook was added.

## Evidence

Head: b4f7c8a154db40acaf0bddc7238e91707630cf23. Verified source tree: 3435fc0d2bd99465ced7827deadd15675dd5800a. Native execution below was supplied from isolated macOS workers, not performed by this Linux session.

| Check | Verified result / limit |
| --- | --- |
| Exact-head native build and complete affected suites | New unmodified-head native log: build complete; all 158 tests in GatewayEndpointStoreTests and GatewayProcessManagerTests pass, including invalid-host and companion-conflict cases. This supersedes the earlier 87/87-only evidence. Remaining-validation ZIP CRC and all 21 listed SHA-256 checks pass. No rerun needed. |
| Actual packaged-app behavior | Both invalid hosts leave the app alive with field-specific errors. A pre-paired live transition recovers after host-only correction under the same app PID, with a new Gateway child and paired-node reconnection. A real cross-profile conflict is rejected while the original remains sole listener. |
| Formatting, lint and localization | Pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 passes the full macOS scope: 0/417 source files and 0/33 other files need formatting. SwiftLint 0.65.1 reports two unchanged file-length violations, reproduced with identical locations/counts on clean base: DashboardManager.swift 1505 and GatewayConnection.swift 1501. This is attributed baseline failure, not a lint pass. Diff whitespace and native localization pass. |
| Review and CI | Independent Auto Review through P2 is clean against base 6941b99db5206045d1508a9717990f1f80999486. Latest completed ClawSweeper review of this head finds no actionable code defect and accepts app behavior proof. Exact-head CI/security gates and native localization pass; automatic PR planning leaves macOS execution unselected. The separate canceled ClawSweeper dispatcher is not a product test failure. |
| Retained-profile upgrade | A complete paired schema-20 baseline is retained through recovery: the candidate app/child identity is linked, authenticated health and approved paired-node reconnection pass after ordinary relaunch, and schema-36 integrity, host/port/token and pairing data persist. First launch still fails; a separate trace now identifies old-runtime selection after schema migration. Upgrade availability remains red. |

### Actual-app host correction

Both captures use the repaired candidate: they compare configuration states, not base versus fix. The original app archive's CRC and all 21 listed SHA-256 checks pass; native captures were inspected and cropped before publication. Task-only credentialless Tart guests used macOS 26.6.2 / Xcode 27 and were cleaned up without operator-state changes. Packaging is ad-hoc debug, not release-signing proof.

**Before correcting the host — the app remains alive with an actionable error.**

![Invalid saved custom host: native app remains alive with actionable IPv4 configuration error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28922dac-1ce6-47e6-82ae-1e8dc2ada601)

**After correcting only the host — same app process, background recovery.** Health and the pre-paired node independently corroborate recovery. The lower health subrow remains pending and is not claimed fixed.

![Host-only correction: same native app process recovers its configured Gateway in the background](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/277d798f-075f-4e7e-a235-c7de8685856e)

<details>
<summary>Conflict controls and app-proof limits</summary>

![Real cross-profile ownership conflict remains rejected in the native Connection window](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dfff262a-9ef9-43c6-9a54-c0cb08f6db4d)

![Hostname containing spaces yields the actionable native IPv4 configuration error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/42c3e3c1-2001-49c5-bed5-716131cacdbe)

The pre-paired transition, not the first run's initial pairing, proves authenticated background recovery. Settled invalid-state samples show the owned child/listeners gone; host correction starts a new child under the same app PID without Retry, reactivation, relaunch or new pairing. Observed listeners/selected route show no substitute Gateway, not exhaustive outbound tracing or zero-credential-exposure proof. Stale/pending presentation rows are disclosed, not fixed. An exploratory 127.0.0.2 bind failure is excluded; successful app runs use real interface IPv4 addresses.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Complete native tests and controlled regression comparison</summary>

The new supplied clean exact-head run uses swift test --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --disable-index-store -Xswiftc -gline-tables-only --filter "GatewayEndpointStoreTests|GatewayProcessManagerTests". Raw output records Build complete! (242.37s), both suites passing and 158 tests passing in 20.886 seconds. The earlier inspected 87/87 process-manager addendum remains valid but is no longer the largest current-head result.

Whole-commit endpoint comparison used base 6941b99db5206045d1508a9717990f1f80999486, reversing the complete base-to-head diff rather than replacing one manager file. The same comparison-compatible test overlay compiled on both sides; resulting production-file hashes matched clean base. Base: 71 endpoint tests, eight invalid-host failures (five SIGTRAP and three incorrect unavailable-state results). Restored head: 71/71 pass, including those same eight cases. This proves endpoint regression red/green against the whole original base; it is not a whole-6ba0edd process-manager comparison. The earlier targeted prior-manager substitution separately failed four recovery cases/eight issues; retain that narrower scope rather than relabeling it.

Test-overlay compatibility changes are limited to makeStore visibility and try! bridging of the base's nonthrowing source-snapshot API. The new unmodified-head 158-test run is separate from that comparison overlay. Production remains unchanged from 93d7bdda13036d283cdde9d7b316e38f7b130b47; the latest source successor repairs tests only.

Source/test accounting covers local/custom IPv4 and TLS, tailnet selection/fallback, credentials, direct/SSH routing and unconfigured handling. Remote/unconfigured branches do not construct the unused invalid local URL. Actual-app proof independently establishes completed recovery beyond unit-test admission.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Retained-profile recovery and reproduced first-launch updater failure</summary>

The earlier versioned pack's 14 checksums and CRC pass; it established candidate schema-36 health but lacked complete baseline/parent identity. The new remaining-validation pack supplies a complete SQLite backup API baseline after release pairing: schema 20, integrity OK, one paired-device row, authenticated release health and a connected approved node. Release app/child/listener were stopped before candidate replacement. The candidate build uses PR-head logic with only a guest-only package.json version bump to 2026.10.10, production bundle ID, ad-hoc signature and omitted optional MLX helper—not byte-identical head or signed Sparkle delivery. onboardingSeen was set manually in the disposable profile.

Initial launch failed after five starts with exit 78 in two fresh retained-profile fixtures. Ordinary quit/relaunch recovered the first: Gateway PID 17367 is a child of app PID 16942; executable mapping and health childRuntime.execPath identify candidate Bun. Health returns ok=true/coreReady=true, schema 36 remains integral, and token hash, paired-device row and node ID persist; node status is paired=true, connected=true, approvalState=approved. Native captures show the initial error and later ready screen. A second profile eventually recovered with Retry; its Retry trace does not identify its initial failing child. Neither recovery erases first-launch failure.

A separate first-failure packet (CRC pass; no internal checksum manifest) positively identifies three initial Gateway children under the candidate app PID. At 18:50:36 the database is schema 20 and runtime/current names release 2026.10.9. At 18:50:37 it is schema 36 while the pointer is still the release. At 18:50:40, 18:50:46 and 18:50:50 the captured Gateway executable and entrypoint are all from that old release. The refusal identifies 8b18b55, supporting schema 20, opening schema 36. Only at 18:51:09 does runtime/current name the candidate; the pin readback remains migrationPending. The sampler is not a complete attempt count. The candidate-bundled credential doctor precedes the schema change, but the trace does not identify its internal writer operation.

Source inspection matches the ordering: MenuBar runs ClientCredentialStartup.prepare before normal launch; that owner invokes the candidate bundle's credential doctor. GatewayProcessManager+Hosting.startAppHostedGateway selects currentBundledRuntime for migrationPending, and that helper returns the already seeded runtime before seeding the replacement. These owners, plus BundledRuntime+Seeding, are byte-identical to PR base 6941b99; the PR's process-manager delta only separates endpoint configuration errors from ownership errors. prs.title: fix(ios): show agent pictures and enlarge Duo side controls
prs.body:
Closes #191539

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agent profile pictures appearing as initials in the native iOS picker, agent list, and chat toolbar even when the same agent has a picture on desktop.

## User Impact

Existing inline and Gateway-served agent pictures now appear in those iOS views. Agents without a readable picture keep their emoji or initials and status indicator. In a phone side toolbar, the sidebar, agent, and actions artwork is 30% larger with 52-point tap targets; horizontal toolbar sizes stay unchanged. Raw SVG pictures still fall back to emoji or initials.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native views only consumed badge text. They now use the existing agent identity image, including workspace identity lookup when the roster omits it. Image loading reuses the shared source policy and authenticated Gateway resource loader, with bounded decoding and route-scoped invalidation. The chat presentation retains its selected image while a response is pinned.

Colin encouraged the agent-picture scope in the iOS Discord thread on November 2.

### Duo toolbar sizing rationale

The larger artwork is a visual-proportion and usability refinement for the Duo's native side-toolbar area. On the physical device, the original fixed-size glyphs looked small beside the nearby system status indicators. The intent is to make the sidebar, agent/status, and actions controls easier to recognize and better balanced within that area.

The artwork is 30% larger, with 52-point tap targets that contain the enlarged controls. This adjustment follows the actual vertical phone-toolbar environment rather than screen dimensions; standard horizontal iPhone toolbars retain their existing artwork and 44-point targets. Brian checked the result on the closed and unfolded Duo and confirmed that the size feels right and all three controls work.

[Apple's Duo guidance](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-iphone-duo#Vertical-controls) supports native side placement, safe-area-aware layout, and consistent control ordering across poses. The 30% enlargement and 52-point targets are our tested design proposal, not Apple-prescribed dimensions or a requirement to match system status icons. Available space varies by pose, so the system continues to own placement and overflow.

**iOS owner decision requested:** Accept the Duo sizing refinement, or request an adjustment before merge. The earlier encouragement for agent pictures is not being presented as approval of these sizing values.

The original branch included a fixture-function extraction to unblock the normal iOS SwiftLint build step. That cleanup has since landed on main in #191296. The conflict repair retains main's fixture implementation unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on a physical iPhone Duo: Sparx had a picture on desktop and initials on iOS before the fix.
- Installed the signed development build on the same Duo. Brian confirmed the picture matches desktop, initials remain for an agent without a picture, switching back restores the photo, and the unfolded view looks correct.
- Full signed iOS build passed, including normal SwiftFormat and SwiftLint phases.
- 29 focused avatar, sidebar, and typography tests passed on a standard iPhone 17 Pro simulator running iOS 27.0. The two existing UI tests covering the extracted review-demo fixtures passed on the earlier avatar-only snapshot; those fixture bytes are unchanged.
- Brian confirmed the final toolbar size on the physical Duo, closed and unfolded, and verified the sidebar, agent/status, and actions controls all open normally. The built app also retains the standard horizontal toolbar on the iPhone 17 Pro simulator.
- The final Duo toolbar UI test passed on iOS 27.1: visible artwork, minimum target bounds, status popover behavior, and the actions-to-Settings flow.
- Native i18n verification passed with no inventory changes. `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent static review of the complete local patch by a separate task agent found no remaining actionable findings. This is not a ClawSweeper verdict or maintainer approval. Avatar commit `4aacaf360ec` and the subsequent four-file toolbar delta `73fe783e0f3` received separate independent passes with no remaining actionable findings. Source hashes and local test results are retained for the final committed range.

### Conflict repair, November 4

Merged main `648b2dd65c578bab7bf34662c658a9515fc16c6c` into the existing branch and kept its fixture cleanup. Updated one stale sidebar regression expectation to match the `displayRows(pinnedSessionNodes)` call introduced on main by #190403. No avatar or toolbar design changes were made.

The merged source passed a fresh native simulator build, all 30 focused avatar/sidebar/typography tests, affected SwiftFormat/SwiftLint checks, and an independent integration review. Published head: `d037fd418fbffc23c7c1f88525ffe73f07b137f8`.

The physical-device checks and screenshots below remain evidence from `73fe783e0f3eb57ef12571c5f53c60c95edc49f6`; the avatar-loading and toolbar-sizing implementations are unchanged by this repair. These earlier checks are not being presented as new-head CI or a fresh physical-device run. Current-head hosted CI and review remain separate from this local validation and from the requested iOS owner sizing decision.

Before and after below are matching crops of native physical-device screenshots. Only the avatar control is retained so private chat and Gateway details are excluded. No avatar pixels were generated or modified.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Native iOS avatar before: initials](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6353f10b-0f4c-4720-901e-7f804435053d) | ![Native iOS avatar after: configured photo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ca0aaa7-5f4e-4bf8-944f-6f53b64f6fc3) |

The toolbar comparison below uses matching crops from the same native offline Duo fixture before and after the sizing change. The physical Duo interaction check is reported separately above.

| Toolbar before | Toolbar after |
| --- | --- |
| ![Duo side toolbar before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7763da45-0fea-441f-8391-e439762fa3b9) | ![Duo side toolbar after: larger controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf1c1740-f095-4e71-917d-c014b36894d0) |

### Wider toolbar proportion comparison

These matching 1398 × 1450 crops retain the full screen width and show the toolbar beside the chat and system status icons. They come from the same native offline Duo fixture as the close-ups above, with identical crop bounds and no resizing. The chat scroll position differs slightly; the toolbar and surrounding UI retain their original scale. Only synthetic demo content is included. Physical-device checks are reported separately above.

| Wider view before | Wider view after |
| --- | --- |
| ![Duo toolbar before, with screen context](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2fc680d6-f371-4581-b5d5-8c58b3c13d72) | ![Duo toolbar after, with screen context](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05cc0664-dabc-41e7-8c87-89c2edd13149) |

The physical picture path was exercised against the existing Gateway. Raw SVG rendering is outside this patch; unsupported or unreadable images use the existing fallback. The side-control sizing is a small refinement of Apple’s adaptive toolbar: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-iphone-duo. No app release or App Store submission is included.

The standard iPhone UI automation runner stalled before starting the test and was stopped after diagnosis. The app itself launched and rendered its horizontal toolbar normally; this is visual inspection rather than a passing standard-iPhone UI automation result.
