prs.title: fix(macos): preserve shortcuts pressed while the dashboard opens
prs.body:
Closes #187486

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes New Session and Command Palette shortcuts silently disappearing when pressed while the macOS dashboard is opening.

## User Impact

With the updated Mac app and Control UI, the first ⌘N or ⌘K waits for the dashboard's listeners instead of requiring another keypress. Older shared-credential UI bundles retain their historical document-load delivery and open-only search fallback; this does not retroactively repair delayed startup in already-built older bundles.

**Validation status:** The native delayed-listener regression is red on the comparison base and green on this exact head. A newly supplied November 1 packaged-app trace covers actual guest ⌘K during an induced startup delay, followed by the native event and visible palette after import of the current UI. This is supplied Mac-run evidence, not a new native run by the publisher, and the six-second delay is test-only. The required CI gate and completed Periphery report builds passed; inherited local matrix/SwiftLint failures remain disclosed below. The completed November 1 exact-head review inspected the supplied startup captures and public observer fixture, accepted them as sufficient shipped-entry-point proof, and reports no actionable findings. The code and head remain unchanged; human maintainer review and any merge decision remain separate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing dashboard controller remains the ordered command-queue owner, and the shell remains the listener-readiness owner. The HTML boot script declares pending readiness before deferred startup; native dispatch observes readiness for every authentication mode. An absent protocol is accepted only for legacy non-browser-identity documents, never an explicit false value. No retry timer, second queue, or replay mechanism was added.

The existing 120-second document-load timeout throws; it is not a delivery fallback. Legacy compatibility uses the explicit undefined-only readiness probe and the existing cancelable-toggle/open-search fallback.

## Evidence

Tested head: 6ddf6c2900bb885d519eb849bf2cd2c48806564b.
Comparison base for native red proof: c0c068e1ecd9ec78a75ad6847e032f4d0f5b1241.

### Packaged-app startup trace — induced delay (November 1)

[Capture, fixture, and provenance supplied by @PollyBot13](https://gist.github.com/PollyBot13/2e4a03665ea2001157c9d2ede5ba0ec8), also linked in the [public proof supplement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188646#issuecomment-6556083073). The supplied run used the unmodified packaged app built from the tested head in a credentialless macOS 26.6.2 Tart guest and a loopback test Gateway.

Only a copied UI HTML module entry was replaced with a test fixture that waits six seconds before importing the reported byte-identical current UI module. **This is a deliberately induced startup interval, not a naturally observed six-second boot and not a production source change.** The fixture observes native events and polls readiness; it does not synthesize events, call preventDefault, or assign readiness.

The supplier reports closing the dashboard and delivering actual guest ⌘K with the packaged app foreground. The pending frame shows the reopened dashboard still loading with readiness=false; the delivered frame shows the command palette open after UI import. The visible overlay records:

| Observation | Time relative to copied HTML fixture |
| --- | ---: |
| HTML readiness=false | 0 ms |
| Begin importing current UI module | 6005 ms |
| Native toggle-search event observed (overlay label: native-command-palette) | 6296 ms |
| Poll observes shell readiness=true | 6308 ms |

**Sampling limit:** Readiness is polled every 20 ms. The sampled ready=true row appearing 12 ms after the event is not evidence that dispatch preceded the actual readiness assignment. No precise key-down timestamp is claimed. This visual startup trace is for ⌘K; the existing native regression covers both commands and the authentication matrix, while the earlier loaded-app captures cover ⌘N/⌘K with current and older UI bundles.

**Pending — dashboard reopened, UI import held, readiness=false**

![Supplied packaged-app startup capture with import delayed and readiness false](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7fa80f44-d6ed-4462-8c51-ca10c1bb751a)

**Delivered — current UI imported, native event recorded, command palette visible**

![Supplied packaged-app startup capture after import with native palette event and visible palette](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d726217-8c8d-43b0-9696-4a1e3ae629fb)

<details>
<summary>Capture provenance and artifact verification</summary>

Execution and binary-identity measurements are supplied provenance, not a publisher-run native reproduction. The record identifies packaged executable SHA-256 3a2e8dbf17495e0e0e7c538477bd0a11be6a7c3850ea2cf9e1fe4577d3f0c462 and original current UI index SHA-256 670eab030f346e3931a4b4874abc279179fd891e848472ec885b7879c1b39b72; the current JS module was reported byte-identical. Those binaries are not included in this packet for independent comparison here.

The five manifest entries in pr188646-roboclaw-proof-handoff-20261101.zip were verified; archive SHA-256 471a5e8d45303902a5104715d4b67d36b7b0062c34b76228532fec9a541907d7. The public gist's README, two SVGs, and delayed-boot.js were fetched and matched the supplied packet byte-for-byte. The fixture was inspected as source, not executed here. Both SVGs contain only the original embedded PNG; those PNG bytes were extracted unchanged, visually inspected for sensitive content, and attached above. The screenshot overlay is part of the supplied live capture, not a new annotation added during publication.

</details>

### Native execution

Requester-supplied evidence from a separate credentialless Tart macOS VM: macOS 26.6.2, Xcode 27.0 / Swift 6.4, Node 26.12.1. The logs were inspected here, not rerun on this Linux host.

- Swift test bundle built successfully on the fixed head (151.14 s) and on the comparison base with only the updated regression test overlaid (194.77 s). The overlay's resulting test-file blob matches the committed regression exactly.
- **Red:** On the base, completedDocumentsRetainCommandsUntilTheirShellListens failed the retained-queue assertion for token, password, and unauthenticated cases; the browser-identity control had no issue. The separate legacy waiter also timed out on the base; that timeout is not the shortcut regression's red target.
- **Green:** DashboardSandboxNavigationTests passed 12/12 test functions (5.246 s), including all four delayed-listener connection cases and both legacy/browser-identity compatibility cases. The tests cover ordered New Session/search/search delivery, repeated readiness without replay, ready-state use, and same-URL reload/stale wakeups.
- DashboardWindowSmokeTests passed 27/27 (5.501 s). DashboardWindowOwnershipTests passed 26/26 when run alone (25.849 s); this isolated pass does not erase the matrix failure below.
- SwiftFormat lint mode passed: zero files required formatting. SwiftLint did **not** pass globally: it reported file-length errors in unchanged DashboardManager.swift (1505 noncomment/nonblank lines) and GatewayConnection.swift (1501), with no changed-file violation. Both files are unchanged from the comparison base.
- The debug app packaged successfully, with its runtime integrity checks and build metadata identifying the exact tested head. Packaging is not proof of successful menu-shortcut delivery.

### Hosted CI

- [CI run 41193481206](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41193481206) completed on this PR head: all 65 jobs enumerated, 39 success and 26 skipped, with no failed or unfinished jobs. Selected UI checks and UI E2E shards passed.
- The [CI-gate job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41193481206/job/124516803542) and reconciled openclaw/ci-gate commit status passed. Dependency review and security-sensitive review passed; the latter reports no sensitive product changes.
- The hosted macos-swift entries were skipped. Native Swift execution evidence is the exact-head Mac VM proof above, not a claim that hosted Swift jobs ran.
- The separate [Periphery workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41193481221) completed: seven jobs passed, including both platform report builds, the selected shared-kit/macOS scans, and the intersection; the iOS dead-code scan was skipped. No unfinished job is being called a pass.

### Investigated native matrix failure

Two fixed-head named-profile matrix runs each failed one local-mode assertion in the unchanged "configured presentation uses its owned health probe" test at DashboardWindowOwnershipTests.swift:718: the selected loopback port differed from the fixture's port. Results: 76 tests / 8 suites, one issue each (47.135 s and 45.988 s).

The comparison-base matrix, omitting the changed shortcut suite, reproduced the same assertion failure: 64 tests / 7 suites, one issue (47.245 s). This establishes a base-existing matrix-only failure rather than a new #188646 regression. Its underlying shared-state/routing cause remains unresolved; no passing rerun is being presented as a repair.

### Actual app and older bundle coverage

- The earlier evidence packet’s keyboard-injection attempt was blocked by guest Automation permission prompts; it is not the success evidence. In the [author’s exact-head follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188646#issuecomment-6541882860), a separate credentialless macOS VM handled actual guest ⌘N and ⌘K in the packaged app, opening the new-session composer and command palette with the current UI. The published openclaw@2026.10.9 UI was then served into that app’s WebKit view and both shortcuts also worked. Execution and provenance are author-reported. The supplied GUI addendum is now available in this conversation: all five image checksums were verified and all five captures were visually inspected here. The four shortcut-result captures are included below.
- The earlier packet separately records byte-for-byte HTTP serving of the published older assets. Its index lacks the initial false readiness declaration; its core contains listener-time readiness signaling. Loaded-app shortcut compatibility is not a claim that this PR retroactively fixes delayed startup inside already-built old bundles.
- The deterministic native regression covers queued commands before listeners exist. The November 1 induced packaged-app ⌘K startup trace above additionally shows the pending and delivered states through the native app path. The four earlier GUI captures below remain loaded-app results, not startup-timing evidence.

<details>
<summary>Loaded-app shortcut captures: current UI and published older UI</summary>

These supplied images show the resulting loaded-app states, not the timing of keypress delivery or the pre-listener startup instant. The native red/green regression proves that boundary.

**Current UI — ⌘N: new-session composer**

![Current UI new-session composer after guest Command-N](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f8833a68-4497-40bf-b1a9-7916d80e0e4d)

**Current UI — ⌘K: command palette**

![Current UI command palette after guest Command-K](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd4ce2ea-3c30-4c57-9cc3-5acde59c2a84)

**Published openclaw@2026.10.9 UI — ⌘N: new-session composer**

![Published older UI new-session composer after guest Command-N](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b1441d0-10f1-43af-8623-00c55f75fc64)

**Published openclaw@2026.10.9 UI — ⌘K: command palette**

![Published older UI command palette after guest Command-K](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a65e6211-14b8-4867-ad94-2708e454c16b)

</details>

### UI checks and review

- The real HTML early-boot regression failed on base (document complete with readiness undefined) and passed with the new declaration.
- Focused UI tests: 41 passed (final local run 2.62 s wall time); UI typechecking, targeted lint/format, production UI build/startup budgets, whitespace and test-line budget checks passed. The packet also includes fixed-head UI test/typecheck/build logs.
- Independent local Auto Review (P0–P3), against the comparison base and full local candidate, found no actionable code defect; a later Promise-executor lint-only cleanup was revalidated.
- [November 1 hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188646#issuecomment-6532233125), reviewed at 09:50 UTC on the exact head above: **Ready for maintainer review**, **Findings: None**, **Before merge: None**. The [exact review execution](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41294537911) and [terminal finalization](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41294927080) completed successfully.
- The reviewer inspected the supplied startup captures and public observer fixture and says they satisfy the prior rank-up request. It classifies the proof path as the shipped entry point while retaining the induced six-second import delay, supplied execution provenance, readiness-sampling limit, and skipped hosted Swift jobs. No reviewer-executed native run or naturally slow six-second startup is claimed. Human maintainer judgment remains.

Evidence source: requester-provided issue-187486-pr188646-native-evidence.zip, SHA-256 c7361f2f93159113cc32a1103a0a0119d59e963f85cef1258137cc602aa99af7; all 18 manifest entries verified. Relevant logs: base-red-test.log, green-test.log, smoke-test.log, named-test.log, named2-test.log, recheck-test.log, and base-matrix-test.log. Checksums establish packet integrity, not independent rerun attestation. GUI addendum: pr188646-gui-addendum-20261031.zip, SHA-256 0797a4513648ba68a421971e9943afb16c406a5c5a0382246e968c37b63f5090; all five image manifest entries verified. The separate older-bundle landing capture was inspected but omitted from the gallery as redundant with its two shortcut-result captures.

Simplification: removed the authentication-mode readiness bypass and observer early return; reused the existing queue and lifecycle resets. Net production growth is seven lines. The 19-line UI regression has its own exact test-line allocation; the native regressions extend the existing owner suite.

Reported by @anmol0b in the linked issue; implementation requested by Eisenh0rn40.

prs.title: refactor(i18n): remove translation glossary enforcement
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The translation glossaries are not maintained consistently across supported languages. There is not currently bandwidth to bring every language’s glossary up to date and test its effect on translations. Rather than continue enforcing uneven terminology rules, this change removes the glossaries and their enforcement end to end.

## User Impact

Translation runs no longer load term dictionaries, inject glossary prompts, perform exact glossary substitutions, require glossary checks, or invalidate work using glossary hashes. Translation memory, normal language/register guidance, brand/code/placeholder protections, and source-identity checks remain.

## Why This Change Was Made

The translation glossaries are not maintained consistently across supported languages. There is not currently bandwidth to bring every language’s glossary up to date and test its effect on translations. Rather than continue enforcing uneven terminology rules, this change removes the glossaries and their enforcement end to end.

This removes an unevenly maintained policy rather than claiming glossaries are universally useless or assuming model quality makes testing unnecessary. Translation memory and the existing code, placeholder, and brand safeguards remain explicit requirements.

 This continues the verified handoff candidate from base `92d500f436eadb94613337886658e71e04521a6c` (source patch SHA-256 `672c322cd81e9b622e947af3b47b8102d4d2f5f3ab9812cfda2b956ceac5c2ef`). It removes dictionary files, loaders, prompt injection, substitutions, CI registrations, hashes, and obsolete tests/documentation across all three product pipelines. Historical release facts and unrelated memory-core concept vocabulary are intentionally preserved.

Native generated metadata is excluded from this source PR and belongs in a separate linked generated-output follow-on. The existing source/generated-artifact guard remains unchanged. The follow-on removes only `glossaryHash` from 21 native artifacts; all 97,104 translation values remain identical.

Companion publisher/parser PR: https://github.com/openclaw/docs/pull/302. The `openclaw/docs` lane owns that work. Eventual source-sync ordering: land this source removal first, then sync from that landed source or verify the publisher candidate is equivalent; do not resurrect removed dictionaries or glossary enforcement. Hannes subsequently authorized landing the product source removal first, then its native metadata follow-on. The docs owner must receive the verified source merge before landing/syncing copied removals.

## Evidence

- Verified the supplied ZIP and patch byte lengths and SHA-256 checksums; patch applied cleanly on its exact base. Fresh independent review found one brand-only gap: `LINE` was absent from the surviving protected-product list. ## What Problem This Solves

Multi-second `chat.send` current-session revalidation timings do not distinguish source preparation, ordered admission, pre-read checks, and the history reader response. This is a maintainer-requested diagnostics enhancement; no latency cause or performance fix is claimed.

## User Impact

Existing chat-send timing details gain four request-local measurements under `detail.admission.current_session`: `source_prepare`, `ordered_admission`, `read_barrier`, and `history_reader`. No configuration or operator action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing async-local observer and phase helper at the ordered-reader owner. Keep admission observations separate from persistence observations. Admission, FIFO ordering, cache decisions, authority checks, errors, and dispatch behavior are unchanged.

`read_barrier` measures admitted host source checks and cache lookup before the reader call. `history_reader` measures the reader call through its response, including downstream database/pool/RPC waits; it is omitted on a retained-fact hit. These are elapsed host spans, not native SQL execution measurements or an exhaustive additive partition of revalidation. Only fixed phase labels and durations are added.

prs.title: fix(codex): redact credentials in dynamic tool error content
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Thrown and failed Codex dynamic-tool paths were putting raw `errorMessage` / failure `message` text into `contentItems` without running it through `sanitizeToolResult`. Successful and middleware-adjusted result paths already redacted credentials, so a thrown tool error that embedded a bearer token (or similar secret) could still surface the credential in the app-server tool-result content.

**Configuration-dependent gap:** `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` → `redactSensitiveText` uses configured `logging.redactPatterns` **in place of** defaults. Model-visible `sanitizeToolResult` / `redactModelVisibleToolPayloadText` **combines** custom patterns with built-in tool payload patterns. So under a nonmatching custom `redactPatterns` config, diagnostic/error formatting alone still leaks an unregistered synthetic bearer, while catch-path `sanitizeToolResult` keeps built-in bearer protection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the shared `sanitizeToolResult` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime` on the two remaining failure content builders:

- `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` catch path in `dynamic-tools.ts` (thrown execution errors)
- `createFailedDynamicToolResponse` in `dynamic-tool-response-state.ts` (failed response factory)

Non-goals: no change to success-path redaction, budget truncation, or middleware ordering.

## User Impact

**Before:** A dynamic tool that threw (or failed via the shared failed-response helper) could return `contentItems` containing unsanitized credentials from the error text — especially when `logging.redactPatterns` replaced diagnostic defaults with patterns that do not cover bearer tokens.

**After:** Thrown/failed dynamic-tool error content is redacted with the same `sanitizeToolResult` used on successful result content (built-ins always apply for model-visible output).

## Evidence

- Production catch path: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.ts` now sets `text: sanitizeToolResult(errorMessage)`.
- Shared failed factory: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-response-state.ts` sanitizes the failure `message` before building `contentItems`.
- Regression: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts` spies `readLoggingConfig` with nonmatching `redactPatterns` `[String.raw`\bunrelated-only-[A-Za-z0-9]+\b`]`, asserts `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` still contains the synthetic bearer (before), and asserts model-visible `contentItems` do not (after `sanitizeToolResult`). Mock restored in `finally`.
- Diagnostic harness: `scripts/codex-dynamic-tool-error-redact-proof.mts` prints the actual protocol response JSON.





### Custom-pattern regression (exact head `67505f4ca5c4`)

```text
Product head: 67505f4ca5c482f9eac9474cd0a6f25bf4afc2bd
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.thrown-error-redaction.test.ts --reporter=verbose
PASS redacts credentials from thrown dynamic tool error content items under custom logging patterns
```

Configures logging.redactPatterns=["never-match-custom-redact-pattern-141271"] via isolated OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH so formatToolExecutionErrorMessage still contains the synthetic bearer (defaults bypassed), then asserts the bridge response does not.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Thrown dynamic-tool error content could include unsanitized credentials when diagnostic redact patterns replace defaults.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` → tool `execute` throws → `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` → catch builds `contentItems` with `sanitizeToolResult(errorMessage)` → `toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse`.
- **Boundary crossed:** Extension dynamic-tool error content → shared `sanitizeToolResult` from plugin-sdk agent-harness-runtime (model-visible policy merges built-ins).
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused existing `sanitizeToolResult`; no new helper.
- **Real environment tested:** Local diagnostic harness against production `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` + `toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse` under custom `logging.redactPatterns`. **Live Codex binary was NOT used** — this records the actual protocol response object returned toward Codex, not a full app-server binary round-trip.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/codex-dynamic-tool-error-redact-proof.mts
# writes /workspace/codex-runtime-proof.txt
```

- **Evidence after fix (diagnostic transcript):**

```text
# Codex dynamic-tool thrown-error redaction diagnostic
# Generated: 2026-09-07T14:53:48.289Z (UTC)
# Proof surface: createCodexDynamicToolBridge → handleToolCall catch path
#               → toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse (JSON contentItems)
# Live Codex binary: NOT used (unavailable / not required for this harness)
# Synthetic credential only — non-usable fixture.

logging.redactPatterns = ["\\bunrelated-only-[A-Za-z0-9]+\\b"]
(nonmatching custom patterns replace diagnostic defaults;
 model-visible sanitizeToolResult merges built-ins.)

## Before catch-path sanitizeToolResult
formatToolExecutionErrorMessage(...) under custom redactPatterns:
{
  "formatted": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer-model-visible-credential-1234567890"
}
contains synthetic credential: true

sanitizeToolResult(formatted) alone (model-visible built-ins):
{
  "sanitizedAlone": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890"
}
contains synthetic credential: false

## After fix: protocol response returned toward Codex app-server
toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse(createCodexDynamicToolBridge.handleToolCall(...)):
{
  "contentItems": [
    {
      "type": "inputText",
      "text": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890"
    }
  ],
  "success": false
}

success: false
contentItems text contains synthetic credential: false
contentItems text contains "Authorization: Bearer": true

## Summary
- Under custom nonmatching redactPatterns, diagnostic formatting LEAKS the synthetic bearer.
- After sanitizeToolResult on the catch path, protocol contentItems do NOT contain it.
- This records the actual protocol response object, not Vitest expect() output.
```

- **Vitest (distinguishing regression):**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts -t 'redacts credentials from thrown' --reporter=verbose
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > redacts credentials from thrown dynamic tool error content items 38ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 172 skipped (173)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 25.56s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Under custom nonmatching `redactPatterns`, diagnostic formatting still contains the synthetic bearer; protocol `contentItems` after the catch-path sanitizer do not (`Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890`).
- **What was not tested:** Live Codex app-server / `@openai/codex` binary round-trip. Proof surface is the real bridge + protocol response object.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

prs.title: test(gateway): channel account routes keep serving after another plugin's config reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A channel account that serves inbound traffic over HTTP must keep its route when a different plugin's config is edited and the Gateway hot-reloads. Nothing tested that path end to end on a real Gateway. If it regresses, the account still reports as running, but its route returns 404 until a restart.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible change; this adds a test only. It protects channels that register an HTTP route when an account starts, such as webhook-style inbound routes.

## Why This Change Was Made

On reload, a retained plugin's routes are projected into the new registry. Today only unit tests in `src/gateway/server/plugins-http.ownership.test.ts` cover that projection. The real-Gateway channel lifecycle tests reload the route's own plugin, not an unrelated one.

The new test follows the existing `server-plugins.lifecycle.*` fixtures and helpers. It starts a channel account that registers a prefix route at `startAccount`. It then hot-reloads another plugin's config three times with `config.patch`. After each reload it checks four things:
- the other plugin really re-registered, with a new instance and a new active registry;
- the account's route still answers 200 from the current registry;
- the route set is unchanged;
- the account was started only once.

Finally, stopping the account still removes the route (404).

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-plugins.lifecycle.channel-routes.test.ts` on current `main`: 1 passed (gateway-server project).
- **Mutation check.** The mutation removes the `target.httpRoutes.push(...)` line from `projectPluginHttpRoutes` in `src/plugins/http-route-owner.ts`.
  - The new test fails at the first reload: `status: 404`, expected 200.
  - Under the same mutation, `server-plugins.lifecycle.channels.test.ts` still passes 3/3 and `plugins-http.ownership.test.ts` fails 3/8.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the file: clean.
- `tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json`: clean. A type error injected into the file makes it fail, so the file is in that project.
- `check:max-lines-ratchet`, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:assertion-safety` and `check:database-worker-ratchet`, run against the parent commit: OK.

prs.title: fix(codex): settled-turn recovery rejects sessions containing a media-only user turn
prs.body:
Closes #185079

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex settled-turn finalization repeatedly fails with `invalid_content` when the session history contains a legitimate media-only user turn — a message persisted with empty text plus ordered `__openclaw.media` facts (for example, a JPEG-only Telegram message) and no upstream-text fallback. The projection validated every earlier message before trimming, so one such historical turn kept rejecting every later finalization context capture on that session.

## User Impact

User impact: a verified historical media-only message no longer invalidates settled-turn recovery. It projects as a bounded, deterministic marker naming the attachment types, and finalization context capture succeeds for sessions that contain one. Empty messages without any well-formed media fact are still rejected, upstream text keeps winning over the placeholder, and current-turn evidence and pairing checks are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`projectUserMessage` required non-empty text and threw `CodexHistoryRejection("invalid_content")` for a blank user turn. The persisted representation for media-only turns is exactly that shape (empty `content`, media metadata under `message.__openclaw.media` — the documented "media-bearing user turns use ordered `message.__openclaw.media` facts" convention). The payloads themselves are not replayable through the text-oriented recovery projection, so the fix projects a deterministic `[User media attachment unavailable in this context: <types>]` marker — the same approach the projector already uses for image tool results (`[Image tool result: <mime>]`) — capped at the first eight entries with a `+N more` suffix, always inside the existing byte budgets.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/settled-turn-projection.test.ts`: against unpatched `origin/main`, exactly the two placeholder-projecting cases fail (media-only turn rejected with `invalid_content`); with the fix all 26 cases pass, including the guards for empty turns without well-formed media facts (still `invalid_content`), upstream-text precedence, and the placeholder cap.
- `pnpm test:extension codex` passes except two `transport-startup.test.ts` cases that fail identically on unpatched `main` on this machine (macOS native process inspection returns a permission error in this environment); the projection suites themselves are fully green.
- `pnpm check:changed` passes typecheck extensions, typecheck extension tests, and lint extension changed files. The only red lane is the pre-existing `deadcode` unused-export scan flagging three exports in files this PR does not touch.


**Remaining proof:** No end-to-end Gateway/Codex recovery run with persisted media-only history has been performed. The regression tests cover the projection boundary; they do not establish the full recovery and finalization flow.

prs.title: fix(cli): duplicate compaction notices when Claude CLI auto-compacts
prs.body:
Related: #189548, #189623

## Summary

### High Level TLDR

With `agents.defaults.compaction.notifyUser: true`, a `claude-cli` chat that auto-compacts could show "🧹 Compacting context..." several times and "🧹 Compaction complete" twice for one compaction. Claude Code repeats its "compacting" status every 30 seconds while a compaction runs, and reports the finish with two records. OpenClaw passed every one of them through. This change publishes exactly one start and one end per compaction.

### What Problem This Solves

Fixes, for every Claude Code auto-compaction in a CLI-backed conversation:

- one extra "Compacting context..." notice (and compaction `start` agent event) for every 30 seconds the compaction runs;
- a duplicate "Compaction complete" notice (and compaction `end` agent event).

A real Telegram chat on Claude Code 2.1.318 showed 3x "Compacting context..." and 2x "Compaction complete" for a single auto-compaction. The replay below reproduces exactly that on `main`.

### User Impact

Each Claude CLI auto-compaction now produces one start and one completion notice, however long it runs. A new compaction after a finished one still notifies. Failed compactions and boundary-only automatic compactions still report their end.

### Root Cause

- **Repeated start.** Claude Code 2.1.318 re-emits the `compacting` status on a 30-second timer while one compaction runs. From the shipped Claude Code bundle:
  ```
  var lcr=30000;function QV(e){let n=setInterval(ucr,lcr,e);return()=>clearInterval(n)}
  function ucr(e){qFi(),e?.({type:"sdk_status",status:"compacting"})}
  ```
  In stream-json this is `{"type":"system","subtype":"status","status":"compacting"}` again and again. `extensions/anthropic/cli-output.ts` maps each copy to `{ kind: "compaction", phase: "start" }`. That is correct per line; the parser is stateless.
- **Repeated end.** Claude Code closes one successful automatic compaction with two records, back to back: a `system/status` record with `compact_result: "success"`, then a `system/compact_boundary` record with `compact_metadata.trigger: "auto"`. Live capture (real `claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose`, auto-compaction forced with a low `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE`; this short compaction finished before the 30-second timer fired), record types only:
  ```
  system/init
  system/status status=compacting
  rate_limit_event
  system/status status=null compact_result=success
  system/compact_boundary trigger=auto pre_tokens=26606
  user
  assistant
  system/informational
  result/success
  ```
  A failed compaction sends only `status=null compact_result=failed`, with no boundary. The parser maps both success records to `phase: "end"`. The `compact_result` mapping already existed; #189623 added the automatic `compact_boundary` mapping based on synthetic streams where an automatic compaction had no status record.
- **Why each became a notice.** `src/agents/cli-runner/execute-events.ts` `emitCliCompaction` forwarded every delta as a `compaction` agent event. `agent-runner-cli-dispatch.ts` turns each one into `onCompactionStart` / `onCompactionEnd`, and since #189548 `agent-runner-cli-candidate.ts` sends a notice on each.

### Why This Change Was Made

The lifecycle parser contract is stateless and per line, so it cannot tell that several records describe one compaction. `emitCliCompaction` already owns per-run compaction state (`compactionActive`, which the no-output watchdog reads), so the pairing goes there:

- A `start` while a compaction is already active is dropped. It still marks CLI activity, and `compactionActive` was already true, so the watchdog sees no change.
- After a successful end closes a started compaction, the next end is dropped once. A start, or the dropped repeat, clears that state. Ends with no start (boundary-only streams) and failed ends never cause a later end to be dropped.

The fix is 14 production lines in one function. It changes no config, parser output, or persisted state.

Accepted edge case: a stream that sends start, success, and then a boundary-only completion for a *different* compaction with no records between them would lose that second end. No observed Claude Code stream mixes the two formats like that.

## Verification

### Real behavior proof

- Behavior fixed: one published compaction `start` and one `end` per Claude Code automatic compaction, including one that runs past the 30-second resend.
- Environment: Linux, Node 24, Claude Code 2.1.318. A real-shape stream (the captured record sequence above, with the `compacting` status repeated twice more as the 30-second timer does during a longer compaction) was replayed through the registered Anthropic CLI backend (`buildAnthropicCliBackend` via the bundled plugin facade), the production `createCliJsonlStreamingParser`, and `createCliEventHandlers`. Published events were collected with `onAgentEvent`.
- Before (base `origin/main`), matching the 3 + 2 notices seen in the live chat:
  ```
  PARSER_DELTAS [{"phase":"start"},{"phase":"start"},{"phase":"start"},{"phase":"end","completed":true},{"phase":"end","completed":true}]
  PUBLISHED     [{"phase":"start"},{"phase":"start"},{"phase":"start"},{"phase":"end","completed":true},{"phase":"end","completed":true}]
  ```
- After (this head):
  ```
  PARSER_DELTAS [{"phase":"start"},{"phase":"start"},{"phase":"start"},{"phase":"end","completed":true},{"phase":"end","completed":true}]
  PUBLISHED     [{"phase":"start"},{"phase":"end","completed":true}]
  ```
- The parser output is unchanged. Only the repeated published events are gone, and those published events are what feed `onCompactionStart` / `onCompactionEnd` and the notices.

### Regression test

`src/agents/cli-output-anthropic.test.ts` › "publishes one start and one completion per Claude automatic compaction" sends real-shape records through the registered Claude backend, the streaming parser, and the CLI event handlers: two boundary-only compactions; a compaction with three `compacting` statuses closed by success status plus boundary; a back-to-back compaction with two `compacting` statuses closed the same way; one more boundary-only compaction; a failed compaction with two `compacting` statuses; and a final boundary-only compaction. It expects `end, end, start, end, start, end, end, start, end, end` and no active compaction afterwards.

- Red on base and on the previous head of this PR (end-only fix): 4 extra published `start` events (`start, start, start` for the first compaction, `start, start` for the back-to-back one and for the failed one).
- Red on an earlier draft of the end fix that latched without consuming (a later boundary-only end was swallowed).
- Green on this head.

### Commands

- `pnpm test src/agents/cli-output-anthropic.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute-events.compaction-tracking.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute.compaction-watchdog.test.ts src/agents/cli-output-events.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-cli-dispatch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-cli-progress.test.ts extensions/anthropic/cli-output.test.ts`: 7 files, 73 tests passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed (format, lint, core and core-test typecheck, ratchets, import cycles).
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`: passed with an 87-line allocation in `config/test-lines-allocations/cli-compaction-end-dedupe.txt`.
- Local autoreview (shared helper), branch mode against the merge base, P0–P2. The default Codex engine was unavailable for this account on the final head (`reviewer_unavailable`), so the Claude engine ran instead. Final head: **scoped-clean**, "patch is correct", no actionable findings. Earlier rounds on the end fix found two problems (a dropped second boundary-only end, an unconsumed latch); both were fixed and covered by the test.

### What was not tested

- No end-to-end run through an isolated Gateway with a real Telegram chat. Proof stops at the published agent events that drive `onCompactionStart` / `onCompactionEnd` and the notices. The notice path from #189548 is unchanged and covered by `agent-runner-execution-cli-progress.test.ts`.
- The live Claude Code capture finished before the 30-second resend fired; the resend is proven from the shipped Claude Code bundle and the observed 3x start notices in a live chat, not from a captured stream.
- Only Claude Code 2.1.318 was checked. Older boundary-only streams are covered by the synthetic test case, not by a live capture.
- No performance benchmark. The change adds two boolean checks per compaction lifecycle event, which happens a few times per compaction and never on the token or tool hot path.

prs.title: fix(plugins): release failed loads when captures close
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated failed native plugin loads keep retired captures’ errors and attached objects reachable for the lifetime of the process.

## User Impact

Closing a plugin source capture releases its native-load failure records. Active captures preserve the original error on retry. This affects the shared native loader, including Bun’s captured-plugin path; it does not explain the separate healthy Node catalog growth.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture disposal already clears its module cache, but [failed modules need not remain in that cache](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v24.22.1/lib/internal/modules/cjs/loader.js#L1346-L1361). The native loader now owns the existing module-cache eviction and clears failure records under the retiring capture at the same synchronous terminal boundary. Ordinary cache invalidation keeps its existing ESM retry behavior.

## Evidence

- A real child-process regression loads a throwing module in two source captures. Synchronous and asynchronous disposal collect the retired error and attached payload; a live sibling retains its diagnostic. Both forced-collection probes explicitly launch Node, where collection is provable. The terminal-ESM retry assertions also run in Node when the parent suite uses Bun; other capture and loader cases retain their host runtime.
- Current head `5c0d2f19a884c17e6264f918d1d0b964454e654e`: **56/56 relevant tests passed** on actual CI merge `1325e69b` into main `2a8bdef`. [Capture/metadata job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41852721680/job/126654499908): 35 capture and 11 metadata tests, including actual failed-load collection (374 ms). [Native-loader job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41852721680/job/126654499806): 10 tests, including actual terminal-ESM retry execution (76 ms). The parent lanes use Bun; the forced-GC and ESM probes explicitly use Node. Full CI is not green: the UI typecheck, baseline-ratchet and six browser-E2E shard failures below remain recorded.
- [Prior-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41809004692) passed at `949316a4c91e5944c04c155312dd61ce3f49c8bb`: capture/metadata [job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41809004692/job/126503740017) and native-loader [job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41809004692/job/126503768878). The new collection regression executed successfully under Bun; the Node-only ESM case was skipped there. The latest commit corrects test-runtime selection only; production is unchanged.
- [Production build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41805940084/job/126493772245), packaging, CLI smoke and built-artifact checks passed at `949316`. The manual-full planner omitted the plugin suites, so that run is not focused-test proof. Its broader matrix had failures and was cancelled; the subsequent normal PR CI above completed successfully.
- Independent source review and local autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issue in the complete production fix against `893451a3d70ad170fe3887b5a398eac08cad74d4`, or in the final test-only delta against `949316`. [ClawSweeper’s current-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192673#issuecomment-6627842506), at `5c0d2f19`, found no actionable finding or before-merge item. Its CI-log access was unavailable; the attribution below comes from separately inspected complete job evidence.
- Rank-up evidence: the linked capture job observes real failed loading, terminal disposal, collection of retired objects and retention of the live sibling. Base-red proof remains unavailable: the [Testbox attempt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41803643889) failed during source sync before tests executed. A live-Gateway load trace is deferred: this patch proves the native owner’s object lifetime, while healthy catalog growth needs its own measurement. No live-Gateway RSS reduction is claimed.
- Formatting, line-cap, staged-content guards and `git diff --check` passed. Production: **+12 lines**. Regression/support: **+63 lines**, with an exact 63-line allocation for collection and retry coverage. No config, persistent-state or protocol change.

## Follow-ups and Limits

The cancelled manual matrix reported unrelated emulator startup, generated UI-baseline, Beam fixture reachability and disk-admission failures. Other HTTP admission/cleanup, hook-event, identity, Doctor, archive-borrower and concurrent-setup failures were investigated but not causally reproduced. They remain named follow-ups; unchanged source is not a baseline replay, and none is labelled a proven flake. Healthy catalog growth and small-device qualification require separate measurements.

Current-CI attribution: `config-mutation.test.ts:50` passes an invalid `disconnected` phase introduced by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192208; exact main and CI merge share the same test, harness, and closed phase union. The mock-export violations in `profiles-view.test.tsx:23` and `sessions-page-cloud-stop.test.ts:18` came from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192225 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192206 respectively; their factories/scanner/ledger are unchanged by this PR. Main already exceeds its test ceiling by 216 lines: this PR adds 63 test lines and exactly 63 allocated lines, preserving that excess. The ratchet still rejects positive growth against an exceeded absolute ceiling. This is source-contract/arithmetic attribution, not a baseline execution or a claim that CI passed.

The same completed run also failed browser E2E shards 1–6: [1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41852721680/job/126654499791), [2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41852721680/job/126654499559), [3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41852721680/job/126654499680), [4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41852721680/job/126654499057), [5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41852721680/job/126654499023), [6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41852721680/job/126654499225). All observed cases were inspected. These use browser MockWebSocket and unchanged UI/test/config/dependency inputs from main; their failing operations do not invoke native capture disposal. Causes include stale translated copy/shortcut expectations, duplicate “Available models” heading selectors, and UI layout/status waits. Some UI timeout/layout root causes remain unresolved. Older scheduled-main jobs had different failing cases, so their job-name-only table is not matching-signature proof. This is concrete source and execution-boundary attribution for an inherited-failure landing exception; CI remains failed, with security-fast independently passing.

Package Acceptance rejects an otherwise valid prerelease candidate when all optional plugin-registry fields are absent. The normalizer intentionally emits no value for that tuple, but `jq -e` treats the empty result as failure.

Release operators can validate candidates that intentionally carry no prerelease plugin registry, while partial, malformed, unexpected, conflicting, or invalid complete tuples still fail closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing normalizer remains the single owner. It now accepts jq's valid empty output and turns failed complete-tuple predicates into an explicit jq error. No new path or state was added.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Part 1 of 5, based on `main`. This generic foundation does not enable the installed lane. Parts 1 and 2 are logically independent; their linear GitHub bases are review transport. Native correction `c6835f0c7d4a0e917eb999ee938b4c8f283000f7` incorporates the fixed `3df082cf325b7105fbf6833faed7f96d04f68bc8` baseline after a concrete failed UI comparison. The retained installed behavior and separate export correction below are source-bound evidence; they do not qualify a later landing retarget. Draft advancement and landing still require the applicable native gates.

Tooling +1,235/-0; tests +1,485/-0; allocation metadata +2/-0; product runtime +0/-0. Base-relative gross: 2,722 lines. The separate 1,485-line allocation covers real native lifetime, SQLite, parity and evidence-boundary regressions; the shared scalar is unchanged and the baseline's 30-line slack is preserved.

## Evidence

- The prior 35-case observer suite and later affected component runs cover this source lineage; they are not new-base full-suite or required CI results. Successful components from [the first retarget run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41909382950) and [the fixture retry](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41911558945) remain tied to their respective source heads. Those runs failed overall; their failed cases were repaired and retried separately. This is not a claim that all cases ran on the final head.
- The original exact-range static review of `1eb343de` was scoped-clean with no findings. Its three files were byte-identical at `4715569e`. Independent review verified the native baseline composition and one-line lifetime-bound simplification. Fresh correction-only review of `d3cde975` → `c6835f0c` was scoped-clean with no findings. This is static review; focused execution is reported separately below.
- [Exact `4715569e` CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41936415778) found the redundant spread and missing test allocation, plus a UI comparison using unequal older source inputs. The correction addresses those source/integration causes without weakening their checks. The complete old run ended with 41 successful, 7 failed and 26 skipped jobs; the seventh failure is the aggregate gate. It also exposed the clock-domain defect below, upstream workshop/QA deadcode (absent in the selected baseline), an unlisted `tokenjuice` dependency in the existing performance script, and an Android device-offline/trust-cleanup failure. Remaining failures are not waived or repaired here; no contaminated emulator is reused. Old-head review/CI does not qualify this corrected head.

Canonical runtime reports, all seven joined phases and native closure were independently verified. Bun still runs the reader/mutation assertions and rejects direct absence capture; real capture uses the same Node monotonic clock as the observed processes. No timestamp calibration, slack or lifetime predicate changed. The canonical local ratchet also passed against the exact baseline: 6,474,883 lines, 6,474,913 ceiling, 30 slack. ## What Problem This Solves

Unrelated iOS project edits can force a cold Watch RTC compilation even when trusted main CI has already cached compatible libraries. This follows the cache audit of [screenshot-only run 41928125596](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41928125596).

## User Impact

Eligible iOS builds, screenshots, and Periphery scans can reuse verified Watch RTC libraries across these edits. There is no app behavior change. End-to-end time savings have not yet been measured.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the exact primary key, then allow one fallback bounded to the same OS, architecture, and Xcode version. The existing build phase still checks every slice's input fingerprint and archive checksum; changed inputs or damaged output rebuild through locked Cargo. All simulator-cache consumers use the same settings. Trusted main CI remains the sole publisher; device-release libraries and Swift package caching stay unchanged.

## Evidence

- The fallback regression failed on the base configuration and passes with the change. All six Apple input-cache tests pass, including fresh-build reuse, changed-source/SDK/deployment-target invalidation, damaged archives, and writer restrictions: 1.94 seconds test time, 3.38 seconds command wall time.

The exact CI typecheck graph (`test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json`) and all six cache tests pass after correcting the consumer tuples identified by initial CI (3.75 seconds test-command wall time).
- All 11 selected Apple cache and macOS CI workflow test files pass: 1,181 tests passed, 10 existing tests skipped; 368.54 seconds command wall time. All attached CI has settled on the corrected head: 72 checks passed, including both Periphery builds and their downstream scans. The branch-related typecheck failure from the initial head is fixed and passes in CI. The remaining UI failures and aggregate gate are detailed below.
- AutoReview: local candidate against `2d0e42c125057af4321fe1c67ebea0282a886620`, patch now committed as `2fca99fcfe9cd652cbf5676ac96a809381eef9e6`, through P2, scoped clean. It used an exact cache hit, so it does not measure fallback-path wall-time savings.
- The 12-line test allocation covers the bounded fallback and consumer parity; existing tests did not protect that restore contract. No release or additional screenshot campaign was dispatched.

### Remaining CI failures inherited from main

[CI run 41940867476](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41940867476) tested merge commit `70194a807056d7f3c1b626834677a0f0227f71ed` against main parent `84097d630e263848e57a3aa98d47f789606a970d`. prs.title: test(qa-lab): expect SIGKILL restart to resume the killed Code Mode run
prs.body:
## Problem

`extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-kill-restart-send.e2e.test.ts` ("leaves a killed run idle until a new user message arrives") is stale on `main`. It asserts that a Gateway restarted after `SIGKILL` makes no provider requests until a fresh user message arrives.

#190964 changed that on purpose: a root session interrupted by `SIGKILL` now gets one ordinary resume input on the next startup. The contract is documented in `docs/gateway/restart-recovery.md` and proven by `test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts`. That PR did not update this qa-lab test, so it now asserts the old behavior. The test is only selected by changed-node rows on broad-scope PRs, which is why it went unnoticed. Because the resume is real, the old assertion fails whenever the resume reaches the mock provider before the test's empty-requests check. That happened in both local `main` runs and two of three #192607 CI runs (`checks-node-changed-7`). The new assertion waits for the resume input, so it does not depend on that timing.

## Solution

Update the test to the current contract. It keeps the same setup: a qa-channel inbound, a Code Mode `wait` still pending, a process-group `SIGKILL`, and a restart with the session row retained. It now asserts that the same session gets the standard Gateway resume input without another inbound message, and that exactly one user-role message (the resume input) follows the pre-kill transcript cursor. The fresh-inbound and empty-mock-requests steps checked the retired "stay idle" behavior, so I removed them.

Test-only change. No production code changed.

## Impact

- Unblocks changed-node CI rows that select this file.
- Keeps qa-channel and Code Mode coverage of crash recovery: the dangling `wait` call is closed and the run resumes in the original session.
- Test lines: net -12 (17 insertions, 29 deletions in one file).

## Evidence

All runs are local, macOS, Node, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner extensions/qa-lab/src/gateway-kill-restart-send.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`:

| Tree | Old test | New test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `99e12c88fe97` (parent of #190964, before SIGKILL resume) | pass (46.7 s) | **fail**: no resume input, times out with only `inbound-message` |
| `919b0567dd1b` (parent of #192501) | fail: two resume requests after restart | n/a |
| `main` (`df93e5d0e9a8` / `1d5bc6779517`) | **fail**: `expected [ {…}, {…} ] to deeply equal []`; the requests carry "The Gateway restarted while you were working. Resume your work:" | **pass** (30.9 s) |

- The CI failure on #192607 matches the local `main` failure: job 126432244272 and job 126648493317.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` pass on the changed file. `check:test-lines-ratchet` reports net delta -12.
- Wall time: 30.9 s, lower than the old 46.7 s. This is a full Gateway kill/restart composition with nothing cheaper to replace it. The SIGKILL resume contract itself stays owned by `test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts`.
- CI: on this PR's run 41854024874, `checks-node-changed` ran the file under pinned Bun and passed in 17.1 s (job 126658791849). The only red check, `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`, fails on `mock-exports` in `ui/src/pages/model-providers/profiles-view.test.tsx` and `ui/src/pages/sessions/sessions-page-cloud-stop.test.ts`. That failure is already on `main` and #192850 fixes it.

Fixes Android notification access appearing disconnected or empty when an old listener disconnects after its replacement has connected.

## Why This Change Was Made

## Evidence

- Real production service callbacks under Robolectric: A connects, B replaces A, then A disconnects/destroys. The baseline run failed the connected-snapshot assertion (8 tests, 1 failure); the fix preserves B and its notification.

prs.title: fix(update): report a missing npm version as an unpublished target
prs.body:
Closes #193023

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update --tag` reports an unpublished exact npm version as a registry connectivity failure and can hide npm's explanation behind generic installation advice.

## User Impact

An explicitly missing version now produces `target-version-resolution` and preserves npm's `No match found for version` or `No matching version found for` explanation. Missing packages, generic HTTP 404 responses, authentication/authorization failures, and network errors retain registry-metadata guidance. No package staging, installation, or Gateway restart behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The metadata reader now owns classification through a `versionMissing` fact; the CLI no longer reparses a display string. An `E404` token alone is not evidence that a version is unpublished.

The reader prefers the structured `npm view --json` error summary even when stderr contains unrelated warnings. For stderr-only npm output, it retains the version-specific reason ahead of the generic trailing advice.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original missing-explanation regression on the PR base. Seven stronger cases fail on the original PR implementation and pass with this repair.
- The CLI regressions restore the real target resolver and metadata reader, stub only npm process output, and assert the exact npm request, literal surfaced explanation, failure classification, and zero package staging. Coverage includes stderr-only E404, JSON E404/ETARGET with stderr warnings, missing packages, E401/E403, and ENOTFOUND.
- Five focused suites pass: `update-check.test.ts`, `update-command-metadata-diagnostics.test.ts`, `update-command-target.n1-prefix.test.ts`, `update-command-timeouts.test.ts`, and `update-cli.target-schema.test.ts` (24 tests, including the previously failing registry-refusal path). The classifier export that broke the shared CLI mock has been removed rather than adding a second classification policy to the mock.
- The changed metadata-diagnostics file passes all **35 tests** with `--maxWorkers=1`; wrapper wall time was **61.55 s**, including compilation. The new cases reuse the existing CLI fixture. CI timing is not yet available for the updated head.
- Core and CLI-update test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, whitespace, and the exact-base test-line ratchet pass. The separate 68-line allocation covers the real CLI regression cases and assertions; the shared budget scalar is unchanged.
- Independent local review completed with no P0 findings (P0-only review scope).

Two additional Node-runtime sibling tests fail identically on the PR base and repaired candidate: the already-current plugin-maintenance cases with `fallback=false, writable=true` and `fallback=true, writable=false` expect the existing broken-TEXT-decoder recovery text. These baseline failures are outside this diagnostic change and are not claimed as passing.

A live read-only `npm view` confirmed the structured missing-version error envelope. No live package replacement, Gateway restart, or upgrade was performed.

### Live npm proof at `83f4b465`

npm 11.19.1 against `https://registry.npmjs.org`. Both calls use `fetchNpmPackageTargetStatus` with `command: "npm"` and the same `npm view <spec> version engines.node openclaw.schemaVersions --json --global` argv the package update path uses. Classification is the update command's expression: an error with `versionMissing` unset selects `target-registry-metadata`; otherwise `target-version-resolution`.

Unpublished exact version `openclaw@2026.11.5-beta.5`:

- npm's JSON `error.summary` is `No match found for version 2026.11.5-beta.5` (`error.code` `E404`).
- stderr also ends with the generic lines `Note that you can also install from a` and `tarball, folder, http url, or git url.` The old last-three-lines summary kept those and dropped the version sentence.
- The reader returned `versionMissing: true` and `npm view failed: E404\nNo match found for version 2026.11.5-beta.5`.
- Classification: `target-version-resolution`.

Missing package `openclaw-no-such-pkg-193037@1.2.3` (registry 404, not a missing version of a real package):

- npm's JSON `error.summary` is `Not Found - GET https://registry.npmjs.org/openclaw-no-such-pkg-193037 - Not found`.
- The reader returned `versionMissing: false` and `npm view failed: E404\nNot Found - GET https://registry.npmjs.org/openclaw-no-such-pkg-193037 - Not found`.
- Classification: `target-registry-metadata`.

No package was installed or staged.

ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End select a terminal tab, but the asynchronous after-render callback steals focus into the PTY, breaking continued tab navigation. Conversely, Enter, Space and clicking the already-selected terminal tab can leave focus on the tab instead of entering the terminal.

This applies to the standalone terminal and the chat's hosted terminal header. Selecting a different tab with the mouse and switching to other panel tabs retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the existing native selection event through the internal UI adapters. The terminal owner selects, refits and repaints without focusing for navigation keys; explicit activation uses the existing per-tab callback. Hosted-header expansion retains priority over terminal activation.

**No Gateway PTY permission, terminal protocol, request schema, input policy or configuration/default changes.** The event objects are local DOM callback arguments, not wire fields. Alix-007's original `d134bbaa6aebf279b78a6907a6162e6f8a1bed8f` commit is preserved.

## Evidence

Client/Gateway build stamps and served entry hashes are checked. No model turn or shell command is typed.

Maintainer validation on macOS with WebKit 27.2 now passes on exact head df49134e63ac812fba7cf0bbcdd972e4e077afb3 against the built candidate, an isolated real Gateway, and real /bin/sh PTYs. Both standalone and actual chat-hosted terminal tabs retain focus for ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End; Enter, Space, and selected-tab click focus terminal input. Neither scenario sent terminal.input frames. The hosted fixture creates its chat through the Gateway CLI and its second PTY through the existing terminal-toggle owner; acceptance uses real browser keyboard/pointer events. prs.title: fix(docker): image build fails at production-deps on builders that scope ARGs per stage
prs.body:
Closes #193039

> **Correction (2026-11-04):** an earlier version of this description argued that the Dockerfile violated Docker's `ARG` scoping rules. That was wrong — `production-deps` is a child of `dependency-inputs`, which declares the ARG, and Docker documents that child stages inherit it. The Dockerfile is correct as written. This is a compatibility workaround for buildah 1.39.7, which does not apply that inheritance. Reframed below; the issue has the same correction.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the image build aborts at the `production-deps` stage on buildah 1.39.7 — the builder OpenShift 4.x uses for its `Docker` build strategy — because that version does not apply documented parent-stage `ARG` inheritance.

## User Impact

User impact: the `production-deps` stage no longer aborts on buildah 1.39.7, removing one of the blockers to building this image in-cluster on OpenShift. No change on BuildKit or buildah 1.43.4, where the stage already resolves correctly.

This does **not** make the full image build on that builder: the same version also fails later in the file on `COPY --from=openclaw_installed_runtime` (lines 237/243), a BuildKit named external context it resolves eagerly. That is a separate problem and is not addressed here.

## Why This Change Was Made

Docker [documents](https://docs.docker.com/build/building/variables/#scoping) that a declared ARG is inherited by child stages:

> Once a build argument is declared or consumed in a stage, it's automatically inherited by child stages.

`dependency-inputs` declares `ARG OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGIN_DIR` at line 64 and `production-deps` is `FROM dependency-inputs`, so the inheritance should apply — and does, on BuildKit and buildah 1.43.4. buildah 1.39.7 does not implement it, and because the stage runs under `set -eu` the unset variable is fatal.

The conforming fix belongs upstream in buildah. This adds the one-line declaration already used by the five stages that declare this ARG explicitly (lines 34, 64, 194, 201, 266), which restores compatibility at no cost and is a no-op wherever inheritance already works. It is entirely reasonable to decline this and require a newer builder instead.

## Evidence

**Inheritance behaviour, isolated.** No global ARG, so only parent-to-child inheritance could resolve the value:

```dockerfile
FROM registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/ubi-minimal:latest AS parent
ARG FOO=hello
RUN echo "parent sees [${FOO:-UNSET}]"

FROM parent AS child
RUN echo "child sees [${FOO:-UNSET}]"
```

| Builder | Result |
|---|---|
| BuildKit (buildx v0.37.1) | `child sees [hello]` — inherits |
| podman 5.8.7 / buildah 1.43.4 | `child sees [hello]` — inherits |
| buildah 1.39.7 (OpenShift) | `unbound variable` — does not inherit |

A global ARG that no stage declares does not reach a stage on BuildKit either (`GLOB: unbound variable`), consistent with the documented global-scope rule — so the mechanism at issue is parent-stage inheritance, not global-ARG leniency.

**This repository's actual `production-deps` stage on buildah 1.39.7.** Real build context from 844d022, real stage body, the file truncated after `production-deps` so it is the final stage (later stages removed only so the build reaches this one; the stage itself is unmodified).

Two builds, same real context, the added `ARG` line the only difference. OpenShift `BuildConfig`, `Docker` strategy, buildah 1.39.7.

**Before — fails in the real stage:**

```

[2/3] STEP 1/38: FROM docker.io/library/node:24.22.1-trixie@sha256:e8bc2eed... AS dependency-inputs
[2/3] STEP 38/38: COPY --from=workspace-deps /out/openclaw-required-platform-packages /tmp/openclaw-required-platform-packages
--> 9bb3579c6956
[3/3] STEP 1/5: FROM 9bb3579c6956... AS production-deps
[3/3] STEP 2/5: RUN --mount=type=cache,id=openclaw-pnpm-store,... set -eu; set -- --filter . --filter ./ui --filter './packages/*'; while IFS= read -r ext; do set -- "$@" --filter "./${OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGIN_DIR}/$ext"; done < /tmp/openclaw-workspace-plugin-dirs; NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=2048 pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prod "$@" ...

error: build error: building at STEP "RUN --mount=type=cache,...": while running runtime: exit status 2
# phase=Failed after 211s
```

Note the real stage reports `parameter not set` rather than the `unbound variable` in the minimal fixture above — the runtime image's `/bin/sh` is dash, not bash. Same defect, different shell diagnostic.

**After — the stage completes and the filters resolve:**

prs.title: fix(talk): stop voice claiming cancelled consult work finished
prs.body:
Closes #189070

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: realtime Talk keeps reporting a task as in progress, then as done, after Google Live cancels the `openclaw_agent_consult` call and OpenClaw aborts the run.

## User Impact

After a cancelled consult, the voice model is told the request was interrupted and its outcome is unknown. It stops claiming the work finished and checks what was done before running it again, since steps that ran before the cancellation are not undone.

## Why This Change Was Made

When Google Live sends `toolCallCancellation`, the relay already aborts the consult run (`cancelTalkRealtimeRelayProviderToolCall`). The Android client then submits `aborted` for that call, but the Google provider deliberately drops results for cancelled call IDs (`submitToolResult` early return, added in 5be95ad4bab). The model's last word on the call was "working" or nothing, and it never learns the work stopped.

The relay's `tool.call.cancelled` handler now sends one notice through the existing bridge `sendUserMessage` path, the same path forced consults use for their "checking" and result prompts. It fires only when the relay actually retired an uncompleted call, so replays and cancellations after an accepted result send nothing. The notice says the outcome is unknown rather than that nothing happened: cancellation aborts only the remaining steps, so an earlier file write may already have landed.

<details>
<summary>Why the default model is exposed</summary>

The default `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` gets no async function calling and no `willContinue` interim result (`supportsAsyncFunctionCalling`, `modelSupportsToolResultContinuation`), so the consult is declared blocking. Speech while it is pending is a likely cancellation trigger; the reporter did not confirm the trigger.

</details>

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/talk/relay/cancellation-recovery.test.ts`: 14 passed. With the one `sendUserMessage` line removed, the new notice test fails with "Number of calls: 0"; the control (cancellation after an accepted result sends nothing) passes both ways.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/talk/relay`: all relay tests passed.
- Live run, partial: an isolated QA Gateway with real Google Live (`gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`) and a real Gemini agent model. A client speaks generated audio through the same RPCs Android uses (`talk.session.create` on `gateway-relay`, `talk.session.appendAudio`, `talk.client.toolCall`, `talk.session.steer`, `talk.session.submitToolResult`). It asks for a 20-second wait plus a file write, interrupts after about 4 s, then asks for status. These trials ran the first wording of the notice ("cancelled … produced no result"); the delivery path is unchanged. Main is `upstream/main`'s `session-create.ts` swapped in with `dist` rebuilt.
  - Google cancelled the running consult in all 9 trials that reached it. Each showed `chat.aborted`, then `toolCallCancelled`, then the dropped `{"error":"aborted"}` submit.
  - Main, 6 cancelled trials: in 1, the voice model claimed success right after the cancellation. It said "the greeting file has now been created in your workspace. Protocol complete!", and no file existed. The other 5 made no such claim.
  - This branch, 3 cancelled trials: none claimed the work finished. No speech followed the cancellation before the user's next turn, so the notice was not spoken over the user.
  - Gaps: the sample is small because the bug is intermittent and free-tier Gemini quota rate-limited the remaining trials. Those trials were excluded (`reason=rate_limit` in the Gateway log). The notice's delivery to Gemini is not logged, so it is shown by the unit test, not by the live run. In 1 main trial and 2 trials on this branch, the voice model started a new consult, and that agent run reported saving `proofnote.txt`. That run checked only for `proof-note.txt`, so whether the agent's claim was true is unverified.

<details>
<summary>Live trial transcript (main, the false-completion trial)</summary>

```
+66.3s talk.toolCall          openclaw_agent_consult
+66.5s toolCall.ack           runId=talk-c684…
+70.6s user.speaks            "Actually, while you do that, what is two plus two?"
+71.9s chat.aborted           runId=talk-c684…
+71.9s talk.toolCallCancelled
+72.0s submitToolResult       {"error":"aborted"}   (dropped by the provider)
+81.0s assistant              "...2 + 2 is 4. And one moment... the greeting file has now been created in your workspace. Protocol complete!"
+129.4s artifact              proof-note.txt exists: false
```

</details>

Production delta +8/-0; test delta +38/-0.

Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the prior behavior with no state or config migration. Blast radius is relay Talk sessions whose provider emits `tool.call.cancelled` (Google Live today).

prs.title: fix(plugins): defer channel admission imports in catalog workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Provider-only model catalogs import Gateway method validators and host channel-admission code while constructing the shared plugin registry. Those modules remain resident even when that catalog never creates an inbound channel runtime.

## User Impact

**Current-head performance HOLD:** the completed 009e campaign against control `82ce072` qualifies all 444 outputs, but cold worker heap improves only 0.556 MiB (0.642%) and 17 overlapping paired timing cells cross the predeclared adverse threshold. The 101-generation trace still grows late. Full current-head results and proof limits are at the end; the earlier comparisons below remain historical evidence.

**Performance hold.** The historical comparison against `f75bd97` (including the scope-import fix now landed separately) used five paired runs that reduce cold post-GC worker heap from **89.596 to 86.372 MiB (−3.598%)**. Warm median latency improves 2.183%, but warm p95 increases 3.923%, CPU increases 0.955%, and the fifth pair regresses 61.981% in warm median / 64.952% in warm p95. These results do not meet the predeclared acceptance rule; no adverse tradeoff has been accepted.

This is a small import-footprint reduction, not a demonstrated Gateway RSS saving or a fixed memory leak. The historical measured worker loads 3,096 scripts; the newly qualified current-head cold capture loads 3,093 against its 3,108-script incremental control. No configuration, migration, operator action, or public runtime API change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Import ADMIN_SCOPE from its canonical lightweight owner instead of Gateway method policy.
- Keep channel trust, record identity, and revocation in the registry owner; obtain host inbound composition through the existing lazy native runtime owner only when a channel needs it.
- Preserve synchronous access, supplemental-media completion, inactive prepared loads, and exact-instance retirement. Remove eager host-admission construction from provider-only registry imports.
- Compose the same private factory in the unpublished source-test SDK facade. Its CI naming repair uses `createPluginTestRegistry` and migrates all 19 callers. Independent scoped review, exact mechanical-diff verification, formatting, and whitespace/privacy checks passed.

Current source delta versus frozen `f75bd97`: **production +93/−54, net +39; tests/test helpers +194/−90, net +104; test-budget metadata +3/−0**. Test-only SDK facades, test helpers, and test-support modules are counted with tests. Production growth supplies the private runtime ownership boundary; it adds no cache. The test ratchet counts +98; a scoped +98 allocation covers the new lifecycle assertions.

## Evidence

Current published PR head: `af67b3e07c15da6133d92cf51012c330d3f8a3f6`, tree `ffb90926046204e8b09540bf920959f29ab902e1`. After the historical measured head, `058e617` renamed the unpublished test-facade factory, migrated its 19 consumers, and allocated the test budget. The new `af67b3e` additionally changes the startup matcher import from `config-contracts.ts` to its existing `config-contract-matches.ts` owner (+1/−1 production line). The historical `b8420c5` table remains preserved evidence for that older source, not a performance result for af67.

[CI attached to af67](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41765145335) is complete. The only failed selected surface is the baseline ratchet; the aggregate CI gate consequently failed. The exact-head security review passed. The native informational classifier calls the ratchet “new” because a scheduled main job passed, explicitly noting that selected scope was not compared; the exact tested-parent arithmetic below establishes the inherited deficit without changing the failed CI outcome. The failed test-line ratchet is inherited: tested merge `1bc9c1e3d9e51f74513a987ad1a1766ed767083e` has ordered parents `f38495f7d044b35810ae1e03792bf9f80a571bf1` and af67. Its 6,452,269 test lines exceed a 6,452,249 ceiling by 20; the exact first-parent reconstruction is 6,452,171 versus 6,452,151, also 20 over. The PR adds 98 counted lines and a matching 98-line allocation. This is source/CI arithmetic, not a baseline rerun; the job remains failed.

The [latest ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191939#issuecomment-6605715158) now covers exact af67: no actionable correctness findings, but merge remains blocked by the performance hold. At review time it recorded missing qualified af67 comparative/cold/post-load proof and red-on-base execution of the new admission assertions. The completed campaign below supplies the comparative proof; the admission-counterfactual rationale remains recorded separately. Its rank-up move is completion of the already-declared comparison without discarding historical failures. No additional review request is needed while the head is unchanged.

[Historical CI for 058e617](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41678071453) passed the naming-collision guard and test-line budget. Its remaining failed test job was UI E2E: Brave and Firecrawl credential-save cases timed out waiting for `config.set` (`plugins-settings-admin.e2e.test.ts:305/426`). This mocked-Gateway path does not activate native plugins; its source/behavior boundary is outside the changed registry factories. That result is not current-head CI.

The Codex consumer edits only rename the test factory. Direct upstream contract inspection used `openai/codex` commit `414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6`: `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs:174–203` and `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs:857–930`. No RPC payload or behavior changes.

Measured source: `b8420c5e132945f10619b83b3896997850074576`, tree `e75e5611fb7f441d01af0d948469f4c4128e18ae`; compiled carrier: `453268180b7017c493a9215074cd79bd32ccaf8c`. Baseline: `f75bd97cda9f6d330cb2967a5816aa5af31e1f9c`, tree `50322a9265e3110258f4197119ad0179f0f5cc13`.

[Completed Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41660095779), Node 24.22.1, Linux x64, CPU affinity 0–3, no CPU/RAM cgroup limit, MemTotal 16,168,148 kB. Both arms have frozen dependency-input digest `20bebc43a6d6f0388e154e06d7fc79a9c9e47be5fcef2ef0ca694e7143c8c8c7`.

- Compiled production-SDK admission checks passed for synchronous/asynchronous context, ordinary unbound context, retirement, and retirement while async context is pending.

These are not reported as passing.
