No measurement existed at predeclaration, and the stopped attempt above produced none. Four further independent in-memory checks verify complete aggregate accounting for 13,995 additions, bounded path samples, root-group overflow and mixed add/remove/kind changes; they do not replace integrated proof.

### Exact-head review response: admission preservation versus optimization proof

The requested red-on-base admission-behavior proof is not applicable to this extraction. At the control, `src/plugins/registry-runtime-channel.ts:31` already constructs the wrapper only for a live trusted registered channel, caches its exact record, and revokes retired owners. The candidate moves that wrapper to `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-channel-admission.ts:15` behind the lazy runtime owner. Host context construction, admission evidence and async liveness checks are unchanged. Identity, authorization and retirement tests therefore protect behavior expected to pass on both revisions; a missing renamed test export or a baseline ignoring a new private-factory callback would be an invalid negative control.

The optimization counterfactual remains required: the baseline's eager registry-to-host import path versus the compiled prepared-catalog worker under the same cold/post-load workload. A source-edge cut alone cannot prove exclusion from shared emitted chunks or a memory improvement. This rationale addresses the review's behavioral red-on-base request without waiving the compiled import/performance gate, historical adverse results or HOLD.

### Follow-up: prepared-session construction boundary

Source audit at `af67b3e` confirms that `AuthStorage.inMemory` imports the standalone directory/config-loading path through `agents/config.ts`. Removing only that construction edge is insufficient: command-backed credentials reach the same path through `resolve-config-value.ts` and `shell-utils.ts`; ModelRegistry defaults, models-config, and plugin runtime getters retain independent config-loading edges. Catalog and per-run stores still require per-instance OAuth registration, mutable fork isolation, and supported environment/command credential and header resolution, including Windows managed-bin PATH.

A complete follow-up must isolate standalone/persistent factories from prepared-session construction while retaining one instance/backend/OAuth implementation and the public factory and request-auth contracts. Check the emitted graph across all backedges before claiming schema exclusion. This audit does not establish an RSS saving or a complete small patch; it does not expand the current candidate.

Correctness: 149 tests across six files, compiled admission checks, full candidate/control builds and same-invocation Twitch qualification passed. prs.title: fix(ios): Learn more links do nothing in embedded Settings
prs.body:
Related: #119906 (the existing trusted-Gateway navigation boundary).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: tapping **Learn more** in the iOS embedded Plugins, Skills, or Skill Workshop page silently leaves the user on the same page instead of opening the documentation.

## User Impact

Users can follow external HTTP(S) links from the embedded Control UI through the system URL handler and return to the app. The system may open a browser or an associated app, depending on the destination and device configuration.

## Why This Change Was Made

These pages already provide links to their documentation, but the native authenticated web view cancels navigation to other origins and new windows. As a result, an existing help action becomes a silent dead end on iOS. This restores that action while preserving the trusted-Gateway boundary introduced in #119906.

The change keeps external content out of the authenticated web view and hands only the destination URL to the system. It does not forward the WebKit request, Gateway headers, cookies, or authentication scripts. The handoff is limited to link activations from the expected main-frame origin in the embedded Control UI; other navigation types, subframes, non-HTTP(S) schemes, URLs containing credentials, and path-restricted views retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on a physical iPhone in the development app with an isolated Gateway: open **Skill Workshop** from Pages (enable it in **Edit Pages** if necessary), switch among the Plugins/Skills/Skill Workshop hub tabs, and tap **Learn more**. Before the fix, the page remained open. With the fix, each of the three links moved the app into the background; returning showed the Safari return indicator. Safari page content was not inspected, so this demonstrates the handoff, not successful loading of every documentation page.
- **19 native `TerminalHubScreenTests` passed**, including two new cases covering external-link admission and frame, scheme, origin, and scope restrictions. Suite execution: **0.271 s**; Xcode test phase: **7.725 s**, excluding compilation. These are policy tests, complemented by the physical-device flow above.
- Native Debug build and signature checks passed. Strict SwiftLint checked **509 files with zero violations**.
- **Automated regression, unchanged test on both versions:** `OpenClawSnapshotUITests.testLiveGatewayWorkshopDocumentationOpensOutsideTheApp` pairs with an isolated Gateway, opens the native Workshop destination, taps the real **Learn more** link, waits for Safari to take the foreground, and verifies return to the Workshop. prs.title: feat(msteams): send private and shared channel files to the channel's own SharePoint site
prs.body:
Closes #185926

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: bots cannot send files in Microsoft Teams private or shared channels unless an operator configures a single central `sharePointSiteId`, which exposes every private channel's files to that site's members and still shows "request access" to channel members.

## User Impact

User impact: in private and shared channels, file sends now land on that channel's own SharePoint site, where exactly the channel's members already have access, and the file card opens without extra permissions. No organization-wide sharing link is created for those files. Standard channels, group chats and explicit `sharePointSiteId` keep their current behavior. No new Graph permissions and no config changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Builds on #189339. Teams keeps a private/shared channel's site membership in sync with the channel, so the channel's own site is the only upload target that preserves the channel audience. For a non-standard `membershipType`, the resolver reads `GET /teams/{groupId}/channels/{channelId}/filesFolder`, then `GET /drives/{driveId}?$select=sharePointIds` (drive resources spell it `sharePointIds`; driveItems use `sharepointIds`), and builds the site ID `{hostname},{siteId},{webId}`. Results are cached per account, tenant, bot, team and channel, like the team-site cache.

`resolveMSTeamsSharePointSiteId` now returns `{ siteId, memberScoped }`. Member-scoped uploads skip `createLink`: the organization link that channel sends create would let anyone in the tenant holding its URL read a private-channel file, and channel membership already grants access through the file card's `webDavUrl`. An incomplete drive response fails closed before upload.

## Evidence

- **Focused tests:** `vitest` msteams config, 92 files / 943 tests pass. New cases run the real send paths (proactive and reply) against stubbed Graph `fetch`: private and shared channels upload to the channel site, never call `/groups/.../sites/root` or `createLink`, and cache the channel site (one `filesFolder` call across two sends); member-scoped uploads create no link; incomplete `sharePointIds` fails closed.
- **Static:** `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`: typecheck (extensions and extension tests), lint, plugin boundaries and the other guards pass. The dead-export scan fails only on `src/gateway/control-ui-session-pr-prepared-read.ts` (`retireControlUiSessionPrState`), unrelated to this change.

### Real behavior proof (production)

Multi-team production deployment, private channel, `sharePointSiteId` absent.

**Before** (#189339's behavior; private channels rejected). Gateway file log, redacted:

```
14:00:01Z [msteams] received message — text: "send me a CSV with 3 rows of test data"
          conversation: 19:<private-channel-id>@thread.tacv2;messageid=<id>
14:00:01Z [msteams] dispatching to agent
14:02:57Z [tools] tool_call failed: msteams file send failed: Automatic SharePoint site discovery
          supports standard channels only. Set channels.msteams.sharePointSiteId to upload to a specific site.
14:03:02Z [msteams] dispatch complete — counts: { tool: 0, block: 0, final: 1 }
```

The user received a text-only reply. No file reached the channel.

**After** (this change, backported onto the deployed release). Same private channel, first file send after a gateway restart (empty cache):

```
11:24:17Z [msteams] received message — text: "send me a CSV with 4 rows of test data"
11:24:17Z [msteams] dispatching to agent — sessionKey: agent:main:msteams:channel:19:<private-channel-id>…
11:24:36Z [msteams:send] sent native file card — fileName: <report> 1.csv
```

Graph check after the send (bot application credentials):

- `<folder>/<report> 1.csv` (created 11:24:35Z) sits on the private channel's own site (`/sites/<team>-<private-channel>`).
- Item permissions are only the channel site's Owners / Members / Visitors groups. No `organization` link.
- The parent team site has no entry for this send.
- The requester opened the file card from the channel.

During rollout, the first build read `sharepointIds` from the drive and failed closed ("incomplete SharePoint IDs") without uploading anything; Graph returns `sharePointIds` on drive resources. A later build still created the organization link; Graph showed it on the item, which is why member-scoped uploads now skip `createLink`.

Gaps: a second channel member and a non-member were not asked to open the card; the Graph permission set above is the access evidence.

prs.title: fix(cron): stop deferred jobs retrying every two seconds
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Timed automations whose admission is deferred retry about every two seconds, churning skipped receipts while the job still looks healthy.

## User Impact

Deferred jobs now show **Waiting: <reason> since <time>**, with a warning after five attempts. They retry after 30 seconds, doubling to a five-minute cap, and run the pending occurrence once admission clears. Their last completed run remains unchanged. This can delay recovery by up to five minutes; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cron worker retains the original occurrence and owns a separate retry deadline. Startup preserves that episode. Retries atomically replace the prior unstarted receipt while retaining a fresh execution fence. Completion, cancellation, or a scheduling change clears waiting. Existing runtime events and full/compact/tool projections publish the reason to clients. Stream retry ownership is unchanged.

Receipt retention already capped stored rows at 64 per job; the defect was continuous write/prune churn and missing visibility, not unbounded retained rows. No SQLite schema, cache, or host-admission handshake was added. Production grows 125 lines to implement the retry lifecycle and its read-only public/UI projections; benchmark tooling is separate.

## Evidence

- Regression is red before the fix: nine service cases lack waiting state, and the pinned baseline performs 300 admission attempts over ten modeled minutes. Afterward, 160 focused service, worker, receipt, scheduler, and protocol tests pass (52.68 seconds including compilation). Tests cover bounded backoff, coalescing, restart, cancellation, no replay after effects, and execution when the blocker clears.
- UI: 22 browser/render/inventory tests pass (2.96 seconds); two UI E2E tests pass (13.31 seconds), including visible waiting → recovery. The before-state E2E fails at the missing waiting reason. The test-line allocation is limited to these regression and projection contracts.
- Isolated Codex autoreview against `12218cbc4e40caddbb11f4a57b273fe0bf35f75a`: scoped clean through P2, no actionable findings.
- Full `pnpm check:changed` passed the runtime/UI type graphs, database ratchets, formatting, dead-code and import-cycle gates. It identified a benchmark worker-context type error and an array-search lint error in the new assertion; both were corrected and their targeted type/lint commands pass. The focused `pnpm check:changed -- scripts/perf/cron-deferred-admission-measure.ts` replay and test-line ratchet also pass.

Synthetic owner benchmark, 1,000 jobs, ten modeled minutes, five serial alternating pairs:

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Admission attempts | 300 | 5 |
| Retained episode receipts | 64 | 1 |
| SQLite row changes | 1,436 | 24 |
| Owner wall median / p95, ms | 2,446.53 / 2,497.40 | 52.38 / 55.30 |
| Owner thread CPU median, ms | 2,444.73 | 52.34 |
| V8 JavaScript allocation median, bytes | 2,898,720,552 | 73,791,392 |

Five A/A pairs: wall differences −8.19% to +3.33%; allocation −0.042% to +0.164%. CPU profiles show repeated cron-row decoding/SQLite reads disappearing with the eliminated attempts. The acceptance rule is fewer attempts/writes, one retained deferred receipt, lower CPU/allocation, and preservation of the original occurrence.

Reproduce each side with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/cron-deferred-admission-measure.ts --output <output.json>`, adding `--revision 12218cbc4e40caddbb11f4a57b273fe0bf35f75a` for the baseline and `--profile` for CPU profiles. Imports and fixture setup are outside measurement; each sample starts a fresh deferral episode. This measures the actual shared-cron owner on macOS/APFS, not whole-Gateway/model latency or large agent-database/btrfs performance. Agent transcripts and workspace files are outside this owner's read set; no production data was copied or live deployment touched.

![Before: overdue job appears healthy](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5cc64ee-e91f-4a48-b393-db40b81f223f)

![After: explicit waiting reason and warning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a9752289-a5a1-4695-bb3d-c49ea4803ff5)

## Hosted CI: inherited main regressions

[Run 41936481448](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41936481448) tested merge `33512ad2ed0430bc79db8ed46d5ec28c59d62fce` of this head into main `943904e8c4cae76b64bf83b1b53a8c230122fb9b`. The two failed shards reproduce with the same assertions on that exact main parent; their failed tests and copy producers are unchanged by this PR:

- `checks-ui (2/3)`: table copy expects “Copied!” and receives “Copied” (new test introduced by #192752, `943904e8c4ca`); offline model catalog expects “Offline” and receives “Disconnected” (copy changed by #192246, `dde5ab39f029`). Focused parent replay: 2 failed, 26 passed, 7.17 seconds.
- `checks-ui-e2e (2/4)`: device-dispatch tests retain “worker slots” and “Local” after #192044 (`2a16e47f90a4`) changed those labels to “session slots” and “This computer”. Focused parent replay: 4 failed, 9 passed, 85.03 seconds, matching CI.

These are main test regressions requiring separate repair, including the newly added table-copy failure; they are not ignored noise. The cron boundary proof and affected UI tests pass. No CI rerun was requested. Landing uses the explicitly authorized, pinned-head inherited-failure route, retaining the failed CI evidence rather than claiming a green run.


## PR-specific media verification waiver

The task lead explicitly waived rendered PR-image verification for this PR only on 2026-11-04. Both synthetic screenshots were inspected, uploaded, embedded, and verified byte-identical after download. Browser automation failed and Peekaboo confirmed that the Mac GUI session is locked, so rendering verification is limited by the environment. The Mac will remain locked. This waiver does not waive CI, inherited-failure attribution, final-head Codex autoreview, or native landing checks.

prs.title: fix(doctor): keep private snapshots forkable for root installs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor --lint` failed on every run for root installs with a live WAL, reporting `core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas` as `retained-snapshot-changed`. No schema or database was at fault. The private snapshot fork now accepts a WAL whose only change is the ctime SQLite itself causes.

Refs #192755

## User Impact

Root installs on Linux (for example default Kali, containers, some VPS setups) get a working default Doctor gate. Post-update automation stops seeing a false failure. Not yet released; no manual step is needed once a release contains this.

## Why This Change Was Made

SQLite's `unixOpen` calls `fchown` on the WAL on every open when `euid` is 0, read-only opens included. On Linux that bumps ctime even though the owner doesn't change. The retained image fingerprint (`captureSqlitePrivateSnapshotFamily`) included ctime, so the first reader to open the retained image made the fingerprint differ, and the later fork refused the image.

This explains the reporter's whole table:
- The default profile and `--only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas` read state first, then fork, so they failed.
- `--all` uses the isolated plugin state mode, which forks before any reader opens the image, so it passed.
- Non-root installs never call `fchown`, which is why earlier reproduction attempts passed 8 of 8.

The reporter's Kali host runs as root. It also needs a WAL with frames, meaning a running Gateway.

`src/infra/sqlite-private-snapshot-fork.ts`: the WAL fingerprint is now device, inode, mtime and size. Ctime goes because of the `fchown`; birthtime goes because libuv derives it from ctime when `statx` is unavailable. The main database keeps its full fingerprint: SQLite never `fchown`s it, and the existing same-size edit test depends on ctime there.

Rejected: excluding root from the check, because that would hide real changes. Rejected: forking first in every profile, because the default profiles deliberately reuse the report's image and defer the fork.

Accepted edge case: an external rewrite of a retained WAL that preserves inode, size and mtime now goes undetected. The image is private to this report and has no supported writer.

## Evidence

Real CLI on Crabbox (AWS Linux, Node 24.22.1, SQLite 3.53.4), running as root with a live Gateway, using the reported sequence twice:

| Build | Default | `--only` schema check | `--all` |
|---|---|---|---|
| published 2026.11.5-beta.1 | rc=1, `retained-snapshot-changed` (2/2) | rc=1 (2/2) | rc=0 (2/2) |
| main `c8094c112b4` | rc=1, `retained-snapshot-changed` (2/2) | rc=1 (2/2) | rc=0 (2/2) |
| this fix, package built from it | rc=0, 42 checks (2/2) | rc=0 (2/2) | rc=0 (2/2) |

The same published beta as a non-root user passed all of these. A minimal `node:sqlite` probe shows it directly: a read-only open as root changes only the WAL's ctime, and `strace` shows the `fchown` calls; as a non-root user nothing changes.

Regression test: the new case in `src/infra/sqlite-private-snapshot-fork.test.ts` fails on base with `reason=retained-snapshot-changed` and passes with the fix. The fork, single-flight, snapshot-admission and Doctor state-isolation suites pass 66/66. Format and lint are clean; the test-line ratchet passes.

Gap: the test simulates `fchown` with a same-mode `chmod`, so only the native run exercises real SQLite as root. The native fix run was on a package built from the fix on top of `c8094c112b4`.

`$autoreview` was scoped-clean at P2. An independent Codex review of the commit returned NO FINDINGS: consumers treat `family.wal` as opaque, and no persisted form needs compatibility.

auto_merge.commit_message:
SQLite fchowns the WAL on every native open when running as root, including
read-only opens. That bumps the WAL's ctime without changing its bytes, so
the retained-image fingerprint reported retained-snapshot-changed once any
reader had opened the image. The default and --only Doctor profiles read
before forking and failed every run with a live WAL; --all forks first and
passed. The WAL fingerprint now covers identity, mtime and size. Main keeps
ctime, since SQLite never fchowns it.

prs.title: fix(bedrock): resolve the in. India inference-profile prefix for known context windows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: OpenClaw on Amazon Bedrock reports the conservative 32,000-token context window for models discovered through India-geo inference profiles, because the discovery code strips the `us.`/`eu.`/`ap.`/`apac.`/`au.`/`jp.`/`global.` geo prefixes but not the `in.` India prefix.

## User Impact

User impact: Bedrock users in India Regions (Mumbai/Hyderabad) whose inference profiles use the `in.` prefix get every known model's context window collapsed to the 32,000-token unknown-model fallback, so context budgeting and compaction under-size models that resolve correctly in other geographies. This includes the Kimi K3 India profile `in.moonshotai.kimi-k3` documented on its AWS model card.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveKnownContextWindow` and the SYSTEM_DEFINED profile base-model extraction in `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts` share a geo-prefix alternation that predates the India geography. AWS documents India geo inference IDs like `in.moonshotai.kimi-k3` on the Kimi K3 model card (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-moonshot-ai-kimi-k3.html — "Geo inference ID: `in.moonshotai.kimi-k3`" routing across Mumbai/Hyderabad). Without `in` in the alternation:

- an `in.`-prefixed profile with empty model ARNs fails the base-model extraction, so it cannot inherit the foundation model's capabilities or context window, and
- `resolveKnownContextWindow("in.<known-model>")` misses the catalog entry and falls back to 32,000.

This adds `in` to both alternations, matching how `au.`/`apac.` were handled when those geographies were introduced (the existing regional-prefix test covers that history).

## What Was Changed

- `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts`: added `in` to the geo-prefix alternations in `resolveKnownContextWindow` and the SYSTEM_DEFINED profile base-model extraction.
- `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts`: extended the existing `au.`/`apac.` regional-prefix test with an `in.` profile and asserted it resolves the base model's known 1,000,000-token window.

Not changed: `isKnownClaudeMythosPreviewModelId` (its `[/.:]`-anchored pattern already matches prefixed ids without stripping), the catalog entries, the 32,000 fallback, and `defaultContextWindow` config.

## Evidence

Real before/after on stock main (only the AWS SDK transport mocked; `discoverBedrockModels` is the production discovery path):

```text
before: an in.xai.grok-4.6 system profile (empty model ARNs, forcing the
        prefix fallback) was discovered but received the 32,000 fallback:
        expected { id: 'in.xai.grok-4.6', …(6) } to match object { contextWindow: 500000 }
after:  full discovery.test.ts — 21/21 passed, including
        "resolves au., apac., and in. prefixes for regional inference profiles"
```

- Focused full-file suite: `scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts` — 21/21 passed.
- Format check (re-run after formatter write) and scoped oxlint on both changed files: pass.
- Latest-main re-check: both alternations on main still lack `in`, so the fix is not already upstream.
- Local full-repo typecheck was not runnable in this environment (it needs the generated `packages/plugin-sdk/dist` declarations, which the local build pipeline does not emit on Windows); the change extends two existing regex alternations and reuses the existing test helper, and CI type coverage applies.

## Risks / Notes for Reviewers

- The `in.` prefix only strips when followed by a dot at the start of the id, exactly like the existing geo prefixes; Bedrock foundation model ids are `vendor.model` shaped, so no vendor namespace collides with `in.`.
- If AWS introduces another geography prefix later, it needs the same one-token addition.

prs.title: fix(release): read waiver aggregate logs with escape sequences allowed
prs.body:
## Problem

`validateReleaseWaiverAggregates` reads the failed `Verify release checks` job log through `gh api .../logs`. gh 2.97+ refuses log bodies containing terminal escape sequences, including when output is piped, so a waived live-provider failure ends Release Decision in `orchestration_error` instead of being evaluated. The sibling readers (`frv.mjs`, `release-ci-summary.mjs`, `release-publish-state.mts`) already pass `--allow-escape-sequences`.

## Solution

Read the job log with `--allow-escape-sequences`, falling back to the plain call when an older gh rejects the flag.

## Impact

Release tooling only. Needed for 2026.11.1: its waivers run through this path for the first time under gh 2.97+.

## Evidence

Ran `scripts/full-release-validation-state.mjs decision` against FRV 41903285518 attempt 2 with its sealed plan on gh 2.103.3 (read-only):

- Before: `orchestration_error`, `the response contains terminal escape sequences; pass --allow-escape-sequences to output it anyway`
- After: `passed`, 0 blockers, waivers exactly `validate_release_live_cache` and `Kova mock provider performance`

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid unnecessary cold-start initialization
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547

## What Problem This Solves

Cold model catalog preparation loads full configuration validation into a worker. OpenAI discovery also loads broad authentication modules for credentials that only need a marker check, and a late discovery helper brings configuration I/O back through an unconditional OAuth import. The small Linux spawn broker separately initializes Gateway recovery and logging through its OOM-score helper.

## User Impact

Catalog preparation and broker startup avoid unnecessary initialization while preserving model discovery, public constructor identity, default configuration capture, SecretRef handling, credential authority, and child-process supervision. No configuration changes or migration are required. Catalog suppression consumes its supplied generation metadata without another ambient lookup.

The latest completed Linux ARM64 trial still failed after readiness. This PR does not yet establish a working 1 GiB Gateway; landing remains held for the unchanged acceptance test.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit-input cores keep internal catalog callers out of ambient configuration I/O while public factories retain their defaults. Runtime getters use the existing snapshot owner. Windows command credentials load shell configuration only when needed and recheck authority before execution. The credential-writer guard follows the core and public facade boundaries.

OpenAI marker-only imports use the existing narrow SDK entrypoint. Profile and mode-none discovery still load the auth runtime in their existing branch; Codex metadata loads only when needed. The discovery helper loads the canonical OAuth resolver only for SecretRef resolution or expiring OAuth refresh. Imports stay outside credential-error catches, and refresh authority is checked again after the new await.

Actual child spawning and OOM-score operations now live in a small leaf shared by the broker, group anchor, and spawn diagnostics. Gateway preparation retains runtime viability, shell hardening, and the original public exports. No memory limits, broker lifecycle, command authority, or cleanup semantics change.

## Evidence

- Current-head [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41936975634) passed on `dc5351f0`: 86 successful, 27 skipped, zero failures. Required CI, dependency and security checks passed. The intervening `124b40df` run exposed a missing native-wrapper inventory entry, now repaired. No inherited-failure exception is needed.
- The real source-broker regression fails on the original recovery import, then passes with actual child output, zero exit, and closure. Its existing Node transport suite passes all 16 cases; 75 distinct relevant cases pass overall, with 7 existing platform skips. The final owner run took 27.12 seconds including fixture preparation. Core production and process-test types, type-aware lint, format/parity, mock-export and test-line ratchets pass. The dedicated 43-line allocation funds exact regression growth; the shared scalar is unchanged.
- The targeted canonical standalone emit removes top-level recovery/subsystem initialization. Logging bodies remain bundled behind the existing Windows-only error path, and external Chalk/tslog imports remain. This establishes deferred cold initialization, not a measured RAM reduction or removal of all logging dependencies.
- The discovery-auth cold catalog and authority regressions pass 63 cases. Original import-edge and removed-authority-guard controls fail as intended. Earlier reviewed source evidence includes 113 credential-writer cases, 64 affected cases, two integration cases, 54 CI-repair cases, 25 upstream integration cases, and 55 OpenAI credential/catalog cases. The prior full native build passed in 239.49 seconds.
- Local ClawSweeper found no correctness or security findings in `003f1f6e..ed9eb35f`, `e5e38a2e..2b6f4adc`, `e6867c55..e28fc70e`, and `e28fc70e..124b40df`. Independent review covered upstream integration and intervening mechanical repairs, including the one-line `124b40df..dc5351f0` wrapper inventory correction. Its five affected closure cases and native provisioning case pass; the temporary local missing-pnpm setup failure is separate from the CI failure.
- The actual `e28fc70e` ARM64 package passed all four artifact gates. Its four catalog roots, including the late discovery-auth helper, had no static-relative path to full configuration I/O or the top-level schema. This proof excludes other dynamic imports, bare dependencies, and runtime memory behavior.
- The completed strict `e28fc70e` trial reached readiness at 14.879 seconds, then suffered service OOM at the unchanged 768 MiB service limit before a real-model success marker or 60-second soak. Classification was UNKNOWN/service-evidence because the service cgroup disappeared; explicit OOM observations remain recorded. Temporary credentials and the VM were removed, and 512 MiB was skipped. The new broker extraction still needs its canonical ARM64 build and strict 1 GiB trial.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes MCP apps such as Excalidraw remaining in a thin top strip after clicking Edit to expand the transcript app.

## User Impact

Expanded apps fill the available editor height, follow viewport resizing, and still return to their original inline height when closed. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript adapter forced `display: block` inline, overriding the existing fullscreen flex layout. Remove that redundant override so the stylesheet remains the single layout owner; inline `display: block` and the existing minimum height stay intact. No sandbox, CSP, permission, or transport policy changes.

## Evidence

- Same browser flow through the real Control UI transcript host, sandbox, and MCP bridge fails before the fix in Chromium and WebKit: an 800px fullscreen host contains a 150px app frame. After the fix, both engines give the app 708px of usable height. Viewport resize and Close back to 450px inline also pass.
- The fixture is a synthetic MCP app with an Edit button and diagram, not the upstream Excalidraw frontend. The Gateway methods are mocked; this proves the production host-layout boundary, not a live-provider or deployed-Gateway result.
- Focused browser regression: 2 tests passed, 5.53s test time / 19.11s wall time including the isolated UI build. Exact-head CI build and the selected UI E2E job also passed.
- Formatting, diff whitespace, assertion-safety and line-cap ratchets pass. Local lint is blocked before analysis because the task checkout links another checkout's dependencies, which the physical dependency-boundary policy rejects. The completed CI attempt reported no lint error in a changed file; inherited failures are recorded below. No guard was bypassed.
- Regression adds 140 test lines for the real nested-frame browser boundary, with its own test-line allocation. Production delta is one replaced line; no new runtime machinery.

- Independent source review confirmed the production fix and found two test issues, now addressed: register this suite for CI WebKit provisioning and verify resized geometry shrinks without viewport overflow.
- Workflow static validation passes (`zizmor`, Git-owned workflow checks, and composite interpolation check). The requested workflow guard corpus exceeded the 180s local command deadline before completion; no failing assertion was observed. The exact-head CI attempt is now complete; its inherited failures are recorded below.

- Local ClawSweeper completed the full committed range `943904e8c4cae76b64bf83b1b53a8c230122fb9b..aa435a560e087fa457654d29518031d818330e9e` with high reasoning effort and P2 triage coverage. No actionable correctness or security findings; no remaining review findings. This was source-only review, not an additional runtime replay.

[CI run 41938414952, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41938414952) finished with failed CI, not a green result. Build artifacts, the selected UI E2E job, and independent security-fast passed. The two root failures are unrelated to this patch:

prs.title: fix(ui): reloaded Claude CLI chats show OpenClaw tools as raw MCP bridge names
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192360

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a Claude CLI backed chat is reloaded, the Control UI shows OpenClaw tool calls under their MCP bridge names (`mcp__openclaw__exec`, ...). This also drops the exec command view and the apply_patch diff.

## User Impact

User impact: reloaded Claude CLI chats now show OpenClaw tools the same way the live run does: Exec with its terminal view, Edited with its +1 -1 diffstat, Read. Tools from other MCP servers keep their catalog names and icons. Stored and invoked tool names do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191217 made the iOS tool display project bridged MCP names onto the tool they call, for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191211. Two parts of the TypeScript side matter here:

- Live CLI tool events already strip the OpenClaw loopback prefix.
- Claude CLI history keeps the raw name on purpose. It reaches `unwrapToolCallForDisplay`, the shared display projection used by the Control UI, the TUI and the Gateway activity projection, and that function only unwrapped the `tool_call` / `dispatch_action` dispatchers.

This change moves the existing `stripOpenClawMcpToolPrefix` into that display module and applies it there. The CLI runner and auto-reply callers now import it from the display module, so the rule has one owner. Unchanged calls are returned as the same object, as before. Against the merge base the diff is production +24/-21 and tests +13/-13 lines.

The strip is limited to OpenClaw's own loopback prefix (`mcp__openclaw__`, and `mcp_openclaw_` for Gemini). Unlike the iOS fix, it does not strip every `mcp__<server>__` prefix. Other MCP servers' tools are cataloged under their raw ids, and the Control UI's plugin icon lookup is keyed by them.

## Evidence

The render below ran at `0eea225a667` (base `upstream/main` `a1d320457f4`). The head `c2411a1fdfa` changes only tests after that, so the production code it renders is the same.

Both sides ran the same steps:

1. A Gateway test harness (its own state directory and port, no credentials) gets a session bound to `claude-cli` and a synthetic Claude CLI transcript. The transcript has bridged `exec`, `apply_patch` and `read` calls.
2. A WebSocket client reads `chat.history`.
3. The Control UI e2e harness serves exactly that reply to the built Control UI in Chromium, opens `/chat` and expands the activity group.

No model is called.

`chat.history` reply (the same on both sides; this change only affects presentation):

```text
assistant toolcall name=mcp__openclaw__exec args={"command":"pnpm test","workdir":"/workspace","timeout":120,"yieldMs":10000}
assistant toolcall name=mcp__openclaw__apply_patch args={"input":"*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: README.md\n@@\n-Old line\n+New line\n*** End Patch"}
assistant toolcall name=mcp__openclaw__read args={"path":"README.md"}
```

| Before (base `a1d320457f4`) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Base: generic rows and "Mcp Openclaw Apply Patch"](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261103-191217-shared-tool-display-mcp-bridge-names/before.png) | ![Fix: terminal view, Edited README.md +1 -1, Read README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261103-191217-shared-tool-display-mcp-bridge-names/after.png) |

Observed result:

- On the base, the three rows are generic:
  - exec shows a "pnpm test" row with a key/value argument list;
  - apply_patch shows "Mcp Openclaw Apply Patch" with no diff;
  - read shows a "README.md" row with `path:`.
- With the fix, the rows are the terminal view `$ pnpm test`, "Edited README.md +1 -1" and "Read README.md". That render is byte-identical to a control run served the same history with the prefix removed by hand.

The composer's model label (`gpt-5.5`) and the session name (`Main`) come from the Control UI harness's mock fixture and are unrelated to this change; the tool rows come from the Gateway's `chat.history` reply.

Tool calls in the Gateway reply: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261103-191217-shared-tool-display-mcp-bridge-names/gateway-chat-history.txt

Regression tests fail on the base and pass with the fix:

- `ui/src/lib/chat/tool-call-view.test.ts` has two new rows in the existing classification table:
  - bridged `mcp__openclaw__apply_patch` with a `changes` payload is classified as the edit view, which needs the projected call to keep its arguments;
  - a bridged `mcp__openclaw__tool_call` dispatcher calling `exec` is classified as the command view.
- `src/agents/tool-display-call.test.ts` adds `mcp__other__tool_call` to the existing "leaves unchanged" table, so another MCP server's dispatcher is not unwrapped. That row passes on the base and guards the narrow prefix.

The `stripOpenClawMcpToolPrefix` assertions moved from `src/agents/cli-runner/tool-policy.test.ts` to `src/agents/tool-display-call.test.ts` along with the function. They are unchanged; only the `describe` wrapper became a top-level test.

Checks:

- the touched test files (wall times in the table below);
- 14 test files of the changed modules' consumers, including `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-tool-icons.test.ts` and `src/infra/agent-activity-events.test.ts`;
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:ui` at `0eea225a667`; `pnpm tsgo:test:src` at `a12983253e8` and `pnpm tsgo:test:ui` at `c2411a1fdfa`;
- oxlint and `oxfmt --check` on the 11 touched files;
- the test-lines ratchet (`Test lines OK: 6440150; ceiling: 6440682; slack: 532` against the merge base).

The broad suites run in this PR's CI. Before opening this PR I also ran a local AI code review of the diff. It reported no findings.

Two CI reds on `0eea225a667`:

- `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` / test-lines (run 41734617010): `Test lines: 6444107; ceiling: 6444035; over by: 72; net delta: +19`. `main` in that run was already 53 lines over its ceiling, so any net growth fails. The ratchet caps allocation credit at the lines this change itself adds, so no allocation record can cover main's 53-line overage. The cost budget's allocation rule covers only net growth. This change folds the regressions into existing tables instead: tests are now +13/-13, net 0, which the ratchet accepts on an over-ceiling tree. No allocation record and no scalar change.
- `control-ui-performance`: startup JS gzip went from 90681 B to 90693 B (+12 B). The enforcement limit is 90687 B (90111 B baseline + 512 B growth + 64 B build variance), so the base had 6 B left. This change adds no startup code. I built the Control UI locally with the base and head `tool-display-call.ts` and the same toolchain. The three startup files (`index`, `rolldown-runtime`, `control-ui-connection`) have the same raw size in the local build, 283753 B (CI logged 283645 B). With the lazy-chunk hashes in their filenames replaced, they are byte-identical. The gzip delta comes from the different hash strings of the lazy chat chunks that the startup code names, and shrinking this change cannot remove it. Chat boot JS shrank 154 B in the same run.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall |
| --- | --- |
| `src/agents/tool-display-call.test.ts` | 1.53 s |
| `ui/src/lib/chat/tool-call-view.test.ts` | 1.75 s |
| `src/agents/cli-runner/tool-policy.test.ts` | 1.48 s |

Not covered:

- The Control UI render used the e2e harness serving the real Gateway's `chat.history` reply, not a live Claude CLI run.
- The TUI and the Android app were not exercised. Android's `ToolDisplayCall.kt` mirrors only the dispatcher unwrap and still shows bridged names; it is left for a separate change with Android proof.
- The full `pnpm check:changed` did not run locally; CI runs it.

prs.title: fix(telegram): cap rich message media at 20
prs.body:
Closes #129004

## What Problem This Solves

Rich Telegram replies can appear successful while losing attachments and trailing content when a message contains more than 20 media items. Direct edits can bypass send pagination.

## User Impact

Twenty media remain in one rich message; 21 are delivered in ordered pages of 20 and 1 with their trailing text intact. An over-limit edit becomes one complete plain replacement when it fits 4096 Unicode code points, or fails locally without overwriting the existing message. No new configuration, SDK surface, or migration is introduced.

**Remaining merge-proof gap:** this environment has no access to the existing Telegram Test Server QA broker. A maintainer with that access still needs to run the required final-revision userbot/recipient verification. The local HTTP tests below are not a substitute for live recipient readback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing rich-block owner now enforces the observed 20-media budget for ordinary blocks, media-heavy list items, and wrappers whose own summary/caption exceeds the local text target. List metadata, gallery captions, ordering, and trailing text remain intact. The edit owner checks the complete normalized plan and preserves current literal-text entities and request authorization.

This refresh integrates main `44b6d7ca4a96074fef68870cc6f3a210b42856b8` with a regular merge, not a force-push. Edit regressions moved into the maintained HTTP suite rather than restoring the retired test file. The duplicate standalone 20/21 unit case was removed; distinct list/gallery contracts remain.

## Evidence

Candidate: `cac84a8fe91e07fef1401bd2faf65bc585e3f62c` (tree `d9a249bc9317cafda8bfad343efc6e0b84df9c7c`).

- **Baseline discrimination:** pinned main plus the same regression tests finished with **14 expected failures / 82 passes / 96 cases**. Failures include 21-media sends, long-summary/caption wrappers, complete Markdown/native edits, Unicode overflow rejection, and list/gallery boundaries. Setup failures are not counted as baseline-red.
- **Candidate:** **96/96 passed** across `rich-blocks.test.ts` (35) and `send.telegram-http.test.ts` (61), including the long-wrapper case through the production HTTP send path. The final lint-repaired snapshot was rerun: Vitest 35.01 s; complete monitored wall time 41.767 s. These are combined-run timings, not individual-file wall times.
- **Local static gates:** six-file format and syntax checks, focused syntax-only boundary lint (0 warnings/errors), and pinned-base whitespace checks passed. Full build, repository-wide typecheck/type-aware lint, and full test suites were not run locally.
- **Independent review:** one completed local Codex autoreview campaign against the pinned base was `scoped-clean` through P2, with no material findings in an additional independent source review. Reviewed tree: `7108acc25f0139b68f246e205d5930cb714f05e8`; that review was followed by formatter-only changes plus the exact test-line allocation, verified mechanically before retesting. The later lint correction received the separate fresh delta review described below. This is not human approval or a new hosted ClawSweeper verdict.

prs.title: fix(bedrock): use known Qwen3 256K context windows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: OpenClaw on Amazon Bedrock treats the Qwen3 Coder 480B A35B, Qwen3 Next 80B A3B, and Qwen3 235B A22B 2507 models as 32k-context models when they appear in the account's model listings, because the extension's known-context-window catalog has no entries for them.

## User Impact

User impact: Bedrock users selecting these Qwen3 variants now get the documented 256K-token context window in the discovered model metadata, so context budgeting and compaction size the models correctly instead of using the conservative 32,000-token unknown-model fallback (8x smaller than documented).

## Why This Change Was Made

`KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` in `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts` is the single catalog mapping Bedrock model IDs to context windows; unknown IDs fall back to a conservative 32,000-token default. Three Qwen3 models listed in the AWS Bedrock catalog were missing, while their siblings (`qwen.qwen3-coder-next`, `qwen.qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-v1:0`) were already present — mirroring the gaps fixed in #192927 and the same-day sibling fixes (#193022, #193035, #193045, #193050). This adds the documented 256K value for each with the AWS model card as the source; resolution goes through the existing prefix-stripping and `:0`-suffix normalization.

- Qwen3 Coder 480B A35B: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-qwen-qwen3-coder-480b-a35b-instruct.html — "Context window: 256K tokens"
- Qwen3 Next 80B A3B: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-qwen-qwen3-next-80b-a3b.html — "Context window: 256K tokens"
- Qwen3 235B A22B 2507: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-qwen-qwen3-235b-a22b-2507.html — "Context window: 256K tokens"

## What Was Changed

- `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts`: added the three Qwen3 entries to `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` with model-card links.
- `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts`: regression test asserting all three base IDs and a `us.qwen.qwen3-next-80b-a3b` inference-profile variant resolve `contextWindow: 256_000`.

Not changed: existing Qwen entries, Claude 5.x / Claude Opus 4.8 special-casing, the conservative 32,000 fallback, and `defaultContextWindow` config.

## Evidence

Real before/after on stock main (only the AWS SDK transport mocked; `discoverBedrockModels` is the production discovery path):

```text
before: red fixture with the three Qwen3 model summaries received
        "contextWindow": 32000 for each (conservative unknown-model fallback)
after:  full discovery.test.ts — 22/22 passed, including the new
        "uses the documented 256K context windows for the Qwen3 Coder 480B, Next 80B, and 235B 2507 models"
```

- Focused full-file suite: `scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts` — 22/22 passed.
- Format check (`scripts/run-format.mts --check`, re-run after formatter write) and scoped oxlint on both changed files: pass.
- Latest-main re-check at `1cd54b32aca0`: the catalog still lacks all three entries, so the fix is not already on main.
- Local full-repo typecheck was not runnable in this environment (it needs the generated `packages/plugin-sdk/dist` declarations, which the local build pipeline does not emit on Windows); the changes only add `Record<string, number>` entries and reuse existing test helpers, and CI type coverage applies.

## Risks / Notes for Reviewers

- Data-only catalog additions; no API, config, schema, or protocol surface changes.
- Qwen3 Coder 480B is in AWS "Legacy" lifecycle (EOL 2027-03-30) but still appears in discovery listings; the entry is correct while the model remains listed.
- If AWS revises a window, the entry needs the same one-line update as its siblings.

prs.title: fix(browser): navigation fails with Invalid InterceptionId when a page cancels a document request
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `browser open` / `browser navigate` fails with `Fetch.continueRequest: Invalid InterceptionId` on pages that start and then cancel a document request, such as an iframe the page removes or re-targets (reproduced 3/3 on https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/ in the managed `openclaw` profile).

## User Impact

User impact: guarded navigations and actions now complete on these pages instead of failing. Pages that are blocked by navigation policy are still blocked and reported, and other CDP errors still fail the navigation as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The navigation authority fence pauses each document request, runs an async policy check, then resumes it with `Fetch.continueRequest` (or cancels it with `Fetch.failRequest`). If the page cancels the request while it is paused, Chromium drops the interception, so the later continue/fail is rejected with `Invalid InterceptionId`. The fence treated that as a fatal navigation error.

Chromium rejects an unknown interception id before it changes anything, and the cancelled request can no longer load. That means there is nothing left to allow or deny, so the fence now treats that one error as settled. Policy denial is still recorded before the cancel is attempted, so a denied document is still reported (and its source still counts as preserved). There are no retries or delays.

The extension relay carries the same Fetch commands, so it needed matching changes or the fix would make things worse there:

- `RelayFetch` retires only the ended pause instead of marking the whole lease uncertain. Before this, later live requests got the stored error back without reaching Chromium, and the fence would now have read that as "settled".
- `RelaySessionOwner` no longer retires the whole physical attachment for this error.
- Owner-close and retirement cleanup treat an already-ended pause as cleaned up, instead of detaching peers.

Every other native Fetch error still fences, retires, or surfaces exactly as before.

<details><summary>Real-Chromium trace (DMV portal, standalone CDP mirror of the fence)</summary>

```
     6 requestPaused interception-job-1.0  Document https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/
    27 continued interception-job-1.0
  5055 requestPaused interception-job-78.0 Document https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/
  5057 Network.loadingFailed B71260A7…  Document net::ERR_ABORTED canceled
  5076 CONTINUE FAILED interception-job-78.0 cdpSession.send: Protocol error (Fetch.continueRequest): Invalid InterceptionId.
  5279 goto ok 200 https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/
```

The page cancels a second document request 2 ms after it is paused. The fence's continue arrives about 20 ms later.

</details>

## Evidence

- New real-Chromium live test `pw-session-navigation-stale-interception.live.test.ts` covers three cases: a guarded goto, a guarded action, and a denied document, each where the page cancels a paused child document. All 3 fail on the base commit with the production error (or with source-preservation lost in the denied case) and pass with the fix.
- Temporary probe (not committed): `gotoPageWithNavigationGuard` against the live DMV portal in an isolated headless Chromium 1248 (not the Gateway's profile). Before the fix it failed. After the fix it went 3/3 `ok 200 https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/`.
- Unit and composed regressions:
  - fence: a retired id is settled on both resume paths, a denied document is still reported when its cancel hits a retired id, and other protocol errors still fail;
  - `RelayFetch`: a retired pause leaves the lease usable;
  - `ExtensionRelayBridge`: a cancelled request does not detach the attachment or other pauses, and owner close finishes cleanup without detaching peers.
  - Each new test fails when its production change is reverted.
- The existing "removes the paused-request listener before detachment" test now asserts that no commands are sent after detach, so the new tolerance cannot mask that regression.
- `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 pnpm test:live -- …stale-interception.live.test.ts …navigation-cors.live.test.ts …navigation-authority.live.test.ts`: 3 files, 20 tests passed.
- `pnpm test:extension browser`: 2976 + 158 passed, 114 skipped, 2 failed. The 2 failures are in `system-profiles.test.ts` (leftover cookie snapshot scratch directory). They are inherited: they fail identically on the base commit `8c9310ee363`, and this PR does not touch that file.
- `pnpm format:check`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json <changed files>`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: clean.
- Four independent review passes. Each finding (relay lease fencing, relay attachment retirement, relay owner-close cleanup, weakened listener test) was fixed with a regression test. The final pass on the head commit was clean.

Accepted edge case: the error is matched by its Chromium message text (`Invalid InterceptionId`). CDP has no structured code for it. Any other error text keeps the existing fail-closed handling.

prs.title: fix(ios): Talk start uses stale provider, transport or voice after Talk settings change
prs.body:
Fixes #192873

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the iOS app starts Talk with the previous realtime provider, transport or voice after `talk.realtime` is changed on the Gateway.

## User Impact

User impact: a Talk start on iPhone now uses the Gateway's current Talk settings, so switching provider, transport or voice in the Control UI takes effect on the next start instead of "sometimes".

## Why This Change Was Made

- Every Talk start now waits for a fresh `talk.config` instead of returning early once any config was loaded.
- A prefetched realtime session is dropped (and an in-flight prefetch cancelled) only when the settings it was created with change: route, realtime provider, model, `voice` and the provider config block. An unchanged reload keeps the prefetch, so the extra fetch per start does not throw away the warm session.
- The identity uses `voice`, the field iOS actually sends on create, not `speakerVoice` (macOS-only projection).

## Risks

1. **Overlapping reloads are unordered.** Talk enable fires its own reload next to the start's reload; there is no generation token, so the last response to arrive wins. This existed before; each start now adds one more request.
2. **A failed refresh at start drops a working realtime route.** The existing failure fallback (local route, realtime settings cleared) now runs on starts that previously used the cached config. It matches what the native per-turn reload already does. A prefetched WebRTC session is not closed on that path and can stay open while the start falls back to native speech.
3. **Server-only changes are not visible to the phone.** Instructions, endpoint or credential changes that do not appear in the `talk.config` payload the phone receives keep a reused prefetch on the old session.

## Evidence

Simulator (iPhone 17, iOS 26.5), `xcodebuild test-without-building`, new suite `TalkConfigRefreshTests` (2 tests):

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| With fix, `-test-iterations 10` | 10/10 repetitions passed for each test, 0 issues |
| Source hunks reverted (tests kept), `-test-iterations 10` | 10/10 failed for each test: `observed == [["xai","ara"],["openai","ember"]]` (second start reuses old provider/voice) and `_test_hasPrefetchedRealtimeSession()` (unchanged reload discards the prefetch) |
| Existing Talk suites (`TalkModeManagerTests`, `TalkRealtimeConsultCancellationTests`, `TalkGatewaySpeechClientTests`) | 62 Swift Testing tests + 5 XCTest passed |

Gaps: the drop-on-voice-change assertion also passes on old code (old code always invalidated), so the revert run proves the keep path, not the voice-vs-`speakerVoice` correction itself. No device run; the Gateway-log timeline behind the root cause is in the linked issue.

prs.title: fix(cron): scheduled jobs time out immediately when the clock jumps during a lane wait
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron's execution watchdog pauses the configured job budget for explicit capacity waits. It used `Date.now()` to charge elapsed execution time, while the timer consumes monotonic elapsed time. A forward wall-clock correction before a capacity pause can exhaust the remaining budget and abort a healthy job as soon as its lane admits it; a backward correction can extend the budget.

## Fix

Use the existing process-local `monotonicNow()` owner at both elapsed-time reads. Keep configured budgets, native timers, setup/pre-execution guards, cancellation and persistence unchanged.

Retains @SunnyShu0925's original fix commit. Consolidates the clock regression into existing lifecycle coverage, shares initial/fallback guard cases, and removes a single-use test helper. Production net +3 lines; tests net -2; no allocation files.

## Evidence

[Built Linux Gateway proof and focused check receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192691#issuecomment-6645636947): secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker, shipped entry point, public cron.add/cron.run and seven genuinely contending model jobs. A process-local +13-second Date.now step causes main to time out after its 15-second lane wait without dispatching the target model. Candidate dispatches and preserves approximately 12 seconds of execution time. No-step controls preserve behavior on both trees. Neither the system clock nor performance/timer scheduling changes.

37 focused regression/consumer tests pass. The consolidated clock case fails on main for the intended premature-timeout assertion. Type-aware lint and formatting pass. The final commit changes tests only; production proof inputs are unchanged.

## Risk

Two-way door: revert fully restores prior timing behavior. No stored-data, schema, configuration, authentication, Doctor, update, model-facing text, or public API changes. Blast radius is process-local cron execution-budget accounting around explicit lane waits; other setup/cleanup timeout policies are unchanged.

prs.title: feat(onepassword): sign in to websites with your own 1Password logins (Agentic Autofill preview)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents can't sign in to websites with a person's own 1Password logins. The bundled 1Password plugin only reads operator service-account secrets, and its `get` tool returns secret values to the model and transcript.

## User Impact

Owners can connect their own 1Password account (US Individual/Family, partner preview) and let an agent request specific logins for a task. They approve the request in the 1Password app on their computer through an **Approve sign-in** card in the Control UI chat. The 1Password extension in OpenClaw's managed browser then fills and submits the form. Passwords, tokens, integration keys and the approval link never reach the model, the transcript or the logs. Existing service-account features are unchanged.

The preview is off by default. To try it you need: `plugins.entries.onepassword.config.agenticAutofill.enabled`, plus `extensionPath` (an operator-supplied, unpacked 1Password Nightly extension ≥ 8.12.46.6) and `browserProfile` (a Chromium or Chrome for Testing managed profile; branded Chrome can't load extensions). Approval currently works only in the Control UI and the 1Password desktop app on the Nightly channel.

## Why This Change Was Made

1Password's Agentic Autofill (partner preview) keeps credentials inside its extension: our code only gets statuses and opaque references. OpenClaw can't ship an OAuth client secret, so connecting and token refresh go through a hosted relay at `connect.openclaw.ai` (separate private repo). The relay sees OAuth tokens only long enough to exchange or refresh them. It hands them back sealed to a key the Gateway generates, and it never sees the integration key in readable form.

- **Browser plugin:** a generic, task-scoped extension host (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/browser-extension-host`). It registers a vetted extension before launch, calls the extension's service worker with secrets passed only as call arguments, maps the agent's tab to a Chrome tab ID, and locks the tab while a fill runs.
- **onepassword plugin:** owner-only connect and disconnect through the relay, sealed pickup, token refresh one at a time per connection, and an optional `onepassword_autofill` tool (request, status, fill) that returns statuses only.
- **Approval card:** the approval link reaches the person through a plugin inline view. The saved tool result holds only the request ID. The Gateway keeps the link in memory for up to 10 minutes and gives it only to a current Control UI admin who has access to the session. Clicking the card starts 1Password's status-check schedule.

Review: @joshavant owns the existing 1Password plugin. Please weigh in on the plugin surface and the security model.

## Evidence

**Approval card** (the bundled Control UI end-to-end test with a synthetic 1Password service; cropped to the card)

| | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ready | ![Ready, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/737ea58a-4882-4767-a2ed-d94089e1c664) | ![Ready, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a12e0fbc-489d-4b91-a4f3-d677569c01ad) |
| Waiting | ![Waiting, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d58cb7f1-1473-484b-a9dd-5be77a93cc86) | ![Waiting, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22f8fc37-f22a-4ec4-980f-1016b1da5deb) |
| Approved | ![Approved, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6bbd709-de5f-4190-9947-7938b52c348f) | ![Approved, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/88a9483d-9c3c-4ea4-a462-a7a8310bf7de) |

| Not approved | Expired |
| --- | --- |
| ![Denied](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a09201f-804d-4101-a8b6-82a69dfe3c1b) | ![Expired](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b84f4e9-0f50-43ff-8b5a-d2d942a7d848) |

There was no "before" image: this card is a new surface.

**What was checked**
- **Real 1Password extension:** Nightly 8.12.48.7, loaded through the production extension host. The adapter's readiness check returns `ready` about 2.8 s after browser launch. No tokens were used and no access requests were made.
- **Live relay:** session create, pickup (pending and wrong-token 401), the start page with its confirmation code, the redirect to 1Password with S256 and the registered client, a second Continue rejected with 409, and refresh passing 1Password's `400 invalid_grant` straight through.
- **Encryption:** an envelope sealed by the relay's own code opens with the Gateway's code, for both the tokens and the integration key. A wrong session or purpose is rejected.
- **Real consent:** a manual OAuth connect against production 1Password reached the OpenClaw consent screen, with name and icon, and redirected to the relay.
- **End-to-end UI test:** the link is never in the saved chat history; contrast meets AA; keyboard focus works; reduced motion is respected; the card height stays steady across states.

**Earlier local checks (before review repairs)**
- `pnpm test extensions/onepassword --maxWorkers=1`: 138 passed, 1 skipped (existing skip).
- `pnpm test extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-host.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: passed.
- `extensions/onepassword/browser/index.test.ts` (UI Vitest config): passed.
- `OPENCLAW_BROWSER_EXTENSION_E2E=1` real Chromium extension-host test: passed. It was run before the rebase.
- Typecheck for extensions, extension tests and the UI: passed.
- `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets`, config baseline and inventory checks, and `git diff --check`: passed.


### Review repairs

- Invocation cancellation and current-session authority now reach the extension adapter separately from serialized vendor arguments. Registration, session attachment, worker initialization, tab mapping, and Agentic Mode enablement recheck authority; the final credential-bearing send is guarded. Cancellation after mode enable still disables the tab's Agentic Mode and releases its exclusive lock.
- The fake-host boundary regression rejects both cancellation and revocation during all five preparation waits; an authorized owner fill sends once. Request creation also rejects cancellation during worker initialization. This is adapter-boundary proof, not the real-account end-to-end flow.
- Classified and inventoried `browser-extension-host`; moved the shared private approval projection to a plugin-local leaf; separated extension launch declarations from runtime gates; moved request types to the existing contract leaf to remove the remaining approval owner cycle.
- Corrected setup documentation to describe the private Control UI approval card and its implemented recovery text. Removed the identified low-value checker test and reduced its allocation by 11 lines.
- Test budget: +114 net browser authority regression lines (including required brace formatting) and +3 service assertion lines require a narrow 117-line allocation. The original workflow/approval tests exceeded the existing allocations by one further line after removing the duplicate; a separate one-line reconciliation records only this PR's tests. Shared scalar and inherited debt are unchanged; the exact ratchet passes; unrelated CI assertion cleanup subsequently removes five net test lines.

### Upgrade/data-model compatibility

The existing service-account config parser, broker (including stored grant/audit/pending value shapes), pending-authorization owner, and credential reader have **no diff** against the PR base `d936d4b5e36d`. The original `grants` V2, `audit`, and `pending` namespaces, capacity/eviction settings, and `credentials/onepassword/service-account-token` path are unchanged. No migration, clear, or rewrite is introduced. Without explicit `agenticAutofill.enabled: true`, registration returns before opening autofill state; opt-in adds only `autofill-connections` and `autofill-requests` namespaces. Existing config, broker, worker, and SecretRef tests passed in the scoped plugin suite. This is focused source-contract and regression evidence, not a live installed-version upgrade.

### Repair validation

- `pnpm test extensions/onepassword --maxWorkers=1` (repository runner): 149 passed, 1 existing skip across two configs; 179.81 s including cold worker compilation. The adapter/service repair pair: 44 passed, 4.54 s wrapper wall; individual adapter: 4.02 s, service: 3.84 s. New-head CI seconds are not available yet.
- Browser extension-host/headless-launch focused tests: 7 passed. SDK package-contract/subpath suites: 35 passed. Private approval view UI tests: 3 passed.
- `pnpm --dir ui test src/styles/sr-only.browser.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 3 passed (4.03 s); the prior CI timeout was not reproduced, so no timer/retry/expectation change was made.
- `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`: 0 cycles. Additional-boundary CI command: passed. `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets`: all nine checks passed, including exact test-line budget, config docs and plugin inventory. SDK export sync/check, scoped docs MDX and all docs links passed.
- Local autoreview of the repair snapshot was attempted at P0–P2 with Codex; authentication failed before a report. This is **not a clean independent review**. No hosted re-review was requested.

- Red/green authority proof: the six cancellation/request-creation regression cases fail with the original adapter (credential worker calls occur after authority loss), then pass with the repair. No live credentials are used.
- CI log transport: all requested `gh run view --job … --log-failed` downloads failed with HTTP/2 stream cancellation; HTTP/1 fallback failed with unexpected EOF. Exact check-run annotations were retrieved instead. Canonical `pnpm test:ci-failed 191921` likewise reported unavailable logs, not inherited proof.
- Other prior-red signatures are not classified inherited: recent main annotations did not reproduce them. Main's UI shard passed at `2ac42c830f3e` (run 41644326924/job 125945832763), while this PR's sr-only timeout passes locally. QA Lab killed-run, hooks JSON, WhatsApp delivery-recovery, and browser relay profile-drift checks are separately being reproduced; no blind retries or assertion/timer weakening was used.
- Additional uncovered SDK gate: `plugin-sdk:surface:check` reports 162/161 public entrypoints, 3864/3859 public exports, and 2234/2232 callable exports. The compatibility scan reports no unauthorized removals. Budgets were not raised to hide this result.

**Not yet proven: real connect/approve/fill.** A full real connect, approve and fill against a 1Password Family account through a Gateway. That test remains outside this repair task; no live Gateway was touched. Approving from 1Password's mobile apps isn't available in their preview yet.

<details><summary>Known follow-ups</summary>

- Relay protocol gaps the Gateway side handles conservatively: there's no cancel endpoint after a local disconnect; a failed pickup doesn't return an already-sealed integration key; `expires_in` has no issue timestamp; and a missing key plus a missing `user_id` forces revoke and reconnect.
- Tokens are stored in the plugin's SQLite state, with the same file protection as other OAuth tokens. They are not in an encrypted vault.
- An inline view can't show different text to the model and to the person, so the summary line reads "…Approve it in OpenClaw." everywhere.

</details>

### Additional CI repairs and current limits

- Reproduced browser relay profile name/port drift: old contexts returned `false` after config replacement instead of rejecting. Captured browser contexts now reject when their configured name disappears or endpoint port changes. Existing relay coexistence and hot-reload sibling suites pass: 20 tests, 116.56 s wrapper wall including cold compilation.
- Reproduced WhatsApp recovery failure: durable recovery correctly preserves the selected account and passes `{ accountId: "default" }` to the native listener. The stale fixture now asserts that argument instead of the obsolete four-argument shape; all 6 tests pass (123.25 s wrapper wall including cold compilation).
- Reproduced hooks blank-parent-agent failure: `hooks` preAction intentionally throws the actionable `hooksCliFailure("--agent must not be blank")`; removed the obsolete generic-error fixture branch. The same failed case passes in the prebuilt-runtime rerun; full file passes: 23 tests, 56.99 s wrapper wall (52.64 s test run), using supported prebuilt runtime reuse.
- Extension production/test and UI typechecks passed. Touched onepassword typed lint passed (8 files), browser/WhatsApp typed lint passed (2 files), browser cycle files passed (6 files). Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- A complete runtime prerequisite build passed (7m 43.4s). A subsequent redundant prerequisite build was stopped before source output changes; hooks validation uses the supported prebuilt-runtime mode. One concurrent relay test setup hit a transient removed `extensions/synology-chat/dist` during asset replacement; the later stable-input replay passed and is the reported product evidence.

- QA Lab killed-run replay passed unchanged: `gateway-kill-restart-send.e2e.test.ts`, 1 test, 66.37 s test time. This does not prove a repair or inherited failure; the prior unexpected request signature remains unexplained and is recorded as non-reproduced. The combined baseline replay's only failing test was the stale hooks fixture, independently fixed and replayed green above.
- Final touched-file lint passed, including hooks fixture; final production extension typecheck passed and final Madge scan reports zero cycles. Extension-test and UI typechecks passed. The full baseline suite passed before the two additional CI fixture corrections; final test-line ratchet passes with five lines of slack after those net deletions.

- `plugin-sdk:api:diff --base d936d4b5e36d --head f061b02c1d57`: blocked by the command's host memory limit (16,429 MiB observed versus 16,053 MiB limit) during parallel declaration rendering; no API-diff result was produced. This report covered the original committed SDK introduction; the repair changes only its classification/inventory, not the SDK exports.

- Final complete `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets`: all nine checks passed (118.65 s slowest database-worker phase); final source tree `0e69be6822d` is byte-identical to the validated pre-author-correction tree. Four repair commits are authored by Josh Lehman; the final push used an exact lease solely to correct task-owned author metadata.

prs.body:
Related: #190403

## What Problem This Solves

The iOS drawer does not let users manage session groups from their headers. The drawer and Sessions tab also need consistent group ordering and new-session defaults.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both surfaces use the same group-header controls and Gateway group catalog, matching the Control UI's catalog behavior in `ui/src/lib/sessions/session-group-catalog.ts`. Device-local groups migrate once into an empty writable catalog; older Gateways retain local group management. Group folding is saved on the device.

## User Impact

Long-press a custom group header to create a session in that group, edit its folder and working-copy defaults, rename or create a group, reorder it, or delete it. Empty groups stay available. Tap a header to fold or unfold its sessions. Sessions whose category has no saved defaults can still create another session in that group.
