prs.title: fix(macos): preserve the selected CLI when inspecting a managed install
prs.body:
Closes #140128

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS CLI selection changing when the app inspects a ready managed CLI while an external CLI is selected.

## User Impact

Inspecting installations no longer changes the selected CLI. A successful managed install or update still selects the verified managed CLI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed inspection returns status without persisting selection. Discovery retains its existing selection behavior, while installation and update record the managed CLI only after their success checks. No preference keys or formats changed, and no CLI is removed.

## Evidence

Current product head: `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36`. The 2 November merge combines the published discovery-test follow-up `64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7` with main `c1b0fc1415a09138c48e3f81055aca0f8e4f12aa`. Evidence below is pinned to the revision actually checked; earlier runs are not current-head native execution.

- **Current PR CI:** [Run 41518373631](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518373631) completed successfully at product `6fc1559`, including selected preflight, security-fast, native-i18n and the CI gate. The [combined gate 41518985777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518985777) and security/dependency review statuses also passed. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed. Periphery build and scan checks passed separately; neither is native test execution.
- **Published discovery regression:** [Commit `64bf55b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7) strengthens the existing selection test: it clears both selection keys, calls real discovery, asserts executable/version persistence before managed inspection, and removes the debug project-path shortcut before checking the resolver. The complete delta is one test file (+11/−1), with no production seam or weakened controls. Exact source-delta, patch-application and whitespace checks passed. Independent source review and scoped AutoReview (P0–P3, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, no findings) covered the prepared test change against `b3ee562`; native compilation/execution and baseline mutation proof were not run. Public source inspection confirms these assertions remain present at `6fc1559`.
- **Current-head review (2 November):** [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) completed a review of exact head `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36` with no actionable code findings. Patch quality is 4/6; overall readiness and proof remain 2/6 because actual app-entry/install-update behavior, current native execution and released-state upgrade qualification are not established. [Review run 41547046623](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41547046623) completed; this is source review, not execution proof. The generic existing-data checklist does not identify a concrete schema or data-model defect; the bounded upgrade/preservation proof remains outstanding.

- **Prior-head native-owner proof:** [Hosted macOS run 38597006067](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/38597006067) passed with QA/workflow `4cf95ff77fae422b8b380f4a2c49c4101a8f38b1` and clean initial/final product `76ee71b`. macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.0, Swift 6.4 arm64: 56 Swift Testing declarations across four suites, expanding to 64 executed cases (50 single-case declarations plus 14 cases from six parameterized declarations). Selection, managed-update success/failure, and older/missing/revoked canonical-verification controls passed. These are executable fixtures, not real npm installations or signed-app proof.
- **Prior-head canonical CI:** [Run 38599555604](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38599555604) passed at exact product `76ee71b`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Its macOS Swift and macOS Node jobs were skipped, not executed; native proof comes from the separate owner run above.
- **Prior applicability:** Source review of then-current main `794d6500f382311cab58f5d474a9ef248598e5f2` still finds the ready `managedStatus` selection write. This is source evidence, not a new live reproduction.
- **Prior-head review (29 October):** [ClawSweeper Revision 14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) reviewed `a2c6197` on 29 October. It reports no findings, patch quality 4/6, and overall/proof 2/6. App-entry inspection and verified installation/update evidence, plus an existing-state upgrade from `v2026.10.9` preserving settings and data, remain required. The completed review does not establish a data-model defect.
- **Fixture follow-up:** [Commit `4298606`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4298606a9e38b4665dc014a71fd81bfb451d97af) changes exactly two positive Node fixture literals, preserving all assertions, old-runtime controls, and production source. Whitespace and exact source-delta checks passed. [Previous-head canonical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121014753) passed, including its CI gate, native i18n, and security-fast. The prior [combined CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121219433) also reports success at `4298606`. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed; no current-head native execution proof is claimed.

### Remaining qualification

- **App entry and update:** The owner tests and retained real-npm evidence cover the affected **unbundled** discovery/inspection path at their recorded revisions. Signed packaged-app proof is separate: it must establish the actual legacy-service inspection/update routing, selection preservation, and verified canonical selection. A fresh bundled no-op or forced override cannot stand in for the original bug. The 56 owner declarations do not directly cover `install(target:)` success/compatibility-failure selection paths. The published discovery regression now asserts persistence from initially unset keys before inspection, but its new assertions still need native execution; the historical 56-declaration run predates them.
- **Existing-state upgrade:** A disposable latest-stable-to-candidate app upgrade with existing settings/data retained remains unrun. No preference/schema format changed, and source review found no data-model incompatibility; the missing upgrade run is a proof gap, not an established migration defect.
- **Current composition:** The fixtures emit `v24.22.1`, which satisfies the current runtime requirement; the 24 October change addressed the higher minimum inspected at that time. This two-line fixture-only repair is published at `4298606`; native execution of the current composition remains unverified. This does not relabel the pinned original-head result or establish a production incompatibility.

### Retained real coexisting-installation proof

[Run 37386979616](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616) compared earlier product `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b` with baseline `3b16db73c0b5209aad2ee7c3fb5ddfb12fb208f9`, governed by corrected QA workflow `b166bce6b7ee4fc86631cb491fd7c17990be6362`. The candidate preserved external selection through ready managed inspection and left initially unset executable/version preferences unset: one native test passed in 74.660 seconds. The baseline failed exactly the five expected selection assertions; its verifier rejected other failures.

Both jobs used two distinct real `openclaw@2026.9.8` npm installations with verified published SHA-512 integrity on disposable hosted macOS runners. Cleanup, preference/environment restoration, and pristine-source checks passed. [Candidate receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11380755806) and [baseline receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11379004102) contain selection cells, installation identities, logs, and strict verification summaries. This covers inspection only at the earlier revision, not current signed-app install/update or upgrade behavior. Preceding failed QA attempts do not establish this result.

<details>
<summary>Historical CI and source qualification</summary>

[CI 37194001816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001816), including native Swift, [macOS Periphery 37194001640](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001640), and [shared OpenClawKit Periphery 37194001665](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001665) passed at earlier head `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b`. Previously reported formatting, whitespace checks, and scoped Codex AutoReview remain historical proof, not a fresh review of the current head.

</details>

Maintainer review remains separate. The fixture-only follow-up changed no production source. The current head also includes the 2 November main merge. Swift owner tests, real installation, and app upgrade remain unverified for the current head; skipped CI lanes do not supply that proof.

prs.title: improve(ios): polish native chat, floating composer, and sidebar
prs.body: Closes #141184 ## What Problem This Solves The iOS chat composer occupies a large fixed footer, preventing messages from flowing behind Liquid Glass. Connection and loading indicators compete with the conversation, and ordinary session actions look destructive. ## Why This Change Was Made Use a compact floating composer with measured trailing transcript space, native menus, and quieter navigation while preserving the existing red/gray palette, typography, attachments, and voice controls. The composer overlays the transcript instead of reducing its viewport. Upstream’s session-bound, one-shot scroll commands handle sending and jumping to the latest reply without retaining row-ID scroll constraints. Shared presentation helpers keep loading and connection chrome consistent. ## User Impact - Messages scroll behind the composer; multiline drafts grow naturally, and the latest reply remains reachable above the input. - Attachments come first in the options menu. Model, effort, context, and permission controls retain their capability restrictions and use catalog-compatible localized labels. - Selected model options remain visible to accessibility. The macOS model menu retains its sign-in action when no models are available. - Ordinary session actions use standard colors; Delete remains destructive. Unread indicators are neutral, and rows announce unread/pinned state. - Overview keeps its toolbar reachable, uses quieter counters, and opens Usage from Tokens. Small sidebar and onboarding controls meet 44-point touch targets. Reduce Motion is respected. - Upstream’s persistent iOS chat owner, gateway switcher, session attention controls, and desktop styling are preserved. ## Evidence October 12 update integrates upstream `a010ee5721f140f5da48c6c761273b5ebda4cd54`, retaining its live-reply deduplication, deferred menus, compact-width avatar treatment, session-bound scroll commands, and operator/node connection distinction. Removed the unused chat-layout parameter reported by shared dead-code CI. The previously blocked keyboard/history flow reproduced on the integrated candidate: after a multiline send, the app consumed a full CPU core in SwiftUI `LazySubviewPlacements`. Ungrouped transcript content now has one stable layout container per lazy-stack child, preserving row IDs and spacing. The unchanged keyboard/history test passes after this repair; assertions were not weakened. Local validation on iPhone 17 / iOS 26.2 with Xcode 27: - 106 iOS tests in six suites pass, including the latest upstream connection/reconnect regressions, sidebar, and typography. - 39 shared chat tests in five suites pass; shared macOS and iOS simulator builds pass. - The full keyboard/history test passes three times after the fix, covering keyboard opening, typing, sending, preserved history position, multiline anchored replies, and jumping back to the latest reply. - Composer/options sizing, restored session history, long-press actions, and Overview/Usage navigation UI tests pass. - Native lint/formatting, localization verification, and `git diff --check` pass (existing test-file length warnings remain). - Interaction proof used layout fix `5fc55fcc218`; the final `66f8e6bb317` integration adds only upstream’s connection-state changes to the native code, validated by the 106-test run. Shared transcript/composer code is identical. No new tests or CI jobs were added; the existing keyboard/history regression supplies the before/after proof. Independent reviews of the full integration and the focused layout repair found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Hosted CI on the pushed head remains separate from this local evidence. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users chatting in the Control UI WebChat would watch a long assistant reply disappear once the turn completed, leaving only a short closing message visible, when the agent ran on an `openai-completions` transport and a tool call followed the reply text.

## Why This Change Was Made

`openai-completions` transports retag already-streamed answer text as commentary once a tool call follows it. The WebChat's completed-turn grouping then folded that text behind the "worked for" row together with the tool activity, so the substantive reply vanished from view.

The fix changes `chat-thread-grouping` to fold only tool groups and text-less assistant groups when a turn completes. Assistant groups that carry text stay visible regardless of how the transport phased them.

Long replies that precede a tool call remain visible after the turn completes. Tool activity still collapses as before.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): queued turn re-compacts a small context when preflight accounting is refused
prs.body:
Related: #140819

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a busy chat session would compact its context again on the very next queued turn, even though the context was far below the compaction budget. Each spurious pass spent minutes summarizing, appended another summary on top of the previous one, blocked the queued message behind the session lane, failed that queued message with `Session changed before compaction maintenance could be recorded`, and surfaced another "Context compacted" card. On one Signal session this repeated four times in fourteen minutes; three of the four ran against a context of roughly 84k, 120k, and 91k tokens against a 252k budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Token-triggered preflight compaction committed the compaction to the transcript inside the queued compactor's session-lane task, but recorded the session-row accounting (count, `totalTokens`, byte latch) only after that task returned and the lane was released. A run waiting on the lane claims the session writer as its first lane write, so the accounting compare-and-swap was correctly refused, the row kept its pre-compaction fresh total, and the next preflight projected pressure from that stale total and compacted again. The queued compactor already exposes a host commit callback that runs while the lane and writer fence are still held; the Codex transcript-byte path used it and the token path did not. This change routes accounting through that callback for every runtime, and supplies the transcript-settled callback for byte-triggered compaction on every runtime so the byte latch keeps measuring the post-maintenance transcript. Nothing about the writer, lifecycle, or session guards changes: a writer that replaces the row before the host commit is still refused, and the after-return path remains only for compactors that emit no host commit.

Non-goals: no retry against a replacement writer, no schema or config change, no change to projection inputs or context limits.

## User Impact

After a preflight compaction, the session's recorded context and compaction count match the transcript, so the following queued turn no longer re-compacts a small context, the queued message is delivered instead of failing, and users stop seeing back-to-back "Context compacted" cards for a session that was not over budget.

## Evidence

- Regression test `lands before a run waiting on the session lane claims the writer` (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts`) models the queued-execution contract against a real SQLite session store: successor acceptance and host commit inside the lane, then a replacement writer claim once the compactor returns. Red/green on this head: with the pre-change `agent-runner-memory.ts` from `upstream/main` swapped in, that test fails with `Session changed before compaction maintenance could be recorded` thrown from `recordCompactionAccounting` (1 failed, 125 passed); with the change it passes, the count and `totalTokens` land, the replacement writer's claim is intact, accounting runs exactly once, and the next preflight does not compact again.
- Guard test `does not account against a writer that replaced the row before the host commit` keeps the newer-writer protection on the in-lane path.
- The byte-latch test now runs for both the Codex and the embedded runtime and asserts the persisted latch right after the first compaction equals the settled (post-maintenance) transcript size. The embedded case would fail if the settled-latch callback were supplied only for Codex, because the in-lane host commit measures the pre-maintenance size.
- Focused suites on this head (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`, one invocation): `agent-runner-memory` (126), `session-updates.lifecycle` (17), `compact.queued-successor` (25), `agent-runner-memory.preflight-stale-tokens` (7), `agent-runner-execution-compaction` (14), `commands-compact.lifecycle` (8): 197 passed. `compact.queued-successor` already pins that `onHostCompactionCommitted` is awaited before the checkpoint and maintenance steps.
- Changed-path gate on this head (`node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main`): all 29 checks pass, including `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and `oxfmt` on the changed files, the max-lines and assertion-safety ratchets, dead-export scan, and import-cycle check; `git diff --check` is clean. A second red check confirms the byte-latch asymmetry: with the settled-latch callback supplied only for Codex, the embedded case fails (`activeBytes` 314 persisted instead of the settled 186).
- Production correlation (sanitized, from the reporter's gateway): each refused accounting was preceded by `lane wait exceeded` on the same session lane 50 to 330 ms before the accounting error, and the one compaction with no lane waiter recorded its accounting normally. Effective harness was `openclaw`; the model route was an OpenAI subscription Responses route.
- Independent review: repository `autoreview` helper on the Claude engine (`claude-fable-5-1`, xhigh), branch mode against `upstream/main`, P2 threshold: `scoped-clean`, no findings. An earlier Codex-engine autoreview of the pre-amend commit (P1 threshold) and an adversarial read-only concurrency review of the diff and tests were also clean at P0/P1; that review's P2 notes (byte-latch timing on non-Codex byte triggers, comment precision, two test-fidelity cleanups) are addressed in this head.

Known gap: this is a source-only repair validated with focused tests; it has not been applied to a live Gateway. The branch includes a merge of current `upstream/main`; upstream did not touch the changed files.

prs.title: fix(telegram): honor group mention activation for commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram currently treats an authorized bare slash command as an effective mention in groups. That lets `/steer` start an agent turn, or `/stop` / `/new` affect a session, even when the group's effective activation is `mention`.

This patch makes Telegram group and forum-topic commands follow the effective mention policy before native dispatch, text-command admission, media download, pending-text cancellation, or ingress supersede. It uses the existing `requireMention` / `/activation` contract; there is no new config surface.

| Context | Bare command | Command addressed to this bot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Group/topic with effective `mention` activation | Ignored | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| Group/topic with effective `always` activation | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| DM, including direct-message topics | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |

Existing mention patterns and reply-to-bot implicit mentions remain recognized. A command addressed to another bot is not treated as addressed to this one. This intentionally changes the documented Telegram group command exception; the issue discusses the compatibility choice.

Fixes #164065.

## Evidence

- Frozen-base maintenance exact head `ca11b494906febdb43343c0cf356636530624027` is signed over immutable base `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`; clean merge tree `5be45911627da8853f95316bb4805a346e309b1a`. The deterministic preflight passes every selected lane, including full core/extension/test/script type graphs, Plugin SDK surface budgets, dead exports, touched lint/format, architecture/ratchet guards, import cycles, and `git diff --check`. A lockfile-frozen dependency refresh changed no tracked source or lockfile bytes.
- The latest exact-head review found media pre-download omitted configured participant mentions. This head now reuses the canonical group-thread mention facts there, preserves exclusive ACP binding behavior, and passes a registered-handler photo-caption regression addressed to a configured participant.
- Telegram command-gate and ingress-supersede tests: **26/26 passed**, including bare `/steer`, `/steer@bot`, other-bot addressing, DM, always-active group, and pre-adoption cancellation cases.
- The targeted native `/login` group test passed after updating its input to `/login@BotUsername`; it still proves that device codes are not sent publicly. The preceding hosted run had one failure because the old fixture expected a response to a bare command in a mention-gated group.
- Worker-backed Plugin SDK session read: the focused `session-store-runtime` read test passed. This replaces the new synchronous SQLite lookup flagged in the first PR review.
- Previous-head CI on `0afec71` found two branch-owned omissions: the new public async read exceeded the Plugin SDK export/callable budgets by one, and a bot-topic fixture still expected bare group `/status` to dispatch. Head `307710f` records that one-export expansion and tests both ignored bare `/status` and addressed `/status@openclaw_bot`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37555349607) passed, including the SDK surface test and the Telegram extension shards; the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` also passed.
- The branch was rebased once onto upstream `b0c330d27df4` and force-pushed as signed head `0a0c63af2c3e`. A merge-tree check against current upstream `ae64a98a4eb1` is clean.
- The prior run also hit SQLite worker admission refusal in an ordinary channel-DM test, followed by a dependent zero-reply assertion. The command gate does not run for that non-command DM input. It did not recur in the exact-head full shard, but its root cause was not established; no code change is claimed as its fix.
- `oxfmt` on the two latest changed files through the repository's qualified tooling-owner pre-commit hook and `git diff --check`: passed. Earlier touched-code `oxlint` and assertion-safety checks passed on preceding heads; the latest changes add no assertions or casts.
- An isolated exact-head `check:changed` run passed the branch-owned gates, including formatting, policy ratchets, Plugin SDK exports/surface budget, plugin boundaries, core typecheck, all 27 core-test typecheck graphs, extension and extension-test typechecks, and script typecheck. The only nonzero gate was the full-tree Knip scan reporting two unused exports already present with identical references in the immutable base (`readSessionEntryCreationTransition` and `RESTART_CONTINUATION_CONTEXT_PREFIX`); neither file nor any reference to either symbol is changed by this PR.
- [Fresh hosted CI on `0a0c63a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37877199608) completed with 65 successful, 23 skipped, and 3 failed jobs. The two root failures are outside this PR's diff and byte-identical from the rebase base/current `main`: an existing two-file Madge cycle in `prepared-model-catalog-{fingerprints,worker}.ts`, and two `unbound-method` lint findings in `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/package-activation-fault.mjs`. The third failure is the aggregate gate reflecting those two. No branch-caused hosted failure was found.
- Repository-supported Crabline Telegram integration proof passed on the exact PR tree: the real Telegram plugin and an ephemeral Gateway ran against a local Bot API transport with a mock provider. In a mention-gated group, bare `/status` and `/steer` produced no outbound reply, zero provider requests, and no session mutation; `/status@crabline_bot` was admitted; another-bot addressing stayed quiet. Bare DM `/status` and bare `/status` in an always-active group remained admitted. This is transport-emulated integration evidence, not Telegram Test Server/TDLib proof.
- Real Telegram Test Server behavior proof is still pending. The exact-head repository doctor was attempted, but no existing Convex launcher could authenticate and no QA broker environment pair was available, so it stopped before acquiring a credential or starting a Gateway. A maintainer/credential-owner run of the group-capable `telegram-e2e-userbot` route is required; the automatic DM-only Mantis plan cannot prove this group-policy change. No live Gateway, Telegram account, or production configuration was changed.

## Review focus

Please confirm that making effective group/topic `mention` activation authoritative for commands is the desired compatibility contract, and review the one-function public Plugin SDK expansion required for the nonblocking session read. The patch keeps bare commands in DMs and `always` groups, and gates the early cancellation paths so an ignored command cannot still interrupt pending work.

prs.title: fix(android): keep realtime Talk alive through slow audio acknowledgments
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/182602

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android realtime Talk over the Gateway relay ends with "Talk failed: request timeout" when the Gateway's answer to one audio append takes longer than 8 seconds, on the phone and through a paired Watch.

## User Impact

User impact: a short network stall or a busy Gateway no longer ends an Android realtime Talk call. Audio past about three seconds in flight is dropped, Talk says "Realtime audio input fell behind; repeat the last part", and "Microphone input recovered; repeat the last part" once the Gateway catches up. A paired Watch shows its own shorter text ("Audio fell behind. Repeat the last part.", "Audio recovered. Repeat the last part.") in place of the elapsed time; each notice stays until the next Talk state change, as on the phone. Talk still ends on an explicit Gateway error, a lost connection, or an append left unanswered for 30 seconds.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser relay and the Apple apps already follow this contract (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155839, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180572, `docs/nodes/talk/realtime-sessions.md`); https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180572 did not reach Android. Both Android relays sent every frame with an 8 second deadline, no limit on audio in flight, and ended Talk on the first timeout.

A small `RealtimeInputAudioBudget` owns the three-second budget and the two notices, and both relays use it: the phone's append loop in `TalkModeManager` and the Watch relay in `WearRealtimeTalkController`. To release audio from the budget when the Gateway answers, `GatewaySession.sendRequestFrameForEndpoint` gains an optional success callback, and the Watch relay's send callback now reports success as well as errors. The append deadline is the 30 second liveness limit from the same contract. The Watch shows the notices from its own strings: the relay's snapshot gains an optional `notice` field (older watches ignore it), and the Watch Talk screen shows it in place of "Listening · 0:00" while listening. The notices are registered for translation; the docs page now says Android follows the same budget.

Trade-off: a Gateway that keeps the socket open but stops answering is now noticed after 30 seconds instead of 8, as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180572 states for the Apple apps.

## Evidence

Tested at `170d5c59956` (base `upstream/main` `315fba74e12`). The Before/After runs below used a build of an earlier revision of this branch with the same phone-side code; the stall run was repeated on a build of this head (see "Re-run at this head").

Real app: the Android app (play debug build of each side) on an Android 16 emulator, paired with an isolated Gateway (empty state directory, loopback port, no outside traffic) whose realtime Talk provider is a local fake that only counts audio. The Gateway is an older source build (2026.9.6, `19afe35954`) on both sides; the bug and the fix are in the Android client. A local WebSocket proxy between the app and the Gateway sets the answer delay: while a stall is on, it holds each `talk.session.appendAudio` answer for a fixed time and logs every 50th held answer as `hold`. Same steps on both sides: open the chat, start realtime Talk, let audio flow, turn the stall on.

Proxy lines are UTC; logcat lines are the emulator's local time (UTC+9), whose clock runs about 1.06 s behind the proxy's. On the proxy clock, Talk closes 8.0 s after the stall starts on the base and 30.0 s after it in the 40 second run.

Before (base, 12 second stall per answer):

```text
11:58:35.244Z req   talk.session.create
12:00:20.447Z hold  held=1   stallMs=12000
12:00:25.441Z hold  held=51  stallMs=12000      (every frame still sent)
21:00:27.401 (UTC+9) W TalkMode: realtime appendAudio failed: request timeout
12:00:28.448Z req   talk.session.close
screen: dialog "Talk failed: request timeout"
```

After (this PR, same stall):

```text
12:17:39.337Z req   talk.session.create
12:17:48.405Z hold  held=1   stallMs=12000
screen: "Realtime audio input fell behind; repeat the last part"
screen: "Microphone input recovered; repeat the last part" (held answers start coming back, about 12 s in)
(stall turned off by the operator at about 12.7 s, not logged)
12:18:03.915Z append appends=151
12:18:13.912Z append appends=251
no talk.session.close, no append failure in logcat, Talk stays on

40 second stall per answer:
12:19:02.948Z hold  held=1   stallMs=40000
21:19:31.897 (UTC+9) W TalkMode: realtime appendAudio failed: request timeout
12:19:32.953Z req   talk.session.close
```

![Before: dialog "Talk failed: request timeout"](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/before.png)
![After: "Realtime audio input fell behind" notice during the stall](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/after-fell-behind.png)
![After: "Microphone input recovered" notice, Talk still on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/after-recovered.png)

Re-run at this head (`170d5c59956`, same Gateway, fake provider and proxy, each held answer delayed 12 s; screenshot times are the host clock, which matches the proxy's):

```text
13:14:31.185Z req    talk.session.create
13:14:44.146Z hold   held=1   stallMs=12000
13:15:01.746Z append appends=301
13:15:08      screen: "Realtime audio input fell behind; repeat the last part"
13:15:15.876Z append appends=351      (14.1 s for 50 appends instead of 5 s: frames past the budget were dropped, not sent)
13:15:16      screen: "Microphone input recovered; repeat the last part", Talk still on
13:15:20.854Z append appends=401
...
13:17:30.856Z append appends=1701
13:17:57.360Z close  who=client code=1006 appends=1952 held=31   (held: running count of held answers; the operator closed the app)
no talk.session.close, no append failure in logcat
```

Watch display (rendered by `WearVoiceLayoutTest` under Robolectric, round 192 dp, not on a watch): before this commit the Watch shows "Listening · 0:00" while the relay reports the notice; now it shows each notice.

![Watch before: "Listening · 0:00" while input fell behind](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/watch-before.png)
![Watch after: "Audio fell behind. Repeat the last part."](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/watch-fell-behind.png)
![Watch after: "Audio recovered. Repeat the last part."](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/watch-recovered.png)

Mixed versions with the latest stable (`v2026.10.9`, `8b18b5578f6`): the new `notice` field crosses the phone-Watch protocol in both directions while one side still runs the stable release. A throwaway JUnit test (not committed) ran in `:wear-shared` of each tree and passed the real encoded bytes between them: this head's `WearProtocolCodec.encode` of a Talk event with each notice, decoded by the stable `WearProtocolCodec.decode` and `WearRealtimeTalkCodec.decode`, and the stable encoding of a listening event decoded by this head.

```text
head wrote    {"type":"event",...,"event":"talk","payload":{...,"status":"LISTENING",...,"notice":"INPUT_FELL_BEHIND"}}
stable read   WearRealtimeTalkSnapshot(attemptId=attempt-1, active=true, listening=true, speaking=false, status=LISTENING, statusText=Listening, conversation=[])
stable read   (same for INPUT_RECOVERED)
stable wrote  {"type":"event",...,"event":"talk","payload":{...,"status":"LISTENING",...,"conversation":[]}}
head read     WearRealtimeTalkSnapshot(..., status=LISTENING, statusText=Listening, conversation=[], notice=null)
```

An updated phone with a stable Watch keeps Talk working and the Watch shows its usual status text; a stable phone with an updated Watch sends no notice and the Watch shows "Listening · 0:00" as before. In the stable release both codecs already share `WearProtocolCodec.json`, which sets `ignoreUnknownKeys = true` and `explicitNulls = false`.

Upgrade from v2026.10.9 (same emulator, same isolated Gateway and proxy, no stall): the stable play debug build was installed on a wiped Android 16 emulator, paired with the Gateway (operator and node approved), and the Talk speaker set to "Muted" in Voice settings. This head's build was then installed over it with `adb install -r` (no uninstall; both builds are version code 2026080201, `firstInstallTime` unchanged, `lastUpdateTime` changed).

```text
14:57:11.572Z close  who=client code=1006   (the install stops the stable app)
14:57:14.909Z req    connect                (same device ID, no pairing request, no onboarding)
screen: Overview with Gateway "Online"; Voice settings still show "Enable speaker · Muted"
14:57:44.825Z req    talk.session.create
14:58:05.492Z append appends=201            (Talk "Listening")
```

After the upgrade the Overview's Nodes row shows "Review node access" instead of "1 online": `openclaw nodes list` on the same Gateway shows the node in `pending-reapproval` with the same 7 caps and 14 commands as approved and one changed permission, `microphone` false to true, because the microphone was granted after the node was approved and 14:57:14 was the first reconnect since; the stable build, installed back over this head, reconnects into the same `pending-reapproval` and shows the same row, so it does not come from this change.

Observed result: on the base, Talk ends 8 seconds into the stall; with this PR it drops audio past the budget with the notice, recovers when the answers arrive, and ends only after an append is unanswered for 30 seconds.

Regression tests: `TalkModeManagerTest.stalledAppendsDropInputPastThreeSecondsWithoutEndingTalk` feeds 31 frames while every append is unanswered, expects 30 appends, the fell-behind notice and Talk still on, then answers one append and expects the recovered notice and the next frame sent. It fails on the base (the 31st frame is sent) and passes with this PR. `WearRealtimeTalkControllerTest` has the same case for the Watch relay and also asserts the 30 second deadline on every append, which pins the deadline constant both relays share; it changes the relay's callback type, so it does not compile on the base. It also asserts the notice the relay sends to the Watch. `WearVoiceLayoutTest` has two new listening cases with each notice; they fail with the previous Watch screen code (the notice text is not on screen) and pass with this PR, and they check the text fits the round screen at font scale 1 and 1.3 in English and in the German locale (which shows the English text until the native locale refresh adds the translation).

Checks at this head: `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.wear.*' --tests ai.openclaw.app.voice.TalkModeManagerTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.gateway.*' :wear:testDebugUnitTest :wear-shared:testDebugUnitTest :wear:lintDebug` (848 tests, 0 failures); `:app`, `:benchmark`, `:wear` and `:wear-shared` `ktlintCheck`; `node scripts/check-native-state-schema-version.mjs`; `pnpm native:i18n:verify`; `git diff --check`. `TalkModeManagerTest` was run again on the base with the test file carried over: the new test times out at 31 appends there, and the other 111 tests pass on both sides. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

CI: the previous head failed `preflight` with "Native generated locale artifacts must be isolated from source changes", and `openclaw/ci-gate` failed because of it. That head carried English placeholders in 21 Watch `values-*/strings.xml` files. This head leaves those files unchanged, so the native locale refresh workflow fills them. `node scripts/ci-changed-scope.mjs --base 315fba74e12` exits 1 with that message on the previous head and exits 0 on this one.

CI at this head ([run 41094221772](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41094221772)): `preflight`, `android-test-play`, `android-test-third-party`, `android-test-wear`, `android-ktlint` and `android-access-native (16384, google_apis_ps16k)` passed. `android-access-native (4096, google_apis)` [failed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41094221772/job/124196671436) while installing the Android Emulator, before the emulator started or any test ran: `sdkmanager` reported "Error reading Zip content from a SeekableByteChannel" while preparing the Android Emulator package, and the job uploaded no test results. `openclaw/ci-gate` is red only because of that job. The same job passed on main in [run 41123124777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41123124777/job/124295092007) (that run is red for unrelated Node and UI jobs). That job has not passed on this head; it needs a rerun.

The CI seconds below come from the JUnit reports of `android-test-play` (phone files) and `android-test-wear` (Watch file). CI tests the PR merged into main, where `TalkModeManagerTest` has 113 tests.

| Test file | Local wall (Gradle, this head) | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeManagerTest.kt` | 0.84 s for the new test (file 17.8 s, 112 tests, Gradle `--max-workers=4` with other modules running) | 0.77 s for the new test (file 14.8 s, 113 tests) |
| `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/wear/WearRealtimeTalkControllerTest.kt` | 0.16 s for the new test (file 1.1 s, 26 tests) | 0.01 s for the new test (file 0.38 s, 26 tests) |
| `apps/android/wear/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/wear/WearVoiceLayoutTest.kt` | two more cases in the existing layout loop (file 7.9 s, 12 tests) | file 4.5 s, 12 tests |

Simplify pass: no change. One budget type serves both relays instead of two copies of the policy, and each new test covers a different relay. Against the merge base: production +147/−15 lines, tests +135/−6, docs +2, Watch English strings +2, translation source +4.

Not covered: no real phone and no real Watch. The phone runs used the Android 16 emulator. No Wear OS device is available, and no Wear OS emulator image is installed; pairing an emulator also needs the Play Store companion app and a Google sign-in. So there are no Watch screenshots or recordings with transport logs from a live call. The phone-side Watch relay is proven by its unit test, the Watch screen by Robolectric renders, and the phone-Watch payload against the latest stable by the codec run above. The device runs used an older Gateway build (see above); the change is client-only. Non-English locales show the English notices on both the phone and the Watch until the native locale refresh translates them.

Follow-up: the microphone transcription stream (`NodeRuntime` `appendTranscriptionAudio`, used by `MicCaptureManager`) also sends `talk.session.appendAudio` with an 8 second deadline. It is a separate feature outside the realtime Talk contract, so it is left for its own change.

prs.title: fix(matrix): stop treating unnamed two-member rooms as DMs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Before the Matrix `m.direct` cache has loaded, an unnamed room with exactly two members is classified as a direct message. Ingress no longer does that. A room is still a direct message when `is_direct` is set, when the room is stored in `m.direct`, when a recent invite was promoted, or when opted-in per-room recovery allows it.

## Evidence

On commit `567572f5adc51a` the direct-room tracker refuses an unnamed two-member room before the cache seeds, and it still accepts `is_direct` and `m.direct`. The QA harness sets the Matrix wildcard group to accept a reply without a mention, because those smoke rooms are groups now.

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/direct.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.test.ts -t "does not treat an exact 2-member|still trusts is_direct|binds Matrix"
 ✓ createDirectRoomTracker > does not treat an exact 2-member room as a DM before the dm cache seeds 24ms
 ✓ createDirectRoomTracker > still trusts is_direct and m.direct before the dm cache seeds 1ms
 ✓ crabline transport > binds Matrix config and normalizes transport targets 3065ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 10.89s
```

QA smoke profile 6, which includes `matrix-restart-resume` and `matrix-restart-replay-dedupe`, passed on this head in CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41541733549/job/125608393398

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** An unnamed two-member Matrix room is not a direct message only because the direct-room cache has not seeded. Explicit direct signals still are.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS Darwin 27.0.0 arm64, Node v26.12.1, worktree at `567572f5adc51a` on `fix/matrix-dm-two-member-fallback`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/direct.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.test.ts -t "does not treat an exact 2-member|still trusts is_direct|binds Matrix"`
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output copied below.
```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/direct.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.test.ts -t "does not treat an exact 2-member|still trusts is_direct|binds Matrix"
 ✓ does not treat an exact 2-member room as a DM before the dm cache seeds 24ms
 ✓ still trusts is_direct and m.direct before the dm cache seeds 1ms
 ✓ binds Matrix config and normalizes transport targets 3065ms
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 10.89s
```
- **Observed result after fix:** The unnamed room is not classified as a direct message, and `setAccountData` is not called. `is_direct` and `m.direct` still are direct before the cache seeds. The QA Matrix config sets `groups.*` to `requireMention: false`. CI smoke profile 6 passed.
- **What was not tested:** A live federated homeserver. Recent-invite promotion and opted-in per-room recovery are unchanged.

## Summary

Remove the pre-seed two-member fallback in `createDirectRoomTracker`. Recent-invite promotion, opted-in per-room recovery, and an explicit `is_direct` or `m.direct` signal are unchanged.

Crabline smoke rooms are ordinary groups. They only received replies because two members counted as a direct message. The harness sets the wildcard group so those rooms can reply without a mention pill. Product group rooms are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(apple): new native chats nest under the previously selected conversation
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

Closes #189432

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where starting an ordinary new conversation from the native iOS chat (new-chat button, new-session popover, or `/new`) while another conversation was selected would silently persist the new session as a child of the previously selected session. In the PWA/Control UI sidebar the new conversation was then nested under an unrelated parent (e.g. a pinned dashboard conversation) instead of being independently discoverable, matching the reporter's saved session metadata (`parentSessionKey` pointing at an unrelated session).
- **Related:** #150054 (open — Control UI creation path incl. Android observations; separate producer, not touched here); #168076 (merged — recovery via *Move to top level* already exists on main); #187077 (open — iOS sidebar presentation, not creation lineage). Fix signals: `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`, `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`, `clawsweeper:source-repro` on the issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** Ordinary native creation is a standalone root. `performStartNewSession` no longer hands `sessions.create` the selected session as an explicit `parentSessionKey`; both native creation call paths (direct `transport.createSession` and route-lease `createSession`) converge on this single producer, so one narrow change fixes both. The gateway already groups standalone roots on its own (`resolveSessionCreateRoot`), and the generated session key still carries the agent identity (`agent:<id>:ios-<uuid>`), so agent inference is unchanged. This aligns native behavior with the web Control UI new-session page, which sends no `parentSessionKey`.
- **Out of scope:** The reported PWA disclosure/disappearance symptom (unverified, likely separate per the ClawSweeper review) and the recovery path (*Move to top level* already shipped in #168076). No gateway or UI changes; forks/children keep their dedicated creation paths (`forkSession`, `forkSessionAtMessage`).
- **Highest-risk area:** Sessions created from native clients no longer inherit parent-derived selection (model/communication) through `inheritSessionCreateParentFields`, because no explicit parent is sent — this matches how web-created sessions already behave.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** Regression tests assert the created request keeps the intended agent (`createdAgentIDs`) and a standalone parent (`nil`) on both call paths; the previously added cross-agent guard test (`ambiguous agent ownership omits the parent session`) stays green. The inheritance delta is now measured rather than assumed (see **Evidence**: `fastMode` inherited pre-patch vs gateway default post-patch, forks/explicit children unchanged), and it is flagged below as an explicit owner decision.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** After this patch, an ordinary new conversation started from native iOS/macOS chat is persisted without a `parentSessionKey` pointing at the previously selected conversation and appears as an independent root row in the PWA sidebar (grouped under the agent main session by the gateway), regardless of which conversation was selected when it was created. Explicit forks and child spawns still carry lineage.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatViewModel+SessionActions.swift` (`performStartNewSession`) and the new/updated cases in `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Tests/OpenClawKitTests/ChatViewModelSessionActionTests.swift` (`same-agent creation from a non-main session omits the parent through a route lease`, `plain new chat from a non-main session omits the parent on the direct transport path`, `active agent identity keeps ordinary creation standalone`).
- **Owner decision requested (unchanged behavior question raised in review):** `parentSessionKey` is the only lever `sessions.create` exposes for parent-derived selection (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/sessions-create.ts`; `inheritSessionCreateParentFields` / `inheritSessionSelection`), so making ordinary native creation standalone necessarily means new native chats start from gateway/agent defaults instead of inheriting the selected conversation's model, account, effort, fast-mode and communication settings. That is already how web Control UI creation behaves (it sends no `parentSessionKey`). This PR keeps the standalone semantics and asks the maintainer to confirm that settings direction; if the preference is to keep inheriting settings, that needs a separate gateway-side knob (inherit-without-lineage) and is not something this client-side fix can preserve on its own.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Yes — three real runtimes, no mocks at the boundaries that matter:
  1. **Apple toolchain (real macOS host):** the shared OpenClawKit Swift suite was compiled and executed at this PR's head on a GitHub-hosted `macos-26` runner — macOS 26.6.2 (25G83, arm64), Xcode 26.6 (17F113), Apple Swift 6.3.3 — with a base-source RED control in the same job.
  2. **Gateway runtime (real gateway + real on-disk store):** a real in-process Gateway (Node v26.12.1, Linux) with a real SQLite session store replayed both native `sessions.create` payloads verbatim, and the resulting rows were fed through the real Control UI sidebar projection code.
  3. **Rendered cross-client sidebar (real browser against that real gateway):** the real Control UI application at this PR's head was served and rendered in headless Chromium 151 (Linux), connected over `ws://` to that same real in-process Gateway after the native payloads were replayed on its wire. The screenshots in **Evidence after fix** §6 are that render (DOM read back out of the live page), not a projection dump — this supersedes the earlier "projection code only" form of the placement evidence.
  - **Correction to the previous revision of this body:** the upstream `macos-swift` / `macos-swift-packages` lanes do **not** execute these tests on this PR. They are gated by `runMacos = !ordinaryPullRequest && …` (`scripts/ci-build-manifest.mjs`), and this PR's checks show `macos-swift (${{ matrix.phase }})` = SKIPPED because it comes from a fork. The suite was therefore executed in a fork-side Actions workflow that runs the same command as the upstream `openclawkit-tests-contract-v1` step (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` "OpenClawKit tests"): [run 41216420220 / job 124581778130](https://github.com/LiuwqGit/openclaw/actions/runs/41216420220/job/124581778130), branch `proof/pr-189467-openclawkit` = PR head `47c8db9ea1a` plus only that workflow file (no PR file is modified).
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # 1) Apple runtime, head GREEN (fork-side macOS runner, PR head 47c8db9ea1a):
  node scripts/prepare-apple-mermaid.mjs      # native asset prerequisites, as in ci.yml
  swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit \
    --scratch-path "$RUNNER_TEMP/openclawkit-proof-scratch" \
    --disable-index-store -Xswiftc -gline-tables-only \
    --filter ChatViewModelSessionActionTests

  # 2) Apple runtime, base RED control in the same job (tests unchanged, only the
  #    patched source file reverted to base 20cdaea4bb5):

    --disable-index-store -Xswiftc -gline-tables-only --filter ChatViewModelSessionActionTests

  # 3) Gateway runtime: real in-process Gateway + real SQLite session store; replay the
  #    exact payloads performStartNewSession emits pre-patch / post-patch, then list:
  #    sessions.create { key: "agent:main:ios-<uuid>", agentId: "main", parentSessionKey: "agent:main:pinned-dashboard-thread" }   # pre-patch

  # 4) Web placement: real Control UI sidebar projection over the real rows

  # 5) Data-model compatibility / stable -> patched upgrade with populated state:

  #    the same state dir, then phase 2 re-reads the store, exercises the shipped recovery

  # 6) Rendered sidebar: real Control UI (Vite source server at PR head) in headless Chromium 151,
  #    connected over ws:// to the same real Gateway used in 3)/5), after replaying on its wire:
  #    sessions.create { key: "agent:main:pinned-dashboard-thread", agentId: "main" }                                              # selected conversation
  #    sessions.create { key: "agent:main:ios-legacy-<n>-pr189467", agentId: "main", parentSessionKey: "agent:main:pinned-dashboard-thread" } x3   # pre-patch native payload
  #    sessions.create { key: "agent:main:ios-fork-pr189467", agentId: "main", parentSessionKey: "…", fork: true }                  # explicit fork
  #    sessions.create { key: "agent:main:ios-patched-pr189467", agentId: "main" }                                                 # patched native payload
  #    then navigate to /chat/main/pinned-dashboard-thread?gatewayUrl=ws://127.0.0.1:<port>, expand the selected
  #    conversation's child toggle, read the rendered rows ([data-session-key], .sidebar-session-tree__children)
  #    and screenshot the shell + the sidebar element.
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  # 1) Head GREEN — real Apple host (macOS 26.6.2, Xcode 26.6, Swift 6.3.3), PR head source:
  Build complete! (564.06s)
  ✔ Test "ambiguous agent ownership omits the parent session" passed after 0.614 seconds.
  ✔ Test "same-agent creation from a non-main session omits the parent through a route lease" passed after 0.614 seconds.
  ✔ Test "plain new chat from a non-main session omits the parent on the direct transport path" passed after 0.614 seconds.
  ✔ Test "active agent identity keeps ordinary creation standalone" passed after 0.657 seconds.

  # 2) Base RED control — same job, only ChatViewModel+SessionActions.swift reverted to base:
  ✘ Test "active agent identity keeps ordinary creation standalone" recorded an issue at
    ChatViewModelSessionActionTests.swift:820:9: Expectation failed: await transport.createdParentKeys() == [nil]
  ✘ Test "same-agent creation from a non-main session omits the parent through a route lease" recorded an issue at
    ChatViewModelSessionActionTests.swift:839:9: Expectation failed: await transport.createdParentKeys() == [nil]
  ✘ Test "plain new chat from a non-main session omits the parent on the direct transport path" recorded an issue at
    ChatViewModelSessionActionTests.swift:852:9: Expectation failed: await transport.createdParentKeys() == [nil]
  ✘ Suite ChatViewModelSessionActionTests failed after 0.322 seconds with 3 issues.

  # 3) Gateway runtime — persisted entries returned by sessions.create (real SQLite store):
  pre-patch payload  { parentSessionKey: "agent:main:pinned-dashboard-thread" }
    -> parentSessionKey "agent:main:pinned-dashboard-thread", parentSessionId d632b880-…, fastMode true (inherited)
  patched payload    { parentSessionKey omitted }
    -> parentSessionKey "agent:main:main" (gateway standalone-root grouping), parentSessionId null,
       chatType "direct", fastMode null / effectiveFastMode false (gateway defaults)

    -> parentSessionKey "agent:main:pinned-dashboard-thread", forkSource {…}, forkedFromParent true (lineage kept)

  #    On-disk rows (…/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite, table session_nodes):
  session_key agent:main:ios-0fab2569-…  parent_session_key agent:main:pinned-dashboard-thread  label "New chat (pre-patch payload)"
  session_key agent:main:ios-cef576b3-…  parent_session_key agent:main:main                      label "New chat (patched payload)"

  "New chat (pre-patch payload)" -> nested child of agent:main:pinned-dashboard-thread

  # 5) Upgrade with populated state — stable-written rows re-read by the restarted gateway:
  before upgrade (written by pre-patch payloads): 5 rows, selected conversation pinned with
    childSessions [3 legacy nested new chats + 1 legacy fork], each legacy row
    parentSessionKey "agent:main:pinned-dashboard-thread", fastMode true (inherited)
  after gateway restart on the same state dir: identical keys, parentSessionKey, parentSessionId,
    sessionId, labels, pinned/fastMode and childSessions for every row
  on-disk session_nodes rows before vs after the restart: identical (no migration, no rewrite)
  legacy rows still usable: chat.history on a legacy nested row -> ok

    row becomes sidebarRoot true while parentSessionKey stays "agent:main:pinned-dashboard-thread"

  rendered rows (in sidebar order):
    agent:main:ios-patched-pr189467      nested=false  "New chat (patched native payload)"   <- independent top-level row
  ```

Successful cold template preparations end with `reason=ready`, hiding why the previous generation could not be reused.

prs.title: fix(codex): record rejected dynamic-tool cleanup on ordinary runs
prs.body:
Fixes #177298

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: ordinary Codex runs silently discard a registered dynamic-tool cleanup rejection, so the existing cleanup diagnostics never report the failed cleanup. Only one-shot CLI runs currently report the same rejection.

## User Impact

Operators can diagnose rejected dynamic-tool cleanup during ordinary Codex runs through the existing `step=codex-dynamic-tool-cleanup` warning. The primary attempt result, final reply, once-only disposal, and subsequent MCP cleanup remain unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

`run-attempt-tool-setup.ts` forwarded collected cleanup rejections only when `params.oneShotCliRun` was true. The existing cleanup settlement owner already records and logs a rejection without rethrowing it, so the one-shot condition only hid ordinary-run failures. This change removes that condition and uses the same reporting path for both run kinds.

## Evidence

- The new ordinary-run regression drives a registered cleanup rejection without `oneShotCliRun`. The attempt resolves normally, cleanup runs once, and the warning contains `step=codex-dynamic-tool-cleanup error=Codex tool cleanup failed`. Restoring the old condition makes this regression fail because no warning is recorded.
- Exact-head focused validation: `npx vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts --project extension-database-workers` passed 127/127. `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` both passed.

That run did not execute this PR's exact head.
- [Independent shipped-entry corroboration](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177317#issuecomment-6268783254) used an ordinary Gateway run, the pinned native Codex 0.162.1 executable, the shipped computer plugin, an isolated synthetic Unix-socket driver, and a loopback mock Responses endpoint. The successful-close control preserved the final reply with zero cleanup warnings; the rejected-close case preserved the final reply with one `codex-dynamic-tool-cleanup` warning. This also used the official base plus the equivalent correction, not this PR's exact head.
- Exact-head shipped-entry validation on `32336c4969205c8c75ceada92eb7c916d423fee9` used the normal QA runtime, ordinary `chat.send`/`agent.wait` Gateway runs, the pinned native Codex 0.162.1 executable, and the shipped computer plugin against isolated synthetic endpoints. The successful-close control completed with the final reply preserved and zero cleanup warnings; rejected close completed with the final reply preserved and one `codex-dynamic-tool-cleanup` warning matched to that run. The QA case passed in 103.66 seconds, and the owned Gateway was confirmed stopped.

prs.title: fix: allow verified upstream workflows in guest publications
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A guest can refresh a feature branch from upstream and still have publication rejected because inherited GitHub workflow changes are mistaken for guest-authored changes once the histories diverge.

## User Impact

Guests can publish ordinary work after inheriting verified upstream workflows without needing full operator write permission. Guest-authored workflow edits remain blocked, including edits whose final contents happen to match upstream. Ambiguous, incomplete, or overly large histories fail closed with a visible next step.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Replace the repository-only blanket divergence refusal with a pinned, complete source-side ancestry proof. Each proof is bounded to 1,000 commits and 32 additional ancestry boundaries.
- Compare the previous publication and the accepted source against their own ancestors. This preserves legitimate upstream merges without laundering source-owned edits.
- Keep exact workflow path, mode, blob, and absence comparisons in one shared owner for local and repository-only publication. Preserve current-authority checks before external effects.
- No new configuration, dependency, schema, or broader guest permission.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original failure through the repository publication coordinator before the fix.
- Both workflow regression suites: **62 tests passed**. Coverage includes first/existing publication, source merges, crisscross ambiguity, pagination beyond 100 commits, malformed pages, bounded work, and authority revocation.
- Guest refresh-to-publish recovery integration: **1 test passed**.
- Core and affected test typechecks, focused lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent source review: no actionable findings. Local autoreview at P0–P2 on an equivalent pinned candidate snapshot (`1db1416…` to `75f7b7d…`, tree `ee26ff5…`): no findings. The CLI review lacked unchanged-repository context; the independent review covered affected owners and callers.

Behavior tests use real Git objects and the production coordinator/tool paths with a mocked GitHub transport. No live publication replay or deployment was performed.

prs.title: docs(ui): design a bounded held window for deep chat history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Loading earlier messages in the Control UI gets slower with every page, and memory keeps growing, because the chat pane holds every row the reader has loaded and re-walks all of them on each older page. The 12 MiB cap applies only to the cached snapshot, not to the live pane.

## User Impact

No user-visible change yet. This draft proposes how to keep per-page cost and memory flat at any depth. It needs the product decisions listed below before any code ships.

## Why This Change Was Made

The task asked for the smallest safe first stage. I didn't find one that avoids product decisions, so this draft has only the design (`docs/reference/control-ui-held-history-window-design.md`). The design covers:

- **Ownership:** `state.chatMessages` stays the only held array and is still published only through `history-merge.ts`. `ChatHistoryPagination`, which already owns the older edge, gains one optional fact: `gap: { afterSource, beforeSource, newerCursor? }`. `ChatPaneHistory` makes the eviction decision through one pure function. `buildChatItems` emits a single `history-gap` boundary item.
- **Window shape:** a deep block, at most one gap, and the live tail block. The alternative was a detached tail (evict the newest rows). I rejected it because `insertSessionProjectionEntry` places a live persisted row after the newest held row, so with the tail evicted, live rows would land straight after the deep rows. Delta reads, send/steer pending rows, input placement, stream rows, end-follow, **Scroll to latest**, `reconcileHistoryTail`, the snapshot cache and the `chat-history-state` read model all assume the held rows reach the live tail. Keeping the tail block preserves that assumption, so none of those writers change.
- **Eviction policy:** runs only after an older-page prepend, once held rows exceed `K_max` (proposed 5,000 rows or 12 MiB weight); it trims to `K_target` (proposed 4,000). It removes only rows between the deep block (prepended page through viewport plus a two-page margin) and the tail block (latest page plus pending, queued or live-run rows). Cuts fall only where a sequence group ends and a user row starts the next turn, so tool calls/results, reasoning and handoffs are never split. Evicted rows are below the viewport, so the anchor doesn't move. Eviction is paused while search is open, during reply navigation and in catalog sessions.
- **Reloading newer rows:** a gap sentinel mirrors the older one, with the same intent, settle and failure gates, plus an explicit **Load newer messages** action. Requests use `chat.history { cursor: newerCursor }`, or a `messageId` probe when no cursor is held, like today's `needsBoundary`. The gap closes when a page reaches `beforeSource` or returns no `newerCursor`. `windowReset` falls back to `reloadChatHistoryWindow`.
- **Live events and Scroll to latest:** both keep working as they do now. Reaching the tail may drop the deep block and the gap.
- **Cache:** with a gap present, only the tail block is cached (with `needsBoundary`), so the persisted schema doesn't change.
- **Reply navigation:** a target inside the gap fills the gap instead of paging older.
- **Stages:** (1) the gap fact, eviction, the gap row, downward fill without top trimming, and tail-only cache commits; (2) sentinel-driven fill plus top trimming, with `TranscriptPrependAnchor` handling leading removals; (3) reply navigation into the gap and shrinking on **Scroll to latest**.

### Decisions needed

1. **Loaded rows can leave the client.** In-app search filters held rows only, and so do browser find and reply previews. Options: pause eviction while search is open (proposed for stage 1), show a "matches in unloaded history are hidden" hint, or add server-side transcript search.
2. **Gap affordance:** a visible **Load newer messages** divider in the middle of the transcript (a visual change), or invisible auto-fill only.
3. **Bound:** `K_max`/`K_target` (proposed 5,000/4,000 rows, capped by the existing 12 MiB weight).
4. **Sequencing with the incremental-render lanes:** ship the bound after that work or alongside it.

## Evidence

- **Work count per older page (code reading):** at least six full passes over held rows: prepend identity, session projection publish (including `createSessionProjection` / `readSessionMessageIdentity` per row), projection compare/copy, snapshot commit, `buildChatItems` (about nine internal passes) and the transcript chain/index/rows projection.
- **Isolated stage timings:** medians of 3 runs, one 1,000-row older page prepended onto `held` rows, measured with a scratch vitest that was not committed. Host load average was about 17, so treat these as relative.

  | held | prepend | projection | buildChatItems | chain+index |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1,000 | 0.3 ms | 0.3 ms | 8.7 ms | 9.5 ms |
  | 4,000 | 0.8 ms | 0.6 ms | 21.1 ms | 28.6 ms |
  | 8,000 | 1.2 ms | 0.9 ms | 37.9 ms | 49.5 ms |
  | 12,000 | 1.8 ms | 1.3 ms | 59.1 ms | 52.8 ms |
  | 16,000 | 2.7 ms | 1.5 ms | 81.5 ms | 75.6 ms |

  That is linear growth at about 10 µs per held row for these two stages. A 4,000-row bound would hold them at about 50 ms per page instead of 157 ms at 16,000 rows.
- **Lead's end-to-end measurement** (isolated Gateway, production bundle, 30,000 messages): Gateway `chat.history` is flat at 35–75 ms per page. Browser script time per page is about 150 ms at pages 1–5 and about 305 ms at pages 21–25 (4x CPU throttle: about 650 ms vs about 1,350 ms).
- **Gateway prerequisite exists:** both-direction anchored paging is already supported and tested. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --maxWorkers=1 src/gateway/server-methods/chat-history-page-cursor.test.ts` passed 21/21, including reversing an older page with its `newerCursor`.
- **Checks:** oxfmt check on the doc passed, `git diff --check` is clean, and local autoreview (`--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`) found nothing actionable.
- **Gaps:** no implementation and no RED/GREEN tests yet, by design. Total memory at 30,000 held messages wasn't measured. The timings above come from a loaded shared host.

prs.title: fix(ui): earlier chat pages still slow down as loaded history grows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in long chat sessions, each "load earlier messages" page still costs more main-thread time than the last, because committing the page re-read every message already loaded instead of only the new page.

## User Impact

User impact: scrolling back through very long sessions keeps a flat pane-side cost per older page; the history merge, session projection, and snapshot cache no longer scale with how much history is already on screen. No behavior or visible change otherwise.

## Why This Change Was Made

After #190249 the older-page commit still did three O(all loaded) passes per page:

- **Overlap detection** (`prependUniqueNativeMessages`) computed the source identity of every loaded row. An older page ends where the loaded transcript begins, so overlap can only lead it; the scan now stops at the first loaded source the page lacks.
- **Projection publication** rebuilt the session projection over the whole transcript (`createSessionProjection` reads every row's identity) and then restored provenance through an occurrence map. A new `prependChatSessionProjectionMessages` in `history-merge.ts` (the projection owner) classifies only the page and keeps every loaded entry as-is. Entry classification only carries state forward, so older rows cannot change the loaded entries after them; this is exactly what the old full rebuild produced, because every loaded row was restored from its existing entry. A changed projection scope still falls back to the full republish.
- **Snapshot cache bound** (`boundChatSessionSnapshot`) weighed every message before trimming from the oldest end. It now weighs from the newest row and stops once the rows alone exceed the 12 MiB budget, then resumes the unchanged trim loop at the next sequence-group boundary. The retained window, its pagination, and `weight === JSON.stringify(snapshot).length` are unchanged.

Accepted edge cases (named, not coded around):
- Pairing-QR retention is skipped for the prepend: loaded entries keep their own QR blocks and transcript rows never carry them (pairing media is live-only).
- An unserializable message older than the retained cache window is now trimmed unread instead of evicting the whole snapshot. Gateway history is JSON, so this needs a locally constructed non-JSON row.
- If a loaded transcript were ever out of source order at its oldest edge, an overlapping duplicate past the first non-matching row would no longer be removed (visible, recoverable by reload). Pages come from transcript cursors, so the overlap is always the leading run.

Unchanged and intentionally out of scope: the pending-user adoption scan (one property pass over entries, no identity reads), the O(N) pointer copies of the immutable message/entry arrays, and render-side transcript building (`chat-thread*.ts`, `components/chat-transcript-*`), which another lane owns.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: per older page, pane-side message reads and commit time stay flat as loaded history grows (base grows linearly).

**Work count and time per 1,000-message older page** through the real pane entry point (`ChatPaneHistory.loadOlderMessages` → prepend → projection → `commitCurrentChatHistorySnapshot`), jsdom/Node, 40,000-message synthetic session (user / assistant with tool call / tool result rows, ~130–600 characters of text each), 5 measured pages per depth after 2 warmups, two interleaved base → candidate runs (B A B A) on a loaded shared host (load avg 10–30). "Metadata reads" counts every `__openclaw` read (identity, source identity, sequence, serialization).

| Loaded before page | Base metadata reads/page | Candidate | Base median ms (max), runs 1 / 2 | Candidate median ms (max), runs 1 / 2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ~4–9k | 41,006 → 69,007 | 9,002–9,006 | 5.9 (5.9) / 7.5 (20.6) | 3.2 (3.3) / 2.8 (2.9) |
| ~14–19k | 111,007 → 139,010 | 9,002–9,006 | 10.2 (12.5) / 11.4 (14.3) | 3.4 (3.5) / 3.9 (17.0) |
| ~26–31k | 207,867 → 243,870 | 8,004–8,008 | 23.2 (33.0) / 18.8 (40.1) | 2.4 (2.5) / 2.1 (2.3) |

Candidate reads are ~8–9 per *page* row and independent of depth; base adds ~7 reads per *loaded* row per page. The 17.0 ms candidate max is a single loaded-host outlier; the other four measured samples in that cell were 3.4–5.9 ms.

**Regression tests (red on `origin/main`, green here):**
- `chat-pane-history.test.ts` "prepends an older page without rereading the loaded transcript": loaded rows read during one older-page load — base 1,000 of 1,000, candidate 1.
- `history-message-identity.test.ts` "bounds prepend serialization": loaded rows inspected — base 1,000, candidate `overlap + 1` (1 and 51).
- `session-message-cache.test.ts` "measures the trimmed envelope once and never weighs the older rows it drops": rows weighed — base 4,000, candidate retained + 1 (3,018); weight still equals `JSON.stringify(snapshot).length`.

**Checks run:**
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui.config.ts ui/src/pages/chat ui/src/lib/chat`: 637 files, 7,646 tests passed.
- Same paths under `vitest.ui-isolated.config.ts` (includes `chat-pane-history.test.ts`, `chat-pane.test.ts`): 32 files, 490 tests passed.
- Browser E2E (`vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts`, production build, Chromium): `chat-history-prepend-anchor.e2e.test.ts`, `chat-history-loading.e2e.test.ts`: 2 files, 20 tests passed (prepend anchoring across shared/manual/touch/momentum variants, coalesced activity at 390/1440 px, empty/failed/retry earlier-history loads).
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`: pass. oxlint and oxfmt on changed files: clean. `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`: OK.
- Local autoreview (`--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`): scoped-clean, no actionable findings.

**Gaps:** the workload above is an uncommitted scratch vitest bench (pane from `chat-pane-history.test-support.ts`, scripted `chat.history` pages, counting getter on `__openclaw`), kept out of the tree to hold test-line growth to the three regression assertions. I also did not rerun the lead's real-Gateway + production-bundle CPU profile at 30,000 messages; the counts above come from the real pane entry point with a synthetic Gateway in jsdom. The remaining per-page browser cost there is render-side transcript building, which this PR does not touch.

- @vyctorbrzezowski
