prs.title: fix(ios): mount Control UI pages under the advertised base path
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191177

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the iOS app's embedded Control UI pages (the Settings tab's Dashboard, session Dashboards, Terminal and Desktop) show the Gateway's "Not Found" when the Gateway serves the Control UI under `gateway.controlUi.basePath` and the app is connected by discovery or by host and port, a connection URL without a path.

## User Impact

User impact: iOS users with a Control UI base path can use those pages without re-pairing by QR code. Connections whose URL already has a path (setup codes since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161620) keep it.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185141 made the Gateway advertise its Control UI mount in hello-ok (`controlUiBasePath`) and made macOS use it: the connection URL's path wins when it has one, else the advertised mount. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190199 proposes the same rule for Android. On iOS, `AuthenticatedControlUI.pageURL`, which builds the URL for every embedded page, used only the connection URL's path, and the operator session dropped the hello-ok field.

This change applies the same rule at the same owners:
- `GatewayNodeSession` admits `controlUiBasePath` from hello-ok next to the methods, scopes and limits it already keeps for the current route, and clears it on disconnect.
- `NodeAppModel` copies it onto the active connect config before it marks the operator connected, because the pages build their URL when they appear on that flag. The field stays out of the connection and WebView identity inputs (`controlUIInputs`, `hasSameConnectionInputs`): it is learned after connect, and putting it there would replace the WebViews and their bridges on every connect.
- `AuthenticatedControlUI.pageURL` uses it, percent-encoded, when the connection URL has no path. All seven callers follow without edits. The native bridge checks that trust a page's origin (`ControlUINativeGatewayAuthHandler.isAvailable`, `IOSDeviceSettingsBridge.isTrustedSource`) derive from the same URL, so they narrow to the mount too, and the chat source preview (`IOSSourceResourceLoader`, through `nativeControlPageURL`) resolves resources under it.

Accepted edge case: a page opened before the operator hello arrives, or kept open while the Gateway changes its mount, keeps its old URL until it is opened again. The Settings Dashboard is not affected: it appears only once the operator is connected, which happens after the mount is stored.

Size against the merge base `eb4881915a0`: production +29/−1 in 4 files, tests +70/−3 in the existing `SessionDashboardScreenTests` and `GatewayNodeSessionTests` suites.

## Evidence

Tested on a real iPhone (iOS 26.7.1) with the iOS app built without and with the fix, against an isolated Gateway (own state, no channels, placeholder token) with `gateway.controlUi.basePath: "/gateway"`. The same UI script ran on both sides: launch with onboarding reset, connect from **Settings → Gateway** by host and port only with the token, relaunch on the Settings tab, and read the embedded page.

The device builds carry one extra proof-only commit on both sides, which this PR does not include. Current main's iOS app needs the iOS 27.1 SDK (`\.toolbarVerticalEdge` in `apps/ios/Sources/Design/ChatProTab.swift`, from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187045), which the build Mac's Xcode 26.6 lacks. An older base does not help here, because every commit with the hello-ok field from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185141 also needs that SDK. So the extra commit replaces the three `#available(iOS 27.1, *)` branches in `ChatProTab.swift` and `OpenClawProComponents.swift` with their `else` branches, which are what iOS 26.7.1 runs anyway, and drops the iOS 27.1-only `ChatToolbarStatusPopover` they used. The fix's diff on the proof branch is identical to this PR's first commit; the second commit only adds tests.

Before (main `eb4881915a0` + the SDK commit):

```text
Settings tab: Dashboard shown for the admin operator   met
Embedded page does not show "Not Found" (held 3 s)     not met
Control UI settings page shown (within 10 s)           not met
```

After (the same + this PR's fix commit):

```text
Settings tab: Dashboard shown for the admin operator   met
Embedded page does not show "Not Found" (held 3 s)     met
Control UI settings page shown (within 10 s)           met
```

Observed result: on main, the embedded page opens `/settings` (the page path without the mount) and shows "Not Found", together with the banner "This Gateway's Dashboard is older than the app" (that banner is the subject of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174957 and is not changed here). With the fix, it opens under `/gateway/` and shows the Control UI settings page.

![Settings tab: Not Found on main, the Control UI settings page with the fix](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261102-185141-ios-control-ui-base-path/before-after-settings.png)

Recording of both runs side by side: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261102-185141-ios-control-ui-base-path/before-after-settings.mp4

Tests: the new test in `SessionDashboardScreenTests`, `dashboard URL mounts under the advertised Control UI base path unless the URL has one`, checks both halves of the rule through `pageURL`: a host:port URL with an advertised `/gateway` mount gives `/gateway/focus/dashboard/...`, and a URL with its own path `/openclaw` keeps that path. On the iOS Simulator (Xcode 26.6), with the SDK commit above on both sides, the suite passes 7 of 8 on main `eb4881915a0` with the test file carried in, the new test failing on its first assertion (the URL without the mount), and 8 of 8 with this PR's fix. To compile on main, that run also carried this PR's `GatewayConnectConfig.swift`, which only adds the field. Its host is now `gateway.example.com` (`http://gateway.example.com:18789/gateway/focus/dashboard/main/~key/main`); the 8 of 8 result below covers that version.

The new test in `GatewayNodeSessionTests`, `control UI base path follows the current hello route`, checks the admission: a hello-ok with `controlUiBasePath: " /gateway "` is kept trimmed as `/gateway` for the current route and not returned once the route is gone (disconnect). It has no run on main, where the field does not exist. The suite belongs to the OpenClawKit package, and the cloud runner used here runs only the iOS app's test target, so the suite ran there on the iOS Simulator with copies of two OpenClawKit test files (the suite and its state-directory trait): on this PR's head with the SDK commit, `GatewayNodeSessionTests` passed 95 of 95 and `SessionDashboardScreenTests` 8 of 8.

Checks: `pnpm check:changed` passes every step except three that fail for reasons outside this PR: formatting (only untracked local scratch files; the formatter matches none of this PR's files), typecheck (`extensions/qa-lab` cannot resolve `@openclaw/crabbox-provider` in the local install) and lint (oxlint could not load its JS plugin locally). None of these steps covers Swift. As on every ordinary pull request, this PR's CI skips the macOS Swift and iOS build jobs.

Overlap: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163765 edits `GatewayConnectConfig.swift`, `GatewayNodeSession.swift` and `authUserScript` in `AuthenticatedControlUIWebView.swift`, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172205 edits `GatewayConnectConfig.swift`, both in other places, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174957 edits the Dashboard's error page, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190961 adds a persistent data store in `AuthenticatedControlUIWebView.swift`, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158051 changes `SessionDashboardScreen.swift` and the `authUserScript` call; none of them changes how page URLs are built.

Not covered: the device proof and the tests ran with the SDK commit above, not on this PR's exact base. The device run connected by host and port, not by discovery; both give a connection URL without a path. Terminal, Desktop and session Dashboards were not driven on the device; they use the same `pageURL`, and the session Dashboard case is in the regression test.

prs.title: fix(imessage): group activation mode now controls replies
prs.body:
Related: #50490

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: iMessage groups keep replying to unmentioned messages after an owner runs `/activation mention`.

## User Impact

User impact: iMessage group owners can use `/activation mention` and `/activation always` to change reply behavior without editing channel config.

## Why This Change Was Made

The iMessage ingress gate only resolved `requireMention` from channel config and never consulted the routed session's persisted `groupActivation`. This change reads the activation mode from that exact session and gives it the same precedence over group config used by Telegram and WhatsApp. Authorized control commands still bypass mention gating so owners can switch modes.

## Evidence (exact head)

- Exact candidate head: `f1c66eb055618f0aa79505abd7bfacb1498445c8`; frozen base: `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`; clean merge tree: `de8299f6f3c4776fce1a0e00db9843f8289c8f7a`.
- Focused test command: `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.activation.test.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor.watch-subscribe-retry.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.session-patch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session.activation.test.ts` → 5 files, **43/43 passing** on the merged tree. Core and extension TypeScript gates and touched-file formatting pass under Node 26.7.0.
- Production path exercised by the mock-Gateway proof: `resolveIMessageInboundDecision` in `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.ts` → `createIMessageGroupActivationResolver` in `group-activation.ts` → runtime `getSessionEntryInWorker` → SQLite worker-backed read; admission uses `createHostChannelIngressRuntime`. The test calls the production decision function with a routed group and real isolated SQLite store, not Apple's Messages transport.
- The proof harness writes persisted activation entries through `runtime.agent.session.upsertSessionEntry` (simulating the command's persistence), rather than issuing live `/activation` commands. Command owner-gating/persistence is separately covered by `commands-session.activation.test.ts`. This distinction matters: it is not a single end-to-end live Apple/command receipt.
- The exact frozen-base deterministic preflight is green after a lockfile-frozen dependency refresh. It passes extension production/test type graphs, touched-file formatting/lint, dead exports, architecture/ratchet guards, import cycles, and `git diff --check`. The refresh exposed and the branch repaired a strict session-entry test fixture that lacked required identity/timestamp fields and literal activation typing.
- Earlier sanitized behavior receipt (the production behavior path is unchanged by the frozen-base replay):

```json
{ "verdict": "PASS", "base": "9bb171bf39b98a6965a47ab4f636e35a5701b409", "head": "68a07b52e5881bc9294ec1ddaa548a605ad7a433", "harness": "real SQLite session store + worker-backed read + mock Gateway iMessage admission", "sessionKey": "agent:main:imessage:group:99", "decisions": { "mention": "drop", "always": "dispatch", "restoredMention": "drop" } }
```

- Reviewer follow-ups: no-mention diagnostic now explains `/activation always` precedence, covered by the monitor test; the public asynchronous worker-read API has a narrowed, documented parameter/store-selection contract. The monitor test fixture now provides its required session runtime and locally passes the hosted-red shard.
- Hosted CI and maintainer proof/compatibility review on this new head remain authoritative; this evidence does not claim their acceptance.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Codex conversations that remain tied to a removed OpenClaw auth profile even after the intended native account is available.

## User Impact

Operators can preview and explicitly migrate the affected binding while preserving its native thread and conversation history. Applying the repair requires confirmation of the native account and endpoint; it is not automatic.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds the `operator.admin` method `codex.migrateAuthProfile`, defaulting to dry run. It validates the exact session, thread, client and retired profile; refuses active writers, native turns, child ownership and configured credential selections; and clears only the obsolete profile through the existing binding lease and transaction authority.

## Evidence

- 21 migration tests and 42 existing session-binding tests passed, including preservation, preview, lease/CAS conflicts, identity checks and refusal paths.
- The preservation regression fails against the base binding implementation because the old profile remains attached, and passes with the repair.
- Production and test extension typechecks, focused native lint/format checks, and `pnpm build` passed. The lazy runtime module is present in the built plugin.
- Independent source review found no actionable P0–P2 issues within the supplied scope.
- Build reported a nonblocking UI startup gzip warning (309.0 KiB versus 308.9 KiB); baseline attribution is not established. SQLite tests required normal process permissions on macOS. Blacksmith validation was unavailable because its CLI was missing.
- No live migration or deployment has been performed. Operator dry run, release approval and verification of the original conversation remain required before calling the incident recovered.

prs.title: feat: schedule automatic updates in Settings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway operators cannot choose when automatic updates start.

## User Impact

User impact: Settings → Updates now offers hourly (the existing default), daily with a time, weekly with a day and time, and a custom cron expression. Times follow the Gateway host’s timezone, not the browser’s.

## Why This Change Was Made

One optional `update.auto.schedule` cron string stores the schedule; presets are UI projections. No timezone field, new package dependency, or storage migration is added. Existing cron calculation and the Gateway scheduler remain the owners.

Configured schedules gate campaign starts, including startup, restart, and interactive Dev refresh. Missed windows are skipped. Stable rollout delays, idle/countdown behavior, restart safety, manual updates, and the one-hour hold remain intact. Schedule changes hot-apply and cancel pending campaigns without interrupting an applying update.

Requested by and implemented for @jacobtomlinson.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jacobtomlinson](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1a6452bb-b935-4086-8f43-3e795f64d30e)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/7bf59300-3432-4c32-b379-9b13390a8546)

## Evidence

- Built Control UI with a synthetic Gateway: all five Updates E2E scenarios passed (151.20 s total). The schedule scenario exercised hourly → daily 04:25 → Tuesday 04:25 → custom cron → hourly and asserted serialized `config.set` writes. Inspected before/after screenshots and weekly/custom states are embedded below.
- Daily campaign admission failed on base because it started at 10:00 despite a 10:30 schedule. The repaired daily, sub-hourly, skipped-window, hot-rearming, and interactive Git behavior passed. Both final extracted schedule regressions also passed (668.00 s including cold preparation; 7.143 s test execution).
- Initial implementation: scheduler/consumer tests 75 passed, 71.61 s wall; campaign/lifecycle/manual-refresh 41 passed; config 74 passed, 19.20 s; existing cron/DST 13 passed, 1.76 s; Updates view 42 passed, 3.12 s.
- Initial implementation: core/UI production typechecks, infra fixture typecheck, targeted lint, Solid controller guard, i18n verification, changed-document formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Initial canonical autoreview against `fb2c420c4e75ea43884869786f5b0e9b7af36c06`: P0–P2 scoped-clean, no actionable findings, confidence 0.84. The review includes the extracted scheduler and test fixture. Lead independently reviewed campaign admission, hot reload, cron reuse, and UI serialization.
- [Published-driver upgrade proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41439871998/job/125269758422) passed on attempt 1: published npm `2026.10.9` → exact candidate `f0fb5907be5e751f345dbd9184558be983061852` (`2026.10.9`), with no candidate relabeling. Readiness returned 200, running version and durable-session survival were verified, and package integrity/npm-12 installer acceptance passed. The cell took 435 seconds; the complete workflow took 2,154 seconds. This uses synthetic state and the maintained systemctl harness, not native-systemd qualification.

### CI repair validation

The [first PR CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41439183580) identified PR-caused import-cycle/extracted-wrapper closure errors, two test static-analysis errors, and omitted config baseline artifacts. The follow-up repair moves the existing cron validator and timezone normalization unchanged into a shared leaf, includes that leaf and the already-pinned `croner` package in extracted wrappers, corrects the test typing/shadowing, and regenerates the baseline. No scheduler policy or visible UI changes were made.

On an isolated AWS Linux runner with 4 vCPUs, 15.3 GiB RAM, Node 24.22.1, and one test worker:

- Selected CI regressions: 35 tooling + 16 native provisioning tests passed, with 2 existing skips; 385.577 s wall. All originally failing test cases passed.
- Cron/config/CLI consumers: 99 tests passed across four files; 89.494 s wall.
- Runtime/tooling lint passed with zero warnings or errors (36.996/158.004 s). UI E2E test types passed (19.200 s); architecture check found zero cycles (42.303 s); config generation/check, test allocation, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- All 37 feature/repair source hashes matched before and after execution. Generated outputs were downloaded unchanged and matched the final worktree; 15 retained proof-artifact hashes were verified. The single temporary runner was released after 35m36s, without extending its lifetime.
- Fresh canonical autoreview of the repair delta against `f0fb5907be5e751f345dbd9184558be983061852`: P0–P2 scoped-clean, no actionable findings, confidence 0.93; final source verification passed.

The config baseline intentionally grows by exactly one core key (2,584 → 2,585) for the requested optional `update.auto.schedule` field. Channel/plugin counts and hashes are unchanged. The 250-line test allocation covers campaign admission/restart, hot policy changes, config rejection, routed UI persistence, and the two additional fixture/import lines needed for the repair; the shared scalar budget is unchanged. Per-test CI seconds are not yet extracted from broad CI artifacts.

### Final CI result and remaining proof gap

[CI run 41455922677](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41455922677) completed with **failure** on head `eaf807dc6c04fe68c7237d9461b2063a3c696372`; all 89 job records are terminal. The sole failed workload was [control-ui-performance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41455922677/job/125313331221); the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` also failed. The [final failure table](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41455922677/job/125323853067) classifies this as **new**: the matching main job passed, and selected scope was not compared. It is not relabeled as inherited-only.

Both performance builds succeeded. Chat boot gzip increased from **1,278,812 B to 1,278,972 B (+160 B)**, with 20 requests unchanged. Because the base already exceeds the 1,277,887 B fixed cap, only the existing **64 B** build-variance allowance applies: the candidate is **96 B over** its effective 1,278,876 B limit. Startup JS increased 9 B, New boot JS 17 B, and CSS growth was zero.

Logged payload growth is confined to the lazy Settings copy and Updates-page chunks at the log's rounded precision. The same schedule UI source previously produced a -4 B Chat gzip delta against an earlier main base. This suggests generated asset-hash/minifier sensitivity, but it does **not** establish hash-only byte equality or a passing budget. The performance job does not retain the paired distributions, and its helper deletes the temporary base build. A matched base/head build with retained JavaScript, compression sidecars, HTML, and source maps is still required for decisive attribution and any justified fix. No performance budget or variance allowance has been changed.

Validation scope: earlier cold-worker attempts timed out before executing the extracted fixture; the final extracted tests passed. The optional full changed-file gate reached its 600-second local budget after its first six checks passed. Focused repair validation is green, but full CI is not green for the reason above. The upgrade rehearsal remains evidence only for `f0fb5907be5e751f345dbd9184558be983061852`; the repair changes runtime module inputs, and no upgrade rehearsal of `eaf807dc6c04fe68c7237d9461b2063a3c696372` is claimed. No live Gateway settings or services were changed.

### Password-free rejection fixture (November 4)

Commit `0eaabb3cc7606d7e381cf70b9919c737093fc16f`, published in head `3679341be3efbae7b466a4eb6bb12ee945186f97`, replaces one synthetic negative-URL fixture in `src/config/config-misc.test.ts` with a transparent username-only URL containing no password. The existing expected-false schema assertion is unchanged. The original combined fixture short-circuited on username; this replacement preserves that rejection without claiming independent password-branch coverage. No encoding, runtime reconstruction, scanner policy, or production behavior changes were made.

- Focused config suite: **74 passed**, 42.97 s test time / 45.28 s wrapper wall, with one worker.
- Actual-schema sensitivity proof verified nonempty username and empty password, rejection by the real schema, acceptance of the clean origin, and that masking only the parsed username in an isolated process makes the unchanged expected-false assertion fail. The URL parser was restored and the production owner remained byte-identical.
- Targeted formatting, lint, config test types, and diff checks passed. Fresh canonical autoreview was P0–P2 scoped-clean with no findings, confidence 0.99, and final source verification passed.
- This delta is test-only; existing screenshots remain representative. It does not repair the prior performance failure or extend the old-head upgrade evidence above.

**Hosted review remains blocked before a verdict.** The [November 4 re-review request at 11:01:54 UTC](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191061#issuecomment-6628986837) targeted head `3679341be3efbae7b466a4eb6bb12ee945186f97`. Its [correlated status changed to Failed at 11:05:46 UTC](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191061#issuecomment-6628989117); [run 41818159154, exact-review job 126534173101](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41818159154/job/126534173101) failed at the `agent_input_scan` stage (`reason_code: findings`, non-retryable), producing no review verdict. The retained manifest reports **two findings**. Only the **first** has been located: the unchanged base synthetic negative-URL fixture at `src/config/config-misc.test.ts:153`, in base revision `fb2c420c4e75ea43884869786f5b0e9b7af36c06`; its blob identity and path hash were independently matched against GitHub. The second finding has not been identified. This is a fresh refusal, separate from the [November 2 refusal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191061#issuecomment-6580594500), and it does not establish that the new username-only literal passed scanning. Base content and removed patch text remain in the review range. No raw fixture values are reproduced here, no scanner policy was changed, and successful local autoreview is not represented as hosted approval.

### Control UI screenshots

Actual built Control UI with synthetic Gateway data, dark theme, 1280 × 1000. The CI repair does not change the pictured UI.

| Before | After — daily schedule |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: automatic updates without schedule controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c9d19c1-6d19-4a6b-a373-23c12b569bc8) | ![After: daily automatic updates at 04:25](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d3349694-4eb9-423c-90aa-81b097ff2e4e) |

<details>
<summary>Weekly and custom cron schedules</summary>

![Weekly: Tuesday automatic updates at 04:25](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ddb15005-21f8-43aa-b699-95c68a2c2d7b)

![Custom cron: every 15 minutes during weekday early-morning hours](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c20ac16-944f-45d4-8f49-2be01724779e)

</details>

prs.title: fix(state): agents refused with database repair advice when a config reload lands during startup
prs.body:
Related: #190307, #161921

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent is refused with `Plugin openai was reloaded or disabled` and told to run `openclaw doctor --fix` on a healthy database when a config reload lands while that agent is finishing startup admission.

## User Impact

User impact: agents admitted during a config reload now retry their runtime publication instead of being refused. If reloads keep replacing the publication past the retry budget, the refusal asks for a Gateway restart rather than a database repair, because Doctor cannot fix that condition.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup admission already retries runtime publication when a model publication is superseded (#172632), but it did not recognize the sibling outcomes of a reload: a retired plugin generation or an unavailable plugin instance. Those escaped as terminal failures. This change uses the existing lifecycle classification at that boundary and adds a short backoff (0.5, 1, 2 s, abortable) so a reload can settle between attempts. Publication reads secrets and models and does not write the agent database, so replaying it is safe.

Genuine publication failures still surface once with their existing guidance, including lock, ownership, and corruption classification. Only exhausted supersession gets the new restart hint.

Accepted edge: the retry budget stays four attempts, so a longer reload can still exhaust it. The hot-reload recovery restart re-admits those agents.

## Evidence

Native proof on Crabbox AWS Linux: 46 seeded agents (17-200 MB) deferred at startup, Gateway pinned to 2 CPUs, main thread stalled 1.5 s in every 2 s by a proof-only preload, and one `openclaw config set agents.entries.a03.model` during admission.

| Build | Agents refused | After settling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Published 2026.10.10 | 46 of 46, `Prepared plugin generation retired before publication`, doctor hint | No restart; still `ready: false` 268 s later |
| Main `ef4ccf4c7d2` | `main` refused, `Plugin openai was reloaded or disabled`, doctor hint | Hot-reload recovery restart re-admits all 46 |
| This fix on main `9e379ebbc97`, run 1 | No plugin-lifecycle refusal; 4 retries logged | Recovery restart; `ready: true` 36 s after it |
| This fix, run 2 | No refusal; 4 retries logged | Recovery restart; `main` still admitting 56 s after it when the run ended |

Those two fix runs used the earlier build of this branch. The final head changes only which failures get the restart hint. Regression coverage is on the final head.

Same fleet with no config edit: 46 of 46 admitted on 10.10 under 2 CPUs with 8 s stalls, SIGKILL, and RPC load. So the trigger is the reload, not fleet size.

Not fixed here, and observed on every build under this load:

- `config set` still returns `persisted but was not applied to the active Gateway`, and main restarts the Gateway once to recover.
- This does not reproduce the `worker task timed out` or `checkpoint expired` refusals reported in #190307 on 10.9, so they stay open there.

Tests: `src/gateway/server-agent-database-startup.preparation.test.ts` adds the retired-generation retry, and exhausted supersession now asserts the restart hint. The retired-generation test and the hint assertions fail on base. Those suites pass 28/28, with lint, format, and `tsgo` core clean on Crabbox. The local pre-commit hook could not run because its tooling owner has a stale `oxfmt`, so format and lint ran on the box instead.

Review: `$autoreview` scoped-clean. An independent Codex review found one P2, that wrapping every publication error hid lock and corruption guidance. That is fixed, and its re-review found nothing.

The 24 added test lines carry an allocation in `config/test-lines-allocations/agent-admission-plugin-reload.txt`.

prs.title: feat: unify theme and Lobster Pack discovery in Appearance
prs.body:
Depends on #184960 and #160093. Registry counterparts: [ClawHub #4065](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4065) and [ClawHub #3837](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/3837).

Companion ClawHub Appearance integration: [ClawHub #4070](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4070).

## What Problem This Solves

Users need one place in Appearance to discover themes and Lobster Packs without confusing theme data with executable plugin packages.

## User Impact

Adds **Explore Appearance → Themes / Lobster Packs** beside the existing theme choices. Themes reuse browse, pinned install-and-apply, and personal-theme removal. Packs show their current installation state and link to existing plugin review/management controls and the LobsterDex. Browsing never records an encounter or installs a plugin; collection history remains browser-local.

**Draft dependency boundary:** this branch currently composes the theme foundation from #184960 and category acceptance from #160093 so the new UI can be built and tested. Its main-targeted diff therefore includes inherited theme changes, not just integration glue. It does not replace or close either original PR. Full custom-pack contribution/rendering support and production theme browsing still require the foundation PRs and the ClawHub Themes API deployment. This PR performs no deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing theme owner, plugin discovery owner, Gateway connection lifecycle, management routes, and collection owner rather than introducing another installer, renderer, preference store, or permission model. Fixed-category discovery keeps pack searches scoped; changing a theme query retires the previous page and cursor before a failed search can reuse it.

Jacqueline Henriksen (@jjjhenriksen) requested and directed this integration. The linked foundation PRs retain their original authorship.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/20481d59-f95b-4760-8f8c-82f1e4d414b4)

## Evidence

- 137 focused tests passed: category/query identity, ClawHub validation and filtering, and Gateway profile/theme persistence and authority boundaries. The two added query regressions failed before the repair and passed afterward.
- Production-bundle browser flow passed for packs: on-demand browse, failed-read retry, category-preserving search, installed management links, empty state, catalog refresh after plugin-change events, mobile fit, no preview collection/install, and Dex navigation (2.6s test body).
- Production-bundle theme flow passed: search/retry, pinned install/apply, reload persistence, inherited-default reset, personal-theme re-selection, and removal (1.7s test body). Its fixture now persists only after observing actual writes and keeps deferred-request cursors bound to the same request predicate.
- Core/UI typechecks, targeted UI lint, stylesheet lint, formatting, English i18n verification, documentation listing, and whitespace checks passed.
- Final independent two-chunk review returned no actionable P0–P2 findings on the frozen candidate.

The browser scenarios use synthetic Gateway responses, not a deployed ClawHub service. No live registry installation or published-release compatibility is claimed. Hosted CI remains separate from these local results.

Before/after captures use the real Control UI, dark mode, a matched 1440×1200 viewport, and synthetic content. Both inspected captures are embedded below.

### Before

![Before: Appearance with built-in themes and import](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63934c26-a075-48de-b456-7d852f4a7010)

### After

![After: Explore Appearance with Themes and Lobster Packs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ababbf8e-0ee9-4bf7-9475-3a0c1f008fb5)

prs.title: fix(trajectory): keep quoted tool arguments parseable in exports
prs.body:
Related: #113709.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes malformed trajectory JSON/JSONL exports when quoted tool arguments contain token-like text, even though the export command reports success.

## User Impact

Diagnostic exports remain parseable while retaining default, configured-pattern and registered-secret masking, along with benign values. No configuration migration is required. Thanks to @nimarosa for isolating the escaped-quote case and @alfred429 for the installed-exporter report.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final support-file safety pass uses the existing JSON scalar editor for JSON and JSONL; plaintext keeps its existing path. Configured patterns retain capture context and bounded scanning. Native-value serialization remains with the JSON token owner.

Current head `a78be9e690326a1f07f989c880a36337f00437d1` normally merges official main `7c2ff8f775acca3e5c93c9c22b6247e37df29bae`, preserving upstream history. The only conflict was the Cron inventory fixture: official [#192826](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192826), commit `d995f780eab8`, already waits for the initial chat-pane child-roster request. The file now exactly matches that canonical implementation, including its original zero-read and read-only assertions. Our duplicate prerequisite leaves the PR diff.

The six production files and the ten remaining author TypeScript/test inputs are byte-identical to published `1b0c3f4e` and the retained reviewed implementation. Own test credit decreases **46→44 LF**: **42** for consolidated exporter regressions and **2** for clipboard isolation. Cron now adds zero relative to main. The shared scalar and every other allocation match the integrated official base.

## Evidence

Validation uses Node 24.22.1 / pnpm 12.15.0 in the actual integration checkout.

- **Fresh canonical Cron replay:** all **5** bundled real-browser/mock-Gateway cases pass, with two startup roster requests and zero extra session reads for the protected churn cases. Wall time **78.37 s**; test time **32.50 s**. This whole-flow test covers the browser/transport request baseline; no operator Gateway or live model is involved. No runtime threshold, request filter or assertion was relaxed.
- **Scoped static checks:** local type-aware lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass. The documented Oxlint/oxfmt fallback was used because the pinned Bun fork could not be staged. The attempted CI lint-parity run failed during Bun setup; parity is not certified.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): allow 256 members and 10 browsers per member on a claw
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An OpenClaw ID claw refuses its 51st member and each person's sixth browser, which is too small for a shared team server: the OpenClaw team server alone has about 73 maintainers and 46–62 guests.

## User Impact

A claw can now have up to 256 members with up to 10 browsers each, and an owner device certificate can carry up to 10 peer keys. Owner devices stay at 20. No Gateway behavior changes until the OpenClaw ID Gateway code that consumes these constants merges.

## Why This Change Was Made

256 members is the statement list limit (`MAX_LIST`), so a snapshot listing every member still validates and no list format changes are needed. A new test builds a snapshot at every cap and checks that one more member hits the list limit. That snapshot is about 275 KiB of JSON (about 600 KiB if every account id character needs a JSON escape). The Discovery change sizes its snapshot publication limit for this and stops rewriting derived rows one statement at a time.

Deploy order: this loosens limits, so Discovery and the loader should take it before Gateways do. Companion changes:
- openclaw/discovery: snapshot publication limit and derived-row writes
- openclaw/claw-loader: re-vendored protocol

## Evidence

- `vitest` over `packages/openclaw-id-protocol`: 19 files, 131 tests passed, including the new cap tests.
- Discovery (vendoring this commit): 30 files, 227 tests passed, including publishing a worst-case snapshot and checking relay admission and member listing.
- claw-loader (vendoring this commit): typecheck and 83 unit tests passed; a reviewer smoke test parsed and verified a 280 KB snapshot at every cap.
- Independent review of all three diffs found no P0–P2 issues.
- Test-lines ratchet: the new cap tests add 46 test lines, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/openclaw-id-claw-limits.txt` (local check against `main` `d7ee885db8f`: OK, slack 17).

prs.title: fix(ios): wrap chat markdown tables instead of clipping the last column
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #191076

## What Problem This Solves

- Fixes an issue where iPhone users reading a markdown table in the native chat saw the last column cut off mid-word ("Sautéing, roasting, driz"), with no cue that the table could be scrolled and with table text visibly smaller than the paragraphs and bullet list in the same reply.
- The same shared renderer draws tables in the macOS chat, where columns likewise never wrapped and cells stayed at footnote size.
- **Related:** #191077 (companion report about card/block padding on small iPhones) is a separate, broader layout question and is intentionally not touched here; the ClawSweeper review on #191076 asks for "a focused repair in the existing shared table view … without a Markdown parser rewrite or the broader card-layout redesign".

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Intended outcome:** table cells wrap to the width the reply actually has, table text renders at the reply's body size, and horizontal scrolling remains available — with a visible indicator — only for tables whose minimum column widths genuinely exceed that width.
- The horizontal `ScrollView` proposed an unbounded width to the `Grid`, so every column took its longest cell's ideal width and the viewport clipped the result; `showsIndicators: false` removed the only cue; cells were pinned to `OpenClawChatTypography.footnote` while surrounding prose uses `ChatMarkdownRenderer.Typography.proseFont` (`OpenClawChatTypography.body`), a fixed ratio that Dynamic Type cannot close.
- The table now measures the width its reply actually gives it (`onGeometryChange` on the card) and bounds every cell to a column width derived from that measurement: `sharedColumnWidth(cardWidth:columns:)` splits the card's content width (card width minus 2 × 10 pt padding minus 14 pt per inter-column gap) equally between the columns, and each cell is laid out at that width with `.frame(width:alignment:)` on top of the existing `.fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)`, so the text wraps and wrapped rows keep their height. GFM per-column alignment now rides on the cell frame's `Alignment` (`cellAlignment(_:)`) as well as the header's `gridColumnAlignment`, because every cell fills its column instead of reporting its own ideal width. Typography is passed down from the renderer exactly like `listView(_:)` already does, so thinking blocks keep their own profile.
- Scrolling is a decision taken **after** the columns are bounded, not a fit test on an unconstrained grid: `overflowsReplyWidth(cardWidth:columns:)` is true only when the equal share drops below `minimumColumnWidth` (120 pt), i.e. when the table cannot keep its columns readable at the reply's width. Then the grid keeps 120 pt columns, ends up wider than the card, and is hosted in a `ScrollView(.horizontal)` carrying `.scrollIndicators(.visible)`; otherwise there is no scroller at all and the grid simply wraps. Before the first measurement (`cardWidth == 0`) the cell width is `nil` and no overflow is reported, so the initial layout pass is exactly the unbounded layout the view had before. An earlier revision of this PR made that choice with `ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal)`; the review pointed out that a fit test compares ideal widths, and an unconstrained grid always reports its unwrapped width, so the measured decision replaced it.
- **Out of scope:** no parser changes, no stacked/card redesign, no new settings, and no change to code or math blocks (they keep their indicator-free scrollers).
- **Highest-risk area:** the table view is shared with macOS, where wide tables must stay fully reachable and column alignment must survive; the card width now also arrives from a layout-pass callback, so the view renders once before the measurement lands.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The scroll branch reuses the same grid and only adds the indicator, per-column GFM alignment is applied to every cell (not just the header), the pre-measurement pass keeps `columnWidth == nil` so nothing collapses to zero width, and two new suites cover the change: `ChatMarkdownTableColumnWidthTests` pins the decision arithmetic (the reported two-column table at a 366 pt card, a six-column table that must scroll, a 1200 pt reply, and the unmeasured case), while `ChatMarkdownTableCompactWidthTests` renders the reported table through `ChatMarkdownRenderer` into an `NSHostingView` bitmap at 390 pt and 1200 pt and compares the rendered cell line pitch against probes built from the prose and footnote fonts.

## User Impact

- **Success criteria:** a two-column reply table on an iPhone shows both columns in full — cells wrap instead of running off the screen — table text is the same size as the reply's body text, and a table too wide to fit still scrolls with a visible indicator.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatMarkdownBlockViews.swift` — `ChatMarkdownTableView`'s measured `cardWidth`, `sharedColumnWidth(cardWidth:columns:)` / `overflowsReplyWidth(cardWidth:columns:)`, `tableLayout`'s scroll decision, and `cell(_:isHeader:column:)`'s bounded frame; the one-line renderer wiring in `ChatMarkdownRenderer.swift`; and the two suites `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Tests/OpenClawKitTests/ChatMarkdownTableColumnWidthTests.swift` and `ChatMarkdownTableCompactWidthTests.swift` (fixture: the oil/uses table reported in #191076).

## Evidence
- **Real environment tested:** worktree `aispace/worktrees/issue-191076`, branch `feat/issue-191076-ios-table-readability`, base `origin/main` `f2884869274`, head `64ae46ce12b`. No Apple toolchain exists on this Linux host (`which swift swiftc xcodebuild` → all absent), so no Swift compilation, `swift test`, simulator run or device screenshot was performed by me. I did try to stop guessing at the pinned formatter: `scripts/install-swift-tools.sh` installs macOS-only release binaries, and building SwiftFormat 0.63.1 from source inside a `swift:6.2` Linux container hangs in the Swift driver (0 % CPU, `hrtimer_nanosleep`, no output after 20 minutes). The formatting fixes below were derived from the pinned rules' published behaviour plus the shapes this repository's already-linted sources use, and were then confirmed by CI.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  # 1. repository pre-commit freshness gate (protocol models + native i18n inventory) — passed on every commit
  git commit --amend --no-edit

  # 2. arithmetic cross-check of the fit decision, re-derived from the Swift source because no Swift
  #    toolchain exists here; mirrors Tests/OpenClawKitTests/ChatMarkdownTableColumnWidthTests.swift
  node column-width-crosscheck.mjs        # exit 0

  # 3. the Swift suites that would execute this code — not runnable here, and not runnable in fork-PR CI
  swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter ChatMarkdownTable
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  # node column-width-crosscheck.mjs — the four cases ChatMarkdownTableColumnWidthTests asserts,
  # recomputed from sharedColumnWidth / overflowsReplyWidth exactly as written in the patch
  PASS  reported table does not scroll                   [overflows=false]
  PASS  two bounded columns + gap == card content width   [width=166 content=332]
  PASS  column stays readable                            [width=166 >= 120]
  PASS  6 columns at phone width scroll                  [shared=46.00 < 120]
  PASS  equal share below readable minimum               [shared=46.00]
  PASS  scrolled content wider than the card             [790 > 366]
  PASS  6 columns at 1200 pt do not scroll               [width=185.00]
  PASS  wide columns above readable minimum              [width=185.00]
  PASS  unmeasured width never scrolls                   [cardWidth=0]
  {"checks":9,"failed":0}                                  exit 0
  ```
  That is a consistency check between the implementation's arithmetic and the expectations its unit test asserts. It is not Swift execution and it renders nothing.
- **CI on head `64ae46ce12b`:** the `CI` workflow is green — all of its checks pass, including `ios-screenshots` (builds the app and runs it in the simulator) and both `openclaw/ci-gate` checks. `Build iOS Periphery reports` / `Build macOS Periphery reports` compile `OpenClawChatUI` for both platforms and run the pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 + SwiftLint phases clean, and `Scan shared kit from iOS` / `Scan shared kit from macOS` — the dead-code scans that cover the changed file — pass. The only red check on the PR is `Scan iOS dead code` in the separate report workflow, detailed below.
  The single red check is `Scan iOS dead code` in the separate `macOS Periphery Dead Code [report]` workflow, whose only finding is
  ```text
  {"hints":["unused"],"name":"scan()","location":"Sources/Settings/ESPSetupSession.swift:76:10","modules":["OpenClaw"]}
  ```
  `apps/ios/Sources/Settings/ESPSetupSession.swift` exists in neither this head nor current `origin/main` (`git cat-file -e origin/main:apps/ios/Sources/Settings/ESPSetupSession.swift` → absent; `git grep ESPSetupSession origin/main` → no match), so that finding comes from the scan's restored index store, not from this diff — which touches three files under `apps/shared/OpenClawKit` and no iOS app-target code. `openclaw/ci-gate` is green, so this report workflow does not gate the PR; I am not chasing it here.
- **Why the fit decision went through three shapes (CI history):**
  1. head `d63058aac10` — `SwiftFormat (lint)` `indent` errors at `ChatMarkdownBlockViews.swift:198-202`: with `--xcodeindentation enabled` a comment between a chain head and its first modifier indents the rest of that chain one extra level (accepted in-repo shapes: `ChatMessageViews.swift:1031-1035`, `ControlUIHubScreen.swift:97-99`). Fixed by moving the comment above the statement (`8f39257913e`).
  2. heads `7e7a2063dbb` / `ece3d361f2a` — the review's P2 on the fitted `ViewThatFits` candidate: `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)` reports the proposed width whatever the grid does, so the scroller was unreachable. That clamp was dropped.
  3. head `5f7dfdeb91c` — `ViewThatFits` replaced outright by the measured-width layout above, which is what the review asked for ("allocate constrained widths in the existing table layout before using scrolling as the overflow fallback"). CI then reported **both** `ChatMarkdownBlockViews.swift:194:1: error: (redundantStaticSelf)` and `(redundantSelf)` on that one line: with `--self insert` and `redundantStaticSelf` both enabled, a statement-initial `return Self.member …` inside a `static func` is claimed by the two rules at once — removing `Self.` makes the insert rule ask for `self.`, which cannot compile in a static context. Fixed in `64ae46ce12b` by binding the values first and returning an expression over locals, the shape this repository's linted sources already use (`apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawKit/GatewayEndpointID.swift:18-23`; 78 further `let x = Self.staticMember` occurrences inside static funcs across `apps/ios/Sources`, `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources` and `apps/macos/Sources`):
  ```diff
       static func overflowsReplyWidth(cardWidth: CGFloat, columns: Int) -> Bool {
           guard cardWidth > 0 else { return false }
  -        return Self.sharedColumnWidth(cardWidth: cardWidth, columns: columns) < Self.minimumColumnWidth
  +        let width = Self.sharedColumnWidth(cardWidth: cardWidth, columns: columns)
  +        let readableMinimum = Self.minimumColumnWidth
  +        return width < readableMinimum
       }
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** no rendering was observed by me — see the tier below. What is observable in this environment: `OpenClawChatUI` compiles for iOS and macOS and passes the pinned SwiftFormat/SwiftLint phases, the iOS app builds and runs in the simulator, and the shared-kit dead-code scans are clean for the changed file. In the code, `ChatMarkdownTableView` measures its card width, bounds every cell to an equal share of that width, renders cells at the reply's prose font, keeps GFM alignment per cell, and only reaches for a `ScrollView(.horizontal)` with a visible indicator when the share would fall below the 120 pt readable minimum.
- **Before evidence (optional, visual changes encouraged):** the reporter's screenshots in #191076 show the clipped second column and the smaller table text. On `origin/main` the table grid only ever lives inside `ScrollView(.horizontal, showsIndicators: false)`, so no cell is ever proposed a bounded width, nothing can wrap, and the hidden columns have no cue.
- **What was not tested:** no Swift compilation, `swift test`, simulator run or device screenshot was performed by me, and neither new suite has been executed anywhere — `scripts/ci-build-manifest.mjs` gates both Apple test lanes on `!ordinaryPullRequest` (`runMacos` :365-371 → `runMacosSwift` :385-388, and `runIosBuild` :399), so on any `pull_request` event `macos-swift (tests|packages)` and `ios-build` report `skipping`, which is what this PR's check list shows; the `OpenClawKit tests` step (`swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:5347-5361`) only runs on a maintainer `workflow_dispatch`/`schedule` run or after merge. Real iPhone/iPad rendering, Dynamic Type sizes, and wide-table behaviour in the macOS chat are therefore unverified by me. One earlier `ios-screenshots` attempt (head `7e7a2063dbb`) failed in `OpenClawSnapshotUITests.testReleaseChatScreenshot` at `:145` on `iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)` only: that test drives the release chat fixture in `apps/ios/Sources/Chat/AppleReviewDemoChatTransport.swift`, which seeds one sentence plus a fenced mermaid block and no markdown table, so the table view is never instantiated on that path; the same job passed on `iPhone 18 Pro Max` in the same run and on every later head.
- **Proof tier:** L1
- **Proof limitations:** runtime behaviour can only be proven on an Apple platform and this environment has none, and fork-PR CI structurally skips the lanes that would run the new Swift suites. The deterministic local evidence is the arithmetic cross-check above plus the CI compile/lint/dead-code results on this head; the rendered-behaviour evidence (wrapping at 390 pt, cell line pitch matching the prose font, scrolling with a visible indicator only below the readable minimum) exists as executable tests but has not been executed by me.
- **Review state:** blocked until live proof — a maintainer-run `macos-swift (packages)` lane executing `ChatMarkdownTable*Tests` on this head, or reporter device confirmation on the oil/uses table from #191076.

prs.title: feat(plugins): extend host APIs for repository integrations
prs.body:
## Summary

Repository plugins need to join OpenClaw's repository selection, checkout, execution, publication, and Control UI flows through public contracts. This PR adds the missing host capabilities to the Plugin SDK. [The companion GitHub migration](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192350) uses them to move the integration into a bundled plugin.

Plugins own vendor policy, authentication, transport, and presentation. OpenClaw retains sessions, approvals, checkout storage, process launch, durable records, and recovery. The SDK exposes reusable repository, execution, tool, and browser capabilities alongside three explicitly GitHub-specific bridges to existing native records and publication contracts.

Native GitHub consumers remain available in this foundation; the companion migration moves the implementation and configuration into the plugin.

## SDK capabilities

### Repository sources

The `openclaw/plugin-sdk/repository-sources` entrypoint supports discovery, managed local checkout, and optional worker preparation:

| Surface | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| Manifest `repositorySources` | Declares a plugin-local ID, label, and Gateway search method. Discovery works without loading browser code or enabling custom UI. |
| `api.registerRepositorySource(source)` | Registers URL admission through `resolve(url)` and preparation through `prepare({ url, agentId, requiredCommit, signal, assertCurrent })`. Preparation returns project facts, a current-authority assertion, and `resolveBase(ref?)` for source-owned base resolution. |
| `sessions.create.repositorySource` | Carries the picker's qualified `pluginId/contributionId`. An explicitly unavailable or incompatible source fails visibly rather than selecting a different source or account. |
| `createManagedProjectCheckoutV1(transport)` | Reuses host checkout leases, storage layout, and project registration. Plugins supply URL policy and authenticated clone, commit-fetch, refresh, and base-resolution operations. `resolveBase(project, ref, options)` holds the same canonical checkout lease. |
| Optional `worker` adapter | Supplies immutable repository/object identity, tree/blob reads, access revalidation, Git-pack preparation, checkout, and optional published-branch/checkpoint restoration. Sources without it report cloud preparation as unavailable. Admitted worker credential readers and cleanup callbacks retain the dispatch owner's authority and issued-token lifecycle. |
| `RepositoryCheckoutTransfer` / `performRepositoryCheckout` | Provides a bounded, one-use checkout operation while the host retains the destination and transport. Credentials stay out of returned metadata and prepared snapshots. |

For a default worktree, `resolveBase()` observes the current remote default through source transport, hydrates its immutable commit, and returns `{ commit, ref }`; remote default-branch renames are included. Explicit refs resolve locally first, and the source is consulted only when the chosen ref is missing. The host verifies the commit without lazy network fetches, retains safe local-default updates under checkout custody, and records the selected ref and commit before setup. Retries reuse that accepted pin. Credentials stay in the source closure; the host does not retry the canonical origin with ambient credentials.

The selected source and pinned commit follow session/worktree dispatch and recovery. Retained plugin workspaces restore the accepted snapshot and worker Git history, consume fresh retained-disk exports, and verify the disk before binding it to the session. Worker `identityKey` values partition cached content; current access is checked separately. The host revalidates the lease around Git-pack preparation, and plugins assert caller and credential authority at transport effects.

Worker preparation supports admitted public HTTPS URLs on other hosts and nested repository paths. Other transports use source-prepared packs; installing a pack preserves an admitted HTTPS, SSH, or SCP-style origin without contacting it. Anonymous worker fetches exclude ambient credentials and redirects.

### Execution environments

`openclaw/plugin-sdk/execution-environment` exposes `ExecutionEnvironmentProviderV1`, registered with `api.registerExecutionEnvironment(provider)`.

- `prepare(...)` returns nonsecret identity/scrub maps, excluded secret-store names, optional Git parameters, and an optional `wrapLocalLaunch(argv)` adapter.
- Local launch adapters enclose the reviewed command after command policy and approval. They can require native harnesses to use host execution; they grant no additional execution permission and add no model-facing tool.
- `prepareSandbox(...)` explicitly prepares Docker/Podman environment maps, read-only mounts, inherited variable names, and launch adapters for a backend and isolation scope. Local identity is not implicitly copied into a container. Unsupported placements reject a contribution rather than ignoring it.
- Optional pure `formatGitCoauthor(...)` formats host-selected, consenting, verified contributors for both local CLI and Gateway execution. Formatting needs no credential preparation; selection and lifetime remain host-owned.
- Manifest SecretRef paths can declare `executionEnvironment: "exclude"`. Secret preparation records environment/store exclusions even for disabled plugins without resolving those credentials.

Conflicting identity values name the contributing owners and key without exposing values. Preparers and returned callbacks belong to the managed plugin instance. The launch owner checks current authority at the process effect, including after approval waits.

### Caller-bound tools and child policy

A V2 plugin tool can use optional `context.gateway` operations under its invoking caller to call its registered Gateway methods and installed publication operations. Read-only client capability and workspace-preparation facts support presentation. Host admission, session access, approvals, and accepted-handoff custody still apply. A handoff can retain the selected requester through the existing host continuation; plugins supply no replacement identity, and retained authority remains subject to revocation.

`inheritToolPolicy` lets a factory describe its declared tools for child-policy capture when the parent workspace cannot construct them. This records the parent's policy ceiling without making the tool callable. Descriptions are factory-scoped; only the owning manifest supplies group membership, and foreign names, forged metadata, and retired registrations are rejected. Children construct and authorize their own tools.

### Control UI V2

`defineControlUiPluginV2` opts into additional browser capabilities while existing `defineControlUiPlugin` entries retain V1 host/view contracts.

| Capability | Integration and ownership |
| --- | --- |
| Profile connections and Agent tools Settings | Declared views use host placement, controls (including native details rows, disclosures, and section help), config reads, serialized mutations, and host-owned reactive projections. The host retains navigation, selection, config writing, and backend authorization. |
| Pages, panels, widgets, replacements, and navigation | Versioned, view-scoped presentation and bounded navigation use the existing browser application and transport. |
| Captured requests and subscription sets | Bind asynchronous work to the active Gateway connection, authenticated handshake, method catalog, and plugin lifetime. Reconnect can retain drafts while rejecting stale replies. |
| Session actions and accessories | Contribute headers, context strips, Environment content, rows, hovercards, activity, summaries, and mobile Details. The host retains layout, keyboard traversal, action admission, and observation cleanup. |
| Passive session badges | Plugins resolve bounded SVG/label/count/tone facts with explicit pending or ready results. Native rows render and persist those facts in the existing scoped sidebar snapshot, preserving them before reconnect; no executable plugin code or catalog is cached. Pending carry-forward is bound to the current complete session target and registration. |
| Retained session operations | `host.sessions.attachOperation(row, factory)` retains admitted work after a pane closes through the existing session owner. Retirement, session deletion, or lost authority ends custody. |
| Text references | `host.ui.registerTextReferenceProvider` resolves prose from immutable captured facts and names an exact `reader: { pluginId, id }`. Both registrations must be active, the reader still filters URLs, and code/existing links are excluded. Native references retain priority. |

A repository plugin can format shorthand while a separate reader owns opening and fetching it. Formatting grants no fetch authority.

### Native GitHub bridges

These entrypoints preserve concrete GitHub records and wire contracts:

| Entrypoint | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `native-github-account-host` | Canonical account records, owner-bound OAuth commits, personal connection authority, and refresh settlement. |
| `native-github-publication-host` | Provider installation, local Git/index transfer custody, prepared content facts, and publication receipts. |
| `native-github-session-read` | Session/source observations, own-PR binding, verified-account admission, and review presentation. |

Publication providers supply typed `NativeGitHubPublisherProvenance` facts and an author. Core records provenance in existing receipt fields, compares it for exact replay, and uses the author for source-integration commits. Request/account assertions authorize effects; provenance does not. Verified participant/consent facts remain host-owned, while the integration formats GitHub authors and coauthors. Recovery observes the recorded destination, validates its original host, and preserves accepted requests while the provider is unavailable; real failed recovery attempts retain upstream’s bounded retry policy. Origin qualification reuses physical checkout facts while checking current provider host policy on every use.

Native source-loaded plugins and compiled SDK consumers share the canonical Gateway owner, request lifetime, installed publication-host lookup, and GitHub HTTP quota/error kernel. Prepared own-PR readers retain admitted account identity inside the host capability. Wrapper capture stays bound to the admitted instance; cleanup, owner replacement, and revocation still end that capability. Publication and checkout transfers retain one-use host custody across loaders, and publication failures retain the same typed classification.

### Board, Doctor, and loading

Declared Board bindings use existing grant and audience preparation. Doctor collects declared health checks per invocation, keeps failed plugin registrations visible through normal selectors and severity thresholds, and preserves native ownership of always-on OpenAI reference checks. Settings-only resolution stays lazy. Browser cron readers use the narrow `@openclaw/gateway-protocol/cron-list-page-validation` subpath. SDK declarations, package exports, source/dist aliases, and plugin browser builds cover these contracts.

## Compatibility

Repository and execution registrations are optional. Existing browser V1 contracts, source/session snapshots, canonical account records, publication receipts, and wire DTOs retain their contracts. Released synchronous account adapters retain their documented compatibility window through December 31, 2026.

This foundation adds no model-facing tool, config option, schema/protocol-version bump, or GitHub credential/configuration migration. The detailed contracts live in `docs/plugins/sdk-repository-sources.md`, `sdk-execution-environments.md`, `sdk-entrypoints.md`, and `feature-plugins.md`.

## Test scope

The net test growth covers distinct SDK admission, retirement, configuration persistence, worker transport/cache, browser lifecycle, and stable consumer boundaries. Dedicated allocations cover the retained-workspace, publication-recovery, origin-policy, shared-observation, Doctor, cold browser-discovery, and installed-publisher readiness regressions. The shared test-line baseline is unchanged. Production dead-code metadata names the exact modules whose exported boundary seams are consumed by policy, source-lifetime, OAuth, publication, profile-retirement, and UI observer tests. The independent full-tree scan still audits every such export; obsolete zero-reference adapters and aliases are removed.

## Validation

- Full local `pnpm build` passes, including SDK declarations, Control UI and all 102 bundled plugins. All 167 public SDK subpaths verify; production typechecks and focused lint pass.
- Installed publishers admit `sessions.githubPublicationReadiness` through the same caller-bound tool policy as publication; its production-path regression passes.
- Focused source-base, publication/recovery, quota, cross-loader lifetime, Board, coauthor, badge/snapshot and reactive-owner suites pass. Browser proof covers cached badge rendering before reconnect, target/registration changes, disposal and cross-tab deletion.
- The stacked consumer's isolated Fake Forge trial passes through canonical Gateway calls: source-owned transport resolves a newer remote commit, the host creates a managed worktree, and a real agent `exec` receives the plugin identity. The model is a synthetic loopback fixture.

Authenticated remote writes, interactive OAuth, private/Enterprise access, real cloud provisioning, factory-native proof issuance/redemption and stable-to-candidate upgrades remain unqualified.

## Browser evidence

Existing sanitized synthetic captures illustrate picker presentation; they do not qualify live OAuth or external services.

| Native picker | Contributed source |
| --- | --- |
| ![Native repository picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f464135-9770-4129-b64d-b80a4a049c06) | ![Repository picker with a plugin source](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa32392e-ad41-4ba4-8e1b-fa623392361a) |
