prs.title: fix(ios): open embedded Dashboard after Cloudflare Access sign-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iOS, Cloudflare Access can admit a native Gateway connection while its embedded Dashboard has no usable session or incorrectly falls back to native settings.

## User Impact

Settings, Automations, Session Dashboard, Desktop and Terminal use the admitted native Access session for the exact Gateway authority. An accepted operator can use the Dashboard even when ingress deliberately issues no reusable Gateway token. Disconnection, local sign-out, expiry and observed revocation retire Dashboard authority and provide native recovery guidance.

Cloudflare sign-in does not grant administrator permission. The Gateway still owns pairing, profiles and accepted scopes. The client refuses automatic reuse of unbound or differently bound saved grants; this is a client safeguard, not server enforcement against a modified client. **Josh Avant accepted the scoped saved-grant client policy. The inherited CI budget reconciliation is incorporated. The final candidate incorporates the landed native fixture build fix from #191296 and builds without a production-source workaround. The final review cleanups and landing are authorized; release and distribution are outside this task.**

Related: #162164, #157874. This preserves Vitor Cepeda Lopes's existing branch and Vincent Koc's Access contributions in merged prerequisites #147238 and #147244.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native session owns challenge signing and accepted operator scopes. Each embedded document receives its Access admission before loading and loses it when the authority changes. WebKit uses a fresh nonpersistent store scoped to the exact HTTPS/WSS Gateway authority.

The Simulator campaign found and repaired three concrete failures:

- Accepted credential-free ingress had admin scopes but Settings inferred permission from persisted tokens, and native/frontend Dashboard signing required a reusable credential. The repair uses current accepted scopes and permits explicit empty auth while retaining signed device proof and malformed-auth rejection.
- Initial profile hydration retired a pending automation inventory request without refreshing the page. The page now uses its existing identity/epoch lifecycle, preserving the draft and rejecting stale inventory.
- Fresh ingress correctly withheld a legacy unbound node credential, but also omitted its compare-and-swap observation, preventing new issuance from replacing that row. The repair observes it only for conditional persistence; it remains absent from request auth and signed token fields, and a newer concurrent write still wins.

The stored-token projection of current admin permission was removed. No new state owner, configuration option, credential store or server permission rule was added. The first repair commit added **51 production lines / removed 52**, added **389 test lines / removed 101**, and added **4 docs/allocation lines**. The exact 37-line regression allocation protects profile hydration and stale inventory without raising the shared scalar.

The subsequent ownership repair addresses both findings in the [review of fb70e007](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158051#issuecomment-5830582035). The existing node reconnect Task directly owns retries again, preserving the simplification from `c430435303491981b78fe4f816d0780f3188b71f`; per-attempt Access binding and token-version handoff stay in that Task. The existing `ControlUINativeGatewayAuthHandler` is now the sole WebKit receiver/parser for Access and ordinary sessions, using the existing document lifecycle and live-session signer. The duplicate handler, parser, stored-token signer and obsolete tests are removed. Authority generation is captured per operation so an already mounted page can recover after a same-route reconnect while in-flight work is retired. Relative to fb70e007, this ownership repair adds **202 / removes 531 production lines** and adds **20 / removes 108 test lines**; these are repair-only deltas, not the whole PR.

The follow-up removes the two test-only node-auth forwarding methods and their injection-only parameters. The replacement test drives production session resets and reconnect Tasks through real WebSocket handshakes: A issuance/binding, B refusal without issuance, actual B rotation/binding, fresh B reuse, A refusal, and ordinary-route fallback. The retained real WebView test now attempts a challenge after same-route principal reassignment and original-admission retirement while its native operator socket stays healthy. A fixture endpoint independently records allowed follow-up I/O and remains unchanged for forbidden requests. Relative to fcd2ea9, this follow-up adds **4 / removes 39 production lines** and adds **200 / removes 114 test lines**; it adds no production testing hooks.

## Evidence

Landing candidate: `49ca93e5a9dcc38ef0b8e1fcb530e6a8edd55cbd`, descendant of fully proved `bd52aae629cdebe71b5d17061ed70811d5b1d452` and contributor head `84acd312831747b3fbc8b91e69c267eb54a11d74`. Before the landing cleanup below, the only committed final-campaign delta was the exact cherry-pick of upstream `ce339781514fbb68499e2f7f623d031895fabaf0` (#191296), preserving author/coauthor credit. It extracts the two review-demo fixture constructors without changing their data/order/timestamps or lint policy. Gateway/UI runtime inputs are unchanged from head84; reuse below is scoped accordingly.

**Final native proof (November 4):** canonical build-for-testing passes and **65 focused tests pass, zero failures/skips**, including principal-bound saved grants, reconnect/rotation, session persistence, fleet and Settings/Session/Terminal consumers, actual five-entrypoint WKWebView admission and older-document warning contracts. Canonical signed Release device build passes; app, widget, share extension and Watch target satisfy signature/profile/team/platform/architecture checks. There are **no production-source overlays**. Generated Xcode/signing/version metadata and six task-only UI-test overlays are separately hashed. No demo/auth-injection mode is enabled. Native main-thread/Simulator runtime warnings remain recorded; this is not a zero-warning claim.

**Final same-install retirement/recovery:** Healthy A → acknowledged local sign-out → Settings fallback → ordinary process relaunch with continued refusal → Reconnect requiring website sign-in → Cancel → usable native fallback all pass in one sequence. Normal recovery then uses **fresh actual QA-A credential entry**, authenticated Gateway-page settlement and encrypted transfer; recovered Settings/Automations pass. Independent Gateway trace accepts A/admin native node/operator and successful `cron.list`; the same public device/key persists with no native pairing request. Original failed runs remain failed.

**Genuine older runtime:** the official immutable `openclaw@2026.9.6` package, embedded source `eb377ac59e6c9fd6c7705028034812becf00271b`, runs with matching released UI on separate state/port behind the real Access route. Registry integrity, embedded build identity, served HTML/module closure and missing native-auth bridge are independently qualified. Its unchanged local source build exhausted the qualified cgroups three times; using the official published package is the supported fallback, **not a source-build success claim**. v2026.9.2 (`3928bad9badfcb6c7d140530435e806fb8092190`) admitted the node but rejected this OIDC identity source with `authenticated-profile-unavailable` / `Cloudflare Access identity is not GitHub-backed`; v2026.9.6 contains the existing OIDC repair [#153556](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153556). No old source or identity/role guard is patched.

**Older-runtime live result:** actual QA-A website credential entry/encrypted transfer and approval of only the exact primary native pairing request establish the same native device on v2026.9.6. The canonical QA-A profile role is assigned administrator; fresh accepted native node/operator connections independently correlate QA-A and post-profile-cap admin elevation. Its actual old embedded page shows **“Approve this browser”** while native Gateway connectivity remains online. A personally inspected screenshot's exact visible request UUID matches the canonical still-pending Control UI browser request, with a different public identity from the approved native device. **No browser request is approved.** The final UI selector passes the real pairing heading, exact existing native sign-in/update guidance, enabled on-screen **“Open Gateway settings”**, and navigation to actual native Gateway settings. It does not claim old web pairing success. The candidate route is then restored; normal native reconnect, current embedded Settings/native device status beyond the compatibility deadline, and Automations admin control all pass. Fresh candidate logs independently accept QA-A/admin native node/operator and `cron.list`; the primary public device/key is unchanged, with no native pairing request.

**Older-runtime limits and failed expectations:** v2026.9.6 already sends device-settings capability status and the native-embed marker, so it does **not** exercise the distinct missing-device-settings warning. The original specific-warning selector remains failed; its WKWebView contract coverage is separate. A second mistaken expectation required “This iPhone” behind the unapproved browser gate. A subsequent task selector could not read the visibly rendered approval command as WebKit StaticText; the successful lane instead uses an independently inspected screenshot/canonical request match without claiming AX extraction. Another attempt stopped before the compatibility page with native browser-sign-in-required state; normal candidate sign-in and old native reconnect re-established the precondition. All original failed results and sources remain failed and attributed. An earlier candidate health preflight timed out before any route write; fresh bounded health probes passed, and later guarded route writes have exact readbacks.

**Final physical shipped-app install-over:** actual TestFlight **2026.10.90 (5)**, independently qualified to source `0468e735508a5ceafca5e855479a7a870f99cbc8`, was replaced in place by signed final candidate **2026.10.9 (124629)** without uninstall/reset. This is development install-over, with a numerically lower marketing version; no TestFlight/App Store update-distribution claim. The final candidate automatically recovered QA-A native node/operator authority without another browser login or pairing prompt. Independent Gateway observations retain the same public key/device identity and node grant metadata, accept A/admin operator authority, and record successful `cron.list`. Embedded Settings → This iPhone bridge and a subsequent green loaded cold-launch Chat pass; no new model turn was sent.

**Physical data:** before explicit first launch and again after actual launch, all **15 allowlisted preferences**, installation `node.instanceId`, **102 messages, 24 cached agent-session rows, two transcripts, 12 migration records**, schemas and integrity are retained. Routing/branch/roster keys remain; only runtime `updated_at`/`last_used_at` timestamps and branch revision change after recovery. Shared relay fields decode identically. This is semantic preservation: cache WAL/SHM and plist metadata differ; onboarding timestamp and Watch bridge metadata changes are recorded. No backup preservation/restoration is required for this dedicated QA installation.

**Physical limits:** empty baseline outbox/Watch journal means populated queued-work migration is unproven. The paired Watch connection/DDI/Developer Mode was not qualified; signed Watch output does not prove installation/runtime. No shipped entitlements extraction, Keychain export or opaque credential-row identity comparison was performed. The shipped baseline connects its node but its tokenless-Access operator-loop guard keeps Chat disconnected; exact shipped/final source and normal reconnect/cold-restart observations establish that premise. Healthy baseline Chat is therefore not claimed. Operational public identity/authentication continuity is proved, while unbound-grant policy retains its separate Simulator/transport evidence.

**Reusable head84 live evidence:** real QA-A website sign-in/encrypted transfer; embedded Settings/Automations; Desktop view-only plus accepted `desktop.observe` and real VNC socket; Terminal plus accepted `terminal.open` and exact session inventory with no input; normal Session Dashboard route plus fresh `board.get`. A UI-created disabled automation has independent API/canonical SQLite proof of A creator, disabled state, system-event payload, no delivery and zero run receipts/history. Exact removal and canonical/API absence are verified. Session fixture removal and empty reaped Terminal inventory are verified. No redundant protected write was run for the fixture-only final source change.

**Reusable authority regressions:** the prior `794052982bb` follow-up has **138 focused tests passed** and two deliberate mutation controls failing at the intended real outgoing-token and retained-WebView-signature boundaries. The same retained page signs for A, refuses B reassignment while the native socket remains healthy, recovers after A restoration/fresh authority generation and refuses retired admission without extra fixture I/O. The broader `fb70e007` campaign covers actual same-install A→B→A/limited-native fallback, local retirement, natural expiry, exact operator-role revocation and acknowledged Access-app revoke, with independent no-effect/readback and recovery. Those receipts retain their original sources; no blanket current-source replay or instantaneous remote-revocation guarantee is claimed. Fixture I/O is not Gateway RPC authorization proof; unavailable UI is not a claimed server mutation denial.

**Failures and recovery:** original historical aggregates remain failed. The final retirement01 failure reaches acknowledged sign-out, refusal after relaunch and renewed website sign-in/Cancel, then taps a header covered by the real sign-in banner despite AX reporting it hittable. Fresh screenshot, geometry, diagnostics and independent source review establish a harness input failure. The task-only correction uses the existing supported root-edge gesture in that observed state, retaining Show disappearance, exact Hide visibility, actual Settings navigation and all admin-refusal checks. Initial final-campaign recovery setup failures involved premature website Done, an unrelated discovered-Gateway sheet and the password-save prompt. Their records are retained; normal exact sheet close/password-save decline and authenticated-page settlement correct setup. Earlier successful recovery using existing A website SSO is labeled accordingly; the final post-retirement recovery separately completes fresh QA-A password entry. The old runtime's initial qualifier also incorrectly expected unmodified HTML; its source-owned serving transformation must be qualified separately from immutable served module bytes.

**Review:** independent P0–P3 source review of the complete 57-file base `258d034391ac` → `bd52aae629cd` range found no actionable findings. The selected [hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158051#issuecomment-5830582035), Revision69, completed on exact `bd52aae629cd` in [run41925763682](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41925763682): no correctness/security findings, proof sufficient, ready for maintainer review. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; local autoreview failed authentication before producing a report and is not claimed clean.

**Landing cleanup:** published `49ca93e5a9dcc38ef0b8e1fcb530e6a8edd55cbd` removes the three helper-only cookie-admission tests (57 test lines) and the consecutive identical Share-extension sign-in guard (8 production lines). The original guard and production cookie-admission owners remain. A separate independent P0–P3 review of this exact two-file delta found no actionable issues or unused support seam. Canonical build-for-testing passes; **9 affected native tests pass, zero failures/skips**, including the remaining SessionDashboard suite and actual five-entrypoint WebKit/native-auth and older-document warning contracts. The real-entrypoint test does not claim branch-for-branch repetition of the deleted private-helper assertions. Existing live/physical/older-runtime proof retains its original head attribution; no unchanged-input full replay is claimed. Local TypeScript deadcode scans could not qualify their environment because workspace UI dependencies are missing; this cleanup changes no TypeScript, package dependencies or exports. **The additional iOS26.2 smoke was explicitly declined and minimum-supported-OS execution remains unproven.**

**Current landing-head CI:** `49ca93e5a9dc` [canonical CI41928957680](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41928957680), attempt1, completed with **62 successful,19 skipped and three failed jobs**. [checks-ui (2/3)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41928957680/job/126921208236) repeats the same single offline catalog assertion from scheduled main41906482889/job126843055034; all six inspected test/composer/catalog/English/i18n inputs are identical across that main, the actual CI baseline `d7ee885db8f7` and tested merge `f33933a20b30`. [Android Access16384](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41928957680/job/126921209499) fails before app build/test because the hosted emulator needs12,288 MB for userdata but has10,907.18 MB free; no Gradle build or native tests execute. Its Android app, toolchain actions, trust script and CI job section are unchanged by this PR. The automatic table labels Android “new” because its main job passed; this independently inspected runner-capacity cause is retained rather than silently relabeled. The third failure is their aggregate gate. **No branch-caused failure remains;CI remains failed.** iOS screenshot capture/evidence, the other Android lanes, Docker E2E, native i18n, branch-related checks and security-fast pass. Landing uses the authorized inherited/unrelated-failure evidence route with exact-head review/security and live writer verification, without rerunning CI or repairing unrelated main. Native local build and9 affected tests pass as detailed above.

**Historical CI:** Pre-cleanup `bd52aae629cd` [canonical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41914089166), attempt1, completed with **63 successful, 19 skipped and two failed jobs**. The only nonaggregate failure is [checks-ui (2/3)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41914089166/job/126869678001): the offline catalog case of `chat-pane-session-controls.test.tsx` expects “Offline” and receives “Disconnected.” Complete logs show the same single test and exact assertion in [scheduled main run 41906482889](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41906482889/job/126843055034) (`aeeff2c634014c2a75ef56b3d10ecab971a987dd`); the relevant test, catalog/composer owner and English/i18n inputs are unchanged by this PR. The second failure is its aggregate CI gate. No new or unknown failures remain. This remains red, not a green CI claim or merge waiver. Final-head [native Periphery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41914088764), attempt1, **passes: seven successful jobs, one skipped**, including iOS build/consumer index, dead-code gate, shared scan and intersection. iOS screenshot/evidence CI also passes. Normal native test lanes are skipped; the final local canonical build and 65-test execution supply explicit native evidence. Earlier source-attributed `ESPSetupSession.scan()` Periphery failures retain their historical attribution and are not relabeled current.

**Budget:** the authorized reconciliation here incorporates upstream [#191696](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191696), exact scalar **6,319,970 → 6,320,804 (+834)**. This supersedes the old +831 proposal; no duplicate grant or separate repair PR. All checker policy, tests and existing allocations remain; the PR's **37 + 32 + 16 = 85** regression lines are accounted independently. Exact prospective merge proof goes from **831 over** before correction to **3 lines slack** after it, and [head4731 canonical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41587374633) independently verifies that result.

Previously inspected, sanitized Settings images retain their historical source attribution; the fixture extraction adds no UI behavior change:

| Before repair: connected Gateway, native fallback | After repair: embedded Settings |
| --- | --- |
| ![Settings native fallback before repair](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0714f3b-43d5-49a9-8a09-8a2c9397c68d) | ![Embedded Settings after repair](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9112da09-e6c8-4360-824d-7c0de78f9bd2) |

Historical physical images (prior source `794052982bb`, not the new final-device captures):

| TestFlight baseline | Candidate embedded Settings after cold launch |
| --- | --- |
| ![Physical TestFlight baseline, native Settings and online Gateway](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f4bba23-d864-4292-be80-8fc1b3bdf83c) | ![Physical candidate, embedded Settings after cold launch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cfbc648e-6dbf-43ba-9ae9-ca027a86f461) |

The yellow ingress guidance is unconditional in this mode. The separate missing-device-settings warning has WKWebView contract evidence; v2026.9.6 already supports those capability signals and does not exercise that warning.

**Resources/closeout:** Final canonical task inventories are empty: no task automation, Terminal session or task session remains. Private UI inputs and Simulator clipboard are cleared. Both task-paused apt timers are restored without changing enablement. The candidate/older Gateways, QA IdP and tunnel are stopped; PID-zero/absent-listener readback reconciles Keycloak's TERM-derived exit 143, whose failed unit state is retained. Both task Simulators and the exact UTM VM are verified stopped. Dedicated Cloudflare resources remain for reproduction with the origin intentionally offline. **37 disposable physical-artifact paths (8,054,207,660 logical bytes) are removed**, with zero retained/errors and 65 protected proof files unchanged; no backup/archive/restoration. Unmerged source worktrees and necessary proof/recovery material remain. Existing apps-signing retrieval was read-only; temporary signing keychains/profiles are cleaned and the original keychain state is preserved. No new Apple ID/profile, 1Password write, production service change, release or distribution occurred. Authorized landing and its final closeout are tracked separately by the maintainer workflow.

prs.title: fix(test): load one Lit runtime in root UI Vitest
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Focused root UI Vitest runs load Lit 3.3.3 twice. Direct `lit/**` imports go through the jsdom dependency optimizer, while `@awesome.me/webawesome` stays on Node's loader and imports native `lit`, which then evaluates native `lit-html`. Lit warns `Multiple versions of Lit loaded` even when the assertions pass.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared and isolated root UI runners now inline `@awesome.me/webawesome` into Vitest's server dependency graph, next to the existing optimizer include of `lit/**`. Web Awesome's `lit` imports then use that same optimized module instead of a second native copy.

The inline is opt-in on those two runners only. The UI package runner already prebundles Web Awesome components and is left unchanged, because inlining that package there double-registers custom elements. Lit itself is not upgraded, and no product UI behavior changes.

## User Impact

No shipped Control UI change. Warning-free acceptance runs of the root UI Vitest lanes no longer fail on this duplicate Lit load.

## Evidence

Head `26717f4b244d7a180390c589043184fbdae2ab60`, rebased onto upstream `main` `0de7e437ff6ab7363165bbc903ce832b229ce3dc`.

- Without the inline (temporary local removal, not committed), `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/vitest-ui-lit-runtime.test.ts` failed: `expected [ /@(?:codemirror|lezer)\// ] to include '@awesome.me/webawesome'` (1 failed, 1 passed, exit 1).
- With the inline restored, the same command passed 2 tests (exit 0).

prs.title: fix(ui): recover when IndexedDB is unavailable on the first open
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openControlUiDatabase` checks `typeof indexedDB === "undefined"` inside the promise executor and rejects there. That rejection runs before the function caches the promise, so the cached value is an already-rejected promise — after one visit where IndexedDB was unavailable (private window, sandboxed iframe, third-party storage blocked), every later `outboxPayloadUnavailable` / draft-store call keeps failing until a full page reload, even though IndexedDB is back.

## Why This Fix

The availability check moved before the promise is constructed: the unavailable case now returns a fresh rejection without touching the cache, so the next call can open normally. The success and `request.error` paths keep their existing `release()` behavior, and the deliberate `blocked` case (which keeps its rejected promise so a queued open stays behind it) is unchanged.

## User Impact

A WebChat session that hits an unavailable IndexedDB recovers on its next attempt instead of staying broken until a reload — the outbox and draft stores open again as soon as the browser exposes IndexedDB.

## Evidence

- New `control-ui-database.runtime.test.ts`: the first call with IndexedDB unavailable rejects, a later call with IndexedDB present opens and resolves; a second case pins that one successful open is still reused. The recovery case fails against the previous code (verified by reverting only the source change).
- `ui` typecheck clean, boundary-guard lint and formatting clean.

Closes #149887

## What Problem This Solves

## Why This Change Was Made

Responsive layouts now use the space available to the settings pane. Existing page rules handle headers, forms, cards, and tables; the tab adapter keeps the selected tab visible and releases resize observations when its view closes.

## Evidence

- **33 pages, 1440 × 900 and 1100 × 900:** page workers captured each surface and separate agents inspected the screenshots, reported defects, and accepted the repairs. **340 before/after pairs**, plus four scroll-reachability images.
- **34 end-to-end tests and 135 focused browser/unit tests passed.** Includes all mobile settings routes, sidebar interactions, Chat/New Session siblings, tab resizing, keyboard activation, and observer cleanup. Layout and tab regressions fail before their fixes.
- **Hosted CI passed all 201 jobs before the final test-fixture corrections**, including the required `openclaw/ci-gate`, both Windows jobs, and the real-Gateway UI suite: [run 35019072619](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35019072619), head `b65d478be6b2e5745d15a490e11911be1c516d12`.
- Three independent code reviews found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Final changed-file checks passed, including typechecks, formatting, lint, i18n, and repository guards.
- Captures use the running Control UI with synthetic Gateway and native-bridge fixtures. The native embedded Settings landing and full Ask OpenClaw page intentionally suppress a second assistant pane; their supported layouts were checked at both widths.

Full screenshot record: [agents & models](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149321#issuecomment-5685651314), [connections](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149321#issuecomment-5685651721), [identity & device](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149321#issuecomment-5685652022), [memory](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149321#issuecomment-5685652293), [plugins & tools](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149321#issuecomment-5685652723), [security & automation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149321#issuecomment-5685653228), [system](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149321#issuecomment-5685653678).

ClawSweeper follow-through (revision 6, reviewed head `b65d478be6b2`): the review reports no actionable correctness findings, accepts the screenshot proof, and explicitly rejects the earlier migration concern. prs.title: fix(bedrock): use known Kimi K2.5 context window
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: OpenClaw on Amazon Bedrock treats Kimi K2.5 as a 32k-context model when Kimi K2.5 appears in the account's model or inference-profile listings, because the extension's known-context-window catalog predates the model's Bedrock launch.

## User Impact

User impact: Bedrock users selecting Kimi K2.5 now get its documented 256,000-token context window in the discovered model metadata, so context budgeting and compaction size the model correctly instead of using the conservative 32,000-token unknown-model fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

`KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` in `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts` is the single catalog mapping Bedrock model IDs to context windows; unknown IDs fall back to a conservative 32,000-token default. Kimi K2.5 (`moonshotai.kimi-k2.5`) was missing, mirroring the Grok 4.6 gap fixed in #192927 and the same-day sibling fixes for Grok 4.7 (#193022), GLM 5.3 (#193035), and Kimi K3 (#193045). This adds the documented value with the AWS model card as the source, and resolves through the existing prefix-stripping (`us.`/`global.` etc.) and `:0`-suffix normalization, so base and cross-region inference-profile IDs are covered.

AWS model card: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-moonshot-ai-kimi-k2-5.html — Context window: 256K tokens; max output 16K; Active.

## What Was Changed

- `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts`: added `"moonshotai.kimi-k2.5": 256_000` to `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` with the model-card link.
- `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts`: regression test asserting the base ID `moonshotai.kimi-k2.5` and a us.moonshotai.kimi-k2.5 inference-profile variant resolve `contextWindow: 256_000`.

Not changed: neighboring catalog entries, Claude 5.x / Claude Opus 4.8 special-casing, the conservative 32,000 fallback, and `defaultContextWindow` config.

## Evidence

Real before/after on stock main (only the AWS SDK transport mocked; `discoverBedrockModels` is the production discovery path):

```text
before: expected { id: 'moonshotai.kimi-k2.5', …(6) } to match object { contextWindow: 256_000 }
        Received: "contextWindow": 32000
after:  full discovery.test.ts — 22/22 passed, including the new regression test
```

- Focused full-file suite: `scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts` — 22/22 passed.
- Format check (`scripts/run-format.mts --check`) and scoped oxlint on both changed files: pass.
- Latest-main re-check at `6e24d6fa240e`: the catalog still lacks `moonshotai.kimi-k2.5`, so the fix is not already on main.
- Local full-repo typecheck was not runnable in this environment (it needs the generated `packages/plugin-sdk/dist` declarations, which the local build pipeline does not emit on Windows); the change only adds a `Record<string, number>` entry and reuses existing test helpers, and CI type coverage applies.

## Risks / Notes for Reviewers

- Data-only catalog addition; no API, config, schema, or protocol surface changes.
- If AWS revises the window, this entry needs the same one-line update as its siblings.

## What Problem This Solves

Authorized guest conversations need disposable remote workspaces and attached browser, file and computer access without running guest workloads on the Gateway or receiving harness/model/provider secrets.

<!--

Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:

-->

## User Impact

Adds Gateway-only automatic per-request allocation using unchanged released Crabbox. Initial support is direct AWS Linux with existing safe resource choices; unsupported or unqualified routes fail closed. Existing trusted worker flows remain unchanged.

Operators must select a released executable and an explicit trusted AMI, same-account subnet and security group meeting the documented disposable-disk/network requirements. Managed routes, other providers/OSs, IPv6, and prepared/retained guest disks are not supported. No new eligibility, quota or machine-recipe system is introduced.

This is implementation and offline qualification, not deployment approval: live AWS isolation/tamper, agent/model bootstrap and captured-video playback have not been qualified. AWS-reserved services outside security-group filtering are not claimed blocked; metadata is independently disabled. Live operator qualification is required before adoption. No live configuration, role, provider or runtime changes were made.

<!--

Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse session admission, ownership/epoch, irreversible grant revocation and attachment-owned command/file/browser/computer transports. A provider-plugin Gateway adapter qualifies AWS account, subnet, security group and effective VPC routes; binds the exact instance/interface/lease; disables metadata with readback; and requalifies retained access. Guest-project configuration and credential forwarding do not control the host-side allocator.

Disposable-volume admission and immutable launch custody precede fallible volume qualification. Partial custody grants neither guest access nor unverified deletion. Guest teardown cannot fall back to receiptless CLI stop; trusted cleanup can recover first-write custody under the current owner and retains ownership until the instance and every captured volume are confirmed absent. Ordinary trusted teardown is unchanged. Unknown, foreign, incomplete or failed-persistence outcomes remain fenced.

All changes are in OpenClaw. No Crabbox fork, new server protocol, upstream patch or static/manual-box substitute is required.

prs.title: fix: spawning child processes and exec calls fails on Linux hosts with glibc < 2.31
prs.body:
Closes #191841

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after upgrading to 2026.10.10, every child process spawn and exec tool call fails immediately with `Error: native child reaping is unavailable | helper-unavailable` on Linux hosts running glibc < 2.31 (e.g. RHEL 8 / CentOS 8 / Rocky Linux 8 / Alibaba Cloud Linux 3).

## User Impact

User impact: users on older enterprise Linux (glibc 2.28) can once again run all child process tools, exec calls, and scheduled script triggers. When the native child-reaping helper is unavailable on those hosts, service children now spawn and are supervised via POSIX process groups, restoring the reliable 2026.10.9 behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The 2026.10.10 release hard-bound the service-child relay to the Linux native subreaper path. On hosts where that binding cannot load (glibc < 2.31), the relay refused to spawn children instead of degrading gracefully. The relay now probes the reaper capability at startup via `@openclaw/proc-safe/reaper` `isSupported()` and, when it is unavailable, selects the existing POSIX process-group supervision anchor (`assertProcessGroupControl`) that OpenClaw already used on other platforms. No new dependencies, no lockfile change, and the output message for the diagnostic companion PR is sourced from the same capability probe.

## Evidence

- New regression test `src/process/supervisor/service-child-relay.reaping-fallback.test.ts`:
  - decision unit test: on a host with native reaping unavailable, `prepareServiceChildRelay` selects the process-group anchor (`useLinuxSubreaper === false`); it is **RED on base** and **GREEN with this fix**;
  - e2e spawn test: a service child is spawned and supervised through the fallback path.
- Live verification on a real git 2.27/glibc 2.28 (RHEL 8) node:
  - `PROC_SAFE_NATIVE=off` (simulating the unavailable native helper): relay reports `useLinuxSubreaper=false` and spawns a child successfully through the process-group anchor — fails on the unchanged base checkout;
  - `pr.py verify` VERIFIED; runtime check exercised both the fallback and the native-available branch.
- Format and line-cap-ratchet checks pass.

prs.title: fix(cron): reject compact digit --at values misread as epoch ms
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: confusing cron rejection when a compact datetime is passed to `--at` / `schedule.at` — `--at 20250101120000` (meant as `yyyyMMddHHmmss`) was read as epoch milliseconds and rejected with `schedule.at is too far in the future: 2611-09-14...`, which shows no trace of the input the user actually typed.

## User Impact

User impact: mistyped or compact numeric `--at` values are now rejected with the original input echoed back — `Invalid schedule.at: expected ISO-8601 timestamp (got 20250101120000)` via Gateway/API, and `Invalid --at "20250101120000". Use an ISO timestamp or a duration like 20m.` via CLI — so users can see what was rejected and why.

Behavior change (single, focused):
- Pure-digit `--at` values whose numeric value is 10,000,000,000,000 ms or more can no longer be parsed. Previously they were misread as epoch ms and rejected with a derived date centuries in the future; now they are rejected directly with the raw input in the message. Realistic epoch-ms input (anything before year 2286, including zero-padded forms like `01798761600000` = 2027-01-01 UTC) is still accepted, exactly as before.

ISO timestamps, documented durations (`20m`, `+30m`, …), and all previously accepted epoch-ms values behave exactly as before. No config, API schema, or stored-data format changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pure-digit strings were parsed as epoch ms, and the original string was destroyed before validation: the CLI converted the misread value to an ISO string, and Gateway normalization rewrote `schedule.at` the same way, so the rejection message could only name the derived date. Two paths now stop the misread at the parse boundary instead. `parseAbsoluteTimeMs` rejects digit strings by comparing the **parsed numeric value** against the upper end of the epoch-ms range reachable within the far-future scheduling cap — a 14-digit `yyyyMMddHHmmss` compact datetime (≈2.0e13 ms) is the realistic input there, while zero-padded epochs for valid dates keep parsing because the bound is on the value, not the digit count (review feedback; earlier revision used a digit-count check that rejected valid leading-zero epochs). The CLI `parseAt` no longer falls back to its bare-number-as-milliseconds duration interpretation for pure-digit input, which had reabsorbed the rejected value as a ~642-year duration. The CLI error message now includes the raw input, and the Gateway validator's existing message already echoes `schedule.at`, which normalization now leaves untouched when parsing fails.

<details>
<summary>Root cause walkthrough</summary>

- `src/cron/parse.ts:11-17` parsed any pure-digit string as epoch ms; `20250101120000` → `2611-09-14T04:05:20.000Z`.
- The 10-year cap in `src/cron/validate-timestamp.ts` did catch it (no silently wrong scheduling), but the message showed only the derived ISO.
- Original input was destroyed pre-validation: CLI `src/cli/cron-cli/shared.ts` converted to ISO, and Gateway `src/cron/normalize.ts:72-74` rewrote `at` to the derived ISO when parsing succeeded.
- Second absorption path: `parseAt`'s duration fallback parses bare numbers as milliseconds (`src/cli/parse-duration.ts:48-52`), turning the rejected compact date into "now + 20250101120000 ms" ≈ year 2668.

</details>

## Evidence

Targeted tests (169/169 passed, incl. new zero-padded-epoch regression that fails on the previous revision): `src/cron/{parse,validate-timestamp,normalize,schedule}.test.ts`, `src/cli/cron-cli/{shared,trigger-options,schedule-options.positional,schedule-options.onexit}.test.ts`. Lint and format clean. Structured self-review after the value-bound revision: PASSED, no P0–P2 findings, best-fix verdict `best`.

Real-behavior proof (shipped CLI + Gateway request path), captured against a fresh isolated gateway state dir (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-proof-state`, loopback port 19008, token auth); the dir and test jobs were removed after capture.

### Proof A — shipped CLI rejects the compact input (exit 1)

```
$ pnpm openclaw cron add --name proof-at-digits --agent main --message hello --at 20250101120000
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "Invalid --at \"20250101120000\". Use an ISO timestamp or a duration like 20m."
  }
}
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```

### Proof B — Gateway request path rejects with the raw input

```
$ pnpm openclaw gateway call cron.add --port 19018 --params \
    '{"name":"proof-at-digits","sessionTarget":"main","wakeMode":"now",
      "schedule":{"kind":"at","at":"20250101120000"},
      "payload":{"kind":"systemEvent","text":"proof-tick"}}' --json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "gateway_request_error",
    "code": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "message": "Invalid schedule.at: expected ISO-8601 timestamp (got 20250101120000)",
    "retryable": false
  }
}
```

### Proof C — zero-padded epoch accepted (numeric-domain compatibility)

```
$ pnpm openclaw gateway call cron.add --port 19018 --params \
    '{"name":"proof-zero-padded-epoch","sessionTarget":"main","wakeMode":"now",
      "schedule":{"kind":"at","at":"01798761600000"},
      "payload":{"kind":"systemEvent","text":"proof-tick"}}' --json
{
  "id": "d1a594b7-a163-4ccf-9467-7a71a27808de",
  "schedule": { "kind": "at", "at": "2027-01-01T00:00:00.000Z" },
  "state": { "nextRunAtMs": 1798761600000 },
  ...
}
```

### Proof D — persisted data still loads after a gateway restart

`cron.list` before and after a full gateway restart both return the persisted job with `schedule.at: "2027-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"` and `nextRunAtMs: 1798761600000` (stored `at` values are ISO after create-time normalization; the parser's accepted digit-string domain is unchanged for every value it accepted before this PR).

### Before/after parser probe (supplementary)

Temporary vitest probe (removed after capture) exercising the parser/validator directly:

Before fix (pre-PR code):
```
parseAbsoluteTimeMs => 20250101120000 2611-09-14T04:05:20.000Z
parseAt => 2611-09-14T04:05:20.000Z
validate => {"ok":false,"message":"schedule.at is too far in the future: 2611-09-14T04:05:20.000Z (584 years ahead). Maximum allowed: 10 years"}
```

After fix (this PR):
```
parseAbsoluteTimeMs => null
parseAt => null
validate => {"ok":false,"message":"Invalid schedule.at: expected ISO-8601 timestamp (got 20250101120000)"}
```

What was not tested: `tsgo` type gates could not run locally (host glibc 2.28 < 2.32 required by the native tsgo binary); covered by CI. The full `src/cron` suite (160 files) was not run locally — the 8 directly affected files were run in full; remaining cron coverage runs in PR CI.

Fixes: the Subagents tab hides a subagent's own workers, so someone watching the main session cannot see the delegated work beneath it.

## User Impact

Nested subagents appear directly beneath their parent in the desktop **Subagents tab**, using the existing rows with a small indent and connector. **Floating Details and mobile direct-child lists are unchanged.** No new badges or waiting-on-name copy, configuration, migrations, or required user action. Rows within a nested family have no horizontal divider; independent top-level rows keep theirs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The panel's scoped roster owner loads and observes descendant lists only when the desktop tab opts in, and retires them when branches or views disappear. Existing grouping, counts, activity, navigation, Stop targeting, and Done reveal remain intact.

## Evidence

- Real-browser regression: the nested reviewer was missing on the base (expected 1 row, received 0); it is visible with the fix.
- 46 focused unit/component checks passed, including denied-list recovery after a shared roster refresh.
- 12 browser checks passed: nesting, live membership, child Open/Stop targeting, parent draft preservation, native/mobile siblings, and floating Details isolation.
- UI typecheck, focused lint, CSS lint, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Independent local autoreview through P2 completed. Its one stale-error recovery finding was reproduced, fixed at the roster owner, and verified red → green. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable within this session's file scope; hosted review is the workflow fallback.
- Screenshots below use synthetic data and were inspected in dark, light, and narrow desktop layouts. No live Gateway or private session data was used. Full CI remains a PR check; one existing Solid lint warning in unchanged Stop initialization is not introduced here.

- Follow-up regressions cover the removed internal separator, retained top-level separators, and mobile → desktop → mobile changes on the same mounted panel.
- The scoped test-line allocation is exactly **324 net lines**, covering roster lifecycle, scoped actions, Details isolation, and presentation regressions. The shared scalar is unchanged. The pinned original base has 62 lines of inherited debt; this allocation does not conceal it.

prs.title: feat(mattermost): add allowBots mention policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mattermost has no equivalent of Slack's `allowBots` policy. When thread participation is enabled, implicit activation also applies to other bot authors, so an allowlisted bot can trigger a turn in an engaged thread without a new explicit mention.

## Solution

- Add `allowBots: true | false | "mentions"` at account and group scope.
- Identify bot authors through the post's `from_bot` property (both boolean and Mattermost's string form) or the Mattermost user's `is_bot` field.
- In `"mentions"` mode, require explicit activation for bot authors even when thread participation would admit a human follow-up. Authorized control-command behavior is preserved.
- Keep `allowBots: false` for disabling bot-triggered turns and the default `true` for existing behavior.
- Avoid a new sender lookup in the default mode when Mattermost already supplies `sender_name`.
- Document the setting and regenerate channel config metadata.

Human thread participation and existing sender/channel restrictions remain unchanged.

The intentional `+4` channel config-surface entries are the root/account and group variants of the new `allowBots` policy (including account-scoped group overrides). This is required for Slack-compatible policy precedence, not an unrelated budget increase; the generated config docs baseline is refreshed with `pnpm config:docs:gen`.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/mattermost/src/config-schema.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 19/19 passed on the fixed tree; the same regression test fails on the pre-fix schema (1 failed / 18 passed), then passes after restoration.
- `pnpm config:channels:check` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check <changed files>` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Independent read-only review (xai/grok-4.7) found two P1 issues; both were fixed and covered with regressions for string/boolean `from_bot`, failed sender lookup, and group precedence. No post-fix independent re-review is claimed.
- Live Mattermost API contract check: the tested bot account returns `is_bot: true`; the tested human account omits the flag, which the `=== true` check handles.

## Local environment gaps / CI-required proof

- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-posts.bot-threads.test.ts` includes the behavioral regressions, but the local suite did not start: its compiled worker was killed with exit 137 twice on the 8 GiB host, including with a 2 GiB heap cap. No passing behavioral result is claimed locally.
- Targeted `run-oxlint` did not reach linting: plugin-sdk boundary dts preparation timed out after 300 seconds. The source tree was verified clean of interruption artifacts.
- PR CI is required for the behavioral suite, lint/typecheck, and broader compatibility proof.

prs.title: fix(discord): preserve fenced code after marker lines with trailing text
prs.body:
Closes #127656

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Allow edits from maintainers is enabled.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users receiving long Discord code blocks would see later code rendered as prose when the block contained a fence-like line with trailing text, such as ` ```not-a-close`. The same defect affects ordinary channel messages and webhook replies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord's chunker closed a block after checking only the fence marker and its length. Its closing rule now matches the existing shared Markdown contract: the marker must match, be at least as long as the opener, and have only spaces or tabs after it. CRLF fence lines are recognized, while backtick-containing info strings are not misclassified as block openers. The outer reasoning italic marker is separated before scanning, and generated closing italics are placed on a separate line after code fences with space reserved in the transport budget.

The repair stays in the Discord chunk owner; no SDK, dependency, or configuration changes. Separating the existing reasoning wrapper preserves its formatting contract while enforcing actual fence endings. Wrapper restoration also runs when only one nonempty message survives, placing the closing delimiter before trailing whitespace.

## User Impact

Code remains fenced across Discord message boundaries, including code that looks like a Markdown heading. Actual closing fences still return following text to prose, and outgoing messages remain within the transport limit.

## Evidence

- September 12 integration: rebased onto main `366335ad9cd6`, preserving the allocation improvements from #142447 and all upstream webhook tests. The only manual conflict joined independent test additions; `git range-diff` confirms unchanged repair logic. **237 tests passed across four suites**, covering chunking, ordinary sends, webhooks, and native-command replies. Targeted formatting, typed lint, `git diff --check`, and a fresh independent branch review passed for the rebased candidate `e211bb56f01b`. [GitHub CI passed on this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34673184167).

- Before the repair: the three affected suites reported **9 failed, 193 passed**. The new failures cover false closers, CRLF, channel HTTP payloads, and webhook HTTP payloads.
- At the previously reviewed head `8a07c53835eb`: three suites reported **207 passed** under Vitest 5.0.0, including an additional regression for reasoning markers after synthetic closing fences. The tests use `mdast-util-from-markdown` as an independent semantic oracle and capture requests through local HTTP servers using the real Discord send paths.
- Review follow-up: the single-surviving-chunk regression failed for both `Reasoning:` and `Thinking...` before correction (**2 failed, 103 passed** in the chunk suite). Both now parse as actual emphasis, including when trailing blank lines are discarded. A further pair of cases for `__hello__` also failed before correction (**2 failed, 105 passed**) and now preserve strong emphasis rather than losing a content-adjacent underscore. The final 207-test run covers this correction.
- The initial repair passed full Discord plugin validation with isolated fork workers: **246 files, 3,343 tests passed**. A subsequent review found the synthetic-fence reasoning edge case; its new test failed before correction, and the final focused run above includes the correction. The default worker run previously exited unexpectedly after 2,812 passing tests; the isolated rerun completed without failures.
- Before the September 12 rebase, changed-scope formatting, lint, production/test typechecks, plugin boundaries, dead-export checks, and runtime import-cycle checks passed; that head also passed [GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34071825635).
- Independent `autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`: **scoped-clean**, with no actionable findings.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command-reply.test.ts
pnpm test:extension discord --pool=forks --isolate --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- extensions/discord/src/chunk.ts extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Validation used Node 24.19.0 on macOS arm64. Live Discord client screenshots were not captured: this environment has no dedicated test bot/channel credentials. Local HTTP payload evidence does not claim a live Discord round trip.

Related follow-up: the shared `hasBalancedFences` test helper still uses the old marker-only closing rule. These regressions deliberately use the independent Markdown parser instead of that helper.

prs.title: fix(runtime): merged Windows env blocks lose PATH entries from differently cased keys
prs.body:
Addresses the `withNodeRuntimePath` duplicate Windows PATH spelling item of #184894.

## What Problem This Solves

A direct call to `withNodeRuntimePath` with both `PATH` and `Path` retains directories only from the first spelling. This proposal concatenates both values before prepending the selected Node runtime.

## User Impact and Open Decision

If differently cased values reach this helper in a production Windows lifecycle, concatenation would retain both lists. That production scenario has not been demonstrated: review notes that the normal spawn caller normalizes duplicate aliases first, and that first-key precedence may be an intentional contract. This PR is a draft until a maintainer decides whether that behavior should change and a relevant Windows flow is demonstrated.

## Why This Change Was Made

The helper currently sorts PATH-keyed variables, reads the first value, and writes it to every spelling. The proposed change instead concatenates the values, retaining the first spelling's order and removing the duplicate runtime entry. Single-key behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- The added helper regression fails on the unpatched base for the dual-spelling input and passes with this change; single-key, duplicate-entry, and no-PATH cases remain unchanged.
- `pnpm test src/process/exec-spawn.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/update-command-node-runtime.test.ts src/infra/node-options.test.ts` passed. The lifecycle script test failed identically on the base because the pinned Bun fork could not be staged locally.
- The changed-file typecheck and lint lanes passed; the broader check reported pre-existing unused exports outside this diff.
- No shipped Windows update or recovery path was exercised. The macOS host cannot establish whether duplicate aliases reach this helper or whether combining them is the intended product behavior.

prs.title: fix: suppress short heartbeat status replies ending in NO_REPLY
prs.body:
Related: #142588

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users receiving scheduled heartbeat notifications would receive short all-clear status text when the model appended a standalone `NO_REPLY` line instead of returning only the silent token.

Synthetic example:

```text
Nothing requires attention.

NO_REPLY
```

The canonical token-only check rejects this mixed reply, and the legacy heartbeat acknowledgment filter recognizes `HEARTBEAT_OK`, not this form of `NO_REPLY`. The reply therefore reaches channel delivery. This is a marker-present variant related to #142588, not a complete fix for that issue's marker-absent narration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply a narrow tolerance at heartbeat delivery normalization: a standalone final `NO_REPLY` line suppresses text only when the preceding trimmed text is at most the existing 300-character acknowledgment budget. Keep ordinary chat and transcript classification unchanged. Explicit failures and error payloads are excluded; execution-completion relays retain message-mode behavior. Structured `heartbeat_respond` notifications remain authoritative, and media/structured reply content stays deliverable.

## User Impact

Short status replies in this shape no longer generate alerts. Explicit `showOk=true` still emits the canonical acknowledgment rather than the original status prose.

Normal actionable alerts should not carry `NO_REPLY`, which expresses a request for silence. The reported production incident was repeated all-clear narration carrying that marker—not a missed actionable alert. We deliberately constructed a contradictory short alert plus a final `NO_REPLY` as an adversarial boundary test; we have not observed that contradictory-alert shape or resulting alert loss in production, and its real-world frequency is unknown. The bounded rule does suppress that constructed input, so this remains a disclosed policy tradeoff, not evidence of an observed production alert-loss regression. Ordinary alerts without the marker remain deliverable. Plain narration without a marker, inline marker mentions, and over-budget replies are outside this fix; structured heartbeat responses express the notification decision explicitly.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through `runHeartbeatOnce` with isolated state and a mocked channel sender: the original code called the sender once for the synthetic mixed reply instead of remaining silent.
- Regression coverage includes final-line whitespace/CRLF, the 300/301-character boundary, inline/prefix/middle mentions, a normal alert, response prefixes, `showOk`, completion relays, explicit errors and failures, media/presentation content, and explicit `notify=true` text.
- Targeted validation passed: 7 files, 277 tests (173 token/transcript helper tests and 104 heartbeat delivery tests), using the repository test runner with Node 26.7.0. Final core and infra-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The broader `check:changed` run was deliberately stopped during unrelated test typecheck shards and is not claimed as passing; no full build/full test suite was run.
- Pre-publication `autoreview` completed as `scoped-clean` at P0–P2 severity; no actionable findings.
- Read-only independent review identified a context-free transcript-filter regression in an earlier approach; the final implementation is delivery-only and the follow-up review found no remaining behavioral issues.
- The initial tests above used mocked channel senders. The follow-up below adds real Discord delivery evidence using isolated Gateway processes; the production Gateway was not stopped, reconfigured or patched.

All examples and test inputs are synthetic. No original chat transcripts, channel/message/account identifiers, local paths, private configuration, credentials, or private model identities are included.

## Follow-up: real Discord delivery evidence and boundary clarification

On 2026-09-12, six synthetic cases were executed through isolated, built Gateway processes and the real Discord REST sender. Before: `3456f50eb1780b6f3296fcba87b8d171dd54ebcf`; after: `e9eb1d68cc6aae724b2c97ac96b4a5b53e579633`; Node `v26.7.0`. Both exact source checkouts were built using the repository runtime-build path. The model was the repository's deterministic QA HTTP Responses fixture, not a live generative model. No Discord sender was mocked or replaced.

| Synthetic case | Before: terminal / Discord messages | After: terminal / Discord messages | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Short all-clear + standalone final `NO_REPLY` | `sent` / 1 | `ok-token` / 0 | Reproduces and corrects the reported incident shape |
| Ordinary short alert without a silent marker | `sent` / 1 | `sent` / 1 | Positive delivery control remains intact |
| Deliberately contradictory alert + standalone final `NO_REPLY` | `sent` / 1 | `ok-token` / 0 | Constructed adversarial boundary, **not an observed production alert-loss case** |

The third case tests inconsistent model output: an actionable sentence asks for notification while its final marker asks for silence. We constructed it intentionally to expose the rule's precedence. Its suppression was observed in the synthetic test over real Discord; that does not establish that real alerts normally contain the marker or that a production alert has been lost. No probability or zero-risk claim is made. Maintainers still decide whether this bounded tolerance is appropriate.

### Execution and verification

1. Each case used a fresh workspace/configuration/state, a dedicated loopback Gateway port, an explicit Discord DM destination, `messages.visibleReplies=automatic`, and `showOk=false`. `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1` disabled inbound monitoring, so the existing Gateway remained running without a competing receiver.
2. The repository QA fixture (`extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.ts`) supplied an exact synthetic reply over HTTP/SSE. Each case had one matching successful provider request; the isolated assistant transcript contained the complete expected text with a normal stop, including the quiet cases.
3. `cron.run(mode=force)` invoked the system heartbeat monitor. Its heartbeat payload follows `source=interval`, `intent=scheduled`, `reason=interval` in `src/cron/service/timer-execution.ts`. This manually exercises the normal scheduled heartbeat runner; it is not a wall-clock timer firing, system-event wake, ordinary chat or announced cron message. A 24-hour configured cadence prevented incidental repeats during each short test.
4. `last-heartbeat` recorded the terminal outcome. Discord server history was fetched for the unique synthetic marker for at least 30 seconds afterward. All visible messages matched the exact expected synthetic text; zero-message cases had a verified nonempty model response and `ok-token`, not an absent or failed run.
5. All isolated Gateway processes and the QA provider were stopped, test ports were released, and production configuration hashes remained unchanged. The original Gateway process remained healthy throughout.

This verifies real Discord outbound delivery and server persistence, not Discord inbound interaction, independent recipient-client observation, real-model behavior, or Telegram Test Server acceptance. The production installation has not received the patch.

Would this additional real Discord evidence satisfy the applicable delivery-proof requirement? Telegram-specific validation, if still required, and acceptance of the bounded-marker precedence remain maintainer decisions. Only synthetic inputs and redacted results are included; no private chat records, identifiers, credentials, local paths or raw logs are published.

## Follow-up: real Telegram delivery and recipient-device observation

On 2026-09-12, the same base `3456f50eb1780b6f3296fcba87b8d171dd54ebcf` and PR head `e9eb1d68cc6aae724b2c97ac96b4a5b53e579633` were tested with the real **Telegram production Bot API**. This is **not Telegram Test Server or Convex-leased userbot evidence**. Six final cases passed using fresh isolated Gateways, the repository deterministic HTTP Responses model fixture, forced scheduled heartbeat execution via `cron.run(mode=force)`, automatic visible replies, and `showOk=false`. Inbound channel startup was disabled; no production Gateway restart, reconfiguration, or patch deployment was required.

| Synthetic case (final `QA-TG2` matrix) | Before: heartbeat / successful Telegram sends | After: heartbeat / successful Telegram sends |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Short all-clear + final standalone `NO_REPLY` | `sent` / 1 | `ok-token` / 0 |
| Ordinary alert without the marker | `sent` / 1 | `sent` / 1 |
| Deliberately contradictory synthetic alert + final `NO_REPLY` | `sent` / 1 | `ok-token` / 0 |

For all six cases, we checked one matching model request, the complete expected assistant text with a normal stop, and the terminal heartbeat result. Each Gateway remained alive for at least 30 seconds after completion. Positive cases had the Telegram sender's `outbound send ok` record with a returned message ID; those records are emitted after delivery results, not merely when a request starts. Quiet cases had a verified nonempty reply and `ok-token`, rather than a failed or missing run. Both runtime normalization-module hashes match the previously documented Discord builds. All test processes were stopped, ports released, and the production configuration hash and Gateway process remained unchanged.

### Recipient-device screenshot observation

The recipient supplied a real-phone Telegram screenshot after the run. We visually inspected the original and the recipient-provided privacy-cropped version. The crop contains only synthetic test messages, without the account header, avatar, or unrelated conversation. It visibly corroborates:

- `QA-TG2-after-alert`: the post-fix ordinary alert reached the recipient client.
- `QA-TG2-before-quiet`: the pre-fix all-clear reached the recipient with the literal final `NO_REPLY`.
- `QA-TG2-before-alert` and `QA-TG2-before-contradictory`: the other positive pre-fix controls also reached the client.
- No `QA-TG2-after-quiet` or `QA-TG2-after-contradictory` appears in the supplied capture. This is corroboration, not standalone proof of absence; the complete model responses and `ok-token` outcomes establish that those cases ran and were intentionally suppressed.

**Recipient-device attachment:** the recipient uploaded the privacy-cropped screenshot in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/144834#issuecomment-5646645925). The published image was re-fetched and visually verified; it shows the synthetic messages described above, without the account header, avatar, or unrelated conversation.

![Privacy-cropped Telegram recipient-device evidence; QA-TG2 is the final matrix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5554a67a-cc2e-48a3-a254-b011e625fead)

The two older `QA-TG-...-alert` entries visible above the final matrix belong to an initial attempt. That attempt included a network send failure and was superseded by new `QA-TG2` markers with an explicitly configured existing proxy. Failed/uncertain deliveries were not blindly replayed. An unused auxiliary HTTP recorder captured no requests and is not counted as proof; the final matrix did not route through it.

The contradictory alert is still a deliberately constructed adversarial input, not an observed production alert-loss incident. Normal alerts should not carry `NO_REPLY`. No claim is made that a screenshot proves the production frequency of that hypothetical case, or that these production-server tests meet the repository's Test Server-specific requirement.

Please reassess the remaining proof gap using this real Telegram transport evidence, the reported recipient-device observation, and the already accepted Discord evidence. If Test Server/userbot coverage remains mandatory, please specify the missing behavior it would establish and the supported route for an external contributor without the QA test-pool access. Maintainer acceptance of the bounded-marker policy remains a separate decision.

prs.title: fix(bedrock): use known Kimi K3 context window
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: OpenClaw on Amazon Bedrock treats Kimi K3 as a 32k-context model when Kimi K3 appears in the account's model or inference-profile listings, because the extension's known-context-window catalog predates the model's Bedrock launch.

## User Impact

User impact: Bedrock users selecting Kimi K3 now get its documented 1,000,000-token context window in the discovered model metadata, so context budgeting and compaction size the model correctly instead of using the conservative 32,000-token unknown-model fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

`KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` in `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts` is the single catalog mapping Bedrock model IDs to context windows; unknown IDs fall back to a conservative 32,000-token default. Kimi K3 (`moonshotai.kimi-k3`) was missing, mirroring the Grok 4.6 gap fixed in #192927 and the same-day sibling fixes for Grok 4.7 (#193022) and GLM 5.3 (#193035). This adds the documented value with the AWS model card as the source, and resolves through the existing prefix-stripping (`us.`/`global.` etc.) and `:0`-suffix normalization, so base and cross-region inference-profile IDs are covered.

AWS model card: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-moonshot-ai-kimi-k3.html — Context window: 1M tokens; launched 2026-09-18.

## What Was Changed

- `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts`: added `"moonshotai.kimi-k3": 1_000_000` to `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` with the model-card link.
- `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts`: regression test asserting the base ID `moonshotai.kimi-k3` and a us.moonshotai.kimi-k3 inference-profile variant resolve `contextWindow: 1_000_000`.

Not changed: neighboring catalog entries, Claude 5.x / Claude Opus 4.8 special-casing, the conservative 32,000 fallback, and `defaultContextWindow` config.

## Evidence

Real before/after on stock main (only the AWS SDK transport mocked; `discoverBedrockModels` is the production discovery path):

```text
before: expected { id: 'moonshotai.kimi-k3', …(6) } to match object { contextWindow: 1_000_000 }
        Received: "contextWindow": 32000
after:  full discovery.test.ts — 22/22 passed, including the new regression test
```

- Focused full-file suite: `scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts` — 22/22 passed.
- Format check (`scripts/run-format.mts --check`) and scoped oxlint on both changed files: pass.
- Latest-main re-check at `cf5c9a8eebe9`: the catalog still lacks `moonshotai.kimi-k3`, so the fix is not already on main.
- Local full-repo typecheck was not runnable in this environment (it needs the generated `packages/plugin-sdk/dist` declarations, which the local build pipeline does not emit on Windows); the change only adds a `Record<string, number>` entry and reuses existing test helpers, and CI type coverage applies.

## Risks / Notes for Reviewers

- Data-only catalog addition; no API, config, schema, or protocol surface changes.
- If AWS revises the window, this entry needs the same one-line update as its siblings.

prs.title: fix(deps): adopt fs-safe 0.27.1 for responsive filesystem operations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw still uses fs-safe 0.27.0, whose native POSIX staged writes and awaited path traversal can block the Gateway event loop on slow storage.

## User Impact

Adopts [fs-safe 0.27.1](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/releases/tag/v0.27.1), which moves those filesystem waits off the JavaScript thread while preserving confinement, identity checks, file modes, and durability. This addresses the affected operations, not every source of event-loop delay.

## Why This Change Was Made

Update all 13 direct pins together, regenerate the pnpm lockfile, and replace the 11 exact-version release-age exemptions. The exemptions expire seven days after the final package publication. The independent acpx dependency on fs-safe 0.26.15 remains unchanged. The lockfile also contains one pnpm-generated normalization of existing `escape-string-regexp@4.0.0` optional metadata; no unrelated dependency versions changed.

Five existing tests now observe the intended boundaries:

- Memory I/O faults target async POSIX traversal or sync Windows traversal, preserving original EIO rejection without retry and EAGAIN recovery.
- Directory-rebinding rejection uses the existing host-root escape classifier and retains the outside-file byte check.
- Catalog cadence observes directory enumeration, excluding unrelated identity probes during thread upserts.
- File-transfer EIO injection starts after real archive extraction, preserving the manifest error identity and absence of a successful audit.
- The restart test now follows the crash-resume contract introduced by [#190964](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190964) and bounded to the preceding Gateway lifetime by [#190995](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190995). Its older idle-after-SIGKILL expectation was stale. It proves one ordinary resume input on the same persisted session without replaying the original prompt, explicitly aborts this isolated test's resumed wait, waits for idle, and proves a fresh message receives its own reply.

The narrow 60-line test allocation matches exact net growth for scoped fault injection, retry assertions, and the existing crash/restart lifecycle proof. No new test cases, production hooks, runtime source, timeouts, or OpenClaw release metadata changed.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190233
Upstream fixes: https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/1052, https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/1053, https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/1054

## Evidence

- [Current ready-PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41924679848) validates `ba2fd98c0e89372decfbfa1005804574e80881dd`. Its [QA lane](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41924679848/job/126906890481) passed the changed real-Gateway restart test (16.15s test time, 53.84s Vitest wall time, 55.46s runner shard) and its sibling. The existing E2E process/restart boundary cannot be proved by a mocked helper; no new test case was added. The complete run, build, PostgreSQL conformance, and aggregate gate passed; required checks are green.

- Upstream [release run](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/actions/runs/41310162643) completed package integrity, signature, and provenance verification. All 11 new lockfile integrity values match the registry.
- pnpm 12.15.0 lockfile-only resolution passed supply-chain policy verification for all 1,748 entries. All 13 manifests and importers agree; the 11 older package records and 11 older snapshots remain unchanged.
- Native formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Independent review of the complete 21-file candidate against `fc5fec19bdefeb475edbccaaf9d19557af59a9e0` found no P0–P2 defects in the working-tree repair; its index-only stale-assertion finding was resolved by staging that repair. A separate review caught and corrected empty-transcript polling during startup.
- On `f210fdaf6180db12f77a732182fdea33d4b5175e`, [ready-PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41919504301) passed the build, catalog, and file-transfer lanes. Its QA failure demonstrated the obsolete no-resume assertion; the current patch corrects that contract. That failure is corrected and the replacement-head run above passed.
- On previous head `a52e5ae6fb0217493e0b929f9f2e58a0b90bb908`, the [exact-source build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41911219304/job/126860062319), [memory lane](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41911219304/job/126860073981), and [agents-core tools lane](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41911219304/job/126860086403) passed. Preflight checkout logs bind that manual-run proof to the source SHA; its workflow ref differs. Subsequent [ready-PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41914869947) reported the catalog/file-transfer measurement failures and the stale SIGKILL expectation described above. These prior results are not presented as final-head proof or a green broad manual run.
- Local runtime/build and focused Testbox proof were unavailable: the code-only worktree has no qualified dependency installation, and the wrapper correctly refused a stale tooling owner before allocation. The config-docs pre-commit check had the same setup gap; commits used the documented hook-skip route after separate native formatting proof. Hosted CI owns the missing checks.

The [initial manual dispatch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41906188062) failed configuration preflight before build or runtime tests. Later dispatches used the documented default validation setting. No failures were hidden with ignores, snapshots, or retries.
