issues.title: WebUI: model button does not reflect the active primary or fallback model
issues.body:
### Bug Description

The WebUI composer model button can be mistaken for the model handling the current request, but it displays the configured/selected preset rather than following the gateway's `turn_model_updated` events. In particular, it does not update when a fallback handles the turn. This makes the interface misleading when the default preset, session selection, and actual response model differ.

In the reported case, the global default was `GPT 6.1 Sol Med`, the user selected `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free` through OpenRouter for a chat, and the interface still appeared to identify GPT as primary during processing. Sanitized gateway logs established that Nemotron was actually attempted as primary. OpenRouter rejected it with HTTP 401, followed by Gemini fallback attempts; `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview` ultimately succeeded. The display discrepancy should not be interpreted as evidence that GPT actually processed that request.

The OpenRouter authentication failure and provider quota errors are separate configuration/service problems. This report concerns accurate model attribution in the WebUI, not bypassing those failures or changing fallback routing.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a default model preset and at least one different fallback preset.
2. Open a WebUI chat and select its intended preset.
3. Submit a request that causes the primary provider to fail and a configured fallback to be used. A mocked provider failure is sufficient; no external outage is required.
4. Observe the gateway's `turn_model_updated` events and the composer model button while processing and after completion.

For a deterministic frontend reproduction, render `ThreadShell` with a default OpenAI Codex preset, emit a chat-scoped `turn_model_updated` event identifying a different primary model, and then emit one with `model_name: "deepseek/deepseek-chat", fallback: true`. The button continues to show the configured preset instead of following the reported runtime model.

### Expected Behavior

The interface should clearly distinguish the preset selected for the next request from the model actually processing the current turn. The model button should reflect the gateway-reported primary/fallback model and provider while processing, with the last reported model visible after completion. Opening the picker should retain the user's selected preset for the next request; using a fallback must not silently change that selection.

Alternatively, if maintainers prefer the button to represent only the next-request selection, its presentation should make that distinction explicit and provide equally visible current-model attribution during processing.

### Actual Behavior / Code Evidence

At upstream revision `cc4dd1ceb`:

- `webui/src/components/thread/ThreadShell.tsx` derives `modelBadge` from `toModelBadgeInfo(modelName, settings, activeModelPreset)`. Non-fallback `turn_model_updated` events only clear the fallback notice; fallback events populate a separate notice without updating the composer model display.
- `webui/src/tests/thread-shell.test.tsx` explicitly covers the existing behavior in the test named “keeps the selected composer preset and attributes only the reply to its actual source”.
- `docs/guides/configure-model-fallback.md` says the composer still shows the selected preset.

This is therefore a request to correct a confusing display contract, not a claim that the existing behavior is accidental or that backend model selection has been proven broken. Fallback notices and per-reply attribution already exist; they do not make the model button itself follow the active model.

### Environment

- nanobot: 0.4.0; source baseline `cc4dd1ceb` with local WhatsApp integration fixes
- Python: 3.13.2
- OS: macOS arm64
- Channel: WebUI / WebSocket
- Connection: local gateway, packaged WebUI
- Browser version: not recorded
- Providers involved in the report: OpenAI Codex default, OpenRouter-selected Nemotron, Gemini fallbacks

### Local Fix and Verification

A local patch now tracks the existing chat-scoped runtime model events for display separately from the selected preset. It updates the button label/provider without changing the picker selection or model-routing policy. No protocol changes are required; hosts without runtime-model events retain the existing configured-preset display.

Verification:

- Regression test reproduced the unchanged fallback label before the fix and passed afterward.
- 335 tests passed across `thread-shell.test.tsx`, `model-preset-badge.test.tsx`, `thread-composer.test.tsx`, and `model-fallback-notice.test.tsx`.
- The updated regression also verifies a reported Nemotron primary differing from the configured default, its OpenRouter branding, fallback display, and resetting to the reported primary on the next turn.
- A picker regression verifies that runtime display does not change the selected preset or its model details.
- Type checking, focused ESLint, client import-boundary checking, and the production WebUI build passed.
- The rebuilt WebUI was installed locally and its served bundle verified. No new live model request was sent to validate this display patch; runtime events were exercised deterministically in tests.

Related reports: #5198 concerns session model switching itself; #6031 concerns fallback notifications on non-WebUI chat channels. This report focuses on the WebUI composer button's runtime-model attribution.

issues.title: Subagents ignore `tools.cliApps.enable: false` (run_cli_app still registered for subagents)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### Bug Description

**Version:** nanobot-ai 0.4.0 (also present on `main` as of 2026-11-04, commit 8632940)

**What happens**
With `tools.cliApps.enable` set to `false`, the main agent correctly no longer offers `run_cli_app`, but subagents still get it.

### Steps to Reproduce

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Config:
   ```json
   { "tools": { "restrictToWorkspace": true, "exec": { "enable": false }, "web": { "enable": false },
                "cliApps": { "enable": false }, "my": { "enable": false } } }
   ```
2. `nanobot agent -m "Use a subagent to count the lines in inbox.md and report the number."`
3. Inspect the tool list sent to the model (e.g. via a logging proxy in front of the provider):
   - main agent requests: no `run_cli_app` ✓
   - subagent requests: `apply_patch, edit_file, find_files, grep, list_dir, read_file, run_cli_app, write_file` ✗

**Cause**
`nanobot/agent/subagent.py`, `SubagentManager._subagent_tools_config()` builds a fresh `ToolsConfig` copying only `exec`, `web`, `file` and `restrict_to_workspace` from the parent config. `cli_apps` falls back to its default (`enable: true`), and `RunCliAppTool` is in the `subagent` scope (`_scopes = {"core", "subagent"}`), so it gets registered for subagents.

### Expected Behavior

**Expected**
Subagents should not get tools the operator disabled for the main agent. Suggested fix: also pass `cli_apps=self.tools_config.cli_apps` in `_subagent_tools_config()` (or derive the subagent config from the parent with `model_copy`, so future tool settings are inherited by default).

issues.title: Add Sprouts Data MCP preset (hosted Streamable HTTP, API key)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
### Problem / Motivation

Sprouts Data runs a hosted MCP server for B2B company and people data (search companies and people, find look-alike companies, look up records by domain / LinkedIn URL / ID, map relationships). Connecting it in nanobot today means building a custom MCP connection by hand. Similar services (Lusha, Hunter, Apollo.io, Clay) already have presets under Apps → MCP.


### Proposed Solution

Add an API-key preset in the crm category, following the existing Lusha preset:

```json
{
  "name": "sprouts_data",
  "display_name": "Sprouts Data",
  "category": "crm",
  "description": "Search companies and people, find look-alikes, and look up records.",
  "docs_url": "https://dashboard.sproutsdata.ai/docs",
  "transport": "streamableHttp",
  "install_supported": true,
  "brand_domain": "sproutsdata.ai",
  "server": {
    "type": "streamableHttp",
    "url": "https://dashboard.sproutsdata.ai/mcp",
    "tool_timeout": 60
  },
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "sprouts_api_key",
      "label": "Sprouts Data API key",
      "target": ["header", "X-API-Key"],
      "env_var": "SPROUTS_API_KEY",
      "placeholder": "Paste your token"
    }
  ],
  "requires": "Sprouts Data API key",
  "note": "Test keys (sk_dsp_test_) are charged 0 credits. Live keys use prepaid Sprouts credits."
}
```

Docs row for docs/mcp-presets.md (Hosted services):
| Sprouts Data | API key | [Official guide](https://dashboard.sproutsdata.ai/docs) |

brand_color is left out; happy to supply one if you need it.

### Alternatives Considered

Browser OAuth instead of an API key. The server also supports OAuth 2.1 with discovery and dynamic client registration (registration_endpoint in https://dashboard.sproutsdata.ai/authsvc/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server), so an "auth": "oauth" preset like Apollo.io's should also work. The API-key preset is the simpler option and matches Lusha.


### Related Component

Skills / Plugins

### Additional Context

- Transport: Streamable HTTP only, at https://dashboard.sproutsdata.ai/mcp. Nothing to install.
- Auth: API key in the X-API-Key header. The MCP server also accepts "Authorization: Bearer <key>".
- Keys are created in the Sprouts dashboard and carry scopes, so a key can be limited to the tools it needs.
- Free testing: test keys (sk_dsp_test_) search the same data and are charged 0 credits, and new workspaces get 1,000 free credits. A quick connection check is the free sprouts_coverage tool.
- 12 tools, including sprouts_search, sprouts_similar and sprouts_entity_lookup.

Disclosure: I work at Sprouts Inc. (doing business as Sprouts.ai), which runs Sprouts Data.

prs.title: feat(webui): inspect file context in a live graph sidebar
prs.body:
The context control opens a persistent file graph beside the conversation. Users can see files used since the latest compaction, open them in the shared preview sidebar, and replay the graph's growth without interrupting chat.

## Behavior

- Show supplied prompt files, explicit skills, successful text-file reads, and discovered local Markdown references. A loaded node records use during this phase; it does not claim that all of the original text remains in the current model request. File-size indicators estimate the content actually read.
- Start a new replay phase after successful compaction. The next actual request supplies the new graph; existing historical snapshots remain readable. Missing historical snapshots are not recreated from today's files.
- Support node dragging, zoom, click-to-open details, transient labels for newly loaded files, adaptive replay, and smooth whole-panel expansion. Share sidebar surfaces and transitions with file previews, keeping the composer usable in split panes and on narrow screens.
- Move preview/source controls into the file header and simplify related navigation and session panels.

## Ownership and compatibility

- A WebUI observer consumes the ordered tool progress stream. It parses successful `read_file` results in a worker, stores compact read facts in display history, and restores observations across turns and restarts. It never rereads source files or linked targets; parsing failures preserve tool results.
- Prompt builders record raw file-use facts in a turn-local capture scope. A composed observer publishes those facts at the prepared-request boundary, before request lifecycle events. Parsing and token estimation run in the delivery worker, outside model execution. Parallel turns and cancellation keep capture scopes isolated.
- The runner exposes a generic `before_model_request` hook and reports individual request usage separately from accumulated usage. It does not read graph metadata. `loop.py`, context governance, runtime context blocks, file-read tools, session message persistence, and memory consolidation have no changes against the PR base.
- Skill loading shares its existing discovery snapshot and records the resolved source, including aliases. Rebuilding prompt files does not multiply their token estimates. Tool working directories belong to individual progress records, rather than the surrounding batch.
- Successful compaction starts a new phase; failed compaction preserves observations. Shell-command file-read inference is out of scope.
- Optional graph wire fields and compressed, self-contained history records remain supported. Compact history responses retain the `webui.context-graph.references.v1` capability; ordinary inline responses remain supported. No database migration or history rewrite is required.
- Canvas rendering retains keyboard/touch access, reduced-motion support, and suspension while hidden.

## Validation

- Backend responsibility refactor at `64bf71076`: 226 passed, 1 Windows symlink-permission skip. Covers queued skill injection, skill aliases, concurrent capture and cancellation cleanup, request/recovery hooks, progress events, compaction, history recovery, parser failure, and ordered individual/batched delivery. After simplifying prompt deduplication, the affected source/observer/outbound subset passed again: 47 passed, the same skip.
- Python import boundaries, changed-file Ruff, focused BasedPyright on the runtime and observer modules, and diff whitespace checks passed. Expanding type checking to CLI entrypoints reports private-import and Typer typing diagnostics in untouched code; this is not a clean repository-wide type-check result.
- The local gateway was restarted and an existing conversation's five graph snapshots and Python-file node were checked through the dev UI. No model messages were added to the user's conversation for this check.
- Frontend files are unchanged in this refactor. Retained evidence from `ba95d8cb9`: 334 frontend tests, TypeScript, and touched-file lint passed. That evidence covers rendering, replay, sidebar transitions and the previous dead-code cleanup; it is not a fresh frontend run.
- An earlier expanded CLI test run encountered six API-serving failures because the available `aiohttp.web` lacks `RequestKey`. Current-head CI and final review remain required.

## Prior performance evidence

These measurements precede this backend simplification and are not a fresh benchmark of this commit. At `b6e9571be`, five alternating desktop Chromium runs with 300 messages and 50 ms stream updates measured closed-panel input P95 at 14.5 ms versus 14.4 ms on main `ce3aa50e7`. Main has no graph/replay feature: replay and graph-animation comparisons used earlier feature commit `15723f611`, not main. The faster 12-snapshot replay reflects changed playback cadence and is not a like-for-like throughput improvement. Cold unique Markdown analysis and persisted graph history still add work even when the panel is closed; this PR does not claim zero overhead.

Tracks [NAN-407](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-407).

## Why

DeepSeek Chat Completions can end with `insufficient_system_resource` or `aborted`. These interruptions were treated as successful completions, so a partial answer could be saved as a normal reply.

## What changed

- Propagate model errors through budget finalization and message delivery, preserving earlier completed length segments.
- Report structured model failures through the OpenAI-compatible API and Python SDK.

## Scope and tradeoffs

Successful Responses requests and ordinary Chat completions are unchanged. Interrupted output that was not streamed is not saved as a completed answer.

prs.title: fix(agent): drain parallel tools before finalizing cancelled runs
prs.body:
Cancelling a parallel tool batch could finish `AgentRunner` while sibling tools were still cleaning up. A cancellation raised by one tool, or a failing tool hook, could also leave siblings running after the run ended. This allows turn finalization and its caller's session-lock release to race outstanding tool work.

Keep ownership of every task in the batch and an explicit collecting task, then cancel and drain that work before propagating the original failure. The collector returns failures to its owner as values so Python 3.14's `shield` does not report a handled cancellation or late hook failure as a shielded-future error. Repeated stop requests cannot interrupt the drain, and successful results retain their input order. A tool that never completes cancellation cleanup can still delay cancellation; this does not force termination of uncooperative code.

Validation:

- All 22 runner tool tests pass separately on actual Python 3.11.17, 3.12.15, and 3.14.7. Regressions cover caller cancellation, repeated cancellation, tool-local cancellation, hook failure, a hook failure arriving during caller cancellation, cleanup before finalization, original exception identity, and loop exception-handler reports.
- Full Ruff, strict BasedPyright, import-boundary checks, and dependency consistency pass. The serial CLI partition has 252 passed / 1 skipped; channel delivery/setup and Feishu domain checks have 60 passed after installing the CI dependencies and isolating the instance directory.
- The broader Agent/session/portable-tool run has 3,538 passed / 8 skipped and one initial-exec-wait timing failure (`test_exec_path_prepend_takes_lookup_precedence`), which passes unchanged in isolation.
- The full main partition is **not green locally**: 10,196 passed / 115 skipped / 69 failed, then it was interrupted at WebSocket readiness. Of those 69 failed nodes, 67 also fail on unchanged `main` with the same environment and concurrency; two Feishu domain cases pass in isolated baseline runs. These failures span machine-proxy-dependent loopback tests, optional channel setup, native Seatbelt output expectations, and the macOS storage benchmark. The readiness hang also reproduces on unchanged `main` and passes when localhost is excluded from this machine's proxy settings. CI remains needed for the complete suite.

Its Python 3.14 coverage job had 11,069 passed / 79 skipped / 2 failed, with 84.96% coverage against the 75% gate; both failures were in the new caller-cancellation tests. prs.title: Checkpoint completed tool results at execution-batch boundaries
prs.body:
Closes #5747

## Problem

During a multi-tool response the durable runtime checkpoint only existed in two shapes: `awaiting_tools` with every call pending, and `tools_completed` with every call done. If tool A finished, tool B started and the gateway crashed before C ran, the checkpoint on disk still said all three were pending. Recovery then threw away A's real result and lost the evidence that a side-effecting tool had already run.

## Change

- `execute_tool_calls` takes an optional `on_batch_complete` callback. It is awaited after every execution batch that leaves further calls pending, with the `(tool_call, result)` pairs completed so far and the calls not started yet. The existing batching (`_partition_tool_batches`) defines the boundaries; nothing is reported after the last batch, the caller already owns that checkpoint.
- `AgentRunner` passes a callback that emits an `awaiting_tools` checkpoint at each boundary: `completed_tool_results` holds the finished calls' normalized tool messages (same builder as the final `tools_completed` payload, so the rows are identical), `pending_tool_calls` the rest. No `provider_state` is attached, so the partial shape is never treated as synchronized.
- `runtime_checkpoint_is_well_formed` accepts the partition for `awaiting_tools`: completed and pending ids must be disjoint, cover the assistant's tool-call ids exactly, contain no duplicates, and at least one call must still be pending (an all-completed turn is `tools_completed`). The legacy all-pending shape stays valid.
- `restore_runtime_checkpoint` needed no change: it already keeps completed rows and materializes `Error: Task interrupted before this tool finished.` rows for pending calls; the web UI still lands in `awaiting_user` / `tool_state_unknown` and never resumes the pending calls.

Invariant: `completed_ids ∪ pending_ids == assistant_tool_call_ids` and `completed_ids ∩ pending_ids == ∅`.

## Non-goals (as in the issue)

No automatic replay, no new ledger or scheduler, no exactly-once guarantee, no change to ordinary agent behaviour or public configuration.

## Tests

- `tests/agent/test_runner_tool_execution.py`
  - `test_tool_execution_reports_completed_batches_before_pending_work`: concurrent (`[read_a, read_b] | [write_a]`) yields one boundary with both reads completed and the write pending; sequential yields a boundary after each of the first two calls; never after the last batch.
  - `test_runner_checkpoints_each_completed_tool_batch`: checkpoint phases become `awaiting_tools (all pending) → awaiting_tools (A completed, B pending) → tools_completed → final_response`; the partial payload carries A's real result, shares the assistant message, and has no provider state.
- `tests/session/test_recovery.py`
  - `test_partially_completed_tools_keep_results_and_interrupt_the_rest`: after a restart A's saved result is kept, B becomes an interrupted result, recovery waits for confirmation, nothing is enqueued.
  - `test_partial_tool_checkpoint_partition_is_validated`: legacy shapes accepted; partition accepted; overlap, gaps, duplicates and an all-completed `awaiting_tools` rejected.

`tests/agent`, `tests/session`, `tests/webui`, `tests/channels` and `nanobot/channels`: 4464 passed locally (the 5 failures are the pre-existing Windows/no-Node ones). `ruff check` clean on the touched files.

prs.title: feat(recovery): persist completed tool results at execution-batch bou…
prs.body:
## Problem

When a model response contains multiple tool calls, the runtime checkpoint is
only written twice: before execution (`awaiting_tools`, all pending) and after
(`tools_completed`, all completed). If the gateway crashes in the middle of a
tool-execution batch, the durable checkpoint still records every call as
pending. On recovery, completed tools — including side-effecting ones — cannot
be distinguished from work that never ran, so they are marked "interrupted"
and the model may re-run them, repeating external side effects.

## Root cause

`execute_tool_calls` (nanobot/agent/tools/execution.py) runs tool batches
internally with no checkpoint emission between batches, so the only persisted
shapes are "all pending" / "all completed". `_runtime_checkpoint_is_well_formed`
(nanobot/session/recovery.py) mirrors that by accepting only those two shapes,
rejecting legitimate partial state.

## Solution

- **execution.py**: `execute_tool_calls` gains an optional `checkpoint_callback`.
  After each batch (concurrent gather or serial tool) it invokes the callback
  with the cumulative `completed_pairs` in stable result order. The serial
  branch now unpacks the `(result, event)` pair explicitly (behaviour
  unchanged).
- **runner.py**: a closure `_on_tool_batch_completed` normalizes each completed
  tool call into a tool-result row, keeps the remaining calls as pending,
  reuses the existing `_emit_checkpoint` path and writes an intermediate
  checkpoint at the batch boundary (phase stays `awaiting_tools`).
- **recovery.py**: the `awaiting_tools` well-formed check is relaxed from the
  all-or-nothing shape to the partition invariant `completed ∪ pending == all
  calls` and `completed ∩ pending == ∅`. Legacy all-pending checkpoints remain
  valid (`completed = ∅`).

## Tests

- `test_partial_checkpoint_partition_is_well_formed` — intermediate state
  (A completed, B/C pending) and the legacy all-pending shape both pass.
- `test_partial_checkpoint_bad_partition_rejected` (parametrized) — overlapping,
  missing, and duplicated partitions are rejected.
- `test_execute_tool_calls_emits_batch_checkpoint_callback` — one callback per
  batch, `completed_pairs` accumulated in call order.
- `test_execute_tool_calls_serial_mode_emits_callback_per_tool` — serial mode
  emits a callback after each tool.
- `test_execute_tool_calls_without_callback_keeps_previous_behavior` — no
  callback ⇒ identical results/events as before.
- `test_partial_checkpoint_restore_keeps_completed_and_marks_pending_interrupted`
  — integration: completed results are materialized as-is, pending ones become
  explicit interrupted tool results.

Full suite locally: 5973 passed, 19 failed. The 19 failures are pre-existing
baseline failures (verified by a revert-control experiment: reverting the two
source files to HEAD leaves them failing; they also fail on the upstream CI
checkout, e.g. `test_runner_reuses_edit_diff_for_summary_and_progress`), and
are unrelated to this change.

Reuse reported usage and measured streaming telemetry; snapshots contain cumulative usage and at most eight runner-visible rounds. Recovery requests update the current round, matching terminal aggregation rather than changing the chart when the turn closes.
- Reuse existing routed delivery and durable display history. Update active-turn usage independently of answer streaming; final snapshots replace rather than duplicate live statistics. Fence duplicate/stale events and reject late usage snapshots after Stop/end.
- Publish per-call tool start/result events, including rejected calls and cancellation, without duplicate batch-end results. This does not change background shell-process observation semantics or absorb the closed, unmerged #6524.
- Preserve context-meter invalidation after successful compaction until a newer request reports context usage.
- Keep protocol v1 compatible: new clients opt into model-request history via `include_model_requests=1`; default history omits the optional event for older clients, with separate ETags. Older hosts still provide end-of-task statistics. Other channels do not receive model-request UI traffic.

- Add opt-in daily Preview candidate preparation to the existing workflow. It stays disabled unless maintainers enable the repository variable. Require successful latest push CI for the exact source and skip an already accepted source/base pair.

- Preserve existing dispatch inputs, Preview numbering, five-platform acceptance and artifact-ID handoffs. Daily runs cannot replace pending manual runs.

## Boundary

This is the preparation step, not a complete automatic publisher. It creates no tags, GitHub Releases, PyPI uploads or catalogue updates. It does not change the signing workflow, client trust policy, repository variables or protection settings. Automatic Preview publication remains follow-up work. No release workflow was dispatched for this PR.

The existing five native runners, including macOS and Linux arm64, and temporary wheel transfers remain unchanged. Enabling daily preparation would incur those costs; it does not retain the optional large installable handoff. Daily preparation is disabled by default.

No application, configuration, session, package-layout or model-request behavior changes. Existing manual inputs remain supported. Website deployment and public channel announcements are outside this PR.

Exclude coverage 7.17.1 from the development extra. It crashes when combining an empty subprocess data file ([upstream report](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2356)). This blocked PR CI after all tests passed. A focused reproduction fails with 7.17.1 and passes with 7.17.0. No tests or coverage thresholds were removed.

## Verification

- 48 focused tests passed: planning and workflow contracts, candidate preparation, manifests and installation-guide regressions.
- A clean planning environment with only Pydantic and packaging ran the CLI against real repository history. A read-only check of the current main CI also passed; no candidate or publication workflow was dispatched.
- Actionlint 1.7.12 passed for the changed workflow (without ShellCheck). Ruff, focused BasedPyright and whitespace checks passed.
- Built a macOS arm64 test package from head `5f5fbc67de456a22a4957bb1b57ba2e160bb3b69`, using candidate `ec26de73d7782b690f4e6410662c1cb1bb5b354f` and private version `0.4.1.dev6557`. Its wheel SHA-256 is `258986eb5d357fa5fb9675f81e96bf0a37a8c95d8f7e27ba8b3216e2b6dad666`.
- Upgraded from the official 0.4.0 macOS arm64 wheel through its own WebUI Update button. The old page reported completion and reconnected to the new gateway. Four isolated test topics, canonical rows, display-only/canonical-only history, configuration bytes and a pending delivery record were preserved. Continued writes and a second gateway start passed.
- The packaged updater also passed a direct 0.4.0 upgrade and a two-step upgrade through a private intermediate Preview. The final target bytes were unchanged. The official baseline wheel SHA-256 matched GitHub and PyPI: `f86088a3cc768e5bc84998011a667f7ed6d1201b6dba51deaa831395bab52a4e`.
- These tests used disposable managed installs and private feed instrumentation in the historical baseline. Local unsigned fixtures do not prove public download or signature acceptance. No user installation or data was used. No release was published. Other native platforms rely on their separate CI evidence, not the macOS test.
- Current-head [CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/41780049091) passed all 15 checks, including Windows compatibility, browser tests and Linux/Windows native package acceptance. Python 3.14 completed with 86% coverage. The tested merge commit contains the current main tip and this PR head.

issues.title: [Bug]: `hermes fallback add` stores a custom endpoint's fallback entry without any credential pointer → 401 (no-key-required)

labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: area/auth
labels.description: Authentication, OAuth, credential pools

labels.name: area/config

issues.body:
### Bug Description

`hermes fallback add`, picking a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint that has a
valid API key, produces a chain that always fails with `401` when it activates:
the provider receives the `no-key-required` placeholder instead of the real key.

Expected: the fallback entry carries (or references) the endpoint's credential,
like the primary `model:` config does after setup.


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`hermes model` → custom), with
   a valid API key. Hermes saves the key to `.env` as
   `HERMES_CUSTOM_API_<HOST>_API_KEY` and sets
   `model.api_key: ${HERMES_CUSTOM_API_<HOST>_API_KEY}`.
2. Run `hermes fallback add`, pick that endpoint, choose a model.
3. Inspect `fallback_providers` in `config.yaml`: the entry has `provider:
   custom`, `model`, `base_url`, `api_mode` — and no `api_key` / `key_env`.
4. Trigger a fallback (primary 4xx). The endpoint replies 401; gateway logs show
   `Token is invalid.` while the same key sent manually (same request shape:
   stream + tools) returns 200.


### Expected Behavior

The stored fallback entry resolves to the endpoint's real API key, so the
fallback request authenticates successfully.


### Actual Behavior

`resolve_entry_api_key(entry)` returns `None` (the entry has no `api_key` /
`key_env`). `resolve_runtime_provider(requested="custom",
explicit_base_url=<endpoint>)` then falls through to the direct-alias rung,
which supplies the literal `no-key-required` placeholder (verified: the
resolved key is exactly 15 chars). The request goes out as
`Authorization: Bearer *** → 401.


### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
omitted on request
```

### Operating System

macOS 26.6.2

### Python Version

3.14.7

### Hermes Version

v0.21.4+canary.20261002T070111Z-97-g0a374d167

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
Gateway log excerpt (SiliconFlow as the fallback target):

Streaming failed before delivery: Error code: 401 - {'code': 30014, 'message':
'Token is invalid.'}
WARNING agent.conversation_loop: API call failed ... provider=custom
base_url=https://api.siliconflow.cn/v1/ model=zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash summary=HTTP 401
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`hermes_cli/fallback_cmd.py::_extract_fallback_from_model_cfg()` copies only
`provider`, `model`, `base_url` and `api_mode` from the post-picker `model`
snapshot. `hermes_cli/model_setup_flows_custom.py::_apply_endpoint()` had
recorded the credential as `model.api_key =
"${HERMES_CUSTOM_API_<HOST>_API_KEY}"` — that pointer is dropped on the way
into `fallback_providers`, so `resolve_entry_api_key()` finds nothing.

Not covered by #71519/#71533 or #43586/#43675:
- #71533 resolves named-provider metadata via
  `_get_named_custom_provider(entry["provider"])` and copies only
  base_url/api_mode. For our entry `provider` is the bare `custom`, and
  `_get_named_custom_provider("custom")` returns `None` (entries match by
  `name`); credentials are never copied in any case.
- #43675 makes the direct-alias rung read `key_env`/`api_key` from the
  **`model:` block** — but the `model:` block here is the primary endpoint and
  has neither, so the lookup stays empty while the fallback targets a
  different endpoint.


### Proposed Fix (optional)

Carry the credential pointer into the entry: copy `api_key` / `key_env` from
the post-picker model snapshot in `_extract_fallback_from_model_cfg()` (or
persist the named custom provider identity so the chain entry resolves through
`custom_providers` the way the primary does).


### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

issues.body:
Summary

hermes profile rename <old> <new> migrates the renamed profile's sessions
rows (session key, profile_name, heartbeats, delivery + routing index — see
_migrate_profile_identity in hermes_cli/profile_identity.py), but the two
state_meta row families the LOCAL session identity fences validate are not
migrated as a set. After a rename, opening the profile's "Bot Chat" from the
desktop app fails, and the bot's forever-chat registry stays wedged until the
rows are rewritten by hand.

Symptoms (observed on a multiplexed gateway, v0.22.5)

Desktop, opening any renamed profile's chat:



Could not check 's Bot Chat registry (profile_mismatch) — not starting a new chat





profile_mismatch — owned_receipt() (gateway/session_local_recovery.py:114)
requires receipt['profile_id'] == authority.profile_id; the stored receipt
(state_meta, key gateway.local_policy.v1:<sid>) still carries the old
profile home, old entry.session_key (agent:<old>:local:dm:<sid>) and old
entry.origin.profile.



storage_unavailable (unlogged) — legacy_lineage_root()
(hermes_state_local_migration.py:90) requires a receipt that carries
legacy_session_id to have a companion state_meta row under
gateway.local_legacy.v1:<legacy_session_id> whose JSON equals
{session_id, profile_id, principal_id, legacy_session_id}. A mismatch here
refuses with storage_unavailable and writes no line to gateway.log —
in our incident the refusal only became visible through the desktop error
string, not the logs.

Repro





Multiplexed gateway; a secondary profile (any name) with at least one local
 session (open its Bot Chat once from the desktop app).



hermes profile rename <old> <new> from a shell; the gateway re-adopts the
 profile.



Desktop app → open the renamed bot's chat.



The registry check is refused (profile_mismatch / storage_unavailable);
 the bot is unusable from the app, because every open re-runs the check.

Where





gateway/session_local_recovery.py — owned_receipt(): profile / identity /
entry checks over the stored receipt. Note the identity check: without
legacy_session_id, chat_id is recomputed as
local_identity(profile_id, principal_id, request_id) — so a plain
profile_id rewrite on a local-… hash-format session id breaks the
sid == chat_id invariant; the field must be pinned.



hermes_state_local_migration.py — legacy_lineage_root(): the
receipt-vs-marker equality check.



hermes_cli/profile_identity.py — _migrate_profile_identity(): migrates
session keys, profile_name, heartbeats, delivery + routing index; the
state_meta receipt/marker families are not covered as a set.



hermes_cli/sessions_repair_profiles.py — hermes sessions repair-profiles
documents six crossing kinds; none covers state_meta rows, so the official
repairer does not settle this damage either.

Observed state after rename (our incident, four profiles)





The gateway.local_policy.v1: receipt rows still carried the old identity
(home, session key, origin profile).



The gateway.local_legacy.v1: marker rows, where present, carried the new
identity — the two families disagreed.



One hash-format receipt (local-… session id) had no marker row at all
(receipts without legacy_session_id never get one written), so pinning
legacy_session_id on it requires the marker to be created.

Suggested fix

In the rename migration (and/or repair-profiles), for every
gateway.local_policy.v1:<sid> receipt in the renamed profile's store whose
profile_id / entry.session_key / entry.origin.profile still name the old
profile:





rewrite profile_id to the new home (same prefix, new name segment),
route and entry.session_key to the migrated session key, and
entry.origin.profile to the new profile name;



for receipts without legacy_session_id whose session_id is a local-…
hash, add legacy_session_id = session_id so the identity check keeps the
stored hash;



ensure the companion gateway.local_legacy.v1:<legacy_session_id> marker
row exists and carries the same four fields as the receipt (create it from
the receipt when absent, migrate it when stale).

Workaround applied (for reference)

Hand-rewrote 10 stale receipt rows and created 1 missing marker row across
four renamed profile stores (sqlite, WAL-safe, with sqlite3 .backup
snapshots taken first). Afterwards session.list with title "Bot Chat"
resolves for all six served profiles again, verified live (no gateway restart
required — the rows are read live per request).

Environment





Hermes Agent v0.22.5+2429.g780d5a3 (2026.9.24), Linux x86_64



Multiplexed gateway serving six profiles; no messaging platforms enabled
(desktop app only)

issues.title: [Bug]: `hermes profile describe default` resolves to the active profile in multi-profile installs (silently overwrites its description)
issues.body:
**Summary**

In a multi-profile install, `hermes profile describe default` resolves `default` to the **currently active** profile instead of the install root. Both the read and the `--text` write land on the caller's own `profile.yaml`, so `--text` silently overwrites the active profile's description.

**Root cause**

`hermes_cli/profile_cmd.py:302-309`:

```python
def _describe_target_dir(name: str) -> Path:
    """Profile dir for ``describe``: ``default`` maps to the CURRENT home (get_hermes_home),
    everything else to its named directory."""
    from hermes_cli import profiles as _profiles_mod
    if _profiles_mod.normalize_profile_name(name) == "default":
        from hermes_constants import get_hermes_home as _hh
        return Path(_hh())
    return _profiles_mod.get_profile_dir(name)
```

Under a multiplexed gateway `get_hermes_home()` is `~/.hermes/profiles/<active>`, so `default` maps to whichever profile the calling session belongs to. The write path reuses the same helper (`hermes_cli/profile_cmd.py:348`), so the correction also goes to the wrong file.

**Repro** — v0.22.7 (b200f5bc60e3), macOS, multiplexed gateway serving 7 profiles

1. From a session hosted by profile `coach`:

```
$ hermes profile describe default
Hermes 教练：教 Ryan 用 Hermes 的机制…          ← coach's description, not default's
```

2. Write a description for `default`:

```
$ hermes profile describe default --text "cross-domain orchestration: nightly digest, batch scheduling"
Description updated for 'default'.
```

…but the text lands in `~/.hermes/profiles/coach/profile.yaml`, and `~/.hermes/profile.yaml` is never created.

3. `hermes profile describe coach` now returns the text that was meant for `default` — the coach description is gone with no warning.

**Expected**

`default` should resolve to the install root `~/.hermes`. That is exactly what the metadata reader already does: `read_profile_meta(Path("~/.hermes"))` returns the contents of `~/.hermes/profile.yaml` correctly. Only the CLI helper disagrees with the reader, so the roster/UI shows one value while `describe` writes another.

**Impact**

Silent clobbering of an unrelated profile's description in any multi-profile install where someone runs `describe default` from a satellite profile's session. The only feedback is `Description updated for 'default'.`

**Workaround**

Edit `~/.hermes/profile.yaml` directly; `read_profile_meta` picks it up and the Bot roster renders it. Non-default profiles are unaffected — `describe <name>` read/write both work correctly for them.

issues.title: [Bug]: state.db: some in-process opens bypass connect_tracked, so has_live_connection() can't see them
issues.body:
### Bug Description

A few places open `state.db` with a raw `sqlite3.connect` instead of `connect_tracked`. Those connections are invisible to the tracked-connection registry in `hermes_cli/sqlite_safe_read.py`. This matters because 13 production call sites (6 of `has_live_connection()`, 7 of `offline_file_access()`) rely on that registry to decide when raw file I/O on a live database is safe. An untracked connection is a live holder those checks can't see. That's the gap #100519 and the howtocorrupt §2.2 work closed for every other connection. I'd like to route the remaining in-process opens through `connect_tracked` and add a check so new ones can't appear.

This is a gap in a safety mechanism found by reading the code, not a reproduced failure.

### Steps to Reproduce

Found by audit, not observed at runtime. To see the gap directly:

1. In one process, open a reader the way `gateway/readiness.py` does: `sqlite3.connect(read_only_db_uri(db), uri=True)`.
2. While it is open, call `hermes_cli.sqlite_safe_read.has_live_connection(db)`.

### Expected Behavior

`True`: a connection on the file is open, so raw byte I/O on it is not safe.

### Actual Behavior

`False`, so `offline_file_access` lets a raw open()/close() proceed while that reader holds POSIX locks on the file.

Output on v0.22.7 (`b200f5bc`), running the steps above and then the real `gateway/readiness._probe_state_db`, checking `has_live_connection` while its connection is open:

```
steps: raw reader open, has_live_connection = False
readiness probe: has_live_connection while open = [False]
```

`gateway/readiness.py` and `hermes_cli/sqlite_safe_read.py` are unchanged on `main` at `cb11094936`.

### Affected Component

Other

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Not attached: this is a code-level gap found by audit, so runtime logs don't show it. File and line references are under Root Cause.
```

### Operating System

Debian 13 (trixie) container on Talos Linux (kernel 6.18), Docker image

### Python Version

3.14.9

### Hermes Version

v0.22.7 (2026.9.24), upstream b200f5bc

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

When a raw read guarded by `offline_file_access` closes its descriptor while an untracked connection on the same file is open, that connection's POSIX locks are cancelled mid-read. Another process can then checkpoint or reset the WAL underneath it, so the reader sees inconsistent data. That doesn't corrupt the database: these openers are read-only. But two of them feed decisions:

- [`tools/tool_result_storage.referenced_spillover_names`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/785c2e5110eb3fbfc5346fd8370ca96910aaa1f3/tools/tool_result_storage.py#L100-L125) decides which spilled tool-result files are still referenced. A wrong but successful read could let cleanup delete files a session still points to. (A failed read is already handled: it fails closed.)
- [`hermes_state_repair.state_db_has_structural_damage`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/785c2e5110eb3fbfc5346fd8370ca96910aaa1f3/hermes_state_repair.py#L745-L765) runs `integrity_check`. A torn read could report damage that isn't there, which feeds into the repair logic.

A third case is not an untracked connection but the same hazard. [`tools/read_extract._extract_sqlite`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/785c2e5110eb3fbfc5346fd8370ca96910aaa1f3/tools/read_extract.py#L566-L576), the `read_file` tool's `.db` extractor, does a raw `open()`/`read()`/`close()` to check the magic bytes. When the agent reads its own `state.db` in the gateway, that close cancels the live writer's locks: the howtocorrupt §2.2 route #100519 closed on the write path. It should go through `read_header_bytes_preopen`.

The first two are rare: the window has to line up with another process's WAL activity. I haven't seen either happen.

Two more effects of the gap:

- The fd monitoring in #96152 counts connections through the same registry, so untracked connections aren't counted. That's the question raised on #96027 about whether per-profile handles are covered.
- #149274 (header-probe fd release) closes a probe only once no other descriptor holds the inode, and it uses `offline_file_access` for tracked connections. An untracked connection that opens in the microseconds between its fd scan and the close is the one case it can't cover.

Read against `main` at `785c2e5110`.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

1. Switch the in-process raw `state.db` opens to `connect_tracked(..., tracking_path=<db>)`, keeping their read-only URIs and timeouts, and route the `read_file` magic check through `read_header_bytes_preopen`. An audit of `main` found these in-process sites: gateway readiness, the lifecycle ledger's integrity and journal-mode reads, the API server response store, the spillover scan, install state, doctor (which also runs in the dashboard console), the repair damage check, shared metrics, and the worktree liveness reads in `hermes_cli/worktree_ops.py` (`_tree_still_served`, `_retained_tree_is_live`), which cron's worktree sweep runs inside the gateway.
2. Audit the other raw `sqlite3.connect` calls that can target a `state.db`. Most are in CLI commands that run in their own process (doctor, backup, recovery, journal-mode), where an untracked connection can't affect the gateway. Code under `hermes_cli/` isn't automatically CLI-only, though: the worktree reads above are reached from both `cli.py` and the gateway's cron sweep, so each site needs its callers traced. They're still worth converting where it's cheap, because the CLI also runs byte probes. List any that are deliberately left raw (offline snapshots, scratch copies) with the reason.
3. Add a code-health rule in `scripts/code_health/` that flags a raw `sqlite3.connect` whose target is a `state.db` path, with the usual `# health: allow <RULE> -- <why>` waiver for offline files. The repo already uses this kind of rule for similar hazards, and it keeps the gap from reopening. Being a heuristic, it would start advisory (`WARN_UNTIL_REPLAYED`).

I have a PR ready for 1 and 3 that also does the audit in 2.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

prs.title: fix(gateway): a stale approval card no longer approves the next request (Telegram, Slack, Feishu, Matrix, WhatsApp Cloud, Teams, relay)
prs.body:
When a dangerous command needs your OK, Hermes posts a card with Approve/Deny buttons. If that request ended some other way (it timed out, or you typed `/approve`) and a second request is waiting in the same chat, pressing the old card's button used to answer the second request, which you hadn't seen yet. Now each card answers only its own request.

**Outcome:** on Telegram, Slack, Feishu, Matrix, WhatsApp Cloud, Teams and the relay connector, a press on a card whose request has already settled reports "expired" and resolves nothing. The next pending approval stays pending until you answer its own card.

**Scope against the unified gateway work on main (re-checked as Teknium asked):** main already carries part of this. `cfed2ca71ff` added `ExecApprovalPrompt.request_id`, and the runner (`gateway/run_turn_runner.py`) passes it. Discord's `ExecApprovalView` binds to it (`4f86e97791f`, `50f57a131fd`). Every other native-button adapter still called `resolve_gateway_approval(session_key, choice)`, which resolves FIFO. This PR is now cut down to those adapters; the old `gateway/run.py` metadata tunnel and the Discord hunk are gone.

- `tools/approval.py`: `resolve_gateway_approval_card(session_key, choice, request_id)` targets only that request when an id is present. Without an id it falls back to FIFO, so cards sent by an older runner still work.
- Each adapter stores `prompt.request_id` next to its existing card state and resolves through the new helper:
  - Telegram: `_approval_request_ids` by approval id.
  - Slack: `_approval_request_ids` under the same key as the double-click guard.
  - Feishu: the approval state dict.
  - Matrix: a `_MatrixApprovalPrompt.request_id` field.
  - WhatsApp Cloud: a bounded map.
  - Teams: the button data.
  - Relay: the minted prompt state.
- Teams: a click that resolves nothing now shows the expired card instead of a false "approved".
- Not covered: QQ Bot. Its `approve:<session_key>:<decision>` button data is pinned byte-for-byte by `tests/gateway/test_qqbot.py`, so adding the id there means changing that contract. It still resolves FIFO.

**Before / after.** Live probe of the real `TelegramAdapter` against the real `tools.approval` blocking wait on agent threads. Request A is answered by typed `/approve`, request B is then raised, and the user presses A's stale card with "always":

| | main `71736c9f325` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| stale card A press | `✅ Approved permanently` | `⌛ Approval expired` |
| request B after that press | resolved, `choice: 'always'` (never shown to the user) | still pending |
| card B press (deny) | n/a | `❌ Denied`, B resolved `deny` |

Tests: `tests/gateway/test_approval_card_request_binding.py` drives send → press through Telegram, Slack and Feishu against a real queued approval. The stale-card cases fail on main's adapters (3 of 3) and pass here; the own-card controls pass on both. The touched approval suites (13 files, 226 tests) pass, and no main test was edited.

## Infographic
Infographic generation attempted with the configured style (`ukiyo-e`, `bento-grid`) but FAL returned `Exhausted balance`; no generated image is attached.

prs.title: fix(aux): auxiliary retry, fallback and refresh decisions come from the shared error classifier (C2)
prs.body:
> **Plan stage C2 (Code Health plan v0.12, lane C, step C2.2): merges after all of stage C1 has landed.** Opened now for review.

## What changes for users

Auxiliary model calls (compression summaries, titles, vision, session search, MCP and approval helpers) now make their retry, fallback, credential-refresh and key-rotation decisions from the same error classifier the main loop uses. Before this PR the auxiliary client kept its own private keyword checks, which disagreed with the main loop in dozens of cases:

- A 503, a 404 "model not found" or a plugin-reclassified error now falls back to the next auxiliary provider after retries, where the call used to re-raise.
- Plugin `transform_api_error_classification` hooks and provider-profile `classify_api_error` hooks now steer auxiliary calls too (they used to be bypassed).
- A failure after a 401 credential refresh (timeout, malformed answer, stream error) is classified as itself, so a freshly refreshed key is no longer benched as a "stale credential".
- Classification uses the backend the request actually reached (provider, model, endpoint, credential), including fallback candidates and async clients.
- OpenCode Go keeps the key on a per-model upstream 429 instead of benching it (salvaged from #140713 by @TurgutKural, authorship kept).

## What changed in code

| Commit | Change |
|---|---|
| `fix(agent)` | #140713 salvage: OpenCode Go per-model upstream 429 keeps the key |
| `fix(classifier)` | `agent/error_classifier.py` absorbs the auxiliary-only phrasings that were already on main; adds shape facts (`rejects_parameter`, route-level model rejection, transport kind); fixes a few main-loop phrasings (404 free tier, 403 quota/subscription, xAI expired OAuth, status-less account wording, Bedrock botocore status) |
| `fix(aux)` | each failed auxiliary request is classified once, with the route the recovery ladder already holds; every retry/fallback/refresh step reads that verdict through a few pure functions in `agent/auxiliary_error_policy.py` (97 lines). Recovery runs after the `except` block, so a retry's failure is classified on its own. All private predicates, keyword tables, `_FALLBACK_REASONS` and `agent/auxiliary_error_shapes.py` are deleted |
| `feat(code-health)` | HX014 ratchet: no new private API-error predicates in `agent/auxiliary*.py`, `agent/context_compressor*.py`, `agent/turn_*.py` (56 hits on main, 23 on this branch, 0 in the aux modules) |

Size: +709 / -655 non-test lines; +561 / -223 test lines (+1,270 / -878 total).

## Deliberate behaviour changes

All were approved before the build; each has a test:

- Transient failures (5xx, 408, connection, DNS, refused) and overload retry the same provider, then fall back.
- A 429 `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` is a rate limit unless it names a daily or weekly window, which makes it billing.
- An account-scoped "model X is not supported for this account" rotates the key for that model only. Feature wording ("Streaming / Image input / Tool use is not supported ...") falls back as "model incompatible" without rotating.
- A 400 that names a request parameter, with no parameter-repair step left, re-raises; if a repair step already ran, it falls back.
- A 429 that says "rate limit" and also names a billing phrase stays a rate limit (main's existing rule).
- A 404 "model not found (free tier)" falls back as a missing model.
- A plugin or profile verdict of `retryable=False` skips the same-provider retry, as the main loop already does. This includes the main loop's own stale-attempt abort.
- A plugin or profile verdict with `should_fallback=False` blocks provider fallback, and `retryable=False` skips the same-key rate-limit retry.
- An interrupted call (`InterruptedError`) stops at once: no retry, no fallback (as on `main`).
- A missing or refused model on a fallback candidate is quarantined for that model only; other models on the same provider stay eligible. Auxiliary pool selection passes the requested model, so a per-model credential cooldown does not hide a key from its other models.
- A verdict that is neither retryable nor allowed to fall back (a data-policy refusal, malformed tool-call arguments) stops the call, even after a parameter repair, so the same content is never resent to another provider.
- Each failed auxiliary request is classified once: plugin and provider classification hooks fire once per failed request.
- The main loop's chained-exception handling is unchanged from `main`; only the auxiliary ladder moved out of its `except` block.
- Not salvaged: #136211, a separate entitlement feature that only overlaps a fragment of this change.

## How it was verified

- `tests/agent/test_auxiliary_error_policy.py`: one behaviour table (every deliberate change above, run through `call_llm`) plus end-to-end regressions: 503/404 fallback, a failure after a 401 refresh does not bench the refreshed key, `retryable=False` honoured, 429-then-403 re-raises the 403, OpenCode Go classified under its concrete provider (sync and async), TLS failure keeps compression's session-preserving abort. Each fails on `main`.
- During development the branch was checked against a 784-row corpus of harvested and synthetic provider errors: auxiliary decisions matched the approved table on every row, and the main loop's classification differs from `main` only on the approved phrasings. The corpus is not committed.
- Every commit passes its targeted tests on its own; the test map over every file touching these modules shows no failure specific to this branch.

## Known follow-ups (not in this PR)

- A bare re-wrap of a 429 with nothing of its own loses the status.
- HX014 does not see predicates written inside `except` blocks.
- Telemetry classifies an HTTP-200 embedded error separately from the ladder's verdict.
- Auxiliary route labels could become a `StrEnum`.

Tracker: #144268

prs.title: fix(agent): intent-ack continuation dies after a session's first tool call (salvage #69779)
prs.body:
Intent-ack continuation (the bounded "you announced an action but called no tool — continue" nudge) works again after the first tool call of a session. Before this, the guard stopped firing for the rest of any session that had ever run a tool, in the gateway, CLI and resumed sessions.

Who sees it: anyone with `agent.intent_ack_continuation: true`, plus default (`auto`) users on the codex_responses API mode, where `auto` already resolves to `codex_only`. Chat-completions users on `auto` see no change. The nudge stays capped at 2 per turn and fires only on a short reply that names workspace work and makes no tool call.

Salvage of #69779 by @ClaySecAI. This keeps only the root-cause atom (current-turn scoping of the prior-tool gate, from their commit `cb7313d9e7f`), credited as the commit author.

Fixes #69778

## Root cause
`looks_like_codex_intermediate_ack` returned `False` when any row in `messages` had `role == "tool"`. The turn loop passes the whole session history there, so a tool call from any earlier turn disabled the guard (`agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`, first line of the detector). What the gate was meant to check (since `ce175d73722`) is that the model hasn't acted yet *this turn*. It now calls `tool_results_this_turn()`, the same window the degenerate-final guard already uses. If a tool ran in the current turn, the turn still ends on the text, so codex_only behaviour inside a turn is unchanged.

## Live A/B (real `AIAgent`, Nous `~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest`, `intent_ack_continuation: true`)
The model is told to reply "I'll run the command now." with no tool call on a new task. History holds one completed `terminal` tool turn.

| leg | earlier tool turn in history | nudges | tool rows this turn | final |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| origin/main (×2) | yes | 0 | 0 | `I'll run the command now.` (stalled) |
| origin/main (control) | no | 1 | 1 | `Output: intentack-ok` |
| this PR (×2) | yes | 1 | 1 | `Output: intentack-ok` |

The history prefix was byte-identical after the turn on every leg. The nudge is appended, never inserted into past context, so the cached prefix is unchanged. No new nudge path, no config change, and the max-2 continuation cap is unchanged.

## Tests
- `test_earlier_turn_tool_rows_do_not_disable_the_guard`: red on origin/main, green here.
- `test_tool_rows_in_the_current_turn_still_end_it`: control, so the same-turn gate is kept.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` on `test_intent_ack_continuation`, `test_verification_continuation_budget`, `test_degenerate_final_recovery`, `test_reply_line_before_silence`, `test_profile_declared_core_sets`: 76 passed, 0 failed. This ran from a tree copy outside `~/.hermes`, because the home-I/O guard trips on the worktree's `.git` path.
- `python scripts/check --only health`: ok.

## Not included from #69779 (and why)
- **Vocabulary widening, the governed-announcement grammar and colon-ended acks:** a detector rewrite of about 600 lines. It adds new false-positive classes that the review thread kept finding round after round (decline, scope change, deferred-report, clarification). It can come back as its own PR with its own evidence.
- **Opted-in "all" mode continuing *after* a tool ran this turn:** this would change an existing `origin/main` contract (`test_does_not_fire_after_a_tool_already_ran`, later pruned). It also overlaps the stall guard (`trailing_continue_intent`), which already covers "did work, announced the next step, stopped" when the reply ends on `let me now`/`I'll now`.
- **Answered-clarification recovery (#117240 graft):** this is a separate feature with its own risk surface.

prs.title: feat(context-engine): resolve compaction authority under checkpoint_required and hand engines the memory manager
prs.body:
## Infographic

![No compaction skips memory. Before: Engine init: compacts unchecked; Prune: no checkpoint first; Subagent: dies at compaction; Engine archive: no memory manager. After: Engine init: refused at init; Prune: held for checkpoint; Subagent: keeps the provider; Engine archive: gets the manager. Change: compacts_outside_compress, memory_manager.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6c35e3ed-1ac4-408a-a9e2-bf7e5be8c32e)

## What does this PR do?

With `compression.checkpoint_required` armed (#94639), lossy compaction could still skip the memory checkpoint:
- a plugin context engine could compact outside `compress()`;
- the proactive prune dropped tool results with no checkpoint first;
- delegated subagents died at their first compaction.

Separately, an engine that drops messages on its own had no way to reach the memory providers. This PR salvages the two outside PRs that fix these:

- **#94983 by @GottZ**: `compacts_outside_compress` on `ContextEngine`; the host refuses at init an engine it can't intercept, suppresses the prune and `on_turn_complete()` under the gate, and lets forks keep the memory provider.
- **#147997 by @John-MiracleWorker**: `on_session_start()` carries `memory_manager`.

Their 14 commits are cherry-picked with `-x`, so each keeps its author. The picked tree equals #94983's head merged onto `main`. A rebase or merge commit keeps those authors on their commits; a squash keeps them as co-authors. My commits on top finish the changes requested in the #147997 review and fix what Greptile found.

Points to review:
- `37f6abfb17`: Desktop/TUI `/compress` handed the engine `None` instead of the manager.
- `4b167ae4a2`: the docs make the handle best effort and not a checkpoint, so it doesn't change the `compacts_outside_compress` answer. That closes the gap between the two PRs.
- `5205df0c4c`: `memory_manager` goes only to an `on_session_start` that accepts it (by name or `**kwargs`), as `compress()` already does for `memory_context`. Before it, an engine with a narrow signature hit a swallowed `TypeError` and silently missed every session start.
- `0dc5b665c1`: under `plugins.isolation: host` every engine method is a proxy, so the `__func__` identity check read the inherited prune no-op as an override and the gate counted a withheld prune every tool iteration. The plugin host now reports the class that defines each method at load. The init check still refuses an undeclared hosted engine.
- `c64e1b5ec0` reverts `7e169c90b3`, which used the same load-time report to skip per-turn hooks: a hook a hosted engine installs after load would never run. Hosted engines are dispatched every turn, as on `main`.
- Left for follow-ups: the `run_agent.py` session-transition `on_session_start` site, and shutting down a refused engine.

## Related Issue

Carries #94983 and #147997 (both stay open); follows up #94639.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## How to Test

```
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_context_engine_compaction_authority.py \
  tests/agent/test_proactive_prune_checkpoint_gate.py tests/agent/test_fork_memory_under_checkpoint_gate.py \
  tests/agent/test_memory_manager_fork_scope.py tests/agent/test_context_engine_memory_manager_handoff.py \
  tests/agent/test_compression_boundary_hook.py tests/gateway/test_session_mutation_compress_plugin_engine.py
```

I tested on Linux arm64 at `c64e1b5ec0`:
- 262 related test files (including every plugin-host test), plus `scripts/check`.
- The gateway test's resident-agent case fails before `37f6abfb17`.
- Dropping the kwarg at any one agent-side call site fails that site's own test.
- A narrow-signature engine misses its session start on `4b167ae4a2` and gets every one on `main` and on `5205df0c4c`; making any one site unconditional again fails that site's assert.
- The only failures fail the same way on `origin/main`: the `acp` and `aiohttp` extras are missing here, and `test_journey_compress_restart_fifo.py` fails on `main` too.

I didn't run the full suite.

prs.title: fix(gemini): a safety-blocked prompt surfaces as a content-policy error instead of a silent empty turn
prs.body:
When Gemini refuses a prompt on safety grounds, it answers "OK" with no reply inside, and Hermes showed the user nothing at all. Now Hermes says the prompt was blocked, why, and moves to the fallback model instead of retrying the same refused prompt.

**Outcome:** a Gemini prompt-level block (`promptFeedback.blockReason`, HTTP 200, zero candidates) is a terminal `content_policy_blocked` error on both the unary and streaming paths, instead of an empty "stop" turn.

- `agent/gemini_native_adapter.py`: `raise_on_prompt_block()` runs first in `translate_gemini_response` and `translate_stream_event`; it raises `GeminiAPIError(code="gemini_prompt_blocked")` with Vertex's `blockReasonMessage` when present, else per-reason guidance (PROHIBITED_CONTENT, SAFETY, BLOCKLIST, IMAGE_SAFETY; others get generic guidance). No HTTP status is synthesized: the wire said 200.
- `agent/error_classifier.py`: matched on the structured error code (walks the cause chain), not message text, and routed to the existing content-policy verdict (no retry, fallback-eligible).
- `agent/context_compressor.py`: a content-policy block of the compression summary request is the refusal class, so `compress()` aborts with the transcript intact rather than committing the lossy fallback summary.
- `tests/e2e/core/providers/test_native_gemini_errors.py`: the #121317 `known_failure` entry is removed; the cell now fails on main's code (`re-sent 9x`) and passes here.
- Tests: the real `GeminiNativeClient` over a stubbed transport answering 200 + blockReason, unary and SSE, classified end to end; plus the control (promptFeedback without blockReason keeps the empty-turn shape). Red on `origin/main`, green here.

| Input | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `{"promptFeedback":{"blockReason":"PROHIBITED_CONTENT"}}` | silent empty turn (no error) | `content_policy_blocked`, retry=False, fallback=True |
| Gemini blocks the compression summary request | aborted, all 12 messages kept | aborted, all 12 messages kept (the PR head before the fix dropped 7) |
| Live control: real Gemini call, `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, unary + stream | `pong` | `pong` (unchanged) |

Real output of the classifier probe and the live control call; a real blocked prompt was not provoked.

Fixes #121317

## Infographic

![Gemini safety blocks: no more silent turns](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab12411/c2ZGoN8arcJgzfYO5gINX_IV9mGVgG.png)

prs.title: Desktop: MCP consent card shows the command or URL each server will run or contact
prs.body:
When the agent asks to install, enable or authorize an MCP server, the Desktop card used to show only the server's name. Now each row also says what approving will actually run (`Runs: npx -y …`) or contact (`Connects to: https://…`), with values whose own name marks them secret masked.

## Outcome

The `manage_connections` MCP consent card names the command line or URL under each row before the user clicks Install / Enable / Authorize. The line disappears once the row resolves.

**Governing rule:** the card exists so the user consents to what will run, so hiding execution is worse than showing a secret. The line is never cut, and only name-identified secrets are masked.

- **Backend builds the line** (`tools/connectors/mcp_launch.py`): install reads the catalog manifest's transport; enable/authorize read the configured `mcp_servers` entry. It rides on each MCP target in `connection.request` as `launch: {kind: stdio|remote, target, env?, cwd?}` (gateway contract + generated TS updated). `env` holds only the names of the env vars the entry adds (values never leave the process); `cwd` is the configured working directory. A string `args` value counts as one argument. The model's tool result drops the field.
- **Never truncated:** the full command is always on the line, however long.
- **Masked only by name:** long flags whose name says secret (`--token`, `--api-key`/`--apiKey`/`--api_key`, `--password`/`--passwd`/`--pass`, `--client-secret`, `--auth`, `--credentials`, `--private-key`, `--bearer`; spaced, `=` and `:` forms). Location/mode names are never masked (`--token-file`, `--key-file`, `--password-stdin`, `--auth-type`), and neither are lookalikes (`--author`, `--keymap`, `--max-tokens`, `--tokenizer`). Also masked: `KEY=VALUE` args where KEY names a secret (`GITHUB_TOKEN`, `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `*_API_KEY`, `docker -e`/`--env=` included); `Authorization`/`Proxy-Authorization`/`Cookie`/`X-Api-Key`/`X-Auth-Token`/`Api-Key` header values (the auth scheme stays); URL userinfo passwords; URL query values whose name is secret (`?token=`, `?access_token=`, `?api_key=`, `?key=`). Host, path, other query values and the fragment stay. A value is masked only when it is plain data: one containing a line break, a shell metacharacter (`;` `|` `&` `$` backtick), a bracket or a quote is shown, and the program given to an interpreter's inline flag (`sh -c`, `python -c`, `node -e`/`--eval`, `perl -e`) is never masked. That way `sh -c 'GITHUB_TOKEN=x; curl …'` and `python -c 'GITHUB_TOKEN=print(731)'` stay whole.
- **Trade-off, stated plainly:** positional args, short flags (`-p`, `-k`, `-t`, `-P`), packages, images, scripts and URL path segments are **never** masked. A secret passed as a bare positional or a short flag (`mysql -phunter2`) is shown, because the user is approving that exact command. The shape-based redactor no longer runs on this line: it masked packages and scripts that only looked like keys (`sk-learn-…`).
- **The line shows what runs**: every control, format (bidi overrides/isolates, zero-width, BOM, soft hyphen), separator and combining-mark (Mn/Me) character, plus U+FFFC, becomes a visible escape such as `\u202e` / `\u0336`. Legitimate non-ASCII letters are left as written; homoglyph detection is out of scope. Each argument is shell-quoted when whitespace, a quote, a backslash, a shell metacharacter or being empty would change how it reads, and spaces are never collapsed, so `shlex.split(line)` gives back exactly the argv that runs (`'review  server.py'`, `''`). The same holds for the cwd.
- **Renderer** (`mcp-setup-tool.tsx`): plain React text (no HTML/markdown rendering), monospace, wrapped in full with `break-all` and `whitespace-pre-wrap` (spaces inside an argument are kept), with no clamp, ellipsis or tooltip-only text. A very long line scrolls inside a bounded box (`max-h-40 overflow-y-auto`), so every argument is reachable without hover. `Working dir: …` and `Env: KEY, …` lines appear when set.
- **i18n**: `launchCommand` / `launchRemote` / `launchEnv` / `launchCwd` in all 9 locales (incl. `ar_assistant.ts`, `zh-hant_assistant.ts`), `locales/_keys.desktop.json` regenerated.

## Screenshots (real Electron app, real `gateway run` backend)

A loopback model called `manage_connections` enable on four configured servers, so the card opened from a real `connection.request`, and each line came from `mcp_launch.launch_for`. All four rows sit in one card. Each shot is scrolled to its own row's line. A and C were taken at 1f93841e285 (unchanged rendering for those rows); B and D were re-taken at 906d413ed5a.

| Scenario | Line (DOM readback) | Shot |
|---|---|---|
| normal + env + cwd | `Runs: npx -y @acme/mcp` · `Working dir: /srv/acme` · `Env: NODE_OPTIONS` (no value) | ![A](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/063829737aeeb9e2063d753519553870/raw/A_normal.png) |
| long command, payload in the middle | `Runs: node server.js` + 15× `--log-level=info` + `--exec /tmp/steal.js` + 15× pad + `--quiet`, all 9 wrapped lines shown in full, nothing cut (scrollHeight = clientHeight = 144, max-height 160px) | ![B](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/063829737aeeb9e2063d753519553870/raw/B_long.png) |
| bidi / zero-width | `Runs: npx safe\u202egnp.evil --x np\u200bx` (literal escapes, nothing reversed) | ![C](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/063829737aeeb9e2063d753519553870/raw/C_bidi.png) |
| named secrets, image kept | `Runs: docker run -i --rm -t -e GITHUB_TOKEN=*** ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server --api-key=*** -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'` (the `-t` image stays visible) | ![D](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/063829737aeeb9e2063d753519553870/raw/D_secrets_r2.png) |

Earlier main-vs-head shots (main shows the name only): [gist 16e0696](https://gist.github.com/teknium1/16e0696ae1af4de45dc03f1981701490).

## Tests

- `tests/tools/test_connectors_mcp_launch.py`: the card payload carries the scrubbed launch line and the model result does not. 33 named-secret shapes never leak; 16 what-runs shapes (npx `-p` package, docker `-t` image and `-p` port, scripts, deno URL paths, `--token-file`/`--keymap`/`--author`/`-k` paths, `sk-`-looking package, `--token --exec`) are never masked; a positional/short-flag secret is shown as approved; a remote URL keeps its path and other query values; Cf/control/combining/U+FFFC characters render as escapes; an overlong line is never cut and keeps a middle `--exec`. 24 of these are red on 1f93841e285.
- `mcp-setup-tool.test.tsx`: the line is plain text, shown in full (a middle `--exec /tmp/steal.js` included) with no clamp, ellipsis or `title`, in a scrollable box; includes the env and cwd lines; goes away once the row resolves. `connection-request.test.ts`: a live frame that changes env or cwd replaces the launch line.
- Also run: `test_connectors_mcp.py`, `test_connectors_operation.py`, `tests/tui_gateway/contracts/` (99 passed with the launch tests), `npm run check:lint` (0 errors), `scripts/check --only health` (0 blocking), ruff.
- The delta review's probe corpus (`probe.py`): 0 false masks (was 12) and 0 leaks for every named form (head leaked `Cookie:`, `GITHUB_TOKEN=`, `--token:`). The 9 rows the probe still flags are shown on purpose under the governing rule: 5 short flags (`-p`/`-k`/`-t`/`-P`, spaced and attached), a nameless `?<value>` query, a `#fragment`, `--key:` (bare `key` is not a secret name for flags; `--key` is often a key file), and `--api-key --<value>` (an arg starting with `--` reads as the next flag, so masking it could hide one).

## Infographic

![MCP consent card — launch targets](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab1242b/MjvIx-orb7_QDqS1i9nNd_Q05pTSQi.png)

prs.title: feat(delegation): opt-in prompt-cache warm-up gate for batch subagents
prs.body:
When the agent hands a batch of tasks to subagents, every subagent starts by sending the same big instructions-and-tools prefix, and only its own task differs. If they all send at once, nobody gets the provider's cached copy; with this opt-in setting the first subagent goes ahead and the rest wait just until its answer starts arriving, so they reuse the cached prefix at ~10% of the price.

**Outcome:** `delegation.prefix_stagger_seconds` (default `0` = off, same behaviour as today) turns on a prompt-cache warm-up gate for `delegate_task` batches. On a real Nous Portal Claude Sonnet 4.5 batch of 3, siblings 2 and 3 read ~92% of their prompt from cache with the gate on, and 0% with it off.

### Do siblings actually share a prefix? (verified)
- Captured the real outgoing request bodies of 3 sibling children from a real `delegate_task` batch (real `AIAgent` parent → loopback body-logging provider, `origin/main` tree):
  - **system prompt byte-identical** across all 3 (5,249 chars), **tools[] byte-identical** (10 tools, 12.4 KB JSON), message list `[system, user]`; the **only** difference is the user message (the goal).
  - Raw chat-completions body LCP is 5,377 B because that wire serialises `messages` before `tools`; on the provider's cache order (tools → system → messages) everything up to the goal is shared.
  - The goal is the child's first user turn, not part of the system prompt (`tools/delegate_tool_progress.py::_build_child_system_prompt`). Per-task `context` is appended at the END of the child system prompt (after the Hermes scaffold and the static cache breakpoint), so tasks with different contexts still share tools + the whole Hermes scaffold.
- Provider-measured shared prefix (real Portal run, same batch): **4,643 of 5,014** prompt tokens read from cache by each sibling (the ~370 uncached tokens are the goal + trailing block).

### What changed
- New sibling `tools/delegate_tool_prefix_gate.py` (`PrefixCacheGate`): the first child starts at once; siblings **on the same provider/model route** wait until the leader's first response **starts streaming** (its request has written the cache), the leader finishes, or the cap elapses — whichever is first. So the cost is ~one time-to-first-token, not a fixed `(N-1)×S` ramp.
- Skipped entirely when the route is not prompt-cached by Hermes (`_use_prompt_caching` false), for siblings on a different model/route, for single-task calls, and when the setting is 0. Cap clamped to 0–60 s.
- A sibling stopped (child or parent interrupt) while waiting is reported `interrupted` and never starts its work.
- `tools/delegate_tool_dispatch.py` only wraps `run_child` when a gate exists; `delegate_tool_config._get_prefix_stagger_seconds` reads the knob through the existing `_knob` loader. Docs in `configuration.md`.
- Rebuilt on current `main` (the old diff targeted the pre-split `delegate_tool.py`).

### Real-provider A/B (Nous Portal, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`, 3-child batch, each arm on a fresh toolset combo so arms can't warm each other)

| arm | sibling start offsets | sibling 2 / 3 cache_read (of prompt) | batch $ | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gate off | +0.00 / +0.01 s | 0 / 0 (of 3,588) | $0.0435 | 4.5 s |
| gate on (cap 15 s) | +1.43 / +1.43 s | 4,643 / 4,643 (of 5,014) | $0.0275 | 5.2 s |
| gate on (cap 15 s) | +1.07 / +1.08 s | 3,381 / 3,381 (of 3,752) | $0.0220 | 6.6 s |

Uncached siblings cost ~$0.0145–0.018 each; cached siblings ~$0.0035. Total billed for the live leg: **$0.13**.

### Loopback controls (stub with 1.5 s first-token latency)
| arm | sibling start offsets |
|---|---|
| head, gate on, cache-marked route | +1.53 / +1.53 s (released at the leader's first chunk) |
| head, gate off | +0.00 / +0.00 s |
| head, gate on, route without prompt caching | +0.00 / +0.00 s (skipped) |
| main | +0.00 / +0.00 s |

### Review items (Enough1122)
1. Latency tax `(N-1)×S`: gone by design — the wait ends at the leader's first chunk (measured +1.1–1.5 s), capped, opt-in, and skipped on non-caching routes or other-model siblings.
2. Child launched after an interrupted wait: now returns `interrupted` without running.
3. Queued children waiting for the ramp: there is no ramp; children past the first wave are queued behind the pool as before, and the gate opens once for the whole batch.

Tests: `tests/tools/test_delegate_prefix_cache_gate.py` (2 behaviour tests) + all 39 `tests/tools/test_delegate*.py` files and `tests/hermes_cli/test_config.py` green locally.
