prs.title: docs(stt): blank provider language inherits stt.language, not auto-detect (#120100)
prs.body:
The config comments said a blank per-provider STT `language: ""` means auto-detect, but Hermes actually falls back to the global `stt.language` (default `en`). Users who followed the comment got English transcripts of non-English audio. This PR corrects the comments and docs. Code behaviour is unchanged.

Outcome: every comment and doc line describing `stt.<provider>.language` now states the real resolution order: provider value → `stt.language` → `HERMES_LOCAL_STT_LANGUAGE` → auto-detect.

- `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py`: the six per-provider `language` / `language_code` comments now read "blank = inherit stt.language".
- `cli-config.yaml.example`: same for the two per-provider lines (the global line already said `""` = auto-detect).
- `website/docs/user-guide/features/voice-mode.md`: the config sample now shows the global `stt.language: "en"` and the full fallback order.

| config | what the old comment promised | what Hermes does (unchanged) |
|---|---|---|
| `stt.local.language: ""` | auto-detect | `en` (inherits global) |
| `stt.language: ""` | auto-detect | auto-detect |
| `stt.language: ja` | Japanese | Japanese |

Root cause: bc997a36a8e made `stt.language: "en"` the global default on purpose (Whisper auto-detect misreads short clips), and the per-provider comments written before it were never updated.

Context: issue #120100 / PR #120130 by @Baophan00 reported this. That PR changes the meaning of `""` instead, which would silently flip OpenAI STT to auto-detect on fresh installs and drop the Language field from Desktop's Voice settings, so we're fixing the misleading text instead. Per-provider auto-detect as an explicit opt-in value is tracked in #133707.

Part of #120100 (the wake-word false-trigger and auto-submit parts of that issue are separate).

prs.title: fix(tui): /save on an older gateway refuses redact, filename and md/html instead of writing raw JSON on its host
prs.body:
When the TUI talks to an older gateway, that gateway can only save one kind of file: raw JSON with no redaction, written on the gateway's own machine. Until now the TUI used that for every `/save`, so `/save md notes.md redact` quietly wrote an unredacted JSON copy somewhere else. Now it says no and explains why, the way the CLI and Desktop already do.

**Outcome:** on a gateway without `session.export`, `/save` with `redact`, a filename or a non-JSON format writes nothing and shows a plain refusal. A bare `/save` still works, and its notice now says the file is raw JSON on the gateway host.

**Who hits this:** a TUI started with `HERMES_TUI_GATEWAY_URL` pointing at a listener that is not a session authority (an older gateway, or a `hermes serve` without one). The default launch attaches to the session-authority gateway and goes through `session.export`. That path is unchanged.

- `ui-tui/src/app/slash/commands/core.ts`: one parser (`parseSaveArgs`) for both branches. The legacy branch refuses `redact`, a filename, or any format other than `json`/`snapshot`, the same rule as `hermes_cli/cli_session_mixin.py::_save_on_older_gateway` and Desktop's `saveLegacyRefused`.
- New strings `slashCmd.core.save.legacyRefused` and `savedOnHost`, translated in all 16 `locales/*.tui.yaml`. `locales/_keys.tui.json` was regenerated with `npm run i18n:keys`.
- The `/save` help line now lists the arguments (`[json|md|html] [filename] [redact]`) instead of "save the current transcript to JSON".

### Live evidence (real Ink TUI build + real `hermes serve`, scratch HOME, loopback fake provider)

Rig: `hermes serve --port 18742` under a scratch `HERMES_HOME` (no session authority, so `gateway.ready` carries no `session_authority`). The TUI was built with `scripts/build/tui.mjs` from each tree and launched with `HERMES_TUI_GATEWAY_URL=ws://127.0.0.1:18742/api/ws?token=…`. One turn sent `my key is sk-proj-ABCD…abcd`.

| Command | main `71736c9f325` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `/save md notes.md redact` | `conversation saved to: <fakehome>/.hermes/sessions/saved/hermes_conversation_20261104_025801.json`. The file is **JSON** and contains the raw `sk-proj-…` key (2 hits). No `notes.md` in the cwd. | `not saved: this gateway predates /save export, so it cannot write a redacted, named or md/html copy. Update the gateway, or run plain /save to write raw JSON on the gateway host.` Nothing written. (Captured on `6f72ce7`; since `f5606437` the refusal reads `not saved: this gateway does not serve /save export (an older gateway, or a sidecar without the session authority), … Attach to the gateway that owns the session or update it, or run plain /save …`.) |
| `/save json --redact` | (same silent raw-JSON write) | refused, nothing written |
| `/save html` | (same silent raw-JSON write) | refused, nothing written |
| `/save` | raw JSON on the host | `conversation saved as raw JSON on the gateway host: <path>` |
| Control: default launch (session-authority gateway, no attach URL), `/save md notes.md redact` | n/a | `conversation saved to: <cwd>/notes.md`. Markdown, key redacted (0 hits) |

### Tests
- `ui-tui/src/__tests__/createSlashHandler.test.ts`: a new `it.each` covers the four option shapes on a non-canonical gateway (no RPC call, refusal shown). It fails 4/4 with main's `core.ts` and passes with the fix. The file's 84 tests pass, and the existing "`/save` forwards to session.save" test is unchanged and still green.
- `tsc --noEmit`, eslint on the touched files, and `npm run i18n:keys:check` all pass.
- `tests/agent/test_i18n_tui_packs.py` and `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_validate_locales.py`: 23 passed.

Found during review of #86858 (docs). This PR has no doc changes: that PR's table already describes the CLI/Desktop behaviour, which the TUI now matches.

prs.title: feat(gateway): llm.oneshot accepts an explicit provider/model pin
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Gives `llm.oneshot` an explicit model pin. Desktop plugin surfaces that carry their own per-task model choice (e.g. a composer picker for prompt enhancement) currently cannot express it: the params contract is `extra="forbid"`, so sending `provider`/`model` fails with a 4000 contract-out-of-sync before the handler runs, and `run_oneshot` can only resolve via `auxiliary.<task>` config or the session/main model.

The resolver's explicit-pin arm already exists — `call_llm(task, provider=, model=)` is the highest-priority route (explicit args > `auxiliary.<task>.*` config > auto). This PR adds the missing wire path from the RPC into that arm, plus one small desktop affordance:

- `LlmOneshotParams` gains optional `provider`/`model`; openrpc + generated TS regenerated via `scripts/gen_gateway_contracts.py`.
- `llm.oneshot` normalizes blank/whitespace strings to `None` (a whitespace pin must not shadow the session/task/main-model arms) and forwards both to `run_oneshot`.
- `run_oneshot` passes them through to `call_llm`.
- `ModelCatalogMenu` gains `showEditModels?: boolean` (default `true`; existing surfaces unchanged) so a plugin-hosted picker can render the curated model list without the composer's curation-management row in its footer.

No new credential surface: the pin is a provider/model name pair resolved server-side through the existing config table — callers never send `base_url`/`api_key`, and the resolver still enforces the configured provider.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. Closest neighbors (neither covers this; the first is a bug in the `auto` route, the second a caching tier unrelated to routing): #118157, #118337.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [x] ✅ Tests

## Changes Made

- `tui_gateway/contracts/sessions.py` — `LlmOneshotParams` + `provider`/`model`
- `tui_gateway/methods_session.py` — normalize + forward the pin
- `agent/oneshot.py` — `run_oneshot(provider=, model=)` → `call_llm`
- `apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.openrpc.json`, `apps/shared/src/gateway-contract.generated.ts` — regenerated
- `apps/desktop/src/app/shell/model-catalog-menu.tsx` — `showEditModels` prop
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_oneshot_model_pin.py` — new

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/tui_gateway/test_oneshot_model_pin.py -q` → 7 passed (contract round-trip; handler forwarding + blank normalization; `run_oneshot` pass-through; openrpc schema).
2. `python scripts/gen_gateway_contracts.py` on this tree reproduces both generated artifacts byte-for-byte (verified in the PR branch).
3. `pytest tests/tui_gateway/contracts/test_generated.py -q` → 2 passed (pydantic ↔ openrpc ↔ TS parity gate).
4. Desktop vitest: `model-catalog-menu.test.tsx` + `model-catalog-menu.search-fold.test.tsx` + `plugins/kanban/model-override.test.tsx` → 17 passed.
5. Full `pytest tests/tui_gateway -q` before/after diff: 13 failures both runs, identical case lists — all pre-existing `origin/main` env failures in this macOS environment, none from this change. (2 reproduce standalone even without the patch: `test_subagent_snapshot`, `test_external_process_picker`; the other 11 depend on whole-suite ordering state.)
6. E2E (manual, on a patched local build): a desktop plugin sends `llm.oneshot` with `provider`+`model`; the one-shot runs on the pinned model (logs show the explicit pin winning over the session model). Omitting the params behaves exactly as before.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits (`feat(gateway):`)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate (#118337/#118157 checked — no overlap)

- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 27 (darwin, Apple Silicon), Python 3.11 venv

prs.title: fix(approval): flag remote content piped to a wrapped or path-qualified shell
prs.body:
Hermes asks before running `curl … | sh`-style commands, but it only recognised a bare shell right after the pipe. So `curl … | sudo bash`, `| /bin/sh` or `| env -i zsh` ran with no prompt. Now the guard sees the shell through launchers, paths, quotes and `.exe`, and also catches `source <(curl …)`.

**Outcome:** remote content piped into a shell prompts for approval when the shell is path-qualified, quoted, `.exe`, or behind a launcher (`sudo`, `env`, `time`, `timeout`, `exec`, `nice`, `stdbuf`, `nohup`, `doas`, `busybox`, `command`). Quoted text that only mentions such a pipe, and lookups like `command -v bash`, don't prompt. Legitimate pipes (`| jq`, `| tar xz`, `| sudo tee`, `| shellcheck -`) still don't prompt.

- `tools/approval_detection.py`: the pipe-to-shell sink accepts launcher words (`sudo`/`doas`/`env`/`exec`/`command`/`nohup`/`nice`/`time`/`timeout`/`stdbuf`/`busybox`, optionally path-qualified, with options, option values and `VAR=value`) before a path-qualified, quoted or `.exe` shell (`bash sh zsh ksh dash fish csh tcsh`). It also accepts `|&` and `tee >(sh)`.
- Options that take a value consume it, so `sudo -u bash cat` reads `bash` as the user name and is not flagged.
- All repeats are atomic/possessive: a 400-wrapper chain scans in 0.4 ms. The first cut of this rule backtracked exponentially; that is fixed and covered by a test.
- `source <(curl …)` / `. <(curl …)` at command position → "execute remote script via process substitution". `diff a.sh <(curl …)` is no longer flagged by that rule.
- Tests in a new `tests/tools/test_approval_pipe_shell.py` (`test_approval.py` is over the size cap and is unchanged from main).

**Before / after** (real `detect_dangerous_command` output, probe of 52 bypass shapes + 36 legitimate commands):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| bypass shapes missed | 38 / 52 | 0 / 52 |
| false positives | 1 / 36 (`diff a.sh <(curl …)`) | 0 / 36 |
| `curl … \| sudo -u root -E bash` | not flagged | pipe remote content to shell |
| `curl … \| sudo -u bash cat` | not flagged | not flagged |
| `source <(curl …)` | not flagged | execute remote script via process substitution |
| existing approval-test literals (1561) | — | identical verdicts |

prs.title: Desktop approval card can approve the rest of the chat in one click (YOLO)
prs.body:
When the agent stops to ask before a dangerous command, the Desktop approval card could only allow that one command, or that one *kind* of command for the session. Now its menu also has **"Approve everything in this chat (YOLO)"**: one click turns on this chat's YOLO and runs every card that's already waiting, so the rest of the run stops asking.

Ported from lobehub/lobehub#22122 ("switch to auto approve from the approval card").

## What changes

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Card menu | Allow this session · Always allow… · Reject | Allow this session · **Approve everything in this chat (YOLO)** · Always allow… · Reject |
| Agent runs `rm -rf ./a`, then `chmod -R 777 ./b` in one turn, user picks the "session" option on card 1 | card 2 still asks (different pattern) | with the YOLO item: card 2 never appears, the command runs |
| Two cards already queued when the user clicks | n/a | YOLO turns on first, then both cards run (`once`) |
| Scope | — | this chat only (`config.set key=yolo session_id=…`, the same flag as `/yolo` and the status-bar zap); global `approvals.mode` is untouched |

- `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/tool/approval.tsx`: the new menu item, plus `switchToYolo()` (turn on YOLO, then answer each waiting card in that chat). The menu-option logic moved into `approvalMenuOptions()` so `ApprovalCard` stays under the complexity cap.
- The item has the same gate as "Allow this session". A request the gateway limits to once/deny (a Smart DENY owner override) gets no YOLO item, so that card can't be widened to the whole chat.
- New `assistant.approval.switchToYolo` string in all 8 Desktop locales plus `_keys.desktop.json`.

Order matters: YOLO goes on BEFORE any card is answered, so the agent's next call (made the moment card 1 resolves) already sees it. Cards are answered one at a time, not with `all: true`, because the canonical gateway protocol (`canonical-protocol.ts::preparePromptResponse`) turns `approval.respond` into a fixed one-prompt payload and drops `all`.

## Ours vs LobeHub

| | LobeHub #22122 | this port |
|---|---|---|
| What gets saved | the agent's `approvalMode=auto-run` (lasts across chats) | this chat's YOLO flag only (Desktop's existing per-session scope; the global switch stays Shift+click on the zap) |
| Queued siblings | approves "covered same-tool siblings" | approves every card waiting in the chat (with YOLO on, every one would pass anyway) |
| Server continuation | patched so a parked run reads the new mode | not needed: hermes checks session YOLO on every guarded call (`tools/approval.py`), so the live turn picks it up right away |

## Validation

- **Live, real backend (loopback model, real `hermes serve` + `/api/ws`, `approvals.mode: manual`).** A throwaway probe (`tests/e2e/core/terminal/_gateway_client.Backend`, not committed). One turn makes two dangerous calls with different patterns:
  - control (`choice: session` on card 1): `card2_asked: true`, second dir stays `0o700`
  - head RPC sequence (`config.set yolo=1` → `{"value":"1","scope":"session"}`, then `approval.respond once` → `{"resolved":1}`): `card2_asked: false`, `chmod` ran (`0o777`)
- **Renderer (worktree Vite renderer in headless Chrome, real `PendingApprovalStack`, two seeded cards, gateway stubbed to record calls).** Clicking the item sent `config.set {key:yolo, session_id, value:"1"}`, then `approval.respond once r1`, then `approval.respond once r2`. The queue emptied.
- `vitest src/components/assistant-ui/tool/` 145/145 (new invariant: YOLO is set before any card is answered, and every waiting card gets `once`); `tsc --noEmit`; eslint 0 errors; `scripts/check --only health` clean.

### Screenshots

Menu (two cards queued, "1 / 2"):

![menu](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3fa564254887ea74b75d4c9d5beae794/raw/945c863f23e8ed41663317dfce7c0c494b2b9c5a/approval-yolo-menu.png)

After clicking: both cards answered, stack empty:

![after](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3fa564254887ea74b75d4c9d5beae794/raw/945c863f23e8ed41663317dfce7c0c494b2b9c5a/approval-yolo-after.png)

**Not covered:** native Electron (rung 3) against a real model, and the remote-owner route (`requestForOwnedSession` routes `config.set` and `approval.respond` to the same owner, but I didn't run a two-backend rig).

Opened by the weekly LobeHub scout cron. Awaiting review; not merged.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab13514/vCITOeS2HN4IMVLlc2k-Z_LKz7RVAO.png)

prs.title: fix(tui): enable copy-on-select for remote sessions, make it configurable
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The mouse-selection auto-copy (copy-on-select) listener in `useMainApp` is gated on `isMac`, evaluated from the **host** process. For a TUI hosted on Linux — Docker, a dev box, a server — and driven from a macOS client over SSH, the listener never registers. Auto-copy structurally cannot exist for the users who need it most: the app holds the alt screen so there is no native terminal selection path, and the host's platform says nothing about the client terminal anyway (`setClipboard()` already routes OSC 52 back over the pty).

Extracted as a pure, unit-tested `copyOnSelectEnabled()` (`ui-tui/src/lib/copyOnSelect.ts`) with a three-level policy:

1. `HERMES_TUI_COPY_ON_SELECT` — boot override, mirroring the existing `HERMES_TUI_MOUSE_TRACKING` "force a value" knob (`ui-tui/src/config/env.ts`) precedence-for-precedence
2. `display.copy_on_select: auto|on|off` in config.yaml (boolean back-compat), synced live via `useConfigSync` — same tri-state shape as `normalizeMouseTracking`
3. `auto` (default): host macOS — unchanged upstream behavior — **or** an inbound SSH session (`SSH_CONNECTION` present)

Plain local Linux/Windows sessions stay **off** by default, deliberately: X11/Wayland already auto-copy selections to the primary register, OSC 52 support there is uneven and sometimes deliberately disabled, and selection-clobbers-clipboard would regress those workflows. The explicit setting exists for exactly the cases the heuristic gets wrong in either direction.

## Related Issue

Fixes #46467 (make copy-on-select work beyond host-macOS / controllable), introduced through the same `display.copy_on_select` key that #46491 adds for it.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix — the `isMac` gate was scoped to the host process rather than the client terminal, so remote sessions have no auto-copy path at all. The config key + boot override are escape hatches for the heuristic's edge cases, not the point of the PR.

## Changes Made

- `ui-tui/src/lib/copyOnSelect.ts` (new) — `copyOnSelectEnabled()` policy + `normalizeCopyOnSelect()` tri-state normalization
- `ui-tui/src/lib/copyOnSelect.test.ts` (new) — normalization (booleans/strings/garbage → `auto`), env-override precedence over config, SSH heuristic on/off, explicit on/off overriding platform
- `ui-tui/src/app/useMainApp.ts` — gate the selection listener through `copyOnSelectEnabled()` instead of `isMac`
- `ui-tui/src/app/useConfigSync.ts`, `ui-tui/src/app/interfaces.ts`, `ui-tui/src/app/uiStore.ts`, `ui-tui/src/gatewayTypes.ts` — plumb `display.copy_on_select` through the live config sync
- `website/docs/user-guide/tui.md` — config-reference entry for `display.copy_on_select` (same block and style as `mouse_tracking`)

## Relationship to existing PRs

- **#46491** — same `display.copy_on_select` key name and the same extract-the-gate direction (it fixes #46467); this extends it with the SSH heuristic and the boot override. Happy to rebase on it if it lands first.
- **#94938** — differs on defaults: this does **not** enable copy-on-select by default on local Linux/Windows (regression reasoning above); the default changes only for remote SSH, everything else is explicit opt-in.
- **#80368** — orthogonal: no write-path policy refactor here, this changes only the enable-gate (and it uses a different key name, `display.tui_copy_on_select`).

Independent of the iTerm2 `tmux load-buffer -w` threshold fix (#149286); neither depends on the other.

## How to Test

1. Reproduce the bug (before): TUI hosted in Docker on Linux, driven from a macOS client over SSH — drag-select never copies; the only clipboard paths are `/copy` and the native-tool fallback.
2. Automated: `npm run check --workspace ui-tui` on this branch rebased onto current `main` — 253/253 test files, 1946 tests, lint clean; pre-commit lefthook `lint tui` green.
3. Manual (after): remote SSH session — drag-select auto-copies into the local pasteboard; local Linux session verified unchanged (no auto-copy, clipboard untouched); `HERMES_TUI_COPY_ON_SELECT=off` overrides `display.copy_on_select: on`.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits (`fix(tui):`)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate — #46491/#94938/#80368 are related attempts, differences stated above
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — N/A: TS-only diff; ran the CI JS lanes instead (`npm run check --workspace ui-tui`, `npm run build --workspace ui-tui`, `tests-js` suite — identical results to pristine `main`)
- [ ] `python scripts/check` passes — N/A for the same reason (no Python touched)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Linux host (Docker) driven from macOS over SSH; local Linux session regression-checked

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation — `website/docs/user-guide/tui.md` config reference
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` — N/A: `display` TUI keys are documented in `tui.md` (precedent: `mouse_tracking` and `inline_images` are absent from `cli-config.yaml.example` too)
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md`/`AGENTS.md` — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact — Windows/Linux local behavior is the unchanged `off` default; `SSH_CONNECTION` is set on Windows OpenSSH servers too, where auto-copy is equally useful (`check-windows-footguns.py` scans Python only; no diff hits)
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas — N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

Manual verification (macOS → ssh → Docker-hosted TUI): drag-select lands in the local macOS pasteboard; a local Linux session shows no behavior change (`xclip -o` before/after a drag is identical). The `auto` heuristic matrix (macOS host, SSH, plain local) is covered by `copyOnSelect.test.ts`.

prs.title: perf(bots): room view reads only the log delta and moves on groups.changed
prs.body:
## What

An open Group Chat stops re-reading its whole log every 2 seconds. It reads only new events from its cursor and refreshes when the gateway pushes `groups.changed`. A slow poll stays as the backstop.

This is step 2 of the Bots architecture plan (https://artifacts.kshitij.md/bots-architecture/). Step 1 (#149118) is merged; step 3 is #149228.

## Why

On main, each open room view calls `groups.state` and then pages `groups.log` from seq 0, every 2 s, for as long as it is open. That cost grows with the log, and a new message can still take up to 2 s to appear. In the plan's implicit-state census this is I6-state-poll.

## How

**Desktop (`canonical-group-workspace.tsx`)**
- Reads `groups.log` from `since_seq = last applied seq`.
- A page is applied only when it starts right after the cursor. A gap is an error, never a silently wrong view.
- If `latest_seq` drops below the cursor (the room was re-hosted), the view rebuilds from 0.
- Refreshes on `groups.changed` for its own route and room (`room_ids`). An untagged event, or one with no room list, refreshes every view.
- `refresh()` is the one read gate for every caller (poll, push, a mutation's settle, Refresh, settings saved): a call during a read joins it and causes one more read, so reads never overlap.
- An empty read keeps the same log array, so nothing downstream re-derives.
- While shown, the view holds its route's socket open (`host.retainProfileSocket`). Without it, a secondary backend's socket closes between reads and its `groups.changed` never arrives.
- Polls every 15 s when `groups.state` reports `change_events`. Older backends, and rooms reached through the forwarding backend, keep the 2 s poll.

**Gateway (`change_watcher.py`)**
- New `groups.changed` watch: checked every 0.5 s, broadcast at most once per second.
- Its payload names the rooms whose signature moved since the last broadcast (`payload_fn(before, after)` on the shared watch loop), or `{}` when process-wide state moved (a room service started or stopped).
- Its signature is per room, across every room store this process serves (launch and served homes, the shared store, each room service's store). It covers:
  - the log head and room revision;
  - each room's live task rows, read through the status index;
  - `HostedRoomService.live_status_sig()`: approvals, route states, tools, stalls and blocked rooms. These live only in memory, so no store write marks them. It copies them without `_policy_lock`, which `prepare_room`/`stop_room` hold across store writes and peer calls.
- The DB read is cached behind the DB/WAL mtime and shares one helper with the existing sessions digest.
- Room services register in a small weak registry, so the watcher doesn't need to know how runners hold authorities.
- A log head moving (a cron or CLI post) wakes only the driver whose store moved, read from the watch's own store cache. That driver answers in about 1 s instead of waiting up to 5 s for its idle poll. This is a server-side latency change beyond the Desktop feed.
- `groups.state` now counts tasks with `GROUP BY`. It decodes only live and retryable rows, both from one read snapshot (`room_task_summary`), instead of every retained task (up to 2048 per room). Native rooms build Discard/Retry from those same rows. The order of actions is unchanged in both room kinds, and tests now pin it.

## Verification

- **Formal model.** `RoomFeed.tla` model-checks the client contract with TLC: 828 states with two reads in flight, and 225 with one, which is what the code does. In that contract, pushes are lossy hints, a page is applied only at the cursor, `has_more` re-reads, and a safety poll with weak fairness is required. Invariants `ViewIsPrefix` and `Converges` hold. Removing the poll breaks `Converges`, which is why the backstop stays.
- **Mutation checks.** Every mutant planted against the new tests makes at least one test fail. They cover:
  - ignoring appends, task rows or live status, and an unregistered service;
  - dropping `room_ids`, removing the floor, or losing rooms behind it;
  - waking every store or waking on every pass, and an unguarded wake that kills the watcher thread;
  - waiting on `_policy_lock`, non-snapshot reads, decoding every task, and the order of actions in each room kind;
  - keeping `change_events` on forwarded rooms;
  - Desktop:
    - no contiguity check and re-reading from 0;
    - ignoring pushes, no backstop, and dropping a signal mid-read;
    - overlapping reads, and copying on empty reads;
    - a page with `has_more` that brings nothing;
    - not holding or not releasing the route socket;
    - no rebuild, and ignoring route or room filtering.
- **Review.** Three review rounds, Greptile's six threads (all answered), and a final four-lens gate: reuse, quality, efficiency, and alignment with the model and the census. Dispositions are recorded per finding.
- **Cost.**
  - An idle watcher tick costs 0.4 ms and opens no DB; this was traced.
  - A read after a store write takes 2.9 ms on a real 7.8 GB `state.db`. The existing sessions digest on the same file takes 833 ms.
  - Per-room live-row reads take 0.57 ms for 10 rooms over 20k retained tasks. A first draft's cross-room query took 1955 ms, scanning the whole table, and was replaced.
- **Tests.** CI on this head.

## Not in this PR

- Server-side round and outcome state, and the chips' 1 s clock (plan step 3).
- The roster's 5 s poll and the room list's 10 s poll. The driver's 5 s idle poll stays as the fallback for its new wake.

prs.title: fix(tui): keep tmux load-buffer -w for iTerm2 >= 3.5
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`tmuxLoadBuffer()` drops `tmux load-buffer -w` for **every** iTerm2 build because tmux's OSC 52 emission was reportedly crashing iTerm2 sessions over SSH. The `-w` flag (tmux 3.2+) is what propagates the buffer to the outer terminal's clipboard via tmux's own OSC 52 emission — so the blanket ban silently kills clipboard propagation for all modern-iTerm2 users in remote tmux, which is the dominant iTerm2 + SSH workflow today. (`setClipboard()` still reports success because the tmux buffer did load — the failure is invisible.)

The drop now applies only to **legacy builds**: `LC_TERMINAL == iTerm2` and `LC_TERMINAL_VERSION < 3.5` (including version-unknown, the conservative fallback). The OSC 52 / tmux integration demonstrably improved in the 3.5 line (late 2023), and `-w` is verified working on 3.7.6 over SSH.

**Provenance honesty, up front:** the original crash report is not traceable — it is not in the iTerm2 changelog or any public tracker we could find. The 3.5 threshold is empirical. The code comment states exactly this and flags the constant for correction by anyone (maintainers especially) who holds the original report with an exact fix version. When `LC_TERMINAL_VERSION` is missing (no shell integration, or SSH without `SendEnv`), iTerm2 keeps the legacy no-`-w` behavior — and the DCS-passthrough path in `setClipboard()` still covers those cases for users with tmux `allow-passthrough on`.

## Related Issue

No open issue tracks the blanket ban itself. Related context: #112785 (open) — competing design for the same function, see Relationship below; #31528 (closed) — the remote-chain `/copy` OSC 52 behavior this path serves.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `ui-tui/packages/hermes-ink/src/ink/termio/osc.ts` — `tmuxLoadBuffer()` drops `-w` only when `LC_TERMINAL == iTerm2` and `LC_TERMINAL_VERSION < 3.5` (or the version is unknown); all other terminals and modern iTerm2 keep it. The comment block documents the empirical threshold and invites correction.
- `ui-tui/packages/hermes-ink/src/ink/termio/osc.test.ts` — new `tmuxLoadBuffer` arg-matrix tests: iTerm2 ≥ 3.5 keeps `-w`; < 3.5 drops it; version-unknown drops it; non-iTerm2 terminals keep it.

## Relationship to existing PRs

- **#112785** (open) rewrites the same function toward the opposite policy: it drops `-w` for everyone and always emits an explicit DCS-wrapped OSC 52 inside tmux, making the outer-terminal clipboard depend on tmux `allow-passthrough on` (off by default). This PR instead keeps tmux's own `-w` forwarding — which needs no tmux config — and only scopes the legacy workaround to the old builds it was for. The two touch the same lines of `osc.ts`/`osc.test.ts`, so whichever lands second rebases; happy to do that.
- **#31528** (closed) established the remote-chain `/copy` expectations (OSC 52 preference, DCS wrapping) that this code path builds on.
- **#149287** is the companion copy-on-select enable-gate work; independent PRs, neither depends on the other.

## How to Test

1. Reproduce the bug (before): TUI hosted in tmux on Linux (e.g. Docker), iTerm2 ≥ 3.5 client over SSH, stock tmux (no `allow-passthrough`) — `/copy` reports success, nothing lands in the macOS pasteboard.
2. Automated: `npm run check --workspace ui-tui` on this branch rebased onto current `main` — 252/252 test files, 1939 tests, lint clean (includes the new arg-matrix tests).
3. Manual (after): same setup with iTerm2 3.7.6 — `/copy` and mouse-selection writes land in the local macOS pasteboard.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits (`fix(tui):`)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate (#112785 overlaps on purpose and is called out above; nothing else targets the iTerm2 version threshold)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — N/A: TS-only diff; ran the CI JS lanes instead (`npm run check --workspace ui-tui`, `npm run build --workspace ui-tui`, `tests-js` suite — identical results to pristine `main`)
- [ ] `python scripts/check` passes — N/A for the same reason (no Python touched)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Linux host (Docker, tmux) driven from macOS / iTerm2 3.7.6 over SSH

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation — or N/A (no user-facing doc describes the `-w` workaround; the code comment carries the provenance note)
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` — N/A (no config key added)
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md`/`AGENTS.md` — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact — the change is gated on iTerm2's exported env vars; non-macOS hosts and non-tmux paths are untouched (`check-windows-footguns.py` scans Python only; no diff hits)
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas — N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

Manual verification (iTerm2 3.7.6 → ssh → tmux → TUI): `/copy` on an assistant message and mouse-selection copy both land in the macOS pasteboard; `tmux show-buffer` matches the copied text. Legacy iTerm2 (< 3.5) and version-unknown cases are covered by the arg-matrix unit tests rather than live clients.

prs.title: fix(desktop): drop a finished turn's journal on reopen instead of replaying it
prs.body:
## Infographic

![Stale-journal fix infographic: the bug, why recovery missed it, the owner pending-list rule, the reopen race, proof and limits](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af809d0c-c153-42fe-a282-d92ab234f206)

## What does this PR do?

I hit this in the Webapp on Firefox for Android. A tab closed while a turn was streaming. When I reopened the chat later, that old prompt and its half-streamed reply showed up below the newest reply, and they came back after every reload. The server transcript was fine: the extra copy came from the tab's in-flight turn journal in `localStorage`.

**Root cause.** On reopen, `recoverInFlightTurnJournal` decides whether the journaled turn finished by finding its completed reply in the loaded transcript. When the loaded rows don't hold the journaled prompt, `mergeInFlightMessages` appends the whole journaled tail, which it has done since the journal landed in 8d8d1d61fe. The loaded rows miss the prompt in several cases:
- a long tool-heavy turn, or newer turns from another device, push the prompt out of the newest 120-row page;
- compaction re-stored the rows;
- the last throttled snapshot differs from the final text, which is #136335's case.

The idle re-persist then refreshes the journal, so it never ages out.

**Approach: ask the owner instead of inferring.** The canonical reopen snapshot already lists every admission the owner has not finished (`queued`, `started`, or `unknown` after a crash). The journal records which admission it belongs to: every owner frame carries the running execution's `admission_id`, so the journal stores the admission whose execution streamed it and checks that against the list. A regenerate keeps the first send's prompt bubble, and a queue drain adds none, so the prompt id alone can't name the turn. An entry from an older build still falls back to its prompt id `user-<submission id>`:

| Owner's pending list | Journal |
|---|---|
| lists the journaled turn as `started` or `queued` | folded live, as today |
| lists it as `unknown` (lost in a crash) | recovered, as today; this is what the journal is for |
| doesn't list it | the turn finished: cleared before any transcript matching |
| journal names no admission (an older entry whose prompt names none either) | cleared only when the list is empty |
| no list at all (owners without an admission ledger, failed-resume fallback) | unchanged from `main` |

The second commit closes a race this opens. A cold reopen reads the newest REST page alongside `session.resume` and normally omits the snapshot's history, so the page can be read before a turn commits its final reply. Until now the stale journal stood in for that reply; once it's cleared, nothing would. `rereadPageAfterResumeBarrier` now re-reads the page once whenever the journal holds a turn the owner no longer lists. That holds even when the owner isn't idle, because a queued successor may already be running. The re-read is safe because `settle_session_input` marks an admission terminal only after the agent wrote the turn's rows. Owners without a list never trigger it. If that re-read fails (it rejects, or answers for another session), the journal still folds and is kept, as on `main`, but as settled output: a turn the owner reports finished never takes the running turn's stream target or clock. The next reopen that reads the page retires it.

Approaches I tried and dropped before this one:
- **Ordering by row id.** It passed unit tests, but a live send's journaled prompt has no row id: the `prompt.submit` admission receipt carries no `user_row_id`.
- **Comparing the send time against server row timestamps with a clock-skew margin.** It still replayed the old turn whenever the chat was reopened within the margin.
- **Paging back until the prompt is found.** Unbounded.

## Related Issue

Refs #136335: the same mechanism, a stale journal re-folded below a finished reply after long tool-heavy turns. I'm not marking it fixed, because the reporter later saw one occurrence with no journal keys stored, which this change doesn't explain.

#77584 (open) also edits `inflight-turn-journal.ts` and `use-session-actions/index.ts`, but for retention and deletion. It doesn't cover this replay.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

Five commits, then `94656028fa` merges main at `0073fa98cf`. Its one conflict is additive: `app/types.ts` keeps `turnAdmissionId` beside main's new `turnAnchorId`.

- `147ec5a92d` **fix(desktop): drop a finished turn's journal on reopen instead of replaying it**
  - `apps/desktop/src/lib/inflight-turn-journal.ts`: `ownerPendingTurns()` reads `info.pending_submissions`. `recoverInFlightTurnJournal` takes an `owner` option and clears a journaled turn the owner has finished before any transcript matching.
  - `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/index.ts`: the reopen path passes the snapshot's pending list. The comment above the call was shortened to keep the file at its code-health size cap.
  - `apps/desktop/src/lib/inflight-turn-journal.test.ts`: retire cases (prompt outside the loaded page, another turn running), plus controls (`unknown` recovered, `started` keeps folding, no list keeps today's transcript check, and the prompt-without-admission cases).
  - `apps/desktop/e2e/core/webapp-stale-journal.spec.ts` (new, Linux like the other Webapp journeys): a real gateway and Webapp build with two tests.
    - **Stale turn:** a tab dies mid-turn, the turn finishes, and another browser runs a tool-heavy turn (4 × 32 `todo_list` calls since `d55f66d47d`) and then a newer one. The reopened and reloaded chat must end at the newest reply, with the journal cleared.
    - **Crash:** the gateway is SIGKILLed mid-turn and restarted. The owner lists the turn as `unknown`, and the reopened chat must still show the streamed reply that only the journal held.
- `19c46310b3` **fix(desktop): re-read the reopen page when a journaled turn has finished**
  - `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/resume-barrier-reread.ts`: re-reads once when the journal holds a finished turn, idle or not.
  - `apps/desktop/src/lib/inflight-turn-journal.ts`: `journaledTurnFinished()` helper.
  - `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/resume-settled-journal-reread.test.tsx` (new): drives the real `resumeSession` with a page read before the final reply.
- `91b122980a` **fix(desktop): keep the journal when a finished turn's page cannot be re-read**, from review ([r4470553504](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/147413#discussion_r4470553504), @unsupportedpastels)
  - `resume-barrier-reread.ts`: returns `{ page, owner }` and withholds the owner's list when the required re-read fails; `index.ts` takes the list from it instead of deriving it again.
  - `resume-settled-journal-reread.test.tsx`: a rejecting second read keeps the journal and its streamed progress.
- `824fbb73b8` **fix(desktop): fold a finished turn's journal as settled when its page is unread**, from review ([r4471401082](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/147413#discussion_r4471401082))
  - `resume-barrier-reread.ts`: marks the list `replyUnread` instead of withholding it.
  - `inflight-turn-journal.ts`: a finished turn beside an unread page folds with no stream target or turn clock, so a running successor's deltas stay on its own row.
  - `resume-settled-journal-reread.test.tsx`: a running successor, a rejecting second read, then one delta.
- `d55f66d47d` **fix(desktop): key the in-flight journal on the owner's execution admission**, from review ([kshitijk4poor](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/147413#pullrequestreview-5773727232); answers @yoniebans's item 3 too)
  - `use-message-stream/gateway-event/index.ts`, `lib/execution-authority.ts`: record the `admission_id` of each fully stamped frame the execution fence accepts as `turnAdmissionId`. An admission-only frame (a queued row's cancellation) names no execution.
  - `inflight-turn-journal.ts`: the journal stores it as `admissionId`, and reopen matches it against the pending rows' `admission_id`. Entries without one keep the prompt-id rule.
  - `resume-barrier-reread.ts`, `index.ts`: a cold resume carries a recovered, unfinished journal's admission onto the state (`recoveredTurnFields`, moved out of `index.ts`). A warm activation takes the snapshot's running execution, unless a frame named a newer one while `session.activate` was in flight. Resume reads the snapshot's own `pending` list, not the derived `info.pending_submissions`.
  - `resume-settled-journal-reread.test.tsx`, `resume-turn-admission.test.ts`: a regenerate the gateway lost (kept across two reopens), a finished queue drain beside a queued successor (retired), the warm-activation and finished-fold cases, a turn retired by the list alone with its prompt off the page, and a pending list the snapshot didn't carry.
  - `e2e/core/harness.ts` and the two Webapp specs: shared `freePort`, `hermesCli` and `webappLaunchLink`. The journal spec finds the journal by what the tab stored, not a versioned key. It reads the off-page premise from the reopened renderer's own newest-page response, so neither the key prefix nor the 120-row page size is hard-coded.

## How to Test

1. E2E: `npm run build:webapp`, then `npx playwright test -c e2e/core/playwright.config.ts webapp-stale-journal` from `apps/desktop`.
   - On `main`, the stale-turn test fails with the old prompt and its partial reply after the newest prompt. On this branch, both tests pass.
2. Units: `npx vitest run --project ui src/lib/inflight-turn-journal.test.ts src/app/session/hooks/resume-settled-journal-reread.test.tsx src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/resume-turn-admission.test.ts`.
3. By hand in the Webapp:
   1. Send a prompt and close the tab while the reply streams.
   2. Let the turn finish, then run a few more turns from another browser.
   3. Reopen the chat. It should end at the newest reply. `hermes.desktop.inflightTurnJournal.v2:*` should be gone from `localStorage`.

## Verification

Run on `d55f66d47d` against base `9a76ac8e4f`, Linux arm64, Node 26.12.1, Playwright Chromium 1248. After the main merge, head `94656028fa` reran the e2e, `test:ui`, both typechecks and `scripts/check`. The Firefox row and the before/after clip ran on `19c46310b3` and were not repeated. The Desktop core E2E lane runs only on release and dispatch, so the e2e runs are local.

| Check | `main` (`9a76ac8e4f`) | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| E2E, Chromium | stale-turn test **fails** (old prompt and partial reply after the newest prompt); crash test passes | both pass (`d55f66d47d`, and again on `94656028fa`), and the three non-Electron `webapp-gateway-attach` tests that now share its helpers |
| E2E, Firefox 157 (Gecko) | stale-turn test **fails** the same way; crash test passes | both pass, 2/2 (`19c46310b3`) |
| `resume-settled-journal-reread.test.tsx` | both race cases **fail**, showing the stale partial "Reading the issue" where the final reply "There are four open issues." should be; the idle failed-re-read case fails only on its read count, since `main` never re-reads; the running-successor case **fails** with the successor's delta on the old reply | 11/11 pass; the idle failed-re-read case **fails** on `19c46310b3` (no reply text, journal cleared), the running-successor case on `91b122980a` (same as `main`); on `824fbb73b8` the regenerate case **fails** (partial lost) and the queue-drain case **fails** (old rows replayed) |
| `inflight-turn-journal.test.ts` | the 7 new tests can't run on `main` (`ownerPendingTurns is not a function`), so their red isn't behavioural; the behavioural red is the three rows above | all pass |
| Commit `147ec5a92d` on its own | | 27 files, 440 tests pass; `tsc` clean; code-health clean |
| Full desktop `test:ui` | | 1,491 files, 12,611 tests pass; after the merge (`94656028fa`), 1,560 files, 13,021 tests |
| `python scripts/check` | | 14/14 checks pass |
| `tsc` (src and e2e), eslint | | clean |

**Before/after**, 34 seconds, recorded at the same time on the two builds: real Webapp and gateway, a scripted mock model, headed Chromium, and a real X pointer. The left side is `main`; the right side is this branch.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9883fe72-1c02-441e-94ff-0fd7326df2ee

| | After reopening | After reload |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | the old prompt and "Reading" sit below the newest reply; journal still stored | same |
| this branch | ends at "Here is the note for the team."; journal cleared | same |

**Not covered.**
- Owners that send no pending list keep `main`'s behaviour, so the replay can still happen there:
  - the legacy JSON-RPC backends, including Desktop remote;
  - the failed-resume fallback.
- Forwarded owners (`tui_gateway/owner_forward.py`) publish their list only as a `session.info` event, which this doesn't read.
- A queue drain's crash recovery. The owner keeps listing the lost drain, so the journal is kept, but its tail opens at the previous turn's prompt (a drain adds no bubble). The transcript merge then reads it as caught up and drops the partial reply, as on `main`.
- Another tab's send admitted after the reopen snapshot reads as finished and its journal is cleared until that tab's next stream update.

prs.title: fix(web): latest-descendant walk skips unmarked subagent children
prs.body:
Fixes #149237

## Root cause

`_DESCENDANTS_SQL` in `hermes_cli/web_server_sessions.py` filtered non-continuation edges by the `/branch`, `/new` and `_delegate_from` markers plus `source != 'tool'`. Batch `delegate_task` child rows are reserved with `source='subagent'` and a `parent_session_id` but carry **no** `_delegate_from` marker, so the recursive walk treated them as continuations. `latest-descendant` therefore resolved to the subagent transcript, and resuming the user's chat into it mounted read-only (`session_read_only` lockout) with the session never appearing in the sidebar.

## Fix

One predicate, applied in both places the walk builds parent→children edges:

- `_NON_CONTINUATION_SOURCES = ("tool", "subagent")`, used in the CTE (`COALESCE(s.source, '') NOT IN ('tool', 'subagent')`) and in the in-Python `children` build when the DB connection is absent.
- `source` is selected through the CTE and the row-shaping keys so the fallback path can apply the same rule.

## Tests

`tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server.py::test_latest_descendant_skips_unmarked_subagent_children` — a `tui` parent with a `source='subagent'` child, parent ended; `GET /api/sessions/<id>/latest-descendant` must return the parent. Red on `main` (it returns the subagent row), green here.

Evidence, run with `scripts/run_tests.sh`:
- base `main` + test file only: 191 passed, **1 failed** (the new test)
- branch: **192 passed**

prs.title: fix(state): orphan sweep must not re-stamp rows with a compression/reset successor
prs.body:
Fixes #149249

## Root cause

`sweep_orphaned_sessions` selected orphans purely on `started_at` / last-activity age, with no regard for lineage position. A row that had already been closed with a legitimate boundary (`compression`, `session_reset`) and then re-opened by a stale resume got re-stamped `end_reason='startup_orphan_reap'`. The local-policy lineage receipt for that conversation (`gateway.local_policy.v1:<id>`) requires the parent of a continuation row to end with `compression`/`session_reset`, so validation then failed on every turn and the profile's canonical Bot Chat was permanently unopenable with `storage_unavailable`. Not self-healing: the next start re-broke a hand-repaired row.

## Fix

- `hermes_state_common.py`: factor the existing fork-marker predicate into `_forked_child_sql(child, parent, markers)` and add `_superseding_child_sql`, which treats `_branched_from`/`_delegate_from` children as forks (excluded) but lets a `_reset_from` child count as a successor. `_non_continuation_child_sql` keeps its exact previous behaviour — single owner, no duplicated SQL.
- `hermes_state_maintenance.py`: the orphan predicate gains `AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sessions succ WHERE succ.parent_session_id = sessions.id AND <superseding predicate>)` — a row that already has a compression continuation or a reset successor is a closed lineage step and is never re-stamped.
- `website/docs/user-guide/sessions.md`: the sweep's never-closed list now names this case.

## Tests

`tests/hermes_state/test_sweep_orphaned_sessions.py::TestSupersededRowsKeepTheirBoundary` — parametrized over the two boundaries (`compression`, `session_reset`), backdates a parent and child, re-opens the parent, and asserts the sweep leaves the parent's `end_reason` NULL while still sweeping the genuinely stale child. Red on `main` (both parameters fail: the parent comes back as `startup_orphan_reap`), green here.

Evidence, run with `scripts/run_tests.sh`:
- base `main` + test file only: 27 passed, **2 failed** — both new parameters
- branch: **29 passed**

prs.title: feat(cli): hermes --cpu-profile PATH writes a CPU profile of the run
prs.body:
`hermes --cpu-profile PATH ...` records where the CPU went during one Hermes run and saves it to a file when the run ends. It also writes a short text summary next to it, so you can see the slowest functions without learning `pstats`.

**Outcome:** a one-flag way to profile any Hermes launch (chat, `-z`, `chat -q`, `--tui`, subcommands) with no config or env setup.

- `PATH` (pstats) + `PATH.txt` (top 80 functions by cumulative time). A relative `PATH` goes under the active profile's `logs/profiles/`; absolute and `~` paths are used as given.
- Turned on right after each launch path parses argv (`main()`, fast chat, Termux CLI and TUI fast paths), before any early return, so `--version` and Termux's deferred interactive chat are profiled too. Exits that skip atexit write it explicitly: `-z`, gateway `os._exit`, and the POSIX `exec` handoffs (`relaunch()`, named-profile dashboard reroute).
- `-z/--oneshot` exits through `os._exit` (atexit skipped on purpose), so `_exit_after_oneshot` writes the profile before the hard exit.
- No env var. The flag is the only switch, and the earlier `HERMES_CPU_PROFILE` export is gone.
- Under `--tui`, the profile covers the launcher process. The agent itself runs in the TUI's own backend process (this is noted in the help text).
- `main.py` stays at its size on main: `_dashboard_validate_serve_args` moved to `main_dashboard.py` to make up for the added lines.

### Live (tmux, real Nous Portal turn, scratch HERMES_HOME)

| Command | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes --cpu-profile base.prof -z 'Reply with just the word ok'` | `hermes: 'base.prof' is not a hermes command.` EXIT=2 | `ok`, EXIT=0; `logs/profiles/live-z.prof` written (187,226 calls, 7.18 s) |
| `hermes --cpu-profile live-q.prof chat -q '…' -Q` | n/a | `ok`, EXIT=0; profile 1,626,786 calls, 7.80 s |
| `hermes --cpu-profile live-tui.prof --tui`, one turn, `/exit` | n/a | turn answered `ok`, EXIT=0; profile written (launcher, 95 s) |
| Early-exit path (provider auth refused) | n/a | profile still written |

### Tests
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_cpu_profile.py`: a relative path lands in `<HERMES_HOME>/logs/profiles` through the real CLI subprocess; the one-shot `os._exit` path still writes the profile.
- 45 related files (startup order, yolo, TUI launch, dashboard, value-flag parity), 921 passed.

prs.title: feat(desktop): finish the Settings → Appearance door map (20 settings keys + host.window)
prs.body:
## What

Completes **#121896 items A, B and C** — the whole Settings → Appearance surface now has a typed plugin door.

Two doors, because the page has two kinds of control:

1. **`host.settings` — the 20 renderer preferences.** Every Appearance control backed by a renderer store, bound to the same atom + setter the Settings page uses.
2. **`host.window` — the three window-level channels.** UI zoom, translucency and minimize-to-tray drive the main process or the window chrome, so they cannot be settings keys; they were reachable only through `window.hermesDesktop.*` raw preload IPC.

## `host.settings`: 13 new keys

Seven hub-consumer rows plus the rest of the page's renderer-backed controls, because landing seven and coming back for six more makes a plugin author trail the app's release cadence for no reason.

| Key | Store | Shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `embed-mode` | `embed-consent.ts` | `ask/always/off` | |
| `hideThreadTimeline` | `thread-timeline.ts` | boolean | |
| `interfaceMode.v1` | `interface-mode.ts` | `simple/advanced` | bound through the exported setter — mode changes also re-scope layout persistence |
| `titlebarAppActions` | `titlebar-app-actions.ts` | `left/right` | |
| `toolView.technical` | `tool-view.ts` | `product/technical` | enum, despite the legacy storage key |
| `toolView.hideCodeDiffs` | `tool-view.ts` | boolean | |
| `user-bubble-transparency.v1` | `user-bubble-transparency.ts` | number 0–100 | band-checked, not clamped |
| `textDirection` | `text-direction.ts` | `auto/ltr/rtl` | |
| `reactions.v1` | `reactions-enabled.ts` | boolean | mirrors to `display.message_reactions` |
| `tours.v1` | `tours.ts` | boolean | mirrors to `display.in_app_tours` |
| `vibeHearts.v1` | `vibe-hearts-enabled.ts` | boolean | |
| `tips.rotation.v1` | `tips.ts` | boolean | mirrors to `display.in_app_tips` |
| `model-pricing.v1` | `model-pricing.ts` | boolean | |

## `host.window`: zoom, translucency, minimize-to-tray

```ts
host.window.zoom.{available, get, setPercent, subscribe}
host.window.translucency.{get, set(patch), subscribe}
host.window.minimizeToTray.{available, get, set, subscribe}
```

- **`zoom` is per window** — same thing ⌘+/⌘− does.
- **`translucency` patches the renderer store field by field** through the native setters (intensity/fade clamped, mode/material/scope normalized), so it never touches the IPC directly.
- **`minimizeToTray` is machine-level** and owned by the main process.
- `zoom` and `minimizeToTray` feature-detect: `available() === false` and `get`/`set` resolve `null` on an older build; `subscribe` returns a no-op disposer, so registration stays unconditional.

The docs also call out the tray trap the native page already documents: `available` is false until the setting is enabled (the tray object is created on enable), so a control gated on `available` alone deadlocks — gate on `available || enabled`.

## Scope: three kinds, not interchangeable

This is the part the multi-profile question turns on, so it is stated in the docs and in the code:

- **The 20 settings keys are desktop-wide.** Renderer preferences keyed `hermes.desktop.*` with no profile segment; `store/text-direction.ts` says it outright — *"global to this desktop install (every window and profile) … not about a backend, profile or session"*. A write from any profile view changes the setting for every profile, exactly as the native control does.
- **The window channels are window-level / machine-level**, as above.
- **The config-backed fonts are `@_profile_scoped`** (`desktop.font_family`, `terminal.font_family`): an unscoped config write names the profile the backend was *launched* with, not the one on screen (#125969). That mismatch has no honest read path today and is tracked separately in #140423.

## The three mirrored toggles

`reactions.v1`, `tours.v1` and `tips.rotation.v1` decide whether a tool is in the model's schema at all, so their stores mirror into the agent-facing config. The mirror is a store subscription, not part of the binding: a plugin write reaches it exactly as a Settings-page click does. No extra authority is granted, and the docs say so next to the key table.

## Deliberately not here

`fileBrowser` — a pane-layout record (`$paneStates`), not an appearance preference; its setter drives side-column geometry, minimized-tree restore and narrow-pane reveal. Different kind of write, deserves its own conversation.

Still declined, unchanged: keybind map, theme selection, `pluginDecisions`, layout geometry.

## Tests

`vitest run src/sdk` — **105 passed (8 files)**.

- Six new keys: read/write through the owning stores, persistence-schema preservation (including the `'on'`/`'off'` encoding reactions and vibe hearts keep), out-of-shape refusal.
- `host.window`: bridge-present and bridge-absent paths for zoom and tray, plus the renderer-owned translucency path.

## Rebase note

Rebased onto `0ab43d4f` after sitting 53k commits behind; conflicts were main's `isChatTextScale` guard (kept alongside the new guards) and the declined-table row (kept main's layout row + this PR's `host.window` row).

Closes nothing yet — #121896 items D (intro content contribution) and F (locale-change event) remain open and are not in this PR.

Related to #121896

prs.title: fix(cron): keep scheduling cadence out of cron job prompts (one schema clause)
prs.body:
The cron tool's description now tells the model, in one clause, that a job's `prompt` holds the work and the timing goes in `schedule`. That way a job created from "every morning at 9, check X" does not store "every morning at 9" as part of the instruction the run reads.

**Outcome:** one clause added to the `prompt` field description of `cronjob_manage`, +10 tokens. Rebuilt on current `main` as one commit; the earlier multi-sentence description block and the schema-text tests are gone.

- `tools/cronjob_tools.py`: `prompt` description reads "the full self-contained prompt, work only (timing goes in 'schedule'; ...)". Nothing else changed.
- No new test: the change is schema prose, and a test asserting that text would be a change-detector.
- Prompt surface: `cronjob_manage` is deferred behind `tool_search` on the CLI/Desktop bundles. Its `tool_search.json` fixture line only carries the first sentence of the description, so no snapshot regen. `tests/ci/test_prompt_surface.py` passes. GitHub won't require a prompt-surface approval: the `prompt-surface-review` ruleset only matches `tests/fixtures/prompt_surface/**`, and this PR doesn't touch that path. It does edit model-facing schema prose, so a maintainer may still want to look, but that's their call and not a merge gate.

## Token cost (o200k_base, `json.dumps` of `CRONJOB_SCHEMA`)

| | origin/main | this PR (before trim) | this PR (now) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cronjob_manage` schema | 1814 | 2132 (vs its base of 2008: +124) | **1824 (+10)** |
| served `hermes-cli` tool list (`measure_tool_tokens.py`) | 8680 | n/a | 8680 (cronjob is deferred) |

## Live check (Nous Portal, forced `cronjob_manage` call, 3 samples per request per leg)

| model / request | main: cadence in `prompt` | head: cadence in `prompt` |
|---|---|---|
| claude-haiku-4.5, "every morning at 9am, check HN..." / "each weekday at 6pm remind me..." | 0/6 | 0/6 |
| gemini-2.5-flash, "every 2 hours check example.com..." / "hourly, look at my disk usage and warn me only if it grew since the last hourly check" | 0/6 | 0/6 (2 prompts keep "since the last hourly check", which is the user's comparison rule, not the cadence) |

To be honest about this: on current models, main did not reproduce the failure. They already put the timing in `schedule`. This clause is a cheap guard for weaker or local models, not a fix for an observed regression. If you don't want any schema growth without an observed failure, closing this is reasonable.

## Infographic

![Cron cadence mission patch infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab12411/6FOzwI88C3zKmqmqdNrPI_3aLnHp4U.png)

prs.title: feat(compression): keep uncertain claims labelled UNVERIFIED through compaction
prs.body:
When Hermes compacts a long conversation, the summary tends to lose words like "I suspect" or "probably". A guess can then come back after compaction looking like a confirmed fact. This change asks the summarizer to write each uncertain claim on its own `UNVERIFIED:` line, so the resumed agent can tell guesses from facts.

**Outcome:** every compaction summary (first and iterative) has a `## Unverified / Working Hypotheses` section listing each uncertain claim as `UNVERIFIED: <claim> — <basis>`.

- `agent/context_compressor_prompt_rules.py` (new sibling): holds the one-sentence rule and the section template. `_today_for_prompt` moved here too, so the 7k-line facade gets shorter (−13 lines) instead of longer.
- `agent/context_compressor.py`: the summarizer preamble and the shared section template interpolate those two strings.
- Only the summarizer prompt changes. The system prompt, the cached prefix and the persisted handoff prefix (`SUMMARY_PREFIX`) are untouched, so per-conversation caching is unaffected.
- Prompt cost, kept lean on purpose: **+288 chars per summary call** (this PR's first version added +756). Measured LIVE: `prompt_tokens` 1473 → 1552 (+79) on `meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct` via the Nous Portal.

### Before / after (LIVE, the real `_generate_summary` prompt sent to llama-3.3-70b via Nous Portal; transcript with 1 confirmed fact + 3 hedged claims)

| | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| prompt_tokens | 1473 | 1552 |
| labelled uncertain claims | none (hedges kept only inline, e.g. "the Telegram long-poll may be getting reset by the ISP NAT" written into a plain-statement section) | `UNVERIFIED: DNS resolution lag on the VPS causes the timeout — suspicion based on timing` / `UNVERIFIED: Proxy dropping idle keepalives contributes to the timeout — unconfirmed` / `UNVERIFIED: Telegram long-poll gets reset by the ISP NAT after ~5 minutes — working hypothesis based on timing` |
| confirmed fact ("timeout fires at 30s") | kept as fact | kept as fact (not hedged) |

This is one sample, shown to illustrate the shape. The direction matches the study's finding (arXiv:2608.06953): a labelled field holds stance better than an inline aside.

Tests: `tests/agent/test_context_compressor_stance_preservation.py` (rule + section reach the prompt on both the first and the iterative path; red on `origin/main`, green here) plus the compressor, temporal-anchoring, task-heading, prompt-reading and gateway compress suites (305 + 323 passed). `scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking.

prs.title: refactor(memory): take the Honcho-specific code out of core
prs.body:
## What

Takes the Honcho-specific code out of Hermes core. Honcho left core on 2026-10-01 (7e53b3ef82, teknium1) and ships from the catalog (plastic-labs/honcho, `hermes-plugin-honcho`), but core still knew its file layout in four places:

| Where | What core did |
|---|---|
| `hermes profile create --clone` | imported the plugin's `cli.clone_honcho_for_profile` |
| `hermes profile rename` | `hermes_cli/profiles_honcho.py` rewrote host blocks in `honcho.json` |
| `hermes update` | called the plugin's `sync_honcho_profiles_quiet()` |
| Dashboard memory panel | a Honcho-only storage kind (`STORAGE_HONCHO_HOST_BLOCK`) that imported the plugin's private `client` and `oauth` modules, lock internals included |

## Change

Two generic seams any memory provider can implement, then delete the Honcho code.

- `MemoryProvider.on_profile_created(profile_name, hermes_home)` / `on_profile_renamed(old, new, hermes_home)`: called from `create_profile` (CLI, dashboard, Desktop/TUI) and `rename_profile` for the provider the profile's config selects, with that profile's home and its own `.env` secrets bound. A failing hook or unreadable config is logged and never fails the create or rename.
- `storage=STORAGE_PROVIDER` in `config_schema.py`, with `read_config_fields(hermes_home)` / `write_config_fields(values, hermes_home)`: the provider owns its file layout. Core keeps value coercion, the `memory.provider` switch, the 400 on a refused write, and saves secrets to `.env` only after the provider accepted the write.

Deleted: `hermes_cli/profiles_honcho.py`, the CLI create's Honcho step, the update-time sync, `STORAGE_HONCHO_HOST_BLOCK` and its reader/writer, the empty `honcho: {}` config root and its template block, `HONCHO_API_KEY` in `_ENV_CONFIG_KEYS` (the `*_API_KEY` rule already routes it to `.env`), a dead `check_config_yaml_readers` exemption, and `"honcho"` as a hardcoded reserved name (alias collision now checks installed memory-provider names).

Session-name parsing (`hermes -c my session honcho sync`) now stops at the active memory provider's command instead of a hardcoded `honcho`.

Kept: Honcho in the left-core migration (moves existing users onto the catalog plugin), its env-var metadata (the child-process secret strip reads it), and comments using it as an example.

`_record_profile_rename` moves to `profile_identity.py` to stay inside the `profiles.py` line budget.

## Behaviour until the plugin adopts the seams

The catalog pin (7dd3702) implements none of the four methods. Until it does:

- its dashboard settings panel is empty (its schema imports the removed `STORAGE_HONCHO_HOST_BLOCK`);
- `--clone` does not create a host block for the new profile, and rename does not re-key it;
- `hermes update` no longer backfills host blocks; `hermes honcho sync` still does it by hand (docs say so).

Honcho memory itself (recall, sync, tools) is untouched.

## Verification

- 14 affected test files, head vs origin/main, file by file: no new failures, none fixed.
- New `tests/hermes_cli/test_profiles_memory_hooks.py`: hooks fire with the right home and the new profile's secrets (not the caller's); fresh profiles without a provider get none; a failing hook or a down config backend never fails create/rename; installed provider names are not free aliases.
- Dashboard fixtures moved onto `STORAGE_PROVIDER`: write-through, secret write-only, placeholders, presence semantics, and a refused write returns 400 with no `.env` write and no provider switch.
- Live check in a scratch home (fake keys, stub SDK) with the existing plugin extended locally by the four methods: CLI `--clone`, rename and dashboard GET/PUT match main with today's plugin, in-process and under `plugins.isolation: host` (corrupt config gives 400 in both).
- ruff clean; `scripts/check --only footguns,health` ok (0 blocking).

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Dashboard storage dispatch treats any non-provider storage value as flat JSON; an unknown value should give an empty panel and a 400.
- Until the plugin updates, every panel GET for a Honcho user logs the schema ImportError traceback.
- The hook binds the profile's secret scope before reading `memory.provider` (needed for `${VAR}` selectors): about 68 ms per create; could short-circuit when the raw config has no provider key.
- Alias collision now enumerates installed providers (about 50 ms) instead of a frozenset test.
- Under `plugins.isolation: host`, the hook spawns a plugin host for the new profile that stays alive in a long-lived dashboard.
- A plugin-host test fixture for the four new methods (verified live only).

prs.title: feat(video-gen): add Wan 2.7 text-to-video and image-to-video on FAL
prs.body:
Hermes can now make videos with Alibaba's Wan 2.7 model through FAL, from a text prompt or from a starting picture. You pick it like any other video model (`video_gen.model: wan-2.7`), and Hermes sends only the settings Wan 2.7 actually accepts.

**Outcome:** a new `wan-2.7` family in the FAL video plugin, routed to `fal-ai/wan/v2.7/text-to-video` (no image) and `fal-ai/wan/v2.7/image-to-video` (with `image_url`).

- Rebased onto current `main`: the entry now uses the compact `_family(...)` catalog form next to Wan 3.0 / 3.0 Prime, instead of the old long-form dict.
- Duration: JSON integer, clamped to the schema enum 2..15.
- Aspect ratio `16:9 / 9:16 / 1:1 / 4:3 / 3:4` on text-to-video only; image-to-video declares no `aspect_ratio` (the output follows the image), so it is dropped there.
- Resolution `720p / 1080p`; `seed` and `negative_prompt` sent on both endpoints.
- Audio is generated automatically when no `audio_url` is given and the schema has no toggle, so the family is `audio_native` (no `generate_audio` key is ever sent).
- One payload-shape test pins the above against the live schema (`tests/plugins/video_gen/test_fal_plugin.py::test_wan_27_payload_matches_live_schema`).

**Schema check (live, fal public OpenAPI, 2026-11-04):**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `openapi.json?endpoint_id=fal-ai/wan/v2.7/text-to-video` | 200, `WanV27TextToVideoInput` |
| `openapi.json?endpoint_id=fal-ai/wan/v2.7/image-to-video` | 200, `WanV27ImageToVideoInput` |
| control: `fal-ai/wan/v2.7/bogus-to-video` | 404 |
| t2v keys | `prompt`, `aspect_ratio` (5 values above), `resolution` (720p/1080p), `duration` int 2..15, `seed`, `negative_prompt`, `audio_url` |
| i2v keys | `image_url`, `end_image_url`, `video_url`, `resolution`, `duration` int 2..15, `seed`, `negative_prompt`, `audio_url` (no `aspect_ratio`) |
| price (model page) | $0.10/s at 720p, $0.15/s at 1080p |

**Payload Hermes builds (real `_build_payload`, request: 20s, 16:9, 720p, seed 7, negative prompt, audio on):**

| Route | Payload |
|---|---|
| text-to-video | `{prompt, seed: 7, aspect_ratio: "16:9", resolution: "720p", duration: 15, negative_prompt}` |
| image-to-video | `{prompt, image_url, seed: 7, resolution: "720p", duration: 15, negative_prompt}` |

A real paid generation was attempted through `FALVideoGenProvider.generate()` from this branch; the FAL account answered `User is locked. Reason: Exhausted balance`, so nothing was billed and the end-to-end render is not covered here. Also not checked: whether the managed Nous gateway (`provider: nous`) already allows these endpoint ids.

prs.title: fix(mcp): plugin remote MCP servers keep their ${VAR} header auth across reconnects
prs.body:
When a plugin adds a remote MCP server with an API key header (`"apikey": "${VENDOR_KEY}"`), Hermes connected fine the first time. Then it broke on the first retry or reconnect: it swapped the real key for the literal text `${VENDOR_KEY}` and parked the server. This PR fills in `${VAR}` for plugin-provided servers the same way it already does for `config.yaml` servers.

## Cause
- `_load_mcp_config` interpolates `config.yaml` entries, but merged portable (`mcp.json`) servers in raw.
- The first connect re-renders the config, so it worked.
- Every transport rebuild (retry, reconnect) runs `_refresh_remote_config`. That compares the running, rendered headers against the raw `${VAR}` from the load and reads the difference as an edited definition. It logs `definition changed in config.yaml (same url -> same url)`, adopts the placeholder, and `_require_rendered_remote` parks the server: `${VAR} in url/headers is not set in this profile's .env`.
- Fix: one line in `_portable_mcp_servers` (`tools/mcp_tool_config.py`): wrap the merged entry in `_interpolate_env_vars`.

## Live evidence
Real portable plugin, NousResearch/hermes-labs-plugins#60 (Patsnap, `streamable-http` with header `apikey: ${PATSNAP_API_KEY}`). Installed into a scratch `HERMES_HOME`, with a placeholder key in `.env`, then `discover_mcp_tools()`:

| attempt | main 71736c9f325 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | reaches Patsnap: `Access token expired or authentication error!` | same |
| 2 | `definition changed in config.yaml` → `${PATSNAP_API_KEY} in url/headers is not set` | reaches Patsnap again |
| 3 | same as 2, then **parks on "not set"** | reaches Patsnap again, parks on Patsnap's real auth error |

On main, a transient first failure leaves the server unrecoverable until restart, and its error names the wrong cause.

## Tests
- New `test_plugin_remote_server_keeps_its_rendered_header_across_a_rebuild` (`tests/tools/test_mcp_config_change_rebind.py`): red on main (`_refresh_remote_config` returns the raw-placeholder dict), green here.
- Every test file that touches `_load_mcp_config` / `_portable_mcp_servers` passes: 20 files, 331 tests, 0 failed.
- `ruff`, `scripts/check --only health` (0 blocking), no-tmp-literals: clean.

## Infographic

![portable-mcp-header-rebuild](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab11af8/o6m_qlUtWmssWXKLLj_sl_vmG6xpZd.png)

prs.title: fix(lsp): an abandoned LSP request sends $/cancelRequest, and its late reply is dropped
prs.body:
When Hermes gives up waiting on a language server (a timeout, or the diagnostics pull/push race cancelling the loser), it now tells the server to stop working on that request. Before this change the server kept computing an answer nobody would read, and the requests queued behind it waited too.

**Outcome:** an abandoned LSP request sends `$/cancelRequest` for its id. The server's late reply to that id is dropped and never reaches a later request.

- `agent/lsp/client.py`: on `CancelledError` in `_send_request`, write `$/cancelRequest {id}` straight to the transport (no drain, because awaiting inside a cancelled task is unreliable), then re-raise. The id is already off `_pending`, so `_dispatch_response` drops any late answer.
- Test mock gains a `late_pull` script: it holds diagnostic pulls, and on cancel it records the id and then answers that id with a result, like a server that finishes work the client gave up on.

### Live: real `pyright-langserver` (~/.hermes/lsp), `documentSymbol` on a 3,000-def file abandoned after 1 ms, then `hover` (id 2)

| | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `$/cancelRequest` sent for id 1 | no | yes |
| pyright's reply to abandoned id 1 | full result (it computed the whole thing) | error `-32800` RequestCancelled |
| follow-up hover id 2 | resolves with its own answer | resolves with its own answer |
| client state / `_pending` after | running / `{}` | running / `{}` |

### Tests
- `test_abandoned_request_is_cancelled_and_its_late_answer_is_dropped`: the cancel carries the abandoned id; the late answer is dropped; the next request gets its own reply; the client stays running. Red on origin/main (no cancel trace written).
- `tests/agent/lsp/`: 116 passed, 1 skipped.

prs.title: fix(vision): bound local image reads during the read; ingest cap 250 MiB
prs.body:
Viewing a local image used to load the entire file into memory before checking it against the size limit, so a multi-GB file used that much RAM before being refused. Now an oversized file is refused before it is opened, and a read never takes more than the limit plus one byte. The limit for image files on this machine goes from 50 MiB to 250 MiB; videos and files read from inside a sandbox stay at 50 MiB.

**Outcome:** host-side reads in `resolve_image_source` are bounded during the read, and the host-file cap for images is 250 MiB (video host reads and sandbox reads stay at 50 MiB; the first read is sized to the file, not the cap).

- `tools/image_source.py`: new `_read_host_bytes_bounded()`. If `stat` reports a size over the cap, it refuses without opening the file (no bytes read). Otherwise it does a single `read(cap+1)`, so the allocation is capped even when `st_size` under-reports (procfs-style files). The in-sandbox exec-read already had the same bound (`head -c cap+1`).
- Caps: host-file reads use the new `_MAX_HOST_READ_BYTES = 250 MiB` (binary, like every other `*_BYTES` cap in `tools/`), which `_finalize` also uses as the overall ceiling. Host reads of videos (`permitted=("video",)`) keep 50 MiB, because videos are never downscaled and `video_analyze` refuses anything over 50 MB of base64. The sandbox exec-read and `data:` sources keep `_MAX_INGEST_BYTES = 50 MiB`: the exec-read returns the file as base64 on stdout, which peaks near 4x the file in the Hermes process, so a 250 MiB budget there would cost ~1 GiB RSS per read. HTTP downloads keep their own 50 MiB stream cap (`vision_tools._VISION_MAX_DOWNLOAD_BYTES`). Downscaling to the 20 MB provider payload limit still happens at the call sites.
- `gateway/media_fetch.py`: comment fixed; its 50 MB fetch cap is independent of the host-read cap.
- `tests/tools/test_image_source.py`: three invariant tests. (1) A sparse file over the host cap is rejected without being opened. (2) When `stat` reports size 0, the read is still capped at cap+1. (3) A 60 MiB file read through the sandbox exec-read is refused (50 MiB budget).

## Live check (real files, `resolve_image_source` and `vision_tools._prepare_image`, peak RSS growth per process)

| file | main (cap 50 MiB) | head (cap 250 MiB) |
|---|---|---|
| normal 64x64 PNG | OK, +6 MiB | OK, +7 MiB |
| 102 MiB BMP (real pixels) | refused "exceeds size limit", +103 MiB | **OK**, normalized to PNG (cap raised) |
| 300 MiB sparse PNG | refused, **+302 MiB** RSS | refused, **+2.6 MiB** |
| 1 GiB sparse PNG | refused, **+1026 MiB** RSS | refused, **+2.6 MiB** |
| 200 MiB file via sandbox exec-read (real `head -c \| base64` in bash) | refused at 50 MiB | refused at 50 MiB, +235 MiB (was +800 MiB before the review fix) |

Tests: `test_image_source.py` + `test_vision*.py` + `test_image_generation*.py` + `test_delegate_native_vision.py` + `test_simplex_plugin.py`: 197 passed. `scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking.

## Review notes
- Enough1122 #2 (FIFO open blocks): `is_file()` gates this path, so a FIFO or devnode never reaches `open()`. `read_bytes()` behaved the same way. No change.
- Enough1122 #3 (boundary case): covered by the sparse cap+1 test, which also asserts the file is never opened.

## Infographic

![Bounded local image reads](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab12416/kUFnZxC6wrVE5lg_kkvVS_B4gNxdhz.png)
