prs.title: feat(feishu): interactive clarify cards + native choice picker
prs.body:
Feishu users can now answer the agent's multiple-choice questions and pick `/reasoning` / `/fast` options by tapping buttons on a card instead of typing a number. This builds on the same card plumbing and click authorization Feishu already uses for exec-approval buttons.

**Outcome:** Feishu joins Telegram, Slack, Discord and Matrix on the generic `send_clarify` / `retire_clarify_card` / `send_choice_picker` adapter contracts in `BasePlatformAdapter`. The gateway needs no changes, and no Feishu-only parallel path is added.

- **Clarify card** (`send_clarify`): one numbered button per option plus "✏️ Other (type answer)". A tap answers through `resolve_gateway_clarify`, and the callback response updates the card in place for every client. "Other" calls `mark_awaiting_text`, so the next message is the answer. A multi-select card also calls `mark_awaiting_text`, as the base text prompt does, so a typed free-form answer works as the hint says. Open-ended questions keep the base text prompt. The answer text comes from the pending clarify entry, so a tap after a timeout or `/new` shows "expired" and never a fake ✓.
- **Card retirement** (`retire_clarify_card`): when a clarify ends without a tap (timeout, session reset, superseding prose, typed answer), the gateway's existing hook PATCHes the card to a button-less state. The card is sent as a shared card (`update_multi: true`), which Feishu requires before an update reaches every recipient.
- **Choice picker** (`send_choice_picker`): one-tap card. The tap settles the card and runs `on_choice_selected` on the adapter loop, then the confirmation is posted. One live picker per chat, like Telegram. The picker card is shared too (`update_multi`), so a group settle reaches everyone. A one-line title (the usage-limit model offer) lists the full choice labels in the body, because buttons cut labels at 40 chars.
- **Webhook mode** (`FEISHU_CONNECTION_MODE=webhook`): a `card.action.trigger` POST keeps the button value as a dict and returns the settled card as the HTTP response body, the same shape the SDK callback gets. Token and signature checks still run first. Approval and update-prompt buttons over webhook use the same route, so they work now too.
- **Auth:** every click goes through `_validate_card_action`, the check approval clicks use: Feishu admins/allowlist, else the gateway pairing check, plus a match between the callback chat and the card's chat. State pops are first-writer-wins, so double taps and stale taps are refused.
- **Shape:** the behaviour lives in a new sibling, `plugins/platforms/feishu/adapter_choice_cards.py` (a mixin). `adapter.py` grows 1 line over main's 4534 (the webhook card-action branch): card-action routing became a key→handler table. New `platform.feishu.clarify.*` / `platform.feishu.picker.apply_error` strings are added in all 17 locales, reusing each locale's existing Telegram/Discord wording.

### Before / after (real adapter + real `tools.clarify_gateway`, SDK-free; agent thread blocked in `wait_for_response`)

| Step | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `send_clarify(["staging","prod"])` | text via `send()`: `❓ Deploy where? 1. staging 2. prod  Reply with the number…` | `msg_type: interactive`, buttons `['1', '2', '✏️ Other (type answer)']` |
| click by non-allowlisted `ou_stranger` | n/a (no buttons) | refused (`Unauthorized clarify click`), question still pending |
| click "2" by allowed user | n/a | card → `Deploy where? / **ou_owner:** prod`; agent thread got `'prod'` |
| stale click after resolution | n/a | refused (no card update) |
| clarify times out → `retire_clarify_card` | n/a | PATCH `om_2`: `Color? / ⏳ This prompt expired…`; later click refused |
| `send_choice_picker` (/reasoning) | no capability → text status card | buttons `['✓ Low', 'High']`; stranger refused; tap → `✓ **High** — ou_owner`; double tap refused; applier ran once: `['high']`, follow-up `Reasoning effort set to high` |

### Tests
- `tests/gateway/test_feishu_clarify_choice_cards.py` (3 behaviour tests: authorized-once clarify tap incl. stale tap; Other → text capture → retire PATCH; picker applies once for an authorized operator). Fails on `origin/main` (3/3), passes on head.
- Related suites: 39 files, 369 passed, 7 skipped (all `tests/gateway/test_feishu*`, `*clarify*`, `test_choice_picker`, i18n catalog parity, and every test referencing `_on_card_action_trigger`/`send_choice_picker`/`retire_clarify_card`).
- `scripts/check` (pre-push, 14 checks) ok; health 0 blocking.

Not covered: a real Feishu tenant (no bot credentials here). PATCH request/body field names were checked against the pinned `lark-oapi==1.7.5` wheel (`PatchMessageRequest`, `PatchMessageRequestBody.content`, `im.v1.message.patch`).

prs.title: fix(terminal): cache the supervised-gateway identity verdict and cap the guard wait
prs.body:
## Symptom

On macOS a long-lived supervised gateway leaks one parked thread per terminal command that fails the pre-exec guard check. Observed on a single gateway: thread count grows monotonically (85 → 87 → 93 within one hour, never decreasing), all parked in the same `open()` inside `_is_supervised_gateway_process()`.

The wedge is now reproducible: any command that runs a referenced script (`bash /path/script.sh`, even a two-line `echo`) is refused after the *full* guard deadline —

```
Terminal pre-execution guard did not finish within 180s (process-identity probe wedged); the command was not run.
```

while trivial commands (`echo`, `ls`, `ps`) pass. Each refusal leaks one more thread, so the failure is self-reinforcing.

## Cause

`_pre_exec_block` → `_is_supervised_gateway_process()` runs on **every** terminal command. The probe imports `gateway.restart` / `gateway.status` and does real filesystem + kernel process work. A single `open()` in that chain can block indefinitely on macOS. The guard already runs on a deadline worker (see #111922), so the *call* returns — but the worker thread is abandoned mid-`open()`, i.e. leaked.

Two multipliers:

1. The verdict is recomputed per command, although it is invariant for one process with one environment.
2. The guard's share of the deadline is `max(plan.effective_timeout, 30)`, so a 600 s command makes each wedged probe burn up to 600 s before failing closed — with the same refusal as a 30 s detection.

## Fix

* `tools/process_registry.py`: cache the identity verdict keyed on `(pid, _HERMES_GATEWAY, HERMES_SUPERVISED_CHILD)`. A changed marker (re-exec, tests, launcher shapes) re-probes. A probe that *raised* is never cached — a transient failure must not be frozen into "not supervised". Added `_reset_supervised_gateway_verdict_cache()` for tests and deliberate re-probes.
* `tools/terminal_tool.py`: add `_PRE_EXEC_GUARD_MAX_TIMEOUT_S = 30` and clamp the guard wait to `min(max(effective_timeout, MIN), MAX)`. A healthy guard finishes in milliseconds; a wedged one now fails closed in 30 s instead of consuming the command's whole deadline.

Net effect: the probe runs once per process instead of once per command, and a wedge costs 30 s and one thread instead of hundreds of seconds plus an unbounded thread leak.

## Tests

Added to `tests/tools/test_terminal_pre_guard_deadline.py`:

* `test_guard_wait_is_capped_well_under_a_long_command_deadline` — a 600 s plan yields a 30 s guard wait.
* `test_supervised_gateway_verdict_is_probed_once_per_process` — one probe across calls, re-probe on marker change, and an exception is not cached as `False`.

Disclosure: I could not execute this suite on the affected host — the wedge above blocks running any script there, which is the bug being fixed. The tests are constructed against the existing fixtures in this file (`_plan`, `stubbed_pipeline`) and the diffs are small and local; CI is the first execution.

prs.title: feat(approval): explain silently auto-approved dangerous commands
prs.body:
When a dangerous command runs without a prompt because you approved it earlier, Hermes used to say nothing about why. Now the terminal result says which earlier decision let it through: your `command_allowlist` entry, an "always" approval, or an approval you gave earlier in this session.

**Outcome:** silently auto-approved dangerous commands are explained. Every approval decision is unchanged.

- `tools/approval_provenance.py` (new): builds the `pre_approved` entries (one per finding, each with its own scope, plus the rule for allowlist matches) and writes the one-line note.
- `tools/approval.py`: `_unapproved_findings` is split into `_command_findings` + `_pending_findings`, so the gates keep the findings list and label it once the existing `is_approved` check has passed. The label comes from `_is_permanently_approved`, the same alias lookup the gate uses.
- `tools/approval_floors.py`: `_matching_permanent_allowlist_entry` returns the matching entry; `_command_matches_permanent_allowlist` wraps it.
- `tools/terminal_tool.py`: `_run_approval_guards` turns `pre_approved` into the existing `approval` field of the result.
- Clean commands, yolo, `approvals.mode: off` and unattended passes keep the exact `{"approved": True, "message": None}` result. Schemas and the system prompt are unchanged.

**Live, real `terminal` calls through `model_tools.handle_function_call` under a scratch `HERMES_HOME` (`approvals.mode: manual`, `command_allowlist` in config.yaml):**

| call | main `approval` | this PR `approval` |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` | — | — |
| `chmod 777 …/f1` (allowlisted) | — | Command was flagged (world/other-writable permissions) and auto-approved by the command_allowlist entry `chmod 777 …/f1` in config.yaml. |
| `chmod 777 …/f2` (session-approved) | — | … auto-approved by an approval the user gave earlier in this session. |
| `git reset --hard` ("always") | — | Command was flagged (git reset --hard (destroys uncommitted changes)) and auto-approved by an 'always' approval the user saved earlier. |

**Decisions unchanged:** a base-vs-head oracle over 10,080 cells (14 commands × manual/smart/off × CLI/gateway/cron-approve/cron-deny/unattended × none/session/permanent/mixed/allowlist-glob/allowlist-exact × yolo on/off × deny/once answer × both guards) gave 0 differences in approved/message/status/user_approved/smart_approved/prompt count.

Tests: `tests/tools/test_approval_provenance.py` (mixed session+permanent findings report each scope, through both guards; allowlist note names the rule; a clean allowlisted command stays bare), plus 55 related files, 1469 passed.

prs.title: fix(patch): V4A ops that spell one file two ways validate as one file (no partial write)
prs.body:
A V4A patch can name the same file twice under different spellings (`dup.txt` and `./dup.txt`). The checker treated those as two different files, so the "check everything, then write" patch could pass the check, write the first edit, fail the second, and leave a half-applied change. Now both spellings count as one file during checking.

**Outcome:** on sandbox/remote backends (docker, ssh, modal), a conflicting second edit to an aliased path is refused before any file is written. Legitimate patterns still work under any spelling: sequential edits to one file, and Delete-then-Add.

- The validation overlay in `_validate_operations` is keyed by `_overlay_key()` instead of the raw header string. The key joins the backend cwd and drops `.` segments and duplicate slashes. It keeps `..`, because the kernel resolves `..` after following symlinks: `sub/link/../f.txt` is `real/f.txt` when `link` points into `real/`.
- Host (local) backends were already safe: `patch_tool` rewrites headers to resolved host paths before apply (`fcd5e2cc61f`). This change closes the same gap for non-host backends, where the parser cannot resolve paths.
- **Changed from the original approach:** rejecting every pair of ops on one path would break main's `test_delete_then_add_same_path_still_validates` (the Delete-then-Add rewrite idiom) and multi-op edits to one file. Keying the overlay keeps those, and the alias edit fails validation the same way a same-spelling conflicting edit already did.
- Case and `..` are folded (ntpath) only on a Windows backend: a local env on a Windows host, or a backend whose cwd is a drive path. On a POSIX backend `C:/A.txt` and `C:/a.txt` stay two files. A POSIX backend may or may not be case-insensitive (macOS APFS vs Linux ext4), and the parser can't tell which; folding on a case-sensitive backend would merge two real files. The key is built from the path the backend opens (`ShellFileOperations._expand_path`: `~` to the backend HOME, a host path under a docker workspace mount to the container path). A trailing `/` or `/.` keeps a directory marker, so it never aliases the regular file. Symlink aliases are out of scope for a lexical check (documented in the docstring).

### Real `ShellFileOperations.patch_v4a` on a non-host-declared LocalEnvironment, main vs this branch

| case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `dup.txt` then `./dup.txt`, both `-before` | **Apply phase failed, file = `first`** (partial write) | validation failed, file unchanged |
| `dup2.txt` then absolute path | **partial write** | validation failed, file unchanged |
| `seq.txt` `a→A` then `./seq.txt` `b→B` | applied | applied |
| Delete `re.txt`, Add `./re.txt` | refused ("file already exists") | applied (`fresh`) |
| two distinct files | applied | applied |
| `sub/f.txt` + `sub/link/../f.txt` (`link -> real/deep`), two real files | applied (two files) | applied (two files) |
| `C:/A.txt` + `C:/a.txt` on a POSIX backend | applied | applied |

Through the real `patch` registry handler on the local backend both legs behave the same (refused before write) because of the header rewrite, so that path is unchanged.

Tests: `tests/tools/test_patch_parser_path_aliases.py` (alias cases red on main; symlinked `..` case red on the earlier head); 10 files that reference the V4A parser/applier: 262 passed.

prs.title: feat(session_search): keyword probe recovers recall when the strict match is thin
prs.body:
When you ask session search about an old conversation in chatty words ("what did we decide about the postgres pool"), the search needs every word in one message. If one unrelated message happens to contain all of them, that's the only result you get; this PR adds one extra keyword-only search, ranked below the strict hits, so the real conversation shows up too.

**Outcome:** recall for the "thin strict" case goes from 0/4 to 4/4 at hit@5 in the eval below. Every other query class is unchanged. On a replay of 102 real queries the model issued, the probe fired 2 times and added 1 lower-ranked session each time. **Held for a maintainer decision: see Eval.**

## What changed
- `tools/query_expansion.py` (new): keyword extractor (stop words dropped, max 6 terms, deduped, identifiers like `chat-send` / `app.config` kept, CJK-aware), FTS5-operator detection, and a no-op guard.
- `tools/session_search_tool.py`: `_supplement_thin_results` runs when the strict rows cover fewer sessions than `limit`. It makes ONE `kw1 OR kw2 …` probe and appends the new rows below every strict row. The payload gets `expanded_terms` plus `expansion_note`.
- It never runs for explicit FTS5 syntax (quotes, `OR`/`NOT`/`AND`, `prefix*`) or when every token is already a keyword.
- Relation to main: main's OR-relaxed retry (`hermes_state_search`) already covers the **zero**-hit case. That includes this PR's original headline example ("that thing we discussed about the API"). This PR now covers only the gap that retry leaves: a strict pass that is non-empty but thin.

## Fixes found by the eval (15577163f42)
- **Ordering:** cron demotion used to run over strict and expanded rows together, so a loose interactive OR row outranked a strict cron hit. On the real-query replay this pushed BOTH strict hits out of a limit-3 result. Now each tier is demoted on its own, and strict rows always come first.
- **Silent failures:** a punctuated keyword (`HOME/.config/hermes`) was sanitized to a bare `.config`, which FTS5 rejects. The error was swallowed and the probe found nothing. Such keywords are now quoted as phrases. `not`/`no` are now stop words, because a lone `NOT` sanitizes to an empty MATCH. 32-probe syntax sweep: 2 FTS errors before, 0 after.

## Eval
Every query goes through the real `session_search` registry handler; main = `origin/main` tree, head = this branch. There are 44 queries in 9 classes: conversational, stopword-heavy, synonym, morphological, short/vague, phrase/operator, non-English (de/es/zh/ja), code identifiers, and thin-strict decoys. Filler text was sampled read-only from a real state.db.

| corpus | metric | main | head |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100k msgs, no decoys | hit@1 / hit@3 / hit@5 | 37 / 40 / 41 of 44 | 37 / 40 / 41 (no result list changed) |
| 100k msgs + 5 thin-strict decoys | hit@1 / hit@3 / hit@5 | 31 / 35 / 36 of 44 | 31 / 40 / 41 |
| same | unrelated sessions in top-3 (sum) | 58 | 62 |
| same, thin-strict class only | hit@5 | 0/4 | 4/4 |
| same, latency p50 / p95 (all queries, 2×5 reps, host load ~25) | ms | 10.6 / 105.8 | 14.2 / 99.7 |
| same, thin-strict queries only | p50 / p95 ms | 4.1 / 4.8 | 10.2 / 24.3 |
| 4,000 real messages, 102 real model-issued queries | probe fired | — | 2 (each added 1 session below the strict hits; top-1 unchanged) |
| 25 special-char probes (`$HOME/...`, `col:term`, `NEAR(`, emoji, 3,000-char, empty) | failures | 0 | 0 |

## Tests
`tests/tools/test_query_expansion.py`: 6 behaviour contracts through the real handler. 2 of them fail on the pre-fix head (cron-tier ordering, punctuated keyword). `test_query_expansion.py` + `test_session_search.py`: 72/72 pass. All 6 other test files that import `session_search_tool`: 27/27 pass.

## Infographic

![Session search query expansion — arcade attract screen](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aa5b592/yQbRkDhJzkMCsrU4NgKgg_KviN2jSl.png)

prs.title: fix(patch): recover old_string pasted with read_file's N| line-number gutter
prs.body:
When a model copies text from `read_file` output it sometimes keeps the `42|` line numbers in front of every line, so the patch tool can't find that text in the file and the edit fails. This makes the patch tool notice that exact copy mistake, strip the numbers, and retry, while refusing anything that might edit the wrong place.

**Outcome:** a `replace`-mode patch whose `old_string` is a verbatim read_file paste now applies, with a note telling the model what happened. Code that really contains `N|`-shaped text is never touched.

- Recovery runs after the precise strategies miss on the raw text and BEFORE `block_anchor`/`context_aware` see it (a `41|` prefix barely moves per-line similarity, so those would otherwise accept the raw paste and write the prefixes into the file). It applies only when **every** non-blank line of `old_string` carries a gutter, the numbers are **strictly consecutive** (a blank line may lose its prefix but still uses up a number), and the stripped text is not whitespace-only (`2|\n3|` would otherwise match every line break). A single numbered line qualifies too, but may only match as a whole line (`line_trimmed`), so `2|4` can't land inside `a = 4`.
- Skipped entirely when the file itself contains `N|`-shaped lines, since the pipes may be real content there.
- The stripped text may only match through the exact/normalizing strategies, never `block_anchor`/`context_aware`, so a near-miss guess can't land on a different region.
- A `new_string` with the gutter on some lines but not others is refused, because writing it would put `N|` into the file. Once `old_string` qualifies, a `new_string` with a single numbered line (deleting down to one line) is accepted.
- The reported strategy stays a real `STRATEGIES` name, so `boundary_note` and the edit-match metrics keep working; the gutter correction goes through `correction_notes`.

Rebased onto current main (the matcher now has `correction_notes` and metrics hooks). The original version had real defects, all fixed here: a partly-prefixed `new_string` wrote `1|` into the file; a `+gutter_stripped` strategy suffix made `boundary_note` and metrics skip the edit; stripped text could reach the similarity strategies; and an 80%-consecutive tolerance was based on the idea that search_files output uses `N|`, which it doesn't (it uses `N: `).

### Real `patch` tool (registry handler, real files), main vs this branch

| case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `old_string` pasted as `1\|def foo():\n2\|    x = 1`, new with gutter | `Could not find a match` | applied, file `x = 2`, note emitted |
| new_string partly prefixed (`1\|…`, bare line, `2\|…`) | no match | refused, file unchanged (old PR: wrote `1\|def foo():` into file) |
| YAML list `- 1\|a` / `- 2\|b` file, old `1\|a\n2\|b` | no match | no match, file unchanged |
| numbered markdown `1. one` / `2. two`, old `1\|one\n2\|two` | no match | no match, file unchanged |
| file containing `7\|x` rows | no match | no match (recovery skipped) |
| wrong-region guess (`x = 9` vs file `x = 1`) | no match | no match, file unchanged |
| long code lines, both strings pasted with `41\|`..`43\|` (review case) | **applied via context_aware, `41\|` written into the file** | applied, clean text, note emitted |
| delete a line: new_string `1\|def foo():` only | no match | applied (`x = 1` line removed) |
| one line `42\|    subtotal = …` → `42\|    subtotal = …` (review case) | **applied via context_aware, `42\|` written into the file** | applied, clean text |
| blank gutter lines `2\|\n3\|` → `2\|`, `replace_all` (review case) | no match | no match, file unchanged |
| control: plain `old_string` | applied | applied |

Tests: `tests/tools/test_fuzzy_match_gutter.py` (recovery cases red on main, guard cases green on both); 24 files that reference `fuzzy_find_and_replace`/`patch_replace`: 621 passed. The reviewer's 27-case corpus: every case without a gutter gives byte-identical results on main and this branch.

## Infographic

![Gutter-Stripped Patch Recovery](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aa59806/HOERzw0b_RWZSROwk7DdG_TnYkZlBj.png)

prs.title: fix(agent): request-body byte-cap 400s trigger compression (payload_too_large) instead of failing
prs.body:
Some API gateways reject a request that is too many bytes with a plain "bad request" error. Hermes read that as a broken request and gave up, so a chat full of images stayed stuck forever. Now Hermes recognises these "request too big" messages and shrinks the conversation, the same as it does for the standard 413 error.

**Outcome:** request-body byte-cap rejections that arrive as HTTP 400 (or status-less) classify as `payload_too_large` (retry + compress) instead of `format_error` or token `context_overflow`.

- `agent/error_classifier.py`: `_is_byte_size_limit_message()` needs a request/body/payload-size subject plus an overflow word ("exceed", "too large", "too big"); "content length" counts only when "request"/"bytes" appear as whole words (an SDK-wrapped body's `invalid_request_error` / `request_id` do not count). It lowercases its own input and never matches a response-scoped subject.
- On the 400 path it runs ahead of the invalid-body and token-overflow rules: Novita tags its byte cap `INVALID_REQUEST_BODY`, and Z.AI's "Request size exceeds the limit" used to trip the token rule's "exceeds the limit". It also runs on the status-less message path.
- Tests (new file `tests/agent/test_error_classifier_byte_size.py`): verbatim gateway / Novita / Z.AI bodies, plus field-length, response-size and parameter controls, and the field-length control as a real OpenAI- and Anthropic-shaped `openai.BadRequestError`. All positives red on `origin/main`; all 44 classifier test files green.

Real `openai.BadRequestError` built from an httpx 400 response with each verbatim body, through `classify_api_error`:

| Body | `origin/main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Novita `request body too large, must be less than 20MB` | format_error, no retry | payload_too_large, retry, compress |
| Z.AI `Request size exceeds the limit of {0}` | context_overflow (token remedy) | payload_too_large, retry, compress |
| Gateway `RequestSize(bytes): 34021227, Limit(bytes): 33554432` | format_error, no retry | payload_too_large, retry, compress |
| control `tools[0].description content length exceeds maximum allowed` | format_error | format_error |
| control `response body size exceeds the maximum allowed` | format_error | format_error |
| control `maximum context length is 128000 tokens` | context_overflow | context_overflow |

Composes cleanly with #85031 (same file): `git merge-tree` is conflict-free and both suites pass on the merged tree.

## Infographic

![Byte-size 400s now trigger compression](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab12411/jOUiX0UJ4ZveuG8I4A2Xi_OELKvnLH.png)

prs.title: fix(agent): recover 'is not a multimodal model' image rejections from text-only endpoints
prs.body:
Some self-hosted servers (vLLM and other OpenAI-compatible hosts running a text-only model) answer a request that contains an image with "<model> is not a multimodal model". Hermes didn't recognise that wording, so the turn failed instead of dropping the image and continuing.

**Outcome:** that 400 now goes down the existing "this model rejects images" path: the model is marked image-rejecting, the retry goes out text-only, and the images stay in session history.

- `agent/message_sanitization.py`: add `"is not a multimodal model"` to `_IMAGE_REJECTION_PHRASES` (4xx-gated, matched only once per model).
- `agent/turn_recovery.py::recover_before_classification`: a model is only marked image-rejecting (and retried) when the failed request actually carried an image part. Some 4xx bodies echo the request back, so a user writing "X is not a multimodal model" could otherwise get a vision model marked by an unrelated 400 and lose every later image until `/new`. The guard covers every phrase in the list, not just the new one.
- `tests/agent/test_image_rejection_fallback.py`: one negative test (phrase echoed in the body, no image in the request → no mark, no retry).
- `tests/agent/test_error_classifier_observed.py`: `main` already carried this exact observed body as a `known_failure` xfail keyed on this PR; it is now a plain passing regression test.

### Before / after (LIVE, loopback provider that 400s any image-bearing request; real `AIAgent.run_conversation`, history with one image, `model.supports_vision: true`)

| | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| console | `❌ custom rejected the request and retrying won't help: HTTP 400: glm-5.2-fp8 is not a multimodal model` | `⚠️ Server rejected image content — sending text only to this model; images stay in the session history.` |
| requests (has image?) | `[False, True]` then stop | `[False, True, False]` |
| final | `failed: True` | `'TEXT-ONLY-OK'`, `failed: False` |
| `_image_rejecting_models` | `set()` | `{('custom', 'glm-5.2-fp8')}` |

### Echoed-text false positive (CODE-PATH probe on `recover_before_classification`, before/after the image guard)

| 400 body | request has image? | before guard | after guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| `glm-5.2-fp8 is not a multimodal model` | yes | retry, model marked | retry, model marked |
| `input_value='...llama-3 is not a multimodal model.'` | no | retry, **model marked, later images stripped** | no retry, not marked |

Tests: `test_error_classifier_observed.py`, `test_image_rejection_fallback.py`, `test_fast_mode_auto.py`, `test_reasoning_replay_routes.py` green (49); `scripts/check --only health` 0 blocking.

Relation to #69104: that PR (xAI "Invalid PNG image" / undecodable base64) landed via #97059 as the separate `image_corrupt` path, which strips one attempt and does NOT mark the model. Its phrases and this one don't overlap and don't interact: a corrupt payload says nothing about the model, while "not a multimodal model" is a statement about the model.

## Infographic

prs.title: Bump sugar catalog entry to v3.10.4 (plugin 0.2.0)
prs.body:
## What

Bumps the `sugar` catalog entry from `eade16940789bc1f927af090f8a3b475e537eddd` to `cce143286814dbf828ae89305cde860d706c0a2d` (v3.10.4, plugin version `0.2.0`, [release](https://github.com/roboticforce/sugar/releases/tag/v3.10.4)).

**This is an installability fix, not just a refresh.** The plugin at the current pin declares `sugarai==3.10.1`, whose own metadata requires `click==8.3.1` exactly. That cannot be satisfied alongside Hermes's click 8.5.0 under the union resolution in rule 10, so `hermes plugins install sugar` cannot resolve the dependency. Sugar 3.10.3 relaxed the pin to `click>=8.3.1,<9` ([sugar#80](https://github.com/roboticforce/sugar/pull/80)); this entry now depends on `sugarai>=3.10.3,<3.11`, so it resolves.

New format compliance: the entry now carries an explicit `version` label (required to match the pinned code, per rule 14) and the plugin manifest declares `requires_hermes: ">=0.19"` to match the entry (rule 14 asks for both).

## Commits adopted (`eade169..cce1432`)

- `10ed99a` — fix(hermes-plugin): start background recall and follow the session workspace
- `2fc2bfc` — Bump version to 3.10.4.dev0 for development
- `128df8d` — Prepare release v3.10.4

## What changed in the plugin

- **Per-turn recall now actually runs.** `queue_prefetch()` never started the thread returned by `agent.memory_provider.spawn_context_thread()`. That helper is deliberately unstarted — it only binds the caller's profile contextvars, and every core call site does `.start()` — so the cached recall block was computed on turn 1 and replayed verbatim for the rest of the session. The plugin's headline feature was effectively one-shot.
- **Project memory follows the session workspace.** `initialize()` honours Hermes's `cwd` kwarg instead of `os.getcwd()`, so a Desktop or gateway backend serving several sessions no longer attaches the wrong `.sugar/` project store (or silently promotes to global).
- A malformed `SUGAR_SEARCH_LIMIT` no longer raises out of provider initialization (coerced and clamped 1–20).
- `recall_status()` reports only what the last `prefetch()` injected, instead of a stale count after a trivial prompt injected nothing.
- New `on_session_switch()` rebinds the session id and drops the cached recall block on `/new`, `/reset` and `/branch`.
- New `backup_paths()` exposes the global and project stores to `hermes backup` / `hermes import`.

## Disclosure (rule 13)

Same posture as the existing entry: no network calls and no credentials. The provider reads and writes two SQLite files outside `HERMES_HOME` — `~/.sugar/memory.db` (global knowledge and guidelines) and the nearest `.sugar/memory.db` at or above the session workspace. Both are now reported through `backup_paths()`. `is_available()` imports no network client and performs no network I/O; nothing leaves the machine.

## Validation

- `hermes plugins validate <dir> --install-deps` against Hermes 0.22.7 at the pinned commit: 15/15 checks pass, 0 warnings (`manifest`, `requires_hermes`, `python dependencies`, `capability probe`, declared tools/hooks/middleware, built-in collisions, `security scan`, `no core override`, `desktop surface`, isolation audit).
- `pytest tests/test_hermes_plugin.py`: 27 passed (16 before). 10 of the new tests fail at the previous pin, so the defects are covered.
- No `desktop/` surface, no `register_tool` calls, no core rebinds — `capabilities` stays `provides_tools: []` for the memory-provider tools, as with the other memory entries.

## What does this PR do?

Adds the official optional `multi-session-coordination` skill. It provides a dependency-free SQLite intention board for concurrent Hermes sessions, subagents, bot profiles, and scheduled jobs that need to coordinate access to shared resources.

Version 2.6.1 adds stale-session claim reaping with an explicit heartbeat (the window is configurable via `HERMES_COORD_STALE_S`), rejects malformed session IDs before creating orphan rows, and adds `coord_run.sh` so one-shot shell work always releases its claims. ## Summary

Adds a new bundled skill for managing PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite databases from the terminal using standard CLI tools (psql, mysql, sqlite3).

## Motivation

Database management is a core developer task, yet there's no skill covering it. Developers frequently need to inspect schemas, run queries, export data, and perform admin tasks. This skill provides the agent with structured knowledge for all three major database engines.

## What's Included

The skill covers:

1. **Connecting** — connection strings, environment variables, Docker exec, connection testing
2. **Schema inspection** — list databases/tables, describe columns, show indexes, foreign keys, table sizes
3. **Running queries** — output formatting (CSV, vertical, column mode), running SQL files
4. **Data export/import** — pg_dump, mysqldump, sqlite3 .dump, restore commands
5. **Admin tasks** — create databases/users, grant permissions, kill long queries, vacuum, connection monitoring
6. **Health checks** — database size, active connections, slow queries, integrity checks
7. **Pitfalls** — COPY vs \copy, auth_socket, SQLite locking, pg_dump version mismatch, encoding issues

## How to Test

1. Copy `skills/software-development/database/SKILL.md` to `~/.hermes/skills/software-development/database/SKILL.md`
2. Start a chat: `hermes chat`
3. Ask: "Show me the schema of all tables in my PostgreSQL database"
4. Verify the agent references the skill's schema inspection section

- Linux (Debian-based, Python 3.11)

prs.title: fix(model-picker): an env base_url override must not hide the row serving the session
prs.body:
## Problem

With `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (or any provider's `*_BASE_URL`) pointed at a private gateway that also
has a `custom_providers:` entry, the TUI `/model` picker drops the user's own row:

```
# custom_providers: [{name: SRouter, base_url: https://seavx.ai.id/v1, key_env: ...}]
# ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://seavx.ai.id/v1
no override: custom:srouter (current), openai-codex, anthropic
with override: openai-codex, anthropic     # <- SRouter gone
```

The surviving `anthropic` row advertises Anthropic's static catalog (14 models), none of which exist
on that endpoint, while the entry that knows the endpoint — `key_env`, the configured `model`, the
discovered `/v1/models` catalog — is the one that was hidden.

## Root cause

`record_builtin_endpoint()` records the provider's **effective** endpoint, preferring the
`*_BASE_URL` env override over the static `inference_base_url`, and section 4 of
`_lap_custom_provider_rows()` skips any `custom_providers` row whose URL is in that set
(`model_switch_providers.py`, "keep the built-in, hide the shadow").

That dedup is right for a duplicate of the built-in's *own* endpoint — the existing test
`test_list_authenticated_providers_dedup_honors_base_url_env_override` pins it. It is wrong when the
override merely redirects the built-in: the built-in's catalog then describes an endpoint it no
longer talks to, and the row it hides is the higher-fidelity one.

## Fix

Keep the shadow-hiding rule, but never apply it to the row that is serving this session. Section 4
computes `is_current` before the dedupe and skips the hide when the `custom_providers` group is the
current provider for that endpoint. Nothing else changes: every other duplicate is still collapsed,
and when a built-in and a configured row resolve to the same URL both stay listed.

## What this does not do

- The built-in row keeps its static catalog even while an env override redirects it. Re-labelling
  that row ("Anthropic → via https://…") is a separate change; this PR only stops it from deleting
  the row that is accurate.
- No change to `providers:` (section 3) rows — they were never shadowed by built-ins.

## Tests

New: `tests/hermes_cli/test_user_providers_model_switch.py::test_current_custom_provider_survives_a_builtin_env_override_shadow`
— `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` = the configured endpoint, `current_provider=custom` on it, asserts
`custom:srouter` is listed, current and user-defined, with the `anthropic` row still present.

- With the fix: `9 files, 52 tests passed, 0 failed` (the picker suites:
  `test_list_picker_providers`, `test_configured_builtin_models`, `test_bare_custom_picker_row`,
  `test_authenticated_providers_exhausted_pool`, `test_model_picker_excluded_providers`,
  `test_user_providers_model_switch`, `test_model_picker_secret_scope`, `test_openai_picker_curated`,
  `test_aux_picker_inventory`).
- Sabotage: source reverted to `upstream/main`, test kept →
  `FAILED ... assert 'custom:srouter' in ['anthropic']` — the reported symptom, with the 17 other
  tests in that file still green.
- Independent probe (the reporter's own script against `build_models_payload`): before the fix the
  custom row disappears with the override; after it, `custom:srouter` is present in both runs.
- `python3 scripts/check --base upstream/main` → `14 checks, ok`.

Closes #149233

## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/anaella.yaml`: Anaella for Hermes, a portable Agent Plugins v1 package (`plugin.json` + `mcp.json` + `skills/`, no Python) in the `hermes/` folder of [dahoai/anaella-agent-plugin](https://github.com/dahoai/anaella-agent-plugin/tree/main/hermes), pinned to `928af2f00eb753d717d1d33fd62b3b75aa4935f1`.

It connects Hermes to the work accounts a user linked in Anaella (Gmail, Outlook or IMAP mail, Google and Outlook calendars, Drive, Docs and Sheets, Slack, Search Console, Analytics, Meta and Google Ads, Business Profile reviews, Stripe, PayPal, n8n, a phone number, a meeting bot and 9 social networks) through one MCP server (`find`, `explain`, `do` over the catalog), plus 24 workflow skills (social publishing, comment replies, inbox triage, scheduling, SEO and ads reports, documents and e-signatures, phone calls, meeting notes, automations and more).

**Hermes surfaces used:** root `mcp.json` (one stdio server) and bundled skills. No hooks, middleware, providers, Desktop UI or core changes.

## Disclosures (rule 13)

- **Network calls to a third-party service:** every tool call goes to `api.anaella.com` with the user's `ANAELLA_API_KEY`.
- **Shell command / background process:** Hermes starts the MCP server with `npx -y @anaella/mcp@0.12.0` (pinned version; needs Node.js 20+ and npm). It runs only while Hermes runs it.
- **Credentials:** `ANAELLA_API_KEY` is read from the Hermes profile `.env` through `mcp.json` env passthrough. The plugin stores nothing.
- **Acts in the user's name:** tools can send email and texts, place AI calls, publish posts, edit sheets, share files, change ad campaigns, and send invoices and refunds on accounts the user connected. Some tools are paid from the user's Anaella wallet within the daily spending limit they set. The skills require showing the content and getting a yes before every write; Hermes itself does not enforce this.
- **No telemetry**, no reads outside the plugin's own files.

`requires_env` stays empty like other portable packages (e.g. `touchdesigner`): the key is passed through `mcp.json`, and the README tells the user to set it.

| `apps/desktop/src/i18n/registry.test.ts` | bundled-language count in the picker test 9 → 10 |
| `web/src/i18n/cs.ts` | Czech web dashboard catalog — **761 / 761 English keys** |
| `web/src/i18n/context.tsx`, `web/src/i18n/types.ts` | `cs` registered in the locale map / `Locale` type |
| `locales/cs.yaml` | CLI + gateway catalog, key and placeholder parity with `en.yaml` (**3,515 / 3,515** keys) |
| `locales/cs.tui.yaml` | `hermes --tui` catalog — **1,390 / 1,390** keys from `locales/_keys.tui.json`, positional `{0}` placeholders |
| `website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md` | `cs` (Czech) added to the supported-language list |

Activation: `display.language: cs` in `config.yaml`, `HERMES_LANGUAGE=cs`, or **Čeština** in the desktop language switcher.

### Provenance of the desktop translation

The desktop wording is **not machine translation**. It is the community-reviewed catalog maintained by @zionzangar in [`zionzangar/hermes-czech-locale`](https://github.com/zionzangar/hermes-czech-locale) (`apps/desktop/src/i18n/cs.ts` @ `2338383`, SHA-256 `98796b2dd33bbe3987ca47285fdb399d32b6e3a88b3ac3bf8d3d98223c436674`), which was offered in #56521 but never landed — that PR was closed before his patch arrived. He is credited as a co-author on the commit.

Adoption was filtered entry by entry against the current `en.ts`, because his baseline is hundreds of commits old:

- **4621** of his entries are adopted (key still in `en` today, English source unchanged since his baseline, same value kind, parameters and `${...}` interpolations preserved)
- Keys his catalog carries that no longer exist in `en` are dropped — keeping them fails the excess-property typecheck
- The entries whose English source changed since his baseline, and everything upstream added after it, are translated here
- His translated `settings.fieldLabels` / `settings.fieldDescriptions` are kept via the `defineFieldCopy({...})` pattern the other locales already use, with the 10 entries upstream added later translated on top — so no settings field is left in English

The review shows in wording: buttons use the Czech UI infinitive (“Vybrat”, “Potvrdit”, “Odstranit” instead of “Vyberte si”, “Potvrďte”, “Smazat”), “Reveal in File Explorer” is “Zobrazit v Průzkumníku souborů” instead of “Odhalit v Průzkumníku souborů”, git terms are real words (“Přidat do indexu”, “Vytvořit commit”), `branch` is “větev” (was “pobočka”), `session` is “relace” (was “sezení”), and the English plural branches inside template literals are gone in favour of Czech count forms (1 / 2–4 / 5+).

### Notes for reviewers

- `types.ts` is only a one-line `Locale` union change — the per-locale payloads live in their own modules since the `defineLocale()` refactor, so no shared type or helper is removed.
- Keys missing from a partial locale fall back to English per key; this PR makes that path unreachable for `cs` (no missing keys in any of the three catalogs).
- **Parity is pinned by a test, not by a one-off diff.** `apps/desktop/src/i18n/catalog-completeness.test.ts` runs the runtime key/kind/interpolated-argument checks on every catalog in `COMPLETE_LOCALES`; `cs` is now in that list, so future drift fails CI instead of surfacing in the UI. It earned its keep on the first run: it caught `settings.fieldLabels.voice.recordKey`, a key upstream had renamed and which the type checker accepted because `fieldLabels` is typed `Record<string, string>`.
- The four `settings.localModels.recommendedReason.*` strings are included even though an AST diff cannot see them: the English catalog wraps them in an `as Record<string, string>` cast.
- Remaining values byte-identical to English are language-neutral tokens only (`MCP`, `RAM`, `Model`, `SSH`, URLs, slash commands, placeholder examples). The reviewer independently checked these and found none that read as untranslated English.

## How to Test

```bash
# backend catalogs
python -m pytest tests/agent/test_i18n.py -q          # 57 passed
python -m pytest tests/agent/test_i18n.py tests/agent/test_i18n_layers.py \
                  tests/agent/test_i18n_tui_packs.py tests/agent/test_i18n_languages.py -q   # 89 passed

# desktop i18n
cd apps/desktop && node_modules/.bin/vitest run --project ui src/i18n   # 89 passed (13 files)
node_modules/.bin/tsc -p . --noEmit                   # 0 errors

# web dashboard
cd web && node_modules/.bin/tsc -p . --noEmit         # 0 errors

# lint/format on the touched desktop files
node_modules/.bin/eslint apps/desktop/src/i18n/       # 0 errors
node_modules/.bin/prettier --check apps/desktop/src/i18n/catalog.ts apps/desktop/src/i18n/languages.ts
```

Runtime parity measured at this head (transpile + evaluate + flatten, not an AST-only walk): desktop **5,552 / 5,552**, web **761 / 761**, CLI **3,515 / 3,515**, TUI **1,390 / 1,390**, Bots canonical group bundle **78 / 78 keys in all ten locales** — 0 missing, 0 obsolete, 0 kind/arity mismatches. A raw-source token scan reports 61 "placeholder" hits on the desktop catalog; they are all the English plural branches (`${count === 1 ? '' : 's'}`) that Czech does not keep — calling both sides with dummy arguments shows no lost interpolation.

Manual check: pick **Čeština** in the desktop language switcher (or set `display.language: cs`) and confirm the settings, sidebar and status bar render Czech.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate

- [x] I've run `pytest tests/agent/test_i18n.py -q` and all tests pass (the full `pytest tests/` suite was not run locally; the change touches only the i18n catalogs, `Locale` union and docs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (locale resolution cases in `languages.test.ts`; the desktop catalog is covered by `catalog-completeness.test.ts`)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu 24.04

### Documentation & Housekeeping

prs.title: /undo also reverts the turn's file edits when checkpoints are on (salvage #130589, #144769)
prs.body:
## What this does (ELI5)

Before: `/undo` took back your last message and the model's answer, but any files the model wrote or edited in that turn stayed changed. Getting them back meant a separate `/rollback`.

After: **if you have checkpoints turned on**, `/undo` puts back both the conversation and the files that turn wrote, in one step, and says which files it reverted:

```
undid 5 messages
↶ Reverted 2 file(s) the undone turn wrote: app.py, notes.md
```

Checkpoints stay **off by default**, exactly as on `main`. Turn them on with `hermes config set checkpoints.enabled true` (or `checkpoints: {enabled: true}` in `config.yaml`), or for one session with `hermes chat --checkpoints`. With checkpoints off, `/undo` is conversation-only, as before.

**The default flip that an earlier revision of this PR carried (checkpoints on by default + a v52→v53 config migration) was dropped by maintainer decision:** snapshotting every project the agent touches can cost real disk and time on big trees (numbers below), so it stays opt-in. No config migration, no `_config_version` bump, and the four `origin/main` tests the flip had edited are restored byte-for-byte.

This came from community feedback comparing against other agent TUIs.

## Behaviour (checkpoints on)

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| `/undo` after a turn that edited/created files | Edited files get their pre-turn content back; created files are deleted |
| `/undo N` (N>1) | Reverts every undone turn, back to the state before the oldest one |
| Turn with no file writes | No file is touched |
| File hand-edited after Hermes wrote it | Kept: `↷ Kept your hand edits: … (/rollback can restore them)` (same rule as safe `/rollback`) |
| Another conversation's writes in the same dir | Never touched |
| Checkpoints off | Conversation-only `/undo`, as before |
| `/retry` | Never touches files |
| `/rollback <N>` (rewinds the chat turn too) | Unchanged; skips the file half (the restore already set the tree) |
| Undo the undo | A pre-undo snapshot is taken first, so `/rollback` lists it |

Surfaces: Ink TUI on the shared gateway (new owner RPC `rollback.undo_files` after the `rewind` mutation, run under the session's mutation lock) and on the sidecar (`session.undo`, `/undo` via `command.dispatch`); classic CLI in-process (`undo_last`) and on the shared gateway (both CLI paths); messaging gateway `/undo`; Desktop's `/undo` calls `rollback.undo_files` after its rewind and shows the same lines. Scope: what Hermes' file tools (`write_file`, `patch`) wrote; files changed only by a terminal command stay with `/rollback`.

While doing this I found that the shared-gateway TUI `/undo N` ignored N and always undid one turn. It now uses the Nth-newest user turn, the same as the classic CLI and the messaging gateway.

## How it works

- At the start of each turn the agent loop calls `CheckpointManager.begin_turn(user_row_timestamp, session_id)`. The first checkpoint the turn takes in a project records that tree as the turn's **mark** (`store/turns/<project>.json`). Every agent write is tagged with its turn in the existing write ledger, with a short history kept so an older turn can still be reverted later.
- `tools/checkpoint_turns.revert_turns(mgr, since, sessions)` restores, project by project, the ledger files written at or after `since` by that conversation (compression lineage included). It restores them to the earliest mark at or after `since`, using the same hand-edit and oversize/excluded rules as safe `/rollback`.
- Remote callers name the rewound user row (`target_message_id`). The row has to belong to the caller's conversation, or nothing is reverted.

## Snapshot safety guards

These apply whenever checkpoints are on, so a snapshot never copies a huge tree:
- `/`, `$HOME` **and every parent of `$HOME`** are skipped before any git work (main skipped only `/` and `$HOME`).
- The 50k-entry cap now counts **without** excluded dirs (`node_modules/`, `.venv/`, `.git/`, `dist/`, caches). A small project with a big dependency tree is still checkpointed, and the walk stays cheap.
- Hermes browser profiles (`chrome_cdp_profile/`, `agent-browser-chrome-*/`) are excluded, after #68723. Stores created by older builds get their `info/exclude` refreshed.
- The store never stages itself (salvaged #130589), and oversized files are never staged or hashed (salvaged #144769).

Measured earlier on this PR with the real `CheckpointManager` against a scratch `HERMES_HOME` (no new measurement this round). This is context for why checkpoints stay opt-in: the first snapshot of a large repo is seconds and ~100 MB of store.

| Working dir | Entries | First snapshot | Store growth | Next turn, no changes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| hermes-agent worktree | 23,509 | 3.95 s | +108 MB | 0.97 s |
| `~/Documents` | 16 | 0.21 s | +4.2 MB | 0.04 s |
| `~/Downloads` | 8 | 0.18 s | 0 | 0.04 s |
| `$HOME` | 50,106 | skipped (0.00 s) | 0 | — |
| `~/.hermes` (profile home) | 50,948 | skipped (0.06 s) | 0 | — |
| `/` | — | skipped (0.00 s) | 0 | — |

## Screenshots

All are real terminal runs in tmux with a real provider (Nous inference, sonnet 4.6) and a scratch `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`. Shots 1–4 come from the earlier revision, whose default had checkpoints on. They show the checkpoints-on behaviour this PR keeps, and it is unchanged. Shots 5–6 are this revision's head.

1. Two turns: the agent creates `hello.py` (v1), then patches it to v2 and creates `notes.md`. `!cat` shows the files, and `/rollback` lists the two automatic checkpoints:

![rollback list ](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/9d6a545ad2af23ba0c83ed39bb0c0ade/raw/2c5c4f24d0b60617f9a52b1120463fc8ce82fade/01-rollback-list-fresh-config.png)

2. `/undo` says `Reverted 2 file(s) the undone turn wrote: hello.py, notes.md`. `!cat hello.py; ls` shows `print('hello v1')` with `notes.md` gone. Asked (with no tools) to list my file-changing requests, the model names only the first one, so the conversation really rewound:

![undo reverts files and rewinds](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/9d6a545ad2af23ba0c83ed39bb0c0ade/raw/2c5c4f24d0b60617f9a52b1120463fc8ce82fade/02-undo-reverts-files-and-rewinds.png)

3. `/undo 2` after a turn that created `a.txt` and a turn that edited it and created `b.txt`: both files are gone, back to the state before the older turn:

![undo 2](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/9d6a545ad2af23ba0c83ed39bb0c0ade/raw/2c5c4f24d0b60617f9a52b1120463fc8ce82fade/03-undo-2-reverts-both-turns.png)

4. Classic CLI (`hermes chat`, no `--tui`), checkpoints on: the agent patches `app.py` to v2 and creates `todo.md`; `/undo` (confirm prompt answered `1`) prints `Reverted 2 file(s) the undone turn wrote: app.py, todo.md` and puts the prompt back in the input. On disk afterwards: `app.py` is `print('v1')`, `todo.md` is gone, history is empty:

![classic CLI undo](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/9d6a545ad2af23ba0c83ed39bb0c0ade/raw/c7b269980382e29b50bb00efb97a59c3db34832f/04-classic-cli-undo-reverts-files.png)

5. **This head, checkpoints explicitly on** (`checkpoints: {enabled: true}`), real `hermes --tui`: the agent creates `app.py` (v1), then patches it to v2 and creates `notes.md`. `/undo` reverts both. On disk afterwards: `app.py` is `print('v1')` and `notes.md` is gone:

![tui undo, checkpoints on](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/9d6a545ad2af23ba0c83ed39bb0c0ade/raw/2b633cf6d58f58520aa7d87f801e0dcb06ce8565/05-tui-undo-checkpoints-on.png)

6. **This head, fresh config (no `checkpoints` key, so off)**, same two turns. `/undo` prints only `undid 5 messages` and no file line. On disk afterwards `app.py` is still `print('v2')`, `notes.md` is still there, and no `checkpoints/` store was created:

![tui undo, checkpoints off](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/9d6a545ad2af23ba0c83ed39bb0c0ade/raw/2b633cf6d58f58520aa7d87f801e0dcb06ce8565/06-tui-undo-checkpoints-off-fresh-config.png)

The hosted files' md5s match the runs' own captures.

## Validation

| Rung | What | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 4 live | this head, real `hermes --tui`, `checkpoints.enabled: true`: create → patch + create → `/undo` | `Reverted 2 file(s)`, `app.py` v1, `notes.md` gone (shot 5) |
| 4 live | this head, real `hermes --tui`, fresh config: same turns → `/undo` | conversation-only: `undid 5 messages`, files unchanged, no store created (shot 6) |
| 4 live | earlier revision (checkpoints on): `/rollback` list, `/undo` reverts + rewinds, no-write turn, hand edit kept, `/undo 2`, classic CLI `hermes chat` | pass (shots 1–4) |
| 2 review | `tests/tools/test_checkpoint_turn_undo_review.py` (8): per-file baselines, size-capped file never deleted, 12 patches in one turn, snapshot budget after undo, newer turn not reverted, compaction-restated row, `/diff` never stages oversize, newly excluded browser profile | pass |
| 2 review | `tests/tui_gateway/test_undo_files_profile_scope.py`: sidecar `/undo` reads the session's profile store | pass |
| 3 owner E2E | `tests/gateway/test_session_tui_ops_undo_files.py`: real owner daemon, `rollback.undo_files` with checkpoints on/off, edit + creation reverted, bad id refused | pass; red on base (method missing) |
| 2 store | `tests/tools/test_checkpoint_turn_undo.py`: N>1, creations deleted, hand edits kept, no-edit turn, other conversation, disabled, by-row scoping, `$HOME`/parents skipped, excluded-dir count | pass; red on base (module missing) |
| 1 TS | `ui-tui/src/__tests__/canonicalUndoTurns.test.ts`, `tsc --noEmit`; Desktop `slash-session-commands.test.tsx` | pass |
| contract | the `origin/main` tests the flip had edited (`test_checkpoints_config_fallback.py`, `test_session_tui_ops.py`, `test_session_tui_ops_session_diff.py`, `test_session_commands_session_scope.py`) are byte-identical to `main` (`git diff origin/main -- <path>` empty) and pass | pass |
| suite | `scripts/run_tests.sh`: 23 files (every checkpoint/rollback/undo/rewind test, the restored contract tests, config migrations 52 + unversioned, `test_cli_retry`, rewind-surface invariant): 261 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped | pass |
| check | `scripts/check --only health` + pre-push hook (pinned ruff) | ok |

`hermes_cli/cli_init_mixin.py` is back to `main` as well. The earlier revision read the classic CLI's checkpoint fallbacks from `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, but `main`'s literals (`False`/20/500/10) already equal `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, so that change fixed no drift.

## CI notes
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_runtime_health.py::test_runtime_status_running_pid_validates_live_gateway_record` can flake on `main` when a real process owns PID 12345 on the runner; fixed in #149212.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_win_pty_bridge.py::...test_paste_to_a_program_that_is_not_reading_lands_at_once` (Windows arm64) is the conhost intake-time race fixed in #149179.

## Salvaged / credited
- #130589 (@skyeyesec333): the store never stages itself. 3 commits cherry-picked, authorship kept.
- #144769 (@andyleo41-bot): skip oversized files before staging. 2 commits cherry-picked. The commits arrived with a placeholder author identity, re-attributed to the PR author.
- #68723 (@Thomasp23): browser profiles excluded. Re-implemented on the current list, `Co-authored-by` trailer.
- Read and not taken here (separate scope): #78603 (messaging-gateway text `/rollback` also undoes the turn; the TUI/CLI owner path already does via `history_removed`, so it is left as its own fix), #87214 (TUI honours `checkpoints.enabled`: already on main via #79625), #90986/#10714 (bare `/rollback` across all dirs), #21994 (rollback labels), #147705 (`/diff turn`), #125633 (`exclude_paths` config).

## NOT_COVERED
- Messaging-gateway `/undo` file revert: unit/E2E rungs only, no live platform run.
- Desktop: the `/undo` file half is covered by the vitest rung only, no Desktop live run.
- Classic CLI live leg was run on the earlier revision (shot 4), not re-run on this head. The code path is unchanged; only defaults/docs/migration were removed.
- Windows/macOS: not run. The new code is pathlib + git only.

## Infographic
![undo-reverts-files-checkpoints-on](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab134da/OeBosM0LZ8wPojdisiVLT_dI4zL72p.png)

prs.title: test(win-pty): the 1 MiB paste test no longer races conhost's intake time on a loaded runner
prs.body:
## ELI5

A test pastes 1 MiB into a Windows terminal whose program isn't reading, and checks the paste doesn't sit waiting for that program. It also required the paste to finish within 2 seconds. On the busy arm64 Windows runners, the console host can take more than 2 seconds just to take in 1 MiB, so the test failed on PRs that changed nothing near it. The test now proves the same point by ordering instead of a stopwatch: the program can't read anything until the test makes a file, and the test only makes that file after the write has returned `True`.

## What was failing

`tests/hermes_cli/test_win_pty_bridge.py::TestWinPtyBridgeIO::test_paste_to_a_program_that_is_not_reading_lands_at_once` failed with `TimeoutError` at `asyncio.wait_for(bridge.write(paste, timeout=None), timeout=2.0)` on `OS-specific tests / Windows-only tests (arm64, 1/2)` in three unrelated PRs, all merged onto the same main `ed1afb082`:

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/41940982698/job/126961509414 (touches only `tools/image_source.py`)
- job 126962775808 (run 41941345110), job 126962083480 (run 41941150448)

On main's own push run at that same commit, the lane passed (job 126882583600). The code was identical. The difference was load: the file took 12.9 s and the lane 134 s of runner wall on main, against ~31 s for the file and ~210 s of runner wall on the three red runs (16 parallel files, same `windows-11-vs2026-arm64` image, same pywinpty 3.1.0).

## Mechanism

`WinPtyBridge.write` hands the bytes to pywinpty, which writes them into conhost's input. Conhost buffers that input whether or not the child reads it, so the write never depends on the child. How fast conhost takes in 1 MiB is CPU-bound work, though, and the test's outer `wait_for(..., 2.0)` was a wall-clock budget on it. Under 16 parallel files on a shared arm64 runner, the intake goes past 2 s and the outer timer cancels a write that would have succeeded. The product is fine: its own deadline for `timeout=None` is `_WRITE_TIMEOUT = 10.0` s, and that deadline is the one that tells a wedged ConPTY from a slow one.

## Fix (test only)

- The child now waits for a `released` file before printing, instead of `time.sleep(1.5)`. The test creates that file only after `write()` has returned, so the child cannot have read anything while the write was in flight.
- The write must still return `True`. A write that waited for the child to read could only end at the bridge's 10 s deadline, which closes the PTY and returns `False`, so the intent ("lands without the child reading") is checked by ordering and the return value, not by a stopwatch.
- The outer `wait_for` goes to 30 s. It only catches a hang now. The product's own 10 s deadline is still the bound that matters.
- The child still prints `SURVIVED` after the paste, so the job keeps running after a paste (same check as before).

No product change: the write does not stall on the child, it is slow when the CPU is busy.

## Proof (real Windows arm64)

Temporary workflow on `proof/win-pty-paste-flake` (never merges), `windows-latest-32-arm-core` (32 cores), base = main's test file, head = this PR's test file, each leg running the test 8 times through `scripts/run_tests.sh`. "Loaded" means 64 busy-loop processes running alongside. Run: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/41944011668

| leg | first-attempt failures (CI's `TimeoutError`) | 1 MiB `write()` wall time |
|---|---|---|
| base, idle ([job](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/41944011668/job/126971600193)) | 0/8 | 1.20 s, 1.20 s, 1.20 s |
| base, loaded ([job](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/41944011668/job/126971599929)) | **2/8** | 1.75 s, 1.76 s, 1.76 s |
| head, idle ([job](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/41944011668/job/126971600092)) | 0/8 | 1.18 s, 1.19 s, 1.19 s |
| head, loaded ([job](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/41944011668/job/126971600148)) | 0/8 | 1.59 s, 1.78 s, 1.82 s |

- On an idle arm64 runner the write already takes ~1.2 s, 60% of the old 2.0 s budget. With the runner loaded it takes ~1.8 s, and the test sometimes goes over: main's test timed out on 2 of 8 first attempts. The fixed test passed all 8.
- Every write returned `True`, so the product never stalls on the child; it is only slow when the CPU is busy.
- About the proof driver: its job ends red only because its "PASSED row" regex was wrong (the runner prints per-test rows only when a test fails). The counts above come from the runner's own summaries and `--- retry output ---` banners in each job log.

## Infographic

![win-pty-paste-flake](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab12ea4/U8z7pYjbDNQB5wllyqV-R_RZABtXcT.png)

prs.title: feat(display): diff-aware tool preview truncation
prs.body:
**Diff-aware tool-preview truncation** — full production path, rebased onto current `main`. Fixes #24298.

Show consecutive tool-call previews under the same ~40-char budget by eliding the shared prefix and revealing the **differing tail** (e.g. `cd /p && alpha` vs `… && beta`), instead of a dumb trailing-`...` head-cut that renders distinct commands identically (and then wrongly collapses them into `(×N)`).

### Before / After
Two consecutive distinct commands sharing a long `cd` prefix, at a ~40-char preview cap:

**Before** (dumb head-cut → identical renders → false repeat):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..."
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/path && run al..." (×2)   ← looks like a stall
```
**After** (diff-aware → differing tail shown, no false collapse):
```
💻 terminal: "cd /very/long/project/…&& run alpha"
💻 terminal: "…&& run beta"
```
A genuine repeat of the *same* command still collapses to `(×2)` — dedup keys on raw identity, not on the rendered string.

### @teknium1's review — both points addressed on the production path
- [x] **Dedup keys on RAW identity, not rendered-truncation equality.** `_progress_emit` (gateway/run_turn_runner.py) now takes a `raw_key` derived from raw inputs (`tool_name` + raw command / preview / args) and dedups on that; truncation can no longer make two distinct commands collapse into `(×N)`. `truncate_middle()` stays presentation-only.
- [x] **The terminal/code-block path no longer head-truncates + bypasses.** `_progress_terminal_blocks` uses `truncate_middle` with a threaded `prev` (same as the ordinary preview path) instead of `cmd[:cap-3]+"..."`.

### Changes
- `agent/display.py`: `truncate_middle` / `_truncate_around_diff` / `_head_tail_truncate`; `prepare_tool_preview` gains optional `prev=`.
- `gateway/platforms/base.py::format_tool_event` **and** `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` (`_progress_build_message` / `_progress_terminal_blocks` / `_progress_emit`) thread `prev` + the raw dedup key via new `gateway/turn_context.py` fields.
- Tests: `tests/agent/test_display_truncate_middle.py` + `tests/gateway/test_run_progress_diff_aware.py` — distinct prefix-sharing commands must NOT collapse to `(×N)`; true repeats must (incl. on the `supports_code_blocks=True` path); covers a non-terminal preview. Stale expectations updated. All green.

The original branch was ~24k commits behind; this is a clean re-application onto current `main`.

prs.title: catalog: add myeline — remote MCP memory with receipts
prs.body:
## What the plugin does

Myeline is a remote MCP memory server by Sandbox Group ([myeline.si](https://myeline.si)). This entry lists a **portable Agent Plugins v1 package** that adds:

- **One remote MCP server** — `cortex.myeline.si/mcp` as a `streamable-http` entry, translated into the native remote MCP runtime (OAuth through Hermes's own flow; the token lives in Hermes, not the package).
- **One skill (`myeline`)** — the product's ritual: offer to remember when something durable surfaces (once, only on a yes), search approved memory before answering questions about the user's own history, file the day's card at sign-off, retire stale facts with a written reason. Every AI-proposed fact is staged in a human review queue; nothing goes live without approval.

## Surfaces used

Portable package only: `plugin.json` (v1 schema), `mcp.json` (one `streamable-http` server), `skills/myeline/SKILL.md`. No Python, no hooks, no middleware, no executable code.

## Rule 13 disclosure

- **Network:** one host, `cortex.myeline.si` (the Myeline service), over the user's own Myeline OAuth account. Tool-call payloads (queries and facts the user asks to save) go to that server and nowhere else.
- **Secrets:** none in the package. `mcp.json` carries only the URL; `requires_env` is empty.
- **Telemetry / self-update:** none. No background work, no fetch-and-replace, nothing to update.
- **Trust gate:** deliberately not declared. The server stages every write server-side in a human review queue (approve or retire with a reason), and its tools carry full readOnly/destructive/openWorld annotations — a per-call harness gate would double-prompt the consent the product already enforces. Happy to add `trust: untrusted` if reviewers prefer.
- **Service availability:** `https://cortex.myeline.si/health` returns 200; the product has been live since October 2026.

## Validation

`hermes plugins validate <tree> --install-deps` passes with zero warnings on Hermes v0.22.6, and `hermes plugins doctor` reports clean discovery/manifest/registration. Pinned sha `df6b3c8` is the only commit on the repo. Free tier: up to 200 live facts, search never capped.

The README at the pinned sha renders on the plugin page and documents the trust posture in full.
