issues.title: Model identifier validation suggests lowercasing unknown provider prefixes, breaking case-sensitive upstream model IDs
issues.body:
## Summary

In the model edit sheet, entering a model identifier whose prefix is **not** a picoclaw provider but is an upstream model namespace (for example `ACME/gpt-4o-mini`, where the upstream API is case-sensitive) shows a warning:

> "ACME" should use "acme" — Fix

Clicking **Fix** rewrites the model to `acme/gpt-4o-mini`. With case-sensitive upstream routing this breaks a previously working configuration (401 / provider not found).

## Steps to reproduce

1. WebUI → Models → Edit (or Add) a model.
2. Provider = OpenAI, API Base = an OpenAI-compatible gateway, Model identifier = `ACME/gpt-4o-mini` (the prefix is an upstream namespace, not a picoclaw provider key).
3. The form shows the warning `"ACME" should use "acme"` with a Fix button.
4. Click Fix → the field becomes `acme/gpt-4o-mini`; saving it makes the upstream reject the request because its provider namespace is case-sensitive.

## Expected

- No "should use" suggestion unless the prefix actually maps to a known provider/alias in the provider catalog.
- When a Provider is selected and the field is documented as a full model ID (the field hint says a slash-containing value is kept as a full ID and not re-split), provider-prefix validation should be skipped.
- At minimum, do not offer a destructive one-click "fix" that lowercases an unknown prefix.

## Root cause (v0.3.1, git 2cf030d2)

- `web/frontend/src/components/models/provider-registry.ts:26-28` — `normalizeProvider()` lowercases the input.
- `web/frontend/src/components/models/provider-registry.ts:76-82` — `getCanonicalProviderKey()` returns `aliasMap[normalized] ?? normalized`; for an **unknown** prefix it falls back to the lowercased input instead of returning empty.
- `web/frontend/src/components/models/model-validation.ts:85-91` — the validator treats that fallback as a real alias and emits `models.validation.shouldUse` with `fix: ${alias}/${model}`.
- `web/frontend/src/components/models/edit-model-sheet.tsx:268-269` — the Fix button applies `modelValidation.fix` to the input.

## Proposed patch

```diff
--- a/web/frontend/src/components/models/provider-registry.ts
+++ b/web/frontend/src/components/models/provider-registry.ts
@@ -79,7 +79,7 @@ export function getCanonicalProviderKey(
   const normalized = normalizeProvider(provider)
   if (!normalized) return ""
-  return getProviderAliasMap(backendOptions)[normalized] ?? normalized
+  return getProviderAliasMap(backendOptions)[normalized] ?? ""
 }

--- a/web/frontend/src/components/models/model-validation.ts
+++ b/web/frontend/src/components/models/model-validation.ts
@@ -64,6 +64,17 @@ export function validateModelField(
   const provider = trimmed.slice(0, slashIdx)
   const model = trimmed.slice(slashIdx + 1)
   if (!model) {
     return { level: "error", messageKey: "models.validation.emptyModel" }
   }
 
+  // When a provider is explicitly selected, a slash-containing identifier is
+  // documented as a full model ID for that provider (see modelIdHint) — do not
+  // re-interpret its first segment as a provider prefix.
+  if (selectedProvider) {
+    return {
+      level: "success",
+      messageKey: "models.validation.parsed",
+      messageParams: { provider: selectedProvider, model: trimmed },
+    }
+  }
+
   if (!knownProviderKeys.has(provider)) {
```

Add a regression test with an uppercase upstream namespace (e.g. `ACME/model`) and a lowercase provider alias in the catalog, asserting that no `shouldUse` warning is produced.

## Impact

One click can silently change a working model ID to a different, invalid one; the UI appears to be helping but breaks the configuration. This is more than a cosmetic warning.

## Environment

- picoclaw v0.3.1 (git 2cf030d2), Linux, WebUI

issues.title: WebUI falsely reports "restart required" after gateway hot-reload has already applied the config
issues.body:
## Summary

With `gateway.hot_reload: true`, changing the default model in the WebUI is applied by the gateway within ~2 seconds (confirmed in the gateway log), but the WebUI still shows the "restart required" toast, and `gateway_restart_required` in the gateway status stays `true` until the launcher/gateway is restarted.

This makes operators think the change did not take effect and repeatedly restart the service, interrupting active chats.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Set `"gateway": {"hot_reload": true}` in `~/.picoclaw/config.json` (default is `false`) and restart `picoclaw-launcher.service` once so the watcher is enabled.
2. In the WebUI, change the default model (or edit a model setting) and save.
3. With `gateway.log_level: info`, `~/.picoclaw/logs/gateway.log` shows:
   ```
   🔄 Config file changed, reloading...
    New model is '<new-alias>', recreating provider...
   Provider and config reloaded successfully
     ✓ Provider, configuration, and services reloaded successfully (thread-safe)
   ```
   The gateway PID does not change, and the new model is actually used.
4. The save toast still says "restart required", and `GET /api/gateway/status` returns `gateway_restart_required: true`.

## Expected

- When hot reload has successfully applied the change, the WebUI should not ask for a restart.
- If a change genuinely requires a process restart, the prompt should only appear in that case.

## Actual

The flag stays `true` after every config save, even though `handleConfigReload` already applied the new provider/config in-process.

## Root cause (v0.3.1, git 2cf030d2)

- The flag is computed by the launcher backend, not the gateway:
  - `web/backend/api/gateway.go:807-814` — `gatewayRestartRequiredBySignature(bootSignature, currentSignature, gatewayStatus)`.
  - `web/backend/api/gateway.go:864-868` — `attachToGatewayProcessLocked()` records `gateway.bootConfigSignature` when the launcher attaches.
  - `web/backend/api/gateway.go:1086` — the launcher records it when it starts the gateway.
  - `web/backend/api/gateway.go:1471-1477` — status compares the recorded signature with the current config signature.
- Hot reload happens inside the gateway process (`pkg/gateway/gateway.go:257` starts the polling watcher; `pkg/gateway/gateway.go:586-660` `handleConfigReload` recreates the provider and restarts services). There is no callback to the launcher, so `bootConfigSignature` is never refreshed.
- The WebUI consumes `gateway.restartRequired` directly (`web/frontend/src/components/models/edit-model-sheet.tsx:395-399`, `web/frontend/src/lib/restart-required.ts`).
- `computeConfigSignature()` only covers model/default/streaming, tool enablement and channel settings — all of which `handleConfigReload` applies. It does not include process-level fields such as `gateway.host`/`gateway.port`, so the current flag is effectively only ever about hot-reloadable config.

## Proposed patch

```diff
--- a/web/backend/api/gateway.go
+++ b/web/backend/api/gateway.go
@@ -804,14 +804,20 @@
-func gatewayRestartRequiredBySignature(bootSignature, currentSignature, gatewayStatus string) bool {
+func gatewayRestartRequiredBySignature(bootSignature, currentSignature, gatewayStatus string, hotReload bool) bool {
 	if gatewayStatus != "running" {
 		return false
 	}
 	if bootSignature == "" || currentSignature == "" {
 		return false
 	}
+	// With hot reload enabled, the gateway watcher applies every field covered
+	// by computeConfigSignature (model/tools/channels) in-process. A launcher-
+	// side restart is not required for these changes.
+	// Process-level settings (host/port) are not part of this signature.
+	if hotReload {
+		return false
+	}
 	return bootSignature != currentSignature
 }
@@ -1468,9 +1474,12 @@
 	gatewayStatus, _ := data["gateway_status"].(string)
 	currentConfigSignature := computeConfigSignature(cfg)
+	hotReload := cfg != nil && cfg.Gateway.HotReload
 	gateway.mu.Lock()
 	bootConfigSignature := gateway.bootConfigSignature
 	gateway.mu.Unlock()
 	data["gateway_restart_required"] = gatewayRestartRequiredBySignature(
 		bootConfigSignature,
 		currentConfigSignature,
 		gatewayStatus,
+		hotReload,
 	)
```

Alternative (more robust long-term): have the gateway publish an "applied config signature" (pid file field or health endpoint), update it on every successful `handleConfigReload`, and have the launcher compare the current config against that value instead of its boot-time value.

## Verification after patch

1. Enable `hot_reload`, restart once.
2. Change the default model in the WebUI and save.
3. The toast should be the normal "saved" success message; `gateway_restart_required` should be `false`.
4. Switch back and repeat.

## Environment

- picoclaw v0.3.1 (git 2cf030d2), Linux, WebUI
- `gateway.hot_reload: true`

issues.title: Add Android API 19 support for x86_32 and x86_64 architectures
issues.body:
## 🎯 The Goal / Use Case

Expand PicoClaw's Android compatibility to cover legacy devices and emulators running **Android 4.4 (API 19)** on **x86_32 (32-bit)** and **x86_64 (64-bit)** architectures. 

Many older TV boxes, tablets, and single-board computers (SBCs) still in use today rely on x86-based Android builds (e.g., Intel Atom or AMD APUs) with API 19. Furthermore, x86 Android emulators are widely used for testing and development. Providing pre-built binaries or APKs for these targets would fulfill the project's goal of being a truly lightweight AI assistant that runs on almost any hardware. 

## 💡 Proposed Solution

Provide dedicated release artifacts (standalone binaries or APK builds) for the following targets:
- `android/386` (x86_32)
- `android/amd64` (x86_64)

These builds should be compiled with a minimum API level of 19.

## 🔧 Potential Implementation (Optional)

- **Go Cross-Compilation**: Since PicoClaw is written in Go, adding these targets to the build matrix (e.g., in `.goreleaser.yaml` or the Makefile) is straightforward:
  - `GOOS=android GOARCH=386 GOARM=` (for x86_32)
  - `GOOS=android GOARCH=amd64 GOARM=` (for x86_64)
- **CGO/NDK**: Ensure any C dependencies (if present) are compiled using the Android NDK with `APP_PLATFORM=android-19`.
- **Binary Size**: The current build is already very small (~10MB); x86 builds should remain similarly lightweight.

## 🚦 Impact & Roadmap Alignment

- [x] This is a Nice-to-Have / Enhancement
- [ ] This is a Core Feature
- [ ] This aligns with the current Roadmap

**Justification**: While modern Android devices are predominantly ARM64, the x86 Android ecosystem (especially for old TV boxes and emulators) is still active. This feature would significantly expand the user base and align with the project's "runs anywhere" philosophy. 

## 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Running via Termux**: The current Termux guide only supports ARM64 devices. Termux on old x86 Android builds is often unstable and not officially supported.
- **Using the current APK**: The current APK requires a minimum of Android 7 (API 24) and is built for ARM64, making it incompatible with API 19 x86 devices.

## 💬 Additional Context

- **Existing 32-bit limitation**: A related issue (#2954) already reports that 32-bit Android is not supported. This request extends that to the x86 architecture.
- **Low resource footprint**: PicoClaw is known for using less than 10MB of RAM. It is an ideal candidate for reviving extremely old x86 Android hardware (e.g., first-generation Intel TV sticks).
- **Testing**: I am willing to test the binaries on an x86_32 Android 4.4 emulator and an old x86_64 TV box if the builds are provided.

issues.title: Security: a failed approval-hook re-initialization during reload leaves the gateway serving with tools ungated
issues.body:
## Summary

PicoClaw supports process approval hooks: before a tool runs, the gateway asks a hook whether the call is approved, and a hook that denies the call produces `exec_skipped`. When the gateway reloads (the `/reload` channel command or a configuration reload), it tears down the old hook and re-initializes the configured hooks. If re-initialization fails, the agent records a warning but the gateway still reports the reload as successful and continues serving with no hooks mounted. Every subsequent tool call then bypasses the approval decision: the built-in `exec` tool runs the command with no approval record, and the operator sees only a warning line followed by "reloaded successfully". The failure is not a transient denial: the gate is absent until the next successful reload or restart.

## Details

### Affected component

`pkg/agent/agent.go` (hook mount and reload), `pkg/agent/hook_mount.go` (hook initialization), `pkg/agent/pipeline_execute.go` (tool execution), `pkg/gateway/gateway.go` (reload completion).

### Vulnerable code

`pkg/agent/agent.go:454-459` and `:485`:

```go
al.hookRuntime.reset(al)
configureHookManagerFromConfig(al.hooks, cfg)
if err := al.ensureHooksInitialized(ctx); err != nil {
    logger.WarnCF("agent", "Configured hooks failed to reinitialize after reload",
        map[string]any{"error": err.Error()})
}
...
logger.InfoCF("agent", "Provider and config reloaded successfully",
    map[string]any{
        "model": cfg.Agents.Defaults.GetModelName(),
```

### Root cause

The reload path treats "hooks failed to reinitialize" as a warning, not as a reload failure. The old hook is already unmounted, the new set is empty, and the gateway publishes a successful reload. The tool pipeline consults the hook manager, finds no approval hook, and proceeds. There is no fail-closed state, no refusal to serve, and no health signal; the warning is the only trace.

### Attack path

1. A deployment uses a process approval hook as its tool gate; the hook denies `exec` calls.
2. The hook becomes unavailable at reload time: its binary is missing, it fails to start, or its configuration is invalid.
3. The operator triggers `/reload`; the gateway unmounts the old hook, fails to mount the new one, logs a warning, and still reports the reload as successful.
4. The gateway continues to accept messages; a user or an agent-driven request causes the LLM to emit an `exec` tool call.
5. The tool pipeline finds no approval hook and executes the command.
6. The operator sees no denial, no `exec_skipped` event, and no error; the command has already run.

### Affected deployments

Deployments that use process approval hooks and reload configuration at runtime. The fault is local (the hook binary or its startup is broken at reload time); the report does not claim a remote way to remove the hook, but the consequence is remote: any user or agent that can drive the gateway can execute ungated tools after the failed reload.

### Remediation

When hook re-initialization fails during a reload, fail closed: keep the previous hook set mounted, abort the reload with an error, or mark the session as degraded and refuse tools that require approval. Surface the failure through the reload response and health/status, not only a log line.

## Proof of concept

Run the gateway with a process approval hook that denies `exec` (`exit 1`), and drive the agent with a scripted LLM that emits:

```json
{"tool":"exec","action":"run","command":"touch /tmp/exec_marker"}
```

Baseline: the hook denies the call; the agent logs `agent.tool.exec_skipped`, and `/tmp/exec_marker` is absent.

```bash
./picoclaw   # gateway with hooks/approval-gate configured
# send: "run the tool"
# expected: exec_skipped; no marker
```

Fault: make the hook unavailable (remove `hooks/approval-gate`, or make it fail to start), then send `/reload` and the same message.

```bash
rm hooks/approval-gate
# send: "/reload"
# gateway log: "Configured hooks failed to reinitialize after reload"
#              "Provider and config reloaded successfully"
# send: "run the tool"
# expected: exec runs; /tmp/exec_marker exists; no exec_skipped
```

Expected difference: with the hook present the call is denied and no marker appears; with the hook unavailable at reload time the same call executes and creates the marker, while the reload reports success. The only changed variable is the hook's availability during reload.

## Impact

Any tool that shares the `ApproveTool` decision point (the observed `exec`; file writes and cron command jobs use the same gate) runs without approval after one failed reload. The gateway keeps serving and reports success, so the operator has no reason to stop or investigate. A user or an agent driven by untrusted content can therefore execute commands the approval hook was meant to block.

## Affected products

- Ecosystem: other (Go binary; GitHub releases)
- Affected versions: `<= 0.3.1`
- Patched versions: (none)

## Weaknesses

`CWE-636` (Not Failing Securely), `CWE-693` (Protection Mechanism Failure).

## Reporting note (why this is a regular issue)

I could not find a `SECURITY.md` or a private vulnerability reporting entry in this repository, so I am filing this as a regular issue rather than a private report. If there is a preferred private channel that I missed, please let me know and I will be glad to move the report there. I have not published this elsewhere, and I am happy to provide any additional detail or to test a patch.

prs.title: fix(config): prevent default ModelList from overriding user config
prs.body:
## Summary

- 修复 issue #680：当用户配置中省略 api_base 时，不再错误继承默认值
- 首次启动的新用户仍会获得完整的默认模型列表模板
- 部分配置的用户不再遇到 api_base 被错误覆盖的问题

## Description

当用户在配置文件中只提供 `model_name` 和 `api_key` 但省略 `api_base` 时，系统返回错误：

```
Status: 401 Body: {"error":{"code":"401","message":"令牌已过期或验证不正确"}}
```


这是因为 Go 的 JSON 解析器在解析用户配置时，会重用 `DefaultConfig()` 中预填充的 ModelList 数组相同索引位置的默认值。

### 修复内容

1. **pkg/config/defaults.go**:
   - 将 `DefaultConfig()` 中的 `ModelList` 设为 `nil`
   - 新增 `GetDefaultModelList()` 函数返回默认模型列表模板

2. **pkg/config/config.go**:
   - 在 `LoadConfig()` 中添加逻辑：仅当 ModelList 和 legacy providers 都为空时才使用默认模板

这样确保：
- 新用户首次启动时获得完整的默认模型列表
- 部分配置的用户不会被默认 ModelList 覆盖
- 只有用户显式提供配置才会被使用

prs.title: WIP: feat: base multi-agent collaboration framework & shared context
prs.body:
## 📝 Description

**WIP** — Base multi-agent collaboration framework with shared context pool, agent handoff, and discovery tools.

Builds on top of the merged PRs #213 (provider protocol refactor) and #131 (model fallback chain + multi-agent routing) to add:

- **Blackboard** — Thread-safe shared key-value context pool (`pkg/multiagent/blackboard.go`) for inter-agent data sharing with scoped entries (author, scope, timestamp)
- **BlackboardTool** — LLM-callable tool for read/write/list/delete on the shared context
- **Agent Handoff** — Synchronous delegation between agents via `ExecuteHandoff()` with automatic context propagation through the blackboard
- **HandoffTool** — LLM-callable tool that resolves target agent, writes context, builds system prompt, and delegates via `RunToolLoop`
- **ListAgentsTool** — Discovery tool listing all registered agents with ID/Name/Role
- **AgentResolver interface** — Decouples `pkg/multiagent` from `pkg/agent` to avoid circular imports
- **AgentLoop integration** — Blackboard snapshot injection into system messages, per-session blackboards via `sync.Map`, tools auto-registered when >1 agent configured
- **Config extensions** — `Role` and `SystemPrompt` fields on `AgentConfig` and `AgentInstance`

### Architecture decisions
- Zero overhead for single-agent setups (multi-agent tools only registered when `len(registry.ListAgentIDs()) > 1`)
- `registryResolver` adapter bridges `AgentRegistry` → `multiagent.AgentResolver` at the integration boundary
- Blackboard entries carry authorship metadata for audit/debugging

prs.title: fix(discord): bump discordgo fork past the gateway handshake deadlock
prs.body:
## 📝 Description

The Discord channel can go permanently deaf: the bot stays "connected", but nothing comes in or goes out, no heartbeat is sent, and nothing is logged. The cause is a deadlock in the pinned `discordgo` fork commit (`yeongaori/discordgo-fork@e8e546f`, 2026-03-19). The fork fixed it a week later. This PR moves the pin forward and adds a regression test.

**The deadlock.** `Session.Open` holds `s.Lock()` (deferred unlock) for the whole handshake. If Discord's first packet after IDENTIFY/RESUME is Op 9 (Invalid Session) or Op 7 (Reconnect), `onEvent` handles it by calling `CloseWithCode`, which calls `s.Lock()` again. `sync.RWMutex` isn't reentrant, so `Open` never returns. The heartbeat goroutine waits behind it, and the reconnect loop never runs. Op 9 is Discord's normal reply to a failed resume, so a network blip followed by a resume is enough to trigger it.

Goroutine dumps from two real wedges on one bot, same stack both times (`wsapi.go:186 → 631 → 931`):

```
sync.(*RWMutex).Lock
github.com/bwmarrin/discordgo.(*Session).CloseWithCode(0xc0002d4708, 0x3f4)   // 1012, wsapi.go:931
github.com/bwmarrin/discordgo.(*Session).onEvent(...)                           // Op 9 branch, wsapi.go:631
github.com/bwmarrin/discordgo.(*Session).Open(...)                              // holds s.Lock(), wsapi.go:186
github.com/bwmarrin/discordgo.(*Session).reconnect(...)
github.com/bwmarrin/discordgo.(*Session).heartbeat(...)   // second dump: (*Session).listen
```

**The fix** was upstreamed to the fork as `16ef341` ("Fix deadlock (#5)", 2026-03-26). `onEvent` now returns `errReconnect` for Op 7 and Op 9, and the caller reconnects once `Open` has released the lock. This PR moves the `replace` to the fork's current head, `a10ba9c`, which also includes the fork's later fixes for the gateway resume loop (`6f7dfa3`) and silent gateway stalls (`a10ba9c`). The only change on our side is `go.mod`/`go.sum` plus a test.

**Regression test.** `pkg/channels/discord/discord_gateway_test.go` runs a fake gateway that answers IDENTIFY with Op 9 or Op 7, and checks that `Open` returns and the session lock is released afterwards. It uses its own `websocket.Dialer`, because the default dialer's `http.ProxyFromEnvironment` caches the environment on first use and would break `TestApplyDiscordProxy_*`.

| pin | result |
|---|---|
| `e8e546f` (current `main`) | both cases FAIL: `session.Open() never returned: deadlocked on the session lock` |
| `a10ba9c` (this PR) | both cases PASS in under 1 ms |

## 🗣️ Type of Change
- [x] 🐞 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 📖 Documentation update
- [ ] ⚡ Code refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)

## 🤖 AI Code Generation
- [x] 🤖 Fully AI-generated (100% AI, 0% Human)
- [ ] 🛠️ Mostly AI-generated (AI draft, Human verified/modified)
- [ ] 👨‍💻 Mostly Human-written (Human lead, AI assisted or none)

Written with Claude Code. The analysis comes from the goroutine dumps above, and the fix and test were verified red then green and on a real bot (below). Opened as a draft so a human reviews it first.

## 🔗 Related Issue

None filed. The description above covers it. I can open an issue if you'd like to track it separately.

## 📚 Technical Context (Skip for Docs)
- **Reference URL:** https://github.com/yeongaori/discordgo-fork/commit/16ef34198ced6c051880166ecbcda6fc9cc7f011 (fork fix), https://discord.com/developers/docs/events/gateway#resuming (Op 9 after a failed resume). The same deadlock is still open in upstream `bwmarrin/discordgo`: https://github.com/bwmarrin/discordgo/pull/1694 (unreviewed since 2026-02-09), so dropping the fork for upstream wouldn't fix this either.
- **Reasoning:** The bug and its fix are in the dependency, and picoclaw already pins that fork with a `replace`, so moving the pin is the smallest correct change. The test guards that pin from regressing, because a future fork bump could bring the deadlock back without anyone noticing. Release branches may want this cherry-picked: `v0.3.1` has the bug.

## 🧪 Test Environment
- **Hardware:** PC (Intel Xeon W-3265, x86_64)
- **OS:** Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, picoclaw in a rootless Podman container (v0.3.1 + this pin)
- **Model/Provider:** N/A (gateway-level change)
- **Channels:** Discord (also running Slack, unaffected)

Checks, run in `golang:1.25` to mirror `.github/workflows/pr.yml`:
- `go test -tags goolm,stdjson ./...`: pass as a non-root user. As root, `pkg/evolution`'s `TestRuntime_RunColdPathOnce_DraftSaveFailureRollsBackAppliedSkill` fails, because it needs an unwritable path. That's the same on `main` and unrelated.

- `golangci-lint fmt --diff`: no diff in changed files. It flags `pkg/providers/bedrock/provider_bedrock.go`, which is already on `main`.
- `govulncheck`: results identical to `main`'s.
- `go vet`, `go mod verify`, `scripts/lint-docs.sh`, `web/backend` tests: pass.

<details>
<summary>Real bot: gateway outage, failed resume answered with Op 9, clean recovery</summary>

Outbound 443 was blocked in the container's network namespace for 150 s, then restored. On reconnect, Discord rejected the resume with Op 9, the sequence that wedged the old pin. The new pin re-identified and recovered without a restart:

```

22:18:03 INF calling reconnect() now

22:20:10 INF Gateway session is not resumable, discarding its information
22:20:10 ERR error reconnecting to gateway, reconnect required by gateway
22:20:14 INF trying to reconnect to gateway

22:20:15 INF We are now connected to Discord, emitting connect event
22:20:15 INF successfully reconnected to gateway
[test] container restarts: 0
```

prs.title: fix(anthropic): make claude-haiku-5-5 (thinking-always models) work with token credentials
prs.body:
## Problem

Every token-based Anthropic call to a thinking-always model (e.g. `claude-haiku-5-5`) fails with:

```
status=400 invalid_request_error: "temperature" is deprecated for this model
```

Repro: model entry with `provider: anthropic`, `auth_method: token` (API key stored in `auth.json`), any Claude 5 model. Reproduced on picoclaw 0.3.1 / Termux armv7; current `main` has the same code path.

## Root cause

Two separate bugs on the token path (`oauth.ClaudeProvider`):

1. The wrapper does not implement `ThinkingCapable`, so `applyTurnThinkingOptions` treats the provider as not thinking-capable, **never injects `thinking_level`**, and the inner SDK provider then always sends an explicit `temperature`. Claude 5 family models reject an explicit `temperature` with 400.
2. `buildParams` sends `temperature` unconditionally, so even when thinking injection is fixed or absent, thinking-always models still get a `temperature` they reject.

## Fix

- `pkg/providers/oauth/claude_provider.go`: delegate `SupportsThinking()` to the inner SDK provider so `thinking_level` is honored for token/OAuth credentials as well.
- `pkg/providers/anthropic/provider.go`: omit `temperature` for models that have thinking enabled by default and reject an explicit one (`haiku-5`, `sonnet-5`, `opus-5`, `opus-4-5`, `sonnet-4-5`).

## Verification

- On-device (Termux armv7, picoclaw 0.3.1 + these patches): `picoclaw agent -m ...` against `claude-haiku-5-5` with `thinking_level: adaptive` now succeeds (verified with a real API round-trip).
- `go test ./pkg/providers/... ./pkg/agent/...` passes with tags `goolm,stdjson,whatsapp_native`.

Note: Claude 5 models only accept `thinking.type: "adaptive"` (not `enabled` + `budget_tokens`); that is a config-side concern and unaffected by this change — with the wrapper fix in place, `thinking_level: adaptive` now actually reaches the API.

## AI assistance disclosure

Per CONTRIBUTING.md ("Disclosure Is Required"): this change is AI-assisted. The patches were written by an AI coding agent (Hermes Agent) on the contributor's machine, tested on-device (Termux armv7) and with the project test suite, and reviewed, submitted and taken responsibility for by the human contributor (sebbY82).

issues.title: Fix add_reaction: 3-part platform ID breaks Telegram setMessageReaction

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
## Symptom
`add_reaction` silently fails in group chats. Tool returns success but no reaction appears in Telegram.

## Root cause (diagnosed Apr 26 2026)
Agent stores platformId as 3-part: `74404502:233:ag-XXXX` (chat_id:msg_id:agent_group_id). The Telegram adapter's `MESSAGE_ID_PATTERN = /^([^:]+):(\d+)$/` is strict 2-part — no match on 3-part. Falls into parseInt fallback which extracts `74404502` (the chat_id, not message_id). Telegram rejects with `Bad Request: message to react not found`.

Same bug affects `edit_message` and `delete` via the same `decodeCompositeMessageId` (adapter lines 663 + 729).

## Fix
In `src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.ts` (~line 365), strip the agent suffix before calling the adapter:
```ts
const tgMessageId = (content.messageId as string).replace(/:ag-[^:]+$/, '');
await adapter.addReaction(tid, tgMessageId, content.emoji as string);
```
Same one-liner needed for edit_message and delete paths. Rebuild + restart.

## Acceptance
- `add_reaction` works in group chats (not just DMs)
- `edit_message` and `delete` also work in group chats
- Regression test covering 2-part and 3-part ID formats

prs.title: fix(setup): make setup diagnostics complete, loss-proof and free of user text
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes setup diagnostics complete, loss-proof and free of user text.

- **Context**: every event (bash and Node) now carries `nanoclaw_version`, `release_channel`, `run_id` and `arch`. The run id is exported, so retries and the `sg docker` re-exec join the same run.
- **Lost events**: the Node emitter used an un-awaited `fetch`. Events sent right before `process.exit()` (such as `uninstall_executed`) or before a `spawnSync` longer than 3 s never left. `emit()` now hands the payload to a detached `curl`, like the bash side, with `fetch` as the fallback.
- **User text**: `setup_aborted.reason` sent the failure message, which can hold agent names and local paths. It is now a fixed `reason_code` per failure branch. `channel_other_named` sends a typed name only if it is on a fixed list of public channel names, else `unknown`.

## Related work

No issue. Found in a review of setup diagnostics; only setup telemetry and its tests change.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `vitest run setup/` → 77 files pass. New: `diagnostics.test.ts`, `initial-setup.test.ts`, and `reason_code` checks in the runner and channel-skill tests.
- `diagnostics.sh` under `/bin/bash -euo pipefail` (bash 3.2) with a fake curl → props right, `.env` channel read, run id inherited, opt-out sends nothing.
- Node 26.13, real `emit()` with curl pointed at a local server: emit then `process.exit()`, and emit then a 5 s `spawnSync`, both arrive. Both were lost with the old `fetch`.

prs.title: fix(telegram): render links with an underscore in the URL as plain text
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops Telegram dropping any reply that contains a link with `_` in its URL. That covers email addresses like `first_last@example.com` and web URLs like `...?agent_name=x`.

- **Problem**: the adapter's GFM parser autolinks bare emails and URLs as `[text](url)` and does not escape `_` inside the URL. Telegram rejects the whole MarkdownV2 message ("Can't find end of Italic entity" / "Can't find end of a URL"), and delivery is dropped after retries. We first hit it with email addresses. It then showed up with a gateway connect link (`...&agent_name=olivia`): every reply carrying that link was dropped, so the agent looked silent to the user.
- **Fix**: before rendering, any link whose URL contains `_` is replaced by plain text. Autolinks and `mailto:` links become their text. A labelled link keeps its label and shows the URL after it in parentheses. The text is escaped normally (`first\_last@example\.com`), and Telegram clients still linkify it.
- **Scope**: only links with `_` in the URL change. All other links render as before.

## Related work

No issue. The fix is small and confined to the Telegram adapter, and regression tests cover it.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/documentation`

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The `channels` side of #4168: text-command answers and the web chat wait for the host too.

- **Problem**: WhatsApp (Baileys), iMessage and the local web chat answered a pending question themselves before the host decided. They closed the question and posted "✅ Approved by <name>" even when the host refused, so the approver could no longer answer.

prs.title: fix(approvals): resolve a clicked card only after the host accepts the click
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

A clicked approval card now changes only after the host accepts the click.

- **Problem**: the channel edited the card (buttons removed, "✅ Approved by <name>") before the host checked who clicked. When the host refused the click, the request stayed pending, but the card showed it as decided and had no buttons left.
- **Fix**: response handlers return what a click did (`accepted`, `refused`, `closed` or `ignored`), and `onAction` passes it back. Both click transports (Chat SDK and Discord's forwarded gateway events) run one pipeline: decode the option, hand it to the host, then show only what the host did. A refused click keeps the card and its buttons; the clicker gets a private note where the channel has one (Slack, Google Chat, Teams, Discord flags 64). `closed` (the request's session, event or target is gone) shows "No longer available". Discord acks at once (type 6) and removes the buttons only after acceptance. Clicks on one card run one at a time, display included; a click that stalls past 10 s lets the next go ahead but can't draw over it.
- **Host-owned card check**: channel registration moves its question to a second card with new options (the agent choice). The host now counts only a click from the card the question lives on (migration 029: nullable `card_message_id`, no backfill; NULL = unchecked, as before), so an old card or a copy can't resolve against the new options. A failed agent-choice delivery puts the question back on the first card. An unknown-sender approval claims its row and adds the member in one transaction, so two racing responses decide once.
- **Each decision once, reported early**: question answers, channel connect and Reject, and unknown-sender approvals claim their row first (with their writes in one transaction where they share the central DB), so two racing clicks decide once. Every deciding path reports acceptance right after its claim, before the agent is woken or a message replayed; a question answer that can't be written closes the question (logged) rather than reviving it for a second answer. A plain Reject on a card whose admin chose "Reject with reason…" is ignored, so the reason isn't lost; "Reject with reason…" arms capture before its prompt is sent and is reported only once armed; if the prompt can't be sent, the request is rejected without a reason. A name reply for a new agent and a Connect or Reject click on the same registration take turns, so the channel is wired once; once it is decided, its name prompt is dropped and the replayed message reaches the agent. An accepted click stays with its handler even if that handler's later work throws. A decision that outlasts the 10 s hold still draws over a card that shows none.
- **Skill seam**: a render may add `afterClick({ outcome, selectedOption, userId, actorName, messageId, platformId, threadId })`, returning a card to draw (drawn as returned, whatever the outcome) and a private note, or nothing for the default. A skill decides in a prepended response handler and draws through its render resolver, without decoding options or dispatching. Clicks carry the card's thread; a Discord click's channel is the encoded one (a thread by its parent). A handler that still returns `true` compiles and owns the click, but shows nothing and logs a warning (such handlers returned `true` for refused clicks).
- **Out of scope**: the native WhatsApp, iMessage and local-web text-command paths on `channels` (their own PR, which also sets WhatsApp Cloud's `cardMessageIdOf` to the card a reply quotes). Non-deciding actions (`registerQuestionActionHandler`) on Discord's forwarded path: a modal can't open after the type-6 ack.

## Related work

Stacked on #4147 (base `fix/approval-card-full-action` @1e2a2291); merge after it. The bug is older than #4147 and affects every channel. No public issue.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run` -> 3927 pass; 3 fail the same way without this change (`setup/gateways/selection` expects a pnpm WARN this machine doesn't print; `scripts/update` e2e timeouts under load, pass alone).
- Tests: a refused click leaves the row pending, the buttons in place and no "Approved by" text; an approver's click still resolves the card; a second click waits for the first; afterClick card/note on both transports; `closed` shows "No longer available"; after the agent choice an old card or a copy is ignored while the new card works; racing clicks decide once (unknown sender, question answer, channel connect and Reject); a plain Reject while a reason is awaited is ignored and the reason still reaches the agent; a reason prompt that can't be sent rejects plainly; a name reply racing a Connect click never leaves an agent unconnected, and the replayed message reaches the agent; acceptance is reported before a wake that hangs; gateway approvals still fail closed.
- `chat-sdk-bridge-late-click.test.ts` (end to end through the real approvals handler, Chat SDK and Discord paths): an approval still being applied, then a late Deny on the same card and on a copy: one edit only, the action runs once.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

A hung send or channel no longer silences a session until restart, or slows other sessions.

- **Problem**: sends were awaited with no limit. One hung send blocked its session silently, and the shared poll tick waited on it.
- **Fix**: after 60 s a send is parked and logged (`Message delivery passed its deadline`), never re-sent while it might still land. A late failure, or no answer after 60 min, is retried. A tick waits at most 5 s per session. Discord acknowledgements time out after 10 s.
- **Limits**:
  - At most 8 background drains (kept on Ethan's call): more hung sessions slow ticks by about 60 s per 8.
  - A send landing after the 60 min give-up posts twice (3 sends at most).
  - A parked message can arrive after later ones. A session holds at most 3 parked sends.
  - A late landing can't change a row already marked failed; a mailbox error during a give-up can leave a stale attempt row.

Refs #2665 (instance A). Overlaps #3059. Not covered: backoff, idempotency keys.

prs.title: fix(setup): restart the host after provider-auth installs host code or a re-auth changes its settings
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

`setup --step provider-auth <provider>` now restarts the running host after it installs a provider, so the first chat on the new provider works.

- **Problem**: provider-auth installed the payload and rebuilt the image, but the service kept running the `dist/` it loaded at start. The payload adds host code (provider contracts and registrations under `src/`), so the first Codex turn failed until a manual rebuild and restart. Found in the OneCLI 1.45 e2e matrix for #4094 (row P3); main behaves the same.
- **Fix**: `applyProviderSkill` reports `hostChanged` (the apply wrote `src/` or `.env`; `--refresh` logs every copied file as written, so it always restarts). provider-auth then runs `pnpm run build` and `setup/lib/restart.sh` right after the image build. That is before auth, because a failed sign-in exits the process and a re-run only re-authenticates. Any run, a re-auth of an installed provider included, restarts after auth when auth changed `.env` (OpenCode saves its endpoint, which its host contract reads only at start). It then prints the `bin/ncl groups restart --id <group-id>` command, because running agent containers keep the old endpoint. With no service installed, that hint rides in the single "nothing was restarted" line. An unchanged `.env` restarts nothing. A settings-only restart still builds first, and never restarts onto a failed build: `tsc` can write `dist/` despite errors, so restarting after a failed build could load broken output. The credential is saved either way.
- **Failure paths**: no service installed → nothing restarted, one line names the service step, exit 0. Restart failed → auth still runs, one line prints `pnpm run build && bash setup/lib/restart.sh`, exit 1. `restart.sh` now exits 2 for "nothing installed" on Linux too, matching macOS.

## Related work

Found while testing https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4094; no issue filed. Safe to review directly: setup-only, the full setup flow (`setup/auto.ts`) is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(sweep): clear a stranded outbound journal so the session can wake again
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Lets the sweep clear a stranded `outbound.db-journal`, so a session killed mid-write wakes again instead of staying stuck.
- **Problem**: a container killed mid-transaction leaves a hot journal. The host's read-only outbound handle cannot roll it back, so every host read fails with `SQLITE_READONLY_ROLLBACK`. The sweep threw before `countDueMessages`, so a session with a due message was never woken until an unrelated inbound message arrived. On one install a gateway-unavailable mass stop (#4258) stranded two sessions for about 50 minutes.
- **Fix**: `AgentMailbox.isRecoverableResidue?(err)` and `OutboundMailbox.recoverResidue?()` (optional). The SQLite mailbox recognises `SQLITE_READONLY_ROLLBACK` and rolls the journal back by opening its writable connection, the one `deleteOrphanProcessingClaims` already uses.
- **Fix**: `reconcileActiveSession` recovers only when no runtime can be writing: nothing in this host holds the session (new `hasHostRuntime()`: registered, spawning, adoption retries, survivors awaiting adoption, pending stops; re-checked right before the writable open) and no other live host process holds its claim (new `isClaimedByLivePeer()`, the check `claimSessionRun` already makes, now shared). Then it re-runs the sweep once. It spawns nothing; the re-run wakes only if a message is due.
- **Out of scope**: delivery and CLI reads still fail until the next sweep clears the journal (at most one sweep interval). A session whose dead runtime is still registered waits for teardown before recovery.

## Related work

Closes #4056.
Related: #4258 (the mass stop that triggered it; separate PR), #4057, #2516, #2640.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm run build` → clean. `pnpm test` → 4243 passed, 1 failed (`src/group-skills.test.ts` legacy-shape case, which also fails on clean `main` on this machine).
- New fixture `src/test-utils/strand-journal.ts`: a real child writer SIGKILLed mid-transaction leaves a hot journal (throws if it does not).
- `src/mailbox/sqlite/journal-recovery.test.ts`: the read-only handle fails with `SQLITE_READONLY_ROLLBACK`; `recoverResidue()` clears it and reads succeed.
- `src/reconcile-session.journal.test.ts` (real central and session DBs): the sweep clears the journal and wakes a session with a due message on the same tick; does not wake an idle one; leaves storage alone under a local runtime, a survivor awaiting adoption, or a live peer's claim.
- Without the `reconcile-session.ts` change, the sweep tests fail with `attempt to write a readonly database`, the production error.
- Running in production on the reporting install since 3 Nov.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
A session whose container was killed mid-write no longer stays stuck: the host sweep clears the stranded outbound journal and wakes the session if it has work due.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

The host now writes (rolls back) `outbound.db`, which the container owns, but only when no runtime in this host or a live peer host can be writing it. It uses the same writable path the host already uses for `deleteOrphanProcessingClaims`. SQLite itself refuses to treat a journal as hot while a writer holds its lock.

prs.title: fix(add-onecli): end sessions only after 3 consecutive failed health probes
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops one slow OneCLI health probe from ending every running session.
- **Problem**: `probeHealth` declared the gateway unavailable on the first failed `/v1/health` (5 s timeout), so container-runner stopped every live agent mid-turn. On a loaded host the gateway is slow, not down: on one Raspberry Pi install, 18 failed probes stopped 124 sessions, and the kills went on to strand sessions for about 50 minutes (#4056).
- **Fix**: unavailable only after `HEALTH_FAILURE_THRESHOLD` (3) consecutive failures; a success resets the count and single failures log at warn. Sessions end about 15 s after the gateway refuses connections, 20–30 s after it stops answering.
- **Fix**: a monitor generation keeps a probe still in flight across a monitor restart from counting toward, or blocking, the new monitor.
- **Fix**: the probe releases the response body (best-effort), so a probe every 5 s does not hold sockets until GC.
- **Trade-off**: a gateway restart shorter than about 15 s no longer recycles sessions.
- **Out of scope**: iron-proxy's availability monitor has the same first-failure kill; the approval long-poll path in #4258 is unchanged. A seam-level debounce could cover all providers.

## Related work

Part of #4258 (the health-probe half; the approval-subscription half is not changed here, so the issue stays open).
Related: #4056 (the stranded journal these kills leave; separate PR), #4057.

prs.title: fix(agent-runner): decode message entities before delivery
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops replies that echo user text from reaching the chat with XML entities still escaped.

- **Problem**: the formatter passes each inbound message through `escapeXml` before the model sees it, so when a reply repeats user text — a URL, a quoted line — it copies the escaped form (`&`, `<`) into its `<message>` block. Both delivery paths in `poll-loop.ts` (`deliverMidTurnBlocks` and `dispatchResultText`) only strip harness-tag artifacts; nothing reverses the escaping, so a link sent as `https://example.com/a?x=1&agent_name=Andy` comes back as `…?x=1&agent_name=Andy` and opens the wrong address.
- **Fix**: `decodeMessageEntities` in `poll-loop.ts` decodes exactly the entities `escapeXml` produces (`<`, `>`, `"`, `'`/`'`, and `&` last), applied to the body at both delivery points. Decoding `&` last undoes exactly one escaping pass (`&lt;` → `<`); a plain `&` and any other entity are left alone. This is the approach @zanvan proposed in the issue and has been running locally.
- **Out of scope**: the failure-notice path, which is not a `<message>` body; inbound formatting is unchanged.

## Related work

Closes #4020

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

- New file `container/agent-runner/src/poll-loop.decode-entities.test.ts`: unit tests pin the decode set, the one-pass rule (`&lt;` → `<`), and that a plain `&` and foreign entities (` `, `©`) pass through untouched; two wiring tests drive the real `processQuery` on the final-result and mid-turn paths and assert the text stored in `messages_out` is decoded. On the pre-fix code the wiring behaviour fails (delivered text keeps `&`, shown by a standalone reproduction through `processQuery`); with the fix all 6 tests pass.
- Container suite (`bun test --isolate` in `container/agent-runner`): 633 passed / 3 skipped / 1 failed with the fix, against 627 passed / 3 skipped / 1 failed on the unmodified tree. The single failure is identical on both sides — `browser-trust.test.ts` (`trustGatewayCaForChromium` without a gateway CA), an environment failure unrelated to this change; the +6 are the new tests.
- `bun run typecheck` (agent-runner tsconfig) -> clean.

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Replies that quote your message no longer show XML entities: a link or line the agent repeats now arrives with the original characters (`&`, `<`, `>`) instead of `&` / `<` / `>`. One trade-off: text the agent deliberately writes as `&` (for example while explaining HTML) is delivered as `&` — consistent with the markup it reads, where `&` already means `&`.
```

None. The decode set is fixed and total — no parsing of untrusted structure, no new input surface; it runs on text already bound for delivery, after the existing harness-tag stripping.

prs.title: feat(channels): add native Proton Mail adapter via Proton Mail Bridge
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-proton-mail`: Proton Mail as a channel through a local Proton Mail Bridge built from source in Docker (arm64 and x86). After review, this PR is the skill only; the adapter, its tests and its deps are in #4218 against `channels`, which the skill copies from.
- **Skill**: copies the adapter from `channels`, appends the barrel line, pins five deps, builds Bridge, signs it in, stores its credentials, runs it, wires the owner.
- **Bridge password**: `bridge/store-secrets.sh` writes it straight to `.env` (mode 600) instead of an `nc:run capture`, which the setup engine logged verbatim. The vault is read inside the container (`bridge-secrets.sh`) and only single fields leave it, under `--log-driver none` — `vault-editor read` prints the whole decrypted vault, refresh token and key passphrase included.
- **Certificate pin**: the same script saves Bridge's own TLS certificate and sets `PROTON_MAIL_TLS_CA_FILE`, so the adapter verifies Bridge even on loopback.
- **Isolation**: Bridge runs on its own Docker network (`nanoclaw-mail`), out of reach of agent containers on the default network, as uid 10001 with `--cap-drop ALL` and `no-new-privileges`; ports published on `127.0.0.1` only.
- **Supply chain**: base images pinned by digest; the release pinned by commit and checked against its tag (Proton's tags are lightweight, so unsigned; the commits are signed).
- **Updates**: Bridge runs without its launcher and the entrypoint discards downloads — the updater fetches Proton's x86 binary, which replaces the pinned build and cannot run on arm64; login turns auto-update off.
- **Docs**: a Security section on what Proton verifies, what the adapter relies on, and how approval cards are bound to their answers; REMOVE.md removes only what apply creates, idempotently.
- **Out of scope**: a `secret` option for `capture:` (engine change); a generic IMAP/SMTP channel (maintainers' call).

## Related work

Adapter: #4218 (lands first). Review: see the comments on this PR.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/skill-directives.ts .claude/skills/add-proton-mail/SKILL.md` → no problems, no warnings
- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts scripts/skill-directives.test.ts scripts/skill-policy.test.ts` → 331 passed (includes this skill's `apply-fixtures.json`)
- `pnpm skill-pins:check` → matches
- Bridge image built from this Dockerfile (v3.27.0, commit check passing). Throwaway containers: Bridge as uid 10001 under `--cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges` on its own network opens IMAP/SMTP; `store-secrets.sh` against a throwaway volume writes `.env` 600 and the certificate, and fails cleanly with no account; a pinned-CA `ImapFlow` verifies the real Bridge certificate while system CAs reject it
- Network probes: a container on Docker's default network reached #3726's socat listener; on `nanoclaw-mail` it cannot, from the default or an `--internal` network; the host still connects through the published port; socat bound to loopback inside the container breaks the published port (why loopback binding was not used)
- Manual, Raspberry Pi 5: an existing root-owned volume chowned to uid 10001 and run with the new flags — the existing login carried over, the adapter connects with the pinned certificate, SMTP STARTTLS + AUTH verified

- [x] User-visible change — release note below

New channel: Proton Mail via a local Proton Mail Bridge (`/add-proton-mail`). Bridge is built from source in Docker so it works on arm64 (Raspberry Pi) as well as x86, and runs unprivileged on its own network. Requires a paid Proton plan.

prs.title: perf(openclaw): skip the dreaming startup scrub when dreaming is off
prs.body:
## Summary
memory-core's `gateway_start` hook scrubs `dreaming-narrative-*` session entries and transcripts that interrupted dreaming runs left behind. It runs right after start and again five minutes later, for every configured agent, **whether or not dreaming is enabled**. Even with nothing to remove, its planning step opens each agent database for writing: lease, integrity check, schema contract, index verification and deletion path fence. That's about 130 ms per agent of synchronous work right after the gateway reports ready, and it delays every request, including the desktop client's first handshake.

LobsterAI defaults dreaming to off (`DEFAULT_DREAMING_ENABLED = false`) and always writes `plugins.entries.memory-core.config.dreaming.enabled`, so for most users the scrub never finds anything.

New `zz-openclaw-dreaming-cleanup-only-when-enabled.patch` (`extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming.ts`):
- resolves the startup dreaming config with the same plugin-config fallback as cron reconciliation, but independently of it, so a failed cron reconciliation still scrubs when dreaming is on;
- skips both the immediate and the deferred scrub when dreaming is disabled;
- still scrubs if the config can't be resolved.

Trade-off: leftovers from an earlier period with dreaming enabled are reclaimed on the first start after dreaming is turned back on (changing the memory-core config restarts the gateway).

LobsterAI side: strong validator in `apply-openclaw-patches.cjs`, the patch registered and content-checked in `v20260801UpgradeDecisions.test.ts`, and a README section with rationale, trade-off and measurements.

## Test plan
- [x] OpenClaw `dreaming-startup-cleanup.test.ts`: 12/12 pass, including 2 new cases (disabled → neither scrub runs; re-enabled → leftovers reclaimed on the next start). Both new cases fail without the source change. oxlint clean.
- [x] All 87 v2026.8.1 patches apply from a clean reset with the new validator; the rebuilt runtime contains the guard (`dist/dreaming-*.js`)
- [x] LobsterAI `src/main/libs/openclawPatches/`: 29 files / 104 tests pass
- [x] Gateway CPU profile (4 agents, dreaming off), 1.8 s after ready: idle **160 ms → 851 ms**; the scrub and its SQLite checks (~560 ms) are gone
- [x] Full app, production renderer, 3 warm starts (on top of #3000): ready→handshake **1.16–1.21 s → 0.67–0.71 s** (1.01 s in one run that was slower throughout)
- Note: 5 cases in OpenClaw's `dreaming-phases.test.ts` (session-corpus redaction, concept-tag normalization) also fail without this patch; they're unrelated to the startup scrub.

prs.title: perf(openclaw): connect the gateway client sooner after startup
prs.body:
## Summary
From the gateway reporting ready to the desktop client's handshake took 2.3–2.7 s on Windows, in three serial main-process steps. This PR removes or moves each:

- **Load only the GatewayClient chunk.** `createGatewayClient` required `dist/plugin-sdk/gateway-runtime.js`, a barrel that pulls in 642 modules (7.1 MB) and blocked the main thread for 1.33 s. The new `openclawGatewayClientLoader` reads the barrel's `import { t as GatewayClient } from "../client-<hash>.js"` line and loads only that chunk (142 modules, 0.41 s). If the import can't be resolved or isn't the client class, it falls back to the barrel. Node's compile cache made both slower (1.8 s / 0.56 s), so it isn't used.
- **Prewarm while the gateway boots.** `OpenClawEngineManager` emits `GatewayLoadingConfig` once per process when the gateway logs `[gateway] loading configuration`. The matcher allows the ANSI color codes the gateway puts between the tag and the message. `main.ts` loads the client module at that point, while the main thread is idle.
- **No re-probe right after startup readiness.** `startGateway('channel-sync-ensure-ready')` probed `/startupz` on a gateway confirmed ready under a second earlier. That probe waited ~600 ms on the gateway's post-ready work. The existing-process path now trusts a startup readiness confirmed for the same process within 5 s, as long as the engine is still `running`. Other callers, older confirmations and other processes are probed as before.

## Test plan
- [x] New `openclawGatewayClientLoader.test.ts`: chunk resolution (aliased, unaliased, ignores look-alikes), barrel fallback when the chunk export is wrong, missing or fails to load, duck-typed exports, per-entry caching, retry after a failed load, and a check against the built runtime's real barrel (skipped when no runtime is present)
- [x] `openclawEngineManager.restart.test.ts`: trust only for the same process, within 5 s and while running; `GatewayLoadingConfig` fires once per process for real colored output
- [x] Related suites: 8 files / 476 tests pass; ESLint (CI rules) clean on touched files; `npm run build` (includes full `tsc`) passes
- [x] Full app, production renderer, 3 warm starts each: ready→handshake **2.32 / 2.68 s → 1.16 / 1.21 / 1.17 s**; the existing-process check takes 11 ms instead of 600 ms; `createGatewayClient` takes 5 ms (module prewarmed in ~430 ms during boot)
- Note: on this machine the remaining ~1.2 s is the gateway's own synchronous post-ready work, so the prewarm moves main-thread blocking off the critical path rather than shortening wall time yet. A companion patch skips the largest piece of that work (memory-core's dreaming scrub when dreaming is off).

prs.title: fix(cowork): stop storing generated images inline in message metadata
prs.body:
## Problem

Opening a session with many generated images froze the app for seconds (reported on a 413-message session with 13 images). Its `cowork_messages.metadata` was **1.12 GB**: the 13 images (52 MB) were stored about 21 times as base64 data URLs.

- The media server returns results as `data:` URLs. After saving the file, `persistGeneratedImageAssets` still kept the data URL as the asset's `url` and `originalUrl`.
- Those details were copied into tool_use, tool_result and delivery (system) rows. `persistMediaTaskCard` wrote them into both `mediaStatusDetails` and `toolResultDetails`, and durable polls spread the whole server task (with `resultUrls`) into every update.
- The first page was 149 MB and each older page about 256 MB (about 3.8 s per scroll-up page).
- `getSessionMessageRailIndex` ran a window query over the full rows. Because `sequence`/`created_at` are stored after `metadata`, it read every overflow chain and materialized the whole session's metadata: 2.7–10 s in SQLite, about 2.5 s of synchronous main-process blocking in the app.
- `kv.media.tasks.v2` held the same data URLs in `savedAssets` (122 MB) and was parsed at least twice every 15 s by `recoverMediaTasks`.

The OpenClaw transcript was not affected; only LobsterAI's local storage was.

## Changes

**Stop the growth**
- `mediaMetadataCompaction.ts` (new): saved assets keep a `file://` URL plus an `inline:sha256:<hash>` source key. `resultUrls` and spread task fields point at the saved file or the hash. Assets without a saved file keep their URL, since it is the only copy. Details of non-media tools are untouched.
- `mediaAssetPersistence.ts`: saved image assets are created this way.
- `main.ts`: poll details, IPC poll updates, task cards and delivery messages are compacted. Download/cache keys use the hash instead of multi-MB strings.
- `coworkStore.ts`: add/insert/replace/update/fork metadata writes go through the same compaction as a guard.
- `mediaTaskStore.ts`: saved assets are compacted on save, and existing records once on read (also run at startup).

**Existing data**
- `mediaMetadataMigration.ts` (new): starts 15 s after launch.
  - Scans in rowid windows of 2000 using `octet_length()`, which never loads the metadata.
  - Rewrites one row at a time, and only while `powerMonitor.getSystemIdleTime() >= 3`.
  - Resumable through `kv.cowork.mediaMetadataCompaction.v1`, and stops scanning once done.
  - An image whose saved file was moved or deleted is first written to `userData/generated-images/<session>/recovered-<hash>.png` and marked `savedToRecoveryDirectory`.

**Read paths**
- `getSessionMessageRailIndex`: numbers offsets with `ROW_NUMBER()` over the order index (rowid only), then reads back the visible user/assistant rows. `isThinking` comes from `json_type()` on assistant rows only; corrupt JSON is still treated as non-thinking.
- `CoworkStore.findMediaTaskMessages` replaces the inline SQL in `persistMediaTaskCard`, with an `instr()` prefilter before any JSON parsing.

**Conversation images**
- `localfile://` accepts `thumb=<px>` and `thumbFit=contain|cover`. `localImageThumbnails.ts` (new) builds them with `nativeImage.createThumbnailFromPath`:
  - It requests an aspect-correct box (other boxes get padded) and resizes to exact pixels (QuickLook returns 2x representations on Retina).
  - Output is JPEG, or PNG when the image has transparency. It is cached under `userData/image-thumbnails` and pruned after 30 days.
  - Small, animated or unsupported images, Linux, and any failure are served as the original.
- `InlineImageGallery`: grid tiles request `cover` at the tile size and lone images `contain` at the column width, both scaled by `devicePixelRatio`, with `loading="lazy"`. Opening, copying and editing still use the original.

## Electron notes

- **Storage**: rewrites existing `cowork_messages.metadata` rows and `kv.media.tasks.v2` once, in the background. The database file keeps its size (`auto_vacuum=0`); freed pages are reused by later writes. No VACUUM is run.
- **New `userData` directories**: `image-thumbnails/` (cache) and `generated-images/<session>/recovered-*` (only for images whose file is gone).
- **Protocol**: `localfile://` responses can now be a cached thumbnail when `thumb` is present; without it, behavior is unchanged.
- **IPC payloads**: `cowork:session:get`, `getMessages` and `MediaStatusPollUpdate` no longer carry inline media.
- No OpenClaw config or restart behavior changes.

## Testing

- New or updated tests: `mediaMetadataCompaction`, `mediaMetadataMigration` (rescue, unrescuable rows, resume, idle gating), `mediaTaskStore`, `mediaAssetPersistence`, `coworkStore` (rail index, media task lookup, write compaction), `artifactLocalFileProtocol`, `localImageThumbnails`, `imageArtifactSource`, `localFileThumbnail`.
- `npm test`: 771/772 files passed. The failure was the timing-based `skillManager.watcher.test.ts`, which this change does not touch; it passed 3/3 when re-run alone.
- ESLint `--max-warnings 0` on all touched files, `tsc` for the renderer, and `npm run compile:electron`: clean.
- On the affected user database (SQLite 3.53.4):
  - Rail index 5827 ms → 5 ms, with identical results for all 2177 sessions.
  - Migration on a backup copy: 113 rows 1378.7 MB → 0.3 MB, 8 images restored, longest synchronous step 196 ms.
- In `npm run electron:dev`, measured over CDP on the same session:
  - Migration finished in 13 s, with main-process lag at most about 180 ms while idle.
  - `getSession` 27 ms / 83 KB; rail index 6 ms; all 8 older pages 27 ms in total.
  - Sidebar click to rendered content: 81–108 ms. Scrolling to the first message produced no long tasks.
  - Grid tiles render 768×512 / 910×512 thumbnails instead of 1536×1024 originals; a 1536×472 panorama keeps its original.

prs.title: perf(openclaw): read Windows process start times natively
prs.body:
## Summary
- OpenClaw's gateway lock / pid-reuse checks read process start times via `readWindowsProcessStartTimeSync`, which spawned PowerShell (`Process.StartTime`, WMIC fallback). Each gateway start ran it 6 times synchronously (~2.5 s blocking the event loop), and `powershell -Command` spawns are a common EDR/AMSI trigger.
- New patch `zz-openclaw-windows-process-start-native.patch` reads the creation time first through koffi (already shipped on Windows) with `kernel32!GetProcessTimes`:
  - own pid: `GetCurrentProcess`, result cached; other pids: `OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION)`
  - missing pid / exited process → `null` (same as before)
  - koffi unavailable, access denied or call failure → existing PowerShell → WMIC fallback
  - FILETIME truncated to ms, identical to what `Date.parse` produced from PowerShell output, so existing lock records still match
- `apply-openclaw-patches.cjs` adds a strong validator for the patch; `v20260801UpgradeDecisions.test.ts` registers it; patch README documents rationale, fallback and removal condition.
- Patch tests: `readCurrentOpenClawPatch` now normalizes CRLF to LF. Patches are LF in the repo, but Git for Windows defaults to `core.autocrlf=true`, so `planCompletionCheck.test.ts`'s multi-line regex failed on every Windows checkout (CI runs on ubuntu only and never saw it).

## Test plan
- [x] OpenClaw `windows-process-start` / `gateway-lock` / `pid-alive` tests: 70 passed, 1 skipped; Windows-only test confirms native start time equals .NET `Process.StartTime` to the ms for own and parent process, exited child and invalid pid return null, no child process spawned
- [x] All 86 v2026.8.1 patches apply from a clean reset with the new validator; rebuilt runtime contains the change
- [x] `src/main/libs/openclawPatches/`: 29 files / 103 tests pass on Windows (including `planCompletionCheck.test.ts`)
- [x] Full-app E2E (warm): PowerShell spawns 6 → 0, gateway spawn→ready 18.93 → 16.83 s, main process sees ready 23.35 → 21.56 s, client handshake 26.93 → 24.55 s
- [x] Lock contention: second gateway on the same state dir detects the live owner and refuses in 2.2 s (no PowerShell/WMIC); owner stays healthy
- [x] Crash recovery, full app: gateway hard-killed 10 s after ready → LobsterAI auto-restarts it, pre-spawn cleanup removes both stale locks (dead owner), new gateway ready, 0 PowerShell
- [x] Crash recovery, OpenClaw only (no LobsterAI cleanup): stale lock with a dead owner pid is reclaimed and the next gateway becomes ready
- [x] Pid reuse: stale lock pointing at a live unrelated process with a different start time is reclaimed via the native start-time check (LobsterAI's pid-only cleanup keeps such locks); gateway ready, 0 PowerShell

prs.title: perf(openclaw): ship only allowlisted bundled skills
prs.body:
## 问题

Windows 上 OpenClaw gateway 启动时，`starting channels and sidecars` 到 `ready` 要 6–7s。抓 CPU profile 后发现，其中约 75% 是同步的 `fs.access`。

## 原因

- runtime 自带的 51 个 skill（`skills/`）和 4 个 custodian skill（`custodian-skills/`）每次启动都会被检查一遍。LobsterAI 的技能管理界面会跳过它们，用户看不到，但 gateway 照样处理：
  - **检查依赖的二进制：** 每个缺失的命令都要按「PATH 目录数 × PATHEXT 扩展名数」逐个调用 `accessSync`。缺的大多是 macOS 或国外服务的工具（blu、codex、spotify_player 等），一次启动要 12,716 次，同步 IO 5.0s。
  - **写进提示词：** 通过检查的会写进 agent 的提示词，其中包括 clawhub、healthcheck、notion、taskflow，以及会用命令行改 OpenClaw 配置和渠道的 custodian skill，而这些配置是 LobsterAI 在管的。
- 内置 skill 在 `skills.load.extraDirs` 之后加载，同名时内置的胜出，所以 LobsterAI 自己的 `skill-creator`（「创建技能」按钮会按名字调用它）和 `weather` 一直被 OpenClaw 的英文版覆盖，线上版本也是这样。
- `skills.allowBundled` 解决不了覆盖问题：同名冲突在过滤之前就已经决出胜负，把胜出的内置 skill 过滤掉，两个版本会一起消失。

## 改动

- `openclaw:prune` 新增一步：`skills/` 只保留白名单里的 `diagram-maker`，`custodian-skills/` 整个删除。这一步在所有平台的 runtime 流水线里都会执行，在打包之前。
- 和已有的 `BUNDLED_EXTENSIONS_TO_KEEP` 一样用白名单：OpenClaw 升级带进来的新 skill 默认会被删掉。
- 新增测试：白名单的取舍；裁剪行为（custodian 被删、零散文件保留、重复执行没有副作用、目录不存在时不报错）；白名单里不能出现仓库 `SKILLs/` 已有的同名 skill。

## 验证

- 用 win-x64 runtime 和一份真实 state 目录的副本，单独起 gateway 测量（不开 profiler）：

| | 裁剪前 | 裁剪后 |
|---|---|---|
| PATH 探测 | 12,716 次 / 5.0s | 53 次 / 7ms |
| `sidecars.model-runtime` | 6.1–6.8s | 1.2s |
| channels → ready | 6.4–7.2s | 1.4s |

- 查询这个 gateway 实际生效的 skill 列表：共 40 个，LobsterAI 的 37 个可用 skill 都在（`skill-creator`、`weather` 现在用的是 LobsterAI 自己的版本），内置的只剩 `diagram-maker`，clawhub 和 custodian skill 都不在了。

prs.title: fix(media): let visible subagents generate images
prs.body:
## Problem

When the main agent delegates image work with `sessions_spawn` (visible mode), the child runs under `agent:<id>:dashboard:<uuid>`. Every `lobsterai_image_generate` call from that child failed with `Media tool has no authenticated run context`, so no task was created. Main-session generation was unaffected.

## Root causes (stacked)

1. **Hooks dropped by OpenClaw.** `lobster-media-generation` is a non-bundled plugin, and OpenClaw v2026.8.1 blocks its `before_model_resolve` / `agent_end` typed hooks unless `hooks.allowConversationAccess` is set. The run owner was never captured.
2. **Per-registration run table.** OpenClaw calls `register()` once per plugin registry in the gateway process. The hook and tool `execute` could use different `MediaRunContexts` instances, so a call bound in `before_tool_call` was not found in `execute`. Desktop keys hid this because unbound desktop calls are allowed.
3. **No Cowork row for the child.** Dashboard children only have a `subagent_runs` row, so main could not resolve a turn account scope and returned `MEDIA_ACCOUNT_CHANGED`.
4. **No local save.** For the same reason, generated files were not persisted, and the child got no file path.

## Changes

- `openclawConfigSync.ts`: grant `hooks.allowConversationAccess: true` to the media plugin entry.
- `lobster-media-generation/runContext.ts`, `index.ts`: one `MediaRunContexts` per process (`globalThis` + `Symbol.for`); a reload only replaces the bridge sender.
- `openclawLocalSessionResolver.ts`: `resolveSubagentRequesterCoworkSessionId()` maps a spawned child key to its requester Cowork session via `subagent_runs`.
- `main.ts` (media callback): when the child has no Cowork session, use the requester session for account scope, media selection, and saving image/video files into the requester working directory. UI events, status cards and durable task tracking still use the child's own session.

## Electron / OpenClaw notes

- Changes generated `openclaw.json` (plugin hook grant), so the gateway restarts once after upgrade.
- Desktop sessions, `agent:<id>:subagent:` children, IM and cron behavior is unchanged when the session already maps to a Cowork row. IM/cron native runs were likely also affected by cause 2 and should now bind correctly (not separately tested).

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/main/libs/openclawLocalSessionResolver.test.ts tests/openclaw-extensions/lobster-media-generation src/main/libs/openclawConfigSync.runtime.test.ts src/main/libs/lobsterMediaStatusPolling.test.ts`: 201 passed (re-run on the current release base: 198 passed, 3 skipped without the local vendor runtime).
- ESLint on touched files with `--max-warnings 0`: clean. `npm run compile:electron`: passes.
- Verified in `npm run electron:dev`: a visible subagent generated an image in one call, the status result linked a file saved in the requester working directory, and the parent reported it. No hook blocks or `MEDIA_ACCOUNT_CHANGED` in gateway/main logs.

Supersedes #2993, which accidentally included the #2991 commit.

prs.title: feat(media): let one confirmation approve the rest of a turn's images
prs.body:
## Summary

When the image model is the **system default**, a turn gets one image without confirmation; every later image asks again. A 16-image task meant 15 clicks, and the agent stalled whenever a card waited (cards are retained for up to 30 minutes).

The extra-image confirmation card now has a **本轮全部继续 / Continue all this turn** button next to Cancel and Generate:

- It approves the remaining images of **this turn**, for the **same model at the same quote**. A new turn, another model or a changed price asks again.
- Requests already queued in the same turn (e.g. parallel subagents) at the same quote are approved together with one click.
- Cancel still ends the turn as before; a stale quote is still re-checked on approval, and a changed price still needs a fresh answer.
- Video confirmations never offer or accept a turn approval; a forged `grant: turn` on a card that did not offer it is denied as an invalid answer.
- Explicitly selected image models are unchanged (they never asked).

## Changes

- `src/main/mediaDefaultExecution.ts`: per-turn-snapshot approvals keyed by model + quote, and a confirmation group id per turn and model.
- `src/main/libs/mediaConfirmationRequests.ts`: `turnGroup` option, `turnGrant` card state, validation of `grant`, and approval of queued siblings at the same quote; `quoteOf` exported as `mediaConfirmationQuote`.
- `src/main/main.ts`: skip the extra-image confirmation when the turn is already approved for this model and quote; record a turn approval (logged once: `[MediaGeneration] user approved the remaining images of this turn ...`).
- `src/shared/media/confirmation.ts`: `MediaConfirmationGrant`, `turnGrant` on the state, `grant`/`quote` on the response.
- `MediaConfirmationCard.tsx` + `copy.ts`: the button and a hint line (zh/en).

Electron notes: no new IPC channel; the existing `cowork:media:confirmation` command carries the optional `grant` field. No storage or OpenClaw config changes; approvals live in memory per turn.

## Testing

- Unit tests added for the budget, the request manager (queued siblings, different quote / other turn, single approval, refused turn grant, stale quote with a new price) and the card rendering. Targeted suites, changed-file ESLint and `tsc -p electron-tsconfig.json` pass.
- End-to-end in `npm run electron:dev` with the system default model (Doubao-Seedream-5.0-pro), asking for 3 images in one turn:
  - image 1 submitted immediately (default allowance);
  - image 2 showed the card with the new button; clicking it submitted at once and logged the turn approval;
  - image 3 submitted 70 ms after the request, with no card.
  - Window focus was emulated over CDP so the card could become visible; parallel-queue release, next-turn reset and cancel were covered by unit tests only.

prs.title: fix(desktop-companion): show selections the hook skips in AppKit apps
prs.body:
## 问题

用户反馈 macOS 上划词悬浮窗时有时无：在备忘录里重复划同一个词，10 次只出 1 次；划不同的词约 5/10；浏览器里表现明显更好。

## 原因

- `selection-hook` 在 macOS 上只有在按下或抬起时光标是 I 形，才把这次手势当作选字。
- 备忘录等 AppKit 应用经常显示箭头：鼠标停在已选中文字上时是箭头；而且光标只在鼠标移动时更新，从页边起划或刚移到文字上就按下，看到的也是箭头。这些手势都被 hook 跳过。
- hook 跳过时，LobsterAI 的兜底读取只接受"手势两端都落在选中文字附近"的选区。划过行尾、三击整段、拿不到文字坐标的第三方 App 都会被丢掉。
- 之前的 #2984 加了这个兜底，但它不在任何已发布的版本里。已发布版本对 hook 跳过的手势一律不显示，和用户反馈的规律一致。

## 改动

- 按 App 记住上一次看到的选中文本（存哈希，最多 32 个 App，hook 停止时清空）。
- hook 跳过手势后，满足以下任一条件就显示：
  - 手势两端都落在选中文字上（即使和上次是同一段文字）；
  - 选区变了，且手势有一端落在选中的那几行上（划过行尾、页边起划、三击）；
  - 选区变了，且 App 不提供文字坐标（窗口放在鼠标抬起的位置）。
- 选区没变、手势也不在它上面的情况（拖窗口、拖滚动条、拖动已选文字）仍不显示。

## 验证

- 用模拟的手势事件序列，对比了已发布版本、#2984 和本次修复：

| 场景 | 已发布版本 | #2984 | 本 PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 备忘录：双击 / 拖选同一个词 10 次 | 1/10 | 10/10 | 10/10 |
| 备忘录：拖选 10 个不同的词（含页边起划、划过行尾、划到空白处） | 4/10 | 6/10 | 10/10 |
| 备忘录：三击整段 | 0/1 | 0/1 | 1/1 |
| 无文字坐标的 App：拖选 10 个不同的词 | 2/10 | 2/10 | 10/10 |
| 留着选区时拖窗口、拖滚动条（误弹） | 不弹 | 不弹 | 不弹 |

- `src/main/desktopCompanion` 与 `src/shared/desktopCompanion` 下的 Vitest 全部通过，改动文件 ESLint 零告警，`tsc --project electron-tsconfig.json --noEmit` 通过。
- **尚未在真机 Mac 上验证**，需要在备忘录里手动复测上面几个场景。日志里出现 `Showing a selection the hook skipped in ... (covers/touches/unknown)` 表示走的是兜底。

## 已知限制

- 既拿不到坐标、又被 hook 跳过的 App 里，原样再选一次完全相同的文字不会重新出窗：无法和"拖窗口后旧选区还在"区分。
- 从没被看到过的选区（如键盘选择），之后在它所在行上拖滚动条，可能误弹一次。

prs.title: fix(account): open account menu without waiting on daily check-in
prs.body:
## Summary

Clicking the sidebar account button (“我的”) felt laggy because `LoginButton.handleClick` awaited `loadDailyCheckInSnapshot()` — two serial activity requests (`getSlot`, then `getContext`), with no cache and no timeout — before calling `setShowMenu(true)`. The prod daily check-in activity is evergreen, so every click paid the round trips.

The preload was added in 3fd0c8489 so the check-in entry would not appear late and shift the menu. This PR keeps that goal and removes the wait:

- New pure `dailyCheckInSnapshotStore.ts`: an account-scoped snapshot cache with in-flight dedupe, a 15 s freshness window, last-known state kept through transient failures, and a `replace()` revision guard so a refresh started before a claim cannot overwrite the claimed state.
- `useDailyCheckInActivity` loads through the store (the home header entry and the menu share requests), writes claim results back, and adopts later `initialSnapshot` updates from the menu.
- `LoginButton` opens the menu at once with the cached snapshot and refreshes in the background. Only a first open with no cache waits, capped at 250 ms. The snapshot is prefetched once the account is ready, and on hover or focus.

No IPC, main-process, storage, or OpenClaw changes.

## Verification

- New `dailyCheckInSnapshotStore.test.ts` (11 cases); full `npm test` passed (8336 tests).
- ESLint (CI rules) on changed files and `tsc --noEmit` pass.
- In `electron:dev`, driven over CDP on a logged-in account:
  - Before: the two serial check-in requests alone took 110–122 ms before the menu could render.
  - After: the menu is in the DOM in 3–10 ms and painted in 15–32 ms, with the check-in entry present from the first frame.
  - No renderer errors.

Not covered in the app: the 250 ms first-open wait path, the hover prefetch, and claiming check-in (already claimed that day). These are covered by the unit tests only.
