prs.title: fix(openclaw): apply IM configuration without restarting the gateway
prs.body:
## Summary

Saving IM configuration currently can force a whole gateway restart, interrupting
unrelated work and racing the configuration file watcher. A successful write RPC
also does not prove that the runtime has applied the edit.

This PR applies eligible configuration changes through the live gateway and
reports the exact mutation's application status. Necessary process replacements
wait for an atomic runtime idle lease and the old process to exit. It also fixes
connection races during that lifecycle while preserving IM history recovery.

## Related Issue

No linked issue. This is one coordinated desktop and pinned-runtime change.

## Changes Made

- Generate live candidates in memory, including enterprise overrides, and make
  the runtime the sole writer of its watched configuration file. IM/binding edits
  and legacy IM restart hints use live synchronization.
- Add a version-scoped OpenClaw patch for opt-in mutation receipts, idempotent
  mutation IDs, exact revision attestation, restart refusal before persistence,
  and idle restart leases. Compare authored/resolved environment placeholders
  correctly so an unchanged authentication token does not trigger a restart.
- Keep write acknowledgement, persistence, and application distinct. Reconcile
  uncertain writes with bounded reads; never infer a restart or duplicate write
  from a timeout. Preserve pending/rejected/applied status through IM IPC and
  Settings, and advance the synchronized fingerprint only after application.
- Join pending handshakes, ignore stale client/process events, prevent reconnect
  from spawning during restart preparation, and cancel late work on shutdown.
  Explicit reconnection still restores IM session discovery/history polling.
- Document the protocol, runtime compatibility boundary, and validation in
  `docs/openclaw-config-delivery.md`.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Code refactoring
- [x] Documentation update

## Testing

- [x] GitHub Linux full suite at `0d9e5ed9`: **497 test files / 5,135 tests
  passed**, 11 files / 121 tests skipped. All applicable PR checks pass, including
  CodeQL, lint, main/renderer builds, Electron Verify and security scans.
- [x] The reviewed patch inventory includes the added runtime patch. Restart leases
  use an opaque random UUID rather than a hash derived from configuration secrets.
- Local Windows full-suite execution also encountered platform-specific filename,
  symlink and native-install fixture failures; the full-suite result above is from
  the successful GitHub Linux run.

- [x] Tested locally with the upstream dependency set (Node 24.18.0, npm 11.17.0,
  desktop Vitest 4.1.11).
- [x] Added new tests and updated existing handshake fixtures.
- [x] Desktop targeted regression: **15 files, 557 passed, 3 skipped**. Covers
  delivery/diagnostics, impact classification, receipt generation, offline receipt
  attestation, idle stop, IM IPC/UI results, engine restart ownership, connection
  races, existing adapter/history behavior, configuration generation, and
  enterprise merging.
- [x] Pinned runtime unit suites: **53 passed** across gateway Vitest projects
  (three source test files; project executions are counted separately).
- [x] Real gateway end-to-end suite: **10 passed**, exercising actual RPCs and the
  watcher, hot apply, token placeholders, restart refusal before persistence,
  duplicate IDs, invalid writes, saved-candidate attestation, lease expiry and
  commit/admission fencing.
- [x] All **49 runtime patches** apply to pinned OpenClaw
  `ea806575e6450e4d1efdfc72c19f04be982a1b9b`; repeating the upstream patch script
  succeeds.
- [x] Changed-file ESLint with zero warnings, `npx tsc --noEmit`,
  `npm run compile:electron`, `npm run build`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- [ ] Manual signed-in IM account / installed Electron release acceptance.

The production build retains existing third-party eval/chunk-size warnings;
Vitest prints the existing Vite CommonJS config-loader advisory.

## Checklist

- [x] Followed project conventions and reviewed the complete diff.
- [x] Added comments for lifecycle ownership and uncertain outcomes.
- [x] Updated documentation and added behavioral regression coverage.
- [x] New and relevant existing tests pass locally.

## Electron-Specific Changes

- [x] Main process
- [x] IPC result contract and renderer Settings status

## Additional Notes

Rebuild the bundled runtime with the included v2026.8.1 patch. An older runtime
without `configMutationReceipts: 1` leaves live edits pending; it is not treated as
evidence that an edit was applied or that the gateway must restart. Legacy runtime
RPC clients retain their non-managed configuration behavior.

This does not promise that every IM transport stays connected after its own
credentials change. Channel plugins may reconnect their own transport. Inherited
secret/proxy changes, plugin installation changes, and runtime-classified
restart-required changes still use a coordinated process replacement.

prs.body:
## Summary
Adds a capability marketplace workflow to upstream LobsterAI: discover skills, create digital employees, install expert teams, browse expert kits and tool plugins, and configure MCP tool exposure. Uses LobsterAI branding, native agents, SQLite persistence and the existing OpenClaw integration.

## Related Issue
Incorporates the changes from #2710 and #2713 into this combined contribution. Those PRs are left open for maintainer coordination.

## Changes Made
- **Skill marketplace:** accurate search/tag result counts, recommended/name/download sorting, grid/list layouts and incremental loading in batches of 40.
- **Digital employees:** a dedicated navigation entry with employee catalog, installed employees and expert teams; 39 portable imported presets alongside the existing upstream presets (duplicate IDs retain upstream definitions). Reuses native agent creation, configuration and conversations. Missing skill dependencies remain visible.
- **Expert teams:** 53 definitions with a lead and native member agents, allowlisted delegation and isolated subagent context. Installation is transactional and idempotent; failures roll back, existing edits are preserved and conflicting IDs are rejected. A saved team remains saved when runtime synchronization is pending.
- **Expert kits and tool plugins:** categorized and filterable kit catalogs, setup notices, refresh and explicit unavailability for missing bundles. Accepts both the existing Overmind response and portable catalog JSON. Existing kit install paths remain in use.
- **MCP:** persists and imports per-server include/exclude tool filters and parallel tool-call settings, exposes them in the editor, forwards them into OpenClaw configuration and incrementally renders large catalogs.
- Adds English and Chinese UI strings. Excludes customer-specific workflows, proprietary service dependencies, credentials and third-party ZIP collections.

## Type of Change
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] Performance improvement

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- Eight focused test files: **215 passed, 3 skipped**. Coverage includes SQLite team installation/rollback/idempotency, expert team contracts, catalog parsing/sorting, MCP persistence/import/filtering/config forwarding and skill tag counts.
- Touched TypeScript/TSX ESLint: passed with zero warnings.
- Renderer TypeScript check, `npm run compile:electron` and `npm run build`: passed. The build retains existing bundler chunk warnings.
- After the final catalog cleanup and accessible-label correction: catalog/team tests (4 tests) and affected-component lint passed again.
- Staged whitespace/diff check: passed.

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing focused unit tests pass locally with my changes

## Electron-Specific Changes
- [x] Changes to main process (src/main/)
- [x] Changes to preload script (src/main/preload.ts)
- [x] Changes to IPC communication

Adds a typed expert-team installation IPC channel. Team records use the existing agent store and transaction API, and runtime synchronization uses the existing OpenClaw config delivery path.

## Additional Notes
Based on upstream `f691f799` (2026.9.20). No new package dependencies.

Full model-backed delegation, authenticated catalog downloads and packaged desktop end-to-end acceptance have **not** been completed. Some catalog templates require optional skills; installation surfaces missing dependencies rather than claiming readiness. This contribution adds plugin catalog/install support, not a bundled third-party plugin archive.

prs.title: feat(renderer): group model choices and improve conversation loading
prs.body:
## Summary

Make large model catalogs easier to browse and keep conversation history loading from getting stuck. Models now have collapsible family groups, duplicate display names expose their original routes, and search reaches models inside the folded "More models" section. The selected route still owns its capabilities, access checks and thinking settings.

## Changes Made

- Group models by family with counts and selected-state indicators. Keep provider identities separate, open the selected family/route, and retain the existing plan/custom tabs and More models section.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): skip integrity checks for cleanly closed agent databases
prs.body:
## Summary

Startup on large profiles was slow because OpenClaw v2026.8.1 runs a whole-file `PRAGMA integrity_check` on every physical agent database open. Quits never closed the gateway cleanly, which made this worse.

- **Clean-close seal (OpenClaw patch).** `openclaw-agent-db-clean-close-seal.patch` backports the upstream v2026.10.10 seal. A database closed cleanly writes `<db>.seal` (dev/inode/birthtime/size/mtimeNs, schema identity, last full-check time, checksum). The next open consumes the seal and skips the whole-file pass while the file is unchanged, no WAL/journal is pending and the last full check is under 7 days old. Anything else falls back to the full check: a crash, a SIGKILL, a modified file, a pending migration or a schema change. Details are in `scripts/patches/v2026.8.1/README.md`.
- **Weixin long-poll abort (plugin patch).** In Weixin plugin 2.4.3 the 35 s `getUpdates` long-poll ignored the channel abort signal. OpenClaw stops channels one by one, so every quit hit LobsterAI's 6 s stop grace and ended in SIGKILL, and no seal was ever written. The patch backports the fix from plugin 2.4.10.
- **Gateway stop grace 6 s → 8 s.** A healthy shutdown measured 5.2–6.2 s; 3.8 s of that is upstream plugin host registry cleanup. 8 s keeps grace plus the SIGKILL exit inside the 10 s `APP_CLEANUP_WATCHDOG_MS`.

## Measurements (macOS, 616 MB main agent DB, 25 agents)

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway ready | 19.2 s | 14.6–16.3 s |
| `startup.maintenance` | 6.5 s | 2.6–3.0 s |
| Main agent DB open | 2.1 s | 51 ms |
| Quit | SIGKILL after 6 s | clean exit (code 0) in 5.2–6.2 s |

The first start after upgrading has no seals yet, so it still runs the full checks.

## Electron-specific behavior

- OpenClaw runtime changes, so the runtime must be rebuilt together with this change.
- The gateway stop grace changes from 6 s to 8 s. This affects quit and hard restarts only when the gateway is slow to exit.
- New `<agent db>.seal` files appear under `userData/openclaw/state/agents/*/agent/`.

## Testing

- OpenClaw: 11 new tests (seal module and agent-db integration). 28 related test files (agent-db, SQLite, backup, snapshot, doctor, migrations) pass: 850 tests. No new oxlint or tsgo errors.
- LobsterAI: `npm test` passes 8321 tests; `npm run compile:electron` passes; ESLint is clean on the changed files.
- Manual: rebuilt the mac-arm64 runtime and ran start → quit → start cycles on the real profile. The logs confirmed seal reuse for all 25 agent databases, an immediate Weixin long-poll abort on stop, and clean gateway exits.

Drop the seal patch when the pinned OpenClaw reaches v2026.10.10.

prs.title: feat(tools): add Keenable as a web search provider
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds Keenable as an opt-in `web_search` provider (`provider = "keenable"` under `[tools.web.search]`). Keenable works without an API key, so this gives a keyless search option that does not depend on the DuckDuckGo fallback. The default provider (`brave`) and the other providers are unchanged.

- `crates/tools/src/web_search/keenable.rs`, next to `brave.rs`: request, response parsing and tests. Without a key it calls `POST https://api.keenable.ai/v1/search/public`. With a key it calls `POST https://api.keenable.ai/v1/search` with `X-API-Key`.
- `SearchProvider::Keenable { base_url }` in `web_search.rs`. `from_config` registers the tool without a key. The key comes from `tools.web.search.api_key` or `KEENABLE_API_KEY` (process env, `[env]`, or the runtime env provider, as for the other providers).
- Keenable is excluded from the "no key, go straight to DuckDuckGo" shortcut in `execute`, because it does not need a key.
- Keenable returns the result text in `snippet` (raw page text, often several KB). The provider maps it to the tool's `description` field, collapses whitespace and caps each result at 1,000 characters.
- A keyless HTTP 429 error says that `KEENABLE_API_KEY` raises the limits.
- `keenable` variant in `moltis_config::schema::SearchProvider`, plus the config template, `configuration.md` and `configuration-reference.md`. No new config fields, so `build_schema_map()` and `check_semantic_warnings()` do not change.

What is sent to Keenable: the query and the result count, the `X-Keenable-Title: Moltis` header, and `X-API-Key` only when the user sets a key.

## Validation

### Completed

- [x] `cargo +nightly-2026-06-20 fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [x] `./scripts/check-file-size.sh` (`web_search.rs` is now 1,477 lines; the new tests live in `keenable.rs`)
- [x] `cargo test -p moltis-tools web_search` (52 passed: 43 existing, 9 new)
- [x] `cargo test -p moltis-config` (392 passed, 1 new)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p moltis-tools -p moltis-config --all-targets -- -D warnings`

New tests (mockito, like the Brave and Firecrawl tests):

- keyless request goes to `/v1/search/public` with `X-Keenable-Title: Moltis`, no `X-API-Key`, body `{"query", "max_results"}`
- keyed request goes to `/v1/search` with `X-API-Key`
- keyless 429 error mentions `KEENABLE_API_KEY`; a keyed error does not
- `from_config` registers the tool without a key
- with `duckduckgo_fallback = true` and no key, `execute` calls Keenable, not DuckDuckGo (this test fails when the new check is removed)
- parsing: rows without a URL are skipped, `description` is a fallback for an empty `snippet`, a missing `results` array gives no results, the snippet cap respects char boundaries
- config: `provider = "keenable"` validates with no errors or search diagnostics

### Remaining

- [ ] `./scripts/local-validate.sh <PR_NUMBER>` and the workspace-wide `just lint` (I ran fmt for the workspace and clippy for the two touched crates only)

## Manual QA

- Live keyless run through `WebSearchTool::from_config` and `execute` (a temporary ignored test, not committed), provider `keenable`, no key: "rust async runtime tokio" returned 5 results in 462 ms, "moltis personal agent server" returned 5 results in 308 ms. Each description was capped at 1,000 characters.
- To check by hand: set `provider = "keenable"` in `[tools.web.search]` with no key, start Moltis and ask a question that triggers `web_search`. The tool result has `"provider": "keenable"`. Then set `KEENABLE_API_KEY` and repeat. I did not run a live keyed call.

No session export is attached. The design decisions are in the Summary.

issues.title: [Bug] recall_history broken on Windows: workspace_dir canonicalized to `\\?\` extended-length path breaks SQLite read-only URI
issues.body:
## Environment
- QwenPaw Desktop **2.3.0-beta.1** (backend: `qwenpaw-backend.exe`, PyInstaller-packaged), Windows 10 x64
- Workspace path: `C:\Users\lxm\.copaw\workspaces\<agent>\`
- **Cross-version**: the failure also occurs on the previously installed 2.2.x build — earliest failure log entry is 2026-10-26 23:28, ~19h **before** the 2.3.0-beta.1 upgrade (2026-10-27 18:27). So this is not a 2.3 regression; it has persisted across at least two major versions.

## Symptom
`recall_history` fails on **every call** since at least 2026-10-26 (verified across 4 rotated log files, dozens of `recall_history failed` warnings per day), while the **write path works fine** (WAL file actively growing, session persistence OK).

Error:
```
OperationalError: unable to open database: file:\\?\C:\Users\<user>\.copaw\workspaces\orchestrator\history.db?mode=ro
```

## Root cause
1. `config.json` stores every agent's `workspace_dir` as a Windows extended-length path, e.g. `"\\\\?\\C:\\Users\\...\\workspaces\\default"`. This appears to be produced by the backend itself (likely `Path.resolve()` on Windows, which returns `\\?\`-prefixed form) — editing the config to a plain path is silently rewritten back to the `\\?\` form on restart (observed: 19 config entries + 19 agent.json files all reverted after manual fix + restart).
2. The recall tool builds a SQLite URI by concatenating this path verbatim: `file:\\?\C:\...history.db?mode=ro`. SQLite's URI parser cannot handle the `\\?\` prefix → `unable to open database`.
3. The write path uses a plain (non-URI) connection, where `\\?\` is a valid Windows path — hence "writes succeed, reads fail".

## Evidence (isolated repro, Python 3.14)
```python
import sqlite3
plain = r'C:\...\history.db'
ext   = r'\\?\C:\...\history.db'

sqlite3.connect('file:' + plain.replace('\\', '/') + '?mode=ro', uri=True)
# -> OK, PRAGMA quick_check returns "ok"  (DB itself is healthy, 740MB)

sqlite3.connect('file:\\\\?\\C:/.../history.db?mode=ro', uri=True)
# -> sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file
```

## Suggested fix
Strip the extended-length prefix before building the URI, e.g.:
```python
path = str(path)
if path.startswith("\\\\?\\"):
    path = path[4:]
uri = "file:" + path.replace("\\", "/") + "?mode=ro"
```
(or normalize via `os.path.normpath` / avoid `Path.resolve()` when persisting `workspace_dir`).

## Impact
Cross-session raw-history recall is unavailable for all agents on Windows; agents silently degrade (workarounds via memory notes / external APIs). Not fatal — writes, sessions, and semantic memory search are unaffected — but it defeats the purpose of the durable history log.

issues.title: code mode: any tool whose parameter is named `name` cannot be called (TypeError: multiple values for argument 'name')
issues.body:
**中文摘要**：code 模式（`run_code`）下，只要工具的入参里有 `name` 字段（如 `harness_task(name=..., gates=...)`、`spawn_teammate(name=..., role=...)`），调用必然抛 `TypeError: ... got multiple values for argument 'name'`；改位置传参则报 "requires keyword arguments"。根因是工具名以位置参数传入，而形参本身也叫 `name`，两处同型。把工具名声明为 positional-only（各加一个 `/`）即可根治，调用方无需改动。

## Environment
- QwenPaw **2.3.0b2**, Windows 10, Python 3.11, code mode enabled
- Reproduced with plugin-provided tools whose JSON schema has a top-level `name` property (`harness_task`, `spawn_teammate`). The bug is not plugin-specific — any tool with a `name` parameter is affected.

## Repro

```python
# inside run_code
r = await tools.harness_task(name="demo", gates="encoding")
```
→ `TypeError: Worker.call() got multiple values for argument 'name'`

Positional form:
```python
r = await tools.harness_task("demo", gates="encoding")
```
→ `RuntimeError: TypeError: tools.harness_task requires keyword arguments; inspect await describe_tool('harness_task') for parameter names.`

So there is no way to call such a tool at all from code mode.

## Root cause

Two call sites pass the tool name **positionally**, and both use `name` as the parameter name — so a tool kwarg `name=` collides.

1. `qwenpaw/modes/coding/_worker.py:72`
```python
async def call(self, name: str, *args, **kwargs):
```
It is bound in the worker namespace as `partial(self.call, f"tools.{tool['python_name']}")`, so `tools.foo(name="x")` becomes `call("tools.foo", name="x")`.

2. `qwenpaw/modes/coding/code_mode.py:401`
```python
async def invoke(self, name: str, *positional, **arguments) -> dict:
```
Called from `_respond` as `await self.invoke(self.aliases[alias], *packet["args"], **packet["kwargs"])`.

Evidence that these are two separate collision points: patching only #1 moves the error from `Worker.call()` to `_Script.invoke()`, i.e. the request gets one step further and dies at #2.

## Suggested fix

Make the tool-name parameter positional-only (PEP 570; Python 3.8+). No caller changes required:

```diff
-    async def call(self, name: str, *args, **kwargs):
+    async def call(self, name: str, /, *args, **kwargs):
```

```diff
-    async def invoke(self, name: str, *positional, **arguments) -> dict:
+    async def invoke(self, name: str, /, *positional, **arguments) -> dict:
```

A/B verified locally on both snippets: the old signature reproduces `TypeError: X.invoke() got multiple values for argument 'name'`; the patched one binds correctly and reaches the function body. Both `harness_task(name=...)` and `spawn_teammate(name=...)` then work as documented.

## Impact

Every tool whose input schema declares a top-level `name` fails in code mode. Plugin authors end up adding workaround aliases (`member` / `member_name`, `task_name`, ...) to dodge it — which is exactly what we had to do before locating this.

## Minor (unrelated, cosmetic)

`_worker.py` has two f-string artifacts that look unintended: `packet.get(f"cancelled")` and `RuntimeError(f"Code host disconnected")`. Harmless, but probably not what was meant.

issues.title: Memory tag index never rebuilds: /memory/tags returns 503 "Memory tag index is unavailable" (tags are generated but unreadable)
issues.body:
**Environment**
- QwenPaw Desktop UI: v2.3.0b2; backend package `qwenpaw` PKG-INFO: 2.4; `reme_ai` 0.4.2.0; Windows 10 (AMD64).
- Config: `running.reme_light_memory_config.auto_memory_generate_tags = true` (set through `PUT /api/agents/{id}`, read-back verified; on-disk `agent.json` diff = exactly 2 lines).

**Observed**
1. After enabling the switch, auto-memory saves DO generate tags. The log shows `[FrontmatterUpdateStep] path=memory/... keys=['memory_tags']` on 2/2 post-enable cycles, and the note frontmatter contains `memory_tags:` with values.
2. But both read endpoints fail permanently:
   - `GET /api/agents/{id}/memory/tags?page=1` -> HTTP 503 `{"detail":"Memory tag index is unavailable"}`
   - `GET /api/agents/{id}/memory/tag-files?tag=<t>&page=1` -> HTTP 503, same detail
   - The Console file panel "tags" tab therefore stays empty.
3. `GET /api/agents/{id}/memory/status` -> 200; `runtime.auto_memory = {enabled: true, interval: 5}`; worker idle; embedding_store / file_graph / file_store / keyword_index components all present.

**Root-cause evidence (from qwenpaw.log)**
- Tag index rebuild fails on historical file paths that contain backslashes: the log carries 159 index entries whose `path` field contains a backslash, and rebuild attempts since 2026-10-28 error out on them.
- There are 18 successful `Rebuilt tag index: files=0, tags=0` lines, all dated 2026-10-28; zero successes afterwards. So the failure predates enabling the switch (the toggle is not the cause).

**Expected**
After enabling `auto_memory_generate_tags` and at least one successful auto-memory save, `/memory/tags` should return 200 with the generated tags; the Console "tags" tab should list them; `memory_search` should accept a `tags` filter.

**Actual**
503 always; tags exist only inside note frontmatter; no error is surfaced in the UI (silent 503).

**Repro**
1. `PUT /api/agents/{id}` with `running.reme_light_memory_config.auto_memory_generate_tags=true`.
2. Wait for an auto-memory save (interval 5 min) or trigger one; confirm the note frontmatter gains `memory_tags`.
3. `GET /api/agents/{id}/memory/tags?page=1` -> 503.

**Impact**
The feature is half-working: write path OK, read path dead. Users see an enabled toggle and an empty tags tab with no explanation.

**Suggested fix**
- Normalize stored paths (backslash -> forward slash) during tag-index rebuild, or skip/quarantine malformed path entries instead of aborting the whole rebuild.
- Surface the rebuild failure in `/memory/status` (e.g. `tag_index: {healthy: false, last_error}`) and in the Console tab instead of a bare 503.

issues.title: [Bug]: Disabling a provider leaves stale agent run-config model — channels fail with ProviderError: Provider is disabled
issues.body:
## 现象

在「模型」页禁用某个 provider（或停用其下模型）后，**智能体「运行配置」里已选定的旧模型不会被联动更新**，仍指向那个已禁用的 provider。此后任何走通道（飞书 / 钉钉 / 企微 / 微信…）发消息，智能体在构建模型阶段直接抛错：

```
qwenpaw.exceptions.ProviderError: Provider is disabled
```

飞书侧对用户只显示一句无信息量的 **「Internal error」**，通道不降级、不回退、也不重试。

## 复现步骤

1. 「模型」页配置 provider A（如下 `kexin_token`，含模型 `glm-5.3-flash`），设为可用。
2. 「智能体」→ 该智能体的**运行配置**里选择 provider A 的模型（写入 workspace `agent.json` 的 `active_model`）。
3. 「模型」页把 provider A **禁用**（`enabled=false`），或全局默认模型改选 provider B。
4. 通过任意 IM 通道给该智能体发消息。
5. → 智能体构建模型即失败，通道返回「Internal error」。

## 实际行为 vs 期望行为

| | 现状 | 期望 |
|---|---|---|
| 禁用 provider 后运行配置 | 仍保留已禁用的 `provider_id`/`model` | 自动回落到全局默认模型，或明确标记为失效并提示用户重选 |
| 构建模型时命中已禁用 provider | 直接抛 `ProviderError: Provider is disabled` | 与「未指定运行配置模型」同等处理：回退到全局默认模型 |
| 通道侧报错 | 笼统的 `Internal error` | 指明「provider X 已被禁用，请为智能体 Y 重新选择模型」这类可操作信息 |

## 根因

模型来源是**两套互斥的优先级链**，「模型」页的禁用状态只作用于第一套：

1. **全局默认模型** —「模型」页的默认选择（`defaultModels` / `defaultChatModel` / `defaultLlm`）。
2. **智能体运行配置** — 各 workspace `agent.json` 的 `active_model`（`provider_id` + `model`）。

`runtime/builder.py:build_model` → `agents/model_factory.py:2446 create_model_and_formatter` 解析到智能体级模型后，去校验 provider 的 `enabled`；被禁用即抛 `ProviderError`。**校验失败时没有任何回落路径**——既不回落到全局默认模型，也不提示「你选的模型已被禁用」。

更关键的是：`model_factory` 的模型选择器只列出 `enabled !== false` 的 provider（`models.list.filter(...)`），所以**用户在运行配置里根本看不到已禁用项**——但**已存下来的旧值会被继续沿用**。用户既看不见、也改不掉（除非主动去改运行配置），于是通道静默坏死。

## 证据

环境：QwenPaw **2.3.0-beta.1** / Windows 11。

**1) 通道构建模型失败（`qwenpaw.log`）**

```
2026-11-04 19:17:06 | ERROR | qwenpaw\runtime\runtime.py:193 | runtime: unhandled error session=76371ed5: Provider is disabled
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "qwenpaw\runtime\runtime.py", line 108, in run
  File "qwenpaw\runtime\builder.py", line 465, in build
  File "qwenpaw\utils\io_utils.py", line 136, in run_sync_io
  File "qwenpaw\runtime\builder.py", line 655, in build_model
  File "qwenpaw\agents\model_factory.py", line 2446, in create_model_and_formatter
qwenpaw.exceptions.ProviderError: Provider is disabled
2026-11-04 19:17:06 | ERROR | qwenpaw\app\channels\base.py:1038 | channel _stream_with_tracker failed: Provider is disabled, session=76371ed5, agent=feishu:sw:76371ed5
```

**2) 智能体运行配置确实指向已禁用的 provider**

```
2026-11-04 14:10:34 | INFO | qwenpaw\app\routers\providers.py:969 | Returning agent-specific model for default: provider_id='kexin_token' model='glm-5.3-flash'
2026-11-04 15:48:25 | INFO | ... provider_id='kexin_token' model='glm-5.3-flash'
2026-11-04 18:50:54 | INFO | ... provider_id='kexin_token' model='glm-5.3-flash'
2026-11-04 19:26:04 | INFO | ... provider_id='kexin_token' model='glm-5.3-flash'
2026-11-04 19:26:47 | INFO | ... provider_id='kexin_token' model='glm-5.3-flash'
2026-11-04 19:26:53 | INFO | ... provider_id='kexin_token' model='glm-5.3-flash'
2026-11-04 19:27:08 | INFO | ... provider_id='minmax' model='MiniMax-M3.1-Flash'   <-- 手工改运行配置后
```

`GET /api/models` 实测 `kexin_token` 为 `enabled=false`（api_key 仍在，只被关掉开关）。provider 总数 42，其中 5 个 `enabled=false`：`opencode`、`ct`、`kexin_token`、`qwen_36`、`qwen_38`。

**3) 时间线完全自洽——报错只在「运行配置仍指向旧 provider」的窗口内出现**

| 时间 | 事件 |
|---|---|
| 19:17:06 | `Provider is disabled`（飞书 `session=76371ed5`） |
| 19:18:18 / 19:18:25 / 19:18:31 / 19:18:36 / 19:18:41 | 同错连发（5 次） |
| 19:23:53 / 19:24:02 | 同错再发（2 次） |
| **19:27:08** | 运行配置改为 `minmax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` |
| 19:27:08 之后 | **再无一次 `Provider is disabled`** |

共 8 次报错（每次在日志里出现 2 行：traceback + 通道侧转发），时间跨度 19:17:06–19:24:02；运行配置一改，通道立刻恢复。

**4) 与本 issue 无关的相邻噪声**（不影响结论）：`feishu get user name api error: code=99991672 Access denied`（缺 `contact:contact.base` 权限）、`Skipping skill 'himalaya' ... CLI binary not found on PATH`、`sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database ... qjYxdu\history.db`（另一 workspace）。

## 建议修复方向

1. **禁用 provider 时级联处理运行配置**：禁用 provider 后，扫描各 workspace `agent.json` 的 `active_model` / `fallback_models`，若指向被禁用 provider → 自动回落到全局默认模型，并在 UI 提示「智能体 X 的运行配置已回退」。
2. **构建模型时兜底**：`create_model_and_formatter` 命中已禁用 provider 时，不要直接抛错，改为回退到全局默认模型（与「未指定运行配置模型」走同一条路径）；若全局默认也不可用，再报错。
3. **可操作的错误信息**：通道侧不应只显示 `Internal error`。至少在错误里带上「provider `kexin_token` 已被禁用，请为智能体 `default` 重新选择模型」。
4. **UI 可见性**：运行配置已选中的模型若被禁用，选择器应把它标为「已禁用」并保留显示（而不是从列表消失），让用户看得到自己正指向一个失效项；禁用 provider 时弹出「N 个智能体正在使用它」。
5. **一致性**：让「模型」页的全局默认与智能体运行配置的禁用状态走同一套 provider 有效性校验，避免两套来源对同一个 provider 给出不一致的可选性。

## 关联

- #8511 — 飞书通道间歇性 `ProviderError: **No active model configured**`。**根因不同**：#8511 是会话路由竞态（消息被 build 进 `active_model` 为空的工作区）；本 issue 是 **provider 被禁用后运行配置的旧模型未联动**，报错本体为 `Provider is disabled`，两者互不覆盖，建议分开处理。

issues.title: [Bug]: Matrix channel plugin fails to activate when multiple workspaces enable it (10s shared startup window only covers the first)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0b2

## Description

In 2.3.0b2 the Matrix channel has been converted to the official channel plugin `matrix-0.1.0.dev0`. On this machine three workspaces (A, B, C) all have Matrix enabled. After the upgrade the plugin fails to activate and none of the three accounts come online.

Authentication is not the problem: the Matrix authentication service returned `200 OK` for all three `/login` requests, and the channel worker produced no error output at all. The failure happens later, in workspace projection, with `CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED`.

Startup timeline (service started at 00:44:05):

| Account | Login succeeded | Time since start |
|:---|:---|:---|
| @alpha (workspace A) | 00:44:11.3 | 6.3s |
| @beta (workspace B) | 00:44:14.95 | 9.95s |
| @gamma (workspace C) | 00:44:17.3 | 12.3s |

Workspace A connected inside the window. Workspaces B and C were reported as timed out around the 10 second mark.

In `qwenpaw/plugins/channel_adapter.py:62`, `ChannelRuntimeSettings.startup_timeout` is a fixed `10.0`, and the comment states `never read from channel configuration`, so it cannot be adjusted via configuration. The three channels log in sequentially inside the same runner process, taking about 13 seconds in total, so only the first channel can fit inside the window.

Additionally, a projection failure in a single workspace marks the whole plugin as FAILED and unregisters it, which also tears down the channel in workspace A that had already connected.

**Related PR(s):** None

**Security considerations:** None

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0b2
- **OS:** Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (x86_64)
- **Install method:** uv environment created by the official install.sh, later upgraded with `uv pip install --upgrade-package qwenpaw`
- **Python version:** 3.12

Matrix server is deployed separately: Synapse v1.158.0 + matrix-authentication-service 1.23.0, exposed as `matrix.example.org`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable Matrix in the `agent.json` of three workspaces, with the same homeserver, `device_name`, and password-based login.
2. Restart the QwenPaw service.
3. Inspect the startup logs and `~/.qwenpaw/workspaces/<workspace>/channel_state/matrix/`.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** All three accounts log in successfully, but only the first workspace establishes a connection within 10 seconds. The other two report `CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED` during projection, the plugin is marked FAILED, and the already-connected channel is unregistered as well. The Matrix channel is entirely unavailable.
- **Expected:** All three workspaces come online; or a failure in one workspace does not affect the others or the plugin's overall state.

## Logs / Screenshots

```
00:44:03  Registered startup hook 'channel_matrix_matrix' from plugin 'matrix' (priority=80)
00:44:15  ERROR plugins/api.py:688 | Plugin 'matrix' Projection channel failed: CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED
00:44:17  ERROR plugins/api.py:688 | Plugin 'matrix' Projection channel failed: CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED
00:44:17  ERROR plugins/loader.py:5287 | Plugin 'matrix' marked FAILED after startup: channel 'matrix' failed: workspace-b@...:Projection channel failed: CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED; workspace-c@...:Projection channel failed: CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED
00:44:17  ERROR plugins/loader.py:5002 | Failed to activate plugin 'matrix': ...
```

Authentication service logs for the same period (all three succeeded):

```
00:44:11  POST /login  200 OK  @alpha
00:44:14  POST /login  200 OK  @beta
00:44:17  POST /login  200 OK  @gamma
```

The channel worker's stderr was empty; no `MatrixChannel:` log lines were produced.

## Additional Notes

On the first start after the upgrade, `DEPENDENCY_PLAN_UNVERIFIED` was reported (hosts qwenpaw-hub / clawhub-hub). Running `qwenpaw plugins prepare-upgrade` cleared that error; the current problem is unrelated to the dependency gate.

Suggestions:

1. `startup_timeout` is currently a single shared window for all workspaces, while channel initialization is serialized. As the number of workspaces grows, the window will always be insufficient. Consider measuring the timeout per channel, or making it configurable.
2. A projection failure in one workspace should not fail the entire plugin, and channels that already connected should not be unregistered.

issues.title: [Bug]: Hub Local runtime cannot start on Windows (AppContainer skill staging, missing CPU architecture, reverse-tunnel readiness timeout)
issues.body:
# [Bug]: Hub Local runtime cannot start on Windows (AppContainer skill staging, missing CPU architecture, reverse-tunnel readiness timeout)

## Environment

- QwenPaw: `2.2.2.post1`
- Install: `pip install "qwenpaw[hub]==2.2.2.post1"`
- OS: Windows `10.0.26300.9711` x64
- Hub provisioner: `local`
- Hub process: started from an Administrator terminal
- Hub data root: clean `QWENPAW_HUB_DIR`
- User: normal Hub user, first runtime start

## Summary

On Windows, a Hub Local personal runtime cannot reach `running`. Startup fails at
three independent points. The Hub control plane, login, user management, and
model settings work; only the user runtime fails.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Initialize Hub and start it on loopback:

   ```powershell
   qwenpaw hub --init-admin admin
   qwenpaw hub --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8088
   ```

2. Create a normal user and start that user's personal runtime through the Hub
   UI/API.

## Failure 1: default skill staging gets WinError 5

```text
PermissionError: [WinError 5] 拒绝访问
working/tmp/qwenpaw_skill_stage_*/QA_source_index

qwenpaw/cli/init_cmd.py
  _sync_default_workspace_skills()
    pool.download_to_workspace()
      copy_skill_dir()
```

`.hub-initialized` is never written, so every retry fails the same way.

## Failure 2: CPU architecture is empty

After running `qwenpaw init --defaults --accept-security` on the host first and
writing `.hub-initialized`, startup proceeds further and fails at local-model
initialization:

```text
RuntimeError: Unsupported architecture:
```

`platform.machine()` is empty because the AppContainer child environment does
not contain `PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE`; `system_environment()` does not pass it.
This is the same root cause as the open PR #7492.

## Failure 3: reverse tunnel / readiness timeout

After restoring `PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE` in the runtime interpreter, the runtime
log reaches:

```text
INFO:     Application startup complete.
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:1297 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
```

Hub still reports:

```text
Runtime personal-... failed to start: timed out
```

and kills the runtime. The Hub readiness probe cannot reach the AppContainer
runtime through `WindowsReverseTunnelBroker` /
`qwenpaw.hub.windows_runtime_bridge`.

## Expected

The personal runtime reaches `running`, Hub proxies `/api/version` and the
Console, and a first-time user can open QwenPaw.

## Actual

The runtime is marked `failed`; the user cannot open their QwenPaw. Hub login,
user management, and model settings still work.

## Workarounds tested

- Host-side `qwenpaw init` + `.hub-initialized`: fixes Failure 1.
- A `sitecustomize.py` shim restoring `PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE` for managed
  Local runtimes: fixes Failure 2.
- No deployment-layer workaround found for Failure 3.

## Related upstream items

- PR #7492 `fix(windows): fall back when CPU architecture is missing` — open,
  not merged; directly addresses Failure 2.
- PR #7270 `test: mark Hub local runtime E2E as xfail on Windows` — closed
  without merge; describes Windows readiness flakiness.
- PR #7273 `test(ci): allow slower Windows Hub cold starts` — merged; raises the
  E2E readiness budget from 60s to 120s, but does not change the Local
  provisioner/readiness path.

## Latest beta check

`v2.3.0-beta.2` (2026-11-02) was checked at source level. These files are
unchanged from `v2.2.2.post1`:

- `src/qwenpaw/hub/windows_reverse_tunnel.py`
- `src/qwenpaw/hub/windows_process_isolation.py`
- `src/qwenpaw/hub/windows_runtime_bridge.py`
- `src/qwenpaw/cli/init_cmd.py`
- `src/qwenpaw/local_models/llamacpp.py`
- `src/qwenpaw/utils/system_info.py`

`local_provisioner.py` only adds `QWENPAW_RUNTIME_MODE=hub`;
`runtime_environment.py` changes pip/certifi handling. No fix for the three
failures above is present in the beta.

## Request

Please fix the Windows Hub Local path end to end:

1. make the AppContainer runtime able to create the default-skill staging
   directories under `working/tmp`;
2. preserve or fall back for CPU architecture detection in managed Local
   runtimes (PR #7492);
3. make the AppContainer reverse tunnel and Hub readiness probe reliable,
   including a realistic startup budget on Windows.

I can provide full runtime/Hub logs and a minimal reproduction script if useful.

issues.title: [Bug] Default agent edit button is disabled in console although the PUT API allows editing
issues.body:
### Environment

- QwenPaw **2.3.0b2** (console assets built 2026-10-30)
- Linux x86_64, self-hosted
- Not browser-specific: the restriction is compiled into the served React bundle (no CSS / cache / third-party plugin involved)

### Description

The built-in `default` agent cannot be edited from the console at all. Every edit entry point is hard-disabled, so single-agent setups cannot configure per-agent features (mail, model routing, approval level, system prompt files, tools, channels) through the UI.

Related: #7644 (same request, still open).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the QwenPaw console → Agents page
2. Locate the built-in agent with `id = "default"`
3. Hover the card: the Edit action is disabled
4. Open the agent detail drawer: the Edit button is also disabled

### Expected

The `default` agent's configuration should be editable like any other agent. `delete`, `pin` and `reorder` may reasonably remain blocked, since `default` is the root profile and fixed at the top of the list.

### Actual

All editing entry points for `id === "default"` are disabled.

### Root cause (frontend only)

In `console/assets/AgentGallery-C3HV5hg2.js` (loaded through `index-BAoMMfzG.js`):

```js
// card: edit
disabled: d || n.id === "default"
// card: pin
disabled: n.id === "default"
// card: drag handle
disabled: d || n.id === "default"
// detail drawer: edit
disabled: s.id === "default"
```

### The backend does allow it

`app/routers/agents.py`:

- `PUT /api/agents/{agentId}` (around L1175) validates existence, workspace canonicalization, mail/backend compatibility and memory config — **no `default` special case**.
- `DELETE /api/agents/{agentId}` (around L1865) is the only endpoint that explicitly protects it:

```python
if agentId == "default":
    raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Cannot delete the default agent")
```

So the update path is a supported API contract; the restriction exists only in the UI layer.

### Docs are inconsistent with the UI

`docs/multi-agent.en.md` / `docs/cli.en.md` only state that the default agent **cannot be deleted**. Neither says it cannot be edited.

### Workaround

Calling the API directly works:

```bash
curl -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8088/api/agents/default \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"id":"default","name":"<current name>","description":"..."}'
```

`id` and `name` are required; `exclude_unset` semantics mean only supplied fields are updated; `workspace_dir` is ignored. Authentication is required when not on loopback.

But there is no visual feedback in the console, and the change cannot be reviewed or adjusted from the UI.

### Suggested fix

Keep `delete` / `pin` / `reorder` protected for `default`, but allow `edit`.

If the read-only behavior is intentional, then:

1. document it explicitly (docs currently mention only deletion), and
2. provide a supported UI path for the per-agent settings that single-agent users need.

issues.title: [Bug]: DingTalk 通道在消息 >3500 字符时整条降级为纯文本，表格/Markdown 全部失效（未复用 split_text 分片）

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body: ### 问题描述 钉钉（DingTalk）通道发送的回复正文超过 **3500 字符**时，整条消息被强制降级为 `msgtype=text`，导致： - Markdown 语法全部失效：`#` 标题、`**` 加粗、```` ``` ```` 代码块、`-` 列表都以字面字符显示； - **GFM 表格失效**：表格退化成一行行带 `|` 的纯文本，长表格基本无法阅读； - 降级是**静默**的：调用方（Agent）拿不到任何"已被降级"的信号，只能靠人肉记住"正文别超过 3000 字符"。 对"数据报表 / 多列表格"类场景影响最大——恰恰是最需要表格渲染的长回复，恰好会掉进纯文本区。 ### 复现步骤 1. 通过钉钉通道让 Agent 回复一段**超过 3500 字符**且**含 Markdown 表格**的正文； 2. 观察钉钉群里收到的消息：无任何渲染，表格变成 `| a | b |` 样式的纯文本； 3. 把同一条正文裁到 ≤3500 字符再发一次：表格正常渲染（带边框）。 （同一内容实测对比过两档，行为稳定复现。） ### 期望行为 长回复在钉钉里也应保持可读，例如： - 按换行/段落边界**自动分片成多条 markdown 消息**（表格不跨片截断，或在每片重复表头）； - 或保留 markdown 并明确截断，提示"完整内容见附件/文件"； - 至少让调用方能感知到"本条已降级"（返回值/日志/事件），以便主动改走"生成文件 + 发文件"的路径。 ### 实际行为与代码定位 `app/channels/dingtalk/channel.py`，两条发送路径里有**同一段**判定： - L1001 `_send_via_session_webhook()`（sessionWebhook 主路径） - L1051 `_send_via_open_api()`（Open API 兜底路径） ```python if len(text) > 3500: payload = {"msgtype": "text", "text": {"content": text}} # 整条降级，Markdown 全丢 else: norm = dingtalk_markdown.normalize_dingtalk_markdown(text) payload = {"msgtype": "markdown", "markdown": {"title": f"💬{norm[:10]}...", "text": norm}} ``` - `len(text)` 按**字符数**统计，且判定发生在 `bot_prefix` 与 `@提及` 文本拼接**之后**，所以实际可用于正文的预算比 3500 还少一截； - 超长时**没有任何分片/截断处理**，整条正文原样塞进单条 text 消息。 ### 根因分析（供参考，若不准确请指正） 钉钉官方对 markdown 消息长度确实有限制，因此设阈值本身是合理的： - 钉钉文档「消息通知类型」：markdown `text` **最大不超过 5000 字符**； - 钉钉文档「消息类型与数据格式」：text `content` **建议 500 字符以内**。 【事实】3500 是对 5000 的保守留白。 【推断】真正的问题不是阈值，而是**越界后的处理方式**：从 markdown 一步跳到纯文本，是全有全无的悬崖式降级；而纯文本路径对"几千字"的长内容同样超出官方建议长度，等于两条路都不适配长回复。 ### 建议修复方向 【事实】本仓库已存在现成的分片工具：`app/channels/utils.py:354 split_text(text, max_len=3000)`，其注释明确写着「GFM pipe tables 会被当作原子单元，只在数据行之间切分，每片重复表头与分隔行，保证每片都是可渲染的合法表格」；代码块围栏也会自动闭合/重开。 它目前被 `onebot`、`yuanbao`、`wecom`、`wechat`、`qq` 使用，**钉钉通道没有 import 它**（钉钉只从 `..utils` 引入了 `file_url_to_local_path`），而是走了上面那段硬降级。 因此最贴合现状的修复是： 1. 钉钉发送前改成 `for chunk in split_text(body, max_len=3500)` 逐片发送（或采用一个尊重钉钉 5000 上限的钉钉专用 `max_len`），表格按行切分并重复表头； 2. 分片时给出"（1/3）"这类续接提示，避免群里顺序错乱； 3. 单条不可再分的超长内容（例如单行超长日志）保留现在的降级或改走文件，但要打日志并在回复里明示； 4. 若产品上倾向于"不分片"，至少把纯文本兜底换成"markdown + 明确截断提示 + 建议附件"。 另可考虑：把阈值/是否分片做成配置项（钉钉自定义机器人、企业内部机器人、专属版的限制并不完全一致）。 ### 环境 - qwenpaw 2.2.2（pip，`site-packages/qwenpaw`） - 通道：DingTalk（企业内部机器人 + sessionWebhook 路径；Open API 兜底路径同源逻辑） - 现象与 [钉钉能正常渲染 MD 表格] 并不冲突：≤3500 字符时表格渲染正常，仅 >3500 时整条降级 ### 目前使用的绕过方案 Agent 侧自己把预算压到 3000 字符以内：超过就生成单文件 HTML 报告作为附件发送，钉钉消息里只留结论级摘要。可行，但把复杂度推给了每个 Agent 的 prompt，而不是由通道层解决。

prs.title: fix(ollama): size context window from num_ctx instead of 128k default
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama already opts out of the static cloud context catalog (`_context_catalog_enabled → False`), which is correct: a local `qwen3-coder:30b` truncates at `num_ctx`, not at the family's cloud window.

But discovery never filled that gap. `fetch_models` reused the OpenAI `/v1/models` parser, whose rows do not carry `context_length` / `num_ctx`, so every Ollama model stayed at the **128k placeholder**. Compaction then compared against `0.8 × 131072` while the server often serves a few thousand to a few tens of thousands of tokens.

This is **independent of #7979** (and of open PR #7986):

| | #7979 / #7986 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Provider | custom / llama.cpp OpenAI-compatible | built-in **Ollama** |
| Failure mode | cloud catalog matches alias → **1M** | catalog already skipped → **128k default** |
| Fix | skip pattern catalog for custom endpoints | read native Ollama context into `max_input_length_auto_detected` |

A fix for #7979 does not call `/api/show` or `/api/ps`, and does not change Ollama.

## Changes

`OllamaProvider.fetch_models` lists models with `/v1/models`, then sets `max_input_length_auto_detected` from native Ollama signals. Precedence:

1. `GET /api/ps` served `context_length` when the model is loaded (reflects `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` and the load-time window). A hit skips `/api/show`.
2. Modelfile `num_ctx` from a successful `POST /api/show`.
3. A conservative **4096** estimate only after a **successful** `/api/show` that has no `num_ctx`. **4096 is a conservative estimate, not a value Ollama reports.** It matches Ollama's smallest documented default so first-session compaction does not assume 128k.

GGUF `*.context_length` is **not** used. That field is the model's maximum supported context, not the window Ollama is serving.

Failed native probes (`None`, 401, 403, timeout, or an invalid payload) leave the model **unchanged**. The 128k default remains until a later successful probe. A failed `/api/show` does not apply 4096.

`check_model_connection` uses the lightweight `/v1/models` list (`super().fetch_models`). It only checks that the model id exists and does not call `/api/show` per model.

Native `/api/ps` and `/api/show` probes reuse `_build_default_headers()` and add `Authorization: Bearer` when an API key is set and Authorization is not already configured. Explicit user `max_input_length` still wins over auto-detection, and the cloud catalog stays disabled for Ollama. `ModelInfo.max_input_length_auto_detected` allows `ge=1` so a small explicit `num_ctx` (for example 512) is kept.

## Testing

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest \
  tests/unit/providers/test_ollama_provider.py \
  tests/unit/providers/test_context_windows.py -q
# 87 passed
```

`black --line-length=79` is clean on the touched files.

Coverage includes precedence (served `/api/ps` → Modelfile `num_ctx` → conservative 4096 only after a successful show with no `num_ctx`), GGUF `*.context_length` ignored, 401/403 and timeout on `/api/show` leaving `max_input_length_auto_detected` unset, `check_model_connection` not calling `/api/show`, authenticated native probes, the catalog still skipped without detection, and explicit `max_input_length` still winning over auto-detected values.

prs.title: fix(matrix): simplify legacy state migration and device locking
prs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #8187.

The previous legacy-state checks could prevent a valid Matrix account from starting when unrelated legacy files were present. Persistent device ownership could also block another workspace after the original workspace had stopped, while the host only reported `CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED`.

This PR simplifies the migration flow:

- Matching identities are migrated automatically by copying state into the current workspace.
- Mismatched identities start with independent workspace state instead of failing.
- Device exclusion is based on runtime locks rather than permanent workspace ownership.

## Changes

- Prefer existing state in the current workspace, including A → B → A account switches.
- Copy legacy sync tokens and crypto stores only when `user_id` and `device_id` match the authenticated identity.
- Preserve all legacy files during migration; fresh credentials are not overwritten by legacy auth data.
- Skip unrelated legacy state without blocking a valid account.
- Replace persistent device-owner enforcement with runtime device locks released when the Channel stops.
- Ignore stale owner/capture records without deleting user files.
- Preserve concurrent-use protection for the same Matrix device while allowing different device IDs.
- Fall back to initial catch-up when a non-E2EE sync-token copy fails.
- Fail explicitly on E2EE copy failures instead of creating a new identity for the same device.
- Propagate Matrix reason codes through the plugin host instead of returning only `CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED`.
- Remove the obsolete Matrix legacy-capture authorization module.
- Add migration, locking, failure-path, and host-error propagation tests.
- Update Matrix documentation in English and Chinese.

## Security and compatibility

- Legacy files remain read-only.
- Crypto state is never adopted across different user/device identities.
- Corrupt current workspace state still fails explicitly rather than being silently replaced.
- Concurrent use of the same account/device remains blocked.
- No access tokens, passwords, or key material are added to diagnostics.
- Other Channel implementations are unchanged.

## Tests

- Matrix migration and Channel tests: **18 passed**
- Channel unit suite: **159 passed, 1 environment-related failure**
- Plugin process suite: **56 passed, 1 skipped**
- `black`, `flake8`, `pylint`, and `git diff --check`: passed

prs.title: fix(providers): reject out-of-range model config values on the write path
prs.body:
Fixes #8549

## What Problem This Solves

`ModelInfo` declares `thinking_budget >= 1` and `max_input_length >= 1000`, but the write path never enforced those bounds: `Provider.update_model_config` assigned `int(...)` results directly (Pydantic does not validate plain attribute assignment), and `ModelConfigRequest.thinking_budget` was the only numeric field in its model without a bound. An invalid value was accepted and persisted, then failed re-validation on every read — after a restart `load_provider` returned `None` and the provider silently disappeared.

## What changed

- `app/routers/providers.py`: add `ge=1` to `ModelConfigRequest.thinking_budget`, matching the existing `ge=1000` on `max_input_length`.
- `providers/provider.py`: `update_model_config` now raises `ValueError` for `thinking_budget < 1` and `max_input_length < 1000` before assigning, consistent with the existing `model_type` / `supports_*` validation in the same method.
- `providers/model_info.py`: `thinking_budget_range` gains a model validator requiring a complete, ordered `[min, max]` pair (mirroring `ThinkingControl` in `providers/thinking.py`); previously `[8000]` constructed fine and `thinking_control()` crashed unpacking it.

## Evidence

New regression tests (10):

- `tests/unit/providers/test_provider_config_validation.py` — `thinking_budget` of -5 / 0 and `max_input_length` of 500 are rejected and not stored; valid values round-trip and clearing with `None` still works; `thinking_budget_range` of length 1 / 3 or `low > high` is rejected, an ordered pair still drives `thinking_control`.
- `tests/unit/app/routers/test_provider_config_request_validation.py` — `ModelConfigRequest(thinking_budget=-5 / 0)` fails request validation, `1` is accepted.

Red/green: with the fix reverted, the 8 rejection tests fail (the 2 valid-value guards pass both ways); with the fix, all 10 pass. The reproduction script that previously showed `update_model_config(..., -5)` returning `True` and poisoning reads now raises `ValueError: thinking_budget must be at least 1` at write time.

Broader subset `tests/unit/providers/` + the provider router tests: 1008 passed; the single failure (`test_typesafe_evaluation.py::test_as_model_injects_same_instance_and_preserves_host_headers`) fails identically on the unmodified baseline in this environment because the optional `reme` package is not installed.

prs.title: fix(matrix): use scoped crypto store filenames on Windows
prs.body:
## Summary
Fix Matrix E2EE crypto-store initialization tests on Windows by using
cross-platform, identity-scoped filenames for the database and device trust
state.
## Root Cause
matrix-nio derives its default database filename from:
```text
{user_id}_{device_id}.db
```
A Matrix user ID such as `@bot:example.com` contains a colon. Linux and macOS
treat this as a regular filename character, but Windows interprets it as an
NTFS alternate data stream separator.
As a result, SQLite can initialize and use the store, but directory enumeration
does not expose a regular `*.db` file. Assertions and state checks based on
`glob("*.db")` therefore fail on Windows.
## Changes
- Derive crypto-store filenames from the existing SHA-256 scope of
  `homeserver`, `user_id`, and `device_id`.
- Use the scoped basename for:
  - The SQLite database.
  - Trusted devices.
  - Blacklisted devices.
  - Ignored devices.
- Preserve matrix-nio's existing `DefaultStore` trust behavior.
- Migrate legacy identity-based filenames before matrix-nio opens the store.
- Support both workspace-scoped state and the legacy shared crypto directory.
- Migrate Windows alternate data streams through a temporary file followed by
  an atomic target replacement.
- Reject startup with `MATRIX_CRYPTO_STORE_CONFLICT` when both legacy and new
  files exist, instead of overwriting either one.
- Replace `*.db` discovery in affected conflict checks so Windows alternate
  data streams cannot bypass them.
## Compatibility
- Different accounts, devices, and homeservers retain distinct database names.
- Existing crypto databases and trust files are migrated without resetting
  the Matrix encryption identity.
- No fixed shared filename such as `matrix.db` is introduced.
## Tests
Added regression coverage for:
- Regular database creation on Windows.
- Account identity reuse after restart.
- Device trust persistence after restart.
- Legacy filename migration in workspace and legacy shared directories.
- Unique filenames for different identities.
- Legacy/new filename conflict detection.
Validated on Windows with matrix-nio 0.26.0 and vodozemac 0.10.0:
```text
pytest tests/unit/channels/test_matrix.py -q
14 passed
```
Black, Flake8, Mypy, and `git diff --check` passed. Pylint reported no E/F
errors.
The complete pre-commit run could not finish because the Prettier environment
installation timed out. An additional `test_channel_host.py` run completed with
32 passed and 2 unrelated failures: one subprocess startup timeout and one
local pip version below the required 26.2.2.

prs.title: fix(code-mode): allow tools with a name parameter
prs.body:
## Description

Code mode fails before invoking any tool with a `name` input parameter. For example, `await tools.named_probe(name="demo", gates="encoding")` raises `TypeError: Worker.call() got multiple values for argument 'name'`. The host-side `_Script.invoke()` has the same collision.

Make the internal routing parameters positional-only in both forwarding methods. Tool keyword arguments then remain in `**kwargs` / `**arguments`, allowing `name=` to reach the native tool unchanged. This also restores `describe_tool(name=...)`.

The implementation changes two function signatures. No parameter renaming, special cases, or compatibility layer is needed.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8581

**Security Considerations:** Existing schema validation, permission checks, and rejection of positional tool arguments remain in place. The existing permission tests pass after the change.

- The same 95 existing tests pass before and after the fix.
- A temporary reproduction script exercises the real CPython worker and native toolkit. prs.title: fix(shell): add opt-in memory protection with live Console settings
prs.body:
## Description

A shell command can exhaust memory through its process tree or unbounded sandbox output capture. Add opt-in protection scoped to `execute_shell_command`, shared by direct and sandbox execution, including coding mode.

`QWENPAW_SHELL_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB` defaults to `0` (disabled). A positive integer sets a per-invocation RSS ceiling in MiB; `auto` uses half of available host memory, capped at 4096 MiB. Explicit ceilings are also capped at half of available memory. An independent watchdog thread samples observed descendants every 250 ms, terminates them on a resource violation, and returns an error alongside the original exit status/output. Sandbox pipe capture is bounded to 1 MiB per stream while enabled. Successful calls stop monitoring without terminating background work. Timeout/cancellation and confirmed resource violations still clean up observed processes. Memory-budget queries and process registration run off the event loop.

The setting is registered as `hot_runtime` in the existing environment registry. Console's existing Environment Variables → Live settings UI, validation, encrypted persistence and reset APIs manage it. One shared parser validates UI writes and execution. Changes apply to subsequent invocations; active commands retain their initial budget.

**Related Issue:** No linked issue; addresses runaway shell memory consumption.

**Security Considerations:** This is best-effort resource monitoring, not a new sandbox boundary or a kernel-enforced memory limit. It does not guarantee the agent survives system OOM. Sampling gaps, escaped/unobservable descendants and concurrent invocations remain limitations. Watchdog termination is reported as resource protection, not misidentified as a native OOM. Sandbox approval and filesystem/network policy remain independent. If a memory query or process-enumeration permission fails, execution continues without memory protection and logs a warning without adding a tool-result message; permission failures alone never trigger termination. Already-active bounded output capture remains in place.

prs.title: fix(providers): bound inline media per request, not just per file
prs.body:
## Summary

The per-file inline cap (`MAX_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES`, 2 MB) does not bound the
**request body**. Media counts ~0 tokens, so token-based context eviction
never fires, and a session that accumulates many *in-spec* images keeps
sending a multi-megabyte body on every turn. Once a gateway's byte limit
answers 413 the session is unusable until the history is stripped by hand.

This adds a cumulative inline-media budget to the shared capping
formatters, so the request body is bounded independently of tokens.

Refs #7671

## What Problem This Solves

The reporter's incident: a design-review session accumulated ~20 MB of
inline base64 screenshots — every one *under* the 2 MB per-file cap — and
every subsequent turn failed with provider 413 until the session JSON was
surgically stripped. A 2,979,813-byte PNG also became
`[Image unavailable: ... exceeds the 2097152-byte image limit.]`, i.e. an
image marginally over the line was dropped even though a slightly smaller
version would have been fine.

PR #7965 fixed the Scroll-side half (reclaim historical media, fold media
into the existing compression flow) and explicitly listed this as remaining:

> **Out of scope / TODO** — HTTP request-body limits: accumulated media can
> still exceed a gateway's byte limit without exceeding the token threshold.

This PR closes that TODO.

## Changes

`src/qwenpaw/providers/capping_formatter.py`:

- New `max_total_bytes` field (default `MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` = 8 MB
  = 4× the per-file cap; `0` disables it, restoring per-file-only behaviour).
  The field is **derived from the instance's per-file cap** when it is not
  set explicitly: `max(8 MiB, 4 × max_bytes)`. A raised per-file cap is
  therefore no longer undercut by a fixed total — with a 16 MiB per-file cap
  a 10 MiB file reaches the wire instead of being dropped by the total — and
  a lowered per-file cap never tightens the total below the 8 MiB default.
  An explicitly configured `max_total_bytes` always wins.
- The budget is spent in two passes. A **measuring** pass records the size of
  every media block in wire order; only when the measured total exceeds the
  budget does an **enforcing** pass run, replacing the oldest media (a byte
  prefix of the wire order) with placeholders. The newest media is what the
  request keeps.
- `_cap_media` runs the per-file cap first, so a file that is already a
  placeholder is never charged to the budget.
- `inline_media_size()` also sizes inline `data:` URLs, and the OpenAI Chat /
  Responses formatters route PDF attachments through `_format_file_source()`,
  so `data:` URLs and PDFs count toward the budget like any other media.
- A base64 payload is measured **without its `=` padding**, for a
  `Base64Source` and for a base64 `data:` URL alike (one shared helper). The
  padding is not payload: a 512-byte image encodes to 684 characters, one of
  which is padding, so it is 512 bytes — not 513, which was enough to push a
  file sitting exactly on the per-file cap over it while the equivalent
  `Base64Source` was kept.
- The per-request media **dedup scope** lives next to the budget policy
  (`SEEN_MEDIA_KEYS`) and is reset between the measuring and the enforcing
  pass — both passes have to observe the same media, otherwise the enforcing
  pass sees every source as "already shown above" and drops all media,
  including the newest one the budget keeps.

`src/qwenpaw/agents/model_factory.py`:

- The Anthropic formatter now only remembers a media source as *seen* once it
  has actually reached the wire. A source the budget dropped is not part of
  the request, so a later copy of it stays eligible: with **A → B → A**
  (512 bytes each, 900-byte budget) the request keeps the newest **A**
  instead of folding it as "already shown above" while the dropped copy is
  nowhere in the request.
- A folded duplicate still occupies a slot in the wire order, but it is never
  sent, so it costs the budget nothing: the plan drops oldest occurrences only
  until the *deduplicated* payload — the distinct sources that actually reach
  the wire — fits the budget, and a folded copy is re-inlined when the budget
  dropped every earlier copy of its source (so A → B → A still keeps the
  newest A).
- **Video is bounded by the budget too.** Video never reaches a media hook:
  Anthropic routes it through `_format_anthropic_video_data_block`, and the
  OpenAI Chat / Responses / DashScope paths substitute it into the request
  around the formatter's `format()` call. The Anthropic path now caps the
  video before formatting it, and the OpenAI-family paths *mark* the video
  block (its `name` becomes the substitution placeholder) instead of
  replacing it, so the formatter's media hook still sees it and the budget
  can account for it at its own position in the wire order. A marked block is
  rendered as the substitution placeholder and resolved to the video wire
  dict afterwards, exactly as before. Assistant-role video is unaffected (it
  was never substituted and still is not).
- **A local PDF is prepared like any other media.** A `file://` PDF used to
  stay a `URLSource`: the asynchronous media preparation did not read it, so
  the formatter could not measure it and the base formatter inlined the whole
  file (with a blocking disk read) while formatting — three 512-byte PDFs
  fitted a 900-byte budget without a single budget placeholder. The
  preparation stage now reads local PDF attachments too, so they spend the
  per-request budget like every other media and obey the per-file cap (a
  local PDF above `max_bytes` becomes the same text placeholder an oversized
  image gets). Remote PDFs follow the same path for the OpenAI Chat /
  Responses formatters, which have to download them anyway: the download
  moves out of the formatter into the bounded, non-blocking preparation
  stage.

Because formatting walks the conversation oldest-first, spending the budget
as it is spent **keeps the newest media and drops the oldest** — the
direction the issue asks for.

A `ContextVar` rather than instance state, because formatter instances are
shared across concurrent requests and a running total on the instance would
let one session spend another's allowance
(`test_concurrent_requests_do_not_share_a_budget` pins this).

Placeholder wording distinguishes the two causes, and every provider shape
is preserved: Chat Completions / Anthropic / DashScope `{"type":"text"}`,
Gemini `{"text"}`, Responses API `{"type":"input_text"}`.

## Evidence

```
$ pytest tests/unit/providers/test_capping_formatter.py -q
89 passed
```

`TestCumulativeBudgetEndToEnd` drives the **real** formatters (OpenAI,
Anthropic, Gemini, DashScope, and the Responses formatter) over a
three-image conversation with a budget that fits only one:

```
[media omitted from model context: this request already inlines 513 bytes
 of media, exceeds the 900-byte per-request limit]     <- oldest, dropped
[media omitted from model context: ... 900-byte ...]   <- middle, dropped
{"inline_data": {...}}                                 <- newest, inlined
```

`TestCumulativeBudgetThroughProductionWrapper` drives the same scenario
through the production formatter wrapper, and
`TestRepeatedMediaSurvivesTheBudget` pins the repeated-source case through
the Anthropic wrapper, the same case with the newest copy arriving in a tool
result, and the OpenAI Chat / Responses paths:

```
A (512 B) -> B (512 B) -> A (512 B), 900-byte budget
  before:  A dropped by the budget, B inlined, newest A folded as
           "[Image omitted - already shown above]"
  after:   A dropped by the budget, B dropped by the budget,
           newest A inlined
```

The two Anthropic cases fail without the fix (verified by reverting the
`model_factory.py` change):

```
FAILED TestRepeatedMediaSurvivesTheBudget::test_anthropic_wrapper_keeps_the_newest_repeated_media
FAILED TestRepeatedMediaSurvivesTheBudget::test_anthropic_wrapper_keeps_the_newest_repeated_tool_media
2 failed, 62 passed
```

`TestVideoUnderThePerRequestBudget` pins the video case on all five provider
paths through the production wrapper (three 312-byte `video/mp4` blocks, a
900-byte budget → two videos inlined, one dropped):

```
$ pytest tests/unit/providers/test_capping_formatter.py -q -k TestVideoUnderThePerRequestBudget
9 passed
```

`TestLocalPdfAttachmentsSpendTheBudget` pins the local-PDF case through the
production wrapper on the OpenAI Chat and Responses paths (three 512-byte
local PDFs, a 900-byte budget → the newest PDF inlined, two budget
placeholders), and the base64 padding case with
`test_data_url_size_matches_the_equivalent_base64_source` (a `data:` URL and
the equivalent `Base64Source` measure the same, padding excluded).

Without the fix the new cases fail:

```
FAILED test_data_url_size_matches_the_equivalent_base64_source[512]
FAILED test_data_url_image_at_the_per_file_cap_is_kept
FAILED TestLocalPdfAttachmentsSpendTheBudget::test_openai_wrapper_caps_local_pdf_attachments
FAILED TestLocalPdfAttachmentsSpendTheBudget::test_responses_wrapper_caps_local_pdf_attachments
FAILED TestLocalPdfAttachmentsSpendTheBudget::test_local_pdf_over_the_per_file_cap_is_dropped
```

Wider runs — no regressions. The failures below are pre-existing in this
environment (missing optional SDKs — `reme`, `typesafe` — and one
network-dependent download test) and are identical on the unmodified head
commit:

```
$ pytest tests/unit/providers tests/unit/agents -q
# this branch:        23 failed, 5098 passed, 3 skipped
# unmodified head:    23 failed, 5086 passed, 3 skipped   (+12 = the new tests)

$ black --line-length=79 / flake8 / pylint (10.00) / mypy   # clean
```

### The 8 MiB budget is raw media, not wire bytes

**Yes — the budget is intentionally in raw (decoded) media bytes.** It is the
same unit as the per-file cap and as the file size the user sees, so one
number describes the media a request carries.

`MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` counts the **decoded** media bytes; base64
encoding expands them by 4/3 on the wire. An 8 MiB raw budget therefore
becomes roughly **10.7 MiB** of base64 in the request body — still above the
**6 MiB** limit of the `dash_anthropic` gateway. To stay inside that gateway
the raw budget has to stay at or below ~4.5 MiB (6 MiB x 3/4).

This is deliberate: the budget bounds the *media a request carries*, in the
same unit as the per-file cap and the file sizes reported to the user. The
alternative — budgeting encoded bytes — would mean the limit no longer
matches the number a user sees for a file, and it would still not track the
provider's own overhead on top of the media.

The default is therefore a bound on the request body, not a guarantee that
every gateway accepts it: deployments behind a 6 MiB gateway should lower
`MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES` (or set `max_total_bytes` explicitly on the
model) to match their gateway limit.

## Notes for review

- **The default changes behaviour**: a request that used to inline ~20 MB of
  media now inlines 8 MB and placeholders the rest. If you would rather this
  be opt-in, set `MAX_TOTAL_INLINE_MEDIA_BYTES = 0` and I will drop the
  default; the plumbing and tests are unaffected.
- The per-request budget now covers **video** as well, on all five provider
  paths. One path is still outside it: the OpenAI-family / Gemini
  **tool-result video promotion** (`_promote_tool_result_videos`) injects the
  video after formatting, so it is capped per file but not per request. The
  Anthropic tool-result video goes through the media hook and is covered.
  Covering the promotion would mean moving it inside the budget's scope —
  worth a follow-up if you want one budget for both paths.
- The issue's other asks (auto-downscale an oversized attachment instead of
  dropping it, and making the cap configurable per provider) are not
  included; the cap is already a provider field, so only the downscale is
  new work.

prs.title: feat(chat): add append-only session storage, paginated history and native Turn forks
prs.body:
## Description

Long conversations previously depended on mutable session snapshots and loading large history windows. That made historical Turn forks, runtime recovery, and reconnect behavior difficult to keep consistent. This branch introduces durable per-session SQLite history with append-only facts and rebuildable projections, and bounds the Console's history and replay work.

This draft covers the complete branch, including:

- Store message/content facts and immutable context revisions separately from current message/runtime projections. Rebuild projections without rewriting historical facts; reuse state component references for usage-only revisions and avoid redundant block events.
- Migrate legacy JSON sessions and history databases, preserve available historical messages, reconstruct legacy runtime where possible, and retain provider session/Turn mappings.
- Fork completed Turns with their historical runtime boundary. Codex/Qoder branches use native provider interfaces and stored Turn mappings rather than rebuilding third-party context. Failed native restoration/reset must not silently create a fresh context.
- Add stable history pagination, bounded rendering, message-directory navigation, streaming/reconnect replay, and safe session switching/deletion.
- Integrate storage with clear/new, compact, dump/load, Scroll/Recall, cloning, backup, checkpoints, statistics, and PawApp/SDK session access. Preserve reset and checkpoint restoration semantics; roll back failed/cancelled compaction.

**Related Issue:** No linked issue.

**Security Considerations:** Session ownership and active-session deletion checks remain part of history access. This PR does not include local databases, conversation exports, screenshots, profiling dumps, or environment credentials. Provider contexts remain provider-owned.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Refactoring
- [x] Breaking change (session storage representation changes; legacy data is imported)
- [ ] Documentation

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] Console
- [x] Channels (Console streaming/reconnect)
- [x] Tests
- [x] Scripts / Deploy (replay verification tooling)

## Checklist

- [ ] Documentation published in this repository
- [ ] Ready for review / merge

## Testing

The latest local validation ran against the committed working tree in the project Conda environment. Groups overlap and should not be summed as unique coverage.

- Chat storage suite: **478 passed** after each of the three storage optimizations.
- Backend combined regression: **2337 passed, 1 platform skip**.
- HTTP integration retry (backup, checkpoints, conversation commands, PawApp context): **54 passed**, using the existing `QWENPAW_INTEGRATION_HTTP_TIMEOUT=180` setting after initial fixture startup timeouts.
- SDK lifecycle: **2 passed** with a 180-second test timeout after a 45-second dependency metadata scan timeout. Other plugin/SDK contracts: **147 passed**.
- TypeScript noEmit, changed-file pre-commit checks, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Frontend full single-worker run: **657 files passed / 2 failed**; **8475 tests passed / 1 failed / 2 expected failures / 9 skipped**. This was not a green default full run.
  - JobDrawer JSON validation did not display its error within `waitFor`; the unchanged complete file passed on isolated retry (**29 passed**).
  - PawApp SDK session routing exceeded the default 10-second initialization hook timeout, also on isolated retry (**45 passed / 9 skipped**). With command-line `--hookTimeout=30000`, all **54 passed**. No source or test configuration was changed to hide this limitation.

## Evidence

Local terminal results retained from this validation:

```text
pytest tests/unit/app/chats/ -q
478 passed

Backend combined regression
2337 passed, 1 skipped

HTTP integration retry
54 passed

SDK lifecycle / other contracts
2 passed / 147 passed

vitest run --maxWorkers=1
Test Files  2 failed | 657 passed (659)
Tests       1 failed | 8475 passed | 2 expected fail | 9 skipped (8487)

Isolated JobDrawer retry: 29 passed
Isolated sessionRouting --hookTimeout=30000: 54 passed
```

Additional behavior checks:

- A database generated by the previous implementation containing four `block.committed` events was rebuilt twice: messages, runtime, and original events remained unchanged.
- Eight database command scenarios and sixteen Fork boundaries verified state preservation, with Codex/Qoder native reset failure protection probes.
- Console browser flow: create two Turns, fork the first, continue with the remembered first-Turn marker, fork again, and reload. Both forks closed the dialog, navigated automatically, and incremented the name. Long-history scrolling and the message directory also loaded.
- Synthetic SQLite usage-write benchmark (1000 context entries, about 1 KiB each): median **34.174 ms → 4.975 ms**, SQL statements **2013 → 10**. JSON state reading/parsing remains; this is not a production latency guarantee.

## Additional Notes

This is a large draft covering the whole storage/pagination branch, not just its final optimization commit. Historical legacy runtime reconstruction can be approximate where exact snapshots were never stored. The latest browser smoke used the built-in agent; native-provider behavior was covered by automated adapters/probes, not a fresh five-Turn provider UI run in this validation. Reconnect checks do not claim a new browser network-disconnect injection run.

Local verification artifacts are retained outside the Git diff. The known default frontend timing failures and upstream CI results need review before promoting this PR out of draft.

## Description

This PR connects the existing **Install/Update** flow to the published `piccolo-v1` runtime, so users can start Flash chat or Piccolo decisions without compiling or replacing binaries manually. Upgrades preserve downloaded models and verify the bundle before replacing the installed engine. The runtime manifest is included in both Python and desktop packages.

A **Source** selector switches between Hugging Face (`agentscope-ai/...`) and ModelScope (`AgentScope/...`), with each service's logo and the existing Download/Start controls. ModelScope Piccolo repositories are recognized as decision models and download the required inference files.

The runtime workflow builds and tests macOS and Linux on x64/ARM64, Windows CPU on x64/ARM64, and Windows CUDA 12.4/13.1 on x64. Versioned releases use the existing official OSS publishing flow; the PR also checks the installer's published package URLs.

Related: #8463.

**Security Considerations:** Installation verifies archive SHA-256 and release identity. Failed replacements restore the previous runtime; model storage is retained.

prs.title: fix(memory): require non-empty api_key for ReMe reranker enablement (#8276)
prs.body:
## Description

Resolves two related issues in `src/qwenpaw/agents/memory/reme_reranker.py`:

1. **Enablement requires non-empty credential:** `load_reranker_config()` previously evaluated enablement from `config.enabled and config.model_name` alone. Since `RerankerConfig.api_key` defaults to `""`, a configuration without an API key was accepted as enabled, causing memory searches to over-fetch `max_results * candidate_multiplier` candidates for a rerank call that cannot succeed. This aligns the reranker enablement rule with the existing embedding path (`src/qwenpaw/agents/memory/reme_config.py:717`), requiring `bool(config.api_key and config.api_key.strip())`.

2. **Pre-flight guard for missing API key:** `call_reranker_api()` previously checked `base_url` but not `api_key`. An empty or whitespace-only API key resulted in an invalid `Authorization: Bearer ` header, which failed serialization in HTTP transport and was caught as an opaque `[rerank] unexpected error`. A pre-flight check now logs `[rerank] api_key not configured` and returns `None` early, matching the `base_url` error reporting pattern.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8276
