prs.title: fix(tools): decode GBK/CP936 in read/edit/grep instead of dropping bytes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`read_file_safe` (used by `read_file` / `edit_file`) and `grep_search` decoded files as UTF-8 with `errors="ignore"`. On Chinese Windows, Notepad/legacy `.txt` / `.csv` / `.md` notes are often GBK/CP936. Every non-UTF-8 byte was deleted with no log line, so:

- `read_file` returned ASCII leftovers (e.g. `姓名: 张三` → `: `)
- `grep_search` for Chinese terms missed the file
- `edit_file` could still report success and persist the damaged snapshot as UTF-8

Markdown/skill loaders already use `decode_text_bytes_with_encoding_fallback` (utf-8 → gbk/cp936 → …). This PR routes the tool read path through the same helper.

## Changes

- `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/utils.py`: `_read_file_safe_sync` uses the shared encoding fallback
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/file_search.py`: `_walk_and_grep` reads bytes and decodes with the same fallback (files already capped at 2MB)
- Regression tests for GBK read, GBK `edit_file`, and GBK grep

## How to reproduce (before)

```python
from pathlib import Path
path = Path("note.txt")
path.write_bytes("姓名: 张三\n".encode("gbk"))
# read_file_safe previously returned ": \n"
```

## Testing

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest \
  tests/unit/agents/tools/test_file_io.py \
  tests/unit/agents/tools/test_file_search.py::test_walk_and_grep_matches_gbk_file -q
# 43 passed
```

Also re-ran the new GBK cases alone after rebase: 4 passed.

## Notes

- After a successful GBK decode, `edit_file` still writes with the existing suffix-based encoding (`.txt` → `utf-8-sig`). Chinese text is preserved; only the on-disk encoding may change to UTF-8, which matches the project’s Windows Excel/Notepad write path.
- CRLF whole-file rewrite and Ollama `num_ctx` sizing are separate follow-ups and are not in this PR.

Happy to adjust if maintainers prefer preserving the original GBK bytes on write as well.

prs.title: fix(plugins): drop stale host evidence when a declaration is withdrawn
prs.body:
## Description

`DependencyUsageRegistry.withdraw()` removed the declaration but kept the
token's host evidence in the in-process registry. After one failed or
unfinished host observation that stale entry made every later dependency
audit for the plugin fail closed with "environment evidence unavailable"
until the process restarted, even after reloading the plugin.

`_observe_host()` also dropped `environment` while retaining the previous
snapshot, leaving a snapshot without environment that the same audit
rejects.

The fix pops the token's host evidence in `withdraw()` and always derives
the environment from the retained snapshot (`from_snapshot` returns None
when nothing usable is left).

## Related Issue

N/A — no existing issue found. Happy to file one if you prefer.

## Security Considerations

None. The change only affects in-process dependency evidence bookkeeping.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Evidence

Local run of the plugin unit tests:

```
$ PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/unit/plugins/test_dependency_usage.py -q
3 passed
```

- `test_withdraw_drops_host_evidence`: registering a host capture, then
  withdrawing the declaration, now leaves `_host` empty and bumps `_revision`;
  before the fix the entry stayed behind and every later audit for that token
  reported the stale capture as unusable for the rest of the process.
- `test_unknown_observation_keeps_last_capture`: an unknown host observation
  now keeps `DependencyEnvironment.from_snapshot(snapshot)` instead of
  dropping the environment to `None`, so the retained capture can still be
  pinned against a fresh read.
- `test_unknown_host_evidence_stays_unusable`: guards the existing behaviour
  that missing host evidence is still rejected.

prs.title: feat(tools): surface stale daily notes as deduplicated Inbox reminders
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Turn ReMe v4 memory on for an agent, let a day pass where the agent writes a daily note but never processes it, and that note stays on disk forever with nothing surfacing it. ReMe stores hot-tier notes at `<daily_dir>/YYYY-MM-DD/<slug>.md` with an optional `status` frontmatter (absent = pending, `completed` / `skipped` = resolved), but nothing in QwenPaw ever read that field — `base_memory_manager.py`'s `status` is the auto-memory *task* status, a different thing. So `memory/2026-10-20/<slug>.md` can sit there for weeks and only be found by browsing the folder.

This PR adds the missing consumer: a read-only, opt-in tool that turns those notes into Inbox events. It does not change any existing behaviour, runs no background job, and writes nothing unless an agent or a cron prompt calls it. Fixes #8537.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking, opt-in)

## What Changed

`check_stale_notes(days=7, dry_run=False, limit=20, cooldown_days=7)` in `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/stale_notes.py`:

- scans `<daily_dir>/YYYY-MM-DD/<slug>.md`; the date comes from the path segment, with file mtime as fallback;
- pending = `status` absent or `pending`; `completed` / `skipped` are ignored;
- pushes one Inbox event per `(file, slug)` with `source_type="stale_notes"`;
- deduplication: after a reminder the note stays quiet for `cooldown_days`, so opening the Inbox does not re-fire the next run; `cooldown_days=0` falls back to "suppress only while the event is unread";
- never edits, deletes or rewrites a note, never writes memory.

## Evidence

Target tests:

```
$ PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/unit/agents/tools/test_stale_notes.py -q
............                                                             [100%]
12 passed in 2.00s
```

Real behaviour, five notes on disk (two pending, one `completed`, one `skipped`, one too fresh), Inbox calls captured in memory so the demo writes no rows:

```
notes on disk: 5 | 2 resolved, 1 too fresh, 2 pending
[run1  ] 2 stale daily note(s); pushed 2, already reported 0 (threshold 7d, cooldown 7d). | - 2026-10-20/never-processed.md (15d) | - 2026-10-26/also-pending.md (9d)
          inbox rows: ['2026-10-20/never-processed.md', '2026-10-26/also-pending.md']
[run2  ] 2 stale daily note(s); pushed 0, already reported 2 (threshold 7d, cooldown 7d).
          inbox rows: 2 (no duplicate)
[dry   ] 2 stale daily note(s); would push 0, already reported 2 (threshold 7d, cooldown 7d).
          inbox rows: 2 (dry run wrote nothing)
```

Before this change the same five notes produced no Inbox event at all, on any run.

## Self-review

1. Happy path -> `test_pending_note_is_reported`, `test_path_date_wins_over_fresh_mtime`, `test_mtime_is_used_when_path_has_no_date`
2. Invalid input -> `test_invalid_params_fall_back_to_defaults` (`days` / `limit` / `cooldown_days` clamped)
3. Existing data -> note without frontmatter counts as pending; unknown `status` skipped (`test_unknown_status_is_not_reported`); resolved notes skipped (`test_resolved_notes_are_ignored`)
4. Dedupe -> `test_dedupe_across_runs`, `test_read_event_still_suppressed_within_cooldown`, `test_renotify_after_cooldown_expires`, `test_cooldown_zero_falls_back_to_unread_only`

## Test scope

- Target: `tests/unit/agents/tools/test_stale_notes.py` (12 passed)
- Neighbour: `tests/unit/agents/tools` (968 passed, 13 skipped)
- Lint: black `--line-length 79`, flake8, pylint 10.00, mypy clean
- Full suite: not run locally (Windows runner has pre-existing environment failures); CI is authoritative.

prs.title: fix(hub): keep AppContainer bridge token as one argv item
prs.body:
## Description

On Windows Hub Local, the AppContainer bridge is started with `--token <value>`. The broker token comes from `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`, so roughly 1 in 64 tokens starts with `-`. `argparse` then treats that value as an option and the bridge exits with:

```text
windows_runtime_bridge.py: error: argument --token: expected one argument
```

The runtime start then fails with `process exited with code 2`. Because the token is random, this is an intermittent startup failure rather than a deterministic one.

This change passes the token as a single argv item (`--token=<value>`), which `argparse` accepts regardless of the token's first character. Token generation and validation are unchanged.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8565

**Security Considerations:** No change to token generation, transport, storage, or comparison. Only the argv representation changes; the token still travels through the same local process boundary.

prs.title: feat(console): add plugin-facing theme token overrides
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugins could only recolour the chat via `chat.theme.set({ colorPrimary })`: there was no way to express a light/dark pair, and no way to touch layout roles (surface, border, text…) at all. #8071 settled on a deliberately small set of six semantic tokens for that.

There is a second, sharper problem behind the "dark-mode surface does not change" report: the console applies the user's theme preset as **inline custom properties on `<html>`** (`--app-surface`, `--app-accent`, … in `App.tsx`), and inline author declarations outrank every stylesheet rule. So a plugin that emitted `--app-surface` in a `<style>` element lost on **all six built-in presets**, silently — the UI kept the preset colour with no error.

## Summary

- `QwenPaw.chat.theme.overrideTokens(pluginId, tokens)` accepts the six `styles/tokens.css` roles without the `--app-` prefix: `bg`, `surface`, `surface-raised`, `border`, `text`, `text-secondary`. Each value must carry **both** `light` and `dark`; unknown keys and half-specified values throw, so a typo surfaces instead of rendering an unchanged UI.
- Registrations go through the existing `chatExtensions` stacks, so per-token LIFO, dispose-fallback to the previous registration and `disposeAll(pluginId)` on plugin unload all come from the one lifecycle that every other chat slot already uses.
- The winning value per token is projected into a single managed `<style>` element with `:root` and `html.dark-mode` blocks. Declarations are emitted with `!important` — the one lever a stylesheet has over `<html style>` — so the plugin layer outranks the preset without touching it. The preset keeps living in the inline `style` attribute, so removing the last override (dispose, or plugin unload on logout) restores the user's current preset exactly, with no extra round-trip.
- The startup hook now lives in `ConsoleApp.tsx` (where host initialisation moved in #8477-era main), before any plugin module loads.
- The public plugin SDK surface is updated in `src/qwenpaw/plugins/frontend/host.d.ts`.

## Evidence

New integration test (`console/src/plugins/themeTokens.integration.test.ts`) drives the real registry and projection, and asserts **`getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)`** — the value the user actually sees — not the text of the emitted stylesheet:

1. preset applied inline (`--app-surface: #ffffff`) → computed `#ffffff`;
2. plugin registers → light `#123456`, dark `#0a0a0a` (the preset is still inline and still loses);
3. preset switched to `#eeeeee` while the plugin is active → computed stays `#0a0a0a`;
4. `dispose()` → stylesheet removed, computed back to `#eeeeee`;
5. `disposeAll(pluginId)` (plugin unload / logout) → same restore;
6. two plugins take turns → LIFO fallback, then the preset.

Test run (local, Windows, QwenPaw `2.2.2.post1` tree at `18e554bf`):

```
src/plugins/themeTokens.test.ts                 6 passed
src/plugins/themeTokens.integration.test.ts     3 passed
src/plugins/hostSdk/install.test.ts            30 passed
src/plugins/registry/chatExtensions.test.ts    15 passed
                                               ---------
                                               54 passed
```

`prettier --check` and `eslint` are clean on every changed file.

## Test scope

- Type: D (cross-layer: console host init + registry + plugin SDK types)

- Neighbouring: `hostSdk/install.test.ts` covers the public `window.QwenPaw` surface end to end

prs.title: feat(crons): per-run sessions to bound cron job history growth
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every cron execution currently appends its conversation to **one dedicated per-job session** (`share_session=False`). The model context is isolated per run via `CronMemoryIsolate`/`Restore` hooks, but the persisted session keeps every run's messages, and the **full history is loaded into memory (and snapshotted) on each execution**.

For high-frequency jobs this grows without bound. Production example: a job running every 5 minutes accumulated **~7,300 messages / ~9M estimated tokens per day** in its per-job session, eventually exhausting container memory (OOM restart loop). This affects any user with frequent scheduled tasks — the session size scales with `run frequency × lifetime`, not with actual usage.

## Solution

Add an **opt-in per-run session mode** that bounds everything to a single execution:

- **`JobRuntimeSpec.per_run_session`** (default `False`, fully backward compatible): when enabled (and `share_session` is `False`), each execution runs in its own session `cron:{target}:job:{job}:run:{run}`, so context loading and persisted history stay O(single run) regardless of job frequency. Run chats carry a timestamp suffix in their display name so operators can tell runs apart.
- **Lazy retention**: after registering the run chat, the job's run chats are trimmed to the newest `QWENPAW_CRON_RUN_SESSION_KEEP` (default 50) — deleting both the chat specs and their session JSON files, so the chat list and disk stay bounded together. Best-effort by design: trimming failures never affect the run outcome. Run audit facts remain available via cron execution records (`CRON_HISTORY_LIMIT`).
- **`SafeJSONSession.delete_session_file`**: remove one persisted session file (reusing the established path conventions), so retention bounds storage along with the chat list.
- **`create_or_replace_job`**: per-field preservation for omitted runtime flags — `share_session` and `per_run_session` are carried over from the previous definition independently when not explicitly set (the previous block-level check would mis-handle the new field since serialized payloads always carry all fields).

The per-run session id reuses the existing `_safe_session_component` derivation rules (length-bounded, collision-resistant), and the cron memory-isolation hooks require no changes — with per-run sessions their snapshot/restore cost is naturally O(single run).

## Out of scope

- Existing per-job sessions created before enabling the flag are not migrated or swept here (different session-id shape); operators can retire them by re-saving jobs with the flag (new sessions start fresh) or deleting stale chats via the existing chat APIs.

## Testing

- New unit tests: per-run ids differ across executions with the `:run:` prefix; retention trims the oldest run chats (specs + session files) beyond the window while never touching unrelated chats; legacy mode is byte-for-byte behavior-preserved (including the existing `":run:" not in session_id` assertion) and never invokes housekeeping.
- Full unit suite: 16,212 passed; the 53 pre-existing environment failures (sqlite FTS5 / plugin subprocess) are identical with and without this change (verified via baseline stash run).


## Type of Change

- [x] Feature (non-breaking, additive: new opt-in `per_run_session` runtime flag, default `False`)
- [ ] Bug fix / Breaking change / Documentation / Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core (`src/qwenpaw/app/crons/`, `src/qwenpaw/app/chats/session.py`)
- [ ] Console / Channels / Skills / CLI / Documentation

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added/updated and passing locally (584 crons+chats+hooks tests; full suite failures identical to baseline via stash comparison)
- [x] `pre-commit run --files ...` passes on all changed files (black/flake8/pylint/mypy)
- [x] Backward compatible: default behavior unchanged (covered by existing assertions)

prs.title: fix(windows): fall back when CPU architecture is missing

## Description

Managed Windows runtimes can start with a minimal process environment where `platform.machine()` returns an empty string because `PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE` is absent. Local-model initialization then fails with `RuntimeError: Unsupported architecture:`. This is one of the independent failures described in #8565.

This change makes `get_architecture()` fall back on Windows only:

prs.title: fix(xiaoyi): emit working frames so long turns stop looking dead in the client
prs.body:
## Description
Issue #8394: the XiaoYi channel writes nothing user-visible during a long turn — the only traffic is the invisible 30s protocol heartbeat, so a multi-minute turn shows a blank client and users reasonably conclude the bot hung (report: 7m36s of silence, then cancelled).

Minimal plugin-side fix (host contract untouched):

- **codec**: `build_working_msg()` — the A2A `status-update` envelope with `state=working` (same shape as the existing `build_completed_msg`, empty text parts, `final=False`).
- **platform**: `send_working(route)` — best-effort effect-wrapped send, returns False on delivery errors instead of raising, so a keepalive tick can never take down a turn.
- **driver**: after the first outbound send of a response route (`_perform_send`), spawn a per-route keepalive loop from `_platform._spawn` (reusing platform task accounting — cancelled on `stop()` via `_tasks` and explicitly via the new `_working_tasks` map). The loop sends an immediate first working frame (the "received" cue the issue asks for), then one frame every `working_frame_interval` (default 12s). It self-cancels when a later send replaces it, when `_before_cleanup_complete` starts (completed/final frames are about to land), and is hard-bounded by `WORKING_FRAME_MAX_WAIT=1800s` so an abandoned session cannot tick forever.
- **channel.json**: new `working_frame_interval` integer property registered in `config_fields` (set 0 to disable), read `config.get()`-style like `task_timeout_ms`.

The frames ride the existing `agent_response` envelope and keepalive loop never touches the shared driver's delivery journal, mirroring `send_finish_step` best-effort semantics (`continue_on_delivery_error=True`).

## Evidence
- `tests/unit/channels/test_xiaoyi.py` — 9 passed, including 2 new cases:
  - `test_working_frames_tick_between_sends_and_stop_at_cleanup`: a send triggers the keepalive (a `status-update.state=working` frame lands on the wire after the artifact), the loop is alive after `send`, and `channel.response.finish` cancels it (task done).
  - `test_working_frame_interval_zero_disables_keepalive`: config interval 0 → `_working_frame_interval()==0.0` and `_resume_working_frames` registers no task.
- The 4 pre-existing count-based assertions were updated to filter by frame kind/`state` instead of exact totals (working frames now appear between sends by design); frame sequences asserted (artifact → completed → final) are unchanged.
- Environment note: dingtalk/matrix/telegram/discord/twilio channel tests don't collect on this machine (deps `dingtalk_stream`/`nio`/`telegram`/`twilio` not installed) — those failures exist on a clean checkout and are unrelated.
- Local validation: same-turn silence eliminated (immediate working frame + periodic refresh), `py_compile` clean for all four touched plugin modules.

prs.title: fix(desktop): open workspace HTML via the decoded local path
prs.body:
## Description

The legacy desktop bridge (`WebViewAPI`, pywebview shell) opened workspace HTML previews by handing the percent-encoded `file://` URI from `GET /api/workspace/html-file-uri` (`Path.as_uri()`, UTF-8 percent-encoded) straight to `webbrowser.open`.

On Windows, `webbrowser`→`os.startfile`→ShellExecute percent-decodes with the **ANSI code page** — GBK on Chinese systems — so the UTF-8 encoding of a Chinese workspace path is decoded to garbage and Windows reports `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` (issue #8502 复现 A; the same failure mode was verified with `ShellExecuteW` in the issue).

This change decodes the URI host-agnostically with `urllib.request.url2pathname` (UTF-8 aware, converts URI separators to native ones) and passes the **native local path** to `webbrowser.open` instead of the `file://` URL.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8502 (复现 A — the pywebview legacy bridge layer)

**Security Considerations:** None — the resolved URI already passed the loopback + `/api/workspace/html-file-uri` gate; this only changes how the resolved `file` URI is handed to the OS opener (same file the endpoint validated — suffix recheck unchanged).

prs.title: fix(console): disable nginx buffering on /console/chat SSE
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #8516

The `/api/console/chat` SSE responses (the stream itself and the empty reconnect response) did not send `X-Accel-Buffering: no`, unlike every other SSE endpoint (`backup.py`, `portability_imports.py`, `project_directory.py`, `skills_stream.py`, `workspace.py`). The `/approval` control command (and its `/approve` / `/deny` shorthands) answers in hard-coded Chinese, whatever language the agent is set to. Example: an agent with `language: "en"` on Telegram asks for approval in English, the user taps approve, and the bot replies:

- 工具: `driver:mcp:aide-knowledge`
- 请求 ID: `4a23a7a0-490c-43`
- 状态: 正在执行...

This PR:

- moves every user-facing text of `runtime/commands/control/approval_handler.py` into a new en/zh bundle, `runtime/commands/control/approval_i18n.py`. prs.title: fix(hub): preserve shared Docker runtime data ownership
prs.body:
## Description

A non-root Hub can fail to restart a Docker runtime with `EACCES` on `working/config.json`. The container initializes and saves configuration as root. Atomic saves replace the destination inode, so even previously Hub-owned configuration can become root-owned while retaining owner-only permissions. On the next start, the Hub reads configuration in `prepare_workspace_paths` before calling the Docker provisioner and fails before a container can be started.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8517

### How the fix works

1. **Select the shared-data identity inside the container.** Add the stdlib-only `qwenpaw-runtime-user` launcher. It reads the mounted working directory's UID/GID as visible inside the container, rather than hard-coding `1000:1000` or copying host IDs. It rejects symlink working-directory roots and the `65534` overflow identity. If the UID has no account, bootstrap creates the matching user/group entries needed by desktop tools.

2. **Use that identity for every managed application writer.** The entrypoint checks the identity before initialization, including when configuration already exists, and runs `qwenpaw init` through the launcher. Supervisor launches both `qwenpaw app` and the XFCE session through the same launcher. Supervisor, system D-Bus, and Xvfb retain their bootstrap privileges.

3. **Prepare the process before importing QwenPaw.** When switching identities, clear supplementary groups, set the GID, then set the UID. Set `HOME`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`, and `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR`, change to the working directory, and check access to working/secrets/backups before executing the command. This prevents application bootstrap from creating root-owned state. Configuration and secret files keep their restrictive permissions, including `0600`. Outside Hub mode, the launcher executes the original command without switching identity.

4. **Repair existing affected data explicitly.** Add `qwenpaw-runtime-user --repair-data` for administrator use while the runtime is stopped. It uses the working directory's owner as the target and repairs root-owned entries in the working, secrets, and backup directories. It preserves ordinary permission bits, skips symbolic links and nested mounts, and refuses root-owned hard-linked regular files. Normal startup does not recursively change shared-data ownership. Host-side configuration permission errors now explain that data must be repaired and the runtime rebuilt with the updated image; English/Chinese Hub documentation includes the command and rebuild steps.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Documentation

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] Scripts / Deploy
- [x] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests

## Checklist

- [x] Relevant tests pass
- [x] Documentation updated

## Testing

**84 tests passed** in the dedicated disposable Linux test container. It runs under `no-new-privileges` with network disabled and the repository mounted read-only.

### Real filesystem ownership and recovery

- Create working/secrets/backups directories owned by UID/GID `12345:12346`, then execute the real launcher in separate processes. Verify the process UID/GID, cleared supplementary groups, working directory, and HOME.
- Use the production `write_json_atomic` utility to create and subsequently replace `config.json`, workspace `agent.json`, and secret `envs.json`. Verify each file remains owned by UID `12345` with mode `0600`.
- Make `config.json` root-owned again and confirm the managed user gets a real `PermissionError`. Run `--repair-data`, confirm ownership returns to UID `12345` without widening `0600`, and verify reading and subsequent atomic saves succeed.
- Verify a symbolic link leaves its external target unchanged and a root-owned hard link is refused. A separate injected mount-point case verifies that the repair traversal skips a nested directory.

### Hub configuration and lifecycle

- Run the real Hub registry and `RuntimeService` as UID `12345` with a fake provisioner. Exercise start/stop twice, then repeat in a new process reopening the same registry. This covers the Hub's real configuration reads/path rewrites and persistent state across process restarts without launching a full runtime image.
- For unreadable root configuration and workspace agent configuration, verify the Hub reports the ownership-repair guidance, records `FAILED`, and never calls the Docker backend's start method.
- Run the existing Docker provisioner and atomic I/O regression tests alongside these cases.

### Production entrypoint and Supervisor wiring

- Run the actual `entrypoint.sh`, installed launcher, and Supervisor application section with a small application stub that performs atomic configuration writes and asserts its UID/GID and HOME. System and desktop service sections are omitted from this smoke test.
- Boot twice against the same data. Assert initialization runs once, the application starts on both boots, configuration stays owned by UID `12345` at `0600`, and Supervisor's PID file remains root-owned.

Unit tests additionally cover different container-visible UID/GID values, mapped root staying UID `0`, rejection of overflow IDs, user-switch ordering for init/app/desktop commands, standalone behavior, and mount-info path decoding. Mapped-root cases use mocks.

Changed-file AST, trailing-comma, mypy, Flake8, and Pylint checks passed. Black 23.3.0 was checked separately under Python 3.11.

prs.title: fix(scroll): recognize url-referenced media in tool-result folding
prs.body:
## Description

When a chat session accumulates enough turns to trigger context compression, historical completed tool results are inspected by `ScrollContextManager._tool_result_fold_candidates()` to collapse long or media-carrying results into compact pointer stubs (`[scroll folded] ...`).

Previously, `_tool_result_has_inline_media()` only checked for `source.get("type") == "base64"` or `source.type == "base64"`. URL-referenced media blocks (`source.type == "url"`), such as video, audio, or image outputs generated by `send_file_to_user` and similar tools, were not recognized as inline media. Consequently, these media tool results failed the `has_media` check and, having short text captions (<= 200 chars), were skipped by `_tool_result_fold_candidates()`.

As a result, uncollapsed media blocks were carried over across turns and re-spliced verbatim into rebuilt request payloads after compression. Subsequent model API requests failed repeatedly with errors such as `400: Video count 2 exceeds limit 1 per request`, permanently hanging the session for that channel.

This change extends `_tool_result_has_inline_media()` to recognize `source.type == "url"` with non-empty URL values for both dictionary-based and object-based sources.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8474

**Security Considerations:** None.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Why the issue happens

In `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/manager.py`:

```python
    @staticmethod
    def _tool_result_has_inline_media(block: Any) -> bool:
        ...
        for item in output:
            if ScrollContextManager._block_type(item) != "data":
                continue
            source = (
                item.get("source")
                if isinstance(item, dict)
                else getattr(item, "source", None)
            )
            if isinstance(source, dict):
                if source.get("type") == "base64" and source.get("data"):
                    return True
            elif getattr(source, "type", None) == "base64" and getattr(
                source,
                "data",
                None,
            ):
                return True
        return False
```

When a tool output provides a data block with a URL source (`source={"type": "url", "url": "https://..."}`), `_tool_result_has_inline_media` returned `False`.

In `_tool_result_fold_candidates`:

```python
    has_media = self._tool_result_has_inline_media(block)
    if (
        not has_media
        and self._tool_result_text_chars(block) <= _PRE_TRIM_MIN_CHARS
    ):
        continue
```

Because `has_media` was `False` and media tool results generally have little or no text characters (`<= 200`), the block was skipped and never folded. During context compression and payload rebuild, the raw media block remained in the active payload.

## The change

1. In `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/manager.py`, `_tool_result_has_inline_media` now also checks:
   - For dict sources: `source.get("type") == "url" and source.get("url")`
   - For object sources: `getattr(source, "type", None) == "url" and getattr(source, "url", None)`
2. In `tests/unit/agents/context/test_scroll_manager.py`:
   - Added `test_tool_result_has_inline_media_recognizes_url_sources` to test both base64 and URL sources across dict and object representations as well as negative cases.
   - Added `test_pressure_fold_recognizes_url_media_independently_of_text_length` to verify that tool results carrying URL media bypass the text length restriction and fold into pointer stubs under context pressure.

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass

prs.title: perf(skills): install a staged pool skill by renaming it in place (#8013)
prs.body:
## Description

Item 4 of #8013: a pool download copies a skill twice — pool → staging directory, then staging → workspace. When both live on one volume, that second hop is a plain directory rename, so it should not be a full tree copy.

This adds:

- `same_volume(path_a, path_b)` in `skill_system/store.py`. It compares `st_dev` and, for a path that does not exist yet, probes through its nearest existing ancestor — the callers ask this question before creating the target.
- `install_staged_skill_dir(staged_dir, target_dir)`, which renames the already-scanned staged tree into place. It falls back to the existing `copy_skill_dir` when the volumes differ or the filesystem refuses the rename, so behaviour there is unchanged.
- The rollback snapshot gets the same treatment: when the workspace shares a volume with the skill directory, the backup is created beside the workspace instead of in system temp, so restoring it renames it back instead of copying every file again. Cross-volume workspaces keep the old temp-dir backup and the copy-based restore.

Staging itself is untouched: it still carries atomicity and scan isolation, and cross-volume installs still go through both copies.

Two things worth calling out for review:

1. `install_staged_skill_dir` installs the staged tree **as it stands**, so it is only equivalent to `copy_skill_dir` when the stage was produced by it — that copy filters OS artifacts and dereferences symlinks, which a rename cannot do. The pool download builds its stage that way, and the docstring now states the prerequisite.
2. The backup lives inside the workspace directory while a download runs, so it becomes visible to anything that lists the workspace root. It is removed by `_restore_workspace_skill` and by the download route's `finally` in both the success and the failure path.

## Evidence

Targeted tests (`tests/unit/agents/skill_system/test_staged_install.py`, plus the two touched router test modules):

```
182 passed in 11.06s
```

Neighbouring package (`tests/unit/agents/skill_system`, 810 tests):

```
810 passed, 1 warning in 16.14s
```

Pre-commit on every touched file — `check-ast`, `check-yaml`, `check-toml`, `check-json`, `docstring-first`, `fix-encoding-pragma`, `detect-private-key`, `trailing-whitespace`, `add-trailing-comma`, `mypy`, `black`, `flake8`, `pylint`: all Passed.

Covered by the new tests: the volume probe (siblings, and a path that does not exist yet), the rename path installing without calling `copy_skill_dir`, replacement of a pre-existing target that still holds stale files, the fallback when `os.rename` raises, the cross-volume path still copying, cancellation touching nothing, the download actually installing the stage instead of copying it, and the rollback renaming a same-volume backup back.

Not measured: no wall-clock benchmark is included. The change removes a full tree copy, but this PR does not claim a number.

Environment note: this worktree is Windows, so the same-volume path is exercised there; the cross-volume behaviour is covered by monkeypatching `same_volume` to return `False` rather than by a real second volume.

…g control (#8439)

feat(jobs): add thinking_level to JobRuntimeSpec for per-job reasoning control  Close #8439

## Description

Adds per-job reasoning control to cron jobs by introducing `thinking_level` (and optional `thinking_budget`) on `JobRuntimeSpec`.

Today every cron job inherits the agent-level thinking configuration. Users running many pipeline-style jobs (data collection, report generation, format conversion) must create a separate lightweight agent for every job just to turn reasoning off, which is error-prone and hard to maintain. This change lets each job choose:

- `inherit` (default): keep the existing agent/session behavior.
- `off`: disable reasoning for this job.
- `minimal` / `low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh` / `max`: force an effort level for this job.
- `budget`: use an explicit token budget via `thinking_budget`.

The value uses the existing `ThinkingLevel` enum instead of inventing a new `enabled` string. `CronExecutor` passes it through `request_context`, and `AgentBuilder` applies it to a request-scoped copy of `agent_config` after session-level thinking resolution and before model construction. It is never persisted to the shared chat/session.

Backward compatibility:
- New jobs default to `inherit`.
- Existing `jobs.json` files without the new fields load as `inherit`.
- Replacement requests from older clients that omit the fields preserve the stored values.
- `inherit` adds no `request_context` keys and leaves the agent config unchanged.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8439

**Security Considerations:** No authentication, channel, or secret-handling changes. The override is request-scoped and never written to the shared session or persisted agent config, so `share_session=True` cannot leak per-job reasoning settings into another conversation. `runtime` is authoritative in `CronExecutor`; stale or hand-written `cron_thinking_*` keys in the passthrough payload are removed. Invalid hand-written `request_context` overrides are ignored with a warning rather than reaching model construction. `off` remains best-effort, matching existing agent-level behavior: models without a disable control keep their defaults. `thinking_budget` is clamped by the existing model-card resolver.

- The `enabled` value from the original issue was intentionally not introduced: `ThinkingLevel` / `resolve_thinking()` only understands `inherit`, `off`, effort levels, and `budget`. Users can express "force on" with an effort level.

prs.title: feat(memory): add reranker model center with service test, multi-query precision history and auto-verify
prs.body:
## Description

**What this PR does:** Adds a reranker model center to the reranker settings (Runtime Config → Memory & Retrieval), mirroring the existing Embedding model center, and upgrades the ranking-precision verification from a single binary smoke test into a multi-query, persisted, and optionally scheduled metric.

**Why:** A misconfigured reranker is currently invisible until retrieval quality degrades. The new center surfaces configuration status, current model, service verification (connectivity + latency) and a meaningful ranking-precision figure (`correct/total`, 10-run rolling average, sparkline) so a bad model is visible at a glance and its trend can be tracked across restarts.

The overview shows four slots: configuration status, current model, service verification and ranking precision.

### Changes

- **Reranker model center**: `RerankerModelCenter` overview on the same 4-column grid and status styles as the embedding card; session-scoped `rerankerVerificationStore` keyed by agent + service fingerprint, invalidated when the service config changes or the agent switches.
- **Service verification**: `POST /workspace/reranker/test` sends a real rerank request with sample documents (one clearly relevant plus two distractors) and returns latency, relevance scores mapped back to request order, and whether the expected most-relevant document ranked first. The outbound call runs under a hard `asyncio.wait_for` deadline, upstream HTML error pages are stripped to plain text, and the API key is masked in returned messages.
- **Multi-query precision**: runs a 5-case multi-domain suite (password / checkout / unit conversion / planet / subscription) and reports `total`, `correct_count`, `precision` and per-case `scores`/`correct`, instead of a single boolean.
- **Persistent history**: new `reranker_history.py` appends each verification to `WORKING_DIR/reranker_history.json`, keyed by a service fingerprint; new endpoint `GET /workspace/reranker/history?fingerprint=`.
- **Trend UI**: the precision slot shows `correct/total = NN%`, a 10-run rolling average and a mini SVG sparkline; history survives restarts and refreshes.
- **Scheduled auto-verification**: `RerankerConfig.auto_verify_interval_hours` (0 = off) plus a background sweep task in the app lifespan that probes due services.
- **i18n**: strings for the overview, verification and precision slots across all 7 locales.

prs.title: fix(scroll): improve token estimates and recover from context overflow
prs.body:
## Problem

Local token estimates can undercount the actual request, leaving Scroll below its compression threshold while the provider rejects the input. This error was previously unrecognized, so it bypassed overflow recovery:

> The input (265309 tokens) is longer than the model's context length (262144 tokens).

## Changes

- Recognize this context-overflow error.
- After a provider rejection, establish a recovery baseline of at least the configured compression threshold (80% by default), then estimate remaining usage as:
  `max(current_estimate, conservative_baseline - net_reclaimed_tokens)`.
- Calculate net savings from complete request estimates, including replacement summaries and placeholders. Retain the correction for subsequent requests and reset it when the model or context size changes.
- Allow at most two context-recovery attempts per model call, sharing the limit across invocation and stream consumption. Stop retrying when recovery makes no progress or meaningful output has already been emitted.

This remains an estimation safeguard, not an exact match for the provider’s tokenizer.

## Validation

- 129 relevant regression tests passed, covering error recognition, conservative estimates, retry limits, and streaming safeguards.
- All commit hooks passed.
- Not yet validated against a live SGLang/vLLM deployment.

prs.title: feat(chats): add keyword and agentic conversation search
prs.body:
## Description

Automatically generated titles do not reliably contain the words users remember from a conversation. With a large history, a title-only filter can miss the exact discussion even when its messages contain the requested information.

This PR adds content search and agentic search to the existing conversation-history sidebar. For example, searching `PostgreSQL` now finds a conversation titled “A technical discussion” when its messages describe a PostgreSQL migration. Users who remember the intent instead of the wording can select **AI search** and describe the conversation in natural language.

Related: #1578.

### User experience

| Mode | Interaction | Retrieval |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keyword | Type in the existing sidebar field; results update after a 275 ms debounce | Case-insensitive literal matching across titles and saved user/assistant messages, with pagination |
| AI search | Enter a description and explicitly submit with Enter or the search button | The current agent's configured model refines queries, pages through candidates, reads matching conversations, and selects relevant results |

Results show the conversation title and a highlighted excerpt. Clicking opens the existing conversation; clearing the field restores the normal grouped history. The compact mode switch and results use the existing sidebar styling and theme variables. Loading, empty results, retry, and partial results have dedicated states. Switching agents or editing the query cancels the client request and prevents stale results from entering the current view.

### Screenshots

Captured from commit `aa9b3f2f` in a local Console connected to the real backend, using three synthetic conversations.

**Search message contents, even when the title does not contain the keyword.** Searching `PostgreSQL` returns two conversations with highlighted matching excerpts; the unrelated reading conversation is excluded.

![Keyword search finds body-only matches and highlights the matching text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hehuang139/QwenPaw/f2787b8022e2d2ff6ba021b24c3a93d77b333e0c/docs/pr-evidence/8367/keyword-search.jpg)

**Open the original conversation from a search result.** Selecting “A technical discussion” opens its saved transcript while keeping the search results available in the sidebar.

![Opening a search result displays the original conversation transcript](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hehuang139/QwenPaw/f2787b8022e2d2ff6ba021b24c3a93d77b333e0c/docs/pr-evidence/8367/open-conversation.jpg)

### Design and implementation

- Add agent-scoped `POST /chats/search` with `query`, `mode`, `limit`, and `offset`. Both modes search the selected agent's unarchived conversations and exclude app-owned dialogues.
- Read current and legacy session snapshots plus the configured Scroll history database, including imported history and older messages removed from live context by compaction. Extract user/assistant text while filtering reasoning, tool results, and tagged runtime messages. Restore original attachment input when snapshot metadata is available, and prefer snapshot message IDs over duplicate durable representations. Older durable attachment turns without original-content metadata can retain generated file-upload descriptions in search results.
- Keep keyword search independent of model configuration. Use existing persistence and SQLite support, with no new dependency, embedding service, index migration, or vector database.
- Implement an ephemeral model-driven search loop with only `search`, `read`, and `finish` actions. It can reformulate terms and inspect older pages. Final results are resolved from retrieved server-side candidates, so invented IDs cannot become links. The search does not instantiate the general-purpose agent or write conversation history.
- Bound each corpus scan to 64 MiB and five seconds; cap individual snapshots/history rows at 16 MiB. AI search allows six model responses in 45 seconds, 60 candidates, and bounded transcript/output sizes. Preserve retrieved results and mark them partial when a budget is exhausted. Missing models, invalid responses, and provider failures return explicit errors.
- Preserve canonical result IDs through sidebar navigation, including results discovered before the next session-list refresh. Add English/Chinese UI strings and Console documentation.

**Security considerations:** reuse the existing agent-scoped request dependencies; constrain transcript files to the session directory; open history SQLite connections read-only and filter by exact agent/session identity. Historical text is treated as data and the model has no filesystem, command, or network tools.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console

Backend tests cover snapshots, durable/imported history, literal/Unicode matching, pagination, agent boundaries, bounded scans, model-guided retrieval and a real HTTP app. Frontend tests cover search submission/cancellation, API integration, canonical navigation and existing sidebar behavior. TypeScript (`tsc -b --noEmit`), ESLint for changed TypeScript files, all applicable changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.

prs.title: feat(desktop): add approval notifications (#8460)
prs.body: ## Description Introduces a unified system notification feature, ensuring users receive timely alerts—such as approval requests, completed responses, and background task updates—even when the application is running in the background. Closed #8460 - Centralized notification management under "Settings → General," featuring a master toggle. Options for approval requests and completed responses include "Disabled," "Background Only," and "Always Enabled." Scheduled tasks, heartbeat signals, and email notifications can be configured individually. - Supports browser-based notifications as well as native system notifications on macOS, Windows, and Linux. On desktop, a Rust-based background polling mechanism ensures alerts are received even when the application window is minimized to the system tray. - Clicking a notification brings the application to the foreground and navigates directly to the relevant Agent, conversation, approval card, or inbox message. If an approval session is no longer valid, the user is redirected to the approval list. - Implements notification deduplication, filters out initial snapshot history, automatically dismisses expired or already-processed approval requests, and includes retry logic for failed deliveries—all to minimize redundant or obsolete alerts. - The backend now stores short-term, non-consumable notification event snapshots. Completion events are triggered only upon the successful finalization of a response, while empty "heartbeat" signals are filtered out. - Enhanced permission management, including streamlined authorization access, automatic UI refreshes upon permission changes, and direct access to system notification settings. prs.title: fix(plugins): trust HOME over the passwd home when locking dependency state
prs.body:
## Description

在受限部署环境（fnOS NAS 应用沙箱）里，专用应用账户的 passwd home 目录往往不存在且 `/home` 不可写。`qwenpaw/plugins/dependency_maintenance.py` 的 `state_root()` 在解析依赖锁根目录时**优先取 `pwd.getpwuid().pw_dir`**，只有在该值为空或非绝对路径时才回落到 `os.environ["HOME"]` — 于是 `_open_lock()` 的 `Path(...).mkdir(parents=True)` 在导入期直接抛出 `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/home/qwenpaw'`，进程必然退出（issue #8515）。

现在代码里其实有覆盖变量 `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR`（优先级最高），但错误提示里没有它的名字，受限环境的用户无从得知。

本 PR：

1. **解析顺序改为 `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR` → $HOME → pw_dir**（与多数 Unix 工具一致；HOME 反映的是实际启动环境）；
2. 非绝对路径候选一律跳过（不再回落依赖路径的可用性假设）；
3. 兜底 RuntimeError 的提示改为**点名覆盖变量**：`Set an absolute shared QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR (checked first) or fix HOME for the service account.`，给出可操作的恢复路径。

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8515

**Security Considerations:** 无（仅路径解析顺序与错误消息；锁目录定位逻辑本身不变，覆盖变量原本就是最高优先级入口）

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] CLI
- [x] Tests

## Testing

```
uv run pytest tests/unit/plugins/test_install_lock.py -q
5 failed, 20 passed, 10 skipped
```
- 5 failed 与改动前（`git stash` 后同号 baseline）完全一致，均为 `test_observation_child_custody_is_temporary[*]` 既存失败（Windows 基线），与本改动无关。
- 新增 `test_state_root_missing_home_error_names_the_override`（POSIX-only，Windows 上 skip）：passwd 指向不存在/不可写目录、HOME 未设时，错误信息必须点名 `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR`。
- `test_state_root_selection_is_stable` 增补 `home_wins_over_passwd` 用例：HOME 与 passwd home 同时存在且 passwd 目录无效时，选择 HOME（旧顺序时它是选 passwd → 改前该用例会失败意义上的行为契约变化）。

## Evidence

```
$ uv run pytest tests/unit/plugins/test_install_lock.py -q
..ss.....ss..s........ss             [100%]
5 failed, 20 passed, 10 skipped in 8.06s

$ git stash && uv run pytest tests/unit/plugins/test_install_lock.py -q | tail -1
5 failed, 20 passed, 8 skipped in 7.16s     # same 5 failures (pre-existing Windows baseline)
```

改动只改变 POSIX 家目录选取顺序与错误文案；Windows 分支（`USERPROFILE`）与 override 分支行为不变。`ruff check` 对两个触点文件通过；`ruff format --check` 报出的 hunks 均为该文件既存未格式化区域（与 stash 后基线一致，未触碰）。

prs.title: fix(pack): force-include console channel in PyInstaller bundle
prs.body:
## Description

`PyInstaller` cannot follow the dynamic `importlib.import_module(".console", ...)` call in `src/qwenpaw/app/channels/registry.py:_load_builtin_channels`. The console channel is therefore silently omitted from the Tauri sidecar bundle, and a packaged QwenPaw Desktop app fails to start with a hard `ModuleNotFoundError` on `qwenpaw.app.channels.console.channel`.

**Related Issue:** Affects only Tauri/PyInstaller desktop builds. Server, Docker, and \`pip install -e\` deployments are unaffected.

## What Problem This Solves

\`_load_builtin_channels\` walks a literal map of channel-id → (module, class) and loads each one with \`importlib.import_module\`. PyInstaller's static analysis only follows syntactic \`import\` statements, so the literal-string import targets are invisible to the bundler. The console channel is also listed in \`_REQUIRED_CHANNEL_KEYS\` (\`registry.py:31\`), so the missing import surfaces as a startup failure rather than a soft skip.

This PR adds an explicit \`hiddenimports\` entry so the package is bundled; the submodule \`console.channel\` is then pulled in by \`console/__init__.py\`'s existing \`from .channel import ConsoleChannel\` re-export, so a single entry is sufficient.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Build / packaging

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Build / Packaging

## Testing

Verify on macOS / Windows after rebuilding the desktop bundle:

\`\`\`bash
pyinstaller scripts/pack-tauri/qwenpaw.spec
# Launch the packaged app; the console channel should load without
# ModuleNotFoundError on qwenpaw.app.channels.console.channel.
\`\`\`

Source install (\`pip install -e\`) and Docker/server deployments are unaffected because they import from the live source tree.

## Evidence

A standalone import reproduces the bundling dependency:

\`\`\`bash
$ python3 -c "
import importlib
m = importlib.import_module('qwenpaw.app.channels.console')
print('imported:', m.__name__)
print('channel attr present:', hasattr(m, 'channel'))
"
imported: qwenpaw.app.channels.console
channel attr present: True
\`\`\`

Importing the parent package triggers \`console/__init__.py\`, which in turn re-exports \`console.channel\` via \`from .channel import ConsoleChannel\`. Therefore a single \`hiddenimports\` entry for \`qwenpaw.app.channels.console\` is enough to guarantee both the package and its submodule ship in the bundle.

prs.title: fix(memory): stop leaking auto-memory-recall payload to channels
prs.body:
## Description

The auto-memory-recall pipeline injected a synthetic `memory_search` tool interaction (`ToolCallBlock` + `ToolResultBlock`) into the LLM context. Two problems followed from that:

- models that observe a tool interaction in their own context tend to imitate it out loud in the next user-facing reply ("I'll check memory for relevant context…"), which leaks the internal recall flow to the user and to outbound channels;
- the payload had to be kept off the wire with a dedicated `AUTO_MEMORY_SEARCH_BLOCK_HIDDEN_KEY` metadata flag plus a channel-renderer guard and a console tool-card guard — three cooperating layers, none of which was actually connected (see *Root cause*).

This PR carries the recall payload in a single `HintBlock` instead. Every provider formatter (OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / DashScope / Ollama) turns a hint into a separate `role="user"` message, so the request never ends with an assistant turn; and the console / PawApp history converter skips hint blocks entirely, so the payload never reaches a transcript. Because the block type already covers both concerns, the hidden flag and the two guards are gone. The middleware recognises the message through the pre-existing `AUTO_MEMORY_SEARCH_BLOCK_IDS_KEY`, which the block-cleanup path already uses, so the transient injection and cleanup behaviour are unchanged.

The branch is rebased onto the latest `main`.

## Root cause

Two independent issues, both reproduced against the real converter and the real formatters before the change:

1. **Assistant prefill.** With the payload in a `TextBlock`, the Anthropic formatter emitted the recall as an assistant turn, so the request ended with `role="assistant"`. Anthropic reads a trailing assistant turn as a prefill continuation, which Claude 4.6+ rejects.
2. **The hiding logic was not connected.** `agentscope_msg_to_message()` nests the original metadata under `message.metadata["metadata"]`, while the renderer guard only checked the top level, so `_is_auto_memory_recall_message()` never fired and the recall text was rendered to the channel as an ordinary assistant message. The console guard did not help either: it lived on the tool-card path, which the payload no longer used, and the tool-card adapter did not forward the metadata the guard checked.

## Evidence

The two issues above were reproduced against the real converter and the real provider formatters before the change, and the same paths were re-checked after it. The payload never appears in an outbound message, and the model request never ends with an assistant turn.

### Before / after, against the real converter and formatters

Request tail, Anthropic:

```
before: [{"role": "user",     "content": [...]},
         {"role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "<auto_memory_recall>..."}]}]   # assistant tail -> prefill
after:  [{"role": "user",     "content": [...]},
         {"role": "user",     "content": [{"text": "<auto_memory_recall>..."}]}]   # no assistant turn
```

History conversion:

```
before: agentscope_msg_to_message([recall]) -> 1 message containing the payload
after:  agentscope_msg_to_message([recall]) -> 0 messages
```

The renderer guard before the change:

```
message.metadata = {"original_id": ..., "original_name": "memory_search",
                    "metadata": {"auto_memory_search_hidden": true, ...}, ...}
                                   ^ nested here
guard checks:    message.metadata.get("auto_memory_search_hidden")   # top level -> misses
=> rendered parts: 1  (full recall payload sent to the channel)
```

### Formatter coverage

The request ends with a `user` turn and contains no `assistant` turn for: Anthropic, OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, Gemini, DashScope, Ollama (and DeepSeek / MiniMax, which share the OpenAI base formatter).

### Local verification evidence

- `tests/unit/agents/memory/test_base_memory_manager.py` + `tests/unit/agents/test_memory_middleware.py` + `tests/unit/agents/memory/test_auto_memory_recall_payload.py` + `tests/unit/app/chats/test_utils.py`: **131 passed**
- `black --line-length=79`, `flake8 --extend-ignore=E203`, `pylint` (repository pre-commit arguments): clean, **10.00/10**

### Regression tests added

`tests/unit/agents/memory/test_auto_memory_recall_payload.py` — four test functions, ten execution cases:

- `test_final_request_carries_the_recall_as_a_user_turn` (parametrized over the six QwenPaw formatter wrappers — Anthropic, OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, Gemini, DashScope and Ollama): the request ends with a `user` turn carrying the recall, the recalled text itself is present, and there is no `assistant` turn;
- `test_recall_is_injected_and_reused_from_the_cache`: the recall is injected right after the user turn without touching the agent context, and the same turn then reuses the serialized cache instead of searching again — the reloaded message is compared against the original payload (same hint text, same block id);
- `test_recall_is_omitted_from_the_converted_transcript`: the real conversion path (`agentscope_msg_to_message`) drops the recall — exactly the user message and the normal reply remain;
- `test_next_user_turn_replaces_the_cached_recall` (parametrized over a second turn with fresh results and with no results): the stale evidence disappears either way.

The two middleware tests that this supersedes — `test_search_result_only_updates_current_model_input` and `test_new_turn_replaces_search_cache` — are removed: they patched the extraction step out, while the new test drives the real path. The tool-call follow-up test and all six formatter variants are kept.

## Changes

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/qwenpaw/agents/memory/base_memory_manager.py` | carry the recall payload in a `HintBlock` instead of a text/thinking/tool_call/tool_result quartet |
| `src/qwenpaw/agents/middlewares.py` | `_is_auto_memory_recall_msg` helper; memory-extraction filter accepts the recall message |
| `src/qwenpaw/constant.py` | remove the now unused `AUTO_MEMORY_SEARCH_TEXT` / `_THINKING_PREFIX` |
| `tests/unit/agents/memory/test_auto_memory_recall_payload.py` | new regression tests (final request, conversion path, middleware injection path) |
| `tests/unit/agents/test_memory_middleware.py` | drop the two middleware tests that the new real-path test supersedes |

5 files, +345 / -127 lines. No new metadata flag and no renderer or frontend guard: the block type handles both, so the payload cannot reach a transcript even if a future channel renders messages directly.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Ready for review

labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: topic:identity-access
labels.description: Authentication, OIDC, principal isolation, and authorization; former milestone #17.

issues.body:
When a request to the gateway carries an OIDC token, the gateway checks it, and in one common setup that check means calling the identity provider over the network. The pairing, webhook and enrollment endpoints all limit how often a client can make the gateway do work like this, but the token-check path has no limit at all. Anyone who can reach the gateway can send junk tokens over and over, and each one makes the gateway call the identity provider, which can get ZeroClaw blocked at the provider and lock out all real users.

### Affected component

gateway/api

### Severity

S1 - workflow blocked

### Current behavior

The config route layer verifies every request that names an `oidc.<alias>` provider through `RpcInboundAuth::authenticate` (`crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/principal_gate.rs:495-570`). With `validation = "introspection"` each verification is one authenticated call to the identity provider with a 15 second timeout (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/security/auth_provider/oidc.rs:713-770`). The gateway's `auth_limiter` guards only `POST /pair` and webhooks (`lib.rs:3163`, `lib.rs:3688`), and the enrollment relay has its own limiter plus a 16-permit outbound semaphore, but this path has neither.

### Expected behavior

Failed bearer verifications should count against a per-client attempt limiter, as pairing and enrollment already do. Outbound introspection calls should be capped in flight so a burst cannot hold many connections to the provider. JWKS verification is already bounded by the 30 second refresh cooldown, and introspection should have a comparable bound.

### Steps to reproduce

```text
1. Configure [oidc.corp] with validation = "introspection" and expose the gateway beyond loopback.
2. From a remote host, send many GET /api/config/list requests with
   "Authorization: Bearer junk" and "X-ZeroClaw-Auth-Provider: oidc.corp".
3. Each request produces one introspection call at the provider, and none is refused early.
Source-traced at master 5d4b18d335; not executed.
```

### Impact

An unauthenticated client can make the gateway call the identity provider once per request using the daemon's client secret. Provider-side throttling or a lockout of the ZeroClaw client then denies every legitimate OIDC user, including RPC clients. The gateway also holds one 15 second outbound connection per request, which is a cheap way to exhaust it. Related tracker #8289.

### Logs / stack traces

_No response_

### ZeroClaw version

master 5d4b18d335 (v0.8.7)

### Rust version

n/a (source review); CI pins 1.98.0

### Operating system

Any; reviewed in source on macOS

### Regression?

No, first-time setup

### Pre-flight checks

- [ ] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
Source-traced at master 5d4b18d335; no runtime reproduction was run.
- [X] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

### Recommended action

Put the OIDC bearer path on an attempt limiter keyed by client address, booking only failed verifications, with the loopback exemption the other limiters share. Add an outbound semaphore for introspection calls, sized like the enrollment relay's 16 permits, and refuse with 503 and `Retry-After` when it is full. Consider a short negative cache for rejected opaque tokens so a replayed junk token costs no second call.

issues.body:
### Affected component

security/sandbox

### Severity

S0 - data loss / security risk

### Current behavior

When an SOP decision-model response omits or malforms the start gate but supplies a valid confident Auto mode answer, the default `gate_on_error = "run_strict"` path can start the run in Auto rather than its strict fallback. This can remove the SOP-level approval that the failure policy promises. Explicit per-step confirmations and the agent's own policy still apply.

Source inspection confirms the branch at master `73e2a4a15ddbdb01ffb4a044dc6c5c8dd7835110`. It was introduced by #11085, commit `e12c773edee5f2038fb0e7e5712cce1eea9ac6a4`. Released-version impact has not been established.

In [decision.rs:434-459](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/73e2a4a15ddbdb01ffb4a044dc6c5c8dd7835110/crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/sop/decision.rs#L434), a missing or malformed `start_sop` answer sets `gate_failed = true`. Under `RunStrict`, `start` becomes true. The mode branch checks `gate_failed` only when the configured modes list is empty; otherwise it accepts a valid high-confidence `execution_mode` answer, including Auto.

The SOP engine applies the decided mode to the run. Auto skips SOP-level approval, while explicit per-step confirmation/checkpoint controls remain separate. The [documented fail-closed contract](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/73e2a4a15ddbdb01ffb4a044dc6c5c8dd7835110/docs/book/src/sop/decision-models.md#L82) says malformed answers never reduce supervision.

### Expected behavior

A missing or malformed gate answer under `run_strict` must select the strict fallback before considering a mode answer. With the example mode list, the result must use StepByStep.

### Steps to reproduce

Source-derived test case; not an executed reproduction:

Use the existing `spec()` and `answers()` resolver fixtures in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/sop/decision.rs`:

1. Use an authored Supervised SOP with a decision gate, default RunStrict, and listed modes Auto, Supervised and StepByStep.
2. Build `answers(0.95, "auto", PROBS_AUTO, 0.9)`, then remove `GATE_QUESTION` from the answer map.
3. Pass the resulting answer to `resolve`.
4. The inspected control flow returns `start = true` and `mode = Some(Auto)`. Expected: `mode = Some(StepByStep)`.

Also cover an out-of-range gate probability with the same valid Auto choice. This is a source-derived test case, not output from an executed test. No runtime reproduction was performed.

### Impact

The SOP must opt into decision-model gating and mode selection, permit Auto among its choices, and retain RunStrict. A partially malformed model response then selects less supervision than the configured error policy. No untrusted actor's ability to cause that response has been demonstrated.

### Logs / stack traces

_No response — no runtime test was executed._

### ZeroClaw version

73e2a4a15ddbdb01ffb4a044dc6c5c8dd7835110 (current master inspected; released-version impact not established)

### Rust version

Not applicable to this source-only report; no build was run.

### Operating system

Platform-independent source path; inspected from macOS. No platform runtime reproduction.

### Regression?

Unknown

The affected path was introduced by the PR identified above; no before/after runtime test was performed.

### Pre-flight checks

- [ ] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
- [x] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

Current master source was verified, but the runtime reproduction checkbox is intentionally unchecked.

### Suggested minimal fix

Choose the strict fallback whenever `gate_failed` is true, before testing whether the modes list is empty or accepting the mode answer. Reuse the existing resolver fixtures for the missing/invalid gate cases and assert that the selected mode retains strict supervision.

### Related work

Introduced by #11085. #11113 and #11115 repair fixtures/build integration, not this decision branch. Searches of open and closed issues for SOP malformed gates and `run_strict` found no duplicate.

issues.body:
### Affected component

security/sandbox

### Severity

S0 - data loss / security risk

### Current behavior

Source review of the landed #10265 commit found that session-data tools can bypass the RPC principal-ownership boundary. A non-admin principal allowed to use `sessions_history` can read another principal's transcript when both sessions use the same agent. I have not executed a runtime reproduction.

The RPC ACP construction path passes the session store into the Agent, which [constructs `AcpSessionReadView` with only the agent alias](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/73e2a4a15ddbdb01ffb4a044dc6c5c8dd7835110/crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/agent.rs#L2317-L2318). The view [classifies and loads records by agent, not principal](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/73e2a4a15ddbdb01ffb4a044dc6c5c8dd7835110/crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/sessions.rs#L45-L92). [`sessions_history`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/73e2a4a15ddbdb01ffb4a044dc6c5c8dd7835110/crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/sessions.rs#L450-L478) then loads same-agent ACP history or a chat backend key without checking its owner. `sessions_list` also enumerates shared chat metadata without principal filtering.

[`sessions_send`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/73e2a4a15ddbdb01ffb4a044dc6c5c8dd7835110/crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/sessions.rs#L665-L709) rejects ACP targets, but its chat fallback resolves an existing chat key and appends a user message without checking the target principal. A non-admin with `sessions_send` and the required tool-action permission can therefore modify another principal's chat history. `sessions_current` is different: it accepts no target ID and reports the turn's current session, so it is not evidence of this arbitrary-target bypass.

The new constrained-session path retains explicitly allowed session tools. The list, history, send, and current tool implementations do not override the default `requires_unrestricted_principal() == false`. Passing the current session ID into the turn identifies the caller's session but does not establish authority over the records a cross-session tool reads or writes. Existing different-agent isolation tests do not cover two principals sharing one agent.

The predecessor refused named/constrained tool sessions; #10265 admits that caller class without making this alternate data-access path principal-aware. #9746 concerns agent scoping, which is related but does not provide principal isolation. This repair belongs under the session-ownership contract in #8290.

### Expected behavior

Cross-session data tools must apply the same canonical principal-ownership boundary as RPC session operations to both reads and writes, including chat fallback. A tool grant authorizes use of the tool, not access to every principal's records.

Either pass principal-aware read views/predicates into the tools or temporarily withhold principal-unaware cross-session tools from all authenticated non-admin callers. The containment must include non-admin callers with wildcard tool and agent selectors: marking the tools `requires_unrestricted_principal` alone is insufficient because that caller path skips narrowing.

A focused two-principal, same-agent test should deny foreign-session history while allowing the caller's own history. Cover the chat append boundary with a harmless message and verify that denial leaves the foreign transcript unchanged. Any temporary exclusion should also verify that wildcard non-admin grants cannot bypass it.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# Source-derived regression scenario; not executed.
# 1. Create principals zeroclaw_user and zeroclaw_operator, neither an admin.
# 2. Allow both to use zeroclaw_agent; allow zeroclaw_operator sessions_history.
# 3. Persist an ACP session owned by zeroclaw_user with a harmless marker.
# 4. Start zeroclaw_operator's own RPC session on the same agent.
# 5. Invoke its retained sessions_history tool with the other session's fixture ID.
# Expected: foreign transcript denied; own-session history remains available.
# Source path: agent-only classification accepts the foreign same-agent record.
```

### Impact

Multi-principal deployments that share an agent and permit session-data tools can expose another principal's conversation content or session metadata. Permitted `sessions_send` use can also append a message to a foreign chat transcript. This does not require administrator status or grant revocation. Separate agent aliases provide a different boundary and do not fix same-agent principal isolation.

### Logs / stack traces

```text
No runtime logs captured. Evidence is the linked source at the landed commit.
```

### ZeroClaw version

`73e2a4a15ddbdb01ffb4a044dc6c5c8dd7835110` (landed #10265).

### Rust version

Not built locally for this report; source inspection only.

### Operating system

No runtime reproduction on a specific OS. The identified data-access path is platform-independent Rust code.

### Regression?

Unknown

Source comparison establishes that constrained sessions are newly admitted; no before/after runtime comparison was performed.

### Pre-flight checks

- [ ] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
- [x] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

The reproduction checkbox is intentionally unchecked because this is a source-review finding.

issues.body:
Some agent tools do things that should be reserved for operators, like scheduling jobs or messaging other agents. The code only removes those tools from a limited user when that user has a named list of tools, so a limited user who is allowed "all tools" keeps every one of them. That means a signed-in user with no cron or SOP permissions can still schedule jobs that run as the daemon, talk to agents they were never given, and run procedures that the normal API would refuse.

### Affected component

security/sandbox

### Severity

S0 - data loss / security risk

### Current behavior

The agent registry removes tools that need an unrestricted principal only when the principal has a named tool list, in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/agent.rs:3043-3046`. A non-admin with `tools = ["execute"]` and `allowed_tools = ["*"]` resolves to no ceiling at all in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/dispatch.rs:601-619`, so nothing is removed for them. Only `delegate`, `spawn_subagent` and `execute_pipeline` carry the marker, while `cron_add`, `cron_update`, `cron_remove`, `cron_run`, `cron_runs`, `schedule`, `send_message_to_peer`, `sop_execute`, `sop_advance` and `sop_approve` do not and check no principal.

### Expected behavior

Every tool that does operator work should be withheld from any non-admin principal, including one with a wildcard selector. The cron, schedule, peer messaging and SOP tools should carry the same marker as `delegate` and `spawn_subagent`. A scoped principal should reach these actions only through the RPC methods, which already require the matching `cron` and `sops` grants (`dispatch.rs:435-441`, `:502-512`).

### Steps to reproduce

```text
1. Configure a non-admin permission profile with sessions create/execute, tools = ["execute"],
   allowed_tools = ["*"], an agent whose risk profile allows the cron tools, and no cron grant.
2. Sign in with an OIDC token that maps to that profile and open a chat session on that agent.
3. Ask the agent to call cron_add with a shell job: the job is created and runs as the daemon,
   although the principal holds no cron grant and cron/add over RPC would be refused.
Source-traced at master 5d4b18d335; not executed.
```

### Impact

A scoped user can schedule jobs that run as the daemon with no principal and, per #10968, no approval checks. They can also run turns on peer agents outside their `allowed_agents` selector, attributed to the sending agent alias (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/send_message_to_peer.rs:469`), and drive SOPs that the RPC methods would refuse. Issues #11127, #11123, #11198, #11239 and #10968 cover neighbouring gaps, and the only fixes for this part are the stale drafts #11230 and #11410; related tracker #8289.

### Logs / stack traces

_No response_

### ZeroClaw version

master 5d4b18d335 (v0.8.7)

### Rust version

n/a (source review); CI pins 1.98.0

### Operating system

Any; reviewed in source on macOS

### Regression?

No, first-time setup

### Pre-flight checks

- [ ] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
Source-traced at master 5d4b18d335; no runtime reproduction was run.
- [X] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

### Recommended action

Mark the cron, schedule, `send_message_to_peer`, `sop_execute`, `sop_advance` and `sop_approve` tools as requiring an unrestricted principal, as draft #11410 does. Strip marked tools for every non-admin principal, not only for principals with a named tool list, as draft #11230 does for the session tools. Add a test that builds a wildcard non-admin session and asserts that none of these tools is present in its registry.
