prs.title: fix(gateway): limit and cap OIDC bearer verification on the config route group
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The config/onboarding route group verified every OIDC bearer with nothing in front of it: no attempt ledger and no cap on verifications in flight, while with `validation = "introspection"` each verification is an authenticated round trip to the identity provider under the daemon's own client credentials. Anyone who could reach the gateway could make it call the provider once per request, get the daemon's client throttled there, and, through session re-verification, end every dashboard session.
  - `config_route_auth` now takes a `ConfigRouteAuth` state carrying `BearerVerificationLimits`: a per-client attempt ledger (the shared thresholds: 10 refused credentials in a minute, then a 5-minute lockout, loopback exempt) on a ledger of its own, and a process-wide 16-permit cap on verifications in flight, held for the verification alone and refused (503, `Retry-After: 5`) rather than queued, loopback included.
  - Only `AUTH_REQUIRED` denials are booked. A `FORBIDDEN` denial is a verified identity the policy grants nothing, or the provider unreachable, throttling or misconfigured; neither says anything about the caller.
  - The client key is `client_key_from_request`, the same derivation every other rate-limited gateway surface uses, so this composes with #12114 unchanged.
  - Docs: the limits are recorded in `security/authentication.md` beside the route-layer description, and `auth_rate_limit.rs` names the three ledgers built from it.
- **Scope boundary:** The config route group's OIDC bearer path only. Not changed: the native pairing-bearer branch (its legacy 401 shape stays byte-for-byte), the enrollment relay and its own three limits, dashboard session classification and re-verification (#12096), the pending-flow store (#12049), forwarded-header keying (#12114), any runtime crate. No negative token cache (recorded as a follow-up option on the issue).
- **Blast radius:** Scripted clients that present an OIDC bearer per request to `/api/config/*`, `/api/quickstart/*`, `/api/channels/bind`: a client refused ten times in a minute gets 429 for five minutes; more than 16 verifications in flight at once get 503 with `Retry-After: 5`. Valid tokens are never booked. Native bearers and dashboard sessions see no change. Test constructors that build the route group now pass a `ConfigRouteAuth`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12047. Related #8289, #12052, #12096.

### What this does, simply

When a client sends the gateway an OIDC token, the gateway checks it, and in one common setup that check is a network call to the identity provider using the daemon's own client secret. Pairing, webhooks and the browser sign-in relay all limit how often one client can make the gateway do that kind of work; the token check did not. A remote client could send junk tokens in a loop, every one costing a call to the provider, until the provider throttled or locked the daemon's client, at which point every real OIDC user was refused and every signed-in dashboard user was signed out at their next check.

Now a client whose tokens keep being refused is locked out for five minutes after ten refusals in a minute, on a ledger of its own so a stale-token loop never locks anyone out of pairing, and at most sixteen token checks are in flight at once across all clients, so a burst cannot hold many connections to the provider. A provider outage is not held against the caller, and a valid token is never counted. Dashboard sessions are checked by their own layer and never wait behind these limits.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes: an A/B against a provider with `validation = "introspection"` makes the delta visible in the provider's own logs.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`, the gateway's config route group over HTTP. No messaging channel.
- **Setup / preconditions:** One `[oidc.<alias>]` with `validation = "introspection"` and a reachable introspection endpoint; the gateway listening beyond loopback.
- **Steps to run:** From a remote host, send 12 requests of `GET /api/config/list` with `Authorization: Bearer junk` and `X-ZeroClaw-Auth-Provider: oidc.<alias>`. Then, from 17 addresses at once (or 17 concurrent connections behind a proxy with `trust_forwarded_headers` off), send the same request while the provider is slow to answer.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The first 10 return 401 and show as 10 introspection calls at the provider; the 11th and 12th return 429 with `Retry-After: 300` and produce no provider call. Of the 17 concurrent ones, 16 reach the provider and one returns 503 with `Retry-After: 5`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** All 12 return 401 and all 12 reach the provider; all 17 concurrent requests reach it, and the loop can continue at any rate.

### How I tested

#### Current fixture validation (2026-11-04)

Revision `462c8f38eca5158193b36fe18f9a6201d1241060`, tree `01f4f9ac2747973b514cdde47099a6c379118bf9`; macOS ARM64 / Rust 1.97.1.

The live forwarded-header test started its true-to-false case with a forwarded loopback address. #12114 correctly bills that request to its remote peer, so the first request already consumes one of the ten attempts; the test then expects an extra allowed request. I reproduced the combined failure at attempt 9 (429 instead of 401). The fixture now starts with a different non-loopback forwarded address, then confirms that publishing the opposite trust setting bills the peer’s fresh ledger. All assertions remain, including both policy directions and the provider-call count. Production behavior is unchanged.

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# passed on 462c8f38eca5158193b36fe18f9a6201d1241060
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib
# 784 passed on 462c8f38eca5158193b36fe18f9a6201d1241060
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
# passed on 462c8f38eca5158193b36fe18f9a6201d1241060

# Temporary local combination with #12114 at 16a4015b010e3638295d5a289e43885db9ad90b3:
git merge --no-commit --no-ff 16a4015b010e3638295d5a289e43885db9ad90b3
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib
# 788 passed, combined tree 479d12a6fe6b279e7310e4e6666de585db279b4b
git merge --abort
# restored the clean candidate; no dependency merge is published
```

The original fixture was also run in an unmodified `3c1c664ca2b8d88fa78ee830e9b658194f7831ec` plus #12114 combination with `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib principal_gate::tests::bearer_client_keys_follow_persisted_forwarded_header_trust -- --exact`: it failed with the expected 429/401 mismatch. The repaired combined suite passes. The final change and evidence were independently checked. Apple’s large `__eh_frame` linker warning appeared during tests; tests and strict Clippy passed.

**Remaining validation:** Full-workspace tests, native Windows execution, and a real identity-provider/reverse-proxy run were not performed in this fixture-only repair. The HTTP regressions use the real route group and mock provider. Hosted CI and required human review must run on the new head. #12114 still needs its own review and landing; this test fix does not deliver its proxy behavior.

Hosted validation update (2026-11-05T04:55:43.427584+00:00): the [required CI gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41969394376/job/127057541060) passed, with 52 successful checks, eight skipped and no failures or pending checks. The [Linux workspace job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41969394376/job/127053849403) passed `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`: 20,066 passed and 43 skipped (one slow, two leaky), including the repaired regression. CI tested merge `0bf2242631a25a61475df8076c9b449a5234a590` / tree `dc1888086aa8b40b8df098194f23fb82c2690269` with master `65f8eb3c9284e396d9de7872c3df6dba993b7093`; this includes two master advances beyond the published candidate and is not a whole-tree match. The repaired `principal_gate.rs` is byte-identical. Native Windows bearer-test execution, a real provider/proxy run, #12114 landing, and required human review remain separate gates.

#### Earlier validation at `f0a3d81`

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Lint` (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`) and `Test` cover the gateway crate, where every changed line lives; `Docs Style` covers the changed Markdown.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live-provider run; the provider is a wiremock in every test. The 2-second delayed-introspection test depends on wall-clock timing within one process and is sized with ample margin.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
exit 0
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s) in 26.26s
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib principal_gate::
test result: ok. 29 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 752 filtered out; finished in 5.19s
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib -- api_pairing:: api_oidc:: dashboard_session::
test result: ok. 117 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 664 filtered out; finished in 43.14s
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway
test result: FAILED. 780 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 78.97s
  # the one failure, api_config::tests::unreadable_existing_config_survives_failed_save_rollback,
  # chmods a file to 0o000 and expects the read to fail; the build box runs as root, and the
  # same test fails identically on unpatched master there (git stash; rerun; stash pop)
DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/security/authentication.md scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Summary: 0 error(s)
DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/security/authentication.md scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
No added links detected in changed docs lines.

# Negative controls, each restored afterwards:
# 1. `record_attempt` call removed:
test principal_gate::tests::ten_failed_bearers_lock_the_client_out ... FAILED   (left: 401, right: 429)
test principal_gate::tests::forwarded_headers_key_the_ledger_when_trusted ... FAILED   (left: 401, right: 429)
# 2. permit bound at function scope so it outlives `next.run`:
test principal_gate::tests::the_permit_is_held_only_for_the_verification ... FAILED
  assertion `left == right` failed: every permit was released before its handler ran  (left: 0, right: 16)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source-traced that the permit scope ends before `method_floor` and `next.run`; that the dashboard-session branch runs before the bearer branch and touches neither limit; that `authenticate_native` is untouched. Not verified: a real identity provider, or a reverse proxy.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `f0a3d81` on `fix/12047-bearer-verification-limits` (master `683d101`), Rust 1.97.0 on Linux x86_64 with 2 cores; gateway unit tests over the real route group with a wiremock identity provider.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The full workspace `cargo test` was not run; the change is confined to `zeroclaw-gateway`, whose complete test target was run.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`) — the ledger stores client keys and timestamps, never tokens.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`) — test addresses are RFC 5737 documentation ranges.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. This hardens the daemon's client credential against being used to flood its identity provider.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`) — a client that relied on unlimited refused verifications was relying on a bug, not a contract.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`No`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <merge sha>`; no state outlives the process.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Unexpected 429 or 503 on `/api/config/*` for OIDC clients. A 429 means a client is failing verification in a loop (check the provider's logs for that client); a 503 means more than 16 verifications were in flight, which with a healthy provider needs sustained concurrent bearer traffic.

prs.title: feat(security): bind gateway pairing tokens to roster users
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A gateway pairing token can now be bound to a `[users.<name>]` roster entry when its code is minted. A device paired with such a code authenticates as `user:<id>` with that user's permission profiles instead of as the shared operator. This was the one credential path in the #8289 principal model that always collapsed to the shared operator, so households and small teams could not give a remote person scoped access without deploying an identity provider.
  - The operator chooses the binding, not the client. `zeroclaw gateway get-paircode --new --user <name>` calls `POST /admin/paircode/new?user=<name>`, which already requires a loopback peer and the gateway's owner-only admin token. The subject travels with the pending code into its reservation and the committed token, and a failed issuance restores the code still bound. `/pair` and `/api/pair` take no user parameter; they now report the `principal_id` the new token authenticates as.
  - Bound tokens are persisted only in a new, gateway-managed `gateway.paired_token_users` map (token SHA-256 hash to durable roster principal id), never also in `gateway.paired_tokens`. Both fields are written in the same `save_dirty`, so a binding cannot be persisted apart from its token and revocation is durable for bound tokens too. `PairingGuard::from_gateway_config` loads both. A malformed or conflicting binding is skipped with a warning, and the token it names fails closed even if `paired_tokens` also lists it.
  - The `native` auth provider resolves a bound token to `IdentitySubject::Roster`, and provenance now admits `(Native, Roster)`. Connection revalidation rebuilds native identities from the token's live subject, so a bound connection survives policy generation changes, and a removed roster entry denies it (`NotEntitled`) instead of widening it.
  - The operator-authority gateway checks (`PairingGuard::is_authenticated` and `authenticate_and_hash`) accept only shared-operator tokens. They sit behind `require_auth`, `/ws/chat`, SSE, ACP, nodes, canvas, plugins, the webhook, and remote reload and SOP approval, so a bound token gets `401` there. Loopback callers of the admin routes stay trusted without a token, as before. A bound token works where principals are resolved: the RPC handshake (local socket, WSS, relay) and the gateway's configuration route group.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to OIDC, per-token grants, channel identity, or the daemon-uid path. Unbound tokens, which is every existing token, behave as before. Roster entries still need a `uid`; uid-less remote-only users are the issue's separate follow-up. No dashboard UI for binding, and the other gateway routes are not made principal-aware.
- **Blast radius:** `PairingGuard` (every surface that authenticates a paired token), pairing persistence in `[gateway]`, the RPC handshake and revalidation path, the admin pairing-code routes and `zeroclaw gateway get-paircode`, device rotation on the admin route and the dashboard, and the device list (`GET /api/devices`).
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10573, Related #8289

### What this does, simply

Today every device paired with the gateway is the same all-powerful operator. If two people share one agent, the only way to give the second person narrower access over the network is to run an OIDC identity provider. With this PR the operator can bind a pairing code to a person listed in `[users]` when minting it. The device that redeems that code signs in as that person and gets only their permissions. Codes minted without `--user`, and every existing token, keep working as before. A bound token is accepted only where ZeroClaw checks per-person permissions: zerocode's connection to the daemon and the gateway's config routes. Everything else, the web dashboard included, refuses it rather than treat it as the operator.

### Design decisions that differ from the issue text

- **The operator binds at mint time.** The issue proposed `pair --user` and a `user` parameter on `/pair`. `/pair` is unauthenticated (the code is the only credential), so a client-chosen user would not be a boundary: whoever holds a code could name any user, or leave the parameter out and pair as the operator. The binding is chosen on the loopback plus admin-token route instead.
- **Bound tokens live only in the binding map.** The issue suggested a map alongside `paired_tokens`. Keeping bound hashes out of `paired_tokens` means an older binary, or a lost map, makes a bound token stop working instead of turning it into an operator token.
- **Operator-authority routes refuse bound tokens.** Those routes act with full operator authority, so letting a bound token through would widen it.

### Other behavior changes

- Device rotation (`--rotate-device`, and the dashboard's rotate) mints the replacement with the revoked token's own subject. It issues no code when that user's roster entry is gone, or when the device's token was already revoked (a stale registry row), unbound devices included, because the binding cannot be determined. When a code is already pending, the dashboard offers it only if it pairs as the rotated device did; otherwise it names the gateway-host command that mints the right one.
- The CLI shows a code requested with `--user` only if the gateway confirms the binding by echoing the user and reporting a `user:` principal. A gateway older than the CLI ignores the parameter and mints an ordinary code, which is withheld with an explanation. Every shown code now says who it pairs as.
- The certificate enrollment endpoint refuses a user-bound code with `409` without consuming it. After #11940, enrollment shares the canonical pairing guard, so this check now protects the live shared authority. Enrollment codes stay in a separate purpose slot and issue certificates without creating bearer tokens.
- The gateway's startup banner names who a pending bound code pairs as.
- `GET /api/devices` reports each device's `principal_id`, read from the pairing guard when the list is built, or `null` once the device's token is no longer paired. An operator retiring a user can find that user's devices and revoke them. The registry stores nothing new.

### Settled in review

- `gateway.paired_token_users` stays in plain text and visible to principals granted `Config:Read`, as documented. It holds hashes, not tokens, and a hash cannot be presented as a credential, so encrypting it would be optional hardening, not a requirement.
- Known edge, not changed here and to follow separately: webhook channel readiness reports authenticated when the only paired tokens are roster-bound, although none of them can call the webhook.

### Merge-order notes

Current integration: `e9e261b3247f4b463541364f577dcaa57e2e40aa` additively merges `master` at `65f8eb3c9284e396d9de7872c3df6dba993b7093`, including #12213’s live pairing limits. The standalone gateway and daemon load roster bindings with `from_gateway_config` and retain the canonical live limit resolver. Dropped reservations keep their original subject and mint time, and the current lifetime is resolved before taking pairing locks. A shortened lifetime expires pending and reserved bound codes; extending it later cannot revive a code already discarded. Both the roster-token route restrictions and the dashboard sign-in pairing checks remain documented.

Previous integration: `6ce9e75a272de6671f168799fbb0c78b7a6cb204` additively merges `master` at `b28d1c3de99099fd565cdedd4d80d8cff7f6a855`, after #11940 landed. It preserves the roster subject and code-purpose slot through reservations and restoration, and keeps enrollment consume-only. `EnrollmentReservation::subject()` borrows the existing subject rather than duplicating authority state. The secure-transport documentation now distinguishes unbound gateway codes from roster-bound codes.

Earlier integration merges include the following two updates. The first merge (`aab2ffb427`) followed #11171. The token map keeps each token's subject behind the `RwLock` #11171 added, and `HeldPairedTokens` gains `subject_of_hash`. Revalidation looks up the token's subject instead of testing membership, so a bound connection revalidates as its roster principal both directly and under an `AuthorityLease`; the lease keeps its membership check for liveness. The second merge (`23893ad3c7`) followed #10911. `persist_pairing_tokens` now saves through an admitted config commit and publishes the result, and inside that commit it still writes both fields from `PairingGuard::persisted_tokens()`.

These open PRs conflict with this branch or change the pairing paths it depends on (checked with `git merge-tree` against each head on 2026-10-12):

- #11182, draft (`pairing.rs`; it also conflicts with `master` alone in the gateway and RPC files): it adds a revocation guard parameter and moves token persistence, code minting and the device list into `zeroclaw-runtime/src/devices.rs` for its RPC `pairing/*` methods. Whichever lands second carries this PR's rules into that module:
  - `persist_pairing_tokens_held` writes both fields from `PairingGuard::persisted_tokens()` and marks both dirty. Writing `tokens()` into `gateway.paired_tokens` alone would store bound hashes as operator tokens, and would leave a revoked binding on disk to authenticate again after a restart; the same holds for its revoke-all path.
  - Single-device rotation keeps the device's binding, or withholds the code, as `rotation_replacement_subject` does here.
  - `list_devices_body` reports each device's `principal_id`, as `GET /api/devices` does here.
  - `pairing/new-code` stays operator-only, because it mints unbound codes.
- #11149, draft, and #11176, draft and stacked on it: both conflict with `master` alone in `api_pairing.rs`, gateway `lib.rs` and `rpc/dispatch.rs`, and the conflict with this branch is about behavior. They move device revocation behind `PairingGuard::revoke_under_config_write_lock` (`revoke_device_credential`, `revoke_token_hash_ordered`) and token persistence into `persist_pairing_tokens_under`. Whichever lands second applies the rules listed for #11182: the locked revoke step uses `revoke_token_hash_subject`, so rotation keeps the device's binding, and `persist_pairing_tokens_under` writes both fields from `PairingGuard::persisted_tokens()`, because writing `pairing.tokens()` into `gateway.paired_tokens` alone would store bound hashes as operator tokens. Under #11149's `is_shared_operator` gating, sessions from bound tokens lose the cron, nested and peer tools, which is the intended result for a scoped user.
- #11264 and #11265 (`schema.rs`, `authentication.md`): they relax the roster's `uid` requirement and add a `UserConfig` field. The `uid` wording here (the validation message, the field docs, the new docs section) describes the current rule, and the new tests spell out `UserConfig` literals, so whichever lands second updates both: after #11264 the literals need `password_hash: None`, and the advice to pick an unused `uid` applies only to entries without a password.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw gateway get-paircode`), `web` (gateway HTTP routes), `tui` (zerocode over WSS)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a daemon with the gateway and `gateway.require_pairing = true`, `[wss]` enabled for step 5, and a roster user whose uid no account on the host holds:

  ```toml
  [permission_profiles.reader.grants]
  sessions = ["read"]
  config = ["read"]

  [users.alice]
  uid = 59999
  permission_profiles = ["reader"]
  ```

- **Steps to run:**
  1. On the gateway host, as the gateway's user: `zeroclaw gateway get-paircode --new --user alice`
  2. `curl -s -X POST -H "X-Pairing-Code: <code>" http://127.0.0.1:42617/pair`
  3. `grep -n -A2 paired_token_users <config.toml>`
  4. With the returned token, request `GET /api/devices`, `GET /api/config`, and a `PATCH /api/config`.
  5. Connect zerocode over WSS with `ZEROCLAW_AUTH_TOKEN=<token>` and read the daemon's `RPC principal bound` log event.
  6. Restart the daemon and repeat steps 4 and 5.
  7. With an unbound operator token, list devices (`GET /api/devices`), run `zeroclaw gateway get-paircode --rotate-device <id>` for alice's device, then repeat after removing `[users.alice]`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):**
  1. A code, followed by "This code pairs as user:alice".
  2. A token and `"principal_id": "user:alice"`.
  3. The token's hash maps to `"alice"` under `[gateway.paired_token_users]` and is absent from `paired_tokens`.
  4. `401` from `/api/devices`, `200` from `GET /api/config`, `403` from the `PATCH`.
  5. `principal_id` is `user:alice`, and a method outside the profile is refused.
  6. Same results after the restart.
  7. The replacement code pairs as `user:alice` and the old token is refused. With the roster entry removed, the rotation revokes and issues no code.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `--user` is an unknown argument, and every paired token authenticates as the shared operator with full access on every route.

```text
# policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception comes from
# master (#11469). It creates `nul` and `NUL` in one directory, which collide on
# macOS's case-insensitive filesystem. policy.rs is unchanged here; Linux is unaffected.

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
test result: FAILED. 5719 passed; 6 failed; 8 ignored
# Five failures pass when run alone: four dispatch::model_provider_update_* tests and
# send_message_to_peer::peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_*, timing flakes
# of the shared-process runner. The sixth, dispatch::new_session_methods_are_denied_
# without_their_grants, comes from master (#11132). It fails on macOS whenever TMPDIR
# sits under the /var symlink and passes with a canonical TMPDIR. This branch only
# adds a test to dispatch.rs.

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw --test architecture

$ scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh   # passed
```

#### End-to-end run

- **Revision:** `eaea62766b`. The locally built debug binary reports `zeroclaw 0.8.5 (v0.8.5-535-geaea62766b)`.
- **Environment:** macOS arm64. One isolated daemon, with `HOME`, `ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR` and the RPC socket in a scratch directory, and nothing read from or written to the real `~/.zeroclaw`. The gateway listens on `127.0.0.1:43617`, WSS on `127.0.0.1:49781` and enrollment on `127.0.0.1:49782`. The config is the setup above: the `reader` profile, and `[users.alice]` with uid 59999, which no account on the host holds.
- **Client:** the WSS client certificate was enrolled with `zerocode --enroll`, after checking the client's SAS against the one on the daemon console. A small JSON-RPC client then connected over mTLS with that certificate and presented the token in `initialize`. Codes and tokens are omitted below.
- **Observed:**
  1. `zeroclaw gateway get-paircode --new --user alice` printed a code and "This code pairs as user:alice: the device that redeems it gets that roster user's permissions, not the operator's."
  2. `POST /pair` returned `200` with `"principal_id": "user:alice"`.
  3. `config.toml` holds the token's hash once, under `[gateway.paired_token_users]` mapped to `"alice"`, and `gateway.paired_tokens` is absent.
  4. With the bound token, `GET /api/devices` returned `401`, `GET /api/config` returned `200`, and `PATCH /api/config` returned `403` ("Principal lacks the config grant required for this method").
  5. Over WSS, `initialize` returned `principal_id: user:alice`, and the daemon logged `RPC principal bound` with `auth_provider: native` and `principal_id: user:alice`. `session/list` and `config/get` succeeded. `config/set` was refused with `-32012` ("Principal is not granted config:update (required by config/set)").
  6. After a daemon restart, steps 4 and 5 gave the same results with the same token.
  7. With an unbound operator token (its code printed "This code pairs as the shared operator, with the operator's full access."), `GET /api/devices` listed alice's device as `user:alice` and the operator's as `shared-operator`. `--rotate-device` on alice's device printed "the device again authenticates as user:alice", and its replacement code paired as `user:alice`. The old token got `401` and `-32010` ("Credential rejected"). After `[users.alice]` was removed and the daemon reloaded, the replacement token was refused at `initialize` with `-32012` ("Authenticated, but no permission profile grants this identity anything"). Rotating that device then revoked the token and issued no code, with the remedy text below.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - The end-to-end run above.
  - Mutation checks. For each guard below, I broke the guard, confirmed the named boundary test failed, and restored it:
    - a dropped reservation restoring the pending code still bound;
    - operator-authority membership refusing bound tokens;
    - a valid binding winning over `paired_tokens` for the same hash;
    - a damaged, conflicting or whitespace-padded binding failing closed;
    - provenance admitting `(Native, Roster)`;
    - revalidation rebuilding a bound identity;
    - after the first merge: revalidation of an unbound token, directly and under an `AuthorityLease`, each path broken on its own;

- **Visual interface evidence:** exact plain-text output from the end-to-end run above. The new CLI lines come from English-only Fluent keys, and other locales fall back to English: `cli-pairing-bound-user`, `cli-pairing-shared-operator`, `cli-pairing-bound-unconfirmed`, `cli-pairing-bound-no-code`, `cli-pairing-rotate-device-no-code` and `cli-pairing-rotate-device-unbound`.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `eaea62766b`; the unit, handler, router and architecture tests above, and the end-to-end run against a live daemon over the CLI, HTTP and WSS.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the transcript above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see "Observed" above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the no-default-features check was not run locally; CI runs it on Linux.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: a roster user can now hold a pairing token, a second credential next to their peer uid. Only the operator can mint one (a loopback peer plus the owner-only admin token), the redeeming client cannot choose or strip the binding, the token carries only the user's permission profiles through the shared resolver, and every operator-authority route refuses it. The new persisted map holds token hashes and principal ids, written in the same atomic save as the token list, and a damaged entry makes its token fail closed at load. The map is stored in plain text; see "Settled in review" above.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Existing tokens are unbound and behave as before; the new field defaults empty.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes:
  - the gateway-managed `gateway.paired_token_users`;
  - `zeroclaw gateway get-paircode --new --user <name>`;
  - a `user` query parameter on `POST /admin/paircode/new`;
  - `principal_id` in the `/pair`, `/api/pair`, `/admin/paircode*` and dashboard rotation responses, on each device in `GET /api/devices`, and in the CLI's `--json` output.

  No schema version change.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: none. An operator opts in by minting a code with `--user`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert the merge. An older binary ignores `gateway.paired_token_users`, so bound tokens stop authenticating there instead of turning into operator tokens, and the affected users re-pair. Entries left in the file work again after a later upgrade, so delete the table when downgrading if the bound devices should stay revoked.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** none. The feature is inert until a code is minted with `--user`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - `RPC principal bound` events with `auth_provider = native` and a `user:` principal id;
  - `RPC authorization denied` events for bound principals;
  - the load-time warning `gateway.paired_token_users has entries that are not a token hash mapped to one valid roster principal id`;
  - `401` for a bound token on the dashboard and other operator routes.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(oidc): bind enrollment callbacks to the initiating browser
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`, true-rebased onto `6ac37f60f142bca5e1e629f59e809a5cee6aaf3e`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Bind gateway OIDC enrollment to the browser that started it. A copied callback URL can no longer reveal a token in a different browser.
  - Generate a separate 32-byte random secret for each flow. Keep only its hash in the existing `PendingPkce` record. Check the cookie before code exchange; refuse and consume mismatched flows.
  - Preserve concurrent tabs, one-time consumption, issuer/provider checks, and the original deadline for a valid capacity retry. The cookie grants no session or API access.
  - Add four endpoint regressions, update existing callback tests to carry their actual issued cookie, and document cookie scope and recovery.
- **Scope boundary:** Enrollment start/callback and their documentation. Dashboard sign-in remains in #11965. Configured origin (#12048), same-host HTTP ports (#12088), broader availability (#12049), and response zeroization (#12090) remain separate.
- **Blast radius:** Clients that complete `/oidc/login/<alias>` through `/oidc/callback` must keep the issued browser cookie. Device flow and bearer-authenticated API routes retain their current behavior. The existing gateway `rand` dependency moves from dev to normal dependencies; no new package or lockfile change.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12050. Related #11965 and #8289.

### What this does, simply

The browser login page returns a token that a user can copy into a client. Before this change, someone could start a login under their own account, then send its final URL to another person. That person could receive and use the wrong account's token.

The gateway now gives the starting browser a short-lived cookie. The final page requires that cookie. A different browser gets the existing refusal page, and no code is exchanged. Start a new login in the intended browser after a refusal; do not forward callback URLs.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes: independent review of the callback boundary and an A/B browser check are useful for this security change.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`, gateway enrollment HTTP routes and the callback page. No messaging channel.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use a test OIDC alias and two isolated browser profiles. Use dedicated test accounts. Keep the gateway scheme/host consistent. The captured mock-provider recipe and source hashes are in [the evidence bundle](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/blob/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/README.md).
- **Steps to run:** Start a login in browser A. Capture the final callback URL before following it. Open that URL in browser B. Then retry it in A. Start two fresh flows in separate tabs of A and finish both normally.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** B receives `Sign-in not completed`, with no token exchange. A cannot replay that consumed flow. Both fresh tab flows succeed, each once. A normal same-browser return succeeds and clears only its flow cookie.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The callback lacks this browser check. The guard-removal negative control reproduces acceptance of a missing-cookie callback (200 instead of 400). A live provider or a full unpatched-daemon A/B run was not performed.

### How I tested

### Current integration after #12200 - 2026-11-02

Current head: a0b660c198c9a8aef8f00b3a2c2096af671ce127. Both original commits were true-rebased onto master 6ac37f60f142bca5e1e629f59e809a5cee6aaf3e, which includes merged #12200 and #11174. Both range-diff entries are unchanged; no manual conflict resolution or extra feature work was added. Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml and deny.toml match this master, including pulldown-cmark 0.13.6. The own scope remains 5 files.

The enrollment source, gateway manifest, locale loader and enrollment client are byte-identical to the previous head. The new master catalog keys are retained alongside the single enrollment error key, with no duplicate message keys. Focused rustfmt and whitespace checks pass. The callbacks, cookie parsing, consume-before-refusal and original-TTL capacity retry were traced again. Local Rust execution remains unavailable under Windows Application Control; the current-head upstream compilation and test results are recorded below. Earlier mock-provider/browser evidence remains historical and is not live-provider or combined dashboard evidence.

Two adversarial self-review passes and a final source review found no new supported defect. These are not independent Core approvals. Fresh [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41531182801/job/125581473661) passes on this exact head, including Security, Lint and Test. The [Test log](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41531182801/job/125571496498) records all 32 OIDC tests passing, including all four browser-binding regressions. Parallel Runtime Test also passes. No new private workflow or live-provider run was used.

### Earlier Fluent follow-up — 2026-11-02

Earlier head: `1bf288ffa29d00ac13a53bfe9304ee4d315e147a`. Both new enrollment-start errors now use `get_required_cli_string("cli-oidc-browser-start-failed")`. The canonical English catalog keeps the exact existing text, `could not start sign-in`. Other locales inherit that English fallback until translated. This uses the existing runtime locale; it does not add per-request language negotiation.

Local `rustfmt --check --edition 2024 crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_oidc.rs` and `git diff --check` pass. An exact inverse source comparison confirms that only the import, these two lookups and one English catalog entry changed. Status 500, the generic JSON error shape and early-return behavior remain. I traced the existing helper, catalog fallback and immediate JSON serialization; this was source validation, not a fresh gateway execution.

Historical CI on 1bf288ffa29d00ac13a53bfe9304ee4d315e147a failed Security on inherited pulldown-cmark 0.13.5 (RUSTSEC-2026-0433), with the aggregate gate also red. The merged #12200 repair is now inherited by the current head above. Historical results do not replace new-head checks.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Historical evidence: a bounded Ubuntu 24.04 job applied the exact patch to base `1c1cd118ac536a1dd1bc79b9cce69cbdc04e4f29`, checked all four source hashes, and ran Rust 1.98.0 tests, strict Clippy and the native browser fixture. Fresh upstream CI on the rebased head is recorded below. Independent Core/CODEOWNER security approvals remain required.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The native browser check uses production enrollment routes, prefix and security headers over loopback HTTP, with a mock IdP. It is not the complete daemon, native TLS, dashboard popup integration, or real-provider acceptance. HTTPS cookie attributes and rejection of an unprefixed cookie have router assertions.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
exit 0
git diff --check
exit 0
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib api_oidc::tests:: -- --nocapture
test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 649 filtered out; finished in 5.95s
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
exit 0

# Temporary guard removal; require the selected regression to fail:
enrollment_binding_refuses_other_browsers_before_exchange_and_consumes_the_flow ... FAILED
left: 200
right: 400
# Exact bytes restored; repeat the OIDC suite:
test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 649 filtered out; finished in 5.89s

# Native browser fixture, then exact restoration and final suite:
5 browser assertions passed; same browser, isolated context, consumed replay and concurrent tabs
test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 649 filtered out; finished in 6.96s
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Two adversarial source passes checked missing/wrong/duplicate cookies, consume-before-refusal, cookie-only API denial, concurrent flows, provider changes, issuer checks, original TTL and capacity retry. Source and dependency hashes were checked again. Both changed Markdown files passed pinned lint. No added documentation links need a new link target check.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshots of the existing success and refusal pages after the changed browser interaction; no layout redesign.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Historical source head `759ae4a5f1e4dffaa5d995503b222fc863e863d8`, exact four-file patch hash `945c228cff4dd8bf0a046630f7df1a22d3a14b34e6981eb64290d1e3fc9d55a9`; native Chrome `Chrome/156.0.8078.47`, Ubuntu 24.04, gateway `localhost`, mock IdP `127.0.0.1`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Same-browser success](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/browser-same-context.png), [other-browser refusal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/browser-other-context.png), and [machine receipt](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/blob/d3ada2e0108dd03005660358428a2a457ba370a8/evidence/receipt.json). All data is synthetic.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Follow the mock IdP page's link back to the prefixed callback: success with one exchange. Open a copied callback in another browser context: refusal with zero extra exchanges. Replay in the original context: refusal. Complete two fresh tab flows: both succeed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local Windows Rust execution was blocked by Application Control, so this source was validated on Linux. No full workspace suite or live IdP run is claimed. The first Linux attempt passed the Rust checks but failed because the mock page had a plain-text MIME type. That fixture was corrected; the complete successful run above uses the corrected harness. No browser assertion was relaxed.

### Earlier rebase and dashboard integration — 2026-11-02

Earlier rebased head: `4ef9abef542eb90153587669f2650cefc1abcb1d`. This is a true rebase onto `b28d1c3de99099fd565cdedd4d80d8cff7f6a855`, which includes #12129. All four enrollment files and the exact patch are byte-for-byte unchanged from the historical tested revision above; range-diff reports the same single commit. Fresh [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41370788934/job/125043937233) passes, including Security, Lint and Test. The [hosted Test log](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41370788934/job/125040616464) records all 32 OIDC tests passing, including all four new browser-binding regressions. Its checkout `0b80216b67e102089eebff5e2f6b7ff598a1e2bb` was verified to include this exact head. The earlier browser captures retain their named revision; no new native-TLS or real-provider acceptance run is claimed.

I also compared #11965 at `13486a064d2be1c05086e4ceaf6b08e94f2bc8b5`. At that historical snapshot, its delayed-start browser-family finding was open. It is now repaired at 02314854b32eb45a55d9d9c004f0bd73bb7b51e8, as recorded in [the repair review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11965#pullrequestreview-5731811340). That dashboard repair is separate from this per-flow enrollment binding. The branches overlap in `api_oidc.rs`; integration must keep one canonical binding in `PendingPkce`, checked before either exchange mode, with shared cookie parsing/cleanup and the original retry deadline. Preserve the dashboard's required ID token, provider pin, return/popup behavior and separate session-family/sign-out repair. Binding cleanup must coexist with the dashboard session cookie. This PR does not contain or validate that combined integration.

@IftekharUddin's [dependency and native-TLS proposal](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12157#issuecomment-6553383007) remains useful, separately attributed candidate evidence. The dependency repair is now inherited from master; no proposal commit was cherry-picked and no contributor source was replaced.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No; the existing discovery and token endpoints remain the only provider calls.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: A new per-flow secret is sent only in an HttpOnly binding cookie; its hash is stored with the pending flow and compared in constant time. Cookies use SameSite=Lax and root Path with no Domain; HTTPS adds Secure and the __Host- prefix. A terminal consumed-flow response clears its cookie. The recorded transport scope preserves the cookie attributes chosen at issuance. A valid 503 retry keeps its original expiry. Remote deployments should use HTTPS; plain HTTP does not isolate applications on different ports of the same host.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for callers that complete an enrollment callback without the starting browser's cookie; this is the intentional security correction.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps: Finish enrollment in the same browser that starts it and permit its cookie. If a callback was copied, the gateway restarted, or the cookie expired/was blocked, start a new login. Existing bearer clients and the device flow require no migration. The new field creates the browser-binding fact in the existing pending-flow store; it does not copy live policy.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the resulting squash commit through a reviewed PR, then restart the gateway. This restores the login-CSRF exposure, so use only as an incident response with an explicit exposure decision.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Device flow is the alternative if browser cookies cannot be used.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A fresh same-browser login reaches `Sign-in not completed`; investigate cookie blocking, scheme/host changes and callback provenance. Do not log cookie secrets or token-bearing callback URLs.

The refreshed head now passes its required upstream CI; earlier results remain attached to their named revisions. This remains open for independent Core/CODEOWNER security review, with Jordan for the manifest and Audacity for the gateway and documentation. I have not approved my own change. After adoption, #11965 should use one binding fact in `PendingPkce` for both modes while preserving its dashboard-specific return, popup and ID-token behavior.

prs.title: fix(rpc): guard SOP and session effects with current authority
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** master. Depends on #11220 and #11234. Prerequisite contributor commits are retained. Review this PR's supplemental changes separately from its cumulative stack. Current head: c9a193ceba32224187e79fbfd8d3ffc16a19d848.
- **What changed and why:** Require administrator authority for SOP RPC start and decisions, including wildcard non-admins. Hold canonical current authority through synchronous effects and use a shared-data store view that immediately refuses connection or SQLite writer contention. Preserve configured operator execution and the existing SOP tool markers.
- **Additional boundary repairs:** Hold current authority before SOP decision lookup, broker outcomes, and final overlay disclosure. Capture the real selection with a recursive read so a queued config writer cannot deadlock an already-held SOP effect lease.
- **Session effect repairs:** Guard append and rename at the durable storage effect, retain live Agent/generation/TUI ownership through publication, and authorize `session/abort` after the real cancellation lock. Revoke queued remote steering when its TUI binding changes, including an A-to-B-to-A transfer. Keep create-only run-once admission distinct from resume and preserve its published generation; preflight the existing close permission and report a late cleanup failure after a completed turn.
- **Scope boundary:** OIDC security hardening and regression coverage. Two-provider acceptance, migration/rollback rehearsal, and milestone closure remain separate work.
- **Blast radius:** SOP RPC dispatch, run-store contention, session storage and live publication, `session/abort`, remote steering, and transient run-once lifecycle.
- **Linked issues:** Related #11127, #11239, and #8289. No milestone closure is claimed.

### What this does, simply

Non-admin SOP RPC execution is now refused. Retry an administrator request when the SOP store is busy; ordinary background store timeouts are unchanged. Model-visible wildcard containment also depends on #11410. Session writes, `session/abort` and queued steering now refuse stale authority or transport ownership at their final effects. Run-once reports a late close failure instead of silently returning success.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, review this exact head and the combined #11423 integration; rerun validation after any subsequent dependency or conflict-resolution change.
- **Interface exercised:** Real RPC handlers and factory-built tool registries with synthetic principals, temporary databases, refusal assertions, and successful owner/operator controls. Storage tests use actual SQLite contention.
- **Setup:** A permitted Rust build environment with the repository's pinned toolchain and locked dependencies.
- **Expected:** Unauthorized requests have no new run, provider, mutation, transcript, or cross-owner audit effect; unchanged authorized controls succeed.

```sh
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-infra --lib session_
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
./scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh
```

### How I tested

- **Current integration:** Head `c9a193ceba32224187e79fbfd8d3ffc16a19d848` retains its previous published head `2e6c2b7835abe169fb0cbaf6ecceafb0e21faefc`, pinned master `7b84f9c806ee78bc1825df007ca14c6e222fb293`, and refreshed adjacent prerequisite `7b84f9c806ee78bc1825df007ca14c6e222fb293` as ancestors. The six draft refreshes were pushed atomically by ordinary fast-forward; contributor histories are retained. The old-to-new changes are six upstream files, with only independent Fluent additions requiring resolution. The separate #11234 author-adoption candidate is not imported into these drafts.
- **Current focused validation:** The [combined-stack job](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38010452447/job/114088977130) passed on exact source `7d5d8f566d14cf3b7e4dc90446711d7a6c6c7fb7`: formatting; `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --tests`; config 7, storage 209, RPC 878, authority 26, principal 92, and steering 15 tests, all with zero failures/ignored; and Clippy for runtime/infra/config with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`. Fourteen selected RPC regressions each have exactly one passing record. Filters overlap; these are per-command results, not a unique-test total or full-workspace run. The separate superseded canonical-admission job in that workflow failed compilation; its failure is not hidden by this successful combined-stack job.
- **Current upstream CI:** Fresh required checks run on the published head above. Their exact status and the landing decision are recorded in the [coordination handoff](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11408#issuecomment-6023921255). A passed fork job is not a substitute for those checks or independent Core review.
- **Adversarial review:** The independent refresh review verified all six old heads and canonical `d5df4214` ancestry, every refreshed stack link, byte identity with master for the five non-Fluent upstream files, and exactly one occurrence of each retained SOP/timeout Fluent key. No actionable finding remained in this bounded refresh review. The broader prior security review remains recorded on its earlier source, not represented as a new full sweep.
- **Historical sensitivity evidence:** [Earlier validation](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000499635) on `29b123f08874cdc28f74e2b2338a8e4bc4eb5231` passed enrollment 46/46 and demonstrated intended failures when append guarding or steering revocation was removed. These tests were not rerun as mutation tests in the current six-draft refresh; the relevant OIDC implementation is unchanged by this upstream-only refresh.
- **Limits:** Local Rust execution remains blocked by Windows Application Control (OS 4551), without a bypass. No production deployment, provider acceptance, migration/rollback rehearsal, or milestone closure occurred. The earlier Keycloak 20/20 and Authentik 10/18 result does not certify this integration. Required CI, Core review, and a safe prerequisite landing decision remain distinct gates.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or filesystem scope? No. The changed boundaries reduce access and retain existing operator controls.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets or credential formats changed? No. Authority is resolved from the existing canonical accepted policy.
- PII or real identities in fixtures? No; principals, payloads, and workspaces are synthetic.
- New prompt-injection source? No. Private run output and captured tools are treated as protected data/effects.

## Compatibility (required)

- **Session compatibility:** This PR requires the existing `Sessions:Update` grant in addition to Create/Execute for `session/run-once`, because it closes the transient session. A late close refusal is reported explicitly after the completed turn; retrying the whole operation can repeat the turn. Unsupported guarded backend operations fail explicitly.
- **Backward compatible?** No for callers relying on the previously unsafe access described above. Non-admin SOP RPC execution is now refused. Retry an administrator request when the SOP store is busy; ordinary background store timeouts are unchanged. Model-visible wildcard containment also depends on #11410.
- **Config/env/CLI surface changed?** No new settings, flags, or schema migration.
- **Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed?** No.
- **Upgrade:** Review the restrictions before rollout; keep this stack together and use existing operator workflows for refused administrative operations.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback path:** Revert the supplemental session/SOP repair commits on an integration branch in reverse dependency order, preserving contributor prerequisites and upstream #11576. Re-run the denied/permitted authority tests before any rollback deployment; reverting these repairs reopens the corresponding boundaries. This refresh does not claim a completed rollback rehearsal.
- **Feature flags/config toggles:** None.
- **Observable symptoms:** Unexpected permission refusals, SOP store-busy errors, missing owner audit records, or failed targeted/parallel runtime tests.

## Supersede Attribution

Not a replacement. Depends on the PRs above; original contributor commits are retained. Overlapping session authorization resolves to #11234's implementation.

prs.title: fix(tools): inherit headless SOP step scope on peer-send turns
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `send_message_to_peer`'s in-process delivery path starts the recipient turn in a detached `zeroclaw_spawn::spawn!` task.
  - Task-locals (including the active headless SOP step scope) do not cross that spawn, so the recipient rebuilt its full tool surface and escaped the step's capability boundary.
  - Capture `active_headless_step_scope()` before spawn and restore it with `with_inherited_headless_step_scope`, matching `delegate` and `spawn_subagent`.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change Act/autonomy checks on the sender, external-peer delivery, or live (non-headless) SOP step scope publishing.
- **Blast radius:** Recipient turns started from a scoped headless step now see the step's tool exclusions; unscoped / non-headless peer sends are unchanged (`None` inherits as a no-op).
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12169

### What this does, simply

When a headless SOP step is only allowed to message a peer, calling `send_message_to_peer` must not give the peer agent the whole tool list. The step's limit was kept in a task-local; the peer turn runs in a new task that never saw that limit. This PR copies the limit into the peer turn the same way `delegate` and `spawn_subagent` already do for the work they start.

`send_message_to_peer` could start another agent's turn (or post to an external peer) without consulting the sender's autonomy level or action budget. prs.title: fix(security): withhold principal-unaware tools and SOP execution from non-admin principals
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Some tools do work that does not carry the caller's principal: SOP steps, scheduled and cron turns, turns on peer agents, nested sub-agents and pipelines, saved daemon config, and the session tools that read or append to other principals' sessions. A non-admin with wildcard selectors kept all of them, because master only withheld such tools for a named tool list or a constrained agent selector, and only `delegate`, `spawn_subagent` and `execute_pipeline` were marked.
  - One rule now covers them. Every tool that reports `requires_unrestricted_principal` is withheld from every non-admin principal, whatever its selectors, at session creation, rehydration, every prompt and accepted steering. Skill aliases forward the marker. A retained `delegate` withholds the same tools from every child registry it builds: bounded, independent, background, parallel and nested.
  - Marked: `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, `sessions_send` (and `sessions_reset`, `sessions_delete`, which no agent registers yet), the six `cron_*` tools, `schedule`, `send_message_to_peer`, `sop_execute`, `sop_advance`, `sop_approve`, `sop_workshop`, `model_routing_config` and `proxy_config`.
  - Over RPC, `sops/run` and `sops/decide` require current administrator authority, rechecked after each wait and held through the start or resume effect. `cron/trigger` and `cron/patch` refuse agent jobs for non-admins, and the patch is authorized again under the SQLite writer.
- **Scope boundary:** this is containment, not principal propagation. The tools' stores do not become principal-aware, SOP steps and cron agent jobs do not carry a caller's ceilings, and nothing changes for administrators, the shared operator, channels or the CLI. SOP authoring over RPC (`sops/create`, `sops/save`) keeps its existing grant check. `backup` and `data_management` (both opt-in) are not changed here.
- **Blast radius:** RPC Chat/ACP sessions of non-admin principals, their steering, delegate children and rehydration; `sops/run`, `sops/decide`, `cron/trigger` and `cron/patch`. Non-admin sessions lose the tools above even with wildcard selectors.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11123. Closes #11127. Closes #12046. Closes #12051. Supersedes #11220. Supersedes #11230. Related #8289, #8290, #12131, #11169.

### What this does, simply

A signed-in user who is not an administrator could still schedule jobs that run as the daemon, start procedures, message other agents, change the daemon's model routing or proxy, and read other users' conversations on the same agent, as long as their profile allowed "all tools". The tools that do this work don't know who asked, so they can't apply that user's limits.

Until they can, a non-administrator doesn't get them at all, including through a skill alias or a delegated sub-agent. Starting or approving a procedure over RPC needs administrator authority too. Everything else the user is allowed to do keeps working, and administrators see no change.

This combines #11220 (SOP containment) and #11230 (session, cron and peer containment) into one change, and replaces their two mechanisms with the single rule above.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the regressions drive real RPC sessions, stores and delegate builds with synthetic principals, demotion and competing writers. An A/B by hand needs an OIDC principal and adds little over them.

### How I tested

On Linux x86_64 with rustc 1.98.0, on top of master `683d10139bc200ab8db768fcb4515f79404846ac`. Every test binary ran in a network namespace with only loopback and a throwaway `HOME`.

The suites ran on tree `30a5a7df65`. The branch tree `26ac164a11` differs from it only by a trailing blank line in one test file, and rustfmt passes on it. The api, config and tools suites, rustdoc and the docs checks ran on an earlier tree (`5aaeb0f9de`). Since then only one runtime test file has changed.

```text
cargo fetch --locked                                                     exit 0
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                               exit 0
cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets
                                                                         exit 0, 0 warnings
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
                                                                         exit 0, 0 warnings
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings
                                                                         exit 0, 0 warnings
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib    test result: ok. 6070 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib      test result: ok. 1384 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib     test result: ok. 1955 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api --lib        test result: ok. 321 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
the 32 regressions listed below, three separate runs                     32/32 each run
cargo doc --locked --no-deps -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime   exit 0, 0 warnings
scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                                       exit 0
BASE_SHA=683d10139b scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh                      Summary: 0 error(s)
BASE_SHA=683d10139b scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh                        No added links detected in changed docs lines.
scripts/ci/check_internal_docs_links.py                                  219 file(s); no broken local targets
git diff --check 683d10139b                                              exit 0
```

**Follow-up commit `1919e9fada`** (Greptile's localization finding): on that head, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` (6070 passed, 0 failed), the 28 SOP and rule regressions and the runtime i18n tests (47 passed) all pass. Restoring the hard-coded message fails the extended decision-wait regression.

**Master merges `fb6b33ef4f` and `fe5ae8ff69`** (#11266, then #12213; no rebase). #11266's two conflicts were both additions at the same spot, and both sides are kept (`agent.rs` and the English `cli.ftl`). On `fe5ae8ff69`, these all pass:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings`, with 0 warnings.
- The lib suites of those four crates: 6104, 1389, 1973 and 321 passed, 0 failed.
- The 32 regressions and #11266's 38 new tests, three runs each.
- `git diff --check 65f8eb3c92`.

Two revert checks in the resolved `agent.rs`:
- Switching off the withholding call fails 10 of the regressions, one of them by the stack overflow described below.
- Switching off master's fail-closed owner check fails `an_owned_session_that_cannot_carry_its_owner_refuses_cross_agent_steps`.

**Follow-up commit `5dde624095`** (Greptile's security finding on the bounded delegate child): the child's finished registry is checked against the live authority again after the last wait, keeping the target-bound delegate. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean; `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` passed 6105, 0 failed; the new `a_bounded_child_built_across_a_demotion_withholds_unrestricted_tools` passed three runs, and the 28 kept regressions pass. Removing the recheck fails the new test: the child is offered `sessions_history`.

The regressions:
- **From #11220:** `sop_run_and_decide_refuse_a_wildcard_selector_without_tools_execute`, `sop_missing_definition_cannot_bypass_the_tool_ceiling`, `sop_rpc_refuses_sqlite_contention_before_start_or_resume_effects`, `sop_run_rechecks_live_authority_and_loaded_agents_after_decision_wait`, `sop_decide_rechecks_live_authority_after_engine_lock_with_a_stale_stamp`, `sop_decide_rechecks_before_lookup_and_final_projection`, `sop_run_and_decide_are_refused_after_admin_demotion`, `sop_entry_tools_and_aliases_cannot_escape_principal_ceilings`, `principal_sop_workshop_refuses_direct_and_alias_effects`, `principal_sop_workshop_queued_demotion_prevents_persistence`, `withheld_sop_tools_do_not_reach_{delegate_children,independent_targets,an_independent_grandchild}`, and `recursive_read_finishes_while_publication_waits_for_effect_read` (config).
- **From #11230:** `withholding_session_data_tools_removes_aliases_and_nested_executors`, `cron_patch_rechecks_authority_and_row_after_sqlite_writer_wait`, `scoped_principals_cannot_reach_session_data_tools_even_with_wildcard_selectors`, `demoted_principal_loses_session_data_tools_at_its_next_prompt`, `principal_native_history_uses_final_admission_and_monotonic_withholding`, `principal_cron_rpc_refuses_agent_jobs_but_keeps_shell_jobs`, `principal_sessions_refuse_headless_tools_and_captured_aliases`, `steering_withholds_session_tools_{before_consumption,after_memory_wait}`, `steering_keeps_session_tools_for_unchanged_admin`, and `withheld_session_tools_do_not_reach_{delegate_children,independent_targets,an_independent_grandchild}`.
- **New:**
  - `wildcard_non_admin_sessions_hold_no_unrestricted_tools`: the rule, at creation and after rehydration, with an administrator control.
  - `demoted_administrator_delegate_withholds_before_the_next_prompt`: the delegate's live binding.
  - `cross_session_tools_require_an_unrestricted_principal`, `model_routing_config_requires_an_unrestricted_principal` and `proxy_config_requires_an_unrestricted_principal` (tools).

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` on the pushed head, for the Windows and macOS legs, the full workspace and the Security job.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Docs Style lints only `docs/book/src/**`; `authentication.md` is in that tree, so it is covered.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Each functional line was switched off on its own in a local probe build. Every switch failed at least one of the tests listed for it, and the same tests passed with no switch set (list below). No live identity provider or interactive TUI run.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no interface change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `fe5ae8ff69` (tree `f88551a1db`, with master `65f8eb3c92` merged in), plus the `5dde624095` follow-up above; RPC dispatcher and tool-registry regressions.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** withheld tools return `Unknown tool` and leave cron rows, run history, SOP runs, proposals and foreign transcripts unchanged; refused RPC effects return `FORBIDDEN`; administrator and ordinary-tool controls succeed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:**
  - Windows and macOS, and `zeroclaw-desktop` (it needs GTK; nothing under `apps/` changes): left to CI.
  - Integration tests: compiled, not run.
  - Suites of crates this doesn't touch.
  - Live identity providers.

**Revert checks.** In a local probe build, each of these lines was switched off on its own, and each switch failed at least one of the tests above.
- **The rule:**
  - with master's old posture (withhold only when the agent selector is constrained), 10 of the regressions fail;
  - steering withholding, the delegate's withholding flag and its live binding, dropping a delegate without a handle, sharing the flag with children and copying the admission into children each fail their own tests;
  - so do the independent-target filter and the bounded-child filter.
- **SOP RPC:** the administrator check, the recheck after the decision wait, and the effect lease.
- **Cron RPC:** the trigger refusal, the patch refusal, and the recheck under the writer.
- **Each marker on its own:** all six cron tools, `schedule`, `send_message_to_peer`, the four SOP tools, the five session tools, and both config tools.

Three switches let a forged cron call really run in the test fixture: master's old posture, the cron trigger refusal and the `cron_run` marker. That overflows the test's stack, so the test fails by aborting. Each was rerun with the aborting test skipped, and the old posture and `cron_run` switches still fail other tests. The trigger refusal is caught only by that abort.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.** This only restricts existing access.
- New external network calls? **No.**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** A delegate keeps a resolver bound to the originating connection's authentication, so each child build checks that credential's current grants, expiry and revocation instead of a stored decision. No bearer token is kept.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No;** fixtures are synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.** Withheld tools leave both the registry and the advertised tool list.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: a child must not run with a later caller's authority. Each child copies its originating resolver at build time, and the authorization layer stays the source of truth.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No.** Non-admin principals, wildcard selectors included, lose the tools listed above and their aliases, and can no longer run or decide SOPs over RPC or trigger and edit cron agent jobs. A live session never gets withheld tools back. A new or rehydrated session picks up a promotion.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No** new setting, flag or RPC method. Existing methods refuse more, with localized messages.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.** The public `SteeringPosture` gains `withhold_unrestricted_tools`; code that builds it with a struct literal must set it from its admission policy (the all-false default withholds nothing).
- Exact upgrade steps: run and approve SOPs as an administrator or the shared operator. Granting `tools:execute` alone no longer restores access. To keep the session tools out of administrator-started SOP runs and cron agent jobs too, list them in the `excluded_tools` of those agents' risk profiles.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <squash commit>`. There is no migration. Reverting reopens the access described above, so keep the affected tools out of non-admin agents through risk-profile `excluded_tools` until a fix is back.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `Unknown tool` for the withheld tools in non-admin sessions and `FORBIDDEN` from `sops/run`, `sops/decide`, `cron/trigger` and `cron/patch` for non-admins are expected. A foreign transcript read, a cron or SOP effect after demotion, or a missing ordinary tool for an unchanged principal is a regression.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors:
  - #11220 by @IftekharUddin
  - #11230 by @IftekharUddin
- Scope materially carried forward:
  - From #11220, all of it: the SOP RPC administrator guard and effect lease, the SOP tool markers, the delegate's live admission resolver, and their regressions. This includes Aarlington's repairs from #11408.
  - From #11230, all of it except two unrelated test-fixture fixes (the Telegram deadline client and case-variant policy aliases): the session, cron and peer containment, steering, cron patch authorization under the writer, and their regressions. This includes Aarlington's cron and peer containment.
  - New here: the single rule, which replaces the session-tool name list and the second delegate flag, plus the markers on the session tools and the two config tools.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? **Yes.** The two ported commits keep IftekharUddin as author with Aarlington as co-author.

## Holding crate

Everything in `zeroclaw-runtime` here restricts an existing tool path or RPC route, and adds no subsystem, tool, route or setting. So this proposes no ADR-016 row. If the Core Team reads the SOP effect lease or the delegate's admission resolver as new functionality, that needs a row before merge.

## Landing notes

- #11169 needs to rebase onto the SOP admission contract here. One `SopAdmissionCheck` returns a held `SopEffectGuard`, and execution keeps the administrator check and the non-blocking store boundary.
- Cross-credential steering and shared-execution renewal stay with #12131.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

## Summary

- **What changed and why:**
