prs.title: fix(tools): report a dismissed ask_user choice as an answer, not an error
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - A structured-only channel can return `Ok(None)` when the user dismisses a choice question. `ask_user` previously reported a tool failure and explicitly told the agent to retry. It now returns success, no error, and `DISMISSED: the question was closed without a choice.`
  - The existing immediate return is preserved: dismissal does not fall through to `send` + `listen`. Selected answers, channel errors, timeouts, and free-form-capable fallback keep their existing behavior.
  - The existing dismissal regression checks success, the exact output, no error, no listener fallback, and prompt completion. Two more tool-level tests, added in fe92ee9cb, cover a selected answer and a channel failure on structured-only channels.
- **Scope boundary:** `crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/ask_user.rs`, plus `WsApprovalChannel::request_choice` in the gateway and the `supports_free_form_ask` doc. No changes to `poll`, channel protocols, configuration, approval policy, or ZeroCode rendering. Free-form questions remain unsupported on structured-only channels.
- **Blast radius:** Choice-style `ask_user` results on structured-only channels, including ACP and the RPC approval bridge used by ZeroCode. Success classification also reaches existing tool observers, receipts when enabled, and provider history. The channel API also uses `Ok(None)` for missing form capability; that case receives the same dismissal text even if no question was displayed.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11623. Companion to #11624, which handles client-side prompt withdrawal and question/outcome presentation. This PR alone does not resolve the broader lost-prompt and transcript issue.

### What this does, simply

An agent can ask you a question with several choices. If you close that question without choosing, the agent should learn that you did not answer. Previously it received an error telling it to ask again. This change reports the dismissal as a completed tool result. It removes that retry instruction; it does not guarantee what the agent will do next. A client that never replies still produces a timeout error.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. A real ZeroCode dismissal verifies the visible result and interaction that tool unit tests cannot establish.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Code pane using its RPC approval bridge. ACP clients are additional affected consumers; no ACP-client capture is supplied.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Build matching daemon/client revisions separately for `master` and this branch. Configure a working provider, enable `ask_user` in the effective tool selection, and use a client advertising form elicitation. Keep the same client revision and configuration for both runs; record whether companion #11624 is included. Use a synthetic question and choices.
- **Steps to run:** In the Code pane, request that the agent call `ask_user` with `question: "Continue?"` and `choices: ["Yes", "No"]`. While the choice prompt is visible, press Esc. Inspect the tool result card and record its completed state. Repeat on `master` with the same setup. Separately select Yes to check ordinary answers.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Dismissal completes promptly with success, no tool error, and output `DISMISSED: the question was closed without a choice.` Selecting Yes returns Yes. Exact card styling and companion-dependent transcript behavior still need real captures.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The same dismissal returns a failed tool result explaining that the structured choice was not completed and telling the agent to retry `ask_user`.

### How I tested

Source review covered the full change against `origin/master`, the local merge, channel trait contracts, ACP/RPC handling, factory registration, and runtime success-result propagation. Formatting, whitespace, and comment-hygiene checks passed. These checks do not prove compilation or the final interface.

The original body reported 14 focused tests passing, clean clippy, and a mutation check. Those historical claims were not tied to the refreshed revision and are not treated as validation of it here.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Published-head CI at `900eb76695d79b7bc2e4e3b98ed256dd39bfa07d` passed `CI Required Gate`, `Test`, `Lint`, and `Format`, plus the reported platform checks. This is historical support for the published implementation, not validation of the local merge or prepared tests. [CI run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39027742759).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Fresh CI runs on the pushed head `6124206a3`, a merge of current master `4f3ca7c38` into `53906de0d`. The merge brings in the Wasmtime 48.0.8 bump (#12129), which fixes the RUSTSEC advisories that failed `Security` on the previous head. Tool-level tests do not exercise the ZeroCode renderer; the real Esc interaction is in the screenshots below.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Run on head `688dfca1ac4` (macOS, `zc-cargo-narrow`, `-j2`):

  | Check | Result |
  |---|---|
  | `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check`, comment hygiene gate | ok |
  | `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-api --all-targets -- -D warnings` | ok |
  | `cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib` | 681 passed; 0 failed (both new `ws_approval` tests fail with the override reverted) |
  | `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib` | 1382 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored (all 16 `ask_user` tests pass) |
  | `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib i18n` | 48 passed; 0 failed |
  | `cargo generate installers --check`, `cargo generate installers tools-en-ftl --check` | in sync |
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Live Esc and pick on a real daemon and ZeroCode client at `53906de0d` (screenshots above). No ACP-client smoke.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real screenshot of the Code pane after Esc, built from `688dfca1ac4`: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11815#issuecomment-6648032895
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Esc screenshot built from `688dfca1ac4` (daemon and ZeroCode from the same debug build, with a local stub provider issuing the `ask_user` call), ZeroCode Code pane over local RPC, Terminal.app at 150×42.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** After Esc the tool card shows `result: DISMISSED: the question was closed without a choice.` and the agent reports a dismissal, not an error. Asked again, picking Yes gives `result: Yes`.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Pressed Esc in a pending Yes/No `ask_user` prompt: the call completed with the dismissal result above. Repeated the question and picked Yes: the call completed with `Yes`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** On the merge head only `zeroclaw-tools` was retested (full lib suite), because the merge doesn't touch this PR's files. No ACP-client smoke was run.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The changed model-visible text is a fixed dismissal string with no interpolated user or external input. It communicates no answer and grants no approval; existing security checks still run before the request.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes at the API/schema level. Intentional behavior change: dismissal is a successful result instead of a failure; consumers using `success` observe that change.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A - no schema, configuration, command, or toolchain migration. Consumers must treat the dismissal output as no answer, not as an affirmative choice.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Ordinary behavioral change; treat as medium risk for review and rollback planning.

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Before squash merge, revert the two behavior commits in reverse order: `git revert 900eb76695d79b7bc2e4e3b98ed256dd39bfa07d 31ee02e3d1649a037040a883f2dd35e38b7937ad`. After squash merge, `git revert <squash-commit-sha>`. Preserve the master merge.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None specific to this behavior.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A dismissed question again appears as a failed tool call or carries a retry instruction; alternatively a real channel error is incorrectly shown as a successful dismissal. Check the `ask_user` result's success, output, and error fields.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A - no Supersedes

prs.title: fix(sop): use the fail-closed mode when the decision answers are unusable
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `resolve` in `sop/decision.rs` now treats the whole answer set as untrusted when the gate answer is missing or invalid, or when `modes` is non-empty and the mode answer is missing, rejected, or below `min_confidence`. In that case the run uses the fail-closed mode and every step runs; the per-step `decide` answers are discarded. Before, a valid-looking set of step answers was still applied next to an unusable gate or mode answer (#11124).
  - `fail_closed_mode` is now one `match` on the authored mode with explicit arms. `priority_based` is no longer reduced below its own gating; it goes to `step_by_step` only when `step_by_step` is listed in `modes`.
  - The rationale note "step answers ignored; every step runs" is written only when the run actually starts.
  - Docs (`decision-models.md`, `syntax.md`, and the `decide` description in `sop/mod.rs`) describe the fail-closed behavior.
- **Scope boundary:** no change to the engine (`engine.rs`), to routing, or to approval handling (see "Related, not fixed here"). No new config keys.
- **Blast radius:** SOPs with a `[decision]` table and `decide` steps, through `resolve` and `apply_decisions` (`dispatch.rs`). SOPs without `[decision]` are not touched.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11124

### What this does, simply

A decision model can answer a gate ("should this SOP start?"), a mode ("how much supervision?") and one yes/no question per step. If the gate or mode answer cannot be trusted, the SOP falls back to a strict mode. The reported bug: the step answers were still used in that case, so steps could be skipped while the run was already in the strict fallback. Now, when the gate or mode answer is unusable, none of the step answers is used and every step runs.

Behavior changes beyond the reported case, declared on purpose:

1. **Mode answer unusable, gate valid.** With `modes` set and the mode answer missing, rejected, or below `min_confidence`, step answers are now ignored too. Before, they were kept (checked in `resolve` at the base commit). This follows the same rule as the gate: one answer set, trusted as a whole or not at all.
2. **`priority_based` with `step_by_step` listed.** An invalid gate answer and the "model unavailable" path now give `step_by_step` instead of leaving the authored mode. It is stricter; the Safety section says so.
3. **Routing guards.** A `switch` whose ports all read `$.decisions` matches no port when the answers are ignored (an absent answer reads as false) and completes the run without its remaining steps. This already happened when the model was down; the fix adds the cases above. Routing is not changed. The docs now say it. No test exercises this consequence.

### Related, not fixed here

A different mechanism, found while reviewing this change and read in the code but not run: for a `supervised` SOP the only approval is tied to step 1 (`execution_mode_needs_approval`, `sop/engine.rs:7116-7118`), and a step skipped by a valid "no" answer is skipped before its approval gate (`skip_for_decision` at `sop/engine.rs:3145`, approval at `:3193`). So a valid "no" on a `decide` question in step 1 appears to leave the run with no approval. `decision-models.md` already says a skipped step never asks for approval. Here `resolve` works as intended and the gap is in the engine, so it is outside this PR's invariant (unusable answers never reduce supervision). I did not reproduce it, did not check whether a third party can influence the answer, and did not search for existing issues. Per-step `requires_confirmation` and checkpoints still gate.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — the behavior is covered by unit tests on `resolve` and by dispatch tests with a scripted decision model; no interface is involved.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test and lint jobs cover `zeroclaw-runtime`; `Docs Style` and the link gate cover the changed Markdown.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** I only ran `sop::` in `zeroclaw-runtime`, not the other crates' tests.
- **Commands run and tail output** (WSL, `-j 1`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, debuginfo off, `--test-threads=1`):
  - Tests without the fix (the first commit alone): `sop::decision` 18 failed, 23 passed; `decision_gating` 4 failed, 10 passed, 1 ignored.
  - Tests with the fix, on `e0a5b436f`: `sop::` 763 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.
  - On the merge with `origin/master` at `683d10139` (built, not only `merge-tree`): `sop::` 763 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.
  - `scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh` on that merge: `cargo fmt --check` OK and `cargo clippy -D clippy::correctness` OK with 0 warnings. The provider-dispatch step of that script fails at `safety_net_loop_recovery.rs:35` and `:58`; those lines are the same on current `master` and this PR does not touch that file.
  - Docs: fmt, hygiene, markdownlint and link gates OK on `e0a5b436f`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The two predictions "these tests fail without the fix" were run, not assumed (counts above). I did not verify other crates, the `--strict` gate mode, how `decided_mode` is persisted, or the web UI consumers of the decision.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** workspace-wide tests were skipped because of local memory limits; only `sop::` was run.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The change makes the fallback stricter (more steps run, never fewer) when model answers are unusable.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes, with the behavior changes listed in the Summary (stricter fallback only).
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert` of the two commits.

prs.title: feat(runtime): retire orphaned remote sessions
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - **The problem:** the daemon keeps at most 64 sessions live. A remote client's sessions stay live after it disconnects, so that it can come back with its identity. One that never comes back, or comes back under a new identity (which can't reach its old sessions), held them until the daemon restarted. Once the map was full, `session/new` failed for every client with `-32001 Session limit reached`.
  - **What tracks departures:** the TUI identity registry now records when an identity's last live connection ended, and whether that connection was remote. A reconnect clears the record.
  - **What retires sessions:** a daemon task closes each live session that meets all of these:
    - its owning identity has had no live connection for `wss.orphaned_session_timeout_secs` (default 1800 s);
    - it has itself been idle that long;
    - it has no turn running and no approval pending.

    It closes it the way `session/close` does: under the session's queue permit, so the transcript is kept and the session-end hook fires. The final decision and the removal are one step under the session map's lock and, inside it, the identity registry's presence lock, so a resume, a recorded activity or a reconnect that completes first keeps the session; a reconnect that completes after the removal finds it closed, never half-retired.
  - **Retirement never writes a transcript:** a chat session is closed only when its stored transcript already holds all of its live history, alone or followed by messages another writer added (the gateway's message route, say).
    - A store that lacks part of the live history (a failed post-turn save), differs from it, or can't be read keeps the session live. It is checked again later and retired once the store holds the history.
    - Because nothing is written, retirement can't recreate a session another writer deleted, reorder another writer's messages, or change stored times.
    - A live ACP session's history is already committed by its turn checkpoints, and a failed checkpoint ends the live session.
  - **SQLite reads fail closed:** `SqliteSessionBackend::try_load` now reports a transcript it can't read, or a row it can't decode, instead of inheriting `load`'s shorter or empty history. Every `try_load` caller (`session/new`'s restore, the gateway's `ws.rs`, the channels orchestrator) already treats an error as fail-closed, as the JSONL store has always reported.
  - **The last connection:** a signed reconnect can register an identity again while its earlier connection is still open. The timer starts only when the identity's last live connection ends. Initializing a connection again replaces its own earlier registration.
  - **Activity:** a turn counts as activity when it finishes, not only when it starts.
  - **The setting:** `0` turns retirement off. The setting is read on every check, so a change applies without a restart.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Sessions of local clients (the RPC socket) are not retired. A local caller can reach any session, so nothing is stranded there.
  - Durable history is untouched.
  - The cap itself (64) is unchanged.
  - There is no early eviction at the cap: an orphan younger than the timeout still holds its place.
  - Surfacing a full map in `status` is not part of this PR.
  - A remote client that returns after its sessions were closed can't list, read or resume them over WSS, because remote access reaches only live sessions its own identity owns. Their transcripts stay in the store, and a local client can resume them. Bringing them back to a returning remote client is the job of durable remote restoration (#11737), which has to keep principal isolation.
- **Blast radius:**
  - The RPC session store, the TUI registry (`TuiEntry` gains `remote`), and the daemon's start-up (one spawned task per daemon generation, holding the RPC context weakly).
  - A remote client that stays away longer than the timeout finds its sessions closed (see the scope boundary).
  - `initialize` on a connection that already holds a registration now releases that registration first.
  - `zeroclaw-infra`: an unreadable SQLite transcript is now an error for `try_load` callers, which already fail closed on it, rather than an empty or shortened history.
- **Linked issue(s):**
  - Fixes #11962
  - Depends on #11963 (the placement row for orphaned-session retirement in `zeroclaw-runtime`; it must merge first, with its Core approval recorded)
  - Related #11737 (durable remote restoration, which would let a returning remote client reach a retired session again)

### What this does, simply

Every chat or coding session a client opens takes one of 64 places in the daemon. When a remote client disconnects, its sessions keep their places so it can come back and continue. If it never comes back, or comes back as a "new" client that can't see its old sessions, those places stay taken until the daemon is restarted. Eventually nobody can start a new session.

With this change, the daemon notices when a remote client has been gone for a while (30 minutes by default) and closes its idle sessions, the same way the client could have closed them. It closes a session only when its conversation history is already stored, and it never writes or deletes stored history itself; a session whose history isn't fully stored stays open. Sessions that are busy (a reply being generated, or waiting for an approval), sessions of clients on the same machine, and sessions whose client still has a connection open are left alone. A remote client that returns later can't reopen a closed session itself; someone on the daemon's machine can.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The new tests drive the same registration and teardown steps the WSS transport runs. The end-to-end form needs a client that disconnects and stays away for the timeout.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:**
  - the Rust test jobs run the new `rpc::dispatch::tests::orphaned_session_retirement` and `rpc::tui_identity` tests;
  - clippy and fmt cover the touched files;
  - Docs Style covers the new section in `rpc-socket.md`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none.

The failure is `daemon_startup_feedback::daemon_feedback_follows_foreground_job_control_transitions`, which needs `expect`; the test machine doesn't have it (CI installs it), and the test fails the same way on master there.
  - CI `Test (opt-in tools)`: 12736 tests run: 12736 passed, 168 skipped.

    - `a_reconnect_while_retirement_is_deciding_keeps_the_session`;

The test records which completed first and checks it against what survived: a registration that completed first must keep its session.
  - **Identity:**
    - `an_identity_with_a_connection_still_open_has_not_left`: a second connection under the same identity comes and goes while the first stays;

  - The race, identity, history, stored-message, timestamp and cancellation tests were written first and failed on the code before their fixes.
  - The reconnect-order test fails on the code before its fix (`registration completed at 1 before removal at 2, but its session was retired`). On this head: with the fix reverted (test hooks kept) it fails with exactly that message, exit 101; with the presence lock released before the final check, the same; with the fix restored it passes (1 passed).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The lock order on the final check: the session map, then the registry's presence lock, both released before notifications, agent locking, lifecycle hooks or any await. Every registry and session-store caller was checked for a reverse edge; none takes the session map while holding presence. Not verified: a real WSS client staying away past the timeout against a running daemon.

- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** tree `92656a1de3` (this head); RPC over the in-process dispatcher, as the WSS transport drives it.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- Note: the daemon now closes sessions without a client request. It closes only sessions owned by a remote identity that has had no connection for the timeout and that are idle, with no turn and no approval pending. It never deletes history. This also covers a remote account whose access was revoked: its sessions no longer stay live until restart.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Existing configs get the 1800 s default. Set `wss.orphaned_session_timeout_secs = 0` to keep the previous behavior.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: one new key, `wss.orphaned_session_timeout_secs`, documented in the config schema and in `docs/book/src/architecture/rpc-socket.md`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- Upgrade steps: none. Operators who relied on remote sessions staying live indefinitely set the key to `0`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` of the merged commit, or set `wss.orphaned_session_timeout_secs = 0` (takes effect within a minute, no restart).
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `wss.orphaned_session_timeout_secs`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a remote client reports its session gone after a long absence. The daemon log has `Closed an orphaned remote session; its transcript is kept` with the session id and owner.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: feat(gateway): scoped dashboard chat through the core
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Stacked on #11965 (dashboard sign-in), #11186 (the in-process RPC client, on #11165) and #11964 (the daemon retires orphaned remote sessions).
- **Commits:** everything up to and including e69cf498aa belongs to those three PRs: their commits, plus three merges (the last one merges master). The change is the seven commits after it:
  - `feat(rpc)`: provider-bound in-process connections, and `Served`;
  - `feat(gateway)`: scoped dashboard chat through the core;
  - `feat(web)`: the chat for these accounts;
  - `docs(security)`: the limits;
  - `fix(gateway)`: a close the client refused to send is tried again;
  - `docs(rpc)`: what `Served` promises;
  - `docs(gateway)`: module docs without links to private items.

  The diff shrinks as each prerequisite lands.
- **Limit to know first: a scoped account's conversation ends with its socket.** Reloading the page, leaving the chat or signing out ends it, and the dashboard can't reopen it. This is deliberate for this release (details under the scope boundary below).
- **What changed and why:**
  - **Non-administrator accounts can now chat in the dashboard.** The daemon runs the chat as that account, under its grants, and keeps the conversation as that account's own. Administrators keep today's in-process chat and its history.
  - **Each chat socket is one conversation.**
    - The socket opens a daemon connection of its own through the in-process connector, presenting the token the account signed in with.
    - It creates one conversation there.
    - The conversation is closed (never deleted) when the socket closes, when the account signs out, shortly before its token expires, when it loses access, and at a daemon reload.
    - No other socket reopens it. So nothing about a conversation is shared between sockets: not its connection, not the identity the daemon holds it under, not its approvals.
  - **The daemon treats that connection as remote**, so it assigns the conversation's id, and only the connection that created a conversation can use it.
  - **At most four chats per sign-in, and 32 per account across its sign-ins.**
    - A conversation still being created, or not yet closed after its chat ended, counts. Signing out and in again therefore frees nothing until it is closed.
    - A creation the chat stopped waiting for (after 10 minutes) stays counted until the daemon answers it. A conversation created after all is closed when the answer lands and then no longer counts, with or without orphan retirement.
    - A conversation whose close failed, or whose creation lost its connection before the answer, stays counted until the next reload, since its fate is unknown.
    - A chat past either limit is accepted, told `CONVERSATION_LIMIT` and closed with `4409`; no other tab's conversation is closed.
  - **A conversation the daemon finishes creating after its socket left is still closed.**
    - The creation runs in a task of its own and waits as long as the daemon takes (MCP servers can make that longer than a request's usual deadline).
    - It keeps the chat's place until its conversation is handed over or closed.
    - Whatever it creates that nobody took, or creates after sign-out, is closed.
  - **The token goes only to the provider that issued it.**
    - Every connection a chat opens is bound to the sign-in's provider, as it was configured at sign-in: `InprocConnector::connect_bound`, verified with `authenticate_bound` in the daemon.
    - If the provider is repointed at another issuer or client, the chat is refused and the token is not sent there.
  - **A chat that ends stops its reply.** The browser leaving, sign-out or a reload closes the conversation at once, which cancels a turn under way.
  - **The identity provider is asked once per chat.**
    - Each chat's connection verifies the token once.
    - The agent list is kept per sign-in for 30 s, under one policy generation only, and the account's current read grant decides on every request.
    - A refused token is presented again only when the policy changed during the handshake.
  - **Writes to the browser never hold up the end.** Every write gives up at sign-out or a reload, or after 10 s on a browser that stopped reading.
  - **A close survives a lost connection, a lapsed binding, or a send the client refused locally.** It is tried again on a new connection, with the chat's own identity and the token the chat kept.
  - **When the daemon asks for a new handshake,** the chat reconnects with its own identity. Between turns it then rebinds the conversation there, so approval requests keep reaching the socket.
  - **Every chat frame is checked against the sign-in before it's acted on,** between turns and mid-turn, as the in-process chat does.
  - **The chat is offered only to accounts that can use, read and close a conversation** (`sessions` create, read, execute and update). Its agent uses only the tools the account is granted.
  - **The chat socket says why it closes:** `CONVERSATION_LIMIT` then `4409`; `CONVERSATION_CLOSED` then `4410`, when the daemon closes the conversation under the socket.
  - **Dashboard chat for scoped accounts (web).** This applies to an account without the operator dashboard, or any session with `features.core_sessions`.
    - Opening the chat opens no socket. The first message does. It goes out once the socket's `session_start` says the conversation exists, so a refusal at the conversation limit keeps the message for Retry.
    - There is no history to load, no conversation list and no resume. The stop button aborts by the id from `session_start`.
    - Any close ends the conversation. The socket never reconnects, and the transcript stays on the page followed by a notice. The next message starts a new conversation on a new socket.
    - New conversation (`/new`, `/clear`) closes the current one and deletes nothing.
    - The empty chat says up front that the conversation ends when the page is left or reloaded, or on sign-out.
    - Administrators and paired browsers keep stored conversations as before.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - **A scoped account's conversation ends with its socket.** Reloading the page, leaving the chat, closing the tab, or a dropped connection ends it, as do sign-out and a daemon reload or restart. The transcript stays on the page and on disk, but the dashboard can't reopen it. This is documented.
  - **What the gateway can't close is left to the daemon,** which retires an orphaned remote conversation after `wss.orphaned_session_timeout_secs` (30 minutes by default).
    - That covers a revoked account, a token that no longer verifies, and the old conversation after a provider repoint (the daemon refuses the old credential's close).
    - A chat's identity is never presented again once the chat is over, so its conversation is always such an orphan.
    - Retirement is conditional: the conversation must be idle, with no reply or approval pending and an up-to-date saved transcript.
    - **With `wss.orphaned_session_timeout_secs = 0` retirement is off, and what the gateway could not close stays live until the daemon restarts.** Until the next reload, such a conversation stays counted against its account.
  - **Identity providers: checked with Keycloak only.** Dashboard sign-in on this branch can't use a provider that needs a private CA, extra scopes such as `groups`, an RFC 8707 resource indicator (Logto issues opaque access tokens without one), or ES384 keys. So neither can this chat. Support for those is separate work for a later release.
  - No change to the daemon's session ownership rules. No image upload for scoped accounts, and no model switching. No gateway split.
- **Blast radius:**
  - **For scoped dashboard sessions:** `/ws/chat`, the session routes and `/api/status`.
    - `GET /api/sessions` lists the sign-in's open chats.
    - `POST /api/sessions/{id}/abort` stops an open chat's turn.
    - The agent list and an abort that must reconnect hold at most 2 daemon connections per account, and 16 in all, at once. Each holds its slot until the daemon is done with the connection. That stays true when the request goes away first, or when the handshake outlives the gateway's 10 s deadline while the daemon is still verifying the token.
    - Messages, rename and delete answer `404`.
  - **New:** `GET /api/agents/available` and `features.core_sessions`.
  - **Runtime:** an in-process connection can be bound to one OIDC provider (`InprocConnector::connect_bound`).
    - The dispatcher then verifies every `initialize` on it with `authenticate_bound`, refusing a bearer whose provider was repointed.
    - `connect_bound` also returns `Served`, which resolves once the daemon's task for that connection has ended.
    - Unbound connections and the wire protocol are unchanged.
    - Its placement exception is the provider-bound connection row in #11963, which must merge first with its Core approval recorded.
  - **The web chat UI** for scoped accounts.
  - **Unchanged:** administrators, paired browsers, and installs without dashboard sign-in.
- **Linked issue(s):**
  - Closes #11984 (dashboard chat for signed-in accounts without administrator rights).
  - Related #11961 (dashboard sign-in with OIDC, closed by #11965, which this builds on).
  - Depends on #11963 (the placement row for this PR's runtime addition; it must merge first, with its Core approval recorded).
  - Depends on #11965, #11186 and #11964: this branch carries their commits until they merge.
  - Related #7432 (the v0.9.0 tracker, which gives this chat a November 3 go/no-go).
  - Related #11985 (gateway tests for this chat under JWKS validation, a failed write and a retirement race).
  - Related #11412: its `chat_core.rs` at 71de465c49 is ported here onto master's session methods, without its unpublished runtime features.
  - Related #11737: restoring a conversation that is no longer live to its owner. With it, a scoped account could get its history back.
  - Related #11962 (the live-session cap, fixed by #11964).

### What this does, simply

**Someone who signs in to the dashboard without administrator rights can now chat** with the agents they're allowed to use. The agent runs as them: it uses their permissions, and nobody else's dashboard sees their conversations.

**A conversation lasts as long as its chat.** Each chat window is one conversation. Closing or reloading the page, signing out, or a daemon restart ends it. The transcript is kept, but the dashboard can't reopen it.

**Each sign-in can have four chats open at once.** A fifth waits until one closes.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `web` (dashboard chat), served by the gateway inside the daemon.
- **Setup / preconditions:**
  - an OIDC provider under `[gateway.dashboard_sign_in]` (Keycloak is the one checked; see the scope boundary);
  - `gateway.require_pairing = true`;
  - a non-admin permission profile granting `sessions` create, read, update and execute (without all four the chat isn't offered);
  - for tool calls, `allowed_tools` and `tools = ["execute"]` in that profile;
  - an agent in its `allowed_agents`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Sign in as the non-admin account and chat with an allowed agent.
  2. Sign in as a second account: the first account's conversation is not listed.
  3. Reload the page: the conversation has ended, and the next message starts a new one.
  4. Open the chat in five tabs and send a message in each: the fifth is refused until one tab closes.
  5. Sign out: the open conversations close.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** a scoped account chats as itself, as in the steps.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no dashboard sign-in. On the sign-in branch, scoped accounts get the configuration pages only, and the chat is administrator-only.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the required Rust checks (format, lint, the workspace rustdoc gate, tests) and the web regressions (including `npm run test:auth`) cover the changed crates and `web/`. The runs below were made on Linux before opening.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:**
  - CI runs no real identity provider and no browser. Those were checked by hand (below), with Keycloak and Chromium only.
  - The slow MCP test is `#[ignore]` and runs alone (below).
  - The gateway's chat tests verify tokens by introspection. JWKS validation, a failed write on a chat's connection, and retirement racing a close are covered by the prerequisites' own tests today. Gateway tests for them are #11985.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
# At this head, 400a32a72d:
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                                                  -> pass
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                                                                     -> pass
cargo check -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-rpc-client --all-targets                    -> pass
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-rpc-client --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings  -> pass
cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop                                                  -> pass, 0 warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib -- dashboard_core:: chat_core:: api_oidc:: dashboard_session::
    test result: ok. 138 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib
    test result: ok. 801 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored

# At 26cc923050, the same code (this head changes three doc-comment lines only):
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- rpc::
    test result: ok. 882 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-rpc-client
    test result: ok. 16 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- security::auth_provider::oidc
    test result: ok. 49 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib -- --ignored a_creation_still_running_at_sign_out_is_closed_when_it_lands
    test result: ok. 1 passed (about 60 s)
bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh                                                                        -> pass
bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh && python3 scripts/ci/check_internal_docs_links.py                       -> pass
```

- **The ignored test runs alone on purpose.** It gives an agent two MCP servers that never answer, so the daemon takes about a minute to create the conversation. While it does, the daemon holds its process-wide config write lock, and every other test's `session/new` in the binary would wait.
- **What the integration tests cover** (a mock identity provider, a mock model provider, a real in-process daemon context with SQLite sessions and orphan retirement):
  - **Isolation between accounts, including across a restart.** The attacks use the victim's real live conversation id, on a daemon connection of the attacker's own: reading its transcript, renaming, deleting or closing it, stopping a running turn, and answering or stopping a pending tool approval. Each is tried both from another account and from the same account's other sign-in.
  - each socket's own conversation, connection and identity;
  - closing at socket close, sign-out, expiry, eviction and sign-in turned off (closed, transcript kept);
  - a creation that lands after sign-out, or after its socket left;
  - a close after a lost connection, a lapsed binding, or a send the client refused locally;
  - a reconnect between turns that keeps the conversation and its approvals;
  - the four-chat limit, which closes no other tab;
  - two tabs on one dashboard id, or on different agents, never stalling each other;
  - a repointed provider receiving the token zero times (renewal, close, new chat), while a compatible publish keeps working;
  - cancelled opens keeping their places, and the account budget holding across sign-in churn;
  - a creation answered after its chat stopped waiting: closed and its share given back, with orphan retirement off;
  - the per-account and global connection bounds holding past the gateway's handshake deadline while the daemon is still verifying;
  - a chat stopping its turn when the browser leaves or the session ends;
  - a browser that stops reading, at sign-out and at a reload;
  - the 4409/4410 frames;
  - a lost grant between turns and mid-turn;
  - administrators staying in-process;
  - a revoked account's conversations retired by the daemon.
- **Revert checks:** each of 46 guards was removed in turn, and its test failed. Among them are the daemon's own ownership checks: with them removed, another account reads the victim's transcript, stops its turn, and answers its pending approval.
- **Test-first:** the one-conversation-per-socket tests were written first and failed on the previous design, each on its intended assertion.
- **Web:** on this `web/` tree: `npm run test:auth` (164 passed), `cargo web check` and `npm run build`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - **Setup:** a build of this head (`zeroclaw 0.8.6 (v0.8.6-222-g400a32a72)`) with Keycloak as the provider. Chromium 145 opened the chat sockets from the dashboard page the gateway serves, as the dashboard opens them. That ran twice over HTTP and twice over TLS, and all 8 flows passed in all 4 runs:
    - **chat as a scoped account:** two turns each reach the model and stream back;
    - **a reload** ends the conversation, and the next socket starts a different one;
    - **a fifth tab** gets `CONVERSATION_LIMIT` then `4409` while the other four stay open, and closing one lets it start;
    - **sign-out** closes both tabs' sockets with `4401`, and the session answers `401`;
    - **token expiry** closes the socket with `4401` within a few seconds;
    - **repointing the provider's client** closes the socket with `4401`. A new sign-in under the new client chats, and restoring the client closes that chat too. The old conversation's close is refused by the daemon, so it is left to orphan retirement, as documented above;
    - **an administrator's chat** still runs in-process and answers;
    - **a socket the browser closes right after opening** records `1006` on both the scoped and the administrator chat, and leaves no conversation open. That pattern predates this PR.
  - **Administrator flows on the same build** pass as on the sign-in branch: off by default, sign-in, expiry and re-auth, sign-out across tabs, a policy change, reloads, sign-in off and on, the chat socket, and a provider repoint.
    - The pairing fallback passes over HTTP. Over TLS it fails as it does on master, because the CLI builds `http://` admin URLs.
    - The one changed answer belongs to this PR: a scoped account's `GET /api/sessions` now returns its open chats instead of `403`.
  - **Not verified:**
    - identity providers other than Keycloak (see the scope boundary);
    - browsers other than Chromium;
    - macOS and Windows.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot (below): the empty scoped chat with its notice, a conversation after its socket closed, and the fifth-tab refusal. In the third, the limit also shows as an `[Error]` chat bubble under the banner; that duplicate is removed at the next refresh of this branch.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 400a32a72d; `surface` = `web`, Chromium 145 on Linux, the dashboard served by the gateway.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Chromium at 1280×800 on this head (tree `47070252e3`), signed in through the reference Keycloak as a placeholder account without administrator rights, with a test model:
  - The empty scoped chat with its notice:
    ![Empty scoped chat with its notice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf89b229-204d-4818-a1c4-80b5c5d3eab1)
  - A conversation after its socket closed; its messages stay, read-only:
    ![Conversation after its socket closed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6dec6d03-b84c-4da4-9b8f-40eaa4dddc90)
  - A fifth tab of the same sign-in, refused:
    ![Fifth tab refused](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/15a66637-7c9e-4403-b55e-aafc09e75fe0)
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** as listed under the manual checks above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full workspace tests. The change is confined to the gateway, the runtime's `rpc` module and the web UI. The gateway lib and the runtime's `rpc::` tests ran in full, as did the web regressions.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- **New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope?** Yes. Non-admin dashboard accounts can chat through the daemon, under their own grants.
- **New external network calls?** No.
- **Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed?** Yes. The session's access token is presented to the in-process daemon connection.
- **PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs?** No. Test identities are synthetic.
- **Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed?** No.
- **Risk and mitigation:**
  - **The token** stays in memory only.
    - Each chat keeps a copy until its conversation is closed, and the copies are wiped when dropped.
    - No code in this PR logs or formats it, and `ConnectOptions` and `RpcClient` redact it in `Debug`.
    - The handshake payload types (`InitializeParams`, `InitializeResult`) still derive `Debug`. Nothing here formats them; redacting them is left to a separate change.
    - The token goes only to the in-process connection's handshake.
  - **Known gap:** the handshake copies the token into the client's `ConnectOptions` and the `initialize` frame as plain strings, which aren't wiped. The exposure is short (`connect_over` drops them after the handshake), and the frame itself is plain text on the in-process duplex either way.
  - **Bound to its provider.** The token is presented only on connections bound to the provider that issued it, checked by the daemon against the policy it would send the token under (`authenticate_bound`). A repointed provider never receives it.
  - **Remote, not local.** That connection is classed as remote for every local-only check: path attachments and chunked upload are refused.
  - **Agents.** The gateway checks the agent before the socket opens, and the daemon re-checks grants at the current policy on every call.

## Compatibility (required)

- **Backward compatible?** Yes. Dashboard sign-in is off by default, and administrators and paired browsers are unchanged.
- **Config / env / CLI surface changed?** No.
- **Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed?** No.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <landed-commit>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** without a revert, remove the providers from `[gateway.dashboard_sign_in]`. Turning sign-in off ends every dashboard session and closes their conversations.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - the log line `dashboard chat opened through the core` without a reply;
  - `a dashboard conversation could not be closed; the core retires it once its client has stayed away`;
  - `a dashboard call to the core lost its connection`;
  - the daemon refusing new sessions with `Session limit reached`.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: feat(rpc): add zeroclaw-rpc-client and an in-process gateway transport
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions). **Depends on #11165** (`zeroclaw-rpc-proto`). This branch merges #11165's current head (19e41b09fa, which merges master through 89bd18484b). Its diff includes #11165's commits until #11165 merges.
- **What changed and why:**
  - New crate `zeroclaw-rpc-client`: the client half of the daemon RPC. It dials the local socket or named pipe, or runs over any byte stream (`RpcClient::connect_over`), performs the `initialize` handshake, multiplexes requests and responses on the api crate's `RpcOutbound`, delivers notifications and server-initiated requests, fails pending requests immediately on disconnect, and ships a jittered `Backoff`. It depends on `zeroclaw-api`, `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` and tokio, never on the runtime.
  - Runtime `rpc::inproc`: an in-memory duplex `RpcTransport` with its own class, `TransportKind::Inproc`, and no peer credential, plus `InprocConnector`, which the daemon creates per generation and binds to that generation's `RpcContext`. The authenticator gives `Inproc` no compatibility path: an `initialize` without an explicit credential is refused with `AUTH_REQUIRED` whether or not a roster exists and whatever `require_pairing` says (this is the fix for the anonymous in-process connection finding). It never becomes the trusted daemon uid because it carries no peer uid. In-process connections are counted separately, so `--ephemeral` daemons still exit with their last real client.
  - The gateway RPC connection: the supervised gateway receives the connector through `GatewayReloadControls.inproc`, dials the core with `RpcClient` over the duplex, and exposes the live handle to every request as the `CoreRpc` axum extension. The gateway has no credential of its own yet, so today the dial is refused and the seam stays idle by design (logged once at INFO); it comes alive when the gateway's service key or forwarded user bearers give it something to present. No route uses it yet.
  - Architecture test: `zeroclaw-rpc-client` keeps a dependency allow-list and the runtime never links the client.
- **Scope boundary:** No wire change. No route behaviour changes; the seam is dormant until a route opts in. zerocode keeps its own client (its WSS and relay dials are not in this crate). No protocol negotiation, no `server_proof`, no service principal: those are follow-up work.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-runtime` (new `rpc::inproc` module, three `pub(crate)` visibilities in `rpc::local`, one new field on `GatewayReloadControls`, connector creation and bind in `daemon::run`), `zeroclaw-gateway` (new `core_rpc` module, one extension layer, one new dependency, three test literals), workspace manifest and lockfile.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11001, #11002, #7432. Depends on #11165.
- **Labels:** as applied by the labelers

### What this does, simply

Until now the only code that could talk to the daemon over RPC was zerocode, and it carried its own hand-rolled client. This PR turns that into a small reusable crate and lets the gateway, still running inside the daemon today, open an RPC connection to the daemon's own dispatcher through an in-memory pipe. Nothing user-visible changes yet; it is the hook that lets each dashboard route be moved onto RPC one at a time before the gateway becomes a separate process.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. No user-visible surface changes; the seam is exercised by the unit and integration tests below and is visible only as one INFO log line at gateway start.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** none user-facing.
- **Setup / preconditions:** n/a
- **Steps to run:** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-rpc-client`; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::inproc::`; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib core_rpc::`; `cargo test --test architecture rpc_proto_boundary`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the tests pass. The gateway has no credential yet, so its connection is refused once and remains dormant. The earlier expected log, "gateway connected to the core over the in-process RPC seam", requires the credential follow-up described above; it is not the expected result on this head.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no `zeroclaw-rpc-client`, no `rpc::inproc`, no seam.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` (fmt, clippy `ci-all`, the rustdoc warnings gate, workspace tests incl. the new unit tests and the `architecture` gate, the OpenRPC drift check, MSRV, Windows and macOS checks). Green on head c04d474f45; re-run at 337d0a186f after merging the updated #11165 (merge commit, not a rebase).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (head `ed92285a87`, which merges #11165 at 19e41b09fa with master 89bd18484b; Linux x86_64; `--locked`; affected crates)

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check                                        # clean
$ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
$ cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-eval -p zeroclaw --all-targets   # exit 0
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-client -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings   # exit 0
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-client
test result: ok. 16 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- rpc:: config_application daemon::tests::reload
test result: ok. 863 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 4954 filtered out
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw --test architecture rpc_
test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 78 filtered out
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib core_rpc
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 657 filtered out
$ cargo doc --locked --no-deps -p zeroclaw-rpc-client -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto   # exit 0
$ cargo generate openrpc --check
openrpc: docs/book/src/architecture/zeroclaw-rpc.openrpc.json is in sync
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The three review sequences below are pinned by tests rather than manual runs (cancelled dial, EOF during `initialize`, a 48 × 1 MiB flood with no consumer). A separate runtime gate started a real daemon on a separate runtime test tree (its revision is not recorded here), connected over the Unix socket, completed `initialize` at protocol version 1, and served the supervised gateway's `/health` and `/api/health`; the dormant seam logged its single expected credential refusal. At ed92285a87, with the writer-failure cleanup's production lines removed and its regression kept, `write_failure_releases_calls_and_transport_despite_stalled_shutdown` fails ("write failure must close the outbound lane"); restored, it passes. With their fixes removed, the drain fix's tests (535b43829a) and the in-process remote-classification tests (e4bd5853e9) fail; restored, they pass.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `ed92285a87`; commands above and CI on this PR.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** None.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`Yes`, narrowing) A new transport class `TransportKind::Inproc` is refused at `initialize` unless it presents an explicit credential; it never takes the local no-roster compatibility path that a socket client gets. Tests pin: anonymous duplex refused with no roster and `require_pairing = false`; refused with a roster; accepted with a paired native token; the transport carries `Credential::None`, so `security.trust_daemon_uid` cannot apply to it. This closes the anonymous in-process connection finding for this PR.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: n/a

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`) Additive: a new crate, a new module, a new optional field on a runtime-internal struct, one dormant extension layer.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`No`)
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert <sha>`. If the seam misbehaves at runtime, the gateway logs it and every route keeps its in-process path; nothing depends on the connection yet.

## Addendum (head 337d0a186f): adversarial review fixes, restack and master merge

Restacked onto master 4f93bf5399 with #11165 underneath, then the updated #11165 (f74d25a0f4, which merges master f0ae8c8bd8) merged in as merge commit 337d0a186f. That merge had no textual conflict but one semantic one: the merged transport hardening changed the local socket writer (`run_writer` now takes a terminal-frame lane, `WriterTimeouts` and a peer label), so the in-process transport was adapted in the merge commit to use the hardened writer with the local peer-write and shutdown deadlines, and to answer an oversized frame with the same terminal error line the socket sends before closing; the writer items it needs became `pub(crate)`. #11165 carries the hub's and the upload surface's wire types into the proto; #11165's rebase ported `config/set-many`, `events/history`, the memory `plane`/`agent` fields and the session-message cursor fields into `zeroclaw-rpc-proto`, and its OpenRPC generator now emits Draft 7 schemas with params described by their real keys, required first. The drift check confirms the tracked document on this head. Master's deletion of the gateway `hardware_context` module is honoured (not resurrected by the seam commit), and master's `golden_frames` gateway test gets the new `inproc: None` field in its `GatewayReloadControls` literal (the miss that turned the `Test` job red at fa507794b1).

An adversarial source review of the earlier head 20594cd171 found three MODERATE client lifecycle defects, none with a demonstrated remote path into today's gateway (the seam presents no credential and is refused), all fixed here:
- **Bounded inbound requests.** Server-initiated requests are held in a bounded lane: at most `INBOUND_REQUEST_QUEUE_DEPTH` (32) requests and `INBOUND_REQUEST_BYTE_BUDGET` (16 MiB of received frames, refunded when the application drops a request). Beyond that, or once the application has dropped its receiver, each request is answered with `INBOUND_REQUEST_REJECTED` (−32050) through a non-blocking writer path, so response dispatch never waits behind an undrained queue. `RpcClient::rejected_inbound_requests()` reports the count; `take_inbound_requests` now returns a bounded `mpsc::Receiver`.
- **Prompt failure on a dropped handshake.** `initialize` races transport closure like every other request (`biased` toward a reply that arrived just before EOF) and returns `Disconnected` immediately instead of waiting out the handshake ceiling.
- **No leaked transport on a cancelled dial.** Reader and writer tasks are held by abort-on-drop guards from the moment they are spawned; only a completed handshake transfers them to the `RpcClient`. Cancelling the dial closes the connection and the peer sees EOF.

Tests: `cancelling_the_dial_releases_the_transport`, `peer_eof_during_initialize_fails_promptly`, `unanswered_server_requests_are_bounded_and_responses_still_flow` (48 × 1 MiB flood with no consumer; a concurrent `status` still completes; every refusal reaches the peer).

### Generation-drain ownership of in-process connections (re-review, SERIOUS), fixed at head 4c454b7ba2

The re-review of head 2c7e5ff2c3 found that the connector spawned each accepted in-process connection as a detached task and kept its own activity counter, which the daemon never consulted: the reload drain read only the socket listeners' client count, so an authenticated in-process connection with work still unwinding could not stop a replacement generation from starting over the same durable state. Now the connector owns its connection tasks in a `JoinSet` and exposes `InprocConnector::drain`, which after the generation's cancellation waits up to the listeners' `CONNECTION_DRAIN_GRACE` for them to unwind, then aborts and joins the rest (the local socket listener's sequence). The daemon runs that drain and waits on the sum of socket clients and in-process activity before `settle_exit_against_drain`, so a reload is refused (downgraded to shutdown) unless both are provably retired. In-process connections stay out of the ephemeral external-client count. Regressions: `rpc::inproc::tests::generation_drain_joins_accepted_connections_and_zeroes_the_count` (cancel, drain, count zero, client sees EOF) and `daemon::tests::reload_is_refused_while_an_in_process_connection_is_still_live` (a held connection yields `Outstanding` at budget expiry and downgrades the reload; after cancel and drain the same reload is admissible). The daemon-side regression holds the connection's own activity token rather than a model turn, since a prompt needs a provider; the token is the same one a prompt task would hold.

**Admission closed atomically with retirement (re-review at 611cdcbe47, SERIOUS), fixed at head 4c454b7ba2.** The first repair joined and counted registered connections, but `connect` checked cancellation before registering, outside the task registry's lock, and `drain` only took the current set, so a connect suspended between its check and its registration could register into a generation whose drain had already observed zero. Now admission (the final cancellation and seal check, the activity registration and the task insertion) is one critical section on the connector's registry, retirement seals admission and takes the set under the same lock, the daemon seals admission synchronously before it starts counting remaining activity, and a connection task that was cancelled before it ran refuses to start a dispatcher. A connect therefore either belongs to the drain or returns `None`. Regressions: `connect_paused_at_admission_is_refused_once_retirement_is_sealed` parks a connect at the admission boundary (test-only gate), retires and drains the generation, then resumes it and requires refusal with no activity or task growth; `concurrent_connects_racing_retirement_are_drained_or_refused` races 32 connects against retirement and requires every admitted connection to end with EOF and the registry to be empty and sealed afterwards. At the daemon boundary, through the real `daemon::run`: `reload_hands_over_once_held_in_process_activity_is_released` (paired-token `initialize` over `reload_controls.inproc`, activity held 1.2 s past the reload request, exit `Reload` only after release) and `reload_is_downgraded_when_in_process_activity_outlives_the_drain_budget` (activity held past the budget, exit `Shutdown`; this test fails if the daemon stops counting in-process activity, since its socket count is zero). The held activity is the token a prompt task holds; a model turn itself needs a provider the daemon harness has none of.

## Addendum (head ed92285a87): review fixes, the #11165 refresh, the in-process connection classed as remote, and writer-failure cleanup

- **535b43829a, the drain fix (review blocker).** The in-process connector kept the retiring generation's `RpcContext` alive through its clones, so reload and shutdown never drained the session leases.
  - The fix is de5cd570ab from #11322, unchanged and credited to @IftekharUddin.
  - `close_admission` and `drain` seal admission and release the bound context in one critical section, `bind` on a sealed connector is a no-op, and a `connect` waiting for a bind gives up when the generation is sealed.
  - It comes with two connector tests. #11322 can drop its copy when it restacks.
- **8a969442bb, `ConnectOptions` Debug.** `Debug` no longer prints credentials. The token and TUI signature show only whether they are set, and the forwarded environment shows variable names only.
- **e4bd5853e9, the in-process connection is remote in every local-only check.**
  - Four dispatcher checks used the peer label alone: path attachments on `session/prompt` and `file/attach`, `sops/run-detail` and `sops/rename`.
  - The in-process connection, which relays a remote browser, passed them as local IPC.
  - `is_remote_caller()` now covers the WSS listener and the in-process seam.
  - Three duplex tests show these refused as over WSS. 3df00a93b4 fixes their setup: a remote caller can't name a session that doesn't exist yet, so the tests use the id the daemon assigns.
- **8105097a8b, merge.** It brings in #11165 at dd9c178dc9: master through 8b77a2de8d, the new session methods and `budget_warning`, and the `SessionPromptAck` result. #11291's writer change (a write error retires the connection) now applies to the in-process duplex too, through the shared `run_writer`.
- **aeb9588be2, writer-failure cleanup.** A write failure used to leave pending calls, queue senders and the transport waiting on a half-close with no deadline. The writer now drops its queue receiver before a half-close bounded to one second, as the daemon's local writer does, and the reader returns once the outbound lane closes. `write_failure_releases_calls_and_transport_despite_stalled_shutdown` covers it.
- **ed92285a87, merge.** It brings in #11165's refresh at 19e41b09fa: master through 89bd18484b. No conflicts, and this PR's own changed lines are unchanged.
- **Runtime placement.** The in-process server adapter, its authentication and remote-classification wiring, and the generation-owned daemon registration need a recorded Core-approved holding-crate exception before this merges. It is proposed in #11963; this PR does not grant it.
- **Not in this PR:**
  - The endpoint and frame-cap single source of truth is #11346.
  - The in-process refusal wording and the note on connection limits are open for a follow-up.
- **Earlier head references** in this body (c04d474f45, 337d0a186f, 4c454b7ba2, 611cdcbe47, 2c7e5ff2c3, 20594cd171, fa507794b1) describe pre-restack revisions. They are kept for history.
