prs.title: refactor(rpc): extract the wire contract into zeroclaw-rpc-proto with an OpenRPC drift check
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Current head:** `19e41b09fa`. It merges master through 89bd18484b and fixes the 10-02 review: `session/prompt` declares `SessionPromptAck`, and the dependency claim is narrowed. The tracked document has 104 methods and 179 component schemas. The `f74d25a0f4` counts further down describe an earlier revision.

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions); rebased onto 4f93bf5399, then `upstream/master` f0ae8c8bd8 merged in (merge commit f74d25a0f4, not a rebase, since the PR is under review). The rebases and the merge carry master's later RPC additions into the proto: `config/set-many`, `events/history`, the memory `plane`/`agent` fields, the session-message cursor fields, and the bounded replayable subscription hub's surface (`events/subscribe`, `subscription/cancel`, the `events/event` and `subscription/lagged` notifications, `SubscribeParams`, the extended `LogsSubscribeResult`, `SubscriptionCancelParams`/`Result`, `SubscriptionLagged`), and the transport-hardening upload surface (`file/upload/begin`, `file/upload/chunk`, `file/upload/commit` with `FileUploadBeginParams`/`Result`, `FileUploadChunkParams`/`Result`, `FileUploadCommitParams`; commit returns the existing `FileEntryResult`). Merge conflicts were the registry (proto note kept, methods ported) and the moved types region (deletion kept, types ported); the tracked OpenRPC document was regenerated (97 methods, 157 schemas).
- **What changed and why:**
  - New crate `zeroclaw-rpc-proto`: the daemon RPC wire contract as pure data. It holds the `Method` enum with its single wire-name table, a per-method params/result contract (`Method::contract`, arm-complete like `authz`), every wire-stable request/response/notification payload type from `rt/rpc/types.rs`, the notification names, the error-code table, and the SOP graph projection re-exports. It depends on `zeroclaw-api`, `zeroclaw-config`, `zeroclaw-sop-graph` and serde, without depending on `zeroclaw-runtime`, so an RPC client can link the contract without linking the daemon. Its foundation dependencies still bring async I/O libraries transitively.
  - The runtime re-exports it. `zeroclaw_runtime::rpc::types::*` and `crate::rpc::dispatch::Method` keep resolving; `Method::authz()` becomes the `MethodAuthzExt` extension trait in `dispatch.rs` because it names runtime grants. Types whose fields are runtime-owned (doctor diagnostics, cron jobs, skill frontmatter, quickstart descriptors) stay in the runtime and are listed as external in the contract.
  - `cargo generate openrpc` renders the contract into `docs/book/src/architecture/zeroclaw-rpc.openrpc.json` (methods, params/result schema refs, authorization classification, notifications, error codes, component schemas). `cargo generate openrpc --check` runs in the `Installer Drift` CI job so the document cannot drift from the code.
  - Schema derives (`schema-export`-gated) added to the `zeroclaw-api` wire types the contract embeds: runtime status, plan entries, token-count source, model pricing.
- **Scope boundary:** No wire change. The contract declaration for `session/prompt` changes from `SessionPromptResult` to `SessionPromptAck`, an empty object, to describe the reply the daemon already sends; the daemon's behavior is unchanged. No method, field, name or default changes. No client (zerocode, gateway) switches to the new crate yet. `Method::authz` classification, dispatch, transport are unchanged. The zerocode exact-version gate, protocol negotiation and turn lifetime are separate PRs.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-runtime` (rpc types/dispatch/session import paths), `zeroclaw-api` (additive cfg-gated derives), `xtask`, CI `installer-drift` job, workspace manifest and lockfile. Every `use zeroclaw_runtime::rpc::types::…` in the gateway and zerocode compiles unchanged. `zeroclaw-runtime::config_application` now re-exports its six report types from `zeroclaw-rpc-proto`; the paths are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11000, #11001, #7432
- **Labels:** `ci`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `runtime`, `tests`, `distinguished contributor`, `domain:architecture`, `risk:medium`, `size:XL`, `type:refactor`, `release:v0.9.0`, `needs-author-action`

### What this does, simply

Until now, the only description of what the daemon's RPC accepts and returns was the Rust code inside the runtime. A client that wanted the types had to link the whole daemon or hand-copy them (zerocode hand-parses JSON for this reason). This PR moves the wire types and the method table into a small crate any client can depend on, and turns them into a machine-readable OpenRPC document that CI keeps in sync with the code.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** none user-facing; the RPC contract document and crate boundary.
- **Setup / preconditions:** a checkout of this branch.
- **Steps to run:** `cargo generate openrpc --check`; then edit any `Method::contract` arm or wire type and rerun to see the drift failure; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto --features schema-export`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the check reports in sync; a contract edit makes it fail with the regenerate hint; the proto tests pass.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` crate, no `cargo generate openrpc` subcommand, no contract document.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` (fmt, clippy `ci-all`, workspace tests including the `architecture` test, `Installer Drift` with the new OpenRPC check).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known. The local runs below are Linux x86_64.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (head `19e41b09fa`, which merges master 89bd18484b; Linux x86_64; `--locked`; affected crates)

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check                                        # clean
$ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
$ cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-eval -p zeroclaw --all-targets   # exit 0
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto -p zeroclaw-runtime -p xtask --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings   # exit 0
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto --features schema-export --lib
test result: ok. 28 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
$ cargo generate openrpc --check
openrpc: docs/book/src/architecture/zeroclaw-rpc.openrpc.json is in sync
$ cargo test --locked -p xtask --lib openrpc
test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 240 filtered out
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- rpc:: config_application
test result: ok. 840 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 4958 filtered out
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw --test architecture rpc_proto
test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 79 filtered out
$ cargo doc --locked --no-deps -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto                # exit 0
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Type parity with master: every one of the 162 types in master's `rpc/types.rs` exists exactly once in `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` or the runtime shim, with identical fields and serde attributes (checked against 8b77a2de8d; master has not changed that file since), and the tracked document's 104 methods equal master's `Method::ALL`. Revert check for the `session/prompt` fix: with only the declaration changed back to `SessionPromptResult`, both `session_prompt_result_accepts_the_dispatcher_reply` (xtask) and `session_prompt_request_reply_is_the_declared_empty_ack` (runtime) fail; restored, both pass. A deliberate contract edit makes `--check` fail with the regenerate hint.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `19e41b09fa`; commands above. The `session/prompt` revert check ran at dd9c178dc9, whose diff against master is the same as this head's.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Workspace-wide clippy and the full runtime test suite were not run locally (disk discipline: affected crates only); CI runs them. `xtask` gains `jsonschema` as a dev-dependency at the version `zeroclaw-plugins` already pins, so the lockfile changes by one entry.

### Adversarial review findings (three MODERATE), fixed at this head

The review of head b1781f2149 found that the OpenRPC document exported every parameter-bearing method as one by-name descriptor named `params` whose schema was the whole params object, so a conforming OpenRPC client would send `{"params": {"params": {...}}}` and the daemon would reject it with `INVALID_PARAMS`. The generator now expands a typed params struct into one descriptor per property, named by the wire key with `required` from the schema (the struct's schema stays in `components`); shapes it cannot enumerate (free-form objects, types another crate owns without an exported schema) produce no descriptors and say so in `x-zeroclaw-params` rather than inventing a key. A contract test builds `session/close` and `initialize` requests from the descriptors and parses them with the daemon's own types.

The re-review of head 2f74e5d0ac found two more contract defects, both fixed here. (1) OpenRPC 1.3.2 schema objects are JSON Schema Draft 7 but the generator used the 2020-12 dialect, so tuple types were emitted as `prefixItems`, which a Draft 7 consumer ignores: the `LogsQueryResult.next_cursor` schema accepted `[1, 2]` although the wire type is `Option<(String, String)>`. The generator now uses Draft 7 settings and builds parameter descriptors from the definitions after the Draft 7 transforms run, records the dialect in `x-zeroclaw.schema_dialect`, and a test walks the whole document for later-dialect keywords and validates the cursor schema with a Draft 7 validator (accepts `null` and two strings; rejects `[1, 2]`, wrong lengths, mixed elements). (2) Nine methods listed optional parameters before required ones; descriptors are now ordered required first, alphabetical within each group, with an assertion across every method.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: n/a. Authorization classification stays in the runtime and is untouched; the proto crate carries no policy.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`) Pure move plus additive derives; every wire name, field and default is unchanged and covered by the moved unit tests.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? (`No`) A new maintainer subcommand `cargo generate openrpc` exists; no user-facing CLI change.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the squash commit for this PR.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Compilation failures in consumers of the moved RPC definitions, or generated contract descriptions that disagree with daemon replies.

## Addendum (head 19e41b09fa): master merges and review fixes

**Master merges.** This revision merges master four times, at cdefa0d0a6, c473221313, 8b77a2de8d and 89bd18484b, with no rebase. The last merge had no conflicts and leaves this PR's own diff unchanged.

Each conflict kept the extraction and moved master's RPC changes to their new owner. The changes now in `zeroclaw-rpc-proto`:
- `session/steer`, `session/abort`, `session/append`, `session/rename` and `session/run-once`, with their params and results (#11132). Their authorization arms are master's, unchanged.
- `SessionListParams.running`, plus `TurnComplete.safeguard_fallback` and `usage` with `SafeguardFallbackWire`, `ProviderUsageTotals` and `TurnUsageTotals` (#11132).
- `ContextUsage.input_tokens_source` (#9453).
- The `budget_warning` notification and `AgentStatusEntry.runtime_profile` (#11692).

**Provider conversion.** The provider's safeguard notice converts to its wire form through a runtime-local function, so the protocol crate gains no dependency on providers.

**Config report types.** Master put the live-config publication report on results this PR moves:
- `revision` on the four config mutation results (#10911);
- `application` on `config/status` (#11466).

The six plain-data report types therefore move into `zeroclaw-rpc-proto`, along with `From<ConfigRevision>`:
- `PublishedConfigRevision`, `ConfigApplicationTarget`, `ConfigApplicationOutcome`, `ConfigApplicationReason`, `ConfigApplicationRecord` and `ConfigApplicationStatus`.

What stays the same:
- `config_application` keeps the ledger and re-exports them.
- There is no new crate edge, and the serde shape is unchanged.

**Review fixes:**
- e0f15058b0: the `session/prompt` result. It comes with an xtask Draft 7 check of the dispatcher's `{}` against the declared schema, and a runtime test of the real request-form reply. The `rpc-socket.md` "Turn streaming" text now describes the empty acknowledgement.
- 0075bab6d9: the manifest, crate overview and boundary test now state the runtime boundary rather than "no async I/O".

prs.title: fix(gateway): enforce the [gateway.pairing_dashboard] pairing limits
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `[gateway.pairing_dashboard]` was accepted and never read (#9394). Its settings now govern the gateway's pairing guard: the pairing code (`/pair`, `/api/pair`, the dashboard, `zeroclaw gateway get-paircode`) and the daemon's certificate-enrollment code. The guard reads them from live config on every code check and failed attempt, so an edit applies without a restart.
  - `code_ttl_secs` now defaults to 600 and is capped at 600, so no code lives longer than the 10 minutes #10142 set. Shorter lifetimes (down to 30 seconds) are honoured. Every full save wrote the old default of 3600, so most files hold it without anyone having chosen it. Those files still load: the value is lowered to 600 with a notice, on every load and in `zeroclaw config migrate`, not only in the version step.
  - `max_failed_attempts` (default 5) and `lockout_secs` (default 300) replace the guard's hard-coded constants for the gateway. A lockout longer than the 15-minute retention window is no longer swept early.
  - `max_pending_codes` is retired with a migration notice, through #11218's retirement table. The gateway keeps one pending code, and issuing a new one cancels the previous code, as before.
  - Expired codes are cleared the same way on every path: a reservation dropped after its code expired no longer puts the code back. The unused `PairingStore` (and `AppState::pending_pairings`) is deleted.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Channel pairing (Telegram, LINE, WeChat) is unchanged. Those guards keep the fixed limits, which equal the new defaults.
  - Code length and character family stay with `[gateway.pairing_code]`.
  - No schema version bump. The retirement and the lifetime cap belong to schema V4, which #11218 introduces and which has not shipped.
  - The gateway's separate request rate limiters (`pair_rate_limit_per_minute`, the auth limiter) are untouched.
- **Blast radius:**
  - The pairing guard in `zeroclaw-config` (used by the gateway, the daemon's RPC auth and certificate enrollment, and the channels).
  - Config load, `config migrate`, full and incremental save (the lifetime cap and the retirement).
  - `Config::validate` (new ranges).
  - `AppState` loses one unused field, so every `AppState` literal in the gateway's tests changes.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #9394. Builds on #11218, which merged on Nov 4.
- **Review scope:** #11218 has merged, and master is merged into this branch in `362b3930c9`, so the diff against `master` is this PR's own change: 19 files, +1006 −124.

### What this does, simply

The gateway has a `[gateway.pairing_dashboard]` config section with settings for how long a pairing code lasts, how many wrong codes a client may try, and how long a client is then locked out. Until now none of it was read: the gateway used fixed values, so changing the settings did nothing.

This PR makes the gateway use them. A code can be made to expire sooner than the default 10 minutes, but never later. The attempt limit and lockout length can be tuned. All three take effect without a restart.

Existing configs keep working. Most of them say `code_ttl_secs = 3600`, the old default that nothing read. On load that becomes 600, with a warning, so an upgrade never makes codes live longer. The `max_pending_codes` setting is removed with a warning, because the gateway only ever holds one pending code.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw config migrate`, `zeroclaw gateway`)
- **Setup / preconditions:** A throwaway config dir with a V4 `config.toml` holding `[gateway.pairing_dashboard] code_ttl_secs = 3600`, `max_pending_codes = 3`, `max_failed_attempts = 2`, `lockout_secs = 60`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. `zeroclaw config migrate`.
  2. Start the gateway, and send three wrong codes to `POST /pair` (`X-Pairing-Code` header).
- **Expected on this branch (after):**
  1. Warnings that `code_ttl_secs` was lowered to 600 and `max_pending_codes` was dropped. The file now says `code_ttl_secs = 600`, with no `max_pending_codes`.
  2. The third attempt gets 429 with `retry_after` about 60.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):**
  1. Nothing to migrate.
  2. 429 only after five attempts, for 300 seconds, whatever the config says.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** CI on `362b3930c9`, the merge with master. Its `Lint`, `Test` and `Docs Style` jobs cover fmt, clippy, rustdoc, the workspace tests and the changed Markdown on the pushed head.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The gateway and daemon wiring (`with_live_limits(PairingLimits::live(..))` at the two guard construction sites) has no test of its own. The resolver it passes is tested against published config, and the walkthrough below exercises the standalone gateway end to end. The daemon-supervised path is covered by review only.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Linux x86_64, toolchain 1.98.0, isolated `target/` and throwaway `HOME`; every test binary ran in a loopback-only network namespace.
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and CI's workspace clippy script: clean.
  - `cargo doc --locked --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop` (with `-D warnings`): clean.
  - `cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets`: clean.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config`: 2093 passed, 0 failed (15 new).
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib`: 678 passed, 0 failed.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- enroll:: rpc::auth security:: daemon:: i18n live_config_authority`: 634 passed, 0 failed.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --test relay_frontdoor_enrollment --test relay_full_path`: 11 passed, 0 failed.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- pair telegram::tests line::tests wechat::tests`: 429 passed, 0 failed.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw`: 551 passed, 0 failed, including the check that every retirement and cap reason is in every CLI locale.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw --test component -- config_ relay_claim_cli degraded_config_remediation`: 92 passed, 0 failed.
  - `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`, `docs_links_gate.sh`, `check_internal_docs_links.py`: pass.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - **Tests first.** The first commit adds the tests with the types they need, inert. On it, the 13 new behaviour tests fail and everything else passes (`zeroclaw-config` 1950 + 106; the locale check in the binary).
  - **A revert check per behaviour.** On the final head, each behaviour was reverted alone, by its functional line only, and exactly its tests failed:
    - the live attempt limit and lockout;
    - the live code lifetime;
    - the guard's ten-minute cap;
    - the sweep keeping a running lockout;
    - the dropped reservation not restoring an expired code;
    - lowering on the value path (this also fails the V1 to V4 fixture and the `config generate` validity check);
    - lowering on the document path;
    - the `max_pending_codes` retirement;
    - validation;
    - the 600 default.

    With nothing reverted, all of those tests pass.
  - **Out-of-range limits.** Startup keeps a config that fails validation, so the guard holds each limit to its validated range itself. `a_zero_lockout_still_locks_the_client_out`, `an_oversized_lockout_stops_at_one_day`, `the_attempt_limit_stays_between_one_and_one_hundred` and the enrollment server's `direct_enrollment_locks_out_with_a_zero_lockout_in_config` fail without the bounds and pass with them.
  - **The V4 negative controls** from #11218's review (28 modes) are identical on this head.
  - **The walkthrough in the reviewer steps,** run in a throwaway config dir with the gateway on a private loopback, on #11218's head (before) and this head (after):

    ```text
    before: config migrate leaves code_ttl_secs = 3600 and max_pending_codes = 3
            /pair: 403, 403, 403
    after:  warning: dropped retired config key `gateway.pairing_dashboard.max_pending_codes` from <tmp>/cfg/config.toml: the gateway keeps one pending pairing code at a time, and issuing a new code cancels the previous one
            warning: lowered config key `gateway.pairing_dashboard.code_ttl_secs` in <tmp>/cfg/config.toml to its maximum: a pairing code stays redeemable for at most 600 seconds (10 minutes)
            [gateway.pairing_dashboard] code_ttl_secs = 600, max_failed_attempts = 2, lockout_secs = 60
            /pair: 403 {"error":"Invalid pairing code"}, 403, 429 {"error":"Too many failed attempts. Try again in 59s.","retry_after":59}
    ```

  - **Not verified:** macOS and Windows; the daemon-supervised gateway end to end; the dashboard UI; channel pairing beyond its unit tests.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output (the two CLI warnings above, English locale)
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `75b2f79df3` (tree `f2028b044e`, the out-of-range limits fix: fmt, the workspace check, CI's clippy and rustdoc, the config and gateway libs, the enrollment tests, the new tests and this PR's 25 tests, with revert checks). `362b3930c9` (tree `6a269e9b05`, the master merge: fmt, the workspace check, CI's clippy and rustdoc, the config, gateway and runtime libs, this PR's 25 tests, #11965's sign-in tests and the revert checks, all re-run on Linux x86_64); before that, `f611400335` (tree `5cb8f02939`; the fmt, rustdoc, config, gateway, walkthrough and workspace-clippy runs were on a local commit with the identical tree), `cli` (`zeroclaw config migrate`, `zeroclaw gateway start`, `POST /pair`)
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** above
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** above
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:**
  - `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` (markdownlint) needs Node 20 or later, which the test machine lacks. The two Markdown edits are single sentences, and CI's `Docs Style` covers them.
  - The full workspace `cargo test` was not run locally; CI runs it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:
  - The change governs the bearer pairing code and the enrollment code: their lifetime and the brute-force limits on guessing them.
  - Risk: a setting could weaken the gate. Mitigations:
    - the lifetime is capped at 600 seconds in three places (load, validation, and the guard itself);
    - the attempt limit is at least 1;
    - the guard holds the attempt limit and lockout to their validated ranges even when startup keeps an out-of-range value;
    - validation refuses out-of-range values;
    - the defaults equal today's fixed values;
    - an upgrade never lengthens a code's life.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users:
  - Nothing is required.
  - A saved `code_ttl_secs` above 600 loads as 600 with a warning, and `max_pending_codes` is dropped with a warning. `zeroclaw config migrate` writes both into the file; otherwise the next save does.
  - New validation ranges: `code_ttl_secs` 30–600, `max_failed_attempts` 1–100, `lockout_secs` 1–86400. A value set outside them, other than a lifetime above 600, is refused at load with the key and the range.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <merge sha>`. Configs that `config migrate` already rewrote keep `code_ttl_secs = 600` and lose `max_pending_codes`, both of which the reverted build still accepts.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Setting `[gateway.pairing_dashboard]` back to the defaults (600 / 5 / 300) restores the previous behaviour exactly.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - a `/pair` or enrollment 429 earlier or later than the configured limits;
  - a pairing code rejected before its lifetime;
  - `lowered config key` or `dropped retired config key` warnings on every start, which means the file was not rewritten.

v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(memory): keep owned-session subagent and pipeline memory private
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - **`spawn_subagent` hands its child the owner's memory.** `child_run_overrides` set `memory: None`, so `agent::run` built the child's memory itself with an unscoped `create_memory_for_agent`, and a subagent of an owned session read and wrote the agent's shared plane. Once the parent session is pinned, the child is now started over the session's routed handle. The child run's SOP engine is built over that same handle: since #11174, a run's SOP engine is built over the run's memory, which is the caller's handle when one is given.
  - **`execute_pipeline` runs memory steps over the owner's memory.** The pipeline runs tools it captured when it was assembled. `rebind_memory_tools` replaces the registry's memory tools when a session is pinned, but it cannot reach the pipeline's captured copies. Once the session is pinned, a memory step now runs over the routed handle, in both sequential and parallel mode.
  - **One route per registry, pinned with the session.** The tool factory creates a `SessionMemoryRoute` and gives it to `spawn_subagent`. `assemble` gives it to the pipeline it mints, and the sealed registry keeps it. `route_memory_to_principal` first checks that the route can take the owner, then runs #11174's one-time rebind of the native memory tools, then pins the route, and only then swaps the session's memory. A routing the rebind refuses leaves the route unpinned. Skill wrappers that captured either tool hold the same instances, so they follow the pin as well.
  - **A cross-agent SOP step keeps the owner.** A SOP step naming another agent re-assembles that agent's execution, and the re-assembly built the step agent's memory from config, unscoped, whether the step ran from the owned session itself or from its subagent. The re-assembly handle now carries the owner of the memory the run is on: the session's routed handle, or the child's. The step agent's memory becomes the owner's plane for that agent, the plane `memory/*` serves for that owner and agent. An owned session whose memory handle does not report its owner refuses cross-agent steps instead. On current master, per-agent SQLite memory does not forward the principal-scoped calls, so such a step's memory writes are refused before any effect. The per-agent forwarding in #11225 turns them into writes on the owner's plane. A step re-assembled through the turn's supplied capabilities (#11174) gets those capabilities' memory, put on the owner's plane for the step agent. It is refused before assembly when the run's memory owner is not the principal those capabilities resolve for, because their provider credentials belong to that principal.
  - **A registry built over an owner's plane is pinned at birth.** The route was pinned only by `route_memory_to_principal`. A registry the factory builds over memory that is already an owner's plane never went through that call, so its spawner and pipeline saw an empty route and fell back to shared memory. That covers a subagent's run, a re-assembled SOP step, and #11225's independent delegate target. The factory now pins the route when the memory it is given reports an owner. `Memory::principal_scope` is the new trait method it reads (default `None`); the principal-plane wrapper reports its scope.
  - **An owned session's SOP runs are audited on its owner's plane.**
    - The SOP tools a session is built with capture the daemon's audit logger, which writes through the shared plane.
    - That logger recorded `sop_execute`'s run, including the caller's payload, and the step outputs of the run it queues. `sop_advance` and `sop_approve` recorded step results the same way, directly or through a pipeline allowed to run `sop_execute`.
    - The three tools now share the registry's session memory route. Once the session is pinned, each call audits through a logger over the owner's routed memory, and `sop_execute` hands that logger to the run it queues.
    - The daemon's shared logger itself is never changed. The operator-facing run views read the engine, not these rows, so nothing visible moves.
  - **An owned run keeps its owner across an approval.**
    - A run that parks for approval can resume away from the session that started it. The approval can come from RPC `sops/decide`, HTTP, WebSocket or a channel on the daemon's headless driver, or from another session's `sop_approve`.
    - Neither path knew the run's owner. The daemon's shared logger then audited the finished run, private payload included, and the resumed step ran on shared memory.
    - The run now records its owner (`SopRun.memory_owner`) when `sop_execute` starts it in a pinned session. It is persisted with the run, so it survives a daemon restart; runs persisted before it restore as unowned.
    - Every driver resolves the run's audit logger from that owner through `audit_for_run`. An unowned run keeps the logger. An owned run keeps its owner's logger, gets the shared logger re-scoped to its owner, and gets no logger when the logger belongs to another owner.
    - The headless driver also gives the resumed step turn the owner's memory for the step agent. If that memory cannot be built, the step fails.
    - A live driver in another session re-assembles the step agent under the run's owner, even for its own agent, and memoizes that execution apart from its own, keyed by the owner's whole scope (principal, agent, namespace and tenant). A step that names no agent runs as the driving session's agent and is attributed to it.
  - **An owned session's SOP tools act only on its own runs** (662acf5fae from #11411 by @Aarlington, adopted here as dd6f10d57c with its authorship kept).
    - `sop_advance`, `sop_approve` and `sop_status` read the session's owner from its route and check `SopRun::is_accessible_from` before they touch a run. An owned session sees and moves only runs recorded with its exact owner. Unowned runs, including runs persisted before this PR, are not visible to it. Unowned operator sessions keep full access.
    - `sop_status` also leaves other owners' runs out of its active and finished lists, and skips the metrics summary in an owned session, because the collector aggregates every owner.
    - `sop_advance` and `sop_approve` audit through `audit_for_run` with the run's recorded owner.
    - The SOP tools registered when no audit logger is configured, and `sop_status`, now take the session route too. Before, only the audited branch did.
  - **Refused where the owner cannot be carried.** A registry that holds a `spawn_subagent`, `execute_pipeline` or SOP tool the runtime built, but has no route (one not assembled from the factory's tool set), refuses the pin, so the owned session fails to start instead of falling back to the shared plane. Only tools the runtime built count: a tool a source supplied keeps the memory handle it was built with, whatever its name, and a registry assembled only from a source's tools pins nothing, so routing changes only the agent's own memory there. A route pins once and refuses a different handle.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - The `delegate` path is #11225's. This PR adds only `DelegateTool::check_principal_scope`, a read-only form of the refusal in `bind_principal_scope` that routing calls before it binds anything. `rebind_memory_tools` and the skill-alias rebinding are untouched.
  - The existing memory tools are still rebound by `rebind_memory_tools`, as before; this PR only adds the route for the tools that start memory work of their own.
  - An unowned session is unchanged: it never pins the route, and both tools keep the agent's shared memory.
  - The delegation doctrine in `docs/book/src/agents/delegation.md` is drafted separately (see the issue).
- **Blast radius:**
  - `rt/tools/spawn_subagent.rs`: the child's memory override.
  - `zeroclaw-tools` `pipeline.rs`: step resolution for sequential and parallel runs, plus a new `session_memory` module.
  - `rt/tools/mod.rs` and `rt/tools/scoped.rs`: a new `AllToolsResult.session_memory` field, and the route carried on `ScopedToolRegistry` with `check_session_memory_pin` and `pin_session_memory`. `NativeMemoryBinding` forwards `principal_scope()`.
  - `rt/agent/agent.rs`: the pin check and the pin in `route_memory_to_principal`, around #11174's one-time rebind and before the session's memory is swapped. Merged with #11225, every check runs before anything binds, including a check that the delegate isn't already bound to another owner.
  - `rt/agent/loop_.rs`: the run's cross-agent step handle carries its memory's owner beside the bound capabilities.
  - `rt/agent/turn/mod.rs`: `SopStepReassembly.memory_owner`; `assemble_owned_execution_with_capabilities` wraps the step agent's memory, config-backed or from the turn's capabilities, in the owner's scope for that agent, and the live driver refuses a bound step whose owner is another principal.
  - `rt/agent/agent.rs`: the session's cross-agent step handle carries its owner, or is withheld when the owner cannot be read.
  - `zeroclaw-api` / `zeroclaw-memory`: `Memory::principal_scope`, reported by `PrincipalPlaneMemory`. #11225 added the same method, so it is on master now and no longer in this diff.
  - `rt/tools/sop_execute.rs`, `sop_advance.rs`, `sop_approve.rs`, `rt/sop/audit.rs`: the SOP tools take the session route, and `session_audit` picks the owner's logger once the session is pinned.
  - `rt/sop/types.rs`, `rt/sop/engine.rs`: `SopRun.memory_owner` and `SopEngine::start_run_for`. `activate_reserved_run` takes the owner, and every headless start passes `None`.
  - `rt/sop/audit.rs`, `rt/sop/executor.rs`, `rt/agent/turn/mod.rs`: `audit_for_run`, the headless driver's logger and step memory, and the live driver's run-owner handling.
  - `rt/tools/sop_advance.rs`, `sop_approve.rs`, `sop_status.rs`, `rt/sop/types.rs`: the run-ownership check (`SopRun::is_accessible_from`) and the route on `sop_status`.
  - `rt/locales/en/cli.ftl`: `cli-sop-run-unavailable`, `cli-sop-step-owner-principal-mismatch` and `cli-sop-step-owner-memory-unavailable`.
  - `docs/book/src/architecture/runtime-composition.md`: which registries an owned session can pin.
  - `rt/composition/supplied_only_traps.rs`: the extra step-owner argument.
  - `zeroclaw-api`: `PrincipalScope` derives `Serialize`/`Deserialize` so a run can persist it.
  - `zeroclaw-channels`: its daemon SOP step handle passes the turn memory's owner (channel sessions are not principal-pinned today, so this is `None` there).
  - Every `AllToolsResult` literal gains the field. Since #11174 the test helpers in `zeroclaw-channels` and `parity.rs` build through `AllToolsResult::from_prebuilt_tools`, so they need no change.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11239. Related #11225, #11198, #11411, tracker #8290.
- **Co-authored:** 662acf5fae (here dd6f10d57c) and the `sop_advance` test update come from @Aarlington's #11411.
- **Labels:** (set after the labelers run)

### What this does, simply

A session that belongs to one user keeps that user's memories private. Two tools could still read and write the agent's shared memory from such a session: a helper agent the session starts, and a chain of tool calls run as one pipeline. Both now use the owner's private memory. A session whose tools cannot be pointed at the owner's memory refuses to start, rather than quietly using the shared one.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The regressions drive the real tool factory and `assemble` into an owned session and observe where rows land.

### How I tested

**Review fixes at ac9069f67e.** Three commits on 64d43dbaaa, one per review comment:
- 592046152d: when an unowned session approves an owned run whose step names no agent, the step agent is re-assembled as the session's own agent. The step's prompt and attribution assumed the step named that agent, and the prompt builder panicked. Both now use the alias the step was re-assembled as. Test: `another_sessions_driver_runs_an_owned_runs_unnamed_step_as_its_own_agent`.
- 4f43785fbe: the live driver memoizes the execution of a foreign-owned step by the owner's whole scope instead of the principal id alone, so runs of one principal in different namespaces or tenants never share an execution. The runtime's own sessions are scoped only by principal and agent, so this takes an embedder that routes with a namespace or tenant. Test: `owned_runs_in_different_scopes_never_share_a_step_execution`. `another_sessions_driver_runs_an_owned_run_under_its_owner` now finds the owner's execution without assuming the key's format.
- ac9069f67e: the bound-step refusal and the headless owner-memory failure come from Fluent keys through the runtime i18n helpers. `a_bound_cross_agent_step_refuses_a_foreign_memory_owner` checks the recorded output against the catalogue, and `an_unavailable_owner_memory_fails_the_step_in_the_catalogues_words` covers the headless failure.
- Linux x86_64, rustc 1.98.0, at ac9069f67e:

  | Check | Result |
  |---|---|
  | `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` | 6024 passed, 0 failed, 10 ignored |
  | `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib` | 1386 passed |
  | `cargo test -p zeroclaw-memory --lib` | 557 passed |
  | `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib` | 2031 passed |
  | `cargo test -p zeroclaw-api --lib` | 321 passed |

  | this PR's 32 runtime regressions, three runs | 32 passed each run |
  | `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, CI's clippy lint command, comment hygiene, docs quality | clean |

  The test binaries ran with `TMPDIR` on a short path outside `/tmp`, because of the stray `/tmp/.git` described below.

Switching back one fix at a time, each fails only its own test: the alias for the prompt alone (the panic) and for the step's attribution alone (no agent recorded), the scope key, the refusal's catalogue string and the owner-memory failure's.

- Otherwise the diff is unchanged: 21 of the 29 files this PR touched carry identical changes against the new base, and the merge adds one argument in `supplied_only_traps.rs`. The resolutions are the ones I prepared against #11174's branch before it landed; replayed onto master, only `cli.ftl` needed a hand edit.
- Three commits on top cover what #11174's supplied capabilities make reachable:

**New tests:**
- `rt::agent::agent`. Each test assembles a session from the real `all_tools` and `assemble`, pinned to `user:alice`, over a shared SQLite memory:
  - `a_pinned_sessions_pipeline_memory_step_lands_on_the_owners_plane`: `execute_pipeline` with a `memory_store` step writes to alice's private plane, and nothing reaches the shared plane.
  - `a_pinned_sessions_subagent_child_runs_on_the_owners_plane`: the child `spawn_subagent` starts is handed the session's routed memory, pointer-equal to it, and a write through that handle lands on alice's plane, not the shared one.
  - `a_registry_that_cannot_carry_the_owner_refuses_the_pin`: a registry with `spawn_subagent` but no route refuses the pin, and the session's memory does not move.
- `rt::tools::spawn_subagent::a_pinned_sessions_child_is_started_over_the_routed_memory`: before the pin the child builds its own memory; after the pin it is given the routed handle.
- `rt::agent::loop_::sop_engine_memory_follows_the_callers_memory` (removed in the #11174 refresh, which builds the run's SOP engine over the caller's handle itself).
- `zeroclaw-tools`:
  - `pipeline::memory_steps_of_a_pinned_session_land_on_the_owners_plane` covers sequential and parallel runs.
  - `pipeline::memory_steps_of_an_unpinned_session_keep_the_shared_plane` is the control.
  - `session_memory::a_route_pins_once_and_refuses_another_plane` and `session_memory::only_memory_tools_are_rebuilt_over_a_handle`.

**Proof on master.** The three regressions that use only master's API (the tool factory, `assemble`, and `route_memory_to_principal`) were run on plain `upstream/master` e16fd898ba, without the fix, and then on this branch. The master run adds only the tests and the same `#[cfg(test)]` task-local that records the memory override `spawn_subagent` gives its child. On master that override is `None`, so `agent::run` builds the agent's unscoped memory for the child. The unit tests of the new route, pipeline resolution and SOP memory exercise types that do not exist on master, so they cannot run there.

Unpatched `upstream/master` e16fd898ba: all three fail. The pipeline's `memory_store` row lands on the shared plane, the child is handed no memory of its own, and the pin is not refused:

```text
an owned session's pipeline must not write the shared plane
thread 'agent::agent::tests::a_pinned_sessions_subagent_child_runs_on_the_owners_plane' panicked at crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/agent.rs:5636:14:
the child is handed the session's memory, not left to build its own
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 3 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5314 filtered out; finished in 0.08s
```

This branch: the same three pass.

```text

test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5316 filtered out; finished in 0.12s
```

**Review follow-up** (second commit, SOP steps and derived registries). New tests:
- `rt::agent::turn::sop_step_reassembly_tests::an_owned_sessions_reassembled_step_keeps_the_owner_for_the_step_agent`:
  - The real `assemble_owned_execution` runs for step agent `stepper` with an owner.
  - Its `memory_store` does not reach `stepper`'s shared plane or another principal's, and its `memory_recall` does not return `stepper`'s shared rows.
  - The store lands on the owner's plane for `stepper`, or is refused for lack of principal scoping. Since #11225, per-agent SQLite forwards the principal-scoped calls, so the refusal is left for backends without private support.
- `…::an_unowned_sessions_reassembled_step_keeps_the_shared_plane`: the control.
- `…::the_driver_reassembles_an_owned_sessions_step_under_its_owner`: the real SOP driver re-assembles the owned step from the handle's owner, and the step's cached registry has the same property.
- `rt::agent::agent::an_owned_sessions_sop_steps_reassemble_under_its_owner` and `…::an_owned_session_that_cannot_carry_its_owner_refuses_cross_agent_steps`: the owned session's step handle carries its owner, an unowned session's carries none, and one whose memory hides the owner withholds the handle.
- `rt::agent::loop_::a_runs_sop_steps_reassemble_under_the_owner_of_its_memory`: a subagent's run, started over the owner's plane, re-assembles its steps under that owner.
- `rt::agent::agent::a_registry_built_over_an_owners_plane_is_pinned_to_it`: the real factory and `assemble` over a principal-plane handle, as a delegated target or child run receives one, without the session routing call. Its pipeline's `memory_store` lands on the owner's plane, and its `spawn_subagent` hands the child that handle.
- `zeroclaw-memory` `principal_plane::a_principal_plane_reports_its_scope_and_a_shared_backend_none`.

Each part was undone in turn and the named test fails:
- re-assembly ignores the owner: both re-assembly tests
- the driver drops the owner: the driver test
- the session carries no owner: both session tests
- the child run carries no owner: the child-run test
- the factory does not pin an owned handle: the factory test

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                     -> exit 0
scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                             -> Comment hygiene gate passed.
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib                           -> 5367 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored
cargo test -p zeroclaw-memory --lib                            -> 544 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib                          -> 1957 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib                             -> 2072 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored (the macOS-only serply test described below)
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-memory -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets --no-deps
                                                               -> one diagnostic, the macOS-only `service/mod.rs` import described below
```

**Review follow-up 2** (third commit, SOP audit). New tests:
- `rt::agent::agent::an_owned_sessions_sop_audit_stays_on_its_owners_plane`:
  - An owned session is built by the real factory with the SOP engine and a shared audit logger, as the daemon supplies one.
  - `sop_execute` runs with a unique payload, and `sop_advance` with a unique step output.
  - A step result is logged through the logger the queued run carries, as the driver does.
  - None of the three markers is in the shared plane's `sop` rows. All three are on the owner's plane.
- `…::an_owned_sessions_approved_run_is_audited_on_its_owners_plane`: an approval that resumes a supervised run hands the resumed step the owner's logger.
- `…::an_owned_sessions_pipeline_sop_audit_stays_on_its_owners_plane`: the same `sop_execute` through a pipeline allowed to run it.
- `rt::sop::audit::a_session_audit_follows_its_pinned_route`: the captured logger before the pin, the owner's after it, and no audit without a captured logger.

Each part was undone in turn and the named test fails:
- the helper ignores the route: both `sop_execute` tests
- the factory does not wire `sop_execute`: both `sop_execute` tests
- `sop_execute` queues the captured logger: the direct test's queued step result
- the factory does not wire `sop_advance`: the direct test's step output
- the factory does not wire `sop_approve`: the approval test

```text
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib   -> 5371 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored (at the third commit)
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets --no-deps -> only the macOS-only `service/mod.rs` import described below
cargo fmt --all -- --check             -> exit 0; comment hygiene gate passed
```

**Review follow-up 3** (fourth commit: the run's owner across approval and restart). New tests:
- `rt::sop::executor::an_owned_run_resumed_off_session_is_audited_on_its_owners_plane`:
  - An owned supervised run starts with a unique payload and parks for approval.
  - It is approved through `resolve_via_broker` and resumed through `drive_resumed_broker_action` with the daemon's shared logger. RPC `sops/decide`, the gateway's HTTP and WebSocket approvals, and channel approvals all resume through that boundary.
  - The resumed step turn is started over the owner's plane for the step agent.
  - The step row and the finished run, payload included, are on the owner's plane, and neither is on the shared plane.
- `…::an_owned_run_restored_and_resumed_off_session_is_audited_on_its_owners_plane`: the same after a restart. The engine is dropped, the run is restored from the same SQLite run store, and it keeps its owner.
- `…::a_headless_step_of_an_owned_run_runs_on_its_owners_plane`: an owned run's step memory is the owner's plane for the step agent. An unowned run gets none.
- `rt::sop::audit::a_runs_audit_is_resolved_from_its_owner`:
  - An unowned run keeps the given logger.
  - An owned run keeps its owner's logger and gets the shared logger re-scoped to its owner.
  - An owned run gets no logger from another owner.
- `rt::agent::turn::sop_step_reassembly_tests::another_sessions_driver_runs_an_owned_run_under_its_owner`: a live driver in a session that does not own the run re-assembles the step agent under the run's owner, memoized under its own key, and audits the step on the owner's plane.
- `rt::sop::types::sop_run_serde_roundtrip` now checks both directions. An unowned run is written without the owner key, which is the shape of a run persisted before this change, and restores unowned. An owned run keeps its owner.
- `rt::agent::agent::an_owned_sessions_sop_audit_stays_on_its_owners_plane` now also checks that the run records its owner. It also drains the step `sop_advance` queues and finds that step's row on the owner's plane.

Each part was undone in turn, and the named test fails:
- the headless driver audits with the given logger: both resume tests
- the engine does not record the owner: both resume tests, the live-driver test and the direct `sop_execute` test
- `sop_execute` records no owner: the direct `sop_execute` test
- the owner is not persisted: the restored-run test and the serde round trip
- an unowned run is written with an owner key: the serde round trip
- the live driver ignores a run owner other than its session's: the live-driver test
- the live driver audits with the queued logger: the live-driver test
- `sop_advance` queues the captured logger: the direct `sop_execute` test (the step it queues)
- the headless step memory ignores the owner: the helper test and both resume tests
- the headless driver starts the step turn without that memory: both resume tests

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                     -> exit 0
scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                             -> Comment hygiene gate passed.
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib                           -> 5477 passed; 1 failed; 8 ignored (the timing test described below)
cargo test -p zeroclaw-memory --lib                            -> 544 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib                          -> 1967 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib                             -> 2072 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored (the macOS-only serply test described below)

                                                               -> one diagnostic, the macOS-only `service/mod.rs` import described below
cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime -> exit 0
```

The one runtime failure in the full run was `rpc::dispatch::tests::configure_refuses_an_incarnation_replaced_under_the_lock`, a test this PR does not touch. It races a 150 ms sleep against a queued configure call and lost that race while other builds loaded the machine. It passed 5 of 5 runs in isolation at this head. `cargo test -p zeroclaw-api --lib` does not compile on its own on master either, because `channel.rs` uses `tokio::time` without that tokio feature. The only `zeroclaw-api` change here is the `PrincipalScope` serde derive, which the runtime tests exercise through the run store.

**Revert sensitivity.** Each part of the fix was undone in turn and the named test fails:
- child handed no memory: the subagent regression
- the pipeline ignores the route: the pipeline regression in both crates
- the factory does not wire `spawn_subagent`: the subagent regression
- `assemble` does not wire the pipeline: the pipeline regression
- the pin call removed: both regressions and the refusal test
- the SOP engine ignores the override: the SOP test

**Commands and output tails** (this branch, rebased on e16fd898ba):

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                     -> exit 0
scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                             -> Comment hygiene gate passed.
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib                           -> 5311 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored
cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib                             -> 2072 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored (see below)
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib                          -> 1957 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
                                                               -> 1 error, not in this diff (see below)
```

Clippy over every target of the three crates reports exactly one diagnostic: `unused import: std::sync::mpsc` at `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/service/mod.rs:15`. That file is identical to master. The import is `#[cfg(any(windows, test))]`, and its only test use is in code gated out of macOS, so a macOS test build flags it and a Linux one does not. With that lint reported rather than denied, the three crates are otherwise clippy-clean.

The one `zeroclaw-tools` failure is `web_search_tool::tests::test_serply_connection_refused_error_is_query_free`, in a file this PR does not touch. It fails the same way on every run on macOS: connecting to a bound but unlistening port hangs there until the 5 s client timeout instead of being refused, so the error is classified `transport=timeout` rather than `transport=connect`. It does not depend on this change.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` (build, clippy, tests on Linux) and `Parallel Runtime Test`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known. The regressions do not depend on the platform.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - The pin runs before the session's memory is swapped, so a refused pin leaves the session unrouted; the refusal test asserts the memory handle did not move.
  - Not verified: a live daemon with a real provider running a subagent turn. The child's model turn is not exercised; the regression stops at the handle the child is started with and proves where a write through it lands.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no user-visible interface state changed)
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** At 64d43dbaaa, none of the Linux checks above; clippy ran on the whole workspace with CI's lint command. The earlier heads below ran clippy on the changed crates only. macOS and Windows were not run for this refresh.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. It narrows where an owned session's subagent and pipeline memory operations land.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- **If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:** N/A. This closes a cross-principal memory isolation gap. The feature is on master only, so no release is exposed.

## Compatibility (required)

- **Backward compatible?** Yes for unowned sessions, which do not change. For owned sessions:
  - a subagent child and pipeline memory steps now use the owner's private plane
  - an owned session whose registry has a `spawn_subagent` or `execute_pipeline` the runtime built, but was not assembled from the tool factory, refuses to start; a registry assembled only from a tool source's tools is accepted, and routing changes only the agent's own memory there
  - a cross-agent SOP step re-assembled through a turn's supplied capabilities is refused when the run's owner is not the principal those capabilities resolve for
  - in an owned session, `sop_advance`, `sop_approve` and `sop_status` answer "SOP run unavailable in this session." for a run recorded with another owner or with none
- **Config / env / CLI surface changed?** No
- **Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed?** No
- **Persisted SOP runs:** a run records its owner in a new optional field. A run persisted before this change has no such field and restores as unowned, and an unowned run is still written without it.
- **Upgrade steps:** None

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Runs written by this version:** an older binary ignores the owner field, so after a rollback an owned run that is still parked resumes unowned, as it does on master today.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** an owned session failing to start with `this session's tools cannot carry its owner's memory plane; refusing to pin it`, or a SOP step failing with `SOP step refused: this run belongs to a different principal than the one this turn's capabilities act for.`

### Notes for reviewers

- **#11225 overlap.** #11225 landed first, and this branch merges it. Both PRs change `route_memory_to_principal`. Every check now runs before anything binds: the owner check, #11225's check that a registered delegate has a binding handle, `check_session_memory_pin`, and `DelegateTool::check_principal_scope`. Then come the native rebind, the route pin, the delegate bind, and the memory swap. Only the rebind can still refuse at that point, and it comes first.
- **Follow-up, not in this PR.** When a registry has no route, the refusal in `check_session_memory_pin` recognises `spawn_subagent`, `execute_pipeline`, `sop_execute`, `sop_advance` and `sop_approve` by their wire names, among the tools the runtime built. A skill wrapper that exposes one of them under another name would pass the check in a hand-built registry passed to the public `assemble`, and so would `sop_status` and `sop_list`. Every production registry comes from the factory and carries a route, so this is hardening for the prebuilt-registry API. #11411's b28be2268c, with the refusal change in c52a1afc7e, covers it. It needs #11225's `builtin_target_name` and the `sop_list` route, so it lands with the SOP-read follow-up rather than here.
- **Why a route rather than the rebind.** The subagent child builds its own memory, which the registry rebind cannot reach; a shared route pinned with the session does, and so does a skill wrapper that captured the tool before policy filtering. Since #11174 the rebind does reach the pipeline's captured native memory tools, so the pipeline's use of the route doesn't change what a memory step runs (see the review thread).
- **#11174.** #11174 landed as 6ac37f60f1, and this refresh merges it. `route_memory_to_principal` keeps #11174's property that a refused rebind leaves the Agent unchanged, and the route stays unpinned too: check that the pin can be taken, rebind, pin, then swap `self.memory`.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(cli): verify the named-pipe server before sending authorization edits on Windows
prs.body:
> Stacked on #11313. Review the two Windows commits, `4e396196` and `8cea3685`, on top of the merged parent base; the later merge commit `983f1609` only brings `master` in and resolves a conflict in `.github/workflows/README.md`. This branch needs rebasing onto `master` after #11313 lands.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - **The gap.** #11313 commits an authorization edit (`[users]`, `[permission_profiles]`, `[oidc]`, `security.trust_daemon_uid`) through the running daemon after checking the Unix socket's peer. A Windows named pipe carries no peer uid and its name is predictable, so on Windows the CLI never sent: it saved `config.toml` and reported `pending_reload` with reason `unverified_endpoint`, and the edit applied only at the next reload. The non-Unix liveness probe also treated any non-zero pid as alive, so a heartbeat left by a daemon that stopped less than 15 s ago still counted as a running daemon.
  - **Verify the pipe's server (new `zeroclaw_config::platform::pipe_server`).** Before anything is written, the CLI asks the kernel which process created the pipe's server end (`GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` on the client handle) and requires it to be the pid the configuration's heartbeat names. It then reads that process's token user (`OpenProcess` + `OpenProcessToken` + `GetTokenInformation(TokenUser)`) and requires this account or SYSTEM. The token *user*, not the token *owner*: an elevated token's owner defaults to the Administrators group. SIDs are compared by bytes; `EqualSid` is bound as `Result<()>` in `windows` 0.61 and sets no error on a plain mismatch.
  - **Fail closed.** A check that errors keeps `unverified_endpoint`, now carrying the check that failed. A pid or account mismatch is `other_daemon`, with nothing written. A missing pipe is `unreachable` after the same 3 s reconnect window as Unix.
  - **Real liveness.** `process_is_alive` on Windows reuses the existing `control_plane::authority::pid_is_definitely_absent` (`OpenProcess` + `WaitForSingleObject(0)`, already required-CI-tested). Not `GetExitCodeProcess`: a process that exited with code 259 is indistinguishable from `STILL_ACTIVE`. A probe that fails counts the daemon as running, so the worst case is a 3 s wait and a pending `unreachable` notice, never a silent local save while the daemon enforces the old policy.
  - **One client, two peers.** `src/daemon_rpc.rs` keeps one `exchange`; the Unix and Windows modules each supply `call()` and what they established about the peer. The Unix behaviour and messages are unchanged (code relocated, tests preserved). The Windows decision (`pipe::verify_server`) is a portable function, so its pid, account and error branches are unit-tested on Linux required CI.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - **Pipe ACL and daemon-side authentication unchanged.** With a `[users]` roster, a token-less pipe client is still refused at the handshake, so the CLI takes the pending `refused` path there; the docs now say so.
  - **Not covered:** `call_local` (agent-targeting mutations) and zerocode's pipe client, tracked by #11324.
  - **Overlap with #11393.** That draft protects the extracted rpc-client's credential-bearing dials with a same-user server check plus pipe-owner and access-list checks; this PR protects the CLI's authorization edits with a heartbeat-pid check plus this-user-or-SYSTEM. Different callers and trust policies. The portable decision function here (`daemon_rpc::pipe::verify_server`) and the Win32 queries in `zeroclaw_config::platform::pipe_server` are reusable by the shared client when it lands.
  - **Merge fixups a stacked branch needs:** one `match` arm in #11313's `rpc/auth.rs` tests for `PropKind::SecretMap`, which `master` added after #11313's base, and one `Cargo.lock` entry cargo re-normalized after the merge. Both disappear on rebase.
- **Blast radius:**
  - Windows CLI only: `config set` / `config patch` now open the pipe whenever a fresh heartbeat names a live pid, and write nothing until the kernel-reported server pid equals the heartbeat pid and the server's token user is this user or SYSTEM. tokio's `ClientOptions` opens with `SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION`, so a rogue server cannot impersonate the CLI.
  - The Win32 queries live in `zeroclaw-config`'s `platform` module, beside the crate's existing Win32 token code, because `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` admits no new functionality to the holding crate without a recorded exception. `zeroclaw-config` gains the `Win32_System_Pipes` feature of its existing `windows` dependency (and `net` on its dev-only tokio, for the in-process pipe test). `zeroclaw-runtime` only makes two existing functions `pub`: `rpc::local::connect_client` and `control_plane::authority::pid_is_definitely_absent`. No new dependency anywhere.
  - CI: the required `windows-task-owner-recovery` job gains two exact-name `zeroclaw-config` tests; `scripts/ci/windows_test_scope.py` selects it for `platform/pipe_server.rs` changes.
  - Restacks: #11265 edits `src/daemon_rpc.rs`, `src/config_publication.rs` and `src/main.rs` (the `exchange` move is a block relocation; the Windows component tests are a new file, so the Unix one stays byte-identical); #11346 renames the pipe (verification does not depend on the name).
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11325. Depends on #11313. Related #10876, #11324.

### What this does, simply

On Linux and macOS, `zeroclaw config set` can hand a change to users, permission profiles or OIDC settings straight to the running daemon, which applies it immediately. On Windows the same command had to play safe: it could not tell whether the thing answering on the daemon's named pipe was really the daemon, so it only saved the file and told you the change would apply after the next reload.

Now it can tell. Windows will say which process created the pipe and whose account that process runs under. The command checks both against the daemon's own heartbeat file before it sends anything. If they match, the change is applied live, as on Linux. If they don't, or if Windows refuses to answer, nothing is sent and you get the same "pending reload" notice as before, with the reason. A daemon that has just stopped is also recognised as stopped, instead of being chased for its last heartbeat.

This changes nothing on Linux or macOS, and nothing about how the daemon itself decides who may connect.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, on Windows.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw config set` / `config patch`) against the daemon's local RPC pipe.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A config dir with no `[users]` roster, e.g. only `schema_version`, `[gateway] host = "127.0.0.1" port = 18799 require_pairing = false` and `[permission_profiles.reader] grants = { sessions = ["read"], config = ["read"] }`; `ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR` pointing at it in each shell.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. `zeroclaw daemon --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18799`
  2. In a second shell: `zeroclaw config set --no-interactive security.trust_daemon_uid false --json`
  3. Stop the daemon with Ctrl+C and, within 15 s, run step 2 again.
- **Expected on this branch (after):**
  - Step 2 prints `{"path":"security.trust_daemon_uid","value":"false","daemon":{"applied":true}}`.
  - Step 3 prints only `path` and `value`, with nothing on stderr.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `master` has no daemon path for these edits at all; on #11313 alone, step 2 reports `"daemon":{"applied":false,"pending_reload":true,"reason":"unverified_endpoint"}` and step 3 reports the same instead of recognising the stopped daemon.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:**
  - The Linux `test` job runs the portable decision tests (`daemon_rpc::pipe::tests`), the relocated `exchange` tests and the un-gated `config_publication` tests; `Lint` compiles the Unix test modules under `-D warnings`.
  - The required `windows-task-owner-recovery` job now runs `platform::pipe_server::tests::the_server_of_a_pipe_this_process_serves_is_this_process` and `platform::pipe_server::tests::this_process_runs_as_this_user` (in `zeroclaw-config`) by name, next to the existing liveness test.
  - `Check x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` compiles the root crate's Windows client.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The root crate's Windows unit tests (`daemon_rpc::windows::tests`, the Windows `config_publication` tests) and the new component module run only in the advisory `windows-tests.yml`; please apply `ci:windows`. Required CI lints only on Linux, so the Windows code was linted locally (below).
- **Commands run and tail output:** Windows 11 Pro 26200, Rust 1.98.0, `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, at `8cea3685`:

  ```text
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  (no output)
  $ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw --no-deps --bin zeroclaw --tests --locked -- -D warnings
      Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 15s
  $ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config --no-deps --lib --tests --locked   # no -D: pre-existing Windows-only findings
  (findings only in platform/docker.rs:32, platform/native.rs:293 and secrets/windows_key_file.rs:65; none in platform/pipe_server.rs)
  $ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --no-deps --lib --tests --locked  # no -D: pre-existing Windows-only findings
  (clippy findings only in agent/turn/vision_route.rs:920, rpc/auth.rs:378 and service/mod.rs:51/1175/1231/1241, plus rustc dead-field warnings from zeroclaw-config; none in rpc/local.rs or control_plane/authority.rs)
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib --locked -- platform::pipe_server
  test platform::pipe_server::tests::this_process_runs_as_this_user ... ok
  test platform::pipe_server::tests::the_server_of_a_pipe_this_process_serves_is_this_process ... ok
  test platform::pipe_server::tests::a_child_process_runs_as_this_user ... ok
  test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1750 filtered out; finished in 0.01s
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --locked -- control_plane::authority::tests
  test control_plane::authority::tests::pid_zero_is_definitely_absent ... ok
  test control_plane::authority::tests::windows_process_exit_is_detected ... ok
  test result: ok. 13 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5597 filtered out; finished in 0.04s
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw --locked -- daemon_rpc config_publication config_patch_reports_a_daemon_verdict
  test result: ok. 41 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 498 filtered out; finished in 3.20s
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw --test component --locked -- config_auth_publication_cli_windows
  test component::config_auth_publication_cli_windows::config_patch_creating_a_roster_is_applied_live_and_closes_the_shared_operator_path ... ok
  test component::config_auth_publication_cli_windows::config_set_with_no_roster_is_applied_and_the_daemon_writes_the_comment ... ok
  test component::config_auth_publication_cli_windows::config_set_with_a_roster_is_refused_at_the_handshake_and_pending ... ok
  test component::config_auth_publication_cli_windows::config_set_refuses_to_publish_through_another_daemon ... ok
  test component::config_auth_publication_cli_windows::config_set_is_sent_nothing_when_another_process_serves_the_pipe ... ok
  test component::config_auth_publication_cli_windows::config_set_contacts_no_endpoint_without_a_running_daemon ... ok
  test component::config_auth_publication_cli_windows::config_set_after_the_daemon_stopped_finds_no_daemon ... ok
  test result: ok. 7 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 259 filtered out; finished in 2.67s
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** A real `zeroclaw daemon` (debug build) on a config dir with no roster, using the default derived pipe name, driven from PowerShell with `ZEROCLAW_CONFIG_DIR` set and no other `ZEROCLAW_*` variable:

  | Step | Command | Observed |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | `zeroclaw config set --no-interactive security.trust_daemon_uid false --json` | `{"daemon":{"applied":true},"path":"security.trust_daemon_uid","value":"false"}`; the daemon wrote `config.toml` |
  | 2 | `config patch --json -` adding `/users/bob/uid` and `/users/bob/permission_profiles` | `"daemon":{"applied":true}`, `"saved":true`, two results |
  | 3 | step 1 again, now with a roster | `"daemon":{"applied":false,"pending_reload":true,"reason":"refused"}`: the roster is enforced with no reload. Human mode: `Saved to config.toml, but the running daemon still enforces the previous authorization policy: the daemon refused this caller (A local user roster is configured: connect from a mapped uid or present auth_token in initialize). It applies at the next daemon reload or restart.` |
  | 4 | `ZEROCLAW_SOCKET=\\.\pipe\zc-squat`, a pipe a PowerShell process serves, then step 1 | `"reason":"other_daemon"` in 70 ms. Human mode: `… the daemon answering at the socket is not the one for this configuration (\\.\pipe\zc-squat: the kernel reports its server as pid 29588, but this configuration's daemon is pid 36664).` The squatter logged `connection 1 read returned 0` and `connection 2 read returned 0`: it was opened and sent nothing. |
  | 5 | `Stop-Process` the daemon; 4 s after its last heartbeat (which still named its pid) run step 1 | `{"path":"security.trust_daemon_uid","value":"false"}`: no `daemon` member, nothing on stderr; human mode prints only `security.trust_daemon_uid updated.` |

  Not verified: an elevated daemon with an unelevated CLI; a daemon running as a SYSTEM service (expected `unverified_endpoint` if its token cannot be read, which is the fail-closed path); macOS and Linux execution, which CI covers; the Unix component module, which is unchanged.

- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact plain-text output of `zeroclaw config set --json` and the CLI's stderr notices, as quoted above; no presentation-sensitive change. Locale `C`, output not terminal-width dependent.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `8cea3685`, `target\debug\zeroclaw.exe`, `cli` surface over the daemon's named pipe.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the exact outputs above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** the table above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:**
  - `scripts/ci/windows_test_scope.test.sh` and `windows_recovery_change_filter.test.sh` need Python, which this machine lacks; the required-jobs step runs both in CI.
  - `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` needs Python too; the same regexes were run over every changed Rust file with a Node port: 0 findings.
  - Workspace-wide `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` on Windows fails on pre-existing Windows-only lints in other crates; linting was per changed crate, with findings compared by file.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The CLI opens the daemon's pipe it already opened for other mutations, and queries the server process with `PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION` and `TOKEN_QUERY` only.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. An authorization edit, which may carry `oidc.<alias>.client_secret`, is now sent over a Windows named pipe, but only to a server process the kernel names as the heartbeat's pid and whose token user is this account or SYSTEM; any failed check sends nothing. Before, nothing was ever sent on Windows.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Residual risks: pid reuse inside the 15 s heartbeat window ends in `unreachable` or `other_daemon`, never a send to the wrong process of another account; two daemons of the same account are told apart by pid only, as on Unix; a SYSTEM service whose token a user cannot read stays `unverified_endpoint`.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. On Windows, edits that were reported pending now apply live when the checks pass; the pending reason codes are unchanged, and `unverified_endpoint` now carries a detail.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the squash commit. Windows returns to `unverified_endpoint` and the `pid != 0` liveness stub; Unix is untouched either way.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `zeroclaw config set --json` on Windows reporting `other_daemon` or `unverified_endpoint` while the daemon is the one serving the pipe; `pending_reload` notices on stderr naming the failed check; a stopped daemon's edits waiting out the 3 s reconnect window.
