prs.title: feat(plugins): support multiple plugin registry origins
prs.body: ## Summary - **Base branch:** master - **What changed and why:** - Accept a JSON array in ZEROCLAW_PLUGIN_REGISTRY_URL so private and public registries can be used together. - Preserve fetched-origin identity through search, caching and selection in install, update and Quickstart so same-name packages cannot silently switch publishers. This does not add durable origin metadata to installed packages. - Carry origin information into suggestions and the web catalog without exposing credential-bearing URLs in catalog responses or display labels. - **Scope boundary:** No changes to plugin execution permissions or package layout. Fork-only validation tooling is not included. - **Blast radius:** Registry/cache consumers, CLI/Quickstart, runtime suggestions, gateway API types and the web Plugins page. - **Linked issue(s):** Related #12109 ### What this does, simply Use multiple plugin registries without losing track of which publisher a package belongs to. Existing single-URL configuration still works. Custom lists replace the default registry rather than automatically adding it. Only one package per name can be installed. ## Testing (required) ### How you can test (when useful) - **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. - **Interface(s) exercised:** cli and web; Quickstart interaction remains unverified. - **Setup / preconditions:** Two reachable registry indexes containing a package named demo. Replace the example URLs below. Use the same fixtures on master and this branch. - **Steps to run:** ~~~sh ZEROCLAW_PLUGIN_REGISTRY_URL='["https://registry-a.example/registry.json","https://registry-b.example/registry.json"]' zeroclaw plugin search demo ~~~ - **Expected on this branch (after):** Results from both registries with distinct publisher labels. - **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The single-registry implementation does not support the JSON list or combined results. Manual A/B confirmation is still pending. ### How I tested - **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Previously recorded focused fork-hosted Linux checks cover registry behavior, compatibility and affected consumers. These are the existing results recorded for revision `645a9ae5fdba6ae9e6026d7d057dfbdfc49ac0d4`, not a fresh CI result for the current head: | Check | Result | |---|---| | [Shared registry](https://github.com/ggettert/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41557780235) | 10 passed | | [CLI](https://github.com/ggettert/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41564605521) | 16 passed | | [Runtime suggestions](https://github.com/ggettert/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41673545578) | 1 passed | | [Gateway catalog/compatibility](https://github.com/ggettert/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41676472684) | 6 unique tests passed; 7 executions (nonadditive) | | [Frontend helpers](https://github.com/ggettert/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41682990141) | 4 passed | | [Schema/typecheck](https://github.com/ggettert/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41683862525) | Export, contract guards and typecheck passed | - **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Current-head required CI is not established by the links above. Standard lint/docs gates, full workspace/default-feature test suites, Windows, MSRV and the full release/feature matrix remain outside the evidence here. The sandbox checks below add actual Linux release CLI/gateway and web coverage, but not Quickstart interaction. - **Commands run and tail output:** The linked historical logs contain the focused CI commands. Frontend output: ~~~sh node --experimental-strip-types --test-reporter=tap --test web/src/pages/pluginCatalog.test.ts ~~~ ~~~text # tests 4 # pass 4 # fail 0 # cancelled 0 # skipped 0 # todo 0 ~~~ The historical schema check ran `cargo run --locked -p xtask --bin web -- gen-api` and `npm run typecheck`, including the generated-file check and `tsc -b`. Three new DTOs passed presence checks in both generated contracts. For the current-head sandbox run, the actual CLI commands included `plugin install tool-fixture@0.0.0 --registry http://127.0.0.1:18281/b.json`, `plugin list --verify` and `plugin info tool-fixture`, using the release binary and an isolated `--config-dir`. Each exited 0; selected output lines: ~~~text Installed plugin tool-fixture v0.0.0 tool-fixture v0.0.0 — (no description) [loads] Loads: yes. The component instantiates against this host's WIT world. ~~~ - **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** On 2026-11-03, exercised the real CLI and paired dashboard/API in an isolated Linux sandbox (Rust 1.98, Node 24.22.2). The PR release CLI/gateway used default features plus `plugins-wasm-cranelift`; the dashboard used the separately built canonical web dist. No source changes were made during validation. - Legacy single-URL search and dashboard/API returned the two expected entries. Two registries returned four rows, including two same-name packages with distinct authoritative origin IDs; publisher-supplied spoof origin metadata was ignored. - Both unpinned and version-pinned duplicate installs rejected ambiguity and required `--registry`. Explicit selection of an origin rejected versions available only from the other origin; request logs showed only the selected index was fetched. - Malformed JSON and connection refusal failed without partial search results or cache publication. Cache bytes, inode and restrictive permissions survived failures; initial mode was `0600`, and a successful refresh preserved deliberately narrowed `0400`. Matching offline cache remained usable; a mismatched explicit source set excluded it. This is failure atomicity and separate offline reuse, not successful-search fallback. - Built the repository's harmless `tool-fixture@0.0.0` for `wasm32-wasip2` and installed it from registry B with normal archive/digest, manifest and host-load checks enabled. B-only index/package requests and matching installed component/manifest hashes proved the selected download. `list --verify` reported `[loads]`; `info` reported `Loads: yes`. Installed metadata does not retain an origin field; this is not a durable installed-origin or signature-authenticity claim. - **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot of the actual paired web Plugins page with all four registry rows and distinct origin IDs. Quickstart screenshots remain unprovided. - **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `342cf3c12683365ee3d1b7f68f9da6fdea86a88f`; actual cli, paired web Plugins page and authenticated catalog API. Current-head evidence is summarized above, with exact CLI output above; the captured dashboard screenshot will be attached separately. Earlier automated evidence is linked separately. - **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** CLI output above. The actual multi-registry dashboard screenshot has been captured; - **Action or changed state and observed result:** Switching the web catalog to Installed hid the uninstalled registry entries; All restored all four rows. The authenticated catalog stayed HTTP 200 with the same four rows after both failed refreshes; unauthenticated access returned 401. The later CLI installation succeeded and the host loaded the fixture; that installation was not a web install flow. - **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Tool invocation/execution was explicitly skipped; no supported safe direct non-provider invocation surface was established. Install/load is not execution. Interactive approval, provider/production integration, Quickstart interaction, an unpatched-master comparison, signature authenticity, timeout behavior and concurrent/crash cache stress were not tested. This was bounded sandbox validation, not a full test/lint or platform matrix. A Google Fonts request blocked by dashboard CSP was observed but did not affect catalog behavior; it was treated as nonblocking for this acceptance run and was not attributed to this PR without a baseline comparison. ## Security & Privacy Impact (required) - New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.** Existing cache location; more restrictive cache writes. - New external network calls? **Yes.** Up to eight configured HTTP(S) indexes, with bounded requests and no partial cache publication. - Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** Catalog responses/display labels use opaque origin IDs; cache writes are private. This is not blanket URL redaction for errors or executable commands. - PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** - Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Registry-backed suggestions retain the fetched origin rather than publisher-declared provenance. Registry metadata remains untrusted. - If any Yes, describe the risk and mitigation: Additional registries expand the publisher trust surface. Ambiguous installs and multi-origin updates require an explicit registry. Source validation and all-or-nothing cache publication prevent silently mixing incomplete results. ## Compatibility (required) - Backward compatible? **Yes**, for existing single-registry configuration and public Rust struct literals. - Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** The existing variable also accepts a JSON array. Ambiguous installs and multi-origin updates require `--registry `. - Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.** - If backward compatibility is No or either surface/floor question is Yes: exact upgrade steps for existing users: No change for single-registry users. To opt in, set ZEROCLAW_PLUGIN_REGISTRY_URL to a JSON array of one to eight HTTP(S) URLs. Include the public registry explicitly if wanted. ## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs) - **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert `. Restore a single registry URL and discard/regenerate the union cache at plugin-registry/registry.json before using the old reader. Installed packages are unchanged. - **Feature flags or config toggles:** No feature flag. A single URL or explicit `--registry ` selects one registry. - **Observable failure symptoms:** Missing catalog entries, unexpected origin-selection errors, cache-source mismatches or failed registry refreshes. ## Supersede Attribution (required only when Supersedes # is used) Not applicable; this PR does not supersede another PR.

prs.title: fix(runtime): withhold session-data tools from non-admin principals
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Depends on #11225 and #11234. This is the cumulative recut, including adopted containment and steering repairs; review its full owned delta, not only the latest test commit. The separately scoped SOP containment is #11220.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Withhold `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, and `sessions_send` from every non-admin RPC session, including wildcard selectors, because these tools do not enforce principal ownership. Keep `sessions_current`, which accepts no foreign target.
  - Withhold principal-unaware cron, schedule, peer-messaging and nested-executor paths, including captured skill aliases. Retained delegates carry the narrowing into bounded, parallel and independent descendants; an Agent without the concrete delegate handle drops that entry. The canonical delegate remains available only when its selectors and retained handle permit it.
  - Apply one complete tool posture to prompt admission and steering. Steering resolves authority when consumed and again after memory writes, so the next accepted steering applies current withholding. This does not add continuous revocation between every action. Narrowing is monotonic: a later grant does not restore withdrawn tools to that live Agent.
  - Authorize cron patches against the actual stored row after acquiring its SQLite write transaction, and retain current authority through the synchronous commit. A queued demotion, revoked grant, changed owner or changed job type cannot reuse an earlier decision.
  - Retain #11234's session-authority and error-handling repairs: immediate approval-channel refusal propagates, deferred installation logs a sanitized refusal, and a Chat running-state write failure preserves the session for retry while ACP checkpoint failure retains its recovery behavior. The latest commit serializes the deferred test's process-wide log capture using the existing writer-then-hook locks.
- **Source of truth:** current grants come from the existing authorization authority. The posture is derived at each applicable boundary; registry removal and shared delegate withholding are narrowing effects, not a second live grant policy.
- **Scope boundary:** this contains principal-unaware tools; it does not make their stores principal-aware, add shared-execution credential renewal, or propagate principal ceilings into SOP runs. #11220 owns the SOP entry/workshop containment. Scheduled work, channels, CLI turns and existing independent triggers are not converted into principal-owned execution by this PR. The #11225 routing integration and full current-parent integration remain separate gates.
- **Blast radius:** RPC Chat/ACP construction, prompts and steering, aliases and delegate descendants, cron patch commits, and the inherited session-authority/storage boundary. Non-admin sessions lose the listed tools even with wildcard selectors.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11127; its containment closure also requires #11220 to land. Depends on #11225. Depends on #11234. Related #11220, #11410, #12046, #8290 and #12131.

### What this does, simply

Two people can use the same agent without owning each other's conversations. Until the cross-session tools check that ownership themselves, non-admin sessions cannot use them or regain them through the named contained cron, peer-message or nested-executor entry points exposed by that session. SOP entry and workshop containment remains in #11220. The same restrictions apply when a former administrator steers an existing turn after demotion. Ordinary tools and the current-session tool remain available when the caller's grants allow them.

The headless tool set withheld here is `cron_add`, `cron_update`, `cron_run`, `cron_list`, `cron_runs`, `cron_remove`, `schedule` and `send_message_to_peer`. The session tools, `spawn_subagent`, `execute_pipeline`, and aliases of the withheld tools or `delegate` are also removed. These restrictions are interim containment, not a claim that the OIDC isolation milestone is complete.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A for an additional manual setup: dispatcher tests drive real session/store boundaries with synthetic principals, controlled demotion and competing writes. Live provider acceptance remains a separate milestone gate.

### How I tested

- **Current repair revision:** `0efa2558924e60fc3397720ffdf4f12e4459ec0a`. This retains the additive four-line log-test fix `9684cf3b5008fb64a17a2b3fc71650f4578f279d` and merges master `f87368a6aa53d16b0bd7411b002331a22622c2a7`, including #12129. - **Exact-revision local results:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passed. `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- rpc::dispatch:: agent::turn::provider_call:: steering principal_scope principal_memory withhold --test-threads=8` passed all 642 selected tests with no failures or ignored tests. `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed. These ran on macOS with jobs=2, incremental=0, debug=0 and an isolated Cargo target.
- **Validation retry:** the initial attempt reused another worktree's Cargo target and failed to see PR-specific trait methods already present in this source. The unchanged head passed after rebuilding in its own target directory; no source suppression or test bypass was added.
- **Current hosted evidence:** new-head checks remain required. The merge and test repair were independently checked. The unchanged dependency files adopt #12129's [successful Security and plugin matrix](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41119606972); those feature suites were not repeated locally.
- **Historical hosted evidence on the preceding PR head:** d69f99d77c6f0b659d1714b44b90de1601107158 passes [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41096212634/job/124202534955), [Parallel Runtime Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41096212634/job/124202737438), [Lint](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41096212634/job/124202534799) and [Docs Style](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41096212634/job/124202723889). Test reports 19,572 passed and 42 skipped in its main group. The source-confirmed shared-log race was not an observed failure in this run.
- **Earlier failed gate:** [Security](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41096212634/job/124202534613) and the [aggregate gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41096212634/job/124212229592) fail on the inherited Wasmtime 48.0.7 advisories, RUSTSEC-2026-0420 through 0424. #12129 has merged the dependency repair; it was not integrated into this preceding head. These failures are not waived.
- **Boundary evidence:** hosted tests cover same-agent foreign-history/append refusal; wildcard and named selectors; canonical and aliased headless tools; descendant withholding; cron transaction contention; prompt admission after waits; and steering demotion both before consumption and during a memory write. Positive controls retain the caller's own session, allowed ordinary tools and unchanged administrator behavior.
- **Steering repair provenance:** dfe06dcf76b20533e622ba7a74b5b02b70335f65 is in the branch. [Its adoption check](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11230#pullrequestreview-5706814602) links the exact earlier hosted steering regressions. The [session-error update](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11230#issuecomment-6528701580) records four passing focused tests, formatting and runtime all-target Clippy on d69f99d77c6f0b659d1714b44b90de1601107158.
- **Beyond CI:** the earlier repair reports include negative controls; they are historical evidence on their named revisions, not new executions on this test-only commit.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: authorization/tool availability and error propagation are proved at dispatcher/store boundaries; this PR introduces no presentation-sensitive interface change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** the linked hosted run covers d69f99d77c6f0b659d1714b44b90de1601107158. Current integrated-head local results are recorded above; historical hosted results are not attributed to it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The owned containment narrows tools and rechecks existing authority.
- New external network calls? No. The inherited #11225 slice places principal-scoped private recall in the existing provider context and restores private autosave; this containment slice adds no new payload type.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No in this slice; the existing authority supplies current decisions.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No; fixtures use synthetic roster identities.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes in inherited #11225: private recall reaches provider context under the existing provenance and owner/tenant/namespace/agent filters. This containment slice narrows the tool registry and adds no new text source.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: recalled memory remains untrusted context and must retain its ownership and provenance filtering. The containment risk is an omitted tool or a missed revocation boundary; foreign-data refusal, mutation preservation and allowed controls cover the specified paths. Related execution and storage work remains explicitly separate.

- Backward compatible? No. Non-admin RPC sessions, including wildcard accounts, lose the tools named above and their aliases. Single-operator and currently authorized administrator sessions retain their ordinary allowed tools. Principal-aware replacements and shared-execution renewal remain follow-up work; granting administrator access is a broad authority change, not an equivalent scoped replacement.

- **Fast rollback command/path:** after landing, `git revert <landed-PR-squash-commit>`, reconciling dependent PRs. There is no persisted migration in the owned containment slice. - **Feature flags or config toggles:** no new toggle. Existing agent tool policy can retain restrictions during rollback.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** non-admin `Unknown tool` responses for withheld capabilities are expected. A foreign transcript read/append, a queued cron mutation after revoked authority, or missing ordinary tools for an unchanged permitted control is a regression.

## Supersede Attribution

This is not a replacement PR. Adopted repairs from @Aarlington and @JordanTheJet retain their commit authorship and the prerequisite history. No contributor branch or published history was rewritten.

prs.title: fix(security): require administrator authority for SOP execution
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Require current administrator authority for `sops/run` and every `sops/decide` decision, including when a non-admin has wildcard selectors and `tools:execute`. SOP steps and their descendants do not carry a scoped caller's principal limits.
  - Retain that authority through synchronous start/approval storage effects after decision-model and engine waits; a contended store refuses immediately rather than holding authority while waiting for a writer.
  - Withhold `sop_execute`, `sop_approve`, `sop_advance`, `sop_workshop`, and their skill aliases from non-admin RPC sessions. Also withhold `spawn_subagent`, `execute_pipeline`, and delegate aliases that cannot carry the restriction.
  - Keep direct delegation for callers with unrestricted selectors, binding bounded, independent, background, parallel, and nested child builders to the originating credential's live authority resolver. The canonical policy remains `RpcInboundAuth`; no copied grant decision authorizes a child registry.
- **Scope boundary:** Cross-credential steering and combined permission checks with credential renewal remain separate work under RFC #12131, pending repository disposition; this branch does not implement them. This is interim containment, not principal propagation inside SOP steps; RPC SOP authoring and non-RPC triggers retain their existing policies. The cumulative diff includes the session-authority prerequisite from #11234 and current master; unrelated session-data and cron repairs from the supplemental drafts are not imported.
- **Blast radius:** Non-admin SOP execution, approval, workshop use, and unsafe nested tool exposure; administrators and the shared operator retain configured access, and ordinary admitted tools remain usable.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11123. Depends on #11234. Related #11408, #11410, #11230, and #11169.

### What this does, simply

A user could reach a procedure through a tool alias or an allowed agent and then run work outside that user's permissions. Until procedures can carry those permissions into every step, only administrators may start or decide them, and non-admin sessions do not receive tools that bypass that restriction.

```text
RPC run / decision ── current admin authority ── guarded storage effect
                         │ no
                         └───────────────────── FORBIDDEN

non-admin session ── ordinary tools / controlled delegate
                         └─ child registry rechecks live authority
                            └─ SOP entry tools and unsafe builders absent
```

The [earlier review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11220#pullrequestreview-5364022889) identifies the tool-entry and descendant gaps; this carries the SOP-specific repairs from [#11408](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11408) and workshop regressions from [#11410](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11410), retaining their authorship and adapting their delegate propagation pattern to live resolution.

### Landing and shared-helper reconciliation

Land #11234 before this PR; the supplemental drafts must drop the SOP changes carried here when they refresh. #11169 must rebase onto this admission contract: one `SopAdmissionCheck` returns a held `SopEffectGuard`, and execution must keep the administrator predicate and nonblocking storage boundary rather than restoring its older wildcard predicate or a check returning `()`.

An integration probe against #11169 at `908a035d3f6b3734fcdf471785def4f6c3a1ad00` reports conflicts in `rpc/dispatch.rs`, `sop/dispatch.rs`, `sop/executor.rs`, and `sop/mod.rs`; its new ingress/cancel methods and authenticated approver changes still require that rebase and combined validation before landing.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes: compare the same scenarios with the previous head `ec5fc1c28760c63c9da9ea4d74e18379c146a2a8`.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Local authenticated JSON-RPC and Chat/ACP tool dispatch used by CLI/TUI clients; model providers in the regressions are synthetic.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A non-admin roster principal with `sops:execute`, `tools:execute`, wildcard selectors, and an approval-gated procedure; retain an administrator control.
- **Steps to run:** Request `sops/run` and an approval/denial through `sops/decide`; ask the session to invoke the direct SOP tools and a built-in skill alias, then repeat as administrator. The `sop_principal` tests also exercise a queued admin demotion and workshop persistence.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Non-admin RPC effects return `FORBIDDEN`; withheld tool calls return `Unknown tool` and leave runs/proposals unchanged; administrator controls and ordinary tools succeed.
- **Prior behavior (before):** Wildcard non-admins could pass the RPC guard, and model-facing SOP tools could enter procedures without the caller's principal ceiling.

### How I tested

#### Current revision: 0ddaef7c1a65aa9a934c03bbfbcef52591a4b65d

The latest change brings the existing writer-then-hook locks from #11234 into the copied deferred-approval log-capture test, keeping both guards through its asynchronous waits. It then additively merges master `f87368a6aa53d16b0bd7411b002331a22622c2a7`, including #12129. The owned production code is unchanged by this update; both dependency files exactly match master.

On this exact revision, all five selected tests passed together with `--test-threads=8`: deferred approval recheck, immediate approval refusal, provider payload capture, Chat state-write retry, and ACP checkpoint failure. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed. The test command was `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- deferred_approval_install_rechecks_after_agent_wait immediate_approval_install_refusal_fails_session_resume llm_request_payload_redacts_truncates_and_off_omits chat_running_state_write_failure_preserves_session_for_retry checkpoint_start_failure_notifies_once_and_releases_session --test-threads=8`.

The four-line repair and master integration were independently checked. New-head hosted checks remain required; the previous Wasmtime failure is addressed by the now-merged #12129 dependency files. The plugin feature matrix was not rerun locally; [#12129's successful run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41119606972) is inherited dependency evidence. The full local workspace and live two-provider acceptance were not rerun. Shared-execution authority/renewal is the separate RFC #12131, pending repository disposition; #11169 integration remains a prerequisite.

#### Earlier integration: f09b08f749cba368959ae05cbbdf8a264b3f033f

This head incorporates the #11234 session-error repair and an additive merge of master at 1c1cd118ac536a1dd1bc79b9cce69cbdc04e4f29. Immediate approval-channel installation errors now fail the request; deferred installation remains nonblocking and logs a sanitized refusal. A Chat state-write failure preserves the live session for retry, while ACP checkpoint failure retains its recovery eviction. The Fluent merge preserves all SOP and turn-recovery entries.

Historical local validation on that exact combined revision:

```sh
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- sop immediate_approval_install_refusal_fails_session_resume deferred_approval_install_rechecks_after_agent_wait chat_running_state_write_failure_preserves_session_for_retry checkpoint_start_failure_notifies_once_and_releases_session
# 853 passed; 0 failed; 1 existing live-model test ignored.
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
# Both passed.
```

[Hosted CI for that earlier head](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41097867322) provides the remaining platform/workspace matrix. Security reports five inherited Wasmtime 48.0.7 advisories (RUSTSEC-2026-0420 through 0424); the merged lockfile is identical to the pinned master. The hosted run is complete: Security and its aggregate required gate failed; the other required checks passed or were skipped as configured. A later metadata-only advisory risk-report job was cancelled; it is not source-validation evidence. The repair and merge were independently checked, but this is not whole-stack approval or resolution of the steering design and #11169 integration.

#### Earlier local validation: 137ae093935d1d216d0c62d6f53d22dea48a2cf2

The following results are preserved for this earlier revision, not attributed to the current head.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The historical local run below preceded hosted CI; current-revision evidence is listed above.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local validation is macOS with Rust/Cargo 1.97.1; cross-platform and full-workspace coverage remain with CI.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
  exit 0
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
  Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo]
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- rpc:: sop:: tools::sop_ tools::delegate:: live_config_authority::
  1883 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib live::
  8 passed; 0 failed
BASE_SHA=4d0d22b9771064827eaa25f2a2d2b56a860fd499 DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/security/authentication.md bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  Summary: 0 error(s)
BASE_SHA=4d0d22b9771064827eaa25f2a2d2b56a860fd499 DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/security/authentication.md bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  6 tests OK; no added links
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Reviewed the registry/factory wiring and the #11169 merge probe; automated controls exercise real run/proposal persistence, SQLite writer contention, queued demotion, credential expiry/revocation, aliases, and all supported delegate construction paths. No external identity-provider or interactive TUI smoke test was performed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no layout or rendering change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `137ae093935d1d216d0c62d6f53d22dea48a2cf2`, local JSON-RPC/tool regressions; local logs in `tmp/oidc-11220-validation/` in the implementation worktree.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Runtime assertions verify `FORBIDDEN` or `Unknown tool: <name>` and unchanged durable/in-memory SOP state, with successful administrator controls.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** A queued principal demotion prevents SOP/workshop effects; a queued config writer cannot deadlock a nested read; busy SQLite refuses before start/resume mutation.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full-workspace/all-feature tests were not duplicated locally; the selected suites cover the changed boundaries. The existing two ignored runtime cases remain ignored.

The runtime test linker emits the pre-existing macOS `__eh_frame section too large (max 16MB)` warning; the same diagnostic was reproduced on clean master `ceb1e11176b7ee86ca3007cb7f6110ae94ff6ecb` during prerequisite validation, and both builds completed successfully.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**; this restricts existing access.
- New external network calls? **No**.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes**; delegate builders retain the originating connection's non-secret authentication evidence in a live resolver, so current revocation/expiry and grants are checked rather than a stored admission decision; no bearer is retained.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**; fixtures are synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**; unsafe tool capabilities are removed from the executable registry and its advertised surface.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: A descendant must not inherit another later caller's authority; each child retains its originating resolver while current policy remains canonical in the auth layer.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No**; non-admin wildcard SOP access is intentionally removed, including deny/amend/revise, and unsafe nested builders/aliases are withheld.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No** new setting, flag, or wire method; existing methods have stricter authorization and localized refusal text.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**.
- Exact upgrade steps: Use a trusted administrator/shared operator for SOP execution and decisions; adding `tools:execute` alone no longer restores access. Parent session tools narrow at the next prompt admission; recreate a session after promotion to regain removed tools, and retry busy-store requests once contention clears.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's eventual merge/squash commit while retaining the #11234 prerequisite; no data migration is required, but reverting restores the unsafe non-admin paths.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None; the restriction is deliberate and fails closed.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `FORBIDDEN` on SOP run/decision, `Unknown tool` for withheld names, localized SOP storage-busy refusals, and matching RPC authorization-denied records.

prs.title: fix(runtime): keep parent prompts out of nested turn loops
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Agent turns keep their prompt variants in the `TOOL_PROTOCOL_PROMPTS` task-local. Task-locals follow awaits, so a foreground delegate's child loop inherited the caller's variants and refreshed its own system prompt from them on every provider request.
  - With a non-zero `max_system_prompt_chars` and native tools, this replaced the child's whole prompt with the caller's. An `independent` target therefore answered as the caller, which contradicts the "runs under its own identity" contract in `docs/book/src/agents/delegation.md`.
  - In text-tool mode, the caller's `## Tools` section replaced the child's, even with no cap. The model was told about tools the child does not have.
  - The task-local is now optional and is cleared around tool execution (`execute_one_tool_with_provenance`), so every tool that runs its own loop is covered in one place. Cross-agent SOP steps run a nested loop directly and clear it at that site. Same-agent SOP steps share the turn's prompt and keep it.
- **Scope boundary:** This does not change how any prompt is composed, the capping logic, the tool registries, or policy enforcement. Channel loops and `run_inner` never set this scope and are unchanged. `delegation.md` is unchanged because it already states the intended behavior.
- **Blast radius:** Turns started through `Agent::turn`, `turn_streamed`, and `turn_streamed_with_steering_state` (ZeroCode RPC, ACP server, gateway HTTP and WebSocket, eval). Their nested children now take the prompt cap from their own config and select the tool protocol the way unscoped loops do. `spawn_subagent` children also stop inheriting the scope. The parent's own requests are unaffected because the clear only applies inside the tool or child future.
- **Linked issue(s):** None. I did not find an existing tracking issue.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw lets one agent hand work to another, and an `independent` target is supposed to act as itself: its own persona, tools, and policy. Enforcement already worked that way, but the model could still receive the caller's instructions. A target asked for its name could answer with the caller's name, and read the caller's security summary, while its tools and shell policy correctly stayed its own.

The cause is a piece of per-turn state meant only for the agent that created it, which nested work picked up by accident. This PR hides that state from anything running as a tool and from SOP steps that belong to another agent, so a child keeps the prompt built for it. It does not grant or remove any permission, because enforcement was never affected.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface`: `tui` (ZeroCode). `web` reaches the same Agent turn path. No `channel`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Two agents on a provider with native tool calling. The caller's runtime profile sets a non-zero `max_system_prompt_chars`, and its risk profile sets `delegation_policy` mode `allow`. The target's runtime profile sets `agentic = true`, and its workspace `IDENTITY.md` defines a distinct name.

  ```toml
  [agents.caller]
  delegates = [{ agent = "target", mode = "independent" }]
  ```

- **Steps to run:** From a ZeroCode session on `caller`, have it run `delegate(agent="target", prompt="State your name exactly as your loaded identity defines it.")`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The target answers with the name from its own `IDENTITY.md`.

With the two clearing sites temporarily disabled, both tests fail, including the SOP case. Before the fix, a throwaway repro on the same base recorded which prompt reached the child:

| Cap 0 | Native | Yes | No | No |
| Cap 0 | Text | Yes | No | Yes |

  ```sh
  test result: ok. 6044 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 34.33s

  $ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets --no-deps

  crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/dispatch.rs:44728:18

  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I built this branch locally and confirmed in ZeroCode that the reported bug is fixed. I did not exercise the gateway path manually. I also read the call paths and confirmed the scope is only set in Agent turns. Background and parallel delegates run in spawned tasks, which do not inherit task-locals, and I did not test them separately.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. The change affects model-visible prompts, not how any interface renders.

prs.title: feat(session): implement append-only session event history
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Replace separate transcript writers with a shared, append-only session history. Record accepted inputs, model attempts and reasoning, tool execution, approvals, failures, model changes, context compression, and child-agent activity so recovery can reconstruct what actually happened.
  - Separate typed contracts and replay (`zeroclaw-api`), storage and migration (`zeroclaw-infra`), execution and authorization (`zeroclaw-kernel`), and application wiring (`zeroclaw-session-host`). CLI, RPC, ACP, channels, gateway, Web, and ZeroCode consume the standard session model.
  - Use one canonical `session_id`, with protocol source recorded only as creation metadata. Add a rebuildable session index, persistent titles and workspace metadata, same-session branches, copied sessions with shared frozen history, child sessions, and disposable temporary sessions.
  - Support SQLite and JSONL, resumable migration from master's stores, source-file backups, backend switching, and interrupted-execution recovery. Keep message, reasoning, tool, and multimodal content typed through the internal pipeline; convert protocols at provider/channel boundaries and parse legacy attachment markers only during import.
  - Store the cost ledger in the selected backend, attributed to actual session IDs where available. Preserve reported input/output tokens, cache reads and cache creation separately, and pricing evidence. Historical provider references remain unchanged when configuration aliases are renamed or deleted.
- **Scope boundary:** Full attachment/blob lifecycle work remains under #9488. This does not add history-content credential filtering, new at-rest encryption, a tamper-detection hash chain, automatic replay of external effects, a dashboard redesign, or a complete runtime extraction. Existing config-reference, authorization, and ownership rules still apply to provider edits.
- **Blast radius:** Session creation, listing, history queries, persistence, resume and TTL handling; provider/tool dispatch and approvals; compression and delegation; CLI/RPC/ACP/channel/gateway adapters; Web/ZeroCode session consumers; cost persistence and legacy migration.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10526. Related #9600. Related #9487. Related #9488. These broader contracts and coordination issues are not automatically closed.

### Crate boundary changes

- **`zeroclaw-runtime → zeroclaw-kernel`:** The runtime calls the extracted session execution, recovery, authorization, approval, context-maintenance, and model-selection code through the kernel's ports. This dependency keeps those decisions in one owner instead of copying them into each entrance or back into the runtime holding crate. Kernel has no production dependency on runtime, providers, or channels, so this does not create a dependency cycle or move concrete model adapters into the kernel.
- **`zeroclaw-runtime → zeroclaw-session-host`:** The shared host wires the configured SQLite/JSONL backend, installation migration, repository, and kernel coordinator for all entrances. Retaining this dependency replaces the old direct ACP/transcript-store construction with one standard session implementation. Its runtime use is transitional: application composition already injects a session source, but daemon startup retains a native fallback and some lifecycle operations still open the repository directly. Those calls can later move behind narrow injected session-management ports; the boundary is not a new independent persistence owner or a claim that runtime extraction is complete. The runtime dependency ratchet also needs these new edges and their owners to be reconciled; adding manifest entries alone does not establish the architectural justification.

### What this does, simply

A transcript records messages, but does not reliably explain which model ran, what a tool did before an interruption, or which context survived compression. This PR records those observations as ordered events and rebuilds conversation views and working context from them.

With persistence enabled, reopening after a restart or TTL expiration restores the same logical session and its retained context. Recovery preserves partial execution and diagnostics; an unproven tool outcome stays unknown rather than being reported as successful or silently executed again. Historical permissions and approvals never grant current access.

SQLite and JSONL share the same logical format. Existing histories are imported into the configured backend and the old files are renamed as backups. ACP no longer owns a separate execution-history database. A session index provides discovery metadata; the event history remains authoritative. A copy gets a new session ID and references a frozen source prefix, while a fork creates a branch inside the same session. Temporary sessions are hidden and removed on close or cleanup after restart.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. Use separate disposable installations for `master` and this branch; migration changes the on-disk writer format.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli`; automated coverage also exercises RPC, ACP and messaging-channel boundaries.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Configure an agent named `fixture` with a working provider and a harmless permitted tool. Stop other writers. Repeat with `channels.session_backend` set to `sqlite` and `jsonl`.
- **Steps to run:** Run `zeroclaw agent -a fixture --session-state-file /tmp/session-events-review.json`, exchange messages and request a harmless tool action, exit, then reopen with the same command. Repeat against a disposable copy of an installation containing legacy session/ACP history. Inspect `<data-dir>/sessions/` and its backups after import.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The standard event store and installation manifest contain execution observations and retained context. Reopening retains the conversation; imported source files become backups. Reading history does not repeat the tool. Renaming a provider alias does not rewrite its old historical references; select an available model manually if an old reference no longer resolves.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Separate transcript stores retain conversation messages, but do not provide this common execution-event history, shared session index, or installation-wide cutover.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** No claim that required CI is fully green. The latest pushed revision is `2fac551de5`; its [CI run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41801200397) reports failures, including default-stack tests, the CLI cost fixtures, and the runtime dependency boundary check. These are not claimed as resolved on that pushed revision. Local evidence below covers the latest functional change and the subsequent master merge.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The full workspace/all-features, platform/MSRV, million-event performance, and VM power-loss matrices were not repeated locally for the latest revision. Runtime tests below used a 16 MiB test-thread stack; they do not prove the default-stack gateway issue is resolved. Search currently builds a disposable authorized FTS view per query; no persistent full-text-index performance claim is made.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Linux, Rust 1.99.0, locked dependencies. Provider-edit checks ran on `ad2c3060d0`'s source; the subsequent `2fac551de5` merge only added master's desktop release workflow, smoke script, documentation and architecture tests.

```sh
TMPDIR=/tmp RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo +1.99.0 test --locked \
  -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib provider_alias_ -- --test-threads=4
# gateway: test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed
# runtime: test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed

TMPDIR=/tmp RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo +1.99.0 test --locked \
  -p zeroclaw --test component provider_rename_cli -- --test-threads=1
# test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed

TMPDIR=/tmp cargo +1.99.0 test --locked \
  -p zeroclaw --test architecture desktop_release -- --test-threads=4
# test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed

TMPDIR=/tmp cargo +1.99.0 test --locked \
  -p zeroclaw --test architecture release_workflow -- --test-threads=4
# test result: ok. 26 passed; 0 failed

cargo +1.99.0 fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0
bash -n scripts/desktop/smoke-dashboard.sh scripts/desktop/prepare-kernel.sh
# exit 0
git diff --check
# exit 0

DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/architecture/session-events.md BASE_SHA=HEAD \
  scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
# Linting: 1 file(s); Summary: 0 error(s)
```

Earlier validation before the last provider-policy change included the config suite (1,958 unit tests plus 131 integration tests), gateway library suite (774 tests), CLI config suite (30 tests), and all-targets Clippy with warnings denied across API, infra, kernel, host, providers, runtime, channels, gateway and the root package. These are earlier evidence, not a fresh whole-PR run. Earlier session-specific suites covered migration/recovery, capture, authorization, compression, branches, copies and temporary cleanup.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Reviewed master's newly merged desktop packaging change against native daemon initialization; it required no storage adaptation. Automated SQLite/JSONL tests compare the original historical event prefix before and after provider configuration edits, verify manual model selection and reopening, and exercise CLI renames during native and incomplete migration states. Config-upgrade regressions preserve backend choice, persistence/TTL settings, history paths and the old config backup. No fresh Windows/macOS installer or VM power-loss smoke is claimed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot evidence remains outstanding for the Web/ZeroCode session-consumer changes. This PR does not redesign their layout, but no fresh final-interface capture is supplied.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `ad2c3060d0` for provider-edit behavior; `2fac551de5` for the merge and architecture checks. Test boundaries: `tests/component/config_patch_cli.rs`, `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/dispatch.rs`, `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_config.rs`, and `tests/architecture/{desktop_release,release_workflow}.rs`. Storage contract: `docs/book/src/architecture/session-events.md`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Automated output tails are included above. They cover storage/protocol behavior and do not replace final-interface evidence for Web/ZeroCode.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Native history no longer blocks provider alias edits; historical selections remain unchanged, manual selection persists, and configuration ownership checks still reject an unauthorized offline writer. The merged release workflow preserves the embedded dashboard dependency and smoke-test ordering.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Platform release builds and VM crash/power-loss tests require their respective environments. The actual packaged-desktop smoke was not run locally. The imported `apps/tauri/TESTING.md` has existing Markdown issues outside the changed lines; its full-file docs gate is not claimed as passing.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Adds session execution/query capabilities and durable files under the configured data directory. Current owner, policy, and reasoning-read authorization are checked at use; stored evidence cannot mint grants.
- New external network calls? **No.** Existing providers, tools and delivery transports remain responsible for network effects; reading/replaying events does not dispatch them.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No for configured credentials.** Existing credential encryption and provider error/log handling remain unchanged. History preserves observed content in plaintext, including credential-shaped text; it is neither filtered nor newly encrypted.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Tests use synthetic fixtures.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Context reconstruction now consumes event-backed content. Unknown provider fields remain evidence rather than instructions or authority, and replay cannot authorize tools or other effects.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: More execution detail, including reasoning and diagnostics, is retained. Authorized reads and explicit payload erasure protect the supported local access boundary; erasure does not certify removal from backups, snapshots or exports. Operators remain responsible for those copies.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No for old writers after storage cutover; master's supported stores are imported.** Migration targets the new format directly, without an intermediate per-session locator or a second ACP store. Unknown event types/codecs retain their raw type and fields while readers skip unsupported semantics.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** Reuses existing backend, persistence and TTL settings; CLI persistence, session IDs and downstream session consumers are wired to native storage. Protocol source is metadata, not part of session identity. Provider aliases may be renamed/deleted under existing configuration rules without rewriting history. No new storage-selection environment variable is required.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.** The declared Rust 1.96.0 floor is unchanged; local commands used 1.99.0.
- Exact upgrade steps for existing users: Stop old writers and take a consistent backup of config and the complete data directory, including SQLite WAL state where applicable. Select `sqlite` or `jsonl`, then start the new binary. Import resumes after interruption and publishes Ready only after successful import and source archival. Legacy session and ACP files are renamed as backups. Existing configuration schema upgrades retain their own backup. Do not run an old binary against the migrated installation. If an old provider reference becomes unresolved after a configuration edit, manually select an available model.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Before storage migration, revert the PR's changes or deploy the prior binary. After migration, stop all writers, preserve the new installation separately, restore the complete pre-upgrade config/data backup, then deploy the prior binary. Code rollback alone does not reverse the format cutover; preserve post-upgrade writes separately for recovery.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No switch restores legacy writers. `channels.session_backend` selects SQLite or JSONL; native backend switching is not a downgrade. Persistence-disabled channels retain their existing in-memory mode.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Session initialization or migration refuses an incomplete/conflicting import; capture failures stop execution; interrupted effects retain unknown outcomes and diagnostics. Inspect initialization/migration/capture errors and `sessions/session-format.json`. Do not delete the manifest or bypass writer fencing to force an older writer.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. This PR does not supersede another PR.

prs.title: fix(tools): per-agent ownership scoping for session tools and discord_search
prs.body:
## Summary

### What this does, simply

Each agent can only list, read, and write its own conversations, and only search the Discord archive rows its own Discord bots recorded. Which conversations are "its own" comes from trusted facts (who the runtime is, which channels the live config assigns to it, and what the storage layer recorded when the conversation was created), never from what the model asks for. Conversations recorded before this release had no owner stamp; the one agent that could have written them adopts them on the next message, and an install with several agents is told how to assign them instead of losing messages.

- **Base branch:** `master`; this head includes `master` through `3c18211b9f` (#11811).
- **What changed and why:**
  - Binds `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, `sessions_send`, and `discord_search` to trusted per-agent ownership. Ownership is checked inside the storage critical section of each read and write, so a check/use race cannot admit a foreign session, and Discord namespace predicates run inside SQLite before ranking and limits.
  - Routing a message to an agent is not permission to take over a transcript. The inbound path *claims* a session: an absent key is created, an explicitly or channel-owned key is admitted only for its owner, and a foreign key refuses the turn before any hydration or append.
  - Authority is resolved at effect time, not captured ahead of storage. `ChannelAuthority` and `NamespaceAuthority` are callbacks the backend invokes after acquiring its connection or mutation guard; the policy read guard is held through the read or commit, so a channel reassigned or an agent disabled during a wait stops being admitted on the same turn.
  - Transcripts written before ownership attribution existed (master stamped nothing on the channel path, so every existing channel conversation is one) are handled by the claim itself. The live policy reader hands the backend a `SessionClaimGrant`: the channels the agent owns plus `adopt_unattributed`, which is true only when the caller is the sole enabled agent (`Config::is_sole_enabled_agent`, the same rule the Discord archive already applied to legacy rows). A sole agent adopts such a transcript and continues the conversation with its history. With several enabled agents the claim refuses, nothing is read or written, and the refusal is logged as `session_owner_unattributed` with the enabled-agent count and the operator remedy. The adoption bit never widens an explicit agent or a channel the caller does not own.
  - Makes typed live config the single agent/channel ownership source. Disabled aliases grant nothing; ambiguous duplicate enabled owners fail closed. The alias view is a typed walk of the channel maps (`map_alias_entries()` from the `Configurable` derive), so resolving ownership never serializes config on a caller's stack.
  - Preserves trusted session attribution across SQLite and JSONL restart, migration, retention, purge, and empty-transcript cases. Startup hydration touches only channel-marked sessions, so gateway and RPC sessions keep their owners.
  - Enforces Discord alias/channel provenance on search and on every archive write; a row already claimed by another alias or channel is never moved.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change `sessions_current`, `send_via`, peer-group semantics, the knowledge graph, or dormant session-tool registration. It adds no CLI; the explicit adoption step for multi-agent installs is a documented manual edit until a migration command lands (see Compatibility and Merge order).
- **Blast radius:** Per-agent tool registration, channel routing/collection, both session backends and hygiene, Discord archive/search/mutation paths, SQLite memory mutations, the `Configurable` derive's generated surface, and affected Fluent tool descriptions.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #9646. Related #9647. Related #8290.

The authorization inputs remain trusted runtime/config identity plus persisted provenance. Model-supplied session IDs and Discord channel IDs are selectors, never grants. A single-agent install, legacy or not, stays deterministic: it owns everything it wrote before and after the upgrade. Duplicate enabled owners are configuration ambiguity and are rejected.

### Review history on this head

- @JordanTheJet's 2026-09-30 blockers (F1 foreign claim of a channel-owned legacy transcript, F3 disabled caller inheriting the legacy Discord archive, F5 grants resolved before storage admission) were fixed in `040046750`, `344b610be`, `a6557147a`, and `0119cfe64` (now `e593ce5b7a`, `27063a7749`, `ba0d69c848`, and `5677f53b3e` after the history rewrite below); @tidux confirmed each on 2026-10-01.
- @tidux's 2026-10-01 blocker (pre-upgrade transcripts without attribution permanently drop their next inbound message) is fixed by the legacy adoption described above, with upgrade regressions on both backends.
- @tidux's `try_read` contention warning no longer applies after the master merge: the live config is now a `LiveConfigHandle` whose publish path holds its write lock only for the pair install and never across storage, so the authority callbacks take a short blocking `read()` instead of dropping the turn when a writer is queued. There is no longer an "authority unavailable" path on the inbound claim.
- The `.gitignore` entry @tidux flagged has been removed from this branch's diff.
- History was force-pushed once on 2026-10-23 to replace the merge commit `a6744b2b56`, which was authored as Claude with an attribution trailer and a session URL (AGENTS.md working rule 9), with the tree-identical `679755cf88` under my identity. Every descendant was re-created with its tree, message, author, and dates unchanged and only its parent re-pointed, so every SHA from that merge on moved; `git diff 6f0fdccc3b d1d9d03d27` is empty. The reviewed head `0119cfe64f` is now `5677f53b3e`, and the three commits on top are `9cc1a14780` (drift-only master merge), `fbbac6880e` (the fix), and `d1d9d03d27` (`.gitignore` chore).

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes; the deterministic regressions exercise the security, retention, and upgrade boundaries without credentials.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` tool registration and `channel` persistence/search.
- **Setup / preconditions:** None for automated tests. A manual Discord A/B needs two neutral agents with distinct enabled, archive-enabled Discord aliases that both watch one channel. A manual upgrade check needs a `data/sessions` directory written by a pre-ownership release (any channel transcript without `agent_alias`).
- **Steps to run:** Run the session ownership, retention, and upgrade tests. For the upgrade path by hand: start a build of this branch with one enabled agent over an old sessions directory and send a message on an existing conversation (the reply uses the old history and `agent_alias` is now set); then enable a second agent and send a message on a different old conversation (no reply, one `session_owner_unattributed` error with the remedy, transcript unchanged). For Discord: let the first alias archive a message and a reaction from the shared channel, let the second alias observe the same two events, and run scoped `discord_search` as each agent.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Foreign sessions and Discord rows remain inaccessible; a sole enabled agent continues pre-upgrade conversations and adopts them; a multi-agent install refuses them with a logged remedy instead of silently dropping them; the owned Discord row stays in the first alias's namespace; archived JSONL sessions cannot reappear through metadata; ambiguous duplicate channel owners expose no scoped grant.

None of those runs covers the master merge or the legacy adoption on the current head. Those SHAs predate the 2026-10-23 history rewrite; their trees are unchanged under the new SHAs listed in Review history.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**; access is narrowed. The only widening is the legacy adoption, and it is available to exactly one principal: the single enabled agent of a single-agent install, for transcripts that agent is the only possible author of.
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**; the channel alias view no longer serializes any config section at all, so the transient copy it used to make of decrypted channel values is gone.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Static tool descriptions are model-visible Fluent strings. The ownership denial messages (`denial_message` in `crates/zeroclaw-tools/src/sessions.rs`) are `format!` literals, following master's existing tool-error convention; the earlier claim that Fluent owns them was wrong. Denials name the owning agent or channel, matching the shipped reset/delete tools. Authorization comes only from trusted runtime identity, live config, and persisted provenance, never model arguments. The new `session_owner_unattributed` log line and its remedy are operator-facing log text, not model-visible.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No**; vulnerable cross-agent access and ambiguous ownership are intentionally denied.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`:
  - Existing attributed SQLite and JSONL sessions need no action.
  - **Pre-upgrade channel transcripts (no `agent_alias`, no `channel_id`; every channel conversation master wrote):** in an install with exactly one enabled agent, nothing to do; the agent adopts each conversation on its next inbound message and continues with the history. In an install with several enabled agents, those conversations are refused until attributed, and each refused message logs `session_owner_unattributed` with the remedy. To attribute one, with the daemon stopped: SQLite, `UPDATE session_metadata SET agent_alias = '<alias>' WHERE session_key = '<key>';` in `data/sessions/sessions.db`; JSONL, write `{"agent_alias": "<alias>"}` to the transcript's `.metadata.json` sidecar in `data/sessions/`. Archiving or deleting the transcript is the other option; the next message then starts a fresh, attributed conversation. The docs page `runtime-state-and-persistence.md` has the same steps under "Legacy session attribution".
  - Ambiguously owned data (two enabled agents bound to one channel) stays fail-closed; restore a unique enabled channel binding.
  - Scoped `sessions_send` no longer creates an unknown session key; establish the session through its owning runtime first. `sessions_list` and `discord_search` enforce the profile's `Read` operation, so restrictive profiles must permit it.
  - Where two enabled Discord aliases watch the same channel, the alias that archives an event first keeps the row and the later observer no longer replaces it.

## Merge order with the overlapping session-backend PRs (proposed)

Several open PRs add authority contracts to `SessionBackend`. Proposed order, so the backend ends up with one claim contract and one effect-time authority shape:

1. **This PR first.** It defines `SessionClaimGrant` / `SessionClaimAuthority` for the inbound claim and `ChannelAuthority` / `NamespaceAuthority` for effect-time reads and writes.
2. **#10412 (@REL-mame)** rebases its `claim_session_agent_alias` / `adopt_session_agent_alias` onto this PR's `SessionOwnerClaim` and `SessionClaimGrant`; its `zeroclaw migrate session-ownership` adopt operation then becomes the command this PR's `session_owner_unattributed` remedy points operators at, replacing the manual edit above.
3. **#11230 (mine)** rebases onto this PR and updates its guard test to the `SessionsListTool::for_agent(backend, security, scope)` constructor; principal scoping and agent/channel scoping compose.
4. **#11234 (mine)** adopts the effect-time callback shape from this PR instead of a parallel `SessionEffectGuard` contract.
5. **#11301 (mine)** and **#10407 (@vrurg)** resolve their `session_sqlite.rs` (and, for #10407, `sessions.rs` / `tools/mod.rs`) textual overlaps at rebase; neither changes the ownership contract.

#11205 is closed. If maintainers prefer #10412's contract to land first, this PR will rebase onto it instead; the adoption rule and the regressions here transfer either way.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the eventual PR landing commit from current `master`; no schema down-migration is required. Transcripts adopted by a sole agent keep their `agent_alias`, which the previous release ignores.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Disabling the affected channel/tool is the immediate containment option.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Unexpected ownership-denial errors, a missing scoped tool for a uniquely configured owner, empty owned Discord results, channel startup errors reporting ambiguous enabled owners, repeated `session_owner_unattributed` errors in a multi-agent install (expected until the legacy transcripts are attributed), or `discord archive row belongs to another alias or channel; not overwritten` debug events for rows an operator expects a given alias to own.

**Earlier validation head:** `640f1c3c47`

prs.title: fix(runtime): report no shell when the native shell cannot be resolved
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A native runtime whose shell is absent (the shell-free distroless `latest` image) advertised POSIX shell access, registered the `shell` tool and told the model it had `sh`, while every command could only fail. With an injected PATH (TUI/ACP) the factory instead failed agent construction.
  - An absent shell is now a missing capability: `NativeRuntime` reports `ShellDialect::None`; `build_shell_command` (and the effective-PATH variant) fail closed; and `shell`, `schedule` and skill `shell`/`script` tools are not registered. `NativeRuntime::new()` and both factory paths decide the same way.
  - "Absent" means every absolute PATH entry (or the absolute `runtime.shell`) was probed and reported `NotFound` or `NotADirectory` (`shell_is_absent`), not the resolver's error kind: the resolver reports the error of *another* PATH entry when the shell is nowhere to be found. Any other probe failure (for example `PermissionDenied` on an unsearchable directory, or a symlink loop in a parent component) does not prove absence: the shell stays "not absent" and the resolver reports its error as before (a construction error with an injected PATH, a failure when the command is built with the ambient PATH).
  - A malformed `runtime.shell` (empty, relative) is still a construction error, and a shell that exists but is unusable (not executable, a directory, a dangling symlink) keeps its earlier behavior.
  - The new shell-absence tests are skipped on Android (`not(target_os = "android")`): it pins `/system/bin/sh` and never reports the shell absent.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Does not add a shell to the image, and does not add the release-container regression test requested in the triage of #9859 (a CI change; follow-up).
  - Does not change Windows, Android or Docker runtime behavior (new code is `cfg(unix)`).
  - Still offering shell-dependent surface without a shell, failing closed through `policy.rs` (`ShellDialect::None` → high risk): `cron_add` / `cron_update` / `cron_run` advertise `job_type: "shell"` (they also create agent jobs). Removing `schedule` also removes its list/cancel/pause actions.
  - Out of this mechanism: `bedrock.rs` and `skills/testing.rs` spawn `sh` directly, not through `RuntimeAdapter`.
  - `with_shell(...)` stays unchecked on purpose (explicit shell, used by tests).
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-config` platform factory and `NativeRuntime`; tool registration in `zeroclaw-runtime` (`all_tools_with_runtime`, `default_tools_with_runtime`, skill tool preparation). Any runtime reporting `ShellDialect::None` no longer registers `shell`; I did not verify whether the wasm runtime reaches these registries.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9859 (not closing it: the container regression test is not included).

### What this does, simply

The official `latest` image has no shell on purpose. Since #10381 the daemon no longer refuses to start without one, but it still told the model it could run shell commands, offered the `shell` tool, and every call failed. This PR makes the runtime say the truth: no shell was found, so shell commands are not offered and any attempt to build one fails with a clear message. Chat turns that need no shell are unaffected.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — covered by the unit and integration tests below; a release-container check is the follow-up left in #9859.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** required CI for `zeroclaw-config` and `zeroclaw-runtime`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no test runs the distroless image; Windows and Android were not built locally.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (WSL Ubuntu 24.04, `-j 1`; head `bca6fd9d7`, which merges `master` `7f39e313e`)
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- platform::` → `83 passed; 0 failed` (on `bca6fd9d7`)
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --test native_shell_absent_ambient_path` → `1 passed` (on `bca6fd9d7`)
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` → pass (on `bca6fd9d7`)
  - On `6afbbcf24`: `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- skills:: tools::` → `1104 passed`; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` and `--tests` with `-D warnings`, and `cargo doc --no-deps -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime` → clean. `bca6fd9d7` only changes tests in `zeroclaw-config`; I did not re-run the runtime commands on it.
  - Earlier runs on `fd9d131a3` / merge commit `809ce20b3` (`cron:: platform:: security::` → `1715 passed`; `agent:: rpc:: sop:: composition::` → `3060 passed`; `scripts/ci/container_build_inputs_gate.sh`, `scripts/dev/act-local.test.sh`) were not repeated.
  - Negative controls: the new tests fail against the earlier probe that read any error as absent (3 failures in `platform::`); the registry and skills controls from before are unchanged.
  - The permission tests (`0o000` directory) return early with a `skipped:` note on stderr when the process runs as root, because permissions are not enforced there. libtest and nextest hide that note for passing tests unless output capture is disabled. Not built or run: Android, Windows.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** On unpatched `master` (`9dbb57231`), with a PATH that contains no `sh`, a throwaway test showed `create_runtime` returning `Ok` with `has_shell_access = true`, profile `sh`, and `build_shell_command` failing. Not verified: a real `/webhook` request, the distroless image itself, Windows/Android builds, `gateway` and `channels` tests. No test plants a relative-PATH decoy (the resolver's handling of relative entries is covered in `executable.rs`; `set_current_dir` is disallowed by clippy here).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no user-visible interface state).
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full-workspace test/clippy skipped for memory limits on the dev machine.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No — the system prompt no longer names a shell when none exists.
- The change only removes capability. Resolution still considers absolute PATH entries only (`executable.rs`), and `shell_is_absent` does the same, so an unresolved shell is never searched for in the workspace (the rule from #10381).

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes, with one behavior change: an injected PATH (TUI/ACP) that is empty, relative-only or lacks the shell used to fail agent construction; it now yields an agent without `shell`/`schedule` and a single WARN per process (a prior status read may have used it up).
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- The no-shell state is computed when the runtime is built, so installing a shell afterwards needs a config reload.
- Trade-off of that rule: probing stops at the first entry that cannot be probed, so a host whose PATH has an unsearchable entry before a readable one that holds the shell is also reported "not absent" (the resolver then decides). That keeps the diagnostic instead of reporting a missing shell.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a one-time WARN `native runtime shell was not found; shell commands are unavailable`; a missing `shell` tool on a host that does have a shell would indicate a wrong "absent" decision.

prs.title: feat(transcription): add default_provider fallback for agents without a transcription alias
prs.body:
## Problem

`TranscriptionManager::transcribe()` fails loud when the runtime agent has no `transcription_provider` configured — there is deliberately no global default. In practice this means voice transcription silently (well, loudly) does nothing for every agent until each one is given its own alias, even when the deployment has exactly one transcription provider and the operator considers it deployment-wide.

## Change

- New optional `[transcription].default_provider`: when set, agents without their own `transcription_provider` fall back to it; agents with their own alias are unaffected. When neither is set, the existing fail-loud behavior is unchanged.
- `TranscriptionManager` gains `resolved_agent_alias()` (agent alias → `default_provider` → empty); `transcribe()` dispatches through it, and the unbound-agent error now points at `[transcription].default_provider` as the remediation.
- The voice path in `telegram.rs` resolves via the same API (`transcribe_with_provider`), keeping its warn-and-skip disposition when nothing is bound.
- The V2→V3 migration used to drop the legacy `[transcription].default_provider` key as having no V3 home; it now carries through, since V3 gains the field back under the same name.

Note: `TranscriptionManager::new`/`from_sections` take the new value as a parameter (all in-repo call sites updated). Happy to switch to reading it from `TranscriptionConfig` inside the constructor if the maintainers prefer a smaller public diff.

## Tests
